The `sync-models` systemd **user service** on amd (Framework laptop) fails on every run. Latest journal evidence (2026-10-22 00:44:49 CDT, `journalctl --user -u sync-models`):

```
[sync-models] Discovered 22 models from Antigravity Language Server
[sync-models] Discovering Codex models...
[sync-models] Discovered 9 models from Codex cache
[sync-models] Error: /nix/.opencode/opencode.jsonc does not exist!
sync-models.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=1/FAILURE
```

Discovery works fine — the failure is purely in resolving the config file the script syncs models into.

## Root cause

`bin/sync-models.mjs` resolves the config relative to its own location:

```js
const ROOT_DIR = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, '..');
const OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH = path.join(ROOT_DIR, '.opencode/opencode.jsonc');
```

That assumption holds in a repo checkout (`<repo>/bin` → `<repo>/.opencode/opencode.jsonc`). But the home-manager unit (`home/common/default.nix`, `systemd.user.services.sync-models`) runs the file from the Nix store: `node ${../../bin/sync-models.mjs}` interpolates to a lone store file (`/nix/store/<hash>-sync-models.mjs`), so `import.meta.dirname` is `/nix/store`, `ROOT_DIR` becomes `/nix`, and the script looks for `/nix/.opencode/opencode.jsonc` — which never exists.

(`POLICY_PATH` has the same store-layout problem, but its loader already tolerates a missing file and falls back to empty defaults, so it degrades silently instead of failing.)

## Fix

Resolve the config path in this order:

1. `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH` env override, if set.
2. The repo-local `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` when it exists (in-checkout runs keep today's behavior).
3. The deployed user config `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` — the file the service actually maintains, and the same file the `opencode-config-normalize` path unit already watches.

## Acceptance

- Installed (store-layout) run no longer dies at the config-exists check; it targets `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`.
- In-repo run behavior unchanged.
- Verified by a dry-run from a store-like layout (script copied alone into a bare directory) passing the config resolution step.

title: codex-proxy follow-up from PR #431: single-source the agy-proxy, clef-proxy and antigravity-ls-proxy ports too
body:
## Finding

PR #431 single-sources the codex-proxy port (18744) and explicitly leaves the same pattern in the sibling proxies as a follow-up — its body and commit message both say: "Follow-up (not in this change): agy-proxy (18743) and clef-proxy have the same two-copies pattern." No issue was ever filed for it (issue searches for `agy-proxy`, `CODEX_PROXY_PORT`, "proxy port" and "codex-proxy" return no tracking issue). This issue files that promised follow-up, and adds a third instance the PR didn't mention.

## Evidence (all on current main, verified 2026-10-20)

- **agy-proxy (18743)** — three copies, identical to the codex case PR #431 fixed:
  - `.opencode/opencode.jsonc:1850`: `"baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18743/v1"` (antigravity-agy provider)
  - `home/common/default.nix:483`: `"AGY_PROXY_PORT=18743"` in the agy-proxy systemd user service
  - `bin/agy-proxy.mjs:7`: fallback `process.env.AGY_PROXY_PORT || '18743'`
- **antigravity-ls-proxy (18745)** — same three copies, not mentioned in PR #431:
  - `.opencode/opencode.jsonc:1932`: `"baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:18745/v1"` (antigravity-ls provider)
  - `home/common/default.nix:529`: `"ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT=18745"` in the service
  - `bin/antigravity-ls-proxy.mjs:7`: fallback `process.env.ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT || '18745'`
- **clef-proxy (18742)** — two copies (no opencode.jsonc consumer; its models go through the Cloudflare gateway, so the copies are the service env and the script fallback):
  - `home/common/default.nix:460`: `"CLEF_PROXY_PORT=18742"`
  - `bin/clef-proxy.mjs:7`: fallback `process.env.CLEF_PROXY_PORT || '18742'`

For comparison, the pattern PR #431 removed for codex was: `home/common/default.nix:506` `"CODEX_PROXY_PORT=18744"` + `.opencode/opencode.jsonc:2668` hardcoded baseURL.

## Why it matters

These are the same silent-drift failure PR #431 fixed for codex: change or collide one copy and the provider dies with an error that looks like a network/auth problem. Leaving them untracked guarantees the pattern is rediscovered per-proxy, one incident at a time.

## Acceptance criteria

- Each proxy's port is defined once (in the `home/common/default.nix` let block, alongside `codexProxyPort`) and flows to its systemd service environment, the shell session variables, and — for agy and antigravity-ls — the opencode.jsonc baseURL, following the PR #431 pattern.
- Any `{env:...}` baseURL introduced by this work handles the variable-unset case consistently with however the CODEX_PROXY_PORT unset case is resolved (the scripts' built-in fallbacks and the client config must not be able to disagree).
- A grep for the literal ports `18742`/`18743`/`18745` in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` and the service `Environment` lists in `home/common/default.nix` returns no remaining hardcoded copies (script fallbacks may keep the literal as the documented default).

title: codex-proxy: PR #431's {env:CODEX_PROXY_PORT} baseURL has no fallback — opencode outside a home-manager shell gets an empty port
body:
## Finding

PR #431 single-sources the codex-proxy port by changing the `openai-codex` provider's baseURL in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` from the hardcoded `http://127.0.0.1:18744/v1` to `http://127.0.0.1:{env:CODEX_PROXY_PORT}/v1`. The only place the new variable is set is `home.sessionVariables` (`home/common/default.nix`, from the single `codexProxyPort` definition) — i.e. it exists only in processes that inherit a home-manager shell session's environment.

OpenCode's `{env:VAR}` substitution has **no fallback**: a missing variable substitutes the empty string. In developing-today/opencode, `packages/core/src/config/variable.ts` (substitute function): `const value = (input.env?.[name] ?? process.env[name]) || ""`. So any opencode process launched without `CODEX_PROXY_PORT` in its environment gets baseURL `http://127.0.0.1:/v1` — a dead provider, and exactly the "looks like a network/auth problem" failure mode PR #431 set out to eliminate. The proxy script itself keeps a fallback (`bin/codex-proxy.mjs:7`: `process.env.CODEX_PROXY_PORT || '18744'`); after this PR the client side no longer has one, so the two sides can now disagree in the opposite direction: proxy listening on 18744, client dialling port "".

## Evidence

- PR #431 (OPEN, head `5be5217f`): `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` baseURL becomes `http://127.0.0.1:{env:CODEX_PROXY_PORT}/v1`; `home/common/default.nix` sets `CODEX_PROXY_PORT = toString codexProxyPort;` only under `home.sessionVariables`.
- PR #431's verification only covers the variable-set case: "a test server with `CODEX_PROXY_PORT=18744` in its environment resolved the provider from the substituted config correctly." The unset case is untested.
- Concrete unset launch path, verified today: the Muse sandbox's `opencode serve` runs as a systemd service whose environment file (`~/tools/secrets.d/opencode-serve.env`) sets the proxy/CA/Cloudflare keys and the PR #430 feature flags but **not** `CODEX_PROXY_PORT` (key list checked 2026-10-20), while its deployed config is this repo's `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Merging #431 as-is turns that server's codex provider from "works when the proxy runs" into "empty port, always dead". Desktop/VS Code launches and other service contexts have the same exposure wherever they don't source the shell session variables.

## Why it matters

The hardcoded port worked in *every* launch context; the env-substituted one silently works only in shell-launched ones. This reintroduces the PR's own failure mode (silently dead provider, misleading error) for a different — and already existing — class of launches.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `CODEX_PROXY_PORT` unset, the `openai-codex` provider's resolved baseURL still points at the proxy's fallback port (18744), OR every supported way of launching opencode with this config (shell, systemd service, desktop/VS Code) demonstrably receives the variable, with the sandbox `opencode-serve` service as the worked example.
- A check or test pins the unset-variable behaviour so it can't regress silently (e.g. rendering/validating the effective config with the variable unset).
- The solution keeps PR #431's single-source property: one definition of the port that all consumers derive from.

title: cold-store-reaper: export-turso.sh passes Turso platform token and per-DB JWTs to curl in argv (process-list exposure, PR #993)

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/cold-store-reaper
labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/scripts/export-turso.sh` (added by PR #993) passes Turso credentials to `curl` as `-H "Authorization: Bearer …"` **argv elements**. Command-line arguments are world-readable via the process list (`ps`, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`) for the whole life of the curl process — this is exactly the exposure pattern this repo has already removed twice:

- #948 / PR #970 removed credential-bearing argv from `push-fleet-feed.sh`.
- #983 / PR #986 removed the R2 secret from `cold_store.py`'s curl argv, moving it to a curl config fed on stdin (`_curl_fetch`, `--config -`). PR #986 merged the same day PR #993 introduced the Turso script with the old pattern.

## Evidence (verified on current main `76672b97df023607d8469d462f21420604fe92d5`, cross-checked via `gh pr diff 993` and the local clone)

`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/scripts/export-turso.sh`:

- Line 58–59: platform token in argv, `--max-time 60`
  ```
  curl -fsS --max-time 60 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TURSO_PLATFORM_API_TOKEN}" \
    "${API_BASE}/v1/organizations/${ORG}/databases"
  ```
- Line 93–94: platform token again in argv for the per-database token mint (`-X POST …/auth/tokens`), `--max-time 60`.
- Line 120–121: the minted per-database JWT in argv for the dump download, `--max-time 300` — up to five minutes of exposure per database:
  ```
  curl -fsS --max-time 300 \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}" \
    "${dump_url}" -o "${dump_sql}"
  ```

The script's own header says "the script stores nothing and never prints a token value" — true for logs and disk, but argv is a third channel it does not cover. The platform token is long-lived and org-wide (it can mint per-database tokens); the per-DB JWTs are shorter-lived but grant full dump access to that database's contents while valid.

Deduped 2026-10-26: `gh issue list --search 'turso curl argv'`, `--search 'export-turso'`, and `--search 'Bearer argv process list'` return no existing issue. #983/#986 are closed and cover `cold_store.py` only, not this script.

## Why it matters

Anyone (or any process) able to read the process list on the machine running the nightly backup can harvest the Turso platform token during any of the three curl windows — the dump download window is up to 300s per database, every night. This reintroduces a credential-exposure class the fleet explicitly decided to eliminate (#948, #983).

## Acceptance criteria

- No Turso credential (platform token or per-database JWT) appears in any process's argv during `export-turso.sh` runs: credentials reach curl via a non-argv channel (e.g. the stdin curl-config pattern `_curl_fetch` established in #986, with the header value escaped the same way).
- A regression test in the existing Turso test harness (`TestTursoExportScript`) asserts no argv element of any spawned curl contains the platform token or a minted JWT (the #986 argv-guard test is the precedent).
- Existing behaviour unchanged: skip contract when `TURSO_PLATFORM_API_TOKEN` is unset, per-database failure isolation, integrity-check gating, and the existing fake-Turso tests all still pass.
- The script header comment is updated so its credential-handling claim covers argv as well as logs/disk.

Source: PR #993 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/993 (commits `db58a67`, `00410ed`). Filed by the pr-diff-review job, 2026-10-26.

title: id(web): link/image destinations with a space are silently rewritten to %20 on save — angle-bracket form lost, relative file links break

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Summary

A link or image destination that contains a space is silently rewritten to its `%20`-encoded form on save, and the ProseMirror document itself changes (no round-trip fixpoint at the PM level). The angle-bracket destination the author wrote — the only CommonMark form that carries a space verbatim — is never re-emitted.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-26 on main `786d2129`, standalone verbatim-codec probe)

Probe: `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1615/out4.log` (crate = current `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` copied verbatim + round-trip harness).

Markdown → PM → markdown:

```
IN : "[notes](<my notes.md>)\n"
PM : href "my notes.md"
OUT: "[notes](my%20notes.md)\n"
PM2: href "my%20notes.md"        SAMEPM: false

IN : "![a](<my pic.png>)\n"
PM : src "my pic.png"
OUT: "![a](my%20pic.png)\n"
PM2: src "my%20pic.png"          SAMEPM: false
```

PM → markdown shows the same: an editor-created link with `href: "https://e.com/a b"` saves as `[t](https://e.com/a%20b)` and reparses with the mutated href (probe case `link-href-space`, `out3.log`).

## Why it matters

The codec passes destinations verbatim in both directions (`markdown.rs:299` parse arm copies `link.url` into the PM `href`; `markdown.rs:1223` save arm copies it back into `NodeLink.url`) — the mutation happens in comrak's CommonMark renderer, which percent-encodes a space in a bare destination instead of emitting the `<…>` angle form. For an absolute URL the encoded form usually still resolves, but for a **relative file link** — the common case in id's own documents — `my%20notes.md` names a file that does not exist, so one save silently breaks the link. It also means the editor's in-memory href and the file's href diverge after the first save.

## Acceptance criteria

- Round trip preserves a destination containing a space exactly: `[notes](<my notes.md>)` saves byte-identically (angle form retained), and PM → markdown → PM returns the identical `href`/`src`.
- Same for image `src`.
- Destinations without spaces are unchanged; existing web::markdown tests pass.

## Suggested direction

The fix layer needs a triage decision: comrak's renderer offers no angle-destination option, so options are (a) a targeted post-process of the rendered output for destinations known (from the AST) to contain spaces, (b) pre-render substitution with a placeholder that is restored afterwards, or (c) documenting + normalizing on the parse side instead (accept `%20` in PM as canonical — but that still rewrites the user's file on first save). Any of these beats the current silent mutation; (a)/(b) preserve the file.

title: id(web): saving a table cell with a hard break or a list panics in the markdown codec — ill-formed comrak AST

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Summary

Saving a document whose table cell contains anything other than plain paragraph text can **panic** in the markdown codec: `prosemirror_to_markdown` builds an ill-formed comrak AST and `format_commonmark` panics instead of returning markdown (or an error).

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-26 on main `786d2129`, standalone verbatim-codec probe)

Probe: `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1615/` (crate = current `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` copied verbatim + round-trip harness).

Case 1 — a `hard_break` inside a table cell (PM JSON: table → table_row → table_cell → paragraph → text `line1`, `hard_break`, text `line2`):

```
thread 'main' panicked at comrak-0.56.0/src/cm.rs:29:9:
The document to format is ill-formed: InvalidChildType {
  parent: <TableCell> [<Text("line1")>, <LineBreak>, <Text("line2")>],
  child: <LineBreak> }
```

Case 2 — a `bullet_list` inside a table cell: same panic, `InvalidChildType { parent: <TableCell>, child: <List …> }`.

## Root cause

`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:1090-1110` (`json_to_ast`, table-cell special case): paragraph children are unwrapped inline into the cell, and **any non-paragraph child is also appended directly to the cell node** via `append_inline_child` (:1106) — including block nodes (lists, code blocks, quotes). `hard_break` maps to `NodeValue::LineBreak` (:1074), which comrak's CommonMark renderer also rejects as a direct child of `TableCell`. comrak validates the tree in `format_commonmark` and panics on the ill-formed AST; the codec returns `Result<_, ConversionError>` everywhere else, so this input escapes the error channel entirely. In the server this is a panic on the save path for a document the editor can plausibly produce (Shift+Enter inside a cell; pasted/structured content with a list in a cell).

Related, already tracked separately: multi-paragraph cells fuse words (#1003) — that is the paragraph-unwrap path; this issue is the non-paragraph / LineBreak path that crashes outright.

## Acceptance criteria

- `prosemirror_to_markdown` never panics for any PM doc the schema can express in a table cell; ill-supported cell content degrades to a defined representation (e.g. hard break → space or literal text; block content → flattened inline text) or returns `ConversionError`.
- Regression tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` covering at least: hard_break in a cell, list in a cell, code_block in a cell — each asserting a non-panicking, content-preserving-as-possible output and a stable second save (fixpoint).
- Existing markdown codec tests still pass.

## Suggested direction

In the table-cell special case, sanitize children before appending: convert `LineBreak` to a space/text node inside cells, and flatten non-inline block children to their inline text (or reject with `ConversionError::UnknownType`-style error) instead of attaching them under `TableCell`.

title: cold-store-reaper: D1 manifest schema still lacks the v1.2 'evicted' CHECK — first evict --apply will break nightly sync-manifest (follow-up left by PRs #965/#971)

body:
## Finding

The cold-store-reaper's local manifest schema and the hosted D1 copy of it have drifted, and the drift is documented in the repo but tracked nowhere:

- PR #971 (merged 2026-10-26, `feat(cold-store-reaper): v4 — R2 S3 client, backup-supabase, eviction`) added the `objects.state = 'evicted'` value as schema v1.2. Local manifests are migrated in place (`ColdStore._migrate_objects_evicted`), but the D1 copy is not.
- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/schema.sql` lines 3–5 (current main `d715adf9`): "v1.2 (reaper v4): objects.state gains 'evicted' … The D1 copy of this schema needs the same one-line CHECK change before evicted rows can sync; sync-manifest fails on the objects statement…"
- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/README.md` lines 256–261 says the same: until the D1 CHECK change is applied, "`sync-manifest` fails on the `objects` statement with D1's own error text (the same caveat the v1.1 `'trash'` direction had)".
- The same pattern already happened once: PR #965 (v3, schema v1.1) added the `'trash'` ledger direction with the identical caveat for prune rows.

Consequence: the first time anyone runs `cold-store evict --apply` (the eviction trial PR #971 prepares), the local manifest gains `'evicted'` rows and every subsequent `sync-manifest` — including the nightly run in `scripts/nightly-backup.sh`, step 4, which runs under `set -e` — fails on the objects statement until someone applies the D1 change by hand. Nothing files or tracks that prerequisite; it exists only as a README/schema comment.

## Why it matters

Eviction is presented as ready (`evict --apply` ships in v4, the nightly files the source backups it will evict), but its prerequisite D1 migration is an undocumented-in-GitHub manual step. The failure mode is also badly timed: it surfaces in the nightly *after* objects have already been deleted from R2, breaking manifest sync at exactly the moment the hosted manifest matters most.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The D1 `cold-store-manifest` database's `objects` table CHECK constraint accepts `'evicted'` (and `transfer_ledger.direction` is confirmed to accept `'trash'` from v1.1, if that was never actually applied either).
- [ ] Verified end-to-end: a manifest containing at least one `'evicted'` object row (and one `'trash'` ledger row) completes `sync-manifest` against D1 without the CHECK error.
- [ ] The caveat text in `schema.sql` and `README.md` is updated to record that the D1 change is applied (with a date), or replaced by a repeatable migration step in the repo so the next schema extension (v1.3+) cannot drift the same way.
- [ ] No `evict --apply` run is treated as complete before the sync verification above passes.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PRs #965 and #971 against current main.

title: security(cold-store-reaper): PR #976's curl S3 fallback passes the R2 secret in argv — the pattern #948/#970 removed the same day

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/cold-store-reaper

body:
## Finding

PR #976 (merged 2026-10-26, `fix(cold-store-reaper): curl fallback for S3 downloads urllib cannot deliver`) added a curl fallback for S3 downloads in `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py`. The fallback passes the R2 credentials to curl as a command-line argument:

- `cold_store.py` `_curl_fetch` (on current main `d715adf9`, ~lines 1526–1545) builds `argv = [curl, "-sS", "--fail", "--aws-sigv4", "aws:amz:auto:s3", "--user", f"{access}:{secret}", url]` and runs it with `subprocess.run`. The docstring acknowledges it: "Credentials travel in argv — the local process list sees them, as with any credentialed CLI".
- Introduced in PR #976, commit `14617a5958` (`fix(cold-store-reaper): curl fallback for S3 downloads urllib cannot deliver`).

Any local process can read another process's argv (`ps`, `/proc/<pid>/cmdline`), so the bucket-scoped `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` is exposed for the whole duration of the download — and this fallback exists specifically for the *large* objects, with `S3_CURL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900`, so the exposure window can be minutes long. The PR does scrub the credentials from error text, but that does not address the argv exposure itself.

## Why it matters

This is the exact pattern this repo removed the same day, twice:

- Issue #948 / PR #970 (merged ~1 hour before #976): the fleet-feed push's socat `ProxyCommand` embedded `proxyauth=<user>:<pw>` in process argv; the fix replaced it with an in-process CONNECT relay that keeps the credential off every process's argv, and added `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/push-fleet-feed.guard.sh`, whose stated rule is: "proxy credential must never be an argv token". That guard only covers `push-fleet-feed.sh`, so #976's reintroduction in another package was not caught.
- The scrubbing in #976 protects logs, not the process list — the leak channel #948 was about.

Fix direction (triage decides): keep the credential out of argv — e.g. hand curl its config via a stdin config (`curl -K -` / `--config` from a pipe or a mode-600 temp file that is unlinked after use, with `user = "access:secret"` inside), or sign the request in-process like the urllib path already does and let curl send a pre-signed request, or another mechanism the worker verifies. The byte-count verification and the one-attempt semantics of the fallback must stay.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The R2 access key / secret never appear in any spawned process's argv on the curl fallback path (verifiable: a test stubs `subprocess.run` — or inspects the spawned argv — and asserts neither credential value is present in any argv element).
- [ ] The curl fallback still works end-to-end: existing `TestS3CurlFallback` coverage (fallback only after urllib exhaustion, byte-count verified against caller size or HEAD, errors scrubbed and named) passes, updated for the new credential channel.
- [ ] Credentials remain scrubbed from all error text raised on this path.
- [ ] Consider a repo-level guard in the spirit of `push-fleet-feed.guard.sh` so a `--user <access>:<secret>`-style argv pattern in `cold_store.py` fails a check instead of relying on review to catch it.
- [ ] The `_curl_fetch` docstring / README wording no longer presents argv credentials as acceptable.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #976 against current main.

title: id(web): marked spans crossing a soft line break corrupt or fragment on save — single-mark, non-fixpoint

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Summary

In the id web editor's markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), a **single-mark span that crosses a soft line break** corrupts on save. When a strong/em/strikethrough span wraps across lines in the source file, saving multiplies the delimiters, inserts ` ` entities, and the result is **not a fixpoint** — every subsequent save makes it worse. A link spanning a soft break does not corrupt but **fragments** into one link per word, including a link whose entire text is a single space.

This is distinct from #968: that issue needs *different overlapping* mark sets on adjacent nodes and notes that single-mark cases round-trip cleanly. Here every text node carries the *identical* single mark — the trigger is the soft break inside the span, which is ordinary wrapped prose (any bold sentence longer than one line).

## Evidence (verified this run on main 24261355)

Standalone probe crate compiling the verbatim codec from `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, markdown → ProseMirror → markdown, twice (logs: goal workspace `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1015/out2.log`):

| Input | After 1st save | After 2nd save |
|---|---|---|
| `**bold\nmore**` | `**bold**** ****more**` | `**bold**\*\* \***more**` (changes again) |
| `*em\nmore*` | `*em** **more*` | `*em*\* \**more*` (changes again) |
| `~~gone\naway~~` | `~~gone~~~~ ~~~~away~~` | `~~gone\~\~\~\~ \~\~\~\~away~~` (changes again) |
| `[a\nb](https://e.com "T")` | `[a](https://e.com "T")[ ](https://e.com "T")[b](https://e.com "T")` | stable, but fragmented |

The parse is faithful: `**bold\nmore**` parses to three text nodes — `bold` [strong], ` ` [strong], `more` [strong]. The middle node comes from the `NodeValue::SoftBreak` arm (markdown.rs:238-241), which emits a standalone `" "` text node carrying the active marks. On the emit side that whitespace-only marked node is rendered by `create_marked_text` / `build_mark_chain` (markdown.rs:1117 / :1167) as its own delimited span (`**** ****`), and re-parsing the result creates new mark boundaries — hence the per-save growth. Links take the same path and fragment instead of corrupting.

## Why it matters

Wrapped bold/italic/linked text is everywhere in real notes and docs. Opening such a file in the web editor and saving it — even with no edits — rewrites it into entity-escaped, delimiter-doubled text (or a chain of one-word links), and repeated saves compound the damage. Silent data corruption of user documents.

## Suggested directions (either may be sufficient; check both)

- Parse side: fold a soft break into the adjacent text node (append `" "` to the previous text node when it carries the same marks) instead of emitting a standalone marked `" "` node.
- Emit side: merge adjacent text nodes with identical mark sets before building the mark chain, and/or never emit a delimited span for a whitespace-only node.
- Coordinate with #968 — the emit-side half of this may share its fix in `build_mark_chain`; if that fix demonstrably covers these inputs too, close this as a duplicate with a pointer. A fix for #968's listed inputs alone does **not** cover this issue (no nesting here).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `**bold\nmore**`, `*em\nmore*`, `~~gone\naway~~` round-trip open → save to the single-line normalized form (`**bold more**` etc.) with no ` ` and no multiplied delimiters, and a second round-trip is a fixpoint.
- [ ] `[a\nb](url)` (with and without title) round-trips as one link, not three.
- [ ] New unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover marked spans crossing soft breaks, including the double round-trip property.
- [ ] Existing codec tests still pass; #944 / #953 / #968 cases do not regress.

title: fix(cold-store-reaper): pack writes orphan frames and inflates member_count/live_bytes when one call gets duplicate content

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Bug

`ColdStore.pack()` in `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py` writes a compressed frame for **every** file it is given, but the manifest records members under the schema's primary key `(bundle_id, object_hash)` (`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/schema.sql`: `members` table, `PRIMARY KEY (bundle_id, object_hash)`). When one `pack` call receives duplicate content — the same file twice, or two different files with identical bytes — the frames after the first are written into the bundle but their member rows are silently swallowed by `INSERT OR IGNORE`, and the bundle accounting is inflated.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `a2eef6f7`)

`pack()` is at `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:432`; it appends one frame per input file and builds `members` with one entry per file, then inserts with `INSERT OR IGNORE` and records `member_count = len(members)` and `live_bytes = sum(m["size"] for m in members)`.

Reproduction (no network, local zstd): create two files with identical content (`b"identical content " * 10`, 180 bytes each) and pack both in one call:

- pack result: `{'bundle_id': 'b_f693af7b02a2cda0', 'bytes': 76, 'members': 2}`
- bundle file is 76 bytes = the 38-byte zstd frame written **twice**
- `bundles` row: `member_count = 2`, `live_bytes = 360`
- `members` table: **1 row** (`offset 0, length 38`)
- `objects` table: 1 row (180 bytes)

Packing the same path twice in one call produces the identical result. The second frame (bytes 38–76 of the bundle) is unreachable orphan data: no member row points at it, `fetch` can never read it, and `member_count`/`live_bytes` overstate what the bundle actually holds. The bundle is then uploaded to Drive at the inflated size, and the D1 manifest sync propagates the wrong `member_count`/`live_bytes`.

## Why it matters

Cold-store bundles are the archive of record: wasted space is uploaded and kept forever, and the accounting fields (`member_count`, `live_bytes`) are what later compaction/reaping decisions will trust. A pack list built from a directory walk can easily contain duplicate content (hardlinked or copied files), so this is reachable in normal use, not just a pathological call.

## Acceptance criteria

- Packing duplicate content in one call stores each distinct object exactly once: the bundle contains one frame per distinct object hash, OR `pack` refuses duplicate content with a clear `ColdStoreError` before writing anything (either behavior is acceptable; silently writing orphan frames is not).
- After such a pack, `bundles.member_count` equals the number of rows in `members` for that bundle, and `live_bytes` equals the sum of the member objects' sizes.
- A regression test in `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/tests/test_cold_store.py` packs duplicate content (same file twice and/or two identical files) and asserts the bundle bytes, `member_count`, `live_bytes`, and `members` rows agree.
- Existing cold-store tests still pass: `python3 -m unittest discover -s pkgs/cold-store-reaper/tests`.
- No behavior change for packs whose inputs are all distinct.

title: security(cf-container-hello): unauthenticated probe Worker fronts a stale unhardened crawler copy — SSRF / file:// fetch (from PR #935)

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/lab-ops-hub
labels.description: Package/app: lab-ops-hub (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: app/cf-container-hello
labels.description: Package/app: cf-container-hello (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding — security: `pkgs/cf-container-hello` ships an unauthenticated Worker in front of a stale, unhardened crawler copy (SSRF / local-file fetch)

PR #935 (merged, head `92d0c6ee`, commits `4a508974`, `60656e73`, `92d0c6ee`) added the diagnostic probe package `pkgs/cf-container-hello` and kept it as the "known-good container reference". Two halves combine into an exposed fetch proxy:

1. **The Worker has no auth gate at all.** `pkgs/cf-container-hello/src/index.ts` (whole file, verified on main `a2eef6f7`) contains no `Authorization` / token check. `fetch()` routes by path prefix: `/probe…` forwards the request as-is to the `CrawlerProbe` container (`getContainer(env.CRAWLER_PROBE, "probe-2").fetch(request)`), `/lite…` and `/name/…` forward to other containers, and anything else goes to the hello container.
2. **The container it fronts is the pre-hardening crawler.** `pkgs/cf-container-hello/image/app.py` `Handler.do_POST` (~lines 76–103) does `url = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length))["url"]` then `urllib.request.urlopen(Request(url), timeout=20, context=CTX)` — no scheme allowlist, no localhost/private-IP policy, no redirect re-validation, and returns the fetched page's extracted text (up to 20,000 chars) as JSON.

Contrast with the production crawler this was copied from: `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/container/app.py` carries an extensive `validate_crawl_url` SSRF policy (the #441 policy, hardened further in #516/#526/#529/#572/#593/#614 — public http(s) only, no localhost-style names, no non-global IP literals, redirect targets held to the same policy, container re-validates independently as defence-in-depth), and `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/index.ts` gates `/api/*` behind the `API_TOKEN` secret, fail-closed (503 when unconfigured, 401 when unauthenticated). The probe copy has none of either layer. The deployed image for the probe is also a stale fork: `pkgs/cf-container-hello/image/container-image-v4.nix` builds this 103-line `app.py`, while production moved to `:v5` built from the hardened `container/app.py` (PR #935 body).

### Verified locally (2026-10-26, this run)

Ran the exact committed `pkgs/cf-container-hello/image/app.py` on localhost and probed `POST /crawl`:

- `{"url":"file:///etc/hostname"}` → handler returned **200**. `urllib` accepted the `file://` scheme and read the local file — there is no scheme validation anywhere in the handler. (Extracted text was empty for that file in the sandbox, but the fetch executed; on the container image the same path reads whatever the process can read and returns its text content.)
- `{"url":"http://127.0.0.1:8080/"}` → the loopback fetch was **attempted with no policy block** (it blocked the single-threaded server on itself until the client timed out). No localhost/private-range check exists.

### Why it matters

PR #935's body says the clean-room Worker was deployed and used live for the container diagnosis, and the package is kept (README: "known-good container reference", `wrangler.jsonc` name `cf-container-hello`). If that deployment (workers.dev or any route) is still live, anyone on the internet has an unauthenticated SSRF/local-file fetch proxy that also burns container minutes. Even if it is currently undeployed, the committed source deploys that way by default — the next diagnostic session that runs `npm run deploy` re-exposes it.

This is a single-repo finding (code only): the production lab-ops-hub crawler is hardened and gated; only the probe copy is exposed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Determine whether the `cf-container-hello` Worker is currently deployed/routed anywhere; record the answer on this issue. If live and unauthenticated, take it down or gate it immediately.
- [ ] `pkgs/cf-container-hello/src/index.ts`: every route that forwards to a container (at minimum `/probe`) requires the same class of bearer-token gate lab-ops-hub uses, fail-closed when the secret is unset — or the forwarding routes are removed.
- [ ] `pkgs/cf-container-hello/image/app.py`: the stale crawler copy is eliminated as a divergence risk — either build the probe image from the production hardened `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/container/app.py`, or port its `validate_crawl_url` policy verbatim (public http(s) only; no `file:`/other schemes; no localhost/private/non-global targets; redirects re-validated).
- [ ] A regression test/probe shows `file://`, `http://127.0.0.1/`, a private-range IP literal, and a redirect to a private target are all rejected by the probe crawler, and an unauthenticated `POST /probe/crawl` is rejected by the Worker.

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

In the id web editor's markdown codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), inline code combined with any other mark loses the other mark on save. The link case is destructive: a linked code span stops being a link.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Round-trip probe on main `a2eef6f7` (standalone crate compiling the verbatim `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` against comrak 0.56.0 + serde_json, `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown`; full log in the goal's `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-0312/out4.log`):

| Input | PM marks on the text node | Saved output |
|---|---|---|
| `` [`code`](https://x.test) `` | `[link(href), code]` | `` `code` `` — **link gone** |
| `[a `code` b](https://x.test)` | link on all three segments, code additionally on the middle | `[a ](https://x.test)`code`[ b](https://x.test)` — **link fragmented, code segment unlinked** |
| `` **`code`** `` | `[strong, code]` | `` `code` `` — strong gone |
| `` *`code`* `` | `[em, code]` | `` `code` `` — em gone |
| `` ~~`code`~~ `` | `[strikethrough, code]` | `` `code` `` — strikethrough gone |
| `` `code` `` (control) | `[code]` | `` `code` `` — correct |

## Root cause

`create_marked_text` (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:1117`, code-precedence early return at :1122-1130): when a `code` mark is present it returns a bare `NodeValue::Code` node immediately, discarding every other mark in the list instead of wrapping the code node in the remaining mark chain (`build_mark_chain`, :1167). The parse direction preserves the combination correctly (see the PM column above), so this is save-direction only.

## Why it matters

Linked code spans (`` [`api_name`](url) ``) are idiomatic in technical notes — exactly the id editor's home turf. One open + save silently unlinks them and rewrites surrounding links into fragments. Same family as #943/#944/#945 (save-direction codec corruption), distinct mechanism.

## Acceptance criteria

- `` [`code`](https://x.test) `` round-trips open→save with the link intact around the code span.
- `[a `code` b](https://x.test)` round-trips as one link containing the code segment.
- `**`code`**`, *`code`*, ~~`code`~~ round-trip with both marks preserved.
- Plain `` `code` `` and the existing codec tests are unchanged; new unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover the code+link and code+strong combinations.
- Saved output is a stable fixpoint on a second round-trip.

## Suggested fix

In `create_marked_text`, when the code mark is present, build the `Code` node first and then wrap it in the chain built from the remaining marks (mirroring `build_mark_chain`), instead of returning early. Note the wrapper order must match the non-code path so nesting (e.g. link outside, code inside) renders as `` [`code`](href) ``.

This one is cross-repo: the evidence was gathered in this repo's PR, the suspected defect is in developing-today/openchamber's config handling. One issue tracks the set (filed here, where the PR was reviewed).

## Evidence

- PR #921 (commits `4d9026b5`, `32ad9377`; merged `46147f67cf1`), body section "One half of the bug is NOT fixed here — flagged with evidence": "`antigravity-ls` also resolved to an empty port in that same serve, **despite** `ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT=18745` being present in the serving process's environ. That points at OpenChamber's own config handling (it demonstrably rewrites some baseURLs — `claude-code`'s effective baseURL there is an OpenChamber-assigned concrete port, not the config value), not at the environment this repo controls. … it needs OpenChamber-side investigation and can only be verified at the laptop's next switch/respawn."
- The environment half is verified fixed on current main in this repo: `home/common/default.nix:24` defines `claudeCodeProxyPort = 18749;` and the `home.sessionVariables` block now exports `MUSE_PROXY_PORT`, `COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT` from the let bindings — so the remaining variable is OpenChamber-side handling of the `{env:ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT:-18745}` baseURL template.
- Affected repos: **developing-today/code** (evidence: PR #921 body + commit `32ad9377` message; config template in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`) and **developing-today/openchamber** (suspected defect: baseURL/env-template resolution in its serve config handling).

## Why it matters

The antigravity-ls provider is silently broken in the laptop's OpenChamber serve — requests go to a port-less URL and fail — and the only record of the defect was prose in a merged PR body, which no sweep or queue will ever pick up. The commandcode half of the same bug is fixed, which makes this half easy to mistake for resolved.

## Acceptance criteria

- At the laptop's next switch/respawn, the OpenChamber serve's effective `antigravity-ls` baseURL is captured (with `ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT` confirmed in the process environ) and the reproduction is recorded on this issue.
- The point in OpenChamber where the `{env:…}` baseURL template is dropped or rewritten to an empty port is identified, **or** the root cause is documented on this issue with a landed workaround.
- After the fix/workaround, the antigravity-ls provider works in the OpenChamber serve with the env var present.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #921. Dedupe: searches for `antigravity` / `antigravity-ls empty port` in both developing-today/code and developing-today/openchamber returned no matching issue (#916, #894, #480, #437 are different defects). Related triage note: PR #921 also partially satisfies open #894 (its `CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT` / `claudeCodeProxyPort` items now exist on main).

body:
## Finding

`isOrchestrationSection` validates only the orchestration section's top level, but the today-view consumer dereferences nested per-goal arrays unconditionally. A section that **passes** the validator can still crash `/today` and `/api/today.json` with a `TypeError` instead of falling back to the locally derived view.

## Evidence

- PR #900 (commit `92d17e356135`) added the validator at `pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:38` (current main `a2eef6f7920a`). It checks only `version`/`generatedAt`/`runId`, that `tiers.needsDrew`/`tiers.needsOrchestrator` are arrays, and that `dependencies`/`goals`/`actions` are arrays. It never checks `provenance`, nor any per-goal field, nor tier-item fields.
- PR #901's `todayFromSection` (current main `pm-stack/aggregator/src/derive.ts`) dereferences the unvalidated fields: `g.linedUp.filter(...)` (:595), `g.stalled.filter` and `g.linedUp.flatMap` (:614-615), `...g.gaps` (:622), `g.progressedSinceLastRun` (:618), `section.actions.slice` (:630).
- Reproduced against current main with a section whose single goal omits `linedUp`: `isOrchestrationSection(s) === true`, then `todayFromSection(s)` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'g.linedUp.filter')`.
- PR #900's own tests (`pm-stack/aggregator/test/orchestration.test.ts:50,56`) only reject a wrong version / missing top-level tier arrays — no nested-shape case exists.

## Why it matters

The section is produced by an LLM-run orchestration job writing JSON by hand — exactly the producer a structural check exists to fail-soft against. The validator's documented contract (feed.ts comment: "Absent or malformed = 'not measured'") promises the derived fallback; instead, one malformed goal takes down the today view with a 500, which is the aggregator's headline page.

## Acceptance criteria

- The validator rejects (or the consumer tolerates) a goal missing any of `linedUp`/`stalled`/`gaps`/`progressedSinceLastRun`, and a section missing `provenance`.
- Regression tests mirror `orchestration.test.ts` for the nested cases (goal missing each array in turn).
- For such a feed, `/today` and `/api/today.json` return the locally derived view, not an error.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PRs #900 and #901 against current main (one finding covering both PRs: #900 introduced the validator, #901 the consumer). Dedupe: searches for `isOrchestrationSection` / `orchestration linedUp validator` returned only the closed implementation issue #899.

title: security(aggregator): fleet-feed push exposes the proxy credential in process argv and disables SSH host-key verification

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Finding

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/push-fleet-feed.sh` (added by PR #892, commit `46584cefaef5`) hands the egress-proxy credential to `socat` by interpolating it into the SSH `ProxyCommand` string, so the proxy username/password appears in the `ssh`/`scp`/`socat` process command lines — readable by any local user via `ps` for the duration of every ~5-minute feed push. The same connection disables SSH host-key verification entirely.

## Evidence (current main `a2eef6f7920a`)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/push-fleet-feed.sh:48`:
  `proxycmd = f"socat - PROXY:{u.hostname}:100.99.113.103:22,proxyport=3130,proxyauth={user}:{pw}"`
- `:54` passes it as `-o ProxyCommand={proxycmd}` to `scp` and `ssh` (`:60-67`). Command lines are world-readable on Linux (`/proc/<pid>/cmdline`), so the shared proxy credential — read at runtime from `HTTPS_PROXY` / the mcpx daemon env — is exposed to any process on the sandbox for each push window.
- `:50-51`: `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` with `UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null` — the laptop's host key is never verified, on a connection authenticated with the sandbox's `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`. A spoofed endpoint on the proxy route silently receives the feed push and the remote `mv`.
- `git grep proxyauth origin/main` hits only this file — the pattern exists nowhere else in the repo.

The credential itself is **not** in the diff or the repo (it is read from a file/env at runtime) — this is about the hand-off mechanism, not a committed secret.

## Why it matters

The proxy credential is a shared fleet secret (the same egress proxy mcpx uses). argv is the weakest place a secret can sit: it needs no file permission, no ptrace, no root — just `ps`. And with host-key checking off, the SSH transport the push relies on provides authentication of the client but none of the server, so the credential exposure and the MITM surface compound on the same connection.

## Acceptance criteria

- The proxy credential no longer appears in any process command line (e.g. env/fd-based hand-off to `socat`, or a mode-600 config file socat reads), verified by inspecting `ps`/`/proc` during a push.
- The laptop host key is pinned and verified (checked-in known-hosts entry, or Tailscale SSH), and a push to a mismatched key fails.
- A grep-level guard or test asserts neither `proxyauth=` interpolation nor `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` reappears in `push-fleet-feed.sh`.
- Normal fleet-feed pushes keep working end to end (feed arrives on the laptop, remote `mv` completes).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #892 against current main. Dedupe: searches for `proxyauth` / `StrictHostKeyChecking push-fleet-feed` returned no existing issue.

title: ci(flake-inputs-update): failure-issue history grows unbounded — the tracking issue will exceed GitHub's body limit and stop updating

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Finding

The `flake-inputs-update` workflow's failure-tracking issue accumulates its entire `## Failure history` verbatim on every failed attempt, with no cap, trim, or rotation. Once the rebuilt body exceeds GitHub's 65,536-character issue-body limit, `gh issue edit` is rejected and the tracking issue silently freezes — exactly when a failure has become chronic and the issue matters most.

## Evidence

- PR #907 (commit `9e95477519e07a880ea7aab5e3c5e79b5c825aa5`) introduced the workflow and its in-place-edited failure issue.
- `.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:166` (current main `a2eef6f7920a`): on each failure the workflow extracts the **entire** prior history — `awk '/^## Failure history/{found=1; next} found'` — into `history_file`.
- `.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:196-198`: the new body re-emits that history verbatim (`cat "${history_file}"`) followed by the new attempt entry. A grep for trimming/capping logic over the file finds none.
- `.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:171`: each attempt entry can carry an error excerpt of up to 5,000 chars, plus its attempt header and run lines. At worst-case entry size, roughly a dozen failed attempts push the body past 65,536 chars, after which the `gh issue edit` at lines 200-204 fails and the attempt count / first / last failure fields stop moving.

## Why it matters

The failure issue is the workflow's only persistent failure signal (runs are daily; run logs age out). An unbounded-append design guarantees it breaks under exactly the conditions it exists for — a long-running chronic failure — and it breaks silently: the workflow step errors on the edit, but there is no fallback record of the newest attempts anywhere durable.

Distinct from #917 (a single excerpt being truncated from the wrong end) and #913 (the failure-issue lookup cap): this is about cumulative history retention across attempts.

## Acceptance criteria

- The rebuilt failure-issue body is bounded: e.g. only the most recent N attempts are kept, or the history section is trimmed to a fixed character budget when the body is rebuilt, while the `Attempts:` / `First failure:` / `Last failure:` header fields stay accurate.
- A body simulated from many prior maximum-size attempts stays comfortably under 65,536 chars and `gh issue edit` succeeds.
- The trimming behaviour is visible in the issue itself (e.g. a note that older attempts were elided, with the total attempt count preserved).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #907 against current main.

title: ci(flake-inputs-update): no dedupe for an already-open update PR — consecutive runs stack duplicate PRs for the same pins

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Finding

The `flake-inputs-update` workflow (added by PR #907, commit `9e95477519e07a880ea7aab5e3c5e79b5c825aa5`) never checks for an already-open update PR before publishing a new one. Consecutive runs stack duplicate PRs for the same flake pins, and nothing ever closes the superseded ones.

## Evidence

- `.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:218` (current main `a2eef6f7920a`): every publishing run builds a unique branch — `branch="automation/flake-inputs-update-$(date -u +%Y%m%d)-${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"` — so no two runs can ever collide or reuse a branch.
- `.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:238-240`: `gh pr create` runs unconditionally once `changed=true`. A grep of the whole workflow on current main finds **no `gh pr list` anywhere** — the only list-style lookup in the file is the failure-*issue* lookup (line 66, tracked separately by #913).
- PR #914 made the stacking path the normal one: a validated PR the workflow token cannot merge is commented as ready and *left open with the run green* (workflow lines 245-264). The next scheduled run still sees the old pins on main, computes `changed=true`, and opens a second branch + PR for the same (or newer) revs. When one is finally merged by a privileged actor, the others stay open with conflicting `flake.lock` files and no automation closes them.

## Why it matters

Duplicate/stale automation PRs are a consolidation burden: a human has to work out which of several near-identical pin PRs is safe to merge, and the stale ones linger indefinitely. This is the same failure mode the workflow's own failure-issue design ("one issue per workflow, edited in place") was built to avoid — applied to issues but not to PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Before `gh pr create`, the publish step lists open PRs whose head matches `automation/flake-inputs-update-*`.
- If an open PR already targets the same openchamber/opencode revs, the run reuses it (logs the existing PR URL and exits green) instead of opening a second PR.
- If the open PR targets older revs, it is superseded in place: either its branch is force-updated with the new `flake.lock`, or it is closed with a comment naming the replacement PR.
- A run executed while a handoff PR from #914 is still open produces no second PR.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #907 (and #914) against current main. Related but distinct: #913 (failure-issue lookup cap), #917 (failure excerpt truncation).

title: id(web): footnotes are backslash-escaped on save — [^1] syntax mangled, definition orphaned

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

Markdown footnotes in a file opened in the id web editor are mangled on save: the footnote syntax is backslash-escaped into literal text.

Verified probe on main `a2eef6f7` (standalone crate compiling the verbatim `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` codec from main; log in the goal's hidden_files `probe-2026-10-25-2312/probe2.log`):

- Input:
  ```
  Text with a note.[^1]

  [^1]: The footnote body.
  ```
- `markdown_to_prosemirror` treats both the reference and the definition as ordinary paragraph text (footnotes never parse as footnotes).
- Save (`prosemirror_to_markdown`) emits:
  ```
  Text with a note.\[^1\]

  \[^1\]: The footnote body.
  ```
  The `\[` escapes mean the saved file no longer contains a footnote at all — it renders as literal `[^1]` characters, and the definition paragraph is orphaned plain text.

## Root cause

- `commonmark_options()` (pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:67) enables strikethrough, tasklist and table extensions but **not** `options.extension.footnotes`, so comrak parses `[^1]` as plain text, and its CommonMark renderer escapes the brackets of text nodes on save.
- Simply enabling the extension is **not** a fix by itself: the `convert_node` arm at markdown.rs:467 explicitly maps `FootnoteDefinition` / `FootnoteReference` to `json!(null)` — footnotes would then be silently deleted on open instead of mangled on save. The ProseMirror schema has no footnote node, so a representation decision is required (e.g. carry reference + definition as preserved raw text that re-emits verbatim, as sized images are carried through HTML forms).

## Why it matters

Footnotes are standard in longer notes/docs. Today, opening a footnoted file in the web editor and saving any edit destroys every footnote in it — silently, and in a way that is hard to notice in a diff. Same silent-save-corruption class as #872/#873/#880/#881/#882.

## Acceptance criteria

- A markdown file with at least one footnote reference + definition round-trips open → save with the footnote still functioning as a footnote in the saved markdown (reference and definition both intact, not escaped, not deleted).
- No regression to the currently passing codec tests; the strikethrough/tasklist/table extensions behave as before.
- New unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover the footnote round-trip, including a definition with more than one paragraph if the chosen representation supports it (otherwise the limitation is named in the PR).
- If the chosen fix is "preserve verbatim as raw text", a re-open of the saved file must show the same preserved form (stable fixpoint, no progressive escaping).

title: id(web): bold links flip spelling on every save — strong+link marks have no round-trip fixpoint

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

A bold link in a markdown file flips its markdown spelling on **every** save in the id web editor — the markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec has no fixpoint for text carrying both `strong` and `link` marks:

- File contains `**[text](https://e.com)**` → open + save emits `[**text**](https://e.com)`
- That output, opened + saved again, emits `**[text](https://e.com)**` again
- …and so on, forever. Every save of a document containing a bold link produces a spurious diff, even if the user changed nothing near the link.

Verified probe on main `a2eef6f7` (standalone crate compiling the verbatim `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` codec from main; logs in the goal's hidden_files `probe-2026-10-25-2312/probe2.log` and `probe3.log`):

- MD→PM→MD case `link-in-strong`: input `**[text](https://e.com)**`, PM marks `[strong, link]`, save #1 `[**text**](https://e.com)`, save #2 `**[text](https://e.com)**` — `STABLE: false`.
- PM→MD case `link-strong-order2`: PM marks `[link, strong]` → save #1 `**[text](https://e.com)**`, reparse gives marks `[strong, link]`, save #2 `[**text**](https://e.com)` — `STABLE: false`.
- Control: `em`+`strong` (`***both***`) round-trips stably, so this is specific to how `link` interacts with the wrapper ordering.

## Root cause (pointers)

The two directions disagree about mark nesting order for links:

- Parse direction: `convert_node`'s `NodeValue::Link` arm (markdown.rs:278) appends the `link` mark after marks already active from enclosing nodes (e.g. `Strong`, markdown.rs:268), so `**[text](url)**` yields marks `[strong, link]`.
- Save direction: `create_marked_text` / `build_mark_chain` (markdown.rs:1117 / 1167) treat the marks array as `[innermost, …, outermost]` and wrap in array order — for `[strong, link]` that builds `Link(Strong(text))`, which comrak renders as `[**text**](url)`, whose reparse yields the opposite nesting.

One of the two directions must change so that parse(emit(doc)) is a fixpoint for link+emphasis/strong combinations (or the PM marks must be canonicalised to a single agreed order in both directions).

## Why it matters

Non-idempotent save means perpetual dirty diffs and needless revision churn for any doc with bold/italic links — a common pattern — and it makes "did my edit change anything else?" unanswerable from the diff. Same codec-fidelity family as #880/#881/#882, but a stability bug rather than data loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- `**[text](url)**` and `[**text**](url)` each reach a fixpoint: open → save → open → save produces byte-identical markdown after the first save, for both spellings.
- Same fixpoint holds for `em`+`link` (`*[text](url)*` / `[*text*](url)`).
- Semantics unchanged: the link href/title and the strong/em emphasis survive every round-trip.
- New unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` assert two consecutive round-trips are identical for the strong+link and em+link cases.

## Problem In the id web editor, any inline HTML in a markdown file other than `` / `` is destroyed on save: the tags come back backslash-escaped as literal text. Verified probe on main `a2eef6f7` (standalone crate compiling the verbatim `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` codec from main; full log in the goal's hidden_files `probe-2026-10-25-2312/probe2.log`): - Input: `water is H2O and x2` - `markdown_to_prosemirror` produces plain text nodes `""`, `"2"`, `""`, … - Save (`prosemirror_to_markdown`) emits: `water is H\2\O and x\2\` - The rendered document now literally shows `\` instead of subscript markup. - Input: `some underlined text` → save emits `some \underlined\ text`. ## Root cause `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:354` — the `NodeValue::HtmlInline` arm of `convert_node` special-cases only img/linked-img tags; every other inline HTML tag falls through to `text_node_with_marks(html, active_marks)`, turning the tag into a plain text node. On save, comrak's CommonMark renderer escapes the `<`/`>` of text nodes, so the tag can never come back as HTML. Note `commonmark_options()` (markdown.rs:67) already sets `render.unsafe = true` for the sized-image HTML forms, so raw inline HTML is not rejected by policy elsewhere in this codec. ## Why it matters ``, ``, ``, ``, ``, `
` etc. are common in notes and technical docs. Opening such a file in the web editor and saving any unrelated edit silently corrupts every inline HTML tag in the file — the same silent-save-corruption class as #872/#873/#880/#881/#882. ## Acceptance criteria - A markdown file containing inline HTML (at minimum ``, ``, ``) round-trips through open → save without the tags being escaped: the saved markdown still contains the tags as HTML (or an explicitly equivalent representation that renders identically). - The existing img / linked-img HTML handling (#872, #880, #893) is unchanged. - New unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover the round-trip for at least ``/``/`` inline HTML. - If full passthrough is judged unsafe, the narrower fix (a whitelist of benign formatting tags) is implemented instead and the rejected set is named in the PR — silently escaping everything is the bug, not a fix. ## Suggested direction Carry non-img `HtmlInline` content through the PM doc in a form the save direction can emit back as a comrak `HtmlInline` node (instead of a `Text` node), mirroring how sized images already round-trip via `NodeValue::HtmlInline` in `json_to_ast` (markdown.rs:~1027). The editor (TS) side may need a matching node/mark handling note — flag it in the PR if the PM representation changes.

title: cold-store-reaper: live Google access token is cached in state.json, which the README calls '(no secrets)' and which is written without 0600 permissions

labels.description: Has a queued queue task

labels.name: app/cold-store-reaper
labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

cold-store-reaper caches a live Google OAuth **access token** in `state.json`, while the README describes `state.json` as "(no secrets)" and the file is written without the restrictive permissions the package applies to real credentials. Anyone or anything that can read `state.json` (backups, sync tools, another process in a less-protected home) holds a working Drive bearer token for its lifetime (~1h).

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #923 (cold-store-reaper v1), 2026-10-25; verified on current main (`92d0c6ee`).

## Evidence

- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/README.md:52`: `state.json # folder IDs + cached access token (no secrets)` — the sentence contradicts itself: a cached access token is a credential.
- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:332` (in `access_token()`): `state["access_token"] = token`, persisted via `save_state()` (lines 228-229) → `_write_json()` (line 207), a plain `path.write_text(...)` with no mode restriction.
- Contrast the package's own credential handling: `_write_private_json()` writes `credentials.json` (client secret + refresh token) with `os.open(..., 0o600)` and an explicit chmod. The access token gets neither treatment.
- The only hardening is `init()` chmodding the home directory to `0o700` (line ~191 area) — that does not run on later invocations, and `$COLD_STORE_HOME` may point at a directory the tool did not create.
- Note the v2 D1 code in the same file is careful to take `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` "from the environment only; it is never stored" — the Drive access token deserves the same rule.

## Why it matters

A short-lived token is still a live credential: with `drive.file` scope it can read/modify everything the cold-store app owns — which is the entire archive. The "(no secrets)" label invites copying `state.json` into places secrets must never go (a synced folder, a debug bundle, a repo).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The access token is no longer persisted in `state.json` (keep it in memory only), OR `state.json` is written with `0o600` permissions via the existing private-write helper and the README stops claiming "(no secrets)".
- [ ] README's file-layout table accurately describes what `state.json` contains.
- [ ] Existing tests still pass; a test or check confirms no token value lands in `state.json` under the chosen design (if in-memory-only).

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PR #923); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.

## Finding

cold-store-reaper's DB-backup retention policy is documented as pending and has no tracking issue: PR #929 shipped `put-backup` / `list-backups` with retention enforcement explicitly out of scope, and nothing files the follow-up. Until it lands, DB backups accumulate in Drive forever and pruning is manual.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #929 (cold-store-reaper v2), 2026-10-25.

## Evidence

- PR #929 body: "Retention enforcement (30/12/12, trash-not-delete) is explicitly **out of scope** and noted as pending in the README."
- Current main (`92d0c6ee`), `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/README.md:98-100`: "**Retention is NOT enforced yet**: the design's 30 daily / 12 weekly / 12 monthly policy (trash, not delete) is pending a later version. Until then, backups accumulate and pruning is manual."
- Same note in code: `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py`, `put_backup()` docstring (line ~672): "Retention enforcement (30 daily / 12 weekly / 12 monthly, trash-not-delete) is NOT implemented yet — see README."
- Dedupe: `gh search issues` for "cold-store-reaper", "retention", and "hard stop upload" returns no tracking issue for this follow-up.

## Why it matters

`put-backup` is the always-growing write path of the package (every DB backup of supabase/turso/d1 lands there with a dated name). With no retention and no tracking issue, the folder grows without bound against the project's Drive budget, and the "pending a later version" note is exactly the kind of promised follow-up that gets lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `prune-backups` command (or retention pass in an existing command) implements 30 daily / 12 weekly / 12 monthly per database, moving expired backups to Drive trash (never hard delete), with a `--dry-run` that lists what would be trashed.
- [ ] Retention decisions are driven by the dated backup names / Drive createdTime already recorded, and are covered by fake-Drive tests (boundary ages: 30th/31st daily, weekly and monthly tiers).
- [ ] README's retention note is updated from "NOT enforced yet" to the enforced behavior.

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PR #929); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.

title: cold-store-reaper: 700 GB/day upload hard stop and 3 TiB budget are reported by status but never enforced in upload / put-backup

body:
## Finding

cold-store-reaper's 700 GB/day upload hard stop and 3 TiB project budget are **reported but never enforced**. `status` computes `hard_stop_ok` / `within_budget`, but no upload path checks them before sending bytes, so the "hard stop" stops nothing.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #923 (cold-store-reaper v1) and PR #929 (v2), 2026-10-25.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/schema.sql:56-57` seeds the guardrails: `project_budget_bytes = 3298534883328` (3 TiB) and `daily_upload_hard_stop_bytes = 700000000000` (700 GB). PR #923's body describes the manifest as holding the "700 GB/day upload hard stop".
- On current main (`92d0c6ee`), `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py`:
  - `upload()` (line 558) goes straight from the bundle-state check to `_resumable_upload(...)` — no read of the transfer ledger, `daily_upload_hard_stop_bytes`, or `project_budget_bytes`.
  - `put_backup()` (line 672, added by PR #929) likewise uploads via `_resumable_upload(...)` (line ~693) with no guardrail check, then writes its `backup-upload` ledger row afterwards.
  - The only consumers of the two meta values are in `status_data()` (lines 888-901), which derives `hard_stop_ok` and `within_budget` for display. `grep -n hard_stop cold_store.py` shows no other use.
- So a loop or operator error that uploads past 700 GB in 24h (Google Drive's own daily upload ceiling — hitting it mid-run strands resumable sessions) or past the 3 TiB project budget is stopped by nothing in the tool that owns those numbers.

## Why it matters

The design's cost/quota guardrail exists only as a status readout. The reaper is meant to run unattended over very large archives; an unenforced hard stop converts a designed safety limit into a false sense of security, and the first notice would be Drive quota failures or budget overrun discovered after the fact.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `upload` and `put-backup` refuse to start (clear `ColdStoreError` naming the limit and the current 24h/project totals) when the transfer would cross `daily_upload_hard_stop_bytes` (last-24h uploads + this transfer) or `project_budget_bytes` (verified cold bytes + this transfer).
- [ ] The check uses the same ledger/meta accounting as `status_data` so `status` and enforcement can never disagree.
- [ ] Tests (fake-Drive, following the existing test style) cover: upload refused at/over the daily stop, upload allowed under it, `put-backup` refused likewise.
- [ ] README's description of the hard stop / budget matches the enforced behavior.

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PRs #923, #929); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.
