body:
## Bug

`id(web)`: the file-list pagination in `get_file_list_page` computes the page offset with unchecked `usize` arithmetic on raw query parameters, and `per_page` has no upper bound.

`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:973-985` (on main 402b5aa1):

```rust
let per_page = query.per_page.unwrap_or(DEFAULT_PER_PAGE).max(1);
let page = query.page.unwrap_or(1).max(1);
let start = (page - 1) * per_page;

let page_files = if start < total {
    files[start..(start + per_page).min(total)].to_vec()
} else {
    Vec::new()
};
```

`page` / `per_page` come straight from the query string (`FileListQuery`, routes.rs:82-90, both `Option<usize>`, no clamping). `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` sets no `overflow-checks` override, so the dev/test profiles panic on overflow and the release profile wraps.

## Verified this run (standalone rustc probe replicating lines 973-985 verbatim)

- Debug semantics (overflow checks on, as in dev/test): `page=3, per_page=9223372036854775808 (2^63), total=10` → **panic: `attempt to multiply with overflow`** at the `start` computation. Through the real handler that is a panicked request task for a well-formed query string.
- Release semantics (overflow checks off): the same input wraps `start` to `0` and returns files `0..10` — **page 3 silently returns page 1's files**, while the response reports `page=3, per_page=2^63`.
- Normal case sanity-checked with the same probe: `page=3, per_page=2, total=10` → slice end 6 (files 4..6), as expected.
- Separately, `per_page` is unbounded: `?per_page=100000000` defeats pagination entirely and returns the whole filtered list in one response.

## Why it matters

The file list is the web UI's main listing endpoint (used by both the page handler at routes.rs:346 and the JSON handler at routes.rs:700). A crafted or buggy client query can panic the request handler in debug/test builds and silently return the wrong page in release builds — wrong-page results are worse than an error, because the UI renders them as if they were the requested page. Unbounded `per_page` also removes the only size control on this response.

## Acceptance criteria

- `page` / `per_page` arithmetic cannot overflow or wrap for any query values: use checked/saturating arithmetic (an out-of-range page returns an empty page, with the requested `page`/`per_page` echoed as today).
- `per_page` is clamped to a sane maximum (pick one, e.g. 200, and note it in the code near `DEFAULT_PER_PAGE`); `page` handling for absurd values returns an empty page instead of wrapping.
- Regression tests cover at least: `page=3, per_page=2^63`; `page=usize::MAX, per_page=50`; a `per_page` above the new maximum; and the existing normal paging cases still pass.
- Targeted test path: the existing `routes.rs` test module / handler tests (`cargo test --features web --lib web::routes`), run on CI or the laptop — not a sandbox build.

## Suggested fix

In `get_file_list_page`: clamp `per_page` with `.clamp(1, MAX_PER_PAGE)`, compute `start` with `page.saturating_sub(1).saturating_mul(per_page)`, and compute the slice end with `start.saturating_add(per_page).min(total)` (keeping the `start < total` guard).

Single-repo: the pattern was checked in this repo only for this filing; no copy of `get_file_list_page` exists in the other three fleet repos (it is `pkgs/id`-local code).

title: ci(flake-inputs-update): failure excerpt truncates the tail from the head (head -c 5000 after tail -n 80) — the actual error never reaches the tracking issue

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation (area)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Problem

The `flake-inputs-update` workflow's failure-issue excerpt truncates the tail of the log **from the head**, so on any realistically long failure the excerpt contains none of the actual error.

`.github/workflows/flake-inputs-update.yml:169` (on main `c4b29e12`):

```bash
grep -v "copying path" "${ERROR_LOG}" | tail -n 80 | sed 's/~~~/---/g' | head -c 5000 > "$RUNNER_TEMP/excerpt.txt" || true
```

`tail -n 80` correctly selects the last 80 lines — where the error lives — but `head -c 5000` then keeps only the **first** 5000 bytes of that selection. When the last 80 lines exceed 5000 bytes (normal for nix build output, ~100+ bytes/line), the excerpt ends mid-line partway through the tail and the final error line never reaches the tracking issue. The issue comment at :166-167 says the excerpt is meant to be the "last lines of the failing step's log … capped" — the cap is applied at the wrong end.

## Verified this run (synthetic probe, exact pipeline from :169)

Synthetic log: 100 `copying path` noise lines, then 80 build lines of ~109 chars each, then a final `error: builder for … failed with exit code 1` line (18,632 bytes total).

- Excerpt produced: exactly 5000 bytes, ending mid-line inside "building step output line 042".
- `grep -c "error: builder" excerpt.txt` → **0** — the actual error is absent from what would be posted to the failure issue.

## Why it matters

This workflow's tracking issue is the primary diagnostic surface for failed automated openchamber/opencode input updates (the same mechanism #913 covers for the issue-lookup cap). A failure excerpt that reliably omits the error forces every diagnosis back to the raw run log and makes the maintained issue history misleading.

## Precedent

The identical pattern in developing-today/openchamber's opencode-update workflow was filed as openchamber #450 and fixed by PR #451 (merged): cap the excerpt from the tail end instead of the head.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The excerpt pipeline keeps the **last** ≤5000 bytes of the filtered tail (e.g. `… | tail -c 5000`), so the excerpt always ends with the log's final line when the log is longer than the cap.
- [ ] Logs whose filtered tail is ≤5000 bytes produce a byte-identical excerpt to today (no behavior change for short failures).
- [ ] The excerpt still strips `copying path` lines and still neutralizes `~~~` fences (`sed 's/~~~/---/g'` or equivalent) before the byte cap, or the ordering is documented if changed.
- [ ] Workflow YAML still parses and the failure-issue step is otherwise unchanged.

## Suggested fix

One-word change at :169: `head -c 5000` → `tail -c 5000`.

Filed by new-issue-creator (standalone run, 2026-10-25). Single-repo: `grep -rn "head -c" .github/workflows/` across developing-today/opencode, developing-today/openchamber and dezren39/nix returns no other instance; openchamber's instance is already fixed (#450/#451).

body:
# design+impl: org-level GitHub Project as the conceptual-project layer — orchestrator-synced, dashboard-read

Drew's questions + direction (2026-10-25), building on the 2026-10-23/24 evaluation (recommended GitHub Projects: org-level, Board + Roadmap views over one item pool, label-gated auto-add, fleet-maintainable via gh/GraphQL, $0 incremental; write-up ~/workspace/your_files/github-projects-vs-linear-2026-10-23.md).

## Why
Issues are the unit of work, but larger conceptual efforts (a program, a wave, a multi-repo set) have no first-class URL of their own today — they live in goal workspaces and epic-ish issues. An org-level Project gives each effort a stable place + URL, and the dashboard a canonical source for status that is not re-derived from scratch every hour.

## Design
- **One org Project now** (developing-today), designed to split later without migration: an **Area** field carries the conceptual project (e.g. `id-train`, `pm-dashboard`, `lab-cluster`). Splitting = filtered views per Area now; separate Projects per Area later is a view change, not a data move. The dashboard reads the same pool and can show all Areas together or filter to one.
- **Fields:** Status (Todo / In Progress / In Review / Done), Area, Horizon (Today / Week / Month / Quarter — mirrors the dashboard horizons), Type (Task / Epic).
- **Items are issues.** Pre-issue ideas may sit as draft items briefly but should become issues.
- **Epics = meta-issues**: an issue with a task list of member issues + the `epic` label, itself a Project item with Type=Epic. **Milestones** connect clusters inside one repo (a wave, a release); the Project connects across repos. Both mechanisms coexist: milestone = time-boxed cluster in a repo, epic = cross-cutting grouping, Project = the whole portfolio.
- **Sync is single-writer.** Agents NEVER write the Project directly — they keep working in GitHub issues only (comments, branches, PRs that reference the issue, assignment). The **orchestrator** reconciles the Project on its hourly pass from observable signals: issue added (label-gated auto-add: `now` / `next` / `epic`, or manual add) -> Todo; a branch or open PR referencing the issue, or an active session lined up on it -> In Progress; PR in review -> In Review; issue closed -> Done; blocked-by carried from issue text + the orchestrator's classification (same blockedBy data the dashboard already publishes). One writer = no sync races, no agent-side knowledge required.
- **Dashboard reads, never writes**: the fleet-feed collector gains a projects section (GraphQL Projects v2 read), the aggregator renders Project views from it alongside the derived data; where the Project and derived state disagree, the disagreement is shown, not hidden (it is the reconciliation bug signal).
- **Known caveat to verify at build time:** org Projects and personal-repo items (dezren39/nix) — the 2026-10-24 research said an org Project can't hold personal-repo items; verify current behavior, and if still true, nix items stay dashboard-only (the feed already covers them) and that limitation is documented on the Project.

## Staged implementation
1. Drew's go (org-level creation is his call).
2. Create the Project + fields + Board and Roadmap views; README on the Project explaining the conventions in one screen.
3. Label-gated auto-add workflow + the epic/milestone conventions written into the four repos' contributor docs where the fleet reads them.
4. Orchestrator: add the reconciliation step to the hourly pass (bounded: at most ~25 item updates per run, mirroring its classification cap).
5. Collector + aggregator: projects section in the feed; dashboard project page (this is a slice-3-manifest page — coordinate with #906).
6. Backfill: current epics/programs (ID train, PM dashboard slices, lab cluster set) become items with Areas set.

## Acceptance
- Project exists with the fields/views above; a new labeled issue appears as a Todo item without human touching the Project.
- Opening a PR that references a tracked issue moves its item to In Progress on the next orchestrator pass; merging/closing moves it to Done.
- Dashboard shows the Project pool with an Area filter; an item's dashboard card links the Project item URL.
- A blocked item shows its blocker on both the Project and the dashboard, from one recorded source.

## Acceptance criteria

- An org-level GitHub Project for developing-today exists with Status / Area / Horizon / Type fields and Board + Roadmap views over one item pool.
- Label-gated auto-add (`now` / `next` / `epic`) is configured; epics are meta-issues carrying the `epic` label and Type=Epic.
- The orchestrator's hourly pass is the single writer: it syncs item Status from issue/PR/session signals (Todo → In Progress → In Review → Done) and carries blocked-by from its existing classification.
- No agent writes the Project directly; the dashboard's fleet-feed collector reads the Project via GraphQL (Projects v2) and renders a projects section without writing back.
- A spot-check of several known issues shows Project Status matching their GitHub state after one orchestrator pass.

title: id(web): /blob serves any blob as text/html via the ?filename= parameter — no CSP/nosniff/disposition headers (same-origin XSS by link)
body: ## Problem `GET /blob/{hash}` chooses its `Content-Type` from the **caller-supplied `?filename=` query parameter** and sends no protective headers, so any stored blob can be served as active content in the id web origin — stored/reflected XSS by link. ## Evidence (verified on main `86e6f300`) - Route: `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:261` — `.route("/blob/{hash}", get(blob_handler))`. - `blob_handler` (`routes.rs:565-600`): the filename comes from `query.filename` (`BlobQuery`, `routes.rs:~398`) when present, falling back to the stored tag name only when the parameter is absent. It then sets `Content-Type: get_content_type(&filename)` and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` — and nothing else: no `Content-Security-Policy`, no `X-Content-Type-Options`, no `Content-Disposition`. - `get_content_type` (`pkgs/id/src/web/content_mode.rs:83-141`) maps by extension, including `html|htm → text/html; charset=utf-8` (`:128`), `svg → image/svg+xml` (`:96`), `js → application/javascript`, `xml → application/xml`. - So `/blob/?filename=evil.html` serves those bytes as `text/html` from the editor's own origin; a top-level visit executes any script in the file with the origin's full API access (save/upload/world admin endpoints are same-origin). Blob hashes are content addresses meant to be shared in this P2P system, so "you need the hash" is not a mitigation. The immutable year-long cache header makes a poisoned URL persistent in the victim's cache. - The codebase already knows the safe patterns this handler misses: `explore.rs:246-247` sets CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` on its pages (with tests at `explore.rs:759-761`), and `download_handler` (`routes.rs:1669-1685`) pairs `get_content_type` with `Content-Disposition: attachment`. - Contributing factor — upload path: `upload_handler` (`routes.rs:1343+`) validates only the multipart field's *declared* Content-Type (`:1364-1377`) and stores the blob under the field's original `file_name()` when one is present, so an upload named `evil.html` declared as `image/png` is tagged `evil.html`; the returned URL is built unencoded as `format!("/blob/{hash_str}?filename={filename}")` (`routes.rs:~1495`). A script-bearing SVG honestly declared `image/svg+xml` is likewise stored and later served as `image/svg+xml` with no sandbox CSP — SVG script runs on top-level navigation. ## Why it matters The web UI is the trusted control surface for the store (edit/save/upload/world administration). One crafted `/blob/…?filename=x.html` link turns any blob already in the store — including content synced from peers — into same-origin script execution for whoever opens it. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `blob_handler` no longer derives an active Content-Type from the unvalidated `?filename=` parameter: either ignore the parameter for typing (use the stored tag name / recorded content-type metadata), or restrict served types to a safe allowlist (images/video/audio/pdf/text-plain) with everything else served as `application/octet-stream` or `Content-Disposition: attachment`. - [ ] Blob responses carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive CSP such as `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; sandbox` (which still permits `` embedding of images, the legitimate use — the upload flow inserts the returned URL as an image node src). - [ ] Regression tests (handler-level, in the style of the existing `upload_router_tests` in `routes.rs`): a blob requested with `?filename=x.html` is NOT served as `text/html`; an SVG blob is served with the protective headers; a PNG blob is still served as `image/png` so embedded images keep working. - [ ] The upload response URL percent-encodes the filename (as `download_handler` already does with `urlencoding::encode`), and an uploaded file's stored name cannot masquerade as a different type than its validated Content-Type (e.g. name extension reconciled with `mime_to_extension`).

title: impl(dashboard): slice 3 — pluggable pages (DNS register first), comments everywhere, agent/session identity registry
body:
# impl(dashboard): slice 3 — pluggable pages (DNS register first), comments everywhere, agent/session identity registry

Owner direction (Drew, 2026-10-25). Builds on slice 2 (#898) — start after #898 merges. The dashboard's primary purpose stays project management, but it also becomes our general **operational dashboard**. Three workstreams:

## 1. Pluggable pages + home-page dropdown
- The home page gets a **page dropdown/select**: pages are registered entries, not hard-coded routes.
- Adding a page should be quick: a small module + one manifest entry (title, route, data source). Document the recipe in the repo README so a new page is a ~30-minute job.
- **First page: the DNS/domain register** (from #902): renders the register (renewal-sorted; next-renewal, completely-unused, and unused-but-earmarked views; per-domain cost/renewal/plan/review flag). Source of truth stays the register file produced by #902's backup job — the page renders it, never edits it. This issue owns the view; #902 owns the data pipeline. Coordinate the format with #902.

## 2. Comments on everything, with clear authorship
Comment threads attach to: needs-Drew items, needs-orchestrator items, roadmap/project items, GitHub-backed tasks, and dashboard objects generally. Requirements:
- **Drew can comment** on any of the above.
- **Two comment kinds, visibly distinct:** (a) *message to Muse/orchestrator* — triaged by the orchestrator on its next pass (may create work); (b) *plain note* — no trigger; read when the task/project is next picked up. Drew picks the kind when posting (default: note).
- **GitHub-backed items** (a single GitHub issue, or a dashboard item that compiles several issues) additionally offer *post as GitHub comment*, with the target issue explicit before posting. Posting uses the fleet's normal GitHub auth; the comment is attributed as the fleet account and notes it was written by Drew via the dashboard.
- **Agents can comment too**, and authorship is unambiguous: every comment carries an author identity — `drew`, `muse`, or an agent identity from workstream 3 (display name + session link). No anonymous comments.
- Storage: one comments store keyed by a stable object ref (the same RefKey scheme as the orchestration feed), so comments survive feed republishes. The orchestrator consumes kind-(a) comments as queue input.

## 3. Agent/session identity + lightweight session registry
Loose v1 — improve over time; do NOT block workstreams 1–2 on a perfect registry.
- Every agent/session gets a **stable ID and a human display name** at start: OpenCode sessions, Muse, Jules runs, fleet cron runs, subagents. Assignment points: the fleet init job and agent launch.
- Provide an **OpenCode tool that auto-injects the caller's session ID** (and parent session ID) so work products, comments, and dispatches can carry it without the agent remembering.
- A **collector** extracts session records — id, parent, source (OpenCode sandbox/laptop, Muse, Jules), start/last-seen, status, token usage where available — into a database the aggregator can query, enabling **loose task ↔ session ↔ token linkage**: given a task, which sessions worked it and roughly what they cost; given a session, what it was working on.
- Dashboard session views (from #898) consume this registry for their labels and attribution instead of scraping raw session lists.

## Acceptance
- Dropdown on the home page lists pages from a manifest; DNS register page live and rendering #902's register data.
- Drew can post both comment kinds on a needs-Drew item, a roadmap item, and a GitHub-backed item; a kind-(a) comment appears in the orchestrator's next run report as triaged input; a GitHub comment lands on the chosen issue.
- An agent-posted comment renders with its agent identity visibly distinct from Drew's and Muse's.
- Session registry holds records for at least OpenCode (both servers), Muse, and Jules sessions with parent links and token totals where the source reports them; a dashboard item shows its linked sessions.

Constraints: existing fleet rules — plan quotas only for any build sessions, measurement gate, no public route for the dashboard (tailnet + MagicDNS links only).

title: fix(pm-stack): fleet-feed-collector units do not survive a sandbox recycle
body:
Found during the #899 audit (2026-10-25): after the sandbox recycled (~16:32Z), the `fleet-feed-collector.service`/`.timer` units were absent (`systemctl` reported the service not found) and the fleet feed went stale ~40 min, because the units live only in `/etc/systemd/system` from an imperative install out of `pm-stack/aggregator/systemd/`.

Units were reinstalled by hand this time (`cp` from the pm-feed clone + `daemon-reload` + `enable --now fleet-feed-collector.timer`) and the feed is flowing again.

Fix direction: install the units from a path that survives recycles — e.g. have the sandbox boot/init flow (or the aggregator's own install tooling) copy them from the pm-feed clone on boot, the way opencode-serve is restored — and/or make the collector's freshness observable (the aggregator already ages the feed in provenance; a stale-feed alert could ride the orchestration pass). Acceptance: recycle the sandbox and observe the timer active and the feed fresh within one cadence, with no manual step.

title: impl(orchestrator): recurring orchestration job — queue triage, priority ladder, blocker awareness, goal measurement
body:
Slice 2B of the PM program, from Drew's direction 2026-10-25: "We need to start integrating so that you have an orchestration job which runs regularly and reviews the 'needs orchestrator' / 'needs decision' jobs. It pushes them back or sends them to me if absolutely required, and measures our top goals and the tasks lined up."

Companion to the aggregator slice-2 issue (dashboard tiers + today view). The dashboard presents; this job does the work behind the NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR tier.

## The job
A recurring orchestration pass (cron) that each run:
1. **Reviews the queues**: NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR and NEEDS DECISION items (sessions stalled on questions, errored runs, pending decisions, blocked tasks — sources: the aggregator's attention feed, jules-review state, the repo backlogs, the goals' tracked items).
2. **Acts on what the fleet can resolve**: route/poke/dispatch sessions, answer machine-answerable questions from recorded context, unblock what's unblockable — following the fleet's standing rules (plan-only quotas, measurement gate, model ladder). Push work BACK into motion instead of letting it sit.
3. **Escalates to Drew only when absolutely required**: a genuine decision, a physical step, a credential only he can supply. Escalations land in the NEEDS DREW tier with a one-line reason. Everything else must NOT reach Drew.
4. **Measures the top goals**: for each of Drew's top goals, compare the goal against the tasks lined up under it — progress since last run, stalls, gaps (a goal with nothing lined up is a finding). Write the measurement summary the dashboard's today view consumes.

## Priority ladder for assigning todo/job work
1. Today's objectives
2. Tomorrow's objectives
3. Next 3 days
4. Longer-horizon goals
5. Random incoming (new GitHub issues, ad-hoc requests)

Not exclusive: **dependency awareness beats ladder order.** Before assigning a task, check whether it is blocked by another task; if the blocker has an active worker, take different work and record the dependency. The dependency picture must be visible in one place: for any task, "blocked by X; X is being worked by session S" — and conversely "to reach this task, session S must first complete prerequisite Y."

## Coordination with existing jobs (do not duplicate)
- **stewardship-cycle** (hourly) owns quota/model routing, the stalled-agenda sweep, and pool health. The orchestrator owns task-level triage and assignment. If the cleanest implementation extends stewardship-cycle with an orchestration step, do that and say so here; if it is a separate cron, draw the boundary explicitly.
- **jules-review** (keeper) owns session-level supervision of running fleet sessions. The orchestrator consumes its state; it does not re-supervise sessions.
- The repo sweeps own issue/PR work inside each repo; the orchestrator sets priorities across them rather than doing their work.

## Done when
The job is scheduled and has completed at least one observed live run: queues reviewed, at least the classification + escalation output recorded, goal-measurement summary written where the dashboard reads it, and a run report exists that a human can audit (what was pushed back into motion, what was escalated and why, what was measured). Plan-only discipline throughout: a quota wall is a stop-and-record, never a spill.

title: impl(aggregator): slice 2 — mobile, needs-Drew/needs-orchestrator tiers, time-granular roadmap, session clarity
body:
Slice 2 of the PM aggregator, from Drew's review of slice 1 (2026-10-25). Builds on #890 (slice 1, merged in #892); designs in #851/#852; data-correction follow-up in #895.

## 1. Mobile-first responsive pass
Every aggregator view (board/roadmap, needs-you, quota, today) must be reviewable on a phone. Drew's report: the dashboard/board view is difficult to review on mobile. Verify at phone width, not just by resizing a desktop window.

## 2. Tier the needs-you view: NEEDS DREW vs NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR
Today's panel mixes three things: items that genuinely require Drew, items the fleet can resolve itself, and stale noise. Split it:
- **NEEDS DREW** (the default view): only items that truly require Drew's decision, input, or a physical step. Nothing else lands here.
- **NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR**: items the fleet can work itself — this is the queue the orchestration job (slice 2B) reviews and pushes back into work. Visible, but separate.
Classification must be explainable per item (why does this need Drew?). Stale/finished items expire out instead of lingering.

## 3. Roadmap granularity
The roadmap board has quarters today. Add the same data at finer grains: **month**, **week**, **next 3 days**, and **today**. One data model, switchable horizon.

## 4. Today view: top objectives + project momentum
A view whose job is: (a) the day's top objectives, prioritized; (b) for each project, whether it is moving forward — what has been accomplished recently, what is stalled, what is blocked and by what. This consumes the goal-measurement summary the orchestration job (2B) writes; until 2B lands, derive from the data already in the feed and mark provenance.

## 5. Session clarity
Drew could not tell what he was looking at: old OpenCode sub-sessions presented as if live, and no visibility of Jules runs or Muse/subagent sessions. Requirements:
- Every session/entry labeled with its **source** (OpenCode sandbox server, OpenCode laptop server, Jules, Muse) and a comprehensible state.
- Sub-sessions collapse under their parent session; finished-run leftovers expire by age instead of presenting as current.
- A **coverage note** on the page: which session sources are wired, which are not yet, and what that means for what Drew is seeing. If Jules or Muse sessions cannot be wired yet, the page says so explicitly and the gap is tracked here.

## 6. Links use the tailnet hostname
All user-facing links use the laptop's MagicDNS name **amd-6.raptor-pumpkinseed.ts.net** (verified live), never the raw 100.99.113.103 IP.

## Done when
PR merged; all views verified from the laptop on loopback + tailnet, including a phone-width render of each view; the tier split live with per-item reasons; roadmap horizons switchable; today view rendering objectives + momentum; session sources labeled with the coverage note present.

title: mcpx: desktop-commander entry in .mcpx.json uses a non-portable absolute home path
body: The tracked project mcpx config (`.mcpx.json`) starts Desktop Commander via the absolute path `/home/user/.local/bin/desktop-commander`, which only resolves on machines whose home is `/home/user`; project scope overrides user scope, so the entry is broken elsewhere. Fix: use the portable `npx -y @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander` form. Implemented by PR #863; this issue is the ledger entry for that PR-only work (sweep directive 2026-10-24). title: id(ci): nightly NixOS VM checks fail — home page no longer contains 'Files' (serve/e2e assertions, integration timeout)
body:
## Finding (issue-sweep-devtoday-code, 2026-10-25 run)

The `id e2e nightly` workflow has failed five consecutive nights (runs 39604059698, 39783189972, 39955079614, 40092359401, 40193900320). The latest run is now root-caused — it is NOT the historical #257 disk failure and NOT the #229 Firefox cluster:

### Run 40193900320 (2026-10-25, head 2d6d1c17) — sole job `nix flake check (full)`

All non-VM checks pass, and the Playwright `test-e2e` check passes 113/113. Exactly the NixOS VM checks fail:

- `nixos-serve` — `AssertionError: [port 3000] Home page missing 'Files'` (`pkgs/id/nix/tests/serve-test.nix:64`). The served home page HTML begins `<!DOCTYPE html><html lang="en" data-theme="sneak">…<title>Home - id</title>` — no `Files` in the initial HTML.
- `nixos-e2e` — `AssertionError: [port 4173] Home page DOM missing 'Files'` (`pkgs/id/nix/tests/e2e-test.nix:81`), same cause.
- `nixos-integration` — VM test driver hit `timeout reached; test terminating…` and the builder died with exit code 143 (`vm-test-run-id-integration.drv`); the server VM booted cleanly (DHCP lease, multi-user target reached), so this looks like the same home-page/content expectation never being satisfied rather than a boot failure.
- `nixos-playwright-e2e` was still running when the run was summarised; the three failures above already fail the job.

### Why it matters

The nightly is the only place the NixOS VM checks run, so it has been red for a week and real regressions in the VM-tested paths are invisible. Either the home page changed (the `Files` section is now client-rendered or moved — cf. `pkgs/id/src/web/templates.rs:154`, `routes.rs:355`, where a `Files` card/page still exists on other routes) and the VM tests' expectations are stale, or the home page regressed and stopped server-rendering content it used to include.

### Acceptance criteria

- Determine which side is wrong: if the home page intentionally no longer server-renders `Files`, update `serve-test.nix` / `e2e-test.nix` (and the integration test's waits) to assert on content the home page actually guarantees (e.g. title / shell markers / a hydrated DOM check like the Playwright suite uses).
- If the home page regressed, restore the server-rendered `Files` content on `/`.
- `nixos-integration` no longer times out: it passes, or its failure mode becomes a fast, legible assertion.
- One full nightly run (or a local/laptop `nix flake check` including the four `nixos-*` checks) is green.

title: id(web): sized linked images still lose their href on reload — PR #888's HTML emission has no parse counterpart (and editor parseDOM drops the wrapping link)
body: ## Finding (from pr-diff-review of PR #888, head d09a4f409a) PR #888 fixes #880 (linked images) for the plain markdown form, but the **sized** linked-image path it introduces does not round-trip, and its own test does not cover it. ### Evidence Save direction (PR #888, `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, `json_to_ast` image arm): an image with `width`/`height` AND `linkHref` is emitted as an `HtmlInline`: ```html ``` Parse direction (current main, unchanged by #888): there is no parse counterpart for that form. - `convert_node`'s `HtmlInline` arm calls `parse_img_tag(html)`, and `parse_img_tag` (markdown.rs, current main) returns `None` unless the literal starts with `` into separate inline HTML nodes, so the `` and `` pieces fall through to `text_node_with_marks(...)` — they become **literal text nodes containing the anchor tags** in the ProseMirror doc — and the `` piece parses to an image node with **no `linkHref`**. - Result on the next open/save cycle: the href is lost anyway, and stray `` / `` text appears in the document — the same save-path data-loss family #880/#872/#873 exist to fix, plus visible corruption. - PR #888's new test `test_linked_image_roundtrip_keeps_href` covers only the unsized form (`[![alt](img.png)](https://example.com)`); no test round-trips a sized linked image. Second facet, same outcome via the editor: PR #888 adds `linkHref`/`linkTitle` to the editor image schema (`pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts`) and renders `["a", ..., ["img", ...]]` in `toDOM`, but the image node's `parseDOM` `getAttrs` still reads only the `` element's own attributes — it never looks at a wrapping `` parent, so a linked image pasted or parsed from HTML enters the editor with its link already dropped. ### Why it matters If PR #888 merges as-is, it closes #880 while the sized variant of the same bug stays live — and gains a new symptom (literal anchor-tag text in documents). Sized images are the common case for linked screenshots/badges with explicit dimensions. ### Acceptance criteria - A sized linked image (`linkHref` + `width` and/or `height`) survives a full markdown → ProseMirror → markdown round trip with href, dimensions, and alt intact, and produces no literal `` text nodes; a Rust test in `web::markdown` pins this (mirroring the unsized test). - The parse direction handles the `` HTML form (e.g. anchor-aware handling in/around `parse_img_tag` or the `HtmlInline` arm), OR the sized emission changes to a form the parser already round-trips — either way the round-trip test above passes. - Editor facet: pasting/parsing `` in the web editor yields an image node with `linkHref` set (parseDOM reads the wrapping anchor), or this facet is explicitly split into its own tracked issue before #880 is closed. - #880 is not closed on the strength of the unsized fix alone while this issue is open.

title: impl(aggregator): slice 1 — live needs-you + quota panels (fleet feed + laptop server)
body:
## Implementation issue — aggregator slice 1

Design sources: #851 (quota + throughput view) and #852 (needs-you attention
view). The aggregator package (`pm-stack/aggregator/`) already renders both
views from fixtures; slice 1 wires them to **real fleet data** and deploys the
page on the laptop with the stack. Read-only: display + classification only —
no starting/stopping/messaging sessions.

### Data path chosen

**Attention (#852)** — `SessionFeedEntry` rows built by a shared mapper from
OpenCode v2 server signals (session `outcome`/`time`, message-level
`error`/`finish`, tool-part states, pending permission requests, open
session forms, consecutive identical errors), classified by the existing
`classifyAttention` in `src/derive.ts` into Drew's six states,
attention-ordered machine-first:

- **Laptop sessions: live** from the laptop's OpenChamber-managed OpenCode
  server (port + password read from
  `~/.config/openchamber/managed-opencode/state.json` at request time),
  45 s in-process cache.
- **Sandbox sessions: from the fleet feed** (below) — the sandbox server
  binds its own loopback and is not reachable from the laptop.
- Inclusion: sessions in the active set, sessions with a pending permission
  request, and sessions updated within 12 h. `jules-review-state.json`
  supervision entries annotate matching sessions as evidence.

**Quota (#851)** — a **fleet feed file** (`fleet-feed.json`) produced by a
collector shipped in this package (`scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts`) that runs
on the sandbox host, where the sources of record live:

- `provider-quota-registry.md` (provider facts + dated observations),
- the stewardship quota view's dated reads,
- `provider-usage-snapshot.json` (check-usage output),
- the sandbox OpenCode server API (session burn attribution).

The collector emits clean `QuotaView` pools; the aggregator renders the feed
and computes the model-choice guidance (headroom / burn-before-reset /
do-not-start) from pool state + reset times. Per-pool extractors fail soft:
a pool whose read pattern stops matching renders with its identity and a
"no current read" note instead of vanishing or inventing numbers.

**Pool map (corrected 2026-10-25):** exactly ONE Meta pool — the Muse API
**High Usage plan**, reached only via the `meta` provider. There is no
"muse plan" pool and the assistant's Power subscription is never a pool.

### Refresh cadence

- Laptop attention: live, 45 s cache.
- Sandbox attention + quota: collector cadence, **~5 min** (collector + scp
  push over the tailnet proxy route, same pattern as `laptop-ssh.sh`).
  Feed age is shown in the page footer/provenance; a stale feed keeps
  rendering with its age stated, fixtures only if no feed exists at all.

### Network exposure — Drew's decision (2026-10-25 09:19 CDT), on the record

LAN/tailnet accessibility is fine. A public endpoint is acceptable **only**
behind a password (Cloudflare Access or equivalent) — never open.

Applied in this slice:

- The aggregator binds **loopback + the laptop tailnet address** (like
  Pad/Grist); **no public hostname** in slice 1.
- **ready-for-agent (6056)** gets the same treatment in this pass: it is
  laptop-loopback-only today; its binary takes a single `--host` (bare
  `--host` = all interfaces), so the unit binds all interfaces, which
  covers loopback + tailnet + LAN per Drew's decision. Verified answering
  on the tailnet address after the change.

### Deferred to slice 2

- Projector-ized quota/attention feeds (per-source live usage APIs from
  #851's source list) replacing the collector's registry extraction.
- Throughput burn segments + token-rate history (slice 1 shows live
  per-pool active-session token attribution only).
- Session → PR join via the projector link registry; Jules sessions in the
  attention feed; any action affordances (poke/switch) — the view stays
  read-only.
- A public, password-gated hostname if Drew wants one.

### Acceptance

- [ ] Page serving on the laptop on loopback + tailnet; `/attention` and
      `/quota` (and their `/api/*.json`) render real current data, with
      provenance stating each facet's source + feed age.
- [ ] ready-for-agent answering on the tailnet address.
- [ ] Tests green (existing suite + new mapper/extractor tests); PR merged.

title: Correct the muse provider comment in .opencode/opencode.jsonc — it misdescribes the route as a Muse subscription route
body:
The disabled `muse` provider block in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` carries this comment:

> DISABLED 2026-10-25 per Drew: the "muse" provider (Muse CLI subscription route) is not a pool plan — the Meta pool plan is the "meta" provider.

That description is wrong (Drew, 2026-10-25). The correct mapping:

- There is ONE Meta pool: the Muse API **High Usage plan**.
- The `meta` provider (API key) is the ONLY door sessions may use into it.
- The `muse` program is a separate terminal program that reaches the SAME High Usage plan through its OAuth login (muse-proxy wraps it and strips META_API_KEY so calls take the OAuth plan route instead of the PAYG key route). The `muse` provider is a second, wasteful door into the same pool — disabled by Drew's order, never to be routed to.
- The assistant Muse (app/website) runs on Drew's separate Power subscription; it is not a pool and the muse program never touches it. There is no "Muse subscription route" for sessions and no separate "muse plan allowance".

Fix: rewrite the comment with the correct mapping (comment-only change; no provider/model definitions touched). The deployed configs (sandbox + laptop) were already corrected 2026-10-25; this brings the repo copy in line.

title: id(web): prosemirror_to_markdown keeps only the first text node of a code_block — multi-node blocks are truncated on save
body:
## Bug

In `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, `json_to_ast`'s `"code_block"` arm reads only the **first** text child of the ProseMirror code block:

```rust
// markdown.rs:~638-642 (main 45c817e0)
let content = json["content"]
    .as_array()
    .and_then(|arr| arr.first())
    .and_then(|n| n["text"].as_str())
    .unwrap_or("");
```

A code block whose ProseMirror content is split into more than one text node — which editors produce legitimately, e.g. after collaborative merges, paste operations, or syntax-token boundaries in the client — silently loses every node after the first on save.

## Verified repro (this run, main 45c817e0)

Temporary probe test run with `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::` (probe removed after the run; assertion below is the acceptance test):

ProseMirror input:

```json
{
  "type": "doc",
  "content": [{
    "type": "code_block",
    "attrs": {"params": "rust"},
    "content": [
      {"type": "text", "text": "fn a() {}\n"},
      {"type": "text", "text": "fn b() {}"}
    ]
  }]
}
```

`prosemirror_to_markdown` emits:

````
```rust
fn a() {}
```
````

`fn b() {}` is deleted with no error. (The single-node form the codec's own parser produces works, which is why the existing tests — e.g. `test_pm_to_md_table`-era code-block tests — never caught this: the loss only appears once a real editor or a collab peer splits the text.)

## Why it matters

This is the save path for the id web editor, and `id` is a collaborative system: a code block edited by multiple peers is exactly the content most likely to arrive as several text nodes. Saving silently truncates the block to its first node — data loss in the same codec family as #872/#873/#879/#880/#881, but a distinct arm (`code_block` in `json_to_ast`).

## Suggested fix

Concatenate the `text` of **all** children of the code block (skipping/handling non-text children the same way the first-child code does today — i.e. treat a missing `text` as empty rather than aborting), e.g.:

```rust
let content = json["content"].as_array().map_or(String::new(), |arr| {
    arr.iter().filter_map(|n| n["text"].as_str()).collect()
});
```

and keep the existing `format!("{content}\n")` literal construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Regression test: a `code_block` with two or more text children round-trips with all text present, in order.
- [ ] Single-node and empty code blocks behave exactly as before.
- [ ] Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass (`cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::`).
- [ ] Coordination: PR #878 (for #872/#873) is in flight in the same file — sequence or rebase so the img-codec changes do not conflict.

title: id(web): table column alignment is dropped by the markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec — save rewrites the delimiter row
body:
## Bug

In `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, table column alignment (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`) is dropped by the markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec in both directions:

- Parse direction: `convert_node`'s `NodeValue::Table` arm (markdown.rs:~379 on main 45c817e0) ignores the comrak `NodeTable.alignments` it already has in hand and emits a bare `{"type":"table"}` with no alignment information.
- Save direction: `json_to_ast`'s `"table"` arm (markdown.rs:~753) hardcodes `alignments: vec![TableAlignment::None; num_columns]`, so comrak renders a plain `|---|` delimiter row regardless of the source.

## Verified repro (this run, main 45c817e0)

Temporary probe test run with `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::` (probe removed after the run; assertions below are the acceptance tests):

Input markdown:

```
| a | b |
|:--|--:|
| 1 | 2 |
```

1. `markdown_to_prosemirror` returns a table whose rows/cells carry no alignment anywhere:
   `{"type":"table","content":[{"type":"table_row","content":[{"type":"table_header",...},{"type":"table_header",...}]}, ...]}`
2. `prosemirror_to_markdown` of that document emits:

```
| a | b |
| - | - |
| 1 | 2 |
```

Left/right alignment is gone after one load/save round trip — the document renders differently (numbers no longer right-aligned) with no error or warning.

## Why it matters

Alignment is the only column-level formatting markdown tables have, and right-aligned numeric columns are the common case in notes/docs edited in the id web UI. Silent formatting loss on save, in the same codec family as #872/#873/#879/#880 but a distinct node (table metadata).

## Suggested fix

- Parse direction: carry the alignments through the ProseMirror representation — e.g. an `alignments` attr on the table node (`["left","none","center","right", ...]`), or per-cell attrs on the first row's header cells if the editor schema prefers cell-level data. Pick whichever the web editor schema can hold without breaking existing documents (absent = all `None`, as today).
- Save direction: read that representation in `json_to_ast`'s table arm and populate `NodeTable.alignments` (defaulting to `None` per column when absent or short), instead of the hardcoded `vec![None; num_columns]`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Round-trip test: a table with left/center/right/unspecified columns survives `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown` with the same delimiter row semantics (re-parsing yields the same `alignments` vector).
- [ ] Tables without alignment markers round-trip exactly as before.
- [ ] Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass (`cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::`).
- [ ] Coordination: PR #878 (for #872/#873) is in flight in the same file — sequence or rebase so the img-codec changes do not conflict.

title: id(web): linked images [![alt](src)](href) lose their link in the markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec — save strips the href
body:
## Bug

In `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, a linked image — `[![alt](img.png)](https://example.com)` — loses its link in the markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec, in both directions:

- Parse direction (`convert_node`, `NodeValue::Link` / `NodeValue::Image` arms, markdown.rs:~291-323 on main 45c817e0): a `Link` node is converted via `collect_inline_children`, which flattens mark wrappers. The `Image` child is **not** a mark wrapper and is converted without the accumulated marks — the image branch never looks at `active_marks` — so the resulting ProseMirror image node carries only `src`/`alt`/`title`. The `href` is gone before the editor ever sees the document.
- Save direction (`json_to_ast`): there is likewise no representation for an image wrapped in a link, so even a ProseMirror doc that somehow held the link could not emit one.

## Verified repro (this run, main 45c817e0)

Temporary probe test run with `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::` (probe removed after the run; assertions below are the acceptance tests):

1. `markdown_to_prosemirror("[![alt](img.png)](https://example.com)")` returns:
   `{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"image","attrs":{"src":"img.png","alt":"alt"}}]}]}` — no trace of `https://example.com`.
2. `prosemirror_to_markdown` of that document emits: `![alt](img.png)` — the link target is silently deleted on the first load/save round trip.

## Why it matters

Linked images (badges, thumbnails linking to full-size images, screenshot links) are common in notes and docs. Opening such a document in the id web editor and saving it — even with no edits — permanently strips the link. Silent data loss on the save path, in the same codec family as #872/#873/#879 but a distinct node combination (Link wrapping Image).

## Suggested fix (either representation is acceptable — pick what the editor schema supports)

- Preferred: when an image is the sole child of a link, represent it in ProseMirror in a form the editor already understands for linked images, and teach `json_to_ast` to wrap the emitted `NodeValue::Image` in a `NodeValue::Link` for that form.
- Or: carry the link as an attribute on the image node (e.g. `linkHref`) through both converters, with `json_to_ast` wrapping the image in a Link node (or emitting the `[![alt](src)](href)` form) when the attribute is present.
- Images with additional siblings inside the link (e.g. `[see ![alt](img.png) now](href)`) should keep the existing text-mark behaviour for the text parts and must not crash or drop the image.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Round-trip test: `[![alt](img.png)](https://example.com)` survives `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown` with the href intact (exact emitted form may differ, but re-parsing it must yield an image inside a link to the same URL).
- [ ] Plain images and plain text links round-trip exactly as before.
- [ ] Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass (`cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::`).
- [ ] Coordination: PR #878 (for #872/#873) is in flight in the same file — sequence or rebase so the img-codec changes do not conflict.

title: id(web): prosemirror_to_markdown emits inline code containing backticks with a single-backtick fence — save corrupts the code span
body:
## Bug

In `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, `create_marked_text` converts a ProseMirror text node with a `code` mark into a comrak `NodeCode` with a hardcoded fence length:

```rust
// markdown.rs:829-834 (main 45c817e0)
return arena.alloc(AstNode::from(NodeValue::Code(comrak::nodes::NodeCode {
    num_backticks: 1,
    literal: text.to_owned(),
})));
```

When the code text itself contains a backtick, the single-backtick fence comrak emits is terminated early by the backtick inside the literal, so the saved markdown no longer means what the editor showed.

## Verified repro (this run, main 45c817e0)

Temporary probe tests run with `cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::` (probes removed after the run; the assertions below are the acceptance tests):

1. `markdown_to_prosemirror("Use ``a`b`` here")` is correct:
   `{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Use "},{"type":"text","text":"a`b","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" here"}]}]}`
2. `prosemirror_to_markdown` of that document emits: ``Use `a`b` here`` — a single-backtick span whose content ends at the inner backtick.
3. Re-parsing the emitted markdown gives a different document: code span `a`, plain text `b`, then a stray unmatched backtick in ` here`:
   `...{"text":"a","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"text":"b"},{"text":"` here"}...`

So one save/load round trip silently corrupts inline code containing a backtick: part of the code becomes plain text and a literal backtick leaks into the prose. The same applies to code text that starts or ends with a backtick (e.g. `` ` `` alone, or `a\``), where CommonMark also requires padding spaces inside the fence.

## Why it matters

This is the save path for the id web editor: any note/document whose inline code mentions a backtick (shell snippets, markdown documentation, template literals) is mangled on save with no error. Same round-trip codec family as #872/#873, but a distinct node type (`code` mark, not `image`).

## Suggested fix

In the `code` branch of `create_marked_text`, choose the fence from the literal:

- `num_backticks` = (longest run of backticks in the text) + 1.
- If the literal starts or ends with a backtick, pad the literal with a space on both ends (the CommonMark convention comrak itself uses when parsing `` `` `a` `` ``), and make sure the parse direction strips exactly that padding — verify what comrak's parser already does with padded code spans before adding manual handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Round-trip test: ` ``a`b`` ` (and variants: text that is only a backtick, text starting/ending with a backtick, text containing a double-backtick run) survives `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown` → `markdown_to_prosemirror` unchanged.
- [ ] Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass (`cargo test --features web --lib web::markdown::`).
- [ ] Coordination: PR #878 (for #872/#873) is in flight in the same file — sequence or rebase so the img-codec and code-mark fixes do not conflict.

body:
Observed 2026-10-25 while connecting opencode + openchamber after the GitHub App installation was extended.

Running `./pm-stack/connect-repo.sh connect opencode` (and `connect openchamber`) completes the import correctly (Kaneo task/link counts update as expected), but the summary-printing snippet fails:

```
import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);print(f"{d[\"imported\"]} imported, {d[\"updated\"]} updated, {d[\"skipped\"]} skipped")
SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character
```

title: Consolidate open PRs #870 and #874: both rewrite the id-check 'check' job for #869 — #874 supersedes #870, merge only one
body:
## Finding (from PR diff review)

Two OPEN PRs both rewrite the same `check` job in `.github/workflows/id-check.yml` for the same issue (#869), from the same base blob (`ca36d574`), and they cannot both land:

- **PR #870** — `ci(id): raise nix flake check job timeout 60m → 90m`. One line: `timeout-minutes: 60` → `90` on the serial `check` job. Described in its own body as the *interim* fix; the durable fix is #869.
- **PR #874** — `ci(id): run PR flake checks as a parallel matrix (#869)`. Restructures the same file: the serial `check` job is replaced by a `guard` job, a per-check `check_each` matrix (30m per-check cap), and a thin aggregator that keeps the required status name `nix flake check`. Its body states: "Supersedes #870 (the 60m → 90m timeout bump): the serial job it padded no longer exists. If this merges first, #870 should be closed as superseded."

## Why it matters

- The two PRs touch the same lines of the same job, so whichever merges second conflicts — and #870's change is meaningless once #874 lands (the job it pads no longer exists).
- Conflicting guidance is live right now: PR #874 says close #870 as superseded if it merges first, while the sweep backlog entry for #870 says "NEXT: merge when its checks land." Following the backlog first would merge the interim bump, immediately force a conflict/rework on #874, and spend another ~51-minute serial flake-check cycle on a job shape that is about to be deleted.
- #874's own verification is still in flight (per-check matrix jobs running at review time), so the sequencing decision is not yet forced — it should be made once, here, instead of being rediscovered by whichever sweep touches either PR next.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly one of #870 / #874 is merged for the #869 timeout problem; the other is closed as superseded with a comment linking this issue and the surviving PR.
- [ ] If #874 merges first: close #870 as superseded (per #874's own note) — do not merge the 90m bump afterwards.
- [ ] If #870 is deliberately merged first as a stopgap (e.g. #874's matrix verification fails), #874 is rebased onto it promptly and this issue records that choice, so the pair is not left drifting.
- [ ] The stale backlog instruction "merge #870 when its checks land" is superseded by the decision recorded here.

Evidence gathered 2026-10-25 by the pr-diff-review job: `gh pr diff 870` (single timeout line, base blob ca36d574), `gh pr diff 874` (full restructure of the same job, same base blob), both PRs OPEN and MERGEABLE at review time, no existing issue naming the pair (search for "870" in titles returned 0).

title: id(web): prosemirror_to_markdown emits img src/alt/title unescaped — quotes truncate values and can inject attributes on reparse
body: ## Problem The reverse conversion in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` emits an HTML `` tag by interpolating the image node's `src`/`alt`/`title` values into double-quoted attributes with no escaping at all (markdown.rs:730-754, the `width.is_some() || height.is_some()` branch; there is no escape helper anywhere in markdown.rs). Any value containing a `"` breaks the tag, and the breakage is lossy on the next load: - Node `{src: "x.png", alt: "a \"quoted\" caption", width: 100}` is written to the saved markdown as ``. Re-parsing that tag yields `alt = "a "` — the rest of the caption is silently dropped. - Worse, a value can inject attributes: `alt = "x\" title=\"injected"` is emitted as ``, and the re-parse produces a real `title = "injected"` the document never had. The same applies to `src` and `title` values containing quotes (a crafted `src` can manufacture `alt`/`width` attributes on reparse). Verified this run (2026-10-25) on main `7ce0d74c` with a standalone rustc harness replicating the emission `format!` code and re-parsing with `parse_img_tag`'s verbatim `attr_value` helper: both cases above reproduce exactly as shown. ## Why it matters Image node attributes are strings the node model places no restriction on: alt text comes from markdown image syntax, from uploaded-file names (`result.name` in the web editor), and from collaborating clients' document JSON. Whenever such an image also carries a width or height — exactly the case the HTML-emission branch exists for — saving the document writes a malformed tag, and the next open/save cycle silently truncates the attribute or invents new ones. That is slow-motion document corruption of the same class as #872 (which covers the parse direction of this same tag codec), but a distinct defect with a distinct fix: this one is missing output escaping, not substring matching. ## Suggested fix Escape attribute values on emission: at minimum `"` → `"` (and `&` → `&` first, so existing entities are not double-decoded), for `src`, `alt`, and `title`. Note the interplay with #872: the parser (`parse_img_tag`) does not currently decode entities, so emission and parsing should agree on one convention — if emission escapes, parsing should decode `"`/`&` in values so the round trip is value-preserving. Coordinate the two fixes so the pair forms a consistent codec rather than two half-codecs. ## Acceptance criteria - Round-trip pin: an image node with `alt = "a \"quoted\" caption"` and a width survives ProseMirror → markdown → ProseMirror with the alt value byte-identical. - An alt/title/src value containing `" title="` (or similar) cannot create or alter other attributes on reparse. - Values containing `&` round-trip without double-escaping or entity corruption (state the chosen convention in a test). - Existing image conversion tests in markdown.rs keep passing. Related: #872 (parse direction of the same `` attribute codec). Single-repo: this conversion code exists only in `developing-today/code` (`pkgs/id`).

title: id(web): parse_img_tag substring search lets data-src/data-width shadow the real img attributes — save rewrites the image URL
body: ## Problem `parse_img_tag` in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:551-597` extracts `` attributes by searching the raw tag string for the first occurrence of `{name}="` (the `attr_value` helper, markdown.rs:558-564). A substring search cannot tell a real attribute from a longer attribute whose name ends with the same text, or from text inside an earlier attribute's value — so prefixed attributes silently shadow the real ones during markdown → ProseMirror conversion: - `` → image node gets `src = "lazy.png"` (the lazy-loading placeholder, not the image) - `` → `width = 5` - `` → `alt = "decoy"` - `` → a spurious `title = "quoted"` is extracted from inside the alt value Verified this run (2026-10-25) on main `7ce0d74c` with a standalone rustc harness running the exact `attr_value` code verbatim: all four cases above return the shadowed/wrong value; the plain `` control returns the correct values. ## Why it matters This is not just a display glitch — it corrupts the document on save. `markdown_to_prosemirror` builds the editor's image node from these attributes (callers at markdown.rs:317 block and :339 inline), and `prosemirror_to_markdown` (markdown.rs:730-754) writes the node's `src`/`alt`/`title`/`width`/`height` back out when the document is saved. Opening a markdown file that uses the extremely common `data-src` lazy-loading pattern (or `data-width`/`data-alt`) in rich mode and saving it — even after editing an unrelated paragraph — silently rewrites the image to point at the placeholder/decoy value. The real URL is lost from the document. The same exact-match pattern also misses legal spellings the conversion silently degrades instead: single-quoted values (`src='x.png'`), whitespace around `=` (`src = "x.png"`), and uppercase attribute names all make `attr_value` return `None` for `src`, so `parse_img_tag` returns `None` and the image falls back to a code block (block context, markdown.rs:324-335) or raw text (inline, markdown.rs:343). Those can be treated as a secondary facet if the fix's parser handles them naturally. ## Suggested fix Parse the tag attribute-by-attribute instead of searching substrings: scan `name=value` pairs left to right from after `` converts to an image node with `src = "real.png"`; attribute order does not matter (`src` first, `data-src` second also yields `real.png`). - `data-width`/`data-height`/`data-alt`/`data-title` no longer shadow the real attributes, in either order. - An attribute-looking substring inside an earlier attribute's quoted value (e.g. `title=` inside `alt="..."`) is not extracted as an attribute. - Round-trip pin: markdown containing a `data-src` + `src` image survives markdown → ProseMirror → markdown with the real `src` unchanged. - Existing image tests keep passing (e.g. `test_image`, the width/height HTML emission tests in markdown.rs); new regression tests cover the cases above. - Single-repo: `parse_img_tag` exists only in `developing-today/code` (`pkgs/id`); no counterpart in the opencode/openchamber/nix repos.

title: CI: id flake check takes ~51min and dies at the job timeout — make the checks faster or move some off the PR path
body:
## Problem

The `id` workflow's `nix flake check` job (`.github/workflows/id-check.yml`) is the bottleneck for every pkgs/id PR:

- When it passes, it takes ~51 minutes (PR #810).
- Roughly as often, it is **cancelled at the 60-minute `timeout-minutes` cap** before finishing (PRs #771 and #833, both 2026-10-25) — the PR then merges on local verification alone, or waits for a re-run that may also be cancelled.
- Evidence and timing data are documented on #551.

An interim bump of the timeout to 90 minutes is landing separately (Drew's directive, 2026-10-25) so fewer runs die at the cap, but that treats the symptom: an hour-plus PR gate is too slow regardless of where the cap sits.

## Ask

Make the PR flake checks fast enough that the timeout stops mattering — or reconsider whether all of them belong on the PR path at all. Directions worth evaluating:

1. **Split the check set across parallel jobs** instead of one serial `nix flake check` run, so wall time is the slowest single check, not the sum.
2. **Move the heaviest checks to the nightly** (`id-e2e-nightly.yml` already exists as the heavy lane, per the #292 split) and keep the PR lane to fast unit/lint/type checks.
3. **Skip checks for changes that cannot affect them** (e.g. docs-only or web-only diffs) via path filtering within pkgs/id.
4. **Improve cache hit rates** — check whether magic-nix-cache throttling (#774's HTTP 418s) is forcing cold rebuilds that inflate run times.

## Acceptance

- Median PR `nix flake check` wall time demonstrably well under the job timeout (target: under ~20 minutes), measured over several merged PRs; or
- A documented decision, with data, on which checks move off the PR path and where they run instead.
- The 90-minute interim timeout can come back down once the speed work lands.

Related: #551 (fast CI lane), #774 (Magic Nix Cache 418 throttling).

title: nix ci red on main: proxy-port guard misses muse/commandcode proxies — opencode.jsonc hardcodes 18747/18748
body:
## Problem

`nix ci` (treefmt job) fails on main since the fleet proxy/config commits (a936e167, f5749275, 187da70d):

- `.github/scripts/check-proxy-port-fallbacks.sh` fails with: `.opencode/opencode.jsonc hardcodes a literal proxy port — use {env:<VAR>:-<port>} so the copies cannot drift (#435).`
- Verified on main a480b6a0 and 7ce0d74c: nix ci runs 40182802819 / 40183235188 FAILURE; the same failure hits unrelated PRs branched from current main (e.g. PR #857's fresh treefmt run 40182863546).

## Root cause

`home/common/default.nix` gained two proxies — `museProxyPort = 18747` and `commandcodeProxyPort = 18748` — whose scripts already use the guarded pattern (`bin/muse-proxy.mjs:32 parseProxyPort('MUSE_PROXY_PORT', 18747)`, `bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs:58 parseProxyPort('COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT', 18748)`, session var COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT at default.nix:614), but:

1. the guard script's proxy table still lists only the original five, so the two new ports are never checked, and
2. `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` keeps literal ports: the live `commandcode` provider baseURL (line 4216, `127.0.0.1:18748`) and the commented-out `muse` provider baseURL (line 4149, `127.0.0.1:18747`), both matching the guard's literal-port grep.

## Fix (in the sweep PR)

- Add MUSE_PROXY_PORT and COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT rows to the guard's proxy table.
- opencode.jsonc: use `{env:MUSE_PROXY_PORT:-18747}` (commented muse provider) and `{env:COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT:-18748}` (commandcode provider).

## Acceptance

- `bash .github/scripts/check-proxy-port-fallbacks.sh` passes (7 proxies).
- nix ci treefmt job green on main again.

title: antigravity-ls-proxy: translate model tool calls into OpenAI tool_calls (route is text-only today)
body:
## Problem

`antigravity-ls` is the fleet's one Antigravity provider (2026-10-24 decision; `antigravity-agy` is disabled as the parked fallback), but no OpenCode session routed through it can execute tools. Models return their tool calls as plain text and `tool_calls` is always null, so a coding session on this provider announces actions and does nothing.

This went unseen because every "verified working" check was a text completion probe (laptop pass 2026-10-24: agy 6s / ls 2s). Tool execution over this route was never verified.

## Evidence (2026-10-25, laptop, direct proxy probes)

`POST http://127.0.0.1:18745/v1/chat/completions` with an OpenAI `tools` payload (a single `run_echo` function, "call the tool, do not answer in text"):

- `gemini-3-flash` → `finish_reason: stop`, `tool_calls: null`, content = a fenced JSON block naming the function and arguments.
- `claude-opus-5-5` in a live OpenCode session (ses_e93894d2, 2026-10-25 ~04:23 CDT) streamed Anthropic `<invoke name="shell">` XML blocks as text; the turn ended "succeeded" with zero tools executed. (A later direct probe of the Claude model returned 429 — the Antigravity account's Claude quota fraction is separately exhausted; that is a quota state, not this bug.)

## Root cause

`bin/antigravity-ls-proxy.mjs` (~907 lines) is a text-flattening bridge:

- Request side: it serializes the conversation — including prior `tool_calls` and tool results — into prompt text (around lines 480–494).
- Response side: there is no tool-call handling at all. `grep` for `functionCall` / `function_call` in the file returns zero hits; nothing parses a language-server response into OpenAI `tool_calls`, and `finish_reason` is never `tool_calls`.

## Fix scope

- Parse LS responses for tool invocations per model family (Claude's XML invoke format; Gemini's function-call parts / JSON blocks) and emit structured OpenAI `tool_calls` with `finish_reason: "tool_calls"`, including on the streaming path if the proxy streams.
- Keep the existing request-side flattening of tool results, or replace it with the LS-native equivalent where one exists.
- Add a regression probe/test: a tools payload against the running proxy must return structured `tool_calls` for at least one Claude and one Gemini model (quota permitting for Claude).

## Acceptance

- An OpenCode session on `antigravity-ls/<model>` executes a shell tool end to end (tool part recorded as executed in the session, result fed back, work continues).
- The direct probe above returns `tool_calls` instead of a text block.

## Related

- code#480 (warm-session proxies) — same proxy family; this is the correctness gap underneath it.
- The still-owed antigravity benchmark (which model works with the plan, draws quota correctly, reuses sessions, caches, and is not ~10s+/command) cannot be run meaningfully for session work until this lands.

title: id(world): terminal shells send frames the host refuses (found by the F13.1 shell-contract check)
body:
## What

The first run of the new shell-contract conformance check (F13.1, #783) found three places where the terminal shells send frames the host refuses. Each passed the code review that created it: nothing checked a shell against the protocol.

1. **`id world join --command-mode` sends invalid frames.** `pump_command_frame` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs`) sent `/stats`, `/caps` and `/records` without the required `capability` field, and `/documents`, `/document`, `/logs` and `/help` as frame types that do not exist (`documents`, `document`, `logs`, `help`). The host answers `invalid world frame` to every one of them.
2. **`/stats` in an SSH `cmd:` session always fails.** `world_ssh` sends `{"type":"info","capability":…}` from the joined session and has a renderer for the `module_info` reply. But `handle_client_frame` (`pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs`) answers `info` with `already joined`, which also marks the SSH shell as errored. No test covered `/stats`.
3. **A wide SSH terminal is refused a view.** A pty wider than 500 columns or taller than 200 rows produces a `resize` outside the host's bounds, and the host answers with an error instead of a view. The browser clamps; SSH did not.

## Fix (in the F13.1 PR on `id/phase-13-impl`)

- The pump fills in the session capability and answers local-only commands on stderr, so stdout stays a pure JSON frame stream. A test checks every frame it sends against the contract.
- The host answers `info` in the joined phase, authorized by the session's own capability, as it already does for `records`. The SSH `cmd:` e2e test now runs `/stats`.
- The SSH shell clamps `resize` to the contract bounds: width 1..=500, height 1..=200.

Refs #783.

title: id(web): parseWorldSeed still silently reinterprets non-decimal forms — '0x10' installs seed 16, '1e3' seed 1000 (#707 residual)
body:
## Problem

`parseWorldSeed` (`pkgs/id/web/src/world-seed.ts:9-14`) — the parser for the world install/compile seed field, used by both flows in `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts:343` and `world.ts:465` — validates with `Number()` coercion:

```ts
const seed = Number(trimmed);
return Number.isSafeInteger(seed) && seed >= 0 ? seed : null;
```

`Number()` accepts every JavaScript numeric literal form, so text the admin typed is silently reinterpreted as a different seed than the digits shown:

| input | parsed seed |
|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | 16 |
| `"0b101"` | 5 |
| `"0o17"` | 15 |
| `"1e3"` | 1000 |
| `"+5"` | 5 |

Verified this run with a node probe of the exact function body on main `d95000a1`.

## Why it matters

- This is the residual half of #707: that fix stopped an *empty* field silently becoming seed 0 because the seed must be "anything the admin did not actually choose" — the module docstring says exactly that. A hex/scientific string is the same class of silent reinterpretation: the field shows one thing, the world installs with another.
- The seed is load-bearing: the install form states "The current world restarts at its module seed" (`pkgs/id/src/web/templates.rs:804`), so a mis-parsed seed silently produces different world state with no error anywhere.
- The sibling numeric parser in the same UI is deliberately strict about surface forms: `goto-line.ts` documents why it avoids bare `parseInt` semantics. `parseWorldSeed` should hold the same line — a seed field is a decimal integer field (the input is `type="number"`, `templates.rs:796`).

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseWorldSeed` accepts only an optional-whitespace-wrapped run of ASCII decimal digits (leading zeros OK) that fits a non-negative safe integer; `"0x10"`, `"0b101"`, `"0o17"`, `"1e3"`, `"+5"` all return `null`.
- Existing behavior is unchanged for `""`/whitespace (null), `"0"` (0), `" 42 "` (42), `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER`, negatives, fractions, and unsafe integers.
- `world-seed.test.ts` gains cases covering the rejected literal forms above.
- The web vitest suite passes.

title: PR #824 (Bolt coords cache): getLeftCoord returns 0 when coordsAtPos fails, defeating clusterOverlappingGroups' separate-cluster fallback

body:
## Finding

Open Jules/Bolt PR #824 ("cache coordsAtPos lookups in collab cursor plugin", commit ff04211f) changes the failure contract of `getLeftCoord` in `pkgs/id/web/src/cursors.ts`:

```ts
// PR #824 version
const getLeftCoord = view
  ? (pos: number): number => {
      const coords = getCachedCoords(pos);   // returns null when coordsAtPos throws (cached)
      return coords ? coords.left : 0;
    }
  : null;
```

On current main, `getLeftCoord` is `(pos) => view.coordsAtPos(pos).left` — it **throws** on failure, and its only consumer is designed around that. `clusterOverlappingGroups` in `pkgs/id/web/src/cursor-utils.ts` (lines 243-288 on main):

- lines 262-272: `try { firstLeft = getLeftCoord(...) ; clusterRightEdge = ... } catch { // If coords fail, put everything in separate clusters — return groups.map(separate) }`
- the per-group loop at line 277+ wraps `getLeftCoord` in the same try/catch pattern.

## Why it matters

With #824, a failed lookup returns `0` instead of throwing, so:

- The separate-cluster fallback in `clusterOverlappingGroups` becomes dead code for this caller.
- A cursor group whose coordinates cannot be measured gets `groupLeft = 0`, and `0 < clusterRightEdge + MIN_GAP(2)` is true in practice — unrelated cursor groups get merged into a single cluster/bar (a merged tooltip bar for cursors that are not actually adjacent), and a first-group failure seeds `clusterRightEdge` from a fictitious left edge of 0.
- The same PR handles the other call site correctly (line grouping: cached `null` still routes the cursor to the separate `-1` group), so the two halves of the function now disagree about what failure means.
- The PR adds no test for the failure path (changed files: `pkgs/id/web/src/cursors.ts` and `.jules/bolt.md` only); the claimed 374 passing tests exercise the happy path only.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `coordsAtPos` failure during clustering still yields separate clusters (preserve the throw contract, or return `null` from `getLeftCoord` and handle it explicitly in `clusterOverlappingGroups`)
- [ ] A regression test simulates `coordsAtPos` throwing and asserts separate clusters / no bar merging at left 0
- [ ] Existing `pkgs/id/web` tests and typecheck still pass

title: id(web): goto-line.test.ts typecheck fails on main — richSchema does not fit helper's narrow rawSchema type, blocks all id PRs
