body:
## Summary

Turso/libsql `GET /dump` output cannot always be replayed by a stock SQLite parser. When a database contains a virtual table whose `CREATE` statement itself contains single quotes — the common case is an FTS5 external-content table, e.g. `content='chunks'` — the dump registers the virtual table inside a `PRAGMA writable_schema=ON; ... OFF;` block with a statement like:

```sql
INSERT INTO sqlite_schema(type,name,tbl_name,rootpage,sql) VALUES('table','chunks_fts','chunks_fts',0,'CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE chunks_fts
      USING fts5(text, content='chunks', content_rowid='id')');
```

The embedded SQL text is emitted **verbatim**: its single quotes are not doubled (`''`), so the string literal terminates early and every stock SQLite parser fails with `near "chunks": syntax error`.

This is an upstream libsql dump-generation bug (the same class of bug stock `sqlite3 .dump` avoids by escaping). It is filed here only to document the quirk and the workaround; nothing is filed upstream.

## Impact

Found live 2026-10-27 on the `atlas` database: `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/scripts/export-turso.sh` downloads `/dump` and rebuilds it with `sqlite3 -bail`, which hard-fails on this statement — so any Turso database with a quoted virtual-table definition (FTS5 `content=` tables in practice) can never be filed into the cold store.

## Workaround (this repo)

`export-turso.sh` runs the downloaded dump through a streaming repair filter before the rebuild. The filter passes every line through byte-identical except `INSERT INTO sqlite_schema(...)` statements inside a `writable_schema` block whose final SQL literal is verifiably mis-escaped (a lone, undoubled single quote in the literal body): for those it rewrites the literal with proper `''` doubling so the statement parses and registers the virtual table exactly as authored. Correctly-escaped statements and all other lines pass through unchanged.

## Notes

- Detection is parse-based and conservative: a statement is only rewritten when its final literal cannot be a valid SQL string literal as emitted.
- The truncation guard (dump must end in `COMMIT;`) applies to the filtered stream.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/scripts/export-turso.sh` (or a helper it calls) contains the streaming repair filter the body describes: only `INSERT INTO sqlite_schema(...)` statements inside a `writable_schema` block whose final SQL literal is verifiably mis-escaped are rewritten, with `''` doubling; every other line passes byte-identical
- [ ] A fixture dump containing an FTS5 external-content virtual table (quoted `content=` definition) rebuilds cleanly through the export path with `sqlite3 -bail`
- [ ] Correctly-escaped dumps are unchanged by the filter (byte-identical output), and the `COMMIT;` truncation guard still applies to the filtered stream
- [ ] A test/fixture covers both the mis-escaped and correctly-escaped cases so the workaround cannot silently rot

title: id(web): image resize west handles (nw/sw) drag in the wrong direction — outward shrinks, inward grows

body:
## Summary

Resizing an image by its left-hand (west) corner handles moves the width in the
wrong direction: pulling the left edge outward (left) **shrinks** the image, and
pushing it inward (right) **grows** it. The east handles (ne/se) behave
correctly. The persisted width/height attrs on mouse-up inherit the inverted
size, so the wrong size is also what gets saved.

## Evidence (verified on main 95bfedb4, this run)

`pkgs/id/web/src/image-node-view.ts`:

- `:164` — `private startResize(e: MouseEvent, _corner: string)` — the corner
  argument is received and deliberately discarded (`_corner`).
- `:180-185` — `onResizeMove` always computes
  `newWidth = Math.max(50, this.startWidth + dx)` regardless of which handle
  started the drag.
- Handles nw/sw are positioned on the **left** edge
  (`pkgs/id/web/src/editor-compat.css:1301-1320`, `left: -5px`,
  `cursor: nw-resize` / `sw-resize`), so for them a leftward drag (negative
  `dx`) is the outward/widening motion — the formula treats it as shrinking.

Probe (targeted vitest, real `ImageNodeView` + real `EditorView`/`richSchema`,
happy-dom; start width falls back to 200px; probe removed after the run, log in
the creator's probe archive):

- se handle, drag right +50px → width `250px` (correct control)
- nw handle, drag left −50px (outward) → width `150px` (expected 250px)
- nw handle, drag right +50px (inward) → width `250px` (expected 150px)
- sw handle, drag left −50px (outward) → width `150px` (expected 250px)

`ImageNodeView` has no test file today (`pkgs/id/web/src/image-node-view.ts`
is the only editor component of its size without one), which is how this
shipped unnoticed.

## Why it matters

Half of the four resize handles do the opposite of what the user drags. Image
sizing is a core rich-editing gesture; users grabbing the natural left edge
get a fighting-the-mouse experience and can persist a wrong size on mouse-up
(`onResizeEnd` commits `offsetWidth/offsetHeight` via `updateAttrs`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Dragging nw/sw handles outward widens the image and inward shrinks it;
      ne/se behaviour unchanged; aspect ratio still maintained.
- [ ] The direction is derived from the corner passed to `startResize`
      (west corners invert the sign of `dx`); the min-width (50px) and
      editor max-width clamps still apply after the sign fix.
- [ ] New `image-node-view.test.ts` (or equivalent) covers all four corners'
      drag directions with a real `EditorView`, including the committed
      width/height attrs on mouse-up.
- [ ] Web unit tests + typecheck pass.

## Notes

Fix is small and self-contained in `image-node-view.ts`. Siblings in the same
component family, distinct defects: #1381 (image browser teardown), #1379 /
#1323 / #1321 (image upload handlers).

body:
Phase 1 of the mcpx supervisor design, #1384 (design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-stdio-supervisor.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace). This phase is deliberately the experiment that proves the attach model before any takeover code changes: everything here is additive and flag-gated.

## Scope

1. **Hidden `mcpx supervise` subcommand.** Re-exec of the same binary. It spawns exactly one stdio MCP server child with the process semantics `NewStdio` has today (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpclient/stdio.go`: own process group via `Setpgid`, plain `os.Pipe()`s rather than `cmd.Std*Pipe`, stderr captured to a ring buffer), owns the child's stdin/stdout/stderr for the child's whole life, and:
   - serves one attached daemon at a time over a unix socket in the mcpx state directory (socket file mode follows the 0600 state-file precedent, `internal/daemon/sessions.go`);
   - pumps stdin/stdout bytes between socket and child without interpreting MCP frames (framing stays in the daemon's transport reader);
   - buffers child output produced while no daemon is attached, up to a bounded limit; on overflow it keeps the tail and counts dropped bytes, reporting the count to the next daemon that attaches;
   - reports child PID and child exit (with exit error) to the attached daemon;
   - exits when its child has exited and no daemon is attached (no lingering supervisors for dead children).
2. **Supervised transport in `internal/mcpclient`** implementing the same transport interface the pool uses for `StdioTransport`, connecting to the supervisor socket instead of spawning a child. `Detach`/adoption semantics of the existing transport are not reused — a supervised transport's `Close` detaches from the supervisor without signalling the child.
3. **Per-server opt-in config flag** selecting the supervised transport for a stdio server. Default **off**. With the flag off, behaviour is byte-for-byte today's (direct spawn, existing takeover path untouched).

Out of scope: any change to `internal/daemon/takeover.go` or `internal/pool/handoff.go` (that is Phase 2); HTTP/SSE upstreams; making supervised the default (Phase 3).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the flag on for a stdio server, the server runs under a supervisor: child PID ≠ daemon-spawned direct child, and the supervisor's parent is not the daemon's serving process (child survives the daemon).
- [ ] Defining test: start daemon + supervised server, make a call, SIGKILL the daemon, start a new daemon — the child's PID is unchanged and a subsequent call on that server succeeds.
- [ ] Child exit while supervised is surfaced to the daemon exactly as a direct child's exit is today (existing pool behaviour/tests apply), and the supervisor process exits afterwards.
- [ ] Unattached-output buffer: a child that writes while no daemon is attached does not block indefinitely or grow memory unboundedly; the dropped-byte count is reported on attach (test covers overflow).
- [ ] With the flag off (default), the full existing mcpx test suite passes unchanged, including `internal/e2e/takeover_test.go`.
- [ ] `go test ./...` in `pkgs/mcpx` passes; new code has tests for the supervisor pump, attach/detach, and buffer overflow.

## Evidence / grounding

- Design: #1384; `pkgs/mcpx/TODO.md:3`; `planning/roadmaps/mcpx.md` (Next, supervisor, `idea`).
- Current spawn semantics to mirror: `internal/mcpclient/stdio.go` `NewStdio` (~line 86 onward).
- State-dir + 0600 precedent: `internal/daemon/sessions.go`.

body:
PLATFORM BLOCKER (split from #1363, findings 2026-10-27): the laptop's opencode server is reachable over the tailnet via `tailscale serve` (HTTPS, verified end-to-end from real tailnet clients), but the Muse sandbox cell cannot use ANY tailscale-serve route:

- The cell has no tailscale interface; its `tailscale` binary is a platform shim reporting "enrolled". Tailnet IPs route via the cell gateway (198.19.0.1); raw TCP to them returns "Operation not permitted".
- DNS for `*.raptor-pumpkinseed.ts.net` resolves to a fake IP (198.18.161.121) owned by the egress stack.
- The only egress is the Hatch egress proxy, which MITMs TLS (peer certs present as issued by "Hatch Sandbox Egress CA"). CONNECT + TLS to a serve endpoint complete, but every HTTP request to every serve port returns an empty reply (curl exit 52) — reproduced against the new opencode HTTPS serve, a temporary raw-TCP serve, and the pre-existing OpenChamber :3000 serve. SSH works only via the purpose-built CONNECT relay in ~/tools/laptop-proxy-connect.py.

What would unblock it (platform-level, any one of):
1. Give the cell a real tailnet node/interface so serve endpoints are reachable directly; or
2. Make the egress proxy pass CONNECT tunnels to tailnet serve ports through without the empty-reply behavior for client-first protocols (HTTP), as it already effectively does for SSH.

Until then the sandbox keeps the SSH-forward pattern (#1357 builds it as a helper) and #1363's from-the-sandbox end-state stays open. Evidence: #1363 result comment + the Tailscale-route addendum in the hub goal's opencode-access-benchmark-2026-10-27.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A platform change lands (real tailnet interface in the cell, OR egress-proxy CONNECT pass-through for tailnet serve ports) and is evidenced by a successful HTTPS request from the sandbox cell to a `*.raptor-pumpkinseed.ts.net` serve endpoint (HTTP response, not an empty reply).
- [ ] The reproduction from this issue (curl to the opencode serve endpoint and the OpenChamber :3000 serve) is re-run after the change and the result commented here.
- [ ] Until then, this issue stays open as the platform-blocker record and #1363's from-the-sandbox end-state references it.

body:
# id(web): image browser survives editor teardown — Insert on the destroyed view throws and the dialog stays stuck over the next document

## Evidence (verified this run, current main 0c37bb15)

`pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.ts`:

- `openImageBrowser(view, schema)` appends its overlay to `document.body` (line 97) and captures `view` in closures. There is **no exported close/cleanup function**, and no production code closes the browser when the editor goes away.
- The editor *does* go away under it: SPA navigation calls `app.closeEditor()` before swapping `#main` (`pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts:660`), and `closeEditor` disconnects collab and calls `view.destroy()` (`main.ts:1289`) — but nothing touches the body-level overlay, and swapping `#main`'s innerHTML does not remove it either. The same happens on collab reconnect, where the editor view is destroyed and re-created in place (`collab.ts`, MSG.INIT reconnect path). This is the same stale-singleton class as #718 (search panel / goto-line), which those two modules were fixed for — the image browser was not.
- Insert is not defensive: the Insert button handler is `insertImage(selectedImage); close();` (lines 72–75; double-click at 145–148 has the same shape), and `insertImage` dispatches on the captured view (line 158). If the view is destroyed, the dispatch throws **before** `close()` runs, so the dialog does not even dismiss itself.

Reproduced this run with a targeted vitest probe (real `EditorView` with `richSchema`, mocked `/api/images` fetch; probe removed after verification, log in the fleet's probe archive `probe-2026-10-27-creator-b2/out2.log`):

- Open the browser, one image card renders; click it → Insert becomes enabled.
- `view.destroy()` (exactly what `closeEditor` does on navigation) → the overlay is **still in the DOM**.
- Click Insert → throws `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'matchesNode')` from dispatching on the destroyed view, and the overlay is **still open afterwards**.

## Why it matters

Open the image browser, then navigate to another file (or get reconnected) before choosing: a modal from the *previous* document floats over the new one, its Insert button crashes with an uncaught error, and the button that should dismiss it is the one that throws — the user has to discover Escape/✕ to escape a dialog that should never have survived. Worse, the failure is silent about its cause: nothing tells the user the editor underneath changed.

## Suggested fix

Give the browser a lifecycle tied to its editor: export a `closeImageBrowser()` (mirroring `destroySearchPanel` / `destroyGotoLineDialog`) and call it from `closeEditor()` (and any other view-teardown path), and/or have `openImageBrowser` track its view and self-close when that view is destroyed / a new browser is opened for a different view. Additionally, make Insert/double-click dismiss in a `finally` (or guard the dispatch) so a failed insert can never trap the dialog open.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Regression test: open the browser, destroy the editor view (simulating `closeEditor` / navigation), and the overlay is no longer in the DOM — or, equivalently, Insert can no longer be reached for a destroyed view.
- [ ] Regression test: clicking Insert (and double-clicking a card) always closes the dialog, even if the insert dispatch throws.
- [ ] Normal path unchanged: with a live view, selecting an image and clicking Insert (or double-clicking) inserts the image node at the selection and closes the dialog.
- [ ] Existing web unit tests pass (`cd pkgs/id/web && bunx vitest run`, at minimum the editor/image suites).

title: id(web): mixed task/plain lists cannot be saved at all — parse builds mixed lists its own placement validation rejects

body:
## Problem

A markdown list that mixes checkbox items with plain items — a very common checklist shape — **cannot be saved at all** in the id web editor. The codec's parse direction produces a ProseMirror doc its own save direction rejects, so every save of the document fails; the doc is also invalid under the editor's own schema.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `0cbb91b1`)

Probe: verbatim copy of `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` in a standalone crate (comrak 0.56.0), `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown`. Logs: fleet bookkeeping `probe-2026-10-27-creator-a/out2.log` + `out3.log`.

All four mixed shapes fail the same way:

| Input | Parsed PM shape | Save result |
|---|---|---|
| `- [ ] todo` / `- plain note` / `- [x] done` | `task_list` containing a `list_item` | `Err: Misplaced node: list_item cannot appear inside task_list` |
| `- plain note` / `- [ ] todo` / `- [x] done` | `bullet_list` containing `task_list_item`s | `Err: Misplaced node: task_list_item cannot appear inside bullet_list` |
| `1. [ ] todo` / `2. plain step` / `3. [x] done` | `task_list` (order 1) containing a `list_item` | `Err: Misplaced node: list_item cannot appear inside task_list` |
| `1. plain step` / `2. [ ] todo` | `ordered_list` containing a `task_list_item` | `Err: Misplaced node: task_list_item cannot appear inside ordered_list` |

Root cause, both directions:

- Parse: the `List` arm decides task-vs-plain from the **first child only** (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:223-226` — `is_task_list` = first child is a `TaskItem`), then converts every child by its own kind, producing a mixed-children list node.
- Save: `prosemirror_to_markdown` first runs the #1043 placement validation (`markdown.rs:1057-1058`), and `placement_allowed` (`markdown.rs:980-981`) allows only `ListItem` under bullet/ordered lists and only `TaskListItem` under `task_list` — so the parse direction's own output is rejected.
- The save route propagates the error (`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1984-1989`, `ContentMode::Markdown`), so the user's save fails outright — not a silent rewrite, a hard failure on any edit to the file.
- The editor schema agrees the doc is invalid: `task_list` declares `content: "task_list_item+"` (`pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:98-100`), so the mixed doc cannot be represented faithfully in the editor either.

Controls from the same probe: pure task lists (bullet, ordered, nested, in blockquotes) and pure plain lists round-trip cleanly; nested task sublists under plain items also work — only same-level mixing breaks.

## Why it matters

Checklists with interleaved plain notes/steps are everywhere (shopping lists with headers, procedures with checkbox steps, meeting notes). Today, opening such a file in id and making any edit makes the file unsavable — the user discovers it only when the save errors, with their edit stranded. The #1043 validation did its job (no panic, clean error); the gap is that the parse direction manufactures docs the rest of the system forbids.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four mixed shapes above open and save without error; checkbox states and plain items are all preserved, and the saved form is a fixpoint on a second save.
- [ ] The chosen representation is coherent across all three layers — codec parse, codec save (placement validation), and the editor schema (`editor.ts`) — with a note in the PR on which shape was picked (e.g. split into adjacent sibling lists at parse time, mirroring the #1032 coalescing precedent in reverse; or mixed children allowed end-to-end) and what it does to list numbering/tightness for ordered lists.
- [ ] Pure task lists and pure plain lists round-trip byte-identically to today (existing tests keep passing).
- [ ] Regression tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover mixed bullet and mixed ordered lists in both first-child orders.
- [ ] No relaxation of the #1043 placement validation for genuinely misplaced nodes (its five panic-shape tests keep passing).

body:
From the access-pattern benchmark (code#1344): both laptop opencode servers (background service :13420, OpenChamber's :37621) bind 127.0.0.1 only, so every network attach pays for an SSH forward and each call carries the DERP RTT (~0.45s). The stack already has a tailnet-bind precedent (pm-aggregator binds 100.99.113.103:4870). Server password auth is enforced (401 unauthenticated), so binding is the only missing piece.

Evaluate (design + small trial, not a config flip): a second, tailnet-bound serve instance or a tailscale-serve-style relay for the background service, restricted to the tailnet interface, password auth on, CORS/origin implications checked against OpenChamber's remote-instance flow. Measure the per-call delta vs the forward (expect RTT-bound improvement only if a direct path exists; DERP hairpin may erase it — measure, don't assume).
Acceptance: a written verdict with measurements; if favorable, the binding ships behind the laptop's normal config flow with the access pattern documented in the benchmark report's terms.

## Acceptance criteria
- A written verdict exists (issue comment or linked doc) on whether a tailnet-bound serve instance or tailscale-serve-style relay is viable for the laptop background service, with password auth on and CORS/origin implications for OpenChamber's remote-instance flow checked.
- The per-call latency delta vs the SSH-forward path is measured (not assumed), including whether a direct tailnet path exists or DERP hairpin erases the gain.
- If the verdict is positive, a follow-up implementation issue is filed; if negative, the reasoning is recorded on this issue and it is closed.

body:
## Work (Drew, 2026-10-27)

A daily pool-intelligence job (`pool-intelligence`) maintains the
fleet's model of the model market — ours and Artificial Analysis's:

- **AA monitoring:** pull current Artificial Analysis intelligence /
  speed / price data for every model in (or adjacent to) our pools.
  If AA's API needs a key we don't have, record that as the gap and
  use the public pages until a key exists; never invent a number.
- **Our own measurements:** from real fleet runs (session records,
  route attempts, babysitter log, queue outcomes), maintain per
  provider/model/effort: output tokens/sec, wall-clock per completed
  task, first-response latency where observable, success/stall
  rates. Our measurements outrank AA's where they disagree — AA is
  the prior, our runs are the evidence; record both.
- **Interpretive model** (living doc, goal workspace `files/`): how
  we read an AA point against our pools — what a 1-point AA
  difference is worth in speed/cost on OUR work, per task class.
  Updated as measurements accumulate; every claim in it cites its
  data window.
- **Add/retire flags:** the standing output. A flag names the model,
  the pool, and the quantified trade: "X is missing: AA ≈ pool
  median +2, 1.8× our measured speed of the pool's slowest member,
  plan-covered" or "Y should retire from workhorse: fast enough but
  costs the pool its scarcest window; Z is −1 AA, faster, and
  cheaper on our measurements." Flags become issues with the numbers
  attached; a flag is a hypothesis, and the controlled-test issue
  (sibling) is how it earns a config change.
- Feed the steward: flags + measurements land where the steward and
  meta-reviewer read them each cycle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Job live; first intelligence report covers every pooled model
      with AA values (or the recorded AA-access gap) + our measured
      speeds where runs exist.
- [ ] The interpretive-model doc exists with its first data window.
- [ ] First add/retire flag filed as its own issue with quantified
      tradeoffs, or an explicit "no flag survives the numbers"
      result with the table that shows why.

body:
## Bug

In the id web editor, pasting (or dropping) images where **every** image exceeds `MAX_IMAGE_SIZE` (10 MB) silently does nothing: the paste/drop is claimed by the image-upload plugin, the browser default is prevented, and no content of any kind is inserted. The only feedback is a `console.warn`, which users never see.

## Evidence

`pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.ts`:

- `handlePaste` (~L185-202): filters `clipboardData.files` to image files; if any image file exists it calls `event.preventDefault()` and returns `true` — before the size check. In the loop, oversized files are skipped with `continue` after a `console.warn` (~L193-196). If all image files are oversized, the handler has already claimed the paste and inserts nothing.
- `handleDrop` (~L204-228) has the identical shape: `preventDefault()` + claim first, size filter inside the loop.

Verified this run on main `1bf2afb2` with a targeted vitest probe against the real plugin props (probe since removed):

- Single oversized PNG (`MAX_IMAGE_SIZE + 1` bytes): `handlePaste` returned `true`, `preventDefault` called once, `view.dispatch` called **0** times — nothing uploaded, nothing inserted, paste swallowed.
- Control (text file only, no image): returned `false`, no `preventDefault` — normal paste proceeds.

Because the event is claimed, any other clipboard content in the same paste (e.g. text/HTML copied alongside an image from a web page) is also lost, not just the image.

## Why it matters

A user pasting a large screenshot or photo (camera photos and retina screenshots routinely exceed 10 MB) gets a completely silent no-op in a collaborative editor — indistinguishable from the app hanging or the paste being lost. This is the same class of silent-failure defect as the txt save data-loss issues (#1306/#1307): the app claims an action and drops user content without a word.

## Acceptance criteria

- When no pasted/dropped file will actually be uploaded (all images oversized), the handler does **not** claim the event: it returns `false` without `preventDefault()`, so ProseMirror's default paste/drop handling (text/HTML content, if any) still runs.
- When at least one image is accepted, oversized siblings are still skipped, and the rejection is surfaced to the user in the UI (not only `console.warn`) — e.g. a visible notice naming the file and the 10 MB limit. (If the notice mechanism needs a design choice, the un-claiming fix alone satisfies the data-loss half; file the notice as a follow-up.)
- Regression tests in `pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.test.ts` driving `handlePaste`/`handleDrop` with stub views/events: oversized-only paste returns `false` and never dispatches; mixed valid+oversized paste uploads only the valid file; oversized-only drop behaves the same as paste.
- Existing web tests still pass (`cd pkgs/id/web && bun run test` / vitest).

body:
# id(web): saving a .txt file silently deletes every list, quote, code block and table

## Summary

A `.txt` document is edited in the full rich editor, but the save path
extracts only paragraph and heading text. Every other block the editor
allows — bullet/ordered/task lists, blockquotes, code blocks, tables,
horizontal rules — is **silently deleted** on save, with a success
response. This is unrecoverable data loss for any `.txt` file whose
author used the toolbar, markdown shortcuts, paste, or a collab peer's
edit to create a non-paragraph block.

## Evidence

- Editor side: `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:288-289` — `getSchema(mode)`
  returns `richSchema` for every mode except `raw`, and `:295`
  `hasToolbar` includes `plain`. The file comment at `:42` says the
  full schema (lists, GFM task lists, tables) applies to
  "rich/markdown/plain modes". So a `.txt` doc legitimately contains
  any block type.
- Save side: `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1976` `convert_doc_to_bytes`
  routes `.txt` (ContentMode::Plain) to `extract_plain_text`
  (`routes.rs:2009`). That function handles only `paragraph` and
  `heading` at the top level; the catch-all arm at `routes.rs:2049`
  is `_ => {}` — every other node is dropped without a log, error, or
  placeholder. (Inline non-text nodes are likewise dropped at `:2032`.)
- Verified this run on origin/main 90f7ea00 with a probe crate holding
  the verbatim `extract_plain_text` body (log:
  `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-2352/out4.log`): a doc containing
  paragraph "intro", a 2-item bullet list, a blockquote, a code block,
  a table cell and a paragraph "outro" extracted to exactly
  `"intro\noutro"` — the list items, quote, code and cell text all
  vanished.

## Why it matters

Silent, success-reported deletion is the worst failure class for a
documents app: the user only discovers the loss on the next open, and
by then the saved bytes are the only copy. The heading arm shows the
authors already knew non-paragraph blocks reach this function; the
remaining block types were simply never handled.

## Acceptance criteria

- Saving a `.txt` doc containing lists, blockquote, code block, table
  or horizontal rule no longer silently discards their text: either
  the text is extracted in a documented plain-text rendering (e.g.
  list item text per line, cell text per line), or the save fails
  loudly for docs it cannot represent — pick one policy, document it
  on `convert_doc_to_bytes`, and pin it with tests.
- A regression test in the web routes/markdown test suite covers at
  least: bullet list, blockquote, code block, table — asserting the
  saved `.txt` bytes contain their text (or the save errors, per the
  chosen policy).
- Paragraph/heading-only `.txt` docs save byte-identically to today.
- The markdown (`.md`) and raw save paths are unchanged.

## Suggested direction

Recursive text extraction over block children (list_item → its
paragraphs, blockquote → its blocks, table rows/cells → their
paragraphs, code_block → its text) is the smallest change that makes
`.txt` save loss-free for text content; formatting marks/structure
are inherently lost in plain text, text must not be.

## Gap found during triage of #241 (queue task 1254)

The bulk LogSync reset in #241 cannot be attributed because the test harness throws away the decisive evidence: in `pkgs/id/src/log_sync.rs`, `test_a_bulk_session_moves_every_event_across_pages` only awaits the responder's result channel (`results.recv()`) on the **success** path. 2. Run the **full** `pkgs/id` test suite (load is the trigger; a solo test run proves nothing) repeatedly — at least 5 runs or until the reset reproduces — and record both sides' errors verbatim here.
3. Verdict on #241: responder `Timeout` + client reset-by-peer ⇒ responder deadline drop; client `Timeout` ⇒ client side; neither ⇒ genuine QUIC-level reset, capture iroh endpoint logs next.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both sides' session errors are captured and posted verbatim for at least one reproduced reset, or 5 consecutive full-suite runs pass with no reset (recorded here)

title: Queue dedupe is a one-way door: a cancelled task permanently blocks re-enqueue of its issue

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: area/infra
labels.description: Infrastructure, deployment, and operations

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Bug (live instance found 2026-10-26, monitor run 23:19 CDT)

`agent.enqueue_repo_task` (migration 0008) inserts with
`on conflict (dedupe_key) do nothing` and then returns the existing
row — for **any** status, including `cancelled`. Combined with the
unique index on `dedupe_key`, a cancelled task permanently owns its
issue's work identity: the issue can never be enqueued again, and the
caller cannot tell, because enqueue returns the cancelled row as if
it had succeeded.

## Live instance

- Issue #551 (id-check flake leg exceeds its 60-minute cap) had an
  inert shadow task 1064 (attempts 0, never worked).
- The fleet monitor's safety net built a live triage packet for #551
  and was blocked by the dedupe wall; the operator cancelled 1064
  (verified `cancelled`, reason superseded) and retried the enqueue.
- The retry returned task 1064 — the cancelled shadow row — with no
  new task created. Verified in `agent.tasks`: exactly one row exists
  for `repo-health:v1:triage:developing-today/code:issue:551`, status
  cancelled. **#551 sits ownerless, and every future monitor run will
  repeat the same silent no-op.**

## Why it matters

The monitor's Duty 1 promise is "a filed issue with the work-order
label must never sit ownerless." This bug breaks that promise
*silently* for any issue whose task was ever cancelled — and the
fleet cancels tasks routinely (orphans, superseded packets,
issue-closed cleanups; e.g. nix task 1172 on 2026-10-26). Any of
those issues reopening hits the same wall.

## Proposed fix (pick one, migration + synthetic test like 0012)

- **(a) Revive on enqueue (recommended):** on conflict where the
  existing row is `cancelled`, update it back to `queued` with the
  new payload/priority/not_before, reset result/last_error, and write
  an `enqueued` event with `revived_from_cancelled: true`. Smallest
  schema change; keeps one row per identity; audit trail preserved.
- (b) Partial unique index on `dedupe_key` covering live statuses
  only — allows a second row per identity; weakens the "dedupe key
  names the task" lookups the monitor relies on.
- (c) An explicit `reopen_repo_task` verb — works, but every producer
  must learn to call it after a failed enqueue, and the silent-no-op
  shape remains for anyone who doesn't.

Decide whether `failed` tasks should revive the same way (probably
not — failure is a worked outcome; cancellation is an operator
decision. Record the reasoning either way).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Synthetic test: enqueue → cancel → enqueue same key returns a
      live `queued` task (revival event present); enqueue →
      enqueue (live) still returns the existing row unchanged.
- [ ] #551's triage packet enqueues successfully to
      repo-health-code-pilot and is claimable.
- [ ] The helper/monitor can distinguish "enqueued new", "already
      live", and "revived" from the returned row + events.

Child of epic #1233. Filed by Muse (operator) 2026-10-27, from the
fleet monitor's #551 flag.

body:
## Why

On 2026-10-26, GPT-6.1 Terra launched for OpenAI users. Our ChatGPT/Codex doors served it the same evening (probe-verified via `codex exec -m gpt-6.1-terra`), but nothing in our system surfaced it: the provider catalogs in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` are hand-curated subsets, last snapshotted 2026-10-24, and no process noticed the new model. Drew's policy (2026-10-26): **provider blocks list ALL models the provider allows, kept current automatically; gating belongs in `disabled_providers` and route membership.**

The one-shot catalog completion is a separate PR. This issue owns the RECURRING system.

## Spec

A scheduled job (suggested cadence: every 6 hours) that:

1. **Refreshes authoritative lists per provider**
   - Local proxies on the laptop: `claude-code` (:18749), `commandcode` (:18748), `openai-codex` (:18744) — `GET /v1/models`.
   - API/catalog providers: each provider's own models endpoint or published catalog (deepseek, meta, …).
   - `https://models.dev/api.json` as a cross-check for providers without a live endpoint.
   - A provider that cannot be enumerated is reported as such — never guessed.
2. **Diffs** each list against the catalog in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`.
3. **On new models**: opens a PR adding the entries — mirroring the sibling family's entry shape in that provider block (full variant ladders where the block carries them, limit-only or name-only where that's the block's style; limits from the provider/models.dev data, flagged in the PR body when a figure is third-party). PR body carries the evidence: source, snapshot time, added ids.
4. **On vanished models**: flags them in the PR body / a comment — never auto-removes (routes may still reference them; removal is a human/keeper call).
5. **On no drift**: silent. No PR, no notification.
6. **Feeds the data pipeline** (#1248): an unknown model id also opens the research trail — a dated note + follow-up issue in the Terra pattern (#1249) — so a launch triggers measurement-hunting automatically, not just a catalog entry.

## Acceptance

- A model appearing in any enumerated provider shows up as a catalog PR within one cadence window, with zero human prompting.
- Two consecutive runs with no upstream change produce no PRs and no noise.
- A run where a provider is unreachable degrades to a per-provider "not enumerable" note in the run log, not a failed job or fabricated entries.

## Context

- Existing tooling to build on: `~/workspace/opencode-provider-sync/` (audit scripts + snapshots from 2026-10-24/25).
- Config-change discipline unchanged: worktree from fresh origin/main, empty branch pushed first, surgical staging, merge commits; pool/route membership changes are NOT part of the auto-PR (catalog only).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A scheduled job (suggested cadence 6h) enumerates the authoritative model list per provider — laptop proxies (claude-code :18749, commandcode :18748, openai-codex :18744) via GET /v1/models, plus each API provider's own catalog source.
- [ ] When a provider's list differs from .opencode/opencode.jsonc, the job opens (or updates) a catalog PR containing the full allowed model list — gating stays in disabled_providers / route membership, never in the catalog subset.
- [ ] A no-change run is silent and opens no PR; a failed enumeration for one provider is reported per-provider and does not block the others.
- [ ] The job's first live catch or clean diff-verified run is recorded on this issue.

body:
## Finding
The delegation design (pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md §2, §4.1, §6 step 5) introduces a state the rest of the stack must join consistently: a needsDrew item whose `delegation.status` is `proposal-ready` (or `unable`). The simple path — proposal published, Drew approves from /attention, pass applies it — is covered by the UI and delegation-execution slices. The seams are not:

- The item can expire out of the section (24h unobserved rule) or be resolved by another path while a proposal is still on display; an approve click then targets a ghost.
- Drew can approve on a stale page render while a newer run has already replaced or withdrawn the proposal.
- A rejection reason, an inability return, and a re-delegation must compose: reject → delegate again → new proposal must not be confused with the rejected one.
- /today and the front-door overview count needsDrew items — a proposal-ready item is still Drew's item and must count and badge as such everywhere, not just on /attention.

## Proposal
A small, explicit state-handling slice:
- Proposal identity: a proposal is identified by (item id + `delegation.runId` + `delegation.updatedAt`); approve/reject actions carry that triple in their payload, and the consumer applies ONLY if it still matches the currently published proposal — a mismatch is `rejected` with note "proposal superseded/withdrawn", never a silent apply.
- Expiry/withdrawal: when the pass withdraws a proposal (item resolved elsewhere, proposal replaced), it publishes the item once with the delegation transition recorded, or expires it with the withdrawal in `actions[]`; the dashboard renders any pending approve/reject action on a vanished proposal as "no longer applicable" from the actions join, not as pending forever.
- One rendering rule everywhere: proposal-ready and unable items render/count as needsDrew with their state badge on /attention, /today's banner, and the front-door overview (#1134) — no surface may drop or double-count them.
- Re-delegation after rejection: the pass must mark a materially-new proposal (new runId) and the card shows "second first pass — previous rejected: <reason>" so Drew can see what changed.

## Acceptance
- Race test (fixture consumer): approve action carrying a stale (runId, updatedAt) → rejected with the superseded note; the current proposal is untouched.
- Expiry test: item expires while proposal-ready → pending proposal actions render "no longer applicable"; no surface counts a ghost item.
- Cross-surface test: one proposal-ready + one unable item in a fixture section → /attention, /today banner, and overview counts agree (2 needsDrew, badges shown).
- Reject → re-delegate → new proposal renders with the previous rejection reason visible.

Refs: #1184 (epic), #1152 (actions store), #1134 (front-door counts). Design: pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md §2.1, §6.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A proposal carries a stable identity (item + run/proposal id) so an approve always targets the proposal Drew saw; approving a superseded, withdrawn, or expired proposal is a visible no-op with an explanation, never a silent apply.
- [ ] Reject → re-delegate produces a new proposal that cannot be confused with the rejected one (identity + history visible), and rejection reasons / inability returns compose with re-delegation per the design (§2, §4.1, §6 step 5).
- [ ] needsDrew counts agree across /today, the front-door overview, and /attention while proposals expire, are replaced, or are resolved by another path (cross-surface count check).
- [ ] Race cases are covered by tests or a scripted verification: expire-while-displayed, approve-on-stale-render, resolve-by-other-path-while-proposed.

body:
## Finding
Drew's requirement (2026-10-26), verbatim intent: "I should be able to pass it off to the orchestrator for a first pass and then approve that, or just say, 'Yeah, no, the orchestrator can do all this unless it defines that it's not able to.'"

Today the orchestration pass has no delegation concept: a needsDrew item is Drew's until he resolves it in chat, or it expires. There is no way for the fleet to draft a first pass for approval, and no structured way for the orchestrator to hand something back with "I cannot do this, here is why, here is what I tried, here is what I need" — inability today is silent (the item just stays, or worse, gets reclassified away).

Design: `~/workspace/pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md` §2 (addendum to the #1184 coherence design).

## Proposal — pass-side delegation execution (orchestration-pass behavior + state)
Consumes `delegate` / `approve-proposal` / `reject-proposal` actions from the dashboard actions store (#1152 + the /attention UI slice) and the `delegation` field from the publisher-contract slice:
- **first-pass**: on `delegate{mode:"first-pass"}`, the pass does a bounded, NON-APPLYING first pass (reads what the item touches; drafts an answer/plan/proposed change set) and republishes the SAME item (same id — never a second item) with `delegation.status: "proposal-ready"` + `proposal{summary, detail?, proposedChanges?, at}`. On `approve-proposal` it applies the changes as single writer and logs the approving action id in the run's `actions[]`; on `reject-proposal{reason}` it clears the proposal, returns the mode to `drew`, and records the reason so it does not re-propose the same draft.
- **auto**: on `delegate{mode:"auto"}` the pass treats the item as its own queue work under its existing ladder/caps/measurement gate. Success → the item expires out with an `actions[]` record. **The only return path is structured inability**: `delegation.status: "unable"` + `unable{reason, whatItTried[≥1], whatItNeeds, at}` republished on the same item in NEEDS DREW. Silent returns and quiet reclassification to NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR are contract violations.
- **Hard exclusions**: `whyDrew` `access`/`policy` items can never enter auto (Drew's browser / Drew's authority by definition); a delegate-auto action on one is rejected via `/api/actions/result` naming the class.
- **No silent rot**: a delegated item stays published in NEEDS DREW with mode/status/age; an item in `working` must reach `proposal-ready`, completion, or `unable` within 2 runs — enforced by the publisher self-check (contract slice), executed here.
- **Dismissals** recorded in orchestrator-state with the §1.5 resurface rule (new material fact, cited, or it stays out).

DECISION PROPOSED in the design (wants Drew's confirmation): auto is per-item explicit opt-in; the pass may SUGGEST auto via `recommendedAction` but never set it; a standing "default to auto" toggle is designed but off until Drew turns it on.

## Acceptance
- First real first-pass cycle evidences in the run log: item delegated from the dashboard → returns `proposal-ready` → approval applies it → item expires out with the action id in `actions[]`.
- First real auto cycle: item resolves and expires out, OR returns `unable` with a tried-list; a run leaving it `working` past the bound fails the self-check.
- Rejection path: delegate-auto on an access/policy item produces a rejected action result naming the class; the item never enters auto.
- No delegated item ever appears twice in a tier or disappears without an outcome.

Refs: #1184 (epic), #1152 (actions consumption), #1148 (no-silent-decay principle). Design: pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md §2.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A needsDrew item can be delegated in two modes — first-pass-then-approve and auto-unless-unable — consuming the `delegate` contract from #1290, and the item's delegation state is visible wherever the item renders.
- [ ] First-pass mode: the orchestrator drafts a proposal and nothing applies until Drew approves it (proposal handling per #1293).
- [ ] Auto-unless-unable mode: the orchestrator completes the item end-to-end, or returns a structured inability: what it cannot do, what it tried, and what it needs — inability is never silent (no quiet reclassification, no item just staying).
- [ ] A delegated run is auditable after the fact: the pass records what it did or why it could not.

## Finding
Drew's requirement (2026-10-26): "things that need Drew should have clear actions I can take and a legible view into them on the dashboard page, with clear next-step options that are standard, but also allow for the issue to incorporate custom choices that it suggests or survey quiz questions to cover what it's missing."

Evidence: `/attention`'s `tierItemCard` (src/render.ts) renders source/kind badges, title, "Why you:" + reason, and optional question/blockedBy/recommendedAction/ref — read-only prose. There is no what-happens-if-nothing line, no action controls, nothing that renders an item's own choices or questions. #1152 builds the generic triage verbs + actions store; it does not cover the structured options/survey/delegation rendering or the new verbs below — this issue is that UI slice, built on #1152's store and the publisher contract slice (options/questions/delegation fields on needsDrew items).

Design: `~/workspace/pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md` §1.2, §4.

## Proposal — /attention needs-Drew card, extended
Card anatomy (mobile-first, existing card CSS, ≥44px targets): header (source/kind badges + **whyDrew class badge** + "in your queue since" + ref + comment badge) → What (title/summary) → Why you (reason) → **If nothing** (`ifIgnored` or the honest computed fallback) → question strip → **item's own options as buttons** (label; description; "→ predicted effect") → **inline survey form** (one form for all `questions[]`: prompt + "Needed: <covers>"; radios for single/yesno, checkboxes for multi, textarea for text) → proposal box / unable box when delegation state carries them → **standard action row on every card**: Answer (free text) · Delegate first-pass · Delegate auto · Snooze-until · Dismiss-with-reason · Escalate (plus #1152's Acknowledge).

New verbs in the existing DashAction envelope (kind `triage`): `answer` (payload `text?` / `optionId?` / `answers[]` — one content verb for text, chosen options, and survey answers), `delegate` (`mode`), `approve-proposal`, `reject-proposal` (reason required), `dismiss` (reason required at the boundary). Forms follow the comment form's `.cform` pattern as a new `.aform` + delegated submit script; clientToken dedupe and pending/applied badges come from #1152's store design. Controls an item's class forbids (Delegate-auto on `access`/`policy` items) render disabled WITH the reason, never hidden. Session-derived cards keep #1156's actions; options/survey/delegation render only on publisher-authored section items.

## Acceptance
- Fixture item with options + questions renders: class badge, If-nothing line, one button per option with effect line, survey with "Needed:" per question, full standard row.
- Each control round-trips through the actions store: POST accepted, badge shows pending, a fixture consumer's result POST flips it to applied.
- Boundary tests: `dismiss`/`reject-proposal` without reason → 400; `answer` with an `optionId` not on the published item → 400; double-submit one clientToken → one record.
- Access-class fixture renders Delegate-auto disabled with reason text.
- 390px-wide render: no horizontal scroll, all controls reachable (joins the #1180 mobile audit).

Refs: #1184 (epic), #1152 (store + generic verbs — this extends, not duplicates), #1139 (honesty states gate controls). Design: pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] /attention item cards render actionable controls: the standard actions, the item's own suggested options (from the #1290 contract), its survey questions inline, and delegation controls — replacing today's read-only prose card (tierItemCard in src/render.ts).
- [ ] Every card shows the what-happens-if-nothing line and the item's whyDrew reason alongside the actions.
- [ ] Actions taken in /attention write through #1152's actions store and reflect on the item without a manual refresh of the underlying data.
- [ ] Items lacking options/questions still render cleanly with the standard actions only.

body:
## Finding
Drew's requirement (2026-10-26): items that need him must carry clear actions — standard next steps, the item's OWN suggested choices, and survey questions covering what information is missing — plus delegation modes (first-pass-then-approve, and auto-unless-unable).

Evidence (read tonight): the published orchestration section (run `orch-2026-10-27T04:13:53Z`, `orchestration.json` on disk) has 11 needsDrew items carrying only `id/kind/title/source/reason/since/lastSeenAt` (+ optional `ref`/`horizon`/`blockedBy`). No item carries `question`, options, or delegation state — so even when the item knows its alternatives (e.g. code #812, a design decision with real branches), the dashboard can only show prose. The aggregator's `TierItem` (src/model.ts) has no fields for any of this.

Design: `~/workspace/pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md` §1 + §3 (addendum to the #1184 coherence design).

## Proposal — publisher-side contract (orchestration pass + aggregator types/sanitizer)
All optional, additive on `TierItem`; section `version` stays 1:
- `whyDrew`: `"decision" | "missing-info" | "approval" | "access" | "policy"` — the blocker class, required from the publisher on every needsDrew item (aggregator falls back from `kind` for older runs).
- `ifIgnored`: one line — what happens if Drew does nothing. `summary`: optional plain-language one-liner.
- `options[]` (≤6): `{id, label, description?, effect?}` — the item's own suggested choices, rendered as buttons by the dashboard slice.
- `questions[]` (≤5): `{id, prompt, type: single|multi|text|yesno, options?, required?, covers}` — `covers` (the missing info the answer supplies) is mandatory.
- `delegation`: `{mode: drew|first-pass|auto, status: idle|working|proposal-ready|unable|done, updatedAt, runId?, proposal?, unable?}` — published state only in this issue; Drew setting modes is the dashboard slice, the pass executing them is the delegation-execution issue.

Validation is PER-ITEM (the #949 lesson, following #1158's nextUp precedent): `isOrchestrationSection` does not change; a live-source sanitizer drops malformed options/questions individually and drops a malformed `delegation` as a unit — never the item, never the section.

Pass self-check additions (same assertion block as the #1110 provenance assertion): whyDrew present + in enum; option ids unique, ≤6; questions ≤5 with non-empty `covers` and ≥2 options for single/multi; no `access`/`policy` item in `auto`; `working` delegations older than 2 runs must carry an outcome; `proposal-ready`/`unable` carry their full payloads.

## Acceptance
- A fixture section with fully-extended items round-trips the section gate unchanged; sanitizer unit tests cover each drop rule (duplicate option id, 1-option question, inconsistent delegation) with item + section intact.
- A real pass run publishes needsDrew items with `whyDrew` on all of them; at least one live decision item carries real `options[]`.
- Self-check tests: each assertion in the list fails a deliberately-broken fixture publish.
- Older sections (no new fields) render exactly as before.

Refs: #1184 (epic), #1152 (the actions these feed), #1158 (per-item validation precedent), #949/#1110 (validation-depth lessons). Design: pm-stack-needs-drew-actions-design-2026-10-26.md.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The needsDrew item contract (design §1 + §3) is implemented: every published needsDrew item carries whyDrew class, structured options[], survey questions[], and delegation state, in both the orchestration publisher output and the aggregator's TierItem model (src/model.ts).
- [ ] A published run's needsDrew items validate against the contract — an item missing its known alternatives (e.g. code #812's design branches) is a contract failure, not silent prose.
- [ ] Existing fields (id/kind/title/source/reason/since/lastSeenAt, optional ref/horizon/blockedBy) keep working; consumers that ignore the new fields degrade gracefully.
- [ ] The contract is documented where the publisher and aggregator are maintained, so the next item producer emits the fields by default.

body:
Found by the #1184 coherence design track (2026-10-26, verified live twice): the aggregator's Provenance facet strings are lazily populated per server process. `live.ts` initializes every facet to a fixture default, and each facet's string is only replaced when that facet's method has actually run in that process. `/api/health` (server.ts) reads `source.provenance()` without exercising the facets — so its answers depend on which pages happened to be visited since boot.

Verified tonight: `/api/health` reported `registry: "fixtures"` in the same minutes `/sessions` was serving 221 merged records. Health that lies by omission, depending on request order, undermines every freshness/honesty surface in epic #1184.

## Fix direction
Health must actively load or probe the facets it reports on (or provenance must be computed from loaded state, not request history). The coherence design doc (~/workspace/pm-stack-coherence-design-2026-10-26.md, health/freshness sections) already stipulates: actively load or probe; never trust the lazy strings. Coordinate with #1140 (absent-vs-invalid diagnosis) — same honesty family, different mechanism: #1140 is about the orchestration section's validation outcome being misreported as absent; this is about facet provenance depending on process request history.

## Acceptance
- Fresh server process, first-ever request is /api/health: every facet reports its true source (live vs fixtures) without any prior page visit.
- Regression test: provenance correctness independent of call order.
- /api/health output for a fully-live deployment contains no false "fixtures" facets.

Refs: epic #1184, #1140, #1138.

body:
Found by queue task 1233 (Lane B worker) while resuming PR #1193: **`nix flake check (clippy-lint)` now fails on current main for every PR**, on code the failing PRs didn't touch.

**Error** (PR #1193 run 40446632847, job 121999626752):
```
error: `panic` should not be present in production code
  --> src/web/markdown.rs:1999:26
1999 |  other => panic!("{name}: expected MisplacedNode error, got {other:?}"),
error: could not compile `id` (lib test) due to 1 previous error
```

The line is in `test_misplaced_nodes_return_error_not_panic`, added by PR #1089 (merged 2026-10-27T03:48:14Z). The crate denies `clippy::panic` (see pkgs/id/AGENTS.md lint rules); the test needs the assertion expressed without `panic!` (e.g. bind the result and `assert!(matches!(...))` with the `{name}`/`{other:?}` context as the assert message), or an explicit scoped allow if that is the local convention.

**Blast radius:** PR #1193 (issue #1044) is blocked on this — its own diff (2 hunks, table arm + tests) contains no `panic`; probe 79/79 passes and all its other checks pass. PR #1238 (issue #1228) branched from current main will hit the same failure. Any PR branched after #1089 merged is affected until this lands; affected branches need a main merge/rebase (or CI re-run after this fix is on main) to go green.

## Acceptance criteria
- `clippy-lint` passes on main (the MisplacedNode test still asserts the same behaviour — no assertion weakened).
- The fix is confined to the test (or a scoped allow on that test); no production code changes.

## Pilot — information gathering for the OpenChamber babysitter

Questions: (1) After a session runs, can we tell which model pool /
route pool it drew on, and how much? (2) Are the quota reads the
babysitter needs (per pool: used %, window reset, freshness) available
for every pool a session can draw on?

Gather and document:

- Per-session attribution: try the session record, OpenChamber's quota
  providers (which read OpenCode credentials), and provider usage
  endpoints. Note the known trap from 2026-10-25: the credential store
  may show only the ACTIVE login (an "OpenAI 2" token-sharing login
  masked the legacy OAuth and broke the wham/usage read) — record
  which login each read reflects.
- Pool coverage table: for each pool in the provider-quota registry
  (DeepSeek routes, OpenAI, Meta High Usage, Claude routes,
  Antigravity), the quota source, its freshness in practice, and
  whether `~/tools/provider-usage/check-usage.py` +
  provider-usage-snapshot.json already cover it.
- Burn measurement: for one finished session, reconstruct its pool
  burn from available records; state the error bars honestly.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A coverage table exists: pool × (quota source, freshness,
      per-session attribution method or gap).
- [ ] One real session's pool + burn is reconstructed end-to-end, or
      the doc states precisely why it cannot be and what instrumentation
      at dispatch time would fix it.
- [ ] The babysitter report spec is updated (comment on this issue)
      to only promise figures this pilot proved readable.

body:
## What

Build v1 of the OpenChamber babysitter from the design doc
(`files/openchamber-dispatch-babysitter-design-2026-10-26.md` in the
keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace): ONE scheduled worker that
makes rounds over every open session bound to a queue task and reports.
Report-only: no nudges, no dispatching, no terminal actions in v1.

## Scope

- Location adapter for `laptop-openchamber` (OpenChamber driving the
  laptop's OpenCode fork): list sessions, inspect status/activity.
  Implement the design's location interface so later locations
  (sandbox-opencode, openclaw, codex-aster) plug in without loop
  changes.
- Session ↔ task binding read from queue task progress (session id,
  location, pool/route recorded at dispatch — for v1, bindings may be
  recorded manually on pilot tasks).
- Per-round report to the fleet chat: sessions active; per session —
  issue, progress verdict (progressing/stalled/done-unreported/
  blocked/walled) from status + last-activity + GitHub state; pool/
  route used where attributable; quota snapshot per pool from the
  existing tooling (`~/tools/provider-usage/check-usage.py` /
  provider-usage-snapshot.json) with read age shown.
- Quiet when nothing is bound and nothing changed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One worker job runs the rounds on a ≤30-min cadence regardless of
      how many sessions are bound.
- [ ] A round over ≥3 concurrently bound sessions produces a report
      whose per-session verdicts match ground truth (verified against
      the sessions and GitHub by hand for the first rounds).
- [ ] Quota figures in the report carry their read age and never exceed
      the POOL MAP measurement-gate staleness (60 min) without being
      flagged stale.
- [ ] Adding a second location is config + adapter only (demonstrated
      by stubbing the sandbox-opencode location, which is currently
      off, without touching the round loop).

Design: OpenChamber dispatch + babysitter design (2026-10-26). Depends
on the session-API inventory pilot. Filed by Muse (operator)
2026-10-26 at Drew's direction.

## Finding
Evidence (live review 2026-10-26 ~22:40 CDT, laptop loopback + gh, cross-checked): The Project is the canonical layer and the orchestrator is its single writer (by design, #910) - but Drew has no dashboard affordance to say "this is actually done / blocked / in progress" when he sees a wrong status on /projects or the board. His only channel is a free-text comment and hope. Status drift (e.g. #910 sat In Progress->Todo mechanically) is exactly what a 5-second correction action exists for.
## Proposal
Per pool item: a "request status change" control (target status + optional note) that writes a dashboard-local action record (same pattern as triage actions issue); the orchestration pass applies it on its next run (it remains the only Project writer) and reports the applied change back; the card shows a "change requested" badge until applied.
## Acceptance
- A requested change appears in the Project within one orchestration cycle, with provenance (requested by Drew via dashboard) in the run log.
- Conflicting derived state after application shows the disagreement badge, not silent override.
Refs: #910.

body:
## Finding
Drew's requirement: "I need to be able to remediate or respond to issues that need my attention, doing basic triage work" - from the dashboard. Today the ONLY write the dashboard supports is comments (POST /api/comments). On /attention Drew can read tiers and open a discuss page, but cannot: acknowledge an item, snooze it, move it between tiers, or answer a waiting session's question in place. Every response means leaving the dashboard.
## Proposal
Dashboard actions modeled on the comments write pattern (dashboard-local store + orchestrator consumption, so the orchestrator remains the single writer of Project/GitHub state): per tier item - Acknowledge (records Drew saw it; item drops from NEEDS DREW until new signal), Snooze (until a chosen horizon), Escalate/De-escalate (tier override with reason), Answer (for stopped-for-question sessions: free-text answer the orchestrator delivers like it does for its own classifications). Each action is an attributed record (author drew, timestamp, item ref) the orchestrator polls and applies/reports.
## Acceptance
- Each action round-trips: taken on the dashboard -> consumed by an orchestration pass -> visible state change on /attention, with the action log inspectable via API.
- Actions on absent-tier-source items are disabled with the reason shown (depends on the attention honesty issue, not blocked by it).
Refs: #899, #906 (comments write pattern), #941 (authz note).

body:
## Summary
The /program page (#1046, PR #1060) documents ONE project — the PM dashboard itself — through a single hard-coded editorial object (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/program.ts`: one `PROGRAM` doc + one `TRACKED_REFS` list). Drew's direction (2026-10-26): these pages must be integrated for **all projects, not just this one**, and the configuration design itself needs improving so that adding/documenting a project is a config change, not a code change per project.

## Design to build
A project registry in the aggregator (new module, e.g. `src/project-config.ts`), one entry per project:

```ts
interface ProjectConfig {
  id: string;              // slug used in /program/<id>
  title: string;
  intro: string;           // one-paragraph description
  poolArea: string | null; // org Project #4 Area value; null = project has no dedicated Area yet (page says so honestly)
  roadmapArea: string | null; // Grist "Program roadmap" area value (RoadmapRow.area)
  homeDoc?: { repo: string; path: string; url: string };  // planning/roadmaps/<project>.md per the project-structure spec
  dashboardLinks?: { label: string; route: string }[];    // e.g. cloud-program -> /quota, pm-dashboard -> /projects
  trackedRefs: RefKey[];   // issues whose live state the page resolves
  editorial?: { done: ProgramEntry[]; next: ProgramEntry[]; longTerm: ProgramEntry[]; gaps: ProgramEntry[] };
}
```

Requirements:
- The existing pm-dashboard `PROGRAM` content migrates into the registry as the `pm-dashboard` entry — no content loss, no duplication (program.ts either becomes the registry or re-exports from it).
- Validation is fail-soft at render and strict in tests: duplicate ids, duplicate poolAreas, malformed refs, and a registry entry whose poolArea/roadmapArea matches nothing are all test failures, not runtime surprises.
- A documented "add a project" recipe (registry entry + optional editorial) in the aggregator README — target: a new project page in under 30 minutes, mirroring the page-manifest recipe.
- The registry is the single source the /program index, per-project pages, and their JSON twins all read.

## Initial project set (verified live 2026-10-26)
| id | poolArea | roadmapArea | home doc |
|---|---|---|---|
| pm-dashboard | `pm-dashboard` (19 pool items) | `PM stack` | design record doc |
| lab-cluster | `lab-cluster` (19) | `Basement cluster` | planning/roadmaps/basement-cluster.md (project-structure spec seed) |
| id | `id-train` (25) | `id` | planning/roadmaps/id.md |
| repo-fleet | `fleet-ops` (9) | `Repo fleet` | planning/roadmaps/repo-and-ci.md |
| mcpx | null yet | null yet | planning/roadmaps/mcpx.md |
| cloud-program | null yet | null yet | /quota hub + ai-subscriptions tracker |

Pool also holds 18 items with Area unset — the config must tolerate that (they belong to no project page until Area is set; the index should surface the unset count so the gap is visible, not hidden).

## Acceptance
- Registry module + validation tests land; pm-dashboard renders identically from the registry (existing /program tests still pass, adapted).
- README recipe added.
- Refs: #1046, #910 (Area as split dimension), project-structure spec in the lab-cluster goal workspace (2026-10-26).

title: fix(aggregator/orchestrator): orchestration section rejected — provenance is an object, isOrchestrationSection requires a string

body:
## Summary

The orchestration section is currently rejected fleet-wide by the aggregator: `/api/orchestration.json` reports "absent", `/today` falls back to derived mode, and the `/program` page's orchestration-freshness card reads "no orchestration section in the current feed yet" — even though the orchestrator publishes hourly and the collector embeds its section in the fleet feed.

Root cause is a contract-shape drift on one field, verified 2026-10-26 from both sides:

- **Publisher** (orchestration-pass, `orchestration.json`): `provenance` is an **object** — `{ "sources": [ "fleet-feed.json …", "laptop attention via laptop-ssh …", … ] }`. Verified in the latest published file (run `orch-2026-10-27T03:14:56Z`).
- **Aggregator check** (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts`, `isOrchestrationSection`, line ~92): requires `typeof s.provenance === "string"`. The type in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/model.ts` (~line 455) likewise declares `provenance: string` ("Sources + run, human-readable").

So the check fails on every current feed, and `src/sources/live.ts` (~lines 587, 791) never takes the live-orchestration branch.

## Background

- The original #899/#900 contract had the orchestrator publish; run 1 had data-shape defects and the cron body gained a CONTRACT FIDELITY self-check — but evidently the check and the publisher have since drifted on this field (the publisher's object form is arguably richer: a list of source notes).
- Found during the #1046 `/program` build (2026-10-26); flagged there as a pre-existing finding, not caused by that PR.
- Not the same as closed #949 (that was validation *depth* below the top level; this is a top-level field type mismatch).

## Fix options (pick one, apply consistently)

1. **Publisher aligns to the existing contract** — orchestrator emits `provenance` as a single human-readable string (its `sources[]` joined), and the orchestration-pass cron body's CONTRACT FIDELITY section / pre-publish self-check is updated to pin the string form so it cannot drift again.
2. **Aggregator aligns to the publisher** — `OrchestrationSection.provenance` becomes the object shape (or `string | { sources: string[] }`), `isOrchestrationSection` validates that shape, and the render/provenance-string usages summarize it.

Either is acceptable; what matters is that publisher, cron-body contract text, aggregator type, and validator all agree afterward. Option 1 is the smaller change; option 2 keeps the richer per-source detail. The chooser should record which contract won, in the PR and on #899's contract notes if they are amended.

## Acceptance

- With a current fleet feed, `/api/orchestration.json` on the laptop aggregator returns the live section (tiers/goals/dependencies) instead of `{status: "absent", …}`.
- `/today` renders from the orchestration section (not labelled derived), and `/program`'s freshness card shows the section's run id / generated-at.
- A regression test feeds an orchestration section in the chosen shape through `isOrchestrationSection` / the live source and asserts acceptance; a mismatched-shape section still fails closed to "absent" rather than crashing.
- The orchestration-pass publisher's self-check validates the same shape the aggregator accepts (no silent drift path).

## Scope notes

- Small, bounded fix. No new fields, no Project writes, no dashboard redesign.
- Refs: #899 (orchestrator), #898 (dashboard contract), #1046 (where this was found).

title: id(web): prosemirror_to_markdown panics on misplaced nodes — json_to_ast never validates block/inline placement

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Bug

`prosemirror_to_markdown` (pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:908) does not validate the *placement* of nodes in the incoming ProseMirror document. `json_to_ast` (markdown.rs:963) recursively appends children without checking that inline nodes only appear in inline contexts and block nodes only in block contexts, so a structurally misplaced node produces an ill-formed comrak AST:

- In debug builds, comrak's `format_commonmark` validation **panics**: `The document to format is ill-formed: InvalidChildType { parent: Document, child: Text("orphan") }` (comrak 0.56 cm.rs:29).
- In release builds the validation is compiled out (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`), so the same input silently emits invalid markdown instead of returning an error.

The function's contract is `Result<String, ConversionError>` — an unknown node *type* already returns `ConversionError::UnknownType` (markdown.rs:1186). A known node in an impossible position should be an error (or a documented coercion), never a panic / silent corruption. The save path is `convert_doc_to_bytes` in pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1986, so a malformed stored/imported/collab document hits this on save or export.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-26 on main cf60812d)

Standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of `src/web/markdown.rs` (comrak 0.56.0 locked) — logs in goal hidden_files `probe-2026-10-26-2145/out3.log` + `out4.log`. Each of these `prosemirror_to_markdown` inputs panics at comrak cm.rs:29:

1. doc with a top-level `text` node: `{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"text","text":"orphan"}]}` → `InvalidChildType { parent: Document, child: Text("orphan") }`
2. doc with a top-level `image` node (inline node at block level)
3. doc with a top-level `hard_break` node
4. a `paragraph` whose content contains a `paragraph`

Controls that behave correctly today: unknown node type → `Err(UnknownType("mention"))`; heading level 9 → clamped to 6; empty doc → `Ok("")`.

Related precedent: #1017 (table-cell special case built an ill-formed AST that panicked in the same comrak validation) — fixed by making the conversion produce a well-formed AST. This issue is the general case: no placement validation anywhere in `json_to_ast`.

## Why it matters

Stored ProseMirror documents are not exclusively editor-produced: they arrive via import, the collab layer, older clients, and direct API writes. Any of those can carry a misplaced node; today that means a panicked handler in debug builds and silently invalid `.md` output in release builds, on a function whose signature promises a `ConversionError`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `prosemirror_to_markdown` never panics and never emits an ill-formed AST for the four shapes above; each returns `Err(ConversionError::…)` (new variant if needed) or a documented, tested coercion (e.g. wrapping stray inline nodes in a paragraph).
- Regression tests in `web::markdown` covering: inline node at doc level (text/image/hard_break), block node inside a paragraph, and at least one misplaced-node case inside a list item / blockquote / table cell.
- Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass; well-formed documents render byte-identically to before.

body:
## Summary

In the id web editor, a **loose task list item** — a checkbox item containing a second paragraph (or a code block) — is corrupted on save. The paragraph boundary is dropped on the first save, and on the second save the item's blocks fuse into a single run of text. A code block inside a task item is destroyed outright (it becomes inline paragraph text).

Bullet and ordered list items with the exact same structure round-trip correctly, so this is specific to the task-list path.

## Evidence (verified on main 70efcd4e, standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, comrak 0.56.0; logs in the goal's hidden_files `probe-2026-10-26-1945/out3.log`)

Multi-paragraph task item:

```
orig:   "- [ ] first\n\n  second para\n- [ ] other\n"
save 1: "- [ ] first\n  second para\n- [ ] other\n"        ← blank separator gone
save 2: "- [ ] first second para\n- [ ] other\n"           ← paragraphs fused into one
```

PM after save 1 confirms the damage is structural, not cosmetic: the item holds ONE paragraph containing `first`, ` `, `second para`.

Task item with a code block:

```
orig:   "- [ ] item\n\n  ```\n  code\n  ```\n"
save 1: "- [ ] item\n      code\n"
save 2: "- [ ] item code\n"                                 ← code block gone, text inlined
```

Controls (same probe, same shapes): multi-paragraph **bullet** and **ordered** items preserve the blank line and are two-save fixpoints; a task item whose second block is a nested list survives. Checked items (`- [x]`) are affected identically.

## Root cause

- Parse direction, `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:214-220`: the `task_list` JSON node carries **no `tight` attr**, unlike `bullet_list`/`ordered_list`, which store `list.tight`.
- Save direction, `markdown.rs:1019-1027`: the `"task_list"` arm hardcodes `tight: true` in the comrak `NodeList`. A loose list rendered tight gets no blank line between an item's block children, so the re-parse merges them.
- `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:98` — the `task_list` schema node likewise declares no attrs, so even a codec-side fix needs the schema/runtime side considered (same pattern as #997).

## Why it matters

Silent data corruption on save for a common construct: anyone who writes a task with a note paragraph underneath it (or a code snippet in a task) loses the structure — first the separation, then the block itself. Because save 1 still *looks* plausible, the damage is easy to miss until the fused text is noticed.

## Acceptance criteria

- A loose (multi-paragraph) task list item round-trips with its paragraph boundary preserved and is a two-save fixpoint, for both `- [ ]` and `- [x]` items.
- A code block inside a task list item survives a save as a code block (not inlined into the paragraph text).
- Tight (single-paragraph) task lists render exactly as before.
- Regression tests in `web::markdown` covering the cases above; existing markdown tests pass.

## Suggested direction

Carry `tight` on the task_list node the way bullet/ordered lists do (parse stores it, save reads it instead of hardcoding `true`), and add the corresponding attr on the editor.ts `task_list` schema node if the runtime needs it. Related but distinct: #997 (ordered task lists lose their start number).

labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
