Observed 2026-10-29 on amd (laptop) by Muse, while verifying the Codex pool after a fresh `codex login`.

## Symptom

After `codex login` refreshed `~/.codex/auth.json` (2026-10-30T02:51:23Z), the laptop codex-proxy's built-in 5-minute `syncCodexTokensToOpenCode` did NOT update the OpenCode credential store. The active `openai` credential row still held a stale token (matching neither the old nor the fresh Codex token) until it was synced by hand. The proxy process runs the current script (since Oct 28), syncs at startup and every 5 minutes, and showed no error anywhere — the failure is invisible by design.

## Root cause (diagnosed + reproduced 2026-10-29)

`bin/codex-proxy.mjs`, `syncCodexTokensToOpenCode`:

```js
execSync(`python3 -c ${JSON.stringify(script)}`, { stdio: 'ignore' });
```

1. **The sync can never run.** `JSON.stringify(script)` encodes the Python script's newlines as literal two-character `\n` sequences. The shell, inside double quotes, does not turn `\n` into a newline, so `python3 -c` receives the whole script as one physical line full of literal `\n`. Python dies instantly with `SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character`. Reproduced in isolation against a scratch sqlite DB with the exact construction from the proxy: same SyntaxError, DB unchanged.
2. **The failure is swallowed twice.** `stdio: 'ignore'` discards the child's stderr, and the surrounding `catch (err) { // Non-fatal background sync }` discards the throw. A failed sync is indistinguishable from a successful one — no log line either way.
3. **Latent overreach (would bite once the sync works):** the embedded SQL selects `WHERE integration_id="openai"` with no `active` filter and updates every `oauth` row it finds. On the live DB that is TWO rows: the active base row (`label='OpenAI'`, `active=1`) and an inactive second row (`label='OpenAI 2'`, `active=0`, untouched since Oct 5). The sync must only ever touch the active base `openai` row — never the inactive row, never `openai.alternate`.

## Fix

- Run Python via `execFileSync('python3', ['-c', script])` (argv, no shell) so the script arrives verbatim; pass the tokens + DB path via environment variables instead of interpolating them into the Python source.
- Restrict the update to `integration_id='openai' AND active=1` (plus the existing `type='oauth'` check in the row value).
- Make outcomes visible: log success (`[codex-proxy] codex-token-sync: updated N credential row(s)`) and log failures to stderr with a clear `codex-token-sync FAILED:` marker including the child's stderr. Never swallow silently again.
- Regression tests in `bin/codex-proxy.test.mjs` using the existing fake-HOME harness: seed `~/.codex/auth.json` + a scratch `opencode.db`, start the proxy, assert only the active base `openai` row was updated (inactive + `openai.alternate` rows untouched) and `time_updated` advanced.

## Related

- #916 — the serving proxy is the supervisor's transient `fps-codex-proxy-18744` unit while `codex-proxy.service` churns on EADDRINUSE; deploy/restart for this fix goes through the fps unit / supervisor path, not the churn unit.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Sync verified live on amd: after a proxy restart, the active `openai` row's `time_updated` advances and its access/refresh hashes match `~/.codex/auth.json`.
- [ ] `GET /api/quota/codex` still returns `ok:true` after the roll.
- [ ] A deliberately broken sync (e.g. unreadable DB) produces a visible `codex-token-sync FAILED` log line in the proxy journal.

body:
# mcpx(logging): PR #1737's Redact mangles URL values under a sensitive keyword — a port is printed as an elided password and the rest of the URL is dropped

## Finding

PR #1737 (merged, fixes #1710) taught `Redact` to elide URL userinfo passwords. Its replacement function (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/logging/trace.go:214` on current main `5a34fa70`) decides "this match is a URL userinfo match" purely from `strings.Index(m, "://")` — but the KEY=VALUE alternative of `sensitiveValue` (`trace.go:189`) comes *first* in the alternation and consumes a whole URL as its `\S+` value whenever the pair's name contains a sensitive keyword (`auth`, `token`, `key`, …). For such a match the function:

- mistakes the URL's **port colon** (or the userinfo colon) for the marker it wants, and
- reconstructs only `prefix + user + ":" + "<elided>@"`, silently discarding the remainder of the match — host, port and path for a userinfo URL; the path (plus a fabricated `@`) for a credential-free URL.

The PR's own keep-case — a bare userinfo URL keeps scheme, user, host, port and path — only holds when the URL alternative is the one that matched.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/1737 — merge `ee07ac6cad82ec5ee0484d8545b15a76a71791ee`, commit `2d5da5a7`.
- Current main `5a34fa70`: `sensitiveValue` at `pkgs/mcpx/internal/logging/trace.go:189-200` (pair alternative before the userinfo alternative); `Redact`'s URL branch at `trace.go:214-220`.
- Probe (verbatim regex + `Redact` copied from current main, run on the laptop: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-redact/main.go`):
  - `Redact("MCPX_SCRIPT_ENV", "AUTH_URL=https://auth.example.com:8443/callback")` → `"AUTH_URL=https://auth.example.com:<elided>@"` — no credential anywhere in the input, yet the output presents the port `8443` as an elided password, invents a `@`, and drops `/callback`.
  - `Redact("MCPX_SCRIPT_ENV", "TOKEN_URL=https://deploy:s3cr3tpw@example.com:8443/path")` → `"TOKEN_URL=https://deploy:<elided>@"` — password elided, but host, port and path are lost (the bare-URL control below keeps all of them).
  - Controls behave: bare `https://deploy:s3cr3tpw@example.com:8443/path` → `https://deploy:<elided>@example.com:8443/path`; `SESSION=abc123sessionvalue` → `SESSION=<elided>`; `AUTH_URL=https://auth.example.com/callback` (no port) → `AUTH_URL=<elided>`.

## Why it matters

`Redact` is the logging safety boundary for mcpx: its outputs are what operators read when diagnosing from traces. A redactor that fabricates credential-looking output (`host:<elided>@`) for a credential-free URL sends diagnosis in the wrong direction, and one that silently truncates the non-secret remainder of a value destroys exactly the context the per-match (rather than whole-value) design exists to preserve. Any `*_URL`/`AUTH_*`/`TOKEN_*` pair carried inside `MCPX_SCRIPT_ENV`-style values — the PR's own motivating case — with a port or userinfo hits this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Regression tests in `redact_test.go`: a sensitive-keyword pair whose value is a URL with a port and no userinfo keeps the URL readable with only the genuinely sensitive part elided (no fabricated `<elided>@`, no dropped path); a keyword pair whose value is a userinfo URL elides only the password and keeps scheme, user, host, port and path — matching the bare-URL keep-case from PR #1737.
- [ ] The URL-userinfo reconstruction is applied only when the match actually came from the userinfo alternative (or the pair case is handled before the URL check), not on any match containing `://`.
- [ ] All PR #1737 regression tests (full JWT, reconciled keywords, bare userinfo, credential-free URLs) still pass, in CI.

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #1737. Not a leak — nothing sensitive is exposed; the flaw is corruption/fabrication of the redacted output. #1710 (closed) covered the leak direction only.

body:
## Problem

The merge queue no longer merges: entries are added and then dropped a couple of minutes later, while the PR stays `OPEN` and `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN`. No pull request has merged since **#2233 at 10:57:51Z** on 2026-10-29, though the queue keeps accepting new entries.

## Evidence (observed 2026-10-29 18:20–18:35Z)

Three independent entries, all ejected:

| PR | added_to_merge_queue | removed_from_merge_queue | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| #2393 | 18:21:35Z | 18:28:11Z | open, not merged, checks never failed |
| #2326 | 17:38:50Z | 17:56:37Z | open, ejected |
| #2326 | 18:04:20Z | 18:07:35Z | open, ejected |
| #2326 | 18:31:12Z | 18:33:57Z | open, ejected 2m45s later |

- Both PRs were `CLEAN` and fully green on their own head SHA before enqueueing; #2393's diff is one added test file, #2326's is one docs file.
- `merge_group` runs are being created and mostly **succeed** — e.g. runs 40931573502 (5665d2b7), 40931476149 (5072cc18), 40931104314 (a803595b), 40930771465 (d93daff4) all `completed success` — so nix ci itself is not reporting a failure. One merge_group run in the same window was `cancelled` (40930683919, afde25bc).
- The queue is running far behind: several `merge_group` runs sat `queued` for minutes at a time (runner saturation), which is why entries spend most of their short life in `AWAITING_CHECKS`.

## Hypotheses to check (in this order)

1. **Required-check name set does not match what reports on `merge_group` SHAs.** #2233 (merged 10:57) was itself *"ci: run nix ci on merge groups so the merge queue sees its required check"*. If the branch-protection required list still names a job that only exists on `pull_request` events (e.g. a per-check name, or a job that is `skipped` on merge groups), the queue entry can never satisfy it and GitHub drops the entry. Compare the required checks in branch protection against the check-runs attached to a `gh-readonly-queue/...` SHA.
2. **Merge-queue check timeout / runner saturation.** If the batch's merge_group run is still `queued` when a queue timeout fires, the entry is ejected and requeued — repeating forever. The observed ~2m45s–6m30s lifetimes are consistent with an early timeout or a batch being cancelled.
3. **`skipped` conclusions counted as not-successful.** On merge groups several jobs report `skipped` (`full (main tier): Nix flake evaluation`, `full (main tier): nix flake check`); a queue rule that requires every check to be `success` would reject those.

## Impact

This is the terminal step for most of the repo-health queue: many tasks are parked at `awaiting_ci` with a green PR that cannot land, and each shift re-verifies, re-enqueues, and parks again — burning lane budget without throughput. It also means `main` has not moved in ~7.5 hours, so CI fixes (e.g. #2401) cannot land either.

## Not caused by the PRs named here

Both examples are single-file, green, up-to-date branches; the ejection happens to any entry. Do not "fix" the PRs.

## Acceptance

- A PR enqueued with green checks merges (test with an already-green low-risk PR after the fix).
- The branch-protection required-check list and the merge_group check-run names agree, documented in `.github/ci-policy.md`.

title: fix(pm-stack): pm-git-sync (PR #1526) restarts a service after its dependency step fails, and a failed redeploy is never retried

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

PR #1526 (commit `64756328e4`, "feat(pm-stack): deploy aggregator + projector as NixOS user services") added `pm-stack/scripts/pm-git-sync.sh`, which keeps the laptop's primary clone on current `main` and redeploys the PM services when their subtree changes. Its redeploy failure handling is broken in two connected ways — verified unchanged on current main (`origin/main` at `5a34fa7070`, 2026-10-29), `pm-stack/scripts/pm-git-sync.sh:44-83`:

1. **A failed dependency step does not stop the restart.** In `redeploy()` (`:54-66`), the dep step — `bun install` for the aggregator when `package.json`/`bun.lock` changed, `bash scripts/setup-deps.sh` for the projector when its `package.json` changed — runs as `(cd "$subtree" && eval "$dep") && echo done || echo "WARN dep step failed"`, and the very next statement unconditionally runs `systemctl --user restart "$unit"`. If the install failed (the projector's own comment in this same script says bun install "cannot reach the registry reliably from this host"), the service is restarted onto new code whose dependencies were never installed — crash-looping a service that was running fine on the old code in memory.
2. **A failed redeploy is never retried.** Redeploys only run in the invocation where `HEAD` moves: at `:44-46`, when `old == new` the script prints "ok clean main, up to date" and exits 0. The `git pull --ff-only` has already advanced the checkout, so on the next 30-second timer run the failed dep step / failed restart is invisible — the service silently stays on the pre-pull code (or down, per point 1) until some later commit happens to touch the same subtree again. Nothing records that a redeploy is still owed.

## Why it matters

pm-git-sync is the deployment path for the aggregator/projector stack (PR #1526 made `nixos-rebuild switch` + this timer the way the stack lands). A single flaky-registry install failure currently either takes a healthy service down or strands it on stale code indefinitely, with only a one-line WARN in a journal nobody is alerted on.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] If a service's dependency step fails, that service is NOT restarted in that run, and the failure is surfaced as a failed (non-zero) sync run, not a WARN-and-continue.
- [ ] An owed redeploy survives across runs: a later pm-git-sync invocation retries the dep step + restart for a subtree whose last redeploy did not complete (e.g. a small state marker per service recording the deployed commit, compared against `HEAD`), even when `HEAD` did not move in that invocation.
- [ ] A failed `systemctl restart` is likewise retried on a later run / recorded as owed, not forgotten.
- [ ] The existing safety rules are unchanged: off-`main` or dirty tree still fails loudly without pulling; nothing is stashed, committed, or discarded.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #1526's diff against current main; deduped against open/closed issues (searched "pm-git-sync", "git-sync dep", "restart failed install" — no covering issue).

body:
Phase 2 of design #2386 (mcpx completion, finished). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-completion-rate-limit-ranking.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. The decision is recorded on #2386. Independent of Phase 1.

## Scope

Relevance ranking inside `localCompletion` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go:402`) — the cached-names fallback used when an upstream never declared `completions`. Today it returns `hasPrefixFold` prefix matches over the pool's name-sorted cache (`internal/pool/pool.go:915`): alphabetical, prefix-only.

Ranking (deterministic), applied to prompt names for `ref/prompt` and template URIs for `ref/resource`:

1. Exact case-folded match first
2. Prefix matches next — shorter name first, alphabetical tiebreak
3. Substring (non-prefix) matches last — by first-match position, then alphabetical (the spec's "fuzzy matching where appropriate" slice; a value typed mid-name currently finds nothing)

The `completion.maxValues` cap (spec max 100) applies **after** ranking; `total`/`hasMore` keep their current meaning.

**Upstream answers are not touched:** when the upstream declares `completions`, its values pass through in its order with its `total` — the upstream ranks with knowledge mcpx does not have.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `localCompletion` tests demonstrate the three tiers in order for both ref types, including a mid-name substring hit that previously returned nothing
- [ ] Cap is applied after ranking (the best matches survive truncation, not the alphabetically first)
- [ ] `total`/`hasMore` unchanged in meaning; the `source: "cache"` / `because` response fields are unchanged
- [ ] A test pins that an upstream-declared server's answer order is passed through unranked
- [ ] Tests run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: rate limiting (Phase 1), register changes (Phase 3), changing what the fallback can complete (still only cached prompt names / template URIs — mcpx cannot invent argument values).

From the bridge-semantics investigation on #2058 (doc PR linked there): prove the hosted↔native seam with the smallest thing that exercises the real rules, reusing the native store machinery unchanged.

## What to build (PoC only)

A bridge sync session between a native `pkgs/id` store and a DO-shaped SQLite store (same table shape as `event_store/`: events by (author, seq), chains, forks, proof_ids, proof_headers) over a WebSocket, reusing `ingest_batch` + resolve with no semantic changes: no bridge-assigned ordering, no re-signing, no authoritative snapshot.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Push and pull across the session converge to identical applied sets and identical live tag claims on both stores
- [x] A fork authored on each side while disconnected is detected by the proof-carrying exchange (not LogSync height comparison) and both sides end holding the same fork proof
- [x] A withholding bridge (drops one author's events) is detected from chain-head / `after`-frontier evidence, and the detection is demonstrated in a test
- [x] Replaying the same journal into an empty hosted-shaped store and an empty native store yields identical stores (tables compared)
- [x] Findings (incl. measured fork-proof exchange cost in rows/CPU terms) recorded on this issue for the #2046 sync-spec decision (Q1 on #2058)

## Not in scope

Permanent feature work on top of this PoC (program rule: an unreviewed PoC making its own decisions is not a foundation), custodial keys, SSO binding (#2258), native multi-hop relay (#2249).

Investigation #2020 (queue task 3339, result posted on that issue 2026-10-29) produced the Jules fit matrix and a proposed first schedule. This issue is that pilot, scoped to exactly what the investigation proposed — no expansion without the 2-week review.

## Pilot

1. **Create one Jules schedule** on the fleet's collected Jules account: weekly (Monday, early UTC) GitHub Actions version-bump sweep on developing-today/code — check `.github/workflows/` for actions pinned to superseded majors; open at most one PR with per-action changelog links and breaking-change flags; never change workflow permissions, triggers, or secrets references; open nothing when nothing is outdated.
   - **Blocker, stated plainly:** schedule creation happens in the Jules web UI under Drew's Google account. Whoever executes this needs that browser session; any Google sign-in challenge goes to Drew immediately (standing rule) — it is a step, not a dead end. If no session is available, record the exact prompt + settings as ready-to-create in the registry (step 2) and block this issue on the session rather than improvising another creation path.
2. **Register the schedule** in the fleet schedule registry (alongside the cron inventory / placement docs): repo, cadence, prompt verbatim, budget expectation, creation date, kill criteria.
3. **Report the first run** on this issue: what Jules opened (or correctly didn't), reviewer time spent, any breakage.

## Review gate (2 weeks after creation)

Pass = PRs correct/mergeable with at most trivial edits, zero attributable workflow breakage, reviewer time < 10 min/PR → propose schedule #2 (docs-drift, one repo) as a new issue. Fail = pause the schedule, record why; conclusion "Jules = ad-hoc only" is an acceptable pilot outcome.

Suggested Tasks (stays off), issue-driven Jules work, additional repos/accounts, any auto-merge of Jules PRs.

title: id: PoC: mutual-concession match attestation on the tic-tac-toe example — genesis agreement + dual signed result claims, offline-first (from #2037)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## From the #2037 investigation (match-result attestation)

Investigation #2037 (queue task 3350, result posted on that issue 2026-10-29) specified the attestation object layer for ID matches: genesis agreement (both players sign game + logic hash + named witness + objection window), per-player signed result claims, `agreed`/`final` states computed from the objects, witness decision and objection as signed events, fork-proof voiding via existing event-store mechanics. This issue is the **proof of concept** for the concession path — the program pattern is design + PoC, and a PoC is not the permanent feature: nothing production is built on top of this without a review round (epic #2056).

## PoC scope (existing tic-tac-toe example, `pkgs/id/examples/tic-tac-toe`)

1. Two players play a match with a signed **genesis agreement** object (game id, logic/version hash, both player IDs, witness slot left unused for this PoC, objection window parameter present).
2. At match end each player emits a signed **result claim** (outcome, final-state hash, both chain frontiers).
3. A viewer computes the result state from the objects alone: `proposed` → `agreed` when both claims concur; conflicting claims → `disputed`.
4. The whole exchange is demonstrated **offline-first**: match + attestation complete with no server, then sync to a second store which computes the identical state.
5. Negative case demonstrated: one player's claim names the wrong winner → state is `disputed`, never `agreed`.

## Out of scope

Witness decision flow, objection handling, audit replay (that is #2038 / synthesis #2039 territory), registries/rankings, any production API.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PoC runs the 5 scope points above against the tic-tac-toe example, with the object shapes documented in the PR/issue
- [ ] The offline-then-sync demonstration shows identical computed state on both stores
- [ ] A short findings note is posted on this issue: what the PoC proved about the #2037 object shapes, and what it did not prove
- [ ] No production attestation feature is claimed or merged under this issue

labels.name: priority/high

labels.name: app/id

body:
## From the #2030 investigation (trust/visibility model)

Investigation #2030 (queue task 3346, result posted on that issue 2026-10-29) verified that `pkgs/id` ingest is validity-only (`src/event_store/ingest.rs`: signature/encoding/chain refusals only; "the store keeps it either way" — `src/event_store/claims.rs`) and specified the missing layer: per-view writer sets. This issue is the **design spec** for that buildable piece. It is a spec, not a build order — no permanent feature is built on the #2030 investigation without a review round (program rule, epic #2056).

## Spec to produce (doc in `pkgs/id/doc/` per repo convention, linked from this issue)

1. **Writer-set object format** — a signed, versioned object owned by the view owner: entries = explicit IDs | one-level group references (via `src/groups/`) | `public` sentinel; optional per-topic scoping; view-level exclusion entries (exclude one writer admitted via a group reference).
2. **Set-change semantics** — prospective by default; "include history" as an explicit add-time choice; removal stops future counting; `rescind` as an explicit, visible set-version event; every computed view names *(set version, frontier)*.
3. **View projection** — author-indexed projection over the event store so view cost is proportional to writer-set size, not store size; counted vs uncounted strictly separated; one-off "count this claim" exceptions recorded at view level.
4. **Discovery query** — subject/topic-first lookup returning counted + uncounted claims, uncounted showing author, signature status, and why-not-counted; author-clustering of results (Sybil-flood readability, #2030 abuse case 2).
5. **Storage tiering interface** — counted = hot/permanent; uncounted = cold with a published expiry unless pinned/counted; quota values themselves come from #2032 (do not invent separate numbers here).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Spec doc landed in `pkgs/id/doc/` and linked from this issue, covering all five points above

title: OpenClaw cannot reach the OpenCode server: build all three dispatch mechanisms (ACP-runtime agent, headless sessions_spawn, opencode-route provider front)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Problem

OpenClaw cannot run jobs carried by the OpenCode **workhorse route** (`opencode-route/workhorse`). Established in the OpenClaw-vs-OpenCode 1v1 round 2 (see #2171, comment 6493787758):

- `openclaw agent --model opencode-route/workhorse` → `Unknown model`. OpenClaw's only providers are four local OpenAI-compatible proxies — `agy` (:18743), `codex-proxy` (:18744), `design-code` (:18746), `commandcode` (:18748) — and **none fronts the OpenCode server**. OpenCode's server speaks its own session API, not the chat-completions shape OpenClaw providers use.
- ACP spawn tooling (`sessions_spawn` with runtime `acp`) is exposed only to non-sandboxed chat-channel sessions; both headless surfaces (CLI agent, embedded exec) run a restricted tool catalog without it. The ACP plumbing itself is healthy (backend acpx, dispatch enabled, `opencode` allowed; merged PR #1728 widens allowedAgents but does not change the dispatch surface).
- Result: round 2 of the 1v1 ran **zero** fixtures; OpenClaw's harness and its Command Code door cannot be varied independently, so the door-vs-platform question stays open.

## Direction (Drew, 2026-10-29)

Build **all three** mechanisms — not a menu. Sequenced most-straightforward first:

1. **ACP-runtime agent** in `home/openclaw/default.nix`: an `agents.list[]` entry with `runtime.type="acp"`, `runtime.acp.agent="opencode"` → `openclaw agent --agent <id>` dispatches turns to the OpenCode harness as a standing capability, model settable per run.
2. **Expose `sessions_spawn` to headless/CLI sessions** (tool-profile change). Determine whether this is `default.nix` config or requires patching upstream OpenClaw source; if source, build it as the fleet's packaging patch and say so plainly here.
3. **opencode-route provider front**: a small local proxy (mirroring the commandcode proxy's pattern, next fixed port per the #437 convention) exposing `opencode-route/*` models in chat-completions shape, backed by the laptop OpenCode server (:13420, default model already the workhorse route), plus the `models.providers` entry in `home/openclaw/default.nix` — so `--model opencode-route/workhorse` works directly.

## Acceptance

- Each mechanism lands as its own commit/PR under repo rules and is tracked here.
- Each mechanism is **proven live** where it allows: an actual OpenClaw run carried by `opencode-route/workhorse`, verified from the OpenCode DB v2 tables (`session_v2` / `session_message`) — the route record, not the request label.
- If a mechanism proves impossible, its precise technical blocker is documented here and the others continue.

Cross-refs: #2171 (comparison program), #437 (fixed ports), #2170 (topology).

## Acceptance criteria

- At least one of the three dispatch mechanisms (ACP-runtime agent, headless `sessions_spawn`, opencode-route provider front) demonstrably runs an OpenClaw job on the `opencode-route/workhorse` route end-to-end, with the run evidence linked here — and the issue's goal is all three, each either working or closed with a named blocker.
- For each mechanism that cannot work, the specific blocking constraint (tool-catalog restriction, provider shape, config surface) is recorded on this issue so the 1v1 comparison (#2171) can cite it.
- The OpenClaw-vs-OpenCode comparison can vary door and harness independently for at least the working mechanism(s): a fixture run through OpenClaw lands on the OpenCode server and is visible in its session store.

title: mcpx: Phase 2 of #2209 — one predicate vocabulary: route scattered revision comparisons through internal/spec

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
Phase 2 of design #2209 (origin #1974, ex-nix#307). Independent of Phase 1. Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-spec-revision-choice.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Scope

One predicate vocabulary for revision comparisons, exactly as `internal/spec`'s package comment already prescribes ("Code asks the active Policy … never by comparing date strings in place"). Today the predicates `spec.AtOrAfter`/`Before`/`Only`/`Between` have zero callers outside `internal/spec`, and comparisons are scattered:

- `internal/mcpserver/revisions.go:40-44` defines a package-local `AtLeast` duplicating `spec.AtOrAfter`'s semantics, used by `Defines` and `internal/mcpserver/conn.go`. Make it delegate to `spec.AtOrAfter`, or delete it in favour of direct predicate use at the call sites. (`internal/mcpserver` already imports `internal/spec` — see `relay.go`.)
- `internal/mcpserver/server.go:1285` `Modern()` is a raw `version >= "2026-07-28"` — use `spec.AtOrAfter("2026-07-28")`.
- `internal/mcpclient/modern.go` `CallerLegacy` uses a raw `v < "2026-07-28"` — use `spec.Before("2026-07-28")`.
- `internal/mcpclient/client.go:455` uses a raw `ir.ProtocolVersion >= "2025-03-26"` — use `spec.AtOrAfter`.

Semantics are identical today (revisions are ISO dates and compare lexically; both forms reject the empty string), so this is a refactor, not a behaviour change. Out of scope, named deliberately: genuine identity equalities such as `internal/mcpclient/request.go:54` (negotiated == one specific revision) stay as they are.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No package outside `internal/spec` implements its own revision-ordering comparison; `mcpserver.AtLeast` delegates or is gone
- [ ] `Modern()`, `CallerLegacy`, and the `client.go:455` check go through `internal/spec` predicates
- [ ] No test changes its verdict (full `pkgs/mcpx` suite in CI); any test that does change is a stop-and-report, not an adjustment
- [ ] No behaviour change: nothing about what mcpx sends, accepts, or answers is different

## Finding

PR #1489 "chore(opencode): raise terra context limit to 1M (rescued)" is conflicting and cannot merge as-is, its intended one-line change is still not on main, and it still carries the `.opencode/opencode.jsonc.backup` file its own body says to drop before merge.

## Evidence

- PR #1489, commit 179d92b091, OPEN since 2026-10-27; 2 files, +2797/−838 — almost all of that is the backup file, not the config change.
- Fresh `gh api repos/developing-today/code/pulls/1489` (2026-10-29): `mergeable: false`, `mergeable_state: dirty`.
- The PR body itself states: "the preserve commit also carries `.opencode/opencode.jsonc.backup`, a backup copy that was sitting in the tree — drop that file before merge if it should not land." That drop was never done.
- Verified against current main (319e6c219d14): the `gpt-6.1-terra` model in `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` still has `"limit": { "context": 500000, "output": 128000 }` (~line 4063) — the 500k → 1M raise has not landed by any other route.
- `.opencode/opencode.jsonc.backup` is tracked on main; the PR would rewrite it wholesale (+580-line snapshot churn) as a side effect of a one-line limit change.
- Issue search found no issue already tracking this stranded PR.

## Why it matters

The terra seat is capped at half its intended context until this lands, and a rescued-work PR left dirty silently rots: every later config change makes the rebase worse, and merging it carelessly would land a stale full-config backup snapshot alongside the fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rebase/repair PR #1489 onto current main (or supersede it with a fresh one-line PR) with the `.opencode/opencode.jsonc.backup` change removed from the diff.
- [ ] Verify on main after merge that `gpt-6.1-terra` has `"context": 1000000` and that no backup-file churn landed with it.

body:
# cold-store-reaper: an offset-less `LastModified` in an S3 listing parses to a naive datetime and crashes `backup_supabase` / `evict_scan`

## Evidence (main `82b019a0`)

`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:138-165` — `_parse_s3_list_page` documents its own contract:

> Each object is {key, size, last_modified}; last_modified **is an aware datetime, or None when absent/unparseable** — callers treat None as oldest, never as 'now'.

The parse at `:162` breaks that contract:

```python
stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(raw.replace("Z", "+00:00"))
```

An ISO-8601 stamp with **no timezone designator** (e.g. `2026-10-01T00:00:00.000` — a form S3-compatible stores emit; this module already anticipates non-AWS reply variation, cf. the namespace note in the same docstring) parses successfully to a **naive** datetime — not aware, not `None`. Every downstream consumer assumes aware:

- `cold_store.py:1780` (`backup_supabase`): `max(objects, key=lambda o: (o["last_modified"] or epoch, o["key"]))` with `epoch` aware — comparing a naive stamp against the aware epoch (or another object's aware stamp) raises `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`.
- `cold_store.py:1837` (`evict_scan`): the same tuple sort over the whole bucket.
- `cold_store.py:1861` (`evict_scan`): `now - obj["last_modified"]` with `now` aware raises `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` for any naive-stamped object that reaches the age check.

## Reproduction (verified this run, shipped module imported unmodified)

```text
_parse_s3_list_page(<Contents>…<LastModified>2026-10-01T00:00:00.000</LastModified>…)
  -> last_modified = 2026-10-01 00:00:00, tzinfo = None        # contract says aware-or-None
datetime.now(timezone.utc) - stamp
  -> TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
sorted(objects, key=lambda o: (o["last_modified"] or aware_epoch, o["key"]))
  -> TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes
```

## Why it matters

One offset-less stamp anywhere in a bucket listing takes down the whole `backup_supabase` run and the whole eviction scan with an unhandled `TypeError` — no object is filed, no verdict is produced, and the traceback names datetime internals rather than the offending key. The configured R2 backend currently emits `Z` stamps, so this is latent until the tool is pointed at (or proxied/stubbed by) a store that omits the offset — exactly the variation this parser already defends against elsewhere. The fix direction is triage's pin: treat an offset-less stamp as unparseable (→ `None`, the documented safe meaning: oldest / never age-eligible) or interpret it as UTC — the two differ in eviction age verdicts, so the choice should be explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_parse_s3_list_page` upholds its documented contract for every input: `last_modified` is always an aware datetime or `None` (offset-less stamps handled by the pinned rule, with a comment naming it).
- [ ] `backup_supabase` and `evict_scan` complete without `TypeError` on a listing mixing aware, offset-less, and missing `LastModified` values.
- [ ] Tests cover: offset-less stamp page; a mixed listing through `evict_scan` (the offset-less object gets a non-evictable verdict, never a crash) and through the `backup_supabase` newest pick.
- [ ] Existing behaviour unchanged for `Z` / explicit-offset stamps and for absent `LastModified`.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `cold-store`, `s3_list`, `LastModified`, `naive`, `evict_scan`: #1632 (open) is the continuation-token loop in the same listing function — a different defect with a different fix; #1427/#1428/#1430/#1435 concern CI, shell plumbing, env validation and test speed. No issue covers offset-less timestamp parsing.

body:
# id(meta_client): over-cap response error prints a literal `(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)` placeholder

## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/meta_client.rs:57` (main `39e8410b`, introduced in fb3d6372 / PR #1719 for #1617):

```rust
ReadToEndError::TooLong => anyhow::anyhow!(
    "response too large: exceeds the {MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES}-byte limit              (MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)"
),
```

The `{MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES}` interpolation works, but the string then contains 14 spaces and a **literal** `(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)` suffix that is printed verbatim. A user whose find/list response exceeds the 64 MiB cap (`MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, meta_client.rs:29) sees:

```
response too large: exceeds the 67108864-byte limit              (MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)
```

The whole point of `capped_response_error` (doc comment, meta_client.rs:50-53) is to replace noq's bare "stream too long" with a message that names the actual cause — the trailing placeholder text undermines that and looks like an unfinished edit.

## Why the existing test does not catch it

`over_cap_error_names_the_limit` (meta_client.rs:248-254) asserts only that the message *contains* "response too large" and the cap's digits — both true despite the junk suffix. Substring assertions cannot see trailing garbage.

## Why it matters

This error is the user-facing diagnosis for every capped meta-protocol response read (remote find in the CLI and the REPL, via `read_capped_response`, meta_client.rs:70-75). It fires exactly when a store is large enough to matter, and the mangled text sends the reader hunting for a placeholder bug instead of the size limit.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `TooLong` error message is exactly `response too large: exceeds the 67108864-byte limit` (number interpolated from `MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES`, no literal placeholder text, no stray whitespace).
- [ ] `over_cap_error_names_the_limit` is tightened to assert the full message (or at least that it does not contain `(MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES)`), so a regression of this shape fails the test.
- [ ] `cargo test` for `meta_client` passes.

Related: #1617 (the cap itself), #1761 (hand-rolled clients still on a 1 MiB cap — different defect, not this one).

title: proxy-supervise: main() never runs when invoked via a symlinked path (~/code -> ~/git/code) — supervisor timer silently no-ops since 2026-10-27

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched

body:
## Bug

`bin/proxy-supervise.mjs` ends with:

```js
if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  main();
}
```

Node resolves `import.meta.url` to the realpath of the entry module, but `process.argv[1]` keeps the path as invoked. On the laptop, `~/code` is a symlink to `~/git/code` (created 2026-10-27 13:39), and the home-manager `proxy-supervisor` unit invokes `$HOME/code/bin/proxy-supervise.mjs` — so the guard is never true, `main()` never runs, and the process exits 0 with no output.

## Impact

Every timer-driven reconcile since the symlink appeared has been a silent no-op (systemd shows Starting/Finished in <1s, status SUCCESS). Consequences observed 2026-10-28:

- Converted fleet proxies sat on alternate ports (19742-19748) for hours while stale home-manager fallback units held the canonical ports; the supervisor never completed a roll.
- Canonical :18748 (commandcode) had no working listener while consumers pointed at it.
- The supervisor only did work when an agent invoked it via a fully resolved path (e.g. from a worktree).

## Repro

```
node ~/code/bin/proxy-supervise.mjs --config ~/.config/proxy-supervisor/config.json --only clef-proxy --status   # prints nothing, rc 0
node ~/git/code/bin/proxy-supervise.mjs --config ~/.config/proxy-supervisor/config.json --only clef-proxy --status # prints the status line
```

## Fix

Compare against the realpath, e.g. `import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1])).href` (guard the realpath call so module import in tests still works). Add a regression test that invokes the guard logic through a symlinked path.

Related: #916 (unit churn), #883 (stale bin/ tree in home-layer eval — separate cause of stale canonical-port code).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Invoking `bin/proxy-supervise.mjs` through a symlinked path (e.g. `~/code` -> `~/git/code`) runs `main()` instead of exiting 0 silently
- [ ] Direct invocation via the real path still works, and a regression test covers the symlinked-invocation case
- [ ] The fix compares canonicalised paths (or an equivalent robust entry check) rather than special-casing one laptop path

body:
Phase 2 of design #2077 (origin umbrella #1935, register row ELI-12, client half). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-elicitation-era-edges.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Decision is recorded on #2077 — this phase implements it as scoped; do not re-file under #1935, this is its implementation slice for ELI-12's client half.

## Scope

On current main, `-32042` (`URLElicitationRequiredError`, 2025-11-25 only) appears nowhere in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpclient` or `internal/daemon`: an upstream's `-32042` propagates as an opaque `rpcError` (code preserved, `internal/mcpclient/client.go` ~L1040, ~L1466-1506) and the call fails — mcpx never runs the URL flow and never retries.

- On a connection negotiated at **2025-11-25**, when a call fails with `-32042`: parse `data.elicitations`; each entry must be url-mode with an `elicitationId` (the spec's MUSTs) — a malformed entry fails the call with the original error, unmodified.
- Open each listed elicitation as a broker URL question via the existing `elicitViaBroker` path (`internal/daemon/hooks.go` ~L121-146), keyed by the upstream's `elicitationId`, so the human flow is the existing one (full URL shown, consent, `OnElicitationComplete` at hooks.go ~L57-68 marks completion).
- On completion, retry the original call **exactly once**. Decline, expiry, or a second `-32042` surface as the call's error — no loop.
- Era discipline: no `-32042` handling on 2026-negotiated connections (code reserved there; `input_required` is the replacement and already works) or pre-2025-11-25 connections (code does not exist).
- Triage check (recorded in the design doc): broker row keying — if broker rows are not namespaced by server, two upstreams choosing the same `elicitationId` collide (register ELI-09 risk note); fix or record on this issue.

Independent of Phase 1 in code (different files, different seam).

## Acceptance

- Upstream `-32042` → broker URL question(s) with the listed URL/id → completion → retried call succeeds, end to end in a test.
- Decline or expiry → the call fails with a named error and no retry occurs; a second `-32042` → error surfaces, no further retry.
- Malformed `data.elicitations` → original `-32042` error propagates untouched.
- Behaviour at 2026 and pre-2025-11-25 revisions is unchanged from today.

---
🤖 `agent-note:v1` — filed by the design-architect job (pass 11) as a sub-issue of design #2077. Audit basis: main `26221fcc`, 2026-10-28.

## Acceptance criteria
- On a 2025-11-25 connection, a call failing with -32042 has its data.elicitations parsed; each entry must be url-mode with an elicitationId, and a malformed entry fails the call with the original error unmodified.
- Each listed elicitation is opened as a broker URL question via the existing elicitViaBroker path, keyed by the upstream's elicitationId.
- After the URL flow completes, the original call is retried exactly once; a second -32042 is not retried again.
- Tests cover the happy path, the malformed-entry path, and the no-second-retry path.

Decision is recorded on #2077 — this phase implements it as scoped; do not re-file under #1935, this is its implementation slice for ELI-04's downgrade half.

## Scope

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go` — `Question.paramsFor` (~L465-507) currently strips `mode`/`elicitationId` per era but never rewrites `requestedSchema`, so a 2025-11-25 upstream's rich enum shapes reach a 2025-06-18 host verbatim and a strict old host rejects the whole `elicitation/create`.

- In `paramsFor`, for a pre-2025-11-25 peer, rewrite each `requestedSchema` property: titled single-select (`oneOf: [{const, title}, …]`) → `{type: "string", enum: [const…], enumNames: [title…]}`; untitled single-select (`enum`) and legacy titled (`enum`+`enumNames`) pass through unchanged.
- Multi-select (either flavour: `type: "array"` with `items.enum` or `items.anyOf`) is NOT downgraded and NOT flattened (flattening changes the answer type `string[]`→`string`; the upstream's validation would reject the elicited answer). A question whose schema carries a multi-select property is not sendable to a pre-2025-11-25 peer — the `Question.Sendable` (~L448-458) refusal pattern url mode already uses — and stays with the broker.
- No answer back-mapping: a downgraded single-select's host answer is the `const` string, the value in both eras.
- Triage check (recorded in the design doc): whether a downgraded property can carry a 2025-11-25 `default` that is illegal at 2025-06-18 (defaults allowed there only on booleans — ELI-05 adjacency); if so, strip non-boolean defaults in the same rewrite and say so on this issue.

## Acceptance

- Titled single-select downgrades to `enum`+`enumNames` for a 2025-06-18 peer, and the host's answer validates against the upstream's original schema unchanged.
- Untitled and legacy-titled properties pass byte-identical; a 2025-11-25 (or modern) peer sees every enum shape byte-identical to today.
- A question carrying a multi-select property is withheld from a 2025-06-18 peer (broker fallback) and offered unchanged to a 2025-11-25 peer.
- Tests pin behaviour per negotiated revision, per the fleet's protocol-edge rule. Neighbours to compose with, not duplicate: #1753's `CanElicit` shape reading at the same seam; #1484 (answer validation) untouched.

---
🤖 `agent-note:v1` — filed by the design-architect job (pass 11) as a sub-issue of design #2077. Audit basis: main `26221fcc`, 2026-10-28.

## Acceptance criteria
- For a pre-2025-11-25 peer, paramsFor rewrites titled single-select oneOf schemas to {type: string, enum: [const…], enumNames: [title…]}; untitled single-select and legacy titled enum shapes pass through unchanged.
- Multi-select questions are withheld from pre-2025-11-25 hosts (not downgraded, not flattened), with the withholding visible in behaviour/tests.
- Tests cover titled single-select rewrite, pass-through shapes, and multi-select withholding.

body:
# PR #1410 is green, clean and mergeable but unmerged — the #1406 Go to Line hard-break fix is stranded

## Finding

Open PR #1410 (Jules, commit `e7997db94f`, created 2026-10-27) fixes open issue #1406 — "Go to Line" undercounts lines in paragraphs with hard breaks. It has been sitting unmerged for ~36 hours despite being ready:

- `gh api repos/developing-today/code/pulls/1410` (verified 2026-10-28, this run): `mergeable=true`, `mergeable_state=clean`.
- Status checks on the PR: 31 SUCCESS, 1 SKIPPED, 0 failures.
- The fix is **not** on current main: `pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.ts` on `origin/main` still computes line starts from `node.textContent` (the exact code #1406 reports as wrong — `textContent` skips `hard_break` nodes), verified via `git show origin/main:pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.ts` this run.
- The PR's diff is small and scoped: `pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.ts` (`getLineStarts` walks inline children via `node.forEach()`, counting `hard_break` nodeSize) plus a regression test in `pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.test.ts` (rich doc with hard_break counts 3 lines and jumps to the right positions).
- No other open issue tracks shepherding this PR (searched "1410 / goto-line / Go to Line hard" across open+closed issues this run — only origin issue #1406 itself).

This is a stale-but-needed PR (pr-diff-review consolidation rule (b)): the work is done and green, the bug is live, and nothing is moving it to merge.

## Why it matters

#1406 stays live for every id(web) user navigating documents with hard breaks — Go to Line lands on the wrong line. A finished, tested fix rotting on an open PR also risks drifting until it conflicts (its base is already an older main, `37418e5633`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Shepherd PR #1410: re-verify CI on its current head (rebase/re-run if the base has drifted), confirm the goto-line regression test passes, and merge it — or state concretely on #1406 why it should not merge.
- [ ] After merge, confirm #1406 closes and `getLineStarts` on main no longer derives line starts from `node.textContent` alone.
- [ ] If the PR is superseded instead, link the superseding PR on #1406 in the same pass (no silent abandonment).

Found by: pr-diff-review job, 2026-10-28 run (batch PRs #1366–#1437, developing-today/code).

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#141 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #95

## Summary

Put every formatter (check mode) and every linter (at warning severity or stricter, not the minimal preset) for mcpx into the test matrix, with tool versions pinned by the flake so `nix fmt` / the dev shell locally gives the same answer as CI. Also run the one TypeScript test file CI has never run (`plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts`). The repo already has most of the plumbing -- `treefmt.nix`, a flake `formatter`, `checks.formatting`, `checks.tidy` -- but none of it covers Go, TypeScript or shell, and none of it runs in CI.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,
>     - all formatters and linters in test matrix, formatters in check mode, linters set to warning or more than minimal.

## Current state

Existing plumbing (repo root, main d0b7e01):
- `treefmt.nix`: `programs.nixfmt` and `programs.rustfmt` enabled; `# programs.shellcheck.enable = true; # failures`. `projectRootFile = "flake.nix"`, so it formats the **whole repo**.
- `flake.nix:422-429`: `formatter` = the treefmt wrapper (`nix fmt`); `checks.formatting` = treefmt's check derivation over `inputs.self`; `checks.tidy` = `flake-tidy all --check`.
- `justfile` `fmt`: `nixfmt *.nix pkgs/*.nix` then `nix run .#flake-tidy -- all || true` -- the glob does not reach `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix`, and the `|| true` swallows tidy failures. `tidy-check`: `nix run .#flake-tidy -- all --check`. So `just fmt` and `nix fmt` disagree about `package.nix`, and a CI check-mode formatter would fail on a file the documented local command cannot fix. Repair (from #169, see the comment below): `just fmt` calls `nix fmt`, which also picks up every program later added to `treefmt.nix` without a second edit.
- `pkgs/mcpx/docs/release-runbook.md:158-168` "Checks" lists `gofmt -l .`, `go vet ./...`, `go test ./... -count=1`, `scripts/stress.sh`, `scripts/bench.sh`, `nix build .#mcpx`, and "`README.md` must stay a symlink to `docs/story.md`" (`test -L README.md`). None of these except `go test` and `nix build` run in CI.
- `go test` already runs a **subset** of vet (atomic, bool, buildtags, directive, errorsas, ifaceassert, nilfunc, printf, stringintconv, tests; `go help test`). Full `go vet` adds copylocks, loopclosure, lostcancel, unusedresult and others.
- No `.golangci.yml`, no `deno.json`, no `.shellcheckrc`, no `.editorconfig` in `pkgs/mcpx`.
- `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts`: 21 tests at 05c78b2 (#182 added two) over the plugin's daemon discovery ladder, written for **`bun test`** (`import ... from "bun:test"`, `Bun.serve({unix})`; the header says `bun test plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts`). Still never run by CI: `.github/workflows/` has no `bun test` or `deno test` step. Plugin direction: #47 (opencode v2), #48 (harness-free core).

Baseline, run read-only on d0b7e01 with the tools installed on a dev machine (not the flake's pinned versions):

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `gofmt -l .` | clean |
| `deno fmt --check plugin` (deno 2.9.6, defaults) | 9 files differ: 4 TS/TSX (`daemon.ts`, `daemon.test.ts`, `mcpx-session.ts`, `mcpx-tui.tsx`) + 5 Markdown (`README.md`, four `SKILL.md`). The plugin is written in opencode's style (no semicolons); deno's default adds them. With `--no-semicolons --line-width=120` all 9 still differ. |
| `deno lint plugin` | 13 problems in 4 files: `no-explicit-any` x6, `require-await` x5, `no-unreachable` x1, `no-unused-vars` x1 (`summarise`) |
| `shellcheck scripts/*.sh` | 3: SC2034 and SC2319 (warnings, `stress.sh:13,87`), SC2012 (info, `bench.sh:60`) |
| `shfmt -l scripts/*.sh` (defaults) | both files differ |
| `nixfmt --check pkgs/mcpx/package.nix` | "not formatted" (system nixfmt; the flake's may differ) |
| golangci-lint, staticcheck, gofumpt, actionlint | not installed; unknown |

So turning any of this on needs one clean-up commit first (or a baseline), and a style decision for TypeScript.

## The tool set

| Area | Formatter (check mode) | Linter (>= warning) | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Go | `gofmt -l` (via treefmt `programs.gofmt`) | `go vet ./...` + `golangci-lint` v2 | gofumpt: stricter, reformats; opt-in, not needed |
| TypeScript (plugin, docs examples) | `deno fmt --check` with a `deno.json` matching the existing style | `deno lint` (recommended rules) + `deno check` | Deno is already a CI runtime; prettier/eslint would need `node_modules` |
| Shell (`scripts/*.sh`) | `shfmt -d` (pick `-i` to match the files) | `shellcheck` at default severity (`style`, the strictest) | the treefmt comment says shellcheck "failures" -- for the whole repo; scope to mcpx first |
| Nix (`pkgs/mcpx/package.nix`, flake) | `nixfmt` (already in treefmt) | `statix`, `deadnix` (optional) | |
| Workflows | -- | `actionlint` (also shellchecks `run:` blocks when shellcheck is on PATH) | covers `mcpx-test.yml`, `format.yaml`; zizmor is security -> deferred |
| Flake | -- | `flake-tidy all --check` (exists: `checks.tidy`, `just tidy-check`) | repo-wide; run when `flake.nix`/`flake.lock` change |
| Repo invariants | -- | `test -L pkgs/mcpx/README.md` | from the release runbook; one line |

golangci-lint configuration, "warning or more than minimal": v2 with `linters.default: standard` (errcheck, govet, ineffassign, staticcheck, unused) **plus** a curated set that fits this codebase -- e.g. `errorlint`, `bodyclose`, `noctx`, `misspell`, `unconvert`, `usestdlibvars`, `gocritic` (diagnostic tags), `revive` (a few rules). From #169: `staticcheck` with `checks: ["all"]` rather than its default subset, and `copyloopvar` (Go 1.22 made the `rt := rt` idiom redundant; `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go:15,47` still carry it). Not `gosec` in the blocking set: security is deferred, and on a process-spawning CLI it yields a large low-signal backlog. Not `default: all`: it enables style linters that contradict each other and would turn the first PR into a rewrite. Commit `pkgs/mcpx/.golangci.yml`; new linters are added one PR at a time with their fixes.

TypeScript style decision: either adopt deno's defaults and reformat the plugin once, or write a `deno.json` `fmt` block that matches the current opencode style. The plugin is loaded by opencode and #47/#48 may move or reshape it -- coordinate there before a mass reformat; lint can start immediately since it is independent of style.

Markdown: `deno fmt` also formats `.md`. The book is the docs tree's; exclude `docs/**` and `AGENTS.md` until the docs tree decides its own formatting.

## Approaches -- how tools are installed and pinned

### A -- marketplace actions per tool (least recommended)

`golangci/golangci-lint-action`, `reviewdog/action-shellcheck`, `raven-actions/actionlint`, each with its own version input. Fast to write, and golangci-lint-action caches well. But every tool's version lives in YAML, local runs use whatever is installed (the baseline above already used unpinned local tools), and Renovate bumps them independently of the flake. This is how "passes locally, fails in CI" starts.

### B -- Go tools via the `tool` directive, the rest via actions

Go 1.24+ `tool` directives in `go.mod` pin Go tools and `go tool golangci-lint run` works locally and in CI. But it adds golangci-lint's large dependency graph to `pkgs/mcpx/go.mod`/`go.sum`, which **changes the Nix `vendorHash`** and Renovate's grouped Go bumps get much bigger (the vendorHash repair exists precisely because those bumps are painful). Pins Go tools only; shell/Nix/TS tools stay unpinned.

### C -- the flake pins everything; treefmt for formatters, a dev shell for linters (recommended)

- Formatters: extend `treefmt.nix` with `programs.gofmt`, `programs.deno` (fmt), `programs.shfmt`, keeping `nixfmt`; scope the new ones to `pkgs/mcpx/**` with per-program `includes` so the rest of the repo is not reformatted by this issue. treefmt-nix ships modules for gofmt, gofumpt, goimports, golangci-lint, deno, prettier, biome, shfmt, shellcheck, actionlint, nixfmt, statix, deadnix (seen in a local copy of the input; confirm against the pinned rev). CI runs `nix fmt -- --ci` (or builds `checks.x86_64-linux.formatting`) -- check mode, non-zero on any diff, prints the diff. Locally `nix fmt` gives byte-identical results because it is the same derivation.
- Linters: the `devShells.mcpx` that #134 proposes (go, gopls, deno, bun, node, git, python3, golangci-lint), extended with `shellcheck`, `actionlint`, `statix`, `deadnix` -- one shell, pinned by `flake.lock`; CI runs `nix develop .#mcpx -c <linter>`; locally the same command. **Do not run golangci-lint through treefmt**: its treefmt module runs `golangci-lint run --fix` per file, which needs module downloads (not available in the `checks` sandbox) and rewrites code.
- Costs: the Nix install (~8 s) plus substitution per lint job; competitive only with a store cache (#135 decision 7). One `flake.lock` bump updates every tool at once -- that is the point, and also a risk (a formatter upgrade reformats; #142 handles that).

Recommended because it is the only option where local == CI by construction, it reuses what the repo already has, and it keeps Go tool dependencies out of mcpx's `go.mod`.

## Matrix layout

Three lint legs, each small, plus a plugin test leg:

| Leg | Runs | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fmt` | `nix fmt -- --ci` (all formatters, scoped) | seconds after Nix setup |
| `lint-go` | `go vet ./...`, `golangci-lint run` (with Go build cache from #135) | the slowest lint leg; type-checks the module |
| `lint-other` | `deno lint`, `deno check`, `shellcheck`, `actionlint`, `statix`/`deadnix`, README symlink, `flake-tidy --check` when the flake changed | seconds |
| `plugin` | `bun test plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts` (needs Bun only; pin the flake's Bun) | seconds |

If queue pressure shows up (#140), `fmt` and `lint-other` merge first. Run `plugin` under Deno and Node too only if #48 makes the core runtime-neutral (today the test imports `bun:test` and `Bun.serve`, so it is Bun-only). `scripts/stress.sh` and `scripts/bench.sh` stay manual (they use real servers from `.mcpx.json`); #97 decides whether a stress leg exists.

## Implementation order (small PRs)

1. `.golangci.yml` with `default: standard`, `go vet`, gofmt check, shellcheck/actionlint -- fix what they find (small: gofmt is clean, shellcheck has 3).
2. `plugin` leg: `bun test` (no reformat needed).
3. `deno lint` (13 fixes) and `deno check`.
4. TS/shell/Nix formatting once the style is agreed: one reformat commit per language, then the check turns on. Add the reformat commits to `.git-blame-ignore-revs`.
5. Curated extra golangci linters, one per PR.

Alternative sequencing (from #169), for any linter whose backlog is too big for one fix-up PR: land it `continue-on-error: true` with `::warning::` annotations, fix the backlog in a dedicated PR, then flip it to blocking. Formatters block from day one either way -- a formatter has no judgement calls. Whichever path, the end state must be "clean and enforced", never another `# ... # failures` line like `treefmt.nix:6`.

## Open questions

1. TypeScript style: deno defaults vs matching opencode's (no semicolons, width 120)? Depends on #47/#48 plans for the plugin.
2. shfmt flags for `scripts/*.sh` (indent width) -- match the existing files.
3. Scope: mcpx only, or turn the whole-repo `checks.formatting` into a CI job too (#49's territory)?
4. Is `nix flake check` usable as a CI step for mcpx, or does it evaluate/build too much of the repo (opencode patches, darwin-only packages)? Prefer building the single `checks.x86_64-linux.formatting` attribute.
5. `deno check` of the plugin needs opencode's plugin types -- available offline, or does it need #48 first?
6. Does `checks.formatting` pass on `main` today? Nothing runs it; the baseline above already found `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix` unformatted by a system nixfmt. If it is red, step one is the backlog, and its size is unknown (from #169).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (mostly clean-up and one style decision) · **Impact** med · **Depends on / related**: #95, #135 (legs, Nix cache, tool-version decision), #142 (auto-applies the same formatters), #140 (merge legs under queue pressure), #134 (the shared `mcpx` dev shell), #47, #48 (plugin shape and its tests), #49 (repo-wide format/tidy checks), #99 (which of these agents run locally: formatters yes, full lint maybe), #35 (version drift), #129 (its settings-effect guard needs this issue's `plugin` leg to cover plugin-scoped settings, which only the plugin's TypeScript reads).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every formatter/linter named in the body's CI matrix runs in CI pinned by the flake, the plugin's bun test runs, and the workflow is green.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links, timings, or probe output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#140 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #95

## Summary

Add a CI time budget: a hardcoded default (overridable per run), a final job after the matrix that measures how long the run took and which part was slow, and a written runbook for what to do when the budget is exceeded. Recommendation: **report several measures, gate on the longest leg, warn rather than fail on PRs, and track sustained overruns on main**. The final job doubles as the single required check (`ci-ok`) defined in #135, so the budget costs no extra job start.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - importantly, as we add more testing agents should not run every single test basically ever. below documents a rough idea of a ci job design/policy, the main priority is being short as possible.
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,
>     - continue until the jobs can't get much faster considering setup/teardown and then set a ci testing budget which is a hardcoded default input. after the test matrix have a time budget job when subtracts github workflow request time from now. (this catches if the jobs are impacted by matrix size, could lessen by taking initial job end or matrix start time.)

> - testing
>   - make a comprehensive github action ci.yaml workflow (or test.yaml) that is as fast as possible,
>     - repeat this process whenever testing exceeds some time budget. make setup faster, rebalance alpha splits, split groups of tests on the longest shard. maybe flag that never tears down because just killing the box after. anything downloaded should be cached, shallow clone a partial path to mcpx dir, if there's unexplainable job start delays, try to keep all job times balanced, 10 ultrafast ones can give you quick signals but may put pressure on runner infra and cause the longest jobs to last a little longer. all that matters is how long the longest jobs take. job runners have 2 or 4 cores, consider if theres lengthy tests which are '1' test but re-exec N times 'in parallel': they will only run 1-3 at a time and so 30 cases _could_ take up to 10 tests worth of time even in parallel and may need to be examined. we're using go so im not too worried about time budget but its best to get this early. main focus is strong tests as each step of the lifecycle.

## Current state

- No budget and no timing report exist. Wall times of the last 20 `mcpx.yml` runs: 3m24s-4m30s; the last 10: 3m57s-4m30s (a ~15 % spread on an unchanged workload -- the budget must have headroom or it flakes). The runs since (8001f23's merge, #182's PR and merge at 05c78b2, Renovate PR #184): 4m03s-4m15s, with e2e now at 209 tests. The gap between summed step time (229 s on 36673523537) and reported run time (237-258 s on the eight runs before it) is 8-29 s of queue and runner provisioning -- the quantity the notes worry about contaminating the number (from #167).
- **There is no run-start timestamp in any expression context.** The `github` context has `run_id`, `run_number`, `run_attempt`, `workflow_sha`, ... but no time ([contexts reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts)). The times come from the REST API with `permissions: actions: read`:
  - `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}` -> `created_at`, `run_started_at`, `updated_at`. `run_started_at` is the start of the **current attempt**; `created_at` is the first attempt's. They are equal on attempt 1 (both `2026-09-30T05:27:57Z` for run 36673523537) and differ on a re-run -- use `run_started_at`, or a re-run is measured from the original push.
  - `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/runs/{run_id}/attempts/{attempt}/jobs` -> per job `created_at` (queued), `started_at`, `completed_at`, and per step `started_at`/`completed_at`. Verified on run 36673523537: job created 05:27:58, started 05:28:00, completed 05:31:53; step times match the log.
- The notes' caveat is real: "now minus run start" includes the budget job's own queue and startup, `init`, and any queueing caused by matrix size (the Free plan runs 20 standard jobs at once account-wide, [limits](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/limits)).

## Approaches

### What to measure

- **A -- only `now - run_started_at` (the notes' first idea).** Simple, and it is what a human waiting on the PR feels. But it mixes queueing, `init`, the budget job's own start (~5 s + queue), and the real test time, so when it goes over, it does not say why. Least recommended as the *only* number.
- **B -- measure from `init` completion / matrix start (the notes' alternative).** `max(completed_at of matrix legs) - init.completed_at`. Removes init and the final job's own start; still includes queue delay for legs. Of the notes' two spellings, prefer `init` end over "matrix start": the gap between `init` finishing and the legs starting *is* the matrix-size effect the notes want caught, and measuring from the first leg's start deletes it (from #167). `init` can also publish its own end time as a job output (`date +%s` into `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`), so this number needs no API call.
- **C -- report all of them, gate on the longest leg (recommended).**

| Measure | Formula (jobs API) | Tells you |
| --- | --- | --- |
| wall | `max(completed_at of needed jobs) - run_started_at` (not `now`, so the final job's own start is excluded) | what the author waits |
| matrix span | `max(completed_at) - init.completed_at` | the notes' "matrix start" variant |
| **longest leg** | `max(completed_at - started_at)` over legs, with its name | the thing sharding controls -- "all that matters is how long the longest jobs take" |
| queue | max and sum of `started_at - created_at` | runner pressure / "unexplainable job start delays" |
| fixed cost per leg | first test step `started_at` - job `started_at`, plus post steps | whether setup or tests dominate (the stop rule in #139) |

Gate on **longest leg** (controllable by us); report **wall** prominently; show **queue** so an over-budget wall with a normal longest leg is visibly GitHub's queue, not our tests. All go into the job summary as one table, plus a `timings.json` artifact merged from the legs' `go test -json` output (the input #139's splitter reads).

### The budget input

"Hardcoded default input" = a literal in the workflow, overridable when dispatched by hand:

```yaml
on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      budget_seconds: { type: number, default: 0 }
env:
  # Longest-leg budget. Changing it is a reviewed edit with a reason; see the runbook.
  BUDGET_SECONDS: ${{ inputs.budget_seconds > 0 && inputs.budget_seconds || 120 }}
```

`inputs` is empty on `push`/`pull_request`, so those use the literal. A repository variable (`vars.MCPX_CI_BUDGET`) would let someone change the budget without a commit -- rejected, because the notes ask for a hardcoded default and a budget that changes silently is not a budget. A committed file (e.g. `.github/ci-budget.json`, `{ "longest_leg_seconds": ..., "wall_seconds": ... }`, read by `init` and passed down as an output) is the other reviewable home: a budget change becomes a one-line data diff beside the timing file #139 reads, and the dispatch input still overrides it (from #167). Either is fine; the literal is one file fewer.

The number: set it after #143's baseline and #139's first sharding, at roughly the p90 longest leg of ~10 main runs plus 15 % (the observed spread), then ratchet down as the runbook wins time. `120` above is a placeholder.

### What happens over budget

- **A -- fail the run.** With a ~15 % run-to-run spread, a tight budget fails healthy PRs, people re-run until green, and the budget becomes noise that costs more runner time than it saves. Not recommended.
- **B -- warn only** (`::warning::` annotation + summary). Cheap and honest, but a warning on every PR is ignored within a week.
- **C -- warn per run; act on sustained overruns; fail only on gross overruns (recommended).**
  - Every run: summary table + a `::warning::` if the longest leg exceeds the budget.
  - On `main` only: if the median longest leg of the last 5 main runs (from the API) exceeds the budget, open or update one issue "mcpx CI over budget" (label `testing`) with the table and a link to the runbook. `permissions: issues: write` on this job, main only.
  - Fail only above 2x the budget: that is a hang or an accidental serialisation, not variance, and it should block.

Run the final job on `ubuntu-slim` (1 vCPU container, meant for short automation jobs; [runner reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/runners/github-hosted-runners)) -- it only needs `gh`/`curl` and `jq`. Whether `ubuntu-slim` starts faster or slower than `ubuntu-latest` is unmeasured; check in #143.

## Runbook (when the budget is exceeded)

Lives as a comment block at the top of `mcpx-test.yml` and is linked from the summary (a longer version can go wherever #99 puts the testing policy doc). Cheapest first; stop as soon as the budget is met:

1. **Read the table.** Which measure is over?
   - *queue* high, longest leg normal -> runner pressure. Merge the smallest legs (lint legs first), or drop a shard. Do not add shards.
   - *fixed cost* high -> setup. Go to 2.
   - a *test leg* long -> go to 3.
   - the `nix` leg longest -> see #135 decision 7 (store cache; question whether `checkPhase` needs to re-run units CI already ran).
2. **Make setup faster.** Look for cache misses in the log (until #182 every run carried `Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found`; since #182 a miss reads `Cache is not found` in the setup-go step); drop `setup-*` steps a leg does not use; ship the compiled `e2e.test` and binaries instead of building per leg.
3. **Rebalance.** With the #139 splitter this is automatic; check the timing file is fresh. If using hand ranges (not recommended), move the boundaries.
4. **Split the longest shard.** Lower `target_leg_seconds` / raise N -- but only while the saving per extra leg exceeds the fixed cost per leg (#139's stop rule).
5. **Make the slowest tests faster.** Top 10 from `timings.json`: fixed `time.Sleep` waits, fan-out tests on too few cores, anything that starts a runtime it does not need. #79's CLI speedups apply to every e2e test.
6. **Parallelise within a leg** (`t.Parallel` in e2e). #52 no longer blocks it (fixed in #182); #138's environment allowlist comes first (see #139).
7. **Raise the budget** only as a reviewed change with the table attached and the reason in the commit message.

Repeat whenever the main-branch issue opens.

## Open questions

1. Budget on longest leg only, or also a separate (looser) wall budget?
2. Where does the long-form runbook live -- workflow comment only, or the testing policy doc from #99?
3. Should the over-budget issue be one rolling issue or a comment on #95?
4. `ubuntu-slim` vs `ubuntu-latest` for the final job: start latency?
5. Are timings from re-run attempts excluded from the median? (They are usually warm and faster.) Record `github.run_attempt` beside every measurement so the history stays interpretable.
6. Should a leg's *setup* have its own threshold? A setup regression is invisible in wall clock while the matrix absorbs it, and setup is the floor on the useful shard count (#139's stop rule) (from #167).
7. #97's environment legs (container, remote, macOS) are legitimately slower: one global budget, or one per matrix dimension (from #167)?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S (the job) + S (runbook) · **Impact** med · **Depends on / related**: #95, #135 (the final `ci-ok` job this lives in), #139 (consumes `timings.json`; stop rule), #143 (baseline that sets the number), #138 (before `t.Parallel`), #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #79, #97 / #134 (environment legs will likely be the longest -- macOS runners are 3 vCPU and capped at 5 concurrent), #130 (its PR job is inside the budget, its nightly run is not), #99.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The final CI job enforces/reports the stated time budget and the over-budget runbook is recorded where the body specifies.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links, timings, or probe output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#819 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

## Problem

mcpx sends no workspace information when it initializes a server: no `rootUri`, no `workspaceFolders` (grep across `internal/mcpclient` and `internal/pool` — none). Workspace-oriented servers therefore start without a workspace session even when mcpx knows exactly which repo the caller is in.

Concrete evidence (live fleet, 2026-10-25): gopls behind mcpx works file-by-file — its file-argument tools load the file ad hoc as a "command-line-arguments" package — but it is not a module workspace session: `go_package_api` on a module path returned **empty after 156 s**. Two missing pieces combine here: the process cwd is static (the spawn-cwd issue), and the initialize handshake carries no root even if the cwd were right.

## Proposed design

When mcpx has a scope-resolved root for an instance (repo/worktree scope resolution already computes it), include it in the initialize params for that server instance:

- `rootUri` set to the resolved root, and
- `workspaceFolders` containing that root,

for servers that declare workspace support in their initialize negotiation. Servers that don't advertise/accept it must be unaffected (send only what the negotiated protocol version and server capabilities allow).

This is step 3 of the 2026-10-25 per-project design note. It builds on the spawn-cwd issue #817, which introduces the resolved-root plumbing this issue reuses; the `${mcpx.root}` substitution issue #818 is the config-level companion. Order: spawn-cwd/substitution first, this after — flipping gopls to `"scope": "worktree"` only becomes fully effective once the workspace reaches the server both via cwd *and* via initialize.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For an instance with a scope-resolved root, the initialize request mcpx sends includes `rootUri`/`workspaceFolders` naming that root (demonstrated by a captured handshake or a test double server that records initialize params).
- [ ] Servers that don't negotiate workspace support initialize exactly as before.
- [ ] `global`-scoped instances (no resolved root) send no rootUri/workspaceFolders — no fabricated daemon-cwd root.
- [ ] With gopls at `"scope": "worktree"` behind the fixed spawn cwd, `go_package_api` on a module path returns the module's API promptly (the 156 s empty result does not recur).
- [ ] Tests cover: root present for repo/worktree scopes, absent for global scope.
