```
cd pkgs/mcpx
TMPDIR=$HOME/tmp go test ./internal/daemon/
```

5 failures, e.g.:

```
--- FAIL: TestResolveNamesTheDaemonKeyedToTheNearestConfig (0.00s)
    routes_resolve_test.go:55: configHash = "70618a007427", want "ffec5674504f"
--- FAIL: TestResolveOverHTTPAnswersForTheAskingDaemonItself (0.00s)
    routes_resolve_test.go:199: sources = [.../003/.mcpx.json /home/hatch/.config/mcpx/config.json], want [.../003/.mcpx.json]
--- FAIL: TestResolveForADirectoryWithNoConfigNamesTheDefaultDaemon (0.00s)
    routes_resolve_test.go:227: configHash = "dc56d4a7680a", want empty: nothing contributed
```

## Root cause

Same class as #196/#221 (fixed there for `internal/config`): `SearchPathFrom` checks `$dir/.config/mcpx/config.json` at **every** ancestor level during the upward walk. The test's `isolate()` set `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to a `t.TempDir`, but the temp tree itself lived under the real $HOME, so the walk passed through the real home directory and picked up the developer's own config — changing the daemon key in `FingerprintConfig` and breaking socket resolution (the leaked hash `dc56d4a7680a` is the same default-daemon hash from #196).

Two Go gotchas made the obvious fix wrong:
- `testing.TempDir` reads `GOTMPDIR`, **not** `TMPDIR` (go1.26 `testing/testing.go:1460`), and caches one parent dir per test — setting `TMPDIR` after the first `t.TempDir` has no effect.
- So the fake home itself must be created outside the real $HOME tree.

## Fix

In PR #221 (commit 995fb9a on branch `mcpx-test-home-isolation`): `isolate()` now creates the fake home with `os.MkdirTemp("/tmp", ...)` and points `GOTMPDIR`+`TMPDIR`+`HOME` at it before any `t.TempDir` call. Full `internal/daemon` package green with the fix; the 5 failures reproduce on pristine 408bc2b.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `go test ./internal/daemon/` passes with TMPDIR under the real $HOME and a real `~/.config/mcpx/config.json` present.
- [ ] The daemon tests are hermetic: config discovery in tests cannot read the operator's real config (test-scoped HOME or config-dir override).
- [ ] No production behavior changes beyond what test hermeticity requires.

title: mcpx testing: bug-shape generators -- registry, versioning, budget, first shapes

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#124 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #93

## Summary

Make generators the primary way mcpx is tested: many seeded variations per run, and **every escaped bug becomes a generator for its shape**, drawing from the same run seed and able to produce unlimited inputs of that shape. This issue designs the generator registry (naming, versioning, budget, the escape loop) and proposes the first six shapes from mcpx's real bug history. The engine is #123; the seed and derivation are #121.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - agents should make at least 1 simple, new test for every bug observed from any source, when cheap to do so-- aggresively test many permutations. 
>     - you can absolutely rely on fuzzing anywhere you can fit it and you should whenever you can-- but you _must_ use a single seed per-run to generate all inputs. (this could eventually be discussed with careful consideration.) it should be appended into a test tracking structured file in the repo and it can be committed. ideally main branch commit's seed or pr merge seed should make it back into file eventually. to prevent churn, maybe ci appends the seed into a gha var (race/overwrite risk?), or attached as artifact to each workflow in init job before tests begin-- a collector job can scoop them up sometime later. once a day/week/on-release/every-100-commits. im thinking touch tests/seeds/<seed> or uv has a seed generate job. anyways ci it should end up in that dir, then as an artifact if gha and main branch, then passed into the test matrix. if uv test without arg- warn, generate and write it yourself pass it to all tests, if some other testing method there should not be a static seed, throw for empty or setup should make the seed. avoid changing how seed generates data. im not sure if a convenient uuid with time, v7?, is valid, but as long as its enough entropy whatever works. either put nothing in their or compact json, consider seeds/v1/id/<first 2 char>/<seed><--symlink: seeds/yyyy/mm/dd/<seed> avoiding conflicts is important.
>       - think a hack job of antithesis/tigerbeetle. this is the primary testing method is throw insane amount of variations. if something is found outside this system and a test that could have had missed it, make a different generator that uses the same seed and makes an infinite amount of things matching the offensive shape.

## Context: what "a hack job of antithesis/tigerbeetle" means here

| System | What it does | What mcpx can borrow now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| TigerBeetle VOPR | Runs a whole cluster in one process with simulated time, network and disk, all driven by one PRNG seed; a failing seed replays the entire run bit-for-bit. Runs continuously on many cores. | One seed per run, printed on failure; volume through many cheap runs; "the seed is the bug report". |
| FoundationDB simulation | Same idea, built in from day one: all I/O and time behind interfaces, fault injection ("buggify") on seeded dice. | Seeded fault injection at interface seams where they already exist. |
| Antithesis | A deterministic hypervisor: runs unmodified containers deterministically, explores interleavings and faults, replays any finding. | The goal state; not reachable by retrofit (see #126). |

The "hack job": mcpx gets the **seeded, high-volume input generation** half of this without the **deterministic execution** half. Consequence, stated plainly: a failing seed always reproduces the *inputs* and test order, but a failure caused by timing (goroutine scheduling, subprocess start, socket readiness) may need several tries under the same seed. Failures should say so.

## Current state

- No generators. The closest thing is the guard-test pattern: `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:2877`, from #74/#75) enumerates a hand-written table; `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` (`internal/e2e/v1ops_test.go:287`); `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault` (`internal/defaults/guard_test.go:92`); the "declared but never read" guard landed in #171 (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:73`). Guards enumerate a *class*; generators vary *inputs within* a class -- they compose (a guard's table becomes the generator's alphabet).
- Real history of escaped bugs (each found by accident, per #91): flags accepted and ignored (#74); registry test reached the internet (#65); macOS-pass/Linux-fail (#35); a flaky test found on a third full run; daemons leaking (#52, fixed in #182); state/cache correctness (#78).
- Cost profile at 05c78b2 (CI run 36693030957): e2e tests spawn the real binary and a runtime; `internal/e2e` is 108.9 s of a 148 s test step. Pure-function packages (`codegen`, `config`, `launcher`, `settings`) run in < 0.2 s each. Generators belong mostly in the latter, with small counts in e2e.

## Design

### Registry

- Package `internal/testsupport/gen`. A generator is `{Name, Version, Origin, Draw func(Source, size) T}`; registered in one table (`gen.All`) so guards can iterate it.
- **Name**: `<area>.<shape>`, e.g. `exec.flagset`, `config.layers`, `codegen.jsonschema`, `launcher.template`, `api.v1request`, `settings.precedence`.
- **Version**: integer; bump on any change to output for the same stream. The substream key is `name@version` (#121 section 2), so bumping one generator never moves another's inputs.
- **Origin**: the issue/PR/bug that motivated it (`#74`). Makes the escape loop auditable.
- **Old versions**: kept while any stored seed (#122) references them, else deleted; or frozen into `gen/legacy_*.go`. The golden-output guard (#121 section 3) runs over `gen.All`.
- Manifest hash of all `name@version` entries goes into every stored seed record (#122).

### The escape loop (bug found outside the generator system)

1. Write the plain regression test (per-bug test policy: #99).
2. **Classify the bug before building anything:** generator, guard, environment axis, or none of these (with the reason recorded in `Origin` or on the bug). Not every escaped bug has an input shape. Of the six on record, three do (#74/#75, #102/#106, #108). #65 needs a hermeticity guard (#129), #35 needs an environment axis (#97), and the third-run flake is ordering or timing (`-shuffle`, #130; #126). The addendum comment below has the table. A generator written for a bug no input can reach looks like coverage and is not.
3. If it is a generator: ask which generator *could* have produced this input? If one exists and its alphabet/distribution missed it, bump its version and widen it. If none exists, create `<area>.<shape>@1` with `Origin` = the bug.
4. Check the new generator finds the bug on the pre-fix commit within its CI budget (the red-first check). If it cannot, it is the wrong shape.
5. The failing input from step 4, minimized, joins the native fuzz corpus or the regression test from step 1.

### Budget per run

- `MCPX_TEST_FUZZ=off|quick|ci|soak` (named in #121): `off` = regression inputs only (nix `checkPhase`); `quick` = local default; `ci` = matrix default; `soak` = scheduled long run.
- Budget is **counts, not time**, so the same seed generates the same inputs everywhere. Suggested starting counts: pure-function generators 200 (`quick`) / 2,000 (`ci`); e2e generators 2 / 10 -- each e2e case costs a subprocess.
- Coverage accumulates **across runs**: at ~20 CI runs/day, 10 e2e flag combinations per run is 200 distinct combinations/day, all reproducible. This is the real payoff of "one seed per run".
- Hard ceiling: generators together must fit #95's CI time budget; #95 sets the numbers, this issue exposes the knob.

### First shapes (from real history)

| Generator | Target | Property | Origin | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exec.flagset` | `mcpx exec` argv: random subsets/orders of flags from the `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` table, `--f=v` vs `--f v`, inline vs file source | each flag's marker appears iff the flag is present, in every combination (flags compose) | #74/#75 | e2e, small count |
| `config.layers` | random stacks of `.mcpx.json` layers (servers, disables, defaults, JSONC comments) through `LoadFrom` (`internal/config/config.go:601`) | nearest wins per server; `disabled` is local; `StripJSONC` of comment-free JSON is identity (`config.go:718`); adding an unrelated far layer never changes a near value | #5, #78 | unit |
| `codegen.jsonschema` | random JSON Schemas (nesting, enums with hostile strings, nullable unions, `$ref`, keyword-named properties) through `TypeFor`/`ArgsTypeFor` (`internal/codegen/ts.go:70,84`) and `ToolFuncName` (`ts.go:397`) | no panic; deterministic; output type-checks (batch all N outputs into **one** `deno check` per run); distinct tool names never collide | codegen bugs to date | unit + one runtime call |
| `launcher.template` | random templates with `@placeholders`, escapes, adjacency, through `Expand`/`Used` (`internal/launcher/template.go:80,419`) | filling every `Used` placeholder never errors; no placeholder survives; text outside placeholders is preserved | #7 | unit |
| `api.v1request` | random bodies per op from the ops table (`internal/api/ops*.go`) / its OpenAPI | no 5xx; responses validate against the declared schema; unknown fields rejected consistently | extends `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` | e2e-lite (one daemon, many requests) |
| `settings.precedence` | random assignment of each registry setting (`settings.Registry()`, `internal/settings/registry.go:13`) across default/config/env/flag | effective value = highest-precedence layer set; `Validate`/`TypedValue` agree; `ParseBytes` round-trips (`value.go:415`). This proves *resolution* only. Whether the resolved value changes behaviour is #129's guard (#181 collision 15); this generator can supply its non-default values | settings registry | unit |

## Approaches

### A -- sprinkle ad-hoc random loops into existing tests (least recommended)
Each test calls `seed.Rand(t, "...")` and invents its own inputs inline. Fast to start, but no registry means no versioning, no golden guard, no manifest in stored seeds, no reuse between a unit property and its native-fuzz target, and "make a different generator" has nowhere to live. Cross-commit replay silently breaks the first time someone edits a loop.

### B -- generators per package, no central registry
Each package owns `gen_test.go` with its generators. Better locality; versioning by convention. But generators in `_test.go` files cannot be imported by e2e or other packages (`config.layers` is needed by both `internal/config` and `internal/e2e`), and a guard cannot enumerate them.

### C -- central registry in `internal/testsupport/gen`, with Origin, versions, budget and the escape loop (recommended)
As designed above. It is the only option where "every escaped bug becomes a generator" is checkable (Origin + a guard that every `bug`-labelled fix since adoption has a regression test and, where cheap, a generator -- that audit is #99's), where versions are enforceable (golden guard), and where one generator feeds unit properties, e2e cases and native fuzz targets alike (#123).

## Open questions

- Should the escape loop be required for every bug, or only "when cheap to do so" as the parent bullet says for tests? Proposed: required to *ask* (a line in the PR), optional to build -- #99 owns the wording.
- A nightly job that replays the last K failing seeds from #122 against main (regression detection for seeds, not just inputs)?
- Fault injection ("buggify"): seeded dice at existing seams (runtime start failure, socket write error, slow MCP server in `fakemcp`) -- in scope here or a later issue?
- `codegen.jsonschema` wants a TS type-check per run; is one `deno check` (~400 ms new program, per the brief) acceptable in `quick`, or `ci` only?
- Who sizes the budget numbers: this issue proposes, #95 decides.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (registry + guard S; each generator S-M; `api.v1request` M) · **Impact** high (the primary testing method per the notes)
**Depends on / related:** #121, #122, #123, #125 (lands the first one), #126; #74/#75, #5, #7, #78, #65, #35, #52 (closed, fixed in #182); #95 (budget), #99 (per-bug test and escape-loop policy), #129 (guards, for bugs with no input shape), #97 (e2e generators run in the environment matrix).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

title: mcpx testing: seed store layout and collector (file per seed, artifact + scheduled collector)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#122 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #93

## Summary

Where run seeds are **kept** in the repo, in what shape, and how they **get there** from CI without churn or conflicts. The notes propose `seeds/v1/id/<first 2 char>/<seed>` plus a date symlink tree; this issue evaluates that layout (it has two concrete problems), the file format, and the collector options (GitHub repository variable, per-run artifact + scheduled collector, deriving the seed from the run id). Seed minting and derivation are #121.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - agents should make at least 1 simple, new test for every bug observed from any source, when cheap to do so-- aggresively test many permutations. 
>     - you can absolutely rely on fuzzing anywhere you can fit it and you should whenever you can-- but you _must_ use a single seed per-run to generate all inputs. (this could eventually be discussed with careful consideration.) it should be appended into a test tracking structured file in the repo and it can be committed. ideally main branch commit's seed or pr merge seed should make it back into file eventually. to prevent churn, maybe ci appends the seed into a gha var (race/overwrite risk?), or attached as artifact to each workflow in init job before tests begin-- a collector job can scoop them up sometime later. once a day/week/on-release/every-100-commits. im thinking touch tests/seeds/<seed> or uv has a seed generate job. anyways ci it should end up in that dir, then as an artifact if gha and main branch, then passed into the test matrix. if uv test without arg- warn, generate and write it yourself pass it to all tests, if some other testing method there should not be a static seed, throw for empty or setup should make the seed. avoid changing how seed generates data. im not sure if a convenient uuid with time, v7?, is valid, but as long as its enough entropy whatever works. either put nothing in their or compact json, consider seeds/v1/id/<first 2 char>/<seed><--symlink: seeds/yyyy/mm/dd/<seed> avoiding conflicts is important.

## Current state

- No seed store, no seeds, no collector. The only CI job that writes to git is the vendorHash repair step in `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml`, which commits and `git push`es on renovate/dependabot branches -- precedent for a bot writing to the repo.
- `dezren39/nix` is **public**. Artifacts and logs are kept 90 days by default; public repositories can configure 1-90 days (private up to 400). A collector must run well inside that window.
- GitHub configuration variables: 48 KB per variable, 500 per repository; 10 MB combined per workflow run on github.com. The `permissions:` block for `GITHUB_TOKEN` has **no `variables` scope**, so writing a variable from a workflow needs a PAT or a GitHub App with "Variables: write". (docs: *Variables reference -> Limits for configuration variables*; *Workflow syntax -> permissions*.)
- UUIDv7 ids (recommended in #121) minted today start `01a0...`: the first 2 hex chars are the top 8 bits of the 48-bit ms timestamp and change every 2^40 ms, about **34.8 years**; the 3rd char changes every ~795 days, the 4th every ~50 days.

## Evaluating the proposed layout

`seeds/v1/id/<first 2 char>/<seed>` + symlink `seeds/yyyy/mm/dd/<seed>`

| Point | Finding |
| --- | --- |
| 2-char shard | With v7, **every seed for the next ~35 years lands in `id/01/`**. Sharding by the first 2 chars only works for random ids (v4) or a hash. To shard a v7 store, use the random tail or a hash -- or shard by date (next row). |
| Date tree | With v7 the date is *derivable from the id* (the first 48 bits are the ms timestamp), so a second index is redundant: one tree sharded by date is both the browsable view and the id lookup (`ls seeds/v1/*/*/<id>*` or compute the path from the id). |
| Symlinks | Git stores symlinks, but a Windows checkout without `core.symlinks=true` (the default for non-admin users) materialises them as small text files containing the target path. Windows is on #97's environment wish-list. Avoid symlinks. |
| `v1` | Good idea; make it the **layout/format** version. Generator versions differ per generator and belong *inside* the record (#124), not in the path. |
| "nothing in there or compact json" | Compact JSON. An empty file loses the commit/run/result association once CI logs expire (90 days), and that association is the point of keeping the seed. |
| "avoiding conflicts is important" | One file per seed gives zero merge conflicts: two adds never touch the same path. This is the strongest property of the user's idea -- keep it. |

## Proposed layout (recommended)

```
pkgs/mcpx/testdata/seeds/v1/<yyyy>/<mm>/<seed-id>.json
```

```json
{"seed":"01a0f101-2378-7c1c-9dc1-5a1ae1571eca","commit":"d0b7e01...","ref":"refs/heads/main","event":"push","run":"https://github.com/dezren39/nix/actions/runs/36673523537","attempt":1,"result":"success","derivation":"v1","generators":"sha256:<manifest>","date":"2026-09-30"}
```

- `testdata/` is ignored by Go package discovery; the notes' `tests/seeds/` also works (no `.go` files there). Open question.
- Month directories hold at most a few thousand files at plausible run rates (tens of runs a day), fine for git and GitHub's UI. No sharding by id needed.
- `generators` is a hash of the `name@version` manifest at that commit (#124), so a replay tool can tell whether today's generators still produce that seed's inputs.
- A tiny `seeds/v1/README.md` documents the schema. A guard test validates every record (parses, id matches filename, date matches the v7 timestamp).

## Which seeds are kept

- **main-branch push runs** and the **run that validated a PR's merge** (per the notes). For a PR, "merge seed" = the last completed run on the PR head before merge (or the merge-queue run, if #95 adopts a merge queue).
- **Every failing seed**, from any branch (a failing seed is a regression candidate even if the PR never merged; the record's commit says which code it failed on).
- Not: passing runs of unmerged PR branches, local runs (#121: local seeds go to a gitignored file).

## Approaches (collector)

### A -- append each seed to a GitHub repository variable (least recommended)
The notes flag the race correctly and it is fatal: the variables REST API is read-modify-write with no compare-and-swap, so two concurrent runs each read the list and the later write drops the earlier seed -- silently. It also needs a PAT/App (the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write variables), which is a long-lived secret to manage; one variable holds ~1,300 ids before its 48 KB cap; and the seeds still have to be moved into git later, so it is a second store, not a replacement for one. The only thing it buys is avoiding artifacts, which are free.

### B -- derive the seed from the run (`H(repo, run_id, run_attempt)`), store nothing
Not static (differs per run), zero storage, zero collector: the Actions run list *is* the index. Honest evaluation: `run_id` is sequential and predictable, and carries ~34 bits of variation -- enough to be distinct, but the derived key is then only as unpredictable as the run id (irrelevant for tests, nobody is attacking the seed). The real costs: the commit/result association disappears with the logs after 90 days, so cross-commit replay of old seeds is impossible after that; local runs have no run id so they need the minting path anyway (two mechanisms); and "Re-run all jobs" gets a new attempt number, so the seed changes on re-run while the id looks the same. Viable as a stopgap before any store exists; not as the design.

### C -- init job uploads a seed artifact; a scheduled collector writes one file per seed (recommended)
1. The `seed` init job (#121 section 7) uploads `seed.json` as artifact `test-seed` on every run.
2. A separate `seed-collector` workflow runs on `schedule` (weekly, well inside the 90-day retention), on `release: published`, and on `workflow_dispatch`. "Every 100 commits" has no native trigger; the collector can simply run weekly and be a no-op when nothing is new -- that covers it.
3. It lists completed runs of the test workflow (`gh run list --workflow <test> --json databaseId,headSha,headBranch,event,conclusion`), keeps the ones in "Which seeds are kept", downloads each `test-seed` artifact, fills `result` from the run conclusion, and writes `seeds/v1/<yyyy>/<mm>/<id>.json`.
4. It opens (or updates) **one** PR `bot/seeds` with all new files, or commits straight to main -- repo policy (#99). Idempotent: an existing file is skipped, so re-running the collector or overlapping windows never duplicates or conflicts.
5. Needs `actions: read` and `contents: write` (+ `pull-requests: write` for the PR form) -- all available to `GITHUB_TOKEN`, no PAT. Caveat: a PR opened with `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger other workflows, which is fine for a data-only PR (or #95 may path-filter `testdata/seeds/**` out of the test workflow anyway).
6. The collector's own commit must not start a test run. The proposed path is inside `mcpx.yml`'s `push.paths` (`pkgs/mcpx/**`, `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:22-25`, unchanged at 05c78b2), so each collector push to `main` would run the whole workflow and mint another seed to collect. Add `!pkgs/mcpx/testdata/seeds/**` to that list and `[skip ci]` to the commit message; the addendum comment below has the detail.

Why C: no race (each run writes its own artifact; the collector is the only writer to git), no secrets, no churn (one PR per week, not one commit per run), conflict-free by construction (file per seed), and records survive log expiry.

## Open questions

- Directory: `pkgs/mcpx/testdata/seeds/` (proposed) vs `pkgs/mcpx/tests/seeds/` (notes) vs a repo-root `tests/seeds/`. The repo-root option sits outside `pkgs/mcpx/**`, so it cannot trigger the test workflow at all (see the addendum).
- Collector cadence: weekly + release + dispatch (proposed) vs daily.
- Collector output: one PR per batch (proposed) vs direct commit to main.
- Do PR-merge seeds come from the last PR-head run, or does #95 adopt a merge queue whose run is unambiguous?
- Pruning: keep everything, or thin passing main-branch seeds older than N months (failing ones forever)?
- Does anything *read* the store automatically -- e.g. a nightly job that replays the last K failing seeds against main (#124), or is it an archive for humans first?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (collector workflow ~80 lines + record schema + guard test) · **Impact** med (reproduction works without it via logs for 90 days; the store is what makes old seeds and failing seeds durable)
**Depends on / related:** #121 (minting, artifact), #124 (generator manifest in the record, replay of failing seeds), #125; #95 (workflow layout, path filters, merge queue), #99 (bot-commit vs PR policy), #97 (Windows checkout / symlinks).

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#235 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

## What fails

`TestCaptureFramesIsAvailableToScripts` (internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:1597) fails on origin/main at `ecdce32` — verified on a pristine worktree with my changes stashed away, so this is **not** caused by PR #221.

## Repro

```sh
git checkout ecdce32   # origin/main
cd pkgs/mcpx
go test -run TestCaptureFramesIsAvailableToScripts ./internal/e2e/
# --- FAIL: TestCaptureFramesIsAvailableToScripts (0.31s)
#     e2e_test.go:1604: captureFrames should be a global and name the caller:
#         {"n":1}
```

Minimal CLI repro (no test harness):

```sh
go run ./cmd/mcpx exec --format bare 'function a() { return captureFrames(0, 4); } const f = a(); console.log(JSON.stringify({ n: f.length, top: f[0]?.function }));'
# {"n":1}
```

The test expects `top: "a"`. Instead the runtime returns a single frame with no `function` name at all.

## Notes

- The touched package for my open PR (`internal/config`) is fully green; this failure lives in `internal/codegen/emit.go`'s `captureFrames` (the `Error.captureStackTrace(holder, captureFrames)` path, lines ~654–686).
- Environment here: Deno 2.9.5 (V8 15.0.245.2-rusty) resolved via PATH. Is CI pinned to an older Deno? If CI is green, this smells like a Deno/V8 behavior change in how `captureStackTrace` handles the `constructorOpt` argument, and the fix may be a Deno version pin or a runtime fallback — I can dig further if useful.

## Acceptance criteria

- `TestCaptureFramesIsAvailableToScripts` passes on current main with the Deno version CI uses (currently Deno 2.9.5 / V8 15.0 per the report), or CI is pinned to a Deno version where it passes and the pin is recorded.
- The minimal CLI repro in the issue body returns the caller frame: `{"n":4, "top":"a"}` shape — at minimum `top` names the caller (`a`) instead of a single unnamed frame.
- No other e2e tests in internal/e2e regress.

title: mcpx docs: build the site in CI and deploy to GitHub Pages
body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#118 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #90

## Summary

Build the docs site in CI and publish it to GitHub Pages: pull requests build only, and pushes to `main` deploy. The build has to produce the `mcpx` binary first, because the reference pages are generated from it. The real decision is where the built site is published, because `dezren39/nix` is the whole nix-config monorepo and GitHub allows one Pages site per repository.

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - github static setup. separately, assign a subdomain

("separately, assign a subdomain" is #119.)

## Current state

- `dezren39/nix` is public and has no Pages site: `gh api repos/dezren39/nix/pages` returns 404.
- The user site `dezren39/dezren39.github.io` is published from a branch (`build_type: legacy`, `master` `/`) with custom domain `www.drewrypope.com` and HTTPS enforced. So a project site from `dezren39/nix` would appear at `https://www.drewrypope.com/nix/` unless it gets its own custom domain (#119).
- `github.com/dezren39/mcpx` is the Go module path, but that repository does not exist (`gh api repos/dezren39/mcpx` returns 404).
- CI:
  - `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml` runs on PRs touching `pkgs/mcpx/**`, `flake.nix`, `flake.lock` or itself, and on pushes to `main` touching `pkgs/mcpx/**`.
  - It installs Nix (`DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action`), Go, Deno, Bun and Node, runs `go test ./...`, and repairs `vendorHash` on bot branches.
  - Its permissions are `contents: write`, `pull-requests: read`.
  - The only other workflow is `opencode.yml`.
- `package.nix` postInstall already runs the built binary (`$out/bin/mcpx man`, `mcpx completion ...`). A docs derivation can do the same with `mcpx` as a build input.

## What the build must do (any approach)

1. **Build `mcpx`**, then run it to emit the generated reference pages (#144 / #145): settings, commands, OpenAPI, tool types. The docs can then never describe a binary other than the one built from the same commit.
2. **Run the generator** chosen in #117, plus the history renderer (#151) and the agent twin (#120).
3. **Bake in the base URL.** The site root is `/` with a custom domain and `/nix/` without one. Take it as a derivation argument so a local build and a CI build differ only in that value.

**Nix or setup-\* actions.** Recommended: `nix build .#mcpx-docs`, a flake output that depends on `.#mcpx`. It is the same build locally and in CI, it is covered by #49's "build every output" job for free, and the generator version is pinned by `flake.lock`. The alternative is `setup-go` plus a generator action. That is faster on a cold runner but drifts from the local build, and it duplicates the pinning. Mitigate Nix's cold-start cost with a Nix store cache (cachix, or the Actions cache via `nix-community/cache-nix-action`), as #49 proposes for all packages.

**Triggers and path filters.**
- Deploy on push to `main` touching `pkgs/mcpx/**`, `flake.lock` (a generator or nixpkgs bump) or the workflow file.
- On PRs with the same paths: build only, upload the site as an ordinary artifact, and run the docs checks.
- Also run on `workflow_dispatch`, for redeploys.
- Use a `concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }` group so two deploys cannot interleave.

**A separate workflow file** (`mcpx-docs.yml`) rather than a job in `mcpx.yml`. A Pages deploy needs `pages: write` and `id-token: write` plus the `github-pages` environment. `mcpx.yml` needs `contents: write` to push hash fixes. Keeping the two apart keeps each job's token minimal.

**PR previews.** GitHub Pages has no native PR previews. The options, cheapest first:
1. **None.** Reviewers download the PR's build artifact and open it locally, e.g. with `nix run .#mcpx-docs-serve`, a tiny static server. Recommended to start with.
2. **`rossjrw/pr-preview-action`** or `koizuka/pr-preview-action`. These only work when Pages is deployed **from a branch**, so they are incompatible with Approach C below.
3. **A separate preview repository** (e.g. `EndBug/pages-preview`) with its own Pages site. It needs a PAT, and the previews live at a different base URL.
4. **An external host with previews** (Cloudflare Pages, Netlify). That adds a service and an account.

Docs checks (links, generated pages current, agent twin in sync) run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97).

## Approaches: where the built site is published

### Approach A (least recommended): a `gh-pages` branch in `dezren39/nix`, pushed by CI

This is the classic setup, and the one most PR-preview actions assume.

Why not:
- It commits generated HTML into the config monorepo on every docs change, so the branch grows forever and the history fills with bot commits.
- The workflow needs `contents: write` on this repository in order to push.
- It is GitHub's "legacy" publishing mode.
- The only thing it buys is option 2 of the PR previews above. That is not worth a permanently growing branch in a repository whose clones every machine pulls.

### Approach B (middle): push the built site to a separate repository

For example `dezren39/mcpx-docs`, with its own Pages site and custom domain.

- It keeps generated output out of the monorepo, allows several docs sites (one per package) without the one-site-per-repo limit, and a separate preview repository becomes natural.
- Costs: a PAT or deploy key stored as a secret in `dezren39/nix`, a second repository to keep alive, and a history of generated commits there instead.
- **Do not use `dezren39/mcpx` for this.** That name is the Go module path. If mcpx ever gets its own repository (so that `go install github.com/dezren39/mcpx/cmd/mcpx@latest` works), that repository must hold the code. If the code moves there, its docs should move with it and Approach C applies in that repository.

### Approach C (recommended): the Actions artifact deploy from `dezren39/nix`, with its own custom domain

- Set the Pages source to "GitHub Actions" (`gh api repos/dezren39/nix/pages -X POST -f build_type=workflow`).
- The workflow builds `.#mcpx-docs`, then runs `actions/upload-pages-artifact` followed by `actions/deploy-pages` in the `github-pages` environment.
- No generated file is ever committed anywhere, and no extra repository or secret is needed.
- It is GitHub's current recommended mode. It also means a `CNAME` file is ignored and not needed: the custom domain is a repository setting ([GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/managing-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site)). See #119.
- The `github-pages` environment's default protection only allows deploys from the default branch, which is what we want.

Limits:
- One site per repository. If other flake packages later want docs, they share this site under subpaths, which is the open question in #117.
- No branch-based PR previews (options 1, 3 and 4 still work).

## Open questions

1. One site for the whole monorepo with mcpx at the root, or an mcpx-only site? This decides whether a second package's docs would push towards Approach B.
2. Deploy on every `main` push touching mcpx, or only on release tags once #158 exists? The install page must not document a channel before it is live, so release-gated deploys (or at least release-gated install instructions) may be needed.
3. Is the Nix cold-start time acceptable for a docs deploy? Measure with `gh run view --log` on the first runs, and compare with `mcpx.yml` timings.
4. Should the docs build be required on `main` together with the mcpx build (#49 proposes making the mcpx check required)?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (workflow + flake output; most of the effort is the flake output that runs `mcpx` to generate pages) · **Impact** high (nothing is public without it) · **Depends on / related**: #117 (generator), #119 (domain), #120, #144, #145, #151, #158, #49

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

title: mcpx docs: choose the site generator (mdBook, MkDocs Material, Docusaurus, Starlight, Hugo)
body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#117 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #90

## Summary

Pick the static site generator for the mcpx docs. The notes ask for "the most common and simple modern choice" and point at "that thing all the rust/k8s people use". That hint is ambiguous: the Rust book and most Rust project docs are **mdBook**, while kubernetes.io is **Hugo + Docsy**. This issue compares five candidates against the requirements the other docs issues place on the generator, and recommends one. The decision is small but everything else in the docs theme builds on it, so it goes first.

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - that thing all the rust/k8s people use is fine

## Current state

- No site, no generator config, no docs build. The docs are plain markdown under `pkgs/mcpx/docs/` (story.md, configuration.md, protocol.md, ...) plus `AGENTS.md` and `plugin/opencode/README.md`. They render on GitHub and nowhere else.
- Some reference output is already generated from single sources: `mcpx man` (roff, written by `package.nix` postInstall), `mcpx config --schema`, `mcpx schema --format ...`, `GET /v1/openapi.json`. The settings table in `docs/configuration.md` is hand-regenerated and guarded by `internal/settings/docs_test.go`. See #144.
- CI: `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml` installs Nix and builds `.#packages.x86_64-linux.mcpx`; #49 generalises builds to every flake output. A docs site should be a flake output too (`nix build .#mcpx-docs`), so it is checked the same way.

## Requirements the generator must serve

These come from sibling issues. Everything here is also possible by hand; the question is how much custom code each generator needs.

- **(a) Hierarchical, collapsible version history** (#150). Raw `<details>`/`<summary>` passes through all five generators. The part that needs code is the "bubbling": computing a parent entry's latest release from its nested children and rendering it collapsed. That needs a preprocessor, hook or component.
- **(b) Generated reference pages** (#144): settings table, CLI help and man page, OpenAPI, tool types. They are produced by the `mcpx` binary at build time and dropped in as markdown files, or included into pages.
- **(c) An agent-markdown twin of every page** (#120): `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, a raw `.md` next to every `.html`.
- **(d) A marketing-style home page** (#155): video, copy buttons, a random rotating prompt.
- **(e) The basics**: search, dark mode, mermaid/diagrams, link checking. Versioned doc sets (v1/, v2/ copies of the whole site) are probably not needed, because #150 puts version history inside the pages. Open question below.

## Comparison

Versions were checked on 2026-09-30 against the nixpkgs pinned by this flake (`nix eval --inputs-from . nixpkgs#<pkg>.version`) and npm/PyPI.

| | **mdBook** | **Hugo + Hextra** (or Docsy) | **MkDocs Material** | **Docusaurus** | **Starlight (Astro)** |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who uses it | Rust book, most Rust projects | kubernetes.io (Docsy), many Go projects | many CNCF / Python projects | Meta and many JS projects | Astro, a growing number of JS/TS projects |
| Runtime | one Rust binary | one Go binary (Hugo extended). Hextra needs no Node. **Docsy needs Node** (PostCSS) | Python + plugins | Node + React, large `node_modules` | Node + Astro |
| Latest / in nixpkgs | 0.5.4 / `mdbook` 0.5.4 | Hugo 0.166.0 / `hugo` 0.166.0. The theme comes in as a Hugo module or a flake input | mkdocs 1.6.1, **unreleased since 2024-08-30**; material 9.7.7 in nixpkgs | 3.10.2 / not packaged | starlight 0.42.4 on astro 7.3.5 / not packaged |
| Maintenance | active. 0.5.0 was a breaking release for preprocessors and renderers ([release notes](https://github.com/rust-lang/mdBook/releases/tag/v0.5.0)). nixpkgs dropped `mdbook-linkcheck` for incompatibility with 0.5 (replaced by `mdbook-linkcheck2`) | active, frequent releases | **Maintenance mode since Nov 2025**: critical fixes only, EOL extended to 2027-05-05 ([announcement](https://squidfunk.github.io/mkdocs-material/blog/2025/11/05/zensical/), [#8523](https://github.com/squidfunk/mkdocs-material/issues/8523)). Its successor **Zensical** is at 0.0.66, pre-1.0, and does not yet support the MkDocs plugin ecosystem | active | active, but pre-1.0: the 0.x minors break things |
| Nix build (`.#mcpx-docs`, #49) | trivial: `runCommand` with `mdbook build` | trivial if the theme is vendored (flake input or `hugo mod vendor`). Hugo modules fetch over the network, which a sandboxed build cannot do | `python3.withPackages`, fine for packaged plugins. Unpackaged ones (e.g. `mkdocs-llmstxt`, not in nixpkgs) need packaging | `buildNpmPackage` + `npmDepsHash`. Every dependency bump needs a hash repair (the #49 generalisation) | same as Docusaurus |
| (a) history bubbling | **preprocessor**: any executable that reads `[context, book]` JSON on stdin and writes the book to stdout ([docs](https://rust-lang.github.io/mdBook/for_developers/preprocessors.html)). It can be written in Go, in this repo | render hooks / shortcodes in Go templates. Tree logic in templates is awkward, so a pre-build step is likely anyway | hooks (Python) or `mkdocs-macros` | MDX + React component, or a remark plugin | remark/rehype plugin or an Astro component |
| (b) generated reference | `{{#include file.md:anchor}}` of files written before the build | files in `content/`, or data files + templates | include-markdown / snippets | MDX imports, or files dropped in | files dropped in, or content collections |
| (c) agent twin | none built in. Options: third-party renderers (`mdbook-llms-txt-tools`, not in nixpkgs), or a preprocessor that writes `.md` + `llms.txt`, as Fluree did ([fluree/db#1340](https://github.com/fluree/db/pull/1340)) | **native**: Hugo has a built-in `markdown` output format (`text/markdown`, [docs](https://gohugo.io/configuration/output-formats/)). `.md` per page and `llms.txt` via one template each | `mkdocs-llmstxt` 0.5.0 (not under Zensical) | `docusaurus-plugin-llms` 0.6.0 (community) | `starlight-llms-txt` 0.12.0 (llms.txt, -full, -small) |
| (d) marketing home | **weakest**: needs a custom theme or a hand-written `index.html` outside the book | good: Hextra ships a landing layout (hero, feature grid). Any custom layout is possible | custom `home.html` override | best: arbitrary React pages | good: `template: splash` + hero, and custom Astro components |
| (e) search | built in (client-side) | Hextra: FlexSearch built in | built in | Algolia, or local plugins | Pagefind built in |
| (e) dark mode | built-in themes | yes | yes | yes | yes |
| (e) mermaid | `mdbook-mermaid` (nixpkgs 0.17.1) | Hextra: built in | built in | `@docusaurus/theme-mermaid` | plugin |
| (e) versioned doc sets | no | manual | `mike` | **native, best in class** | plugin (`starlight-versions`) |
| (e) link check | `mdbook-linkcheck2` (nixpkgs 0.13.0), or `lychee` (nixpkgs 0.24.2) on the output | `lychee` on the output | built-in warnings plus `lychee` | built-in broken-link check at build time | `starlight-links-validator` |
| Authoring complexity | lowest: `book.toml` + `SUMMARY.md` | highest: Go templates, lookup order, modules | low | medium: React/MDX | medium: Astro/MDX |

`lychee` works on the built HTML of any generator, so link checking does not decide anything. Docs checks run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97).

## Approaches

### Approach A (least recommended): a Node generator, Starlight or Docusaurus

This covers the most requirements out of the box: a splash home page, llms.txt plugins, Pagefind or Algolia search, and native versioning in Docusaurus.

Why not:
- It adds a Node toolchain and a lockfile to a repository whose product is a Go binary.
- Every npm bump changes `npmDepsHash`. #49 already has to automate that for the packages that need it, and this would add one more.
- Starlight is pre-1.0 and follows Astro majors: `starlight-llms-txt` dropped Astro 6 to support Astro 7 ([PR #127](https://github.com/delucis/starlight-llms-txt/pull/127)). Expect that churn to repeat.
- None of this is "simple" in the sense the notes ask for.

MkDocs Material is excluded outright rather than listed as an approach. It is in maintenance mode with an announced end of life, MkDocs 1.x itself has had no release since August 2024, and the successor is pre-1.0 without plugin support. Starting a new site on it in 2026 would mean migrating it within a year.

### Approach B (middle): Hugo + Hextra

One Go binary in nixpkgs that covers all five requirements natively. It has a built-in `markdown` output format for the agent twin, templates for `llms.txt`, a landing-page layout for the home page, built-in search and mermaid, and render hooks and shortcodes for the history.

This is the "k8s" reading of the hint, though kubernetes.io uses Docsy, not Hextra. Docsy pulls in Node for PostCSS, so it loses the single-binary advantage. Pick Hextra or another Node-free theme.

Costs:
- Go templates are the hardest authoring model of the five. The tree logic in #150 fits a template badly, so it would probably become a pre-build step anyway.
- The theme has to be vendored for a sandboxed Nix build.
- "Book" is not Hugo's native shape: navigation comes from the section structure and weights, not from one `SUMMARY.md`.

Choose B over C if the home page and site chrome become a larger share of the work than the book itself.

### Approach C (recommended): mdBook for the book, a hand-built static home page, and generator-independent build steps

- **mdBook** renders the book: the level-1 and level-2 pages, the reference and the compendium. It is literally "a book", it is the "rust" reading of the hint, it is the simplest configuration of the five, and it is a single binary already in nixpkgs.
- **The home page is one hand-written `index.html`** plus a little JS: the video, copy buttons and a random rotating prompt (#155). mdBook is weakest here, and a hybrid avoids fighting its theme. One static page is fully under our control, and its bot twin is a plain `index.md` (#120).
- **Everything clever is a Go program in this repo**, run as an mdBook preprocessor over stdin/stdout or as a step before or after the build:
  - the history bubbling (#151);
  - the `.md` twin and `llms.txt` / `llms-full.txt` (#120);
  - the reference emitters, which are `mcpx` itself (#145).

  None of that code depends on mdBook's internals beyond the JSON book format, so switching to Hugo later means rewriting only the glue.
- The whole site is one flake output, `nix build .#mcpx-docs`, depending on `.#mcpx` for the generated pages (#118, #49).

Risks:
- mdBook 0.5 already broke third-party preprocessors once. We depend only on the JSON protocol, and the flake lock pins the version, so an upgrade is a deliberate bump that CI checks.
- There are no versioned doc sets. #150 makes that unnecessary, but see the open questions.
- Search covers the book, not the home page. That is acceptable for a one-page home.

Why C over B: the notes ask for simple, and a book. mdBook gives both, and the requirements it lacks natively (the twin, the home page, the history) need custom code in every generator, B included. Keeping that code in Go, next to the binary it documents, is the smaller long-term cost.

**Decision to make now: C.** Of the open questions below, only a "yes" to 3 (whole-site versioned doc sets) would reopen it, in favour of Docusaurus. Questions 1, 2 and 4 are answered after the pick and do not change it (1 and 2 follow #158's repository decision). #118's flake output and deploy, #120's twin emitter, #151's preprocessor hook and #155's home page all assume the answer, so this goes first. If there is doubt, the spike in the footer settles it in hours.

## Open questions

1. Does the site live in this monorepo (`pkgs/mcpx/docs-site/` or similar) or move with mcpx if it ever gets its own repo (`github.com/dezren39/mcpx` is already the Go module path)? See #118.
2. One generator and one site for every flake package's docs, or mcpx only? One Pages site per repo (#118) pushes towards "one site, mcpx first".
3. Are versioned doc sets (a whole site per release) ever wanted, or does in-page history (#150) replace them? If they are wanted, Docusaurus's advantage matters and C would need a `v<version>/` directory scheme.
4. Does the home page need to share the book's CSS and theme, or can it look deliberately different?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S (decision; a spike building three existing pages in mdBook and Hugo would take hours) · **Impact** high (every docs issue builds on it) · **Depends on / related**: #49, #118, #120, #155, #144, #145, #150, #151

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

Relocated from dezren39/nix#217 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

The plugin's `instructions` option pushes onto `output.parts`, but opencode v1 calls `experimental.chat.system.transform` with `{system: string[]}`. Nothing is injected, silently, on every turn.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [PLG-16](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/plugin-apis.md#plg-16-experimentalchatsystemtransform-output-is-system-string) | `experimental.chat.system.transform` output is `{system: string[]}` | ✗ broken — writes `output.parts`; never injected | S |

## Evidence

`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:745-746`; `v1:packages/opencode/src/session/llm/request.ts:69-73` (opencode 1.18.31).

## What to do

`output.system.push(text)`, and a test that runs the hook against v1's call shape.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S · **Impact** low · **Related**: #189, #47

## Acceptance criteria

- The plugin's `instructions` option actually reaches the system prompt on opencode v1: the hook writes to `output.system` (a `string[]`), not `output.parts`.
- A regression test runs the hook against opencode v1's actual call shape (`experimental.chat.system.transform` with `{system: string[]}`).
- Setting the option with no instructions configured remains a no-op (no empty injection).

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#211 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

A host that reaches mcpx over MCP is keyed as `mcp-<pid>` of the serving process. Over the daemon's `/mcp` that pid is the daemon's, so every HTTP host shares one session scope and one browser. The comment says a host has "no way to tell us" its session. opencode v2 does tell: every `tools/call`, including calls from inside its code mode, carries `_meta["ai.opencode/sessionID"]`. 2026-07-28 also forbids treating connection or process identity as session continuity. Reading the key from the request would give each opencode session its own stateful servers without the `shell.env` plugin hook, which v2 no longer provides.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [META-09](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/meta.md#meta-09-aiopencodesessionid-on-every-opencode-v2-toolscall) | `ai.opencode/sessionID` on every opencode v2 `tools/call` | ✗ — ignored; every host shares one scope | M |
| [PM-10](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/process-model.md#pm-10-every-http-mcp-host-shares-one-pool-session-key) | Every HTTP MCP host shares one pool session key | ✗ — key is the daemon's pid | S |

## Evidence

- `internal/cli/serve.go:287-297` (`mcpSession`), `internal/cli/serve_ask.go:31-37`.
- `v2:packages/core/src/mcp/client.ts:278` (opencode v2 2.0.3).
- `2026-07-28/basic/index.mdx:204-208`.

## What to do

Take the scope key from a configured list of `_meta` keys (default `ai.opencode/sessionID`), falling back to today's behaviour; thread it through `Backend.Call`/`Exec`. A setting, not a hard-coded key.

Parent: #177

## Summary

mcpx advertises `extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks"]` to 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 hosts, plus the core `tasks` capability to both. It implements only the 2025-11-25 core shape, and the two are not wire-compatible (SEP-2663). A 2026 host gets `{task}` stamped `resultType: "complete"` instead of a flat `Task` with `resultType: "task"`. It also gets `ttl`/`pollInterval` instead of `ttlMs`/`pollIntervalMs`, no `tasks/update`, `tasks/list` and `tasks/result` the extension removed, and no inline result in `tasks/get`. `tasks.requests.tools.call` is declared though no tool allows task execution. Tasks are served to clients that did not declare support, listed across every connection (wire W23), never carry `related-task`, and live in two stores (MCP and `/v1`) whose comment says they are one. `tasks/cancel` on a finished task returns the task rather than `-32602`. As a client, mcpx never task-augments, so an upstream tool with `taskSupport: "required"` cannot be called.

- Wire W22 (2025-11-25 shape to a 2026 client), W23 (another client's task listed).
- `seps/2663-tasks-extension.md:944` ("not wire-compatible"), `:949`.

## What to do

- Stop advertising what is not built: no `extensions` to 2025-11-25, no core `tasks` to 2026, no `tasks.requests.tools.call` without task-capable tools.
- Implement the extension for 2026 peers (flat `Task`, `resultType: "task"`, `ttlMs`, `pollIntervalMs`, `DetailedTask`, `tasks/update`, ack-only cancel), dispatching on revision.
- Bind tasks to their requestor; one store for MCP and `/v1`; reject cancel of a terminal task; attach `related-task` on 2025-11-25.
- Client: parse `execution.taskSupport` and task-augment calls that require it.

**Ease** L · **Impact** med · **Related**: #177, #77 (task status); `docs/compare/conflicts.md` C-07, C-61

## Acceptance criteria

- 2026 hosts get the wire-correct tasks shape: flat `Task` with `resultType: "task"`, `ttlMs`/`pollIntervalMs`, `tasks/update` present, methods the extension removed are gone, and `tasks/get` carries the inline result (SEP-2663).

- MCP and `/v1` tasks live in one store (the two-store split and its false comment are gone). Cross-repo: the durable-store slice is also tracked as developing-today/code#1575 — handle as one set per the fleet cross-repo rule, do not duplicate.
- `tasks/cancel` on a finished task returns `-32602`.
- As a client, mcpx task-augments calls, so an upstream tool with `taskSupport: "required"` can be called.
- `tasks.requests.tools.call` is declared only when some tool actually allows task execution.
- Conformance tests pin the 2025-11-25 and 2026 shapes separately.

## Summary

`docs/protocol.md` §6 says OAuth for remote servers is "declared and not performed". The gap is wider: the whole per-server `auth` block (bearer, basic, header, query, env) is never applied. `mcpauth.Auth.Resolve` has no caller, so a remote server configured with `auth:` is reached without credentials, and only plain `headers:` works. `Describe`, documented as used by `mcpx config` and `mcpx doctor`, has no caller either.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [AUTH-22](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/auth.md#auth-22-per-server-auth-block-parsed-and-never-applied) | Per-server `auth:` block parsed and never applied | ✗ broken — `Auth.Resolve` has no caller | S |

## Evidence

- `internal/mcpauth/mcpauth.go:93` (`Resolve`), `:186-189` (`Describe`); the only reference to the package is the type at `internal/config/config.go:141`.
- Headers are applied at `internal/pool/pool.go:377-380`; `auth` is not.

## What to do

Apply `Resolve()` where headers are applied, fail with a clear message when a required credential is missing, and add the guard test #177 describes (every config field declared on a server has an observable effect).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S · **Impact** med · **Related**: #177, #172 (declared and unread)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The per-server `auth:` block is applied where `headers:` are applied: `mcpauth.Auth.Resolve` has a caller on the remote-server connect path, and bearer/basic/header/query/env credentials from the block reach the upstream request.
- [ ] A required credential that cannot be resolved fails with a clear message naming the server and the missing credential — never a silent unauthenticated connection.
- [ ] `Describe` is wired to its documented callers (`mcpx config` / `mcpx doctor`) or the documentation is corrected.
- [ ] The #177 guard test exists: every config field declared on a server has an observable effect, and it fails if `auth:` is dropped again.
- [ ] Existing `headers:`-only servers behave exactly as before; tests pass in CI.

Relocated from dezren39/nix#203 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Summary

Against legacy upstreams mcpx's client works on the happy path and is fragile off it. It accepts any version an `initialize` returns without checking it is one it speaks. It sends `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2025-11-25` regardless of what was negotiated, and never opens the GET stream, so unsolicited legacy messages are lost. It ignores SSE `retry` and never reconnects, and treats a session 404 as a plain error instead of re-initializing. It silently drops server requests whose id is a string, which JSON-RPC allows. Its HTTP timeout caps whole SSE responses at 10 minutes. It always cancels with reason "timeout", sends `notifications/cancelled` for a timed-out `initialize` (forbidden), and on 2026 HTTP both aborts and notifies. On stdio shutdown it sends SIGTERM immediately after closing stdin. It hides `prompts/list` errors and does not paginate `resources/templates/list`.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

| [TR-45](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/transports.md#tr-45-client-http-timeout-caps-whole-sse-responses) | Client HTTP timeout caps whole SSE responses | ✗ — 10 min cap cuts long streams | S |
| [PC-08](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/progress-cancellation.md#pc-08-cancellation-reason) | Cancellation `reason` | ✗ — client always says `"timeout"` | S |
| [PC-09](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/progress-cancellation.md#pc-09-initialize-must-not-be-cancelled) | `initialize` MUST NOT be cancelled | ✗ — a timed-out `initialize` gets a cancel | S |
| [PC-13](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/progress-cancellation.md#pc-13-client-notificationscancelled-stdio-only-in-2026) | Client `notifications/cancelled`: stdio only in 2026 | partial — aborts the POST and also sends the notification | S |
| [PG-07](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-07-mcpx-client-swallows-list-errors) | mcpx client swallows list errors and skips template pages | ✗ — `prompts/list` and templates errors hidden | S |

## Evidence

Each row's block in the register cites the lines; the main ones: `internal/mcpclient/http.go:81-85` (version header), `internal/mcpclient/client.go:709-716` (cancel reason), `internal/mcpclient/stdio.go` (shutdown and id decoding).

## What to do

One change per row; none needs design. Suggested order: string ids, the version check, and the session 404 re-initialize, because each can make a working server look dead. Then the header value, the SSE timeout and the rest.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** med · **Related**: #77 (cancellation), sibling issue for the 2026 client

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The client validates the version an `initialize` answer carries, sends the negotiated version in `MCP-Protocol-Version` (not a hard-coded one), and opens the GET stream so unsolicited legacy messages are received.
- [ ] SSE `retry` is honoured and the stream reconnects; a session 404 triggers re-initialization instead of surfacing as a plain error.
- [ ] Server requests with string ids are handled (JSON-RPC allows them); cancellation uses the real reason, no `notifications/cancelled` is sent for a timed-out `initialize`, and the HTTP timeout no longer caps whole SSE responses at 10 minutes.
- [ ] Stdio shutdown does not SIGTERM immediately after closing stdin; `prompts/list` errors are surfaced and `resources/templates/list` is paginated.
- [ ] Each register row in the issue is either fixed with a test or explicitly split out to a named follow-up issue; tests pass in CI.

Legacy clients hit rules mcpx breaks. `initialize` with a version mcpx does not speak (2024-11-05, a future date, or 2026-07-28) is refused with `-32022`, a 2026-only code; every legacy revision says the server MUST counter-offer a version it supports. mcpx lists 2025-03-26 as supported but rejects JSON-RPC batches, which that revision says servers MUST receive. | [PG-03](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-03-invalid-cursors) | invalid cursor SHOULD be `-32602` | ✗ — undecodable cursor silently restarts at zero | S |

## Evidence

- `internal/mcpserver/server.go:844-859` (`negotiate`), `:506-509`; wire W1/W4/S1.
- Batches: `internal/mcpserver/server.go:1041-1044`; wire W16, S3. `2025-03-26/basic/index.mdx:97`.
- Notification replies: `internal/mcpserver/server.go:766`; wire S5 (`notifications/roots/list_changed`, `notifications/progress` each answered `-32601`).
- Sessions: `internal/mcpserver/server.go:1208-1230`.

## In flight

PR #198 (open when this was filed) says it adds 2025-03-26 batches, never answering notifications, concurrent stdio requests, 404 for unknown sessions, and validation of the legacy `MCP-Protocol-Version` header: TR-09, SUB-18, TR-05, TR-28, TR-35, TR-36. Re-check those rows when it merges. The counter-offer, the error-code rows and the cursor are not in its description.

## What to do

- `negotiate`: counter-offer `Latest` for any well-formed legacy request mcpx does not speak; keep `-32022` for `_meta` requests. If 2024-11-05 is to be served, add its `floors` rows at the same time (audio, tool annotations, `completions`).
- Accept batches from 2025-03-26 peers (or stop listing 2025-03-26).
- Never answer a message without an `id`.
- Mint sessions only on a successful `initialize`; 404 an unknown session; validate the legacy header and use it as the version when present.
- `-32002` to legacy peers for resource-not-found, `-32603` for internal failures, pass upstream codes through, `-32602` for a bad cursor.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** med · **Related**: #77, sibling issue for 2026 serving; `docs/compare/conflicts.md` C-02, C-03, C-09

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `initialize` with an unsupported version (older legacy, future, or 2026-07-28) counter-offers a version mcpx supports, per the legacy revisions — it is not refused with the 2026-only `-32022`.
- [ ] JSON-RPC batches from 2025-03-26 clients are received and answered per that revision; unknown notifications get no error response.
- [ ] A refused `initialize` mints no session; an unknown session gets a 404 (not stateless service); `MCP-Protocol-Version` is validated and honoured.
- [ ] Error codes match the caller's era (resource-not-found is `-32002` for legacy), upstream error codes survive as codes (not only text), and an undecodable cursor errors instead of silently restarting at zero.
- [ ] Each register row in the issue is either fixed with a test or explicitly split out to a named follow-up issue; tests pass in CI.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#201 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

A conformant 2026-07-28 client has no `Mcp-Session-Id`, so mcpx cannot bind a `requestState` to it. `docs/protocol.md` §3.3 says such a question then stays with the broker. What happens instead: the ask loop `continue`s without waiting, counts a round per iteration, and after `proto.askRounds` (8) abandons the upstream call and answers `-32603 "tools/call was still asking for input after 8 rounds"`, in about 40 ms. With a session (taken from `server/discover`) it works, but the token binds call, session and expiry rather than the principal and the method/argument digest the specification recommends, and a state presented on a different call was not rejected. The final result of any call that asked is flattened to one text block, `elicitationId` leaks to 2026 hosts, and the "(via mcpx)" originator prefix is applied only on the legacy path.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [ELI-17](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/elicitation.md#eli-17-stateless-2026-host-plus-eliciting-upstream) | Stateless 2026 host plus eliciting upstream | ✗ — `-32603` after 8 busy rounds (wire M1) | M |
| [MRTR-08](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/mrtr.md#mrtr-08-requeststate-should-bind-the-authenticated-principal) | `requestState` SHOULD bind the authenticated principal | ✗ — bound to `Mcp-Session-Id`, which 2026 removed | M |
| [MRTR-10](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/mrtr.md#mrtr-10-requeststate-should-identify-method-and-parameters-digest) | `requestState` SHOULD identify method and parameters digest | ✗ — call id only; retry params ignored | S |
| [MRTR-19](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/mrtr.md#mrtr-19-results-returned-through-mrtr-keep-their-full-shape) | Results returned through MRTR keep their full shape | ✗ — flattened to one text block | M |
| [ELI-10](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/elicitation.md#eli-10-elicitationid-added-then-removed) | `elicitationId` added, then removed | partial — stripped for old hosts, leaked to 2026 hosts | S |
| [ELI-18](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/elicitation.md#eli-18-naming-the-originating-server-in-a-relayed-question) | Naming the originating server in a relayed question | partial — legacy prefixed "(via mcpx)"; 2026 path raw | S |

## Evidence

- Loop: `internal/mcpserver/ask.go:195-209` (`continue` at `:207` skips the wait at `:181-187`); `canAsk` is true for any modern peer regardless of binding (`internal/mcpserver/ask.go:75`).
- Binding: `internal/mcpserver/state.go:47-51` (`{c, b, e}`), `internal/mcpserver/ask.go:300-306`.
- Flattening: `internal/mcpserver/ask.go:268-296`.
- Wire: M1 (no session → `-32603`), M2–M3 (with session → works), M4 (retry without the header → "belongs to another session").
- Spec: `2026-07-28/basic/patterns/mrtr.mdx:232-243` (principal, TTL, method + params digest).

## What to do

- Bind `requestState` to the request: method, a digest of the arguments, the principal when there is one, and the expiry. Keep the HMAC. Stop depending on `Mcp-Session-Id` for modern peers.
- When no state can be minted, return the question to the broker and wait, as the comment says, instead of spinning; do not count a round that asked nothing.
- Render the final result in the method's full shape (content blocks, `structuredContent`, `isError`), not text.
- Strip 2025-11-25-only fields (`elicitationId`) for 2026 hosts and apply the originator prefix on both paths.
- A test that drives a sessionless 2026 client through an eliciting upstream and fails on today's behaviour.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** high · **Related**: #177, #77 (inline answers from scripts), sibling issue for 2026 serving; `docs/compare/input-required.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stateless 2026 host driving an eliciting upstream no longer busy-loops: the ask loop waits for the broker-held question (per `docs/protocol.md` §3.3) instead of burning `proto.askRounds` in ~40 ms and answering `-32603`.
- [ ] The request-state token binds the principal and the method/argument digest the specification recommends, and state presented on a different call is rejected.
- [ ] A call that asked returns its real final result (not one flattened text block), `elicitationId` does not leak to 2026 hosts, and the "(via mcpx)" originator prefix is consistent across legacy and modern paths.
- [ ] Tests cover the stateless-host elicitation path end-to-end; tests pass in CI.

Parent: #177

## Summary

Every modern-only upstream fails. mcpx probes legacy first; a modern-only server answers `initialize` with `-32022`, which the client treats as fatal instead of trying `server/discover`. If discovery is reached, it reads `protocolVersions` where the schema has `supportedVersions` (tracked with the server half in the sibling issue). Past that: no `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`/`Mcp-Param-*` headers (a conformant HTTP server answers 400), a session id echoed to modern servers, legacy-shaped capabilities in `_meta` (`roots.listChanged`, no `extensions`, no url elicitation), the removed `logging/setLevel` sent after connect, `""` treated as the end of a cursor, and no `subscriptions/listen` for list changes. `ttlMs` on upstream lists is ignored.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

| [TR-39](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/transports.md#tr-39-mirror-x-mcp-header-arguments-into-mcp-param-name) | Mirror `x-mcp-header` arguments into `Mcp-Param-{Name}` | ✗ — not implemented | M |
| [TOOL-09](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/tools.md#tool-09-x-mcp-header-parameter-annotation) | `x-mcp-header` on inputSchema properties; HTTP clients drop invalid tools | ✗ — neither validated nor mirrored | M |
| [CAP-03](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/capabilities.md#cap-03-client-rootslistchanged) | client `roots.listChanged` removed in 2026 | ✗ — `listChanged:false` sent to 2026 upstreams too | S |

| [CAP-11](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/capabilities.md#cap-11-client-extensions-map) | client `extensions` map | ✗ — never declared, so no upstream extension is reachable | S |
| [LOG-02](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/logging.md#log-02-per-request-_meta-iomodelcontextprotocolloglevel) | Per-request `_meta` `io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel` | ✗ — never sent upstream, never read from hosts | S |
| [LOG-07](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/logging.md#log-07-mcpx-client-sends-setlevel-info-to-every-logging-upstream) | mcpx client sends `setLevel info` to every logging upstream | ✗ — removed method sent to modern upstreams; level hard-coded | S |
| [PG-02](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-02-the-empty-string-cursor) | `""` is a valid cursor and MUST NOT end the list | ✗ — client stops paging on `""` | S |
| [PG-13](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-13-mcpxs-upstream-schema-cache-ignores-ttlms) | mcpx's upstream schema cache ignores `ttlMs` | ✗ — cached until list_changed or refresh, persisted to disk | S |
| [SUB-15](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/notifications.md#sub-15-client-subscribes-upstream-for-changes) | Client subscribes upstream for changes | ✗ — never listens, never subscribes upstream | M |

## Evidence

- `-32022` abort: `internal/mcpclient/client.go:244-248`; era detection by substring: `internal/mcpclient/client.go:329-331`.
- Client capabilities: `internal/mcpclient/modern.go:46-58` (`roots: {listChanged:false}`, bare `elicitation: {}`, no `extensions`).
- `setLevel` to every upstream: `internal/pool/pool.go:414-415`, `internal/daemon/hooks.go:29`.
- Cursor: `internal/mcpclient/client.go:744`.

## What to do

- Treat `-32022` (and any recognised modern error) from `initialize` as a modern server and retry with `server/discover`; the probe order itself is being changed by the protocol work.
- Send `Mcp-Method` on every POST, `Mcp-Name` for `tools/call`/`resources/read`/`prompts/get`, and mirror `x-mcp-header` arguments into `Mcp-Param-*`; drop tools whose `x-mcp-header` is invalid.
- Do not send a session id to a modern server. Build `_meta` capabilities in the 2026 shape (`roots: {}`, `elicitation: {form, url}`, `extensions` when implemented).
- Per-request `logLevel` instead of `logging/setLevel` for modern upstreams; decode `nextCursor` as a pointer; honour `ttlMs` in the schema cache; open `subscriptions/listen` for list changes.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** high · **Related**: #177, sibling issue for the server half (discover field names), #77

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A modern-only upstream is reachable: an `initialize` refusal (`-32022`) is treated as "try `server/discover`", not as fatal.
- [ ] Discovery reads the schema's `supportedVersions` field (with the server half tracked in the sibling issue #199), and modern requests carry the required `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` / `Mcp-Param-*` headers.
- [ ] No session id is echoed to modern servers; `_meta` capabilities are modern-shaped (`extensions`, url elicitation; no legacy `roots.listChanged` shape); the removed `logging/setLevel` is not sent after connect.
- [ ] Cursor handling treats only a genuinely absent cursor as the end, and `subscriptions/listen` is used for list changes; `ttlMs` on upstream lists is honoured.
- [ ] A conformance test against a modern-only fixture server passes in CI.
