body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#199 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

mcpx declares 2026-07-28 and answers it in a shape only mcpx's own client reads. `server/discover` returns `protocolVersions` and a top-level `serverInfo`; the schema says `supportedVersions`, puts identity in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`, and requires `ttlMs` and `cacheScope` on discover, list and read results. Modern requests missing required `_meta` are served rather than rejected, `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name` are never checked, a header mismatch gets a non-JSON-RPC 400, `-32022` reports `requested: ""`, and every modern error goes out as HTTP 200 where 2026 requires 400/404. `server/discover` also mints an `Mcp-Session-Id`, which 2026 does not define. The tests pin the wrong field name on both sides, which is how it passed CI.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [LV-22](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/lifecycle-versioning.md#lv-22-iomodelcontextprotocolserverinfo-in-every-results-_meta) | `io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo` in every result's `_meta` | ✗ — never emitted; client never reads it | S |
| [LV-23](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/lifecycle-versioning.md#lv-23-discoverresult-has-no-top-level-serverinfo) | `DiscoverResult` has no top-level `serverInfo` | ✗ — sends undefined field; client reads it there | S |
| [LV-24](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/lifecycle-versioning.md#lv-24-a-2026-request-missing-required-_meta-is-malformed) | A 2026 request missing required `_meta` is malformed | partial — no version ⇒ served as 2025-03-26; no caps ⇒ none | S |
| [LV-26](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/lifecycle-versioning.md#lv-26-discoverresultsupportedversions) | `DiscoverResult.supportedVersions` | ✗ — `protocolVersions` on both server and client | S |
| [PG-08](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-08-which-results-must-carry-cache-hints) | six results MUST carry cache hints; changelog names five | ✗ — none of the six carry them (wire W5, W6, W18, W19) | S |
| [PG-09](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-09-ttlms) | `ttlMs`: integer ms ≥ 0; absent means 0 | ✗ — never emitted | S |
| [PG-10](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/pagination-caching.md#pg-10-cachescope) | `cacheScope`: `"public"` or `"private"` | ✗ — never emitted | S |
| [ERR-07](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/errors.md#err-07--32020-headermismatch) | `-32020` HeaderMismatch | ✗ — plain-JSON 400 for one case; others unchecked | S |
| [ERR-09](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/errors.md#err-09--32022-unsupportedprotocolversion) | `-32022` UnsupportedProtocolVersion | partial — right shape; `requested` empty; HTTP 200 | S |
| [ERR-13](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/errors.md#err-13-http-status-for-modern-json-rpc-errors-400--404) | HTTP status for modern JSON-RPC errors (400 / 404) | ✗ — every error goes out as 200 | S |
| [TR-26](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/transports.md#tr-26-mcp-session-id-minted-on-serverdiscover) | `Mcp-Session-Id` minted on `server/discover` | ✗ — minted for every discover, modern or not | M |
| [TR-37](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/transports.md#tr-37-mcp-method-header-2026) | `Mcp-Method` header (2026) | ✗ — client never sends it; server never checks it | S |
| [TR-38](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/transports.md#tr-38-mcp-name-header-2026) | `Mcp-Name` header (2026) | ✗ — client never sends it; server never checks it | S |

## Evidence

- `internal/mcpserver/server.go:534-535` sends `protocolVersions` and `serverInfo`; `schema/2026-07-28/schema.ts:678-697` (`DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult`, `supportedVersions`).
- Tests pinning it: `internal/mcpserver/server_test.go:393`, `internal/mcpclient/era_test.go:87`, `internal/mcpclient/modern_test.go:88`.
- Session minted on discover: `internal/mcpserver/server.go:1214-1229`.
- Wire (binary built from `05c78b2`): `server/discover` → 200 with `Mcp-Session-Id` and `protocolVersions`; unknown method with 2026 `_meta` → HTTP 200 `-32601`; `_meta` version `9999-01-01` → HTTP 200, `-32022`, `"requested":""`.

## In flight

PR #198 (open when this was filed; PROTOCOL work) says it adds the server-side `Mcp-Method`/`Mcp-Name`/`MCP-Protocol-Version` checks with `-32020`, the 400/404 status mapping, and no legacy session for modern requests: ERR-07, ERR-13, TR-37/TR-38 (server half), and perhaps TR-26. Re-check those rows when it merges. The `server/discover` field names, `serverInfo` in `_meta`, cache hints and the missing-`_meta` rejection are not in its description.

## What to do

- `supportedVersions` on both server and client, fix the three tests, and add one that decodes a `DiscoverResult` fixture taken from the specification's own examples (`schema/2026-07-28/examples/DiscoverResult/` in the specification repository), so the field names are checked against the schema rather than against mcpx.
- `serverInfo` into result `_meta` for modern peers; `ttlMs` + `cacheScope` on discover, `tools/list`, `prompts/list`, `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list`, `resources/read` (values as settings).
- For modern requests: reject missing `protocolVersion`/`clientCapabilities` with `-32602`; check `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` against the body and answer `-32020` as a JSON-RPC error with HTTP 400; map `-32601` → 404 and `-32602`/`-32021`/`-32022` → 400; fill `requested`.
- Do not mint `Mcp-Session-Id` on `server/discover`. This depends on the `input_required` binding fix (sibling issue), which is the only thing that needs the session today.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** high · **Related**: #177 (the class: declared and not delivered), #77 (protocol follow-ups), sibling issues for the 2026 client and `input_required`; `docs/compare/stateless.md` §5 items 1 and 4

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `server/discover` returns the schema shape: `supportedVersions`, identity in `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`, and `ttlMs` + `cacheScope` on discover, list, and read results.
- [ ] Modern requests missing required `_meta` are rejected; `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` are checked and a header mismatch gets a JSON-RPC error (not a bare non-JSON-RPC 400); `-32022` reports the requested version.
- [ ] Modern errors use the 2026 HTTP status codes (400/404) instead of HTTP 200, and `server/discover` mints no `Mcp-Session-Id`.
- [ ] The tests that pinned the wrong field name on both sides are corrected to the schema, and a conformance test against the published 2026-07-28 schema passes in CI.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#193 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

`GET /v1/events` promises lossless reconnection: "Reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` ... or `?since=N` and everything
after N is replayed", and a reconnect older than the retained history "gets an in-band `gap` event"
(`docs/story.md:2203-2214`). A replay of more than **256** matching events keeps the oldest 256 and silently drops the
rest, with no `gap` event. The retained history is 1024 by default (`events.history`), so a `?since=0` against a busy
daemon can lose up to three quarters of what it asked for, and the client is told nothing.

Found by reading the code in the 2026-09-30 issues pass (worker "ext", confirmed by the architect). **Not yet
reproduced against a running daemon**; the first step is the reproduction.

## Current state (05c78b2)

`Bus.SubscribeFrom` (`internal/events/events.go:176-199`):

- makes the subscription channel with a buffer of 256 (`:177`);
- holds the bus lock for the whole replay (`:178-179`), and the subscription has not been returned yet, so nothing
  can drain the channel while the replay fills it;
- replays each retained event into the channel with a non-blocking send; when the buffer is full it increments
  `sub.Dropped` and moves on (`:190-194`);
- sets `gap` only when `since` predates the retained history (`:185-187`), never for drops.

`Dropped` has no reader outside `internal/events` (`:147`, `:193`, `:230`), and the daemon's handler
(`internal/daemon/server.go:826`) sees only `gap`. The same counter is raised for a slow *live* reader (`:230`), which
is the documented trade-off ("one slow reader cannot stall the daemon"); the replay case is different because it
happens before the reader has had any chance to read.

## Approaches

**A -- enlarge the buffer to `events.history`.** One line; replays of up to the whole history fit. Costs memory per
subscriber (1024 events each) and still loses silently if a live burst arrives before the reader drains; the promise
remains unguarded.

**B -- replay outside the lock, from a snapshot, with blocking sends.** Copy the matching history under the lock,
register the subscription, then feed the snapshot to the reader at its own pace before live events. Lossless for the
replay; live-burst loss still silent.

**C -- recommended: B, plus make every loss visible with the gap contract #6 owns.** When `Dropped` rises -- during
replay or live -- emit the in-band `gap {since, latest}` marker #6 defines (#181 collision 13), so a consumer always
knows it missed something and can resynchronise with `?since=`. Add the test that would have caught this: replay more
than the buffer and assert either every event or a `gap`. Recommended because "lossless" is a documented promise and
the only honest versions of it are "you got everything" or "you were told you did not".

## Open questions

- Should `/v1/events` report `Dropped` in its stream or only as the `gap` marker?
- Does the MCP notification path (`internal/pool/pool.go:411`) share the bus and the same failure?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S (A, B) / M (C, with #6's gap contract) · **Impact** med -- silent loss on the one path documented as
lossless; #81's hooks and #86's browser surface consume this stream.
Related: #177 (class), #6 (owns gap semantics, collision 13), #81 (hooks over the bus), #86 (browser reconnect,
`Last-Event-ID`), #87 (lifetime), #129 (guard mechanics).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Reproduction first: a replay through `Bus.SubscribeFrom` with more than 256 matching retained events demonstrates the silent drop on current code (the issue is code-read, not yet reproduced against a running daemon).
- [ ] After the fix, a replay larger than the channel buffer loses nothing silently: either all retained events after `since` are delivered, or the client receives an in-band `gap` event naming the loss — matching the `docs/story.md` reconnection promise.
- [ ] The `Dropped` counter has a reader that surfaces drops (gap event, metric, or log), including drops after the subscription is live.
- [ ] A `?since=0` replay against a full 1024-event history is covered by a test; tests pass in CI.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#190 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

`canonical()` (`internal/config/scope.go:188-201`) resolves symlinks but keeps the spelling it was
given. On a case-insensitive volume — APFS by default, and SMB/vfat mounts on Linux —
`/Users/x/Repo` and `/users/x/repo` are one directory and produce two scope keys, so one checkout
gets two server instances. The `cwd` scope has always behaved this way; the `repo` and `worktree`
scopes did not, because `git rev-parse` starts from `getcwd()`, which returns the on-disk
spelling. Replacing the git fork with native discovery removes that accidental protection, which
is how this was found.

The error is always **over-isolation** — a second process — never accidental sharing. That is the
safe direction, and it is why this is a design issue rather than a hotfix.

## Original notes

Not from the user's notes. Reported during the 2026-09-30 build-out by the GIT architect:

> Found while replacing the git fork in the `repo`/`worktree` scopes with native discovery (PR to follow from branch `git-native`).
>
> **What happens.** On a case-insensitive volume (APFS default, also SMB/vfat mounts on Linux) `/Users/x/Repo` and `/users/x/repo` are one directory. `canonical()` in `internal/config/scope.go` uses `filepath.EvalSymlinks`, which resolves symlinks but keeps the spelling it was given, so the two spellings produce two keys -- two server instances for one checkout. The `cwd` scope has always behaved this way. `git rev-parse` did not, because git starts from `getcwd()`, which returns the on-disk spelling; so the old git-backed `repo`/`worktree` keys were case-canonical and the native ones are not.
>
> How a wrong spelling arrives: the CLI sends `os.Getwd()`, which returns `$PWD` when it names the same directory, and a shell keeps whatever case the user typed after `cd`.
>
> **Direction of the error.** Over-isolation (a second process), never accidental sharing.
>
> **Pinned by** `TestGitCaseOfAWrongCaseCwdIsKept` (internal/config/gitdiscover_test.go), which asserts the difference is exactly case: same directory, `strings.EqualFold` equal.
>
> **Why not fixed there.** The on-disk spelling needs `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` on macOS. `syscall` has no wrapper; `golang.org/x/sys/unix.FcntlInt` takes the buffer pointer as an `int`, which is outside the `unsafe.Pointer` rules, and a raw `syscall.Syscall` on darwin bypasses libSystem, which Apple does not support. Reading each parent directory to find the stored name costs a readdir per path component per call. The fix belongs in `canonical()` for every scope, not in git discovery, and deserves its own decision.

## Current state (at `05c78b2`)

```go
// internal/config/scope.go:188-201
func canonical(p string) string {
	if p == "" { return p }
	if !filepath.IsAbs(p) {
		if wd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil { p = filepath.Join(wd, p) }
	}
	if resolved, err := filepath.EvalSymlinks(p); err == nil { return resolved }
	return filepath.Clean(p)
}
```

`canonical` is on the key path for three scopes: `ScopeCwd` (`scope.go:55`), and the `repo` and
`worktree` fallbacks (`:62`, `:71`). `filepath.EvalSymlinks` walks the path resolving symlinks; it
does not ask the filesystem what the stored name is, and on a case-insensitive volume a `lstat` of
the wrong-case name succeeds, so nothing signals the mismatch.

The same class touches #88 (socket resolution through the info file) and #78 (daemon state keyed
on paths): any key derived from a user-supplied path inherits this.

## Approaches

**A — least recommended: case-fold the key on case-insensitive platforms.**
`strings.ToLower` the path (or the volume-relative part) before keying, on darwin and Windows.
Three lines, no syscalls, fixes the reported symptom immediately.

Why not: it is wrong in the other direction. APFS can be formatted case-*sensitive*, and a Linux
box can mount a case-insensitive volume, so the platform is not the right predicate — the
*filesystem* is. Case-folding a genuinely case-sensitive path merges two real directories into
one key, which is the unsafe direction: two different checkouts share one stateful server process.
Trading over-isolation for accidental sharing is a bad trade, and Unicode case folding on
arbitrary path bytes has its own edge cases. If you take A anyway, probe the volume rather than
the GOOS.

**B — ask the filesystem, per platform.**
Get the on-disk spelling directly: `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` on darwin, `GetFinalPathNameByHandle` on
Windows, identity on Linux. This is exactly correct and it is what the reporter looked at first.
The costs are real and were measured against the Go API surface: `syscall` has no `F_GETPATH`
wrapper; `golang.org/x/sys/unix.FcntlInt` takes the buffer pointer as an `int`, which is outside
the `unsafe.Pointer` rules and so is not safe to use for this; and a raw `syscall.Syscall` on
darwin bypasses libSystem, which Apple does not support and which breaks on OS upgrades. The
portable alternative — reading each parent directory to find the stored name — costs one `readdir`
per path component, per call, on the hot path of every scoped call.

So B needs either a cgo `fcntl` (which reintroduces the `CGO_ENABLED` question #136 is trying to
settle) or a per-call readdir walk. Both are defensible; neither is free, and the correctness win
is over a failure mode whose only consequence is an extra process.

**C — recommended: make it observable and cheap, and only then decide whether to make it exact.**

1. **Open the directory and key on its identity, not its name.** `os.Stat` the canonical path and
   include `(dev, inode)` — `syscall.Stat_t.Dev`/`Ino`, already available with no new dependency —
   in the key alongside the path. Two spellings of one directory have one `(dev, inode)`, so they
   key together, and two genuinely different directories never do, so the unsafe direction of A is
   impossible. Keep the path in the key for human readability (`cwd:/Users/x/Repo#dev:ino`) or map
   through a side table if the key is user-visible.
2. **Fall back to the path alone** when `Stat` fails (a deleted or unreadable cwd), which is the
   current behaviour.
3. **Cache** the resolution per path for the daemon's lifetime, so the cost is one `Stat` per
   distinct spelling rather than per call. This is the same caching question as #187.

Recommended because it is correct in both directions, needs no syscall the standard library will
not give you, costs one `Stat` instead of a readdir walk, and is portable — `Dev`/`Ino` exist on
darwin and Linux, and Windows has `GetFileInformationByHandle`'s volume+index pair with the same
semantics. It also fixes symlinked-but-not-EvalSymlink-resolvable cases for free.

The one thing to decide before implementing: whether the scope key is a user-visible string. It
appears in `mcpx daemons` output and in the degraded-scope log line (#191), so an opaque
`dev:ino` suffix hurts readability. Prefer path-plus-identity, or resolve to a canonical *display*
path by remembering the first spelling seen for an identity.

## Open questions

- Is the scope key persisted anywhere across daemon restarts? If so, `(dev, inode)` is unstable
  across a filesystem rebuild or a bind-mount change, and the key needs a migration or a
  path-primary/identity-secondary design.
- Containers: a bind-mounted host directory has a different `(dev, inode)` inside and outside the
  container. That is arguably correct — they are different daemons — but it should be stated.
- `TestGitCaseOfAWrongCaseCwdIsKept` (`internal/config/gitdiscover_test.go`) currently **pins the
  bug**. Whichever approach lands must invert that test, not delete it, and the inverted test must
  be shown to fail before the fix.
- Does this interact with #88's info-file resolution, which keys daemons by a hash that may include
  a path?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M — the fix is small; the decision and the cross-platform verification are the work.
**Impact** med — one extra server process per wrong-case spelling, silently, with no wrong
answers. Higher for anyone on macOS with a shell that preserves typed case, which is most of them.

**Related:** #177 (parent), #191 (the log line that reports this degradation, and reports it
wrongly), #88 (socket resolution — the same "derive a key from a path" class), #78 (daemon state
and caches keyed on paths), #187 (the caching question in C3), #136 (approach B's cgo cost lands
on the `CGO_ENABLED` decision). The `git-native` branch replaces `gitDir`; this issue is
independent of it but was uncovered by it.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A design decision is recorded on the issue: how scope keys canonicalize case on case-insensitive volumes (on-disk spelling via the native discovery, a case-folded key, or an explicit platform-gated rule) — including why the over-isolation failure direction stays safe.
- [ ] After the fix, two spellings of one directory (`/Users/x/Repo` vs `/users/x/repo` on a case-insensitive volume) produce one scope key and one server instance, on the `cwd`, `repo`, and `worktree` scopes alike.
- [ ] Case-sensitive volumes are unaffected: genuinely different directories that differ only by case keep separate scopes.
- [ ] Tests cover both volume kinds (or the platform-gated equivalent); tests pass in CI.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#189 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

Three defects in the opencode plugin's daemon client, all the same shape: the plugin and the
daemon disagree about a field name, and nothing fails — the daemon ignores what it does not
recognise and the plugin prints what it did not receive. `DaemonClient.call` sends `arguments`,
`sessionId` and `callId`; `POST /v1/call` reads `args`, `session` and `context`, so **both the
tool's arguments and the session are silently dropped**. The plugin's own README documents this
call. Separately, `mcpx_exec` passes no session at all, and renders a field the result type does
not have.

Found by the PROTOCOL architect's conflict audit, reproduced against the real binary.
Code owner: SURFACES (`plugin/**`).

## Original notes

Not from the user's notes. Reported during the 2026-09-30 build-out:

> Found by the PROTOCOL architect's conflict audit (reproduced against the real binary). Owner: SURFACES (plugin/**).
>
> - `DaemonClient.call` sends `arguments`, `sessionId`, `callId`; `/v1/call` reads `args`, `context`, `session`. Arguments and session are silently dropped -- and the plugin README documents this call.
> - plugin `mcpx_exec` sends no session, so state does not persist between runs of one opencode session.
> - it reads an `output` field that `execsvc.Result` does not have, and so dumps the whole response.
>
> Fix: send the daemon's field names (a shared type or a test that round-trips the plugin request through the real route), pass the session, render `stdout`/`emits` like `mcpx_exec` over MCP does.

## Current state (at `05c78b2`)

**1. `call` sends three names the route does not read.**

```ts
// plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts:462-474
call(namespace, tool, args, session?) {
  return this.post("/v1/call", {
    server: namespace,
    tool,
    arguments: args,     // route reads "args"
    sessionId: session,  // route reads "session"
    callId: session,     // route reads "context.callId"
  })
}
```

The route's parameters are declared once, in the ops table: `args` at `internal/api/ops.go:382`,
and `session` plus `context` from `callContextParams()` at `internal/api/ops.go:110-113`
(`context` is the object carrying `sessionId`, `callId`, `parentSessionId`, `cwd`, `pid`,
`ephemeral`). `server` and `tool` are the only two fields that match. So every plugin `call`
invokes the tool **with no arguments and no session**, which means the wrong pooled instance
serves it as well.

`plugin/opencode/README.md:305` shows `client.call("fff", "grep", { query: "x" }, sessionID)` as
the documented example — following the documentation exactly produces a call with neither the
query nor the session.

**2. `mcpx_exec` never passes a session.** `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:619` calls
`viaDaemon((c) => c.exec(args.source))`, and `exec` takes only a source:
`async exec(source: string)` at `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts:451`. There is no parameter to
pass a session through. State therefore does not persist between two `mcpx_exec` calls in one
opencode session, which is the whole point of a session-scoped pool.

**3. It renders a field that does not exist.** `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:623` reads
`out.output ?? pretty(out.result ?? out)`. `execsvc.Result`
(`internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:201-213`) has `runId`, `result`, `emits`, `logs`, `stdout`,
`artifacts`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `runtime`, `timedOut`, `error` — **no `output`**. The
invented name is in the declared return type too (`daemon.ts:451`:
`Promise<{ output?: string; result?: unknown } | undefined>`), so TypeScript endorses it. `output`
is always `undefined`, so the fallback fires and the user gets `pretty(result)` — or, when a
script's value is undefined, `pretty(out)`: the whole response object, logs and all, dumped into
the model's context. That is the opposite of what the plugin exists to do.

This is #177's thesis in one file: three declared things, none delivered, and no test that walks
the declaration.

## Approaches

The three fixes are not in question. The decision is how the plugin and the daemon stay in
agreement afterwards, because hand-writing the request body is what produced all three.

**A — least recommended: fix the three call sites and move on.**
Rename the fields, thread a session parameter through `exec`, render `stdout`/`emits`. An hour's
work and the bugs are gone. The risk is that nothing changed: the plugin still hand-writes request
bodies against a route declared in Go, the next parameter added to the ops table still lands
silently, and the failure mode remains "works, wrongly". The plugin already has
`plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts`; a unit test that asserts the plugin sends `args` proves the
plugin is self-consistent, not that the daemon reads it.

**B — a round-trip test through the real route.**
Fix the three, then add a test that starts a daemon, issues the plugin's request through
`DaemonClient`, and asserts the effect at the other end: the tool received the arguments, the call
landed in the named session's pool, `mcpx_exec` state survives a second call. This is the guard
that would have caught all three, and it catches a future rename of any field that matters. Its
cost is that it is an integration test — it needs a daemon and a mock server (#133), and it runs
in the e2e suite rather than in `bun test`. Its limit is that it only covers fields a test
happens to exercise; an unused new parameter still lands unnoticed.

**C — recommended: generate the plugin's request types from the ops table, and keep B's
round-trip test for the semantics.**
The ops table (`internal/api/ops*.go`) already generates routes, MCP tools and OpenAPI from one
declaration. The plugin is the one consumer that re-types it by hand. Emit a `.d.ts` of the
request and response shapes from the same table — mcpx already ships a TypeScript emitter
(`internal/codegen/emit.go`) and already publishes types — and have `DaemonClient` use them. Then
`arguments:` is a compile error, `output` is a compile error, and a new required parameter is a
compile error at the next `bun test`. Keep B's round-trip test for what types cannot express:
that the session actually selects the pool, and that `mcpx_exec` state persists. Add a drift check
so the committed `.d.ts` cannot fall behind the table (#145's pattern).

Recommended because the generated-from-one-declaration approach is what the rest of this surface
already does, and because it converts an entire class of silent mismatch into a build failure. The
cost is real — an emitter, a committed artifact and a drift check — and it is roughly the cost of
B plus a day. Do the three fixes immediately under A as a stop-gap if the plugin is in use; do not
stop there.

## Open questions

- Does `POST /v1/call` reject unknown body fields, or ignore them? If it ignores them, that is a
  second, larger instance of the same class — a strict-decode setting would have made all three of
  these loud. Worth deciding with #172/#177 rather than here.
- Should `exec` take a full options object rather than growing a second positional parameter?
  `ExecOptions` already exists server-side (#40); the plugin should probably mirror it.
- Is there any consumer of the `output` name — an older daemon revision, a fixture — or was it
  always invented? If it was ever real, the compatibility note belongs in `docs/opencode-plugin.md`.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S for the three fixes · M for the round-trip test · M–L for the generated types.
**Impact** high — the documented way to call a tool from the plugin passes neither arguments nor
session, and the exec renderer can dump a whole response into the model's context.

**Related:** #177 (parent: the declared/actual class), #47 (the opencode v2 port, which rewrites
this client — do not let it inherit the hand-written bodies), #48 (a harness-free plugin core:
the generated types belong there, not in the opencode adapter), #188 (same class, different
file), #145 (drift check for a generated artifact), #133 (the mock MCP server the round-trip test
needs).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `DaemonClient.call` sends the field names `POST /v1/call` actually reads (`args`, `session`, `context`), so a tool's arguments and session reach the daemon.
- [ ] `mcpx_exec` passes the session, so state persists between runs of one opencode session, and renders the fields `execsvc.Result` actually has instead of dumping the whole response for a missing `output` field.
- [ ] The plugin README's documented call matches the real request shape.
- [ ] A round-trip test (plugin request through the real route, or a shared request type) fails if the two sides drift again; tests pass in CI.

title: mcpx: one definition of 'close' -- a shared near-miss matcher for search, diagnostics and launcher placeholders

labels.name: enhancement

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#186 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #176

## Summary

mcpx already has **two** "is this name close to that one?" implementations, and two open issues propose more: #109's
typo tolerance in search and #111's near-miss detection on a failed call. Written separately they diverge, and
search, diagnostics and the launcher end up disagreeing about what "close" means -- a user sees "did you mean
`list_issues`?" from one surface and no match from another for the same typo. This issue owns one definition.

**Owns #181 collision 6:** one definition of "close" -- normalisation, distance and threshold -- for search (#109),
diagnostics (#111 and today's `diagnose`) and the launcher.

## Original notes

> - better natural language processing search

The other source is the "they used search instead of query" clause of the long "check inputs" bullet, quoted in full
in #111.

## Current state (05c78b2)

| Where | What | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:417-455` | `nearest` + plain Levenshtein `editDistance`, lower-cased, accepted within `1+len/3` (`:432`) | "the closest name it does have is ..." (`:298`) in deterministic diagnostics (#58) |
| `internal/launcher/template.go:341-381` | `looksLikePlaceholder`: distance <= 1, or one adjacent swap, or a prefix of length > 2 | refusing a misspelt `@placeholder` (#7) |
| #109 (proposed) | typo tolerance over tool and namespace names (not descriptions), after exact scoring finds nothing | search ranking |
| #111 (proposed) | near-miss on a failed call | repair ladder rung 1 |

The two shipped ones already disagree: the launcher counts a transposition as one edit and accepts prefixes;
diagnostics count a transposition as two and do not.

## Approaches

**A -- leave each caller its own.** Zero work now; guaranteed divergence, and the tests of each encode a different
answer for the same pair of strings.

**B -- extract `diagnose.editDistance` and have #109 call it.** Small and cheap. Leaves the launcher's (different)
definition in place, and fixes only the distance, not the normalisation (case, `_`/`-`/camelCase splitting) or the
threshold, which is where the disagreements actually show.

**C -- recommended: one small package that defines "close".** Normalise (case-fold; split `snake_case`, `kebab-case`
and `camelCase` -- the same splitting #109 proposes for search), measure with Damerau-Levenshtein (a transposition is
one edit, as the launcher already assumes), accept within a length-relative threshold, and break ties
deterministically. Diagnostics, the launcher and #109/#111 all call it; a table test pins the examples each issue gives.
#109 keeps everything that is *ranking* (tags, synonyms, BM25-style scoring); only the near-miss predicate and the
distance are shared. Recommended because it is the only option where fixing a false positive in one surface fixes it
in all of them.

**Out of scope: argument-shape matching.** #111's own example ("they used search instead of query") is not a typo:
`search`->`query` is edit distance 5 and `olderThan`->`olderThanDays` is 4, beyond any sane threshold. Those are found by
which tool's schema the supplied arguments fit, which stays in #111. This issue answers only "is this string a
misspelling of that one".

## Open questions

- Threshold: absolute (<=1 for short names, <=2 otherwise) or a ratio? Pick using real tool names from the catalogue.
- Should a namespace be matched separately from the tool (`gihtub.list_issues` vs `github.list_isues`)?
- Does the launcher's fixed placeholder vocabulary want a stricter threshold than open-ended tool names?
- The launcher checks near misses against the **built-in** placeholder names only (`internal/launcher/template.go:299-358`), so a misspelt *declared* placeholder (#7) passes silently. The shared matcher should take the corpus as an argument so the launcher can pass built-ins plus declared names.
- Line numbers above are at 05c78b2. #116 (in flight with SURFACES) edits `CallError` in the same file, below these
  lines; on its current branch `nearest`/`editDistance` are untouched.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S · **Impact** med
Related: #109, #111 (consumers), #7 (launcher placeholders), #181 (collision 6).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria
- One shared near-miss matcher exists and is used by search, diagnostics, and every other surface the issue names; no surface keeps its own definition of 'close'.
- Tests pin the matcher semantics (thresholds, tie-breaking) once, in the shared implementation.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#185 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #176

## Summary

Three issues need the same settings capability and none of them owns it: a value the **daemon** sets as a ceiling,
which a **caller** may lower but never raise. #111 needs it for how much repair mcpx may do on its own, #112 for what a
hook is allowed to do, #113 for whether an intent may act or only plan. Today it exists only as a paragraph inside #111
(the `ClampedBy` idea). This issue owns the mechanism; the dials themselves belong to their issues, and their
vocabulary to the autonomy-dial decision record SURFACES is writing under `docs/decisions/` (#181 collision 3).

**Owns #181 collision 5:** the one mechanism by which a daemon-set value bounds what a caller may ask for. #111, #112
and #113 consume it; none implements its own clamp.

## Original notes

> - mcp-owned opencode api support
>   - check inputs, reject any request with/without reason, [...] (full bullet quoted in #111)
>     - need ways for server and client both to control their section maybe need auth

The nested bullet is the source. Its security half is deferred; its non-security half -- whose policy wins when the
daemon and the caller disagree -- is this issue.

## Current state (05c78b2)

- A setting has a `Scope` (`internal/settings/schema.go:181`; values daemon, client, call, plugin) and `Hot`. It has no
  notion of one layer bounding another.
- Values resolve by `Layer`, highest wins: default < file < env < flag < runtime (`internal/settings/value.go:13-25`).
  A call-scoped value supplied by a caller therefore simply wins.
- The only existing answer to "the caller must not decide this" is to make the setting daemon-scoped outright:
  `elicit.confirmDestructive` is `ScopeDaemon` (`internal/settings/consumer.go:47`), and `docs/consumer.md` explains why.
  That is all-or-nothing: the caller cannot even choose to be *more* careful.

## Approaches

**A -- each consumer clamps in its own code.** Repair, hooks and intent each compare the caller's value with the
daemon's before acting. Least recommended: three implementations with three orderings and three error messages,
invisible to `/v1/settings` and `mcpx settings`, and the fourth dial gets a fourth. This is what happens by default if
nobody owns it.

**B -- a naming convention plus a helper.** Pair each dial with a daemon-scoped twin (`repair.level` +
`repair.maxLevel`) and add `settings.Clamp(call, max)`. Works in today's registry with no schema change. Costs: twice
the settings per dial, the pairing is only a naming convention (a guard test would have to discover pairs by name), and
every reader must remember to call the helper -- the "declared but not delivered" shape #177 exists to stop.

**C -- recommended: a registry field.** A call-scoped setting declares that the daemon's resolved value is its ceiling
(field name open; `Clamp: Ceiling`). Resolution returns `min(caller, daemon)` over an ordered Kind (numbers,
durations, and enums in declared order), and reports the resolved value, the layer that set it, and `clamped: true`
when a caller asked for more. One implementation; flags, env, `/v1/settings`, the MCP settings tool and help text
inherit it; a guard test asserts every clamped setting has an ordered Kind and a daemon-side value. Recommended because
it is the only option where the rule is declared once next to the setting and enforced by the resolver rather than by
each reader's memory.

## Open questions

- Raise attempts: clamp and report (recommended), or refuse the call? Refusing is safer for automation that assumed it
  got what it asked for; clamping is friendlier for humans.
- Is a **floor** needed too (the daemon insists on at least "diagnose")? Same mechanism, other direction.
- Enum order: declared order, or an explicit rank per value? Declared order is free: enum settings already list their
  values in order (`script.typecheck`: `Enum: []string{"off", "on", "strict"}`, `internal/settings/registry.go:246`).
- Which dials use it is decided by #111/#112/#113 and the autonomy-dial decision record, not here.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** med (high once #111, #112 or #113 implements a dial)
Related: #111, #112, #113 (consumers; #111 carries the dial vocabulary, #181 collision 3), #172 (settings being declared
now), #129 (the guard-test pattern C's test follows), #181 (collision 5).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria
- The daemon-set ceiling exists in settings, is enforced on every caller path, and a caller may lower but never raise it; attempts to raise it fail validation with a clear error.
- Tests cover raise/lower/equal cases and the settings docs describe the ceiling.

Relocated from dezren39/nix#180 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #177

## Summary

Twelve findings were reported by earlier passes and handed over for filing. Every one was re-checked against the source at **`8001f23`** (current `origin/main`, one commit ahead of the `d0b7e01` the surrounding issues were written against) and against the live CI logs and the live MCP registry.

**Eleven of the twelve are already filed** — in #135, #136, #158, #159, #161, #168 and #172 — so this issue does not restate them. (#161 and #168 have since been closed as duplicates; their survivors are #134 and #135.) What it does is record the verification, because the re-check found **four numbers that are wrong in issue bodies that exist** and **two claims whose framing is wrong**, and those corrections have nowhere else to live: the findings are spread across seven issues, none of which is the right home for "the other six are also slightly off."

The twelfth finding (registry deduplication) is disproved and has its own issue.

This is a `review` artefact. The action item is short and sits at the bottom: six edits to five existing issue bodies.

## Status at `05c78b2` (added 2026-09-30, after #182)

The verification below is anchored at `8001f23` and is left intact as the record it is. Three of
its rows have since moved, and one of them was wrong at the time:

| Row | What changed |
| --- | --- |
| **A1** — no Containerfile | **Fixed.** #182 added `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` (three stages pinned by tag and digest, `debian:bookworm-slim` runtime, ships bun, `ENV MCPX_SCRIPT_RUNTIME=bun`, 413 MB), plus `.dockerignore` and `docs/container.md`. Nothing in CI builds or tests it yet — that is #134. The "docs presume one" half stays disproved. |
| **A3** — the Go build cache has never restored | **Fixed.** #182 added `cache-dependency-path: pkgs/mcpx/go.sum` to `actions/setup-go@v7` (`.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:50`). The rest of the caching design — the nix store cache, the duplicated `checkPhase`, sparse checkout — is still open in #135. |
| **A2** — the "static binary" claim is false | **The framing was wrong, and this row is the correction.** `os/user` and `net` pull libc **only under cgo**. With `CGO_ENABLED=0` Go uses its pure-Go implementations, and #182 verified the result by cross-compiling: a `GOOS=linux CGO_ENABLED=0` build is a fully static 21 MB working ELF (`ldd`: "not a dynamic executable"; `--version`, `ls`, `call` and `exec` all pass — `docs/container.md` §4). So **nothing in mcpx prevents a static binary.** What stays true is narrower and is about the *shipped* artifacts, by choice rather than necessity: `package.nix` sets no `CGO_ENABLED` so the nix package inherits nixpkgs' cgo default, `postInstall` wraps the binary with `--suffix PATH : [git deno bun node]` (`package.nix:96`) so it is not self-contained either way, and the Containerfile threads `ARG CGO_ENABLED=1` deliberately. **#136 is therefore a policy decision, not a feasibility one**: pure-Go `os/user` reads `/etc/passwd` rather than NSS/LDAP, and the pure-Go resolver ignores `nsswitch.conf` and the macOS resolver (VPN split DNS) — irrelevant in a container, relevant on a corporate laptop. And `mcpx exec` needs a JavaScript runtime whatever the binary is. **Any sentence saying mcpx "cannot" be static, or that `os/user`/`net` "prevent" it, is wrong and should be struck.** |

**Closed-duplicate links repaired.** This issue was written when #161 and #168 were open; both were
later closed as duplicates. The surviving issues are **#134** (was #161) and **#135**/**#139**/**#143**
(was #168). References below have been updated. #52 is also closed, fixed in #182.

## What was verified

Source refs are `pkgs/mcpx/…` at `8001f23`, read from a read-only checkout. Nothing was built, modified or committed. CI evidence is run [36680520713](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/actions/runs/36680520713), the push-to-`main` run for `8001f23` itself.

| # | Claim as reported | How verified | Result | Owned by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | There is no Containerfile, **though docs presume one** | `find . -iname '*containerfile*' -o -iname '*dockerfile*'` over the whole repo → nothing. `rg -i 'container\|docker\|podman\|image'` over `pkgs/mcpx` → every hit is a *deployment environment* aside (`docs/plugin-discovery.md:22` "a daemon may be running under launchd, in a container"; `internal/settings/registry.go:386`; `internal/registry/registry.go:254` maps the registry's `oci` package type to `docker run --rm -i`). **No mcpx document presumes a Containerfile exists in this repo** | **PARTIALLY** — no Containerfile: **verified**. "docs presume one": **disproved**; the presumption is in the planning notes, which is exactly how #134 already states it (formerly #161, closed as a duplicate) | #134 |
| A2 | The "static binary" claim is false | `rg -n 'CGO\|env =' package.nix` → no match, so `buildGoModule` inherits the nixpkgs default. `os/user` imported at `internal/logging/trace.go:9`; `net` imported by 7 files across 5 packages (`internal/logging/trace.go`, `internal/cli/client.go`, `internal/cli/connect.go`, `internal/daemon/routes_resolve.go`, `internal/daemon/server.go`). `package.nix` `postInstall` runs `wrapProgram $out/bin/mcpx --suffix PATH : <git deno bun-bin nodejs>`, so the installed `bin/mcpx` is a `makeBinaryWrapper` launcher, not the Go binary. **Separately: `rg -i 'static binar\|statically linked\|self-contained'` over `pkgs/mcpx` returns no claim at all** | **VERIFIED** on the technical substance. **The claim is not made in mcpx's docs or source** — it appears only in the planning notes, quoted in #136 and #134 | #136 (the claim + platform matrix — **see the A2 correction above: this is a policy question, not a feasibility one**), #134 (the packaged-form consequence; formerly #161) |

Run 36680520713, `Run actions/setup-go@v7`: `cache: true` … `##[warning]Restore cache failed: Dependencies file is not found in /home/runner/work/nix/nix. Supported file pattern: go.mod`. `Post Run actions/setup-go@v7`: `Primary key was not generated. Please check the log messages above for more errors or information` | **VERIFIED** at `8001f23`; **fixed in #182**, see the status block above | #135 (the workflow and the rest of the caching design; formerly also #168, closed as a duplicate) |
| A4 | The version is hard-coded in three places | `package.nix:19`, `package.nix:61`, `cmd/mcpx/main.go:18`. Two further echoes that are not build inputs: `plugin/opencode/skills/mcpx-daemon/SKILL.md:35`, `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts:132` | **VERIFIED — exactly three** | #158, #159 item 16, and the sibling derivation issue |
| A5 | The man page stamps a build date, so it is not reproducible | `internal/cli/manual.go:335` — `date := time.Now().UTC().Format("2006-01-02")` → `.TH MCPX 1 %q …` at `:337`. `package.nix` `postInstall` runs `$out/bin/mcpx man > $out/share/man/man1/mcpx.1` at build time. It is the only wall-clock input in the derivation | **VERIFIED** | #159 item 5 (as a docs problem); the sibling derivation issue adds the nix consequence and the fix |
| B1 | `mcpx init` writes a `mode` key the loader ignores | `internal/cli/commands.go:1390` `"mode": "shared"`, `:1400` `"mode": "session"`, both inside the `"mcpx"` block. `internal/config/config.go:93-94` — the server struct has `Sharing` and `Scope`; there is no `Mode` field. `rg -n 'DisallowUnknownFields'` over all Go → only `internal/defaults/defaults.go:245` and its test, so config decoding drops unknown keys silently. The chrome-devtools example's comment promises "One browser per script run"; `"mode": "session"` is ignored and it gets the defaults, `sharing=shared` / `scope=global` — one shared browser | **VERIFIED** | #159 item 2 |
| B2 | `mcpx openapi` describes a removed server | `internal/cli/openapi.go:98` — `servers: [{url: "http://127.0.0.1:8787", description: "mcpx serve --transport http"}]`; paths `/mcp`, `/health`, `/openapi.json` (`:23,45,52`). `internal/cli/serve.go:360-376` rejects every transport but `stdio` and its comment at `:303` says the HTTP one "existed". The daemon serves `/v1/health` (`internal/daemon/server.go:408`) and `/v1/openapi.json` (`internal/daemon/ops.go:38`), not the un-prefixed paths. The function's own doc comment at `internal/cli/openapi.go:14-20` claims it "cannot describe an endpoint that does not exist" | **VERIFIED** | #159 item 3 |
| B3 | `/v1/openapi.json` includes the running daemon's configured tools | `internal/daemon/ops.go:498-509` — `handleOpenAPI` takes the static `api.OpenAPI(version)` and merges `s.toolPaths()` into its `paths`. `:513-525` — `toolPaths` iterates `s.reg.Tools(nil)`, the **live** catalogue, emitting `/v1/call/{namespace}/{tool}` with `operationId: "call_<ns>_<tool>"` and the upstream tool's own input schema. The comment at `:500` records that this is per-request and deliberate | **VERIFIED — it is built from the live catalogue** | #159 item 4; fix shape below |
| B4 | `Commands()` has 32 entries while 7 more commands run | `internal/cli/manual.go:33` — `Commands()` returns exactly **32** entries. `cmd/mcpx/main.go:119-161` — the `handlers` map has 42 keys, of which 3 are aliases (`list`, `namespaces` → `CmdLs`; `logs` → `CmdLog`), so **39 distinct commands**. The 7-command difference is exactly `serve`, `openapi`, `adapter`, `registry`, `api`, `man`, `completion` | **VERIFIED — 32, 39, 7, and the list is exact** | #159 item 1; class tracker elsewhere |
| B5 | `parity.md` has no row for 26 of 60 operations | Ops extracted with `rg -oIN 'Name: "([a-z_0-9]+)", Method:' internal/api/ops*.go` → **60 distinct**, same count at `d0b7e01`. `docs/parity.md` `## /v1 operations` is lines 23-70 and holds **33** rows, all 33 matching a real op. 60 − 33 = **27**, and each of the 27 was re-checked against the whole file to rule out a differently-formatted row | **PARTIALLY — 27, not 26** | #159 item 11 |
| B6 | Several docs are stale | see the table below | **PARTIALLY — three verified, one wrong** | #159 items 12, 13, 14 |
| C | `internal/registry` returns the same package up to nine times | See the sibling registry issue: `Search` sends `version=latest` unconditionally (`internal/registry/registry.go:157`), it is the only query builder, and five live searches returned zero repeated names | **DISPROVED** | sibling issue |

### B6, item by item

| Sub-claim | Evidence | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dependency claims are stale | `docs/dependencies.md:8` — "**One.** `modernc.org/sqlite`". `docs/story.md:2394` — "`buildGoModule` with `vendorHash = null`". `docs/story.md:2398` — "mcpx has one third-party Go dependency". `ASSESSMENT.md:17` — "dependency-free Go". `OPENCODE-V2.md:139` — "no dependencies". Actual `go.mod`: **5 direct** (bubbles, bubbletea, lipgloss, yaml.v3, modernc.org/sqlite) **+ 29 indirect = 34**, and `package.nix:54` pins a real `vendorHash` | **VERIFIED** |
| Size figures are stale | `ASSESSMENT.md:16-17` — "~3,500 lines of dependency-free Go, 84 passing tests, a 7 MB binary". `OPENCODE-V2.md:139` — "~4.2 k LOC, Go". Measured at `8001f23`: **44,916** non-test Go lines, **17,196** test lines, **734** `func Test*` | **VERIFIED — and the real numbers are 12.8× and 8.7× the stated ones** |
| `MCPX_SESSION` naming | `docs/opencode-plugin.md:405` — "Sets `MCPX_SESSION`, `MCPX_CALL` and friends". The plugin sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID` (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:670`) and `MCPX_CALL_ID` (`:677`). **But `MCPX_SESSION` is a real, live variable elsewhere**: set at `internal/cli/commands.go:672`, `internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:575` and `internal/daemon/consumer.go:536`, read by the generated client at `internal/codegen/emit.go:253` (`const SESSION = env("MCPX_SESSION") \|\| DEFAULT_SESSION`) and asserted by `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go:43,65`. `MCPX_CALL`, by contrast, exists **nowhere** | **PARTIALLY — the doc line is stale, but #159 item 13's explanation is wrong** |
| `ASSESSMENT.md`'s darwin module | `ASSESSMENT.md:278-279` — "Replace the `lootbox` launchd agent with `services.mcpx` from `nix/darwin-module.nix`". `find . -name 'darwin-module.nix'` over the whole repo → nothing. `rg -l 'services\.mcpx'` excluding `ASSESSMENT.md` → nothing | **VERIFIED — the file and the option both do not exist** |

## Current state: the corrections

### 1. `parity.md` — 27 of 60, not 26

The 27 operations with no row in `docs/parity.md` `## /v1 operations`:

```
artifact_delete  artifact_get   artifact_put   artifacts_list
ask_abandon      ask_answers    ask_begin      ask_poll
call_path        catalog_history diagnose      exec
intent           protocol       recipe_get     recipe_run
recipe_save      recipes_list   resolve        servers_add
servers_list     servers_remove settings_get   settings_list
settings_set     settings_unset tool_invoke
```

Shape of the gap, which matters more than the count: the missing rows are not scattered. They are **whole feature families** — every artifact op, every `ask` op, every recipe op, every settings op, every servers op, plus `exec`, `diagnose`, `intent`, `resolve`, `protocol`, `call_path`, `tool_invoke` and `catalog_history`. `docs/parity.md` documents the surface mcpx had before artifacts (#40), recipes/intent (#41), live server management and the settings API landed. It is not drifting; it stopped. That also means the file's `## Known gaps` section (`:112-131`) is an honest list of gaps *within the 33 documented ops* and says nothing about the 27 undocumented ones — a reader has no way to tell the two apart. `/v1` op count was 60 at `d0b7e01` too, so the 26 → 27 difference is a miscount rather than drift.

Relevant to #76: eight of the 27 (`resolve`, `protocol`, the four artifact ops, and the task ops it lists) are exactly the operations #76 says have no CLI command. They have no parity row either, which is presumably why the gap survived.

### 2. `MCPX_SESSION` is real; `MCPX_CALL` is not

#159 item 13 reads "the code sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID`", which implies `MCPX_SESSION` is a typo for it. It is not. There are two separate variables with different owners:

| Variable | Set by | Read by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MCPX_SESSION` | `internal/cli/commands.go:672`, `internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:575`, `internal/daemon/consumer.go:536` | the generated TypeScript client, `internal/codegen/emit.go:253` |
| `MCPX_SESSION_ID` | the opencode plugin, `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:670`; also `internal/config/scope.go` for session scoping | `internal/config/scope.go`, `internal/execsvc/execsvc.go` |
| `MCPX_CALL` | nothing | nothing |

So `docs/opencode-plugin.md:405` is wrong twice over: it attributes a variable to the plugin that the plugin does not set, and it names a second one that does not exist. The correct line is "Sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID`, `MCPX_CALL_ID` and friends" — the full list the plugin sets is in `plugin/opencode/README.md:180-202`. Anyone fixing this by renaming `MCPX_SESSION` → `MCPX_SESSION_ID` in the *code* would break the generated client and `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go`.

This also bears on #172: `MCPX_SESSION` is one of the variables read by non-test code with no setting declaring it, and `MCPX_CALL` is the shape of a variable a documentation-derived allowlist would happily invent.

### 3. `/v1/openapi.json` — the fix shape

Since this one has a genuine design decision and #159 states it in one line, the options, briefly:

- **A — least recommended: strip the live paths.** Serve only `api.OpenAPI(version)`, drop `toolPaths()`. One line, and it deletes a real capability: the per-tool REST paths are how a non-MCP HTTP client discovers what it can call, which `internal/daemon/ops.go:500-503` explicitly says is the useful half.
- **B — middle: a query parameter.** `GET /v1/openapi.json?tools=0` returns the static document. Keeps both, costs nothing, and leaves the leak as the **default** — so the docs build, the browser tab, and every naive `curl` still get the builder's server list.
- **C — recommended: make the static document the default and the live one opt-in, under a setting.** `GET /v1/openapi.json` returns the ops-table document; `?tools=1` (or a `registry`-scoped setting such as `proto.openapiTools`, default off for a daemon that is not loopback-only) adds them. This inverts the risk correctly: the safe answer is what you get by not thinking, the useful-but-revealing answer is what you get by asking. It also gives #144's generated reference a stable document to build from without a filter step. The cost is that an existing consumer relying on the tool paths must add a parameter — acceptable, since the daemon is unauthenticated loopback and has no external consumers yet.

Note this is not a security issue in the deferred sense — it is a "publishing a generated artefact leaks the generator's environment" hazard, which bites the docs pipeline (#144) whether or not anyone is attacking anything.

## Approaches

For this issue itself: **no real choice.** It is a set of corrections to issues that exist and must not be edited by the agent that found them.

## Open questions

- Is the 26 → 27 parity discrepancy worth tracking down in #159's history, or just corrected? Corrected, here; the ops count was 60 at both commits, so nothing moved.
- `docs/parity.md` has no generator and no test (#159 item 11, confirmed: `internal/api/parity_test.go:21` checks routes/ops/tools by regex and never opens the file). Should the 27 rows be written by hand now, or should the file wait for #145's generator and be deleted in the meantime? Writing 27 rows by hand that a generator will overwrite is waste; leaving a file that documents 55% of the surface with no indication of the fact is worse. A one-line header saying which commit it was last true for would cost nothing and is not in anyone's scope yet.
- Should `ASSESSMENT.md` and `OPENCODE-V2.md` carry their measured-at-the-time numbers with a dated correction block (as #159 item 14 recommends, and as `OPENCODE-V2.md` already does once) or be marked historical wholesale? The 12.8× gap in `ASSESSMENT.md:16` is large enough that a reader who does not notice the date will draw a badly wrong conclusion about the size of the thing.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease: S** (six edits to five issue bodies; no code) · **Impact: med** (the corrections are small, but three of them — the parity count, the `MCPX_SESSION` framing and the "docs presume a Containerfile" framing — would each have sent an implementer in a wrong direction, and the `MCPX_SESSION` one would have broken the generated client)

Related, with what each owns: **#159** — items 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16 are the findings re-verified here; it owns the fixes. **#134** — the Containerfile and the packaged-form facts (formerly #161, closed as a duplicate); one now exists, untested, from #182. **#136** — the platform matrix, and the static-binary claim, **which the A2 correction above turns from a feasibility question into a policy one**. **#135** — the CI workflow shape and the rest of the caching design; the `cache-dependency-path` line itself was fixed in #182 (formerly also #168, closed as a duplicate). **#158** — release prerequisites, including the three version sites. **#172** — `MCPX_*` variables no setting declares; `MCPX_SESSION` is one, `MCPX_CALL` is a phantom. **#144**/**#145** — the generated reference and drift check that all of this blocks. **#76** — eight of the 27 undocumented ops are the CLI gaps it lists. **#52** — why no test suite was run here (**closed, fixed in #182**: cleanup now calls `stop --all` through the `daemon-<key>.json` info files and every test env sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s`; the environment-inheritance half is #138, still open). **#102**, **#108**, **#116**, and closed **#74**/**#75** — the same promise-versus-behaviour class.

### Action items (the only work in this issue)

1. #159 item 11: `26 of the 60 ops` → **`27 of the 60 ops`**; add the list above.
2. #159 item 13: replace with "`docs/opencode-plugin.md:405` says the plugin sets `MCPX_SESSION` and `MCPX_CALL`; it sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID` and `MCPX_CALL_ID` (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:670,677`). `MCPX_SESSION` is a separate, live variable — do not rename it. `MCPX_CALL` does not exist."
3. #159 item 12: add the measured figures — 5 direct + 29 indirect modules; 44,916 non-test Go lines; 734 test functions.
4. #159 item 14: same figures, replacing "~44k non-test Go lines".
5. #159 item 4: link the A/B/C fix shape above, or fold it in.
