body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#149 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #94

## Summary

The notes end the level-2 list with five questions, written in the voice of a skeptical first-time reader. They become the FAQ. Each line is a heading **word for word**, including the quotes, the `, no.` and the `..`, and each gets a short, candid answer in the same voice, based on facts in the repo.

Proposed placement: one level-2 page, `faq`, with a fixed anchor per question (listed in #146's page map). The home page's "now what" (#157) and the home page itself (#155) link to it. The pages each question touches also link back to it: "is it safe?" from `scripts#script`, the code-mode question from the opencode plugin pages (#148).

## Original notes

Source-notes lines 1, 2, 7, 49-52 (parents) and 78-82 (this issue). The lines in between are quoted in sibling issues.

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 'ok i just installed this thing what even is it' layer
>         - basically a more normal set of docs
>         - new person might assume this is all there is and wont be upset
>         - a page or section in a page for
>           - "so why'd you get rid of all the mcp and then make one, do you like mcp or not"
>           - "i mean, opencodemode is right there"
>           - "is it safe?", no.
>           - "but why would you.."
>           - "but can i get some examples?"

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

There is no FAQ. The material for the answers exists but is spread across files:

- story.md "# Summary" and "mcpx speaks MCP"
- `OPENCODE-V2.md`, and its 2026-09-29 correction block
- `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §1
- `AGENTS.md` "Scripts"
- `internal/runner/runner.go:41-66`
- `ASSESSMENT.md`
- the story.md opening walk
- `manual.go` `Examples` fields, and `mcpx recipes`

Paths are relative to `pkgs/mcpx/` on `main` (`d0b7e01`; re-checked at `05c78b2` on 2026-09-30, with no drift in the cited lines). Every command cited below is in `Commands()`, except `mcpx serve` (dispatched but not listed; see #147 Finding 1).

One trap: `OPENCODE-V2.md`'s body predates its own correction. Its side-by-side table ("TypeScript is rejected") and its "If you stay on opencode v1 ... none of v2's Code Mode is available to you today" are both wrong according to the correction block and `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §1. The FAQ must use the corrected facts.

## Approaches: where the FAQ lives

- **A (least recommended): no FAQ page; scatter the questions as callouts on the relevant pages.** This loses the thing that makes these five lines valuable: they are the questions everyone asks first, in the order they ask them, in a voice that admits the obvious objection. A reader who wonders "is it safe?" should not have to guess that the answer sits on the scripts page.
- **B (middle): put the FAQ in the compendium** next to the comparisons and history (#153). The long answers do live there. But lines 50-51 say a new person may assume level 2 is all there is. Those readers are exactly the ones asking these questions, and they would never find the answers.
- **C (recommended): a level-2 `faq` page, one anchor per question.** Each answer is at most about 120 words and ends with one "more" link into level 2, or into the compendium (#153) for history. It is linked from home's "now what" and from the pages above. The agent twin (#120) carries it as a single file, which suits `llms.txt`. The short answers keep it at level 2, and the links give the long form to anyone who wants it.

## Answer direction per question

These are drafts of tone and content, not final copy. They are candid, short, and they admit weaknesses where they exist.

### "so why'd you get rid of all the mcp and then make one, do you like mcp or not"

Anchor `faq#do-you-like-mcp`.

We like MCP fine. mcpx didn't get rid of it. It got rid of **tool schemas in the model's context**:

- "mcpx puts every MCP server behind one command so their schemas stay out of the model's context until something asks for them" (story.md "# Summary").
- Underneath, mcpx is an MCP client of every server you configure, across four protocol revisions (`docs/protocol.md` §1). It reads the same `mcpServers` config every other host reads.
- It is also an MCP server itself: `/mcp` on the daemon, `mcpx serve --transport stdio`.

The one it "made" is deliberately tiny, because "Exposing three hundred tools over MCP would rebuild the problem mcpx was built to solve, with extra steps" (story.md "mcpx speaks MCP"). `mcpx_exec` is the tool that matters.

More: `mcp#mcp` (#147).

### "i mean, opencodemode is right there"

Anchor `faq#opencode-code-mode`.

It is, and not only in v2. opencode v1 ships code mode behind `OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE`, it is on by default in v2, and both accept TypeScript (`OPENCODE-V2.md` corrections; `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §1).

Where opencode's is better, said plainly:

- **Confinement.** Its purpose-built interpreter runs "only the language features we implement", which is a stronger security posture than any permission flag mcpx has.
- **OAuth and elicitation for remote servers.**

(mcpx has since copied its budgeted catalog, catalog diffs and in-script `search()`.)

What mcpx does that it does not:

1. **It works outside a model turn.** A shell script, CI, cron or a different harness can call it. There is "no `opencode2 exec`".
2. **One daemon serves every harness,** with real per-session processes for stateful servers. opencode keeps "one MCP connection per server per location", so two sessions share one Chrome.
3. **Scripts run on a real runtime** with imports and a filesystem.

The recommendation in `OPENCODE-V2.md` still holds: let code mode own ordinary MCP for opencode's own loop, and use mcpx for stateful servers and for everything outside a turn.

More: #153.

### "is it safe?", no.

Anchor `faq#is-it-safe`.

The answer starts with **"No."**

- Scripts run on a real runtime with your full authority: "filesystem, network, subprocesses" (`AGENTS.md` "Scripts").
- `script.permissions` defaults to `all` (`--allow-all` on Deno). The narrower profiles (`net`, `read`, `read-net`, `strict`) apply **only on Deno**: "bun and node run with the user's own authority whatever is asked" (`internal/runner/runner.go:41-49`).
- The daemon API is unauthenticated. It listens on loopback and on a socket only you can open, and binding wider prints a warning (story.md "One daemon, many clients").
- `mcpx prompt` hands a generated script back instead of running it, "because generated code runs with your credentials".

What this means for the reader:

- Treat a script like a shell command you are about to paste.
- Configure only servers you would run by hand.
- Do not expose the port.

That is the whole answer. This issue does not design security (see the footer).

### "but why would you.."

Anchor `faq#why`.

Three reasons, then the history:

1. **Context cost.** Tool schemas sit in every request, whether or not the tools get used. mcpx's always-on cost is zero (`OPENCODE-V2.md` side-by-side). In the opening walk, "There are 27 Chrome tools live on this machine and not one byte of their schemas is in the agent's context".
2. **Stateful servers under concurrency.** Two agents sharing one browser corrupt each other. mcpx leases a process per session (story.md "Sharing and scope").
3. **Reach.** The same tools from a shell, CI or any harness.

History: this replaced lootbox, which the user was maintaining as a fork 51 commits ahead of a quiet upstream. Discovery there was uncached (about 650 ms per request), and "an architecture that cannot express the one thing you actually need (more than one Chrome)" (`ASSESSMENT.md` "Summary").

More: #153.

### "but can i get some examples?"

Anchor `faq#examples`.

Yes. The answer is short and points at an **examples gallery**, which is where the real work of this item lies. Material that exists today:

- the story.md opening walk (a real prompt, one script, two screenshots, with exact bytes);
- `mcpx recipes` (saved scripts with `// @param` holes);
- named scripts in `.mcpx/scripts/`;
- the per-command `Examples` in `internal/cli/manual.go`;
- the snippets in `AGENTS.md` and `docs/exec.md`.

**Approaches for the gallery:**

- **A (least): examples written inline in pages, never run.** They rot on the first schema change, and a broken example teaches a new user that the docs lie.
- **B (middle): a gallery page of copy-paste snippets.** Better to browse, but it rots the same way.
- **C (recommended): an `examples/` directory of runnable scripts, each with its expected output.** CI executes them, pages embed from them, and the gallery page is generated.
  - They should run against deterministic servers: a fixture server from `internal/testsupport`, or a pinned `@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem` on a temp directory. Not live Chrome.
  - Some of them can double as installed recipes.
  - The runnable example on the home page (#156) should be one of these.
  - Daemon hygiene: #52 (the e2e suite leaking daemons) is closed, fixed in #182. That fix isolates `MCPX_STATE_DIR`, sets `MCPX_AUTOSTART_IDLE_EXIT=60s` and runs `mcpx stop --all` on cleanup (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:60-83`). An examples job should reuse that pattern, not start daemons that live for the default four hours.

  Docs checks run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97).

## Open questions

1. **Voice.** Should the answers use "we", "I" (as `OPENCODE-V2.md` and `ASSESSMENT.md` do), or no pronoun? The notes are first person and casual.
2. **Scope of "but why would you..".** Does it mean "why would you use this over plain MCP / code mode" (drafted above), or "why would you build it", which is the history? The draft covers both briefly.
3. **Examples.** Should the gallery be a sibling page (`examples`) that the FAQ links to? Or should it stay as a section of the FAQ until there are more than a handful of examples?
4. **Correcting `OPENCODE-V2.md`.** Should its stale body be corrected in place, not just prefaced by the correction block, before the FAQ links to it? #153 owns the comparison pages.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S for the FAQ page; the examples gallery under C is M and depends on the testing CI · **Impact** med-high: these five answers decide whether a skeptical first-time reader stays · **Depends on / related:** #94, #47, #49, #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #155, #156, #157, #146, #147, #148, #153, #120

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

title: mcpx docs: plugin pages -- plugins, compatibility, interface and config, opencode v1 and v2, vibeMcp
body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#148 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #94

## Summary

This issue covers the level-2 plugin pages: plugins, plugin compatibility, plugin interface & config, the opencode v1 plugin, the opencode v2 plugin, and vibeMcp. Anchors are under `plugins#…` in #146's page map. The pages may split into a plugins index plus an `opencode` page, with the same anchors either way.

"Plugin" means two different things in this project, and the pages must say which one each section means:

| meaning | direction | exists today | where it is designed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **harness plugin**: code that plugs mcpx *into* an agent harness (the opencode plugin) | a consumer of mcpx | yes: `plugin/opencode/` | this issue; #47, #48 |
| **mcpx plugin**: an extension *of* mcpx (Go, binary, script or remote plugins, hooks, variables) | extends mcpx | no: "There is no plugin concept in the daemon at all" (#80) | extensibility theme: #80, #82, #83 |

Nearly everything in the notes' plugin lines is about the first meaning. "vibeMcp" appears nowhere in the repo, and its meaning is the first open question.

## Original notes

Source-notes lines 1, 2, 7, 49-52 (parents) and 72-77 (this issue). The lines in between are quoted in sibling issues.

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 'ok i just installed this thing what even is it' layer
>         - basically a more normal set of docs
>         - new person might assume this is all there is and wont be upset
>         - a page or section in a page for
>           - plugins
>           - plugin compatibility
>           - plugin interface & config
>           - opencode v1 plugin
>           - opencode v2 plugin
>           - vibeMcp

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

Paths are relative to `pkgs/mcpx/` on `main` (`d0b7e01`); re-checked at `05c78b2` in the 2026-09-30 issues pass, after #171 changed the plugin settings.

- **What ships:**
  - `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts`, the opencode adapter: hooks, tools, toasts, session id.
  - `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts`, the portable core: `DaemonClient`, the discovery ladder, the remembered-choice file. It imports nothing from opencode.
  - `mcpx-tui.tsx`, an optional TUI picker.
  - Four skills: `mcpx-basics`, `mcpx-observability`, `mcpx-browser`, `mcpx-daemon`.

  Source: `plugin/opencode/README.md` "The files".
- **How it is installed:** by hand with `cp -R` into `~/.config/opencode/plugin/`, and `mcpx/` must stay a subdirectory (README "Install"). Nothing in `~/.config/nix` outside `pkgs/mcpx` references it (`git grep mcpx-session origin/main` finds nothing), so the Nix config does not install it.
- **Versions:** opencode v1 is `1.18.31`; the v2 CLI `opencode2` is `2.0.3` (`docs/opencode-plugin.md` §1). v1 plugins do not load in v2 (#47). v1.18.31 runs both plugin systems, so a v2 plugin file dropped into v1 is loaded by the v2 host and rejected, harmlessly, by the v1 loader (§1).
- **No binary needed:** the plugin needs no `mcpx` on `PATH` (#44, closed, fixed in #53). It reaches the daemon over the unix socket. It spawns `mcpx --json status` only at rung 4 of discovery, the last fallback, used when a binary exists and the daemons are too old to answer `GET /v1/resolve` (`plugin/opencode/README.md:99-112`, `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts`). `backend: v1` never spawns, and `bin: ""` forbids spawning (README:83-85). The pages say "never needs the binary", not "never runs it".
- **Two sources for plugin configuration** (as written at `d0b7e01`, struck where #171 changed it):
  - ~~The registry has 9 `plugin.*` settings: `backend`, `bin`, `binArgs`, `discoveryRetry`, `env`, `instructions`, `skills`, `toolTiming`, `tools` (`docs/configuration.md` "plugin").~~ At `05c78b2` the registry has **10**: those minus `skills` (deleted, since nothing registers skills), plus `remember` and `annotate` (added) (`internal/settings/plugin.go`; `docs/configuration.md:346-355`).
  - The README's options table has 13 (`plugin/opencode/README.md:79-93`). ~~Six of them are not `plugin.*` settings: `endpoint` and `socket` (mapped to `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT`/`MCPX_ENDPOINT` and `MCPX_SOCKET`), `remember`, `daemonTools`, `annotate`, `headless`.~~ Four of them are not `plugin.*` settings: `endpoint` and `socket` (mapped to `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT`/`MCPX_ENDPOINT` and `MCPX_SOCKET`), `daemonTools` and `headless`. #171 allowlisted all four with a reason each (`pluginEnvAllowed`, `internal/settings/consumed_test.go:188-200`). `headless` and `daemonTools` have defaults computed at boot, so a declared default would be wrong in one realm.
  - `discoveryRetry` is in the registry, and since #171 actually read (`mcpx-session.ts:196`), but is still missing from the README table. ~~`skills`~~ is gone.
  - `docs/configuration.md:85-86` says "The plugin reads `process.env` directly, so the variable names are the contract between the two and a test pins them". ~~The test pins only the registry's names.~~ Since #171 this holds in both directions. `TestEverySettingIsReadSomewhere` requires every `plugin.*` variable to appear in the plugin's sources, and `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` (`consumed_test.go:209`) fails on any variable the plugin reads that is neither a setting nor allowlisted. What no test pins is the README table itself.
- **Stale variable name:** `docs/opencode-plugin.md:406` (§6) says the plugin sets "`MCPX_SESSION`, `MCPX_CALL` and friends". The code sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID` (`mcpx-session.ts:670`), `MCPX_CALL_ID` (`:677`) and `MCPX_PARENT_SESSION_ID` (`:713`), which are the names `session` and `parent-session` scopes read (story.md "Sharing and scope"). The pages use the code's names. This is a doc fix only. `MCPX_SESSION` is a different, live variable: mcpx sets it for each script and the generated client reads it (`internal/codegen/emit.go:253`). It must not be renamed. `MCPX_CALL` exists nowhere (#159 item 13, struck and corrected).
- **Other harnesses:** codex, claude code, pi and manus have no plugin. #48 designs a harness-free core plus adapters. `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §5 lists what an adapter must provide. Only (1) a directory and (2) a session identifier are required; everything else degrades.
- **Commands referenced below** that are dispatched but missing from `Commands()`: `mcpx api` and `mcpx adapter` (see #147 Finding 1). All others are in `Commands()`.

## Content per item

### `plugins#plugins`

**Approaches: naming the two meanings.**

- **A (least recommended): use "plugin" for both and rely on prose to tell them apart.** A reader who arrives from a search engine at "plugin config" has no way to know whether it is about opencode or about extending mcpx. The confusion then spreads into issues, and into the agent twin (#120), where an agent will happily mix them up.
- **B (middle): rename one of them everywhere, for example harness plugins become "integrations",** including `plugin/` in the repo. This is clear, but it fights every harness's own vocabulary (opencode calls them plugins, and so will its users). It also needs a code-and-path rename that belongs to #48, not to docs.
- **C (recommended): keep the word and qualify it every time.** The page is titled "Plugins" and has two top-level sections: **"Harness plugins: mcpx inside your agent"** and **"mcpx plugins: extending mcpx"**. The second is a short status stub ("not built; designed in #80") until #80 lands. A glossary entry and a one-line callout at the top of every plugin page say which meaning the page uses. This matches the words users will search for, needs no rename, and scales when #80 ships.

**Content** for the harness-plugin section:

- **What a harness plugin adds, and that it is optional.** Any harness with a shell can use mcpx through `AGENTS.md` alone. The plugin adds:
  - the session id, so `session`-scoped servers persist across commands (README "Why");
  - the socket fast path (0.17 ms versus a 23 ms spawn);
  - optional tools, a system-prompt line, timing records and the daemon picker.
- **Hosts that only speak MCP** need no plugin: `mcpx serve --transport stdio` or `/mcp`, linking `modes#server-modes` (#146).

### `plugins#plugin-compatibility`

A matrix. Every cell cites a source or says "unknown", with nothing guessed:

| harness | plugin | how mcpx reaches it today | session id | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| opencode v1 (1.18.31) | yes, `plugin/opencode` | plugin, or shell + `AGENTS.md` | injected by the `shell.env` hook | README; `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §2, §6 |
| opencode v2 (2.0.3) | no: v1 plugins do not load | shell + `AGENTS.md`, or mcpx as an MCP server in its `mcp` config | not injected; needs the v2 session environment API (#47) | `docs/opencode-plugin.md` §4; #47 |
| codex | no | shell + `AGENTS.md`; MCP | unknown | #48 |
| claude code | no | shell + `AGENTS.md`; MCP | unknown | #48 |
| pi | no | unknown | unknown | #48 |
| manus | no | unknown | unknown | #48 |
| any MCP host | not needed | `/mcp` or stdio | none (MCP carries no harness session) | #147 `mcp#mcp` |

Also one runtime note from the README: the core dials the socket with Bun's `fetch(url, {unix})`. A Node-based harness has to use `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` and the TCP listener instead.

### `plugins#plugin-interface-and-config`

Two interfaces and one configuration surface:

1. **Plugin to harness.** The four opencode hooks mcpx uses (`docs/opencode-plugin.md` §2.2), and what each one degrades to without it (§6).
2. **Plugin to daemon.** `DaemonClient` / `connect()`, and the discovery ladder (`plugin/opencode/README.md:104-112`): 0 a named endpoint or socket; 1 the choice remembered for this directory; 2 the `daemon-*.json` info files (the usual case, no binary); 3 `GET /v1/resolve`; 4 spawn `mcpx --json status`, the only rung that runs the binary, used as a last fallback and never under `backend: v1` or `bin: ""`; 5 ask the user; 6 the best candidate, with a warning (`docs/plugin-discovery.md` §2-§5).
3. **For authors of plugins for other harnesses:** the adapter contract (§5's six items, two of them required). This is what #48 builds on.
4. **Configuration:**
   - precedence is plugin option > environment variable > default;
   - options reach the plugin only when it is named in opencode config as a two-element array (README "Passing options");
   - the options table must be generated from one list.

   **Approaches for that one list** (revised 2026-09-30: #171 settled part of this. It registered `remember` and `annotate`, deleted `skills`, and allowlisted the other four with reasons. The original C, "declare every plugin option in the registry", is kept below as B because #171 rejected it for two of the four):
   - **A (least): the README table stays the source.** It already disagrees with the registry: it omits `discoveryRetry`.
   - **B (middle): register the remaining four too** (the original recommendation): `endpoint` and `socket` as aliases of `daemon.endpoint` and a socket setting, and `headless` and `daemonTools` as settings. The existing plugin-variable test then pins all of them, and #144 generates the table. The cost is the one #171 recorded: `headless` and `daemonTools` default to something computed at boot, so any declared default is wrong in one of the two realms the plugin runs in. `MCPX_SOCKET` is also read before any settings exist.
   - **C (recommended): generate the table from the registry's `plugin.*` settings plus a declared list of the non-setting options.** Move `pluginEnvAllowed` out of the test into a non-test declaration that gives each entry its option name, variable, default description and effect. The test and the generator both read it. That declaration is the plugin slice of #172's table of non-setting variables, so use #172's shape rather than inventing one. This keeps #171's reasoning, needs no behaviour change, and makes the README and docs table impossible to leave incomplete, which is exactly how `discoveryRetry` went missing.

### `plugins#opencode-v1-plugin`

What ships today:

- the files, the install commands and why `mcpx/` must stay a subdirectory;
- skills installation;
- options via config;
- what gets injected (README "What gets injected"; `minimal`/`standard`/`full` via `plugin.env`);
- the tools: `mcpx_discover`, `mcpx_exec` and `mcpx_observe`, off by default because each adds a tool to every request; plus the daemon tools;
- `instructions`, `toolTiming`, trace ids, the TUI picker.

One paragraph on interplay with opencode's own code mode (`OPENCODE_EXPERIMENTAL_CODE_MODE`, #149 `faq#opencode-code-mode`): the two do not conflict, and the plugin needs nothing in opencode's `mcp` config.

Install friction is real: `cp -R` by hand, and the Nix config does not install it. Open question 4 asks whether the page should promise a packaged install.

### `plugins#opencode-v2-plugin`

**Approaches: documenting something not yet built.**

- **A (least recommended): leave it out until #47 ships.** The notes list it, and a v2 user who lands on the plugin pages would find nothing about their version, not even that nothing exists.
- **B (middle): document the planned design** (the §4 lists: unnecessary / possible / breaks / same). This is accurate as a design, but it reads as a feature, and a reader will try it.
- **C (recommended): a short status section.** It says: "Not built; tracked in #47. On opencode v2 today:"
  1. shell + `AGENTS.md` works, with no session id, so `session`-scoped servers are isolated per call;
  2. alternatively add `mcpx serve --transport stdio` to v2's `mcp` config.

  It also states what the rewrite will change, in four bullets taken from §4, and links the compendium (#152) for the full design.

  One caveat for option 2: v2 defaults MCP servers to code mode, so mcpx's own tools end up wrapped inside v2's code mode. `OPENCODE-V2.md` records that v2 ships `mcp-codemode-defaults.ts` to turn that off for servers that are themselves code mode. Whether it recognises mcpx is unknown (open question 3).

  This is honest, useful today, and cannot be mistaken for a shipped feature.

### `plugins#vibemcp`

The term does not appear in the repo, in `~/git`, or in the other notes (`rg -il 'vibe.?mcp'` finds only the notes files). A web search on 2026-09-30 found four unrelated projects with the name:

| project | what it is | relevance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [VibeTensor/vibemcp](https://github.com/VibeTensor/vibemcp) (`@vibetensor/vibemcp`) | a Gmail + Microsoft 365 MCP server that returns TOON rather than JSON, "One server. Two ecosystems. Half the tokens." | the same concern as mcpx (tokens), addressed inside one server's output format |
| [VibeTechnologies/vibe-mcp](https://github.com/VibeTechnologies/vibe-mcp) (`@vibebrowser/mcp`) | browser automation that lets "multiple AI agents control the same browser simultaneously" through a relay daemon | the Chrome problem again, solved the opposite way: a *shared* browser, where mcpx gives each session its own |
| [VibeCodingInc/vibe-mcp](https://github.com/VibeCodingInc/vibe-mcp) (`slashvibe-mcp`) | presence and DMs between developers across coding sessions | none |
| [Jinjos/vibe-mcp](https://github.com/Jinjos/vibe-mcp) | AI coding-rules management for `vibe-cli` | none |

Candidate readings, for the user to choose from (open question 1):

1. **"Vibe-coding an MCP server": getting tools without writing a server.** mcpx already does three versions of this:
   - a command-line program becomes tools through `paths.adapters` (`mcpx adapter`);
   - an OpenAPI document becomes tools through `mcpx api --spec` or `paths.apis`;
   - a saved script or recipe runs by name (`mcpx recipes`, `mcpx run`).

   Caveat: adapter and OpenAPI tools are MCP tools, not script namespaces, so they are absent from `tools.<ns>` (#102). #83 plans to make them first-class. If this is the reading, the page probably moves out of the plugin block, to `configuration#server-config` or an "extending mcpx" page.
2. **A named external project**, most plausibly the multi-agent browser (VibeTechnologies). It would appear as a comparison, or as a server known to work behind mcpx.
3. **Vibe-coding *with* mcpx:** the user describes a task and gets a script back (`mcpx prompt`, recipes, `POST /v1/intent`; `docs/consumer.md`).
4. **A planned name** for an mcpx mode or product not yet written down anywhere.

Until this is answered, the page map keeps the item verbatim at `plugins#vibemcp`, and the page holds a one-line placeholder rather than a guess.

## Open questions

1. **What does "vibeMcp" mean?** One of the four readings above, or something else? This decides whether the page stays under plugins.
2. **Plugin config source (Approach C in interface & config):** ~~register the six extra plugin options in the registry?~~ #171 registered two and allowlisted four with reasons. Is that split final? And should the README table be generated from the registry plus #172's declared list, as C proposes?
3. **opencode v2 as an MCP host of mcpx:** does v2's code-mode default wrap mcpx's `mcpx_exec`, and should mcpx declare itself so `mcp-codemode-defaults.ts` turns code mode off for it?
4. **Packaging:** should the v1 plugin be installable from the Nix config or a release artifact before the page describes installing it? Or does the page document the `cp -R` flow as-is (#158)?
5. **The compatibility matrix:** who fills in the "unknown" cells for codex, claude code, pi and manus? #48 is where the work lives. The docs should not claim support before an adapter exists.

Docs checks run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S-M (mostly assembly from `plugin/opencode/README.md` and `docs/opencode-plugin.md`; the config table waits on the registry decision; vibeMcp waits on the user) · **Impact** med: it matters to every opencode user and to anyone porting to another harness · **Depends on / related:** #94, #44 (closed, fixed in #53), #47, #48, #80, #82, #83, #102, #88, #146, #147, #149, #144, #158, #152, #153, #159 (item 9: the plugin option sources; item 13: the `MCPX_SESSION` doc line), #172 (the declared list of non-setting variables that Approach C builds on)

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#292 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): The session-recording tooling idea (a tool/plugin to accept AI session recordings, append-only JSONL) is agent/fleet infrastructure, not nix configuration. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

---

Today an agent session produced roughly a dozen observations worth keeping and every one would have died with the session. They are now hand-appended to `~/git/ai_recordings.jsonl`, and `instructions/recordings.md` asks agents to keep doing that (wired into `opencode.jsonc`). This issue is for the tooling that should eventually replace the hand-append.

## What gets recorded

The moments an agent **already stops to explain to the user**. That framing is the whole trick — it needs no new judgement call, just a second destination for something already being written:

- a significant discovery
- a mistake the agent made, including miscounted or stale numbers
- a subagent that ignored its brief, *or* followed it too rigidly
- a review finding that was wrong, or right for the wrong reason
- a fix that made things worse
- a tool that lied — reported success while the thing it checked was broken
- anything producing surprise, guilt, irritation or relief

Real examples from the first session:

- *"Adding a 120s ceiling without an outstanding-worker guard made pool exhaustion **faster** than the bug it fixed — before the ceiling, a user hammering retry was throttled by the hang itself."*
- *"The test was shaped like the assumption under test."* (An httpx float `timeout=30` is four independent inactivity limits, not a total deadline; the stub modelled it as one budget, so the test certified the same misunderstanding as the code.)
- *"I told the agent `__proto__` was the same family as `hasOwnProperty`. It measured, and it is the only name with that divergence — a transport hazard, not a runtime one. My framing would have sent the fix to the wrong layer."*
- *"The verifier had five independent soundness bugs, and the entire cutover proof rested on it."*

## Schema — deliberately almost none

**`sentiment` is `any`.** A dict of arrays (`{"positive": [...], "negative": [...]}`), a bare `"good"`, a tag list, `{"fixed": true}` — whatever expresses it. Do not make agents flatten a feeling to fit a shape; the flattening is where the signal goes.

A starting shape, all fields optional, unknown keys allowed:

```json
{"ts":"2026-09-30T22:41:00Z","pwd":"/where/it/happened","repo":"operations-portal","origin":"git@github.com:org/repo.git","kind":"short-slug","sentiment":{"positive":["measured instead of trusting the brief"],"negative":["my framing sent it to the wrong layer"]},"note":"What happened, with evidence.","lesson":"What to do differently."}
```

Three submission styles should all be accepted, because all three beat silence:

1. **Copy the segment sent to the user**, plus a sentiment tail. Lowest effort, still useful.
2. **Loosely structured, would fail a parser.** `category=bad judgement | finding: ... | result: ... {grade: F, ...}`. Normalise later.
3. **Fully populated schema** with the real request/response objects embedded. Ideal.

Only hard rule: **append, never edit or rewrite**. Reading is allowed but not required.

## What the tool should do

- Accept a line over some cheap interface — a CLI (`record '<json>'`), an opencode plugin hook, or an MCP tool. Cheapest possible call site; an agent mid-task will not stop for ceremony.
- **Never reject.** A malformed line costs one normalisation pass later; a rejected line costs the observation permanently, and the observation is the scarce part. Quarantine unparseable input to a sibling file rather than erroring.
- Stamp what the agent would otherwise have to gather: timestamp, `pwd`, repo common dir, origin URL, session id, model, maybe git HEAD.
- Rotate by size, like the JSONL journals elsewhere in this config.
- Be a no-op when the target is unwritable — recording must never fail a task.

Later, a dedicated agent extracts these into a database. That is why detail now is cheap and absence is permanent.

## Open questions

- Should the plugin capture automatically (on subagent completion, on a failed gate) or stay agent-initiated? Automatic capture gets volume; agent-initiated gets judgement. Probably both, tagged by origin.
- Per-repo files or one global? Currently global at `~/git/ai_recordings.jsonl` with `repo`/`origin` fields, which keeps cross-repo patterns visible.
- Is there a privacy boundary? Recordings quote real failure text and file paths, and a leak like `DETAIL: Key (secret)=(...)` was found in a log path today. Probably worth reusing whatever redaction the host repo already has.
- A `schema.md` with all-optional fields, common value types, and notes on when each is used — useful without becoming a gate.

Related: `instructions/recordings.md`, `opencode.jsonc` (instructions array).

## Acceptance criteria

- A tool (CLI or plugin) appends a recording entry to the recordings file in the documented JSONL shape, replacing the hand-append workflow described in the issue.
- All schema fields are optional and unknown keys are preserved; `sentiment` accepts any shape (string, list, or dict of arrays) without flattening or validation loss.
- Appends are append-only and safe under concurrent agent sessions (no truncation or interleaved partial lines).
- `instructions/recordings.md` / `opencode.jsonc` wiring points agents at the tool instead of the manual file edit.
- A round-trip test shows an entry written by the tool reads back byte-identical in the fields the agent supplied.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#7 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Already shipped

Placeholders take arguments and users can declare their own:

```
@console(header, prefix)            # arguments naming fragments
@timed(entry, "the script")         # a user-declared placeholder
// @mcpx:placeholder timed(body, label)
```

Declarations come from a comment, an exported `MCPX_PLACEHOLDER` constant, or
the filename, on `paths.placeholders`.

Since this was filed (checked at 05c78b2):

- **#75: launchers apply to inline snippets too.** `mcpx exec '<ts>'` now goes
  through the launcher like a file, and `--launcher`, `--no-launcher`,
  `--allow-repeat` are honoured for both (`internal/cli/commands.go:461-470`,
  `:748-785`). The two shapes still differ on purpose: a snippet gets
  `@prefix`/`@suffix` spliced into its own scope (they may declare bindings), a
  file gets them wrapped around its import (they may act, not declare). Anything
  below that moves code between fragments -- import hoisting especially -- has to
  work for both shapes.
- **#73: a launcher is named for its contents.** The generated entry is the hash
  of the expanded launcher, so two runs of one script with different placeholder
  fills are two files, not one overwritten file (`internal/runner/runner.go`,
  #73). Placeholder features no longer risk the last-writer-wins bug.
- **The near-miss check only knows built-in names.** `checkUnknown` treats
  declared names as known, but `looksLikePlaceholder` compares a misspelling only
  against the built-ins, and the "available are" list names only built-ins
  (`internal/launcher/template.go:299-358`). So `@baner` for a declared `@banner`
  passes through as literal text. #186 (#181 collision 6) owns what "close"
  means across search, diagnostics and the launcher; this issue should feed
  declared names into it, and namespacing below changes what a name is.

## What is left

### Arguments that are expressions

Today an argument either names a placeholder or is literal. `@timed(entry,
"label")` works; `@timed(entry, config.name)` does not, because there is no
evaluation, only substitution.

Probably correct as-is. Substitution that cannot compute is easy to reason
about, and the generated file is TypeScript that can compute for itself.
Worth revisiting only if real templates keep wanting it.

### Default arguments in a declaration

```
// @mcpx:placeholder timed(body, label = "unnamed")
```

Small, obvious, not yet done. (Still true: the declaration's parameter list is
split on commas only, so `label = "unnamed"` becomes a parameter literally named
that -- `internal/launcher/define.go:119`, `:163-170`.)

### Declarations that pull in dependencies

A fragment needing an import has to assume the header provides it. Letting a
declaration state its imports, hoisted and deduplicated into the header, would
make fragments genuinely self-contained.

This is the one with real value and real design cost: it means parsing import
statements, merging specifiers, and deciding what happens when two fragments
import the same name from different modules.

### Namespacing

Two projects each declaring `@banner` cannot both be on the path. Refused
today, which is right, but a prefix (`@mine:banner`) would let both exist.
Nobody has hit this yet. (Still refused: `Bind`, `internal/launcher/define.go:203-233`.)

## Notes

The single-resolution rule already handles the composition concern from the
original note: if `@console` uses `@header` and `@prefix`, and the template
also uses them directly, that is a repeat and is refused unless named in
`plumbing.launcherPlaceholderRepeat` (`internal/settings/registry.go:529`) or
`--allow-repeat` (honoured for snippets since #75). So "as long as those weren't
used in two places once put together" is enforced rather than assumed.

No real choice for three of the four items (expressions: leave; defaults: do;
namespacing: a prefix, when someone hits it). The one open design is import
hoisting -- how two fragments importing the same name from different modules are
resolved -- and it must hold for both the snippet and the file shape.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (defaults S; import hoisting is the M) · **Impact** med.

Related: #186 (one near-miss matcher; the launcher's is one of the two today),
#81 and #112 (the `script.*` phases these placeholders splice are one of the
hook vocabularies #81 reconciles, collision 2), #83 (recipes share the
`@param` header spelling).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

title: mcpx docs: level-2 page map, and the configuration, modes and transport pages
body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#146 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #94

## Summary

Level 2 is the layer a person reads right after installing mcpx. The notes set its bar: "basically a more normal set of docs", and "new person might assume this is all there is and wont be upset". So level 2 has to be complete by itself. Every page answers its question in full. A link to the compendium can offer history or a deeper "why", but never the rest of the answer.

This issue does two things:

1. **The page map.** It maps all 30 items the notes list to a page and an anchor, and records for each one the repo material to draw on, the issue that writes it (#146 to #149), and which parts come from the generated reference (#144).
2. **Content for the first seven items:** common config, server config, client config, env vars, client modes, transport options and server modes.

While reading the code for this, I found three places where current docs or behaviour contradict each other. The pages must not copy them (see "Findings" below).

## Original notes

Source-notes lines 1, 2, 7 and 49-82. Lines 49-59 are this issue's content, and lines 53-82 as a whole are the page map. The lines in between are quoted in sibling issues.

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 'ok i just installed this thing what even is it' layer
>         - basically a more normal set of docs
>         - new person might assume this is all there is and wont be upset
>         - a page or section in a page for
>           - common config
>           - server config
>           - client config
>           - env vars
>           - client modes
>           - transport options
>           - server modes
>           - abstract interfaces
>           - client interfaces
>           - cli
>           - cli arguments
>           - cli commands
>           - mcp
>           - mcp sdk
>           - mcp compatibility
>           - binary
>           - script
>           - /v1
>           - /v1 sdk
>           - plugins
>           - plugin compatibility
>           - plugin interface & config
>           - opencode v1 plugin
>           - opencode v2 plugin
>           - vibeMcp
>           - "so why'd you get rid of all the mcp and then make one, do you like mcp or not"
>           - "i mean, opencodemode is right there"
>           - "is it safe?", no.
>           - "but why would you.."
>           - "but can i get some examples?"

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

Paths are relative to `pkgs/mcpx/` on `main` (`d0b7e01`); re-checked at `05c78b2` in the 2026-09-30 issues pass, and drifted line numbers re-cited.

| topic | where it is documented today | shape |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sources, precedence, scope, hot, reaching settings | `docs/configuration.md` "Where a value can come from", "Scope: who reads it", "Hot", "Reaching them" | prose, good; reusable nearly as-is |
| every setting | `docs/configuration.md` "Every setting" | hand-regenerated table; `internal/settings/docs_test.go` fails on a missing path or `MCPX_*` name |
| the server block | `internal/config/config.go:24-157`; story.md "Sharing and scope", "Profiles and aliases", "Remote servers without a shim"; `docs/configuration.md` "Servers" | no single page describes the whole shape |
| config file search | `internal/config/config.go:528-590` | only in code. The man page FILES section (`internal/cli/manual.go`, `ManPage`) lists 2 of the 9 locations |
| client ladder | story.md "Running without a daemon", "One daemon, many clients"; `docs/exec.md` "Where a script runs" | prose |
| transports | `docs/protocol.md` §5; story.md "What each transport costs", "Server-sent events, not WebSockets"; `docs/dependencies.md` "Network" | spread over four files |
| mcpx as MCP server | story.md "mcpx speaks MCP"; `docs/protocol.md` §2, §5 | prose |

Commands used below that are in `Commands()` (`internal/cli/manual.go`): `config`, `settings`, `servers`, `init`, `ls`, `status`, `daemon`, `daemons`, `stop`, `exec`, `run`, `tui`, `explore`. Two commands this issue has to mention are dispatched (`cmd/mcpx/main.go:119-161`) but missing from `Commands()`: `serve` and `registry`. #147 covers that gap.

### Findings the pages must not copy

1. **The file key is `mcpServers`, not `servers`.** `Config.MCPServers` is `json:"mcpServers"` (`config.go:161`). The package comment explains the choice: it is "the same `mcpServers` object that Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Codex and most other MCP hosts already use", and mcpx's own options go under a per-server `"mcpx"` key that other hosts ignore (`config.go:3-6`). "servers" is the name of the CLI command and the `/v1` resource (`mcpx servers`, `/v1/servers`). The page has to show both names and say which one goes where.
2. **`mcpx init` writes a starter config that does not do what its comments say.** `starterConfig` (`internal/cli/commands.go:1379-1407`) sets `"mode": "shared"` and `"mode": "session"` (`:1390`, `:1400`; still true at `05c78b2`). `mode` was split into `sharing` and `scope` (story.md "Sharing and scope": "A single `mode` setting used to answer both questions at once ... They are now separate"). `Extras` has no `mode` field (`config.go:90-128`), and the loader's `json.Unmarshal` (`config.go:695`) drops unknown fields. So the chrome-devtools entry, which the comment describes as "One browser per script run, up to 4 at once", actually gets the defaults `shared`/`global`: one browser shared by everyone. That is the exact failure mcpx exists to prevent. This is a bug outside docs, filed as #159 item 2. It has to be fixed before the quick start (#157) tells anyone to run `mcpx init`. The top-level `mcpx help` text teaches the same dead key in its CONCURRENCY block (`internal/cli/root.go:597-604`, with a `pooled` value that does not exist). The pages must teach `sharing`/`scope` and copy neither.
3. **The config search path is wider than anything documented.** `SearchPathFrom` (`config.go:542-579`) works like this:
   - If `MCPX_CONFIG` is set, that one file is used and nothing else is read.
   - Otherwise, at each directory from the working directory up to `/`, it checks `.config/mcpx/config.json`, `.mcpx.json`, `.mcpx/config.json` and **`.mcp.json`**.
   - Then it checks `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mcpx/config.json`, `~/.config/mcpx/config.json`, `~/.mcpx.json` and `/etc/mcpx/config.json`.
   - Files are merged per server name and the nearest one wins. `"disabled": true` drops a server inherited from a farther file. An explicit `--config` is used alone (`config.go:581-590`).

   `.mcp.json` is Claude Code's project file, which means mcpx picks up a project's Claude Code servers. That is useful, and nothing says so today. `paths.config` is declared in the registry but nothing reads it (#5).

Two smaller points the pages have to get right:

- **Environment variables outside the registry.** Many `MCPX_*` names appear in non-test code (`internal`, `cmd`, `plugin`) and not in `docs/configuration.md`. This issue counted roughly 49. #172 counts 44 undeclared of 64 referenced, at `8001f23`, and owns the count and the allowlist (#181 collision 17), so the page uses #172's list. Some are registry aliases (`MCPX_LOG_LEVEL` and `MCPX_STATE_DIR` both appear in `internal/settings/registry.go`). The rest fall into five groups:
  - config selection: `MCPX_CONFIG`, `config.go:549`
  - caller identity: `MCPX_SESSION_ID` and `MCPX_PARENT_SESSION_ID`, set by the plugin at `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:670,713`
  - names the generated client reads: `MCPX_ENDPOINT`, `MCPX_SESSION`, `MCPX_SOCKET` (`internal/codegen/emit.go:252-268`), `MCPX_CONFIG_PATH` (`:411`), `MCPX_RUNTIME` (`:883`) and others. mcpx sets these for the scripts it runs. `MCPX_SESSION` is the run's session key: `--session`, else the harness's `MCPX_SESSION_ID`, else a fresh key (`internal/cli/commands.go:537-545`). It is derived from `MCPX_SESSION_ID`, not a misspelling of it (#159 item 13, struck).
  - plugin-only options: `MCPX_PLUGIN_DAEMON_TOOLS`, `_HEADLESS` and `MCPX_SOCKET`, in `plugin/opencode/README.md` "Configuration". These are allowlisted with reasons in `pluginEnvAllowed` (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:188-200`). `MCPX_PLUGIN_REMEMBER` and `_ANNOTATE` were in this group until #171 made them the settings `plugin.remember` and `plugin.annotate`.
  - harness context the plugin injects: `MCPX_HARNESS*`, `MCPX_SESSION_*` and `MCPX_OPENCODE_*`

  An env-var page generated only from the registry would leave all of these out.
- **Upstream "sse" is not the legacy SSE transport.** `POST /v1/servers` accepts `transport: stdio|http|sse` (`internal/api/ops_settings.go:100`). But the pool builds only two things: a stdio transport, or `mcpclient.NewHTTP` (`internal/pool/pool.go:368-380`). `NewHTTP` is Streamable HTTP whose replies may arrive as an SSE stream (`internal/mcpclient/http.go:18-23`, `:144`). I found no client for the deprecated 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE transport, the one with a separate `GET` stream and an `endpoint` event. So in mcpx, "SSE" upstream means the SSE framing inside Streamable HTTP. The transport page must say this, not imply support for SSE-only servers (open question 5).

## Part 1: the page map

### Approaches: page granularity

**Approach A (least recommended): one page per item, 30 pages.** Each item gets a URL of its own for free. But at least a third of the items are one or two paragraphs: "mcp sdk", "/v1 sdk", "binary", "client config", "vibeMcp", and each FAQ question. The result is a 30-entry sidebar, the same context repeated at the top of every thin page, and a cross-link every time two items touch (client modes vs transport options vs server modes are one topic seen from three sides). The agent twin (#120) inherits 30 tiny `.md` files that an agent has to fetch one by one. It also cuts against lines 50-51: a reader who lands on "client modes" alone gets a fragment, not "a more normal set of docs".

**Approach B (middle): everything in one long manual page with 30 sections.** In its favour: Ctrl-F finds everything, the agent twin is a single file, and there is nothing to navigate. Against it: config alone is several screens, and the page mixes three audiences (script writers, MCP-host integrators, harness-plugin authors). Every regeneration of an embedded generated table churns one huge file, and a new person facing one enormous page reads it as "this is a lot" rather than "this is all there is". Most generators produce a single-page print view from a multi-page book for free (mdBook's `print.html`, for example; #117 picks the generator). So B's benefits are best taken as a byproduct of C rather than as the structure.

**Approach C (recommended): about ten grouped pages, each item with a fixed anchor.** Every item keeps a URL of its own (`page#anchor`). Related items share a page so that each page is complete by itself. The print view gives B's benefits for free. Anchors are set explicitly rather than derived from headings, because headings like "plugin interface & config" and "/v1" slug badly and differently in each generator, and a renamed heading must not break links. Recommended because it is the only option that satisfies lines 50-51 (complete, unintimidating) and still gives the user's list one addressable place per item.

### The map (Approach C)

The navigation order follows the notes. Open question 3 asks whether task order would be better.

| # | Item (verbatim) | Page `#anchor` | Source material in the repo | Written by | Generated part (#144) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 53 | common config | `configuration#common-config` | `docs/configuration.md` "Where a value can come from", "Scope", "Hot", "Reaching them"; `config.go:528-590`; `manual.go` entries `config`, `settings`, `init` | #146 | link to the settings table; no copy |
| 54 | server config | `configuration#server-config` | `config.go:24-157`; story.md "Sharing and scope", "Profiles and aliases", "Remote servers without a shim"; `docs/configuration.md` "Servers"; `manual.go` `servers` | #146 | open: a JSON Schema for the file (`pool.*` rows are generated) |
| 55 | client config | `configuration#client-config` | `docs/configuration.md` "Scope: who reads it"; registry rows with scope `client` and `call` | #146 | the client- and call-scoped settings, filtered from the registry |
| 56 | env vars | `configuration#env-vars` | `docs/configuration.md` "variable" column; the names listed in Findings above | #146 | registry names generated; the others hand-written until declared |
| 57 | client modes | `modes#client-modes` | story.md "Running without a daemon", "One daemon, many clients"; `docs/exec.md` "Where a script runs"; `AGENTS.md` "Profiles" | #146 | - |
| 58 | transport options | `modes#transport-options` | `docs/protocol.md` §5; story.md "What each transport costs", "Server-sent events, not WebSockets", "Lossless reconnection", "Remote servers without a shim"; `docs/dependencies.md` "Network" | #146 | - |
| 59 | server modes | `modes#server-modes` | story.md "mcpx speaks MCP", "Sharing and scope"; `docs/protocol.md` §5 | #146 | - |
| 60 | abstract interfaces | `interfaces#abstract-interfaces` | `internal/api/ops*.go`; `docs/parity.md` | #147 | the parity table |
| 61 | client interfaces | `interfaces#client-interfaces` | `mcpx client`; `internal/codegen`; `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts` `DaemonClient` | #147 | - |
| 62 | cli | `cli#cli` | `AGENTS.md` "The loop"; `cmd/mcpx/main.go` | #147 | - |
| 63 | cli arguments | `cli#cli-arguments` | `cmd/mcpx/main.go:61-104`; `internal/settings/bind.go` | #147 | per-command registry flags |
| 64 | cli commands | `cli#cli-commands` | `internal/cli/manual.go` `Commands()` | #147 | yes: the whole command table |

**Rule for generated content at level 2.** When a page needs reference data, such as the client-scoped settings on `configuration#client-config`, it embeds the relevant slice generated from the same source instead of just linking to the full reference. Linking would break "this is all there is". Embedding means #144 has to support filtered embeds (for example "settings where scope = client"), not only whole pages.

## Part 2: content for the seven pages

### `configuration#common-config`

- **Where config lives.** List the search path from Finding 3 exactly, in order, including `.mcp.json` and `MCPX_CONFIG`. Show `mcpx config --path` (the nearest file), `--sources` (every file that contributed and which server each defined), `--defaults` (the built-in layer from `internal/defaults/defaults.json`) and `--schema [--plumbing]` (every setting with its flag and variable).
- **Format.** JSONC, with comments allowed (`config.StripJSONC`). The top level holds `mcpServers`, the `pool` defaults block, and any registry setting at its dotted path. Open question 4 covers the top-level `runtime`/`permissions` keys.
- **Precedence.** default < file (nearest wins) < env < flag < runtime (`docs/configuration.md` "Where a value can come from"). `mcpx settings get <path>` shows the winning value and what it displaced, which answers "why is this not what my config says".
- **Scope and hot.** One paragraph each, reused from `docs/configuration.md`. Use the example that motivated scopes: a flag given to a command, for something the already-running daemon reads, used to be silently ignored.
- **Changing settings.** `mcpx settings list|get|set|unset [--persist runtime|project|user]`, `mcpx settings list --daemon`, and the matching `/v1/settings` and `mcpx_settings_*` rows (the "Reaching them" table).
- **Starting.** `mcpx init [--global]` writes `.mcpx.json` or `~/.config/mcpx/config.json`, but only once Finding 2 is fixed. Until then, the page shows a hand-written starter.
- **`paths.config`.** Until #5 lands, the page states that the search path is fixed and that `MCPX_CONFIG` and `--config` are the only overrides. It must not advertise `paths.config`, `--paths-config` or `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG`. `docs/configuration.md:336` lists them, and the settings guard's allowlist claims `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` is read, but nothing reads it (#159 item 19).

### `configuration#server-config`

- **Shape of one entry**, from `config.go:91-157`:
  - Stdio servers: `command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd`.
  - Remote servers: `url`, `transport`, `headers`.
  - Any server: `auth`, `protocol` (`legacy` | `modern` | `force-legacy` | `force-modern`), `aliasOf`.
  - The `mcpx` block: `sharing`, `scope`, `max`, `min`, `idleTimeout`, `callTimeout`, `startTimeout`, `namespace`, `disabled`, `logging`, `prelude`, `profiles`, `default`, `description`, `tools`, `excludeTools`.
  - Each entry needs one of `command`, `url` or `aliasOf` (`config.go:703-705`). A `url` with no `transport` means `http` (`:706-708`).
- **The top-level `pool` block** sets defaults for every server's `mcpx` block. It uses the same names as the `pool.*` settings (`config.go:163-167`).
- **Sharing × scope.** Two independent axes. Include the story.md table: `shared`/`exclusive`, and `global`/`repo`/`worktree`/`cwd`/`session`/`parent-session`/`pid`/`call`. Include the degrade rule: `session` without an id falls back to per-call isolation and logs once. Give a stateful and a stateless worked example; the chrome-devtools one from story.md is right, the one from `mcpx init` is not.
- **Profiles and aliases**, including how the profile selection also limits the generated client.
- **Adding servers live.** `mcpx servers add|remove|list`, and `mcpx registry add` (dispatched but not in `Commands()`; see #147). The same operations exist as `/v1/servers` and `mcpx_servers_*`. `daemon.watchConfig` reloads after hand edits within `daemon.reapInterval`. Servers whose definition did not change keep their process.
- **Compatibility.** An existing `mcpServers` object pastes in unchanged, and other hosts ignore the `mcpx` key. The page also says that `.mcp.json` is picked up.
- **Naming.** The namespace is the server name with non-identifier characters replaced (`fancy-name` becomes `fancy_name`, per `AGENTS.md`), unless `mcpx.namespace` overrides it.
- **Not servers (yet).** `paths.adapters` and `paths.apis` produce MCP tools, not namespaces (#102, #83). The page links them but does not present them as a kind of server.

### `configuration#client-config`

This interprets "client config" as the settings read by the process you run: the CLI and the scripts it launches (scope `client`), plus the per-request `call` scope. The page covers:

- `daemon.endpoint`, `daemon.autostart`, `daemon.inline`, `autostart.*`, `output.*`, `logging.format`, `script.*`, `paths.*`, `http.requestTimeout`, `registry.*`, `doctor.timeout`, `events.reconnect`. This list is a generated embed.
- How call-scoped settings travel with each request in `X-Mcpx-Settings`, and why only call-scoped ones are honoured from that header.
- Why `mcpx settings list` (which is what the client resolves) and `mcpx settings list --daemon` can legitimately differ.

A second reading, "how to configure an MCP client (a host) to use mcpx", belongs in `modes#server-modes`, with a one-line pointer from here (open question 2).

### `configuration#env-vars`

**Approaches.**

- **A (least): a hand-written list.** It drifts. The 44 unlisted names #172 found show that it already has.
- **B (middle): generate the registry part, hand-write the rest.** Complete today, but nothing stops a new unlisted name tomorrow.
- **C (recommended): declare every externally meaningful non-setting variable once** (identity, script-facing, plugin-only, harness context), next to the registry, with a test that fails on any `MCPX_[A-Z_]+` literal in non-test code that is neither a setting nor declared. The whole page is then generated. This follows the pattern `docs/configuration.md` already describes for the plugin ("a test pins them"; since #171 that is `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` plus `pluginEnvAllowed`). #172 owns the declaration and its test (#181 collision 17), and #144/#145 generate the page from it. This issue only needs the page to be complete.

The page groups variables by who sets them: you (settings), the host or harness (identity and context), and mcpx for your script (endpoint, runtime). It publishes derived names as they are, for example `MCPX_DAEMON_LEASE_T_T_L` (`docs/configuration.md:216`), unless #144 adds explicit names.

### `modes#client-modes`

This is an interpretation, flagged as such (open question 1). "Client mode" is read as how a command reaches the servers. That is a ladder, which story.md "Running without a daemon" states:

| rung | how | set by | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. socket | an existing local daemon | default | 0.17 ms per request with keep-alive |
| 2. url | a named daemon elsewhere | `daemon.endpoint` = `http://host:port` or `unix:///path` | stops the ladder: no autostart, no local fallback ("would silently answer from the wrong machine") |
| 3. spawn | start a daemon, then use it | `daemon.autostart` (default true); idles out after `autostart.idleExit` (4h) | about 23 ms, once |
| 4. inline | servers inside this process | `daemon.inline` (default false) | nothing is kept warm; a browser dies with the command. Include the lifetime table from story.md |

Settings that apply across every rung:

- **Where a script runs:** `exec.where` = `auto|local|remote`, also `--local`/`--remote` (`docs/exec.md` "Where a script runs"). `--local` against a remote daemon is refused.
- **Which servers are visible:** `--profile`, `--skip-default`, `--all-profiles`.
- **Output shape:** `--json`, and `exec.output` = `text|structured|stream`.
- **Interactive vs scripted:** `mcpx tui`, `mcpx explore`, and bare `mcpx`, which opens the TUI when there is a terminal and prints help otherwise (`cmd/mcpx/main.go:107-116`).

Supervision: `mcpx daemon [--detached]` runs the daemon in the foreground. Installing it as a service is `status: proposed` in story.md "Service installation", and the page must say so.

### `modes#transport-options`

One table for each direction, because "transport" means different things on the two sides of mcpx.

**Upstream (mcpx talking to MCP servers):**

| transport | config | notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stdio | `command` | the default |
| Streamable HTTP | `url` (+ `transport: http`) | reply bodies may be SSE streams; `Mcp-Session-Id` is tracked and released with `DELETE` (story.md "Remote servers without a shim") |
| legacy HTTP+SSE | none | not implemented (Findings); open question 5 |
| protocol era | `protocol` | `docs/protocol.md` §1 |
| OAuth | none | not performed (`docs/protocol.md` §6) |

**Downstream (clients talking to mcpx):**

| transport | who uses it | where | cost / notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| unix socket | CLI, plugin | state directory, mode 0600 | 0.17 ms keep-alive |
| TCP loopback | generated script clients (`fetch` over a unix socket is not portable across the three runtimes) | `127.0.0.1`, ephemeral port, or `daemon.port` | 0.65 ms keep-alive |
| TCP beyond loopback | remote clients via `daemon.endpoint` | `daemon.address` + `daemon.port` | the API is unauthenticated and a warning is printed once |
| HTTP `/v1/*` | everything | every listener above | #147 |
| MCP Streamable HTTP `/mcp` | MCP hosts | every listener above; `proto.mcpPath`, `proto.serveMCP` | no extra listener, by design (`docs/protocol.md` §5 "Why not an extra listener") |
| MCP stdio | hosts that spawn their servers | `mcpx serve --transport stdio` (not in `Commands()`; #147) | `--transport http` was removed and fails naming `/mcp` instead (`internal/cli/serve.go:360-376`) |
| SSE `GET /v1/events` | plugin, TUI, scripts, curl | every listener | `Last-Event-ID` / `?since=N`; `gap` events; SSE rather than WebSockets |
| MCP `subscriptions/listen` | MCP clients | `/mcp` | only the four notification kinds the spec defines |

Include the spawn-versus-socket numbers and one sentence of why (story.md "What each transport costs"). State plainly that there is no tailnet-specific feature: remote access is `daemon.address` + `daemon.port` on the daemon and `daemon.endpoint` on clients.

### `modes#server-modes`

"Server" has three meanings in mcpx. Each subsection opens by saying which one it means.

1. **mcpx as an MCP server.** There are two ways in:
   - The daemon's `/mcp`: Streamable HTTP, shares the daemon's pooled servers and lifetime, and is disabled with `proto.serveMCP=false`.
   - `mcpx serve --transport stdio`: a thin shim for hosts that can only spawn a process.

   Cover what the host sees: a deliberately small tool surface with `mcpx_exec` as the tool that matters (story.md "mcpx speaks MCP"), plus one generated `mcpx_<operation>` tool per `/v1` operation (`docs/parity.md`). Include a copy-paste `mcpServers` snippet for putting mcpx into another host. That snippet is the second reading of "client config".
2. **Modes of an upstream server.** Sharing and scope, `min`/`max`, and the idle timeout. How to read them: the SHARING and SCOPE columns in `mcpx ls`, and the KEY column in `mcpx status`.
3. **Modes of the daemon process.** Autostarted and detached, foreground (`mcpx daemon`), inline, and the idle exits (`autostart.idleExit`, `daemon.idleExit`). Also `mcpx daemons` and `mcpx stop [--all]`, plus a pointer to #78 for state and cache behaviour.

## Open questions

1. **"client modes" and "server modes".** Is the ladder / three-meanings reading above what was meant? Other possible readings: the plugin's `backend` = `auto|v1|cli` (that is #148's), or human vs agent vs CI usage.
2. **"client config".** Does it mean mcpx's client-scoped settings (drafted above), or configuring an MCP host to use mcpx (drafted under server modes)? Both are covered. Which one owns the anchor?
3. **Navigation order.** The notes' order puts configuration first. Someone who has just installed mcpx arguably needs `scripts` and `cli` first. Keep the notes' order, or use task order?
4. **Top-level `runtime` and `permissions`.** `Config` also has top-level `runtime` and `permissions` keys (`config.go:181-184`), and `docs/dependencies.md` teaches "the `runtime` config key". The registry names are `script.runtime` and `script.permissions`, with flag aliases `--runtime` and `--permissions` (`registry.go:175-189`). Which spelling do the docs teach, and are the top-level keys legacy?
5. **Legacy SSE servers.** Does `transport: "sse"` work against an HTTP+SSE-only (2024-11-05) server? If not, should the enum reject it, or should mcpx implement the legacy transport? The page states whichever is true.
6. **The starter config (Finding 2).** Fixed where, and by whom? The quick start depends on it.
7. **Filtered embeds.** Can #144 provide filtered generated embeds (settings by scope, by prefix)? The "level 2 is complete" rule depends on it.

Docs checks run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (page map S; seven page drafts M) · **Impact** high: this is the backbone of level 2, and three of the pages correct things current docs get wrong · **Depends on / related:** #94, #5, #78, #83, #102, #88, #147, #148, #149, #144, #117, #120, #157, #152, #159 (Findings 2 and the env-var and `paths.config` points are filed there), #172 (owns the `MCPX_*` allowlist the env-var page is generated from)

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#1055 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): codex-remote-control home-manager module was relocated to code (#1044 / PR #1043); the finding (daemon dies mid-session, never restarted) was verified against the live code copy. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

## Finding

PR #1030's `codex-remote-control` home-manager module starts the Codex app-server daemon exactly once — at user-session activation — and nothing ever restarts it if the daemon dies mid-session. The unit is `Type=oneshot` + `RemainAfterExit`, so once `codex remote-control start` daemonizes and exits, systemd records the unit as active (exited) forever, regardless of whether the daemon process is still alive. A daemon crash, OOM kill, or a failed auto-update leaves the machine silently absent as a remote Codex environment until the next login/reboot or a manual `codex remote-control start` — with no signal anywhere, because the unit still shows active.

This is the exact failure the module's own header says motivated it: "Before this module the daemon was started ad-hoc only: it ran 2026-10-23..26 and died with the session, and nothing restarted it." The module fixes the login/boot case only; the died-mid-session case it names is still unhandled.

Cross-repo: the module was relocated out of this repo by PR #1043 (Drew's rule: laptop services live in the code flake), so the live copy is now in developing-today/code — and it carries the identical oneshot-only definition. One fix, tracked here (the repo where the change originated, per the cross-repo rule); the code copy is where the change lands.

## Evidence

- Source PR: dezren39/nix#1030 (merged, merge commit `2aebfa908c8ecde88b5f17bec9446156693aedb2`, commit `b839d749`), which added `modules/codex-remote-control.nix` for dezren39/nix#1028 / developing-today/code#1685.
- PR #1030 diff, `modules/codex-remote-control.nix` Service block: `Type = "oneshot"`, `RemainAfterExit = true`, `ExecStart = "${cfg.codexPath} remote-control start"`, `ExecStop = "${cfg.codexPath} remote-control stop"` — no `Restart`, no companion timer, no health check.
- Verified on the current live copy, developing-today/code `nixos/home/codex-remote-control.nix:60-64` (read 2026-10-28): the same oneshot-only Service block, unchanged by the relocation. No timer or watchdog for this service exists in either repo (grep of the module in both repos).
- Deduped 2026-10-28: no open or closed issue in dezren39/nix or developing-today/code covers daemon-death recovery for this service (dezren39/nix#1028 and code#1685 are the closed feature requests; dezren39/nix#1044 covers the relocation duplicates, a different finding).

## Why it matters

Remote control is the point of the service: when the daemon is down, the laptop simply doesn't appear as a Codex remote environment, and the failure is invisible — `systemctl --user status codex-remote-control` reports active. The 2026-10-23..26 silent-death incident in the module header is the precedent; the current design repeats it for any mid-session death.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] If the Codex daemon process dies while the user session is up, it is restarted automatically (e.g. a periodic timer/user service that checks `codex app-server daemon version` / the control socket and runs `remote-control start` when down), OR the module documents an explicit, deliberate decision that login-time start is sufficient, with the daemon-death symptom named.
- [ ] The mechanism (or the documented decision) is present in the live copy at developing-today/code `nixos/home/codex-remote-control.nix`; this repo carries no second copy (per #1044).
- [ ] A dead daemon is detectable: the check's result surfaces somewhere visible (unit state, log line) rather than the unit reporting active while the daemon is gone.

title: paths.config should govern the rest of the config chain

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#5 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #181

## Problem

`paths.config` is declared in the settings registry but nothing reads it. The
config search path is still the hardcoded upward walk in `config.SearchPath()`.

**Still true at 05c78b2** (#171 left it open on purpose). `paths.config` appears
in Go only at its declaration (`internal/settings/registry.go:270`) and in the
#171 guard's allowlist (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:67-70`).
`SearchPathFrom` (`internal/config/config.go:542-579`) reads `MCPX_CONFIG`,
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` and the home directory, nothing else.

One correction to what #171 recorded: the allowlist reason and
`docs/declared-but-unread.md:93-96` both say `config.SearchPath` reads
`MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` directly. It does not -- `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` occurs nowhere in
Go code outside that string. So the setting is inert through **all three**
channels, and `docs/configuration.md:336` advertises `--paths-config` and
`MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG`, both of which parse and do nothing. The allowlist entry is
defending a mechanism that does not exist.

That is the same advertised-but-inert failure fixed for `paths.scripts`,
`pool.*` and the logging group in #4, left in one place because the fix there
is genuinely harder.

## Why it is harder

Circular. To know where to look for config files you would read a setting —
which comes from a config file.

## Approaches

**A -- delete the setting.** Honest and immediate: a knob that parses and does
nothing is the #177 bug class. Loses the "a repo config can say also look here"
capability, which nobody can use today anyway.

**B -- environment and flag only.** Read `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` / `--paths-config`
before discovery and prepend (or splice) them into the search path; ignore the
key in files. Not circular, small, and it makes the allowlist sentence true. It
does not let a *file* extend the chain, which is the part the rest of this issue
is about.

**C -- recommended: the two-pass resolution below, with B as its first input.**
The environment/flag value seeds pass 1; files found then extend the chain in
pass 2. Recommended because it is the only option where the declared setting
means the same thing from all three channels, which is the registry's promise.

## Proposed resolution (Approach C)

Two passes, with the boundary stated rather than implied.

1. **Discovery pass.** Walk the default locations. Read only `paths.config`
   from whatever is found, honouring the null splice.
2. **Load pass.** Resolve that list and load everything on it, nearest last.

A file's `paths.config` therefore governs *the rest of the chain from that
point*, not the search that found the file itself. So a repo config can say
"also look here", and a parent cannot be redirected by a child it has never
read.

## Rules worth pinning

- A `paths.config` found in pass 2 that differs from pass 1 is **reported**,
  not silently applied. Applying it means re-running discovery with different
  roots, which can not terminate.
- A cycle (A adds B, B adds A) is refused by identity, the way the launcher
  refuses placeholder cycles.
- `MCPX_CONFIG` continues to win outright and skip both passes, because "this
  file, nothing else" has to stay expressible.

## Done when

- `paths.config` from a discovered file changes which files load afterwards
- a cycle is refused, naming the path that closed it
- `mcpx config --sources` shows both passes distinctly
- `MCPX_CONFIG` still bypasses everything

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S-M · **Impact** med -- small, and #103 assumes it; also the gate on what
a project config may add to the chain before hooks (#81) and plugin directories
(#80) make that a larger grant.

Related: #103 (assumes it), #81 and #80 (a project config that declares hooks or
a plugin search path is an escalation this rule has to allow for; #173's
warnings), #177 / #129 (the inert-setting class and the guard whose allowlist
reason is wrong here).

body:
## Phase 1 of #1834 — typed sampling errors

Design: #1834 (mcpx sampling trust boundary). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-sampling-trust-boundary.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Origin: dezren39/nix#256.

### Problem

Every sampling failure reaches the upstream as `-32603`. The 2025-11-25 sampling error table assigns `-1` to user rejection and `-32602` to tool-shape violations (tool result missing in a request; tool results mixed with other content), but mcpx produces neither: a declined sampling answer becomes `errors.New("the sampling request was " + action)` in `sampleViaBroker` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/hooks.go`), an expired/cancelled wait becomes the raw broker `Await` error, and `Client.answer`'s handler wrap (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpclient/modern.go` ~L296-303) flattens every handler error to `&rpcError{Code: -32603}`. Gap: `sampling-client-errors-user-rejected-and-tool-shape` in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/conformance/coverage_clientfeatures.go`.

### Scope

- A typed sampling-rejection error in the daemon sampling path, carrying its JSON-RPC code.
- Answerer **decline or cancel** of a sampling question surfaces to the upstream as **`-1`** with the action named in the message.
- **Expiry / no answerer stays `-32603`**, with a message explicitly naming expiry — nobody chose, so it is not a rejection. Do not map it to `-1`.
- `Client.answer`'s handler-error wrap preserves a typed error's code instead of flattening it to `-32603` (typed errors pass through; untyped handler errors keep today's `-32603`).
- Define the `-32602` tool-shape error type here so Phase 2 (#1834's validation phase) raises it; Phase 1 does not itself add content checks.

Out of scope: any message/result validation (Phase 2), CLI rendering (Phase 3), elicitation error paths (untouched), sampling rate limits (nix#257).

### Tests (defining)

- Declined sampling answer → upstream sees `-1` naming the decline.
- Cancelled sampling answer → upstream sees `-1`.
- Expired wait (broker TTL) → upstream sees `-32603` with expiry named in the message.
- Untyped handler failure → still `-32603`.
- Elicitation decline/cancel behaviour unchanged (existing tests pass).

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=design-architect state=filed at=2026-10-28T21:34:31Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- Declined/cancelled sampling reaches the upstream as `-1`; expired waits as `-32603` naming expiry; the typed-error passthrough in `Client.answer` is covered by tests in both the legacy wire path and the modern `input_required` path (the answer path is shared — verify both).
- Gap `sampling-client-errors-user-rejected-and-tool-shape` is retired for its `-1` half; the `-32602` half is exercised end-to-end by Phase 2.
- No elicitation error behaviour changes.

title: id(tag): --value-hex refuses an uppercase 0X prefix as an 'invalid hex digit' and silently accepts a doubled 0x0x prefix — hex_decode's prefix strip is lowercase-only and repeats
