labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`id tag set/del --value-hex` documents its hex input as "case-insensitive, optional `0x` prefix, whitespace ignored", but the prefix handling only honours that for a lowercase `0x`, exactly once-or-more:

- `--value-hex 0XAB` is refused with `invalid hex digit in "0XAB"` — the digits are fine; the uppercase prefix is never stripped, so the `X` is fed to the digit parser and blamed as a bad digit. Hex copied from tools that print `0X…` (or a user naturally uppercasing the whole string, which the "case-insensitive" promise invites) fails.
- `--value-hex 0x0xAB` is silently accepted as `AB` — the strip is `trim_start_matches`, which removes the prefix repeatedly, so a doubled prefix is not the "a prefix" the contract describes.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `e91098f1`, by code reading — the function is pure string logic)

- `pkgs/id/src/commands/tag.rs:68-70` — the doc comment: "Decode a hex string (case-insensitive, optional `0x` prefix, whitespace ignored)."
- `pkgs/id/src/commands/tag.rs:71-76` — `hex_decode` does `input.trim().trim_start_matches("0x")` and only then filters whitespace and parses digit pairs with `to_digit(16)`. `trim_start_matches` matches the literal lowercase `"0x"` and repeats: `"0XAB"` keeps its prefix (first pair becomes `0X` → `to_digit` fails on `X`), `"0x0xAB"` loses both prefixes and parses as `AB`.
- `pkgs/id/src/commands/tag.rs:466-477` — the existing tests pin `"0xAB cd"` (lowercase prefix, uppercase digits, interior space) and rejections for odd length / non-hex, but have no uppercase-prefix and no doubled-prefix case, so both behaviours are unpinned.
- Sole caller: `resolve_value` (`tag.rs:213`), reached from `id tag set` and `id tag del` `--value-hex` (`pkgs/id/src/cli.rs:2134`, `:2162`). The REPL tag commands share `run_*` in the same module, so they inherit it.

## Why it matters

`--value-hex` exists for binary tag values — checksums, hashes, raw bytes — exactly the values users copy out of other tools, which do not all spell the prefix lowercase. The failure message points at the wrong character ("invalid hex digit"), sending the user to check digits that are valid. The doubled-prefix acceptance is the same line's other face: the accepted grammar is neither "one optional prefix" nor documented anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hex_decode("0XAB")` (and mixed spellings like `0Xab cd`) decodes the same bytes as `0xAB`, matching the documented case-insensitivity — or, if triage prefers refusing uppercase prefixes, the doc comment and the error message are changed to say so plainly instead of blaming a digit. (Pin one behaviour in tests.)
- [ ] At most one prefix is stripped: `0x0xAB` is refused (or explicitly documented as accepted) — pinned by a test either way.
- [ ] Existing behaviour is preserved: `"0xAB cd"`, bare hex, odd-length and non-hex rejections (existing `hex_roundtrip` / `hex_decode_rejects_bad_input` tests keep passing).
- [ ] New tests cover the uppercase-prefix and doubled-prefix spellings.
- [ ] Existing tag command tests pass (`cargo test` for the id crate on laptop or CI).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `hex_decode`, "value-hex" and "hex decode" before filing: no filing covers this decoder. #1517 (closed) was about an empty `module_hash` passing a different validator in world-manifest, not this function.

labels.name: effort/xs

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id`'s collaborative-editing codec cannot decode one of its own message types. `CollabMessage::CursorRemove` (tag 6, "a client's cursor is gone") encodes fine, but `CollabMessage::decode` has no branch for tag 6, so every CursorRemove frame decodes to `None` — the same result as corrupt input.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 35726e8e)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs:80` — `pub const CURSOR_REMOVE: u8 = 6;`
- `pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs:497-498` — `encode()` serializes `CursorRemove` as `(msg::CURSOR_REMOVE, client_id)`.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs:513-615` — `decode()` tries, in order: Init (0), Steps (1), Update (2), Ack (3), Cursor (4, two forms), Error (5), NewVersion (7), Auth (8), AuthOk (9, two forms). Tag 6 is never tried.
- The server broadcasts CursorRemove on every client disconnect (`collab.rs:1175`), so this is a live wire type, not a dead variant. The TypeScript client decodes tag 6 itself (`pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` protocol table), which is why the gap is invisible in the browser today — but the Rust codec is the canonical definition, and any Rust-side consumer (tests, future Rust client, protocol tooling) silently drops these frames as undecodable.
- Test gap that let it survive: roundtrip tests exist for Init/Steps/Update/Ack/Cursor/Error/NewVersion (`collab.rs:1240-1460`) but none for CursorRemove (nor Auth/AuthOk); `test_message_type_constants` (`collab.rs:1479-1487`) asserts only tags 0–5.

### Probe (laptop, verbatim codec)

Probe crate `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-28-laneA-collab-decode` on the laptop (collab.rs sha256 55e04270… identical in the laptop clone and sandbox main 35726e8e; `msg` + `Step` + `CollabMessage` encode/decode extracted verbatim, lines 73–84 / 162–168 / 417–615), `cargo run --release`:

- Init, Steps, Update, Ack, Cursor (both forms), Error, NewVersion, Auth, AuthOk (both forms): all `decode(encode(x)) == Some(x)`.
- `CursorRemove { client_id: 54321 }`: encodes to 5 bytes `[92, 06, cd, d4, 31]`, `decode` returns **None** — the only failure in the set.

## Why it matters

An asymmetric codec is a trap: the one message that tells every client "this cursor is gone" is indistinguishable from garbage to the crate's own decoder. Today the TS client masks it; any Rust consumer inherits silent message loss, and the missing test coverage means the next added variant can regress the same way unnoticed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CollabMessage::decode` handles tag 6 and returns `CursorRemove { client_id }` for a well-formed frame.
- Roundtrip tests cover every `CollabMessage` variant and form (including CursorRemove, Auth, and AuthOk with and without token), so encode/decode asymmetry fails CI.
- `test_message_type_constants` (or equivalent) asserts all tags 0–9.
- Existing collab tests still pass (laptop or CI).

Related but distinct: #1618 (collab steps are broadcast without validation).

body:
## Phase 2 — PR-tier slimming: basic validation on PRs, full suite on main

Design: #1779 (doc §3). Cross-repo: one issue, per-repo PRs in
rollout order code → opencode → openchamber → nix. Depends on
Phase 1 landing first (separate issue).

### Problem

PRs currently trigger the full check matrix on every push, and the
matrix is what floods the runner queue: code's `id` workflow alone
fans out to 27 flake-check jobs per run (104.8m wall for ≤13.8m of
execution per job on 2026-10-28); opencode `test` runs build + e2e
on every PR (e2e waited 65–76m for 0.1m of execution). Per Drew's
directive, regular PRs need only very basic validation — everything
else runs on merge to main, and all tests run against main before
any release anyway.

### The policy surface

Implement the change-class table (design doc §3.3) as path-glob
data each repo's workflows consume:

| class | examples | PR tier |
|---|---|---|
| 0 prose | `**.md`, docs/ | nothing / markdown lint |
| 1 config/data | json/yaml/toml, non-workflow `.github/**` | syntax parse + lint |
| 2 package source (default) | one package's src+tests | lint/format + typecheck/syntax of affected + affected unit tests |
| 3 elevated | lockfiles, module roots, `flake.nix`, build defs, `.github/workflows/**`, shared libs | class 2 + compile of affected |
| 4 nix | `**.nix` | parse/eval of changed files only |

Highest class wins on mixed changes. Tuning = editing the table.

### Per-repo scope

- **code:** `nix ci` — treefmt stays on PRs, `flake-check` job →
  main+nightly. `id` — PR keeps guard + affected-crate checks;
  27-job flake-check matrix → main. `mcpx conformance` → main
  (spec-parity leg may stay if <5m). `id bench` → main only.
  Build workflows (go modules build, identity build, map build,
  mcpx nix build) compile only for class-3 changes.
- **opencode:** `test` — PR runs `affected` + affected unit only;
  `build` + `e2e` → main. `check` (typecheck) unchanged — it is
  the PR tier's core. `nix-eval` paths-gated on PRs.
- **openchamber:** `pr checks` — PR keeps lint + type-check;
  `tests` + `build` → main.
- **dezren39/nix:** `mcpx nix build` — PR tier eval-only of
  changed modules; full build → main.

Every workflow that leaves the PR trigger keeps (or gains) a
push-to-main trigger plus a nightly schedule backstop, so main-tier
coverage is total.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Per-repo PR merged implementing the class table + trigger
      changes above; the policy table lives in-repo as data.
- [ ] A docs-only PR and a class-2 PR on each repo show only the
      PR-tier checks running (evidence on the PRs).
- [ ] Main pushes run the full suite in every repo (first main run
      after merge linked as evidence).
- [ ] No check that ran on main before this change is lost: the
      union of main-tier + nightly jobs covers the old PR matrix.

## Phase 3 of #1753 — elicitation form gate + register truth-up + nix#210 evidence

Design: #1753 (mcpx sub-capability gating). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-subcapability-gating.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Origin: [dezren39/nix#210](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/issues/210). **Gated on Phase 1 of #1753** (same file, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go`).

### Problem (verified on main `f6760a69`)

`Peer.CanElicit` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go` ~L232-249) special-cases `url` (revision ≥ 2025-11-25 plus the declared `url` key) but returns `true` for form against *any* elicitation declaration — including a 2025-11-25+ host that declared only `{"url": {}}`, which cannot render a form and would receive a request with a `requestedSchema` it never agreed to. Compare-register row CAP-08: "`{}` means form only"; the form gate ignores a url-only declaration.

### Scope (decision recorded on #1753)

- `CanElicit("form")` reads the declaration's shape where the revision defines sub-keys:
  - Peer revision ≥ 2025-11-25: form is sendable iff the declaration carries a `form` key **or is empty** (`elicitation: {}` is the form-only declaration). A declaration carrying only `url` is not form-capable.
  - Peer revision < 2025-11-25: elicitation has no sub-keys; presence means form, exactly as today.
  - The `url` branch is unchanged. `AnswersInline` inherits the corrected form answer.
  - Malformed declaration values behave as undeclared (existing tolerance).
- Truth-up (after Phases 1–2 have landed):
  - Compare-register rows CAP-02, CAP-04, CAP-05, CAP-06, CAP-08, SMP-09, SMP-11 in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/` updated to as-built — several were stale before this design (roots answering and handler-gated declaration landed earlier; cite those PRs/commits where the register names them).
  - Completion evidence comment on [dezren39/nix#210](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/issues/210) covering each of its acceptance bullets with its landing PR; close nix#210 if and only if every bullet is met, otherwise name the unmet bullet on both issues. (Commenting/closing on the nix repo is the cross-repo set rule: nix#210 is the origin record, #1753 is the design of record in the canonical repo.)

### Out of scope

- `includeContext` values across a relay (open question on #1753; gap `sampling-server-avoid-includecontext-values` stays open and must be named as remaining in the nix#210 evidence if it is still open).
- Any change to the `url` gate, roots behaviour, or upstream declarations.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tests cover declarations: url-only (form refused at 2025-11-25+), form-only, both keys, `{}` (form allowed), legacy pre-2025-11-25 (form allowed), malformed (treated as undeclared).
- [ ] A url-only host is no longer offered form elicitations on either the legacy wire path or the modern `input_required` path (`sendableTo` covers both); form-declaring hosts are unaffected.
- [ ] Register rows listed above match the code; the nix#210 evidence comment is posted and nix#210 is closed iff all its acceptance bullets are met.
- [ ] CI green (GitHub Actions; per fleet rule, no builds on the sandbox).

body:
## Phase 1 of #1753 — server-side sampling relay gating

Design: #1753 (mcpx sub-capability gating). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-subcapability-gating.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Origin: [dezren39/nix#210](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/issues/210).

### Problem (verified on main `f6760a69`)

`Peer.CanSample` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go` ~L251-252) is `Declared("sampling")` and nothing more. `Question.Sendable` (~L448-458) therefore offers any sampling question to any host that declared the parent capability, and `Question.paramsFor` (~L466+) shapes elicitation params per era but passes sampling params verbatim — `tools` and `includeContext` reach a host that never declared `sampling.tools` or `sampling.context`. Conformance gaps (both `internal/conformance/coverage_clientfeatures.go`, tagged `#210`): `sampling-server-no-tools-without-capability`, `sampling-server-includecontext-only-with-context-capability`.

### Scope (decision recorded on #1753)

In `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver`:

- `Peer` gains sub-capability reads: whether the peer's `sampling` declaration carries `tools` / `context` keys. Malformed declaration values behave as undeclared (the tolerance `CanElicit`'s url branch already uses).
- `Question.Sendable` for `sampling/createMessage` returns false for a tools-carrying question (`tools` or `toolChoice` present) when the peer declared no `sampling.tools`. The question then follows the existing unsendable path (`sendableTo` / broker fallback) — it is not offered to this host, and it is NOT degraded by stripping: a stripped `toolChoice: "required"` request is a different request.
- `Question.paramsFor` drops `includeContext` from a relayed sampling question when the peer declared no `sampling.context` (context inclusion is expressly ignorable; dropping preserves the plain completion). When the peer did declare `context`, the field passes unchanged in this phase.
- `CanSample` keeps its parent meaning (other callers, e.g. `AnswersInline`, ask "can this peer sample at all"); shape logic lives in `Sendable`/`paramsFor`, where the question's shape is known.

### Out of scope

- Client-side enforcement in `internal/mcpclient` (Phase 2 of #1753).
- Elicitation form gate and register truth-up (Phase 3 of #1753).
- `includeContext` *values* (`thisServer`/`allServers`) across a relay — open question on #1753; gap `sampling-server-avoid-includecontext-values` stays open.
- Declaring `sampling.tools`/`context` anywhere new.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Host declaring bare `sampling` receives a plain sampling question unchanged; a tools-carrying question is not offered to it; `includeContext` is absent from what it receives.
- [ ] Host declaring `sampling.tools` + `sampling.context` receives the question verbatim.
- [ ] Malformed `sampling` declaration behaves as undeclared in tests.
- [ ] Conformance gaps `sampling-server-no-tools-without-capability` and `sampling-server-includecontext-only-with-context-capability` retired from `coverage_clientfeatures.go` with passing conformance rows.
- [ ] CI green (GitHub Actions; per fleet rule, no builds on the sandbox).

title: id(local_events): clear_tag can never clear a name with more than 256 live claims — it builds one tag.clear over the 256-claim cap and every attempt fails

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`id claim clear` can never clear a tag name once a subject carries more than 256 live claims of that name. The clear is unrecoverable through the CLI/library: every attempt fails with the same error and no claim is removed, so the tag name is stuck on that subject forever (short of hand-editing the store).

## Evidence (verified this run on main `7248a166`)

- `pkgs/id/src/local_events.rs:213-228` — `LocalEvents::clear_tag` collects **every** live claim matching `(subject, name)` into one `TagOp::Clear { claims }` and records it as a single event. There is no chunking and no partial-clear path.
- `pkgs/id/src/tag_claims.rs:36` — `MAX_CLEAR_CLAIMS = 256` ("The most claims one `tag.clear` may name").
- `pkgs/id/src/tag_claims.rs:130-138` — `check_op` refuses a clear naming more than 256 claims.
- `pkgs/id/src/chain.rs:216` — building/signing the event runs `check_op`, so `record()` fails before ingest; the error surfaces to `id claim clear` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/claim.rs:69`).
- Nothing stops a subject accumulating >256 live claims of one name: `live_claims`/`compacted_claims` key sets by event ID (`tag_claims.rs:182+`), so repeated `set_tag` calls — by one node or by many authors sharing/syncing a store — each add a distinct live claim. No dedup by (author, name, value) exists.

### Reproduction (probe in the real crate, run on the laptop)

Probe test (`LocalEvents` over a temp store, `--no-default-features`), probe + log preserved in the goal bookkeeping (`probe-2026-10-28-laneB-clear256/`):

- Control: set 3 claims named `city` on one subject → `clear_tag` succeeds, count = 3, 0 live claims remain.
- Bug case: set 257 claims named `topic` on the same subject → 257 live claims; then:

```text
PROBE live topic claims before clear: 257
PROBE clear_tag(257) ERR: extension refused: 257 claims, the most is 256
PROBE live claims after clear attempt: 257
test result: ok. 1 passed
```

## Why it matters

Tag clearing is the only removal path for claims (`id claim clear`, `LocalEvents::clear_tag`). A busy or contested subject — exactly the subjects most likely to need clearing (spam, a popular document, many authors setting the same tag) — crosses 256 live claims and becomes permanently unclearable. The failure gives the user no workaround and no partial progress.

## Suggested direction (for triage to pin)

Have `clear_tag` emit as many `tag.clear` events as needed, each naming at most `MAX_CLEAR_CLAIMS` of the collected claims (each subsequent clear's causal past includes the earlier events, and a clear only needs its named claims in its own past — the claims themselves, not the prior clears). The returned count should be the total cleared; the returned event ID shape needs a small contract decision (e.g. the last clear's ID). Raising the cap instead is not a fix: the header decoder's array bound is what the cap mirrors.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Clearing a name with >256 live claims on a subject succeeds: all of those claims are removed (regression test at e.g. 257 and at a multi-chunk size such as 600).
- [ ] Clearing ≤256 claims still records exactly one `tag.clear` event and returns the same count/ID behaviour as today.
- [ ] `clear_tag`'s return contract for the multi-event case is documented at its definition (which event ID is returned, or the shape changes deliberately).
- [ ] No live claim of the cleared name remains afterwards, and claims of other names / on other subjects are untouched.
- [ ] Existing tag/local-events tests still pass (`cargo test` for the id crate on laptop or CI).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `clear_tag`, `MAX_CLEAR`, "256 claims", and tag-clear terms before filing: no filing covers this cap interaction. #185 ("who may clear a tag claim") is the separate policy question of clear permission, not the count cap. #1421 is a validation/mutation-testing gap for the fold, unrelated.

body:
## Problem

`SaveRateLimiter` (`pkgs/id/src/web/mod.rs:94-132`) tracks the last save of each file in `last_save: Arc<Mutex<HashMap<String, Instant>>>`. Nothing ever removes an entry: `check()` only reads the map, `record()` only inserts. The cooldown is 5 seconds (`DEFAULT_SAVE_COOLDOWN`, `web/mod.rs:86`), so an entry older than 5s can never change a decision again — `check` treats it as allowed and `record` would overwrite it anyway — yet it is kept for the life of the `id serve` process.

The map therefore grows by one permanent entry for every distinct filename ever saved. Filenames are client-supplied (`SaveRequest.name`, checked at `web/routes.rs:1203`, recorded at `web/routes.rs:1327` after each successful save), so growth is driven by normal use (every new document name) and can be minted deliberately by saving many distinct names once each.

## Evidence (verified on main `f7b70714`, this run)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/mod.rs:94-99` — the limiter is a plain `HashMap<String, Instant>` behind a mutex; no eviction field or policy.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/mod.rs:114-125` — `check()` only does `map.get(name)`; an expired entry is left in place.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/mod.rs:128-131` — `record()` only does `map.insert(...)`.
- Full-tree grep for `save_limiter` / `SaveRateLimiter` / `last_save` across `pkgs/id/src` and `pkgs/id/tests`: the only uses are the definition, `AppState` construction (`web/mod.rs:208`, 5s cooldown), `check` (`web/routes.rs:1203`) and `record` (`web/routes.rs:1327`). No `remove`, `retain`, `clear`, or periodic sweep exists anywhere.
- Dedup: `gh issue list --search "rate limiter OR SaveRateLimiter OR save cooldown"` (open + closed) returns no filing for this; #1230 is a Firefox e2e autosave race, unrelated.

## Why it matters

`id serve` is a long-running home server. A rate limiter whose state grows monotonically with distinct filenames is a slow, unbounded memory leak in exactly the process that is never restarted, and the retained entries serve no purpose after 5 seconds. It is also a small integrity wart: the one structure whose job is bounding save behaviour is itself unbounded.

## Fix direction (for triage to pin)

Evict expired entries so the map holds only names inside their cooldown window — e.g. `check()` removes the entry it finds expired (it no longer limits anything), and/or `record()` sweeps expired entries while it holds the lock. Semantics must stay identical: a save within 5s of the same name's last save is still refused with the remaining time; a save after the cooldown is allowed. No new dependencies, no API change.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a name's cooldown expires, its entry no longer occupies the map (evicted on a subsequent `check`/`record`, or by an equivalent bounded sweep).
- [ ] Rate-limit behaviour is unchanged: same-name save inside the cooldown is refused with the remaining duration; after the cooldown it is allowed and re-recorded.
- [ ] A regression test shows the map does not retain expired entries (e.g. record several names under a short cooldown, let it lapse, trigger the eviction path, assert the map shrank) — the limiter's existing behaviour tests still pass.
- [ ] `cargo test` for the web module passes on laptop/CI.

body:
Phase 1 of design #1675 (mcpx elicitation broker hygiene). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-elicitation-broker-hygiene.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Scope

Give the elicitation broker store an owner-only home, and migrate existing installs without losing pending questions.

- Add one store-path helper in `internal/elicit` (working name `StorePath`) that both open sites use — today `internal/daemon/hooks.go` `OpenBroker` (~L288-294) and `internal/cli/elicit.go` `broker()` (~L37-44) each assemble `<state>/logs/elicit.db` independently with `defaults.PublicDirMode` (`0755`).
- The store moves to a dedicated subdirectory of the state dir (name settled in triage), created at `defaults.DirMode` (`0700`); the DB, `-wal` and `-shm` files are `0600` after open.
- Migration on open: if a legacy `logs/elicit.db` exists and the new path does not, move it before opening (rename; copy-then-delete fallback across filesystems). If migration fails, fall back to opening the legacy path tightened in place rather than losing state. Pending questions must survive: a question pending across the upgrade stays answerable (the broker's core promise — asker and answerer are different processes, possibly days apart).
- Tightening on open: after opening, chmod the store dir to `0700` and DB files to `0600` if looser (covers dirs/files created by older binaries or a permissive umask — `MkdirAll` does not chmod an existing directory). Failure to tighten is a returned error, not a log line. Tightening must be idempotent and safe when the daemon and CLI open the store concurrently (re-stat; SQLite WAL + busy_timeout already handle concurrent access).
- The shared logs directory keeps `PublicDirMode` — out of scope (recorded decision on #1675).
- Retire conformance gap `elicitation-state-storage-protected` (`internal/conformance/coverage_clientfeatures.go`).

## Evidence (main d39e6111, 2026-10-28)

- Origin dezren39/nix#255 acceptance: "The elicitation broker store is permission-restricted to the owner (no world/group read) and this is verified on disk."
- `internal/defaults/defaults.json:214`: `publicDirMode: 0755` vs `dirMode: 0700` at :211 — the codebase already distinguishes the two; the broker's open sites chose the public one.
- Owner-only precedent in-tree: `internal/artifacts` creates dirs at `0o700` throughout; daemon `Paths.Ensure` (`internal/daemon/paths.go` ~L411-419) creates state/cache at `0o700`.
- What is at risk in the store: `elicit.Route` (`internal/elicit/elicit.go` ~L504-527) sends password/credential-shaped fields to the human audience because an agent should not hold them; sampling requests are "stored exactly as sent" (`internal/daemon/hooks.go` `sampleViaBroker` ~L180-187).

## Acceptance

- Fresh open: store dir mode `0700`, `elicit.db`/`-wal`/`-shm` mode `0600`, asserted in tests via `stat`.
- Legacy `logs/elicit.db` containing a pending question: after open at the new path, the question is listed and answerable; the legacy file is gone (or, in the fallback path, tightened in place).
- Pre-loosened store dir/files (simulating an older install): modes tightened on open.
- Daemon + CLI opening the store concurrently does not error on the tightening step.
- Gap `elicitation-state-storage-protected` retired with the tests as evidence.
- CI green for `pkgs/mcpx` (tests run in GitHub Actions).

title: aggregator: quota gatherer snapshot dedup ignores credentialId — two ok credentials of one provider interleave into one series and append an alternating noise point every tick

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
## Summary

The quota gatherer's snapshot dedup (`recordsFromEntries`, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts:243-274`) keys its "value last appended" state by `serviceId|window` only — but the gatherer produces one entry **per credential** (`scripts/gather-quota.ts`: `fetchQuotaForProviderInstances` → `entryFromResult` per result; `serviceIdFor` maps by provider, `quota-gather-map.ts:63-78`), and `SnapshotRecord` has no credential dimension (`src/model.ts:1256-1267`). When two credentials of one provider are both `ok` in a tick, their readings interleave into a single series and the dedup — whose stated purpose is "the store gains a point when a reading moves, not every 15 minutes" (`quota-gather-map.ts:228-242`) — appends a noise point **every tick forever**, even when neither value ever changes.

Mechanics, all in `recordsFromEntries` + the caller's merge (`gather-quota.ts:322-340`):

- The dedup key is `${entry.serviceId}|${w.name}` (`quota-gather-map.ts:254`); `entry.credentialId` is carefully carried onto the entry (`:188`) and then never used.
- The comparison reads the *input* `lastAppended` map (`:256`), never the values appended earlier in the same tick, so tick 1 appends **both** credentials' points for the same series at the same `ts`.
- The state map afterwards holds whichever credential was processed last. Next tick, the other credential's (unchanged) value differs from the stored stamp and appends; the merge flips the stored stamp; the following tick the first credential appends again — alternating 10, 20, 10, 20… at the 15-minute tick cadence, indefinitely.

## Verified (this run, on main 9752a47b)

Probe ON THE LAPTOP (Bun, driving the real `recordsFromEntries` from `quota-gather-map.ts`, sha256 `b18d3fd9…` identical in both clones; state merged between ticks exactly as `gather-quota.ts:339` does; probe + log in the goal's `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-28-laneB-gatherdedup/`):

- Two ok entries, same serviceId `anthropic:claude-pro`, window `5h`, credential A at 10% and credential B at 20%, values **never changing**:
  - tick 1 → 2 records appended, same series, same ts: `…|5h=10` and `…|5h=20`
  - tick 2 → 1 record (`=10`), tick 3 → 1 record (`=20`), tick 4 → 1 record (`=10`) — one noise point per tick, alternating, forever.
- Control, single credential at a constant 10%: tick 1 → 1 record, ticks 2-3 → 0 records; a genuine move 10→15 appends exactly 1. The dedup works precisely as documented for the single-credential case.

Reachability: per-credential results are the gatherer's normal shape — `gather-quota.ts` reads OpenCode's credential store and fetches per credential (its own comments describe multiple credential rows per provider, e.g. Codex's token-sharing login row). Any provider with two ok credentials (two stored Claude/Codex logins) triggers it; error/unconfigured rows are skipped by the `state !== "ok"` guard, so a refused second credential does not.

## Why it matters

The snapshot store is the hub's long-term usage series (§4): it feeds history, trend and cost views, and its writers are deliberately append-on-change so the series stays sparse and meaningful. In the multi-credential case the series instead gains a fabricated sawtooth — the line oscillates between two accounts' real readings at one point per 15-minute tick — which reads as usage swinging up and down, corrupts any per-service history derived from it, and grows the store ~96 points/day/window for data that never moved. It also makes the two accounts' readings indistinguishable: both are recorded under one serviceId with no credential attribution.

Distinct from #1540 (SnapshotStore append-time validation of non-finite/ non-ISO records — different layer, the store's gate; these records are individually valid) and from #1560 (registry merge forgetting fields).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With two ok credentials of one provider in a tick and unchanged values across ticks, the gatherer appends no per-tick noise: either the dedup/series key distinguishes credentials (and the record/series shape documents that), or the mapper's per-provider series rule is made explicit and only one deterministic reading per serviceId+window is recorded per tick — pinned by a test.
- [ ] Tick 1 with two ok credentials no longer appends two contradictory points for the same series at the same timestamp (or the two points are credential-distinguishable, per the pinned rule).
- [ ] Regression tests cover: two-credential constant values over ≥3 ticks (no alternating appends), the single-credential constant case (append once), and a genuine value move (append once).
- [ ] Existing aggregator test suites still pass.

title: id(peers): a peer's announced name is printed raw — a newline in a gossip announcement forges extra TSV rows in id peers and the REPL

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`id peers` and the REPL `peers` commands print a peer's announced `name` **raw** in a tab-separated, one-row-per-peer format. The name comes from a `PeerAnnouncement` that any gossip participant can broadcast: announcements are unsigned postcard on a public topic, are decoded and stored with no validation of `name` at any point in the chain, and are later served verbatim via `ListPeers`. A name containing a newline forges extra peer rows (including a fully-formed fake node row); a name containing a tab shifts the columns. One malicious or merely oddly-named peer controls the shape of every other node's peer listing.

This is the remote-input sibling of #1611 (locally-authored tag names/values printed raw by the claim/doc/group commands): different data, different trust boundary (unsigned network input vs the local store), different printers, different fix surface.

## The chain (all on main `63ba1705`)

1. **Ingest, no validation.** `PeerAnnouncement` (`pkgs/id/src/discovery.rs:356-368`) declares `name: Option<String>` with no constraint. The serve gossip receive loop postcard-decodes any announcement and stores it (`pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs:1278-1285`), and `id peers`' own gossip collection does the same (`pkgs/id/src/commands/peers.rs:434-440`). `PeerDiscovery::update` inserts it verbatim (`pkgs/id/src/discovery.rs:430-437`). (Announcements carrying unchecked data is also the root of #1552's replay finding; that issue is about `timestamp_secs` freshness, not the name.)
2. **Serving, verbatim.** The `ListPeers` handler returns the stored announcements unchanged (`pkgs/id/src/protocol.rs:644-651`).
3. **Printing, raw.** Three sites interpolate `name` directly into a `\t`-joined `println!` row:
   - `pkgs/id/src/commands/peers.rs:191-199` — `"{}\t{}\t{}\t{}"` (node_id, name, blob_count, timestamp_secs)
   - `pkgs/id/src/commands/repl.rs:1043-1052` — REPL `peers`
   - `pkgs/id/src/commands/repl.rs:1091-1106` — REPL `peers_on_node`

Nothing anywhere in the chain strips, escapes, or rejects control characters in `name`.

## Verification (this run)

Verbatim-logic probe crate on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-28-laneA-peersout`; `peers.rs` sha256 `41956ade…`, `repl.rs` `e61aa516…`, `discovery.rs` `52b897d2…` — identical in the sandbox and laptop clones): a forged announcement with name `"innocent\nbbbb\tforged-name\t999\t1700000000"` survives postcard ingest byte-for-byte, and:

- the `id peers` print block renders **2 peers as 3 lines** — the third line is the fully-formed forged row `bbbb  forged-name  999  1700000000`;
- the REPL print block likewise renders 2 peers as 3 lines;
- a name of `"a\tb"` (no newline) yields a row with **5 tab-separated fields instead of 4**, silently corrupting any TSV consumer;
- control (name `my-server`) renders one clean row in both printers.

Full probe source + output log are in the goal bookkeeping (`hidden_files/probe-2026-10-28-laneA-peersout/`).

Note the codebase's own `serve` currently announces `name: None` (`commands/serve.rs:1243-1248`), so today the field is populated only by other implementations / future versions — but the receive, store, serve, and print paths are all live, and the protocol documents `name` as a supported field (discovery.rs doc example). The fix should land before a named server makes this routinely reachable, and gossip peers are not limited to this build.

## Why it matters

`id peers` output is exactly the kind of text an operator (or a script) trusts to answer "who is on my network": node IDs, names, blob counts. A forged row invents a peer with an attacker-chosen node ID string and blob count; at minimum it corrupts TSV parsing and terminal display for anyone who lists peers on a network with one hostile or compromised participant. Every other name-like input in this codebase is sanitized at ingest (cf. the web identity `sanitize_name`, world `sanitize_chat`/`display_name`); peer announcement names are the unguarded exception.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A peer name containing `\n`, `\r`, or `\t` can no longer produce extra rows or shifted columns in any of the three print sites (`commands/peers.rs`, REPL `peers`, REPL `peers_on_node`) — whether the ruling is sanitize/reject at announcement ingest, escape at print time, or both; the ruling is stated in the PR.
- [ ] The stored/served announcement and the printed output agree: a `ListPeers` consumer cannot observe a name that the printers would render differently (no print-only fix that leaves other consumers exposed, unless that is the explicit ruling).
- [ ] Tests: an announcement whose name carries newline/tab/CR (and a control-character-only name) round-trips ingest → `ListPeers` → both printers with exactly one row per peer and four fields per row; ordinary names (spaces, Unicode) still display unchanged.
- [ ] Cross-link #1611 in the PR: the two fixes should not drift into inconsistent escaping conventions for CLI plain-text output.

title: id(web): GET /api/tags silently drops the value filter without a key — ?value= returns the whole namespace, ?subject=&value= returns all the subject's tags

body:
## Summary

`GET /api/tags` silently discards the `value` query parameter in two of its dispatch combinations, returning unfiltered results with a 200 as if the filter had been applied:

- `GET /api/tags?value=rust` (value, no key, no subject) returns **every tag in the namespace** — the request is indistinguishable from `GET /api/tags` with no filters at all.
- `GET /api/tags?subject=a.md&value=rust` (subject + value, no key) returns **all of the subject's tags**, including values other than `rust`.

`TagQuery::value` is documented as "Filter by tag value (requires `key`)" (`pkgs/id/src/web/tags_ws.rs:125`), but nothing enforces the requirement and nothing applies the filter in these arms — the parameter is accepted and dropped.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `63ba1705`)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/tags_ws.rs:275-307` — `get_tags_handler` dispatches on `(subject, key, value)`:
  - `(Some(subject), None, _)` at `:294` calls `get_tags(subject)` — the `_` discards `value`.
  - `(None, None, _)` at `:304` calls `list_all(ns)` — the `_` discards `value`.
  - The combinations that do honour `value` are `(Some, Some, value)` (`:280-293`, post-filter) and `(None, Some(key), Some(value))` (`:296-300`, `find_by_key_value`).
- Probe (verbatim dispatch arms copied from the handler, stub store recording which query ran; run on the laptop, `tags_ws.rs` sha256 `645c8e20` identical both sides):
  - CTRL `key=label&value=rust` → `find_by_key_value`, 2 tags (both `rust`).
  - CTRL `subject=a.md&key=label&value=rust` → `get_by_key` + filter, 1 tag.
  - CTRL `subject=a.md` → 2 tags; CTRL no filters → 4 tags.
  - BUG1 `value=rust` alone → arm `list_all`, **4 tags** — including `label=python` and a value-less tag; byte-for-byte the no-filter result.
  - BUG2 `subject=a.md&value=rust` → arm `get_tags(subject)`, **2 tags** — `rust` and `python`; the `python` tag proves the filter never ran.
- No test pins either combination: the handler has no unit tests for the `value`-without-`key` shapes, and the web UI only ever calls `?subject=` (`pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts:909`), so this is an API-surface defect, not a UI one.

## Why it matters

A caller that passes `value` without `key` — an easy mistake, since the parameter is accepted with a 200 — gets a superset of what it asked for and no signal that the filter was ignored. For a value-only caller that superset is the entire namespace. This is the silent-wrong-answer shape: the response looks like a successful filtered query, so downstream code (scripts, the REPL, future UI) will act on tags it never asked for. Every other loosely-formed input on this surface is refused (`request_value` rejects `value`+`value_b64` together, `resolve_ns` 400s an unknown namespace) — `value` without `key` is the loose one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/tags?value=...` without `key` never returns unfiltered results: either a 400 naming the missing `key` (matching the documented "requires `key`"), or a real value search — one behaviour, pinned by tests.
- [ ] `GET /api/tags?subject=...&value=...` without `key` gets the same treatment (400, or the subject's tags filtered by value).
- [ ] Handler-level tests pin both shapes plus the existing controls: `key+value`, `subject+key+value`, `subject` only, and no filters all keep their current results.
- [ ] No behaviour change for well-formed callers (the web UI's `?subject=` calls included).

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `tags value filter`, `api/tags value`, and related terms: no filing covers the tags REST dispatch. Adjacent but distinct: #1547 (projector read-API `limit` validation — different repo component and parameter), #1208 (Project pool truncation — names `fetchProjectPool`, not this handler).

body:
## Request (Drew, 2026-10-27)

> "make easy config to enable disable providers — I'll add it back one day and want it to just work besides fixing signin"

Context: the Claude plan went to the free tier today and `claude-code` is paused in the canonical config (PR #1316). When Drew adds Claude — or any provider — back, the ONLY step left for him should be that provider's sign-in itself. Config, model definitions, and route-pool seats must already be in place so flipping the provider on just works.

## Current state (verified on main, 2026-10-27)

`.opencode/opencode.jsonc` disables providers THREE different ways:

1. **List-only** — built-in providers with no local definition (`google-vertex`, `nvidia`, `vercel`, `huggingface`, `opencode`, `github-copilot`): re-enabling is already one flip.
2. **Definition in place + in `disabled_providers`** (`google`, `antigravity-agy`, `cloudflare-ai-gateway`, `groq`, `openai-codex`, `chatgpt`, `claude-code`): the good pattern — one flip.
3. **Definition commented out + in the list** (`cloudflare-gateway`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, `openrouter`): re-enabling is TWO edits (uncomment the block AND remove from the list).
4. **`muse` is comment-only** — commented out and NOT in `disabled_providers` at all, so its off-state doesn't even show in the one place a reader would look.

And the Claude pause's own header note makes re-enabling a second edit by instruction: "delete `claude-code` from disabled_providers **and restore the `default`**" — even though `haiku-plan` already seats `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5` and every tier consuming `haiku-plan` (scout, workhorse, speed, luna-haiku-100k) picks it up automatically once the provider is on. The default restore is a preference, not a requirement for Claude to work.

## Design

- `disabled_providers` becomes THE provider switchboard: one obvious place, with a comment block at that spot explaining the mechanism — a provider is ON unless its id is in the list; flip = add/remove one line; nothing else needs editing.
- Every fleet provider keeps its FULL definition (models, options) in the `provider` block at all times, disabled or not — re-enabling never requires config reconstruction. The commented-out definitions (`cloudflare-gateway`, `cloudflare-workers-ai`, `openrouter`, `muse`) are restored as live definitions, held off solely by the list. `muse` is added to `disabled_providers` (it stays OFF — standing ban: duplicate door into the Meta pool; the only Meta door is `meta`).
- Built-in providers stay list-only (opencode ships their catalogs; no local definition by design) and the switchboard comment says so, so the absence of a definition isn't mistaken for a gap.
- Claude is the worked example, documented at the switchboard: `claude-code` off today (free-tier pause); delete its line from the list and Claude's definition, catalog entries, and `haiku-plan` seat are already in place — the only remaining step is the claude.ai sign-in. Restoring the old Haiku `default` is called out as an optional preference, explicitly NOT part of enabling.
- Route pools are otherwise untouched (membership and ordering); pools already tolerate off-provider leaves (a disabled leaf yields nothing until its provider returns — the current canonical config ships exactly that: `haiku-plan` references `claude-code` while it is disabled).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One place (`disabled_providers` + its switchboard comment) shows every provider's on/off state; flipping any provider is a single one-line edit there.
- [ ] No provider or model definition is deleted or gutted; the four commented-out definitions are live again and held off only by the list; `muse` is in `disabled_providers` and remains disabled.
- [ ] Config loads cleanly with Claude disabled (today's state), verified by loading the config with opencode on the laptop from a worktree of this branch.
- [ ] Config loads cleanly with Claude flipped ON in a scratch copy (no sign-in performed), and `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5` resolves in the model catalog.
- [ ] No unrelated changes: pool membership/ordering, agent configs, and all other settings untouched; diff confined to `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`.

## Non-goals / related

- Deploying the canonical config to the laptop and reconciling the deployed working-tree drift is #1425 (this issue only changes the canonical file through the PR flow; #1425's deploy step is what makes it live).
- The `design-code` / `code-design` / `open-design` proxy blocks stay as they are: that commented region holds FOUR blocks for three ids (two keyed `design-code`), so it cannot join the one-flip pattern until someone makes a dedupe decision. They remain off via the list; the switchboard comment names this exception so it isn't discovered by surprise. Their live door is `opendesign` (enabled).
- Routing policy alignment stays with #1272.

body:
## Summary

The world page's records view (`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts`) corrupts its result whenever a second records fetch starts while a paginated fetch is still in flight — which is the common case, because `requestRecords()` is called on **every input event from any participant** (:170) and on snapshot (:158). The re-request resets the shared pagination state without invalidating the in-flight chain, so the stale chain's final page closes out the *new* fetch and renders a lone stale page, and every page of the fresh fetch is then silently discarded. The records panel ends up showing an incomplete, out-of-date subset presented as the complete record set.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `95cd41f0`)

State and flow (`world.ts`):

- Shared mutable pagination state: `records`, `recordsAfter`, `recordsPending` (:119-121).
- `requestRecords` (:212-226) unconditionally does `records = {}; recordsAfter = null; recordsPending = true;` and sends a fresh first-page request — even when a chain is mid-pagination.
- The `records` frame handler (:178-198): `if (!recordsPending) return;` then `Object.assign(records, frame.records)`, `recordsAfter = frame.next_after`, and when `next_after === null` it sets `recordsPending = false` and renders `JSON.stringify(records)`. It cannot distinguish pages of different fetches (no fetch id / generation), and pages are answered in request order on the one socket: continuation of fetch A, then page 1 of fetch B.

Probe: verbatim `world.ts` + `world-surface.ts` + `world-keyboard.ts` + `world-seed.ts` (sha256 identical both sides, e.g. world.ts `0a7217c4…`) run under Bun + happy-dom 21 with a mock WebSocket, on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-27-laneB-worldrecords`, log `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-laneB-worldrecords/out.log`). Server answers in request order in both runs:

| run | sequence | displayed records |
|---|---|---|
| control | snapshot → fetch A page 1 `{a1}` (next_after `"x"`) → A page 2 `{a2}` (next_after null) | `{a1: 1, a2: 2}` — complete ✅ |
| interleave | same, but one `input` event frame arrives between A page 1 and A page 2, starting fetch B; then A page 2 `{a2}` (null), then B page 1 `{b1}` (null) | `{a2: 2}` — a lone **stale** page ❌ |

In the interleave run the request log confirms three requests on the wire (A first page, A continuation `after:"x"`, B first page). A's terminal page flipped `recordsPending` to false and rendered the partially-reset map (`a1` lost in the reset, `b1` not yet arrived); B's page then hit the `!recordsPending` guard and was dropped. Nothing retries — the panel keeps showing `{a2}` until the next manual refresh or input event happens to start a fetch that completes uninterrupted.

## Why it matters

The records panel is the page's view of authoritative world state (game/record data). In any active world — input events arriving while a multi-page record set loads — it silently displays a truncated stale subset labelled as the full set, with no error. Single-page record sets are unaffected (no continuation window), which is presumably why it survives: the corruption needs `next_after != null` on an early page plus any input/snapshot/refresh during the chain.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Concurrent/overlapping records fetches cannot interleave pages: one fetch wins (e.g. a generation counter — responses and continuations from a superseded generation are ignored and do not touch `recordsPending`/rendering), or re-requests are coalesced while a fetch is pending (with a dirty flag to refetch once it completes).
- [ ] The rendered records are always exactly one complete fetch's pages: in the interleave sequence above the final render is the fresh fetch's complete set, never a single stale page.
- [ ] A regression test (vitest/happy-dom, mock WebSocket, in-order answers) pins: control two-page fetch renders both pages; input-event re-request mid-pagination renders the fresh complete set; a superseded chain's terminal page does not close the live fetch.
- [ ] Single-page fetches, the records refresh button, and the snapshot-triggered fetch behave as before.

Found by new-issue-creator lane B, verified this run. Related but distinct: #1440 (AutoSaveManager concurrency — different module, same "no in-flight guard" shape).

Question from Drew (2026-10-27): the dashboard stores are JSON files (actions.json, comments.json in ~/pm-stack/aggregator) — should they be a database? Evaluate migrating the actions/comments stores to SQLite (bun:sqlite, built into the runtime — no new service) preserving today's semantics exactly: full append-only history, supersedes-never-delete undo, outcome/byRun write-backs, atomicity. Include: current file sizes + growth rate, the in-memory load-once behavior of ActionsStore (loads the file once per process; external changes invisible until restart — the API is the only writer today, so this is latent), corruption/recovery story, and a migration path that keeps the JSON files as an export. Deliverable: a short evaluation + recommendation on this issue; implement only on Drew's go.

## Acceptance criteria
- A short evaluation is posted on this issue comparing the JSON-file stores vs SQLite (bun:sqlite) on: current file sizes + growth rate, the load-once in-memory behavior and its external-change blindness, corruption/recovery story, and atomicity/history semantics (append-only history, supersedes-never-delete undo, outcome/byRun write-backs).
- The evaluation ends with a clear recommendation; the JSON files remain exportable in any migration path.
- No implementation is started without Drew's go (this issue is the evaluation only).

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/cf-container-hello` carries the regression test suite for the #955 SSRF hardening — and nothing runs it. The suite can silently rot (or the hardening can silently regress) because no CI ever executes it.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `95cd41f0`)

- The suite exists and passes: `pkgs/cf-container-hello/test/test_probe_hardening.py` (119 lines, 11 tests) — run this run: `python3 -m unittest discover -s test -p "test_*.py"` → **11 tests, OK, in 1.14s**. `pkgs/cf-container-hello/package.json` wires it as `npm test`.
- Nothing runs it:
  - `grep -rn "cf-container-hello" .github/workflows/` → no matches (no workflow triggers on `pkgs/cf-container-hello/**`, and no workflow invokes its test command).
  - No reference in the root `flake.nix` checks or the root `justfile` either (grep for `cf-container-hello` / `test_probe_hardening` across `.github/`, `flake.nix`, `justfile` finds only the package's own `wrangler.jsonc` name field).
- What the suite pins is security-critical (test file header, `test_probe_hardening.py:1-20`): the production lab-ops-hub validator refuses `file://` / non-http schemes / loopback / private literals, the package contains **no stale local crawler copy** (`image/app.py` must not exist), `wrangler.jsonc` points at the hardened production image, and every container-forwarding Worker route sits **behind the fail-closed `API_TOKEN` gate** (`test_worker_gate_is_fail_closed_and_before_forwards` checks source ordering: gate before every `env.CRAWLER_PROBE` / `env.HELLO_CONTAINER` / `env.HELLO_LITE` forward). Several of these are source-shape checks — exactly the kind that fail silently when nobody runs them, because a refactor can reorder the gate or re-add a copy without any other signal.

## Why it matters

#955 was an unauthenticated SSRF / `file://` fetch through a stale unhardened crawler copy. Its regression tests exist precisely so that state cannot return unnoticed — but unwatched tests provide no protection. This is the same failure class as #1427 (cold-store-reaper suites run by no workflow) and #470 (lab-ops-hub suites, since fixed with a dedicated workflow — the pattern to copy).

## Suggested fix

Add a small workflow modelled on `.github/workflows/lab-ops-hub.yml`: trigger on pull requests and pushes to main with `paths: ["pkgs/cf-container-hello/**", ".github/workflows/<new>.yml"]`, set up Python 3.12 (the suite is stdlib-only — no `npm install` needed, per the test design), and run the package's documented command (`npm test`, or the underlying `python3 -m unittest discover -s test -p "test_*.py"` from the package directory). Keep the push-to-main concurrency pattern from the lab-ops workflow so merged trees each get their own run.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow runs the cf-container-hello test suite on every PR touching `pkgs/cf-container-hello/**` and on pushes to main touching it
- [ ] The workflow's test step passes on current main (suite verified green this run: 11 tests OK)
- [ ] Deliberately breaking one pinned invariant (e.g. moving a container forward above the auth gate in `src/index.ts`) makes the new workflow fail — demonstrated on the implementing PR
- [ ] No production code changes are needed; if the suite needs changes to run in CI, they are called out separately

Found by the new-issue-creator (code lane A) run, 2026-10-27.

labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Bug

`scripts/nightly-backup.sh`'s status step can mark the whole nightly run FAILED even when `cold-store status` succeeds — a race between `head` closing the pipe and the producer finishing its writes.

The step (nightly-backup.sh, status block):

```bash
if "${COLD_STORE}" status | head -n 20; then
```

The script runs with `set -uo pipefail`, so the pipeline's exit status is the producer's when the producer is the failing element. When status output exceeds 20 lines, `head` exits after line 20 and closes the read end; a producer still writing gets SIGPIPE (a shell producer exits 141; the real `cold-store` is Python, which converts SIGPIPE into `BrokenPipeError` at flush and exits non-zero). Whether the producer finishes first depends on output size and scheduling — so the step flips between ok and FAILED on identical healthy state.

## Reproduction (verified this run, main `37418e56`)

Using the script's own documented test seams (`COLD_STORE_BIN`, `EXPORT_TURSO_BIN`) with a stub `cold-store` whose `status` prints 100 lines and always exits 0, and a stub export-turso that succeeds:

- run 1: `step status: ok`, exit 0
- run 2: `step status: ok`, exit 0
- run 3: `step status: FAILED`, script exit 1, `FAILED steps: status` — every step actually succeeded

The existing tests in `tests/test_nightly_backup.py` cannot catch this: their stub status prints exactly one line (`stub status summary: objects 0 cold`), so `head` never closes early.

## Why it matters

The nightly backup is the cold store's core ritual, and PR #1373 just reworked this script specifically so failures stay loud but not contagious. This bug does the opposite: a spurious `status` failure makes a fully healthy night exit 1 and report `FAILED steps: status`, training the operator to ignore the run's verdict — and the failure probability grows every time `cold-store status` output grows past 20 lines (it is described in the script header itself as a summary shown via `head`, i.e. truncation is expected).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The status step reports ok whenever `cold-store status` itself exits 0, regardless of how many lines it prints (verify with a stub printing several hundred lines, run repeatedly — e.g. 20 consecutive runs, zero spurious failures).
- [ ] A genuinely failing `cold-store status` (non-zero exit) still marks the step FAILED and the script still exits non-zero at the end.
- [ ] The printed summary is still truncated for display (~20 lines) — the fix must not dump unbounded status output into the nightly log.
- [ ] `tests/test_nightly_backup.py` gains a case whose stub status prints more than 20 lines and asserts `step status: ok` + exit 0, alongside the existing isolation cases.

body:
## Bug

In the markdown codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), a pipe character inside an inline code span in a table cell splits the cell when a document is opened. The code mark is destroyed and the row gains a column; on save the fragments are re-emitted as plain text with escaped backticks.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `37418e56`)

Round-trip probe against `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown` (the exact functions the web collab layer uses, `src/web/collab.rs:147`):

Input:

```markdown
| A | B |
|---|---|
| `a|b` | c |
```

Parsed ProseMirror doc — the first body cell is already split at parse time; the row's cells are the plain texts `` `a `` and `` b` `` (no `code` mark anywhere):

```json
{"type":"table_cell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"text":"`a","type":"text"}]}]}
{"type":"table_cell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"text":"b`","type":"text"}]}]}
{"type":"table_cell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"text":"c","type":"text"}]}]}
```

Saved output (3 columns in the body row of a 2-column table, code span gone):

```markdown
| A | B |
| --- | --- |
| \`a | b\` | c |
```

With a 1-column header (`| A |` / `| \`a|b\` |`) the split-off fragment is dropped entirely, because the table's column count comes from the header row — the cell content after the pipe is silently lost.

Root cause (to confirm in triage): the parse direction enables comrak's table extension (`commonmark_options`, `markdown.rs:86`) and converts `NodeValue::Table` at `markdown.rs:438`; the row is split on the unescaped pipe before inline parsing, so the code span never forms. Note the plain-text escaped form `a\|b` in a cell round-trips correctly today — only the code-span form breaks.

## Why it matters

Tables documenting flags, formats, or code idioms commonly contain code spans with pipes (shell pipelines, bitwise OR, alternation in grammars, `a | b` type unions). Opening such a document in the web editor silently restructures the table and strips the code formatting; with a narrower header the overflow text is deleted outright. That is silent data corruption in a documented-supported construct (tables + inline code both have codec support and tests: `test_table`, `test_table_with_formatting`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `` `a|b` `` (and code spans containing pipes generally) survive open → edit → save in a table cell: the saved markdown still contains one cell whose content is a code span holding the full `a|b` text (escaped as `\|` inside the span if that is the chosen spelling), and the column count is unchanged.
- [ ] The 1-column-header case no longer drops cell content.
- [ ] New round-trip fixpoint tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover: pipe in a code span in a body cell, in a header cell, and a code span that is the cell's only content.
- [ ] Existing table tests (`test_table`, `test_table_with_formatting`, `test_roundtrip_table`, `test_table_alignment_roundtrip`, the table-cell does-not-panic tests) pass unmodified.

body:
# id(web): Go to Line undercounts lines in paragraphs with hard breaks — jump lands on the wrong line

## Evidence (verified this run, main 37418e56)

Vitest probe against the real goto-line dialog (real `EditorView`, richSchema; probe removed after the run):

Document (3 markdown source lines):

```
foo\
bar

baz
```

i.e. PM doc = `paragraph[text "foo", hard_break, text "bar"]` + `paragraph[text "baz"]`.

- Open Go to Line (Mod-g): the dialog reports **"Line # (1–2)", max=2** — expected 3 lines.
- Consequently "go to line 2" targets the `baz` paragraph, not the `bar` segment after the hard break; every line after the first hard break in a document is off by the number of hard breaks above it.

## Root cause

`pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.ts`, `getLineStarts` (lines 34–49): line starts inside a textblock are derived from `node.textContent`, scanning for `"\n"` characters. A `hard_break` is an inline **node**, not a character — ProseMirror's `textContent` for `foo<hard_break>bar` is `"foobar"`, so the break contributes no line start. Code blocks work because their breaks are literal `\n` text; rich paragraphs/headings/list items with Shift+Enter hard breaks are silently merged into one "line".

The fix must walk the textblock's inline content (text nodes and `hard_break` nodes) accumulating positions — a hard_break node has size 1, so the segment after it starts at `contentStart + offsetBeforeBreak + 1`.

## Why it matters

Go to Line exists to jump to a line the user knows from outside the editor — a compiler/linter message, a diff, the raw file. Hard breaks are common in pasted/poetry/address/verse content and in any paragraph where someone pressed Shift+Enter. Every such break silently shifts all subsequent line numbers, so the feature lands the user on the wrong line with no indication anything is off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A textblock containing N `hard_break` nodes contributes N+1 lines (plus its `\n` segments for code blocks, unchanged); the dialog's reported line count (placeholder/max) matches the markdown source line count for hard-broken documents.
- [ ] Go to Line for a line after a hard break places the cursor at the start of that segment (position accounts for the hard_break node's size), including breaks inside headings and list items.
- [ ] Regression tests in `pkgs/id/web/src/goto-line.test.ts`: hard-broken paragraph counts 2 lines and line 2 jumps to the post-break segment; a doc mixing hard breaks and plain paragraphs counts and jumps correctly.
- [ ] Existing goto-line tests (raw code_block counting, #712 validation, #745 semantics) still pass.

# id(web): Find panel match count goes stale when the document is edited — highlights update, the count does not

## Evidence (verified this run, main 37418e56)

Vitest probe against the real search panel (real `EditorView` + `createSearchPlugins()`, richSchema; probe removed after the run, log in the creator's sweep records):

1. Document `foo foo foo`, open Find (Mod-f), type `foo` → match count label reads **"3 matches"** ✓
2. Delete two occurrences directly in the document (`tr.delete(1, 9)`, doc is now `foo`) while the panel stays open
3. Match count label still reads **"3 matches"** — expected "1 match"

The prosemirror-search highlights themselves update correctly (they are decoration-driven); only the panel's count label is wrong, and it stays wrong until the user next types in the find box, toggles case/regex, or runs a replace.

## Root cause

`pkgs/id/web/src/search-panel.ts`:

- `updateMatchCount(view)` (line 64) is only called from `syncQuery` (line 91 — input/checkbox changes) and the replace handlers (lines 167, 184, 188).
- Nothing observes document changes: `createSearchPlugins()` (line 268) returns only the `search()` plugin and the keymap; the panel has no `Plugin` view/update hook and `countMatches` is never recomputed on `docChanged` transactions.

## Why it matters

The count is the user's only signal for "how many places does this string occur" during an edit session. A user who deletes or rewrites matches while Find is open is told there are still N matches, and may keep hunting for occurrences that no longer exist — or trust a "No results"→stale-positive in the other direction after pasting new matches in. Find panels in every mainstream editor keep the count live.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With the Find panel open and a valid query, editing the document (typing, paste, delete, collab/remote change) updates the match count label to the true number of matches, including transitions to/from "No results" and the singular "1 match" form.
- [ ] The update path is efficient: no full re-count on transactions that neither change the document nor the search state (selection-only transactions must not thrash the label).
- [ ] Regression test in `pkgs/id/web/src/search-panel.test.ts`: open panel, set a query with multiple matches, edit the document, assert the label reflects the new count (both decrease and increase).
- [ ] Existing web vitest suite passes; panel open/close, replace, and replace-all behaviour unchanged.

body:
Part of epic #1149; implements the #1167 investigation (completed 2026-10-27, report: usage-billing-hub goal hidden_files/meta-console-investigation-2026-10-26.md). Priority P1.

Findings the build rests on: the laptop's Helium browser holds a live dev.meta.ai session (CDP port 19222 on the laptop; profile copy at ~/atlas/helium-chatgpt-profile-copy). Console quota = cookie-auth GETs, no bearer token: GET dev.meta.ai/api/portal/teams/{team_id}/subscription-quota (weighted used/limit + reset epochs, both windows), .../billing-banner (free credits), .../usage/batch (daily spend/tokens). Session cookie llama_dev_sess, httpOnly, expires 2027-10-27. One risk: possible session binding (sessionBindingId in auth/me) — a 401 means "re-capture needed", never zeros.

Phase 1 build (this issue): a laptop-side exporter on a 15-minute schedule that uses the session's own device/egress (SSH-forwarded CDP or a laptop-local script — follow the investigation report's specified design) to call subscription-quota + billing-banner, and writes a dated quota-read file in the gatherer's file-export format (source labelled file-export/meta-laptop) where the #1151 gatherer's ingest picks it up. Failure states: session-expired / laptop-unreachable / unparseable each produce a distinct stale state on the Meta card, never a zero reading.
Phase 2 (separate, after Phase 1 proves stable): trial off-laptop replay from the gatherer host.
Acceptance: Meta windows (5h %, weekly %, resets) + free credits arrive at 15-minute cadence on /quota with measuredAt + source; killing the laptop session produces the expired state, not stale-as-current data.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A laptop-side exporter runs on a 15-minute schedule using the enrolled Meta/dev.meta.ai session's own device/egress and writes the subscription-quota, billing-banner, and usage/batch data to the export location the quota plane consumes.
- [ ] A 401 / session-binding failure surfaces as an explicit 're-capture needed' state — never as zero quota values.
- [ ] No credential value appears in any repo file, commit, or log; the session/cookie is referenced by its secure home only.
- [ ] The export is verified end-to-end against a live quota read (weighted used/limit and both reset windows present and sane).

# id: TODO.md backlog rollup — small ideas not yet covered elsewhere

Drew's rule (2026-10-26): every feature, concept, or idea gets a GitHub issue, even small ones, so nothing lives only in a doc. `pkgs/id/TODO.md` is the last un-issued idea pile. This rollup captures its still-relevant themes; **triage splits any item that is still wanted into its own issue and drops the rest with a note** (drop rule). The worlds platform superseded some of the file-era context — judge each item against the current platform, not the old one.

- [ ] Cursor presence UX: inactive-cursor fade/strobe stop at minimum opacity, hover restores full visibility, click-to-enlarge tooltip, tooltip modes (full / minimal / hidden) with per-cursor minimize/restore lists, pin/unpin — plus client+server logging of cursor lifecycle and a check that inactivity is based on connection liveness, not pointer idleness
- [ ] Structured logging everywhere: JSON log lines with trace ids and context properties, nanosecond RFC timestamps (host tz, UTC fallback, override), CLI flag for log level alongside RUST_LOG, log-to-file with per-destination levels
- [ ] Web shell: header/footer occasionally doubling (suspected stale page across redeploys) — verify and fix
- [ ] Web settings: client id shows 0s; id should persist across in-site navigation (server-issued, unspoofable), name setting propagates to other clients' cursors, theme names below their icons in theme colors
- [ ] Petnames: clients can name nodes/peers and see petnames across CLI/REPL/web, local-only or shared
- [ ] Tags on files/nodes with provenance (who tagged, when, order) + tag search across CLI/REPL/web; uploaded-file origin (node/time) shown in listings with sort/filter
- [ ] Send files server-to-server from CLI/REPL and web
- [ ] Mail outbox (`--world-mail-outbox`) removal decision once envelope/mail paths settle
- [ ] ProseMirror wire format: measure JSON-in-binary cost; evaluate true binary or compression (client/server CPU vs latency vs size)
- [ ] Build hygiene: build-variants file as a cargo build artifact, justfile formatting in CI (`--check`), `just ci` running duplicated test blocks

Source: `pkgs/id/TODO.md` (254 lines). Related: #792 (ProseMirror replication gap), F11.8 search work, F12.6 audit/telemetry (#1063) — the logging item overlaps F12.6 only for world audit; this is app-wide log hygiene.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every still-relevant theme in pkgs/id/TODO.md is either split into its own issue (linked from a disposition comment here) or dropped with a one-line reason on this issue — the drop rule from the body.
- [ ] Each item is judged against the current worlds platform, not the file-era context the TODO was written in.
- [ ] When the disposition is complete, pkgs/id/TODO.md is updated to point at the issues (or emptied of the rolled-up items) and this rollup closes.

body: Follow-up to #229, from queue task 1240's classification of the isolated Firefox dispatch run [40402931464](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/40402931464) (PR #987 branch). Two failures in `pkgs/id/e2e/tests/editor-features.spec.ts` are proven **test defects**, not product bugs: 1. **:1098 "image node renders in markdown editor"** — the uploaded image DID render with the correct `/blob/…` src (see the job-log failure block), but `page.locator("#editor .ProseMirror img")` also matches ProseMirror's internal ``, so `toBeVisible()` fails with a strict-mode violation on both attempts. Fix: scope the locator to the real image (e.g. `img.pm-image`). 2. **:1601 (Image Alt-Text) and :1665 (Image Resize)** — both POST `/api/save` with `{ name, doc }` and **no `doc_id`**. `SaveRequest.doc_id` is a required `String` (`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1077`), so the payload is rejected before the handler and `expect(saveResp.ok())` fails deterministically (~2–5s, both attempts). Every passing save in the same spec sends `doc_id: hash` from its `/api/new` response. Fix: do the same in these two tests. Verified non-causes: a standalone codec probe converts both exact image docs to markdown successfully on current main, so PM→MD conversion is not the failure. ## Acceptance criteria - :1098 locator matches only the uploaded image and the test passes in an isolated Firefox run. - :1601 and :1665 send `doc_id` from their `/api/new` response and pass the save assertion in an isolated Firefox run. - No product code changed; no other assertions weakened. Evidence pack: goal `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-t1240/failures.txt` (failure blocks editor-features 2/3/4), classification comment on #229 by queue task 1240.

## Pilot — information gathering for the OpenChamber babysitter

Question: what can a babysitter process actually read and do against
the laptop's OpenChamber/OpenCode stack, programmatically, from a
different host?

Gather and document (in the fleet goal workspace, linked from this
issue):

- Session list/inspect endpoints: fields available per session (id,
  title, status, directory, created/updated, last activity, current
  model/provider, parent/child sessions).
- Message injection: how to send a follow-up message into a running
  session (the babysitter's nudge), and how to create a session bound
  to a project directory/worktree.
- Auth: what credential the babysitter needs, where it lives
  (Bitwarden name only in the doc — never a value), and whether the
  sandbox can reach the laptop endpoints (Tailscale) with acceptable
  latency.
- Gaps: anything the babysitter design needs that the API does not
  expose (e.g. per-session token usage, pool attribution) — name each
  gap and a workaround if one exists (session metadata written at
  dispatch time is an acceptable workaround; record it as such).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An inventory doc exists listing endpoints + fields, verified by
      live calls against the laptop stack (not from docs alone).
- [ ] A babysitter-host process on the sandbox lists the laptop's
      current sessions and reads one session's activity end-to-end.
- [ ] Every design dependency on the API is marked confirmed or gap,
      with the workaround named for each gap.

Part of the OpenChamber dispatch + babysitter design (2026-10-26).

body:
## Finding
Found during the #1046 deploy (2026-10-26, flagged on that issue, never separately filed): install.sh's `systemctl --user enable --now` does not restart an already-running pm-aggregator - the first post-install check 404'd on new routes while the new code was on disk. A deploy that looks successful but serves old code is a coherence hazard for every future slice.
## Proposal
install.sh restarts pm-aggregator when the deployed tree changes (hash or mtime comparison), then self-verifies: poll /api/health plus one route per newly shipped page (or a version marker the server exposes - e.g. build commit in /api/health) and fail loudly on mismatch.
## Acceptance
- Re-running install.sh on unchanged code is a no-op; on changed code the service restarts and the version marker in /api/health matches the deployed commit.

## Acceptance criteria

- Re-running `install.sh` on unchanged code is a no-op (no restart).
- Re-running `install.sh` after the deployed tree changes restarts pm-aggregator, and the version marker exposed by `/api/health` matches the deployed commit.
- `install.sh` self-verifies after a deploy (polls `/api/health` plus one route per newly shipped page, or the version marker) and fails loudly on a mismatch instead of reporting success while old code serves.

body:
## Finding
Evidence (live review 2026-10-26 ~22:40 CDT, laptop loopback + gh, cross-checked): Nothing alerts when a PM-stack input dies: the feed could stop, the orchestrator could stop publishing, Kaneo could go down, and every dashboard page would keep rendering yesterday's data with ages buried in a footer line. The orchestration rejection ran ~a day unnoticed. Drew's standing rule: automation alerts only on genuinely new information.
## Proposal
A check owned by the orchestration pass (or collector): thresholds per input (feed >15m, orchestration >90m, Kaneo/Grist/Pad probe fail, registry stale >1h) -> publish a NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR item (existing tier mechanism) naming the input and age; auto-resolves when the input recovers. No Drew-facing alert unless it persists across 2 runs or hits NEEDS DREW criteria.
## Acceptance
- Simulated stale input (fixture/threshold test) produces exactly one tier item; recovery clears it.
- Thresholds documented in the job body.
Refs: #899.

## Acceptance criteria

- A watchdog check (owned by the orchestration pass or the collector) applies documented per-input thresholds: feed >15m stale, orchestration >90m stale, Kaneo/Grist/Pad probe failure, registry stale >1h.
- A breached threshold publishes exactly one NEEDS ORCHESTRATOR tier item naming the input and its age; the item auto-resolves when the input recovers.
- A simulated stale input (fixture/threshold test) produces exactly one tier item, and recovery clears it.
- No Drew-facing alert fires unless the condition persists across 2 runs or meets NEEDS DREW criteria; thresholds are documented in the owning job body.

## Summary
Phase B of the per-project pages: the complexity-weighted visualization from the project-structure spec (2026-10-26, lab-cluster goal workspace). The v1 pages (epic's build issue) show counts and items; this issue adds the weighted, graph-aware view — and the feed data it needs, which the aggregator does not currently ingest.

## Data gap to close first
Project-pool items today carry Status/Area/Horizon/Kind only. The spec's visualization needs, per issue:
- `effort/*` label (weights: xs=1, s=4, m=12, l=40; unlabeled = unsized weight, shown separately, never zero)
- `mode/*` label family (online/hybrid/physical — creation of this family across the four repos is part of the cluster seeding; this issue consumes it, and must render gracefully before it exists)
- Issue graph edges: sub-issue parents, blocked-by/blocks, epic membership

Extend the fleet-feed collector's Project section (or a companion section) to carry labels + edges for pool items, with the aggregator model/check updated in lockstep — one contract change, both sides in one PR where feasible.

## Per-project section (rendered on /program/<id>)
1. Weighted rollup bar — total weight, weighted % done (closed weight / total), raw issue count as secondary metric
2. Hands queue — open mode/physical + mode/hybrid weight (hands-hours waiting) vs online weight
3. Blocked weight — weight behind an open blocker + longest dependency chain (depth)
4. Link/depth graph — epic → issue tree; node size = weight, color = status, border = mode (solid online, dashed hybrid, thick physical); edges = parent/blocks. Server-rendered (SVG) in keeping with the aggregator's no-client-JS pattern.

Project header rolls sections up the same way (weighted progress first, counts second, deepest chain + physical weight remaining as headlines).

## Acceptance
- A project with effort/mode/graph data renders all four elements from live feed data; a project without it renders the v1 sections plus an explicit "not yet sized/ graphed" note — never a fake 0%.
- Collector + aggregator contract change covered by tests on both sides.
- Works at phone width (the dashboard is mobile-first).

Refs: project-structure spec §Visualization; #910 (pool), epic for per-project pages.
