labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Bug

Saving a ProseMirror table whose first row is made of `table_cell` nodes (no `table_header` row) produces output that is not a table at all:

```json
{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"table","content":[
  {"type":"table_row","content":[
    {"type":"table_cell","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"x"}]}]}
  ]}
]}]}
```

`prosemirror_to_markdown` returns `Ok("| x |\n")` — a single pipe row with **no delimiter row** (`| --- |`). Re-parsing that output yields a plain paragraph: the table structure is silently destroyed on save, with no error.

Root cause: in `json_to_ast`'s `table_row` arm (pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs, ~:1087), a row is marked as the header row only when its first cell is a `table_header` node. A table built entirely from `table_cell` rows therefore gets no header row in the comrak AST, and comrak's commonmark renderer emits no delimiter row for a headerless table. Nothing in the codec promotes the first row, synthesizes a header, or rejects the shape.

## Evidence (verified 2026-10-26 on main cf60812d)

Standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of `src/web/markdown.rs` (comrak 0.56.0 locked) — log in goal hidden_files `probe-2026-10-26-2145/out4.log`, case `t_table_no_header`: `SAVE4 table_no_header | ok="| x |\n"`. Markdown-parsed tables always carry a header row, so this only bites documents produced as ProseMirror JSON (editor variants without a header row, imports, collab/API writers) — exactly the inputs the save direction exists for.

Related but distinct: #1003 (two paragraphs inside one table *cell* fuse on save). This issue is about the table's header row, not cell contents.

## Why it matters

A document containing a headerless table saves "successfully" while its table silently becomes a paragraph — structural data loss with no signal, the same failure family as the other codec save-direction losses (#1003, #1004, #1036).

## Acceptance criteria

- Saving a PM table whose rows are all `table_cell` preserves the table: either the first row is promoted to a header row (delimiter row emitted, re-parse yields an equivalent table), or the conversion returns a `ConversionError` — silently emitting a non-table is not acceptable.
- Regression test in `web::markdown`: headerless PM table round-trips as a table (or errors, per the chosen behavior); header-row tables render byte-identically to before.
- Existing `web::markdown` tests still pass.

body:
## Finding

The design specifies search by author and by kind, and multi-term AND over tag claims, but neither is built and no issue tracks the gap. The tag-search CLI verb is wired (`id claim search NAME [VALUE]`), so this is purely the library-side scope expansion.

## Evidence

- Phase 5 record `doc/2026-10-12T14-33-36Z_phase_5_tags_documents/...md`, P5.5 Open: "Search by author and by kind (design §9.4) is not built. The index has no author key." and "Multi-term AND (task 06, item 3) is not built."
- Plan `doc/2026-10-11T11-08-42Z_design_remaining_work/plan-phases.md` §10, P5.5: "Search over the tag index" — done (`src/search.rs`, `tests/search.rs`), but the design §9.4 / task 06 item 3 scope is broader than the delivered single-name search.
- `pkgs/id/src/search.rs`: `search` takes one name (`ValueMatch::{Any, Bare, Exact}`); no author key in `src/tag_index.rs` (`named` only).

## Why it matters

Plausible improvement over the delivered P5.5, already designed, so it should either be built or explicitly descoped with a note. Left untracked it will be silently dropped.

## Suggested scope

Add an author key to the tag index and author/kind search terms, plus multi-term AND; or record a decision that single-name search is the intended scope and close this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Library search supports searching by author and by kind, in addition to the existing name/value search, and the tag index carries the author key needed for it.
- [ ] Multi-term search combines terms with AND semantics.
- [ ] Tests cover author search, kind search, and multi-term AND in the search / tag-index test suites; existing single-name search behavior is unchanged and its tests still pass.
- [ ] OR, as an alternative closing path: a descope decision is recorded on this issue (single-name search is the intended scope) and the Phase 5 design record (P5.5) is updated to match.

body:
## Finding

The platform-completion work implemented signed document revisions on ProseMirror save, but those revisions are published only to the local node's event store and are never synced to other peers. This is the one known-incomplete platform-completion item and it has no dedicated tracking issue.

## Evidence (plan vs implementation)

- `doc/2026-10-14T_platform_completion/acceptance-brief.md` line 27: "**Known gap:** the sibling `LocalEvents` store is not replicated to other peers; collaboration is live in the hosted web session, but event-backed revision discovery is currently local-only."
- Acceptance brief line 50, workstream item is unchecked: "Join the ProseMirror collaboration persistence path to signed document revisions and blob storage **and replicate those revisions**. Implemented locally: ... **Not complete:** the local event store is not synced to other peers, so another node cannot yet discover those signed revisions through this path."
- `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1114-1132`: the `/api/save` path stores the blob, then `state.local_events.lock().await; events.publish(...)` returns a `document_id`.
- `pkgs/id/src/local_events.rs:3-11` (module doc): "The store stands in for sync. ... Nothing here moves events between machines."

## Why it matters

Signed revision discovery is the durability/authority backbone for collaborative documents. Without peer replication, a second node cannot discover the signed revisions another node published — the collaboration is live-only within the hosting session, so revision history is not portable across the network as the signed-document model intends.

## Suggested scope (do not assume; for the implementer to plan)

Replicate the LocalEvents store across peers (likely via the existing sync path that ingests signed events) so another node can discover published `document.put` revisions, or otherwise connect the save path to cross-node event transport. This is large; it is intentionally left as an issue, not a quick fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- ProseMirror save revisions are cryptographically signed and stored locally in `id` in a way consistent with the sibling phase-8 / platform-completion issues, with the signing identity and storage location named in the implementation.
- A stored revision can be loaded back and its signature verified; a tampered or unsigned revision is rejected (or clearly flagged) rather than silently trusted.
- Tests cover the round-trip (save -> store -> load -> verify) and the tamper case.
- No regression to existing ProseMirror save/load behaviour when revision signing is absent or disabled.

title: id(app_manifest): discovery registers apps whose program.source does not exist — manifest is never checked against its folder

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`discover_apps` (`pkgs/id/src/app_manifest.rs:152-200`, main @ df3f836e) validates the manifest's text but never checks it against the folder it describes: a `[program].source` path that does not exist inside the app folder is accepted, and the app is returned in `apps` with no error. `parse_app_manifest` checks the source path's *shape* (relative, `Component::Normal` only, app_manifest.rs:124-133) — shape is all that is ever checked; nothing stats the path, in either the parser or discovery.

Verified this run with a probe crate on the laptop compiling a sha256-identical copy of `app_manifest.rs` from main df3f836e (probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-appmanifest-20261101`, `probe2` binary): an app folder `ghost-app/` whose `app.toml` declares

```toml
[program]
kind = "roc-world"
source = "program/does-not-exist.wasm"
```

with no `program/` directory on disk at all → `discover_apps` returns `apps=1, errors=0` — the ghost app is fully "discovered", and `cmd_serve` (`src/commands/serve.rs:786-788`) logs it as a discovered app.

## Why it matters

Discovery is the host's registration gate (#2324: "validates … and registers the app"; design §3 same). Its per-app error isolation exists so a broken app folder disables *itself with a named error* instead of failing mysteriously later. A moved/renamed program directory — the exact accident that just happened in-repo when tic-tac-toe moved from `examples/` to `apps/tic-tac-toe/program/` in #3926 — currently produces a successfully-discovered app that will only fail at launch time, in a different code path, with no pointer back to the manifest.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Discovery (or a validation step it calls) checks that a declared `program.source` exists inside the app folder (file or directory — the checked-in manifest uses the `program/` directory) and records a named per-app error, excluding the app from `apps`, when it does not.
- [ ] A unit test covers the ghost-source case: app excluded, one error naming the missing source path.
- [ ] The checked-in tic-tac-toe app (source `program/`, a directory) still discovers cleanly, and module_hash-only manifests (no source) are unaffected.
- [ ] Serve's discovered-app logging therefore never reports an app whose declared program is absent.

body:
# pm-dispatch(sessions): directory confinement is lexical only — committed symlinks in the clone escape it (residual of #2903)

## Summary

`resolveSessionDirectory` (pm-stack/dispatch/src/validate.ts:159-176) confines a
`POST /v1/sessions` directory to the target repo's clone using only lexical
normalization (`normalizeDirectory`, validate.ts:182-199): it collapses `.`/`..`
segments and checks the `root/` prefix. Nothing canonicalizes the path
(no `realpath` anywhere in pm-stack/dispatch/src), so a path that is lexically
inside the clone but passes through a symlink pointing outside is accepted —
and the directory is handed verbatim to the OpenCode session create
(server.ts:191, opencode.ts:53-59 `location: { directory }`).

The code repo itself commits two such symlinks at its root (both mode 120000
in `git ls-files` on main 83709fac):

- `nixpkgs` → `../nixpkgs` (a sibling path outside the clone)
- `worktrees` → `/home/user/.local/share/opencode/worktree/code` (absolute,
  outside the clone)

## Verified (laptop probe, this run)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-dispatchdir/` — verbatim copy of
validate.ts (sha256 c98ce808…, identical to main), REPO_DIRS value for
developing-today/code from config.ts:37 (`/home/user/git/code`), run with bun:

- control `/home/user/git/code/pm-stack` → ACCEPTED, realpath inside clone ✓
- control `/home/user/git/nix` → REJECTED ✓
- control `/home/user/git/code/../nix` → REJECTED ✓
- `/home/user/git/code/worktrees` → **ACCEPTED** as inside the clone, but
  `realpath` = `/home/user/.local/share/opencode/worktree/code` — **outside the
  clone**, and the target directory exists on the laptop, so a session can
  actually be rooted there
- `/home/user/git/code/nixpkgs` → **ACCEPTED**, symlink target `../nixpkgs`
  resolves outside the clone (currently dangling on this laptop; the checker's
  verdict is wrong regardless of whether the target exists today)

## Why it matters

The directory scope is the confinement boundary the #2903 fix (priority/high,
kind/security) and #2664 established: "OIDC callers may only run inside the
target repo clone". A caller whose own repo is allowlisted (or a bearer
caller) can name a directory in a *different* repo's clone area that a
committed symlink reaches — e.g. dispatching against developing-today/code
with directory `/home/user/git/code/worktrees` starts the session in the
OpenCode worktree store, outside the code clone entirely. The same lexical
gap applies to any symlink a repo gains in the future, and to `..` segments
that follow a symlinked component (lexical collapse happens before the OS
resolves the symlink, so the two disagree).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Session-directory resolution canonicalizes the candidate (and the
      configured root) with realpath semantics before the prefix check, so a
      lexically-inside path whose real location is outside the clone is
      rejected with the same ValidationError as other out-of-scope paths.
- [ ] Nonexistent candidate directories keep working or fail with a clear
      validation error (today a not-yet-created subdirectory of the clone is
      accepted lexically; the fix must state and test what happens for them —
      e.g. canonicalize the nearest existing ancestor).
- [ ] Regression tests cover: a symlinked component inside the clone pointing
      outside (rejected), a symlinked component pointing elsewhere inside the
      same clone (accepted), `..` after a symlinked component, and the two
      committed cases (`nixpkgs`, `worktrees`) by name or equivalent fixture.
- [ ] Existing directory tests still pass: missing/blank → clone root,
      plain outside path and plain `..` escape → rejected (#2664/#2903 cases).

Related: #2903 (original escape, fixed lexically), #2664 (directory
validation), #2668 (directory-scope design).

`nixos-rebuild switch` on the laptop fails building `id-0.1.0.drv`:

```
error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate `vt100` in this scope
error: could not compile `id-core` (lib test) due to 4 previous errors
```

Hit 2026-11-01 13:36 CST evaluating main `1b1e3abd` (log: laptop `~/switch-20261101-132033.log`). This is a *different* id breakage from #3787 (voiding_scenarios runtime failures, fixed by #3871) — that fix is in the tree; this one surfaced behind it.

`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_presentation.rs` uses `vt100::Parser` in its test module (ANSI replay assertions). title: aggregator(dns): isDnsSection never checks totalAnnualListUsd, entry priceUsd or status — a missing total or a string price crashes renderDns, an infinite price renders as $Infinity

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: status/duplicate
labels.description: Already tracked elsewhere

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Finding

`isDnsSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/dns.ts:74-90) — the structural check "shared by the collector and the live source" for the DNS register section — checks only `generatedAt`, that `entries` is a non-empty array, and that each entry has a string `domain` and `renewal`. It never checks the section's `totalAnnualListUsd` or `source`, nor an entry's `priceUsd` / `status` / remaining string fields, although `DnsSection`/`DnsEntry` (model.ts:702-710 and the DnsEntry interface) require them and `renderDns` dereferences them unguarded. A section no producer can emit passes the gate and crashes or falsifies the /dns page.

The producer path always emits the full shape: `dnsSectionFromRegister` (dns.ts:66-72) computes `totalAnnualListUsd` as a rounded number and `parseDnsRegister` sets every entry field, deriving `priceUsd` via `parsePriceUsd` (number or null) and `status` via `classifyDnsStatus`.

## Evidence (main 33aefa7f, verified this run)

- dns.ts:74-90 — no check on `s.totalAnnualListUsd`, `s.source`, `e.priceUsd`, `e.status`, `e.registrar`, `e.autoRenew`, `e.plan`, or `e.review`; `renewal` is any string.
- render.ts:3002 — `$${section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed(2)}` unguarded; render.ts:2980 and :3006 — `e.priceUsd != null ? e.priceUsd.toFixed(2)`; render.ts:3000 — `soonTotal` sums `e.priceUsd ?? 0` into a rendered dollar total.
- dns.ts summarizeDns (:103-118) — buckets entries by `e.status === "active"/"earmarked"/"unused"` and compares `e.renewal` lexicographically against today/cutoff, so a missing status silently drops the entry from every bucket and a non-date renewal sorts as future.
- Laptop Bun probe (~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-dnsgate/, real dns.ts/render.ts from the laptop primary at 33aefa7f; sha256 dns.ts 8217f569…, render.ts 061fc8ad… — identical to sandbox main; well-formed control renders OK, 27,592 bytes):
  - `totalAnnualListUsd` missing → gate `true`, `renderDns` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed')`
  - `totalAnnualListUsd: "11.08"` → gate `true`, throws `TypeError: section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed is not a function`
  - entry `priceUsd: "11.08"` (string) → gate `true`, throws `TypeError: next.priceUsd.toFixed is not a function`
  - entry `priceUsd: Infinity` (what JSON `1e999` parses to) → gate `true`, renders — the price renders as `$Infinity` and poisons the renewing-soon total
  - entry `renewal: "banana"` → gate `true`, renders verbatim and is treated as a future renewal by summarizeDns; `renewal: "2026-02-30"` likewise passes (shape-only string)
  - entry without `status` → gate `true`, renders, but the entry vanishes from all three status buckets while still counting in `entries.length` ("N domains" disagrees with the portfolio-shape card)

## Why it matters

/dns is the domain-portfolio page — renewal spend and lapse visibility. The section rides the fleet feed as hand-/script-produced JSON, exactly the input this shared gate exists to fail soft against (the live source falls back when the gate rejects). Today one malformed section takes the whole page down, or worse, quietly misstates it: an infinite price in the spend total, a domain invisible in every status bucket, a nonsense renewal presented as next. Sibling section gates (#2429 quota, #2446 subscriptions) validate the fields their renderers dereference; this one validates almost none of them.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isDnsSection` (or a load-boundary sanitizer in the #2429/#2446 pattern, layer pinned in triage) validates: `totalAnnualListUsd` a finite number, `source` a string, and per entry `priceUsd` a finite number or null, `status` one of the three classes, the remaining rendered string fields strings, and `renewal` a real calendar date in YYYY-MM-DD form (the shared `isIsoDate`/calendar helper, not a bare string).
- A section failing those checks is rejected/dropped at the boundary so /dns falls back instead of throwing; a well-formed section (existing fixtures/tests) renders unchanged.
- Regression tests cover at least: missing/string `totalAnnualListUsd`, string `priceUsd`, `priceUsd` Infinity, a status-less entry, and a non-date renewal.

Dedup: #3441 (open) covers this gate's `generatedAt` only (bare Date.parse rolling 2026-02-30) — different fields, cross-linked, not covering totals/prices/status/renewal. #2412/#2415 are the aa/quota-current stamps. Searches for "isDnsSection", "totalAnnualListUsd", and "dns priceUsd" across open and closed issues return no covering issue.

title: route-proxy: overnight window gates check daysOfWeek against the wrong day — the after-midnight leg follows the calendar day, not the day the window opened

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/opencode-route-proxy
labels.description: bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs fleet proxy

body:
## Bug

`windowActive` in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` (lines 406–431) checks `daysOfWeek` against the **current** calendar day before it ever looks at the time range, so an overnight window (end ≤ start, e.g. Fri 22:00 → Sat 02:00) attributes its after-midnight leg to the wrong day:

- The day filter runs first (lines 425–428): the weekday of `now` must be in `daysOfWeek`.
- Only then does the wrap branch run (line 431): `mins >= start || mins < end`.

For a window `{ daysOfWeek: ["fri"], start: "22:00", end: "02:00", timezone: "UTC" }`:

- **Sat 01:00 is reported inactive**, although it is inside the window that opened Fri 22:00 — the gate drops the target for the last two hours of its own window.
- **Fri 01:00 is reported active**, although that after-midnight leg belongs to a window that would have opened Thu 22:00, and Thursday is not in `daysOfWeek` — the gate admits the target on a day the operator never listed.

Inverted gates (`window: { name, invert: true }`, `targetEligible` lines 433–437) inherit both errors flipped.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-windowwrap/`): `parseHHMM` + `windowActive` extracted **verbatim** (lines 398–432) from `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` at main `064ce9e5` (file sha256 prefix `6269e7bf933138a0`), driven with the Fri 22:00→02:00 UTC window above:

- FAIL Sat 01:00 — got `false`, want `true` (after-midnight leg of the Friday window)
- FAIL Fri 01:00 — got `true`, want `false` (after-midnight leg belongs to Thursday)
- PASS Thu 23:00 `false`, Fri 21:59 `false`, Fri 23:00 `true`, Sat 02:00 `false`, Sat 23:00 `false`
- Controls pass: the existing non-wrapping fixture shape (Fri 01:00–04:00) gives Fri 02:30 `true`, Sat 02:30 `false`.

The existing tests (`bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs`, window-gate tests from #3225) only exercise a non-wrapping window (`peak`, Mon–Fri 01:00–04:00), so the wrap/day interaction is untested. Related: #3225 (window gates), #3256 (provider routes in the same file).

## Why it matters

Window gates exist to route traffic to specific providers at specific times (peak/off-peak pools). An overnight window silently loses its last hours and gains hours on an unlisted day — the route sends traffic to the wrong pool with no error anywhere; the only symptom is cost/quota behaviour nobody can explain from the config.

## Acceptance criteria

- For a wrapping window (end ≤ start): the evening leg (`mins >= start`) is active iff the current day is in `daysOfWeek`; the after-midnight leg (`mins < end`) is active iff the **previous** day is in `daysOfWeek`. With no `daysOfWeek` (or an empty list), both legs stay governed by the time range alone, as today.
- Non-wrapping windows behave exactly as today; unknown windows still fail closed; inverted gates invert the corrected result.
- New tests in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` cover at least: Fri-only 22:00–02:00 window active at Sat 01:00, inactive at Fri 01:00, active Fri 23:00, inactive Sat 23:00 — plus the existing window-gate tests still passing.

title: id(trust): idset schema types + canonical body encoding + sign/decode round-trip (writer-set spec slice 1 of #3789)

## What and why

Slice 1 of the implementation routing in the writer-set spec (`doc/2026-10-30T13-15-00Z_design_id_writer_set_view_projection/`, §9 item 1) for origin issue #3789 (Phase 2 of #2031). The spec sequences the build so no counting path exists before the set object and its versioning do; this slice is the foundation: **schema types only, library only, no projection yet.**

## Build

- `WriterSet` body type for the signed event kind `idset.writer` (spec §D1): `{ set_id, version, owner, scope?, entries: Vec<Entry>, excludes: Vec<Entry> }` carried in the event **body** (canonical CBOR, length-prefixed like `DocumentRef` content), never in `ChainExt` — reusing `chain::sign` / `chain::decode` so `verify_strict` checks it with no new crypto (`pkgs/id/src/chain.rs`).
- `Entry` as the three-shape union (spec §D3): `Key { author, include_history }`, `Group { id, role_min, include_history }`, `Public { include_history }` — `include_history` on every shape, omitted = `false` (the prospective default).
- `Excludes` as entries that win over includes (spec §D6), and a `Rescind` type (spec §3.3 shape) — types and encoding only; no semantics evaluated in this slice.
- `version` is the owner's chain sequence (spec §D2): the type does not carry an owner-invented counter; `set_id` is the stable derived ID (BLAKE3 over `(owner, purpose)`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Golden-header / round-trip tests in the style of `chain.rs:733-852`: a `WriterSet` body signs, decodes, and verifies through the existing strict path
- [ ] A decode test asserts an entry written before `include_history` existed decodes as `include_history: false` rather than failing
- [ ] No projection, expansion, or counting code lands in this slice (spec §9 sequencing)

## Origin

Filed by queue task 5775's worker (lane B, 2026-11-01): the #3789 packet bundled spec §9 slices 1+2+4 into one 45-minute `small_fix` and was blocked as a packet defect; this slice is its sequenced successor. Parent: #2048 (ID Zettelkasten design). Phase 1 — foundational, no hard dependency.

Implement the approved #2048 model in `pkgs/id`: a stable logical note identity, distinct from immutable content-revision event IDs, with append-only signed revisions and explicit causal parent revision IDs. Use blob-backed content snapshots and expose deterministic note history/head state. Concurrent revisions must remain separate heads; an explicit merge revision names the heads it joins. Preserve existing `document.put` and `document.remove` behavior for non-note documents.

Scope: core event representation, validation, local event-store fold/history, and focused tests. No editor/UI, full-text or backlink index, shared-write authorization, cross-store resolver, or migration of existing files. Do not add a deletion/erasure API in this phase: #2048 has an open product question about tombstone vs cryptographic erasure, and the current `document.remove` retains content.

Acceptance:
- Note ID remains stable across revisions and is not a mutable filename or alias.
- Every revision is signed, immutable, content-hash verified, and names its note plus causal parent revision(s).
- Two concurrent revisions produce two deterministic heads; a merge explicitly names both; arrival order does not change history.
- Existing document event fixtures and public behavior remain compatible.
- Unit/integration tests cover validation, revision lookup, concurrent heads and explicit merge.

Related inputs: #2047 (friendly names resolve to stable IDs); #2238 (writer-set/view projection is a separate visibility layer). This phase establishes data identity only; it does not decide who may write a shared note.

body:
# mcpx(completion): completionCaller keys the per-caller rate limit on the daemon's own PID for /v1/exec callers — PIDShared is ignored, so unrelated exec callers share one completion.perMinute budget

## Summary

The completion rate limiter added in #2387 (PR #3730) derives its per-caller key from
`completionCaller` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go:443-452`):

```go
func completionCaller(cc config.CallContext) string {
	switch {
	case cc.SessionID != "":
		return "session:" + cc.SessionID
	case cc.PID > 0:
		return "pid:" + strconv.Itoa(cc.PID)
	default:
		return "call:" + cc.CallID
	}
}
```

The `cc.PID > 0` arm never checks `cc.PIDShared`. That flag exists precisely for a PID
that does **not** identify the caller: `callContext` sets it when the reported PID is
the daemon's own (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/server.go:1079-1081`), which is what every
`/v1/exec` run reports — the exec service puts the daemon's `os.Getpid()` in the script
environment as `MCPX_PID` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:989`), and the generated
client forwards it as the `x-mcpx-pid` header (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/codegen/emit.go:722`).

`config.CallContext` documents the doctrine (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/config/scope.go:34-39`):
a shared PID "is a shared instance key, never caller-private", and `CallerOwned` guards
its pid arm with `!c.PIDShared` (`scope.go:64`). `completionCaller` is the one consumer
that doesn't.

## Verified behavior (this run, main b4c4a99a)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-pidshared/` (verbatim `completionCaller`
+ `rateLimiter.admit`; ops.go md5 7851998d, ratelimit.go md5 f49ba6ff, scope.go md5
34a729d6, all @ b4c4a99a):

```
CASE shared-pid caller A key: "pid:4242"
CASE shared-pid caller B key: "pid:4242"
CASE admit A (limit 1): refused=<nil>
CASE admit B (limit 1): refused=true by completion.perMinute
CTRL own-pid keys: "pid:111" vs "pid:222"; admit C refused=<nil>, admit D refused=<nil>
CTRL session keys: "session:s1" vs "session:s2"
```

Two distinct session-less exec callers (each with its own per-call id, `PIDShared=true`)
collapse into the single bucket `caller\x00pid:<daemon-pid>\x00<server>` used at
`ops.go:371`. The first caller's admissions exhaust `completion.perMinute` for **every**
exec caller of that server until the window rolls; the rest get 429s naming a limit they
never personally consumed.

This also contradicts `completionCaller`'s own doc comment: the per-call fallback is
supposed to leave a caller with nothing stable to bind "effectively unwindowed per
caller" — a session-less exec caller has nothing stable of its own (its PID is the
daemon's), yet it is windowed, collectively with all other exec callers.

## Why it matters

- Spurious cross-caller 429s on the completion path for exactly the caller class
  (agent exec scripts) that drives the daemon hardest; the failure looks like the
  caller's own quota and is undiagnosable from the 429 text.
- The per-server window (`completion.serverPerMinute`) is the designed backstop for
  unbindable callers; the per-caller window silently becoming a second, accidental
  aggregate window defeats the two-window design from #2386/#2387.

## Acceptance criteria

- `completionCaller` treats a `PIDShared` PID as no PID: a session-less caller with
  `PIDShared=true` keys on its per-call id (`call:<CallID>`), matching `CallerOwned`'s
  `!PIDShared` guard.
- Regression tests: two `PIDShared` contexts with distinct CallIDs get distinct keys
  and do not refuse each other at limit 1; own-PID and session keying unchanged
  (existing `ratelimit_test.go` / `completion_ratelimit_test.go` cases still pass).
- A handler-level case (following the `TestHandleComplete…` pattern) shows one
  exec-style caller (daemon PID, no session) no longer 429s a second such caller
  under `completion.perMinute` alone.

## Dedup / related

- #2387 (closed) built the limiter; its tests never exercise a `PIDShared` context —
  no `PIDShared` reference exists in the daemon tests.
- #1942 follow-up (in `server.go` comments) established the daemon-PID sharing trap
  for instance keys; this is the same trap in the new rate-limit key.
- Searched open + closed for `completionCaller`, `PIDShared completion`, and `2387`:
  no existing issue covers this.

# id(cli): pkgs/id does not compile on main — PR #3738 inserted parse_result_limit between Command's derive and the enum

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01, main e49c0beeb)

`pkgs/id/src/cli.rs` lines ~199–212 on current main:

```rust
#[derive(Subcommand, Debug)]
/// Parses a result limit (`--first` / `--last` / peek `--lines`): zero is
/// rejected with a clear error instead of silently producing an empty result
/// or a header-only preview (#3059). ...
fn parse_result_limit(raw: &str) -> Result<usize, String> { ... }

pub enum Command {
```

The `parse_result_limit` function (added by PR #3738, "id(cli/repl): reject zero result limits at both boundaries (#3059)", merged 2026-11-01 09:03 CST as 5fa06504a) was inserted **between** `#[derive(Subcommand, Debug)]` and the `pub enum Command` it belongs to. The derive now targets a function and the enum has no derive.

`cargo test --lib` in pkgs/id on main therefore fails with 24 errors, including:

- `error[E0774]: derive may only be applied to structs, enums and unions` (the misplaced attribute)
- `error[E0277]: cli::Command doesn't implement Debug` (×15, from test code formatting `{other:?}`)
- `error[E0277]: the trait bound cli::Command: Subcommand is not satisfied`
- `error[E0609]: no field format / format_error on Result<FindArgs, anyhow::Error>` (cascade)

Full log from the discovering run: laptop `/tmp/test-4789.log` (queue task 4789's verification build, 2026-11-01).

## Impact

pkgs/id does not compile on main at all — every id change is unverifiable and any CI leg building pkgs/id is red until this is fixed. Discovered while verifying task 4789 / PR #3748 (directory_auth, #1732), which is unrelated and blocked on this for its test run.

## Fix

Move `parse_result_limit` (with its doc comment) so `#[derive(Subcommand, Debug)]` sits directly above `pub enum Command` again — e.g. place the function after the enum or above the derive. No behaviour change: the function body and all `value_parser = parse_result_limit` call sites stay as PR #3738 wrote them.

## Acceptance

- `cargo check` / `cargo test --lib` in pkgs/id compiles on main.
- The #3059 zero-limit rejection still works (existing tests from PR #3738 pass).
- No other behaviour change.

title: aggregator(alerts): runAlertTick marks incidents delivered when every push send failed — critical incidents are silently lost, never retried

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/alerts.ts` — the alert throat engine from #3676 — marks a critical incident **delivered** even when every push send failed. `runAlertTick` (alerts.ts:490-503) discards the delivery outcome:

```ts
const summary = await deliverToAll(store, targets, incident, cfg.publicOrigin, false);
await store.markDelivered(incident.id, { ...summary });
```

It calls `markDelivered` unconditionally. `deliverToAll` (alerts.ts:439-471) counts per-subscription outcomes in the summary (`sent` / `gone` / `errors`), but nothing checks them. `markDelivered` sets `delivered_at`, and `pendingDeliveries` only selects `delivered_at is null` — so an incident whose sends all errored is never retried. Worse, `pendingEscalations` keys off `delivered_at is not null`, so after the ack window the same incident gets "escalated" — and `markEscalated` is called just as unconditionally (alerts.ts:499-502), burning the one escalation on sends that may also all fail. The ledger then records a `delivered` (and `escalated`) event for a notification nobody ever received.

The systemic case is not exotic: `sendPush` (src/push.ts:44-47) returns `{ ok: false, gone: false, error: "VAPID private key unavailable (bws)" }` for **every** subscription when the VAPID key cannot be resolved (bws outage, rotation, sandbox env). One bad tick during such a window permanently swallows every pending critical incident — for the breakthrough class whose entire design premise (#3676, design #3450) is that it "delivers immediately, quiet hours or not, because the sentinels are external to the thing that might be down."

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop with the real `alerts.ts` + `push.ts` at main `9be9c229` (sha256-matched in both clones: alerts.ts `868f4c78…`, push.ts `34745ee0…`; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-alerttick/`, log `probe.log`). A fake in-memory store (recorders only — the SQL layer is not under test) returns one incident-class subscription with an unreachable endpoint and one open critical incident; the real `sendPush` chain runs:

- `logSend` outcomes: `["error"]` — the only send failed (not `gone`, not `sent`)
- store calls: `markDelivered {"subscriptions":1,"sent":0,"gone":0,"errors":1}` — **`markDelivered` was still called with `sent: 0`**
- Result line: `sent=false markDeliveredCalled=true`

Coverage gap that let this ship: `test/alerts.test.ts` pins only the pure helpers (its header says so); `runAlertTick` / `deliverToAll` have no tests at all.

## Why it matters

- A transient push-path failure (VAPID/bws blip, push-service 5xx, network) converts a **retryable** delivery into a **permanent, silent loss** of a critical incident notification — the exact failure the alert throat exists to prevent.
- The ledger lies: `delivered` / `escalated` events and `delivered_at` / `escalated_at` timestamps assert delivery that never happened, so the /alerts page and any later audit show the incident as notified.
- Duplicate posts of the same incident are then treated as `duplicate_suppressed` (because `delivered_at` is set) even though no delivery ever succeeded.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An incident is marked delivered only when at least one subscription send succeeded (`sent >= 1`); when every send errors, `delivered_at` stays null and the next tick retries it. (Sends that return `gone` prune/mark the subscription per the existing §4 rule and do not count as success.)
- [ ] The symmetric rule for escalation: `markEscalated` only after at least one successful escalation send; otherwise the escalation stays pending and is retried.
- [ ] The `delivered` / `escalated` event detail records the summary as today, and a tick where all sends fail leaves an observable trace (event or log) naming the failed delivery attempt and its error count.
- [ ] Regression tests drive `runAlertTick` with a stub store and a failing push path: all-error tick → no `markDelivered`; a later all-error→success sequence → delivered exactly once. (This needs the push sender injectable or an equivalent seam — the pure-helper-only test pattern in `test/alerts.test.ts` cannot reach the engine today.)
- [ ] Existing `alerts.test.ts` tests still pass; behaviour with zero subscriptions is unchanged (incident stays undelivered, per the current documented design).

Distinct from: #3681 (chargesAttention validation in the confirm-charges script — different module, different path), #3676 (the feature build this bug ships in), #3450 (design).

body:
Build the alert throat (Drew approved 2026-11-01, main chat): every sentinel posts incidents to ONE intake; one engine owns dedupe, delivery, escalation, and ack; every transition lands in a durable ledger.

Drew's amendments to the original design (#3450):
- Delivery uses the #1254 PWA Web Push design (doc/2026-11-01T03-54-00Z_design_pwa_push_notifications.md, PR #3314) — this issue builds the push plumbing of #3316 plus an `incident` notification class, ahead of the dashboard-surface classes in #3317.
- The ledger lives in **Supabase muse-dev2**, not local state files: schema `alerts` is already created — `incidents` (with a partial unique index on (source, incident_key) for non-closed rows), `incident_events`, `push_subscriptions`, `notification_sends`.
- It ties into the PM stack: intake, engine, and the ack surface are aggregator features; incidents surface on a new `/alerts` page.

Already done:
- Supabase `alerts` schema (above) in muse-dev2.
- VAPID keypair generated; private key in Bitwarden Secrets Manager as `pm-aggregator.vapid-private-key`; public key ships in the page/worker. VAPID subject: mailto:drewrypope@gmail.com (design Q4 default).

Scope:
1. PWA installability per #3315 (manifest, icons, meta; `PM_AGG_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` defaulting to the Tailscale Serve HTTPS origin — verify serve 443→4870 on the laptop).
2. Real service worker per #3316 with push + notificationclick handlers and eviction-on-activate for foreign registrations (design §6 fallback path; no probe data exists yet), plus `/api/sw-probe` reporting.
3. Subscription API backed by Supabase `alerts.push_subscriptions` (per-class map + quiet prefs round-trip; 404/410 gone-count pruning).
4. Incident intake `POST /api/alerts` (bearer token in Bitwarden as `pm-aggregator.alerts-intake-token`): {source, key, severity, title, body}; dedupe on (source, key); every post writes incident + `incident_events` rows.
5. Engine tick: new critical incident → Web Push to subscriptions with the `incident` class on, `delivered_at` + send log; unacked critical after the ack window (config, default 15 min) → exactly one escalation push. Incident class delivers immediately (it is the breakthrough class — the sentinels are external, so the #3317 §2 "engine is down" reasoning does not apply); dashboard classes keep the design's quiet-hours rules.
6. `/alerts` page: open incidents, ack (exactly once; second ack is a no-op) and close actions, history from Supabase. Push payload deep-links to the incident on this page.
7. A `scripts/post-alert.ts` CLI in the aggregator for sources to post incidents (first wired source: the Globalping watch failure path; second: manual seed for acceptance).

Acceptance: subscription round-trips through Supabase; a seeded critical pushes to a real subscription; a duplicate post sends no second push; escalation fires exactly once inside a shortened test window; ack stops the ladder and is exactly-once; all transitions present in `alerts.incident_events`; no secret material in repo, store, or logs.

## Acceptance criteria
- PWA installability landed per #3315: manifest, icons, and meta in place; `PM_AGG_PUBLIC_ORIGIN` defaults to the Tailscale Serve HTTPS origin.
- Service worker per #3316 serves push and notificationclick handlers, evicts foreign registrations on activate, and `/api/sw-probe` reports registration state.
- Subscription API is backed by Supabase `alerts.push_subscriptions`: per-class map and quiet preferences round-trip; 404/410 responses prune dead subscriptions.
- Incident intake `POST /api/alerts` accepts sentinel incidents (bearer auth), dedupes on (source, incident_key) for non-closed rows in the `alerts` schema, and records every transition in `incident_events`.
- Incidents surface on the aggregator `/alerts` page with ack/escalation state matching the ledger.
- The `incident` notification class delivers via the #1254 Web Push design ahead of the #3317 dashboard-surface classes.

title: openai-cred-watchdog cron check broken: prescribed laptop script path missing (exit 127)
body:
## Problem

The hourly sandbox cron `openai-cred-watchdog` (guard against recurrence of #3216) prescribes running:

```
~/tools/laptop-ssh.sh /home/user/hatch/tools/openai-cred-watchdog.py
```

That command fails on every run — the script does not exist at that laptop path.

## Evidence (2026-11-01 05:21 CST run)

- Exit code: 127
- Error verbatim: `bash: line 1: /home/user/hatch/tools/openai-cred-watchdog.py: No such file or directory`
- Verified independently: `ls /home/user/hatch/tools/` on the laptop contains no `openai-cred-watchdog.py`.

## Mitigating evidence — credential invariant currently holds

The laptop's own systemd user service is the working implementation:

- `openai-cred-watchdog.service`: `ExecStart=/nix/store/phwksv80kc2d5y6cwz2l48v1q27f671i-openai-cred-watchdog/bin/openai-cred-watchdog /home/user/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`
- `openai-cred-watchdog.timer`: hourly, Persistent=true
- Last run 2026-11-01 05:05:53 CST exited 0 with: `OK: openai credential invariant holds (no token-sharing row; active methods browser/headless)`

So this is a broken *sandbox-side check path*, not a credential violation. Per the job body a broken check must be loud, never silent — hence this issue.

## Fix options

1. Point the cron job body at the Nix-built binary (or a stable wrapper path, e.g. via the systemd service / `systemctl --user start openai-cred-watchdog` + journal read), or
2. Restore/deploy `openai-cred-watchdog.py` at `/home/user/hatch/tools/` on the laptop.

Also update the cron definition file (hatch-personal is source of truth for cron definitions) to match whatever path is chosen, per the CRON DEFINITIONS ARE TRUTH rule.

## Acceptance

- The prescribed watchdog command exits 0 with an `OK:` line when the invariant holds.
- A forced/missing-path failure is still reported loudly, not silently.

labels.description: infra/github-backup estate mirror system

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

Codex P2 on PR #3280 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-01T01:33:18Z): "Include secrets in the version advertised for rollback" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3280#discussion_r4434009063

> On a fresh Worker, the tagged version is uploaded before either required secret exists. This subsequent call changes the deployed version: Cloudflare documents that `wrangler secret put` "creates a new version of the Worker and deploys it immediately." Consequently, the version ID printed as live below is not the final secret-bearing version. The `--deploy-version` path deploys that advertised ID without provisioning secrets, so it does not restore the working configuration: the tagged bootstrap version lacks the bearer token required by `/queue` and the HMAC secret required by `/github`. Include the secrets before selecting the tagged deployment version, or retain and advertise the final configured version for rollback.

(Secret names only — no values are involved in this issue: the Worker secrets are `DRAIN_BEARER` and `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, provisioned from Bitwarden by name in `setWorkerSecrets()`.)

## No-response evidence

- PR #3280 merged with the finding unaddressed: the inline comment has no replies, and GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #3280 shows all 3 threads `isResolved=false`.
- No fix commit after the comment: the ordering is still present on current main (below).

## Still-live evidence (verified this run, current main)

`infra/github-backup/worker/deploy.mjs` (current main), normal deploy flow:

1. `versions upload` → tagged `version.id`
2. `createDeployment(version.id)` (when not already live)
3. `setWorkerSecrets()` — each `wrangler secret put` creates and deploys a NEW version, per Cloudflare's documentation
4. `reportLive()` + `console.log("live: ... at version ${version.id}")` — advertising the pre-secrets version id as the live/rollback target

And the `--deploy-version` branch (`createDeployment(deployVersion); reportLive(); process.exit(0)`) never calls `setWorkerSecrets()` at all, so rolling back to the advertised bootstrap version restores a Worker with no `DRAIN_BEARER` / `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: `/queue` auth and `/github` HMAC verification both fail.

## Dedupe

Searched open and closed issues for "github-backup rollback version secrets" (2026-11-01): no issue covers this.

## Acceptance criteria

- The version advertised as live/for rollback is the final secret-bearing version (secrets provisioned before the tagged deployment version is selected, or the final configured version is retained and advertised).
- The `--deploy-version` rollback path provisions (or verifies) the required Worker secrets as part of restoring the working configuration.
- Or the finding is resolved by a documented decision on this issue.

title: github-backup(deploy): --dry-run is ignored on the --deploy-version path — a rollback preview creates a real 100% deployment

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/high

labels.name: effort/s

labels.name: source/pr-comment-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-comment-review job

labels.name: app/github-backup

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

Codex P1 on PR #3280 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-01T01:33:18Z): "Honor dry-run when deploying an existing version" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3280#discussion_r4434009066

> When an operator combines `--dry-run` with `--deploy-version <id>` to preview a rollback, this branch runs before the dry-run check and immediately changes the production deployment. Running the actual script with mocked executables confirmed that it invokes `wrangler versions deploy <id>@100% --name developing-today-backup --yes`, without forwarding `--dry-run`. Wrangler documents the deployment command's `--dry-run` option as "Don't actually deploy," but the wrapper silently discards that protection and bypasses confirmation. Forward the dry-run flag for existing-version deployments, or reject the combination before making any changes.

## No-response evidence

- PR #3280 merged with the finding unaddressed: the inline comment has no replies, and GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #3280 shows all 3 threads `isResolved=false`.
- No fix commit after the comment: the defect is still present on current main (below).

## Still-live evidence (verified this run, current main)

`infra/github-backup/worker/deploy.mjs` (current main):

- The `--deploy-version` branch runs before the dry-run check and exits:
  ```js
  if (deployVersion !== null) {
    createDeployment(deployVersion);
    reportLive();
    process.exit(0);
  }
  if (dryRun) { /* wrangler deploy --dry-run ... */ }
  ```
- `createDeployment()` unconditionally runs `wrangler versions deploy <id>@100% --name developing-today-backup --yes` — no `--dry-run` forwarding, no rejection of the combination.

So `deploy.mjs --dry-run --deploy-version <id>` — the safest-looking way to preview a rollback — performs the real 100% deployment.

## Dedupe / related

title: Quota reads: Command Code reports plan windows, not the top-up balance (extractor renders stale read)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

body:
## Ruling (Drew, 2026-11-01)

All Command Code quota reads report the **plan windows only**: monthly limit (% used, or $ used of the $10 included credits), weekly %, 5-hour %. The extra/top-up credit balance (the studio billing/credits figure) is **not** a quota figure — never report it as the pool's state, never wall the pool on it.

## Defect 1 — aggregator renders a stale Command Code read as current

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` `extractCommandCode` takes the *first* `$X of $Y used` match in the quota view's Command Code section. The section's freshest dated read (console, 2026-10-27: monthly limit **69%** used, weekly **14%**, 5h **0%**, top-up balance $0.00 recorded separately) is percentage-only, so it never matches. The extractor falls back to the 2026-10-25 line ($6.57 of $10 used; 5h 1.2%, weekly 8.8%) and `/api/quota.json` presents week-old figures as the current pool state (verified live 2026-11-01 01:45 CDT).

Fix: select the **latest dated read** in the section; support the percentage-only console format ("monthly limit N% used", "weekly limit N%", "5-hour limit N%"); if the freshest read cannot be parsed, render no windows rather than a stale one. Add a regression test pinning latest-read selection (the section carries several dated reads by design).

## Defect 2 — balance read as quota in hub/steward reporting

Hub reads on 2026-10-30/31 reported Command Code as "credits 0.1" (the top-up balance) for 20+ consecutive intervals and the pool was treated as walled-in-effect on that basis, while the plan windows showed room. Any reader/collector path that maps a balance field into the `commandcode:go` pool's quota state must be removed or remapped to the plan windows per the ruling above.

## Acceptance

- `/api/quota.json` `commandcode:go` reflects the freshest dated plan read in the quota view.
- A test pins latest-dated-read selection in `extractCommandCode`.
- No code path emits the top-up balance as Command Code quota.

title: agy-proxy(test): findAgyBinary puts the system agy first with no override — the test suite's HOME stub is shadowed on every fleet host, 10/11 tests fail there

labels.name: kind/test
labels.description: Test coverage, test infrastructure, or test-only fixes

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: bin/agy-proxy.mjs warm-session proxy

body:
## Problem

`bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs` cannot pass on a fleet NixOS host — the machines agy-proxy actually runs on. 10 of its 11 tests fail there, not because the proxy is broken, but because the test's stub `agy` is never invoked: the proxy resolves the host's real `agy` binary first.

- `bin/agy-proxy.mjs:99-113` — `findAgyBinary()` tries, in order: `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy`, `$HOME/.gemini/bin/agy`, `$HOME/.local/bin/agy`, then bare `agy`. There is **no environment override**.
- `bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs:13-16,97-113` — the harness sets `HOME` to a temp dir and plants its stub at `$HOME/.local/bin/agy`, noting the proxy "reaches it when no system agy exists". On a NixOS fleet host a system agy always exists at the first candidate path, so resolution never reaches the stub.
- The sibling proxies already solved exactly this: `bin/codex-proxy.mjs:135-137` — "Explicit override first: the test suite points this at its stub so a host-installed codex can never shadow it (#694)" (`CODEX_PROXY_CODEX_BIN`); `bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs:139` puts `CLAUDE_CODE_BIN` first; `bin/antigravity-ls-proxy.mjs:186` puts `ANTIGRAVITY_LS_BIN` first; `bin/muse-proxy.mjs:60-63` at least puts `$HOME/.local/bin/muse` ahead of the system path. agy-proxy is the only one with a system path first and no override.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop `amd`, agy files byte-identical at sandbox main `04ab5bcc` and laptop HEAD — sha256 `8b1fe33e…` / `efef177b…`)

- The laptop has the real binary at the first two candidate shapes: `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy` → nix store `antigravity-cli-1.2.16`, and `~/.gemini/bin/agy` (233 MB, Oct 30).
- Full suite: `node --test bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs` → **tests 11, pass 1, fail 10** (log: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-agytest/run1.log`). Failures are the stub-protocol tests (#678/#683 failure detection, resident-worker reuse, live model list): chat requests return 502 and the catalog source is `fallback`, never the stub's `live` list.
- Marker probe (same directory, `probe.py`): proxy started with the test's exact setup (`HOME`=temp, stub at `.local/bin/agy` that appends to a marker file on every invocation). Result: **stub marker file never created**; proxy log says `Live 'agy models' pull failed; serving last-known-good catalog`; `GET /v1/models` serves the static `FALLBACK_MODELS` list and never contains the stub-only `gemini-9-testonly` model. The proxy talked to the real agy (unauthenticated in the isolated `AGY_HOME`) the whole time.

## Why it matters

The suite is the only regression coverage for agy-proxy's failure detection (#678), resume-retry (#683), resident-worker reuse, and the live-pull model catalog. On any machine where agy is actually installed — every fleet host — that coverage is silently void: the tests fail for a harness reason, so a real regression in the same tests would be indistinguishable from the standing noise, and nobody can run the suite where the proxy is developed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] agy-proxy gains an explicit binary override (e.g. `AGY_PROXY_AGY_BIN`, matching the `CODEX_PROXY_CODEX_BIN` / `ANTIGRAVITY_LS_BIN` pattern) that `findAgyBinary()` consults before all candidate paths.
- [ ] `bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs` pins its stub through that override (as `codex-proxy.test.mjs:221` does), so a host-installed agy can never shadow it.
- [ ] `node --test bin/agy-proxy.test.mjs` passes 11/11 on a host where `/run/current-system/sw/bin/agy` exists (verify on the laptop).
- [ ] With no override set, production resolution order and behaviour are unchanged.

title: AA explorer: default the view to the newest benchmark version (v5) — mixed vintages by default mislead every ranking
body:
User report (Drew, 2026-11-01): 'why not showing v5 if v5 exists??' — the explorer's current dataset carries BOTH benchmark vintages (140 rows AA v5 + 138 rows AA v4.3.2 from the same workbook batch) and the page's benchmark filter defaults to unset (render.ts state bench: ""), so every table and chart mixes vintages. Concrete harm observed live: MiMo-V2.6-Pro's v4.3.2 score (46) ranks it above Haiku 5.5 xhigh's v5 score (34); vintage-matched on v5 the order flips (Haiku 34 > MiMo 30). Seat decisions were nearly made off the mixed view.

The data is fine — the workbook legitimately tracks current + previous benchmark versions, and the collector should keep shipping all of it (catalog completeness). The defect is the VIEW default.

Fix (render.ts / AA explorer):
1. Default the benchmark filter to the NEWEST benchmarkVersionKey present in the payload (today: AA|v5). The default view shows that vintage only (140 rows today) and the counts/labels on the page say which vintage is shown.
2. The benchmark filter remains a user control: v4.3.2 and 'all versions' stay selectable; the choice persists in page state like the other filters.
3. Charts, frontier computation, and rank displays all operate on the filtered set (they already consume the filtered rows — verify no chart reads the unfiltered payload).
4. When a future batch introduces a newer vintage, the default follows it automatically (compute from data, never hardcode 'v5').

Acceptance: fresh load of /aa shows v5 only with the vintage named in the UI; MiMo Pro no longer ranks above Haiku xhigh in the default view; switching the filter to v4.3.2 or all restores those rows; no change to the collector payload or ainventory.

title: AA explorer scatters: color all dots by lab, frontier as emphasis — current frontier-only coloring collapses on real data
body:
User report (Drew, 2026-10-31, live on the current v5 dataset): the Cost × Completion time scatter (and the sibling scatters) show almost entirely grey dots and no visible lines; GPT-6 Luna reads grey.

Verified mechanics (render.ts + live /api/aa.json, 2026-10-31 23:44 CDT):
- Dots are colored ONLY when they sit on that chart's Pareto frontier (`onF`); everything else renders grey #9aa0a6 by design ('solid dots sit on the frontier, gray are beaten').
- On the current dataset that design collapses: only 70 of 278 ranked configs are plottable on cost×time at all (the rest lack timed runs), and among those 70 exactly ONE point is Pareto-optimal on (cost, time) — GPT-6 Luna at $0.0045/task, 14.13s — because it is simultaneously cheapest and fastest and therefore dominates the entire plane. Consequences: the white dashed frontier 'line' degenerates to a single point (nothing to draw), every other Luna rung is dominated by Luna's own cheapest rung (hence 'Luna is grey'), and ~69 of 70 visible dots are grey.
- The comparison-line overlays Drew remembers from the old explorer (smoothed upper tail, smoothed envelope, OLS trend) are separately missing — tracked in #1400; this issue is about the COLOR model, which is broken even where lines exist (effort-rung connectors render among grey dots).

Fix:
1. Color ALL plotted dots by lab/creator (the per-family PALETTE machinery already exists in render.ts for the band charts — reuse/extend it), in all three main scatters and the band scatters.
2. Frontier membership becomes EMPHASIS on top of the lab color (white ring / larger radius / full opacity — the selected-point styling at render.ts:3204 is a model), with non-frontier dots at reduced opacity but still lab-colored.
3. Keep the frontier dashed line; when the frontier has <2 points, draw the frontier point(s) with the emphasis treatment and note it in the chart footnote instead of silently producing a lineless chart.
4. The provider/lab choice control must list the labs present in the data (creator values incl. casing variants like 'Openai' vs 'OpenAI' — normalize in the collector payload or the render, one place, and say which).

Acceptance: on the current dataset, Cost × Completion time shows lab-colored dots for all 70 plottable configs, the Luna frontier point is visibly emphasized, other Luna rungs are colored-but-dimmed (not grey), and the provider/lab control lists the labs in the data and filters the chart.

title: mcpx(scripting): delimiter scanner remaining heuristic false-positive shapes (follow-up to #1659)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## mcpx(scripting): delimiter scanner still misclassifies a tail of exotic valid shapes (follow-up to #1659)

#1659 added the regex-literal state to `checkSyntaxAndDelimiters` in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/scripting/validator.go` and fixed its six filed probe shapes. The Codex re-review of PR #3047 at head `66f5294fd` (2026-11-01T04:25Z) found 9 further P2 false-positive shapes in the same heuristic scanner. They are dispositioned out of #1659's scope (its acceptance criteria are met) and collected here so they are tracked, not lost. Each was reported against `validator.go` at that head:

1. **`new` keyword operand** (validator.go:902) — `const r = new /a+/.constructor("x");` — `new` stays classified as an operand, so the regex slash is read as division.
2. **Class heritage object literal** (:675) — `const q = class extends {C: Object}.C {} / 2;` — the pending class-expression frame is consumed at the heritage object literal.
3. **Newline-triggered frame cleanup scope** (:414) — `const f = function(a = () => {debugger\n}) {} / 2;` (real newline) — the nested `debugger` statement clears frames beyond its own statement.
4. **Spread token across trivia** (:666) — `const obj = {... /*c*/ {} / 2};` — the adjacency check misses the spread token across the comment, classifying the object operand as a statement block.
5. **Line break pending through comments before `++`** (:439) — `let n=1; n\n/*comment*/++/a+/.lastIndex;` (real newline) — the comment opener consumes `lineBreakPending`.
6. **Braced Unicode identifier escapes** (:948) — `const \u{61} = 4; const q = \u{61} / 2;` — the escape's braces are read as structural delimiters.
7. **TypeScript instantiation expressions** (:776) — `function f<T>() { return 4; } const q = f<number> / 2;` — the closing `>` falls through to operator classification.
8. **Private identifier names** (:297) — `class C { #return=4; f(){ return this.#return / 2; } }` — the identifier after `#` is classified as the `return` keyword.
9. **Object property named `import`** (:360) — `const obj = { import: "foo"\n / 2 };` (real newline) — the property name activates static-module declaration state.

### Acceptance
- Each shape above validates as valid (regression test per shape), OR is explicitly documented in code as a pinned blind spot of the heuristic scanner with the reasoning.
- Division controls keep working (`a / b / c`, `x /= 2`, unclosed delimiter/string after division still caught).
- Full `go test ./internal/scripting/ -count=1` passes.

Refs: #1659, PR #3047 (Codex review round 2026-11-01T04:25Z, threads PRRT_kwDOJWP4786yXRL3 / yXRL7 / yXRL_ / yXRMB / yXRME / yXRMI / yXRML / yXRMN / yXRMQ).

title: AA collector: a transient Supabase 403 wipes the explorer — keep last-good payload, skip query when batch unchanged
body:
Observed live 2026-10-31 ~23:34 CDT: a fleet-feed collector tick got HTTP 403 from the Supabase Management API database/query endpoint and overwrote a healthy AA section (278 rankings, written by the 23:32 tick) with aaAbsent. The /aa explorer went empty/grey for the user (no providers selectable, points uncolored) until a manual rerun succeeded immediately — the 403 is transient/rate-limit-shaped (the same sbp_ management token serves several jobs, and the AA payload query is one giant jsonb build every 5 min).

Fixes, in pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:
1. **Keep-last-good on failure.** When the AA query fails, reuse the PREVIOUS feed's aa section verbatim, marked stale (keep its original generatedAt; set a stale/failure note in the section) instead of replacing it with aaAbsent. aaAbsent should mean 'never succeeded', not 'failed once'. Same treatment is worth auditing for the collector's other fail-soft sections.
2. **Skip the query when the batch hasn't changed.** The AA payload only changes when ainventory.v_latest_workbook_batch changes. Do a cheap batch-id check first; if it equals the batch of the last successful payload build, reuse the cached payload and skip the giant query. This removes ~288 heavy Management API queries/day and most of the rate-limit pressure that causes (1).

Acceptance: kill the AA query artificially (bad ref in a test env) and confirm the feed keeps serving the last good aa section with a stale marker; confirm a tick with an unchanged batch performs no payload query (log line); explorer stays populated across a forced failure.

title: github-backup: drainer needs an owner allowlist — public App admits foreign installs
body:
## Problem

The backup GitHub App `developing-today-backup` (ID 5562183) was made **public** on 2026-10-31 — GitHub does not allow a private App to be installed by organizations, and org installs were a hard requirement. A side effect: **anyone** can now install the App on their own repositories.

Their webhook deliveries verify against the App secret (it is genuinely our App), reach the Worker queue, and `bin/drain_queue.py` currently acts on any queued event whose repo appears in `plan.json` — and files fetch attempts / state for anything else it is handed. A foreign install could make the laptop drainer clone/fetch strangers' repositories into `~/backups/github`, burning disk, bandwidth, and the App installation rate limit, and polluting the backup tree.

## Fix

Drop foreign events at the drainer door, before any fetch work:

- Determine each queued event's owner (`repository.owner.login`; fall back to the installation account login where the payload carries it; the queued `repo` full_name carries the owner for Worker-flattened events).
- Allowed set = `owners` in `infra/github-backup/config.json` (the same set reconcile plans from). Case-insensitive compare.
- Foreign owner (or owner not determinable — malformed event): DROP — ack it as handled-by-policy (never retried, never counted toward the #3219 DRAIN-CHRONIC failure streak), log one loud greppable line `DRAIN-DROP foreign owner=<login> repo=<full_name> delivery=<id>`, and count drops in the run summary.
- Allowed-owner behavior is unchanged, including the #3219/#3229 ack semantics.

## Tests

Extend `tests/test_drain_queue.py`: allowed owner proceeds exactly as today; foreign owner dropped + acked + logged (even if the repo is in plan.json); missing-owner payload dropped; repository-owner precedence over installation account; #3219 failure semantics unchanged for allowed owners.

## Deploy / proof

Merge → pull on the laptop primary → `just github-backup-units` → one drain run Result=success → hand-inject one foreign event through the Worker and show the `DRAIN-DROP` line with no clone attempted.

Refs #3215 (system issue). Approved by Drew 2026-10-31 23:08 CDT.

body:
# aggregator(snapshots): append-usage-snapshots `--by` with no value silently discards every derived record — exit 0, "no records derived"

## Evidence (verified this run, main `fdfb377c`)

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/append-usage-snapshots.ts:54-62` reads the observer name with the bare index-of pattern, in both modes:

```ts
const byArg = process.argv.indexOf("--by");
const observedBy = byArg >= 0 ? process.argv[byArg + 1] : "check-usage";        // --from-provider-usage mode (:57)
const observedBy = byArg >= 0 ? process.argv[byArg + 1] : "stewardship-cycle";  // default mode (:61)
```

When `--by` is the last argument, `process.argv[byArg + 1]` is `undefined`; with `--by ""` it is the empty string. There is no validation of the value. Every derived record then carries that `observedBy`, and the script's own filter drops all of them: `isSnapshotRecord` requires a non-empty string observer (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts:310`, `!isNonEmptyString(r.observedBy)` → false). The script then reaches the empty-result branch (`append-usage-snapshots.ts:71-80`) and prints the misleading `no records derived; outbox untouched` — and exits 0.

Probe (laptop, real script run from the laptop clone; script sha256 `e2612f0f…` and `src/snapshots.ts` `c6685035…` identical on both clones; fixture `provider-usage.json` = `{"generated_at":"2026-10-31T12:00:00.000Z","sessions":[{},{}]}`, which derives exactly one record; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-appendby/`):

| run | result |
|---|---|
| control: `--from-provider-usage --by tester` | `appended 1 record(s)`; outbox holds the `sessions-listed` record with `"observedBy":"tester"`; exit 0 |
| `--from-provider-usage --by` (trailing, no value) | **`no records derived; outbox untouched`; no outbox file created; exit 0** |
| `--from-provider-usage --by ""` | same: `no records derived; outbox untouched`; no outbox file; exit 0 |

## Why it matters

This script is a snapshot writer (hub design §4): stewardship / check-usage runs append the dated quota observations that become the fleet's measured usage history. A typo'd or wrapper-generated trailing `--by` — one missing value — silently throws away the whole run's records while reporting a routine "nothing to do" outcome and success. Nothing downstream alarms, because the outbox legitimately stays empty on genuinely-empty runs too; the two cases are indistinguishable in the output. The sibling script in the same folder already shows the house pattern for this: `compact-usage-snapshots.ts:28-31` validates its `--months` value and exits 2 naming the bad value.

## Acceptance criteria

- `append-usage-snapshots.ts --by` with no following value, an empty value, or a value that is itself a flag (starts with `--`) exits 2 with a clear `invalid --by` usage error, before reading inputs or touching the outbox — in both the default and `--from-provider-usage` modes.
- `--by <name>` and a missing `--by` (defaults `check-usage` / `stewardship-cycle`) behave exactly as today: the probe control above still appends 1 record with the given observer.
- The "no records derived" message is only reachable when records were actually derived-and-filtered for content reasons; a test (or script-level check) pins the trailing-`--by` refusal so the silent-discard path cannot return.
- Existing aggregator snapshot tests still pass.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `append-usage-snapshots` and `observedBy` — neighbours are #3285 (compact `--months 0`, same folder, different script/guard), #2568 / #2571 (percent range checks), #2941 (`__proto__` grouping) and #1205 (writer-health epic); none covers the `--by` value going unvalidated and voiding the run.

body:
## Problem

`nixos/services/id-mail/worker/deploy.mjs` decides dry-run vs. real deploy with a single membership test and never validates the argument list:

- deploy.mjs:17 — `const dryRun = process.argv.includes("--dry-run");`
- There is no check for unrecognized arguments anywhere in the script.

So a typo'd preview — `deploy.mjs --dry-rnu`, `--dryrun`, or any stray flag — is silently treated as a **real deploy**. The real path is destructive, in order (deploy.mjs:70-84):

1. `wrangler deploy --dry-run` (validation only, always runs),
2. for each name in `config.retire` (currently `["id-mail"]`, config.json): `retire(name)` — checks the Worker over the Cloudflare API and runs `wrangler delete --name <name> --force`,
3. `wrangler deploy` (real, takes the retired Worker's routes),
4. `wrangler secret put CALLERS`.

A one-character typo in the preview flag therefore deletes the retired Worker and ships a real deployment instead of printing "nothing deployed".

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-10-31)

Code: deploy.mjs:17 (only arg handling in the file), retire/deploy/secret sequence at :70-84, `wrangler delete --force` in `retire()` at :86-99.

Laptop probe (deploy.mjs sha256 `057188ab95473d1df98b793dbf1f5f7611076884bd86fa19bc50387f41b439db`, identical on sandbox main `ed3a285e` and the laptop copy; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-idmail-deploy/`, script `run3.sh`, with stub `bws`/`wrangler` binaries on PATH logging every call, fake account/token):

- Control `node deploy.mjs --dry-run` → exit 0, output `dry run: mail config is valid, nothing deployed`; wrangler log shows only the validation call `deploy --dry-run --config …`.
- `node deploy.mjs --dry-rnu` → **exit 0, full real deploy sequence**: output `retire: id-mail is already gone` then `deployed mail with callers: amd, admin`; wrangler log shows the validation call, then a real `deploy --config …` (no `--dry-run`), then `secret put CALLERS --config …`. (The retire step's Cloudflare API check answered 404 for the fake token, which `retire()` treats as "already gone" — with a real token for an existing `id-mail` Worker it would run the `wrangler delete --force` first; either way the typo performed a real deployment and a real secret put, not a preview.)
- `node deploy.mjs --bogus-flag` → identical: exit 0, full real deploy + secret-put sequence.

## Why it matters

This is the mail Worker's deploy path for the id system (routes `mail.security.cab` et al.). The `--dry-run` flag is the only safety preview the script offers, and it fails silently in exactly the situation it exists for — an operator checking a deploy before running it. The first destructive action (force-deleting the `id-mail` Worker) happens before the real deploy, so a typo can cause an outage window even if the subsequent deploy then fails.

## Distinct from

- #3264 (pkarr-worker deploy.mjs — same arg pattern, different script/target; that issue's fix does not touch this file).
- #3278 (opencode-claimant install.mjs — same pattern, install path, no Worker deletion).

This file needs its own guard; if a shared strict-args helper is the chosen fix shape, applying it here as part of that work also satisfies this issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argument other than `--dry-run` (and no arguments) aborts with a usage error and exit non-zero **before** any bws/wrangler/API call.
- [ ] `--dry-run` still validates and exits 0 having made no retire/deploy/secret calls.
- [ ] A stubbed-binary probe or test pins all three cases: `--dry-run` (no destructive calls), `--dry-rnu` (usage error, no calls at all), no args (real sequence).

body:
## Finding (2026-10-31 evening, from the route_attempt ledger + live probes)

The standalone route proxy (`bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs`, :18750 — OpenClaw's door) currently cannot address **either** GPT provider:

- Every proxy walk since ~15:29 CDT that reaches a GPT leaf records `error_tag=UnknownProvider` — **"no endpoint configured for provider openai"** / **"no endpoint configured for provider openai.alternate"** (rows 41997/41998 at 18:38:49, 18:39:32 walks, session_id NULL = proxy-direct).
- The proxy's last successful `openai` attempt was at **~15:29 CDT** (MAX(time_started) for outcome=success); before that it served terra leaves all day.
- The deployed config's `openai` and `openai.alternate` provider blocks are now empty shells — no `npm`, no `options`, no `baseURL` (verified by parsing `~/code/.opencode/opencode.jsonc`). OpenCode itself tolerates that (built-in provider defaults), but the proxy's `providerBaseURL()` resolves endpoints from the config and finds nothing.

This coincides with today's route-config edits (Antigravity removal and related surgery on the same file). The blocks presumably carried an explicit baseURL (historically the codex-proxy door on 127.0.0.1:18744) that the edits dropped. Recent commits touching the file, for the archaeology: `ab6df37f4` (Antigravity out of workhorse), `45a1572ef` (workhorse primary swaps to Codex Terra), `c1af58e34`, `90b6d92d5` — all 2026-10-31.

## This is distinct from #3216

#3216 is the OpenCode-internal routing failure: fleet sessions reach the real API and get 401 "Missing scopes: api.responses.write" — an OAuth scope/role defect on the GPT credentials, quota-independent. This issue is the standalone proxy never reaching the API at all. Both must be fixed before a GPT leaf can serve through the proxy; fixing this one alone still leaves #3216's 401 behind it.

## Ask

Restore the proxy's ability to address the two GPT providers — either:

1. put the explicit endpoint back in the two provider blocks in the canonical config (confirm the pre-edit value from the config's git history), or
2. teach `providerBaseURL()` the built-in defaults for these providers so an empty block is not a dead leaf.

And note the general hazard this exposes: the proxy and OpenCode read the same config file with different tolerance for empty provider blocks, so a config edit that is safe for OpenCode can silently kill leaves for the proxy. The route validation sweeps should cover the proxy's view of the config, not only OpenCode's.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The standalone route proxy can address both GPT providers again: a proxy walk reaching an `openai` or `openai.alternate` leaf no longer records `error_tag=UnknownProvider` / "no endpoint configured".
- [ ] The chosen resolution is recorded on this issue: explicit endpoint restored in the two provider blocks (value confirmed from the config's git history), or `providerBaseURL()` taught the built-in defaults so an empty provider block is not a dead leaf.
- [ ] Route validation covers the proxy's view of the canonical config (not only OpenCode's), so a config edit that empties a provider block is caught before it silently kills proxy leaves.
- [ ] Verified against the route_attempt ledger / a live proxy probe after the fix (note: #3216's 401 may still stand behind this — it is a separate defect).
