body:
Phase 1 of design #2497 (mcpx tasks, bounded — operational limits, cooperative cancel, audit, and the small truths). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-operational-limits.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. The decisions are recorded on #2497; this phase implements its first slice. Independent of Phase 2.

## Scope

Limits in the store, keyed by requestor, valued in `protoTasks.*`:

- `Store.Start` (`internal/tasks/tasks.go:355`) gains a requestor key (optional parameter / options field). Every creation site passes what it holds: the MCP seam (`internal/mcpserver/tasks.go` `startTask`, which already tracks `taskOwners`), the modern-task seam, and the daemon's `/v1` Start sites (`internal/daemon/ops.go:525`, `routes_proto.go:434`, `routes_exec.go:245`, `input_required.go:100`). The empty key is a real bucket named "unbound", capped like any other — never a bypass.
- `protoTasks.maxTTL` (duration, default 1h) in `internal/settings/prototasks.go`: a requested TTL above the cap is **clamped**, not refused; the stored/returned task shows the capped TTL. Default TTL (10m) unchanged.
- `protoTasks.maxPerRequestor` (int, default 32): concurrent non-terminal tasks per requestor key, counted in the store. Creation beyond the cap is refused at the seam with a named error (-32603 on MCP, 429 on /v1) naming the limit.
- `protoTasks.perMinute` (int, default 120, 0 disables): one fixed-window counter per requestor key over all `tasks/*` method calls (get/list/result/update/cancel), counted on admission at the two dispatch seams (MCP tasks handler, daemon /v1 task routes); refusal shaped like the cap refusal. Use a shared fixed-window limiter type if one has landed from #2333/#2386 by implementation time; otherwise keep the copy local to the tasks seams — do not build a general rate-limit framework. (Design-doc open question: triage may exempt `tasks/result` long polls from the window if it can say why in one sentence on this issue.)
- `NewID` (tasks.go:344) moves from 8 to 16 random bytes (128 bits).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A task requested with a TTL above `protoTasks.maxTTL` runs with the capped TTL, and the returned task object shows the capped value, on both the MCP and /v1 surfaces
- [ ] The 33rd concurrent non-terminal task for one requestor key is refused with the named error while another requestor's creation still succeeds; the unbound bucket is capped the same way
- [ ] `tasks/*` calls beyond `protoTasks.perMinute` for one requestor are refused with the named error / 429; 0 disables the window
- [ ] Every `Store.Start` call site in the tree passes a requestor key or is explicitly the unbound bucket (grep-verifiable)
- [ ] New task IDs are 128-bit; existing ID parsing/lookup is unaffected
- [ ] The conformance gap rows `tasks-resource-limits` and `tasks-rate-limit` in `internal/conformance/coverage_stateful.go` are retired (or reworded to name what remains)
- [ ] Tests run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: cooperative cancel and `statusMessage` (Phase 2), audit logging and docs (Phase 3), per-server (upstream) concurrency caps, any change to task shapes on the wire.

🤖 Design-architect pass 17 — agent note: triage this phase against design #2497's recorded decisions; do not re-derive the limit values or the clamp-vs-refuse choice in triage.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Store.Start` takes a requestor key from every creation seam (MCP startTask, modern-task seam, the four /v1 Start sites); the empty key is the capped `unbound` bucket, never a bypass
- [ ] `protoTasks.maxTTL` (default 1h) clamps requested TTLs (stored/returned task shows the capped TTL); `protoTasks.maxPerRequestor` (default 32) refuses creation beyond the cap with a named error (-32603 MCP / 429 /v1); `protoTasks.perMinute` (default 120, 0 disables) windows all tasks/* calls per requestor
- [ ] Tests pin clamp-not-refuse for TTL, refusal naming the limit for the cap, and the unbound bucket being capped like any other

title: aggregator(github-billing): billing items never validated — an impossible date discards the whole month's collection, negative amounts are stored as usage

labels.name: effort/xs

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`aggregateBillingUsage` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/github-billing.ts:78-113` (the #1051 collector core, merged in PR #2236) validates almost nothing about the unified billing endpoint's items:

- **Date:** the only check is `typeof item.date === "string" && item.date.length < 10` skip (`:81`); the first 10 chars are taken verbatim (`:82`). `"2026-13-99"` and `"2026-02-30"` both pass.
- **Amounts:** `quantity`, `grossAmount`, and `netAmount` are summed whenever `typeof === "number"` (`:84`, `:99-100`) — negative values pass; no finiteness or sign check anywhere in the file.

The two failure modes land in different places, and both are bad:

1. **One impossible date discards the whole month's collection.** `recordsFromBillingUsage` (`:149-168`) stamps each day with `dayTs(date)` (`snapshot-records.ts:32-34` — plain string interpolation, `"2026-13-99T12:00:00Z"`). Those records fail `isSnapshotRecord` (`snapshots.ts:304`, `Date.parse` is NaN), and the collector treats *any* invalid derived record as fatal: `scripts/collect-github-billing.ts:84-86` throws and appends **nothing** — every good day in the month is lost because one item's date was malformed. A Feb-30 date is worse in the opposite direction: `Date.parse` rolls it over, so the record *passes* validation while carrying a literal nonexistent day as its `ts` (and dedupe key).
2. **Negative usage is stored as fact.** A negative `quantity`/`grossAmount`/`netAmount` produces negative day aggregates, and the derived records (e.g. `actions-minutes: -120`, `billing-gross: -0.96`) **pass** `isSnapshotRecord` (finite is all it asks) and are appended to the snapshot store, corrupting the GitHub service's usage/billing series.

Sibling collectors in this repo all guard this: the Supabase exporter rejects negative/non-finite reads (`parseDbSize`, `parseRequestCount` in `pm-stack/supabase-export/supabase-quota-export.mjs`), and `quota-gather-map.ts`'s `num()` is finite-gated. This file is the unguarded outlier.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `7d1b081c`)

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-billing/probe2.ts`, real `github-billing.ts` + `snapshots.ts` from a fresh clone at main, run with bun):

```
control (120 min, $0.96)            => day aggregates correct; 3 records, all isSnapshotRecord = true
quantity/gross/net all negative     => aggregates -120 / -0.96 / -0.96; records emitted with
                                       value -120 and -0.96, isSnapshotRecord = true for all (stored)
date "2026-13-99T00:00:00Z"         => day "2026-13-99" aggregates fine; records ts
                                       "2026-13-99T12:00:00Z", isSnapshotRecord = false for all
                                       => collector throws, whole month appended: nothing
date "2026-02-30"                   => records ts "2026-02-30T12:00:00Z", isSnapshotRecord = true
                                       (Date.parse rollover) — nonexistent day stored as-is
mixed good day + one month-13 item  => 6 records, only 3 valid — the good day is discarded with the bad one
```

## Why it matters

This collector is the GitHub billing series' only writer. Either failure silently degrades it: a single malformed item from the endpoint (shape drift, a partial response, a future SKU/date format) zeros out a month of Actions/Codespaces/billing history with only a thrown error in a daily job log, and a negative row — which no downstream check rejects — permanently writes negative minutes/dollars into the snapshot store that quota views and reconciliation read.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Items with a non-calendar date (month 13, Feb 30, non-date prefix) are rejected or skipped at aggregation time with the day/item identifiable — they never produce a record, and never take the month's good days down with them.
- [ ] Negative (and non-finite, for direct API callers of the pure functions) `quantity`/`grossAmount`/`netAmount` values cannot produce negative aggregates or stored records; the chosen treatment (skip item vs skip field vs fail the run) is pinned by triage and documented in the file header.
- [ ] The collector's all-or-nothing validation throw (`collect-github-billing.ts:84-86`) is reconsidered for whatever validation remains downstream: one bad item must not discard a month of valid records.
- [ ] Regression tests in `test/github-billing.test.ts` cover: month-13 date, Feb-30 date, negative quantity, negative gross/net, and a mixed good+bad month that still yields the good days' records.
- [ ] Well-formed items are unchanged: existing `github-billing.test.ts` expectations still pass.

Dedup: #1051 (closed) specified this collector; PR #2236 built it. #1540/#2483 concern the snapshot *store* validators (`snapshots.ts` pairs/limit/resetsAt) — this is the producer-side item validation in `sources/github-billing.ts`, which neither covers. Title/body searches for `github-billing`, `aggregateBillingUsage`, and "billing usage" returned no covering issue, open or closed.

title: supabase-export: billedFromAddons silently zeroes unpriced selected addons (and accepts negative amounts) — a paid addon reports as measured $0

body:
## Problem

`billedFromAddons` in `pm-stack/supabase-export/supabase-quota-export.mjs:101-113` silently treats a selected addon whose price is missing, null, or a string as **$0**, and accepts a negative amount verbatim. `run()` then stamps the result as a *measured* billing read (`supabase-quota-export.mjs:280-285`: `billedUsd: usd, measured: true`), so the aggregator trusts it: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:742-743` copies any finite `billedUsd` onto the Supabase card whenever `measured !== false`.

That breaks the exporter's own contract in both directions:

- The module header (lines 115-117 of the sibling pattern / function doc at :99-100) says billed is "Measured $0 (or more) from billing/addons" — an addon the API selected but whose price shape drifted is **unknown**, not $0. The fleet already fixed the mirror-image bug on the consumer side ("billed amount unknown when supabase billing probe unavailable", #1050 follow-up): unknown must not be reported as a measured zero.
- A negative `amount` yields a negative `billedUsd` on a `measured: true` document, which the consumer accepts (finite check only).

The function is also inconsistent with its own file: it throws `ExportError("unparseable", 6, …)` when `selected_addons` is missing (`:104-106`), and `parseDbSize` (`:91-98`) throws on any invalid row — but per-addon price drift is silently zeroed instead of throwing.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `7d1b081c`)

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-billing/probe.mjs`, real module imported from a fresh clone at main):

```
control: priced addon 25            => billedFromAddons = 25
selected addon, price missing       => billedFromAddons = 0
selected addon, amount is string    => billedFromAddons = 0
selected addon, amount null         => billedFromAddons = 0
selected addon, amount negative -25 => billedFromAddons = -25
one priced + one unpriced           => billedFromAddons = 25  (unpriced silently dropped)
contrast parseDbSize bad bytes      => THROWS unparseable
contrast billedFromAddons({})       => THROWS unparseable (selected_addons missing)
```

## Why it matters

The Supabase card's billed figure is the fleet's paid-trigger signal for the muse-dev project. A paid addon whose price shape changes (or a new addon type with usage pricing and no fixed `price.amount`) would be reported as a *measured $0*, hiding real spend behind the strongest trust marker the format has (`measured: true`). A negative amount would corrupt the figure outright.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A selected addon with a missing, null, non-numeric, non-finite, or negative `price.amount` makes the billing read fail closed in the file's own style (throw `ExportError("unparseable", 6, …)`), OR the document's billing is emitted as unmeasured/null — triage pins which; it must never be `measured: true` with a silently-zeroed or negative total.
- [ ] Well-formed payloads are unchanged: `[{price:{amount:25}}]` → 25, `[]` → measured 0.
- [ ] Regression tests in `supabase-quota-export.test.mjs` cover: price missing, amount as string, amount null, amount negative, and a priced+unpriced mix.
- [ ] The consumer behaviour is considered: with the fix, `saas-extract.ts` must not display a $0/negative measured billed figure for these payloads.

Dedup: #1050 (closed) built this exporter; its follow-up fixed the *consumer* treating an unavailable probe as $0 — this is the producer-side mirror. #2460/#2461 are the meta-exporter (different producer, different functions). No open or closed issue covers `billedFromAddons` per-addon price validation.

title: aggregator(snapshots): isSnapshotRecord never checks limit/resetsAt — a numeric resetsAt crashes the service history chart, a non-numeric limit NaNs it

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: status/needs-triage

labels.description: Has a queued queue task

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Summary

`isSnapshotRecord` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts:26-42`) — the structural validator every snapshot-store read and append gates on — never checks the record's two optional fields, `limit` and `resetsAt` (model: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/model.ts:1266-1267`, `limit?: number | null`, `resetsAt?: string | null`). A stored JSONL record carrying either field in the wrong type passes validation, is returned by `SnapshotStore.readAll`/`byService`, and then breaks the service-detail history chart:

- **`resetsAt` as a number crashes the chart.** `resetMarkers` (`src/derive.ts:975-991`) treats any truthy `resetsAt` as a string: `Date.parse(prev.resetsAt)` coerces a number to a string and can parse it as a date (e.g. `2026` → 2026-01-01), so the marker is emitted with the number as its `ts`/`resetsAt`. `historyChartHtml` (`src/render.ts:1869-1875`) then calls `m.resetsAt.slice(0, 10)` on that number → `TypeError: m.resetsAt.slice is not a function`. The call site is the `/quota/service/<id>` route (`src/server.ts:527`, `renderServiceDetail` → `historyChartHtml`), which has no try/catch around the render, so one poisoned history record 500s that service's detail page on every load until the record ages out of the store.
- **A non-numeric `limit` silently NaNs the chart.** `historyChartHtml` (`src/render.ts:1866`) folds `r.limit ?? 0` into the `Math.max(...)` that computes `vmax`; an object/array/non-numeric-string limit makes `vmax` NaN, so every chart coordinate renders as `NaN` — the chart is garbage with no error anywhere.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `1ddc7720`)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-snapreset/` (verbatim aggregator `src/` copied from current main; sha256 of `snapshots.ts`/`render.ts`/`derive.ts` identical on sandbox and probe), Bun, driving the real modules:

- `isSnapshotRecord({...valid, resetsAt: 2026})` → `true`; `limit: "not-a-number"` → `true`; `limit: {x:1}` → `true`.
- `resetMarkers([record(resetsAt: 2026, ts 2025-12-01), record(ts 2026-11-01)], "m")` → `[{ts: 2026, resetsAt: 2026}]`.
- `historyChartHtml(same pair, "m")` → **throws `TypeError: m.resetsAt.slice is not a function`**.
- Control (string `resetsAt: "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"`): chart renders, marker present.
- `historyChartHtml` with `limit: {x:1}`: output contains `NaN` coordinates.
- Reachability: live source loads history via `SnapshotStore.byService()` (`src/sources/live.ts:799`) into `usage.history`, keyed by service id — exactly what the service route renders.

## Why it matters

The snapshot store is append-only history written by several jobs and a backfill; the validator is the only boundary between an on-disk JSONL line and the renderers, and it already type-checks every other field (including finiteness for scalar `value`). One malformed line — a writer emitting a numeric epoch-year or a string limit — permanently breaks one service's detail page (crash) or its history chart (NaN), with the failure surfacing far from the bad record.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSnapshotRecord` rejects a record whose `limit` is present and not a finite number or `null`, and whose `resetsAt` is present and not a string that `Date.parse` accepts (or `null`).
- Regression tests: a numeric-`resetsAt` record and an object-`limit` record each fail validation / are skipped by `readAll`; the string-`resetsAt` + numeric-`limit` control still renders a chart with its reset marker.
- No change to the on-disk format, the dedupe key, or behaviour for records whose optional fields are absent or well-typed.

## Notes

- Distinct from #1540 (same validator: non-finite estimate pairs + non-ISO `ts` pass and can never be read back — different fields, different failure) and #2346 (validator-passing *scalar* pct values make `projectPace` throw — different consumer).
- Not self-solved: whether to also harden `resetMarkers`/`historyChartHtml` against already-stored poisoned records, or validator-only, is triage's pin.

title: lab-ops-hub: POST /api/machines|notes|tasks return 500 (raw SQLite/SyntaxError text) for missing fields and non-JSON bodies — never a 400

body:
## Bug: lab-ops-hub POST routes return 500 for client-bad input — missing required fields and non-JSON bodies are never a 400

In `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/index.ts`, every JSON POST handler parses and binds the request body with no presence/type validation, inside the Worker's single outer `try/catch` that converts **every** throw into `500 {error: String(e)}`:

- `POST /api/machines`: `const b = await req.json()` then `.bind(b.name, b.role ?? "compute", …)` — optional fields get `??` defaults, but `name` is passed through raw. `schema.sql` declares `machines.name TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`.
- `POST /api/notes`: `.bind(b.title, b.body, b.tags ?? "")` — `notes.title` and `notes.body` are both `NOT NULL`.
- `POST /api/tasks`: `.bind(b.title, …)` — `tasks.title` is `NOT NULL`.
- All of them (plus `POST /api/crawl`): a body that is not valid JSON makes `await req.json()` throw a `SyntaxError`, which lands in the same outer catch.

So `POST /api/machines` with `{}`, `POST /api/notes` with `{"title":"x"}` (no body), `POST /api/tasks` with `{}`, or any of these routes with a malformed-JSON body all return **500 with a raw `SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed…` / `SyntaxError: …` string** instead of a 400 naming the missing field. The handlers already know the intended contract — `POST /api/crawl` returns `400 {error: "url required"}` when `b.url` is absent, and `POST /api/files` returns 400 when the multipart field is missing — the D1-backed routes just never got the same check.

### Verified this run (main `5a34fa70`)

Sandbox Bun probe replaying the handlers' exact INSERT statements and column definitions from `schema.sql` against `bun:sqlite` (`hidden_files/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-uploadkey/probe2.ts` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace):

- machines insert with a null name → `SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: machines.name`
- notes insert with null title/body → `SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: notes.title`
- tasks insert with a null title → `SQLiteError: NOT NULL constraint failed: tasks.title`
- `JSON.parse` of a malformed body → `SyntaxError` (the `req.json()` failure mode; no handler catches it locally, so the outer catch's 500 is the only possible response)

(In the Worker, an absent JSON key arrives at `.bind()` as `undefined`, which D1 either rejects at bind time or stores as NULL — both paths throw inside the same try and surface as the same 500; there is no code path that returns 400 for a missing required field.)

### Why it matters

A 500 tells the dashboard (and any scripted caller) "the server broke" for what is actually "your request is missing `name`" — it misdirects debugging toward the deployment, leaks raw SQLite error text as the API contract, and makes client-side form validation impossible to test against a stable response. It is also inconsistent with the two routes in the same file that do validate (`/api/crawl`, `/api/files`).

### Acceptance criteria

- `POST /api/machines|notes|tasks` with a missing/empty required field (`name`; `title`/`body`; `title`) returns **400** with an error naming the field; valid requests unchanged (201 + id).
- A non-JSON body on any JSON POST route returns **400**, not 500.
- No raw SQLite/SyntaxError text in 400 responses; genuine server failures still 500.
- Regression coverage for the 400 cases (the validation helper, if factored into `src/lib.ts` per the #524 pattern, is unit-tested there).

### Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for lab-ops-hub + 400/validation/missing/malformed return only crawler-validator issues (#502 etc.) — nothing covers the D1 POST routes' input validation.

— filed by new-issue-creator-code-b (Lane B), 2026-10-29 run

title: lab-ops-hub: file-upload R2 key is Date.now()+filename — same-millisecond uploads collide, overwrite the object, then 500 on the UNIQUE r2_key

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

body:
## Bug: lab-ops-hub file-upload R2 key is `Date.now()` + sanitized filename — same-millisecond uploads collide, overwrite the object, and 500 on the UNIQUE key

`POST /api/files` in `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/index.ts` derives the R2 key from the wall-clock millisecond and the sanitized filename only:

```ts
const key = `uploads/${Date.now()}-${file.name.replace(/[^\w.\-]+/g, "_")}`;
await env.FILES.put(key, buf, { ... });
const r = await env.DB.prepare("INSERT INTO files (r2_key, filename, content_type, size) VALUES (?1,?2,?3,?4)")
  .bind(key, file.name, file.type || null, buf.byteLength)
  .run();
await env.JOBS.send({ type: "index-file", r2Key: key });
```

But `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/schema.sql` declares `files.r2_key TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`. Two uploads that resolve to the same key therefore corrupt state instead of both succeeding:

- **Same filename, same millisecond** (a scripted double-submit, a retried upload, a test loop): the keys are byte-identical. The second `FILES.put` silently **overwrites the first file's R2 object**, then its D1 `INSERT` throws `UNIQUE constraint failed: files.r2_key` and the request 500s via the outer catch. The surviving D1 row still describes the *first* upload (filename/size), while `GET /api/files/<key>` now serves the *second* upload's bytes — and the first upload's queued `index-file` job hashes those wrong bytes and stamps that sha256 + `indexed=1` onto the first row.
- **Different filenames that sanitize to the same string** (e.g. `my file.pdf` vs `my:file.pdf` → both `my_file.pdf`) collide the same way in the same millisecond.

### Verified this run (main `5a34fa70`)

Sandbox Bun probe using the verbatim key expression plus a `bun:sqlite` table built from the real schema's `files` definition, replaying the handler's put → insert order:

- `keyFor("report.pdf", t)` called twice at the same `t` → identical keys (`uploads/1761782400000-report.pdf`).
- `keyFor("my file.pdf", t) === keyFor("my:file.pdf", t)` → identical keys.
- Upload A (`report.pdf`, body `ORIGINAL-A`) → 201; upload B (same name, same ms, body `REPLACEMENT-B`) → `INSERT FAILED (SQLiteError: UNIQUE constraint failed: files.r2_key)`; the R2 map for the key then holds `REPLACEMENT-B` while the only D1 row still records size 10 (A's size).

Probe: `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-uploadkey/probe.ts` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

### Why it matters

The files table is the hub's record of what was uploaded; a collision silently swaps the bytes behind an existing record (the row's size/content-type/sha256 no longer describe what a download returns) and turns a legitimate second upload into an opaque 500. Millisecond collisions are not exotic for automated callers — retries and double-submits are exactly the traffic that hits an upload endpoint twice in the same millisecond.

### Acceptance criteria

- Two uploads of the same filename in the same millisecond both succeed (201) with **distinct** R2 keys and two correct D1 rows (e.g. a random/UUID or row-id component in the key), and each download returns its own bytes.
- Filenames that sanitize to the same string no longer collide.
- A regression test exercises back-to-back same-name uploads (the key derivation should live somewhere testable, per the #524 pattern of moving logic out of the Worker entry into `src/lib.ts`).
- Existing behavior otherwise unchanged: key prefix `uploads/`, filename sanitization, queue `index-file` message per successful upload.

### Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `r2_key`, `uploads/`, `UNIQUE constraint`, and lab-ops-hub file/upload terms return only pkgs/id upload issues (#1549, #2363 — different codebase, filename-keyed store) and #441 (lab-ops auth, closed). No issue covers the lab-ops-hub upload key derivation.

— filed by new-issue-creator-code-b (Lane B), 2026-10-29 run

body:
# id(fileops): PR #1706's free_archive_name is check-then-act — concurrent same-second replaces can still lose a replaced version's archive

## Finding

PR #1706 (merged, fixes #1612) made archive tag names unique for the *sequential* case: `free_archive_name` (`pkgs/id/src/fileops.rs:107` on current main `5a34fa70`) loops `store.tags().get(candidate)` until it finds a free `{name}.archive.{ts}` name, and the caller only afterwards claims it with `tags().set`. The check and the claim are two separate awaited store operations with nothing serialising them, and iroh-blobs `tags().set` is an unconditional write — the same check-then-act shape as #2363 (the upload uniquifier), at a different site.

Interleaving that still loses data, for two concurrent replaces of the same name in the same second (rename/copy at `fileops.rs:260`/`:346`, put, or the web save path via `archive_original_tag` at `web/routes.rs:2209`, called at `routes.rs:1261`):

1. A reads current hash v1, `free_archive_name` returns `doc.archive.{ts}`.
2. B reads current hash v1, `free_archive_name` also returns `doc.archive.{ts}` (A has not set it yet).
3. A sets `doc.archive.{ts}` = v1, then sets `doc` = v2.
4. B sets `doc.archive.{ts}` = v1 (same value, harmless), then sets `doc` = v3.

v2 was live and is now referenced by no tag: it was never archived, so it lost exactly the archive/GC protection #1612 exists to provide. The PR's regression tests (`fileops.rs:464` `same_second_archives_never_overwrite`) are sequential — each archive is fully set before the next name is resolved — so they cannot see this window.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/1706 — merge `d29f867ca765f1e89025d9c499ac25d1e46ffa2b`, head commits `5fb1d2cf`, `a3be7eeb`.
- Current main `5a34fa70`: `free_archive_name` at `pkgs/id/src/fileops.rs:107-118` (get-loop, returns unclaimed name); claim sites `archive_existing` (`fileops.rs:173`, set follows at its end), `rename` (`:260`), copy (`:346`), web `archive_original_tag` (`web/routes.rs:2209`, used at `:1261`).
- No lock/mutex serialises these paths: `grep Mutex/lock pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs` shows only the unrelated `local_events` lock; `FileOps` holds no lock field.

## Why it matters

The archive tag is the only reference keeping a replaced version alive for GC. The sequential same-second collision #1612 reported is fixed, but the concurrent case — two clients/CLI processes against one store, or a web save racing a rename — silently drops a version's archive with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two concurrent same-name replaces within one second both leave an archive tag pointing at their respective replaced versions (a regression test that interleaves the two `free_archive_name` resolutions before either claim, or an equivalent concurrency test, fails before and passes after).
- [ ] The claim is made atomic or serialised (e.g. a set-if-absent claim loop inside `free_archive_name`'s callers, or a per-store lock around resolve+claim) at all three call sites including the web layer's `archive_original_tag`.
- [ ] Sequential behaviour and name shape unchanged: uncontested name is exactly `{name}.archive.{ts}`; existing `archive_name_tests` and protocol archive tests still pass (in CI).

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #1706. Sibling, not duplicate: #2363 covers the upload-name uniquifier in `upload_handler`; this is the archive-name path from #1612.

body:
# meta-exporter: `parsePaygBalance` silently truncates any balance whose decimals aren't exactly two — "$1,234.5" exports 1234 and "$1,234.567" exports 1234.56

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

`pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs`, `parsePaygBalance` (lines 113–119):

```js
const m = iframeText.match(/Current balance\s*\n?\s*\$\s*([\d,]+(?:\.\d{2})?)/);
```

The capture is not anchored at the end of the amount: the regex matches a *prefix* of a longer number and returns it as the balance.

Probe (node, importing the real module from main):

| iframe text | exported `paygBalanceUsd` |
|---|---|
| `Current balance\n$1,234.56` | `1234.56` ✅ (existing test case) |
| `Current balance\n$1,234.5` | `1234` — the `.5` is silently dropped |
| `Current balance\n$1,234.567` | `1234.56` — the third decimal is silently dropped |

## Why it matters

The function's own documented contract is that a balance it cannot read stays `null` — "an absent read must stay absent, never become a fake $0." A truncated balance is a fake value of exactly the same kind: if the billing page's format drifts (one decimal shown, a trailing digit group, a different rounding), the exporter publishes a wrong — always lower — PAYG balance as a measured fact in a `status: "ok"` document, and the quota gatherer (#1151) ingests it. Returning `null` on anything that isn't a clean, fully-consumed amount preserves the fail-closed design; silently truncating does not.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parsePaygBalance` returns the exact value only when the amount is consumed completely; a digit or decimal point immediately following the matched amount makes the read `null` (amount-ending boundary pinned by triage — e.g. a negative lookahead or an explicit end anchor that still tolerates the text that follows the balance on the real page).
- New tests in `meta-quota-export.test.mjs`: `"$1,234.5"` → `null`; `"$1,234.567"` → `null`; the existing cases (`$0.00` → 0, `$1,234.56` → 1234.56, no-match → `null`, non-string → `null`) still pass (`node --test pm-stack/meta-exporter/`).

## Dedup

`#2175` (CDP timeouts), `#2350` (entry-point check), `#1566` (closed, `window_duration_secs`) are distinct mechanisms. Sibling filed this run: #2460 (subscription-quota epoch range validation — different function, different mechanism).

# meta-exporter: subscription-quota timestamps are never range-checked — an ms-scale `resets_at` exports a year-58790 reset as a successful reading, and an out-of-Date-range value throws a bare RangeError misclassified as fetch-failed

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

`pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs`, `parseSubscriptionQuota` (lines 61–97):

- The numeric validation loop (line 76) checks only `Number.isFinite(v) || v < 0` for `window_resets_at` / `weekly_resets_at`. There is no upper bound and no plausibility window.
- `iso` (line 87) is `new Date(epochSecs * 1000).toISOString()` — unbounded.
- `as_of` is not in the validated field set at all; `consoleAsOf` (line 90) calls the same `iso()` whenever `num(q.as_of)` is finite.

Probe (node, importing the real module from main):

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `window_resets_at = 1793090405000` (millisecond-scale, finite, ≥ 0 — passes validation) | exported window `resetAt: "+058790-10-10T04:03:20.000Z"` inside a `status: "ok"` success document |
| `window_resets_at = 1e300` (finite, ≥ 0 — passes validation) | bare `RangeError: Invalid time value` escapes `parseSubscriptionQuota` — `err.status`/`err.exitCode` are `undefined`, it is not an `ExportError` |
| `as_of = 1e300` | same bare `RangeError` from the `consoleAsOf` path |

The escaped RangeError lands in `main()`'s catch-all, which wraps any non-`ExportError` as `fetch-failed` (exit 7). Per the file's own contract, shape drift is `unparseable` (exit 6): the header documents the failure taxonomy and the parser is documented "Throws on any shape drift — fail-closed, never partial zeros."

## Why it matters

This exporter's whole design is fail-closed: "a failed tick can never be mistaken for a reading." Both failure modes break that contract:

1. A units drift at the Meta console API (seconds → milliseconds is the classic one) silently exports a garbage `resetAt` as a successful reading; the quota gatherer (#1151) ingests these windows for reset/burn display, so the corruption propagates downstream as fact.
2. The RangeError path writes a failure document with the *wrong status* (`fetch-failed` instead of `unparseable`), sending whoever investigates hunting a network/page problem when the payload shape drifted.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseSubscriptionQuota` rejects epoch fields (`window_resets_at`, `weekly_resets_at`, and `as_of` when present) that do not produce a valid, plausible date — e.g. outside a sane window around now, or of millisecond magnitude — by throwing `ExportError("unparseable", 6, …)`.
- No bare `RangeError` escapes any `parse*` function: every shape drift surfaces as `unparseable` / exit 6.
- New tests in `meta-quota-export.test.mjs`: ms-scale `window_resets_at` rejected; huge finite `window_resets_at` rejected with `err.status === "unparseable"`; huge `as_of` rejected (or explicitly pinned to `null`); the captured-payload test and all existing tests still pass (`node --test pm-stack/meta-exporter/`).

## Dedup

`#2175` is the CDP-plumbing timeout (transport, open); `#2350` is the entry-point symlink check (open); `#1566` (closed) added the `window_duration_secs` validation only. No open or closed issue covers the epoch/`resets_at`/`as_of` range validation. Sibling filed this run: the `parsePaygBalance` truncation issue (different function, different mechanism).

body:
## Problem

The live source's two Project-pool consumers assume the fleet feed's
`projects` section is an array without ever checking:
`(feed?.projects ?? []).filter(isProjectPoolItem)`
(`pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:703` in `items()` and
`:742` in `projects()`). `isFleetFeed`
(`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:207-219`) never checks `projects`
at all, so a feed whose `projects` is a string, object or number
passes the gate — and `.filter` does not exist on those values, so
both consumers throw a `TypeError` instead of serving an empty pool.
The entry-level filter works fine (a `[null]` pool is filtered to
empty); it is the container shape that is unguarded.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- `feed.ts:61-66`: `FleetFeed.projects?: ProjectPoolItem[]` — absent
  when the collector had no Projects token or the read failed.
- `feed.ts:207-219`: `isFleetFeed` contains no `projects` check.
- `sources/live.ts:703`: `items()` computes the pool with
  `(feed?.projects ?? []).filter(isProjectPoolItem)` before any
  other work; `:740-743`: `projects()` does the same.
- Most `projects()` call sites are defended
  (`server.ts:267,558,574,586,609,620,745` use
  `.catch(() => [])`, and the provenance primer at `:95-112` uses
  `Promise.allSettled`) — but `items()` is not: `boardContext()`
  (`server.ts:222-227`) and `roadmapContext()` (`:229-234`) await
  `source.items(refs)` with no catch, and they back the board page
  (`boardRender`, `:263-265`), `/today` (`todayContext`, `:306-307`),
  `/roadmap` (`:479`), `/api/board.json` (`:644`) and
  `/api/roadmap.json` (`:648`). A throw in `items()` 500s all of
  them — the aggregator's main board surfaces, not just a pool facet.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedpayg/`
`probe3.ts`, the REAL `liveSource` built exactly as
`test/projects.test.ts:158` builds it — real `config.ts` +
`sources/live.ts` from main `5a34fa70`, md5-identical `feed.ts`,
Bun 1.4.2; feed files written to a temp dir):

| `projects` in feed | `src.projects()` | `src.items([])` |
|---|---|---|
| valid pool (control) | OK — 1 served | OK |
| `[null]` (entry-level) | OK — 0 served (filtered) | OK |
| `"oops"` (non-array string) | **throws** `TypeError: (feed?.projects ?? []).filter is not a function` | **throws** same |
| `{...}` (non-array object) | **throws** same | **throws** same |
| `42` (number) | **throws** same | **throws** same |

## Why it matters

The collector writes `projects` from a GraphQL read that can fail or
drift independently of the rest of the feed; the section is documented
as absent on failure, but nothing enforces array-ness when it is
present-but-wrong. One bad container value takes down the board,
today and roadmap pages plus their JSON twins — a much larger blast
radius than the pool facet itself, and a different failure mode from
the entry-level gaps: here even the defensive `.filter(...)` call is
the crash site. Related but distinct: #2418 (entry-level —
`isProjectPoolItem` never checks `labels` *inside* an entry that
passes the filter) and the feed-gate siblings #2427/#2429/#2439/
#2445/#2446/#2450/#2451 (`isFleetFeed` never checks those sections at
all; their consumers dereference entries rather than calling
`.filter` on the container).

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` with a non-array `projects` (string,
  object, number) can no longer throw in `items()` or `projects()`:
  the pool degrades to empty (the documented absent-section
  behaviour), and the board / today / roadmap pages and their JSON
  twins render normally.
- The guard lives at a layer consistent with the feed-gate sibling
  rulings (#2427/#2429/#2439/#2445/#2446/#2450/#2451): gate-level
  array check in `isFleetFeed`, or an `Array.isArray` guard at both
  live-source consumers — pinned by triage, applied to both call
  sites (`live.ts:703` and `:742`), not just one.
- Regression tests cover: `projects` as a string, as an object, and
  as a number — `projects()` returns `[]`, `items()` resolves, and a
  well-formed pool still serves its entries unchanged (the existing
  `test/projects.test.ts` pool test keeps passing).

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `projects filter aggregator`,
`payg`, `isFleetFeed` and `isFleetFeed never checks` returned no
covering issue. #2418 is the entry-level labels gap inside
`isProjectPoolItem` — the filter this issue's consumers call — not
the container shape those consumers assume.

body:
## Summary

In the charges producer's Gmail path, a message whose `message_sent_at.user_local` is empty/missing and whose fallback `date` is missing or unparseable does not get skipped — it throws. The per-message date line calls `isoDay(new Date(m.date ?? ""))`, and `isoDay` is `d.toISOString()`, which throws `RangeError: Invalid Date` on an invalid Date. The throw happens *before* the format guard on the very next lines that was written to skip such messages, and there is no per-message try around it: it propagates out of `gmailCandidates`, so `main()`'s catch discards the **entire Gmail candidate batch** for the period (every good message already collected is lost with it) and logs a misleading `gmail read failed … plaid candidates only`. One malformed triage row silently zeroes the Gmail half of the charges evidence for that run.

## Evidence (main 5a34fa70)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts:57-59` — `isoDay(d)` is `d.toISOString().slice(0, 10)`; `toISOString()` on an invalid Date throws RangeError.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts:193` — per-message: `const at = (m.message_sent_at?.user_local ?? "").slice(0, 10) || isoDay(new Date(m.date ?? ""))`. `TriageMessage` (lines 109-115) makes both `message_sent_at` and `date` optional, so the fallback is reachable with `""` or any unparseable string.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts:194-197` — the regex guard + `skipped++` that was meant to handle exactly this case sits *after* the throwing call and never runs for it.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts:242-246` — the only catch is in `main()` around the whole `gmailCandidates()` call; it logs `gmail read failed` and continues with Plaid only. The candidates array accumulated inside `gmailCandidates` is lost.
- Same pattern, operator-input variant: `:165` computes the Gmail `before:` bound as `isoDay(new Date(Date.parse(end) + 86_400_000))` — an invalid `--end` value makes `Date.parse` return NaN and throws the same way, again reported as a Gmail read failure.

Verified this run with a laptop Bun probe using the verbatim `isoDay` + date-line logic (file md5 `0f4dba2a441e7c0894cdd2ca2ceefe81`, main 5a34fa70):

```
control-good-rfc2822   -> 2026-10-27
control-good-userlocal -> 2026-10-28
missing-date           THREW: RangeError Invalid Date
garbage-date           THREW: RangeError Invalid Date
empty-both             THREW: RangeError Invalid Date
batch-all-good         -> [ "g1@2026-10-27", "g2@2026-10-28" ]
batch-one-bad          THREW: RangeError — whole gmailCandidates result lost
```

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-chargeproducer/probe.ts` (laptop).

## Why it matters

The producer is the only source of Gmail charge candidates for the charges matcher (#1057 pipeline; scheduling tracked separately in #2205). A single triage message with a missing/garbled date field — data the producer does not control — silently drops *all* Gmail-sourced charges for the period, and the log line blames a "gmail read" failure, sending any investigation toward the CLI/auth instead of the one bad message. The skip-and-count path the author wrote for malformed messages (the regex guard + `skipped`) is unreachable for precisely the malformed shape it targets.

## Acceptance criteria

- A triage message with empty/missing `message_sent_at.user_local` and a missing or unparseable `date` is counted as skipped (the existing `skipped` counter / log), and processing continues with the remaining messages — the rest of the Gmail batch is still produced.
- `isoDay` (or its call sites) cannot throw on an invalid Date: invalid input is handled at the date-derivation site, not by the whole-batch catch in `main()`.
- An invalid `--end` value is rejected with an error naming the argument (or handled equivalently explicitly), not surfaced as a Gmail read failure.
- Regression tests cover: missing `date`, garbage `date`, empty-both message interleaved with good messages (batch survives, good candidates present, skip counted), and the two control shapes (RFC 2822 `date`, `user_local` present) producing the same `at` values as today.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `produce-charge-candidates` / `isoDay` / charge-producer terms: #2194 (open) is the *consumer* side — `parseChargeCandidates` in `charges-collect.ts` accepting impossible calendar dates — a different file, function, and failure mode; #2205 (open) is about scheduling the producer; #1057 (closed) is the original charges-matching feature. No issue covers the producer's Gmail date derivation throwing and discarding the batch.

body:
## Problem

`isFleetFeed` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:207-219`) never validates
the optional `subscriptions` section at all — it checks only `version`,
`generatedAt`, `quota.pools` being an array, and `attention` being an
array. But the live source serves `feed.subscriptions` verbatim as the
usage view's flat-subscription rows, and the `/quota` renderer
dereferences every row unguarded, so one malformed row in a feed that
passes the gate crashes the whole Usage & billing page.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- `feed.ts:53-54`: `FleetFeed.subscriptions?: { name: string; plan:
  string; renewsAt: string | null }[]` (same shape at `model.ts:1280`).
- `feed.ts:207-219`: `isFleetFeed` contains no `subscriptions` check of
  any kind — not array-ness, not entry shape.
- `sources/live.ts:808-815`: in `usage()`'s feed branch (taken whenever
  `feed.saas` is non-empty), the section is passed through verbatim:
  `subscriptions: feed.subscriptions ?? []` — no filter or per-entry
  guard, unlike the registry / projects / snapshots consumers in the
  same file, which validate or filter first.
- `render.ts:1816-1826`: the subscriptions strip maps rows with
  `esc(s.name)` / `esc(s.plan)` / `s.renewsAt` — a null row throws on
  `s.name`; a non-array string `subscriptions` throws on `.map`.
- `server.ts:486-487`: `/quota` awaits `source.usage()` and calls
  `renderQuota(...)` with no catch, so the throw becomes a 500 for the
  entire usage hub page — not just a missing subscriptions strip.
  `/api/quota.json` (`server.ts:656-665`) does not crash, but serializes
  the malformed rows verbatim to API consumers.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedcharges/`, real
`feed.ts` + `render.ts` from main `5a34fa70`, md5-identical, Bun 1.4.2;
usage view assembled exactly as `live.ts:811-815` assembles it):

| `subscriptions` | `isFleetFeed` | `renderQuota` (the real `/quota` render) |
|---|---|---|
| valid entry (control) | `true` | OK — row renders |
| `[null]` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 's.name')` |
| entry missing `name` | `true` | OK — renders with an empty name (no crash, silently degraded) |
| `"oops"` (non-array string) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: usage.subscriptions.map is not a function` |
| `[valid, null]` mixed | `true` | **throws** — the valid row never renders |

## Why it matters

`subscriptions` is the hub's flat/renewal-only strip (Q5): the collector
emits these rows from the subscription records, so a single drifted or
hand-edited feed row takes down `/quota` entirely instead of dropping
one row, and the JSON twin silently serves the garbage onward. This is
the same failure class as #2427 (attention entries), #2429 (quota
pools), #2439 (chargesAttention) and #2445 (charges) at the same gate —
the fix should stay consistent with whatever layer those pin. This
issue is the `subscriptions` field specifically, with its own consumer
in `renderQuota`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `/quota`: either the
  gate validates `subscriptions` (array of entries with string
  `name`/`plan` and `renewsAt` string-or-null), or the live source
  filters/defaults malformed entries before the view is built — the
  layer pinned consistently with the #2427/#2429/#2439/#2445 rulings.
- Malformed entries are dropped individually; well-formed entries in
  the same array still render.
- Regression tests cover: `[null]` entry, non-array `subscriptions`,
  `[valid, null]` mixed — each rendering the valid remainder, never
  throwing; a well-formed feed unchanged, and the collector still
  accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `subscriptions isFleetFeed` and `feed
subscriptions validator` returned no covering issue. Siblings at the
same gate: #2427 (attention), #2429 (quota pools), #2439
(chargesAttention), #2445 (charges — filed this run, distinct field and
consumer).

  `/api/quota.json` (`server.ts:656-665`) does not crash, but serializes
  the malformed rows verbatim to API consumers. A non-array object
  `charges` is silently swallowed instead (`length` is undefined, so the
  strip renders "No charge evidence") — real charge rows vanish with no
  signal.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedcharges/`, real
`feed.ts` + `render.ts` from main `5a34fa70`, md5-identical, Bun 1.4.2;
usage view assembled exactly as `live.ts:811-815` assembles it):

| `charges` | `isFleetFeed` | `renderQuota` (the real `/quota` render) |
|---|---|---|
| valid entry (control) | `true` | OK — renders, `$12.50` row present |
| `[null]` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'c.at')` |
| entry missing `amountUsd` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'c.amountUsd.toFixed')` |
| `amountUsd: "12.50"` (string) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: c.amountUsd.toFixed is not a function` |
| `"oops"` (non-array string) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: usage.charges.map is not a function` |
| `{amountUsd: 1}` (non-array object) | `true` | no throw — charges strip silently renders "No charge evidence" |
| `[valid, null]` mixed | `true` | **throws** — the valid row never renders |

## Why it matters

`charges` is the hub's charge-evidence strip (§2.4): the collector emits
these rows from Plaid/Gmail receipt records, so a single drifted or
hand-edited feed row takes down `/quota` entirely instead of dropping
one row, and the JSON twin silently serves the garbage onward. This is
the same failure class as #2427 (attention entries), #2429 (quota pools)
and #2439 (chargesAttention) at the same gate — the fix should stay
consistent with whatever layer those pin. Note this issue is the
`charges` field specifically: #2439 covers the separate
`chargesAttention` field and its `usage()` flag map.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `/quota`: either the
  gate validates `charges` (array of entries with string
  `at`/`label`/`method`/`source` and finite number `amountUsd`), or the
  live source filters/defaults malformed entries before the view is
  built — the layer pinned consistently with the #2427/#2429/#2439
  rulings.
- Malformed entries are dropped individually; well-formed entries in the
  same array still render, and the strip total sums only valid rows.
- A non-array `charges` degrades the same way (rows dropped, page
  renders), never throws and never silently masquerades as "no charge
  evidence" when valid rows were present.
- Regression tests cover: `[null]` entry, entry missing `amountUsd`,
  string `amountUsd`, non-array `charges` (string and object) — each
  rendering the valid remainder, never throwing; a well-formed feed
  unchanged, and the collector still accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `charges isFleetFeed` and `feed
charges validator` returned no covering issue. Siblings at the same
gate: #2427 (attention), #2429 (quota pools), #2439 (chargesAttention —
distinct field, distinct consumer in `usage()`). #2130/#2194 cover
charges-match/charges-collect internals, not the feed gate, the live
`usage()` pass-through, or the `/quota` render.

title: aggregator(card-state): actions load filter never checks payload — a null/malformed payload crashes cardState on every render, a string answers fabricates a survey answer

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Summary

The actions store's load filter checks only that a record has a string `id` — its `payload` is never shape-checked on load — and `cardState()` (the render-time derivation every dashboard card goes through) dereferences `payload` unguarded. One stored action record with a malformed payload crashes card rendering for every page that shows that object, and the store re-persists the record forever. The write path validates payloads thoroughly (`validateActionInput`, actions.ts:226-313), so this is reachable only through the store file itself: a hand edit, a partial/rolled-back write from an older build, or any future writer that skips the boundary validator — exactly the class of record the load filter exists to contain (cf. #2347, the same filter's `createdAt` hole).

## Evidence (main 5a34fa70)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts:438-443` — `doLoad()` keeps any record with a string `id`; `payload` (and everything else) passes through unchecked.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/card-state.ts:75` — `snooze.payload.until`: `payload: null` (or a missing payload on a snooze) throws `TypeError: null is not an object`.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/card-state.ts:89-90` — the answer merge does `a.payload.answers ?? []` and iterates entries as `entry.questionId` / `entry.value`, plus `a.payload.optionId`:
  - `answers: [null]` throws (`entry.questionId` on null).
  - `answers: {…}` (non-array object) throws (`{} is not iterable`).
  - `answers: "ab"` (string) does **not** throw — it iterates characters and writes a fabricated answer keyed `undefined`, silently corrupting the card's survey state.
- Consumers: `cardState` is called per card from render.ts:1984, :2035, :2265, :2329, fed by `ActionsStore.byObject()` (actions.ts:471) in the board/attention render contexts (server.ts:266, :285, :546, :557) — a throw propagates out of the page render. `persist()` (actions.ts:449+) re-writes the record on every store write, so the poisoned record never ages out.

Verified this run with a laptop Bun probe driving the **real** `ActionsStore` + `cardState` (files byte-identical to main, md5 card-state.ts 99991e54…, actions.ts 6a43e179…), one malformed record per store file, valid `id`/`createdAt` so the record loads and sorts cleanly:

```
control            OK loaded 1 suppressed: "snoozed" answered: []
payload-null       THREW: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'snooze.payload.until')
answers-null-entry THREW: TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'entry.questionId')
answers-object     THREW: TypeError: {} is not iterable
answers-string     OK loaded 1 suppressed: null answered: [[null,null]]   <- fabricated answer
```

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-cardpayload/probe.ts` (laptop).

## Why it matters

The actions store is the dashboard's own write-ahead record of user intent (snoozes, dismissals, survey answers). A single malformed record — which the load path explicitly tolerates keeping — takes down every board/attention render that includes its object and keeps doing so across restarts, because the record is re-persisted verbatim. The string-`answers` shape is worse than a crash: it fabricates a survey answer that was never given.

## Acceptance criteria

- A stored action whose `payload` is null/missing/not an object, or whose `payload.answers` is not an array of `{questionId, value}` entries, cannot throw out of `cardState()` and cannot fabricate an `answered` entry.
- Regression tests at the layer triage pins (load filter rejecting/normalizing the record, and/or `cardState` tolerating it): the four probe shapes above (null payload on a snooze; `answers: [null]`; `answers` as a plain object; `answers` as a string) each render a card without throwing and without a phantom answer.
- Well-formed records behave exactly as today (the probe's control case: snooze suppresses, answers merge latest-wins).
- Sibling of #2347 (same load filter, `createdAt` field): fixing both in the load filter is welcome, but this issue is complete on the payload shapes alone.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `cardState`, `payload answers`: #1474 (closed — rejected-restore semantics in card-state, different defect), #1451 (closed — the multi-question feature itself). #2347 (open) covers the same load filter's `createdAt` sort crash in `all()`/`CommentsStore`, not payload dereference in `cardState`. No open issue covers payload shape at load or in card-state.

body:
## Problem

`isFleetFeed` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:207-219`) never validates the
optional `chargesAttention` section at all — it checks only `version`,
`generatedAt`, `quota.pools` being an array, and `attention` being an array.
But the live source dereferences every `chargesAttention` entry unguarded,
so one malformed entry in a feed that passes the gate crashes `usage()` —
and with it every route that awaits it.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- `feed.ts:25-52`: `FleetFeed.chargesAttention?: UnmatchedCharge[]`, where
  `UnmatchedCharge` (`charges-match.ts:44-50`) requires `merchant: string`,
  `amountUsd: number`, `at: string`, `source`.
- `feed.ts:207-219`: `isFleetFeed` contains no `chargesAttention` check of
  any kind — not array-ness, not entry shape.
- `sources/live.ts:820-827`: in `usage()`'s feed branch (taken whenever
  `feed.saas` is non-empty), the entries are mapped verbatim:

  ```ts
  const chargeFlags = (feed.chargesAttention ?? []).map((u) => ({
    label: `${u.merchant} — unrecognized SaaS/AI charge`,
    detail: `$${u.amountUsd.toFixed(2)} on ${u.at} via ${u.source === "plaid" ? "Plaid" : "Gmail alert"} …`,
    severity: u.amountUsd,
  }));
  ```

  There is no filter or per-entry guard — unlike the registry / projects /
  snapshots consumers in the same file, which validate or filter first.
- `server.ts:486,492,656,669`: `/quota`, `/quota/service/<id>`,
  `/api/quota.json` and `/api/quota/service.json` all `await source.usage()`
  with no catch, so the throw becomes a 500 for the whole usage hub — not
  just a missing charge flag.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-chargeattn/`, real
`feed.ts` from main `5a34fa70`, md5-identical, Bun 1.4.2; the map above
copied verbatim from `live.ts:820-827`):

| `chargesAttention` | `isFleetFeed` | verbatim map |
|---|---|---|
| valid entry (control) | `true` | OK — 1 flag, `$12.50` |
| `[null]` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'u.merchant')` |
| entry missing `amountUsd` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'u.amountUsd.toFixed')` |
| `amountUsd: "12.50"` (string) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: u.amountUsd.toFixed is not a function` |
| `"oops"` (non-array) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: (feed.chargesAttention ?? []).map is not a function` |

## Why it matters

`chargesAttention` is the exactly-once surfacing channel for unmatched
SaaS/AI charges (#1057): the collector emits these entries from Plaid/Gmail
candidate data, so a single drifted or hand-edited feed entry takes down
`/quota` and both quota JSON twins entirely instead of dropping one flag.
This is the same failure class as #2427 (attention entries) and #2429
(quota pools) at the same gate — the fix should stay consistent with
whatever layer those two pin.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `usage()`: either the
  gate validates `chargesAttention` (array of entries with string
  `merchant`/`at` and finite number `amountUsd`), or the live source
  filters/defaults malformed entries before the map — the layer pinned
  consistently with the #2427/#2429 rulings.
- Malformed entries are dropped individually; well-formed entries in the
  same array still surface as attention flags.
- Regression tests cover: `[null]` entry, entry missing `amountUsd`,
  string `amountUsd`, non-array `chargesAttention` — each rendering the
  valid remainder (or fixture fallback), never throwing; a well-formed
  feed unchanged, and the collector still accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `chargesAttention` and `isFleetFeed
charges` returned no covering issue. Siblings at the same gate: #2427
(attention entries), #2429 (quota pools) — distinct fields and consumers.
#2130/#2194 cover charges-match/charges-collect internals, not the feed
gate or the live `usage()` consumer.

labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
Phase 2 of design #2434 (mcpx error honesty, finished). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-error-honesty.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Independent of Phase 1. The decision is recorded on #2434; this phase implements its second slice.

## Scope

Dispatch consults the same capability map advertisement used. One gate in `internal/mcpserver` dispatch, evaluated after the existing `Removed()` check (server.go:785, whose precedence it keeps): compute the capability map exactly as `capabilities()` (server.go:2410) does for this peer/version/connection, and refuse with **-32601** ("no method X: capability Y not advertised") any method whose gating capability is absent or false in that map. Modern HTTP already pairs -32601 with 404 (`modernStatus`, `internal/mcpserver/transport.go`).

The gated set is ONLY the two proven disagreements — do not widen it in this phase:

- `completion/complete` ← `completions`: today answered for every revision ("completion/complete is answered for every revision; only the capability that declares it is newer than 2024-11-05", capabilities() comment) — refuse only for revisions that cannot advertise `completions` (2024-11-05); revisions that can advertise it always do, so no served behaviour changes there.
- `resources/subscribe` / `resources/unsubscribe` ← `resources.subscribe`: today dispatched unconditionally (server.go:938) even when advertisement said `subscribe: false` (no push channel). Refuse when the advertisement the peer actually saw said false.

Exempt by construction: negotiation methods (`initialize`, `server/discover`, `ping` where defined). Tasks keep their own -32021/-32601 logic. Accept-liberally stands for everything not in the gated set.

**Triage must check first:** when is `push` evaluated for the advertisement vs at dispatch — the gate must use the same evaluation the peer's advertisement used; if those can differ, that discrepancy is itself a bug to fix inside this phase before gating on it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A 2024-11-05 peer calling `completion/complete` gets -32601; 2025-03-26+ peers are served exactly as today
- [ ] `resources/subscribe` on a connection whose advertisement said `subscribe: false` gets -32601; with push available it works as today
- [ ] The gate reads the same `capabilities()` computation as advertisement (single source — no second hand-maintained table of what is advertised)
- [ ] Removed-method refusals keep precedence and their existing tests pass unchanged
- [ ] Tests run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: growing the gated set (needs its own evidence, per #2434), Phase 1's carriage, Phase 3's -32021.

## Acceptance criteria

- Dispatch refuses with -32601 (modern HTTP pairing 404 preserved) exactly the two proven disagreements named in the scope — `completion/complete` for revisions that cannot advertise `completions`, plus the second listed there — and nothing wider.
- The gate consults the same capability map `capabilities()` computes for this peer/version/connection, evaluated after the existing `Removed()` check, whose precedence is kept.
- Tests pin both refusals and that methods whose capability IS advertised still dispatch normally.

body:
## Bug

`pm-stack/aggregator` — the fleet feed's gate `isFleetFeed` checks the quota section even more thinly than the rest: it requires only that `quota.pools` is an array. It never checks `burn` or `choices` (both mandatory in `QuotaView`, `src/model.ts:274-286`), never checks pool entries, and never checks a pool's `windows`. The live source serves `feed.quota` verbatim, so one malformed pool — or a feed written by an older collector that lacks `burn`/`choices` — crashes the /quota page instead of degrading.

Sibling of #2427 (same gate, attention entries); filed separately because the section, consumers, and fix differ.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- Gate: `src/feed.ts:207-219` — the entire quota check is `typeof f.quota === "object" && f.quota !== null && Array.isArray((f.quota as QuotaView).pools)`. `burn`, `choices`, pool shape, and window shape are unchecked.
- Verbatim consumer: `src/sources/live.ts:754-785` — `quota()` sets `view = feed.quota` and returns it (the gatherer overlay aside); there is no pool/window filter anywhere on this path, unlike the registry/projects/snapshots filters in the same file.
- Unguarded dereferences: `src/render.ts:1754` `view.pools.map(p => p.windows.map(...))`, `:1776` `view.burn.map(...)`, `:1785-1787` `view.choices.hasHeadroom/...`; `src/derive.ts:813` `buildAttentionFlags` iterates `pool.windows` and `windowPercent(w)` reads `w.limit` (derive.ts:155-158) — called uncaught from `usage()`'s feed-saas branch (live.ts:832). The /quota route (server.ts:485-488) and /api/quota.json (server.ts:651) await these with no catch, and `fetchHandler` has no top-level catch.

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedquota/`, real aggregator `src/` from origin/main — feed.ts/render.ts md5-identical to the sandbox clone — Bun 1.4.2, real `isFleetFeed` + `renderQuota` + `buildAttentionFlags`):

```
== control: well-formed quota
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota: ok, html bytes = 18339
buildAttentionFlags: ok, flags = 0

== quota missing burn+choices (gate only checks pools)
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota THROWS: TypeError - undefined is not an object (evaluating 'view.burn.map')

== pools [null]
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota THROWS: TypeError - null is not an object (evaluating 'p.windows')
buildAttentionFlags THROWS: TypeError - null is not an object (evaluating 'pool.windows')

== pool missing windows
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota THROWS: TypeError - undefined is not an object (evaluating 'p.windows.map')
buildAttentionFlags THROWS: TypeError

== pool windows [null]
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota THROWS: TypeError - null is not an object (evaluating 'w.limit')
buildAttentionFlags THROWS: TypeError - null is not an object (evaluating 'w.limit')

== pool windows non-array (string "soon")
isFleetFeed: true
renderQuota THROWS: TypeError - p.windows.map is not a function
buildAttentionFlags: ok, flags = 4   (iterates the string's characters as windows — bogus flags)
```

## Why it matters

/quota is the page the fleet's pool discipline runs off (headroom, burn-before-reset, do-not-start guidance). The feed is written by a separate collector job and the aggregator's stated contract is that a stale or partial feed "keeps rendering with its age stated" — instead, schema drift in one pool (a renamed `windows`, a null placeholder, an older collector omitting `burn`/`choices`) takes the whole page down, and a non-array `windows` silently fabricates attention flags in the usage view. Every sibling section got a validator or an element filter for exactly this class; the quota section — the feed's original payload — never did.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `renderQuota` or `buildAttentionFlags`: either the gate validates the full `QuotaView` shape the renderers dereference (`burn` and `choices` present with their arrays, every pool an object with a `windows` array of window objects), or the live source filters/defaults malformed pools and windows the way it filters registry/projects records — triage pins the layer, and a rejected feed must fall back to fixtures like other invalid feeds rather than 500.
- Malformed pools/windows are dropped or defaulted individually; the well-formed pools still render on /quota and /api/quota.json.
- No fabricated attention flags: a non-array `windows` value can never be iterated as a collection of windows.
- Regression tests (aggregator suite) cover: quota missing `burn`/`choices`; `pools: [null]`; a pool missing `windows`; `windows: [null]`; `windows` as a string — each rendering the valid remainder or the fixture fallback, never throwing; a fully well-formed feed is unchanged, and the collector (which shares `isFleetFeed`) still accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for "quota pools / pool windows / poolState" return #1170 (per-pool read age display), #1119 (contract tests for the /api/quota.json saas/payg schema), #1114 (disabled providers in quota), and #2416 (quota-current.ts overlay windows — a different file and pipeline stage: the gatherer overlay, not the feed's own quota section). No open or closed issue covers `isFleetFeed`'s quota check or feed pool/window validation. Related: #2427 (attention entries, same gate).

body:
# cold-store-reaper: Drive `list_backups` never follows `nextPageToken` — retention plans from a silently truncated listing

## Evidence (verified this run, main 5a34fa70)

`ColdStore.list_backups` (`pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:992-1031`) issues exactly one Drive `files.list` request per db folder with `pageSize: 1000` and reads only `resp["files"]`. It never looks at `nextPageToken` and never sends a `pageToken`, so when a `db-backups/<db>/` folder holds more than one page of files, every file past the first page is invisible to all consumers.

The listing is ordered `createdTime desc` (`cold_store.py:1011`), so the invisible files are the **oldest** ones — precisely the files retention exists to trash:

- `prune_backups` (`cold_store.py:1092+`) builds its 30 daily / 12 weekly / 12 monthly plan (`_retention_plan`, `cold_store.py:1048`) from `list_backups` rows only. Files beyond page 1 are never kept, never pruned, and never reported as unparseable — they silently accumulate in Drive forever.
- The plan's "distinct days/weeks/months present" computation is likewise computed over a truncated set whenever the folder exceeds one page.

Probe (this run, sandbox python3, real `cold_store.py` with a stubbed `http_request` emulating the Drive API — page 1 returns 2 files plus `nextPageToken: tok2`, page 2 returns a third, older file):

```
rows returned: 2 ['d1-20261029T010000Z-a.sql', 'd1-20261028T010000Z-a.sql']
requests made: 1
any request carried pageToken: False
```

The third (oldest, 2025-01-01) backup is dropped with no error.

Probe kept at `~/workspace/goals/keep-the-four-repos-healthy/hidden_files/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-drivepage/probe.py`.

## Contrast in the same file

The S3 listing path paginates correctly: `_parse_s3_list_page` returns the continuation token (`cold_store.py:138-172`) and its caller loops over pages — the test suite even asserts the page sequence ("fake pages are 2, 2, 1", `tests/test_cold_store.py:1325`). The Drive path has no equivalent loop, and the test fake (`FakeDrive`) implements no pagination at all, so the gap is untestable today.

## Why it matters

Retention is the only mechanism that bounds Drive growth for DB backups, and it runs nightly (`scripts/nightly-backup.sh` step 4: `prune-backups --apply`). Parseable backups are capped by retention itself (~54 per db), but unparseable names are never pruned by design (reported only), pre-retention/manual files count too, and any folder that crosses 1000 files permanently hides its oldest members from the one tool meant to remove them. The failure is silent: the nightly run reports success while Drive grows.

Related but distinct: #1632 is the same class of bug in the **S3** listing loop (continuation-token handling); this issue is the **Drive** `files.list` path, which never paginates at all.

## Acceptance criteria

- `list_backups` follows `nextPageToken` until the listing is exhausted, preserving newest-first order across pages.
- A folder whose listing spans multiple pages yields the full row set; `prune_backups` plans over the complete set (an over-page oldest excess file appears in the prune plan in a test).
- The `FakeDrive` test double implements Drive pagination (honours `pageSize` / emits `nextPageToken`), with a regression test that a multi-page folder is fully listed.
- Existing cold-store test suites still pass.

body:
## Problem

The AA (Cost Explorer) section's only structural gate never checks two required arrays that the renderer dereferences unconditionally, so a section missing them passes validation and crashes the /aa page instead of degrading to "not collected yet".

- `AaSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/model.ts:937-960) declares `sources: AaSourceInfo[]` (:943) and `thresholds: AaThreshold[]` (:945) as required, non-optional fields.
- `isAaSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts:1070-1085) — described at :1069 as the "structural check shared by the collector and the live source" — checks only `generatedAt`, `batch`, `rankings` (non-empty, entries have string `testRunKey`/`family`), `configs` (array) and `testRuns` (array). It never checks `sources` or `thresholds` at all, and `testRuns`/`configs` entries are not checked for null.
- Consumers dereference them bare: `summarizeAa` iterates `section.thresholds` (aa.ts:1101) and maps `section.testRuns[].snapshotDate` (aa.ts:1096-1099); the /aa renderer does `s.sources.map(...)` (render.ts:4213) immediately after calling `summarizeAa(s)` (render.ts:4212).
- The live source (src/sources/live.ts:961-971) is built to fail soft: a section that fails `isAaSection` returns null and the page renders the "has not reached the dashboard yet" banner. A section that passes the gate but lacks `thresholds`/`sources` bypasses that degradation and throws inside the render instead.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `5a34fa70`)

Sandbox Bun probe importing the real `aa.ts` (probe at /tmp/probe-laneB-aa/probe.ts):

- `{status:"ok", generatedAt, batch, rankings:[{testRunKey:"k1",family:"Fam"}], configs:[], testRuns:[]}` (no `thresholds`, no `sources`) → `isAaSection` returns **true**; `summarizeAa` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 't of section.thresholds')`; `section.sources.map(...)` throws the same class of TypeError.
- Same section with `testRuns:[null]` → passes the gate; `summarizeAa` throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'r.snapshotDate')`.
- Control: the same section with `thresholds:[]` and `sources:[]` added passes and `summarizeAa` returns normally.

## Why it matters

The fleet feed is produced by a separate collector on another host and ages through absent/degraded forms by design; the gate is the one place that decides "renderable" vs "degrade". Every other section validator in this codebase that feeds a renderer was held to the rule that whatever the renderer dereferences must be gated (see feed.ts's per-goal gate comment, #949). Here a single malformed or older-format feed write takes down the whole Cost Explorer page with a 500-class throw rather than the designed banner — and the failure mode is invisible until someone opens /aa.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isAaSection` rejects an "ok" section whose `thresholds` or `sources` is missing or not an array (entries checked to the same depth the renderer/summarize uses them: at minimum non-null objects for `testRuns` entries, whose `snapshotDate` is read).
- [ ] A section failing the strengthened gate degrades through the existing live-source path: `aa()` returns null and /aa renders the "not collected yet" banner, never a throw.
- [ ] A regression test (aggregator test suite, aa coverage) pins: missing-`thresholds`, missing-`sources`, and null-`testRuns`-entry sections all fail `isAaSection`; a complete minimal section still passes.
- [ ] Sections the current collector actually emits still pass unchanged (no producer change required, or it is named in the fix).

## Dedup

- #2242 (OPEN) is about aa/dns `generatedAt` stamps never being validated for health age rendering — different fields, different failure. This issue is the missing/invalid `thresholds`/`sources` arrays crashing the /aa render.
- #2412/#2408/#2376 are other aggregator section/record validators (dns, registry) with different fields and consumers.
- `isAaSection` / thresholds-gate searches over open+closed issues returned no match for this defect.

title: clef-proxy: client-supplied model is interpolated into the upstream URL unvalidated — any @cf/* model runs, and ../ and ? payloads rewrite the gateway path/query
