title: pm-stack(aggregator): saas-extract export overlays accept impossible/non-ISO measuredAt (and cycleStart) — Date.parse-only freshness gates vs the file's own parseIsoDate rule

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts` applies two live file-export overlays — `applyCloudflareExport` (#1048) and `applySupabaseExport` (#1050) — whose freshness gates are `Date.parse`-only:

- Cloudflare `measuredAt`: `const measuredMs = Date.parse(doc.measuredAt)` (saas-extract.ts:811), checked only for finiteness and a 30-minute / +5-minute freshness window (:812-813).
- Cloudflare `cycleStart`: `const cycleMs = Date.parse(doc.cycleStart)` (saas-extract.ts:819-821), checked only for finiteness before its year/month are compared against now to reject a previous cycle's totals.
- Supabase `measuredAt`: `const measuredMs = Date.parse(doc.measuredAt)` (saas-extract.ts:933), same finiteness + freshness checks (:934-935).

`Date.parse` rolls day-overflow dates over and accepts non-ISO strings, so an export document stamped `2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z` parses as March 2 and passes freshness at a wall-clock time near March 2. The overlay then stamps `doc.measuredAt.slice(0, 10)` verbatim onto the card (Cloudflare :846, Supabase :996), so the card displays a measured date that never existed — for a non-ISO stamp like `March 2, 2026 12:00 UTC` the slice is literally `March 2, 2`.

An impossible `cycleStart` of `2026-02-30` likewise rolls into March, evading the same-month check whose whole purpose is to keep a previous cycle's totals off a fresh month's card.

The same file already holds its other dates to the real-calendar rule: `datesIn` filters through `parseIsoDate` (saas-extract.ts:26, comment: "Real calendar dates only (#2264)") and the subscription `renewsAt` extraction requires `parseIsoDate(...) !== null` (:1175). The shared `validate.ts` contract (`parseIsoDate`/`isIsoDate`) also already lives in this file's imports. These three overlay fields are the residual gap.

## Verified this run (laptop bun probe, origin/main bb592a618)

Probe `/tmp/probe-saas.ts` on the laptop (log `/tmp/probe-saas.log`), driving `applyCloudflareExport` / `applySupabaseExport` directly over `extractSaasServices`, with `now = 2026-03-02T12:05:00Z`:

```
CF measuredAt="2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z" cycle="2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z" -> used=75225 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=2026-02-30
CF measuredAt="March 2, 2026 12:00 UTC" cycle="2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z" -> used=75225 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=March 2, 2
CF measuredAt="2026-03-02T12:00:00.000Z" cycle="2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z" -> used=75225 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=2026-03-02
CF measuredAt="2026-03-02T12:00:00.000Z" cycle="2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z" -> used=75225 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=2026-03-02
CF measuredAt="not-a-date" cycle="2026-03-01T00:00:00.000Z" -> used=null sourceClass=manual cardMeasuredAt=2026-10-20
SB measuredAt="2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z" -> used=1.154 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=2026-02-30
SB measuredAt="2026-03-02T12:00:00.000Z" -> used=1.154 sourceClass=api cardMeasuredAt=2026-03-02
SB measuredAt="not-a-date" -> used=null sourceClass=manual cardMeasuredAt=2026-10-28
```

So: impossible and non-ISO `measuredAt` values are applied as live `api` data on both cards and displayed verbatim; garbage is refused (control); a valid stamp behaves identically (control); an impossible `cycleStart` passes the month check a real February cycle start would fail.

## Why it matters

These overlays are the "live measured data" path for the Cloudflare and Supabase cards: a passing document replaces the recorded prose values and re-classes the card's source as `api`. A drifted, skewed, or hand-edited export write whose stamp names no real instant should fall back to the prose, exactly as a stale or unparseable one does — instead the rollover gives it a real, possibly-fresh instant, it wins, and the card confidently displays a nonexistent measured date. That is the same failure mode the file's #2264 real-calendar rule was adopted to stop everywhere else.

## Acceptance criteria

- `applyCloudflareExport` changes nothing (returns the services untouched, prose fallback) when `doc.measuredAt` is not a real ISO calendar date/time under the shared `validate.ts` rule — e.g. `2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z`, `2026-04-31T12:00:00.000Z`, `March 2, 2026 12:00 UTC` are refused; valid `toISOString()` stamps are unchanged.
- `applyCloudflareExport` likewise changes nothing when a present `doc.cycleStart` is not a real ISO calendar date/time, instead of rolling it into a neighbouring month for the same-month check.
- `applySupabaseExport` applies the same `measuredAt` rule.
- Real timestamps still overlay, including leap dates (`2024-02-29T12:00:00.000Z`); the existing tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/cloudflare-export.test.ts` and `pm-stack/aggregator/test/supabase-export.test.ts` stay green.
- New tests in those two files cover the impossible-date and non-ISO refusals for `measuredAt` (both overlays) and for `cycleStart` (Cloudflare), plus a leap-date control that is kept.

## Dedup / related

- Distinct from open #4942 (same file/function: Cloudflare negative `used` values — a value-range rule, not the date gates) and closed #2508 (Supabase doc shape/range checks, including a non-string `measuredAt`; a *string* impossible date still passes today, verified above).
- Distinct from open #4987 (`quota-current.ts` `measuredAt` gates) and the other aggregator date-gate filings: same defect class, different file and gates.
- Dedup checked this run: `gh search issues` for `saas-extract measuredAt`, `applyCloudflareExport`, `applySupabaseExport`, and open `saas-extract` returned only #4942, closed #2508, and the closed feature issues #1048/#1050 — none covers these date gates.

body:
From the placement-framework v1 synthesis on #2024 (design doc PR linked there); the registry requirement was first specified in the #2020 Jules investigation.

## What
One fleet-side schedule registry covering ALL THREE schedule surfaces, as a single committable record:

- **Muse cron** — judgement-bearing fleet jobs
- **OpenCode schedules** — OS timer + `opencode run` units (#2019 pattern; implementation #2232)
- **Jules schedules** — web-UI CRUD on the one collected account (pilot #2265)

Per schedule: surface, name/id, repo/scope, cadence, route or pool, prompt/brief pointer (verbatim for Jules), budget expectation, owner, kill criteria, date created, last review.

## Why
Each surface's native UI/state is invisible to the other two. Without one registry, schedules are invisible to fleet reviews — the failure mode #2020 named — and the placement framework's "which surface owns this recurring work" question cannot be answered from evidence.

## Acceptance
- Registry file created and populated for all currently-known schedules on the three surfaces (Jules section may start with the #2265 pilot entry + an explicit "none others known" note).
- Creating/retiring a schedule on any surface updates the registry in the same pass (written into the relevant job/runbook text).
- Registry is an input to the placement audit proposed in the framework doc.

Refs #2024, #2020, #2232, #2265.

title: pm-stack(aggregator): parseQuotaCurrent accepts impossible and non-ISO measuredAt — entry and window measuredAt are typeof-only, unlike the isIsoDate gates on resetsAt/credentialExpiresAt in the same functions

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-current.ts` gates the gatherer's `quota-current.json` with `parseQuotaCurrent`. In the same two gate functions, some date fields are held to the shared real-calendar rule and the most load-bearing one is not:

- window `resetsAt` must pass `isIsoDate` (quota-current.ts:61)
- entry `credentialExpiresAt` must pass `isIsoDate` (quota-current.ts:80)
- entry `measuredAt` is only `typeof value.measuredAt === "string"` (quota-current.ts:75)
- window `measuredAt` is only `typeof value.measuredAt === "string"` (quota-current.ts:62)

`measuredAt` is the field the whole overlay runs on: `entryState` (quota-current.ts:137) classifies an entry fresh/stale from `Date.parse(entry.measuredAt)`, `newestFirst` (quota-current.ts:161) picks the winning entry by it, and `applyEntry` (quota-current.ts:208) stamps it verbatim onto the pool as its displayed freshness.

`Date.parse` rolls day-overflow dates over and accepts non-ISO strings, so a gatherer entry stamped `2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z` passes the gate, parses as March 2, and — at a wall-clock time near March 2 — classifies as a fresh "ok" read: its windows replace the pool's windows, the pool recomputes healthy, and the freshness stamp shown for the pool is a date that never existed. A stamp of `March 2, 2026` passes the same way. Every sibling date field in the same gate, and the shared `validate.ts` contract (`parseIsoDate`/`isIsoDate`: impossible calendar dates FAIL instead of rolling over), say this input is malformed.

## Verified this run (laptop bun probe, origin/main 314fbbebc)

Probe `/tmp/probe-qc.ts` on the laptop (log `/tmp/probe-qc.log`), driving `parseQuotaCurrent` and `overlayQuotaCurrent` directly:

```
impossible-entry+window 2026-02-30   providersKept=1 dropped=0 winKept=1
noniso-entry "March 2, 2026"         providersKept=1 dropped=0 winKept=1
contrast credentialExpiresAt 2026-02-30 (measuredAt valid)  providersKept=null (entry refused)
contrast window resetsAt 2026-02-30 (measuredAts valid)     providersKept=1 winKept=0 (window dropped)
control leap 2024-02-29              providersKept=1 dropped=0 winKept=1
overlay freshness={"measuredAt":"2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z","source":"probe","state":"ok"} poolState=healthy windows=1
```

The overlay case: an entry stamped `2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z`, viewed at 2026-03-02T12:05:00Z, is classified fresh, replaces the pool's windows, sets the pool healthy, and displays the impossible stamp verbatim as the pool's freshness.

## Why it matters

`quota-current.json` is written by an external gatherer process on a 15-minute tick; a skewed, hand-edited, or drifted write is exactly what this gate exists to isolate (the file's own history: #1541 future-dated reads, #2253 garbage stamps winning the stale-path pick, #2416 malformed windows). Those fixes finite-gated the *consumers* of `measuredAt`, but the gate still admits stamps that name no real instant — and the rollover makes them *more* dangerous than garbage: a garbage stamp parses to NaN and loses, while an impossible stamp parses to a real, possibly-fresh instant and wins, wearing a freshness label that never existed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isQuotaCurrentEntry` refuses (drops, per the gate's existing per-entry isolation) an entry whose `measuredAt` is not a real ISO calendar date/time, using the shared `isIsoDate` primitive from `validate.ts` — e.g. `2026-02-30T12:00:00.000Z`, `2026-04-31T12:00:00.000Z`, `March 2, 2026` are refused; this matches the existing treatment of `credentialExpiresAt` in the same function.
- `isQuotaCurrentWindow` applies the same rule to a window's `measuredAt`, matching its existing `resetsAt` rule — a malformed window drops without dropping its entry's valid windows.
- Real timestamps still validate, including leap dates (`2024-02-29T12:00:00.000Z`) and the `new Date().toISOString()` shapes the gatherer writes — the existing tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota-current.test.ts` stay green.
- New tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota-current.test.ts` cover the impossible-date and non-ISO refusals for both the entry and the window, plus a leap-date control that is kept.

## Dedup / related

- Distinct from closed #1541 / #2253 (future-dated and garbage stamps at the freshness/newest-pick consumers — finite-gating, not calendar validity at the gate) and from closed #3427 (`feed.ts` `isQuotaWindow`, a different gate).
- Distinct from open #4955 (`credential-lifecycle.ts` row gate) and open #4968 (`quota-gather-map.ts` `normalizeResetAt`): same defect class, different files and gates.

title: pm-stack(aggregator): isSavedView accepts impossible and non-ISO timestamps — createdAt/updatedAt are Date.parse-only, unlike the isIsoDate gates in every sibling store

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

The aggregator's ingest contract (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/validate.ts`) provides `parseIsoDate`/`isIsoDate` so that "impossible calendar dates FAIL instead of rolling over: 2026-02-30 and 2026-13-01 are null, not March dates." Every comparable persisted-store gate uses it — snapshot records/rollups (`snapshots.ts`), quota windows/freshness (`feed.ts`), DNS sections, charges rows.

The saved-views store gate never got that check. `isSavedView` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/views.ts:88-103`) validates `createdAt`/`updatedAt` with `Date.parse` only:

```ts
typeof view.createdAt === "string" &&
Number.isFinite(Date.parse(view.createdAt)) &&
typeof view.updatedAt === "string" &&
Number.isFinite(Date.parse(view.updatedAt))
```

`Date.parse` rolls day-overflow dates over and accepts non-ISO strings, so a view stamped `2026-02-30T10:00:00.000Z` or `March 2, 2026` passes the gate and is stored/kept verbatim, while every parsed view of it is a different day (2026-03-02). `ViewsStore.all()` (`views.ts:259`) orders views by string-comparing `createdAt`, so a non-ISO stamp also sorts lexicographically instead of chronologically against the ISO stamps every real writer produces (`save()`/`rename()` write `new Date().toISOString()`, `views.ts:288,304`).

This gate is the load boundary: `ViewsStore.doLoad` (`views.ts:217-221`) quarantines the whole store when any row fails `isSavedView` (the behaviour the existing tests pin for other malformed rows, e.g. a missing name). A garbage stamp (`not-a-date`) is correctly treated as malformed today — an impossible or non-ISO stamp is the same class of corruption and should meet the same fate, instead of surviving reload as a seemingly valid view.

## Verified this run (laptop probe, origin/main 91c3b1938)

Probe `/tmp/probe-views.ts` on the laptop (log `/tmp/probe-scan22-views.log`), driving `ViewsStore` against hand-written store files:

```
control-valid              kept=2  quarantined=0  parsedCreated=[2026-01-15, 2026-03-01]
impossible-2026-02-30      kept=2  quarantined=0  parsedCreated=[2026-01-15, 2026-03-02]  (stored string: 2026-02-30)
noniso-March2              kept=1  quarantined=0  parsedCreated=[2026-03-02]  (stored string: "March 2, 2026")
impossible-2026-04-31-updated  kept=1  quarantined=0
garbage-created ("not-a-date") kept=0  quarantined=1  (existing correct behaviour)
```

So month-13/garbage are refused only because `Date.parse` happens to return NaN for them; day-overflow within a real month and plain non-ISO date strings — the cases `parseIsoDate` was written for — sail through.

## Why it matters

Saved views are a user's persisted, per-person filter sets. A hand-edited, corrupt, or drifted views file carrying an impossible/non-ISO timestamp currently survives reload as valid, renders/orders by a string that names a day that never existed, and disagrees with every parsed view of it. The boundary's own shared primitive and every sibling store gate say this input is malformed; the views gate should agree.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSavedView` refuses a `createdAt` or `updatedAt` that is not a real ISO calendar date/time (e.g. `2026-02-30T10:00:00.000Z`, `2026-04-31T10:00:00.000Z`, `March 2, 2026`), using the shared `isIsoDate`/`parseIsoDate` primitive from `validate.ts` rather than a new local parser.
- Real timestamps still validate, including leap dates (`2024-02-29T10:00:00.000Z`) and the `new Date().toISOString()` shapes `save()`/`rename()` write (fractional seconds, `Z` offset) — the existing round-trip tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/views.test.ts` stay green.
- On load, a store containing an impossible/non-ISO-stamped row follows the store's existing malformed-row behaviour (quarantine with bytes preserved, start empty) — no new load semantics.
- New tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/views.test.ts` cover the impossible-date and non-ISO refusals (quarantine on load) and a leap-date control that loads normally.

## Dedup / related

- Distinct from #4301 (duplicate ids/names/defaults in the same store) and closed #4150 (missing-name / non-object-filters rows).
- The stream-event analogue was prepared separately as outbox OB-2026-11-03-096 (its body flags this views site as a separate change); this issue is that separate change for `views.ts` only.

title: Follow-up to #2954: deepMergeProviders is a recursive assignment-semantics merge over external config keys
body:
Filed by the Phase 3 closing inventory audit of design #2953 (issue #2954, queue task 7683, PR #4956) as its named deep-merge follow-up.

## Finding
`bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs` exports `deepMergeProviders(base, over)` — a recursive merge used to fold the runtime config overlay into the effective provider config (runSync). A recursive merge is assignment semantics at every depth: keys spelled by the overlay file (a file-spelled, external source) are written into the merged object per level, so a `__proto__` key at any depth goes through the [[Set]] setter instead of becoming an own property — the exact class design #2953 contracts against.

## Why this is a follow-up, not part of PR #4956
The #2953 design doc records deep-merge helpers as an explicit open question: "a recursive merge is assignment semantics at every depth; no in-tree instance is known — Phase 3's audit reports one if it exists rather than this design pre-deciding its shape." This is that report. The fix shape needs its own decision: convert the merge to Map/null-prototype containers per level, or write leaves with define semantics (Object.defineProperty) while recursing — weighing that the merged result feeds config serialization and the catalog-sync guard (`assertCatalogOnly`) compares parsed before/after configs.

## Acceptance
- deepMergeProviders (and any caller-visible result) stores a `__proto__` key at any depth as an own property with its value; the merged object's prototype and Object.prototype never move.
- Probe matrix per #2953 corollary 4 at depth ≥2: `__proto__` string value, `__proto__` object value, `constructor`, `toString`, ordinary key — own property present, JSON round-trip preserves.
- `node --test bin/provider-catalog-sync.test.mjs` passes.

Refs: #2953 (design), #2954 (Phase 3 audit).

title: ci: nix-ci basic tier has no pull_request trigger — bin/-only PRs merge with zero basic checks

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/queue-worker

labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched

body:
## Problem

`.github/ci-policy.md` states the PR tier is the merge requirement and describes `basic: proxy port fallbacks` as the required context, and `.github/workflows/nix-ci.yml`'s own header comment says the job "runs on every PR". The workflow's `on:` block, however, is:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 8 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
```

There is no `pull_request` trigger, so the basic tier never runs on a PR. A `bin/`-only PR therefore gets no basic-tier verification at all: the check rollup contains only CodeRabbit (neutral/skipping) and `gh run list --branch <branch>` returns no Actions runs.

## Evidence

While landing PR #3487 (`bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs` shape validation, `bin/` + tests only):

- `gh run list --branch queue/5433-2827-catalogsync-shape` → only the two scheduled `jules-daily-*` push workflows, both failing in 0s; no `nix ci` run, before or after a fresh push to the branch.
- `gh pr checks 3487` → only `CodeRabbit skipping`.
- `gh pr view 3487 --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus` → `MERGEABLE CLEAN`, so the merge proceeded without the required context ever being reported.
- Local evidence stood in for CI: `node --test bin/provider-catalog-sync.test.mjs` → 35 pass / 0 fail.

This is the same class of gap as #4533 (mcpx PR test tier never triggers) and #3039 (host-eval not a required check), for the nix-ci basic tier.

## Impact

Any PR touching only `bin/`, docs, or other paths outside the PR-triggered workflows (id, mcpx*, mod-tidy, opencode-config-guard, production-line-guard, repo-sweeper) merges unverified by Actions. The proxy-port-fallback check is exactly the guard for `bin/*.mjs` port defaults, i.e. the one job that should have run here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `nix-ci.yml` gains a `pull_request` trigger (with or without a paths filter that includes `bin/**`, `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`, `home/common/default.nix`, and the workflow itself).
- [ ] `basic: proxy port fallbacks` reports on a `bin/`-only PR (verify with a scratch PR, not just by reading the YAML).
- [ ] `ci-policy.md`, the workflow comment, and the actual trigger agree; if a path filter is deliberate, the policy says which paths each basic-tier job covers.
- [ ] Merge-queue behaviour is unchanged (the `merge_group` trigger, if required by the ruleset, is preserved).

title: fix(pm-dispatch): failed launches leave orphan tracking issues open (66 open, #3499–#4899)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Problem

A dispatch whose launch fails after the tracking issue is created leaves that issue **open, empty and uncommented** — an orphan. There are 66 such issues open right now, all titled with the literal test prompt `do the thing`:

#3499 #3500 #3501 #3502 #3503 #3504 #3863 #3864 #4029 #4030 #4037 #4038 #4039 #4040 #4042 #4043 #4228 #4229 #4237 #4239 #4244 #4245 #4247 #4248 #4343 #4344 #4348 #4349 #4531 #4532 #4859 #4860 #4892 #4893 #4894 #4895 #4896 #4897 #4898 #4899 (and older)

Every one has body exactly:

```
do the thing

---
Launched by pm-dispatch for developing-today/code. Queue task and OpenCode session ids follow in a comment below.
```

and **zero** comments until the coverage loop-back pass of 2026-11-03 began adding its own `reviewed` notes.

## Evidence / root cause

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts` `handleSessions`:

1. step 1 creates the tracking issue (`maybeCreateIssue`, line ~199);
2. step 2 enqueues the task (`enqueueDispatchTask`); its failure path returns **502 without touching the issue** (`server.ts` ~482–493);
3. step 3 creates the session; a session failure likewise returns with the issue left behind.

The comment that would have carried "Queue task #… OpenCode session #…" is only posted *after* the launch succeeds (`annotateLaunch`, ~500+). So exactly the failure shape above — issue created, no comment ever — is the signature of a launch that died between issue creation and the first annotation. That is the 66-issue pattern.

The prompt is the literal test string from `pm-stack/dispatch/test/validate.test.ts` / `test/server.test.ts` (`prompt: "do the thing"`), so these are manual/test dispatches fired against the production repo (`developing-today/code`) with a deliberately meaningless prompt — and the successful ones among them are where the orphans come from when only part of the launch path worked.

Design #2668 states the principle "validate the whole request at the boundary, one commit point, nothing after it can fail the launch"; the tracking issue is created *before* the commit point and has no compensating action, which is the gap.

## Scoped fix

1. **Compensation**: when the launch fails after `maybeCreateIssue` succeeded (enqueue 502 path, session creation failure), post a short failure comment on the issue and close it as `not planned` — or move issue creation after the enqueue/session commit point, keeping the issue as the record only once the launch is real.
2. **Cleanup**: close the existing 66 orphans (they carry no spec), each with a one-line reason pointing here.
3. **Guard**: optionally refuse `POST /v1/sessions` with the test prompt against a production repo, or keep test dispatches on a scratch repo, so the smoke path cannot file issues in `developing-today/code`.

## For other triage lanes

Any further `do the thing` issue is the same artifact: triage it by closing it with a pointer here. Do not open a second fix issue for this class.

Found by triage of #4898 (queue task 7881, repo-health-code-pilot).

body:
Found by queue task 7577 (lane code-i, 2026-11-03) while trying to deploy the #4886 pm-dispatch fix.

## Problem

The laptop primary clone `~/git/code` cannot fast-forward, so `pm-git-sync` fails every run and pm-stack services (aggregator, dispatch, projector) cannot redeploy from main:

- `pm-stack/aggregator/events.json` is **tracked in main** (blob `3adadadb`, swept in by a repo-keeper snapshot commit) but is also the aggregator's **live runtime output file** in the checkout (local copy updated 2026-11-03 04:24, `actor: aggregator` session-outcome events). At the primary's current HEAD it is untracked, so a fast-forward pull refuses: the untracked runtime file would be overwritten by the tracked copy.
- `pm-git-sync.service` journal (2026-11-03 06:53 CST) fails loudly naming the dirt, by design: ` M pkgs/id/src/chat.rs` and `?? pm-stack/aggregator/events.json`. The chat.rs modification is separate in-progress work and is not part of this issue.

## Impact

Any pm-stack fix merged to main (e.g. PR #4900 for #4886) cannot deploy until the primary can fast-forward again.

## Fix sketch

- Remove `pm-stack/aggregator/events.json` from tracking and gitignore it (runtime state belongs under `~/.local/state/`, cf. the pm-aggregator runtime-state move on 2026-10-27), or point the aggregator's events output at an untracked/state path.
- Reconcile the laptop's live events file with whatever history matters before untracking.

Acceptance: `pm-git-sync` can fast-forward the primary again with the aggregator running; `git status` in the primary stays clean while the aggregator writes events.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pm-stack/aggregator/events.json` is no longer tracked in main (removed from the index and gitignored, or the aggregator's events output points at an untracked/state path such as `~/.local/state/`).
- The laptop primary clone `~/git/code` can fast-forward again: `pm-git-sync` succeeds and pm-stack services redeploy from main (the separately-noted `pkgs/id/src/chat.rs` dirt in the primary is not part of this issue).
- The laptop's live events history is reconciled before untracking (no session-outcome history silently dropped), and the handling is noted on this issue.

title: id(world): records.read cap pages can exceed the result_event size cap — admitted 768 KiB pages are replaced by result_too_large above 64 KiB

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

body:
## Finding (from PR #4856 CodeRabbit review, dispositioned by task 4880)

`records.read` pages are admitted up to `MAX_RECORDS_PAGE_BYTES` (768 KiB), but cap results are delivered through `result_event` (pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs), which replaces any serialized result event larger than `MAX_EVENT_BYTES` (64 KiB) with a `result_too_large` error. A records page between 64 KiB and 768 KiB therefore passes the page check in `execute_records_read` (pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs) yet can never reach the program as records.

## Evidence
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs`: `MAX_EVENT_BYTES = 64 * 1024`; `result_event` returns the `result_too_large` error above that size; `RECORDS_READ_BOUNDS` (added by PR #4856) reports `ProviderBound::ResponseBytes(MAX_RECORDS_PAGE_BYTES)`.
- `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs`: `execute_records_read` admits records until `used + size > MAX_RECORDS_PAGE_BYTES` (768 KiB).
- Note `MAX_RECORDS_PAGE_BYTES` also bounds the session-protocol page path (pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs), which is a different consumer from cap result events — the fix must distinguish the two budgets, not blindly shrink the shared constant.

## Why this is a follow-up, not part of PR #4856
PR #4856 (issue #1061 slice 1) is a no-behavior-change registry refactor; bounding the records page changes runtime behavior and belongs in its own change with its own tests.

## Acceptance
- A `records.read` cap result can never be admitted at a size `result_event` will refuse: derive the cap-result page bound from the event limit minus the result envelope, or route the result so the admitted page is deliverable.
- `RECORDS_READ_BOUNDS` reports the bound that actually applies to cap results.
- Regression test: a records page near the bound is delivered as records (not replaced by `result_too_large`), and the session-protocol page budget is unchanged.

body:
Found 2026-11-03 while building the home-manager activation for the service-cascade migration (PR #4880) on the laptop (amd). This blocks ANY home-manager switch from current main on that machine, independent of #4880: the failing derivation's inputs (`pkgs/latest-cli` at c19c1d8b, nixpkgs f9887a8a) are untouched by that PR.

## Symptom

`nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.home-manager.users.user.home.activationPackage` fails at:

```
error: Cannot build '/nix/store/7cx4lzd1wf3ghwrz9ajf4y9j1ilzxiin-t3-0.1.2.drv'.
       Reason: builder failed with exit code 139.
       > Running phase: installCheckPhase
       > .../stdenv-linux-no-cc/setup: line 1773:   269 Segmentation fault (core dumped) "$out/bin/t3" --version > /dev/null
```

The t3 package (pkgs/latest-cli — prebuilt upstream binary, autoPatchelf'd) segfaults on `$out/bin/t3 --version` in its installCheckPhase, inside the nix build sandbox.

## Reproducibility

- Reproduced 2/2 independent build attempts of the same derivation on amd (2026-11-03, ~05:5x and ~06:0x CST), identical failure.
- Building the derivation directly (`nix build /nix/store/7cx4lzd1wf3ghwrz9ajf4y9j1ilzxiin-t3-0.1.2.drv`) fails the same way — it is a property of the package on this machine, not of the activation graph.
- Not yet determined: whether the binary also segfaults outside the build sandbox (the failed output is discarded, so there is no built copy to run by hand), and whether the cause is the sandbox environment, the patchelf rewriting, or the upstream binary on this CPU.

## Impact

- The laptop's home-manager generation is stuck at the 2026-11-01 generation until this is fixed or the package is worked around; every pending HM change (including #4880's service-cascade migration) is undeployable.
- The live t3 server keeps running from the older generation's build, so nothing is down — this is a deploy blocker, not an outage.

## Suggested next steps

- Reproduce the segfault with a kept output (`--keep-failed`) and run the binary under the same conditions the check does; check dmesg/core for the faulting library after patchelf.
- If the binary is fine outside the sandbox, consider what installCheck actually proves for a prebuilt upstream binary and whether it should run `--version` differently — do not just delete the check without recording why it failed.

title: id(hosted_binding): create_pairing_code mints multiple live codes for one challenge (no supersession)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Problem

In `pkgs/id/src/hosted_binding.rs` (own-node ceremony variant, §3.3b), `create_pairing_code` (hosted_binding.rs:813) mints a fresh 6-digit pairing code for a challenge **without invalidating any previously minted codes for the same challenge**. Each code is stored independently in `pairing_codes` (insert at hosted_binding.rs:851-857; `PairingCode` records the `challenge_id`, hosted_binding.rs:390-397), and `exchange_pairing_code` (hosted_binding.rs:870) honours every live code — exchanging a code does not consume the challenge or any sibling code.

So one pending ceremony can have many simultaneously valid bearer codes (bounded only by `MAX_PAIRINGS_PER_HOUR` = 10 per account), each able to fetch the full challenge (sub, iroh_id, nonce) until the challenge's 5-minute expiry. The §3.3b flow describes *a* short-lived pairing code tied to the pending ceremony; nothing in the module documents multiple live codes per ceremony, and there is no way to revoke an earlier code (e.g. one displayed to the wrong screen, or mistyped into the wrong node) short of abandoning the whole challenge.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Re-verified by new-issue-creator lane A at origin/main 2194bd4c2 (laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-laneA-hosted`, since removed; temporary integration test `pkgs/id/tests/probe_hosted_a.rs`, log `/tmp/probe-laneA-hosted.log` on the laptop):

- One challenge, two `create_pairing_code` calls: two distinct live codes (probe printed `096628` vs `017728`). Exchanging the first succeeded, exchanging the second also succeeded, and both returned the same challenge — the first code was not superseded or invalidated by minting the second, and neither exchange affected the other code.

Code reading at the same commit: `create_pairing_code` (hosted_binding.rs:813) never removes or marks existing `pairing_codes` entries whose `challenge_id` matches; the collision loop only avoids reusing a code string that is currently present. Originally found by lane B (creator-b) at 550b611eb; its filing was blocked by a GitHub secondary rate limit, so lane A re-verified and filed it.

## Why it matters

The pairing code is the bearer handoff between the authenticated browser session and the user's node. Keeping every previously minted code valid for the challenge's whole lifetime multiplies the exposure of a 6-digit (10^6) secret and defeats the natural user recovery action — "that code went to the wrong place, give me a new one" — because the old code keeps working. Binding still requires the root key's signature, so this is a hardening/contract gap rather than a direct takeover; it is cheap to fix now, in the slice that introduced the flow (#3808), before the Worker API slice (#3811) exposes it over HTTP.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Minting a pairing code for a challenge supersedes (invalidates) all previously minted, unexchanged codes for the same `challenge_id` — or the module docs are amended in the same change to state that multiple live codes per ceremony are intended, with the reasoning recorded.
- [ ] Regression test: code A minted, code B minted for the same challenge, exchanging A fails (`UnknownChallenge`), exchanging B succeeds and returns the challenge.
- [ ] Existing behaviour preserved: a single code still exchanges once and only once; per-account pairing rate limit unchanged; expired codes still return `ChallengeExpired` on exchange.
- [ ] Existing hosted_binding tests still pass (`cargo test -p id --lib hosted_binding`).

Found by new-issue-creator lane B (creator-b) during a scan of the newly landed #3808 module, re-verified and filed by lane A; not covered by #3808/#3809/#3811 as filed.

body:
## Problem

In `pkgs/id/src/hosted_binding.rs` (hosted account + ID binding ceremony, slice 1 of #3808), the handling of *dead* challenges (expired or consumed) contradicts the module's own §3.4 failure-semantics table in two places:

1. **An expired challenge is recorded as consumed on first presentation.** The module header (hosted_binding.rs:43-44) says "expired challenges die without state", and `CeremonyError::ChallengeExpired`'s own doc (hosted_binding.rs:415) says "State change: none; the challenge is dead." But the expiry branch of `submit_proof` (hosted_binding.rs:674-678) removes the challenge **and inserts its ID into `consumed_challenges`**. Observable consequence: presenting the same expired challenge a second time returns `ChallengeReplay` ("already presented") instead of `ChallengeExpired` — even though expiry was specified as creating no state. It also makes the consumed set retain IDs whose only sin was expiring.

2. **`create_pairing_code`'s `ChallengeReplay` branch is unreachable.** Its doc comment (hosted_binding.rs:807-812) promises `ChallengeReplay` for a dead (consumed) challenge. But the function first looks the challenge up in `self.challenges` and returns `UnknownChallenge` if absent (hosted_binding.rs:818-822), and only *then* checks `consumed_challenges` (hosted_binding.rs:823-825). Consumed challenges are always removed from `self.challenges` (`consume()`, hosted_binding.rs:769-772; the expiry branch above), so a consumed ID can never reach the replay check — the branch is dead code, and callers get `UnknownChallenge` for a challenge that was in fact consumed.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Re-verified by new-issue-creator lane A at origin/main 2194bd4c2 (laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-laneA-hosted`, since removed; temporary integration test `pkgs/id/tests/probe_hosted_a.rs`, log `/tmp/probe-laneA-hosted.log` on the laptop):

- Expired challenge presented twice: first `Err(ChallengeExpired)`, second `Err(ChallengeReplay)` — expiry did create state (the consumed entry), contradicting the "state change: none" specification.
- Challenge consumed by a bad-signature submit (`Err(BadSignature)`), then `create_pairing_code` for it: `Err(UnknownChallenge)` — never the documented `ChallengeReplay`.
- Control: `create_pairing_code` for a live challenge succeeds.

Code reading at the same commit confirms the mechanism for both: expiry inserts into `consumed_challenges` (hosted_binding.rs:676); `create_pairing_code` checks the live map (hosted_binding.rs:820) before the consumed set (hosted_binding.rs:824), and `consume()` (hosted_binding.rs:769-772) always removes from the live map first. Originally found by lane B (creator-b) at 550b611eb; its filing was blocked by a GitHub secondary rate limit, so lane A re-verified and filed it.

## Why it matters

This module is the security ceremony that binds a Google identity to an Iroh root key. Its error taxonomy is the contract the §3.4 table specifies for clients and for the follow-up slices (rebind #3809, Worker API #3811): "expired" and "replayed" drive different client behaviour (plain retry vs. replay handling/logging). Today the two are conflated for expired challenges, one documented error can never be returned, and the consumed-ID set grows with expired IDs it was not specified to hold. The divergence is in brand-new code (landed today in #3808), so fixing the contract now is cheap; after slice 2/3 build on it, it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Presenting an expired challenge repeatedly yields the §3.4-specified result for expired challenges on every presentation (per the table, expiry records no consumed state), OR the §3.4 docs/header/`ChallengeExpired` doc are amended in the same change to specify the recorded-as-consumed behaviour — code and docs agree either way, with the chosen semantics stated on the issue/PR.
- [ ] `create_pairing_code` for a consumed challenge returns the error its documentation promises (`ChallengeReplay`), i.e. the consumed check is reachable — regression test covers consumed, expired, unknown, and live challenges.
- [ ] Regression tests in `hosted_binding.rs`: expired challenge presented twice; pairing-code creation against a challenge consumed by a failed submit.
- [ ] Existing hosted_binding tests still pass (`cargo test -p id --lib hosted_binding`).

Found by new-issue-creator lane B (creator-b) during a scan of the newly landed #3808 module, re-verified and filed by lane A; not covered by #3808/#3809/#3811 as filed.

title: OpenCode picker stuck Unavailable: provider probe races model activation (fires once at serve spawn, never retries)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

body:
### What happened

After the opencode server lifecycle change (T3 now spawns its own managed `opencode serve` on demand, on a random port, instead of reusing a long-lived server on :4096), the OpenCode provider card in the app shows:

```
OpenCode 2 is running, but it did not list any models yet.
```

and every opencode model in the picker shows **Unavailable**. The state never recovers on its own.

### Root cause (verified with live debugging on a 3-box fleet)

1. T3 spawns the managed serve and probes the model list **once, immediately after the port binds** (probe timestamp == spawn timestamp in `userdata/caches/opencode.json`).
2. opencode 2.2.5 (official `@opencode/cli`, published 2026-10-30) needs **~60s** from port-bind until `/api/model` starts answering. During that window it returns:
   ```json
   {"_tag":"ServiceUnavailableError","message":"Location plugins did not finish activating","service":"plugin"}
   ```
3. The spawn-time probe always lands inside that window, so T3 caches `status: "warning", models: []` and **never re-probes** (`checkedAt` stays frozen; no retry, no probe on app-open, no probe on later sessions).
4. Sessions themselves work fine (turns complete normally on opencode models) - only the cached provider state is poisoned, so the picker stays Unavailable indefinitely.

Ruled out as causes (A/B tested): custom user plugins (removed - same 503), MCP servers (disabled - same 503), minimal single-provider config (same 503), serve cwd (same 503). The ~60s activation is intrinsic to opencode 2.2.5 cold starts (built-in location plugin activation: models.dev catalog fetch + provider checks). The same warning is also tracked from the other direction in #1241 / opencode#560, but on the current official build the provider resource still does not surface models until activation completes.

### Why it started now

Before the lifecycle change, the opencode serve was long-lived (spawned once, survived T3 restarts), so T3's probe always hit a warm process and cached `ready`. Once the serve became per-spawn, every spawn probe races the ~60s activation and loses.

### Suggested fix (either/both)

- T3: retry the provider probe with backoff (e.g. 5s intervals for 90s) before caching a negative result, and/or re-probe when the app requests the provider card / model picker instead of serving the stale cache forever.
- opencode: serve the config-resolved catalog from `/api/model` immediately (the data is available - `/api/config` already carries it) and let location plugins activate asynchronously, per the spirit of opencode#560.

### Environment

- t3 `0.1.7-nightly.20261103.4119` (reproducible since the lifecycle change, ~`0.1.7-nightly.20261103.4106`)
- opencode `@opencode/cli` 2.2.5 (official npm)
- Linux x64, fleet of 3 remote environments - 100% reproducible on every T3 restart + fresh opencode session

### Workaround we use today

After each upgrade, run one throwaway opencode-model session to force the serve to spawn (sessions work fine even while the picker shows Unavailable). The picker itself only heals if the probe is retried, so upstream retry is the real fix.

body:
## Problem

On the laptop's primary clone (`~/git/code`) there is a **local branch literally named `origin/main`** in addition to the normal remote-tracking ref `refs/remotes/origin/main`. Git then treats the name `origin/main` as ambiguous and `git rev-parse origin/main` resolves to the **local branch** (stale) rather than the remote-tracking ref (current).

Observed 2026-11-03 by the OpenChamber scheduled lane while triaging:

```
$ git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main
74064cbb31f0778a820690448bef51cb42bb23d3  refs/heads/main

$ git for-each-ref --format='%(refname) %(objectname:short)' | grep 'origin/main'
refs/heads/origin/main       1e3763faf   <-- stray local branch
refs/remotes/origin/main     74064cbb3   <-- real remote-tracking ref

$ git rev-parse origin/main
warning: refname 'origin/main' is ambiguous.
1e3763faf            <-- the stale local branch wins
```

Every `git log origin/main`, `git show origin/main:<path>`, `git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/main` and `git merge origin/main` in that clone silently used a main snapshot that was ~an hour stale. It also printed the lifecycle warning but scripts and one-liners ignore stderr.

## Why it matters

- Wrong "already landed / not landed" verdicts: a commit merged to main after the stale snapshot is reported as *not an ancestor*, which is exactly the check workers use when closing preserved-branch issues and deciding whether a fix has shipped.
- Wrong bases: `git merge origin/main` merges the stale ref, so a PR can appear up to date while missing the newest main; in this run merging the real ref was required to pick up PR #4842's fix before the aggregator suite went green.
- Silent: the only signal is the `refname ... is ambiguous` warning on stderr.

## Evidence from this run

While shepherding PR #4786 (aggregator quiet-hours fix), the full aggregator suite failed 2 tests that were already fixed on real main by PR #4842. Root cause was the shadowed ref — after merging `refs/remotes/origin/main` (74064cbb3) explicitly, the suite was 1296 pass / 0 fail.

## Suggested fix

1. Delete the stray local branch in the primary clone: `git -C ~/git/code branch -D origin/main` (it shadows a remote-tracking ref and cannot be normal working state).
2. Audit `~/git/fleet/*` and the other primaries (`opencode`, `openchamber-fork`, `dezren39-nix`) for the same pattern.
3. Optional hardening: a short preflight in the queue worker runbook — `git for-each-ref refs/heads/origin/main` must be empty, and workers should prefer `refs/remotes/origin/main` or `git rev-parse --verify refs/remotes/origin/main`.

Not fixed here: this worker's run was scoped to queue tasks and deleting a branch in the shared primary clone is a host-ops action, not a task-scoped edit.

Found by: OpenChamber scheduled lane 8ac61616-3815-4e7b-b33d-840a3829154a (queue task 7427), 2026-11-03.

title: id(chat): ChatMessage::check accepts duplicate links — every sibling list check refuses repeats

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/chat.rs:170-195` — `ChatMessage::check` is the validation gate for
chat messages ("Checks the rules every message meets. The builder and the
decoder both apply them"). It refuses empty/oversize/unsanitized text
(`chat.rs:171-184`), more than `MAX_LINKS` (16) links (`chat.rs:185-190`), and
a failing per-link check (`chat.rs:191-193`) — but it never checks whether the
same link appears twice.

Verified this run with a laptop probe at origin/main `1e3763faf`
(worktree `probe-2026-11-03-laneB-scan17`, logs `/tmp/probe-scan17.log` and
`/tmp/probe-scan17b.log` on the laptop, both read back from disk):

- `ChatMessage::new("hello", vec![link.clone(), link.clone()])` → `Ok` with 2 links (identical `kind`/`hash`/`author`/`hint`)
- The same message constructed directly (the decoder path) → `check()` returns `Ok(())`
- Control: two distinct links → `Ok` (as expected)

Sibling list checks in the same validation family all refuse repeats:

- `chain.rs` `ChainExt::validate`: a hash repeated in `after` → `DuplicateAfter`
- `notes.rs:128ff` `check_note_op`: a revision parent named twice → refused
- `session_checkpoint.rs:240ff`: a participant named twice → refused
- `tag_claims.rs` `check_op`: a clear naming a claim twice → refused (fix for #4765)
- `boards.rs` `validate_shape`: duplicate attachment / source-frontier / theme-asset references → refused
- `chat_presence.rs`: heartbeat channels/typing are deduplicated and bounded on store

## Why it matters

A `chat.message.v1` message can carry the same object reference up to 16
times, wasting most of its bounded link budget on copies of one reference and
leaving downstream consumers (retrieval via `ChatLink::holders`, link
rendering, future chat wiring in the #3799/#3795 line) to decide whether
repeats mean anything. Every other checked list in this codebase made the
opposite call — repeats are a malformed operation, refused at the gate — so a
conforming sender never emits them, and accepting them only preserves a
dialect no other module speaks.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ChatMessage::check` refuses a message whose `links` contain the same link
  twice (full `ChatLink` equality: kind, hash, author, hint), with a
  `ChatError` that names the duplication.
- `ChatMessage::new` refuses the same input through `check` (no separate
  builder-only path).
- The fixer decides and documents whether two links that agree on
  (kind, hash, author) but differ in `hint` are also duplicates; either
  decision is acceptable if it is stated in the code/tests.
- Regression tests in `pkgs/id/src/chat.rs` cover: identical duplicate
  refused, distinct links accepted, and the at-cap (16 distinct) case still
  accepted.
- `cargo test -p id --lib chat` passes.

title: id(directory): a friend_remove artifact voids any pair's request IDs — receive/apply never binds requests to the (a, b) pair

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Summary

A `friend_remove` artifact's `requests` list is never bound to the pair it names. `SignedArtifact::parsed()` (artifact.rs:338-350, after #3146) checks the list's count (≤ `MAX_FRIEND_REMOVE_REQUESTS` = 3) and that each entry is a well-formed request ID — but not that any entry is a request of the `(a, b)` pair. `Directory::receive_artifact` (directory.rs:1379-1395) then applies the removal whenever `are_friends(a, b) || !removal.requests.is_empty()`, and `Directory::apply`'s `FriendRemoved` arm (directory.rs:1705-1712) extends the **global** `removed_requests` void set with every named ID. So either party to any pair can permanently void up to 3 arbitrary request IDs on a receiving server — including the formed-by or pending request ID of a completely different pair — and a removal for a pair that was never friends applies purely because its list is non-empty.

Every legitimate producer names only pair-bound IDs: `friendship_requests` (directory.rs:1717-1731) returns exactly {the pair's formed-by request, `pending_id(a, b)`, `pending_id(b, a)`}. And `Directory::open`'s re-application of stored removals (directory.rs:~475) uses a stricter guard — it applies one only when the pair `are_friends` **and** the formed-by ID is in `requests`. The live receive path enforces neither condition.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe)

Probe: temporary unit test in `pkgs/id/src/directory.rs` tests, laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-03-laneB-scan16` at origin/main `1e3763faf` (worktree removed after; log `/tmp/probe-scan16.log` on the laptop):

- Ann↔Bo become friends across home/away (envelope flow, as in `friends_across_servers`).
- Cy (on home) sends Di (on away) a friend request; the envelope is **not yet delivered** to away.
- Ann's legitimate `remove_friend` artifact is applied on away (friendship ends).
- Ann signs a second `friend_remove` (seq 2, chained) for the same `(ann, bo)` pair whose `requests` lists **Cy→Di's request ID** — a pair Ann and Bo have no part in.
- Result, from the probe log:
  - `PROBE cross stored: New` — `away.receive_artifact(&cross)` returned `Ok(Stored::New)` and applied the effect;
  - `PROBE away removed_requests contains cy/di id: true`;
  - `PROBE cy->di request after cross removal: Err(request c678e8c39430f578a89bda612f21179b was voided by a friend removal)` — when the genuine Cy→Di request envelope is finally delivered, away refuses it with the void-guard `Conflict` at directory.rs:1677, permanently: `removed_requests` is journaled and replayed on every open.

## Why it matters

The void set is the mechanism that keeps a removed friendship's request from being resurrected by late delivery (see the existing test `a_removal_ends_the_friendship_on_both_servers_and_voids_a_request_it_never_delivered`). Because it is global and the receive path never binds the IDs to the pair, that mechanism can be aimed at other pairs: any account that learns a request ID (the ID travels with the envelope to both home servers and anyone relaying it) can kill that request on a server by naming it in an unrelated removal — the requester and recipient never removed anything, and the block is permanent and silent (the refusal reads as if the pair themselves had removed it). It also breaks the module's own invariant that a stored known-kind artifact is one whose body obeys the same rules its producers obey: producers can only name the pair's own 3 IDs, and `open()`'s replay guard already encodes exactly that stricter rule.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `friend_remove` received via `Directory::receive_artifact` has no directory effect for request IDs that are not the named pair's own: each named ID must be the pair's formed-by request or a pending request in either direction on the receiving server (the `friendship_requests` set), matching the guard `Directory::open` already applies on replay. IDs outside that set are ignored for the void set, or the artifact's effect is refused — one stated rule, tested either way.
- [ ] A removal for a pair that is not friends and has no pending/formed request between them on the receiving server is stored alone (no effect), like the no-requests case the `receive_artifact` comment already describes.
- [ ] Regression test mirroring the probe: Ann's second removal naming Cy→Di's request ID does not void it, and the genuine Cy→Di request delivered afterwards applies; the existing removal tests (legitimate void of a never-delivered request, concurrent removals by both sides, #3146 count/format refusals) still pass.
- [ ] No change to the wire format, `FriendRemove`'s fields, or the semantics of legitimate removals.

Distinct from: #3146 (closed — count/format validation of `requests` in `parsed()`; it did not bind the IDs to the pair), #3187 / #4459 (other artifact kinds' receipt).

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

`pm-stack/ready-for-agent/install.sh`: if `install.sh clone` upgrades the pinned npm package but the subsequent Git clone/fetch fails, the script exits (`set -e`) after npm has already replaced the on-disk binary, while the old process keeps serving. On the next invocation, both on-disk comparisons match — the binary at `~/.local/bin/ready-for-agent` reports the pinned version and the unit is unchanged — so the script takes the no-restart path and reports the pinned version as running, even though the still-running old process serves requests. The version checks read the on-disk binary (`ready-for-agent --version` spawns a fresh process from the new binary), never the serving process, and there is no pending-restart marker, so the failed deployment is silently forgotten.

- Raised by: Codex (P2), 2026-11-02T05:12:14Z, on PR #4190 (fix(pm-stack): restart ready-for-agent only on change)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4190#discussion_r4439108345 — "Preserve pending restarts across failed installation attempts" (`pm-stack/ready-for-agent/install.sh:107` in the PR diff)
- Essence: "Preserve a pending-restart marker until deployment completes, or otherwise verify that the running process corresponds to the installed package before taking the no-op path."

## No-response evidence

- The thread has the single Codex comment and no replies; GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #4190 (checked this run): the thread is unresolved.
- PR #4190 had a single commit (`95addedd4`, 2026-11-02T05:09:06Z, before the comment) and merged 2026-11-02T15:36:34Z (merge commit `58857615c`) with no fix commit after the comment.
- Held under the open-PR 24h grace rule by the pr-comment-review run of 2026-11-02 03:54 CST; grace expired 2026-11-03T05:12:14Z and the PR has since merged unaddressed, so it is filed now.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-03 via `gh api` raw read)

`pm-stack/ready-for-agent/install.sh` on main:

- Line 53–58: `package_changed` is derived solely from the on-disk binary's `--version` vs `PINNED_VERSION`.
- Lines 64–77: the `clone` step runs after the npm install; a Git failure exits the script before any restart.
- Lines 101–108: when neither package nor unit changed, the script prints "no package or unit changes detected; leaving ready-for-agent.service running" (`service_action=unchanged`) — no check that the running process corresponds to the installed package, and no pending-restart state anywhere in the script.
- Lines 135–150: the "unchanged" verification path marks the process verified unconditionally and again reads the version from the on-disk binary, then reports `ready-for-agent@<pinned> is already running (no restart)`.

Dedupe: `gh issue list --state all` searches (ready-for-agent install pending restart / install.sh restart / 4190) found no issue tracking this residual failure mode. Related but distinct: issue #2513 (closed — install.sh never restarted at all; PR #4190 was its fix, and this finding is a hole in that fix), issue #1150 / #1332 (aggregator install.sh, a different script).

## Acceptance criteria

- A deployment that changes the installed package but fails before the restart completes is not forgotten: a later `install.sh` run restarts the service (e.g. a pending-restart marker written when the package changes and cleared only after a verified restart), or the no-op path verifies the running process actually corresponds to the installed package before reporting success.
- A regression case in the stubbed harness covers the sequence: npm succeeds, Git clone/fetch fails, retry succeeds without a service PID change must no longer be reported as the pinned version running.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue explaining why this failure sequence is accepted, stated explicitly.

Found by the pr-comment-review job from an unaddressed PR review comment.

body:
## Purpose

Write the remaining first seven content items in the mcpx level-2 manual: the "more normal set of docs" a new user can rely on after installation. This is the replacement for **part 2 only** of #1848, whose page-map part 1 merged as PR #2433. Per the 2026-11-03 ruling on tracker #1898, **do not reopen #1848**; this issue owns the remaining content.

Parent/order tracker: #1898. Map and fixed anchors: [`pkgs/mcpx/docs/level-2-page-map.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/level-2-page-map.md), items 53–59.

## Scope

Write all seven mapped sections, verifying factual claims against current `pkgs/mcpx` main at implementation time:

1. `configuration#common-config` — config sources, search/discovery and load passes, precedence, and how to inspect effective values.
2. `configuration#server-config` — server blocks, profiles/aliases, sharing and scope; distinguish config key `mcpServers` from CLI/API "servers".
3. `configuration#client-config` — client/call-scoped settings and what a host configures to use mcpx; explain their distinct meanings.
4. `configuration#env-vars` — setting variables versus host/harness/script context; use generated `docs/environment.md` / registry data rather than maintaining a competing variable list.
5. `modes#client-modes` — socket, remote URL, autostart/spawn, and inline modes, with where scripts run and profile/output controls.
6. `modes#transport-options` — upstream server transports versus downstream client transports; current HTTP/SSE/MCP behavior, listeners, and remote-access constraints.
7. `modes#server-modes` — mcpx as an MCP server, upstream server sharing/scope, and daemon process modes; make the three meanings explicit.

Use the sources and per-item notes in the page map. In particular, do not reintroduce the obsolete `mode` config key or `pooled` value; document `sharing`/`scope`, the actual config search path, and the current legacy-SSE behavior. Keep generated facts generated: do not hand-copy tables owned by the settings registry, environment generator, parity table, OpenAPI document, or generated-reference work (#1843).

## Acceptance

- The seven items have substantive, newcomer-readable content at the exact fixed anchors above; each explains practical choices and commands rather than only linking to the compendium.
- Existing source pages are reused where appropriate; update the level-2 page map's "Written by" references from closed #1848 to this issue, and keep compendium navigation/manifest consistent with the resulting pages.
- Verify links and generated/reference content against current main. Resolve the map's relevant open questions in the docs or record a precise follow-up; do not silently publish contradictory facts.
- Run the targeted documentation checks, including `go test ./internal/settings ./internal/defaults` from `pkgs/mcpx`, plus `git diff --check`; report any unrelated baseline failure separately.
- No code behavior changes or unrelated documentation areas are in scope.

## Context

- Tracker: #1898; level-2 map PR: #2433 (merged at `7d7851ddef77c96cfb1e6fda3c52b6c7342a9d79`).
- #1848 is closed and remains closed by explicit ruling; this is its replacement child for the seven content sections only.
- Adjacent documentation issues are distinct: #1851 owns the interface/CLI/MCP/binary/scripts/API items; #1855 and #1859 are closed.

title: mcpx: run ops.gen.ts codegen as part of treefmt (auto-format), like just-recipes.json

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

body:
Follow-up to #4807 (merged), which made the mcpx nix build regenerate plugin/opencode/mcpx/ops.gen.ts in preCheck so a build can never go red on a stale checked-in copy. That protects the BUILD. The TREE can still carry a stale copy for anyone consuming the plugin as raw source between regenerations (Drew's stale-type-hint principle, and Drew's suggestion 2026-11-03: "make code Gen part of the auto format").

Precedent in this repo: `just fix` already regenerates just-recipes.json as part of the format path — generated files refreshing alongside formatting is an established pattern here.

Proposal: register the ops regeneration as a treefmt formatter in treefmt.toml:
- command: a small wrapper that runs `go test ./internal/api -run TestPluginOpsAreGenerated -update` (the generator's home package, from the repo root, mirroring package.nix's preCheck exports if needed).
- include: the files whose change can alter the /v1 table the generator renders from (internal/api/**/*.go — refine to the table's actual inputs).
- effect: `just fmt` refreshes ops.gen.ts with everything else, and lefthook's treefmt --fail-on-change pre-commit check rejects a stale copy exactly the way it rejects unformatted code — no new mental model, no new habit.

The two mechanisms compose: treefmt keeps the tree fresh for raw-source consumers; the nix preCheck guarantees the build regardless of how the tree was produced. Go availability in the format environment is the same requirement class as the existing gofmt formatter.

body:
Per Drew (2026-11-03), refining the mcpx consolidation design: the standalone daemon mode is mcpx's own feature, so its Nix modules originate HERE, with mcpx — not in a consumer. Layering:
- code (this repo): the canonical module source beside pkgs/mcpx — a shared option set (services.mcpx) with platform implementations: systemd on Linux (NixOS + home-manager user units), launchd on darwin.
- developing-today/opencode: RE-EXPORTS these modules as its own flake outputs (imported from its mcpx-src input), alongside any modules of its own.
- developing-today/openchamber: passes both through, alongside its own modules.
- dezren39/nix consumes the whole stack through its single openchamber input (dezren39/nix#1384) and deletes its modules/mcpx copies.

This supersedes the original step-2 framing in developing-today/opencode#1502 (modules authored in the fork). Package default in the modules: the mcpx build of whichever flake layer exposes them (ultimately this repo's pkgs/mcpx/package.nix, which also absorbs the platform checkPhase adaptations — #4798).

body:
dezren39/nix's flake currently rewrites this package's checkPhase from downstream (guarded replaceStrings in its mcpx override): on Linux it adds '-p 1' (serial package tests so the timing-sensitive retention/reopen test is not starved), on darwin it adds a -skip list of the 20 Linux-only takeover/handoff tests (#418). The coupling is fragile by design — the package's own comment documents that the exact 'go test -timeout 30m $pkgs' line is load-bearing downstream, and nix carries a flake check (mcpx-darwin-skip) whose only job is policing the coupling.

Per Drew (2026-11-03): the adaptations belong in the package itself, as platform conditionals. This issue is step 1 of a three-repo simplification:
1. (this repo) package.nix constructs its checkPhase with the platform flags directly; the downstream-coupling comment is replaced.
2. (developing-today/opencode) expose the mcpx daemon modules (NixOS / home-manager / darwin) as flake outputs, package defaulting to the fork's mcpx build.
3. (dezren39/nix) drop the opencode + mcpx-src inputs (consume everything through the openchamber input), drop the private mcpx build, the checkPhase rewrites, the mcpx-darwin-skip check, the opencode mcpx override, and modules/mcpx — services.mcpx comes from the fork's module, so the daemon and the mcpx bundled in opencode are one build by construction.

title: id(web): web_interface_from_app_toml still accepts route/socket shapes that panic axum — invalid capture syntax and renamed-capture conflicts with host routes pass the #4779 checks

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`web_interface_from_app_toml` (pkgs/id/src/web/app_interface.rs:214) still accepts `route`/`socket` values that panic when the router is built — the #4779 fix covered the leading-slash check, exact host-route collisions (`HOST_RESERVED_ROUTES`, app_interface.rs:105-150), the `/api/world/*` prefix, and route==socket, but it never validates the path's axum route syntax or its pattern-level conflicts with host routes.

Two verified classes survive the parser and panic in `create_router_inner` / `world_routes_at`:

1. **Syntactically invalid axum paths** — unbalanced or empty captures: `/foo/{bar`, `/foo/{}`, `/foo/{*}`, and the legacy colon segment `/:`.
2. **Pattern conflicts with host routes that are not exact duplicates** — `/edit/{*other}` (same shape as the host's `/edit/{*name}` under a different wildcard name) and `/hash/{other}` (same shape as `/hash/{hash}` under a different capture name). The reserved check is exact-string only, so neither matches it.

The panic sites are the registrations the parser is supposed to make safe: `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:322` (`.route(&world_route, get(world_page_handler))`, after every host route has already been registered) and `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:60` (`world_routes_at(socket)` registers the socket the same way, and the socket side of `web_interface_from_app_toml` has exactly the same missing syntax/conflict check).

## Evidence (verified this run; corrected — see the correction comment)

Laptop probe (worktree at origin/main 2897a2130, temporary unit test in `app_interface.rs` tests, `web/dist` placeholder copied from the primary clone, worktree removed after; log `/tmp/probe-scan12c.log` on the laptop, read back independently after the run): for each candidate, `web_interface_from_app_toml` was called, then the candidate was registered on an axum `Router` after the host routes `/`, `/files`, `/edit/{*name}`, `/hash/{hash}`, `/api/files` — the same registration `create_router_inner` performs.

```text
PROBE route="/foo/{bar"       parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/foo/{}"          parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/foo/{*}"         parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/edit/{*other}"   parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/hash/{other}"    parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/:"               parsed_ok=true axum_panics=true
PROBE route="/arena"           parsed_ok=true axum_panics=false   (control)
PROBE route="/{*path}"         parsed_ok=true axum_panics=false   (NOT claimed)
PROBE route="/foo/{bar}/{bar}" parsed_ok=true axum_panics=false   (NOT claimed)
PROBE route="/api/{name}"      parsed_ok=true axum_panics=false   (not claimed)
PROBE route="/foo//bar"        parsed_ok=true axum_panics=false   (not claimed)
```

The mimicked router is a subset of the real host table, so the real `create_router_inner` (which registers ~35 host routes before the app route) can only panic on a superset of these conflicts.

## Why it matters

#4779's stated contract is that this parser rejects every binding that "would panic router construction" instead of aborting startup (its doc comment at app_interface.rs:205-213 says exactly that). An app author who writes a capture in their page route — a natural thing to try for a packaged app — or who mistypes a brace still crashes `id serve` at router construction with an axum panic, with no parse error naming the offending field. The reserved-list approach also remains a drift hazard for pattern conflicts: any future host route with a capture creates a new conflicting shape the exact-match list cannot see.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `web_interface_from_app_toml` rejects, with a named `WebInterfaceError` variant, any `route` or `socket` that is not valid axum path syntax: unbalanced braces, empty capture/wildcard names, and legacy `:`-prefixed segments.
- [ ] It also rejects a `route`/`socket` whose pattern conflicts with a host-registered pattern under a different capture/wildcard name (at minimum the `/edit/{*name}`, `/view/{*name}`, `/hash/{hash}`, `/blob/{hash}`, `/assets/{*path}`, `/ws/collab/{doc_id}` shapes), not only exact string duplicates of host routes.
- [ ] Preferably the check is structural (parse the candidate's segments/captures and compare shapes against the host table) rather than a longer exact-string list, so future host capture routes cannot drift past it; if a list is kept, a test ties it to the routes registered in `create_router_inner`/`world_http_routes`.
- [ ] Regression tests beside the existing #4779 tests in `app_interface.rs` cover the six panicking shapes above for `route`, and at least the invalid-syntax shapes for `socket`; the valid control `/arena` + `/ws/arena` still parses.
- [ ] `cargo test --lib --features web app_interface` passes (laptop or CI).

## Dedup

Searched open and closed issues 2026-11-03 for `web_interface`, route panic, axum route syntax, capture/wildcard conflicts: the only covering item is #4779 (closed, fixed on main) — this issue is its residual gap: #4779's fix checks leading slash, exact reserved strings, `/api/world/*` prefix, and route==socket only, and its tests do not cover capture syntax or renamed-capture conflicts. Distinct from #4060 (parse_app_manifest's separate route/socket criteria).

title: id(world-doctor): check_profile misses total_memory_bytes — a profile validate() refuses (Some(0)) reports 'bounds are valid'

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`id world doctor --profile <file>` reports `ok profile — execution profile bounds are valid` for a profile that every other path refuses: one with `total_memory_bytes: 0`.

`check_profile` (`pkgs/id/src/world_doctor.rs:294-335`) hand-duplicates the bound checks from `WorldExecutionProfile::validate()` — wasm_fuel, wasm_memory_bytes, wasm_message_bytes, native_memory_bytes, native_cpu_seconds, native_call_deadline_ms — but never checks `total_memory_bytes`. That field was added later (#557 Phase 1), and the doctor's copy was not updated.

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main 496d9f346)

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_limits.rs:332-360`: `WorldExecutionProfile::validate()` ends with `ensure!(self.total_memory_bytes != Some(0), "world total memory budget must be nonzero")` (line 355-358). Its doc calls `validate()` "the single source of truth for the bound checks" — the doctor does not use it.
- `pkgs/id/src/world_doctor.rs`: `grep total_memory` returns no hits in the file; `check_profile` (line 294) enumerates the other six bounds only. Its own doc (line 292-293) promises "The execution profile's requested bounds are nonzero and above their minimums, so `resolve` can accept them" — `resolve()` calls `validate()` first (world_limits.rs:362-363), so that promise is false for this profile.
- The check is live from the CLI: `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:445-468` parses `--profile` JSON into a `WorldExecutionProfile` and passes it into `DoctorInputs`, so this is reachable by a user, not only in tests.
- Laptop probe (worktree at origin/main 496d9f346, temporary unit test in `world_doctor::tests`, removed after; log `/tmp/laneA-scan11-probe.log` on the laptop): a profile with only `total_memory_bytes: Some(0)` — `profile.validate()` errors as expected, but `check_profile` returned `Severity::Ok` with detail "execution profile bounds are valid" (probe assertion `Fail` failed: left `Ok`, right `Fail`).

## Why it matters

The doctor's whole job is to diagnose a broken world setup before a world fails to start. A zero total memory budget is exactly the class of misconfiguration it exists to catch, and it currently certifies it as valid — the operator then hits the refusal later in `resolve()`/apply with no doctor guidance. The hand-duplicated check list is also a standing drift hazard: the next bound added to `validate()` will silently drift the same way unless the doctor delegates to it (the manifest validator already learned this lesson in #3015 and now calls `profile.validate()`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `check_profile` reports `Severity::Fail` for a profile with `total_memory_bytes: Some(0)`, naming the bound in the detail.
- [ ] Preferably, `check_profile` derives its verdict from `WorldExecutionProfile::validate()` (the documented single source of truth) instead of a hand-maintained parallel list, so future bounds cannot drift again; if the parallel list is kept, a comment/test must tie it to `validate()`.

title: id(web): web_interface_from_app_toml accepts route/socket values that panic in create_router_for_app (no leading-slash or host-route collision check)

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator
