body:
## Problem

On the laptop, most user units resolve into `/nix/store` — they are home-manager modules in this flake (`nixos/home/*`, enabled from `nixos/hosts/default.nix`) and deploy with `nixos-rebuild switch`. A set of newer systems was instead installed as plain unit files in `~/.config/systemd/user/` by install scripts. They run fine, but:

- a machine rebuild / DR restore from the flake alone would not bring them back;
- unit changes bypass the flake's review flow — drift between "what the repo says runs" and "what runs" is invisible;
- there are two sources of truth for the laptop's service set.

Drew's standing rule (code#1723) is that all laptop services are made by this flake; the script-installed units are the remaining exceptions. Ordered folded in 2026-11-01 ("fix all now").

## Scope (verified live 2026-11-01: plain files in `~/.config/systemd/user/`, not store symlinks)

- `github-backup-drain` / `github-backup-fetch` / `github-backup-reconcile` (.service + .timer each)
- `worktree-reaper` (.service + .timer)
- `cloudflare-quota-export`, `meta-quota-export`, `dashboard-backup` (.service + .timer each)
- `oc-password-sync` (.service)

Not in scope: `rustdesk.service` (vendor unit), `git-maintenance@` (git's own), `oc-sumauto` (transient unit, no file exists).

## Plan

- One home-manager module per system under `nixos/home/`, enabled from `nixos/hosts/default.nix` next to the existing laptop modules, replicating the current units' semantics exactly (ExecStart, WorkingDirectory, timer schedules, timeouts, Nice). Executed scripts stay at their checkout paths, per the fleet-feed-collector precedent — only unit provenance changes.
- Equivalence is proven before activation: build the `amd` configuration and diff the generated units against the installed files field-by-field; any intentional difference is called out in the PR.
- Activation is careful and reversible: the plain unit files are first moved (not deleted) to `~/.local/state/flake-fold-backup-2026-11-01/` on the laptop, then the established switch path runs; each migrated unit is verified (resolves into `/nix/store`, timer armed, one functional run per system). Rollback = restore the plain files (+ previous generation) if any check fails.

## Dependency

`worktree-reaper`'s ExecStart currently points at the bootstrap worktree `~/git/code-wt-reaper` (PR #3698). The fold points it at the canonical primary path `~/git/code/infra/worktree-reaper/...` and retires the bootstrap install per that PR's README — so this lands after #3698 merges.

## Acceptance criteria
- Every unit listed in Scope (github-backup drain/fetch/reconcile, worktree-reaper, cloudflare-quota-export, meta-quota-export, dashboard-backup, oc-password-sync) is defined by a home-manager module in this flake under `nixos/home/`, enabled from `nixos/hosts/default.nix`.
- The generated units are diffed against the currently installed files before activation and match on ExecStart, WorkingDirectory, timer schedules, timeouts, and Nice (or every difference is named and justified on this issue).
- After a rebuild, the script-installed plain files in `~/.config/systemd/user/` are removed or superseded so the flake is the single source of truth, and the services still run.
- Out of scope units (`rustdesk.service`, `git-maintenance@`) are untouched.

body:
# aggregator(registry): `limit`/`offset` are prefix-parsed with `parseInt` while `window` in the same function is strict — `limit=1e2` returns 1 record, `offset=1e3` starts at 1, `limit=10junk` is honoured as 10

## Problem

`parseRegistryQuery` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/registry-view.ts:80`) parses its three numeric query parameters two different ways:

- `window` is strict: it is accepted only when it matches `/^\d+$/` (registry-view.ts:84), otherwise the default (7 days) applies — `window=1e2` and `window=10junk` both fall back to 7.
- `limit` and `offset` go through `parsePositiveInt` (registry-view.ts:69-73), which is `Number.parseInt(raw, 10)` — a **prefix** parse that stops at the first non-digit and reports success:

```ts
function parsePositiveInt(raw: string | null, fallback: number): number {
  if (raw === null) return fallback;
  const n = Number.parseInt(raw, 10);
  return Number.isFinite(n) && n >= 0 ? n : fallback;
}
```

So a malformed limit/offset is neither honoured as written nor rejected to the fallback — it is silently reinterpreted as a different number:

- `limit=1e2` → limit **1** (not 100, and not the fallback 100 either)
- `limit=10junk` → limit **10**
- `limit=5.9` → limit **5**
- `offset=1e3` → offset **1** (a shared/bookmarked deep page starts at the second record)
- `offset=5.9` → offset **5**, `offset=10junk` → offset **10**
- `limit=0x10` → 0 → then the `limitRaw || REGISTRY_DEFAULT_LIMIT` step turns it into **100**, a third outcome for a third spelling of "not a plain decimal"

Both call sites are live routes: `src/server.ts:724` and `:741` feed `parseRegistryQuery(url.searchParams)` into `queryRegistry` for the HTML and JSON registry views, so a hand-edited or shared URL paginates differently from what it says, with no hint.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `85537203`)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/registry-view.ts` sha256 `45c713adaa456aef04820023ff14040fb97dea020ead4fb335e8a69b29e20522`, identical in the sandbox and laptop clones.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-registry/probe.ts` (bun, importing the real `parseRegistryQuery` from the laptop clone; output read back from `probe-run.log`):

| Query | Result |
|---|---|
| *(empty)* (control) | windowDays=7, limit=100, offset=0 |
| `limit=25` (control) | limit=25 |
| `limit=1e2` | limit=**1** |
| `limit=10junk` | limit=**10** |
| `limit=0x10` | limit=**100** (via the 0 → default step) |
| `limit=5.9` | limit=**5** |
| `offset=1e3` | offset=**1** |
| `offset=5.9` | offset=**5** |
| `offset=10junk` | offset=**10** |
| `window=1e2` / `window=10junk` (strict control) | windowDays=7 (fallback) |

- Existing tests (`test/registry-view.test.ts`, `parseRegistryQuery` describe) pin only plain decimals, `limit=9999` clamping and `limit=0` → default; no non-decimal spelling is covered.

## Why it matters

The registry view is paginated by URL: the app's own `registryQueryString` round-trips canonical values, but any URL a person edits, shortens, or shares with a scientific/float/junk-suffixed limit or offset silently shows a different page than the URL states — `limit=1e2` is the natural way to write 100 and returns a single record. The inconsistency is inside one function: the `window` parameter already demonstrates the house contract (strict decimal or fallback), and `limit`/`offset` quietly break it.

Distinct from #2971 (pm-dispatch's `parseLimit`, a different service and function — the same prefix-parse shape, never fixed here) and from the charges/quota numeric extractors. Creator dedupe 2026-11-01 searched open+closed for registry-view / parsePositiveInt / parseRegistryQuery: no covering issue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `limit` and `offset` accept only the same strict decimal grammar `window` uses (`/^\d+$/` or an equivalent whole-string parse); any other spelling (`1e2`, `5.9`, `10junk`, `0x10`, `+5`, leading/trailing spaces) falls back to the parameter's default (limit 100, offset 0) instead of a prefix value.
- [ ] `limit=1e2` yields the default limit (or 100 as written — triage pins one; it must not yield 1) and `offset=1e3` yields offset 0 (or 1000), never 1.
- [ ] Plain behaviour is unchanged: `limit=25` → 25, clamping to 1..500, `limit=0` → default, negative values → fallback, absent parameters → defaults.
- [ ] Tests in `test/registry-view.test.ts` pin the non-decimal spellings above for both parameters alongside the existing window cases; existing registry tests pass.

body:
# id(world): `sanitize_display_name` takes its 48 characters before trimming — leading spaces spend the budget, so a padded name is truncated to its first letters or refused as empty

## Problem

`sanitize_display_name` (`pkgs/id/src/world/util.rs:69-76`) builds a participant's display name in this order: filter control characters → `take(48)` → `collect` → `trim()`. The 48-character budget is measured **before** the trim, so leading whitespace that the trim is about to delete consumes the budget first:

- A name of 48 spaces followed by `Bob` sanitizes to `""` — and the join path (`pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs:877-880`) then refuses the join with "participant display name must not be empty", even though the name has real content.
- 47 spaces + `Bob` sanitizes to `"B"`; 46 spaces + `Bob` to `"Bo"` — the participant joins under a silently truncated name.
- A single leading space in front of an exactly-48-character name drops the name's last character (47 survive).

The ordering is also internally inconsistent: control characters (including tab) are filtered **before** `take(48)`, so 50 control characters or 60 tabs in front of `Bob` cost no budget at all and `Bob` survives whole — only whitespace that survives the filter but is later trimmed is charged against the budget.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `a9318ea8`)

- `pkgs/id/src/world/util.rs:69-76`: `.filter(|ch| !ch.is_control()).take(48).collect::<String>().trim()` — take precedes trim.
- Only production caller: `pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs:877` (`let display_name = sanitize_display_name(display_name);`), immediately followed at `:878-881` by the non-empty refusal that the padded-name case trips.
- Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-dispname/` (verbatim copy of the function; laptop clone at the same HEAD `a9318ea8`, `world/util.rs` sha256 `6c6cab0187e41519eb4fd8b55633b905f33006073e27f42743a024400d2bfb39` on both clones; output read back from `probe-run.log` in a second call):

| input | output |
|---|---|
| `Bob` (control) | `"Bob"` |
| `  Bob  ` (control) | `"Bob"` |
| 48 spaces + `Bob` | `""` (empty — join refused) |
| 47 spaces + `Bob` | `"B"` |
| 46 spaces + `Bob` | `"Bo"` |
| 1 space + 48-char name | 47 chars (last char dropped) |
| 50 × U+0007 + `Bob` (control) | `"Bob"` |
| 60 tabs + `Bob` (control) | `"Bob"` |

## Why it matters

Display names arrive from join/delegate callers that do not pre-trim (the sanitizer is the single choke point, and its own contract is "filter, bound, trim"). A user whose client pads a name — or whose name legitimately starts with spaces that will be trimmed anyway — is either refused a join for an "empty" name that is not empty, or appears in the world under a one- or two-letter truncation of their name with no error anywhere. The fix is a reorder, but the current order also means the documented 48-character limit is not the limit on the name that is actually stored: it is a limit on the untrimmed string.

Distinct from #2112 (same function, different defect: category-Cf characters pass the filter — its acceptance criteria cover Cf removal and Cf-only names, not the take/trim order or whitespace padding). No other open or closed issue covers this: creator dedupe 2026-11-01 searched open+closed for the sanitizer, the 48-char budget, and trim/take ordering; the only hit was #2112.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `sanitize_display_name` applies the 48-character budget to the trimmed name: leading/trailing whitespace is removed before (or otherwise not charged against) the budget — e.g. trim first, then filter, then take, with a final trim if the filter can expose new edges.
- [ ] 48 spaces + `Bob` sanitizes to `"Bob"` (and the join at `world/core.rs` accepts it); 47/46 spaces + `Bob` also yield `"Bob"`, not `"B"`/`"Bo"`.
- [ ] A leading space + an exactly-48-character name yields all 48 characters; a name whose trimmed form exceeds 48 characters is still truncated to 48.
- [ ] Existing behaviour is preserved: control characters are stripped and do not consume the budget, an all-whitespace name still sanitizes to empty (join refusal still fires for genuinely empty names), and interior whitespace is untouched.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the padded cases above (48/47/46 spaces, space + 48-char name, controls control case); existing world tests pass.

body:
## Summary

The alert throat (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/alerts.ts` + `push.ts`, landed 2026-11-01 in #3676 under the #1254 push design) is the one PM-stack system whose entire value is that Drew can believe it — and within hours of landing, three filings, one per trust boundary, showed its claims about itself going unchecked:

- **#3685** — `runAlertTick` marked incidents delivered (and escalated) even when every push send failed: a transient VAPID/bws outage permanently swallowed critical incidents, never retried, with the ledger asserting delivery that never happened. **Landed during this design's audit** (PR #3690, merge `a3acf3b0`): both marks now gate on `sent > 0`, with an injectable `PushSender` seam and a warning on all-failed ticks. It is Rule 1's embodiment — cited here, not adopted as a phase (the #2787/#2789 precedent).
- **#3693** — `GET /api/push/subscriptions` returns every subscription's full store row — `endpoint`, `p256dh`, and the RFC 8291 `auth` secret — unauthenticated, while the /alerts page for the same data projects the keys away and no client uses the GET.
- **#3686** — `mergeQuiet` validates quiet times by shape (`/^\d{2}:\d{2}$/`) only, so `99:99` / `24:60` are stored and silently reinterpreted as a different suppression window, in the one parser whose established contract is reject-to-default.

Full design doc: `files/designs/code-aggregator-alert-throat-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## The contract (stated once, in the alerts.ts module header)

> The alert throat's records and responses tell the truth and keep its secrets. A state transition is recorded only when the event it names happened (delivered / escalated require at least one accepted send; `gone` is not a send). Subscription key material (`p256dh`, `auth`) never leaves the server: store rows are internal, and any HTTP surface projects — the page's projection is the only read shape. Subscription preferences are validated as values, not shapes, and an invalid value falls back per-field to the default — never stored, never reinterpreted.

## Recorded decisions

1. **The unused subscriptions GET is removed, not projected** (#3693 allows either). No in-repo client calls it (push-client.js POST/DELETE only; /alerts is server-rendered; the engine reads in-process), and even a projected GET would enumerate every subscription endpoint — the input the unauthenticated DELETE needs. A future consumer re-adds a read returning the page's projected shape; the projection rule is the standing requirement for that day.
2. **Fixes stay on their own side of the store seam.** `listSubscriptions()` has two consumers with opposite needs (engine: full rows, in-process; HTTP: no secrets, ever). #3693's fix removes the HTTP surface, never narrows the store read — projecting the store query would break `deliverToAll`.
3. **Quiet validation is per-field value validation at merge time** (hour 00–23, minute 00–59, else that field's default) — the parser's existing reject-to-default contract extended to digit-shaped input. Already-stored out-of-range rows are not silently rewritten; their disposition is a required output of Phase 3.

## Phased breakdown

- **Phase 1 — subscription secrets never leave the server (adopted: #3693).** Remove the GET handler on `/api/push/subscriptions`; engine reads unchanged; sentinel-row test pins that no subscriptions response contains `p256dh`/`auth`; /alerts rendering unchanged.
- **Phase 2 — quiet prefs validated as clock values (adopted: #3686).** `mergeQuiet` range validation + per-field fallback, tests per the origin's acceptance. Independent of Phase 1.
- **Phase 3 — closing audit + contract statement (new issue, gated on Phases 1–2).** Contract into the `alerts.ts` header; seam check (no HTTP route returns a store row verbatim); required dispositions recorded here with reasons: stored out-of-range quiet rows, the unauthenticated DELETE + ack/close posture (aggregator-wide stance), `mergeQuiet` tz acceptance (fails open on unknown zones), `mergeClasses` unbounded class keys; closing evidence incl. Rule 1 as-built (PR #3690) and a note to #3317/#3319 that quiet semantics and delivery state are now contractual.

Open questions stay in the design doc (an aggregator-wide auth model; digest-class state following Rule 1; delivery backoff/dead-letter on operational evidence; sends-ledger retention).

Related: #3676 (the throat build), #1254 (push design), #3317 / #3319 (consumers of quiet + delivery truth), #1260 (pm-stack SLOs — the layer above, not this contract). Not this design: #3681 (chargesAttention shape — #3068/#3161's module), the feed gates (#2576's family).

🤖 Design architect pass 32 (2026-11-01), audit at origin/main `a3acf3b0`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The design names the alert throat's truth contract: what 'delivered' (and each sibling claim) means, which evidence backs it, and what happens when that evidence is absent.
- Every phase of the design is filed as its own implementation issue (or explicitly marked no-action with rationale) and linked from this epic — the design does not sit without an implementation path (protocol §11).
- The already-landed #3685 fix is cited as Rule 1's embodiment, not re-adopted as a phase.

body:
## Problem

`GET /api/push/subscriptions` returns every push subscription's full database row — including the Web Push `auth` secret and `p256dh` key — to any caller who can reach the aggregator, with no authentication. No in-repo client uses this endpoint.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `0bb00794`)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:976` — the GET handler is `return json({ subscriptions: await store.listSubscriptions() })`. Unlike the incident intake (`POST /api/alerts`, gated by `alertsIntakeAuthorized`, server.ts:1000-1001), this route has no auth check.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/alerts.ts:265-267` — `listSubscriptions()` is `select * from alerts.push_subscriptions`, so the wire payload carries `endpoint`, `p256dh`, and `auth` verbatim for every subscriber.
- The `auth` value is the RFC 8291 push-encryption secret for that subscription; `p256dh` is its encryption public key. Together with the endpoint they are the complete per-subscription key material the server itself uses in `deliverToAll` (alerts.ts:447-448).
- Contrast — the HTML surface for the same data deliberately does not expose the keys: `subscriptionRow` (render.ts:5550-5560) renders only the endpoint **host**, classes, quiet window, and user agent.
- No consumer needs the GET: repo-wide grep shows `push-client.js` only POSTs/DELETEs `/api/push/subscriptions`, and the inline `/alerts` script only DELETEs. The engine reads subscriptions internally via the store, never over HTTP.

### Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-subs-leak/probe.ts`, blobs sha-matched to origin/main)

`AlertsStore` backed by a fake DB returning one sentinel row, serialized exactly as the GET handler serializes it:

```
GET wire contains p256dh sentinel: true
GET wire contains auth sentinel:    true
GET wire contains endpoint sentinel: true
HTML /alerts contains p256dh sentinel: false
HTML /alerts contains auth sentinel:    false
HTML /alerts contains endpoint host:    true
```

## Why it matters

The alert throat (#3676) exists so critical incidents reliably reach Drew's devices. This endpoint hands every subscriber's push key material to any tailnet-reachable caller (the aggregator binds loopback + tailnet and is fronted by Tailscale Serve at `cfg.publicOrigin`), and enumerates the exact endpoints that the likewise-unauthenticated `DELETE /api/push/subscriptions` (server.ts:986-994) accepts — so a caller can both harvest the secrets and silently unsubscribe every device from critical alerts. The keys serve no client need: the one legitimate read surface (the `/alerts` page) already projects them away.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `GET /api/push/subscriptions` no longer returns `p256dh` or `auth` values for any subscription (project each row to the non-secret fields the page uses — id, endpoint host or endpoint, classes, quiet, user_agent, created_at/last_seen_at, gone_count — or remove the GET route entirely if nothing needs it).
- [ ] A test pins the redaction: a subscription row with sentinel `p256dh`/`auth` values serialized through the GET path contains neither sentinel (mirroring the probe above).
- [ ] Internal delivery is unaffected: `runAlertTick`/`deliverToAll` keep reading full rows through the store directly, and the existing alerts test suite passes.
- [ ] The `/alerts` page subscription list renders unchanged.

title: aggregator(alerts): mergeQuiet accepts out-of-range times (99:99, 24:60) — a malformed quiet window is silently reinterpreted instead of falling back to the default

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/alerts.ts` `mergeQuiet` (alerts.ts:89-99) validates quiet-window times with a shape-only regex:

```ts
if (typeof q.start === "string" && /^\d{2}:\d{2}$/.test(q.start)) out.start = q.start;
if (typeof q.end === "string" && /^\d{2}:\d{2}$/.test(q.end)) out.end = q.end;
```

Any two-digit pair passes: `99:99`, `24:60`, `23:60` are all stored as the subscription's quiet prefs. `inQuietHours` (alerts.ts:110-132) then converts with `toMin` — `(h || 0) * 60 + (m || 0)` — with no range check either, so the garbage silently becomes a *different* window instead of being rejected back to the default:

- `start: "99:99"` → 6039 minutes; with `end: "07:00"` the wrap branch (`mins >= start || mins < end`) makes the window **00:00–07:00** — the 23:00 start the user asked for (default) silently vanishes, and 23:00–24:00 is no longer quiet.
- `end: "24:60"` → 1500 minutes, extending any window 60+ minutes past its stated end.

The existing test (test/alerts.test.ts, "quiet defaults…") pins only that a non-numeric spelling (`"9pm"`) falls back to the default; digit-shaped nonsense is untested and unhandled. This is the same shape-only-validation class as the feed gates (#3458, #3427, #3428), in the one prefs parser that has an explicit reject-to-default contract for malformed input.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe importing the real `alerts.ts` at main `9be9c229` (sha256 `868f4c78…`, identical in both clones; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-alerttick/`, log `probe.log`):

- `mergeQuiet({ start: "99:99" })` → `{ start: "99:99", end: "07:00", tz: "America/Chicago" }` — accepted verbatim
- `mergeQuiet({ end: "24:60" })` → `{ start: "23:00", end: "24:60", … }` — accepted verbatim
- `inQuietHours({ start: "99:99", end: "07:00" }, 2026-01-15T06:00Z = 00:00 CST)` → `true`; at `18:00Z = 12:00 CST` → `false` — i.e. the effective window is 00:00–07:00, not an error and not the default 23:00–07:00

## Why it matters

Quiet prefs are user-supplied subscription input persisted via `validateNewSubscription` → `upsertSubscription`. A client bug or a hand-edited prefs payload that emits an out-of-range time is silently stored and then silently *reinterpreted* as a different suppression window for the dashboard classes that consult `inQuietHours` (#3317) — notifications suppressed at the wrong hours, with no error anywhere, and the stored value looks plausible (`99:99` reads as a typo only if a human opens the row). Reject-to-default is the parser's own established behaviour for malformed strings; out-of-range digit strings are the gap in it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `mergeQuiet` accepts only real clock times: hour `00`–`23`, minute `00`–`59`; anything else (including `99:99`, `24:00`, `23:60`) falls back to the default for that field, like other malformed values do today.
- [ ] Regression tests pin: `99:99` and `24:60` fall back to defaults; boundary values `00:00` and `23:59` are accepted; the existing `"9pm"` fallback test still passes.
- [ ] No other `mergeQuiet` / `inQuietHours` behaviour changes (midnight-wrap and end-exclusive semantics unchanged).

Distinct from: #3685 (same module — the delivery engine's unconditional markDelivered; different function, different failure), #3317 (the dashboard classes that will consume quiet hours), #3458/#3427/#3428 (feed gates, same shape-only class in a different parser).

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/confirm-charges-surfaced.ts` — the post-delivery confirmation step of the fleet-feed push (its whole job, per #3122, is to mark the charges in the *successfully delivered* feed as surfaced, exactly once) — validates only that `chargesAttention` is an array (line 13). It never validates the array's elements, and it never validates the feed's top-level shape beyond property access. It then calls `unmatchedKey(charge)` (`src/charges-collect.ts:119-121`) on each raw element:

```ts
return `${u.normalized}|${u.amountUsd.toFixed(2)}|${u.at}`;
```

That dereferences `normalized`, calls `.toFixed(2)` on `amountUsd`, and interpolates `at`, with no check that any of them exist or have the right type. The render path got this exact protection in #2439 (closed): `loadFeed` now sanitizes `chargesAttention` element-by-element with `isUnmatchedCharge` (`src/feed.ts:502-506`). The confirm script bypasses `loadFeed`/`isFleetFeed` entirely — it does its own `JSON.parse` of the delivered file — so the fix never covered it.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop with the verbatim script and its real import chain at main `c6bf9337` (sha256-matched: confirm script `49675ccf…`, charges-collect.ts `20e3c5b4…`; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-confirmcharges/`, log `probe.log`):

- **Control** — one well-formed element (`{merchant, normalized:"acmeai", amountUsd:12.5, at:"2026-10-30", source}`): exit 0, state file gains key `acmeai|12.50|2026-10-30`. ✔
- **`chargesAttention: [null]`**: exit 1 — `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'u.normalized')`; **no state file written**.
- **String amount** (`amountUsd: "12.50"`): exit 1 — `TypeError: u.amountUsd.toFixed is not a function`; no state written.
- **Mixed `[valid, null]`**: exit 1 and the *valid* charge is **not** confirmed either — the key loop (line 24) runs before the atomic write (lines 25-30), so one bad element discards the whole feed's confirmations.
- **Top-level feed `null`**: exit 1 — `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'feed.chargesAttention')` at line 13/14.
- **Top-level feed `[]`**: exit 0, silently — `chargesAttention` is `undefined`, attention is empty, nothing is confirmed and nothing says so.
- **Element missing `normalized`** (`{merchant, amountUsd:12.5, at, source}` — a shape the house gate `isUnmatchedCharge` in `src/feed.ts:350-353` explicitly accepts, since it does not require `normalized`): exit 0, but the persisted surfaced key is the bogus `undefined|12.50|2026-10-30`, which can never match the key the collector computes for the real charge (`filterNewUnmatched`, charges-collect.ts:130-144) — the real charge is never marked surfaced, and the bogus key stays in the state file forever.

## Why it matters

`scripts/push-fleet-feed.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail` on a ~5-minute systemd cadence, and the confirm script is its **last line** (line 209), run *after* the feed has already been scp'd and mv'd into place on the laptop. So one malformed element (a hand-edited feed, an older/newer producer shape, a partially written file that still parses):

1. makes the whole push unit exit non-zero even though delivery succeeded — a phantom push failure every 5 minutes, indistinguishable from a real transport failure; and
2. persists **none** of the confirmations, so every charge in that feed re-surfaces as a fresh attention flag on the next cycle, forever, until the element is removed — the exact duplicate-alert failure the surfaced-once state exists to prevent (#3122).

The silent variants are worse in the other direction: a top-level array feed, or any element missing `normalized`, exits 0 while confirming nothing (or confirming a bogus `undefined|…` key), so the push looks healthy while charges re-alert indefinitely.

Producers today emit well-formed `UnmatchedCharge`s (`collect-fleet-feed.ts:520-539,766`), so this is a trust-boundary gap, not a live producer bug — the same class as #2439/#2445/#2446 for the render path. The confirm script is the one consumer of the feed file that still trusts it completely.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The confirm script validates each `chargesAttention` element before keying it (reuse `isUnmatchedCharge` from `src/feed.ts`, extended if needed so a keyable element must also carry a string `normalized` — or validate equivalently inline): malformed elements are dropped with a loud stderr note naming the dropped count, never keyed, and never abort the confirmation of the well-formed elements.
- [ ] A non-object top-level feed (`null`, array, string, number) fails with a clear `invalid feed` error naming the shape problem — never a raw `TypeError`, and never a silent exit 0.
- [ ] A persisted surfaced key is never built from missing/coerced fields: no `undefined|…` keys can enter the state file.
- [ ] Regression tests (or a scripted probe in the fix PR) cover: control, null element, string amount, mixed valid+invalid (valid still confirmed), top-level null, top-level array, missing-`normalized` element.
- [ ] `push-fleet-feed.sh` behaviour is unchanged for well-formed feeds: exit 0 and the same keys persisted as today.

Distinct from: #2439 (closed — the *render* path gate in `feed.ts`; this is the *push/confirm* path, which does not use that gate), #3122 (closed — moved confirmation after delivery; this script is that fix's implementation), #3458 (open — `isChargeRow`/`isUnmatchedCharge` accept negative amounts and non-date `at` on the render path; if that lands first, this fix should reuse the tightened gate).

title: mcpx(settings): daemon.port accepts any integer — 65536/99999/-1 validate at every layer, then the daemon dies at net.Listen with an error naming neither the setting nor its source

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`mcpx`'s `daemon.port` setting accepts any integer — `65536`, `99999`, `-1` and `-8080` all pass validation at every layer (file / env / flag / preset / runtime) — and the daemon then fails late at startup when `net.Listen` refuses the port, with an error (`listen tcp: address 99999: invalid port`) that names neither the setting nor where its value came from. A TCP port is one of the few settings whose entire valid range is known at declaration time (0–65535, with 0 documented as "the daemon picks a free port"), so this belongs in the settings validator, not in a bind error an operator has to reverse-engineer.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 4d6692d0)

Line trace, pkgs/mcpx:

- `internal/settings/registry.go:534-540` declares `daemon.port` as `KindInt` with default `"0"` and no range bound. The settings system's only integer bound is `Floor` (`internal/settings/schema.go:133-138`), which is a minimum only — it cannot express a port ceiling — and `daemon.port` does not set even that.
- `internal/settings/value.go:491-498` (`Validate`, KindInt branch) checks only that the value parses with `strconv.Atoi` and meets `Floor`; `Normalize`/`NormalizePath` therefore accept every integer.
- The value reaches the bind unchecked: `internal/cli/root.go:450` calls `srv.Listen(a.Settings().Int("daemon.port"))`, and `internal/daemon/server.go:316` (`(*Server).Listen`) binds the TCP listener via `net.JoinHostPort(host, strconv.Itoa(tcpPort))` — after the unix socket has already been bound and any stale socket cleared. Only there does the bad value surface, as a bare net error.
- 0 is legitimate and documented for this setting (`internal/api/openapi.go:68`: "its default of 0 means the daemon picks a free port"), so the range to enforce is 0–65535 — unlike a target port (cf. #3207 in pkgs/id, where 0 is useless), 0 must stay valid here.

Laptop probe (real `internal/settings` package from the laptop clone, whose `value.go`/`registry.go` are md5-identical to sandbox main — b55906a4 / 836d87aa; probe + log at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-daemonport/` on the laptop):

```
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "0")     -> "0" err=<nil>      (control)
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "8080")  -> "8080" err=<nil>   (control)
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "65535") -> "65535" err=<nil>  (control)
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "65536") -> "65536" err=<nil>
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "99999") -> "99999" err=<nil>
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "-1")    -> "-1" err=<nil>
NormalizePath(daemon.port, "-8080") -> "-8080" err=<nil>
net.Listen(:0)     -> ok (127.0.0.1:46421)
net.Listen(:65536) -> err=listen tcp: address 65536: invalid port
net.Listen(:99999) -> err=listen tcp: address 99999: invalid port
net.Listen(:-1)    -> err=listen tcp: address -1: invalid port
```

## Why it matters

The settings system is the choke point whose job is keeping an invalid value out of a running process, and it reports layer errors with provenance ("logging.level is debug, from MCPX_LOG_LEVEL"). A port typo in an env var or config file currently sails through that choke point and kills daemon startup with a raw net error that does not say which setting, which layer, or which value is at fault — the operator's first debugging step is guessing that `MCPX_DAEMON_PORT` / `--port` was the input. The same class was filed for the projector (#2172) and the aggregator (#2161); mcpx's daemon port is the remaining instance, and it is the easiest of the three to fix because the settings layer already validates everything else about the value.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `daemon.port` values outside 0–65535 are refused at apply/validate time (file, env, flag, preset and runtime layers alike) with an error naming the setting and the offending value; `0`, `8080` and `65535` still validate.
- [ ] The mechanism is the settings layer's, not a second check at the bind site: e.g. an optional ceiling alongside `Floor` on `Setting`, or an equivalent per-setting range check inside `Validate` — the bind error may remain as a backstop but is no longer the first place a bad port is caught.
- [ ] Regression tests cover `-1`, `65536` and a large value (e.g. `99999`) as refused, and `0`/`65535` as accepted, for `daemon.port`.
- [ ] No other KindInt setting's accepted range changes unless its own declaration gains a bound.

body:
## Problem

`isSessionRecord` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/registry.ts:155-175`) is the only hygiene gate on every path that admits a session-registry record from parsed JSON:

- the durable registry store file (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:654`, `parsed.filter(isSessionRecord)`)
- the feed's `registry` section (`live.ts:1094`)
- Muse launch-record JSONL (`registry.ts:93-105`, `parseLaunchRecords` → `recordFromLaunch` → `isSessionRecord`)

It validates `id`/`source`/`label`, the two timestamps (#2376) and `taskRefs` (#2408) — but it never checks three fields its consumers dereference unconditionally:

- **`status`** — `sessionRecordIsLive` (`render.ts:1470-1473`) calls `r.status.toLowerCase()`, and `sessionRecordLine` calls it whenever identities are present.
- **`tokensTotal`** — `renderSessions` sums it arithmetically (`render.ts:4816`, printed as the page total at `render.ts:4864`) and `sessionRecordLine` formats it with `toLocaleString()` (`render.ts:1810`).
- **`agentId` / `agentLabel`** — required fields on `SessionRecord` (`model.ts:1093-1095`); `identitiesFromRecords` (`registry.ts:184-192`) interpolates `agentLabel` into the identity label.

No real producer can emit the bad shapes: `recordFromSessionEntry` (`registry.ts:31-55`) always builds a string `status` and string agent identity, and `tokensTotal` comes from the numeric `tokensBySession` map; `recordFromLaunch` (`registry.ts:73-90`) defaults `status` to `"launched"`. The exposure is exactly the one #2376/#2408 were filed for: a poisoned store file, feed section, or hand-edited launch JSONL line reaches the renderers unchecked.

## Verified (laptop probe, real sources at main `690c550a`, sha256-matched `registry.ts`/`render.ts`; probe copy of `feed.ts` differs only by the missing brace tracked in #3452)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-sessionrecord/` (`probe-run.log`). Control record (all fields well-formed) passes the gate and `sessionRecordIsLive` returns `true`. Then:

1. **Status-less record passes, render crashes.** `{...valid}` with `status` deleted → `isSessionRecord` returns `true`; `sessionRecordIsLive` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'r.status.toLowerCase')`, and `sessionRecordLine(record, { identities })` throws the same — one poisoned record takes down the sessions-page render instead of dropping at the gate.
2. **Non-string status passes, same crash.** `status: 42` → gate `true`; `sessionRecordIsLive` throws `TypeError: r.status.toLowerCase is not a function`.
3. **String `tokensTotal` poisons the page total.** `tokensTotal: "5000"` → gate `true`; `renderSessions` prints **`05000 tokens recorded`** (the reduce at `render.ts:4816` string-concatenates) instead of a numeric total.
4. **Infinite `tokensTotal` passes via ordinary JSON.** `JSON.parse('{"tokensTotal":1e999, ...}')` yields `Infinity` → gate `true`; the page prints **∞ tokens recorded** and the record line shows `· ∞ tok`.
5. **Negative and object `tokensTotal` pass.** `-500` → gate `true` (a negative cumulative total silently reduces the page sum for a singleton record; `mergeRecords`' `Math.max` only repairs the duplicate-key path). `{x:1}` → gate `true`; the line renders `· [object Object] tok` and the page total is poisoned to a string.
6. **The launch-JSONL path admits all of it.** `parseLaunchRecords('{"id":"launch1","label":"L","status":42,"tokensTotal":"9000"}')` returns 1 record with numeric `status` and string `tokensTotal` — the gate is the only filter on that path.
7. **Missing agent identity passes.** A record with `agentId`/`agentLabel` deleted → gate `true`; `identitiesFromRecords` renders its label with `undefined` interpolated.

## Why it matters

The registry store is durable and self-perpetuating: once a malformed record is merged in, `mergeIntoRegistry` writes it back to the store file, so a single bad feed section or launch line permanently (a) crashes the sessions page (missing/non-string `status`), or (b) falsifies the fleet-wide token total every reader sees (string/Infinity/object `tokensTotal`). This is the same failure family the gate already owns for timestamps (#2376, fixed) and `taskRefs` (#2408, fixed); these three fields were simply missed.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSessionRecord` rejects a record whose `status` is absent or not a string, whose `agentId`/`agentLabel` are absent or not strings, and whose `tokensTotal` is present but not a finite number ≥ 0 — following the validator-owns-the-rule precedent in the #2376/#2408 comments (reject the record; never coerce).
- Well-formed records from both real producers (`recordFromSessionEntry`, `recordFromLaunch`) pass unchanged, including a record with `tokensTotal` absent.
- The #2376/#2408 hygiene tests' minimal fixture (`{id, source, label}`) is updated to the new contract (it currently asserts a status-less record passes, `test/registry-hygiene-2376.test.ts:40`), and new regression tests cover: missing status, numeric status, string/Infinity (`1e999`)/negative/object `tokensTotal`, and the launch-JSONL admission path.
- A poisoned record in the store/feed/JSONL drops individually; the sessions page renders and its token total stays numeric.
- Note: the aggregator suite cannot run cleanly on current main until the `feed.ts` parse break (#3452) lands; sequence after it if needed.

## Distinct from

- #2376 (closed): `lastSeenAt`/`startedAt` timestamp types in this same gate.
- #2408 (closed): `taskRefs` shape in this same gate.
- #3452 (open): `feed.ts` parse breakage — unrelated, but it gates running the suite.

body:
## Summary

`settings.ParseBytes` (pkgs/mcpx/internal/settings/value.go:450) accepts the non-finite float spellings `NaN` and `Inf` — bare and with size suffixes (`NaNMB`, `InfGB`) — and converts them to `math.MinInt64` (-9223372036854775808) with no error. `Validate`'s KindBytes branch (value.go:510-513) accepts anything `ParseBytes` does not error on, so a `KindBytes` setting (e.g. `http.streamBufferInit`, `http.bodyLimit`, `artifacts.quota`, `logging.maxBytes`) can be applied at any layer (file/env/flag/preset/runtime) with the value `NaN` and every reader then sees the most negative int64 there is.

This is a residual of #1697 (byte sizes accept negatives and int64 overflow), not a duplicate of it: #1697's acceptance pins refusing "negative results and magnitudes that do not fit in an int64". NaN is neither — every comparison against NaN is false, so a fix that adds the obvious sign/range checks (`f < 0`, `f * mult > MaxInt64`) still admits `NaN` (and a `> MaxInt64` check alone admits `+Inf` spellings only via the conversion, not via the check). The non-finite spellings need an explicit `math.IsNaN` / `math.IsInf` rejection, and regression tests that name them.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 74bf3420)

Line trace, pkgs/mcpx/internal/settings/value.go:

- `ParseBytes` (:450-479) strips a suffix, then `strconv.ParseFloat(v, 64)` + `int64(f * float64(mult))` with no finiteness check. Go's `ParseFloat` accepts `NaN`, `nan`, `Inf`, `+Inf`, `Infinity` (case-insensitive); converting a non-finite float to int64 yields `math.MinInt64` on amd64/arm64.
- `Validate` KindBytes case (:510-513) returns an error only when `ParseBytes` errors — so the values above are *valid* settings. `Set.Bytes()` (:325) discards the parse error the same way.
- Consumers spend the result as in #1697: `make([]byte, 0, set.Bytes("http.streamBufferInit"))` (internal/cli/opcmd.go:557-558, internal/cli/client.go:1238) panics on the negative cap; `http.MaxBytesReader` with a negative limit (internal/daemon/routes_secrets.go:49,114 and the other `http.bodyLimit` call sites, whose `bodyBytes` helper at internal/daemon/server.go:1196 does not guard `<= 0` either) rejects every request body; guarded consumers (artifacts `Quota <= 0` = no ceiling, internal/artifacts/artifacts.go:483; logging `maxBytes <= 0` = default, internal/logging/file.go:86) silently reinterpret a configured cap as no cap / default.

Laptop probe (real `ParseBytes` extracted verbatim from internal/settings/value.go; the laptop clone's file is md5-identical to sandbox main, b55906a4286878d8897d1e60300e0f5c; probe + logs at ~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-parsebytes/ on the laptop):

```
"16MB"                     -> 16000000 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true   (control)
"64KiB"                    -> 65536 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true      (control)
"banana"                   -> 0 err=not a size: "banana" validateAccepts=false  (control)
"1e999"                    -> 0 err=not a size: "1e999" validateAccepts=false   (ParseFloat range error — correctly refused)
"NaN"                      -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
"nan"                      -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
"Inf"                      -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
"+Inf"                     -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
"NaNMB"                    -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
"InfGB"                    -> -9223372036854775808 err=<nil> validateAccepts=true
```

Note the contrast the probe pins: `1e999` is refused because `ParseFloat` itself range-errors, while the named non-finite spellings sail through the same parser — the hole is specifically the non-finite names, not float parsing in general.

## Why it matters

The settings system is the choke point whose job is keeping an invalid value out of a running process. A generated or fat-fingered config carrying `NaN` (a spelling JSON-adjacent tooling and template engines readily emit for "unknown") currently validates cleanly and then either crashes the CLI at the first streaming read, makes the daemon reject every request body, or silently uncaps a store quota the operator believed was set — the same three failure shapes as #1697, reachable through a spelling its fix does not obviously cover.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ParseBytes` refuses non-finite results: `NaN`, `nan`, `Inf`, `+Inf`, `Infinity` — bare and with every size suffix (e.g. `NaNMB`, `InfGB`) — with an error naming the offending value.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the non-finite spellings alongside #1697's negative/overflow cases (if #1697 lands first, extend its test table; the two issues' test cases must coexist).
- [ ] A `KindBytes` setting therefore cannot be applied at any layer with a non-finite spelling; the error surfaces at apply time, not at first use.
- [ ] Existing internal/settings, internal/cli and internal/daemon tests keep passing.

## Notes for triage

- Related: #1697 (negatives + finite overflow in the same function — coordinate the fix; one `ParseBytes` change can close both, but this issue's non-finite test cases are the part a sign/range-only fix misses). Distinct from #3467 (non-positive ticker intervals, KindDuration) and #3490 (Go duration spellings in the plugin's TS parser).
- Found by new-issue-creator-code-a, 2026-11-01.

body:
## Problem

`isProjectPoolItem` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts:236-252) — the shared per-item gate for the feed's GitHub Project pool (the collector parses against it, `poolFromFeed` in feed.ts:266-271 filters with it) — checks the issue/PR number with a bare type test at projects.ts:243:

```ts
typeof p.number === "number" &&
```

Every real number comes from the GitHub GraphQL API (projects.ts:37-38, mapped at :135-149), where `number` is always a positive integer. The gate admits values no producer can emit: fractional, negative, zero, `NaN`, and `Infinity` (the last two arrive via hand/corrupt feed JSON as `null`-adjacent spellings or via a JS producer bug — `typeof NaN === "number"`).

Consumers trust the gate: the pool renders the number verbatim in link text — render.ts:5132, :5402, :5415 interpolate `${esc(p.repo)}#${p.number}` — so a poisoned item renders as `developing-today/code#NaN`, `…#1.5`, or `…#-3`, a fabricated cross-reference that matches no real issue (and a `ref`/`number` pair that can disagree with each other, since neither is checked against the other).

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real code)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-subsdate/probe2.ts` on the laptop — verbatim copy of pm-stack/aggregator at main 5abd39af (feed.ts sha256 cf7ea03d…, validate.ts sha256 1f72539a…, matched to the sandbox clone). Output (probe2.log), base item valid in every other field:

- control `number: 12` → `isProjectPoolItem = true` (correct)
- `number: 1.5` → **true**
- `number: -3` → **true**
- `number: 0` → **true**
- `number: NaN` → **true**
- `number: Infinity` → **true**

## Why it matters

The pool section is the dashboard's cross-project work view; its items are rendered as `repo#number` links throughout /projects and the board cards. A gate that admits impossible numbers lets one corrupt feed item fabricate references and pollute derived state keyed off the pool, instead of dropping just that item — the per-item drop is the gate's documented contract (feed.ts:239-248).

## Acceptance criteria

- `isProjectPoolItem` requires `number` to be a positive integer (`Number.isInteger(n) && n > 0`): `1.5`, `-3`, `0`, `NaN`, and `Infinity` items fail the gate and drop individually in `poolFromFeed` (the section itself survives).
- Valid positive-integer items pass unchanged.
- Regression tests cover the five rejected values plus the valid control, following the existing projects/feed gate test pattern.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed for `isProjectPoolItem` / pool number: #2418 (open) covers the same function's unchecked `labels` field — a different field with a different failure (render crash); this filing is the `number` field only. #2453 (closed) was the non-array projects crash. No issue covers the number's value domain.

body:
## Problem

`isSubscriptionRow` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:472-479) — the gate behind `sanitizeSubscriptions` (feed.ts:486-493), applied at the `loadFeed` boundary (feed.ts:507) — accepts **any string** as `renewsAt`:

```ts
(typeof v.renewsAt === "string" || v.renewsAt === null)
```

The only producer never emits such a value: `extractSubscriptions` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:1063-1064) sets `renewsAt` only when `parseIsoDate(...) !== null`, otherwise `null` ("never a verbatim renewsAt"). The shared strict primitive already exists in the same aggregator: `isIsoDate` (src/validate.ts:113-115), which rejects impossible calendar dates instead of rolling them over.

The renderer trusts the gate: render.ts:2039 interpolates the string verbatim (escaped only) as ` · renews ${esc(s.renewsAt)}`.

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real code)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-subsdate/` on the laptop — verbatim copy of pm-stack/aggregator at main 5abd39af (feed.ts sha256 cf7ea03d…, validate.ts sha256 1f72539a…, matched to the sandbox clone; probe copy differs only by the #3452 closing brace, without which feed.ts does not parse). `bun probe.ts` output (probe.log):

- control `{renewsAt:"2026-12-01"}` → `isSubscriptionRow = true` (correct)
- control `{renewsAt:null}` → `true` (correct)
- `renewsAt:"banana"` → **true** (isIsoDate = false)
- `renewsAt:"2026-02-30"` → **true** (isIsoDate = false)
- `renewsAt:"2026-13-01"` → **true** (isIsoDate = false)
- `renewsAt:"12/01/2026"` → **true** (isIsoDate = false)
- `renewsAt:"2026-12-01banana"` → **true** (isIsoDate = false)
- `sanitizeSubscriptions` over the mixed set: all 7 rows kept, **dropped: 0**

So a corrupt or hand-edited feed renders `renews banana`, `renews 2026-02-30` (a date that does not exist) etc. on /quota as if they were measured renewal dates, and `/api/quota.json` serves them verbatim — the exact falsified-date class the sibling gates were fixed for (#3458 charges `at`, #3428 burn `from`/`to`, #3427 quota `resetsAt`).

## Why it matters

The subscriptions strip is renewal-only guidance: a bogus or impossible renewal date is presented as fact. The gate's own comment (feed.ts:469-471) says the row must be "safe to hand to the renderers" — a non-date `renewsAt` is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSubscriptionRow` requires `renewsAt` to be `null` or a string passing `isIsoDate` (validate.ts) — `"banana"`, `"2026-02-30"`, `"2026-13-01"`, `"12/01/2026"`, and `"2026-12-01banana"` rows are dropped by `sanitizeSubscriptions` and counted in `dropped`.
- Valid ISO dates and `null` rows pass unchanged (producer output from `extractSubscriptions` is unaffected).
- Regression tests cover the five rejected spellings plus the two controls, following the existing feed-gate test pattern.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed for `isSubscriptionRow`, `subscriptions renewsAt`: #2446 (closed) was the null-row crash that created this gate — it never checked the date's validity; #2206 (closed) fixed the producer side in saas-extract. No issue covers the feed gate accepting a non-date `renewsAt`. Distinct fields from #3458/#3428/#3427 (other gates, same file).

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts` reads its one CLI argument by position with no validation (line 111-112):

```ts
const outArg = process.argv.indexOf("--out");
const outPath = outArg >= 0 ? process.argv[outArg + 1] : (process.env.FLEET_FEED_OUT ?? join(PKG, "fleet-feed.json"));
```

Three failure modes, all verified this run (below):

1. **Trailing `--out` crashes with a raw TypeError before any work.** `outPath` is `undefined`, and the module-top-level `aaLastGoodPath` computation at line 362 — `join(dirname(outPath), "aa-last-good.json")` — throws `TypeError: The "path" property must be of type string, got undefined` at startup. The operator gets a stack trace pointing at the AA last-good store, not a usage error naming `--out`.
2. **A flag token is accepted as the `--out` value.** `--out --weird` runs the full collection and then writes the feed to a file literally named `--weird` in the working directory, exiting 0 and logging `collector: wrote --weird`. `dirname("--weird")` is `.`, so the AA last-good store would also land in the working directory instead of beside the real feed. The intended feed file is never updated, and nothing in the output says so.
3. **Unrecognized arguments are silently ignored.** `--otu <path>` (typo) is not an error: `indexOf("--out")` misses, so the collector writes to the **default** `fleet-feed.json` — in production the live feed — exiting 0, while the operator believes the feed went to `<path>`.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-01, laptop probe)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-fleetfeedout/` on the laptop — a verbatim copy of `pm-stack/aggregator` at main `9f48e293`; `collect-fleet-feed.ts` sha256 `adb4320333d9ec5ead3436376b5ea0ca7dc1d7431bd947f36d9dd8e48adf5dae`, identical to the sandbox checkout. (The probe copy of `src/feed.ts` differs from main by exactly one added closing brace for `isUnmatchedCharge` — the already-filed breakage #3452, without which nothing in the aggregator parses; the script under test is byte-identical.) All runs had every state-path env var redirected into the probe dir, so no real feed or state was touched. Logs: `case-trailing.log`, `case-control.log`, `case-flaglike.log`, `case-typo.log` in the probe dir.

- Control: `bun scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts --out <probe>/out/feed.json` → exit 0, `collector: wrote <probe>/out/feed.json`, file present.
- Trailing: `bun scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts --out` → exit 1, `TypeError: The "path" property must be of type string, got undefined` at `collect-fleet-feed.ts:362:29`, before any collection.
- Flag-like: `bun scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts --out --weird` → exit 0, `collector: wrote --weird`, and a 663-byte file named `--weird` in the working directory; the default feed was not written.
- Typo: `bun scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts --otu <probe>/out/typo.json` → exit 0, `collector: wrote <aggregator>/fleet-feed.json` (the default); `typo.json` was never created.

## Why it matters

This collector is the scheduled producer of the fleet feed (see #3362/#3363 for how load-bearing — and how confusing its overwrites already are). A hand run with a mistyped or truncated command line either dies with a misleading stack trace, silently writes the feed to a stray `--`-named file while the dashboard goes stale, or — worst — overwrites the live default feed when the operator explicitly asked for a scratch path to test with. This is the same arg-parsing class as #3330 (backfill `--dir`), #3333 (charges producer) and #3415 (record-claude-launch), under the strict-argument-contract umbrella #3352; this script is the remaining `indexOf` reader in `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/` not yet covered.

## Acceptance criteria

- `collect-fleet-feed.ts --out` with no following token exits non-zero with a usage error naming `--out` (no stack trace, no file written).
- `--out` followed by a token starting with `--` is refused the same way.
- Any unrecognized argument exits non-zero naming the offending token, before collection starts.
- `--out <path>` and the no-argument default (`FLEET_FEED_OUT` / package `fleet-feed.json`) behave exactly as today.
- Regression tests cover the three failure modes plus the control, following the arg-parsing test pattern used for the sibling scripts fixed under #3352.

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
# mcpx(daemon): six handlers silently discard invalid numeric query params — `?limit=banana` returns 200 with the default-sized result, indistinguishable from a valid request

## Evidence (verified this run, main `69632f23`)

Six `/v1` handlers parse a numeric query parameter with `strconv.Atoi` and discard the error (`limit, _ :=` / `top, _ :=` / `budget, _ :=`). A parse failure yields `0`, which each handler then replaces with its configured default — so a present-but-invalid value is silently treated as absent:

| Route | Param | Site |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /v1/log` | `limit` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go:131` |
| `GET /v1/stats` | `top` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go:203` |
| `GET /v1/registry/search` | `limit` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go:278` |
| `GET /v1/recipes?q=…` | `limit` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/routes_consumer.go:157` |
| `GET /v1/search` | `limit` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/server.go:941` |
| `GET /v1/catalog` | `budget` | `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/server.go:988` |

Verified with a probe on the laptop (test file `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/probe_laneA_test.go` in worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-mcpxlimit/`; `ops.go`/`server.go`/`routes_consumer.go` md5-identical to this main — `187cd534`/`d1d900c9`/`f1b056c6`; real handlers via `httptest`, empty store; `go test` PASS, log in the probe dir):

- `GET /v1/log?limit=5` (control) → **200** `{"records":[]}`
- `GET /v1/log?limit=banana` → **200** `{"records":[]}` — identical to the control
- `GET /v1/log?limit=2.7` → **200**; `?limit=1e3` → **200**
- `GET /v1/log?since=banana` (same handler, contrast) → **400** naming the bad value — the handler already rejects one invalid parameter and silently defaults another
- `GET /v1/stats?top=5` (control) → **200**; `?top=banana` → **200**; `?top=2.7` → **200**

## Why it matters

This is the exact silent-drop shape the daemon has already ruled against twice: #1679 made a malformed `since`/`Last-Event-ID` on `/v1/events` a 400 naming the parameter, and #2223 (closed) did the same for `minScore`/`maxScore`/`limit`/`offset` on `/v1/interactions`, with the comment in `routes_feedback.go` recording the rule: "silently dropping a bound made a typo'd minScore return the unfiltered list with 200 … both read as real answers." A caller who typos `limit`/`top`/`budget` on these six routes still gets a real-looking 200 answer computed with a different bound than the one they asked for — a truncated-looking result set, a stats table aggregated over the default top-N, or a catalog built to the default budget — with no signal anything was ignored.

Negative values have the same fate today (`limit=-5` on `/v1/log` reaches `logstore` as a non-positive limit and becomes the default there), so the fix should state the rule for them rather than leaving a second silent path.

## Acceptance criteria

- A present-but-unparseable numeric parameter on all six routes above is a **400 naming the parameter and the bad value** (the `parseIntParam` shape already in `routes_feedback.go`, ideally factored so the handlers share one helper).
- Absent parameter behaviour is unchanged: the configured default applies, exactly as today.
- Valid values behave exactly as today, including the existing clamping/defaulting for `0` and negative values — or, if a negative is also made a 400, that is stated in the PR and pinned by a test (no silent change either way).
- Regression tests per route (handler-level, following `events_cursor_test.go` / `routes_feedback_test.go`): invalid spellings (`banana`, `2.7`, `1e3`) → 400; absent → 200 with default; valid → 200.
- No other query parameters or routes change behaviour.

Distinct from: #2223 (closed; `/v1/interactions` only — its fix did not touch these six handlers), #1679 (closed; `/v1/events` cursors), #2878 (`/v1/complete` value cap, different mechanism).

title: provider-catalog-sync: stripJsonc's trailing-comma pass is not string-aware — a comma before } or ] inside a string literal is silently deleted

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs catalog sync

body:
# provider-catalog-sync: stripJsonc's trailing-comma pass is not string-aware — a comma before } or ] inside a string literal is silently deleted

## Evidence (verified this run, main a17ae136)

`bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs`:

- `:88-122` — `stripJsonc` carefully tracks string state (`instr`/`esc`) while stripping `//` and `/* */` comments, so comment markers inside strings survive.
- `:121` — the final trailing-comma fix is a plain regex over the whole output, with no string awareness: `return out.join('').replace(/,(\s*[}\]])/g, '$1');`. A comma that sits immediately before a `}` or `]` **inside a string literal** matches the pattern and is deleted.
- `:125-127` — `parseJsonc` is `JSON.parse(stripJsonc(text))`, so the corrupted value is what every caller sees. There is no error: the parse succeeds with the wrong string.

Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-jsoncstr/`; real `provider-catalog-sync.mjs` copied from the laptop clone at the same HEAD, sha256 `08e742c0…` matched to sandbox main `a17ae136`; `node probe.mjs`, log `run.log`):

| Input | `parseJsonc` result | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `{"a": 1,}` (control) | `{"a":1}` | correct — real trailing comma removed |
| `// hi\n{"a": [1, 2,], "b": {"c": 3,}}` (control) | `{"a":[1,2],"b":{"c":3}}` | correct |
| `{"url": "https://example.com//x"}` (control) | url unchanged | correct — comment pass is string-aware |
| `{"note": "hello, world"}` (control) | note unchanged | correct |
| `{"note": "x,}", "n": 1}` | `{"note":"x}","n":1}` | **comma deleted inside the string** |
| `{"note": "a,]", "n": 1}` | `{"note":"a]","n":1}` | **comma deleted** |
| `{"note": "a, }", "n": 1}` | `{"note":"a }","n":1}` | **comma deleted** |
| `{"list": ["x, ]", "y"]}` | `{"list":["x ]","y"]}` | **comma deleted** |
| nested `{"provider":{"p":{"models":{"m":{"variants":{"v":{"headers":"a,}"}}}}}}}` | `headers` becomes `"a}"` | **comma deleted at depth** |

`stripJsonc('{"note": "x,}", "n": 1}')` returns `{"note": "x}", "n": 1}` — the corruption is in the stripper itself, before `JSON.parse`.

## Why it matters

`runSync` reads the live OpenCode config through `parseJsonc` (`:462-465`). Keys are unaffected, so enumeration and classification look right, but **values** are silently wrong wherever a config string ends in `,}` / `,]` / `, }` / `, ]` — e.g. a variant header, a prompt fragment, or an option value cloned by `makeEntry` (`:404-439`), which deep-clones the nearest sibling's `variants` from the *parsed* config and writes them into the new catalog entry inserted into the file. The corrupted string is then committed to the config as if it were the operator's own text. `assertCatalogOnly` (`:619`) cannot catch it: it compares `parseJsonc(before)` with `parseJsonc(after)`, and both sides go through the same lossy stripper. The existing test at `bin/provider-catalog-sync.test.mjs:45` pins comments + trailing commas but has no case with a `,`+bracket sequence inside a string.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parseJsonc` returns string values byte-for-byte: a comma inside a string literal is never removed, including `,}`, `,]`, `, }`, `, ]` and the same shapes at any nesting depth.
- Real trailing commas (outside strings) in objects and arrays are still removed, and comment stripping stays string-aware (the current controls keep passing).
- The trailing-comma removal is done in the same string-aware pass as comment stripping (or an equivalent state machine) — not as a whole-text regex.
- Tests pin: the control cases above, plus string cases `x,}`, `a,]`, `a, }`, an array element `x, ]`, and a nested variant-style value.

Distinct from #2827 (enumerateProxy `/v1/models` shape — live-source side), #2235 (this script's entry-point symlink check), and #2832 (sync-models, a different file's JSONC handling). Sibling lesson: `blankComments` in the same file (`:132-178`) already does a same-length string-aware pass — the fix can follow that pattern.

body:
## Problem

KindDuration validation currently accepts syntactically valid zero and negative durations. Three settings are passed directly to time.NewTicker, which panics for non-positive values:

- daemon.reapInterval — internal/daemon/server.go:580
- daemon.saveInterval — internal/daemon/server.go:582
- http.ssePing — internal/daemon/server.go:1560

## Triage evidence

- internal/settings/value.go:499-509 parses KindDuration values but only has a special minimum for protoTasks.maxTTL; there is no positive-interval rule.
- daemon.reapInterval and daemon.saveInterval are declared in internal/settings/registry.go:522-531 with positive defaults.
- http.ssePing is declared in internal/settings/wire.go:61-67 with a positive default.
- daemon/routes_exec.go:117-121 guards artifacts.gcInterval <= 0 by substituting the default; internal/mcpserver/timing.go:85-87 similarly resolves nonpositive transport.sseKeepAlive to its default. Preserve these existing fallback behaviors.
- daemon.idleExit is intentionally zero-capable: internal/settings/wire.go:276-282 says zero means never, and daemon/server.go:661-665 treats <=0 as disabled.
- Other ticker sites in mcpx use fixed or built-in default intervals, not registry settings.

## Scope

Make validation reject zero and negative values for the three direct ticker settings above, with an error naming the setting/value. Keep legitimate-zero settings such as daemon.idleExit accepted; do not blanket-reject zero for all KindDuration values. Preserve the guarded fallback semantics for artifacts.gcInterval and transport.sseKeepAlive.

## Acceptance

- Tests show 0s and -5s are rejected for daemon.reapInterval, daemon.saveInterval, and http.ssePing.
- A test shows daemon.idleExit=0s remains valid.
- Guarded settings retain their fallback behavior and no validated duration reaches a direct NewTicker with a nonpositive period.
- Existing internal/settings and internal/daemon tests pass.

Related: #2613, #1697, #1758.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Non-positive or non-finite ticker intervals in mcpx settings are rejected at validation time with a clear error naming the setting, before any `NewTicker` call can panic.
- [ ] Valid positive intervals behave exactly as before (existing settings tests unchanged and green).
- [ ] A regression test covers zero, negative, and (where representable) NaN interval inputs.

title: aggregator(feed): isBurnSegment accepts negative tokens, non-date from/to and inverted ranges — garbage burn rows survive sanitizeQuotaView and render as measured history

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Problem

`isBurnSegment` — the element guard for the quota view's burn history, used by `sanitizeQuotaView` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:322-331` — checks only types:

```ts
typeof v.provider === "string" &&
typeof v.pool === "string" &&
typeof v.from === "string" &&
typeof v.to === "string" &&
isFiniteNumber(v.tokens)
```

So a segment with a **negative** token count, a non-date `from`/`to`, an impossible calendar date, or an inverted range (`from` after `to`) passes the gate, is counted as well-formed, and renders in the "Burn between resets" table (`src/render.ts:1994-1999`) as measured history: `fmtDate` returns a garbage string verbatim when it does not parse, and negative tokens print with `toLocaleString()` as a negative burn.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 574c04a7)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-feedquota/` (copies of the real `src/` tree, `feed.ts` md5 `e564f17aea918d5281fd37d433a01017`, identical to main; bun 1.4.2, real `isBurnSegment`). Control: a well-formed segment passes. Also passing (`isBurnSegment=true`):

- `tokens: -12345`
- `from: "banana"`
- `to: "2026-02-30T01:00:00Z"` (a day that never existed; `Date.parse` rolls it to Mar 2)
- `from: "2026-10-02T00:00:00Z", to: "2026-10-01T01:00:00Z"` (inverted range)

The shared strict primitives already exist in the same package — `isIsoDate` and `isNonNegative` in `src/validate.ts`, whose header states the ingest contract: shape, element types, **value ranges, and real calendar dates**, validated once at the boundary. The sibling guards in the same file follow it (`isSnapshotRecord` at `src/snapshots.ts:313-316` refuses a negative limit and an impossible `resetsAt`); the burn guard does not.

## Why it matters

Burn segments are the historical record the quota page presents as measured throughput between resets. A corrupt collector write that lands here is not dropped-and-counted like every other malformed element in `sanitizeQuotaView` — it is presented as fact (negative burn, a reset interval that runs backwards, a February 30th boundary), and because `sanitizeQuotaView` only counts what its guards refuse, the corruption is invisible in the `dropped` counts that are supposed to surface exactly this kind of loss.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isBurnSegment` refuses: a `from` or `to` that is not a real ISO calendar date (`isIsoDate`); a negative `tokens` (`isNonNegative`); an inverted range (`from > to`).
- Malformed segments drop individually in `sanitizeQuotaView` with `droppedBurn` counting them (existing #2429 behaviour for shape failures).
- Regression tests in `test/feed.test.ts` next to the existing "malformed burn segments drop individually" test: negative tokens, garbage/impossible `from`/`to`, and an inverted range all drop and count; the well-formed segment fixture is unchanged.

## Dedup

Distinct from the quota-window gate gap filed alongside this one (different guard, different consumers — pool state/guidance vs the burn-history table; cross-linked there), #3365 (snapshot rollup guard), #2470 (quota-extract `resetsAt` emission), and #3364 (coverage census guard). Searched open + closed for `isBurnSegment` before filing.

body:
Follow-up to #2568.

`recordsFromProviderUsage` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshot-records.ts:296-313` checks only `typeof used_percent === "number"` before emitting a pct record. The append CLI filters records through `isSnapshotRecord` (`append-usage-snapshots.ts:71`), whose current guard rejects negative pct values (`snapshots.ts:317-323`) but accepts finite values above 100. A real-module probe on main `199d9f2e222c17826533dc3d9320aebd88aab533` confirmed: -20 is emitted but rejected by the store; 150 and 1e9 are emitted and accepted; 42 is emitted and accepted. The original #2568 report that negative values pass the current store gate is stale, but the upper-bound defect remains.

## Goal
Skip an invalid Codex window rather than clamp or invent a value, while continuing to derive the session record and any other valid window.

## Acceptance
- `recordsFromProviderUsage` emits a Codex window only when `used_percent` is finite and in the inclusive range [0,100].
- `snapshot-writers.test.ts` covers negative and >100 values, plus valid boundary/control values; an invalid window does not suppress the other valid window or the sessions record.
- Existing `bun test test/snapshot-writers.test.ts` passes.

## Scope
Writer-side `recordsFromProviderUsage` and its focused tests only. Do not change the general store gate, other snapshot writers, or rollup validation (#3365). No clamping.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Snapshot records whose Codex `used_percent` is NaN, infinite, or outside [0,100] are skipped (with the existing drop accounting, if any) instead of being recorded.
- [ ] In-range values, including exactly 0 and exactly 100, are recorded unchanged.
- [ ] Tests cover below-range, above-range, and non-finite inputs alongside an in-range control.

title: aggregator(feed): isQuotaWindow accepts any string as resetsAt and any finite used/limit/percent — an impossible reset date is clocked as Mar 2 in guidance, a -50% window reads healthy and a 15000% window walls a pool

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`isQuotaWindow` — the feed boundary guard behind `sanitizeQuotaView` / `loadFeed` (#2429) in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:286-296` — checks only types, never values:

- `resetsAt` passes as **any** string (`feed.ts:293`: `v.resetsAt === null || typeof v.resetsAt === "string"`)
- `limit` passes as any finite number, including negative (`feed.ts:291`)
- `used` passes as any finite number, including negative (`feed.ts:292`)
- `percent` passes as any finite number, including negative or ≫100 (`feed.ts:294`)

The sister boundary for the same fields already refuses exactly these shapes: `isSnapshotRecord` (`src/snapshots.ts:313-316`) requires `isNonNegative(limit)` and `isIsoDate(resetsAt)`, with the comment that downstream code dereferences them (pct-of-limit, reset comparisons). The feed gate does not, and the shared strict primitive (`isIsoDate` / `parseIsoDate`, `src/validate.ts`) is already imported by `feed.ts` for other sections.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 574c04a7)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-feedquota/` (copies of the real `src/` tree, `feed.ts` md5 `e564f17aea918d5281fd37d433a01017`, identical to main; run with bun 1.4.2 against the real `isQuotaWindow`, `windowPercent`, `poolState`, `computeChoices`, `sanitizeQuotaView`). Control: a well-formed window passes. Every malformed case below also passes (`isQuotaWindow=true`) and survives `sanitizeQuotaView` with `droppedWindows=0`:

| case | result |
|---|---|
| `resetsAt: "2026-02-30T05:00:00Z"` | kept; `Date.parse` rolls it to **2026-03-02T05:00:00Z** |
| `resetsAt: "banana"` / `resetsAt: ""` | kept verbatim |
| `percent: -50`, `limit: null` | `windowPercent = -50`, pool reads **healthy** |
| `percent: 15000`, `limit: null` | `windowPercent = 15000`, pool reads **walled** |
| `used: -500`, `limit: 1000` | `windowPercent = -50`, pool reads healthy |
| `limit: -5`, no percent | `windowPercent = 100` (the `limit <= 0` fallback in `derive.ts:156`), pool reads **walled** with zero usage |

Guidance effect, same probe: a healthy pool whose only window carries `resetsAt: "2026-02-30T05:00:00Z"` is returned in `computeChoices(...)`'s `burnBeforeReset` list at `2026-03-01T12:00Z` — a burn-it-before-reset recommendation clocked from a day that never existed (the Mar 2 rollover is 17h out, inside `RESET_SOON_MS`). `quota-guidance.ts:18` (`soonestReset`) filters only non-finite `Date.parse` results, so impossible-but-parseable dates sail through, while `derive.ts:839` prints `resetsAt.slice(0, 10)` verbatim in attention flags and `render.ts` `fmtDate` renders the rolled-over March date as the reset date.

## Why it matters

The ingest contract (`src/validate.ts` header) is that every ingested document is validated once at its boundary — shape, element types, **value ranges, and real calendar dates** — before any consumer sees it. The quota section is the one section whose gate stops at types: a corrupt or buggy collector write (or a hand-edited feed) injects windows that flip pools between healthy and walled and fabricate reset timing in the guidance every session-placement decision reads, instead of being dropped-and-counted by the sanitizer like every other malformed element in the same view.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isQuotaWindow` refuses: a `resetsAt` that is not null and not a real ISO calendar date (`isIsoDate`); a negative `limit`; a negative `used`; a `percent` outside `[0, 100]` — or, if a percent above 100 is considered legitimate for over-limit windows, the bound is stated in a comment and pinned by a test (the snapshot boundary's `isPercentOf(limit)` vocabulary is the precedent).
- Malformed windows drop individually in `sanitizeQuotaView` with `droppedWindows` counting them (existing #2429 behaviour for shape failures) — the pool and feed survive.
- Regression tests in `test/feed.test.ts` next to the existing #2429 gate tests: impossible/garbage/empty `resetsAt`, negative `used`/`limit`, out-of-range `percent` all drop; the well-formed window fixture is unchanged.
- No change to `windowPercent`/`poolState` semantics for windows that pass the gate.

## Dedup

Distinct from #2470 (quota-extract emitting unvalidated `resetsAt` upstream — this is the feed-ingest gate that must refuse them regardless of source), #3365 (snapshot **rollup** guard re-admitting shapes), #2416 (`parseQuotaCurrent` window entries in the gatherer overlay), and #3396/#3393/#3379 (tier-items / actions / snapshot-records date gates). Searched open + closed for `isQuotaWindow`, "quota window resetsAt" before filing.

title: aggregator(feed): charge gates accept negative/zero amounts and non-date 'at' — isChargeRow and isUnmatchedCharge pass rows no producer can emit, falsifying the charges total and attention-flag severity
