labels.description: has a fix task queued

body:
## Finding

The feed's two charge gates — `isChargeRow` and `isUnmatchedCharge` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts` — check only the *shape* of a charge (strings present, `amountUsd` a finite number). They accept values no producer can emit: a negative or zero `amountUsd`, and an `at` that is not a date at all (`"banana"`, `""`, `2026-02-30`, `2026-13-01`). Those rows survive `loadFeed`'s drop-and-count sanitization and are rendered / converted to attention flags verbatim, so one drifted or hand-edited feed row falsifies the charges strip total and publishes a nonsense attention flag instead of being dropped and counted like other malformed rows.

## Evidence (main d61aec48, verified this run)

- `feed.ts:350-353` `isUnmatchedCharge`: `merchant` string, `isFiniteNumber(amountUsd)`, `at` string — no positivity, no date check.
- `feed.ts:358-368` `isChargeRow`: same shape for `at`/`amountUsd`.
- Producer invariants the gates fail to mirror: `charges-match.ts:195` filters candidates to `amountUsd > 0` before any `ChargeRow`/`UnmatchedCharge` can exist; `charges-collect.ts:42-51` requires `at` to start `YYYY-MM-DD` and slices it to 10 chars. A negative/zero amount or a non-date `at` in a feed is therefore always corruption, never data.
- Consumers trust the gate: `render.ts:1949-1952` renders `c.at` verbatim and totals `usage.charges.reduce((sum, c) => sum + c.amountUsd, 0)`; `sources/live.ts:899-904` maps each unmatched charge to an attention flag with `detail: "$<amountUsd> on <at> …"` and `severity: u.amountUsd` (flags sort by severity, `derive.ts:885`).
- The shared real-date helper already exists and is already imported by feed.ts: `isIsoDate` (`validate.ts:113`, used for the orchestration section's `generatedAt`).

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-chargegate/`, real `feed.ts`/`charges-match.ts` from origin/main — `feed.ts` md5 `3bae075e` identical at d61aec48 and at laptop HEAD 4501d41e; probe copy differs from main by exactly the one missing `}` documented in #3452, diff shown in the probe dir):

- Control: valid ChargeRow → `true`; valid UnmatchedCharge → `true`; producer `matchCharges(+12.50)` → 1 row.
- `isChargeRow`: amount `-5` → `true`, `0` → `true`, `at: "banana"` → `true`, `"2026-02-30"` → `true`, `"2026-13-01"` → `true`, `""` → `true`.
- `isUnmatchedCharge`: amount `-5` → `true`, `0` → `true`, `at: "banana"` → `true`, `"2026-02-30"` → `true`.
- Renderer expression on `[12.50, -5]` rows: total `$7.50` instead of `$12.50`.
- Live flag for the negative/banana unmatched row: detail `$-5.00 on banana`, severity `-5`.
- Producer control: `matchCharges(-5 candidate)` → 0 rows — the pipeline itself never emits what the gate accepts.

## Why it matters

`charges` / `chargesAttention` are the hub's charge-evidence surfaces (§2.4). #2445 hardened these gates against *shape* damage (a malformed row crashing /quota); this is the semantic remainder: a row that is well-shaped but impossible passes sanitization silently — no drop count, no provenance note — understates the period total, and turns into an attention flag with a negative severity and a nonsense date. The fix belongs at the same gate, so the existing drop-and-count machinery in `loadFeed` surfaces the loss exactly as it does for shape damage.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isChargeRow` and `isUnmatchedCharge` refuse `amountUsd <= 0` and any `at` that is not a real ISO calendar date (the shared `isIsoDate` from validate.ts, or an equivalent real-calendar check — `2026-02-30` and `2026-13-01` must fail, not roll over).
- Such rows drop through the existing `loadFeed` sanitization with their counts surfaced (`chargesDropped` / `chargesAttentionDropped`), never render, and never become attention flags.
- Regression tests beside the existing feed gate tests cover at least: negative amount, zero amount, `at: "banana"`, `at: "2026-02-30"`, for both gates; the valid-row controls still pass and existing feed tests stay green.
- Note: on current main this work sits behind #3452 (feed.ts does not parse); the gate change and its tests should land on a feed.ts that parses.

Dedup: #2445 (closed) covered shape/crash only — its acceptance never mentions amount sign or date validity; #3428 is `isBurnSegment` (quota burn rows, different gate/fields); #3224 is the producer-side verb tier in produce-charge-candidates.ts; #2194/#2448 are producer-side date guards in charges-collect.ts. No open or closed issue covers the feed charge gates' amount/date semantics.

body:
Design (design-architect pass 31, 2026-11-01). Full design doc: `files/designs/code-id-plain-output-rendering.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audited at origin/main `70c20625`. No `user/review`: every origin carries explicit acceptance with a verified probe, and the judgment calls below (one shared character set; escape vs strip by surface kind) are the architect's recorded decisions.

## Summary

pkgs/id's plain-text ruling (#1613, recorded in `src/commands/text.rs`'s module doc) is *a printer never lets a value break row structure* — but every guard in the family tests `char::is_control()` (category Cc only), so Unicode format characters (category Cf) reach the terminal raw and act on the rendering: bidi overrides/isolates (U+202A–U+202E, U+2066–U+2069) visually reorder the fields after them, and zero-width characters (U+200B, U+FEFF, U+00AD) make look-alike rows with different bytes — the Trojan-Source class applied to live CLI output. Three surfaces, one class:

- **#2839** — `plain_field` (`commands/text.rs:42-44`): a gossip peer name carrying only U+202E returns byte-identical unquoted; quoted, the override is still raw inside the quotes, before the blob-count/timestamp columns it can falsify.
- **#3111** — the shared `key=value` renderer `text()` (`commands/group.rs:64-72`; group/doc/claim via `tokens()`): Cf is raw in both paths — the trigger is `is_whitespace() || is_control()`, and the quoted path is a serde_json literal, which never escapes Cf. Claim values are other nodes' signed tag events (ingest checks length + NFC only; Cf is NFC-stable) sitting before the row's real `author=`/`event=` fields.
- **#3089** — `id world list`'s plain branch (`commands/world.rs:683`) prints host-supplied world names verbatim (neither renderer used): a newline forges a fully-formed extra row, a tab forges columns. Names arrive from a host's wire reply with no validation; #1613's ruling exists precisely for non-conforming hosts.

The character set already exists in-tree, stated once: `petname.rs:237-262` `is_format_char` is the complete Unicode 16 Cf range set, with the doc ruling that Cf characters "are invisible or reorder the text around them" — petnames refuse them at ingest (#1674), but the definition is a private fn the renderers never saw. `world/util.rs:69-84`'s sanitizers (`sanitize_display_name`/`sanitize_chat`) share the `is_control`-only blind spot one layer down.

## The contract (recorded decisions)

> **A plain-text field is row-safe only if it contains no character that can act on the terminal: no structure character (Cc controls, U+2028/U+2029) and no format character (category Cf, the crate's one shared set). Every plain renderer in pkgs/id accounts for both classes; the disposition differs by surface kind — row renderers escape, stripping sanitizers strip, ingest validators refuse — and no surface re-derives the character set.**

1. **One set: the petname set, shared.** `is_format_char` is promoted to a single `pub(crate)` definition all phases use. It includes the zero-width characters #2839 left to triage (U+200B–U+200D, U+FEFF, U+00AD, U+2060): #3111's look-alike argument covers them, and a renderer-specific subset is the per-site re-derivation this design stops. Recorded cost: a ZWJ-emoji or ZWNJ-joined name renders quoted-with-escapes in row renderers — content preserved in full, JSON-parseable — and petnames already refuse these characters outright. Reversible in one place if fleet evidence shows real names harmed.
2. **Escape, don't strip, at row renderers; the two renderers stay distinct.** Their trigger asymmetries are deliberate (space quotes in `key=value`, never in TSV). Cf joins each trigger and is rendered `\uXXXX` inside quotes (`plain_field`'s existing form). For `group::text` the quoted path must escape Cf itself — serde_json's `to_string()` alone never will; that escaping is Phase 2's real work, not the trigger widening. Ordinary values render byte-identically; `--json` unchanged everywhere.
3. **The printer, not ingest.** No new ingest validation for peer names, claim values or world names — #1613's ruling and #3089's non-conforming-host model make rendering the only total gate. Existing ingest checks stay as they are; the closing audit dispositions them separately.

Alternatives rejected in the doc: fixing the three sites independently as filed (the pattern that produced the family — #3111 exists because #2839's fix wouldn't touch its code); one unified renderer (trigger semantics genuinely differ; the shared artefact is the set + contract); stripping at renderers (destroys the printed-in-full, JSON-recoverable property and makes different values print identically); refusing at ingest as the primary fix (cannot clean stored values or non-conforming hosts; refusing other nodes' signed claim events is a federation decision); a bidi-only subset (misses the look-alike half, creates a second drifting set).

## Phases (adopted origins — no parallel issues)

- **Phase 1** = #2839 (`plain_field` honours Cf; creates the shared set + `text.rs` doc truth-up; lands first).
- **Phase 2** = #3111 (`group::text` honours Cf, incl. escaping inside the quoted path; gated on Phase 1 for the shared set definition only).
- **Phase 3a** = #3089 (world list plain branch routes the name through `plain_field`; marker comparison stays on the raw name; not gated — correct today for structure characters, Cf coverage arrives with Phase 1).
- **Phase 3b** = closing inventory + contract statement (filed as a sub-issue, gated on Phases 1–2): every remaining `is_control`-only guard in `pkgs/id/src` dispositioned escape / strip / refuse / deliberately-local with reason — starting population includes the `world/util.rs` sanitizers (expected: strip-Cf for `sanitize_display_name`; `sanitize_chat` decided against its downstream rendering), the directory/world/ssh validator sites, and `world_presentation`/`world_session` payload validation (#3265's width mechanism is different and not adopted); contract + the set's home and Unicode version written into the `text.rs` module doc; closing evidence here, including the sibling-audit evidence #2839's acceptance requires.

Open questions stay in the design doc (ingest-side Cf refusal as defence in depth — federation decision, evidence-gated; `sanitize_chat`'s final disposition if ZWJ-stripping would corrupt legitimate chat text; shared-set placement; ANSI/OSC terminal sequences — no filed instance).

Standing-candidate note: passes 28–30 named this family the standing candidate for this pass (displaced once at pass 30 by #3352's cluster, under its stated terms). Same-day clusters assessed and not taken: the aggregator impossible-date family is #2576's already-stated strict-date rule applied per site; the new operator value-option filings #3449/#3415/#3419 are #3352's contract — provider-catalog-sync is already a named candidate in #3353's closing inventory.

body:
## Finding

PR #3042 (merged, merge commit `8df594037e0756bfb1c53704c28aca9d7abb2274`) replaced the `secrets.References` scan with a single lexical token pass and documented three deliberate blind spots in the package doc. They are still present on current main — `pkgs/mcpx/internal/secrets/refs.go:25-31` (verified 2026-11-01 against main `70c206250c`):

> Known blind spots, kept deliberately: binding is source-global (a name bound anywhere counts as declared everywhere, with no block-scoped shadowing precision); a "/" directly after a value-closing "}" is read as division, so a regex literal starting a statement right after a block may be scanned as code; parameters of method shorthand and destructuring assignments without a declaration keyword are not collected as bindings.

No open or closed issue tracks any of the three (searches for the blind spots / method shorthand / destructuring-assignment bindings / refs follow-ups return only #1644 itself, verified 2026-11-01). The sibling delimiter scanner in `internal/scripting` got tracked follow-ups for exactly this class of gap (#3334, closed; #3346, open) — the References scanner's gaps have no equivalent tracker, so they exist only as a code comment.

## The three blind spots, by error direction

1. **Source-global binding — fail-open.** `References` is the sole input to `Registry.Preflight` / `refuseScript`. If a script binds a name anywhere (e.g. a function parameter or local named `demo` in one function), a genuine bare `demo.<tool>` reach in another scope where `demo` is *not* bound is treated as a local reference and cleared — the preflight silently does not refuse a script that reaches a configured namespace.
2. **Regex after a value-closing `}` read as division — fail-safe.** A regex literal starting a statement right after a block is scanned as code, so reach-shaped text inside it can be reported as a phantom reference and refuse a script that reaches nothing.
3. **Method-shorthand parameters and declaration-less destructuring assignments not collected as bindings — fail-safe.** Names bound only in those shapes can be misread as namespace reaches, again refusing scripts that reach nothing.

## Why it matters

Blind spot 1 weakens the one gate this scanner exists to be, in a shape an author can hit by accident (a common short name bound in one helper, a namespace reach in another). Blind spots 2 and 3 erode trust in refusals. Documented-in-code is not tracked: nothing will ever re-check whether the trade-off still holds as the scanner evolves.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage rules on each of the three blind spots individually: fix, or accept with the rationale recorded on this issue (not only in the code comment).
- [ ] If blind spot 1 is fixed: block/scope-aware binding (or an equivalently conservative rule) with `refs_test.go` cases pinning the cross-scope shape — name bound in one function, genuine reach of the same name in another — plus the existing suite unchanged and passing.
- [ ] If blind spots 2 or 3 are fixed: regression cases in `refs_test.go` for a statement-leading regex after a block, method-shorthand parameters, and declaration-less destructuring assignments.
- [ ] If any blind spot is accepted: the package doc comment is updated to reference this issue's ruling, so the next reader finds the decision, not just the caveat.

Found by: pr-diff-review run 2026-11-01 (PR #3042 in batch 3042–3063). Cross-repo check: the scanner lives in `pkgs/mcpx` in this repo; the dezren39/nix mcpx packaging consumes upstream code and has no separate copy of `refs.go` to fix — one issue here tracks the finding.

body:
# aggregator(collect-github-billing): --year/--month/--user values are never validated — NaN, month 13, month 0, fractional and flag-token values go straight into the billing API URL, and the failure is blamed on the gh token scope

## Evidence (verified this run, main f1eac954)

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-github-billing.ts`:

- `:42-45` — `argValue(flag)` returns `process.argv[i + 1]` unchecked: a flag token is accepted as the previous flag's value, and a trailing flag yields `undefined`.
- `:72-74` — `year`/`month` are `Number(argValue(...))` with no integer/range check; `user` is the raw string. All three are interpolated straight into the API path at `:52` (``users/${user}/settings/billing/usage?year=${year}&month=${month}``).
- `:58-61` — on any `gh` failure the script's error says a 404 "usually means the scope, not a missing user", so a self-inflicted bad URL is reported as a token-scope problem.

Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-ghbilling/`; real script + `src/`, sha256 of the script `5f8d8100…` matched to main; `gh` stubbed to log its argv and return `{"usageItems":[]}`):

| Invocation | API call issued | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `--year 2026 --month 10 --print` (control) | `users/dezren39/settings/billing/usage?year=2026&month=10` | exit 0, correct |
| `--month banana` | `…?year=2026&month=NaN` | exit 0, prints `2026-NaN` |
| `--month 13` | `…&month=13` | exit 0 |
| `--month 0` | `…&month=0` | exit 0 |
| `--year 2026.5 --month 2.5` | `…?year=2026.5&month=2.5` | exit 0 |
| `--month --print` | `…&month=NaN` (the flag token is consumed as the value, and `--print` still takes effect) | exit 0 |
| `--user --print` | `users/--print/settings/billing/usage?…` | exit 0 |
| `--print --user` (trailing) | user silently falls back to the default `dezren39` | exit 0 |

Against the real endpoint every malformed case 404s, and the script then misreports it as a missing `user` scope on the gh token — the exact misdiagnosis the error text at `:58-61` was written to prevent, pointed the wrong way.

## Why it matters

This is the daily GitHub billing collector (#1051): its records feed the usage snapshot store. A typo'd month in a manual or scheduled invocation either fails with a misleading scope error (sending the operator to re-auth `gh` instead of fixing the argument) or, for a trailing flag, silently collects a different month/user than the one named. Every sibling script that validates its period args locally fails fast with a usage error; this one validates nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--year` must be an integer in a sane range (e.g. 2000–2100) and `--month` an integer 1–12; anything else (non-numeric, fractional, out of range) exits non-zero with a usage error naming the bad value, before any `gh` call.
- A value-taking flag that is last, or whose next token is another flag, is a usage error — never silently replaced by the default and never consumed as a value.
- `--user` must be a non-empty, non-flag value.
- The `gh`-failure error keeps its scope hint only for calls whose arguments passed validation.
- Tests pin: the control case, `banana`, `13`, `0`, `2.5`, flag-as-value, and trailing-flag cases.

Distinct from #2493 (billing *items* never validated — response side; this is the request/CLI side) and from the per-script flag-token filings for other scripts (#3295, #3330, #3333, #3415 — different files). Family: #3352/#3353 argument-contract inventory.

body:
## Problem

`bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs` parses its options with a blind next-token helper and never validates the argument list:

- `main()` at bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs:687-698 — `opt(name, dflt)` returns `argv[idx + 1]` whatever it is; the flag set is `new Set(argv)`; no argument is ever rejected.
- `--config` (:694-695), `--models-dev` (:696), `--source-dir` (:697) and `--repo` (in the `--open-pr` path) all go through `opt()`; `--apply` / `--open-pr` / `--json` are membership tests on the same argv.

Consequences, all verified below:

1. **A flag token is consumed as a value.** `--config --apply` tries to open a file literally named `--apply`.
2. **A trailing value-flag crashes unnamed.** `--config` as the last argument makes `opt()` return `undefined`, and the run dies with a raw `TypeError` that never mentions `--config`.
3. **One token is consumed twice.** `--models-dev --apply` takes `--apply` as the models.dev spec (the fetch of a URL named `--apply` fails and the cross-check silently degrades to "unavailable") AND still honours `--apply` as the apply flag — so the run **writes the config** with the models.dev cross-check silently lost (entry limits that come from models.dev are absent), and in `--apply` mode no report is printed that would show the loss.
4. **Unknown arguments are silently ignored.** A typo'd `--aply` performs a dry-run report and exits 3 (validated additions found) with the config untouched and no word that the flag was not recognised — the operator asked for an apply and got a report.

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-11-01)

Code: bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs:687-702 (`main`/`opt`), :463 (`fs.readFileSync(configPath)` in `runSync`).

Laptop probe (sha-matched copy of the script, sha256 `08e742c0cc241413f5a478040ee68174555d68c7fa34b9f3ccc6f2c53204f7cb`, identical to sandbox main `98a4eb8f`; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-catalogsync/`, script `run.sh`; fully offline: minimal config with one `claude-code` provider, `--source-dir` snapshot `18749.json` advertising one new model `new-model`, local empty models.dev file):

- Control dry-run → exit 3, `+ VALIDATED ADDITION: new-model`, config untouched.
- Control `--apply` → exit 0, `new-model` written into the config.
- `--aply` (typo) → exit 3, report only, config untouched, **no warning** that `--aply` is not a recognised argument.
- `--config --apply …` → exit 2, `[catalog-sync] fatal: Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '--apply'` (runSync at :463).
- `… --config` (trailing) → exit 2, `TypeError [ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE]: The "path" argument must be of type string … Received undefined` — `--config` is never named.
- `--config cfg --source-dir src --models-dev --apply` → exit 0 and the **config was written** (new-model added): `--apply` was used both as the `--models-dev` value and as the apply flag; the models.dev load failed on the "URL" `--apply` and degraded silently.

## Why it matters

This is the PR-based catalog updater for the live OpenCode config (#1297): `--apply` writes `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` in place. Its argument handling fails in both directions — a typo silently turns an apply into a report, and a misplaced flag silently turns a cross-checked apply into an un-cross-checked one that still writes. The script's own contract (dry-run exit 3 vs apply exit 0) only protects an operator whose flags parse exactly as intended, and nothing tells them when they did not.

## Distinct from

- #3430 (same script: `stripJsonc` trailing-comma string-awareness — a different function and failure).
- #2827 (same script: `enumerateProxy` /v1/models shape — enumeration, not argv).
- #2235 (same script: symlink entry-point check).
- #3352 / #3353 (the repo-wide strict-argv design/audit — this is the per-script verified instance for provider-catalog-sync, as with the sibling filings it tracks).
- #3297 (sync-models.mjs, the predecessor script — different file; its fix does not touch this one).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any unrecognised argument aborts with a usage error and a non-zero exit **before** any file read, fetch, or write.
- [ ] A value-flag (`--config`, `--models-dev`, `--source-dir`, `--repo`) followed by another flag token or by nothing aborts with a usage error naming that flag, instead of consuming the flag or crashing with a raw TypeError/ENOENT.
- [ ] No argv token is consumed twice: `--models-dev --apply` is a usage error, not an apply with a silently lost cross-check.
- [ ] `--apply`, `--open-pr`, `--json` and the documented value options keep working exactly as before (the probe's control cases: dry-run exit 3 with no write; `--apply` exit 0 with the validated addition written).
- [ ] A stubbed/offline probe or test pins the cases above (typo'd flag, flag-as-value, trailing flag, double consumption).

title: fleet: cargo target duplication across worktrees — shared compile cache, seeding, and a storage cap

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

body:
## Problem

Every fleet worktree compiles the same dependency graph into its own cargo `target` dir, and the storage + CPU cost keeps biting:

- 2026-10-26 cleanup: 84 cargo target dirs totalling **1,182.8 GiB** deleted from this laptop.
- 2026-11-01 ~01:26 CST: /home hit **100% full** (0 bytes free) — the immediate cause of a failed NixOS switch (SQLite fetcher-cache I/O error). Drew ordered a target/cache cleanup; disk recovered to ~55%.
- 2026-11-01 ~03:23 CST, roughly two hours after that cleanup deleted every target dir: **12 fleet worktree `pkgs/id/target` dirs already exist again, 198G total** across fleet + primary + worktrees — each one a from-scratch copy of the same ~760-package graph (debug and release profiles multiply it further).
- Same night: 12 concurrent lane cargo builds drove load to **118 on 16 cores**, and the nix side built the `id` package twice concurrently from divergent checkout sources (different drv/output hashes for identical intent) — one was a stale Oct-30 toplevel build still holding daemon slots; both had to be found and killed by hand during a production switch.
- Nothing is configured today: no sccache (not installed), no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, no shared cargo config on the laptop.

## What to evaluate (measure, then adopt what the data supports)

1. **sccache** (or equivalent content-addressed compile cache) shared across all worktrees — kills the repeated dependency compilation without target-dir locking between concurrent lanes.
2. **Shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`** per repo across worktrees — proven manually on 2026-10-26 (a worktree pointed at the primary's target reuses the warm cache); the trade-off is cargo's target-dir lock serializing concurrent lane builds. May suit a hybrid: shared for deps-heavy phases, per-lane for final artifacts, if the tooling allows.
3. **Cache seeding** for fresh worktrees (reflink/copy-on-write copy of a warm target where the filesystem supports it) so a new lane never starts cold.
4. **Profile discipline** for lanes: build only the profile the task needs (check vs test vs release), instead of several profiles per worktree by default.
5. **Nix side:** a shared binary cache for the fleet's own builds (the `id` package and the system toplevel) so identical checkouts substitute instead of rebuilding; plus keeping fleet checkouts converged on the same main so drv hashes dedupe in the store.
6. **A storage cap with a janitor**: a bounded, automatic pruning rule for target dirs (age/size based, never touching a target with a build in flight) so /home can never silently refill to 100% again — tonight's disk-full broke a production switch.

## Acceptance

- Measured before/after on the laptop: total target-dir storage across the fleet after a representative day of lane work, and cold-start build time for a fresh worktree.
- The adopted setup is the default for new fleet worktrees (encoded wherever lanes are provisioned), not a per-lane manual trick.
- No lane workflow regression: concurrent lanes can still build without corrupting each other's artifacts.

Related: #3195 (pkgs/id build-time review — its build-hygiene line names sccache / shared target), and the pkgs/id crate-split issue filed alongside this one (splitting reduces per-build work; this issue removes the duplicated work).

body:
# id(directory_mail): SMTP reply reader accepts any non-`-` byte as the code terminator — `2500 …`, `250OK` and a `2500` multiline tail all pass as reply 250

## Problem

`pkgs/id/src/directory_mail.rs` — `SmtpSink`'s reply reader `expect()` (lines 233–252) never validates the byte after the 3-digit reply code.

```rust
ensure!(
    line.get(..3).and_then(|c| c.parse::<u16>().ok()) == Some(code),
    "the mail relay replied: {line}"
);
if line.as_bytes().get(3) != Some(&b'-') {
    return Ok(());
}
```

It checks only that the first three bytes parse to the expected code, and that the fourth byte is not `-` (the multiline continuation marker). **Any** other fourth byte — a digit, a letter, punctuation — is treated as the end of a successful reply. An SMTP reply code is exactly three digits followed by a space (or end of line for a bare code), per RFC 5321 §4.2; a line whose fourth byte is anything else is not that code at all:

- `2500 bogus code` is read as reply **250** (the code is 2500, or 250 glued to a `0` — either way not `250<SP>`);
- `250OK no separator` is read as reply **250**;
- a multiline reply `250-first line` / `2500 final line` is accepted as a complete 250 reply at its final line.

Every stage of the exchange uses this reader: the greeting (`expect(..., 220)`, :168), EHLO / MAIL FROM / RCPT TO (`smtp_command(..., 250)`, :169–183), DATA (`354`, :184) and the post-body acceptance (`expect(..., 250)`, :193) — so a malformed reply at any stage is taken as that stage's success, and the sink reports the confirmation mail as sent.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `674f7eee`)

`directory_mail.rs` sha256 `dc6f7935072687eee55b0a659ed48d1aa2d24b51a8445808719c38688a7da682` — identical on the sandbox clone, the laptop clone, and origin/main.

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-smtpcode/` (the probe crate compiles `directory_mail.rs` itself as a module — copied from the laptop clone with only the 7 leading `//!` module-doc lines dropped, since those cannot survive inclusion as a submodule; `diff` verified every code byte from line 8 on is identical — and drives the real `SmtpSink::send` against scripted fake relays on loopback):

```
control-good        => OK
control-wrong-code  => ERR the mail relay replied: 251 not 250   (EHLO answered 251 — the code check itself works)
case-greeting-2200  => OK    (greeting "2200 fake ready" accepted as 220)
case-ehlo-2500      => OK    (EHLO reply "2500 bogus code" accepted as 250)
case-rcpt-250OK     => OK    (RCPT reply "250OK no separator" accepted as 250)
case-multiline-tail => OK    ("250-first line" / "2500 final line" accepted as a complete 250)
control-multiline   => OK    ("250-first line" / "250 final line" — well-formed multiline still works)
```

So `send()` returns `Ok` — the confirmation mail is reported sent — for every malformed-code case, while a genuinely different code (251) is refused as it should be.

## Why it matters

The relay is loopback and operator-chosen, but it is a separate process: a wrong service squatting on the configured port, a buggy/misconfigured local daemon, or a spam-filter front-end that speaks a near-SMTP dialect can answer with lines that merely *start* with the expected digits. Today the sink cannot tell that apart from success at any stage — greeting, envelope, or final acceptance — so a directory confirmation code (the sign-in path this sink serves, `world_session` awaits `sink.send(...)`) can be reported delivered when the relay never actually accepted the message with the required reply. Every neighbouring gate in this file is strict about shape (loopback-only relay, ASCII/plain-address checks, control-free subject); the reply code's own shape is the one unchecked piece. This is distinct from #1899 (the same reader's missing deadline/line bound — a hang, not a misread code) and #2637 (the address-shape gate).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `expect()` accepts a line as the final line of the expected reply only when the code is exactly three digits and the fourth byte is a space or the line ends there (bare code); a fourth byte of `-` continues a multiline reply, and anything else fails the send with the existing "the mail relay replied: …" error.
- [ ] The rule applies uniformly to every stage (greeting 220, EHLO/MAIL/RCPT 250, DATA 354, post-body 250, QUIT 221).
- [ ] Regression tests with the fake-relay harness already in `directory_mail.rs`'s tests (or equivalent): `2500 …`, `250OK`, and a `2500` multiline final line are each refused; well-formed single-line (`250 ok`, bare `250`) and multiline (`250-…` / `250 …`) replies still pass; a wrong code (251 for 250) still fails.
- [ ] No change to the timeout behaviour tracked in #1899, and no change to what a successful send means.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `directory_mail` / SMTP reply / `expect` on 2026-11-01 — #1899 (reply-reader deadline + line bound), #1788 (CommandSink timeout), #2637 (plain_address shape), #2404 (OutboxSink headers) are the neighbours; none covers the reply-code terminator shape.

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/record-claude-launch.ts` reads every value-taking option through one helper that takes the next argv token blindly:

```ts
function arg(name: string): string | undefined {
  const i = process.argv.indexOf(`--${name}`);
  return i >= 0 ? process.argv[i + 1] : undefined;
}
```

(record-claude-launch.ts:29-32). A token that is itself a flag is accepted as the previous flag's value, and the same token is then consumed a second time as a flag in its own right. The script exits 0 and appends the corrupted record to the launch-records JSONL the fleet-feed collector merges into the session registry (collect-fleet-feed.ts:603-611, `parseLaunchRecords`).

## Evidence (verified this run, main `674f7eee`)

Real script run under bun on the laptop (script sha256 `fd0d3309…`, identical on sandbox and laptop clones; probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-claudelaunch/`, log `probe-run.log`):

- Control `--label "Slice 3 builder" --task developing-today/code#123` → correct record: label `Slice 3 builder`, `taskRefs: ["developing-today/code#123"]`.
- `--label "Slice" --task --model gpt-x` → `"taskRefs": ["--model"]` **and** `"model": "gpt-x"` — the `--model` token is consumed twice: once as the task ref, once as the flag. The session's task linkage now points at a ref that is not a ref.
- `--label --id claude-x` → `"id": "claude-x"`, `"label": "--id"` — the dashboard's identity registry gains a session whose display name is a flag.
- `--label "Slice" --model --file ./out.jsonl` → `"model": "--file"` — and `--file` still took effect (the record landed in out.jsonl), so the flag token served as both value and flag.

Downstream: `taskRefs` elements are rendered through `refUrl`/`parseRef` (model.ts:452-470), which throws `not a repo-qualified ref` on a value like `--model` — the malformed-ref render crash class already tracked for registry records in #2485, here planted at the producer by an ordinary flag-ordering slip (a `--task` with its value forgotten, or flags reordered).

## Why it matters

This script is how Muse sessions register themselves in the identity registry that drives the dashboard's task ↔ session linkage (#906 §3). There is no later validation of the label or model, and the taskRefs are trusted as refs. One mistyped invocation silently writes a record that misnames the session, links it to a non-existent task, and can feed a throwing ref into the session views — with exit 0 and a success line, so the launcher never notices.

Related: this is one more hand-rolled argv parser for the #3352/#3353 strict-argument-contract inventory (it is not among #3353's named starting candidates); it can be dispositioned there as this issue's follow-up.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A value-taking option (`--label`, `--id`, `--parent`, `--task`, `--model`, `--status`, `--file`) whose next token is missing or starts with `--` is refused with a usage error (exit non-zero) and **no record is appended**.
- [ ] The same token is never consumed as both a value and a flag.
- [ ] Control behaviour unchanged: a normal `--label … --task owner/repo#N` invocation records exactly the given label and ref; repeated `--task` still collects multiple refs.
- [ ] A test or scripted check covers at least: flag-as-value for `--task`, flag-as-value for `--label`, a value flag in last position, and the normal control.

## Dedup

Searched open + closed issues for `record-claude-launch`, `launch-records`, and the flag-as-value class: the trailing/flag-like filings cover other scripts (#3330 backfill `--dir`, #3333 charges-producer `--start/--end/--out`, #3295 append `--by`, #3312 mcpx docs-history); none covers this script. #3353's closing inventory is expected to disposition remaining parsers — this filing is the named follow-up that item 2(b) of its scope calls for.

body:
## Bug

`isSnapshotRollup` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts:91`) checks the rollup's record count with only:

```ts
if (typeof r.count !== "number" || !(r.count >= 1)) return false;
```

That refuses 0 and negatives, but a count is a count of raw records — it must be a positive integer. Today the gate also passes:

- a fractional count (`1.5`), and
- an infinite count (`Infinity` — reachable from a real JSONL line, because `JSON.parse("1e999")` is `Infinity`, so a rollup line carrying `"count": 1e999` parses to an infinite count).

`count` is not decorative. Compaction trusts it arithmetically: `compactSnapshotMonth` sums existing rollup counts into the report (`snapshots.ts:725` per-service `before += r.count`; `:732` `recordsBefore: records.length + existing.reduce((n, r) => n + r.count, 0)`), and re-compaction seeds from existing rollups and increments the carried count (`aggAddRecord`, `:154` `o.count += 1`), so a fractional count stays fractional forever (1.5 → 2.5 → 3.5 …) and an infinite count makes every later compaction report for that month report `recordsBefore: Infinity`. Rollup files are kept indefinitely, so the corrupted count is re-seeded on every compaction rather than aging out.

This is the one numeric field #3365's hardening of this same gate did not cover: its acceptance pins the timestamp, `limit`/`resetsAt`, pair-value, and `month` rules, but not `count`.

## Evidence (verified this run, main ba2e97dd)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-gendates/probe.ts` (Bun 1.4.2), importing the real `snapshots.ts` from the laptop clone — `snapshots.ts` md5 298f32a5, identical on sandbox main ba2e97dd and the probe clone; output in `probe.txt` in the same directory:

- Control rollup (`count: 3`, otherwise well-formed) → `isSnapshotRollup` = `true`.
- `count: 1.5` → **`true`**.
- `count: Infinity` → **`true`**; the same value reached via `JSON.parse` of a line with `"count":1e999` → `Infinity` → gate **`true`**.
- Controls on the existing rule: `count: 0` → `false`, `count: -2` → `false` (already refused).

## Why it matters

The snapshot store is the usage hub's history, and its compaction reports ("records before/after", per-service counts) are the operator's evidence that retention is lossless. A count the gate certifies but no writer can produce silently falsifies those reports for the affected month — permanently, because rollups never expire and each compaction re-seeds from the last. Every other count-like field in this codebase's gates is checked as an integer (e.g. `isRepoCensus` uses `Number.isInteger`); this one was left as a bare range check.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSnapshotRollup` refuses a `count` that is not a positive integer (`Number.isInteger(count) && count >= 1`): fractional, infinite, and NaN counts fail the gate, alongside the already-refused 0/negatives.
- A rollup line with `"count": 1e999` or `"count": 1.5` in a rollup file is dropped by `readAll`/`rollupKeys`/compaction seeding like any other malformed rollup line; a well-formed rollup still passes and expands unchanged.
- Regression tests beside the existing snapshot gate tests pin each refused shape plus the valid control.
- No change to the rollup file format or to compaction output for valid rollups.

Distinct from #3365 (same function's timestamp/limit/resetsAt/pair/month rules — its acceptance does not mention `count`), #3364 (coverage census counts), #3285 (compact script `--months` argument).

body:
## Bug

Two fleet-feed section gates validate their `generatedAt` stamp with bare `Date.parse`, so a day-overflow date that never existed passes as a real collection time:

- `isAaSection` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts:1096` absent form, `:1100` ok form): `Number.isFinite(Date.parse(s.generatedAt))`.
- `isDnsSection` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/dns.ts:79`): the same expression.

`Date.parse("2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z")` does not fail — it rolls over to 2026-03-02. So a section stamped February 30 passes both gates and is served/rendered as data collected on March 2: the live source builds provenance from it (`feedAgeText`, `collected ${feed.aa.generatedAt}`, `register parsed ${feed.dns.generatedAt}` in `src/sources/live.ts`), and `renderAa`/`renderDns` print it via `fmtDate`. The stamp is the freshness signal for both pages; a fabricated March date makes stale or hand-edited data look freshly collected.

The codebase already has the strict primitive for exactly this: `isIsoDate`/`parseIsoDate` in `src/validate.ts` re-checks calendar components so 2026-02-30 fails instead of rolling over, and sibling gates use it (`orchestrationSectionProblem` checks `isIsoDate(s.generatedAt)`; `isSnapshotRecord` uses it for `ts`/`resetsAt` with the comment "Date.parse rolls 2026-02-30 into March, so the strict primitive is the gate"). The AA and DNS gates were never migrated.

## Evidence (verified this run, main ba2e97dd)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-gendates/probe.ts` (Bun 1.4.2), importing the real `aa.ts`/`dns.ts`/`validate.ts` from the laptop clone — `aa.ts` md5 2dc10e70, `dns.ts` md5 03aab48e, `validate.ts` md5 2078ddfd, identical on sandbox main ba2e97dd and the probe clone; full output in `probe.txt` in the same directory:

- `Date.parse("2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z")` → `2026-03-02T00:00:00.000Z` (rollover); `isIsoDate(same)` → `false`.
- AA control (real stamp): `isAaSection` → `true`. With `generatedAt: "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z"` → **`true`** (ok form and absent form both).
- DNS control (real stamp): `isDnsSection` → `true`. With the Feb-30 stamp → **`true`**.
- (Month 13 is already refused, because `Date.parse` returns NaN for it — the hole is specifically day-of-month overflow: Feb 29 in a non-leap year, Feb 30/31, Apr/Jun/Sep/Nov 31.)

## Why it matters

`generatedAt` is how every surface answers "how old is this data". A stamp that silently becomes a different, real-looking date defeats the staleness banners and provenance lines these pages rely on, and it does so invisibly — no NaN, no "unknown", just the wrong day. The feed is a file boundary shared with the collector, older feeds, and hand/backfill tooling; the section gates are the one place supposed to keep impossible stamps out.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isAaSection` (both ok and absent forms) and `isDnsSection` refuse a `generatedAt` that is not a real ISO calendar date — at minimum the day-overflow shapes above — using the shared `isIsoDate` primitive from `validate.ts` (or an equivalent component re-check).
- A Feb-30-stamped AA or DNS section in the feed is treated as absent/invalid by the live source (existing provenance wording), not rendered with a March 2 collection date.
- Regression tests beside the existing aa/dns gate tests: Feb-30, Feb-29-2026 (non-leap), and Apr-31 stamps fail both gates; the well-formed fixture sections still pass unchanged.
- No change to the on-disk feed format or to what the collector emits for valid sections.

Distinct from: #2242 (health.ts age computation over dns/aa stamps — different file, NaN/future ages; these are the section gates themselves certifying an impossible date), #2199 (DNS register *renewal* dates in `parseDnsRegister`), #2412/#2415 (dns/aa gates' unchecked numeric/thresholds/sources fields — crash class, not the stamp), #3396/#3393 (tier-items/actions date gates).

## Problem
In the `pkgs/id` test binary, `cli::tests::test_cli_parse_cat` aborts with a stack overflow, even run in isolation:

```
$ id-<hash> cli::tests::test_cli_parse_cat --exact --test-threads=1
thread 'cli::tests::test_cli_parse_cat' has overflowed its stack
fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
```

Found 2026-11-01 by queue task 5262 (lane F) while running the full `pkgs/id` suite on the laptop from PR 3420's head (74c1a6e75). The PR's diff touches only `pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs` (`is_process_alive` + its test), which the CLI parse path does not call — so this failure is pre-existing relative to that change, not caused by it. All `commands::serve` tests pass (15/15).

## Acceptance
- Reproduce on clean `main` and confirm the overflow is in the parse path (likely clap derive recursion / large nested subcommand graph exceeding the test-thread stack).
- Fix so `test_cli_parse_cat` passes in the normal test-thread configuration (e.g. parse on a spawned thread with a larger stack in the test, or reduce parse recursion), or document the required `RUST_MIN_STACK` if that is the intended configuration.
- Full `pkgs/id` test binary run completes without aborting.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test_cli_parse_cat` runs to completion in the pkgs/id test binary without a stack overflow (pass, or a normal assertion failure if the underlying parse behavior is separately wrong).
- [ ] The root cause is identified in the PR: either the recursive parse path gains a depth bound / iterative shape, or the test's input is shown to be invalid and corrected — not merely a larger test-thread stack.
- [ ] The rest of the pkgs/id test suite stays green in CI.

body:
# aggregator(tier-items): `isIso` accepts impossible calendar dates — delegation timestamps (updatedAt, proposal.at, unable.at) pass on a bare `Date.parse`, are stored verbatim, and the proposal TTL is clocked from a day that never existed

## Summary

`sanitizeDelegation` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/tier-items.ts`) is the boundary sanitizer for tier-item delegation extensions — the fail-soft gate that decides which publisher-supplied delegation fields survive into the dashboard. Its only timestamp check is the local helper at tier-items.ts:68-70:

```ts
function isIso(v: unknown): v is string {
  return typeof v === "string" && v.includes("T") && !Number.isNaN(Date.parse(v));
}
```

`Date.parse` normalizes impossible calendar days instead of refusing them (`2026-02-30` → 2026-03-02), so `isIso` admits them at all three call sites:

- `delegation.updatedAt` — tier-items.ts:153
- `delegation.proposal.at` — tier-items.ts:168
- `delegation.unable.at` — tier-items.ts:185

The impossible string is then stored **verbatim** on the sanitized delegation (`d.updatedAt = raw.updatedAt`, `d.proposal = { summary, at: p.at }`, `d.unable = { …, at: u.at }`).

The repo already has the strict rule, one module over: `validate.ts` `parseIsoDate` refuses `2026-02-30` (returns `null`), and `isTimestampNotFuture` refuses `2026-02-30T00:00:00Z` (pinned by test/validate.test.ts:197). The tier-item sanitizer just never uses it — the same asymmetry pattern as #3393 (actions.ts) and #3365 (snapshots.ts), in a different gate with different consumers.

## Why it matters

`proposal.at` is not decorative: `proposalExpired` (tier-items.ts:308-313) clocks the 48-hour proposal TTL (#1293, `PROPOSAL_TTL_MS`) from it with the same normalizing `Date.parse`. A proposal stamped `2026-02-30T00:00:00Z` is read as drafted on Mar 2, so at Mar 3 00:00Z it is exactly 48h old and **not** expired — while the Feb 28 control at the same instant is 72h old and expired. The impossible date silently extends the proposal's approvable life by ~2 days (and `updatedAt`/`unable.at` feed ordering and rendering consumers that re-parse the stored string the same way). A publisher typo or a non-leap-year Feb 29 passes every check, is stored naming a day that never existed, and no surface ever reports it.

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-11-01)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-tieriso/` (bun 1.4.2, importing the real `sanitizeTierItemExtensions` / `proposalExpired` from `pm-stack/aggregator/src/tier-items.ts` and `parseIsoDate` / `isTimestampNotFuture` from `src/validate.ts`; tier-items.ts md5 `ab984916…` and validate.ts md5 `2078ddfd…` identical in the sandbox clone at main `d85e4098` and the laptop clone):

```
control valid 2026-02-27: KEPT
control garbage at: DROPPED
control no-T date 2026-02-27: DROPPED
impossible 2026-02-30T00:00:00Z: proposal.at KEPT stored=2026-02-30T00:00:00Z | updatedAt KEPT stored=2026-02-30T00:00:00Z
impossible 2026-02-29T00:00:00Z: proposal.at KEPT stored=2026-02-29T00:00:00Z | updatedAt KEPT stored=2026-02-29T00:00:00Z
impossible 2026-04-31T00:00:00Z: proposal.at KEPT stored=2026-04-31T00:00:00Z | updatedAt KEPT stored=2026-04-31T00:00:00Z
impossible 2026-02-30T25:00:00Z: proposal.at DROPPED | updatedAt DROPPED   (hour range IS checked by Date.parse)
unable.at 2026-02-30 / 2026-02-29 / 2026-04-31: KEPT (probe.ts run 1)

validate.parseIsoDate("2026-02-30") = null
validate.isTimestampNotFuture("2026-02-30T00:00:00Z", …) = false
Date.parse("2026-02-30T00:00:00Z") = 2026-03-02T00:00:00.000Z
proposalExpired(at=2026-02-30, now=2026-03-03T00:00Z) = false   (rolled to Mar 2 → exactly 48h, not > TTL)
proposalExpired(at=2026-02-28, now=2026-03-03T00:00Z) = true    (control: 72h > TTL, expired)
```

Dedup: open + recently closed search for tier-items / isIso / sanitizeTierItemExtensions / proposalExpired — no existing issue covers this gate. Distinct from #3393 (actions.ts `validateNewAction` payload.until / proposalUpdatedAt — different file, fields, and writer path) and from #3365/#3379 (snapshots).

## Acceptance criteria

- `isIso` (or its replacement) refuses impossible calendar dates — e.g. `2026-02-30T…`, `2026-02-29T…` in a non-leap year, `2026-04-31T…` — at all three call sites (updatedAt, proposal.at, unable.at), reusing or matching the strictness of `validate.ts` (`parseIsoDate` / a round-trip component check), so a delegation carrying one is dropped by the sanitizer exactly as a garbage timestamp is today.
- Timestamps that are valid today stay valid: the fix must not narrow the accepted formats beyond the impossible-date rule (existing published shapes with a `T` and a parseable, real date/time keep passing); tests pin at least one offset-bearing and one fractional-second valid timestamp.
- New tests in the aggregator suite pin each refused shape for each of the three fields, plus the `proposalExpired` consequence (an impossible `proposal.at` can no longer extend the TTL window).
- No change to the fail-soft contract: a refused timestamp drops the delegation field, never the item or the section.

`recordsFromDeepseekBalance` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshot-records.ts:173-190`, the DeepSeek PAYG CNY balance derivation from #1052) takes its observation date from the ¥ line with a bare date-shaped regex and never checks it is a real calendar date:

```ts
const date = /\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}/.exec(line)?.[0] ?? lastCheckedDate(section) ?? freshestDate(section);  // :182
```

Both fallbacks it shadows are #2264-hardened: `freshestDate` (same file, :45) filters candidates through `parseIsoDate` precisely so "an impossible date like 2026-02-30 or 2026-13-01 in prose must not win", and `recordsFromPools` (:206) uses only those validated fallbacks. The DeepSeek path is the one derivation in the file that bypasses the discipline — and because the regex *matches* an impossible date, the `??` chain never falls through to the section's valid **Last checked:** date.

## Verified (laptop probe, real files at main e6577a96, snapshot-records.ts sha256 dc4d2b62…)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-deepseekdate/` (imports the real `recordsFromDeepseekBalance` / `freshestDate` / `lastCheckedDate` and the real `isSnapshotRecord` gate):

- Control — ¥ line `(2026-10-25 read)`: record `ts=2026-10-25T12:00:00Z`, `isSnapshotRecord=true`.
- ¥ line `(2026-02-30 read)`, section **Last checked: 2026-10-30**: record `ts=2026-02-30T12:00:00Z`, `isSnapshotRecord=false`.
- ¥ line `(2026-13-01 read)`: record `ts=2026-13-01T12:00:00Z`, `isSnapshotRecord=false`.
- Control — no date on the ¥ line: falls back correctly to `ts=2026-10-30T12:00:00Z` (Last checked), gate passes.

## Why it matters

The poisoned record is not stored — it is *silently lost*: `SnapshotStore.appendLocked` drops gate-failing records with `records.filter(isSnapshotRecord)` (`snapshots.ts:610`, no warning), and the backfill's summary counts everything not appended as "already present" (`scripts/backfill-usage-snapshots.ts:434`), so a mistyped/impossible date in the quota-view prose (e.g. `2026-02-30` for a Feb 28 read, or a month/day transposition) makes the DeepSeek reserve's balance observation vanish while the run reports it as a dedupe. The correct read date was sitting in the same section's **Last checked:** bullet the whole time. This is exactly the failure #2264 fixed for `freshestDate`; this one call site was missed.

## Fix sketch

Validate the on-line candidate the same way the rest of the file does — e.g. take the first *real* date on the line (`parseIsoDate(d) !== null`, mirroring `freshestDate`), and only then fall back to `lastCheckedDate(section) ?? freshestDate(section)`. An impossible on-line date should behave like no on-line date, not like a successful match.

## Acceptance criteria

- A ¥ line carrying an impossible date (2026-02-30, 2026-13-01, 2026-04-31) with a valid **Last checked:** date in the section derives a record stamped at the Last-checked (or freshest valid) date, and the record passes `isSnapshotRecord`.
- A ¥ line carrying an impossible date and no other valid date in the section yields no record (fail-soft, as today for dateless lines).
- Existing behavior is unchanged for a real on-line date and for the no-date fallback (existing DeepSeek tests in `test/snapshot-writers.test.ts` still pass).
- New tests cover both impossible-date cases above.

Distinct from: #2568 (`recordsFromProviderUsage` percent range-check, different function), #2493 (github-billing impossible dates, different pipeline), #3365/#3364 (rollup/census gates).

body:
Follow-up to #2144.

## Viewing model
Guest join remains the way a guest enters a world. Add an explicit, authenticated host/owner view as a convenience for the node operator; do not make all visitors hosts by default and do not mint, consume, or expose a guest capability just to show the host its own world. Start read-only: render the authoritative program view and records without adding the host as a guest participant. Keep host authorization out of URLs and preserve the existing guest-capability flow.

## Current evidence
- `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts:288-314,606` connects only when a guest capability is present and sends a `join` frame.
- `pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs:1058-1067` routes a join through capability validation.
- Program installation already exists: `id world install` (`pkgs/id/src/cli.rs:1434-1454`), is documented in `pkgs/id/examples/roc-counter/README.md:33-43`, and the web page has Wasm and Roc install controls (`pkgs/id/src/web/templates.rs:806-823`). Those controls currently sit under the misleading “Host: create a guest invite” disclosure.

## Scope
Add the explicit host-view path and make the existing install path discoverable from the host view/empty-program state. This is the world-host control surface, not a program-as-website feature.

## Acceptance
- An explicitly authenticated host can view the current authoritative program surface and records without joining as a guest or consuming a guest capability.
- Missing or invalid host authorization cannot enter host view; the existing guest view still requires a valid guest capability and remains unchanged.
- The host is not counted as a guest participant, and the initial host view is read-only.
- A world without an installed program shows an actionable empty state; Wasm/Roc install controls live under a clearly named, separate “Install or update program” host section and remain functional.
- Tests cover host authorization, guest-flow preservation, and the no-program/install UI state.

## Out of scope
Listener/binding redesign (#2145), program-as-website routing and authentication model (#2146), dynamic publish/unpublish (#2147), and guest role/capability changes.

body:
# id(server_config): `[create]` lists silently dedupe a repeated key — the one list parse never duplicate-checks, so a typo'd second entry vanishes and the intended principal never gets create permission

## Summary

`ServerConfig::parse` (`pkgs/id/src/server_config/parse.rs`) refuses a repeated
entry everywhere a list names keys — except `[create]`:

- a user or group key declared twice → `ConfigError::DuplicateKey` (`claim`)
- two user keys naming the same public key → `ConfigError::DuplicateId`
- a group listing one member twice → `ConfigError::DuplicateMember`
  (parse.rs, members pass: `members.iter().any(|(listed, _)| *listed == key)`)

But `create_rule` (parse.rs) builds both lists by inserting into a
`BTreeSet` and never checks the insert result:

```rust
let mut users = BTreeSet::new();
for key in &rule.users {
    users.insert(user_of(names, key, "[create].users")?);
}
let mut groups = BTreeSet::new();
for key in &rule.groups {
    groups.insert(group_of(names, key, "[create].groups")?);
}
```

So `[create] users = ["ann", "ann"]` and `groups = ["team", "team"]` parse
cleanly and start the server, with the repetition silently collapsed.

## Why it matters

A duplicate in `[create]` is far more likely a typo than an intent: the
operator meant to list a second user or group and repeated the first. Every
other list in this file treats that exact shape as a startup-refusing error
naming the key, because the consequence of silence is not cosmetic — the
intended principal is simply absent from the `CreateRule::Listed` set, the
config passes every startup check, and the failure only surfaces later, in
production, as that user or group's members being unable to create groups
with no config error pointing at the cause. The module doc's promise —
"`ServerConfig::parse` checks the whole file … so a bad file fails at
startup" — holds for members, keys and IDs, but not for the create rule.

## Evidence (verified this run, main ee8bc80c / parse.rs sha256 16a97dbf…)

Laptop probe in the real crate (worktree of origin/main at
`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-createdup`, integration test
`pkgs/id/tests/probe_createdup.rs` calling the public
`ServerConfig::parse`; parse.rs sha256 identical across the sandbox clone,
the laptop clone, and origin/main):

- `[create] users = ["ann", "ann"]` → `Ok` (silently deduped)
- `[create] groups = ["team", "team"]` (with `users = ["ann"]`) → `Ok`
- Control, same probe: a group listing member `bo` twice →
  `Err(ConfigError::DuplicateMember { .. })`
- Control, same probe: a group key in `[create].users` →
  `Err(ConfigError::WrongKind { .. })` (the parser is strict here in
  every other dimension)

## Acceptance criteria

- `ServerConfig::parse` refuses a repeated key in `[create].users` and in
  `[create].groups` with a `ConfigError` that names the repeated key and
  the list it appeared in (a dedicated variant, or a reuse of an existing
  duplicate variant with the place recorded — implementer's choice,
  consistent with the file's "every refusal names the key" rule).
- Repetition is judged on the resolved key (the ID the key names), as
  `DuplicateMember` already is, not on the raw string alone.
- New unit tests in `parse.rs` cover: duplicate user entry refused,
  duplicate group entry refused, and a non-duplicate `[create]` table
  (users + groups + `min_role`) still parses to the same `CreateRule`.
- No behavior change for any config that parses today without duplicates.

## Dedup

Open + recently closed search this run for server_config / `[create]` /
duplicate: #1824 (blank/padded keys — different field, different failure),
#1700 (closed; two keys naming one ID — the users pass, not `[create]`
lists). No existing issue covers the `[create]` lists' silent dedup.

title: id(world): journal restore issues a capability under an already-revoked parent — a Revoked entry that precedes the child's Issued entry revokes nothing, and the restored child acts with a live token

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`WorldCore::restore` (`pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs`) accepts a journal in which a capability is **issued after its parent was already revoked**, and the restored child then acts with a live token — a state no live path can produce.

Restore's `Issued` arm validates the neighbouring fields — digest shape, duplicate participant id, the parent must already exist (`core.capabilities.contains_key(&parent)`), `uses >= 1`, and a delegate's expiry may not outlive its parent's — but existence is the only parent check. It never asks whether the parent is **revoked**.

The `Revoked` arm is not a backstop: it calls `revoke_tree(participant_id)`, which marks that participant and every descendant **issued so far**. A child whose `Issued` entry appears later in the journal does not exist yet at that moment, so nothing marks it, and it is inserted afterwards with `revoked: false`.

`authorize()` then has no way to catch it: it checks only the presented token's own record (`!record.revoked`), and `effective_scopes()` walks the ancestor chain intersecting scopes and subject ceilings — it never checks an ancestor's `revoked` flag. So the restored child's token passes `authorize` and can chat/input like any live participant.

Every live path refuses this shape:

- `delegate()` / `attenuate()` / `delegate_to_friend()` first run `authorize(token, JOIN)` on the parent, which fails for a revoked parent — you cannot delegate from a revoked capability.
- A live `revoke_tree()` revokes the parent and **every existing descendant** with it, so a live world never holds an active child under a revoked parent.

Checkpoint-written journals are safe by construction (compaction emits each participant's `Issued` entry immediately followed by its own `Revoked` entry when revoked, in id order), but restore is the trust boundary for journals that travel — forks copy them, backups restore them under newer binaries — and the design of record (#2898, "reconstruction is admission") says the rebuilding code validates the same invariants the live path enforces and refuses, never partially applies.

## Evidence (verified this run, main ca2471a3 / laptop 5c172f3d2; `world/core.rs` and `world/mod.rs` md5-identical on both clones)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-revokedparent/`, a detached worktree of `origin/main`; `pkgs/id/tests/probe_revokedparent.rs`, an integration test against the real `id` crate, token digests built exactly as `mint` builds them — `"<id>.<hex secret>"`, SHA-256):

- CONTROL A: journal `Issued(1, GUEST|DELEGATE)`, `Issued(2, GUEST, parent=1)`, `Revoked(1)` restores, and participant 2's token **cannot** chat — revoke-after-issue takes the whole tree, as designed.
- CONTROL B: on a live `WorldCore`, `attenuate` with a just-revoked parent's token returns `Err` — live delegation from a revoked parent is refused.
- CASE: journal `Issued(1, GUEST|DELEGATE)`, `Revoked(1)`, `Issued(2, GUEST, parent=1)` restores `Ok`, and participant 2's token **chats `Ok`** — an active capability delegated from an already-revoked parent, restored from a journal no live writer could produce.

Code points (main ca2471a3): the `Issued` arm's parent check is `parent.is_none_or(|parent| core.capabilities.contains_key(&parent))` in `WorldCore::restore` (`src/world/core.rs`, restore `Issued` arm); the `Revoked` arm calls `core.revoke_tree(participant_id)`; `revoke_tree` (same file) only visits records already in `core.capabilities`; `authorize` checks `!record.revoked` for the presented token's record only; `effective_scopes` intersects scopes/ceilings up the parent chain with no revoked test. The existing test `a_restored_delegation_keeps_its_parent_link` (src/world/tests.rs) covers revoke-after-issue only.

## Why it matters

Revocation is the world's moderation/incident-response primitive: revoking a capability is supposed to end its whole delegation line. A journal that revokes a parent before issuing its child — from a buggy or partial writer, a hand-repaired journal, or a fork/backup assembled out of order — silently resurrects the revoked line on restore: the child was never live-revoked because, in journal order, it did not exist when the revocation landed. This is the same reconstruction-as-admission family as #2890/#2958/#2960/#2972, but a distinct field and mechanism (parent revocation state at issue time, not scopes, limits, names, or participant 0); #2890's closing acceptance item covers delegate scopes-vs-parent, not this.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Restore refuses an `Issued` entry whose parent is already revoked at that point in the journal, naming the participant in the error, in the style of the neighbouring restore errors (e.g. "participant N delegated from revoked capability M").
- [ ] Regression tests beside the existing restore tests: issuance-after-parent-revocation refused; the control shapes still restore — parent and child issued then revoked together (revoke-after-issue), and a live delegation chain with no revocation.
- [ ] Checkpoint/compaction round-trip unchanged: a world with a revoked parent and revoked descendants checkpoints and restores to the same state (the per-participant `Revoked` entries compaction emits must still satisfy the new check — a revoked child issued *before* its own `Revoked` entry is fine; only a parent already revoked *at the child's `Issued` entry* is refused).
- [ ] Triage confirms no legitimate historical journal shape issues a capability under an already-revoked parent; if one exists, name it explicitly instead of loosening the check silently.

title: laptop-autocommit: pull-conflict abort test uses a relative MERGE_HEAD path, so a conflicted merge-pull is never aborted

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: source/pr-comment-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-comment-review job

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

Codex P1 on PR #3175 — "Resolve MERGE_HEAD to an absolute path before testing it":

> When invoked outside the target repository, as in `laptop-autocommit.nix`'s service without a repository working directory, this command returns `.git/MERGE_HEAD`, but the shell tests that path relative to its own directory. A real merge conflict therefore skips the abort and exits successfully, leaving unresolved files behind. I reproduced this with two diverged clones: the next sweep's `git add -u` staged the conflict markers, committed them as a merge, and pushed the corrupted file. Request `--path-format=absolute` before `--git-path`.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3175 (merged 2026-10-31T18:19:39Z, merge commit f1594c7eb)
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3175#discussion_r4432725449 — chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-10-31T18:05:12Z, `nixos/home/laptop-autocommit.sh:39`
- Flagged code: `mh="$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"` followed by `[ -f "$mh" ]`

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads`: isResolved=false) and its only author is the Codex bot — no reply from the PR author or any maintainer.
- The PR merged at the reviewed head (`fd7144e91d`); no fix commit followed the comment.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-01)

- `nixos/home/laptop-autocommit.sh:38-39` on current main still reads:
  `mh="$(git -C "$d" rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD)"` / `if [ -f "$mh" ]; then` — no `--path-format=absolute`.
- `nixos/home/laptop-autocommit.nix` defines the user service with `ExecStart = ".../laptop-autocommit ${path}"` and no `WorkingDirectory`, so the script runs with a working directory other than the target repo (`$d` arrives only as an argument); the relative `.git/MERGE_HEAD` is tested against the wrong directory, the conflict abort is skipped, and the in-progress conflicted merge is left for the next every-minute sweep.
- Related but distinct: #1807 tracks the missing start-of-sweep in-progress-operation guard on the same script; this issue is the separate defect in the pull-conflict abort path added by #3175 itself.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The MERGE_HEAD test in `laptop-autocommit.sh` resolves to an absolute path (e.g. `git -C "$d" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-path MERGE_HEAD`), so a conflicted merge-pull is reliably detected and aborted with the loud failure the PR intended.
- [ ] A regression test or scripted probe covers the invoked-outside-the-repo case: a diverged pull that conflicts ends with the merge aborted, no conflict markers staged/committed by a later sweep, and exit 1.
- [ ] Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why the current behavior is safe.

title: aggregator(snapshots): isSnapshotRollup re-admits the shapes isSnapshotRecord was hardened to refuse — impossible dates, negative/string limit, unparseable resetsAt, inverted pairs expand into the reading path unchecked

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Bug

`SnapshotStore.readAll` has two doors into the same reading path, and only one of them is hardened. Raw lines must pass `isSnapshotRecord` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts:296`), which was deliberately tightened (#2264/#2483): timestamps must be real ISO calendar dates via the strict `isIsoDate` primitive (because `Date.parse` rolls `2026-02-30` into March), `limit` must be a non-negative finite number when present, `resetsAt` must be a real ISO date when present, and pair values must have finite endpoints with `low <= high`.

Rollup lines take the other door: `readAll` gates them only on `isSnapshotRollup` (`snapshots.ts:82`, used at `snapshots.ts:552`) and then `expandRollup` (`snapshots.ts:226`) emits records straight into the reading path — the expanded records are never passed through `isSnapshotRecord`. But `isSnapshotRollup` does not apply the record-side rules:

- Timestamps (`firstTs`/`lastTs`/`minTs`/`maxTs`) are checked with `Number.isNaN(Date.parse(f))` (`snapshots.ts:94-95`) — exactly the loose check the record validator was fixed away from. `2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z` passes.
- `limit` and `resetsAt` are not checked at all, even though `expandRollup` copies them onto the expanded `last` record and the record-side comment says these fields "are dereferenced downstream (pct-of-limit, reset comparisons), so a non-finite/negative limit or an impossible resetsAt date must refuse the record here, at the boundary."
- Pair values (`valueMin`/`valueMax`/`valueLast`) accept any `{low, high}` with `typeof === "number"` endpoints (`snapshots.ts:97-103`): an inverted pair `{low: 10, high: 5}` passes, while the record side explicitly refuses inverted pairs.

The same loose gate also seeds compaction: existing rollups are re-aggregated through `isSnapshotRollup` at `snapshots.ts:707`, so a malformed rollup line is not just read, it is carried forward into the next compaction.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 1a68d6af)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-rollupgate/probe.ts` driving the real `snapshots.ts` (sha256 `c6685035…` matched on both clones; output in `probe.txt` in the same directory):

- Control: a valid rollup passes `isSnapshotRollup`, expands to 3 records, and all 3 pass `isSnapshotRecord`.
- `lastTs = "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z"` → `isSnapshotRollup=true`; one expanded record fails `isSnapshotRecord`.
- `limit = -5` → passes; the expanded `last` record (the one carrying `limit`) fails `isSnapshotRecord`.
- `limit = "100"` (string) → passes; expanded `last` record fails `isSnapshotRecord`.
- `resetsAt = "not-a-date"` → passes; expanded `last` record fails `isSnapshotRecord`.
- `valueMin = {low: 10, high: 5}` (unit `usd-est`) → passes; expanded min record fails `isSnapshotRecord`.

Rollup files are kept indefinitely (13-month raw retention, rollups forever), so a single malformed or hand-edited rollup line poisons the reading path permanently, where a malformed raw line would only be dropped.

Minor, same function: the `month` check (`/^\d{4}-\d{2}$/`, `snapshots.ts:86`) accepts `2026-13` / `2026-00`, months no writer produces.

## Why it matters

The snapshot store is the usage hub's history: latest-value readers, pct-of-limit computations, and reset markers all consume `readAll` output trusting that the boundary validators refused impossible data. The record side of that boundary was hardened after real incidents (#2264/#2483); the rollup side silently re-admits the same shapes, and compaction re-seeds them forward, so the corruption is self-perpetuating rather than one-off.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isSnapshotRollup` refuses a rollup whose `firstTs`/`lastTs`/`minTs`/`maxTs` (and `resetsAtTs`/`limitTs` when present) are not strict ISO calendar dates (same `isIsoDate` primitive as `isSnapshotRecord`).
- `isSnapshotRollup` refuses a present non-null `limit` that is not a non-negative finite number, and a present non-null `resetsAt` that is not a strict ISO date — mirroring the record-side rules.
- `isSnapshotRollup` refuses pair values with non-finite endpoints or `low > high`, mirroring the record side.
- `month` refuses impossible months (`00`, `13`+).
- Tests pin each refused shape above plus a valid rollup (including a valid pair-valued rollup and one carrying `limit`/`resetsAt`) still passing and expanding to records that all pass `isSnapshotRecord`.
- No change to the compaction writer's output format or to `expandRollup`'s expansion semantics for valid rollups.

Distinct from #2568 (recordsFromProviderUsage `used_percent` range, writer side) and #3295/#3285 (snapshot script argument handling). Found by comparing the two store-read validators in `snapshots.ts`.

body:
## Summary

`isRepoCensus` — the structural gate for the fleet-feed coverage census behind the #1220 coverage panel (merged in PR #3309) — accepts census rows that cannot describe a real repo: negative counts, gate counts larger than the repo's open-issue total, a repo of `"/"` or `"a/"`, and duplicate rows for the same repo. Those rows flow straight into the report, are **persisted** into the weekly coverage snapshot (including the frozen `weekly` baseline), and render on `/projects` — so one bad feed read can show negative/impossible backlog numbers and poison the week-over-week baseline for a full week. Duplicate rows are resolved by silent last-wins overwrite in `computeCoverage`, with none of the drop-and-count diagnostics the aggregator's other feed gates (#2429 quota sanitization) surface.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `1a68d6af`; `coverage.ts` sha256 `2c166cdf…b301`, `feed.ts` sha256 `d7416455…36a4`, both matched on the laptop clone)

The gate, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/coverage.ts:88-98`, checks only `typeof repo === "string" && repo.includes("/")` and `Number.isInteger` on the three counts. Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-census/probe.ts`, bun, importing the real `coverage.ts`/`feed.ts`; full output in `run.log`):

- `isRepoCensus({repo:"developing-today/code", openIssues:-5, gateNow:0, gateNext:0})` → `true`
- `isRepoCensus({…, openIssues:3, gateNow:10, gateNext:7})` → `true` (gate counts are label-filtered subsets of the same open-issue search in `scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:684-696`, so each must be ≤ `openIssues`)
- `isRepoCensus({…, openIssues:10, gateNow:-2, gateNext:0})` → `true`
- `isRepoCensus({repo:"/", …})` and `{repo:"a/", …}` → `true`
- `computeCoverage` on two rows for `developing-today/code` (`openIssues:100` then `openIssues:7, gateNow:9, gateNext:9`) → one row with the **last** values, no diagnostic; `coverageFromFeed` (`src/feed.ts:275-282`) keeps all 4 rows of a mixed feed (negative + impossible + duplicates)
- A negative census row yields a report row with `openIssues:-5` and a week-over-week delta of `-55` against a baseline of 50 (`diffCoverage`)

Downstream, `src/server.ts:81` (`coverageSnapshot`) persists whatever `computeCoverage` returns via `CoverageSnapshotStore`, and `nextCoverageSnapshot` freezes the week's first report into `weekly`, which becomes next week's `baseline` — so impossible values are not a transient render glitch; they are stored and compared against for a week. `coverageSectionHtml` (`src/render.ts:4910-4925`) renders the numbers verbatim.

## Why it matters

The coverage panel's whole contract (per the `coverage.ts` header and PR #3309's Codex rounds) is that unavailable or malformed source data renders as unavailable, never as invented numbers. Every sibling feed gate enforces its section's invariants (e.g. `isQuotaWindow`/`sanitizeQuotaView` drop-and-count, `isProjectPoolItem` shape-strictness). The census gate enforces only types, so the one section whose values are **snapshotted to disk and frozen as a weekly baseline** is the one that can store impossible values. A collector bug, a hand-edited feed, or a future collector change that double-emits a repo silently rewrites the panel and the baseline instead of dropping the row.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isRepoCensus` refuses: negative counts; `gateNow > openIssues` or `gateNext > openIssues`; a `repo` that is not an `owner/name` pair (both sides non-empty, exactly the shape the collector emits for the four fleet repos).
- Duplicate census rows for one repo are handled explicitly — refused/dropped at the gate (with the surviving row's provenance clear), or counted/surfaced like `sanitizeQuotaView`'s drop counts — never silent last-wins.
- Regression tests in `test/coverage.test.ts` pin each refusal and the duplicate behavior; existing coverage tests (absent census → null fields, pool-unavailable → null pool fields, weekly rotation) keep passing.
- No change to the collector's emitted shape, the snapshot file format, or the panel layout.

Distinct from: #1220 (the feature, closed), #1218 (Project export auditability), #3332/#3309 (AA keep-last-good / the coverage panel PR itself). Dedup checked this run against open + closed issues for `isRepoCensus` / `RepoCensus` / coverage-census terms — no existing issue covers this gate.

title: id(membership): decode_body accepts a member whose outer kind and identity tag disagree — a group hash decodes as an Individual and a key as a Group

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
