labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id/src/membership/body.rs` — `decode_body` accepts a group-operation member whose two kind markers disagree.

The body format carries the member kind **twice** (module docs, `body.rs:21-22`):

- the outer member kind: `[kind, id]`, `0` = individual, `1` = group;
- the tag byte inside the 33-byte identity: `0` = key, `1` = group hash.

`decode_member` (`body.rs:272-283`) decodes the identity from the inner tag (`decode_auth`, `body.rs:285-308`), then wraps it in `GroupMember::Individual` / `GroupMember::Group` from the outer kind — **without ever checking the two markers agree**. Every neighbouring rule in the same decoder is enforced exactly: member kind `2` is refused, identity tag `2` is refused, identity length must be exactly 33, access must be 0–3, CBOR must be canonical. The agreement between the two kind bytes is the one rule missing.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `a8189c21`)

`membership/body.rs` sha256 `49e0b856d6ef781515f1d29a8a0082e20b5fa4fe9ac6f8295915f0efec7f2e24` — identical on the sandbox clone and the laptop clone. Laptop probe `probe-2026-11-01-laneA-membertag` (hand-built canonical CBOR bodies through the real `decode_body`):

- control `remove` kind=0 tag=0 → `Individual(Key(..))` (accepted, correct)
- control `remove` kind=1 tag=1 → `Group(Group(..))` (accepted, correct)
- control `join` kind=0 tag=0 access=3 → accepted, correct
- **mismatch `remove` kind=0 tag=1 → ACCEPTED as `Individual(Group(..))`**
- **mismatch `remove` kind=1 tag=0 → ACCEPTED as `Group(Key(..))`**
- **mismatch `join` kind=0 tag=1 access=3 (manage) → ACCEPTED**
- **mismatch `join` kind=1 tag=0 access=3 (manage) → ACCEPTED**
- known-refused controls kind=2 and tag=2 → both refused, as the existing tests pin

Existing test coverage (`body.rs:535`, `test_a_malformed_member_is_refused`) varies tag and length but always with outer kind 0 and a matching key tag — the cross-combination is never tested.

## Why it matters

The same 32 bytes can be enrolled under two different membership semantics chosen by the body's author: `GroupMember::Group` is expanded transitively by p2panda-auth (members of that group gain access), `GroupMember::Individual` is not; the membership layer's self-removal and member lookups pattern-match on the variant (`membership/layer.rs:323`, `membership/layer.rs:427`). A mismatched body therefore creates phantom members no well-typed encoder call site produces (every production construction is `Individual(Key)` or `Group(Group)`): a group hash enrolled as a fake "individual", or a key enrolled as a "group" that can never have been created (group ids are create-event hashes, `membership/mod.rs:38`). Two peers interpreting the identity by its tag vs by its variant would disagree about who holds access. This is the decode gate for bodies arriving from remote events (`event_store/ingest.rs:430` maps `decode_body` errors to `Refusal::Malformed` — accepted mismatches flow straight into the membership layer).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `decode_member` (or `decode_body`) refuses a member whose outer kind and identity tag disagree — both directions — with `BodyError::Shape` naming the mismatch.
- [ ] Tests pin all four kind×tag combinations for at least `remove` and one access-bearing kind (`join`/`create`): the two matching pairs decode, the two mismatched pairs are refused.
- [ ] Round-trip property unchanged: every action `encode_body` can produce still decodes to itself (`test_every_kind_round_trips` passes).
- [ ] No change to the wire format, `CLAIM`, or the canonical-CBOR rule.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `decode_body`, "membership body member kind tag", and GroupMember/tag terms on 2026-11-01 — no existing issue covers this; closed #1075 is the phases 0–8 validation audit umbrella.

body:
Follow-up to #3334 / PR #3339. The Codex review of PR #3339 head `27c8ea305` (2026-11-01T05:03Z) found 4 further heuristic false-positive shapes in `checkSyntaxAndDelimiters` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/scripting/validator.go`). Each was dispositioned from PR #3339 to this issue (fix-or-pin, same acceptance as #3334) so PR #3339's 9 in-scope shapes are not held hostage to an open-ended tail of exotic corners.

1. **Relational comparison chains with a regex operand** (thread PRRT_kwDOJWP4786yXfUz): `const yes = 1 < Number > /[)]/.source.length;` — accepting `/` as an instantiation follower misclassifies the regex as division/TypeScript generics; valid JS, passes the parent scanner. Preserve the relational interpretation.
2. **Nested statement blocks inside class heritage object literals** (thread PRRT_kwDOJWP4786yXfU0): `class C extends {C: function(){ {} /[}]/.test('}'); }}.C {}` — `heritageBraceDepth > 0` forces every nested brace to be an operand closure, including statement blocks inside function bodies; the following regex is read as division. Track nested block context separately.
3. **Escaped identifiers at line start leave `lineBreakPending` unconsumed** (thread PRRT_kwDOJWP4786yXfU3): `let a=1;\n\u0061++ / 2;` (actual newline) — the early `continue` for Unicode-escape identifiers bypasses consuming the pending line break, so `++`/`--` is misclassified as prefix and the division slash reports a fatal unclosed regex. Consume the pending line break as the ordinary identifier path does.
4. **Property named `new` before an ASI-separated declaration** (thread PRRT_kwDOJWP4786yXfU4): `const obj={new:1}; obj.new\nclass C {} /[)]/.test(')');` (actual newline) — `isExprPositionStart` checks `prevIdent` without the member-access guard, so the following class/function declaration is classified as an expression and its body closes as an operand. Preserve property-name context.

Acceptance (mirrors #3334):
- Each shape validates as valid with a regression test in `TestValidationRegexLiteralsAreOpaque`, or is documented in code as a pinned blind spot with reasoning.
- Division controls (`a / b / c`, `x /= 2`, unclosed delimiter/string after division) unchanged.
- `go test ./internal/scripting/ -count=1` passes (laptop or CI).

Evidence: Codex review threads on PR #3339 at head `27c8ea305`, 2026-11-01T05:03:13Z.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each of the 4 Codex shapes from PR #3339 is dispositioned fix-or-pin with the same acceptance as #3334: valid JS in the named shapes is accepted by `checkSyntaxAndDelimiters`, and genuinely unbalanced input in the same shapes is still rejected.
- [ ] Regression tests cover all 4 shapes (relational chain with regex operand; nested statement blocks in class heritage literals; and the remaining two shapes named in the full issue body).
- [ ] The follow-up PR's Codex review raises no new false-positive shape in the delimiter scanner, or any new shape is dispositioned to a named follow-up in the same pass.

title: agent-backup: two runs in the same second share one snapshot dir — the second run can delete the first run's snapshot and leave `latest` dangling

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.description: Package/app: agent-backup (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Bug: two agent-backup runs in the same second share one snapshot directory — the second run can delete the first run's snapshot and leave `latest` dangling

`pkgs/agent-backup/backup.sh` names each snapshot with one-second resolution and never checks whether that directory already exists:

- `backup.sh:28-29` — `STAMP="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%S)"`, `DEST="$ROOT/$STAMP"`. Two runs started within the same second (the script runs "on change", so a watcher/timer firing twice, or a timer run overlapping a manual run, is enough) compute the **same** `DEST`.
- `backup.sh:59` — the second run `cp -p`s its files **into the first run's snapshot directory**, overwriting/merging in place. The first snapshot is silently no longer the state it captured.
- `backup.sh:71-76` — the dedup step then compares that shared directory against `PREV` (which excludes only the current stamp name). If the second run's content matches `PREV`, it runs `rm -rf "$DEST"` — deleting the **first** run's snapshot too.
- `backup.sh:80` — `latest` was already pointed at `$STAMP` by the first run (`ln -sfn`), and the no-change path exits before re-pointing it, so `latest` is left **dangling**: it names a snapshot that no longer exists.

### Verified this run (laptop probe, sha-matched script)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-agentbackup/` on the laptop — the verbatim `backup.sh` from main `a8189c21` (sha256 `d3c9978b7e96fd18fd038d9bb321bde2cdf070d95c398fee857dd6c0b62b4303`, matched on sandbox and laptop), `HOME`/`AGENT_BACKUP_DIR` pointed at a scratch tree, `date` stubbed via `PATH` to a fixed stamp (the standard way to hit a one-second window deterministically), one candidate file (`~/.claude/settings.json`), and a pre-seeded previous snapshot `2025-12-31T23-59-59` containing `OLD`:

1. Run 1 (source = `NEW`, stamp `2026-01-01T00-00-00`): snapshot created containing `NEW`; `latest -> 2026-01-01T00-00-00`. Correct.
2. Run 2 (same stamp, source reverted to `OLD`, i.e. equal to PREV): exits 0 with `no change since 2025-12-31T23-59-59` — but the stamp directory is **gone** (`test -d` = NO) and `latest` still points at it (`test -e latest` = NO — dangling). Run 1's `NEW` snapshot was destroyed by a run that reported "no change".
3. Control (fresh stamp `2026-01-01T00-00-01`, source = `OLD` = PREV): no new directory, exit 0 — the dedup path behaves as designed when the stamp is unique.

### Why it matters

This script is the only backup of the machine's irreplaceable agent credentials (auth.json files, API keys — see the header comment). Its whole contract is "the history only ever grows when something actually differs" and "`latest` points at the newest snapshot". A same-second pair of runs breaks both halves of that contract silently, with exit 0: a real snapshot is destroyed, and anything restoring from `latest` (the documented entry point) finds nothing. The failure needs no exotic setup — the script is designed to be fired on change, where double-fires inside one second are routine.

### Acceptance criteria

- Two runs started in the same second never share a snapshot directory: the second run either gets a distinct directory (e.g. suffix/sub-second component) or is refused/coalesced explicitly — it never writes into or deletes another run's snapshot.
- After any sequence of same-second runs, `latest` resolves to an existing snapshot directory (`test -e latest` succeeds).
- The no-change path only ever removes a directory the same run created.
- Normal behaviour unchanged: a run whose content differs from the previous snapshot creates exactly one new snapshot and repoints `latest`; a run identical to the previous snapshot creates none.
- A regression test/harness case covers the same-second pair (stubbed `date` is an acceptable mechanism).

title: github-backup(drain): owner allowlist crashes the whole drain run on a non-dict owner/account — malformed event becomes a poison pill instead of a DRAIN-DROP

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/github-backup
labels.description: infra/github-backup estate mirror system

body:
## Summary

`infra/github-backup/bin/drain_queue.py` — the #3326 owner allowlist crashes the whole drain run on a queued event whose `repository.owner` (or `installation.account`) is present but **not a JSON object**. The allowlist's stated contract (module docstring, #3326) is that "malformed events whose owner cannot be determined are dropped: acked as handled-by-policy, logged as one loud DRAIN-DROP line". A non-dict owner instead raises `AttributeError` before any drop, fetch, or ack happens — and because the event is never acked, it stays at the head of the queue and crashes **every** subsequent 5-minute drain run the same way: a poison pill that stalls all mirror fetches until someone removes the event by hand.

## Evidence (verified this run, current main `72e34760`)

`event_owner` at `drain_queue.py:111-127` guards the containers it was thinking of, but not the leaf containers:

```python
rep = ev.get("repository")
if isinstance(rep, dict):
    login = (rep.get("owner") or {}).get("login")   # owner may be str/list/int -> AttributeError
    ...
inst = ev.get("installation")
if isinstance(inst, dict):
    login = (inst.get("account") or {}).get("login") # account may be str/int -> AttributeError
```

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-drainowner/probe.py` driving the **real** module (sha256 `af2fbb2c7d1af7da31aa36b8d3ce39185f1ea33785ca989b7425272e37ff4480`, byte-identical to main):

```
control-missing-owner:  event_owner -> None
control-owner-dict:     event_owner -> 'mallory'
bug-owner-string:       event_owner RAISED AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
bug-owner-list:         event_owner RAISED AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'
bug-owner-int:          event_owner RAISED AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
bug-account-string:     event_owner RAISED AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'get'
bug-account-int:        event_owner RAISED AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'get'
main-poison: main() RAISED AttributeError — fetch_calls=[] ack_calls=[]
main-control (valid planned event only): rc=0 fetch_calls=['owner/repo'] ack_calls=[['good1']]
```

The `main-poison` case puts the malformed event first and a valid, planned `owner/repo` event second: the valid event is **never fetched and never acked**, no `DRAIN-DROP` line is written, and `main()` exits via the exception — the exact opposite of the #3326 design, in which this event class is acked and counted in `dropped_foreign`.

The existing tests in `infra/github-backup/tests/test_drain_queue.py` cover the missing-owner shape (`{"id": "e10", ...}` with no repository/installation at all, case 10) but no shape where `owner`/`account` is present with a non-object type — the shapes a hand-built or future payload (which `event_repo`'s docstring explicitly says the drainer accepts) can carry.

## Why it matters

- The drainer is the 5-minute mirror-fetch path for the whole github-backup estate. One malformed queued event stops fetches for **every** repo, not just its own, and the failure self-repeats indefinitely because the crashing event is never acked or dropped.
- This defeats the security fix it lives in: #3326's allowlist exists so untrusted input (the App is public; anyone can install it) is handled at the door. Untrusted-shaped input that crashes the door is worse than the pre-allowlist behavior for availability — before #3326 this event shape would have fallen through to the repo grouping instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `event_owner` returns `None` (→ DRAIN-DROP + ack + `dropped_foreign` count) for events whose `repository.owner` or `installation.account` is any non-dict value (string, list, number, bool), instead of raising.
- [ ] A drain run containing such an event first still fetches and acks the valid planned events behind it and exits 0.
- [ ] Regression cases in `infra/github-backup/tests/test_drain_queue.py` for at least the string-owner and string-account shapes, asserting drop + ack + no fetch for the malformed event and normal processing for a following valid event.
- [ ] No behavior change for well-formed events: existing 54 drain-queue tests still pass.

Related: #3326 (the allowlist this bug lives in; its implementation commit `cc35ae40` is on current main). Distinct from #3300 (reconcile clone-pass exit code), #3279/#3240 (non-atomic state writes), #3238/#3229 (inventory/mirror validity).

title: aggregator(backfill): trailing --dir crashes with a raw TypeError, and a flag-like value (--dir --print) silently writes the rebuilt history into a directory named '--print'

body:
## Bug

`backfill-usage-snapshots` (the one-shot usage-snapshot backfill, `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/backfill-usage-snapshots.ts`) reads its only flag with a bare index lookup and no validation:

```ts
// backfill-usage-snapshots.ts:32-33
const dirArg = process.argv.indexOf("--dir");
const storeDir = dirArg >= 0 ? process.argv[dirArg + 1] : (process.env.PM_AGG_SNAPSHOTS_DIR ?? join(PKG, "snapshots"));
```

Two failure modes, both verified this run:

1. **Trailing `--dir` crashes with a raw `TypeError`, not a usage error.** `process.argv[dirArg + 1]` is `undefined`, so `storeDir` is `undefined`, and the run dies inside `SnapshotStore.append` → `withSnapshotStoreLock` at `mkdir(dir)` (`src/snapshots.ts:347`): `TypeError: path must be a string or TypedArray` with a Bun stack trace, exit 1. Nothing names `--dir` or its missing value.
2. **A flag-like next token is silently taken as the directory.** `--dir --print` appends the derived records into a newly created directory literally named `--print` in the current working directory and exits 0 reporting `appended to --print` — the real snapshot store is untouched while the report claims success. Any mistyped following token does the same.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-backfilldir/`): script run verbatim from main `6e7f8fcf` (`backfill-usage-snapshots.ts` sha256 `f55386364648275ac53f35752dee2302006f23545c68a5c409ca6d47c22d8da7` on both laptop and sandbox clones), Bun 1.4.2, fixture `QUOTA_VIEW_PATH` carrying one DeepSeek ¥44.63 / 2026-10-25 line (exactly 1 derived record; the 31 unmatched-pattern warnings are the script's normal fail-soft behaviour):

```
=== CONTROL: --dir <valid temp dir> ===
backfill: 1 record(s) appended to .../store-control (0 already present, 31 skipped)   exit=0
store-control/usage-2026-10.jsonl written

=== BUG 1: --dir            (trailing, no value) ===
TypeError: path must be a string or TypedArray
  at mkdir (node:fs/promises)
  at withSnapshotStoreLock (src/snapshots.ts:347)
  at append (src/snapshots.ts:606)
  at main (scripts/backfill-usage-snapshots.ts:431)                                     exit=1

=== BUG 2: --dir --print    (flag-like value) ===
backfill: 1 record(s) appended to --print (0 already present, 31 skipped)             exit=0
# a directory named `--print` was created in the CWD (the aggregator package dir)
# containing usage-2026-10.jsonl; the real store never saw the record.
# (Probe cleanup: the stray `--print` directory was removed from the laptop clone.)
```

Contrast with the sibling scripts in the same package: `compact-usage-snapshots.ts:28-31` validates its `--months` value and exits 2 with `invalid --months '<value>'`, and `append-usage-snapshots.ts` was already filed for its `--by` variant of this shape (#3295). This script has no guard at all.

## Why it matters

The backfill is the recovery/seed path for the usage snapshot store — it is run by hand, rarely, exactly when history needs rebuilding. A forgotten `--dir` value currently either crashes with a stack trace that points into the store lock code (suggesting store corruption, not a typo) or, worse, silently writes the rebuilt history into a stray flag-named directory in the working tree and reports success, so the operator believes the store was seeded when nothing was. Because re-running is documented as safe (dedupe), the silent case can go unnoticed until the missing history is queried.

## Acceptance criteria

- `backfill-usage-snapshots.ts --dir` with no following value, or with a following token that starts with `--`, prints a usage/error message naming `--dir` and its missing value to stderr and exits 2 — no stack trace, no directory created, no records written.
- `--dir <valid path>` behaves exactly as today (records appended to that store, exit 0, same summary line).
- The no-flag default (env `PM_AGG_SNAPSHOTS_DIR`, else the package `snapshots/` directory) is unchanged.
- A regression test (or script-level test harness case) covers the trailing-`--dir` and flag-like-value cases.

Distinct from: #3295 (append-usage-snapshots `--by` voiding `observedBy`), #3285 (compact `--months 0` guard gap — compact does validate non-numeric values), #3312 (docs-history trailing flag panic, Go tool). Same family, different script and different failure: this one both crashes *and* silently misdirects the write.

body:
# mcpx(affected-tests): untracked new files are listed as changed but their contents never reach the diff-text analysis — T2 name matching and T1b silently skip them pre-commit

## Summary

`pkgs/mcpx/scripts/affected-tests.py` promises in its header (lines 26–29):

> The diff is the working tree against the base (committed + uncommitted +
> untracked), so the selector works before anything is committed:
> `git diff --name-only <base>` + `git ls-files --others`

The changed-file *list* honours that (line 336–339: `git diff --name-only` ∪
`git ls-files --others`), so an untracked new file counts as changed, its
package gets T0/T1, and its registry area fires T3 guards. But the diff *text*
the rest of the analysis reads is built with a plain
`git diff <base> -- <paths>` (lines 396–400), which emits **nothing for
untracked files**. Everything derived from that text silently treats a new
untracked file as empty:

- **T2 name matching** (`names = diff_names(diff_text)`, line 448): quoted
  names (setting paths, op names, flag/command names) that exist only in a
  new untracked registry file are never extracted, so e2e tests mentioning
  them are not selected.
- **T1b** (`exported = changed_exported_idents(diff_text)`, line 403):
  exported declarations in a new untracked file are never seen, so importer
  packages are not added.
- **Harness detection** (the e2e diff at line ~466): `newEnv` defined in a
  new untracked e2e helper file is missed, so the rule-4 sample is not
  selected.

## Verified (laptop probe, script sha256 2b908c49… = current main a1aa07d8)

Fixture repo with the real script; base commit contains a test-first e2e
test `TestBrandNewSettingFlows` mentioning `"pool.brandnewsetting"`. The
change is one new file `internal/settings/newreg.go` defining that setting:

- **Untracked** (`git status`: `?? newreg.go`; `git diff origin/main --
  newreg.go` is empty): selector reports "1 changed file(s)", selects T1
  for `internal/settings` and the T3 settings guards, but T2 selects only
  the generic guard `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` —
  `TestBrandNewSettingFlows` is **not** selected.
- **Same file staged** (`git add`): T2 selects
  `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket|TestBrandNewSettingFlows`.

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-affected/probe2.sh`.

## Why it matters

The selector's whole purpose (#1966 / TESTING.md tiers) is choosing the
right tests *before* committing. Test-first work — a committed failing test
waiting on a brand-new implementation/registry file that is still
untracked — is exactly the shape this fleet produces, and in exactly that
moment the selector under-selects: the waiting e2e test does not run, and
nothing in the output says the file's contents were skipped (the header
count even claims the file was considered). CI still runs the full suite,
so this is a local-feedback correctness bug, not a merge-safety hole.

## Acceptance criteria

- For an untracked new file under `pkgs/mcpx`, its contents feed the same
  diff-text analysis as a tracked change (e.g. via `git diff --no-index
  /dev/null <path>` or by intent-to-add), so:
  - T2 selects e2e tests mentioning names introduced only in an untracked
    registry file (the staged/untracked outputs match for the fixture
    above);
  - exported declarations in an untracked file drive T1b importer
    selection;
  - `newEnv` in an untracked e2e file triggers the rule-4 harness sample.
- A regression test/fixture covers the untracked case (the staged and
  untracked runs of the probe fixture select the same T2 set).
- Tracked/staged behaviour is unchanged; deleted-file handling (paths that
  no longer exist are excluded from reads) still works.

title: mcpx(gotest-report): a package-level fail with no Test event (build failure) is invisible — report says 0 failed, exits 0, and the broken run poisons the MCPX_GO_TESTS skip record down to the tests that ran

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`pkgs/mcpx/scripts/gotest-report.py` — the script that summarises `go test -json` in the mcpx workflow and guards the skipped-test record (`MCPX_GO_TESTS`) — never sees a package-level failure. A package that fails to build (or whose `TestMain`/setup fails) produces a `fail` event with **no `Test` field** in `go test -json` output; `read()` drops every event without a `Test` before counting, so the report says **0 failed** and exits **0**. Worse, because that package's tests never ran, its previously-skipped tests vanish from the run's skip list, so `decide()` reads the broken run as "skips went down" and writes a **new record with a lower (here: zero) skip ceiling** — and the workflow saves that record to `MCPX_GO_TESTS` on main whenever the record file exists, poisoning the guard for the next healthy run.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/gotest-report.py:36-48` — `read()`: `test = e.get("Test"); if not test: continue` runs **before** the `Action` counting, so a package-level `{"Action":"fail","Package":...}` event (the only failure signal for a build failure) is discarded. Failed counts, the failed list, and the exit code (`return 1 if (failed or rose) else 0`, :103) all derive from per-test events only.
- `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/gotest-report.py:55-68` — `decide()` compares only the skipped-name list against the stored record: fewer skips → returns a new record (`cur`), whatever the reason the skips are missing.
- `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml:182` captures `go test`'s own exit code separately, so the step still fails on a build break — but `mcpx.yml:211-220` then saves `$RUNNER_TEMP/gotest-record.json` via `gh variable set MCPX_GO_TESTS` on main **whenever the file exists**, with no check that the run was healthy. The corrupted record lands even on the red run.
- The script has no test file (`pkgs/mcpx/scripts/` contains no `test_gotest_report.py`), so none of this is pinned.

## Reproduced (laptop probe, sha-matched)

Probe `probe-2026-10-31-laneB-gotest/` on the laptop, script sha256 `7f09b7ae8cee0b5212bbb252207c46f55f711d6054eb13008f7ece7357d581fd` (identical in the sandbox clone at main `efc4e182` and the laptop clone). Synthetic `go test -json` stream: package `example/util` passes one test; package `example/daemon` fails to build (output events + `{"Action":"fail","Package":"example/daemon"}` with no `Test`). Stored record: 50 passed, 0 failed, `skipped_count: 2` (`daemon.TestA`, `daemon.TestB`).

Observed:

```text
exit code: 0
stdout: go tests: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (record: 2)
summary: | 1 | 0 | **0** | 2 (run 1/1) |
         "Skipped tests **down** from 2 to 0 (no longer skipped: daemon.TestA, daemon.TestB).
          On main this becomes the new record."
new record written: {"passed_count":1,"failed_count":0,"skipped_count":0,"skipped":[]}
```

A control stream of ordinary per-test pass/fail/skip events counts correctly — the gap is specifically the no-`Test` package events.

## Why it matters

- The report's own verdict is wrong on exactly the runs that matter most (a broken build): "0 failed", green exit from the script, and a summary table that shows the package's tests as un-skipped rather than never-run.
- The skip record is the anti-creep guard for the whole mcpx suite ("a skip cannot creep back in", script header). One build-broken main run rewrites it to the broken run's numbers (here ceiling 2 → 0, passed 50 → 1); the next healthy run then trips "more tests skipped than the record" and fails for tests that were skipped all along, with the original record's names lost.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A package-level `fail` event with no `Test` field is counted and reported as a failure (the package is named in the summary), and the script exits non-zero on it — independent of `go test`'s own exit code.
- [ ] A run containing any package-level failure (or, more generally, any failure) never produces a new skip record: `decide()`/main writes no record file when the run is not clean, so a broken run cannot move the ceiling in either direction.
- [ ] New tests for the script (synthetic JSON streams, in the style of the other `pkgs/mcpx/scripts` checks) pin: build-failed package + stored record → failure reported, exit 1, no new record; `TestMain`-failure package (same event shape) likewise; ordinary pass/fail/skip stream unchanged, including the quarantine exemption.
- [ ] Workflow behaviour after the fix: on a build-broken main run, `MCPX_GO_TESTS` is left untouched.

## Distinct from

Searched open + closed issues for `gotest-report`, package-level fail, and the `MCPX_GO_TESTS` record: no existing issue covers this script. The conformance-record scripts (`conformance-record.py`, `spec-parity.py`) are separate tools with their own records. Filed by new-issue-creator lane B, 2026-10-31.

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
# id(invite): `Invite::from_query` now percent-decodes key/node — non-canonical spellings (`%61…`, leading `+`) are accepted in both invite paths, and the pinning test's comments claim the opposite

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/src/invite.rs:91-99` — since the #2717 fix merged in PR #2737 (commit 57e42fa4), `from_query` runs `decode()` on the `key` and `node` fields. `decode()` (invite.rs:154-176) percent-decodes and maps `+` to a space.
- `pkgs/id/src/invite.rs:122-129` — `hex_key` then `trim()`s the decoded value, so a leading `+` (decoded to a space), a leading `%20`, or any percent-encoded hex digit (e.g. `%61` for `a`) is silently canonicalized and accepted.
- `Invite::query()` (invite.rs:62-68) never encodes key/node — it emits them as raw 64-char hex; only `name` is percent-encoded. Decoding key/node is therefore unnecessary for round-tripping and only widens the accepted spellings.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/explore.rs:1039-1055` — the pinning test's comments still say "Verify that web path refuses non-canonical hex encodings (percent-encoded key)" and "(leading plus in key)", but the assertions were flipped in the same PR to `StatusCode::OK`. Comment and assertion now contradict each other.
- Before PR #2737, both spellings were refused in both paths (the web handler's decoding was the discrepancy #2717 reported; the fix unified by loosening the strict parser instead of keeping key/node raw).

## Verification (this run)

Laptop probe worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-invite` at origin/main (37f9590b9), `pkgs/id/src/invite.rs` sha256 `01b1ca6f…` matched to the sandbox clone of main:

- `cargo test --lib invite::` — 8/8 pass.
- `cargo test --lib the_invite_page_names_the_account_and_carries_its_qr_code` — passes, i.e. on current main `GET /invite?key=%61a11…&node=…&name=Ann` returns **200** and `GET /invite?key=+{64-hex}&node=…&name=Ann` returns **200**, where the pre-#2737 behavior (and the test's own comments) say 400.

## Why it matters

An invite's key/node are canonical identifiers: the same account key now has arbitrarily many equivalent invite spellings (percent-encode any subset of hex digits, add a leading `+`/`%20`). This is the duplicate-spelling class the fleet already treats as a bug elsewhere (#2517, `+`-encoded pairs in directory/auth hex decoders), and it re-opens the exact parser-disagreement #2717 was filed to close — this time by making the lax reading canonical in both paths, with the regression test asserting the lax behavior under comments that claim refusal, so a future reader cannot tell the acceptance was unintended.

Secondary: `decode()`'s UTF-8 error says "the name is not UTF-8" (invite.rs:176) even when the failing field is key/node.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Invite::from_query` accepts key/node only in the canonical form `Invite::query()` emits (raw 64-char lowercase-or-uppercase hex, no percent-decoding, no `+`/whitespace trimming); percent-encoded or `+`-prefixed key/node values are refused in both the string (`Invite::parse`) and web (`/invite`) paths. Name decoding is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests pin refusal for `key=%61…` and `key=+…` in both paths, and the explore.rs test comments match the assertions.
- [ ] Or, if acceptance is a deliberate decision: the test comments, the invite module docs, and this issue are updated to say so explicitly, and the canonicalization is documented — silence/flipped assertions do not count.
- [ ] The `decode()` UTF-8 error message names the field being decoded, or is made field-neutral.

## Dedup

#2717 (closed) was the parser disagreement; this is the regression in its fix (PR #2737, merged today). #2517 is the same class in a different call site (directory/auth `hex_to_array`/`hex_bytes`) and does not cover invite parsing. #1770 is invite name control characters — different field, different fix.

title: sandbox backup: full-home restic backup built — the all-files gap (8,261 session originals lost) is closed

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

body:
## Summary

A full-home sandbox backup now exists and is verified. Before this build, **no scheduled backup covered the sandbox's files** — only `~/.config` had one.

## The gap

- Drew designed `sandbox-state-backup` on 2026-10-28: restic, `~/.config` only → R2 bucket `supabase-backups`, prefix `restic-sandbox-config`, system systemd timer daily 03:37 America/Chicago. Verified healthy at build time: 5 snapshots since 2026-10-28 (first id `9017c5d6`, ~84 MiB each), latest raw-data 40.9 MiB stored.
- Nothing scheduled covered the rest of `/home/hatch`. An Oct 27 record claiming a "sandbox-to-laptop rsync cron" was **false** — no such cron existed, enabled or disabled.
- The gap had already caused loss: platform rotation of `~/agents` destroyed **8,261 session originals**, which now survive only inside Atlas's canonical DB.

## What was built — `sandbox-home-backup`

Same pattern as the config backup, extended to the full home (Drew's directive 2026-10-31: all files backed up at least daily; delta-only uploads fine, nothing lost going forward):

- **restic 0.19.1 → R2** bucket `supabase-backups`, prefix `restic-sandbox-home` (separate repo). Password generated at build time and stored only in Bitwarden Secrets Manager as `restic.sandbox-home-password`; R2 keys fetched from Bitwarden by name at runtime, like the sibling.
- **Scope:** everything under `/home/hatch`. Excludes, each measured first: `~/.config` (has its own repo above — deliberately not double-backed-up), `~/nix-persist` (content-addressed nix store, reproducible from the backed-up nix configs), `~/.cache` (8.17 GB regenerable caches), `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (SECRET-SKIP per the muse-backup rule; the value lives in Bitwarden as `ssh.id-ed25519`; path+size recorded per run in a skip manifest, never the value).
- **Checkpointed per-entry design:** the sandbox VM recycled repeatedly during the seed (boots ~17:23, 19:44, 21:24, 21:29, 23:56 UTC on 2026-10-31, ~02:15 on 2026-11-01), killing two monolithic full-home runs with zero snapshots (a restic snapshot lands only at run end). The script now backs up each top-level entry as its own snapshot and `~/git` (~110 worktrees) one level deeper per entry, so a recycle loses at most the entry in flight. Entry list is enumerated at runtime.
- **Schedule:** system systemd timer `sandbox-home-backup.timer`, daily 04:37 America/Chicago, Persistent=true. Units don't survive VM recycles (`/etc/systemd/system` is volatile), so `install-backup-units.sh` reinstalls them and is wired into `~/tools/init.sh` — proven end-to-end when the 2026-10-31 23:00 UTC init restored both backup timers unattended. Known limitation: init is demand-triggered, so after a recycle the timers return when agent activity resumes, not at boot.
- **Retention:** `forget --keep-daily 14 --keep-weekly 8 --keep-monthly 12 --prune` in the same run, gated on all entries completing.

## Verification (2026-10-31 → 2026-11-01)

- Seed run completed 2026-11-01 01:55 UTC, `failures=0`: **547 snapshots; 335 expected entries checked against the snapshot list — 0 missing**; repo 22.8 GiB stored / 52.9 GiB logical (2.32× compression, 1,778,470 blobs).
- `restic check` (full structure, 547/547 snapshots): **no errors**. `restic check --read-data-subset=1%` (112 packs): **no errors**. (A 5% subset attempt was recycle-killed once and later abandoned at 30 min; the 1% subset plus restore tests carry the data-level proof.)
- Restore spot-test: an `~/agents` session `.jsonl`, a hatch-personal file, and `~/.gitconfig` restored to /tmp — all three **sha256-identical** to the live files.
- Two bugs found and fixed during the build: (1) restic exit code 1 originally passed silently (only rc=3/rc>3 handled) — now 0 ok / 3 note / anything else is a recorded failure; (2) recycle-killed runs leave stale repo locks that block later runs — the script now runs `restic unlock` at start (safe: removes only locks whose holder is gone).

## Locations

- Script, units, installer, README (with exact restore commands): `hatch-personal/scripts/sandbox-home-backup/` on the sandbox.
- Caution recorded in the README: `restic check --read-data*` needs `TMPDIR=~/tmp` on this sandbox — its default temp cache fills the 512 MiB /tmp tmpfs and breaks unrelated tools.

Related but distinct: #1516 (2026-10-27 backup coverage audit), #1849 (laptop non-git data has no routine backup).

title: github-backup(reconcile): a failed clone pass exits 0 and is absent from the dated report — clone_all's verdict is dropped by its only scheduled caller

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/github-backup
labels.description: infra/github-backup estate mirror system

body:
## Problem

In the weekly reconcile (`infra/github-backup/bin/reconcile.py`) — the sweep the module calls its correctness floor — **a failed clone pass is invisible to every surface that could alarm on it**: `main()` returns 0, and the dated reconcile report is written *before* the clone pass runs, so it never records the clone outcome at all.

`clone_all.py` computes a meaningful exit code (0 only when every planned repo cloned ok), and reconcile is its only scheduled caller — but reconcile drops that code on the floor. A week where every missing mirror fails to clone (bad token, disk full, network down) therefore looks exactly like a clean week to the systemd timer, and the only trace is a stdout line in the journal and the per-repo rows in `clone-status.jsonl`, which nothing alarms on.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `7d8a3ca5`)

- `reconcile.py:108-113` — the clone pass: `r = subprocess.run([... clone_all.py])`; on `r.returncode != 0` it only `print("clone pass had failures; see clone-status.jsonl")`. The value is never stored or returned.
- `reconcile.py:115` — `return 1 if errors else 0`: the exit code reflects owner-level inventory errors only (docstring :13-14 states this as the design). Clone-pass failure is not an input.
- `reconcile.py:102-105` — the dated report `reconcile-<today>.md` is written before the clone pass (:108), so the report cannot and does not record whether the clones it triggered succeeded; its mirror count is explicitly "missing on disk **before** clone pass" (:88).
- `clone_all.py:106-107` — `return 0 if ok == len(plan) else 1`: the callee's verdict exists and is discarded by its caller.
- `manifest_mod.build(root)` (:114) runs after the clone pass and will list the repos as `missing` in MANIFEST.json — but per #3270, nothing reads MANIFEST as an alarm; the exit code is this system's stated alarm channel.

### Probe (laptop, verbatim copies, sha256-matched)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-reconcileexit/` (laptop) — `reconcile.py` sha256 `762a7639…` identical to sandbox main `7d8a3ca5`; the copied tree's config pointed at a probe backup root with one planned repo missing on disk; `inventory`/`build_plan` stubbed, the `clone_all.py` subprocess stubbed to a chosen return code, everything else (report write, manifest build, exit return) the real code:

```text
laptop reconcile.py sha256: 762a763977e823247f1576fcf2d58fb83a29ff39521f7d8d16ba44635e073e25 MATCH
CASE clone_rc=1 errors=False -> main() returned 0; report mentions failure: False
CASE clone_rc=0 errors=False -> main() returned 0; report mentions failure: False
CASE clone_rc=0 errors=True  -> main() returned 1; report mentions failure: False
```

The control proves the exit channel works — for inventory errors only. Clone success and clone failure are indistinguishable in both the exit code and the dated report.

## Why it matters

Reconcile is the weekly guarantee that nothing is missed (#3215): it is the only path that *creates* mirrors for newly planned repos. If that creation fails, the daily fetch cannot fetch a mirror that does not exist — and per #3270 a missing mirror never trips the daily chronic alarm either — so a failed clone pass plus a missing mirror is a repo with **no backup and no alarm on any cadence**, discovered at disaster-recovery time. The fix is small: the verdict already exists in `clone_all.py`'s exit code; reconcile just has to keep it.

Related, not duplicates: #3270 (daily fetch's chronic alarm cannot see a missing mirror; its body notes the clone-pass-fails scenario as background, but its acceptance is entirely in `fetch_mirrors.py`). #3282 (the mirror contract design) adopts #3238/#3233/#3250/#3219/#3270/#3257/#3240/#3229 in its phases — reconcile's exit code and report are not among them; this filing is the reconcile-side recorded outcome its rule 3 ("every attempt ends in a recorded outcome") currently lacks. #3240 (atomic state writes) covers torn writes, not dropped exit codes.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the clone pass exits non-zero, `reconcile.py` exits non-zero (in addition to the existing inventory-error path), so the weekly timer unit surfaces the failure.
- [ ] The dated reconcile report records the clone-pass outcome (attempted count / ok / fail, or at minimum pass vs fail with the failing repos named or pointed to `clone-status.jsonl`) — the report is amended or written after the clone pass, not before it alone.
- [ ] A run with no missing mirrors, or a fully successful clone pass, still exits 0 when inventory is clean; the inventory-error exit behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression coverage (script-level test or probe harness): clone-pass rc=1 → reconcile rc=1 and report names the failure; clone-pass rc=0 → reconcile rc=0.

body:
# sync-models: unrecognized arguments are silently ignored — a typo'd `--dry-rnu` rewrites the live OpenCode config in place (and reloads opencode)

## Summary

`bin/sync-models.mjs` — the legacy model sync that, per `bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs`'s header, "rewrites the deployed config in place (and auto-removes)" and is still the script the sync-models service maintains the deployed user config with — parses its CLI flags by membership only and never rejects an argument it does not recognize:

- `bin/sync-models.mjs:6-7` — `const DRY_RUN = process.argv.includes('--dry-run')`, `const VERBOSE = process.argv.includes('--verbose') || …`. There is no allowlist check over `process.argv` anywhere in the file.

So `sync-models.mjs --dry-rnu` (or any unknown flag, e.g. `--bogus-flag`) is silently treated as a full APPLY run: it rewrites the target OpenCode config in place (`bin/sync-models.mjs:693-696`, after writing a `.backup`), including **removals**, and then triggers `opencode reload` (:700) — exiting 0 and printing "Successfully updated". The operator who typo'd the dry-run flag gets no signal the live config was just rewritten.

This is the same defect class already filed for the sibling deploy/install scripts — #3264 (pkarr-worker `deploy.mjs`), #3278 (opencode-claimant `install.mjs`), #3281 (id-mail worker `deploy.mjs`), #3287 (github-backup worker `deploy.mjs`) — but a different script none of them covers. The repo's shell tools already meet the stricter standard: `lib/bws-to-sops.sh` dies on `unknown argument` and `scripts/stage-docs.sh` exits 1 on an unknown option.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-syncmodels/` (sync-models.mjs + sync-models.policy.json copied verbatim; sha256 `f53c214ae40f9358113c19c9458b517a7859932f2e5cbbedee49b3d328d3ca5e` / `73807ce822c1d477f02e9a9b9456141a5fcacc8f905954792204bba5b0a70590`, matching main `b56ccda5`). Deterministic change source: temp `HOME` whose `.codex/models_cache.json` holds one model (`probe-model-1`) that the temp target config lacks; `agy` stubbed off via PATH; target config pointed at a temp file via `OPENCODE_CONFIG_PATH`:

- Control — `--dry-run`: `Mode: DRY-RUN (no files will be changed)`, `+ Adding openai-codex/probe-model-1`, `Dry run complete. No files written.`, exit 0; config unchanged, no `.backup`.
- `--dry-rnu`: `Mode: APPLY`, same addition, then `Created backup at …/config.jsonc.backup` and `Successfully updated …/config.jsonc!`, exit 0; the config on disk now contains `probe-model-1`.
- `--bogus-flag`: exit 0, identical APPLY outcome (backup written, config rewritten).

## Why it matters

Unlike its PR-based successor (`provider-catalog-sync.mjs`, dry-run by default, changes land through a reviewable PR), this script edits the deployed config directly and auto-removes models the sources no longer list. A typo in the one safety flag turns a preview into an unreviewed rewrite of the live config plus an `opencode reload`, with a success exit code — the class of surprise the successor tool was built to eliminate, still reachable through the legacy path the service actually runs.

## Acceptance criteria

- Any argument that is not `--dry-run`, `--verbose` or `-v` makes the script exit non-zero with a usage error naming the offending argument, before any fetch, discovery, or file write.
- `--dry-run`, `--verbose`/`-v`, and bare (APPLY) behavior is unchanged.
- A stubbed/temp-HOME test (or equivalent) pins: unknown flag → non-zero exit + config untouched + no `.backup`; `--dry-run` → no writes even when changes exist.

# proxy-supervise: unrecognized arguments are silently ignored — a typo'd `--dry-rnu` starts/rolls real proxies, and a typo'd `--statuz` reconciles instead of reporting status

## Summary

`bin/proxy-supervise.mjs` (the supervisor that starts/stops/rolls the local proxy instances on its timer) parses its CLI flags by membership only and never rejects an argument it does not recognize:

- `bin/proxy-supervise.mjs:603-629` — `const args = process.argv.slice(2)`; flags are read with `args.indexOf('--config')` / `args.indexOf('--only')` (:604-608), `args.includes('--status')` (:620) and `args.includes('--dry-run')` (:629). There is no allowlist check over `args` anywhere in `main()`; the only validation is that `--config` is present.

So `proxy-supervise.mjs --config <cfg> --dry-rnu` is silently treated as a real reconcile: it acquires the per-proxy lock and **starts a new proxy instance** (or rolls/stops the existing one). Worse, the read-only path has the same flaw in reverse: `--statuz` (a typo of `--status`) falls through to a full reconcile instead of printing status. Both exit 0.

This is the same defect class already filed for the sibling deploy/install scripts — #3264 (pkarr-worker `deploy.mjs`), #3278 (opencode-claimant `install.mjs`), #3281 (id-mail worker `deploy.mjs`), #3287 (github-backup worker `deploy.mjs`) — but this script is a different, long-lived operator tool none of them covers. The repo's shell tools already meet the stricter standard: `lib/bws-to-sops.sh` dies on `unknown argument` and `scripts/stage-docs.sh` exits 1 on an unknown option.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-supervise/` (proxy-supervise.mjs copied verbatim; sha256 `1926654cf1148a65a59e6b0c05f66a42552307de68d194153fcefbe25e7252bb`, matching main `b56ccda5`), with a fixture config in a temp dir (one proxy whose command is a tiny HTTP server answering `/health`, `stateDir`/`endpointDir` inside the probe dir, port 18999):

- Control — `--dry-run`: exit 0, action `would-start`, port stays FREE, no state or endpoint files written.
- `--dry-rnu`: exit 0, action **`started`** — a real server process (pid recorded in `state/probeproxy.json`), port 18999 HEALTHY afterwards.
- `--bogus-flag`: exit 0, identical real start (new pid, state file written, port healthy).
- `--statuz`: exit 0, action `started` — the intended read-only status check reconciled and started the proxy instead.

(The probe cleaned up every instance it started; final port check FREE.)

## Why it matters

This supervisor owns the lifecycle of the local proxy fleet: a real reconcile can start, roll, drain and stop live proxy processes. A one-character typo in either safety flag — the preview flag `--dry-run` or the read-only `--status` — silently becomes the mutating operation, with a success exit code and a normal JSON result line, so the operator has no signal anything beyond a preview/status just happened.

## Acceptance criteria

- Any argument that is not `--config <path>`, `--only <name>`, `--status` or `--dry-run` makes the script exit non-zero with a usage error naming the offending argument, before any lock is taken or any reconcile runs.
- `--config` / `--only` with a missing value or a value that is another flag are rejected the same way.
- `--status`, `--dry-run`, and bare reconcile behavior is unchanged.
- A test (the script already has importable exports / a test file pattern in `bin/`) pins: unknown flag → non-zero exit + zero spawned processes; `--dry-run` → `would-start` only; `--statuz`-style typos do not fall through to reconcile.

# github-backup(worker deploy): unrecognized arguments are silently ignored — a typo'd `--dry-rnu` performs a real deploy (upload + secret reset)

## Summary

`infra/github-backup/worker/deploy.mjs` (landed today in #3280 / commit 307a2501) parses its CLI flags by membership only and never rejects an argument it does not recognize:

- `deploy.mjs:40-47` — `const dryRun = args.includes("--dry-run")`, `args.indexOf("--deploy-version")`; there is no allowlist check over `args` anywhere in the file.

So `deploy.mjs --dry-rnu` (or any unknown flag, e.g. `--bogus-flag`) is silently treated as a plain deploy of HEAD: it uploads a new Worker version, creates the 100% deployment when the version is not already live, and (re)sets the live Worker secrets `DRAIN_BEARER` and `GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET` from Bitwarden — then exits 0 reporting the Worker live. The operator who typo'd the dry-run flag gets no signal that a production deploy just happened.

This is the same defect class already filed for the sibling deploy/install scripts — #3264 (pkarr-worker `deploy.mjs`), #3278 (opencode-claimant `install.mjs`), #3281 (id-mail worker `deploy.mjs`) — but this script is new code merged after those filings and is not covered by any of them.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-ghbdeploy/` (deploy.mjs copied verbatim; sha256 `feb5ebfc3d11a9a592d444e9722b8548973e533651fa9ffdac982dac28ee2ad7`, matching main `cf1b243f`), with `bws` / `wrangler` / `git` stubbed to log every invocation and return canned JSON:

- Control — `node deploy.mjs --dry-run`: exit 0; the only stub call is `wrangler deploy --dry-run`; prints "dry run: config builds, nothing uploaded".
- `node deploy.mjs --dry-rnu`: exit 0; stub log shows the FULL real deploy sequence — `git rev-parse HEAD`, `wrangler versions list`, `wrangler versions upload --tag git-abcdef012345 …`, `wrangler deployments list`, `wrangler secret put DRAIN_BEARER`, `wrangler secret put GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, and the live report (`live: https://developing-today-backup.developing-today.workers.dev at version …`). (No `versions deploy` call in this run only because the stub reported the just-uploaded version as already live; against real wrangler state a fresh upload is not live, so the deployment-create step runs too.)
- `node deploy.mjs --bogus-flag`: exit 0; identical full deploy sequence.

## Why it matters

This script is the deploy path for the backup webhook receiver Worker. A one-character typo in the safety flag turns a no-op validation into a production deploy of whatever HEAD happens to be, including resetting the live Worker's secrets — with a success exit code and a normal "live:" report, so the mistake is invisible in the moment and only surfaces if the deployed code misbehaves.

## Acceptance criteria

- Any argument that is not `--dry-run` or `--deploy-version <id>` (with a present, non-flag value) makes the script exit non-zero with a usage error naming the offending argument, before any `bws`/`wrangler`/`git` call.
- `--deploy-version` followed by another flag or nothing is rejected the same way.
- `--dry-run`, bare (deploy HEAD), and `--deploy-version <id>` behavior is unchanged.
- A stubbed-CLI test (or equivalent) pins: unknown flag → zero stub calls + non-zero exit; `--dry-run` → only the dry-run validation call.

body:
# aggregator(snapshots): compact-usage-snapshots accepts `--months 0` — `--apply` compacts the in-progress month, deleting its raw file and leaving only min/max/last

## Evidence (verified this run, main `0f969120`)

The retention guard in `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/compact-usage-snapshots.ts:26-31` accepts zero:

```ts
const retentionMonths = monthsArg >= 0 ? Number(process.argv[monthsArg + 1]) : 13;
if (!Number.isInteger(retentionMonths) || retentionMonths < 0) { /* exit 2 */ }
```

`SnapshotStore.compact` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts:656-673`) computes `cutoffMonth = shiftMonth(currentMonth, -retentionMonths)` and compacts every raw month with `month <= cutoffMonth`. With `retentionMonths = 0` the cutoff **is** the current month, so the month still being appended to is eligible — contradicting the script header ("raw monthly files are kept 13 months, then replaced by a rollup") and the `compact()` doc ("compact every raw monthly file **older than** `retentionMonths`", snapshots.ts:643-644). No other caller passes `retentionMonths` (grep over `*.ts`: only this script and `snapshots.ts` itself).

Probe (laptop, real script + real `SnapshotStore`, both files sha256-matched between the sandbox and laptop clones: script `d65e504a…`, snapshots.ts `c6685035…`; temp store seeded with 3 raw records in the current month, values 40 / 85 / 10; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-compact0/`):

| run | result |
|---|---|
| control: `--apply --months 13` | current month untouched — `usage-2026-11.jsonl` stays raw, "no months at or before the 2025-10 cutoff — nothing to do" |
| `--apply --months 0` | **current month compacted: "2026-11: 3 records -> 1 rollups (compacted)"; `usage-2026-11.jsonl` deleted**, only `usage-2026-11.rollup.jsonl` remains (one rollup holding count/min/max/last) |

The intermediate raw observations for the live month (every value that is not the min, max, or last) are irreversibly gone; `readAll`/`byService` thereafter expand the rollup into synthetic min/max/last records for the month everyone actually looks at. Later appends re-create a raw file and merge on the next compaction (the store tolerates it), so this is silent history loss, not corruption — which is exactly why a guard matters: the run reports success.

## Why it matters

This is the fleet's destructive retention tool for usage-snapshot history (design §6, #1117). Its one safety property is that compaction only touches months safely in the past. A single plausible flag value — `0`, e.g. from an operator or a wrapper script intending "no extra retention" — silently destroys the raw fidelity of the in-progress month while exiting 0 with a normal-looking report. The boundary semantics already pin "a month exactly at the cutoff is eligible" for the 13-month case (`test/snapshot-retention.test.ts`: 2025-09 at exactly 13 months back compacts, 2025-10 at 12 stays raw), so the fix must state the floor, not just shift the comparison.

## Acceptance criteria

- `compact-usage-snapshots.ts --months 0` (and any value `< 1`) exits 2 with the existing invalid-`--months` error, before touching the store — in both dry-run and `--apply` modes.
- Defense in depth at the library seam: `SnapshotStore.compact({ retentionMonths: 0 })` never compacts the current month (reject the value, or clamp the cutoff to at most the previous month), so a future caller cannot reintroduce this.
- A pinning test (extending `pm-stack/aggregator/test/snapshot-retention.test.ts`) shows the current month stays raw under the smallest accepted retention, and existing retention tests (boundary month eligible, recent month raw, idempotence, late-record merge) still pass.
- `--months 1` and the default (13) behave exactly as today for past months.

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `compact-usage-snapshots`, snapshot retention and `--months` — #1117 (closed, the original retention feature) and #2941 (unrelated `__proto__` grouping bug in the same store) are the only neighbours; neither covers the zero-retention / current-month case.

title: cold-store-reaper: state.json and credentials.json are written in place with O_TRUNC — one torn write wedges every later run with a raw JSONDecodeError

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator

labels.description: Package/app: cold-store-reaper (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`ColdStore._write_private_json` (pkgs/cold-store-reaper/cold_store.py:373-378) writes `credentials.json` and `state.json` **in place**: `os.open(path, O_WRONLY|O_CREAT|O_TRUNC)` followed by `json.dump` directly into the destination file. There is no temp file, no `os.replace`, and no fsync. A crash, power loss, OOM kill, or any exception mid-`json.dump` leaves the destination truncated to a partial JSON document.

Both readers then fail hard with a **raw** error, not the module's own error type:

- `load_state` (cold_store.py:393-396) does a bare `json.loads(self.state_path.read_text())` — a torn `state.json` raises `json.decoder.JSONDecodeError` uncaught. `load_state` is on the path of `ensure_folders` (:687) and `_folder_id`/`_d1_endpoint` (:709, :1242), so one torn write wedges every later run until a human hand-repairs the file.
- `load_credentials` (cold_store.py:381-391) does the same bare `json.loads` — a torn `credentials.json` raises raw `JSONDecodeError` instead of the `ColdStoreError("credentials.json is missing …")`-style actionable errors the function otherwise raises, masking the real cause (the file exists; it is half-written).

`save_state` (cold_store.py:398-405) is called on routine paths (e.g. after folder discovery, :705), so the exposure window is every run, not just `init`.

## Evidence (verified this run, 2026-10-31)

Code: cold_store.py:373-378 (in-place O_TRUNC write), :381-396 (bare `json.loads` in both loaders), :398-405 (`save_state` via the same writer).

Laptop probe (source sha-matched: cold_store.py sha256 `fba42e08027514abae2de1602e755854ebfd6a3b578a5eece34b6c0becd39b95` on both sandbox main `ed3a285e` and the laptop copy; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-coldstore-atomic/`):

- Control: `save_state({"folders": {"a": "1"}})` then `load_state()` returns the dict.
- Simulated crash mid-write (partial JSON flushed, then the write aborts): `state.json` is left as `b'{"folders": {"a": "1"'`.
- After that, `load_state()` **raises `JSONDecodeError: Expecting ',' delimiter: line 1 column 22`** — and `isinstance(e, ColdStoreError)` is `False`.
- Same simulation against `_write_private_json(credentials_path, …)`: `load_credentials()` raises the same raw `JSONDecodeError`.

Contrast within the same repo: pkgs/id's JSONL stores treat a crash-torn tail as a normal, repairable case (e.g. `Petnames::open` drops and truncates a torn final line). Cold-store's two most state-critical JSON files get no such protection.

## Why it matters

Cold-store is the backup system: its `state.json` carries the Drive folder map every backup/restore run depends on, and `credentials.json` is hand-filled from Bitwarden — a torn credentials file destroyed by a crash during an unrelated `save_state`-adjacent write forces manual credential re-entry. A backup tool whose own state files are the least crash-safe part of the system will eventually wedge a nightly run with an inscrutable stdlib traceback instead of an actionable error.

## Distinct from

- #3240 (github-backup's plan/state/MANIFEST non-atomic writes — different tool, different files).
- #2550 (prune_backups Drive/ledger crash-consistency — remote side, not the local JSON writers).
- #940 (closed; token cached in state.json + file permissions — not write atomicity).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `_write_private_json` writes to a temp file in the same directory, fsyncs, and `os.replace`s onto the destination (preserving 0600), so a crash at any point leaves either the old or the new complete document.
- [ ] `load_state` / `load_credentials` on a corrupt file raise `ColdStoreError` naming the file and the parse problem (or recover to a documented default), never a raw `JSONDecodeError`.
- [ ] Regression test: simulate a mid-write failure (partial write + raise) and assert the previous complete document still loads, for both state and credentials paths.
- [ ] Existing cold-store test suite passes.

labels.name: task/triage

labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/install.mjs` — the installer that writes the #3026 claimant scheduled task into the laptop's real OpenChamber project store — performs **no argument validation**. `main()` (install.mjs:65-71) collects only the spellings it knows:

```js
const args = new Set(argv.filter((a) => a.startsWith("--")));
const storeIdx = argv.indexOf("--store");
const storePath = storeIdx >= 0 ? argv[storeIdx + 1] : DEFAULT_STORE;
...
enabled: args.has("--enable") ? true : (existing?.enabled ?? false),
```

Everything else on the command line is silently dropped, and the script proceeds to do a **real install**: it backs up and then atomically renames over the target store (install.mjs:91-94). Three concrete failure shapes:

1. **A typo'd `--dry-rnu` performs a real install.** The operator believes they are previewing; the store is actually rewritten and the claimant task inserted/refreshed. If the task already exists *enabled* in that store, this also silently refreshes the live task's prompt to the current `prompt.md` — a production behavior change made by a preview command.
2. **Any unknown flag (`--bogus-flag`, a stray positional) is ignored the same way**, with exit 0 and a normal-looking summary. The only difference between the dry-run and real-run summaries is a `dry_run: true` field the operator has to notice the *absence* of.
3. **A typo'd `--stor <path>` falls back to `DEFAULT_STORE`** (install.mjs:69-71: `indexOf("--store")` misses, so the real `~/.config/openchamber/projects/…` store is used) — a preview aimed at a scratch store writes the operator's real OpenChamber store instead. (Code-read consequence; not probed, for obvious reasons.)

## Evidence (verified this run, main 3186e252)

`install.mjs` sha256 `2ff84f5a48b2…` and `prompt.md` sha256 `dec788608534…` are identical in the sandbox clone at 3186e252 and the laptop clone. Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-claimant-install/` (node v24.21.0, real `install.mjs`, temp stores seeded with one unrelated task):

- `node install.mjs --store store-typo.json --dry-rnu` → exit 0, summary `{action: "inserted", tasks_before: 1, tasks_after: 2}` with **no** `dry_run` marker; the store afterwards contains the claimant task `f1b4a33b-14d5-4a69-9ad6-d221e42e3ac9` alongside the seed task, and a `store-typo.json.bak-<stamp>` backup was created — i.e. a real write happened.
- Control: the same command with correctly spelled `--dry-run` → store byte-identical afterwards (still only the seed task, 84 bytes), no backup file created.
- `node install.mjs --store store-bogus.json --bogus-flag` → same real write as the typo case (task inserted, backup created, exit 0).

Existing tests (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test/install.test.mjs`, 7 tests) cover `buildTask`/`mergeTasks` only; nothing exercises `main()`'s argument handling, so no test pins the unknown-argument behavior either way.

## Why it matters

This installer's whole safety story is in its header comment: the store "is runtime state", installing is an idempotent merge, and the task "installs DISABLED … enabling is the parallel-run gate's decision". A silent-argument-drop defeats the two operator-facing safeguards on that story — `--dry-run` (preview before touching runtime state) and `--store` (aim at a scratch store, not the real one). The failure is silent and exit-0, so scripts and operators cannot tell a preview from a write except by diffing the store afterwards.

Distinct from #3264 (same silent-args pattern in `pkgs/pkarr-worker/deploy.mjs`, a different tool whose consequence is a production deploy; that issue's fix does not touch this file) and from #3252/#3261 (pkarr-worker deploy/retention arguments).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any unrecognized argument — unknown `--flag`, unexpected positional, or a `--store` with no following value — makes `install.mjs` exit non-zero with a usage error naming the offending argument, and writes nothing (no store write, no backup file).
- [ ] `--dry-rnu`, `--bogus-flag`, and `--stor <path>` are each refused by a regression test that drives `main()` (or an extracted argument parser) against a temp store and asserts the store is byte-identical afterwards.
- [ ] The documented invocations keep working exactly as before: bare install, `--dry-run` (no write, no backup), `--store <path>`, `--enable`, and their combinations; the existing 7 `install.test.mjs` tests still pass.
- [ ] `--enable` handling is unchanged in meaning: a typo must never silently *enable*, and a refused invocation must never change an existing task's `enabled` state.

body:
# chat: pressing Enter on an empty input broadcasts an empty message to every session

## Evidence (verified this run, main 2bc0bf99)

In `pkgs/chat/main.go`, the `tea.KeyEnter` arm of `model.Update` sends whatever the textarea holds, unconditionally:

- `main.go:158-166` — `case tea.KeyEnter:` calls `m.app.send(chatMsg{id: m.id, text: m.textarea.Value()})` with no emptiness check, then resets the textarea.
- `main.go:171-174` — every received `chatMsg` is appended to `m.messages` and re-rendered, so the empty message lands in every connected session's history as a bare `name: ` line (and, per #3268, that history is never trimmed).

Reproduced end-to-end on the laptop with the real binary (source sha-matched to main 2bc0bf99 via `git hash-object` on main.go/go.mod/go.sum; probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-chatempty/` on the laptop):

1. Built `pkgs/chat` and started the server; connected one SSH client (`tester`) over a PTY.
2. Pressed Enter once with the textarea empty, then typed `hello` and pressed Enter.
3. The rendered history contained a `tester: ` line with no text (from the first, empty Enter) ahead of `tester: hello`. The blank line is a stored broadcast message, not a rendering artifact — it is in `m.messages` on every session.

Whitespace-only input (`"   "`) takes the same path and broadcasts an effectively blank line.

## Why it matters

An accidental Enter (easy in a TUI, e.g. after a message is sent and the textarea is already reset) spams a permanent blank line into every participant's scrollback. There is no way to recall it, and it compounds the unbounded-history growth in #3268. Every chat program treats empty Enter as a no-op; this one treats it as a message.

## Acceptance criteria

- Pressing Enter with an empty or whitespace-only textarea sends nothing: no `chatMsg` is broadcast, nothing is appended to any session's history, and the textarea state is unchanged.
- Pressing Enter with real text (including text with leading/trailing spaces around content) still broadcasts exactly that text, once.
- A regression test or scripted probe covers the empty-Enter case (e.g. model-level Update test driving `initialModel` + a KeyEnter msg with a recording app, or the PTY probe above).

## Dedup / distinctness

Distinct from #3201 (progs registry never pruned — fan-out plumbing), #3209 (graceful shutdown exits 1) and #3268 (history never trimmed — this issue is about a bogus entry being created, not about retention). Open+closed search for chat empty-message/broadcast on 2026-10-31 returned no existing issue.

title: id(world-ssh): SshTarget accepts whitespace/control/slash in user and host — only emptiness is checked, so 'exam ple.org', ' @host' and newline-bearing hosts parse and fail later in russh

labels.name: task/triage

body:
## Problem

`SshTarget::from_str` (`pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs:1008-1051`, main `4b0f9ceb`) validates the user and host only for emptiness:

```rust
anyhow::ensure!(
    !host.is_empty() && !user.is_empty(),
    "`{text}` is not [user@]host[:port]"
);
```

Every other character is accepted. A host or login containing a space, tab, newline, slash, or leading/trailing whitespace parses successfully, and the bad value only fails later — inside russh's connect (`world_ssh.rs:1133`, `(target.host.as_str(), target.port)`) as an opaque DNS/socket error, or at `authenticate_password(target.user.as_str(), "")` (`world_ssh.rs:1150`) as an unexplained auth failure. The parser's own test (`world_ssh.rs:2387-2410`) already refuses the neighbouring bad spellings (`""`, `host:`, `::1`, `[::1`, `@host`, `[::1]x`); whitespace/control/slash-bearing user and host parts are the gap that slips through, because "non-empty" is not a host or login grammar.

This is the user/host sibling of #3207 (same parser, port range only — port 0 / `+22`).

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneB-sshtarget-host/`, rustc, `FromStr` body transcribed verbatim with anyhow macros replaced by equivalent `Err` returns; `world_ssh.rs` sha256 `5c6900cdb2412280…` identical on the sandbox clone at `4b0f9ceb` and the laptop clone `~/git/code`):

```text
"example.org"            -> Ok(user="id" host="example.org" port=22)      (control)
"ada@example.org:2222"   -> Ok(user="ada" host="example.org" port=2222)   (control)
"[::1]:2022"             -> Ok(user="id" host="::1" port=2022)            (control)
"exam ple.org"           -> Ok(host="exam ple.org")
"ada@exam ple.org:2222"  -> Ok(host="exam ple.org")
"user name@example.org"  -> Ok(user="user name")
" @example.org"          -> Ok(user=" ")
"user@exa\tmple.org"     -> Ok(host="exa\tmple.org")
"us\ter@example.org"     -> Ok(user="us\ter")
"a/b@example.org"        -> Ok(user="a/b")
"user@ho/st"             -> Ok(host="ho/st")
"[:: 1]"                 -> Ok(host=":: 1")
"user@example.org "      -> Ok(host="example.org ")
" example.org"           -> Ok(host=" example.org")
"user@example.org\n.evil" -> Ok(host="example.org\n.evil")
"" / "@host" / "host:" / "[::1]x" -> Err   (already refused today)
```

Dedup: open + closed search for `SshTarget` returns only #3207, which covers the port field exclusively (its acceptance criteria name port 0 and `+22` only). No existing issue covers the user/host fields of this parser.

## Why it matters

A typo'd, pasted, or scripted target with an invisible character (a trailing space from a copy-paste, a tab, a newline) starts down the SSH path and fails with a misleading connect/auth error that sends the user debugging host keys and networks instead of the target string. A newline-bearing host also lands verbatim in error messages and the known-hosts lookup key (`HostKeyTrust.host`, `world_ssh.rs:1126`). Every other malformed target is refused at parse time with the target named; user and host should be too.

## Acceptance criteria

- `SshTarget::from_str` refuses a user or host containing whitespace or control characters (space, tab, CR, LF, leading/trailing whitespace), with an error naming the target, consistent with the existing bad-spelling tests.
- The bracketed-IPv6 host form is held to the same rule (e.g. `[:: 1]` is refused; a valid IPv6 literal keeps parsing).
- A user or host containing `/` is refused, or explicitly accepted-and-documented — no silent third behaviour.
- Valid targets keep parsing exactly as today: `example.org` → user `id`, port 22; `ada@example.org:2222`; `[::1]:2022`; `me@[::1]` → 22.
- Tests in `ssh_targets_parse_user_host_and_port` (or a sibling) pin the user/host refusals.

title: id(web): world presenter widens every U+FE0F cluster to 2 — a letter+VS16 cell (a️) is Rust-valid at columns 1 but renderWorldSurface refuses the whole screen

body:
## Summary

`id(web)`: the TS world presenter's `graphemeWidth` (`pkgs/id/web/src/world-surface.ts:321`) returns width **2 for every grapheme cluster that contains U+FE0F** (variation selector 16):

```ts
if (codePoints.includes(0xfe0f)) return 2;
```

Rust's `unicode-width` 0.2.2 — the validator the server side uses (`pkgs/id/src/world_presentation.rs`, `parse_surface` assigns each cell's `columns` from `UnicodeWidthStr::width(grapheme)`) — widens a base+FE0F cluster to 2 **only for its emoji-presentable bases** (digits, `#`, `*`, ©, ®, ™, suits, ▶/◀, ↔/↩/⤴, 〰/〽/㊗/㊙, actual emoji, …). For ordinary bases the cluster stays width 1, and a lone U+FE0F is width 0.

So a Rust-valid screen whose row contains e.g. `a️` (U+0061 U+FE0F) is built by `parse_surface` with `columns: 1` — and the web presenter then computes TS width 2 ≠ 1 and `renderWorldSurface` returns `false` for the **whole screen**, which falls back to raw text. This is exactly the #1581/#761 failure mode (one mis-measured cell rejects the entire frame), in a class those fixes and the #2962 differential never scoped: #2962 covers single code points **alone** and **+U+FE0E**; it never tested multi-codepoint clusters ending in U+FE0F.

## Evidence (main `c0fb853a`; both files sha256-identical in the sandbox and laptop clones)

TS side — verbatim extraction of `WIDE_RANGES`/`codePointWidth`/`graphemeWidth` from `world-surface.ts` (sha256 `5e04c698…`), run under bun on the laptop; Rust side — standalone probe pinned to `unicode-width = "=0.2.2"` (the crate/version `world_presentation.rs` uses), same inputs. Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-31-laneA-vs16/` (laptop).

| cluster | Rust 0.2.2 | TS `graphemeWidth` |
|---|---|---|
| `a` + FE0F | 1 | **2** |
| `x` / `Z` / `é` / `Ω` + FE0F | 1 | **2** |
| `→` (U+2192) + FE0F | 1 | **2** |
| `!` / `?` / `%` / space + FE0F | 1 | **2** |
| lone FE0F | 0 | **2** |
| `1` / `#` / `*` / `0` + FE0F | 2 | 2 (agree) |
| © / ® / ™ + FE0F | 2 | 2 (agree) |
| ♠ / ♥ / ♦ / ▶ / ◀ / ↔ / ↩ / ⤴ / 〰 / 〽 / ㊗ / ㊙ + FE0F | 2 | 2 (agree) |
| ⚠ (U+26A0) + FE0F, ☝ + FE0F, ❤ + FE0F, 😀 + FE0F | 2 | 2 (agree) |
| ZWJ alone (U+200D) | 0 | **1** (same function, minor: Rust rejects width-0 cells, TS would admit one at `columns: 1`) |

Existing tests only cover the agreeing cases: `world-surface.test.ts:271-272` exercises U+26A0+FE0F (⚠️) among its wide glyphs; no test pairs FE0F with a non-emoji-presentable base.

## Why it matters

The two validators are a matched pair by design — the TS file's own comments insist "The two validators must not disagree" (`world-surface.ts`, on the symbol-cap removal). Any world program that emits a letter, digit-free symbol, or arrow followed by VS16 (copy-pasted text and styled labels do this in the wild) produces a screen the server accepts and the browser refuses wholesale, degrading the world view to raw text with no error pointing at the cell. The fix is small and well-scoped: gate the FE0F shortcut on the same emoji-presentable base set unicode-width uses (the file already maintains exactly such a table for the FE0E narrowing case, `TEXT_PRESENTATION_RANGES`, plus the extra VS16-only bases like digits/`#`/`*` — the Rust probe above enumerates the agreeing set to seed it).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `graphemeWidth` widens a cluster containing U+FE0F to 2 only when the base is one unicode-width 0.2.2 widens (its VS16/emoji-presentation set); a cluster of a letter/punctuation/arrow/space + FE0F measures 1, and a lone FE0F measures 0.
- [ ] The ZWJ-alone case (Rust 0 vs TS 1) is dispositioned in the same pass — fixed or explicitly documented as unreachable, with the reasoning recorded.
- [ ] Parity tests in `world-surface.test.ts`: Rust-valid cells `a`+FE0F, `→`+FE0F, `!`+FE0F at `columns: 1` render; the agreeing wide cases (⚠️, ☝️, keycap `9`+FE0F+U+20E3, ©️) still render at `columns: 2`.
- [ ] Re-verified by a differential probe (real TS `graphemeWidth` vs `unicode-width = "=0.2.2"`) over base+FE0F clusters for a representative base set spanning both classes — zero mismatches.
- [ ] Distinct from, and does not reopen: #1581 (closed; ZWJ/modifier/FE0E classes), #2962 (open; single-code-point alone/+FE0E residual tables — this issue is the multi-codepoint FE0F cluster path only).
