## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts`'s shared scalar gate is finite-only, and neither quota-current mapper range-checks the percent it publishes:

- `num()` (quota-gather-map.ts:38) is `typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v)` — no range.
- `entryFromResult`'s `pushWindow` (:197-211) copies `num(raw?.usedPercent)` verbatim into both `value` and `pctOfLimit`, with the entry stamped `state: "ok"` for a healthy provider result.
- `entryFromFileExport` (:137-151) does the same with `num(w.usedPct)` for the Meta file-export document, and its `labelWindow` (:154-168) accepts any finite USD amount, rendering a negative `freeCreditsUsd` as the label `"$-42.50"`.

Downstream, nothing range-checks the percent either:

- `recordsFromEntries` (quota-gather-map.ts:268+) takes any non-null `pctOfLimit` as a `pct` snapshot record stamped `limit: 100` — and its pool-level collapse keeps the **max** pct per key, so one glitched 1e9 reading beats every sane credential's reading for that tick.
- `isSnapshotRecord` (snapshots.ts:295-310) is finite-only for numeric values, so the out-of-range records pass the store gate and enter the append-only snapshot store, where rollup min/max preserves the extremum.
- `parseQuotaCurrent` (quota-current.ts:90-96) is also finite-only, converting `pctOfLimit` into the pool window's `used`/`percent` served on /quota.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 627cbc90)

Laptop Bun probe importing the real `quota-gather-map.ts` + `snapshots.ts` (file md5 `86fa3547e81f325f9211dfe1c4577894`, identical in the sandbox clone at 627cbc90 and the laptop clone; probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-30-laneA-gatherpct/`):

- `entryFromResult` with `usedPercent: -20` → entry `state:"ok"`, window `value:-20, pctOfLimit:-20`; `recordsFromEntries` emits a pct record `value:-20, limit:100` and `isSnapshotRecord` returns `true`.
- Same for `usedPercent: 150` → record `value:150`; and `usedPercent: 1e9` → record `value:1000000000`, gate `true`.
- `entryFromFileExport` with windows `usedPct: 150` / `usedPct: -20` and `freeCreditsUsd: -42.5` → entry `state:"ok"`, both out-of-range windows published, plus a `free_credits` label window `valueLabel:"$-42.50"`; `recordsFromEntries` emits pct records `150` and `-20`, both passing the store gate.
- Control: `usedPercent: 42` → window and record `42`, as expected.

No existing test pins the out-of-range acceptance (no range cases in `test/quota-gather-map.test.ts`).

## Why it matters

These two mappers are the gatherer's front door for every provider-module result and every laptop file-export: one glitched or drifting upstream read (a provider returning a fraction instead of a percent, a scaled value, a negative placeholder) is published as live, measured, `ok` quota data, mis-states pool headroom/wall decisions on /quota, and is then permanently appended to the snapshot history as a pct point against `limit:100` — the same poisoned-history failure already filed for the sibling writers (#2553 Turso, #2568 provider-usage), through a different, uncovered pair of entry points.

## Dedup

- #2553 covers `entryFromTurso`'s native-unit counts only; #2568 covers `recordsFromProviderUsage` in snapshot-records.ts only (its packet explicitly scopes out other writers); #2332 is `entryFromResult`'s `fetchedAt` RangeError, not its percent range; #2416 is `parseQuotaCurrent`'s null-window crash. None covers `usedPercent`/`usedPct` range in `entryFromResult`/`entryFromFileExport`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage pins the treatment for an out-of-[0,100] percent in both mappers (skip that window is the file's own pattern for unusable windows — `entryFromFileExport` already skips a window whose pct is null — but pin it explicitly), and pins whether a negative `freeCreditsUsd`/`paygBalanceUsd` label is skipped or the entry degrades.
- [ ] After the fix: `entryFromResult` and `entryFromFileExport` never publish a window with `pctOfLimit` outside [0,100] as `state:"ok"` measured data, and `recordsFromEntries` therefore cannot append an out-of-range pct record from these entries.
- [ ] `test/quota-gather-map.test.ts` covers negative, >100, and absurd (1e9) `usedPercent` and `usedPct` cases, with the sibling in-range windows of the same result/document unaffected, plus the negative-USD label case per the pinned treatment.
- [ ] Existing quota-gather-map / quota-current tests stay green.

body:
## Problem

`recordsFromProviderUsage` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshot-records.ts:236-279) derives Codex quota snapshot records from the keeper's provider-usage snapshot JSON, but the window check is only `typeof win.used_percent === "number"` (snapshot-records.ts:261). Any finite number — negative, over 100, or absurd — becomes a `pct` record stamped with `limit: 100`:

- `used_percent: -20` → record `{serviceId: "openai:codex", metricId: "7-day", value: -20, unit: "pct", limit: 100, source: "api"}`
- `used_percent: 150` → value 150 against its own stated limit of 100
- `used_percent: 1e9` → value 1000000000

## Evidence (verified this run, main 86b7d012)

Laptop Bun probe importing the real `snapshot-records.ts` + `snapshots.ts` (md5-matched to this repo's main; probe at laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-codexpct/`):

- `used_percent=-20` → 7-day record value -20, `isSnapshotRecord(record) === true`
- `used_percent=150` → value 150, passes the store gate
- `used_percent=1e9` → value 1000000000, passes the store gate
- `used_percent=42` (control) → value 42, passes

The append path offers no second line of defence: `scripts/append-usage-snapshots.ts` (`--from-provider-usage` mode) filters derived records through `isSnapshotRecord` (src/snapshots.ts:295-310), which checks only that a numeric value is finite — no pct range check (the limit/resetsAt side of that gap is #2483). The records then enter the append-only snapshot store via the outbox/collector, and monthly compaction (snapshots.ts rollups) preserves each series' min/max indefinitely — a single glitched keeper read (the Codex usage endpoint is an external API whose values this code does not control) permanently poisons the openai:codex history series and every chart/pace consumer that assumes a pct value sits within its own record's limit (cf. #2346, where validator-passing pct records throw in projectPace).

The sibling writers in the same file validate their domains (window seconds must match a known window exactly or the window is skipped); only the percent value itself is unchecked. Note the contrast inside the same function: a window with an unrecognised `limit_window_seconds` is dropped silently rather than recorded under a guessed metric — the percent deserves the same fail-closed treatment.

## Why it matters

Snapshot history is append-only and treated as measured fact (`source: "api"`). A negative or 1e9-percent record is not a display glitch that ages out: compaction keeps it as the series extremum forever, and it misstates Codex usage in the quota history the stewardship cycle reads.

## Acceptance criteria

- `recordsFromProviderUsage` emits a Codex window record only when `used_percent` is a finite number in [0, 100]; out-of-range windows are skipped (the rest of the snapshot's records are still derived).
- `test/snapshot-writers.test.ts` gains cases: negative, >100, and non-finite-shaped used_percent values produce no Codex record for that window, while the other window and the sessions record are unaffected.
- Existing snapshot-writers tests stay green (the 12% / 3% happy path at test lines ~184-185 unchanged).

## Dedup

Checked this run against open + recently closed issues: #2553 is the Turso writer's negative counts (different writer/function), #2264 is snapshot-records' shape-only dates (different field), #2483 is the store gate's limit/resetsAt checks, #2346 is the downstream projectPace throw. No existing issue covers `recordsFromProviderUsage`'s percent range.

body:
## Summary

`readRememberedDaemon` (`pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/remember.ts:43-52`) is the gate between host namespaced storage (`ctx.storage`) and every consumer of the remembered daemon choice — but it validates almost nothing about the record's `target`:

```ts
if (typeof record.seenAt !== "number" || record.target === undefined) return undefined;
return record;
```

Any non-null object with a numeric `seenAt` and a `target` that is merely not `undefined` passes, whatever shape the target has. The module's own test ("malformed records read as absent", `v2.test.ts`) only covers a non-object record (`"not-a-record"`).

## Verified (this run, main 069aff53)

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-forgetcool/`, real `remember.ts`/`daemon.ts`, md5-matched to main), Map-backed stub storage:

- `{ target: { kind: "socket" }, seenAt: 5 }` (no `path`) → record **returned**, and `targetKey(record.target)` yields the literal string `"unix://undefined"`.
- `{ target: "unix:///tmp/x.sock", seenAt: 5 }` (string, not a Target object) → record **returned**, and `targetKey(...)` yields `undefined`.

## Why it matters

The returned record is trusted downstream without further checks:

- `tools.ts:184` (`refreshRemembered`) keys change-detection on `targetKey(record.target)` — `"unix://undefined"` or `undefined` become the remembered key, so a malformed record can mask or fabricate a "the choice moved" transition.
- `tools.ts:208,348,401` pass `record.target` into the discovery ladder as the `remembered` target — a garbage target is health-checked / connected to as if a user had chosen it.
- `remember.ts:65` (`recallDaemon`) health-checks the unvalidated target for the `until-gone` lifetime rule.

Storage is host-provided and shared across plugin versions: a record written by an earlier/newer build, a partially migrated record, or plain corruption currently poisons discovery for the directory instead of reading as absent — which is exactly the contract the function documents and tests for non-object records.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `readRememberedDaemon` returns `undefined` unless the target is a well-formed `Target`: `kind: "socket"` with a non-empty string `path`, or `kind: "url"` with a non-empty string `base`.
- [ ] Tests in `v2.test.ts` extend "malformed records read as absent" to object records: socket target missing `path`, url target missing `base`, string target, numeric target, and an unknown `kind`.
- [ ] Well-formed records written by `rememberDaemon` still round-trip unchanged (existing tests green).

Dedup: no existing issue covers `readRememberedDaemon` validation; #2557 is the same probe run's distinct finding (forget/cooldown in `tools.ts`).

body:
## Summary

In the mcpx opencode plugin, one transient daemon failure suppresses daemon rediscovery for the whole miss-cooldown (60s by default) — even when a daemon is healthy again immediately. The failure path and the no-daemon path share the same `missedAt` stamp, so the cooldown written for "no daemon exists on this machine" also applies to "a daemon existed and just hiccuped".

Present in both trees (same code shape, ported):

- v2: `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/tools.ts`
  - `:143` `discoveryRetryMs = options.discoveryRetryMs ?? TUNING.missCooldownMs` (60_000, `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts:65`)
  - `:196` `look()` returns a synthetic `{ candidates: [], rung: 6, reason: "none" }` while `Date.now() - missedAt < discoveryRetryMs` — without calling `discoverFn`
  - `:213` a genuine no-target discovery stamps `missedAt` (the intended cooldown)
  - `:226-229` `forget()` **also** stamps `missedAt = Date.now()`
  - `:245-247` `viaDaemon`'s catch calls `forget()` under the comment "Stopped, restarted, or its socket moved. Forget it; the next call asks again." — but the next call does not ask again until the cooldown expires
- v1: `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:249,257,265-267,348` — identical pattern and identical comment.

Note the inconsistency that gives the intent away: the `daemon_forget` tool (v2 `tools.ts:437-439`) clears `found` directly **without** stamping `missedAt`, so a user-initiated forget rediscovers immediately, while an error-initiated forget waits out the cooldown.

## Verified (this run, main 069aff53)

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-forgetcool/`, real `v2/tools.ts`/`remember.ts`/`daemon.ts`, md5-matched to main; stub storage/discover/client in the style of `tools.test.ts`), runtime created with **no** `discoveryRetryMs` (production default):

1. `mcpx_exec` succeeds — `discoverFn` called once.
2. The client's `exec` throws once ("daemon went away") — the tool call rejects, `viaDaemon` forgets.
3. The daemon is healthy again; the next `mcpx_exec` returns `mcpx: no daemon is reachable and no mcpx binary could be run…` and `discoverFn` is **still at 1 call** — rediscovery never ran.

The existing rediscovery-precedence test (`v2/tools.test.ts`, "a session choice survives a transient failure") only passes because it sets `discoveryRetryMs: 0`, sidestepping the interaction.

## Why it matters

- After any daemon restart/blip, every mcpx tool call for up to 60s either spawns the CLI fallback (the ~135x-slower path the ladder exists to avoid, per `daemon.ts`'s header) — and the CLI walks its **own** ladder, so it can answer from a different daemon than the session's chosen one — or, with no binary available, fails outright with a misleading "no daemon is reachable" while one is running.
- `daemon_status`/`annotation()` go through the same `look()`, so the plugin reports "none" about a healthy daemon.
- With `MCPX_PLUGIN_DISCOVERY_RETRY` set longer, the blind window grows proportionally.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a transient daemon error, the next tool call re-runs discovery immediately (a restarted/healthy daemon is picked up on the first call after the failure), while a genuine no-target discovery still arms the miss cooldown so daemon-less machines don't rescan on every call.
- [ ] The fix lands in the v2 tree and, if triage judges the ported flaw in scope, in v1 `mcpx-session.ts` as well — or the issue records why v1 is excluded.
- [ ] A regression test in `v2/tools.test.ts` exercises the transient-failure path with the **default** (non-zero) `discoveryRetryMs`: fail once, succeed on the very next call, with `discoverFn` called again.
- [ ] The "next call asks again" comment and the behavior agree.

Dedup: #2309 is `goDurationMs` returning Infinity for overflow durations (the retry value itself), distinct from this forget/cooldown conflation at the default value. #1858 is the v2 port tracker.

body:
## Problem

`entryFromTurso` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts:405) never range-checks the Turso usage counts it maps. Its only numeric gate is the shared helper at quota-gather-map.ts:38:

```ts
const num = (v: unknown): number | null => (typeof v === "number" && Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null);
```

Finite is the whole check — a negative count passes. The five usage fields are read through it (databases :453, storage_bytes :455, rows_read :463, rows_written, bytes_synced :479), converted with `gb()` (:390) / `pct3()` (:391), and pushed as windows on an entry whose state becomes `"ok"` (no error) as long as at least one window exists. The gatherer caller passes the raw API JSON straight in with no intervening validation (pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:301, `entryFromTurso(usage, subscription, { measuredAt: tickIso })`).

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real module, main 02c774a2)

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-tursoneg/probe.ts` (Bun, imports the real `quota-gather-map.ts`; the laptop copy is md5-identical to sandbox main).

Feeding `usage = { databases: -3, storage_bytes: -2_000_000_000, rows_read: -1000, rows_written: -5, bytes_synced: -1_000_000_000 }` with a normal Starter subscription doc:

- Entry state is `ok`, error `null`.
- Windows publish impossible values: `databases value -3, pct -3, label "-3 / 100"`; `storage value -2, pct -40, label "-2 GB / 5 GB"`; `sync value -1, pct -33.333`; rows windows carry negative raw values (their pct rounds to `-0`).
- `recordsFromEntries([entry], …)` then appends **negative snapshot records** for the native-unit series: `{metricId: "databases", value: -3, unit: "count"}`, `{metricId: "storage", value: -2, unit: "gb"}`, `{metricId: "sync", value: -1, unit: "gb"}` — so one bad read does not just render badly, it writes impossible points into the pool's snapshot history.
- A mixed read (`databases: 3, rows_read: -42`) is also `ok`, with the negative metric published alongside the good one — there is no per-metric rejection either.

Control: a normal read (`databases: 3`) maps to `ok` with only that window, as the existing tests expect.

## Why it matters

Usage counts (databases, bytes stored/synced, rows read/written) cannot be negative. A Turso API shape drift, a partial/incorrect response, or a future endpoint change that returns a signed delta instead of a total would currently be stamped as fresh live measured data, shown on the Turso SaaS card as negative usage / negative percent-of-limit, and persisted as negative snapshot points that later pace/chart/history code has to interpret. Every sibling mapper in this stack that was audited for the same class treats negative amounts as invalid (cf. #2508 saas-extract, #2493 github-billing, #2492 supabase-export) — the Turso mapper is the one that was missed. Whether one negative metric should poison the whole entry (fail-closed error entry, the file-export adapter discipline) or just that metric (omit, like missing metrics) is the triage decision this issue asks for — silently publishing it is the one outcome that is wrong either way.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A Turso usage doc carrying a negative value for any of `databases`, `storage_bytes`, `rows_read`, `rows_written`, or `bytes_synced` no longer produces an `ok` entry with a negative window: either the affected metric is omitted or the entry is an error entry (triage pins which, consistent with this module's fail-soft conventions), and the chosen behaviour is documented at the mapper.
- [ ] `recordsFromEntries` on such an entry appends no negative-value snapshot record.
- [ ] Regression tests in pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota-gather-map.test.ts cover at least: an all-negative usage doc, and a mixed doc with one negative metric among valid ones.
- [ ] Existing behaviour is unchanged for valid, missing (omitted, never zeroed), and non-numeric metrics, and the existing `entryFromTurso` tests still pass.

## Dedup notes

Searched open + closed for `entryFromTurso`, "turso negative", and `quota-gather-map`: #2332 is this file's `entryFromResult` fetchedAt RangeError (a different function and failure), #2416 is `parseQuotaCurrent` window entries, #1049 is the original Turso collector feature. The negative-amount issues #2492/#2493/#2508 cover the supabase-export, github-billing, and saas-extract mappers respectively — none touches `entryFromTurso`.

body:
Follow-up to #1884 (split remainder, named there per its acceptance criteria). The touch-on-read TTL convention is adopted in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0005-ttl-touch-on-read.md` and implemented for the elicit family in PR #2544. This issue covers the **ask** family (`proto.askTTL`).

Verified 2026-10-29 at `origin/main` 7d1b081c (queue worker task 3120): `proto.askTTL` is consumed at `internal/daemon/routes_proto.go:424` and `internal/daemon/input_required.go:100` (`taskStore().Start(...)`); `internal/pool/budget.go:35` notes `proto.askTTL` and `proto.stateTTL` bound the /v1/ask task and the requestState. The ask task's expiry is absolute.

Note: if the ask family rides the same task store as the tasks family (see the tasks follow-up issue filed alongside this one), this issue may be closed as superseded by that one with a pointer — do not build two mechanisms.

## Acceptance

- Ask tasks adopt decision 0005 (or this issue is closed as superseded by the tasks-family implementation, with the pointer recorded on #1884): item reads renew to `min(created + maxAge, lastTouched + ttl)`; collection reads do not touch.
- A paired maxAge ceiling setting is declared in the registry.
- Representations touched by the change carry `expiresAt` (RFC 3339), `lastTouched`, `ttlRemainingMs`.
- No `/renew` endpoint or per-resource renew operation. `proto.stateTTL` is out of scope (documented exception in decision 0005: signed expiry, renewed by re-minting).
- Targeted tests cover touch renewal and the maxAge ceiling; `go test ./...` in pkgs/mcpx passes via CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Ask tasks adopt decision 0005 touch-on-read, OR this issue is closed as superseded by the tasks-family implementation (#2546) with the pointer recorded on #1884.
- [ ] A paired maxAge ceiling setting is declared in the registry; representations touched by the change carry `expiresAt` (RFC 3339), `lastTouched`, `ttlRemainingMs`; no `/renew` endpoint is added; `proto.stateTTL` stays out of scope.
- [ ] Targeted tests cover touch renewal and the maxAge ceiling (or the superseded closure is recorded); mcpx tests pass via CI.

body:
# aggregator(opencode): mapServerSessions never validates the v2 wire containers — a non-array `data` on any endpoint, or one null session entry, throws out of the mapper and drops every session from that server; an id-less entry fabricates an undefined-sessionId row

## Summary

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts` maps an OpenCode v2 server's responses into feed entries with no validation of the wire containers or the session entries themselves. `mapServerSessions` (opencode.ts:116) trusts that every endpoint's `data` is an array and that every session entry is an object with an `id`:

- The session list is used unguarded: `const sessions = list.data` (:125), the token loop dereferences `s.tokens` on every entry (:145-148), and the inclusion filter/sort dereference `s.time` / `s.id` (:150-157).
- The permission list is iterated unguarded (:139, `for (const p of permResp?.data ?? [])`).
- In `mapOne`, the message list is iterated unguarded (:225, `for (const m of data)` where `data = msgs?.data ?? []`, :213).

Any of these shapes therefore throws a `TypeError` out of `mapServerSessions` instead of returning entries or `null`. Both callers are deliberately fail-soft per server — the collector wraps the call in one catch and logs "sandbox server read failed; attention empty" (scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:464-502), and live.ts catches around `laptopSessions()` / `laptopMapped()` and marks the laptop part failed (live.ts:907-918, :1012-1019) — so the throw drops **every** session from that server for the run/read (attention, registry records, and pool-burn attribution), even when all but one element were well-formed. Separately, a session entry with no `id` passes the inclusion filter when recently updated and is mapped into an entry whose `sessionId` is `undefined`, which then keys the live `byId` map and registry records under `undefined`.

The v2 wire shapes are a moving external contract (the file header notes they were "probed live 2026-10-25" against two servers, and the two servers run different builds — the laptop's managed server and the sandbox's), so shape drift on one endpoint or one corrupt entry is exactly the failure this mapper must degrade through, the way `getJson` already degrades a failed fetch to `null`.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 7d1b081c)

Probe: laptop Bun 1.4.2, the real `src/sources/opencode.ts` (verbatim copy, md5 28215b8ddcefd61d13188b5d4663f4bf) driven against a stub v2 server (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-ocmap/probe.ts` on the laptop; copy in the goal's hidden_files):

- Control (well-formed shapes): `RETURNED entries=1 ids=ses_good`.
- Session-list `data` is an object (`{ ses_good: {...} }`): `THREW TypeError: {} is not iterable` — zero entries.
- Session list `[good, null]`: `THREW TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 's.tokens')` — the good session is lost too.
- Permission `data` is an object: `THREW TypeError: {} is not iterable` — zero entries.
- Message `data` is an object for the one included session: `THREW TypeError: {} is not iterable` — zero entries.
- Session list `[good, { title, time.updated }]` (no `id`): `RETURNED entries=2 ids=ses_good,` — a second entry with an empty/undefined sessionId is fabricated.
- Benign controls: a string entry in the session list is excluded by the inclusion filter (no crash); `active` `data` as an array still works via `Object.keys`.

File:line (main 7d1b081c):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts:122-125` — list fetch; `if (!list?.data) return null; const sessions = list.data;` — truthiness is the only check.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts:137-142` — permission iteration unguarded.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts:145-157` — token loop and inclusion filter dereference every entry.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/opencode.ts:206-225` — `mapOne` message iteration unguarded (forms at :199-200 index `[0]` only, so an object `data` there is benign).
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:464-502` — collector catch: one throw = sandbox attention empty, no registry records, no burn attribution.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:907-918,1012-1019` — live catches: one throw = laptop sessions/registry contribution silently absent.

## Why it matters

This mapper is the only path for live OpenCode sessions (both servers) into the attention feed, the durable session registry, and per-pool burn attribution. Its contract with callers is "null or entries, fail soft per server" — but a single malformed element or one endpoint's shape drift currently has the same blast radius as the whole server being down, with a log line that says "read failed" rather than naming the shape problem. As the v2 API evolves independently on the two servers, this is the most likely way the fleet silently loses sight of running sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage pins the degradation shape (expected: each endpoint's `data` is array-checked — a non-array degrades that endpoint's contribution the way a failed fetch already does; session entries that are not objects or carry no string `id` are skipped per entry so valid siblings still map; `mapOne`'s message/form reads degrade per session instead of rejecting the whole server's map — or triage pins a different shape; throwing out of `mapServerSessions` for a parseable-but-malformed response is the one ruled-out option).
- [ ] Regression tests in the aggregator suite (opencode.test.ts's stub-server home): list `data` as an object, a `[valid, null]` list, permission `data` as an object, and message `data` as an object each still return the valid session's entry; an id-less entry produces no entry.
- [ ] No behavior change for well-formed wire shapes: the existing opencode.test.ts expectations (inclusion window, signals, source stamp, unreachable-server null) pass unchanged.

Filed by new-issue-creator-code-b (lane B), run 2026-10-29 22:20 CDT. Dedup: #2286 is `iso()` RangeError on out-of-range timestamps in otherwise-valid entries (different function/failure — a huge numeric timestamp, not container/entry shape); #2531 is the Jules keeper-state mapper (different source/file); the isFleetFeed gate family (#2439/#2445/#2446/#2450/#2451/#2539) covers feed-file sections in live.ts, not this live-server mapper. gh searches for mapServerSessions / "not iterable" returned no covering issue.

body:
## Problem

The fleet feed's `registry` section is never checked by `isFleetFeed`
(`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:207-219`), and its two live-source
consumers handle it in two different unguarded ways:

- `registry()` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:1009-1010`)
  iterates it directly: `for (const r of feed.registry) if
  (isSessionRecord(r)) incoming.push(r)`. A non-iterable container
  (plain object, number) throws `TypeError: ... is not iterable`
  before the entry filter ever runs.
- `coverage()` (`live.ts:1073`) calls
  `(feed?.registry ?? []).filter((r) => r.source === "claude-code")`
  — with **no `isSessionRecord` filter at all**. A non-array container
  (string, object, number) has no `.filter` and throws; and an array
  containing a `null` entry also throws (`r.source` dereferences
  null), even though `registry()` filters that same entry out fine.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `7d1b081c`)

- `feed.ts:38-39`: `FleetFeed.registry?: SessionRecord[]` — identity
  records (#906 §3) from sandbox OpenCode + Jules + Muse launches.
- `feed.ts:207-219`: `isFleetFeed` checks only `version`,
  `generatedAt`, `quota.pools` and `attention` — no `registry` check.
- `live.ts:1009-1010`: `registry()` for-of over the raw container.
- `live.ts:1073`: `coverage()` unfiltered `.filter((r) => r.source
  === "claude-code")` — the only registry consumer that does not pass
  entries through `isSessionRecord` (the durable-store load at
  `live.ts:632` does `Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed.filter(
  isSessionRecord) : []`, so the store path is safe; the feed path
  is not).
- Uncaught call sites: `server.ts:604` (`/sessions`) and `:613`
  (`/api/registry.json`) await `source.registry()` with no catch;
  `attentionContext()` (`server.ts:273`) awaits `source.coverage()`
  with no catch and backs `/attention`, `/today`, the board render
  and `/api/coverage.json` (`:753-755`). (Other `registry()` callers
  at `:159/:172/:822` do catch.)

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedregistry/`,
the REAL `liveSource` built via `loadConfig` exactly as
`test/orchestration.test.ts` builds it; `feed.ts`, `sources/live.ts`
and `config.ts` md5-identical to main `7d1b081c`, Bun 1.4.2; feeds
written to a temp dir, registry store pointed at the temp dir —
entry counts include the laptop server's live sessions, which
`registry()` merges in by design):

| `registry` in feed | `isFleetFeed` | `src.registry()` | `src.coverage()` |
|---|---|---|---|
| absent (control) | true | OK | OK |
| valid array (1 record) | true | OK — record merged | OK |
| `[null]` (entry-level) | true | OK — filtered by `isSessionRecord` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'r.source')` |
| `"abc"` (string) | true | OK — chars filtered out | **throws** `TypeError: (feed?.registry ?? []).filter is not a function` |
| `{...}` (object) | true | **throws** `TypeError: {} is not iterable` | **throws** `.filter is not a function` |
| `42` (number) | true | **throws** `TypeError: number is not iterable` | **throws** `.filter is not a function` |

## Why it matters

The collector assembles the registry from three independent launch
sources; the section is documented as the identity record of record
for `/sessions`, author identities and cross-repo session links.
One drifted container value 500s `/sessions` and
`/api/registry.json`; one `null` entry — which the sibling consumer
handles correctly — 500s every surface backed by `coverage()`
(attention, today, board, coverage JSON). The two consumers
disagreeing about the same section's hygiene is the bug: the feed
path needs the same array + `isSessionRecord` discipline the
durable-store path already has (`live.ts:632`).

Related but distinct: #2408/#2376/#2485 are field-level gaps
*inside* records that pass `isSessionRecord` (taskRefs, lastSeenAt);
#2453 is the `projects` container in `items()`/`projects()`. This
one is the `registry` container plus `coverage()`'s missing entry
filter — no open or recently closed issue covers it (checked this
run: title/keyword searches for the feed registry gate return only
the field-level registry issues above and the other feed siblings
#2427/#2429/#2439/#2445/#2446/#2450/#2451).

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer throw in `registry()`
  or `coverage()` over its `registry` section: a non-array container
  (string, object, number) and an array containing `null`/non-record
  entries both degrade to "no feed records" (the documented
  absent-section behaviour), and `/sessions`, `/api/registry.json`,
  `/attention`, `/today` and `/api/coverage.json` render normally.
- `coverage()`'s Claude-record count uses the same entry hygiene as
  every other registry consumer (`isSessionRecord`, or the gate
  guarantees it) — pinned by triage together with the layer choice
  (gate-level array check in `isFleetFeed` vs `Array.isArray` guards
  at both consumers), consistent with the feed-gate sibling rulings.
- Regression tests cover: `registry` as a string, as an object, as a
  number, and as `[null]` — `registry()` resolves, `coverage()`
  resolves, and a well-formed registry still merges and counts its
  records unchanged.

body:
## Problem

`mapJulesItems` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/jules.ts` maps the keeper-written `jules-review-state.json` into attention-feed entries with **no validation of the `items` container or its elements** — the file is parsed with a bare `as JulesReviewState` cast at the only call site, and every field is dereferenced as if the declared TypeScript shape were guaranteed.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `7d1b081c`)

- `src/sources/jules.ts:43` — `Object.entries(state.items ?? {})` accepts any non-nullish `items` (object, array, or string).
- `src/sources/jules.ts:47` — `title: item.title` throws on a `null` item; `:54` — `(item.state ?? "").toUpperCase()` throws on a non-string `state` (e.g. a number).
- `scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:506-512` — the sole caller wraps the whole block in one `catch` that logs `collector: jules-review state unreadable; no Jules sessions this run`, so one malformed element discards **every** Jules session *and* the keeper totals for that run, under a message that claims the file was unreadable when it parsed fine.
- `src/sources/jules.ts:85` — `julesSummary` counts `Object.keys(state.items ?? {})`, so a string `items` is counted per character.

Probe (Bun, importing the real `src/sources/jules.ts`, main `7d1b081c`):

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `items: { ses1: null, ses2: {state:"COMPLETED", …} }` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'item.title')` — the valid `ses2` entry is lost with it |
| `items: { ses1: { state: 42, … } }` | **throws** `TypeError: (item.state ?? "").toUpperCase is not a function` |
| top-level `null` state | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'state.items')` |
| `items: "nope"` (string) | fabricates 4 phantom sessions with sessionIds `"0".."3"`, all `Jules UNKNOWN`; `julesSummary.tracked` reports 4 |
| `items: [ {state:"FAILED", …} ]` (array) | fabricates a session with sessionId `"0"` |

## Why it matters

The collector is the only path by which supervised Jules sessions reach the dashboard's needs-you feed and the identity registry (`recordFromSessionEntry` per entry, same block). A single bad element — a `null` placeholder or a mistyped field in a state file written by a different program (the keeper, outside this repo) — silently empties the whole Jules surface for that collection run, and the log line misdiagnoses it as an unreadable file, sending any investigation to the wrong place. The string/array shapes are worse in the other direction: they invent sessions that do not exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- `mapJulesItems` never throws on a malformed state: a non-object top level, a non-plain-object `items`, and non-object elements are skipped (per element where possible), so valid sibling entries still map.
- Non-string scalar fields on an otherwise usable item (e.g. numeric `state`) do not kill the entry or the batch; the entry degrades the way a missing field already does (`Jules UNKNOWN`).
- `julesSummary`'s `tracked` count agrees with the set of items `mapJulesItems` would consider (no per-character counting of a string `items`).
- The collector's Jules block no longer reports a parseable-but-malformed state as "unreadable" — the log distinguishes unreadable/unparseable from malformed-but-recovered, or the mapper's per-element skips are counted/logged.
- Tests in the aggregator suite (slice2 jules mapping describes) cover: null element among valid ones, numeric `state`, string `items`, array `items`, top-level `null`.

## Dedup

`#1587` is `julesSummary`'s freshest-note HHMM selection — a different function and defect. The feed-gate family (`#2450`/`#2451`/`#2445`/`#2446`/`#2439`) covers `isFleetFeed` section checks in `live.ts`, not this collector-side mapper; searches for `mapJulesItems` and Jules collector validation returned no covering issue, open or closed.

title: opencode-route door must be routing-only: no OpenCode session/loop per model request
body:
## Directive (Drew, 2026-10-29 21:45 CDT, main chat)

"opencode shouldn't do work besides routing — it shouldn't do any loop etc."

## Problem

The opencode-route provider (#2250) currently serves each model request by creating a full OpenCode session and prompting it. That means the embedded OpenClaw agent's turn runs inside a second agent loop: OpenCode assembles its own context, tools, and plugins around a request that already carries OpenClaw's context. Two loops stacked — heavier, and the wrong ownership split.

## Required shape

For the MODEL door (OpenClaw embedded agent → opencode-route/*), OpenCode's job is routing only:

1. Resolve the route name (speed / workhorse / specialist / summit / scout) to a concrete pool member, using the existing route-pool state: weights, round-robin across workspaces, quota demotion, expiry.
2. Make a plain completion call to that member's provider endpoint with the member's credential.
3. Stream the response back to OpenClaw untouched (OpenAI-compatible, as today).
4. Record the attempt in the route ledger (route_attempt) exactly as the session path does, so quota accounting and demotion keep working.

No OpenCode session is created, no OpenCode agent loop runs, no OpenCode tools/plugins/context are applied. Loop ownership stays with the caller (OpenClaw embedded).

Out of scope: dispatch paths are different by design — ACP (#2256) and sessions_spawn (#2257) hand off whole tasks, and OpenCode doing the work there is the point.

## Acceptance

- A workhorse request through the door completes with ZERO new rows in OpenCode's session tables for that request.
- route_attempt gains the attempt row with the same fields the session path writes (pool, member, outcome).
- Pool behavior preserved under test: a demoted/closed pool member is skipped; the fallback order from the route config is honored.
- OpenClaw's provider definition (name `opencode-route`, port 18750) does not change — the door's internals are replaced behind the same endpoint, so no OpenClaw config change rides along.
- The session-based implementation from #2250 is removed or kept only as an explicitly separate dispatch door, not as the model path.

Context: #2250 (built door), #2229 (parent), #2256 / #2257 (dispatch options), quota doctrine in the provider registry (route pools, demotion ≥3 quota errors/4h → weight ×0.01).

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/ready-for-agent/install.sh` installs/upgrades the pinned package and the systemd unit, but never restarts the service — so on any host where ready-for-agent is already running, an install run silently leaves the OLD process serving while reporting success.

Evidence (main 7d1b081c):

- `install.sh:27,38-40` — `PINNED_VERSION="1.1.0"`; when the on-disk binary's version differs, the script replaces it with `npm install -g --prefix "$HOME/.local" ready-for-agent@$PINNED_VERSION`.
- `systemd/ready-for-agent.service` — `ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/ready-for-agent start …`: the running service is that same binary. Replacing a binary on disk does not change the already-running process.
- `install.sh:62-65` — the unit is overwritten (`install -Dm644 …`) and `systemctl --user daemon-reload` runs, then `systemctl --user enable --now ready-for-agent.service`. `enable --now` starts a stopped unit; for an already-running unit it is a no-op — it does not restart it, and `daemon-reload` alone does not make a running service pick up a changed unit or binary. There is no `restart` / `try-restart` anywhere in the script (verified: `grep -n restart install.sh` returns nothing).
- `install.sh:68-77` — the success gate only curls `http://127.0.0.1:6056/` until anything answers. The old process answers, so the script prints "ready-for-agent is up" and exits 0 even though the pinned upgrade / unit change never took effect.

Net effect: bumping `PINNED_VERSION` (the script's own documented upgrade path: "bump it deliberately after reading the upstream release notes") or editing the unit, then running `./install.sh`, produces a green install of a change that is not live — the exact silent-no-op deploy failure #1150 fixed for the aggregator's install.sh, still present in this sibling script. (The aggregator's fix also verifies the deployed version via /api/health; this script verifies nothing about which version is serving.)

Related, distinct: #1150 (aggregator install.sh, fixed — different script); #1213 (extending tests to the deploy scripts — coverage, not this defect); #1203 (ready-for-agent config/dispatch surfacing — different scope).

## Why it matters

ready-for-agent is the pm-stack dispatch layer. A pinned-version security/bugfix upgrade or a unit change (bind, PATH, WorkingDirectory) can be "installed" and health-checked green while the old code keeps dispatching work indefinitely — and nothing anywhere reports the divergence, because the script's own check cannot distinguish old from new.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] When the package version or the unit file changes, `install.sh` restarts `ready-for-agent.service` (e.g. `systemctl --user restart`, or `try-restart` when already active) so the running process is the one just installed; a first-time install still just starts it.
- [ ] The post-install check verifies the SERVING process matches the install (at minimum that the service was (re)started during this run when a change was applied — e.g. check `ActiveEnterTimestamp` / MainPID changed, or a version endpoint if upstream exposes one), and fails loudly when it cannot confirm that.
- [ ] A re-run with no version/unit change remains a no-op success (no unnecessary restart), or the script explicitly reports that it restarted the service.
- [ ] The behaviour is covered alongside the deploy-script tests tracked in #1213, or by a documented manual verification on the host.

body:
# mcpx(sampling): broker validator accepts degenerate empties — zero messages, empty content arrays, and a result with role `""` / `"user"` all pass

Residual of #1836 (Phase 2 of #1834), on main `7d1b081c`, after PR #2443 merged the broker validator. Open PR #2487 (block-field validation, the Codex P2 follow-up) does **not** cover any of this — its diff only adds per-block field checks inside `decodeSampleContent`.

## Evidence

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/elicit/sampling.go`:

- `ValidateSampleRequest` (line 76) unmarshals `messages` (line 78) and loops over it, but never checks that the list is non-empty. `{}`, `{"messages":null}` and `{"messages":[]}` all return `nil`.
- `decodeSampleContent` (line 49) returns an empty block list for a `[]` content array with no error, so in the array era (2025-11-25) a message — and a result — whose content is `[]` passes every check.
- `ValidateSampleResult` (line 131) checks the result role for presence only (line 145: `r.Role == nil`), while the very next check rejects an empty model (line 148: `r.Model == nil || *r.Model == ""`). A result with `"role":""` or `"role":"user"` passes; `"model":""` fails. That asymmetry marks the role check as an oversight, not a policy.
- `stopReason` is only special-cased for the exact string `"toolUse"` when the request carried no tools; with tools present, any string (probe used `"banana"`) passes unchecked.

Verified this run with the byte-identical `sampling.go` from main compiled on the laptop (probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-sampling/` on the laptop, `go test` with the real package code, md5 of the copy matches the clone):

```
REQ  empty object {}                                arrayOK=true  -> err=<nil>
REQ  messages null                                  arrayOK=true  -> err=<nil>
REQ  messages empty array                           arrayOK=false -> err=<nil>
REQ  one user msg, content empty array              arrayOK=true  -> err=<nil>
REQ  one user msg, no content field (control)       arrayOK=true  -> err=message 0: content is missing
RES  result content empty array                     tools=false   -> err=<nil>
RES  result role=user                               tools=false   -> err=<nil>
RES  result role empty string                       tools=false   -> err=<nil>
RES  result stopReason banana, tools=true           tools=true    -> err=<nil>
RES  result ok (control)                            tools=false   -> err=<nil>
```

Call sites: `pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/hooks.go:202` (request, before a broker question opens) and `hooks.go:267` / `pkgs/mcpx/internal/elicit/elicit.go:331` (result) — both wrap failures as `SamplingInvalidParams` (-32602), which is exactly the error these shapes never raise.

## Why it matters

The validator exists (#1836) so a malformed sampling exchange is refused with -32602 at the broker instead of consuming an answerer's attention or being relayed upstream as a question/answer nobody can act on. A request with no messages is a sampling question with nothing in it: it opens a broker question, an answerer answers nothing, and the result side then validates an answer to an empty prompt. An empty content array is the same degeneracy one level down, in both directions. A result claiming role `""` or `"user"` is not a `CreateMessageResult` an upstream can trust — and the model check right below proves the code intends non-empty identity fields.

## Acceptance criteria

- `ValidateSampleRequest` rejects a request whose `messages` is missing, null, or empty, in both eras, with the typed -32602 path unchanged.
- A message or result whose content decodes to zero blocks (empty array) is rejected in the array era (the single-block era already rejects arrays entirely).
- `ValidateSampleResult` rejects a role that is empty or not `"assistant"`, symmetric with the existing model check.
- Triage pins whether `stopReason` is checked against the era's enum (`endTurn` / `maxTokens` / `stopSequence` / `toolUse`) or deliberately left open for forward compatibility — either way the decision is recorded in a test.
- Regression tests beside `sampling_test.go` cover each rejected shape above plus the passing controls (a normal text message, a normal result); existing sampling/conformance tests stay green.

body:
## Problem

`parseBillingBanner` (pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs:99-111) converts the billing banner's `remaining_minor_units` to USD with only a type/finiteness/sign check:

```js
if (typeof minor !== "number" || !Number.isFinite(minor) || minor < 0) throw …
return minor / 100;
```

Minor units are integer cents by definition — a fractional value is shape drift, and this exporter's parsers are documented to fail closed on shape drift ("Throws on any shape drift — fail-closed, never partial zeros", parseSubscriptionQuota header). But a fractional or absurd value passes here and is exported in a `status: "ok"` document as `freeCreditsUsd`:

Verified against the real module (main 7d1b081c, node probe):

- `remaining_minor_units: 1050.5` → `freeCreditsUsd = 10.505` (a half-cent that cannot exist)
- `remaining_minor_units: 0.1` → `0.001`
- `remaining_minor_units: 1e15` → `10000000000000` ($10 trillion of "free credits")
- Controls behave: integer `14857` → `148.57`; negative and string values throw as intended.

## Why it matters

`freeCreditsUsd` lands in the export document the aggregator's quota plane reads as the Meta card's measured free-credit balance. A drifted banner payload (API change, partial response, wrong field) currently produces a precise-looking but impossible balance instead of the exporter's `unparseable` (exit 6) failure document — the failure mode every sibling parser in this file is built to produce.

Related, distinct: #2460 (subscription-quota timestamps) and #2461 (parsePaygBalance truncation) are different functions in this file; neither covers the banner parser. #1301 is the null-resets_at diagnosis in parseSubscriptionQuota.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseBillingBanner` throws `unparseable` (exit 6) when `remaining_minor_units` is not an integer (`Number.isInteger`), and when it exceeds a stated plausible bound if triage chooses to add one.
- [ ] Regression tests in meta-quota-export.test.mjs: fractional (1050.5, 0.1) throws; the existing integer/currency/missing cases still behave as today.

body:
## Problem

`applySupabaseExport` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:701) is the trust boundary for the supabase-export file document: live.ts reads the file with `JSON.parse` (src/sources/live.ts:833-835) and passes the result straight in. The overlay checks shapes only loosely — `typeof === "number" && Number.isFinite` for metric values and billing, and a `Date.parse` freshness check for `measuredAt` — so values the producer could never legitimately emit are accepted and stamped on the Supabase card as live, measured, `sourceClass: "api"` data:

1. **Negative numbers pass.** saas-extract.ts:721-722 accepts any finite `used`/`limit`; :741-743 accepts any finite `billing.billedUsd`. Verified against the real module (main 7d1b081c): a fresh, `status:"ok"` doc with `used: -3.25` for db-size yields `used = -3.25`, `percent = -650`; `billedUsd: -42.5` is stored verbatim (renders as a measured `$-42.50` billed line); `limit: -0.5` is stored as the metric's limit.
2. **`measuredAt` is never type-checked.** saas-extract.ts:707-708 only requires truthiness and a finite `Date.parse(doc.measuredAt)`. `Date.parse` coerces its argument, so a JSON array `measuredAt: ["2026-10-29T11:59:00.000Z"]` passes the freshness gate, and :753 `doc.measuredAt.slice(0, 10)` then stores the **array itself** as the service's `measuredAt` (verified: `typeof` becomes `object`). Downstream, `freshness()` (derive.ts:899) treats its length (1) as a date-only stamp and builds an unparseable string, and `tsFor` (snapshot-records.ts:37-39) interpolates the array slice into a snapshot record's `ts`, producing `2026-10-29T11:59:00.000ZT12:00:00Z`.

The module's own contract says the opposite: "Missing, failed, unparseable or stale documents change nothing", and the billing branch's comment says a failed billing probe must never render as a measured amount. A corrupted, hand-edited, or older-producer export file currently changes the card — with negative or type-corrupted values presented as the live API read.

House precedent in the same codebase: the quota-current overlay gate rejects a document outright when `typeof p.measuredAt !== "string"` (src/quota-current.ts:60), and the producer's own parsers reject negative sizes/counts (supabase-export `parseDbSize`/`parseRequestCount`).

## Evidence

Probe (real `applySupabaseExport` + `extractSaasServices` imported from main 7d1b081c, Bun): `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-supaoverlay/probe.ts`

- Case 1 (negative used/billed): `used= -3.25 percent= -650 billedUsd= -42.5 sourceClass= api`
- Case 2 (negative limit): `used= 1 limit= -0.5`
- Case 3 (array measuredAt): `typeof= object value= ["2026-10-29T11:59:00.000Z"] sourceClass= api`
- Case 4 (control, well-formed fresh doc): applies cleanly, `measuredAt` a string
- Case 5 (control, garbage-string measuredAt): correctly rejected, services unchanged

Related but distinct: #2492 is the *producer* (`billedFromAddons` in supabase-quota-export.mjs) accepting negatives at write time. This issue is the *consumer* gate: even with the producer fixed, the overlay reads a file from disk and must not trust values outside the domain the card renders. #2451 (isFleetFeed saas) is the feed gate for a different input and does not cover this overlay.

## Why it matters

The Supabase card is the fleet's paid-trigger surface for the muse-dev project (80%-of-Free-limit flag, billed amounts). Negative or corrupted "measured" values suppress or invert the percent math, fabricate a negative billed amount, and poison snapshot history with an unparseable `ts` — all under an "api / measured" provenance stamp that tells the reader the numbers are trustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `applySupabaseExport` rejects (changes nothing) or drops the offending metric when `used` or `limit` is negative; percent is never computed from a negative used/limit.
- [ ] A negative `billing.billedUsd` is treated as "no valid billing measurement" (the existing `billedUsd = null` path), never stored.
- [ ] `doc.measuredAt` must be a string before the freshness check (mirror quota-current.ts:60); non-string values change nothing.
- [ ] Regression tests in aggregator/test/supabase-export.test.ts for: negative used, negative limit, negative billedUsd, array measuredAt — each leaves the services unchanged (or the metric/billing unset), while the existing fresh-doc tests still pass.

body:
## Context

PR #2477 (queue task 3059, issue #1842, `paths.config` two-pass chain resolution) merged as `0b06b277` at 2026-10-30T01:09:11Z. The implementation landed, but **6 Codex P2 review threads from round `bcf91515` remain open and undispositioned** on the merged PR — the PR merged while the queue task was parked on that gate.

This issue exists so the findings are not silently dropped: each needs either a fix-forward or a reply on its thread explaining why the current behaviour is intended. Nothing here reopens #1842's acceptance criteria; they were met and the mechanism is in `main`.

## Findings to disposition (all at head `e013229f`)

1. **`pkgs/mcpx/cmd/mcpx/main.go` — forward the bootstrap seed to auto-started daemons.** The seed installed in the bootstrap interception is not forwarded to daemons started by the same invocation, so an auto-started daemon resolves a different chain than the parent.
2. **`pkgs/mcpx/internal/config/chain.go:308` — preserve the seed list's null splice around default locations.** For `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG='[null,"/custom/config.json"]'`, `expandAll` discards the splice position and places the custom file before every default location (higher precedence instead of lower). A seed *without* null also retains all default locations instead of replacing them, contradicting the registry help "Without a null the list replaces outright".
3. **`pkgs/mcpx/cmd/mcpx/main.go:101` — accumulate repeated config-search flags.** `mcpx --paths-config /a --paths-config /b config` replaces `flagSeed` on each call, so only `/b` participates. The setting is `Repeatable: true` and the normal binding accumulates repeated occurrences.
4. **`pkgs/mcpx/internal/config/chain.go:185` — accept existing string-valued path lists during discovery.** `{"paths":{"config":"./shared"}}` fails discovery with a JSON unmarshal error because discovery requires arrays, while `ApplyFile`/`Set.List` accept comma/newline strings. Because chain resolution now runs before dispatch, a previously valid config prevents commands from running at all.
5. **`pkgs/mcpx/internal/config/chain.go:340` — canonicalize cycle-graph endpoints by file identity.** Symlink aliases are recognised by the membership test but the graph stores raw path strings, so `findCycle` treats aliases as unrelated vertices and accepts a real cycle. Reproducible with A declaring a symlink to B and B a symlink to A.
6. **`pkgs/mcpx/internal/config/chain.go:365` — apply declarations in resolved chain order.** Declarations are applied in discovery order, not load order: for discovery order A,B,C where A declares `[C,B]`, B declares `[X]`, C declares `[B]` (no null), the result is A,C,B and `X` is dropped even though B stays in the chain.

## Done when

Each of the 6 threads above carries either a commit that fixes it (with a test in `internal/config` or `cmd/mcpx` where testable) or a reply on the thread with the rationale, and `go test ./pkgs/mcpx/...` is green.

## Links

- Merged PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/2477
- Closed issue: #1842
- Queue task: 3059 (completed `fixed_merged`)

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=repo-worker-code state=filed-followup at=2026-10-30T01:58:00Z -->


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All 6 Codex P2 findings from PR #2477 round `bcf91515` are dispositioned: each either fixed forward (PR linked) or answered on its thread with the intended-behaviour rationale
- [ ] The seed-forwarding, null-splice, and repeated-flag findings (items 1–3 in the body) are verified against current main before disposition — a finding already fixed by a later merge is dispositioned as such with the commit cited
- [ ] No thread on PR #2477 is left open without a reply

body:
Phase 3 of design #2497 (mcpx tasks, bounded — operational limits, cooperative cancel, audit, and the small truths). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-operational-limits.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. The decisions are recorded on #2497; this phase implements its third slice. Gated on Phases 1–2 (the audit lines include the limit refusals Phase 1 creates).

## Scope

Audit, documentation, and register truth-up:

- **Audit lines** through `internal/logging` (the daemon's existing logging), ids and metadata only — no results, no tool arguments, no content (#1675 precedent):
  - task created, at info: task id, requestor key or `unbound`, effective TTL (and that it was clamped, when it was) — at the creation seams / via the store's existing `Watch` seam (`internal/tasks/tasks.go:106`);
  - task terminal, at info: task id, final status, duration;
  - limit refusals (Phase 1's creation cap and per-minute window), at info: which limit, requestor key;
  - retrieval (`tasks/get` / `tasks/result` on both surfaces), at debug at the handler seams — the trail exists without logging every poll at info.
- **Documentation.** Correct `docs/protocol.md`'s task visibility row (line ~140: "a task is visible only to the connection that started it" is false for unbound tasks) and document the model where tasks are described for users: a task started without a connection identity is reachable by anyone holding its ID, IDs are unguessable (128-bit after Phase 1), `tasks/list` lists only a connection's own tasks so an identity-less connection lists nothing, and a client that wants listable tasks must present an identity. This is the recorded disposition for the gap `tasks-get-implies-list` — document, don't change: listing unbound tasks to an identity-less caller would enumerate other callers' work.
- **Truth-up.** Retire the remaining gap rows in `internal/conformance/coverage_stateful.go` (`tasks-audit`, `tasks-document-unbound`, `tasks-get-implies-list`, plus any of the other four rows Phases 1–2 did not already retire), each retirement traceable to its phase's merged PR. Post the evidence note toward #1557 (Phase 3 of #1554) — closure of dezren39/nix#209 itself stays #1557's job; this phase does not steal it.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The daemon log answers "which tasks ran, whose were they, how did they end, and what did the limits refuse" for tasks created on both the MCP and /v1 surfaces, with no task content in any line
- [ ] Retrieval is visible at debug level and absent at info level in normal operation
- [ ] `docs/protocol.md` no longer claims connection-only visibility, and the unbound model (reachable by ID, never listed, identity ⇒ listable) is documented where users read about tasks
- [ ] All seven task gap rows in `coverage_stateful.go` are retired or reworded to name a remaining open question from the design doc, each citing its landing PR
- [ ] The evidence note is posted toward #1557 and dezren39/nix#209 is NOT closed by this phase
- [ ] Tests/docs checks run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: audit export beyond the daemon log (event bus) — a design-doc open question, only on a named consumer; closing nix#209 (that's #1557); any behaviour change to visibility or listing.

🤖 Design-architect pass 17 — agent note: triage this phase against design #2497's recorded decisions; the get/list disposition (document, don't change) is recorded there and is not triage's to re-open.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Audit lines exist at info for task created (id, requestor key or `unbound`, effective TTL + clamp flag), task terminal (id, status, duration), and limit refusals (which limit, requestor key); retrieval is logged at debug at both handler seams — ids and metadata only, no results or tool arguments
- [ ] `docs/protocol.md`'s task-visibility row is corrected and the unbound-task model (reachable by ID holder, 128-bit unguessable IDs) is documented where tasks are described for users
- [ ] The conformance/register truth-up for the #2497 design is posted, reflecting Phases 1–2 as landed

body:
Phase 2 of design #2497 (mcpx tasks, bounded — operational limits, cooperative cancel, audit, and the small truths). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-operational-limits.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. The decisions are recorded on #2497; this phase implements its second slice. Independent of Phase 1.

## Scope

Honest endings in `internal/tasks/tasks.go`:

- **Cooperative cancel.** `CancelWithReason` (tasks.go:519) currently sets `t.Status = Cancelled` under the lock *before* invoking the task's `OnCancel` hook and context cancel, and `finish()` (tasks.go:405) then discards whatever the work produces. Change to: cancel records an internal *cancelling* mark (never a wire status — neither era's task status enum has one), invokes `OnCancel` and the context cancel as today, and starts the grace clock on the new setting `protoTasks.cancelGrace` (duration, default 5s, in `internal/settings/prototasks.go`).
  - Work finishing within the grace window: `finish()` records its own terminal status (`completed` / `failed`); if its `statusMessage` would otherwise be empty, note it completed during cancellation.
  - Grace window expires first: the store flips the task to `cancelled` with the caller's reason (as today) and any late result is discarded (as today).
  - First terminal recording under the store lock wins; the grace flip checks for a recorded terminal state before firing.
  - `tasks/cancel` returns after initiating, as today — the window is the store's, not the caller's wait. The persisted (SQLite) task shape gains no new wire field; the cancelling mark is in-memory only, and a daemon restart during the window resolves via the existing restart path.
- **Failed tasks say why.** In `finish()`'s `isError` branch (tasks.go:424-431), derive `StatusMessage` from the result: the first text content block of the tool result, truncated to 512 characters; if there is no text content, the fixed string `tool returned an error result`. The fault path above it already sets the message and is untouched.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A task whose work completes successfully within the grace window after `tasks/cancel` reports `completed`, not `cancelled` (store test)
- [ ] A task whose work fails with a real fault within the grace window reports `failed` with that fault's message (store test)
- [ ] A task still running after `protoTasks.cancelGrace` reports `cancelled` with the caller's reason, and its late result never overwrites that (store test)
- [ ] No new status value appears on either era's wire shapes; a poll during the grace window shows the pre-cancel status
- [ ] A task failed by an `isError` tool result carries a `statusMessage` taken from the result's first text block (truncated at 512 chars), or the fixed fallback string when the result has no text
- [ ] The conformance gap rows `ext-tasks-cancel-cooperative` and `tasks-failed-status-message` in `internal/conformance/coverage_stateful.go` are retired (or reworded to name what remains)
- [ ] Tests run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: limits and rate windows (Phase 1), audit logging and docs (Phase 3), any change to the `OnCancel` hook contract with upstreams, a wire-visible cancelling status.

🤖 Design-architect pass 17 — agent note: triage this phase against design #2497's recorded decisions; do not re-derive the grace-window mechanism or the statusMessage derivation in triage.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `CancelWithReason` records an internal cancelling mark (never a wire status), invokes OnCancel + context cancel as today, and starts the `protoTasks.cancelGrace` clock (default 5s)
- [ ] Work finishing within the grace window records its own terminal status; an empty statusMessage notes it completed during cancellation; after the window the store flips to `cancelled` with the caller's reason and late results are discarded
- [ ] First terminal recording under the store lock wins, pinned by tests including the grace-expiry race

body:
Design from the design-architect pass 17 (2026-10-29). Full design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-operational-limits.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Follow-on to design #1554: this answers the operational questions #1554's design doc deliberately left open, now that its Phase 1 (one durable `tasks.Store` shared by MCP and /v1, #1555 via PR #1575) gives every limit one place to live. Origin: the seven remaining conformance gaps under dezren39/nix#209, all still registered in `internal/conformance/coverage_stateful.go:117-123`. Audited against origin/main `7d1b081c`.

## Problem

mcpx's tasks are structurally sound and operationally unbounded:

1. **Nothing bounds a task's cost.** `Store.Start` (`internal/tasks/tasks.go:355`) honours any positive caller TTL verbatim (only `ttl <= 0` falls back to the 10m default); there is no per-requestor concurrency cap and no `tasks/*` rate limit (gaps `tasks-resource-limits`, `tasks-rate-limit`). The store has no requestor dimension at all — ownership lives one layer up (`mcpserver.Server.taskOwners`), and the daemon's four `/v1` Start sites share no requestor key.
2. **Cancel lies about what happened.** `Store.CancelWithReason` (tasks.go:519) sets the status to `cancelled` *before* invoking `OnCancel`/context-cancel — its comment claims a "cooperative cancellation handshake" the code does not perform — and `finish()` discards whatever the work then produces, so work that completed in the race window is reported as cancelled (gap `ext-tasks-cancel-cooperative`).
3. **A failed task can fail silently.** In `finish()` (tasks.go:424-431) an `isError` tool result flips the task to `failed` with no `statusMessage`; the fault path directly above sets one (gap `tasks-failed-status-message`).
4. **Nobody can see tasks happen.** Creation, completion and retrieval are logged nowhere (gap `tasks-audit`); the store's `Watch`/`changed` seam is the one existing transition feed.
5. **The unbound-task model is undocumented — and the doc says the opposite.** `visible()` (internal/mcpserver/tasks.go ~L92) states the model: an unowned task "is reachable by its id alone, which is unguessable: that is the tasks extension's whole model", and `tasks/list` lists only owner-matching tasks, so identity-less connections list nothing. `docs/protocol.md:140` nevertheless says "a task is visible only to the connection that started it" (gaps `tasks-document-unbound`, `tasks-get-implies-list`). The ID carrying this model is 64 random bits (`NewID`, tasks.go:344).

## Decisions recorded

1. **Limits live in the store, keyed by requestor, valued in `protoTasks.*`** (the existing settings family in `internal/settings/prototasks.go`). `Store.Start` gains a requestor key; callers pass what they hold (MCP connection identity, /v1 caller identity); the empty key is a real capped "unbound" bucket, not a bypass. Values: `protoTasks.maxTTL` default **1h** — over-cap TTLs are **clamped**, not refused, and the returned task shows the capped value; `protoTasks.maxPerRequestor` default **32** concurrent non-terminal tasks — creation beyond is refused with a named error (-32603 MCP / 429 /v1); `protoTasks.perMinute` default **120** (0 disables) — one fixed window per requestor over all `tasks/*` calls at both dispatch seams, the #2333/#2386 fixed-window shape (use a shared limiter type if one has landed; otherwise the tasks-local copy — no general framework for three call sites). `NewID` moves to 128 bits.
2. **Cancel asks first; the work's own ending wins the grace window.** `CancelWithReason` records an internal *cancelling* mark (never a wire status), invokes `OnCancel` + context cancel as today, and starts `protoTasks.cancelGrace` (default **5s**): work finishing inside the window has its own terminal status recorded by `finish()`; after the window the store flips to `cancelled` and late results are discarded as today. `tasks/cancel` returns after initiating, as today.
3. **A failed task says why.** `finish()`'s `isError` branch derives `statusMessage` from the first text content block of the result (truncated to 512 chars), else the fixed string `tool returned an error result`.
4. **The unbound model is documented, not changed; audit rides the existing seams.** `tasks-get-implies-list` closes as documentation, not behaviour: listing unbound tasks to an identity-less caller would enumerate other callers' work. Phase 3 corrects `docs/protocol.md`'s visibility row and documents reachability-by-ID where tasks are described. Audit: structured log lines via `internal/logging` — creation (id, requestor or `unbound`, clamped TTL) and terminal transitions (id, status, duration) and limit refusals at info; retrieval at debug at the handler seams; ids and metadata only, no task content (#1675 precedent).

## Phases

- Phase 1: limits in the store (requestor plumbing, maxTTL clamp, maxPerRequestor, perMinute window, 128-bit IDs) — retires `tasks-resource-limits` + `tasks-rate-limit`. Independent.
- Phase 2: honest endings (cooperative cancel grace window + `isError` statusMessage) — retires `ext-tasks-cancel-cooperative` + `tasks-failed-status-message`. Independent of Phase 1.
- Phase 3: audit + docs + truth-up (audit lines, protocol.md correction, unbound-model documentation, all seven gap rows retired as their phases land, evidence note toward #1557 — closure of nix#209 itself stays #1557's job). Gated on Phases 1–2.

Open questions stay in the design doc (client input relay — also #1554's question, untouched; per-server upstream concurrency on evidence; whether `tasks/result` long polls count at full window weight — Phase 1 triage may exempt with a one-sentence reason; audit export beyond the daemon log only on a named consumer).

🤖 Design-architect pass 17 — agent note: this issue is the design of record; phases are its sub-issues. Do not re-derive the decisions above in triage; flag genuine blockers here instead.

## Acceptance criteria

- The three implementation phases stay linked from this design issue until each merges or is explicitly declined with rationale recorded here.
- Each phase meets its own acceptance criteria; no phase widens scope beyond the design doc (`files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-operational-limits.md`).
- When all phases have landed or been declined, this issue closes with a summary linking the merged PRs.

2. Then at `git pull --ff-only`: the tree was clean but main had **diverged — ahead 9 / behind 254**. The 9 local commits were all `repo-keeper: snapshot code ...` commits taken through the day (04:23–18:24 CDT). The keeper snapshots whatever live edits agents have made in the primary working tree (that day: .opencode/opencode.jsonc live-applied config and bin/sessions.json runtime state) and commits them directly onto main. Those same changes later land properly through PRs, so the snapshots are pure divergence: origin's opencode.jsonc was strictly newer than the local snapshot state.

Resolution applied with Drew's approval (2026-10-29 ~20:32 CDT): backup branch `backup/primary-local-2026-10-29` pushed at c3b779ca (all 9 snapshots preserved), primary reset --hard to origin/main (7d1b081c), chain re-armed.

Durable fixes wanted:
- **Untrack bin/sessions.json** (git rm --cached + .gitignore): it is live runtime state; tracking it guarantees the primary dirties and diverges whenever sessions run. Same treatment check for any other runtime-state files the keeper keeps sweeping up.
- **Keeper should not commit on a primary clone's main at all** — or should snapshot to a dedicated snapshot branch instead of main. A primary is a deploy source (Drew's standing rule: primaries stay on main + clean, deploys run from the primary at origin/main); any automation that commits to its main breaks every ff-only deploy.
- Until fixed, any deploy/switch flow that pulls the primary must expect this failure mode; the chain's state files from 2026-10-29 (deploy-chain-2220-state.failed*.json in the repo-health goal workspace) hold the evidence.

Related: #2268 (keeper secret guard), #1807 (autocommit merge-in-progress guard), #2230 (autocommit changes under the fleet-expansion umbrella).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bin/sessions.json` is untracked (git rm --cached + .gitignore) and any other runtime-state files the keeper sweeps up get the same treatment, verified by a keeper run leaving the primary clean
- [ ] The laptop-repo-keeper no longer commits onto a primary clone's main — snapshots go to a dedicated snapshot branch (or are not taken on primaries), so a primary's main can only move by fast-forward
- [ ] A deploy chain run after a keeper snapshot completes its ff-only pull without manual rescue

body:
## Bug: a registry record whose `taskRefs` is a well-formed array with malformed elements passes every gate, merges, persists — then crashes `/sessions` at render

`#2408` covered a non-array `taskRefs` crashing `mergeRecords`' spread. The element-level remainder is still open: when `taskRefs` IS an array, nobody ever checks what is inside it, and the one consumer that interprets the elements throws on anything that is not exactly `owner/repo#<digits>`.

The unchecked path:

- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/record-claude-launch.ts:44-46` — `--task` values are copied from argv verbatim into the launch record's `taskRefs`. The plausible short form `--task code#2480` (or a bare `--task 2480`) writes a malformed ref; nothing validates it.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/registry.ts:93-110` — `parseLaunchRecords` checks only that `id` is a string; `recordFromLaunch` (`registry.ts:88`) copies `l.taskRefs ?? []` verbatim, elements included — a string like `"code#2480"` or a non-string element like `42` passes through unchanged.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/registry.ts:138-142` — `isSessionRecord`, the hygiene check at both load sites (fleet-feed registry at `src/sources/live.ts:982`, durable store via `loadRegistryStore`/`mergeIntoRegistry` at `live.ts:610-621`), checks only `id`/`source`/`label` strings. An array of malformed elements passes.
- The merge is fine with them (`registry.ts:130` spreads the array), so the poisoned record is written into the durable registry store and survives restarts.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts:1637-1638` — `sessionRecordLine` maps every taskRef through `refUrl`, and `parseRef` (`src/model.ts:399-405`) **throws** `not a repo-qualified ref: <value>` on any element that is not `owner/repo#<digits>`. `renderSessions` maps that over every record, and `/sessions` calls it uncaught (`src/server.ts:576-579`). One malformed element therefore 500s the whole sessions page — for every record, not just the poisoned one — until the store file is hand-repaired.

Adjacent, same function: `parseRef` converts the digits with `Number(...)` unchecked, so a syntactically valid ref with an oversized number (`developing-today/code#99999999999999999999999`, producible by `refsInText` from a URL in a session title) parses to `1e+23` and `refUrl` emits `https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/1e+23` — a silently wrong link instead of a rejection.

### Verified this run (main `562663fa`)

Sandbox Bun probe importing the real `registry.ts`, `render.ts` and `model.ts` (probe: goal `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-taskrefelems/probe.ts`):

- `parseLaunchRecords` on `{"id":"claude-x1","taskRefs":["code#2480"]}` and `{"id":"claude-x2","taskRefs":[42]}` → both records returned with elements verbatim; `isSessionRecord` returns `true` for both.
- `mergeRecords(records, records)` → succeeds; merged taskRefs `[["code#2480"],[42],["developing-today/code#2480"]]`.
- `refUrl("code#2480")` → throws `not a repo-qualified ref: code#2480`; `refUrl(42)` → throws the same; control `refUrl("developing-today/code#2480")` → the correct URL.
- `renderSessions([goodRecord])` → renders OK (18,608 chars); `renderSessions(merged)` → **throws `not a repo-qualified ref: code#2480`**.
- `parseRef("developing-today/code#99999999999999999999999")` → `{number: 1e+23}`; `refUrl` of it → `.../issues/1e+23`.

### Why it matters

Launch records are appended by hand / by launch scripts (`--task` is free-form argv), feed registry entries arrive from a collector on another host, and the durable store is a hand-editable file — all three producers are exactly the untrusted-boundary inputs this registry's hygiene check exists for. The failure is maximally disproportionate: one typo'd `--task code#123` at some past launch permanently takes down `/sessions` (the fleet's session-identity page), the poison lives in the durable store so restarts don't help, and the thrown error names the value but not the record carrying it. The huge-number sub-case never crashes at all — it just links a session to a wrong, scientific-notation URL.

### Acceptance criteria

- A registry record whose `taskRefs` array contains a malformed element (non-string, or a string that is not `owner/repo#<digits>` with a safe-integer number) can no longer crash `renderSessions`/`/sessions`: the owning layer is pinned by triage (gate rejects/filters elements in `isSessionRecord` + `recordFromLaunch`/`parseLaunchRecords`, vs the renderer skipping unparseable refs) and applied consistently at the feed, store, and launch-record entry points.
- A poisoned record already in the durable store does not wedge the page: `/sessions` keeps serving the remaining records (and ideally the poisoned record renders without its bad refs rather than vanishing).
- `record-claude-launch.ts` either validates `--task` values against the ref shape and refuses/warns at write time, or the issue records why write-time validation is the wrong layer.
- Regression tests cover at least: launch record with `taskRefs: ["code#2480"]`, launch record with `taskRefs: [42]`, a feed/store record with a malformed-element array rendering `/sessions` without throwing, and an oversized-number ref not producing a scientific-notation URL.
- No behaviour change for well-formed records: existing registry/render tests keep passing and good refs render identical links.

### Dedup

- #2408 (open) — non-array `taskRefs` (number/null/string whole value) crashing the merge spread / splitting into character refs. Its acceptance pins an array-shape check; an array of malformed elements passes that fix and crashes later, at render. Different value shape, different crash site (`render.ts:1638` via `model.ts:399`, not `registry.ts:130`).
- #2376 (open) — non-string `lastSeenAt` crashing the merge sort; different field and site.
- Searches for `parseRef` / `taskRefs refUrl` over open+closed issues returned no filing covering element-level validation or the `Number()` precision loss.

— filed by new-issue-creator-code-b (Lane B), 2026-10-29 run
