body:
## Summary

mcpx's client-capability gates treat a JSON `null` declaration as a declared capability. A client that sends `"elicitation": null` — no usable declaration at all — is passed by the form-elicitation gate at protocol revisions 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28, and `null` sub-keys count as declared everywhere the gates parse sub-capabilities: `{"form": null}` grants form mode, `{"url": null}` grants url mode, and sampling's `{"tools": null}` / `{"context": null}` grant `sampling.tools` / `sampling.context`. This is the exact failure the sub-capability gating work (#1753, #1755, #1757) exists to prevent: mcpx will offer elicitations (with a `requestedSchema` the client never agreed to render) and relay tool-carrying sampling questions to a client that declared nothing usable.

## Evidence

All in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go` at main `5a34fa70` (file sha256 `466e1f7c…`):

- `Peer.Declared` (conn.go:219) is key presence only, so `"elicitation": null` counts as declared.
- The form branch of `CanElicit` (conn.go:235-256, added by #1757) unmarshals the declaration into a struct of `json.RawMessage` fields and returns `len(e.Form) > 0 || len(e.URL) == 0`. Go's `json.Unmarshal` of the literal `null` into a struct succeeds as a no-op, so a `null` declaration is indistinguishable from `{}` — and `{}` is the form-only declaration, so the gate opens. A `null` sub-key is stored as the 4-byte RawMessage `null`, so `len(...) > 0` reads it as declared.
- The url branch (conn.go:258-267) has the same sub-key flaw: `{"url": null}` returns true.
- `samplingSub` (conn.go:273-286) repeats the pattern for sampling: `len(s.Tools) > 0` / `len(s.Context) > 0` are true for `null` values. Its own comment states the house rule this violates: "a declaration mcpx cannot parse grants nothing".
- The existing declaration matrix (`internal/mcpserver/proto_test.go`, `TestAClientIsNeverSentSomethingItDidNotDeclare`) covers a malformed string declaration (`"yes"` → refused) but no `null` case — `null` is the one malformed shape that parses without error in Go.

Verified this run with a laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-elicitnull/`, the verbatim mcpx tree from main `5a34fa70` — conn.go sha256 identical on sandbox and in the probe tree — driven through the real `Peer.CanElicit` / `CanSampleTools` / `CanSampleContext`):

```
control {} form                      CanElicit(form) = true  want true  [ok]
control url-only form                CanElicit(form) = false want false [ok]
control malformed 'yes' form         CanElicit(form) = false want false [ok]
control form-declared url            CanElicit(url)  = false want false [ok]
null declaration form 2025-11-25     CanElicit(form) = true  want false [MISMATCH]
null declaration form 2026-07-28     CanElicit(form) = true  want false [MISMATCH]
form:null form                       CanElicit(form) = true  want false [MISMATCH]
url:null url                         CanElicit(url)  = true  want false [MISMATCH]
url:null form                        CanElicit(form) = false want false [ok — the null url key's length blocks form]
null declaration url                 CanElicit(url)  = false want false [ok]
sampling tools:null                  CanSampleTools   = true  want false
sampling context:null                CanSampleContext = true  want false
sampling tools:{}                    CanSampleTools   = true  want true
```

(Probe log: goal hidden_files `probe-2026-10-29-laneA-elicitnull/out.log`.)

## Why it matters

The gates are the trust boundary of #1753's design: a capability a client did not declare must not be used. Clients that serialize an unset capability as `null` instead of omitting the key are realistic (several SDKs emit explicit nulls for optional capability objects), and for those clients every sub-capability gate added by #1755/#1757 is silently open — form elicitations and tool-carrying sampling relays go to a peer that declared nothing. The failure is silent: no parse error is logged, because in Go nothing failed to parse.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CanElicit("form")` and `CanElicit("url")` return false for an elicitation declaration of `null`, and for a mode whose sub-key value is `null` (`{"form": null}` does not grant form; `{"url": null}` does not grant url).
- `CanSampleTools` / `CanSampleContext` return false for `{"tools": null}` / `{"context": null}`.
- Existing behaviour is unchanged for well-formed declarations: `{}` stays the form-only declaration at 2025-11-25+, declared sub-keys (`{}` values) still grant, url-only still refuses form, and pre-2025-11-25 presence semantics are untouched.
- The declaration matrix in `proto_test.go` gains the null cases (whole-declaration null at 2025-11-25+, `form: null`, `url: null`, and the sampling `tools: null` / `context: null` cases) alongside the existing `"yes"` malformed control.
- Triage note: the same RawMessage-length pattern should be checked at the other presence sites the fix touches (e.g. `DeclaredExtension`'s map presence) — either fixed in the same change or explicitly ruled out of scope with a reason.

body:
# aggregator(quota-extract): Claude and Meta reset dates are never validated — an impossible date is emitted verbatim as resetsAt, and a Feb-30 Meta reset silently discards the pool's whole read

## Summary

`extractClaude` and `extractMeta` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` capture a reset date/time from the human-written quota view with shape-only regexes (`(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) (\d{2}:\d{2})`) and pass the captures through `dateTimeCDT`, which is a pure string interpolator — it builds `${date}T${hhmm}:00-05:00` with no calendar or clock validation at all. The result:

- **Claude:** a reset read of `2026-13-28 14:00`, `2026-10-28 99:99`, or `2026-10-39 14:00` is emitted verbatim as the window's `resetsAt` (`"2026-13-28T14:00:00-05:00"` etc.). `Date.parse` of those strings is `NaN`, so every downstream consumer that parses the value (quota-guidance's reset-time filter, derive's pace/reset logic) silently drops or mis-handles it, and render's `fmtDate` falls back to printing the raw impossible string as the reset date. A `2026-02-30` reset is worse: `Date.parse` rolls it over to 2026-03-02, so downstream treats a phantom date as the real reset.
- **Meta:** the same invalid string feeds the reset-passed check `now >= Date.parse(resetIso)`. For month-13 / `99:99` the parse is `NaN`, the comparison is false, and the invalid string is emitted verbatim (and, on the burned-to-empty path, also becomes `wallLiftsAt`). For a `2026-02-30` reset the parse rolls over to 2026-03-02 — which is *before* now in the probe — so the extractor takes the "window already reset, no post-reset read yet" branch and **discards the pool's entire matched 46% read**, windows and all.

This is the module's own fail-soft contract failing in the opposite direction from the usual drop: the percentages were successfully read, so an invalid *reset* should degrade to `resetsAt: null`, not be published as a fact or take the whole read down with it.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 5a34fa70)

Laptop probe driving the real `extractQuotaPools` (Bun 1.4.2; laptop `quota-extract.ts`/`derive.ts` sha256-identical to main 5a34fa70; probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-claudereset/probe.ts` on the laptop), minimal Claude + Meta sections, `now = 2026-10-25T15:00:00Z`:

| reset read | Claude window | Meta result |
|---|---|---|
| control `2026-10-28 14:00` / `2026-10-25 19:00` | 68%, resetsAt `2026-10-28T14:00:00-05:00` ✅ | 46%, resetsAt `2026-10-25T19:00:00-05:00` ✅ |
| month-13 (`2026-13-…`) | 68%, resetsAt `2026-13-28T14:00:00-05:00` verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ | 46%, resetsAt `2026-13-25T19:00:00-05:00` verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ |
| Feb-30 (`2026-02-30 …`) | 68%, resetsAt `2026-02-30T14:00:00-05:00`; `Date.parse` → 2026-03-02 (phantom rollover) ❌ | **windows [] — whole 46% read discarded** as "reset already passed" (rolled-over Mar 2 < now) ❌ |
| time `99:99` | 68%, resetsAt `2026-10-28T99:99:00-05:00` verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ | 46%, resetsAt verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ |
| day-39 (`2026-10-39 …`) | 68%, resetsAt `2026-10-39T14:00:00-05:00` verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ | 46%, resetsAt verbatim, `Date.parse` → NaN ❌ |

File:line (main 5a34fa70):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts:43-45` — `dateTimeCDT`: pure interpolation, no validation of the date or time components.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts:98-100` — `extractClaude`: shape-only reset capture, result becomes the window's `resetsAt` unchecked.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts:132-149` — `extractMeta`: same capture → `resetIso`; the `now >= Date.parse(resetIso)` reset-passed branch (:135), the burned path's `wallLiftsAt: resetIso`, and the normal path's `resetsAt` all consume the unvalidated string.
- Downstream: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts:92-95` — `fmtDate` prints an unparseable `resetsAt` verbatim; `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-guidance.ts:18` — `Date.parse` + finite filter silently drops NaN resets; `pm-stack/aggregator/src/derive.ts:820` — attention-flag detail interpolates `resetsAt.slice(0, 10)`.

## Why it matters

The quota view is a human-written document, and these two pools' resets are typed by hand — a typo'd month, day, or time is exactly the input the fail-soft design exists to absorb. Today one bad digit either publishes an impossible reset date as a measured fact (which the stewardship rotation then reads), or — the Feb-30 Meta case — makes a healthy, current read vanish with a plausible-looking "no post-reset read yet" note, so nothing signals that anything went wrong.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage pins the rule for the `dateTimeCDT` call sites in `extractClaude`/`extractMeta` (expected: validate the captured date as a real calendar date and the time as a real clock time — e.g. the `isCalendarDate` discipline already used in derive.ts — and treat an invalid reset as `resetsAt: null` for that window, keeping the matched percentage windows; Meta's reset-passed and burned/`wallLiftsAt` branches must not consume an invalid reset string).
- [ ] Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts`: month-13, Feb-30, day-39, and `99:99` resets keep the Claude 68% and Meta 46% windows with `resetsAt: null`; the Feb-30 Meta read is NOT discarded as already-reset; the existing control cases (Claude `2026-10-28T14:00:00-05:00`, Meta walled-until-reset) are unchanged.
- [ ] No change to `extractQuotaPools`' per-pool try/catch semantics for genuinely unmatched sections (shell note still renders).

Filed by new-issue-creator-code-b (lane B), run 2026-10-29 18:50 CDT. Dedup: #2197 is `dateTimeCDT`'s fixed UTC-5 offset for *valid* dates (an hour-early error, not validation); #2383 is `extractClinePass`'s Measured anchor through the same helper (its fix validates the ClinePass base/rel path only, and its failure mode is throw-and-drop); #2196 is `monthDayTime` (Codex / OpenCode Go / Command Code). No open or closed issue covers validation at the Claude/Meta reset call sites. NOT self-solved: where validation lives (helper vs call sites) and its interplay with #2197's pending offset fix are triage's pin.

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Summary

`POST /api/save`'s per-file rate limiter cannot stop overlapping saves of the same file: `SaveRateLimiter::check` and `SaveRateLimiter::record` are separate calls with the entire save in between, and `check` only ever sees *completed* saves. Two concurrent saves of one file both pass the 5-second cooldown gate, run in parallel, and finish in arbitrary order — so the filename tag can end up pointing at the *older* revision, silently reverting the newer save.

## Evidence (main `5a34fa70`)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/mod.rs:94-137` — `SaveRateLimiter` is a `HashMap<String, Instant>` of **last completed** save times. `check()` (line 114) only reads the map; `record()` (line 128) inserts after a save finishes. Nothing marks a save as in-flight.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1203` — `save_handler` calls `state.save_limiter.check(&req.name)` and returns 429 on `Err`.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1327` — `state.save_limiter.record(&req.name)` runs only at the very end of the handler, after conversion, blob add, event publish, the archive step, and the filename tag set (`routes.rs:1265`, `state.store.tags().set(tag, new_hash)`).
- The limiter's own doc (`web/mod.rs:88-92`) states its purpose: "rejects saves that happen within the cooldown period… prevents rapid-fire saves from creating excessive archive entries." Overlapping saves defeat both halves: each creates its own archive entry, and neither is rejected.
- Nothing else serializes saves per file in the handler: the `local_events` mutex is held only around the synchronous publish (`routes.rs:1244`), not across check → tag-set → record.

## Verified this run

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-saverace/` — the verbatim `SaveRateLimiter` from `web/mod.rs` driven exactly as `save_handler` drives it (check → simulated save work → record), cooldown 5s:

- Sequential control: first save allowed, second save immediately after is rejected (limiter works as intended for sequential saves).
- Two concurrent saves of the same file (300 ms of work each): **both allowed** — each checks before the other records.
- Slow-save variant: a second save arriving 100 ms into a 400 ms first save is **also allowed**, because the first save has not recorded yet.

## Why it matters

The web editor's clients save through this endpoint (`saveFile` in `web/src/main.ts`), and more than one client can hold the same file open (two tabs, two browsers, a tab plus a collab peer). When two saves overlap, completion order — not edit order — decides which revision the filename tag names, so the file can silently revert to the older content while both clients were told their save succeeded (both get a 200 with their own hash). The newer revision still exists as a published event, but nothing points the filename at it. This is the server-side counterpart of the client-side concurrency fixed in closed #1440; the endpoint itself never got the same guarantee.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A second `POST /api/save` for the same file that arrives while a save for that file is in flight (or within the cooldown of one starting) is rejected with 429 and the same "Try again in Ns" contract, OR same-file saves are serialized so completion order matches arrival order — the behaviour is pinned in the fix.
- [ ] The filename tag always ends up naming the revision from the **last-accepted** save, never an earlier in-flight one, under concurrent load.
- [ ] Sequential behaviour is unchanged: a save more than the cooldown after the previous completed save is accepted; the existing save-handler tests keep passing.
- [ ] A regression test drives two overlapping saves of the same name through the handler (or the limiter in the handler's call pattern) and asserts only one proceeds / the tag names the later revision.

## Dedup / related

- #1713 (open) is the same component's *other* defect — the map is never evicted. This issue is the check/record race; the fixes are independent (eviction does not close the race, closing the race does not evict).
- #1440 (closed) fixed concurrent saves in the client `AutoSaveManager`; this is the server endpoint it calls.
- #2437 (open) is the client auto-save cancel/in-flight defect, a different layer.

## Finding

PR #1715 (OPEN, draft, Jules) — "feat(id): add admin-protected prometheus metrics and tracing spans", for #553 — contains, at its current head `17cdeeb3e01ac94ec10890c851eaba89a59c9036`:

1. **A stray scratch file at the repository root: `get_plan.py`.** Its entire content is an agent's internal monologue:

   ```python
   print("""
   I cannot use `git push --force`. The submit tool will handle pushing.
   Wait! The `submit` tool will push my current branch to origin.
   I'll just call the submit tool.
   """)
   ```

   Verified present on the PR head via the contents API (`get_plan.py` at ref `17cdeeb3…`); it is not on main. If the PR merges as-is, this lands at the root of developing-today/code.

2. **No tests for the behaviour it adds.** The PR's three files are `get_plan.py`, `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs` (+141: the new admin-token-gated `GET /api/world/metrics` handler and its Prometheus rendering, including the histogram bucket rendering) and `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs` (+43: per-command tracing spans). No test file is touched: nothing pins the admin-token rejection path, the metrics text format, or the histogram `_bucket`/`_sum`/`_count` rendering — for an endpoint whose whole point is a format other tools (Prometheus) parse strictly.

The PR has been a draft with no updates since 2026-10-28 19:12 UTC, and #553 is still open, so the slice is not superseded — it needs shepherding, not abandonment.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/1715 — draft, created 2026-10-28T15:51:31Z, last updated 2026-10-28T19:12:29Z, head `17cdeeb3e01ac94ec10890c851eaba89a59c9036` (branch `feat/issue-553-world-metrics-7717747048733320682`), commits `1b225e3b`, `ff93a7c8`, `436f6a9d`, `17cdeeb3`.
- `get_plan.py` confirmed on the PR head (contents API, ref = head sha); absent from main `5a34fa70`.
- PR file list (gh): `get_plan.py +5/-0`, `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs +141/-0`, `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs +43/-1` — no `*_test*`/`tests` file.
- Tracking issue #553 ("id(world): F11.7 host metrics, Prometheus endpoint and tracing spans") is OPEN.

## Why it matters

Repo-root junk from an agent scratch file is exactly the class of artifact that then needs a cleanup PR and confuses every future root listing/tooling scan; catching it is cheapest before merge. And an untested Prometheus exporter tends to be discovered broken by the first scrape, not by CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `get_plan.py` is removed from PR #1715's branch (and does not reach main).
- [ ] PR #1715 gains tests covering: unauthenticated/wrong-token requests to `/api/world/metrics` are rejected; an admin-token request returns the documented metric families; the histogram rendering emits cumulative `le` buckets ending at `+Inf` with `_sum`/`_count` consistent with the snapshot.
- [ ] PR #1715 is then either marked ready and merged, or closed with a comment naming what supersedes it — it does not sit as a stale draft.

body:
## Problem

`fetchProjectPool` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts:153-175) paginates the org Project pool with a hard cap of 10 pages (`for (let page = 0; page < 10; page++)`, :159; query page size `items(first: 100)` at :28, so at most 1,000 items). When the loop exits because the cap was hit — `hasNextPage` still true — the function returns the partial pool exactly as if it were complete: no throw, no truncation marker, no log. The page's own `totalCount` is available on every response and is even parsed by `projectPageInfo` (projects.ts:142-149), but `fetchProjectPool` never compares it against what it collected.

The sole caller, the fleet-feed collector (pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts:558), treats only a thrown error or a zero-length result as failure (either omits the projects section, :559-568). A truncated pool is published into the fleet feed as the whole pool, and the aggregator then resolves refs and renders /projects, board and program counts from it — every item past page 10 silently vanishes from every dashboard surface, with nothing anywhere saying the pool is incomplete.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 5a34fa70)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-poolpages/` (verbatim projects.ts + model.ts from main, Bun, using the injectable `fetchFn` the module provides for tests):

- Mock fetch returning 2 items per page, `hasNextPage: true` forever, `totalCount: 25`: `fetchProjectPool` stopped after exactly **10 fetch calls and returned 20 items** — 5 items short of the stated totalCount — with no error and no truncation signal.
- Control (3 pages, then `hasNextPage: false`, totalCount 6): returned all 6 items in 3 calls — the finite path is correct; only the cap exit is silent.

## Why it matters

The Project pool is the dashboard's live resolution source for GitHub items (#910 stage 5, projects.ts header). A silently truncated pool is worse than an omitted section: an omitted section makes the aggregator fall back to its previous chain and the health views can say the section is missing, while a partial pool looks authoritative — items simply stop existing on the board, /projects counts understate, and nobody is alerted as the real pool grows past 1,000 items.

## Acceptance criteria

- When the 10-page cap is reached with `hasNextPage` still true (or the collected count is short of the pages' `totalCount`), the read is treated as incomplete in an observable way — e.g. `fetchProjectPool` throws so the collector's existing fail-soft path omits the section and logs why, or the truncation is otherwise surfaced (collector log + a completeness signal in the published section) — triage pins which.
- A pool that fits within the cap is returned complete and unchanged (existing pagination behaviour and tests keep passing).
- Regression test with a mock `fetchFn`: an always-`hasNextPage` sequence past the cap produces the pinned incomplete-read behaviour instead of a silently partial array; a finite multi-page sequence still returns every item.

## Dedup / related

- #2426 (cold-store-reaper Drive `list_backups` pagination) is the same failure pattern in a different component; this is the Project-pool collector read, distinct code and consumer.
- #1208 (/projects browsability, "honest truncation") is about rendering the pool in the UI, not the collector's fetch cap.
- Searched open+closed issues for `fetchProjectPool`, pagination/totalCount and pool truncation: no covering issue.

title: projector(webhook): a delivery that fails to apply can never be retried — its error row makes every redelivery a 'duplicate', and push events are lost permanently

labels.name: source/design-architect

body:
## Summary

In the PM projector's webhook intake, a delivery whose application **fails** is permanently dropped — GitHub's redelivery of the same delivery GUID is answered `200 {"status":"duplicate"}` and never applied. The idempotency check asks only whether *any* row exists for the delivery id, but the failure paths record a row too (with `outcome: "error"`). So one transient failure at apply time (a locked/restarting DB, a mid-migration schema gap, a Turso hiccup) converts a retryable 500 into silent, permanent data loss. For `push` events the loss is absolute: pushes have no reconciliation stream (`reconcile.ts` covers issues, PRs, issue comments, review comments, and reviews only), so a dropped push never appears in `pmp_push_events`. Item/comment events are partially healed by the next reconcile poll — but only when reconcile is enabled and reaches that repo/stream, and the audit row still claims the delivery was handled.

## Evidence (main 5a34fa70)

- `pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts:337-343` — `deliveryApplied(db, deliveryId)` is `SELECT 1 FROM pmp_deliveries WHERE delivery_id = ?` with **no outcome filter**: any recorded row, applied or errored, counts as "applied". (The schema comment in `schema.sql` states the intent as "a redelivered webhook is applied at most once" — the check as written enforces "recorded at most once".)
- `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts:76-80` — the webhook handler returns `200 {status: "duplicate"}` whenever `deliveryApplied` is true, before parsing or applying.
- `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts:99` — when `applyEvent` throws, the handler records the delivery with `outcome: "error"` and returns 500. GitHub redelivers on 5xx — straight into the duplicate short-circuit above. (The `invalid_json` error row at :84 has the same effect for its delivery id, harmlessly, since the payload cannot change; the apply-failure row is the harmful one.)

Verified this run with a laptop Bun probe driving the **real** `handleRequest` (HMAC-signed push webhook, real `store.ts`, real libSQL file DB; files md5-identical to main 5a34fa70):

```
attempt 1 (apply fails):        500 {"error":"apply_failed"}
deliveries row after failure:   [{"delivery_id":"delivery-xyz","outcome":"error"}]
attempt 2 (redelivery, same GUID): 200 {"status":"duplicate"}
push_events rows after redelivery: [{"n":0}]
```

The transient failure was simulated by dropping `pmp_push_events` for the first attempt and restoring the schema (via the real `migrate`) before the redelivery — the exact shape of a mid-deploy/migration hiccup. After the schema was healthy, the redelivery was still refused and the push was never recorded.

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-projdel/probe2.ts` (laptop).

## Why it matters

Webhook intake is the projector's live path; reconciliation is explicitly the safety net, not the primary feed, and it does not cover pushes at all. The current code turns the one failure mode redelivery exists for — a transient 5xx — into the one outcome redelivery cannot fix. Worse, the response on redelivery is a success-shaped `200 duplicate`, so nothing in GitHub's delivery log or the projector's own responses signals the loss; only the `outcome: "error"` audit row knows, and nothing reads it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A delivery whose application failed (an `outcome: "error"` row, or no row) is **applied** when redelivered with the same delivery GUID; only successfully applied (or genuinely ignored-after-successful-processing) deliveries short-circuit as duplicates.
- Recording a redelivery attempt does not violate the `pmp_deliveries` primary key or lose the original error audit (triage pins the shape: e.g. outcome-filtered check + upsert/update on retry, or not recording failures as delivery rows while keeping an error log).
- Regression tests cover: apply-failure then same-GUID redelivery succeeds and the event's rows exist (push event recorded); successful delivery then same-GUID redelivery still returns duplicate and applies nothing twice; the invalid-JSON path's behaviour is unchanged or explicitly re-pinned by triage.
- The duplicate response remains `200` for true duplicates (GitHub must not keep retrying those).

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `deliveryApplied`, "projector delivery", "webhook redeliver": no issue covers failed-delivery retry. #2455 (filed this run) is the projector comments monotonic guard — different mechanism in the same service. #1547 (open) is the read-API limit parameter; #1529 (open) is GitHub App key decoding.

body:
## Summary

In the PM projector, a comment that GitHub deleted can come back. The comments table's monotonic guard — the `ON CONFLICT … WHERE excluded.source_updated_at >= pmp_comments.source_updated_at` clause that is supposed to stop stale writes overwriting newer state — keys on the comment's **creation** time, not its last-update time, and the delete path never advances it. So any stale `created`/`edited` upsert for that comment (a redelivered or out-of-order webhook delivery under a new delivery id, a replayed fixture, a delayed retry) satisfies the guard with equality and overwrites the row wholesale — including setting `deleted` back to 0 and restoring the pre-edit body. Nothing ever re-deletes it: the comment no longer exists in GitHub's comment lists, so reconciliation never sees it again. The deleted comment is permanently back in the unified activity stream (`getComments` / subject activity) with its original text.

Items do not have this flaw: `fromIssueOrPr` sets `source_updated_at: updatedAt` (projector.ts:68), so a stale item write is genuinely refused. Comments are the asymmetric case.

## Evidence (main 5a34fa70)

- `pm-stack/projector/src/projector.ts:95` — `commentCommon` builds every webhook comment row with `source_updated_at: createdAt`, even for `edited` events whose `updated_at` is newer. The row's own `updated_at` field (line ~86) is set correctly; only the guard key is wrong.
- `pm-stack/projector/src/reconcile.ts:91` and `:131` — both reconciliation comment builders (issue/review comments, and reviews) also set `source_updated_at: createdAt`, so reconcile writes carry the same broken guard key. (Schema comment in `schema.sql` describes the field as "created_at (or updated_at)" — the code always picks created_at.)
- `pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts:205-224` — `upsertComment`'s conflict update sets every column, including `deleted = excluded.deleted` (:221), gated only by `WHERE excluded.source_updated_at >= pmp_comments.source_updated_at` (:224). A stale upsert's guard key (created_at) is *equal* to the stored one, so it always passes.
- `pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts:247-252` — `markCommentDeleted` sets `deleted = 1` and `fetched_at`, but does **not** advance `source_updated_at`, so the delete leaves no trace the guard can compare against. It is called from the `issue_comment` deleted branch (projector.ts:159) and the `pull_request_review_comment` deleted branch (projector.ts:213) — both event kinds are affected.

Verified this run with a laptop Bun probe driving the **real** `applyEvent` + real `store.ts` against a real libSQL file DB (files md5-identical to main 5a34fa70: store.ts `448fc963…`, projector.ts `d692044c…`, schema.sql `afaecba…`):

```
after created:               {"body":"original","deleted":0,"source_updated_at":"2026-10-01T01:00:00Z"}
after edited:                {"body":"EDITED",  "deleted":0,"source_updated_at":"2026-10-01T01:00:00Z"}
after deleted:               {"body":"EDITED",  "deleted":1,"source_updated_at":"2026-10-01T01:00:00Z"}
after stale created replay:  {"body":"original","deleted":0,"source_updated_at":"2026-10-01T01:00:00Z"}
```

Note the second row: even a legitimate *edit* does not advance `source_updated_at`, so the stale replay in step 4 also reverts the body from `EDITED` back to `original` — the guard cannot order any two versions of a comment, only refuse writes older than its creation (which never exist).

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-projdel/probe.ts` (laptop).

## Why it matters

The projector is the fleet dashboard's unified comment-activity projection (aggregator requirement #2): a deleted comment reappearing — with the text its author deliberately removed — is a correctness and trust problem in exactly the stream people read to know what was said. Deletes are also how spam/abuse removals and mistaken posts are retracted; the projection silently un-retracts them on any out-of-order or redelivered delivery, and no subsequent reconciliation repairs it, because GitHub's lists no longer contain the comment. The same broken guard key also means comment *edits* have no ordering protection at all: a delayed pre-edit delivery overwrites the edited body (self-heals only if a later reconcile happens to re-fetch that comment).

## Acceptance criteria

- After a comment is marked deleted, no upsert whose source state predates the delete can set `deleted` back to 0 or otherwise modify the row (a stale `created`/`edited` replay leaves `deleted = 1` and the last body intact).
- The comments guard key reflects last-update time: an `edited` upsert advances it, and a stale pre-edit upsert is refused (body stays at the edited text), matching the items behaviour.
- `markCommentDeleted` records delete-time ordering information (or an equivalent tombstone rule) so the delete wins against earlier-created source states, for both `issue_comment` and `pull_request_review_comment` deletes, and for webhook- and reconcile-sourced writes.
- Regression tests cover: create → edit → delete → stale-create replay (stays deleted, edited body kept); create → edit → stale-create replay without a delete (edited body kept); the equivalent review-comment delete path; and a fresh legitimate post-delete write ordering case triage defines (e.g. a genuinely newer update still applies, if triage decides one exists).

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `markCommentDeleted`, `pmp_comments`, `source_updated_at`, "projector deleted comment", "projector comment monotonic": no issue covers comment guard ordering or delete resurrection. #1547 (open) is the projector read-API `limit` parameter — different defect, same service. #1529 (open) is the projector's GitHub App key decoding. Sibling guard asymmetry: items (projector.ts:68) already use `updatedAt` correctly and are not in scope.

title: aggregator(feed): isFleetFeed never checks saas — one malformed service crashes usage() and /quota, a non-array silently switches the whole usage view to fallback

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Problem

`isFleetFeed` (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:207-219`) never validates
the optional `saas` section at all — it checks only `version`,
`generatedAt`, `quota.pools` being an array, and `attention` being an
array. But `saas` is the section that *gates* the live source's whole
usage branch, and the services it carries are served verbatim into the
attention-flag builder and the `/quota` service cards, which
dereference every entry unguarded. One malformed entry in a feed that
passes the gate crashes the entire Usage & billing page — inside
`usage()` itself, before rendering starts.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- `feed.ts:42-43`: `FleetFeed.saas?: SaasService[]` (shape at
  `model.ts:1121-1147`: string `id`/`name`/`plan`, `metrics:
  UsageMetric[]`, `conflicts: string[]`, `paygEstimate` object-or-null,
  numeric `cadenceDays`, etc.).
- `feed.ts:207-219`: `isFleetFeed` contains no `saas` check of any
  kind — not array-ness, not entry shape.
- `sources/live.ts:808-815`: `usage()`'s feed branch is taken whenever
  `feed.saas` is truthy with a non-zero `length`, and the section is
  passed through verbatim: `services: feed.saas` — no filter or
  per-entry guard, unlike the registry / projects / snapshots
  consumers in the same file, which validate or filter first.
- `sources/live.ts:832`: `usage()` calls
  `buildAttentionFlags(feed.quota, partial)` while building its return
  value; `derive.ts:823-848` dereferences `svc.metrics` and
  `svc.paygEstimate.high` per entry — a null entry or an entry missing
  `metrics` throws here, inside `usage()`, so every route that awaits
  `usage()` fails.
- `render.ts:1808-1809,1703-1720`: `renderQuota` filters
  `usage.services` by `s.group` and each surviving card dereferences
  `svc.metrics.filter(...)`, `svc.conflicts.length`,
  `svc.billedUsd.toFixed(2)`, `svc.paygEstimate.low|high.toFixed(2)` —
  an entry with a valid `group` but missing `conflicts` throws in the
  render even though the flag builder passed it.
- `server.ts:486-487` (`/quota`), `:492` (`/quota/service/:id` — also
  `usage.services.find((s) => s.id ...)`), `:656-665`
  (`/api/quota.json`): all await `source.usage()` with no catch, so
  the throw becomes a 500 for the whole hub page and both JSON twins.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedpayg/`
`probe2.ts`, real `feed.ts` + `derive.ts` + `render.ts` from main
`5a34fa70`, md5-identical, Bun 1.4.2; usage view assembled exactly as
`live.ts:811-815` assembles it, flags built exactly as `live.ts:832`):

| `saas` | `isFleetFeed` | feed branch taken (`live.ts:808`) | `buildAttentionFlags` (in `usage()`) | `renderQuota` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| valid entry (control) | `true` | yes | OK | OK — card renders |
| `[null]` | `true` | yes | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'svc.metrics')` | **throws** on `s.group` |
| `"oops"` (non-array string) | `true` | yes (`.length` 4) | **throws** on `svc.metrics` (iterates chars) | **throws** `usage.services.filter is not a function` |
| `{...}` (non-array object) | `true` | **no** — `.length` undefined, `usage()` silently falls back to direct extraction and the feed section is ignored | n/a on the live path | n/a on the live path |
| entry missing `metrics` | `true` | yes | **throws** on `svc.metrics` | **throws** on `svc.metrics.filter` |
| entry missing `conflicts` (valid `group`) | `true` | yes | OK | **throws** `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'svc.conflicts.length')` |
| `[valid, null]` mixed | `true` | yes | **throws** on `svc.metrics` | **throws** — the valid card never renders |

## Why it matters

`saas` is the hub's core section (§2.3): the service cards are the
page, and this section is also the switch that selects the feed path
for the *entire* usage view — so a single drifted or hand-edited
collector entry doesn't just drop one card, it takes down `/quota`,
`/quota/service/:id` and `/api/quota.json` (and every other `usage()`
consumer), or — in the non-array-object case — silently discards the
feed's hub sections in favour of a stale direct read with no signal.
This is the same failure class as #2427 (attention), #2429 (quota
pools), #2439 (chargesAttention), #2445 (charges), #2446
(subscriptions) and #2450 (payg) at the same gate — the fix should
stay consistent with whatever layer those pin. This issue is the
`saas` field specifically, with its own consumers
(`buildAttentionFlags` + the service cards) and its branch-switch role.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `usage()` or
  `/quota` via `saas`: either the gate validates `saas` (array of
  entries with string `id`/`name`/`plan`, array `metrics`/`conflicts`,
  well-formed `paygEstimate` when non-null), or the live source
  filters/defaults malformed entries before the view is built — the
  layer pinned consistently with the
  #2427/#2429/#2439/#2445/#2446/#2450 rulings.
- Malformed entries are dropped individually; well-formed entries in
  the same array still render and still contribute attention flags.
- A non-array `saas` value no longer silently switches the whole
  usage view to the fallback path without any provenance/diagnostic
  signal.
- Regression tests cover: `[null]` entry, non-array `saas` (string
  and object), entry missing `metrics`, entry missing `conflicts`,
  `[valid, null]` mixed — each rendering the valid remainder, never
  throwing; a well-formed feed unchanged, and the collector still
  accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `payg`, `isFleetFeed`, `saas feed`
and `isFleetFeed never checks` returned no covering issue for the feed
`saas` gate. #1119 is a contract-test request for the
`/api/quota.json` saas/payg schema — related, but it does not track
this verified crash at the feed gate. Siblings at the same gate:
#2427 (attention), #2429 (quota pools), #2439 (chargesAttention),
#2445 (charges), #2446 (subscriptions), #2450 (payg — filed this run)
— each a distinct field and consumer.

  `feed.saas` is non-empty), the section is passed through verbatim:
  `payg: feed.payg ?? []` — no filter or per-entry guard.
- `sources/live.ts:832`: `usage()` then calls
  `buildAttentionFlags(feed.quota, partial)` while building its return
  value; `derive.ts:852-862` dereferences `line.unbilledUsd` /
  `line.estimate.low|high` per line — a null line throws here, inside
  `usage()`, so every route that awaits `usage()` fails.
- `render.ts:1684-1700`: `paygCardHtml` maps lines with
  `l.accruedUsd.toFixed(2)` / `l.estimate.low.toFixed(2)` etc. — a
  string `accruedUsd` or a null line throws in the render too.
- `server.ts:486-487` (`/quota`), `:492` (`/quota/service/:id`),
  `:656-665` (`/api/quota.json`): all await `source.usage()` with no
  catch, so the throw becomes a 500 for the whole hub page and both
  JSON twins — not just a missing PAYG card.

Laptop Bun probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedpayg/`, real
`feed.ts` + `derive.ts` + `render.ts` from main `5a34fa70`,
md5-identical, Bun 1.4.2; usage view assembled exactly as
`live.ts:811-815` assembles it, flags built exactly as `live.ts:832`):

| `payg` | `isFleetFeed` | `buildAttentionFlags` (in `usage()`) | `renderQuota` |
|---|---|---|---|
| valid line (control) | `true` | OK | OK — line renders |
| `[null]` | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'line.unbilledUsd')` | **throws** on `l.accruedUsd` |
| `"oops"` (non-array string) | `true` | OK (iterates chars, no flags) | **throws** `usage.payg.map is not a function` |
| `{...}` (non-array object) | `true` | **throws** `TypeError: {} is not iterable` | OK (empty card — but `usage()` already threw) |
| entry with string `accruedUsd` | `true` | OK | **throws** `l.accruedUsd.toFixed is not a function` |
| `[valid, null]` mixed | `true` | **throws** on `line.unbilledUsd` | **throws** — the valid line never renders |

## Why it matters

`payg` is the hub's PAYG dollars card (§1.2) — the metered-spill lines
the fleet's spend discipline reads. The collector emits these lines
from the quota records, so a single drifted or hand-edited feed line
takes down `/quota`, `/quota/service/:id` and `/api/quota.json`
entirely instead of dropping one line. This is the same failure class
as #2427 (attention entries), #2429 (quota pools), #2439
(chargesAttention), #2445 (charges) and #2446 (subscriptions) at the
same gate — the fix should stay consistent with whatever layer those
pin. This issue is the `payg` field specifically, with its own
consumers (`buildAttentionFlags` + `paygCardHtml`).

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed passing `isFleetFeed` can no longer crash `usage()` or
  `/quota`: either the gate validates `payg` (array of lines with
  string `id`/`label`/`note`, numeric-or-null `accruedUsd`/
  `unbilledUsd`, and a well-formed `estimate` when present), or the
  live source filters/defaults malformed lines before the view is
  built — the layer pinned consistently with the
  #2427/#2429/#2439/#2445/#2446 rulings.
- Malformed lines are dropped individually; well-formed lines in the
  same array still render and still contribute attention flags.
- Regression tests cover: `[null]` line, non-array `payg` (string and
  object), string `accruedUsd`, `[valid, null]` mixed — each rendering
  the valid remainder, never throwing; a well-formed feed unchanged,
  and the collector still accepts its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for `payg`, `isFleetFeed` and `saas feed`
returned no covering issue for the feed `payg` gate. #1119 is a
contract-test request for the `/api/quota.json` saas/payg schema —
related, but it does not track this verified crash at the feed gate.
Siblings at the same gate: #2427 (attention), #2429 (quota pools),
#2439 (chargesAttention), #2445 (charges), #2446 (subscriptions) —
each a distinct field and consumer.

title: id(web/auto-save): cancel() does not stop an in-flight save — its retry/follow-up runs after the editor closes and saveFile() targets the newly opened document

body:
## Problem

`AutoSaveManager.cancel()` (`pkgs/id/web/src/auto-save.ts:104-121`) — called when the editor closes (`pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts:1015`, in `closeEditor()`, which then drops the manager) — clears the pending timers and resets the indicator, but it does nothing about a save that is **already in flight**. There is no disposed/cancelled flag, and `onSaveResult` (`auto-save.ts:160+`) never checks whether the manager was cancelled while its save was unresolved:

- A rate-limit result schedules a fresh retry unconditionally (`auto-save.ts:188-191`): the retry timer is created *after* `cancel()` cleared the old one, so it fires and calls `saveFn()` for a closed editor.
- An ok result with edits that arrived during the flight runs the coalesced follow-up (`auto-save.ts:162-167`): `triggerSave()` calls `saveFn()` again after `cancel()`.
- A generic-error result with a coalesced edit does the same (`auto-save.ts:199-213`).
- Every one of these paths also calls `updateIndicator()`, which writes to the shared `#save-btn` element by global id — by then that button belongs to whatever document was opened next.

This matters because `saveFn` is not document-bound: the manager is constructed as `new AutoSaveManager(() => this.saveFile())` (`main.ts:976`), and `saveFile()` (`main.ts:1044-1056`) reads the **current** `this.collab.editor` and the **current** `#editor-container` dataset (`docId`/`hash`). A stale manager's post-cancel retry/follow-up therefore saves *the newly opened document's* current state under its name/hash — an unrequested save that bypasses that document's own manager, breaking the one-save-in-flight serialization #1440 established (two managers can now have saves in flight for the same document), and its indicator writes can re-enable/relabel the new editor's save button mid-save. With no editor open it is "only" a spurious save attempt and state churn on a dropped manager.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

Laptop probe (verbatim `auto-save.ts`, md5 `7448db377c7567650a5ef5d4a0428652`, bun, deferred saveFn; probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-autosave/` on the laptop):

- Case 1 — `saveNow()`, then `cancel()`, then resolve `{ok:false, retryAfterMs:200}`: state went `idle` (cancel) → `rate-limited` (completion), the retry fired, **saveFn calls = 2 — a save ran after cancel**.
- Case 2 — `saveNow()`, edit during flight, `cancel()`, then resolve `{ok:true}`: **saveFn calls = 2 — the follow-up save ran after cancel**, state back to `saving`.
- Case 3 (control, no cancel): rate-limit retry runs as designed (calls = 2).
- Case 4 (control, cancel before any save starts): calls = 0 — cancel works for not-yet-started saves; only the in-flight completion leaks through.

`auto-save.test.ts` covers the #1440 serialization and the #1616 follow-up, but has no cancel-during-flight case (no `cancel()` test at all).

## Why it matters

Closing a document is the one moment the manager's owner explicitly declares "no more saves from me". A save that fires afterwards acts on a different document than the one it was created for, because `saveFile()` resolves its target from live app state at call time. That is a wrong-document write path — the severity is bounded (it saves the new document's own current content under its own name, not the closed document's content into it), but it defeats the serialization invariant the class exists to provide, and the shared-button indicator writes race the new manager.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After `cancel()`, a completing in-flight save schedules nothing: no retry timer, no follow-up `triggerSave()`, no `saveFn()` call, and no indicator writes from the cancelled manager (e.g. a disposed flag checked in `onSaveResult`/`triggerSave`, or an equivalent generation guard).
- [ ] New tests in `auto-save.test.ts` (fake timers, deferred saveFn, mirroring the probe): cancel-during-flight + rate-limit result → no retry save; cancel-during-flight + edit-during-flight + ok result → no follow-up save; cancel-during-flight + generic-error result → no follow-up save.
- [ ] Existing behavior unchanged when not cancelled: the #1440/#1616 tests and the rate-limit retry test still pass.
- [ ] `closeEditor()` needs no compensating change in `main.ts` (the fix lives in the manager's lifecycle), or any needed change there is called out explicitly.

Related: #1440 (serialization, closed), #1616 (generic-error follow-up, closed), #1494 (saveFile name decoding — different defect, open).

labels.name: app/pm-stack

body:
## Bug

`pm-stack/aggregator` — the fleet feed's top-level gate `isFleetFeed` checks only that `attention` is an array, never its entries, and the live source is the one feed consumer that does **not** element-filter its array before use. One malformed entry therefore takes down the attention and today surfaces instead of being dropped like every sibling section's bad entries are.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

- Gate: `src/feed.ts:207-219` — `isFleetFeed` requires `version === 1`, a parseable `generatedAt`, a `quota` object with an array `pools`, and `Array.isArray(f.attention)`. Nothing checks that attention entries are objects, or that `sessionId` (the field every consumer keys on, `src/model.ts:316`) is a string.
- Unguarded consumer: `src/sources/live.ts:864-896` — `attention()` runs `for (const e of feed.attention) byId.set(e.sessionId, e)` (line 873) with no filter and no try/catch around the feed loop (the laptop-sessions half below it *is* fail-soft). Every other array the live source ingests is element-filtered first: registry records via `isSessionRecord` (live.ts:611, 980), project pool items via `isProjectPoolItem` (live.ts:703, 742), snapshot records via `isSnapshotRecord` inside `SnapshotStore.append` (snapshots.ts). Attention is the exception.
- No rescue downstream: `server.ts` `attentionContext()` (line 237) and `todayContext()` (line 308) await `source.attention()` with no `.catch`, and `fetchHandler` (line 794) has no top-level catch — so the throw surfaces as a failed request on `/attention`, `/today`, `/frag/attention/*`, `/api/attention.json`, and `/api/today.json`.

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-feedattn/`, real `feed.ts` + `derive.ts` from origin/main — md5-identical to the sandbox clone — Bun 1.4.2, live.ts loop reproduced verbatim):

```
== control: one well-formed entry
isFleetFeed: true
live byId loop: ok, size = 1 keys = [ "s1" ]
buildAttention: ok, all = 1

== attention [null]
isFleetFeed: true
THROWS: TypeError - null is not an object (evaluating 'e.sessionId')

== two entries, both missing sessionId
isFleetFeed: true
live byId loop: ok, size = 1 keys = [ "undefined" ]
buildAttention: ok, all = 1
```

- Secondary, silent: entries whose `sessionId` is missing or not a string do not crash — they collide on the single `undefined` map key (probe: two distinct sessions collapse to one; a `42` / `"x"` entry is keyed `undefined` too), so sessions silently vanish from the attention view with no error anywhere.

## Why it matters

The feed file is produced by a different job (the collector) and already has a house pattern for exactly this failure class: validate at the gate or filter at the consumer, degrade to the remaining good entries, never let one bad record fail the whole facet (see the dns/aa/orchestration/registry section validators). Attention missed that treatment, so a single corrupt or schema-drifted session entry — e.g. a collector change emitting a null placeholder — blacks out the two most-used pages (/today, /attention) instead of dropping one session, and subtler drift (a renamed/dropped `sessionId`) silently under-reports live sessions.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feed whose `attention` array contains a `null`, a non-object, or an entry without a string `sessionId` no longer throws in `attention()`: the malformed entries are dropped (at the `isFleetFeed` gate or filtered in the live source, matching the registry/projects pattern — triage pins the layer) and the well-formed entries still render on /attention and /today.
- Entries are never silently merged under an `undefined`/non-string key: either they are rejected by the same validation, or the dedupe key is only ever a validated string sessionId.
- Regression tests (aggregator test suite) cover: `[valid, null]` renders just the valid entry; two entries missing `sessionId` do not collapse into one rendered session; a fully well-formed feed is unchanged.
- The gate/filter choice is consistent for the collector's own use of `isFleetFeed` (scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts imports the same gate) — a stricter gate must not make the collector reject its own emitted feed.

## Dedup

`gh` searches (open + closed) for "isFleetFeed" and "feed attention entries" return only #2242 (health section stamps — different fields/functions) and #1176 (open, a broad contract-test-suite impl request across all publisher→collector→aggregator schemas; it does not name this crash, and every sibling section validator — #2376 registry, #2408 taskRefs, #2415 aa, #2412 dns, #2417 orchestration — was filed individually alongside it). No open or closed issue covers attention-entry validation.

body:
## Problem

The fleet feed's Project-pool gate never checks `labels` (or several other fields its consumers treat as typed), so one malformed pool entry passes validation, is converted verbatim into a `GhItem`, and crashes the board/item renders that call `.some`/`.toLowerCase` on its labels.

- `ProjectPoolItem` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/model.ts:55-82) declares `labels?: string[]`, required `url`/`projectUrl`/`contentKind`, and `status`/`area`/`horizon`/`kind` as `string | null`.
- `isProjectPoolItem` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts:182-195) — the only filter applied to the feed's `projects` array, at src/sources/live.ts:703 (`items()`) and :742 (`projects()`) — checks only `id`, `ref`, `repo`, `number`, `issueUrl`, `title`, and `state`. It never checks `labels`, `url`, `projectUrl`, `contentKind`, `status`/`area`/`horizon`/`kind`, `author`, or `updatedAt`.
- `poolItemToGhItem` (projects.ts:197-215) passes the unchecked values through verbatim: `labels: p.labels ?? []` (:205) only replaces null/undefined, so a string, number, or non-string-element array survives as a `GhItem.labels` that is not a `string[]`.
- Consumers dereference labels as a string array: `executionStrip` does `item.labels.some((l) => IMPLEMENTING_LABELS.has(l.toLowerCase()))` (src/derive.ts:48) and derive.ts:776 does `i.labels.some((l) => /blocked/i.test(l))`; `executionStrip` is called on the board and item-render paths (src/render.ts:1334 `stripHtml`, :1568 `renderItem`, which also does `i.labels.join(", ")` at :1573).

## Evidence (verified this run on main `5a34fa70`)

Laptop Bun probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-poolgate/` importing the real `src/projects.ts`, `src/program.ts`, and `src/derive.ts` (projects.ts md5 `55c76253fa2fced0858e115f97cc8155`, identical to main):

- Control: a well-formed pool item passes `isProjectPoolItem` and `executionStrip` returns it as queued (1).
- `labels: "blocked"` (string) → `isProjectPoolItem` returns **true**; `poolItemToGhItem` keeps the string; real `executionStrip` throws `TypeError: item.labels.some is not a function`.
- `labels: [42]` → gate returns **true**; real `executionStrip` throws `TypeError: l.toLowerCase is not a function`.
- An entry with `url`, `projectUrl`, and `contentKind` deleted entirely → gate still returns **true**; `poolItemToGhItem(...).kind` is `undefined` (broken badge/link rendering, silently).
- `updatedAt: 12345` (number) → gate returns **true** and the resulting `GhItem.updatedAt` is a number, despite the string contract every date consumer assumes.

## Why it matters

The pool is carried in the fleet feed — a file written by a separate collector on another host — and `isProjectPoolItem` is the single line of defence between that file and the dashboard's item resolution (`items()` feeds the board, roadmap, program, and item pages). The collector's own parser (projects.ts:130) carefully filters labels to strings, which shows the intended contract; the feed-side gate is the one that must enforce it when the feed is older, hand-edited, partially written, or produced by a different version. Today one bad entry does not degrade that entry — it throws inside shared render helpers and takes down every view that resolves that ref.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isProjectPoolItem` rejects an entry whose `labels` is present but not an array of strings (string/number/object labels, or an array containing non-string elements), and rejects entries missing the required string fields it currently skips (`url`, `projectUrl`, `contentKind` checked against its `GhKind` values).
- [ ] `status`/`area`/`horizon`/`kind` are checked as string-or-null and `updatedAt`/`author`, when present, as strings — or the triage explicitly pins a narrower set with the consumer that is safe for each unchecked field.
- [ ] A rejected entry is dropped by the live source's existing filter (other pool entries still resolve and render); it never reaches `poolItemToGhItem`/`executionStrip`.
- [ ] Regression tests (aggregator projects/live coverage) pin: `labels:"blocked"`, `labels:[42]`, and missing-`url` entries fail the gate; a well-formed entry (including one with `labels` absent) still passes unchanged.

## Dedup

- Searched open+closed issues for `isProjectPoolItem` and `ProjectPoolItem`: no hits. #2417 (OPEN) is the orchestration section gate's tier/goal elements — different file, different section; the derived-state helper in projects.ts only reads a pool item's `ref`/`status` there.
- #2376/#2408 (registry record gate) and #2347 (comments/actions load filter) are the same pattern in different modules with different fields and consumers.

body:
## Finding

`orchestrationSectionProblem` / `isOrchestrationSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts) check that the orchestration section's arrays *exist*, but never check the *elements* of `tiers.needsDrew` / `tiers.needsOrchestrator`, `goals[].linedUp`, or `goals[].stalled`. A section whose arrays contain `null`, a number, or an empty object passes the gate — the only gate on the live path (`normalizeOrchestrationSection`, feed.ts:200-201, used at sources/live.ts:661 and :911) — and then crashes the consumers that dereference the elements, instead of being diagnosed "invalid" and falling back to the derived view.

This is the element-level remainder of closed #949, which fixed the *presence* of the per-goal arrays (`isGoalMeasurement`, feed.ts:89-98, checks only `Array.isArray` on `linedUp`/`stalled`/`gaps`). Element shapes were never checked.

## Evidence (main 5a34fa70, verified this run)

- feed.ts:130-143 `orchestrationSectionProblem`: `tiers.needsDrew`/`needsOrchestrator`, `dependencies`, `actions` checked with `Array.isArray` only; `goals` checked with `s.goals.every(isGoalMeasurement)`, and `isGoalMeasurement` (feed.ts:89-98) checks only that `linedUp`/`stalled`/`gaps` are arrays — never their elements, and never the tier arrays' elements at all.
- derive.ts:299-305 `tierItemSessionId(item)` dereferences `item.sessionId`, then `item.id.startsWith(...)` — called on every tier element at derive.ts:412-419 (`buildAttention`) and again in the extras filter at :438.
- derive.ts:674 `g.linedUp.filter((t) => t.horizon === "today")` and derive.ts:693 `g.stalled.filter((s) => s.blocker)` in `todayFromSection` dereference every goal element.
- Laptop Bun probe (~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-orch-elements/, real feed.ts/derive.ts from a fresh clone at 5a34fa70; control section passes and renders fine):
  - `goals: [{...valid, linedUp: [null]}]` → validator `true`, `todayFromSection` throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 't.horizon')`
  - `goals: [{...valid, stalled: [null]}]` → validator `true`, throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 's.blocker')`
  - `tiers.needsDrew: [null]` → validator `true`, `buildAttention` throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'item.sessionId')`
  - `tiers.needsDrew: [42]` and `[{}]` → validator `true`, `buildAttention` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'item.id.startsWith')`

## Why it matters

The orchestration section is produced by an LLM-run job writing JSON by hand — exactly the producer the gate exists to fail-soft against (#949's rationale). One malformed element in a tier list or a goal's lined-up/stalled list currently takes down the attention/today derivation for the whole feed instead of the section being diagnosed invalid (feed.ts's `diagnoseOrchestrationSection` machinery already exists to surface exactly this) and the aggregator falling back to its locally derived view.

## Acceptance criteria

- A section whose `tiers.needsDrew`/`needsOrchestrator` contains a non-object element (or one without a string `id`), or whose `goals[].linedUp`/`goals[].stalled` contains a non-object element, no longer crashes `buildAttention` or `todayFromSection`; the owning layer is pinned (gate rejects the section as invalid vs consumers skip bad elements) and applied consistently to both tier arrays and both goal arrays.
- A poisoned section is treated as invalid/absent with the existing diagnosis wording instead of throwing on the live read path.
- Regression tests cover at least: tier element `null`, tier element `42`/`{}`, goal `linedUp: [null]`, goal `stalled: [null]`; a well-formed section (existing orchestration fixtures/tests) still derives unchanged.
- Triage records a ruling on the adjacent unchecked surfaces in the same gate: `actions` elements (sliced at derive.ts:709, rendered by field in render.ts) and `dependencies` elements — validate, tolerate, or explicitly leave with a reason.

Dedup: #949 (closed) covered missing per-goal arrays and missing provenance — presence, not element shapes; searches for "orchestration validator / tierItem null / isGoalMeasurement elements" returned only #949/#1110/#898, none covering element-level validation. The dns/aa/quota-current gate issues (#2412/#2415/#2416) are different files and fields.

body:
## Problem

`parseQuotaCurrent` never checks the entries inside a provider's `windows` array, so one malformed entry crashes the whole Stage-2 quota overlay — and the live source's fail-soft catch then silently drops the gatherer data for **every** pool while its provenance still claims the gatherer was applied.

- `parseQuotaCurrent` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-current.ts:49-62) is the structural check for the gatherer's quota-current.json. For each provider it checks id/state/measuredAt/source types and that `windows` is an array (:60) — it never checks that the array's entries are objects.
- `pctWindows` (quota-current.ts:85-97) dereferences every entry in its filter: `typeof w.pctOfLimit === "number"` (:87). A `null` entry throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'w.pctOfLimit')`. A string entry survives the filter (its `pctOfLimit` is undefined), but an entry with a numeric `pctOfLimit` and a non-string `name` or a non-string `resetsAt` passes both layers verbatim into the pool's windows.
- The live caller (src/sources/live.ts:775-782) appends `· gatherer <generatedAt>` to `provenance.quota` **before** calling `overlayQuotaCurrent`, inside a try/catch whose catch is commented "base view stands". When the overlay throws, the base view is indeed served — but with provenance claiming the gatherer overlay was applied, and with the fresh reads of every other, well-formed provider discarded too: one null in one provider's windows disables the whole overlay.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `5a34fa70`)

Sandbox Bun probe importing the real `quota-current.ts` (probe at /tmp/probe-laneB-aa/probe2.ts):

- A v1 doc whose single provider has `windows:[null]`, state `ok`, fresh `measuredAt` → `parseQuotaCurrent` returns non-null; `overlayQuotaCurrent` on a matching pool throws `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'w.pctOfLimit')`.
- A window `{name: 42, pctOfLimit: 50, resetsAt: {bad: true}}` → passes `parseQuotaCurrent`; the overlay emits a pool window with `name: 42` and `resetsAt: {bad: true}` verbatim.
- Control (from the module's own tests/semantics): well-formed windows overlay normally — the defect is only the missing entry-level gate.

## Why it matters

quota-current.json is rewritten every 15 minutes by a gatherer on another host; the parser is the trust boundary for that file, exactly like the feed section gates. Today a single corrupt entry produces the worst of both worlds: all fresh gatherer data is silently lost (pools fall back to dated reads with no signal anything is wrong) while the page's provenance asserts the gatherer was applied. Per-entry validation — drop or reject only the bad entry/provider — keeps one provider's corruption from taking the other providers' fresh reads down with it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parseQuotaCurrent` (or `pctWindows`) validates window entries: non-object entries (including `null`) can never reach the `pctOfLimit` dereference; a bad entry is dropped or its provider rejected, without discarding other providers' entries.
- [ ] Window `name` and `resetsAt` are type-checked before they can enter a pool's windows (string name; string-or-null `resetsAt`), matching the `QuotaCurrentWindow` contract in model.ts.
- [ ] The live quota path's provenance only claims the gatherer overlay when it was actually applied (or the overlay can no longer throw on gate-passing input — either pin is acceptable, triage decides).
- [ ] Regression tests pin: `windows:[null]` does not throw and the remaining providers still overlay; a numeric-`name`/object-`resetsAt` window is refused or normalized; well-formed files overlay unchanged.

## Dedup

- #2253 (OPEN) is the stale-path newest-pick `measuredAt` finite gate in the same file — different field, different failure.
- #2332 (OPEN) is the producer side (`entryFromResult` throwing on `fetchedAt`) in quota-gather-map.ts — this is the reader/parser side.
- #1541 (CLOSED) was the future-`measuredAt` freshness bound, already fixed and present at quota-current.ts:70-74.
- Searches for `parseQuotaCurrent` / "quota-current windows" over open+closed issues returned no match for window-entry validation.

body:
# aggregator(dns): isDnsSection never checks totalAnnualListUsd or entry priceUsd — a feed section that passes validation crashes /dns and the usage view on .toFixed

## Summary

`isDnsSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/dns.ts:73-88) is the structural gate for the DNS register section in the fleet feed: `sources/live.ts` only serves `feed.dns` (live.ts:946-950, `dns()`) and only builds the usage view's `domains` block from it (live.ts:800-807) when this check passes. The check validates only `generatedAt` (string), a non-empty `entries` array, and each entry's `domain`/`renewal` strings. It never checks:

- `totalAnnualListUsd` — declared `number` in the model (model.ts:650), and
- each entry's `priceUsd` — used as a number everywhere it renders.

Both unchecked values are dereferenced with `.toFixed(2)` on live render paths, so a feed section that passes validation crashes rendering instead of being rejected as invalid:

- `renderDns`: `section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed(2)` (render.ts:2537), `next.priceUsd.toFixed(2)` (render.ts:2541), and `dnsTable`'s `e.priceUsd.toFixed(2)` (render.ts:2515).
- Usage view: live.ts:803 copies `feed.dns.totalAnnualListUsd` verbatim into `domains.totalAnnualUsd`, which render.ts:1813 formats with `.toFixed(2)`.

The `/dns` route (server.ts:526-528) awaits `source.dns()` and calls `renderDns` with no try/catch, and `Bun.serve` is configured with no `error` handler (server.ts:809-815), so the throw surfaces as a 500 for the whole page — permanently, on every request, for as long as the poisoned section stays in the feed. The same poisoned section also breaks the usage page that embeds the domains card.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 5a34fa70)

Probe: laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneA-dnsvalidator/probe.ts` (Bun 1.4.2), importing the real `dns.ts` and `render.ts` from the laptop clone — both files md5-identical to sandbox main 5a34fa70 (`dns.ts` b5829b32b50a5a0b7484a05123c94790, `render.ts` ab6a7524f90bf11d80b71fd0c6a0b756). A minimal provenance stub is the only stand-in.

- Control: a well-formed section (`totalAnnualListUsd: 11.08`, entry `priceUsd: 11.08`) — `isDnsSection` true, `renderDns` OK (19,979 chars).
- `totalAnnualListUsd` **missing** — `isDnsSection` **true**; `renderDns` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed')`.
- `totalAnnualListUsd: "11.08"` (string) — `isDnsSection` **true**; `renderDns` throws `TypeError: section.totalAnnualListUsd.toFixed is not a function`.
- `totalAnnualListUsd: null` — `isDnsSection` **true**; `renderDns` throws the same TypeError on null.
- Entry `priceUsd: "11.08"` (string, valid total) — `isDnsSection` **true**; `renderDns` throws `TypeError: next.priceUsd.toFixed is not a function`.
- Usage path with the missing-total section: `domains.totalAnnualUsd.toFixed(2)` throws the identical TypeError.

The producer in this repo always builds a numeric total (`dnsSectionFromRegister`, dns.ts:64-69 sums `priceUsd ?? 0`), so this is a validator/render contract gap, not a claim that the current collector emits bad values: the feed is a file boundary shared with the collector, older feeds, and hand/backfill tooling, and `isDnsSection` is documented (dns.ts:72) as "the structural check shared by the collector and the live source" — the one place that is supposed to keep a malformed section out of the renderers. Sibling validators in this codebase were hardened for exactly this shape (e.g. #2376/#2408 registry, #2347 comments/actions); the DNS gate was not.

Secondary, same gate: entry `status` is also unchecked — an entry with a missing/unknown status is counted in the register total and the full table but silently appears in none of `summarizeDns`'s active/earmarked/unused buckets (dns.ts:99-110), so the "Portfolio shape" counts on /dns under-count without any crash. Triage may fold this into the same fix or split it; the crash is the primary defect.

## Why it matters

/dns is the fleet's domain-spend register page and the usage hub embeds its total. One malformed feed section — a renamed/retyped field from a collector change, a hand-edited feed, a partial backfill — takes both pages down with a 500 on every hit instead of the section being treated as absent/invalid (the honest states the rest of the aggregator already implements for other sections). The validator exists precisely to draw that line; today it certifies records the renderers cannot render.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isDnsSection` rejects a section whose `totalAnnualListUsd` is not a finite number, and rejects an entry whose `priceUsd` is present but not a finite number (or, equivalently, the renderers never call `.toFixed` on a value the validator has not guaranteed numeric — the owning layer is triage's pin, applied consistently to `dns()`, the usage `domains` block, and `/api/dns.json` consumers).
- A poisoned section in the feed no longer 500s /dns or the usage page: it is treated as absent/invalid with the existing provenance wording, while `/api/dns.json` keeps serving the absent form.
- Regression tests: sections with missing, string, and null `totalAnnualListUsd`, and an entry with a string `priceUsd`, each fail the gate (or render safely, per the pinned rule); the well-formed fixture section (slice3.test.ts) still renders unchanged, including its totals.
- Triage rules on the secondary `status` gap (validate it in the same gate, coerce unknown to `unused`, or explicitly leave it) and records the ruling on this issue.
- No change to the on-disk feed format or to `dnsSectionFromRegister` output for valid registers.

## Notes

- Not self-solved by the creator lane: whether the numeric rule belongs in the validator or the renderers (and whether a non-finite total should reject the whole section or just the domains card) is a small contract decision for triage, and this gate is shared by the collector and the live source.
- Related, different defect: #2242 (health.ts age computation never validates dns/aa `generatedAt` stamps — NaN/future ages, no crash, different file and field). This issue is the dns.ts gate itself and the render-time `.toFixed` crashes.

title: bin proxies: per-key serialization chain maps never delete settled entries — claude-code (chains), muse (warmChains) and commandcode (acp.locks) leak one entry per conversation, and per request on the anon/ephemeral paths

body:
## Problem

Three of the fleet's warm proxies serialize turns per conversation key with a promise-chain `Map` that is **written on every request and never deleted from** — not when the chain settles, not on session eviction, not ever. The fourth proxy in the same directory implements the same pattern correctly, which makes the omission visible:

**The correct in-tree pattern** — `bin/agy-proxy.mjs:756-763`:

```js
const chains = new Map();
const enqueue = (key, job) => {
  const prev = chains.get(key) || Promise.resolve();
  const run = prev.then(job, job);
  const stored = run.catch(() => {});
  chains.set(key, stored);
  stored.then(() => { if (chains.get(key) === stored) chains.delete(key); }); // <-- self-cleanup
  return run;
};
```

**The three leaking sites:**

1. `bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs:489-494` — `chains`: `chains.set(key, run.catch(() => {}))` and no `chains.delete` anywhere in the file. Worse, the request handler mints a **brand-new key for every keyless request** (`const key = getSessionKey(req, body) || \`anon:${crypto.randomUUID()}\``, :733), so growth is per-request, not per-conversation, for that traffic.
2. `bin/muse-proxy.mjs:656-662` — `warmChains`: same shape (`warmChains.set(key, run.catch(() => {}))`, no delete). Keys are `conversationKey()` hashes (system prompt + first user message, :337-344), so every distinct conversation ever served leaves a permanent entry.
3. `bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs` — `acp.locks` (declared :537; set in `runChat`, :770-777): `this.locks.set(lockKey, run.catch(() => {}))`, no `locks.delete` anywhere. Sessionless calls use `ephemeral: !sessionKey` (:1167), and `runChat` turns those into `` `ephemeral:${crypto.randomUUID()}` `` (:770) — again a guaranteed-never-reused key per request.

These proxies are long-lived systemd services, so the maps grow monotonically for the whole process lifetime: one retained settled promise + key string per distinct conversation — and per *request* on the anon/ephemeral paths. Nothing else bounds them: `claude-code-proxy` caps live sessions at 32 and sweeps idle sessions (`evictIfNeeded`), and `commandcode`/`muse` have their own session TTLs, but none of those touch the chain maps.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `5a34fa70`)

Files are md5-identical on sandbox main and the laptop (`bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs` `7280c4bb…`, `bin/muse-proxy.mjs` `2f87df2e…`, `bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs` `a5223632…`, `bin/agy-proxy.mjs` `988ab4c0…`).

Deletion-site census over each whole file: `claude-code-proxy` `chains.set` ×1 / `chains.delete` ×0; `muse-proxy` `warmChains.set` ×1 / `warmChains.delete` ×0; `commandcode-proxy` `locks.set` ×1 / `locks.delete` ×0; `agy-proxy` (control) `chains.set` ×1 / `chains.delete` ×1.

Laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-laneB-chainleak/probe.mjs`) extracted the **verbatim** `chains`/`enqueue`, `warmChains`/`enqueueWarm`, and agy `chains`/`enqueue` code from the real files, ran 50 distinct keys with instantly-settling jobs through each, and let cleanup callbacks run:

```
after 50 distinct keys, all jobs settled:
  claude-code chains.size = 50
  muse warmChains.size    = 50
  agy chains.size (control, self-deleting) = 0
  same-key order sanity: 1,2 ; chains.size now 51
```

Serialization itself works (same-key jobs run in order) — the entries simply never leave.

## Why it matters

A slow, unbounded memory leak in always-on infrastructure: the proxies run for weeks between restarts, and the busiest key spaces (anon/ephemeral, one entry per request) are exactly the ones that can never be reused. Each entry is small, so this will never page anyone — it is the kind of leak that surfaces months later as a proxy holding far more RSS than its session caps suggest, with the cause invisible in the session/TTL accounting that does exist. The fix pattern already exists in-tree (agy) and is three lines per file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All three chain maps remove a key's entry once its chain settles and no newer job has replaced it (the agy pattern: capture the stored promise, `stored.then(() => { if (map.get(key) === stored) map.delete(key); })`), at: `bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs` (`chains`), `bin/muse-proxy.mjs` (`warmChains`), `bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs` (`acp.locks` in `runChat`).
- [ ] Serialization semantics are unchanged: two jobs enqueued back-to-back on the same key still run in order and never concurrently, including when a second job is enqueued while the first is still in flight (the delete must only fire for the latest stored promise).
- [ ] A regression test per proxy (the existing `*.test.mjs` files sit beside each proxy) drives ≥2 distinct keys through the enqueue helper and asserts the map is empty after all jobs settle, plus a same-key ordering assertion.
- [ ] Out of scope: session-store persistence/TTL behaviour (`sessions.json`, warm store) — bounded separately and unchanged; agy-proxy itself (already correct, it is the reference pattern).

title: id(directory_mail): OutboxSink writes To/Subject into the .eml header block with none of SmtpSink's validation — a newline in either forges arbitrary headers

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
