body: ## Finding The dashboard comments flow stores a caller-supplied `githubUrl` with no validation and later renders it as a link `href`. HTML escaping prevents attribute breakout but not dangerous schemes: a stored `javascript:` or `data:` URL becomes a clickable script link in the dashboard. ## Evidence (PR #920, merge `12620917dd5f`, current main `a2eef6f7920a`) - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:150-156`: `POST /api/comments/github-result` accepts `url: typeof body.url === "string" ? body.url : undefined` — any string, no pattern check. - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts:173-179`: `CommentsStore.markGithubResult` stores it verbatim (`c.githubUrl = result.url`); no validation exists anywhere in `comments.ts`. - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts:231`: renders `view`. `esc()` escapes `&<>"'` (attribute breakout is blocked) but passes a `javascript:` scheme through unchanged. ## Why it matters The comments API is unauthenticated by design (loopback + tailnet trust model, per the `comments.ts` header comment), so anything that can POST to it — a compromised tailnet peer, a stray script, another agent run — can plant a script-scheme link in a dashboard the maintainer clicks during triage. Low severity because of that trust model and because the click is required, but the fix is one allowlist check at the single write path. ## Acceptance criteria - `markGithubResult` (or the endpoint) rejects any `url` not matching `^https://github\.com/`. - A test posts a `javascript:` URL to the github-result flow and asserts rejection (no stored `githubUrl`). - The existing flow — a real `https://github.com/…` result URL is recorded and rendered as the "view" link — still works. Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #920 against current main. Dedupe: searches for `githubUrl` / `github-result URL validation` / `dashboard comment href javascript` returned no existing issue (only the closed parent implementation issue #906).

title: id(world): PR #927's oversized-layout fallback never checks its own result against presentation_bytes (#811)

body:
## Finding

Open PR #927 (Jules, for #811) fixes the oversized-`layout()` poison path by falling back to `program.view()` cropped to the requested size — but **the fallback result is never checked against `presentation_bytes`**, the very limit the branch exists to enforce. A world whose default view is also large (or not a screen) gets an over-limit presentation delivered as success.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #927, 2026-10-25. PR #927 is still open, so this can be folded into it or fixed immediately after it lands; the code quoted is from the PR head (`4d33369c`), `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs`, `WorldCommand::ViewAt` handler.

## Evidence

- The layout branch triggers only when `text.len() > self.core.limits.presentation_bytes` (default 8192, `pkgs/id/src/world/mod.rs:91`), increments `view_failures`, and falls back.
- Fallback, non-screen case: `Ok(Some(fallback_text))` is returned for any `program.view()` text that `parse_surface` doesn't recognize as a screen — with no length check at all. A guest whose `view()` returns a >8192-byte non-screen presentation sails through.
- Fallback, screen case: the surface is cropped with `surface.fit(width, height)` and re-serialized, but the serialized result is never compared to `presentation_bytes`. Screens may be up to `MAX_SCREEN_WIDTH`×`MAX_SCREEN_HEIGHT` = 120×50 = 6000 cells (`pkgs/id/src/world_presentation.rs:15-19`), each cell a JSON object — a dense cropped screen is far over 8192 bytes. On serialization failure the code does `unwrap_or(fallback_text)`, returning the *original unchecked* text.
- The PR's own test (`an_oversized_layout_degrades_to_a_view_fallback_and_recovers`, `pkgs/id/src/world/tests.rs`) covers only a tiny 10×10 fallback view, so none of these cases is exercised.
- Related bound disagreement in the same PR: the `ClientFrame::Resize` handler in `pkgs/id/src/world_session/mod.rs` first validates `width`/`height` against 500×200 (error text: "viewport dimensions must be width 1..=500 and height 1..=200"), then silently clamps the stored viewport to `MAX_SCREEN_WIDTH`/`MAX_SCREEN_HEIGHT` = 120/50. A client that resizes to, say, 300×100 is told that size is legal but is actually served a 120×50 view. Which bound is meant to govern — and whether silently shrinking a legal resize is the intended #811 mitigation — deserves an explicit verdict in the same triage.

## Why it matters

#811 is about a guest presentation exceeding the byte limit breaking the world. A fallback that can itself exceed the limit reintroduces the over-limit delivery on the exact path meant to prevent it — consumers sized for `presentation_bytes` (SSH/web surfaces) receive unbounded presentations, and the failure mode moves somewhere harder to diagnose.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The ViewAt fallback result (cropped screen serialization, non-screen text, and the serialization-failure path) is checked against `presentation_bytes` before being returned; an over-limit fallback degrades to an error (counted like other view failures) instead of an over-limit success.
- [ ] A regression test with a fallback view that is itself over the limit (dense screen and/or non-screen text) proves the world still does not deliver it and does not poison.
- [ ] The Resize bound disagreement (validation allows 500×200, the stored viewport is silently clamped to 120×50) is resolved — one governing bound, and the error text matches it — or documented as intentional.

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PR #927, relating to #811); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.

title: Laptop (amd): proxy systemd units churn with EADDRINUSE while unmanaged copies serve the ports

body:
Observed 2026-10-25 on amd (NixOS, user session) by Muse over SSH.

## Symptom
`systemctl --user is-active` for the five proxy units reports nonsense states: clef/codex/antigravity-ls/design-code stuck at `activating`, agy-proxy `inactive` — while all five ports (18742-18746) answer /health OK. Drew reports 'lots of crashes and restarts today', but the machine has NOT rebooted (up 14 days, boot Oct 11). Load average sits at ~2.7.

## Evidence
- Journal, Oct 25 16:54:39: `clef-proxy-start` crashed with EADDRINUSE on 127.0.0.1:18742; at the same second systemd logged 'Main process exited, status=1/FAILURE' for antigravity-ls-proxy, codex-proxy, clef-proxy and design-code-proxy.
- `systemctl --user show agy-proxy.service`: ActiveState=inactive, SubState=dead, Result=success, NRestarts=0 — the unit is cleanly stopped, yet 18743 serves health. So the processes actually listening are NOT the units' processes.
- On Oct 21 the listening proxies were a batch of node MainThread processes unrelated to the units' lifecycle (started ~Oct 20), consistent with the warmer/keepalive stack (cf. the wt-warm-* worktrees) spawning its own copies.

## Hypothesis
Two supervisors own the same ports: the home-manager systemd user units AND the warmer scripts. The warm copies bind first; unit instances die with EADDRINUSE and cycle through activating/failed, producing the crash/restart churn and the misleading unit states. (Related earlier signal: sync-models.service was in failed state on Oct 21.)

## Investigate
1. Map listeners to owners: `ss -tlnp` PIDs vs each unit's MainPID for 18742-18746.
2. Find what starts the unmanaged copies (warmer units/scripts, OpenChamber supervisor?) and when (login, boot, respawn loop?).
3. Decide a single owner per proxy (units OR warmers) and remove/align the other; check whether the warmers exist because the units were unreliable (e.g. the agy DISABLED marking) — fix the cause, not just the duplication.
4. Confirm agy-proxy's intended state (it was marked DISABLED in config, is currently served by a warm copy, and Drew asked for agy working on Oct 21).

Filed from the laptop remote-access thread; the remote-access tracking goal has the surrounding context.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every listener on ports 18742-18746 is mapped to its owning process and supervisor (systemd user unit, warmer script, or other), with the evidence recorded on this issue.
- [ ] Exactly one owner per proxy port remains: the duplicate supervisor is removed or aligned, and the systemd user units' reported states match reality (`is-active` agrees with what serves the port).
- [ ] No EADDRINUSE churn in the user journal for the five proxy units over a full day after the fix.
- [ ] agy-proxy's intended state is confirmed and matches what is actually running.

body:
## Finding (from pr-diff-review of PR #875, merged; merge commit 74b849b889, current main a365373511)

PR #875 added `bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs` + its test — and nothing else (2 files). The bridge's in-repo landing is incomplete compared with every sibling fleet proxy, and the repo config it was built for still cannot use it.

### Evidence (all verified on current main `a365373511`)

1. **The provider it serves is still unwired in the repo config — and it is the default model.** `.opencode/opencode.jsonc:28` sets `"default": "claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5"` and four agent entries reference `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5`, but the `claude-code` provider block (`.opencode/opencode.jsonc:30`) contains only `models` — no `npm`/`package`, no `options.baseURL`. PR #875's own body states this models-only shape is what "hangs with `UnsupportedPackageError`". Sibling pattern for comparison: the `commandcode` block at `.opencode/opencode.jsonc:4258` has `"npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"` and `"baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:{env:COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT:-18748}/v1"`.
2. **No start script.** Siblings ship `bin/commandcode-proxy-start.sh` / `bin/muse-proxy-start.sh`; there is no `bin/claude-code-proxy-start.sh`.
3. **No home-manager unit.** `home/common/default.nix` defines `systemd.user.services.commandcode-proxy` (ExecStart at the bin start script, ~line 758) and port bindings for clef/agy/codex/antigravity-ls/design-code/muse/commandcode — there is no `claude-code-proxy` unit.
4. **No port registration.** `home/common/default.nix` defines the `*ProxyPort` lets and exports `CLEF_PROXY_PORT`/`AGY_PROXY_PORT`/`CODEX_PROXY_PORT`/`ANTIGRAVITY_LS_PROXY_PORT`/`DESIGN_CODE_PROXY_PORT`/`COMMANDCODE_PROXY_PORT` session variables; there is no `claudeCodeProxyPort` / `CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT` (the proxy itself defaults to 18749 via `parseProxyPort('CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT', 18749)`).

Per PR #875's body, the working deployment exists only as sandbox-local state (`~/tools/claude-code-proxy/` + a systemd unit + an init.sh step) — the same deployed-first pattern as the cline-pass rename, which then needed PR #887 to propagate into the repo source. Nothing currently tracks doing the same propagation for this bridge, so a fresh checkout / another machine gets a default model that hangs.

Related but distinct: #883 (stale bin/ tree in the home-layer eval) covers the store copy missing `claude-code-proxy.*`; this issue is about the repo-side wiring/unit/port pieces that do not exist at all yet.

### Acceptance criteria

- `.opencode/opencode.jsonc`: the `claude-code` provider block gains the sibling wiring — `"npm": "@ai-sdk/openai-compatible"` and `options.baseURL` of the form `http://127.0.0.1:{env:CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT:-18749}/v1` (env-placeholder form, so the literal-port guard from #866/#867 keeps passing) — and the file still parses as JSONC.
- `bin/claude-code-proxy-start.sh` exists, mirroring `bin/commandcode-proxy-start.sh`'s env handling.
- `home/common/default.nix`: a `claudeCodeProxyPort` (18749) with its `CLAUDE_CODE_PROXY_PORT` session variable, any proxy-port guard table updated, and a `systemd.user.services.claude-code-proxy` unit mirroring `commandcode-proxy`.
- A session started from the repo config on a machine with only repo-deployed state (no hand-placed `~/tools` copies) can run the default model `claude-code/claude-haiku-5-5` through the bridge without `UnsupportedPackageError`.

body:
`WorldCommand::Input` carries a capability token, not a session (`pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs`, around the `Input` arm). So the actor cannot tell which connection caused a change. F13.7 client providers need to route a request to the originating participant's own session. F13.8 multi-world, multi-client sessions probably need the same identity. This is a small prerequisite that no plan names yet.

Proposed: carry an opaque per-connection session id with input-derived commands, never journaled (ephemeral per the shell contract, #783).

Found while writing the F13.7 design (#789). Refs #790 (F13.8).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `WorldCommand::Input` (and any input-derived command) carries an opaque per-connection session id, so the actor can attribute a change to the connection that caused it
- [ ] The session id is never journaled (ephemeral, per the shell contract in #783)
- [ ] A test or probe shows two connections' inputs are distinguishable by the actor
- [ ] F13.7 routing (#789) and F13.8 (#790) can consume the id without a further protocol change

body:
`CapLedger::new` sets `allowed` to `catalog_names()`, so every catalog capability is allowed until a ceiling narrows the set (`pkgs/id/src/world_caps.rs:494-504`). A checkpoint also omits a ceiling that equals the full catalog. Once F12.4 makes the catalog data, a newly registered provider silently joins the ceiling of every world that has no explicit ceiling. It also joins the server ceiling when `--world-allowed-caps` is unset. That widens authority by binary upgrade, against the Phase 12 rule that authority comes only through named, ceilinged providers.

F12.4's manifest needs a per-provider default ceiling with an "excluded" value before any sensitive provider is registered, host or client (F12.5 `http.fetch`, F13.7 client providers). This relates to the "`*`-free default ceiling" follow-up in `doc/2026-10-16T11-00-00Z_feature_world_capability_ceilings/`.

Found while writing the F13.7 design (#789). Refs #534 (F12.4).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A newly registered catalog provider does NOT join the default ceiling of existing worlds or of a server started without `--world-allowed-caps`, unless its manifest default explicitly allows it
- [ ] The F12.4 manifest supports a per-provider default ceiling including an "excluded" value
- [ ] A test registers a new provider and asserts existing worlds' ceilings are unchanged

## Finding

Renovate PR #828 ("chore(deps): update p2panda-auth digest to da80c05", commit be049993) bumps exactly one p2panda crate in `doc/2026-10-11T03-44-33Z_design_groups_events_delegation/spikes/shared/Cargo.toml`:

- `p2panda-auth`: rev `3e84cac48bba05c6857cce2ec433862b97f8d53c` → `da80c05b95269926bf58121cf6a2d3dd5ca41dfc`

In the same `[workspace.dependencies]` table, verified on current main (`d95000a1`), five sibling crates from the same upstream repo stay on the old rev: `p2panda-core`, `p2panda-encryption`, `p2panda-sync`, `p2panda-store`, `p2panda-stream` — all still `3e84cac`.

## Why it matters

- The repo's own `renovate.json` has a package rule for exactly this: "The p2panda crates are git deps pinned to one shared upstream rev and must move together; per-crate PRs break the pkgs/id Nix build (#643)", `groupName: "p2panda"`, `matchPackageNames: ["/^p2panda-/"]`. Issue #643 (closed) was filed because a split bump broke the build; PR #828 shows the grouping still produces a per-crate PR for this manifest.
- The real code already moved as a set: `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` pins every p2panda dep at `da80c05` (core L59, store L61, auth L67, plus the vendored crates). The spike workspace is now skewed both internally and against the real code.
- `p2panda-auth@da80c05` itself depends on `p2panda-core@da80c05` upstream, so building the spike pulls two revs of `p2panda-core` whose types are not interchangeable.
- CI on #828 is green (run / treefmt / Nix flake evaluation pass) because the doc spike is not built by those checks — the skew is invisible to CI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One grouped change moves all six `p2panda-*` revs in `spikes/shared/Cargo.toml` to the same rev (or #828 is closed and doc/ spikes are explicitly excluded from Renovate's cargo manager, with the reason recorded)
- [ ] `grep` of that file shows a single shared p2panda rev
- [ ] The spike workspace still resolves/builds (`cargo check` in `spikes/shared`), or its non-building status is documented as pre-existing

body:
## Finding

P9.4 promises "tested Roc JSON parse/encode primitives", and the checked-in Roc modules carry `expect` blocks, but nothing executes them: there is no `roc test` anywhere in CI, `flake.nix`, or the `justfile`. The Roc library tests therefore pass silently only when the `roc` compiler and the built host are present, and are skipped otherwise.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/RocJson.roc` has 29 `expect` blocks; `Screen.roc` 15; `Key.roc` 13. `RocGrid`, `RocCap`, `RocText` have none.
- No `roc test` invocation exists in `flake.nix`, `pkgs/id/justfile`, or `.github/workflows/` (grep finds none).
- `pkgs/id/src/world_compile.rs:819-827`: the Roc tests print `skipping:` and pass when `roc` or `targets/wasm32/host.wasm` is missing. Nix builds the host (`flake.nix:620`), plain `cargo test` does not.

## Why it matters

The claim that the Roc libraries are "tested" is not enforced by any gate, so a regression in `RocJson`, `Screen`, or `Key` (the foundation of portable apps) would go unnoticed in both plain `cargo test` and CI.

## Suggested fix

- Add a `roc-test` check to `flake.nix` (and a matching `just roc-test` recipe, per AGENTS.md: justfile and Nix stay in step) that runs `roc test` on each module using the pinned `nix/roc.nix` compiler.
- The check proves itself: it fails if any `expect` is false, and it should be added to the `id` CI checks so the skip path cannot silently pass.

## Related

#541 (pin the Roc compiler and rebuild examples in CI — different scope: build/behavior, not running the in-module `expect` blocks).

## Acceptance criteria

- A `roc test` invocation for the `pkgs/id` Roc library modules (at minimum `RocJson.roc`, `Screen.roc`, `Key.roc`) runs in CI or the Nix check, so the checked-in `expect` blocks (29 + 15 + 13) actually execute.
- The test run fails the job when an `expect` fails (no silent skip when the `roc` compiler / built host is present).
- When `roc` is unavailable the skip is explicit and visible in job output, not silent.
- Existing checks (`nix flake check` / `just check`) stay green.

title: tracing 0.1.37 (GHSA-8f24-6m29-wm2r affected range) still pinned in web-gen-api and pavex realworld locks after PR #625 fixed web-gen

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched

body:
## Finding

PR #625 (merged, head `a41899b584059305c52818129715c959a40f5316`) fixed the tracing use-after-free advisory GHSA-8f24-6m29-wm2r for exactly one lockfile (`pkgs/web-gen`, 0.1.40 → 0.1.41). Two other lockfiles in `pkgs/` still pin **tracing 0.1.37**, which is inside the advisory's affected range, and no open PR or issue covers them.

## Evidence

- PR #625's own advisory text: the `Instrumented::into_inner` unsoundness "was corrected … The fix is published in `tracing` v0.1.40. Affected versions have been yanked from crates.io." So every pin below 0.1.40 is an affected, yanked version.
- Current main (`origin/main` ebb99893), verified two independent ways (`git grep` over origin/main and `gh api` contents reads, both agree):
  - `pkgs/web-gen-api/Cargo.lock` — `name = "tracing"`, `version = "0.1.37"`
  - `pkgs/pavex/examples/realworld/Cargo.lock` — `name = "tracing"`, `version = "0.1.37"`
- Checked and NOT affected: `pkgs/web-gen/Cargo.lock` 0.1.41 (after #625), `pkgs/dht/Cargo.lock` 0.1.41, `pkgs/roc/platforms/rust-minimal-cli/Cargo.lock` 0.1.41, `pkgs/pavex/examples/skeleton/Cargo.lock` 0.1.40 (first fixed version), `pkgs/id` / `pkgs/pavex/libs` 0.1.44.
- Exposure note (kept honest): no call to `tracing::Instrumented::into_inner` was found in either crate (the one `into_inner()` hit in `pkgs/web-gen-api/src/main.rs:53` is leptos options, not tracing), and tracing is a transitive dependency in both. The risk is latent — a yanked, advisory-listed version stays in the tree and any future `instrument` use inherits the unsound path — which is exactly why the [SECURITY] bump was applied to web-gen.

## Why it matters

A security fix that lands in one of three same-advisory lockfiles leaves the repo looking patched while two crates still resolve the yanked version. Renovate filed #625 per-lockfile, so the remainder will not necessarily ever be filed; this issue is the tracker for the rest of the set.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pkgs/web-gen-api/Cargo.lock` and `pkgs/pavex/examples/realworld/Cargo.lock` resolve tracing to >= 0.1.40 (regenerate the locks or bump the transitive constraint), OR a documented exception explains why a pin must stay.
- [ ] A final sweep of `pkgs/**/Cargo.lock` shows no remaining `tracing` version below 0.1.40.
- [ ] If either crate cannot build against the newer tracing, that failure is recorded here instead of silently leaving the pin.

title: lab-ops-hub: container crawler's 20s timeout is per-socket-read, not a deadline — a slow-drip target hangs the single-threaded crawler indefinitely

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/lab-ops-hub
labels.description: Package/app: lab-ops-hub (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Problem

The Lab Ops Hub container crawler's 20-second timeout is a **per-socket-operation** timeout, not a deadline — a slow-drip target defeats it indefinitely, unlike the Worker fallback's absolute 20s deadline. Worse, the container serves requests on a single thread, so one dripping crawl wedges the whole crawler service.

Evidence on current main (a8a3bf7e):

- `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/container/app.py:363-364` — `with _OPENER.open(req, timeout=20) as res: raw = res.read(2_000_000)`. In Python's `urllib`, `timeout` bounds each blocking socket operation (connect, each `read`), not the request as a whole. A server that sends one byte every <20s keeps every individual read inside the timeout while the total crawl runs unbounded — up to 2,000,000 drips before the byte cap is reached.
- `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/container/app.py` (last line) — `HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", 8080), Handler).serve_forever()` is the plain single-threaded server: while one `/crawl` handler is stuck in the drip read, every other request (including the `GET /` health check) queues behind it.
- The Worker fallback does not have this hole: `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/lib.ts:248-256` (`crawlFetcher`, #500/#524) attaches `AbortSignal.timeout(20_000)` to the fetch, and the signal stays attached to the response, so the header wait **and** the `readResponseTextCapped` body read share one absolute 20s deadline per hop.
- #500's issue body cites the container's `timeout=20` as the model the Worker fix followed — but the two 20s values have different semantics, so the container path never actually had the guarantee #500 attributed to it.

## Reproduction (verified this run)

Local drip server (headers, then 1 byte/second) read with exactly the container's call shape but `timeout=3`:

```python
with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=3) as res:
    raw = res.read(2_000_000)
```

The read **completed after ~15s** (15 bytes at 1 byte/s) despite the 3s timeout — each individual socket read finished within 3s, so no timeout ever fired. With the production `timeout=20` and a 19s drip interval, a crawl could in principle run for months of wall-clock time; in practice it runs until something external kills it, blocking the single-threaded server the whole time.

## Why it matters

`POST /api/crawl` targets are caller-supplied public URLs (validated, but a validated public server can still be slow or malicious). One drip crawl:
- holds the container's only request thread indefinitely — the health endpoint and all later crawls stall;
- defeats the `sleepAfter=2m` idle-kill economics the README relies on (the container is busy, not idle, and burns container minutes);
- makes the Worker's 120s container-dispatch timeout fire while the container keeps crawling in the background, so retries pile onto an already-wedged service.

## Acceptance criteria

- The container crawl enforces a **total** deadline for a whole `/crawl` fetch (headers + body, per redirect hop or overall — document which), comparable to the Worker fallback's 20s `AbortSignal.timeout` semantics.
- A regression test in `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/test/test_container_validate.py` (or a sibling suite run by `npm test`) drives a drip/slow server (or a fake transport with the same per-read behaviour) and shows the crawl aborting at the deadline instead of completing.
- The fix does not weaken any existing validation: `npm test` in `pkgs/lab-ops-hub` passes (both TS and Python suites).
- Optional but welcome: note the single-threaded `HTTPServer` coupling in the fix or file it as a follow-up — a `ThreadingHTTPServer` alone does not fix the unbounded crawl, so it is not a substitute for the deadline.

## Suggested fix

Track a monotonic deadline in the crawl path: e.g. wrap the response read in a loop with `res.read1`/`read(65536)` chunks accumulating to the existing 2,000,000-byte cap, checking `time.monotonic()` against a start timestamp before each chunk and aborting past the deadline (chunked reads also match the Worker's capped-reader shape). Redirect hops go through the same opener, so decide and document whether the deadline is per hop (matching the Worker) or for the whole crawl.

body:
## Finding

The two wave-2 workflow branches disagree on the generated-view contract, and a package built by following the templates can never pass `check` — `render` does not repair it.

- PR #486 (`planning/workflow/templates/design.md`, head 593e62f6) teaches a `## Run table` section holding `<!-- workflow:view run-table -->` (design.md:29-36).
- PR #490 (`scripts/research_workflow_items.py`, head 2b0cbbcb) knows no `run-table` view. Its expected design views are `waves` and `run-status` (research_workflow_items.py:701, placed under the existing `## Review status` heading with the placeholder keyed `"run-status"` at :72 — the shape the current `init` scaffold on main already writes). Its `check()` fails any other view name: `unknown generated view <name>` (research_workflow_items.py:794).

## Evidence (experiment at PR #490 head 2b0cbbcb)

Using the real package `doc/2026-10-19T06-09-02Z_research_research-intake-to-implementation/`:

1. `render` then `check` → exit 0, `"ok": true` (design.md gets `waves` + `run-status` views).
2. Renamed the `run-status` view markers to `run-table`, exactly as the PR #486 template prescribes → `check` exits 1: `error: .../design.md: unknown generated view run-table`.
3. Ran `render` again → it did **not** repair the package: it inserted a second, duplicate `run-status` view alongside the `run-table` one, and `check` still exits 1 with the same error.

So the first package whose design.md is filled in from the new template fails the workflow-contract gate with no tool-supported way back.

Same contract, secondary mismatches in PR #486's `templates/main.md` (would surface as perpetual stale-view failures for template-filled packages):

- Concept heading `## C001 <title>` (main.md:29) vs the tool's `CONCEPT_HEADING = ^## (C…): ` (research_workflow_items.py:65; the `init` scaffold on main also writes `## C001: <title>`), so `sections()` does not recognise the template's concept sections.
- Concept view example `- **State**: S0 \`created\` · \`proposed\` · priority …` (main.md:33) vs the generator's `- **State:** \`status\` · stage S<n> · …`.
- `issues-and-prs` view example uses `### C001 <title>` subsections with `- None yet.`, vs the generator's flat per-concept bullet list / `No issues or PRs are recorded yet.`
- The template's closing note describes `render`'s issue/PR line form (`- [#<n>](…) <title> — \`<state>\` · S<n> · covers C001.2 — …`), which does not match the generator's `reference_line()` output (`Issue [#n](url) · S<n> · \`state\` — title (for item); reason`).

## Why it matters

PRs #486 and #490 are parallel wave-2 branches meant to land together: the templates tell authors (human and agent) what to copy, and the tool is the gate that validates it (`check` runs in the workflow-contract CI job). Where they disagree, the docs actively produce packages the gate rejects, and the failure mode is confusing — an "unknown view" the author was told to write, which the documented fix (`render`) duplicates instead of resolving. Neither PR's body lists this alignment as remaining work.

## Acceptance criteria

- One agreed generated-view contract: view names, section headings, and view content shapes are identical in `planning/workflow/templates/` (PR #486) and `scripts/research_workflow_items.py` (PR #490) — whichever side changes, they match, including the concept-heading form and the issue/PR line form.
- A package whose `main.md`/`design.md` start from the templates passes `render` followed by `check` (exit 0), with no duplicate or unknown views.
- A regression guard exists (e.g. a test or fixture in `scripts/tests/` that runs the template view names/shapes through `check`, or renders a template-derived package), so the templates and the tool cannot silently drift apart again.

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review of #267)

`TestTerminateOrphanedSessionEndsTheUpstreamSession` — added by PR #267 in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/pool/upstream_session_test.go` — has failed intermittently in the Nix build gate, on a PR that did not touch it.

## Evidence

- PR #275 (head `a72a2fa79`) CI run 39121884524, job `build`: the mcpx Nix derivation failed with:
  `--- FAIL: TestTerminateOrphanedSessionEndsTheUpstreamSession (0.00s)` / `upstream_session_test.go:185: the orphaned session saw 0 DELETE(s), want exactly 1` / `FAIL github.com/dezren39/mcpx/internal/pool 18.974s`.
- The same run's host `go test` step passed all 3370 tests, and PR #267's own build, plus the builds for PRs #277 and #279 (which contain the same test), were green — so this is intermittent and environment/load-specific (Nix sandbox), not a deterministic break.
- Verified on current main (`60f7a634`): the test still exists unchanged at `pkgs/mcpx/internal/pool/upstream_session_test.go:170`. Locally it passes 100/100 (`go test ./internal/pool/ -run TestTerminateOrphanedSessionEndsTheUpstreamSession -count=100`) and 20/20 with its sibling test, so the failure does not reproduce in a plain dev environment.
- Diagnosability gap in the test itself: when the count check at line ~185 fails, the test never surfaces *why* termination failed. `pool.TerminateOrphanedSession` carefully reports failures via the `upstream.session.orphaned` lifecycle event (with server, session and reason), but the test only captures `upstream.session.terminated` events and checks the DELETE count first — the one piece of evidence that would identify the cause is discarded.

## Why it matters

The Nix build is a merge gate for every mcpx change. A test that flakes there makes unrelated PRs (like #275) show a red build, which trains everyone to merge past red builds — and the standing rule of merging past unrelated infra failures then also lets real regressions through. The sibling daemon-level test from the same PR (`TestTakeoverTerminatesARemovedServersUpstreamSession` in `internal/daemon/registry_handoff_test.go`) exercises the same termination path and likely shares the failure mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The failure mode is identified (e.g. capture and print the `upstream.session.orphaned` event/reason when the DELETE count is wrong; run the pool tests under the Nix build repeatedly to reproduce).
- [ ] The test (and its daemon-level sibling, if it shares the mode) is deterministic under the Nix build sandbox — repeated `nix build` / check runs of the mcpx package pass without this failure.
- [ ] If the root cause is in the termination path itself (not only the test), the fix lands in `TerminateOrphanedSession`/`TerminateHTTPSession` and the test pins it.
- [ ] On failure, the test output states why termination failed (the orphaned reason), not only the DELETE count.

body:
## Problem
Host-originated events (presence, capability results, ticks) reach the program but are not retained in the event stream, so `events_after` never returns them. Recorded fixtures (PR #239) therefore cannot contain them, and any program that consumes them replays to a mismatch. `territory` is one example.

## Options
- **Record from the journal, not the event stream.** Export the journaled host events through an admin-authorized path. This needs a rule about which host events a joiner may see.
- **Retain host events in the stream.** This changes what joiners receive and needs a visibility rule for capability results.

Either way, `world.rs` needs a decision on visibility before fixtures can be complete for interactive programs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A visibility decision for host-originated events is recorded on this issue: which host events a joiner may see, including capability results.
- [ ] Per that decision, host-originated events are either retained in the event stream or exportable from the journal through an authorized path.
- [ ] `events_after` returns the retained host events in order, and recorded fixtures (PR #239) can contain them.
- [ ] Replaying a program that consumes host events (e.g. `territory`) matches live behavior, with tests covering the retention path.

body:
# deploy(deploy.py): validate() crashes with a TypeError traceback on unhashable restart/class values instead of reporting a validation error

`pkgs/deploy/deploy.py`'s module docstring states the contract: validation "is the oracle for 'well-formed definition'… Any violation is reported by field and makes `list` exit non-zero". For two fields, a wrong-typed value does not get a field report at all — `validate()` itself raises, `deploy list` dies with an unhandled traceback, and no validation errors (including unrelated, correctly-detectable ones in other services) are ever printed.

Verified on the laptop against `origin/main` (5c56f76053; the file at the laptop primary's HEAD is identical for these lines) with a probe driving the real `deploy.py` against hand-written registries (probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-deploy-validate-crash/` on the laptop):

## The defect

- deploy.py:125 — `if "restart" in defn and defn["restart"] not in RESTART_POLICIES:` — `RESTART_POLICIES` is a `set` (deploy.py:30). Set membership hashes the candidate, so a JSON array or object value is unhashable.
- deploy.py:144 — the same shape for `class` against `CLASSES` (a set, deploy.py:29).

Every other field check in `validate()` guards with `isinstance(...)` before use (e.g. `ports` requires `isinstance(p, int)`, `healthCheck` requires `isinstance(hc, str)` before `startswith`); the two set-membership checks are the only ones that consume the raw value unguarded.

## Observed behavior (real deploy.py, probe registries)

- Valid control registry → exit 0, normal table.
- `"restart": ["always"]` → exit 1 with an unhandled traceback ending `TypeError: cannot use 'list' as a set element (unhashable type: 'list')` — no `deploy: invalid definition:` line.
- `"class": {"x": 1}` → exit 1, traceback ending `TypeError: cannot use 'dict' as a set element (unhashable type: 'dict')`.
- `"class": ["systemd"]` → same list crash.
- `"restart": 5` (hashable but wrong) → correctly reported: exit 1, `deploy: invalid definition: service 'svc': restart must be one of …` — so the crash is specific to unhashable JSON values (arrays/objects), the exact shapes a hand-authored or generated registry typo produces.
- Because the exception escapes `validate()` (called from `cmd_list`, deploy.py:167; `main()` catches only load errors), one crashing service also suppresses the field reports for every other service in the same registry: the registry author gets a Python traceback pointing into the validator instead of the list of what's wrong with their definitions.

## Why it matters

`validate()` is the stated oracle that every later #5766 slice trusts (renderers and activation consume `class`/`restart` verbatim). A validator that crashes on malformed input inverts its job: the malformed registries are precisely the ones it exists to explain. The traceback also leaks implementation detail (set internals) as the only diagnostic, in a CLI whose other failure paths (`cannot load registry`, per-field `invalid definition:` lines) are deliberately clean.

Distinct from #6383 (same file): that issue is `validate()` *accepting* invalid shapes with exit 0 (newline names, duplicate targets/secrets, host-less healthCheck). This one is `validate()` *crashing* on invalid shapes — opposite failure mode, different lines, different fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- `validate()` returns field-named errors (existing style) for non-string `restart` and `class` values — including arrays and objects — and `deploy list` exits 1 with those `deploy: invalid definition:` lines and no traceback.
- A registry mixing a crashing-shape service with another service's ordinary error reports both services' errors in one run.
- Sane controls unchanged: the shipped registry (`pkgs/deploy/services.nix` via the flake) still validates; a hashable wrong value (`"restart": 5`, `"restart": "sometimes"`) still gets the existing "must be one of" error.
- Regression coverage: extend the malformed-registry flake check (`deploy-list-malformed`, lib/default.nix) or add an equivalent case exercising array/object `restart` and `class` values.

Related: #6383 (validate() accepts-shapes class, same file), #6384 (duplicate-key load rejection, fixed), #5766 (the deploy tool epic this validation gates).

body:
## Summary

`pkgs/id/worker-poc/smoke/participant-validation.mjs` — the regression pin for #4074 (merged in PR #4796: `PlazaGuest.update` must reject participant values the native u64 host can never produce — NaN and -Infinity collapsed to participant 0, negative/fractional participants were delivered/truncated) — is the only smoke file in the package with **no entry point at all**:

- It is not in the `smoke` script chain (`package.json`: `smoke` runs only `counter-smoke.mjs` and `post-update-failure.mjs`).
- It has no script of its own — every sibling does: `post-update-failure` and `participant-clamp` each have a dedicated script entry, and `counter-smoke` is in the chain.
- The README's smoke section (worker-poc/README.md:42-50) documents `counter-smoke` and `post-update-failure` and never mentions `participant-validation`.
- No workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe runs any worker-poc smoke (the package is manual-smoke by design), so the package's own script chain + README are the only execution contract there is — and this file is in neither.

A regression of the #4074 fix would therefore pass every documented check in the package unnoticed: the pin exists, passes, and is never run.

## Evidence (file:line, main @ 1dae17e457 — the 6 newer origin/main commits touch only pm-stack/aggregator + opencode config)

- `pkgs/id/worker-poc/package.json` scripts: `smoke` = `node smoke/counter-smoke.mjs && node smoke/post-update-failure.mjs`; separate entries exist for `post-update-failure` and `participant-clamp`; no entry names `participant-validation`.
- Repo-wide grep for `participant-validation` across `*.json` / `*.md` / `*.nix` / `*.toml` / workflows: zero references outside the file's own header comment.
- `pkgs/id/worker-poc/smoke/participant-validation.mjs:1-9` — header: "Participant validation regression (#4074)… Run: `node smoke/participant-validation.mjs`" (manual path only).

## Verified this run (laptop primary, real package)

```
$ cd pkgs/id/worker-poc && node smoke/participant-validation.mjs
participant-validation: ok (rejects -1/1.5/NaN/-Infinity; preserves 0/1/i32::MAX clamp)   exit 0

$ node smoke/participant-clamp.mjs
participant-clamp: ok (i32::MAX view "chat seen=0 last= input=x"; participant 0 view …)   exit 0
```

The suite is green today — this is a wiring gap, not a live regression.

## Why it matters

- #4074 was a silent state-divergence bug class (hosted isolate vs native host evolving different state for the same event). Its only regression coverage is this file; orphaned, the divergence can return with no signal — the same "a suite that never runs is not a test" failure class as #6185's coverage contract.
- The asymmetry is invisible: a reader of `package.json` or the README reasonably believes the smoke chain covers the package's regressions — `participant-clamp`, the sibling participant regression, IS reachable (own script); this one is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `participant-validation.mjs` is reachable through the package's documented entry points: added to the `smoke` script chain in `pkgs/id/worker-poc/package.json` and/or given its own script entry (matching the `participant-clamp` precedent), so `npm run smoke` (or the named script) executes it.
- [ ] The README smoke section names `participant-validation` and what it pins (#4074), alongside the existing counter / post-update-failure entries.
- [ ] The full smoke chain passes after the change (all four smoke files green on Node ≥ 22, no install needed, as the README promises for the existing smokes).

## Dedup

`gh search issues` for "participant-validation", "worker-poc smoke", "4074" (2026-11-05): #4074 (closed, the bug) and PR #4796 (closed, the fix) cover the behaviour, not the wiring; #6370 covers the *hosted-worker* package's smoke (`pkgs/id/hosted-worker/smoke/smoke.mjs`) — a different package and file. No open or closed issue covers this file's orphaned status.

title: id(worker-poc): isolate-runner.mjs entry-point check is a raw template-literal compare — symlinked standalone invocation silently emits nothing at exit 0 (the spelling #5099's closure grep misses)

body:
## What

`pkgs/id/worker-poc/compare/isolate-runner.mjs:86` guards its standalone mode with a raw template-literal entry-point check — a spelling no other file in the repo uses:

```js
if (import.meta.url === `file://${process.argv[1]}`) {
  for (const line of await runIsolateSequences()) console.log(JSON.stringify(line));
}
```

`process.argv[1]` is the path exactly as invoked; `import.meta.url` is the resolved module URL. Through any symlink — a symlinked file, or a path through a symlinked directory (the fleet's own `~/code -> ~/git/code` alias) — they never match, the standalone body never runs, and Node **exits 0 with no output**. The same spelling also breaks for any path needing percent-encoding (e.g. a space in the checkout path), where `import.meta.url` carries `%20` and the template string carries the raw space.

This is the #2083/#2350 bug class, in the one spelling the class's own closure greps missed: open #5099's acceptance grep (`pathToFileURL\(process\.argv\[1\]\)|resolve\(process\.argv\[1\]\)`) does not match the template-literal form, and #6343 (meta-exporter) / #5099 (opencode-usage-export) cover the two `pathToFileURL` instances only. A repo-wide scan this run confirms this is the only remaining raw compare: every other entry point (`bin/proxy-supervise.mjs:892`, `bin/record.mjs:243`, `bin/codedb-bridge.mjs:321`, `pm-stack/supabase-export/supabase-quota-export.mjs:403`, `pm-stack/cloudflare-export/cloudflare-quota-export.mjs:649`, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/install.mjs:135`, …) uses the guarded `realpathSync` form.

## Verified this run (laptop primary @50237a7deb, HEAD == origin/main)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-isolate-entry/` on the laptop, real runner, no credentials needed (checked-in example guests):

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `node pkgs/id/worker-poc/compare/isolate-runner.mjs` | exit 0, **13 JSON step lines** on stdout (roc-counter 4 + tic-tac-toe 9) |
| `node <file-symlink to isolate-runner.mjs>` | exit 0, **0 lines, no output** — standalone body never ran |
| `node <symlinked-dir>/compare/isolate-runner.mjs` | exit 0, **0 lines, no output** |

The direct run proves the runner works; both symlinked runs prove the guard silently swallows it.

## Why it matters

`isolate-runner.mjs` is the isolate half of the #2271 journal-equality harness: standalone, it emits the per-step JSON lines that `compare/compare.mjs` diffs against the native reference (`pkgs/id/tests/worker_poc_reference.rs`, 13 lines for the same sequences). The import path (`compare.mjs` imports `runIsolateSequences()`) is unaffected — but anyone running the runner standalone through a symlinked checkout or link (the documented fleet layout has `~/code` as a symlink alias) gets an **empty evidence file at exit 0**: `node <link> > isolate.jsonl` succeeds and produces nothing, so the isolate side looks like it emitted zero steps rather than failing. Silent success with no output is the failure shape this bug class keeps being filed for; this instance survived two closure passes only because its spelling differs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The entry-point check compares real paths (`fs.realpathSync` on both sides, the house shape at `bin/proxy-supervise.mjs:885-892`), or an equivalent that resolves symlinks and percent-encodes correctly — not the raw template-literal compare.
- [ ] Direct, file-symlink, and directory-symlink standalone invocations all emit the same 13 JSON step lines.
- [ ] Importing the module (as `compare/compare.mjs` does) still does not run the standalone body.
- [ ] The closure grep for this bug class is widened to catch this spelling too (e.g. also matches `` `file://${process.argv[1]}` ``), and that widened grep is empty repo-wide after the fix (the two `pathToFileURL` instances are #6343 / #5099, not this issue).

## Dedup

- #6343 (OPEN) covers `pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs:624` only; #5099 (OPEN) covers `pm-stack/opencode-usage-export/opencode-usage-export.mjs:383` only — neither names this file, and #5099's acceptance grep cannot match this spelling.
- #4325 (CLOSED) fixed four named files; this file was not among them.
- Searched open + closed for `isolate-runner` on 2026-11-05: no issue covers its entry-point guard.

body:
## What

`pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs:624` (landed today in #6333, the re-home of the retired Meta exporter) guards `main()` with the pre-#2083 raw-path entry-point check:

```js
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) {
  await main();
}
```

Invoked through any symlink (a symlinked file, or a path through a symlinked directory), the raw `process.argv[1]` string never equals `import.meta.url`, `main()` is skipped, and Node exits **0 with no output and no files written** — a silent no-op that looks like a successful export.

This is the exact bug #2350 reported, fixed, and closed for this same file before the exporter was retired in `1d0944333f` ("retire the Meta console-scrape exporter"). The re-homed copy in #6333 (commit `b4cf60a2db`) carries the old guard again. The sibling exporters kept the fix: `pm-stack/supabase-export/supabase-quota-export.mjs:403` and `pm-stack/cloudflare-export/cloudflare-quota-export.mjs:649` both use the established guarded form `fs.realpathSync(process.argv[1]) === fs.realpathSync(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url))` (pattern also at `bin/proxy-supervise.mjs:892`). Meta is now the only exporter with the raw-path form.

## Verified this run (laptop primary @560febee0d, HEAD == origin/main)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-meta-entry/` on the laptop, real exporter, `--cdp-port 1` (loopback-refused, so a run must produce the `cdp-unavailable` failure document):

| Invocation | Result |
|---|---|
| `node pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs --cdp-port 1 --out-dir <scratch>/out-direct` | exit 4, stderr `meta-quota-export: cdp-unavailable: CDP http://127.0.0.1:1/json/list unreachable`, wrote `latest.json` + `history.jsonl` |
| `node <symlink-to-the-same-file> --cdp-port 1 --out-dir <scratch>/out-symlink` | **exit 0, no output, output directory empty** — `main()` never ran |

The direct run proves the exporter works; the symlinked run proves the guard silently swallows it. (The installed systemd path is not affected today — `install-laptop.sh` copies the file to `~/atlas/meta-quota-export/` and the unit runs that real path — but any symlinked invocation, e.g. a `~/bin` link or a checkout reached through a symlinked directory, silently produces no export and no failure document, which for a quota exporter means the gatherer reads stale data with no error anywhere.)

## Why it matters

A quota exporter that exits 0 while doing nothing is the worst failure shape for this subsystem: no failure document, no log line, and downstream consumers (pm-dashboard backup requires `meta-quota-export/latest.json` + `history.jsonl`, `nixos/home/pm-dashboard-backup.sh:341-342`) see only staleness. #2350 already established both the bug and the house fix; the re-home regressed it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `meta-quota-export.mjs` uses the guarded `realpathSync` entry-point comparison (same shape as supabase-export:403 / cloudflare-export:649), or an equivalent that resolves symlinks on both sides.
- [ ] Regression coverage: invoking the exporter through a symlinked path with an unreachable CDP port exits non-zero and writes the failure document, matching direct invocation (the suite added in #6333, `meta-quota-export.test.mjs`, is the natural home — note it is currently run by no workflow; see the companion CI filing).
- [ ] Direct invocation behavior unchanged (exit codes, documents, console output).
- [ ] The other `opt()` argv-helper instance in this file is **not** in scope here — it is already tracked by #3469, which names this file.

## Dedup

- #2350 (CLOSED) fixed this exact check for this file pre-retirement; the re-home in #6333 re-introduced it — this filing is the regression report, not a duplicate.
- #4325 (CLOSED) and open #5099 cover the same check class in other files (opencode-usage-export is #5099's file); neither covers meta-exporter.
- #3469 (OPEN) covers this file's `opt()` helper only, not the entry-point guard.

title: fleet(queue): brokers accept an empty token file — empty X-Agent-Token header authenticates to queue-broker and secrets-broker

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/fleet
labels.description: pkgs/fleet multicall binary + platform crates

body:
## Summary

fleet(queue): both broker daemons accept an **empty token file** as a valid shared token. If the token file exists but is empty (or whitespace-only), the broker starts normally with expected token `""`, and any client that sends an **empty `X-Agent-Token` header** authenticates — including to the secrets-broker, which serves secret values. Neither broker validates that the loaded token is non-empty; a missing/unreadable file exits 3, but an empty one silently disables authentication.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @2aefba02b4, real built binaries)

Token loading — the read succeeds on an empty file, the value is only trimmed, never checked:

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/secrets_broker.rs:311-320` — `SECRETS_BROKER_TOKEN_FILE` / `~/.config/secrets-broker/token` read + trim; the `unwrap_or_else` exit-3 arm fires only on a read *error*.
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/queue_broker.rs:593-602` — same pattern for the client-facing token, and `:606-615` again for the outbound secrets-broker token.
- Auth check in both brokers (`secrets_broker.rs:299`, `queue_broker.rs:581`): `token_ok` is `header.value == expected` — with `expected == ""`, an empty header value is a match.
- Client side shares the gap: `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:94-98` reads `REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE` and trims it with no empty check, so a client with an empty token file happily sends the empty header that an empty-token broker accepts.

Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-broker-empty-token`, real `secrets-broker`/`queue-broker` bins built from `pkgs/fleet`, loopback binds, stub environment):

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| secrets-broker, empty token file, **no** header | `401 {"error":"unauthorized"}` |
| secrets-broker, empty token file, **empty** `X-Agent-Token` header, `GET /secret/some-name` | `503 {"error":"secrets not loaded yet"}` — the **post-auth** branch (identical to the correct-token control below) |
| secrets-broker, empty token file, empty header, `GET /secrets` | `200 {"names":[]}` — post-auth endpoint served |
| secrets-broker, empty token file, wrong header | `401` |
| secrets-broker, **whitespace-only** token file, empty header | `503` (post-auth) — trim makes it empty too |
| secrets-broker, real token file (control), empty header | `401` |
| secrets-broker, real token file (control), correct header | `503` (post-auth) |
| queue-broker, empty token files, no header, `POST /nope` | `401` |
| queue-broker, empty token files, **empty** header, `POST /nope` | `200 {"ok":false,"exit":2,"error":"unknown command /nope"}` — dispatch reached, auth passed |

## Why it matters

- The secrets-broker is the fleet's secret-value server: on a loaded cache, the same empty-header request to `/secret/<name>` returns the secret **value**. The brokers bind to tailnet addresses by default (`100.99.113.103:4800`/`:4801`), so any tailnet peer — or anything that can reach those ports — needs no credential at all when a token file lands empty.
- An empty token file is a realistic accident, not an exotic state: provisioning that touches/creates the file before writing the secret, a truncated write, or a restore that recreates zero-length files all produce it — and today every one of those starts a silently unauthenticated broker instead of failing loudly at startup. This is the fail-open mirror of the fail-loud fix for empty secret *values* in #6275 (distinct: that covers values read through from Bitwarden, not the broker's own auth token).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both brokers refuse to start (non-zero exit, log line naming the token file) when the loaded token is empty or whitespace-only — same fail-loud shape as the existing unreadable-file exit.
- [ ] The queue-broker applies the same check to its outbound secrets-broker token, and the repo-queue client refuses to send an empty token (clear error naming the token file).
- [ ] Regression coverage: empty and whitespace-only token files fail startup for both brokers; a non-empty token still authenticates, and missing/wrong/empty headers still get 401 against a real token.
- [ ] No change to the wire protocol or to behaviour with a properly provisioned token file.

title: fleet(queue): repo-queue client accepts empty REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE / REPO_QUEUE_SIGNAL_PATH — silently uses queue "" and fails signal writes with a blank path

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
# fleet(queue): repo-queue client accepts empty `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` / `REPO_QUEUE_SIGNAL_PATH` — silently talks to queue `""` and fails signal writes with a blank path

## Bug

In `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` (developing-today/code @ `6f5df296e2`):

- `default_queue()` (client.rs:585-587) returns `std::env::var("REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE")` verbatim whenever the variable is *set*, falling back to `DEFAULT_QUEUE` only when it is unset:

  ```rust
  fn default_queue() -> String {
      std::env::var("REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE").unwrap_or_else(|_| DEFAULT_QUEUE.to_string())
  }
  ```

  An exported-but-empty value (a common shell/systemd accident: `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE=` in an env file, an unset variable expanded by a wrapper) therefore becomes the queue name for **every** verb that goes through `opt_queue()` — `list`, `enqueue`, `claim`, `signal`, etc.

- `cmd_signal` (client.rs:1257) has the same shape for `REPO_QUEUE_SIGNAL_PATH`: an empty value becomes the signal file path.

The same file already shows the intended pattern: `direct_broker_url()` (client.rs:69-76) trims `REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL` and treats empty as unset. The fleet-search client does the same for `ATLAS_SEARCH_URL` / `ATLAS_SEARCH_TOKEN`. These two sites were missed.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ `6f5df296e2`; code identical at probe build)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-queue-empty-env` (laptop) — real `repo-queue` binary against a recording loopback stub broker (`REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port>`, stub token file):

| Case | Request recorded at stub | Client output |
|---|---|---|
| `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` unset (control) | `POST /list {"queue":"repo-health-code-shadow",…}` | `(no tasks)` |
| `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE=` (empty) | `POST /list {"queue":"",…}` | `(no tasks)` — no error, no warning |
| `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE="   "` (whitespace) | `POST /list {"queue":"   ",…}` | `(no tasks)` — no error, no warning |
| `REPO_QUEUE_SIGNAL_PATH=` (empty), `signal --reason probe` | `/signal-count` posted normally | exit 3, stderr: `repo-queue: cannot write : No such file or directory (os error 2)` — blank path in the message, signal file never written |

So with an empty default-queue variable, an operator (or a fleet script) is silently shown an empty queue that is not the real queue, and an `enqueue` would be addressed to queue `""` instead of the pilot queue — work addressed somewhere no worker claims, with no error anywhere. With an empty signal path, the wake-up signal that follows an enqueue dies with a message that names no path, so the failure is hard to trace back to the variable.

## Why it matters

The repo-queue client is the fleet's control plane (producers enqueue, workers claim, signals wake workers). Its failure mode for a plausible configuration accident should be a loud usage error or the documented default — never silent redirection to a nonexistent queue. This is the same silent-misdirection class as #5939 (client parser silently overwriting/misreading flags, fixed) and the HOME-fallback filings #6238/#5640, but a distinct site and mechanism (env-var empty acceptance), not covered by either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` set to empty or whitespace-only is treated as unset (fall back to `DEFAULT_QUEUE`), or rejected with a usage error naming the variable and its value — matching the `direct_broker_url()` trim-and-ignore-empty precedent in the same file; the chosen behavior is pinned by a test.
- [ ] `REPO_QUEUE_SIGNAL_PATH` set to empty or whitespace-only gets the same treatment (default path or a named usage error); a signal write failure never reports a blank path.
- [ ] Tests pin: unset → default; empty → default/error; whitespace → default/error; a normal value is used verbatim (trimmed per the broker-URL precedent).
- [ ] Audit the client's remaining env reads (`REPO_QUEUE_TOKEN_FILE`, `REPO_QUEUE_BROKER_URL` — the latter already guards empty) for the same acceptance and note the result on this issue.
- [ ] No behavior change when the variables are unset or set to ordinary values: `list` against the stub broker sends the same queue name as before.

## Related

- #5939 — repo-queue client parser flag handling (fixed; same silent-misdirection class, different input surface)
- #6238 — repo-queue client `home()` HOME-unset fallback (different variable, different mechanism)
- #5640 — fleet-search/atlas HOME fallback sites

title: secrets broker: no read-through on cache miss — newly minted secrets invisible up to 15 min, client returned empty
body:
**Finding (diagnosed 2026-11-05, flagged by the Atlas ask-ledger build lane): `fleet secrets get` returned EMPTY repeatedly for secrets Bitwarden verifiably held.**

## Root cause (evidence-backed)
1. **The secrets broker is cache-only with no read-through.** `pkgs/fleet-brokers/.../secrets-broker/src/main.rs`: `GET /secret/<name>` serves only the in-memory cache; a miss returns 404 (503 before first load). The cache refreshes on a 900s TTL (stale-while-revalidate; partial refresh keeps the old snapshot). A secret newly created in Bitwarden is therefore **invisible to the broker for up to ~15 minutes**.
2. **The window matches exactly.** Broker journal (laptop): refreshes logged every ~15 min all morning, count **118 secrets at 09:31 → 124 at 09:46** — the morning's newly minted secrets (Sunshine admin, the ask-ledger Turso token, the notes-pilot token, …) only became broker-visible at the 09:46 refresh. The broker itself never failed: continuous uptime since 08:31, zero refresh failures.
3. **The client's Bitwarden fallback did not save the read in that window.** The sandbox had just recycled (boot d9e67e18, 09:43). Per TOOLS.md the verb is broker-first with a Bitwarden fallback inside it, yet callers saw empty values (exit 0) instead of the BWS-held values or a loud error. Post-window the defect is **not reproducible**: sandbox and laptop reads (x2 each, two names) now return identical values/fingerprints, and a genuinely missing name fails loudly (exit 3, "2 source(s) failed"). The sandbox fleet binary is also the known-stale rev from #5760.

## Impact
Any lane that mints a secret and immediately reads it back through the broker can proceed on an empty value unless it defensively falls back (the ask-ledger lane did — loudly — which is how this surfaced). Worst case is a silent empty credential wired into a config.

## Recommended fixes
- Broker: read-through on cache miss (fetch the single secret from BWS on a 404 path) OR have `fleet secrets` writes/creates POST `/refresh` (the endpoint already exists, returns 202) so mint-then-read works immediately.
- Client: never exit 0 with an empty value when sources disagree/fail — the loud exit-3 path already exists for fully-missing names; extend it to the broker-miss + fallback-failure case.
- Until then, the mint-then-read pattern must trigger a broker refresh or read via the bws fallback route and verify non-empty.

title: pm-stack(aggregator): /queue and /today throw on a queued/blocked lined-up task with a non-GitHub ref — buildQueueView calls refUrl unguarded on lined-up refs and out-of-pool epicRefs

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Summary

The aggregator's queue view — served at `/queue`, `/frag/queue`, and `/api/queue.json`, and also built as part of every `/today` context — throws whenever a feed-valid input carries a ref `parseRef` rejects in a position `buildQueueView` passes to `refUrl` unguarded. Two verified producer paths:

1. **A queued or blocked lined-up task with a non-GitHub ref.** `buildQueueView` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/queue-view.ts) builds its `nextUp` rows from orchestration `linedUp` tasks with `status === "queued"` and its `blocked` rows from `status === "blocked"`, passing `task.ref` straight to `row()` — whose URL fallback at queue-view.ts:139 is `refUrl(args.ref, ...)` with no `isValidRef` check. The feed gate for lined-up elements, `isLinedUpElement` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts:223-232), validates `title`/`horizon`/`status`/`horizonWhy` only — it never checks `ref` — and `normalizeOrchestrationSection` passes a gate-valid section through verbatim, so a lined-up ref of `goal_a243772844c3`, `812`, or `developing-today/code#99999999999999999999` (unsafe integer) reaches `buildQueueView` exactly as published. Lined-up tasks legitimately carry non-GitHub refs in the real feed (goal ids, bare numbers — the same data reality behind #6174 / #6195 / #6205).
2. **A pool item whose `epicRef` points outside the pool with a bad ref.** `epicFor` (queue-view.ts:110-114) resolves a pool item's epic parent; when the epic is not itself in the pool, the fallback at queue-view.ts:113 is unguarded `refUrl(ref)`. `isProjectPoolItem` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts:281) checks `epicRef` only as "any string", so an unsafe-integer or non-repo-qualified `epicRef` passes the shared gate.

Callers have no guard around the throw: `queueContext` (server.ts:713) feeds `/queue` (server.ts:1395), `/frag/queue` (:1398), and `/api/queue.json` (:1921); `todayContext` (server.ts:696) builds the same view for the `/today` pages (:1370/:1374/:1899), so one bad lined-up entry also breaks `/today`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ cc45860abb, HEAD == origin/main)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-queue-view-ref/probe.ts` (bun, real aggregator sources, run synchronously — imports the real `buildQueueView`, `isProjectPoolItem`, `isValidRef`):

```
isValidRef goal/plain/unsafe/good: false false false true
linedUp queued ref=goal_a243772844c3: THREW: not a repo-qualified ref: goal_a243772844c3
linedUp queued ref=812: THREW: not a repo-qualified ref: 812
linedUp queued ref=developing-today/code#99999999999999999999: THREW: ref number is not a safe integer: developing-today/code#99999999999999999999
linedUp blocked ref=goal_a243772844c3: THREW: not a repo-qualified ref: goal_a243772844c3
linedUp blocked ref=developing-today/code#99999999999999999999: THREW: ref number is not a safe integer: developing-today/code#99999999999999999999
linedUp queued GOOD control: OK (nextUp row with the GitHub URL)
linedUp queued no-ref control: OK
gate pool epicRef=BAD_UNSAFE: true
pool queued epicRef=BAD_UNSAFE (not in pool): THREW: ref number is not a safe integer: developing-today/code#99999999999999999999
pool queued epicRef=812 (not in pool): THREW: not a repo-qualified ref: 812
pool queued epicRef=GOOD-not-in-pool control: OK
pool queued own ref=812: OK (its own URL comes from issueUrl — not claimed as a vector)
```

## Why it matters

The queue view is the fleet's work-order surface — who is doing what, what is blocked, what is next — and it is also embedded in `/today`. The orchestration section is republished every run from free-form lined-up data; a single queued task carrying a goal-id ref (a normal, recurring shape in this feed) takes down `/queue`, its JSON API, and `/today` for every viewer until the next orchestration run happens to change the lined-up set. It does not degrade to a missing row.

Distinct from the siblings: #6205 covers `deriveOverview`'s in-progress path only (its own probe showed a **queued** lined-up task is skipped there and renders OK — `buildQueueView` is exactly where queued/blocked lined-up tasks are consumed); #6174 covers /today objectives (render.ts:3368), not the queue view embedded in the same page; #6224 covers pool `blockedBy`/`blocks` edges and the brief/pool-graph/epic-graph consumers — its gate-side fix would not protect `buildQueueView` against the lined-up path, whose gate (`isLinedUpElement`) is a different predicate that #6224 does not touch. The house precedent for a consumer-side guard already exists: `sessionRecordLine` (render.ts:1912) wraps `refUrl` in try/catch so one malformed ref omits only its own link, and render.ts:2524 guards with `isValidRef` before calling `refUrl`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `buildQueueView` never throws for a feed-valid orchestration section or a gate-valid pool: a lined-up queued/blocked task whose ref fails `isValidRef` produces a row with no URL (or no row for that ref), and the rest of the queue view renders normally.
- A pool item whose out-of-pool `epicRef` fails `isValidRef` renders without an epic link (or with the epic shown unlinked); a valid out-of-pool `epicRef` still links, as today.
- The guard lives at the queue-view layer (row/epic URL construction routes through `isValidRef`, mirroring render.ts:2524) so in-memory/live sources that bypass the feed gates are covered too; additionally validating `ref` in `isLinedUpElement` is welcome but not sufficient alone.
- Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/queue-view.test.ts` pin: queued lined-up with a goal-id ref, blocked lined-up with an unsafe-integer ref, and a pool item with an out-of-pool unsafe `epicRef` — each with a valid-ref control.
- Existing behavior unchanged for valid refs (controls above).

Related: #6205 (overview in-progress path), #6174 (/today objectives), #6195 / #6210 (board in-flight), #6224 (pool blockedBy/blocks edges + brief/graph consumers), #4952 (the shared ref-validity rule), #2399 (pool edge contract).

title: opencode-claimant: binding rate - standing claimant stuck in shadow mode, cap starved launches (12 to 36)
body:
## Summary

The fleet queue's claimant binding rate is the OpenCode throughput bottleneck (ID program census, 2026-11-05 ~03:22 CST; Drew's directive 2026-11-05: "fix it"). Tasks claimed by Muse shift lanes and handed off to the opencode execution lane sit unbound while the laptop has session headroom. Diagnosis below was measured fresh on 2026-11-05 ~15:05-15:20Z; every consequential figure was read twice (two early reads of the claimant fire log in this session were fabricated by the tool layer and were discarded — the figures below are the grep/poll-verified ones).

## Diagnosis

1. **The standing claimant launches nothing: its mode file is `shadow`.** `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode` = `shadow` (verified 3x). The OpenChamber claimant task fires every 10 min and, per prompt.md, shadow mode discovers and reports but never claims/binds/launches — a slice-1 safety gate left pending a "parallel-run gate" packet that never landed. Its 2026-11-05T15:10:00Z fire saw 43 candidates, computed cap_room 2, launched 0.
2. **All actual binding is ad-hoc.** `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/inflight.jsonl` (grep-verified: 108 lines, 29 `bound` events) shows every bind since 2026-11-04T14:23Z came from agent-driven `drive_fire.py` batches (max 6 per drive, hardcoded order) — i.e. an operator session happening to drive it. Last bind 2026-11-05T09:13:45Z; **zero binds in the ~6h before this fix** while 26-43 candidates waited. The census's "2 claimant sessions launching serially" were these manual drives.
3. **The cap starves launches even when live.** CAP = 12 active root sessions server-wide (poll.py, claimant.py, prompt.md), counted across ALL server tenants — scheduled lane runners, the claimant's own session, zombies (see the filed note `issue-5016-cap-composition` in the claimant state dir: cap_room 0 with 44 candidates on 2026-11-03). Live read at fix time: 10 active roots -> cap_room 2. The census ran 18-19 roots at load 4.5-7.5 on 16 cores, so 12 is below demonstrated headroom.
4. **Per-launch cost is not the problem.** Driven batches bind at ~2-4 s/task (inflight timestamps). Serialization that matters = shadow mode (0 launches) + 10-min fire cadence executed by an LLM session working prompt.md step-by-step + cap_room ~0-2.
5. **The deterministic executor was never committed.** `claimant.py` (the prompt.md implementation: supervision, gate, cap, launch loop, fire log) exists only as an untracked file in the laptop primary checkout. The repo ships poll.py/prompt.md/install.mjs but not the executor, so the fleet kept running the LLM-prompt form.
6. **Watchdog reconciliation — same root.** `agent.claim_repo_task` (migration-0023) only returns tasks with `attempts < max_attempts` and `not_before` due. A handed-off task whose lease expires unbound returns to `queued` with attempts+1; re-claim + re-handoff loops burn attempts until the task is permanently unclaimable while still counted in `queued_count`. That is why worker-shift lanes sporadically report all-null claims against a deep queue (and their watchdog failure streaks: repo-queue-worker-shift-nix cf=6, -openchamber cf=25, -opencode cf=24, -openchamber-b cf=14 at the 06:10 check): claim-side eligibility divergence, produced by the bind-side failure. Health attempts distribution shows the pile-up (135 tasks at exactly 24 attempts).

## Before-metrics (2026-11-05 ~15:05-15:15Z, two reads)

- repo-health-code-pilot: queued 205 -> 202, claimed 31 -> 36, parked 247 -> 243, blocked 215
- Unbound claimant candidates (poll.py): 26 (code 18, openchamber 4, nix 3, opencode 1)
- Active root sessions 10 / cap 12 -> cap_room 2
- Binds in the last ~25h: 29, all ad-hoc; binds in the last 6h: 0
- Candidate claim leases: 45 min; sampled candidates had already waited >= 40 min unbound

## Fix (this issue's PR)

- Commit `claimant.py` (pre-existing untracked implementation) so the deterministic executor is versioned.
- CAP 12 -> 20 in poll.py, claimant.py, prompt.md (headroom-matched; active-root counting with the 30-min window unchanged; fires still launch at most cap_room).
- claimant.py: single-instance flock (overlapping fires can never double-launch) + bounded parallel launch pool (4 workers) across distinct candidates; exactly-once stays anchored on the atomic DB bind (`bind_repo_task_lane_session`), with re-verification inside each worker and session cleanup on bind failure (existing behavior).
- Claimant task cadence */10 -> */5 (install.mjs CRON) and the task prompt directs the fire to execute claimant.py deterministically.
- Runtime: reinstall the task (enabled) and flip the mode file to `live`.

## Follow-ups named, not fixed here

- Attempts-capped queued tasks (the 24-attempt pile-up) are unclaimable until their attempts/max_attempts are revisited — a separate queue-data decision.
- Cap composition visibility: the fire log reports totals only; per-tenant composition (lane runners vs bound workers vs other) would make future cap tuning direct (partially covered by the issue-5016 note).

title: Wire globalping-watch failures into the alert throat (#3676 scope item 7)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
Scope item 7 of #3676, held since 2026-11-01 pending Drew's go. Drew gave the go 2026-11-05 (~09:00 CST, main chat: the Globalping ledger item answered "Go").

Work: when the hourly `globalping-watch` cron (owner: account-connection campaign goal) finds a target DOWN, it posts an incident to the alert throat via the proven caller interface `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/post-alert.ts` (on the laptop), with:
- `--source globalping-watch`
- `--key <target hostname>` (the throat dedupes server-side on (source, key): a continuing outage bumps occurrences on the open incident instead of re-paging; closing the incident on /alerts re-arms it)
- `--severity critical` (external-reachability failure = paging class; only criticals are delivered/escalated by the throat engine)
- title/body naming the target and the status/error the probes saw

The existing chat message + daily-log behavior on down targets stays unchanged; the throat post is additive. If the post itself fails, the run's chat message must say so (no silent drop).
