## Finding (from PR review)

Codex P2 on PR #3290 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-01T02:00:06Z): "Allow queue polling to progress past retained failed events" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3290#discussion_r4434070386

> If the queue contains 500 older events for unavailable planned mirrors, retaining those events now prevents later events for healthy repositories from being processed. The Worker in `infra/github-backup/worker/src/index.js:55-61` returns only the first 500 entries and neither follows nor exposes a pagination cursor, so every drain retries the same failed batch until recovery or expiration of the seven-day TTL. I reproduced this with 500 missing-mirror events followed by one healthy-repository event: repeated drains never attempted the healthy repository. Preserve failed events, but add pagination or another mechanism that allows polling to advance past them.

Context: PR #3290 itself introduced the retain-on-failure ack discipline (an event is acked only after a successful fetch), which is what makes retained events accumulate at the head of the queue.

## No-response evidence

- PR #3290 merged with the finding unaddressed: the inline comment has no replies, and GraphQL `reviewThreads` for PR #3290 shows its sole thread `isResolved=false`.
- No fix commit after the comment: the 500-entry cap with no cursor is still present on current main (below).

## Still-live evidence (verified this run, current main)

- `infra/github-backup/worker/src/index.js`, `GET /queue` handler: `const list = await env.GHB_EVENTS.list({ prefix: "ev:", limit: 500 });` — it iterates only `list.keys`, never follows `list.cursor` / `list_complete`, and the response exposes no cursor to the drainer.
- `infra/github-backup/bin/drain_queue.py` polls that endpoint once per run and processes only the returned `events`; retained failed events (acked only on a successful fetch, per the #3219 discipline documented in its header) therefore re-occupy the same first-500 window on every drain until their mirrors recover or the 7-day KV TTL expires.

## Dedupe

Searched open and closed issues for "drain queue 500 pagination" and "github-backup queue polling retained" (2026-11-01): no issue covers this.

## Acceptance criteria

- Queue polling can progress past 500 retained events: the Worker follows the KV list cursor (or exposes pagination) and the drainer can reach events beyond the first 500.
- Failed events are still preserved (the retain-on-failure ack discipline is not weakened).
- A regression test/repro with >500 retained failed events followed by a healthy-repo event shows the healthy event being processed.
- Or the finding is resolved by a documented decision on this issue.

body:
`pkgs/id/src/world_ssh.rs:202` `load_or_create_host_key` has no first-run creation-race handling at all (found during triage of #2627, verified on main 98371127):

- Existing-key branch: `tokio::fs::read_to_string` → `PrivateKey::from_openssh(pem)` immediately. A concurrent first start that reads the file between the winner's `write_private_file` `create_new` and its `write_all` gets a partial PEM and fails with an OpenSSH parse error.
- NotFound branch: if two first starts race, the loser's `write_private_file` returns `AlreadyExists` and `load_or_create_host_key` propagates it as a hard error (`?` at world_ssh.rs:210) — the loser never reads the winner's key, unlike `load_or_create_keypair`'s `read_key_after_creation_race` path (store.rs:110).

Impact: concurrent first starts of the SSH server (scripted setup, service+CLI) can fail spuriously on first boot; the parse error reads as a corrupt host key, inviting deletion of the winner's valid key.

Acceptance:
- A bounded wait/retry (consistent with store.rs's 1s creation-race helper) on the load path: a partial/unparseable PEM observed during the create→write window is retried until it parses or the deadline passes; a still-unparseable file after the deadline errors as corrupt and is never regenerated.
- The AlreadyExists loser reads and returns the winner's host key.
- Deterministic regression test covering both interleavings; both concurrent first starts end with the winner's host key.

Note: the store.rs helper is fixed-32-byte shape, so this needs its own parse-based retry — do not force-fit `read_key_after_creation_race`. Related: #2627 (keypair side, fix routed separately).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Two concurrent first-run `load_or_create_host_key` calls converge on a single valid host key: one creates it, the other loads the created key instead of erroring or parsing a partial file.
- [ ] A partially-written PEM is never returned as a valid key (readers retry/re-read or the write is atomic via rename).
- [ ] A regression test exercises the creation race (or an equivalent interleaving) and passes consistently.

body:
## Directive (Drew, 2026-10-31 23:10 CDT)

"use unstable" — the amd configuration should not draw packages from a master-tracking nixpkgs. Kill the master input; anything it feeds should come from the nixos-unstable set (or a deliberately pinned exception, justified in place).

## Current state (verified on the laptop, 2026-10-31)

- `flake.nix:98`: `nixpkgs-master.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs"` — no ref, so it tracks **master**. Its pin is currently `086873f31aea` (also, oddly, the exact rev `nixpkgs-stable` is pinned to).
- Consumers of `inputs.nixpkgs-master.legacyPackages`:
  - `nixos/environment/default.nix` — system packages: `ghostty`, `zed-editor`, `framework-tool`, `musl`, `fish`; plus `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` from master's `playwright-driver.browsers` (~line 379).
  - `home/common/default.nix:1226` — `ghostty` package.
- The system's base nixpkgs is already the root `nixpkgs` input on `nixos-unstable`; master feeds only the list above.

## Why this matters (tonight's evidence)

The 2026-10-30 nixpkgs-update run bumped master `c61a74e1` -> `086873f31aea`. A master rev that fresh has not been through Hydra, so master-fed packages and their closures build from source. The acceptance build (`nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` in `~/git/fleet/nixpkgs-update-2026-10-30`) ran 13h13m under fleet load before Drew ordered it killed on 2026-10-31 — and its load is what flaked the watchdog activation switch via code#3199. Completed derivations are cached in the store, so the update itself is resumable; the structural problem is the master input, not the run.

## Asks

1. Repoint every `nixpkgs-master` consumer (system packages above, the Playwright browsers path, the home ghostty) to the nixos-unstable package set (`nixpkgs-25` / root `nixpkgs`, matching what the surrounding config uses). If a specific package genuinely needs to be fresher than unstable, pin THAT package's input deliberately with a comment saying why — no general master set.
2. Remove the `nixpkgs-master` input from `flake.nix` / `flake.lock` (and check `nixpkgs-stable`'s pin, which currently equals the master rev — stable should be a release branch or go away too).
3. Acceptance: `nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath` clean and the toplevel builds; no remaining `nixpkgs-master` references in the tree.

Related: the nixpkgs-update procedure (Muse cron `nixpkgs-update-amd`) is being restricted to the nixos-unstable set in the same pass, so future updates stop bumping master even before this lands.


## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `nixpkgs-master` input is removed from `flake.nix` (or any retained exception is pinned and justified in place per the directive).
- [ ] Every former master consumer (system packages in `nixos/environment/default.nix`, `ghostty` in `home/common/default.nix`, `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`) resolves from the nixos-unstable set.
- [ ] The amd configuration evaluates/builds in CI with no master-tracking input in `flake.lock`.

body:
Phase 3 (closing audit) of design #3231 — "a signed artifact is validated as strictly as it is built: one receipt contract for pkgs/id artifacts" (design doc: `files/designs/code-id-artifact-receipt-validation.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace). Filed by design-architect pass 28 (2026-10-31); **gated on Phases 1–2 of #3231 landing** (Phase 1: #3196 + #3146, list integrity; Phase 2: #3192 + #3187, text fields).

## Scope

Build the field-by-field disposition table for `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs`: every field of every known kind (`friend_remove`, `home_declared`, `document`, `tag`) plus every envelope field (`author`, `seq`, `prev`, `kind`, `body`, `after`, `hash`, `signature`), set against the producer or sibling-validator rule that governs it (`directory.rs` producers, `documents.rs` `DocumentRef::check`, `tag_claims.rs` `check_text`, `chain.rs` `ChainExt::validate`, `world_hub.rs` `validate_world_name`). Each field is dispositioned in the closing evidence:

- (a) enforced at receipt — name the check in `check()`/`parsed()` and the phase that landed it, or
- (b) deliberately unvalidated — with the one-line reason, or
- (c) a gap the phases missed and rule 1 of #3231 covers — file it as a named follow-up and link it here; do not fix it inside this audit.

## Explicit dispositions required

- **The `kind` string** of unknown kinds: length/NFC bounds (chain kinds are 1..=MAX_KIND_BYTES and NFC) versus the module's stored-but-never-applied forward-compatibility rule for future kinds. Decide and record the trade.
- **`document.content` internal strings**: `chain.rs` `check_value` requires NFC for every text string including map keys; the artifact document rule governs only `media_type` (the `documents.rs` precedent). Disposition whether content text is governed data or opaque payload.
- **`prev`'s shape** beyond the chain-position equality `ArtifactLog::store` already enforces.
- **Full builder-side symmetry**: `documents.rs`/`chain.rs` builders apply their checks at build time; artifact `sign` is generic over kind strings including future kinds. Record whether `sign` should run `parsed()` for known kinds, with the reasoning (Phase 1 pins only the duplicate-`after` refusal in `sign_after`).
- **`world_id` charset evidence**: gather how `ArtifactLog::declared()` consumers resolve a `world_id` to a served world (the design doc's open question — `validate_world_name`'s `a-z0-9-_` versus `WorldCore::new`'s any-non-blank rule). Record the evidence here; pinning the charset, if warranted, is a follow-up filed from this audit, not a fix inside it.

## Contract statement

Write the #3231 rule into the `artifact.rs` module doc — the builder/decoder symmetry sentence `documents.rs` and `chain.rs` already carry, in artifact terms: a signed artifact is validated at receipt (`check()` + `parsed()`) against every rule its producers and the crate's sibling validators obey; a signed list names each thing once; text fields follow the crate's text rules. Note the unknown-kind exception in the same paragraph.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Disposition table posted on this issue (or a linked PR): every known-kind field and envelope field with a disposition (a)/(b)/(c)
- [ ] The five explicit dispositions above are each recorded with their reasoning
- [ ] Any (c) follow-ups filed and linked; no fixes landed inside this audit issue itself
- [ ] Contract statement landed in the `artifact.rs` module doc; design issue #3231 closed with a link to this evidence
- [ ] This phase did not start before #3231 Phases 1–2 landed (record their closing state in the evidence)

body:
Design-architect pass 28 (2026-10-31), audit at origin/main `357ec7fb`. Full design doc: `files/designs/code-id-artifact-receipt-validation.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. NO `user/review` — every origin carries explicit acceptance with verified probe evidence, and the judgment calls below are the architect's recorded decisions.

## Problem

`pkgs/id` has three signed-statement types, and two state the same contract in their docs — `documents.rs`: *"The builder and the decoder both apply them, so a signed document always passes them on receipt"*; `chain.rs` (`ChainExt::validate`): the same sentence for signed events. The third type, artifacts (`pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs`), never applied it to itself: its receipt gates `check()` (envelope) and `parsed()` (the four known kinds) each enforce some of the rules the crate's own producers and sibling validators obey and silently omit others — one omission per field, filed one at a time. Four filings in two days (three in the hours after pass 27 assessed #3146 as a single): #3146 (`friend_remove.requests` never inspected), #3187 (`home_declared.world_id` only `is_empty`-checked; duplicate endpoints pass), #3192 (`document`/`tag` text accepts non-NFC every sibling path refuses), #3196 (`check()` accepts a duplicated `after` frontier `chain.rs` refuses as `DuplicateAfter`).

## The rules (recorded decisions)

1. **Receipt is construction.** `parsed()` refuses a known-kind body no in-tree producer could build; `check()` refuses an envelope no legitimate signer could build — `Refusal::Forbidden` naming the rule, existing per-arm style. Unknown kinds untouched (stored, never applied, envelope-only — the module's deliberate forward-compatibility rule).
2. **A signed list names each thing once.** Duplicates refused, never silently deduped on receipt (the signed bytes are evidence; rewriting falsifies them and breaks the hash). Covers `after`, `friend_remove.requests`, and `home_declared` servers by endpoint. `sign_after` refuses a duplicated `after` at build time — the builder/decoder symmetry the sibling types document.
3. **Text in a signed body follows the crate's text rules.** `document.media_type`, `tag.name`, `tag.value` must be NFC via the same `unicode_normalization::is_nfc` the three sibling validators import. `world_id` gets `MAX_WORLD_ID_BYTES = 64` (aligned with `MAX_WORLD_NAME_BYTES`): 1–64 bytes, not whitespace-only, no control (Cc) or format (Cf) characters.

Field pins: `requests` ≤ `MAX_FRIEND_REQUESTS = 3` (the sole producer `Directory::friendship_requests`, directory.rs:1710–1721, structurally builds at most 3, sorted+deduped), each entry exactly 32 lowercase hex characters (the envelope-ID shape), no duplicates. Junk `requests` entries are not inert — `Directory::apply` extends the permanent `removed_requests` void guard with every string (directory.rs:1698–1705).

## Phases (adopt the origins — no parallels)

- **Phase 1 — List integrity:** #3196 + #3146.
- **Phase 2 — Text fields:** #3192 + #3187. Independent of Phase 1.
- **Phase 3 — Closing audit + contract statement:** filed this pass as a sub-issue, gated on Phases 1–2 (`status/blocked`). Field-by-field disposition table for every known-kind and envelope field; must explicitly disposition the `kind` string (unknown kinds), `document.content` internal strings, `prev`'s shape beyond `store()`'s position check, and full builder-side symmetry; writes the contract sentence into the `artifact.rs` module doc, where `documents.rs`/`chain.rs` already carry it.

## Alternatives rejected (in the doc)

Fixing the four independently (rules diverge — the drift is how the family arose: the artifact arms already mirror the sibling *caps* while missing the NFC half); validating at application time instead of `parsed()` (the log would still store and serve junk; `parsed()` is the single gate insert/open/pull all pass); normalizing on receipt (breaks hash/signature — refusal is the only honest outcome); folding into #3068 (JS/TS shape contract — different gate, different failure mode; cross-referenced, neither gates the other — this answers #3187's triage note); pinning the full `a-z0-9-_` world-name charset for `world_id` now (`WorldCore::new` accepts any non-blank ID — charset stays an open question, below).

## Risks (in the doc)

`ArtifactLog::open()` replays through the same gates, so tightened rules apply to stored chains — legitimate chains unaffected (no producer emits these shapes), refusal-on-open with the line named is existing behaviour; `MAX_FRIEND_REQUESTS = 3` is a producer invariant (constant and producer change together); Cf refusal in `world_id` is safe for machine-chosen IDs (`"home"`/`"lobby"` today).

## Open questions (in the doc, never as issues)

`world_id` charset (`validate_world_name`'s `a-z0-9-_`?) — needs evidence of how `declared()` consumers resolve it; `document.content` internal text NFC (chain's all-text rule vs the `documents.rs` media-type-only precedent); unknown-kind `kind`-string bounds vs forward compatibility; full builder symmetry for `sign`. The neighbouring plain-output rendering family (#2839, #3111, #3089, `world/util.rs` sanitizers) governs *printing* untrusted text, not storing it — not adopted; #3187's Cf pin is deliberately aligned with it.



## Acceptance criteria

- Phase 1 (adopting #3196 + #3146) and Phase 2 (adopting #3192 + #3187) land under the recorded rules: receipt (`check()` / `parsed()`) refuses with `Refusal::Forbidden` any envelope or known-kind body no in-tree producer could build; duplicates are refused, never silently deduped on receipt.
- The Phase 3 closing audit completes the field-by-field disposition table (including `kind`, `document.content` internal strings, `prev` shape, builder-side symmetry) and writes the receipt contract sentence into the `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs` module docs, alongside `documents.rs` / `chain.rs`.
- No legitimate producer output is refused: existing stored artifact chains replay through `ArtifactLog::open()` unchanged.

title: id(artifact): home_declared world_id gets only an is_empty check in parsed() — a 100 KB, whitespace-only, control- or bidi-bearing world_id is accepted and stored, and the same endpoint can be listed twice with different worlds

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## Problem

`SignedArtifact::parsed()` (`pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs`) validates every field of every known kind against an explicit bound — except `HomeServer.world_id` in a `home_declared` body. The `HOME_DECLARED` arm (artifact.rs:334-355) checks the account key, that the author is the account, that there are at most `MAX_HOME_SERVERS` (8) servers, and that each `endpoint` parses via `check_target` (an endpoint ticket or a bare node ID — a tightly bounded format). For `world_id` it checks only `!is_empty()` (artifact.rs:350-352).

So a signed `home_declared` artifact carrying a `world_id` that is:

- 100,000 bytes long,
- whitespace-only (`"   "` — non-empty, so it passes),
- bearing control characters or a newline,
- or bearing a bidi format character (U+202E),

is accepted by `parsed()`, stored in the author's artifact chain, and returned verbatim by `ArtifactLog::declared()` (artifact.rs:519-525) to every consumer. Duplicate servers are accepted too: the same endpoint listed twice, even with two different `world_id`s, passes — there is no duplicate check.

Every sibling field has a named bound: `Document.media_type` 1–128 bytes and content ≤ `MAX_DOCUMENT_BYTES` (artifact.rs:358-368), `Tag.name` 1–64 bytes and `Tag.value` ≤ 256 bytes (artifact.rs:376-380), `FriendRemove` keys checked as canonical account keys (artifact.rs:322-324). `world_id` is the odd one out in this arm. (The overall 1 MiB frame cap in `ArtifactLog::store` bounds the total artifact, not this field: a 100 KB `world_id` fits comfortably inside one frame.)

## Evidence (verified this run, main 99ae0339)

- Code read: `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs:346-353` — the only `world_id` check is `if server.world_id.is_empty()`. `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs:150-156` — `HomeServer { endpoint: String, world_id: String }`, no other validation anywhere (`grep world_id` across `pkgs/id/src`: no consumer sanitises it either).
- Laptop probe (`probe-2026-10-31-laneA-homeworld/` on the laptop under `~/git/fleet/`, path-dep on `pkgs/id`, `artifact.rs` sha256 `bdc11bbe…` identical on both clones) driving the real `SignedArtifact::sign` + `parsed()`:
  - control `"home"` → ACCEPTED
  - `""` → REFUSED (the one existing check)
  - `"home\nFORGED"` → ACCEPTED
  - control characters (`\u{1}`, `\u{7f}`) → ACCEPTED
  - U+202E bidi → ACCEPTED
  - `"   "` whitespace-only → ACCEPTED
  - 100,000-byte `world_id` → ACCEPTED
  - same endpoint three times (twice with different `world_id`s) → ACCEPTED, 3 servers

## Why it matters

A home declaration is how an account tells the network where its artifacts live; `declared()` feeds directory views and home-server selection. An unbounded, unsanitised `world_id` is stored and propagated exactly as signed — oversized values bloat every chain page that carries the declaration, and control/bidi-bearing values reach any present or future rendering of the declaration unchecked, the same stored-payload class the neighbouring fields' bounds exist to prevent. The duplicate-endpoint case makes the declaration ambiguous: two entries claim the same endpoint holds the account in two different worlds, and nothing downstream disambiguates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parsed()` refuses a `home_declared` whose any `world_id` exceeds a named bound (in line with the sibling fields, e.g. 64 bytes), is whitespace-only, or contains control/format characters — with tests pinning each refusal at the `parsed()` level.
- [ ] `parsed()` refuses a declaration that names the same endpoint twice (or the triage pins, with a test, why duplicates are harmless and which entry wins).
- [ ] Ordinary declarations (the existing tests' `"home"` / `"lobby"` world IDs, ≤ 8 distinct endpoints) parse exactly as today.

body:
# id(web): image uploads can dispatch against a destroyed editor view

## Fresh triage (2026-11-03; current main `b7ee423027cc90ad50819d7c54160896b9bfe175`)

The issue remains valid, but some earlier details are stale. `closeEditor()` destroys the ProseMirror view (`pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts:1039`) without invalidating in-flight uploads. `handleImageUpload()` later dispatches the image insertion at `pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.ts:289`; if that dispatch fails because the view was destroyed, it logs **“Insertion failed”** and then unconditionally dispatches placeholder cleanup at lines 301–303. A genuine failed upload also reaches that cleanup dispatch. `startImageUploadBatch()` does not consume the returned promise, so an exception from cleanup can become an unhandled rejection.

A previous deferred-fetch probe against main `69632f23977cf538441b85fc066ccb5d2adcfd54` reproduced the destroyed-view rejection. The upload-completion and `closeEditor()` paths relevant to this issue are unchanged through current main `b7ee423`; intervening edits in these files concern MIME lookup, shortcut handling, and WebSocket URL construction. This run verified the current code paths but did not rerun Vitest (the fresh worktree has no installed dependencies).

This is distinct from #1379: that issue concerns a live view whose document shrank, while this race targets a view that has been destroyed.

## Impact

Closing a document or switching documents while an image upload is pending can lose the insertion, log an insertion error for a successful upload, and produce an unhandled rejection. A real upload failure after teardown can also reject during placeholder cleanup.

## Follow-up scope

Add an editor-lifetime guard invalidated on view teardown, and check it before both insertion and placeholder-cleanup dispatches. Do not change upload endpoint behavior or the live-view insertion/order semantics.

## Acceptance criteria

- Deferred upload success after `view.destroy()` causes no dispatch against the destroyed view, no insertion-failure warning, and no unhandled rejection.
- Deferred upload failure after `view.destroy()` does not attempt placeholder cleanup against the destroyed view and causes no unhandled rejection; logging the genuine upload failure once is acceptable.
- Uploads completing on a live view still insert at the mapped placeholder position; failures still remove only their placeholder and log the upload failure.
- Add regression tests in `pkgs/id/web/src/image-upload.test.ts`; run `cd pkgs/id/web && bunx vitest run src/image-upload.test.ts` and the full web Vitest suite.

title: design(path-decode): one decode for path segments — a malformed percent-encoding is a 400, never a 500

labels.name: task/triage

body:
**Design (design-architect pass 20, 2026-10-30): one decode for path segments.** Full design doc: `files/designs/code-path-segment-decode.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. No `user/review` — the three origin issues carry explicit acceptance with verified reproductions, the repo already embodies the correct behaviour in two other stacks (below), and the one judgment call the origins left open (400 vs 404) is the architect's to record, which this design does.

## Summary

Four of this repo's HTTP services pull a caller-supplied key out of a URL path segment with `decodeURIComponent` — as an R2 key, a store key, an item/discussion id, a container name. The decode throws `URIError` on any malformed percent sequence, and in every service that throw becomes a server fault (escapes the handler, or an outer catch returns 500 with raw engine text). A malformed encoding is a client syntax error, not a server fault. Five sites, four apps, audited at origin/main `72545cb9` — the complete server-side inventory in `pm-stack/` + `pkgs/`:

| Site | Route | Today | Filed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:730` | `GET /discuss/<ref>` | `fetchHandler` has no catch → escapes `Bun.serve`, 500, no body | **no — Phase 1** |
| `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:842` | `GET /item/<id>` | same | **no — Phase 1** |
| `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts:176` | `GET /subjects/<subject>` | unhandled 500, no JSON body | #2693 |
| `pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/index.ts:364` | `GET /api/files/<key>` | outer catch → 500 `{error: String(e)}`, raw `URIError` text | #2633 |
| `pkgs/cf-container-hello/src/index.ts:104` | `GET /name/<name>` | no try/catch → Worker exception / 500 | #2720 |

The repo already does this right elsewhere: pavex decodes path params with a typed error on failure (`pkgs/pavex/libs/pavex/src/extract/route/route_params.rs:242`), and lab-ops-hub's own Python container strictly validates percent escapes and refuses malformed spellings (`pkgs/lab-ops-hub/container/app.py:733`, `_percent_decode_host`) — the TS services are the ones improvising.

## The contract (recorded in the doc)

1. **Malformed is 400, uniformly; unknown is 404; neither is ever a 500.** The origins each left "400 (or 404)" open; this design settles **400** — a misspelled escape and a well-formed miss are different facts, and one code across four apps is the point. The body is the app's JSON error shape naming the bad encoding, never raw `URIError` text. For the aggregator's HTML routes the 400 is JSON (its established bad-input shape: JSON 400s on its POST routes, JSON 404 for an unknown project id).
2. **Decode exactly once, at the route, through a per-app guard** — a `decodePathSegment(raw) -> string | null`-shaped helper in each app's own util module, called right after the route match; `null` → the 400; only the decoded value goes downstream. Decode-once semantics for well-formed input are unchanged (`%2F` still decodes inside values; `100%25` still yields the literal `100%`).
3. **The contract is shared, the code is per-app.** The apps deploy independently (separate package.json/lockfiles; two Workers, two Bun services; zero cross-app imports today). What is shared is the contract and its probe matrix, carried as tests in each app.
4. **The guard wraps the decode only.** Genuine downstream failures (R2/store errors) keep their current 500 behaviour; the helper is not a route-level try/catch.

**Shared probe matrix** (every phase's tests): malformed → 400: `%`, `%zz`, truncated escape (`uploads%2`), truncated UTF-8 (`%E0%A4%A`). Controls unchanged: plain segment, `%20`, the app's legitimate encoded form (`%2F` keys), `100%25` → literal `100%` (valid — must not 400), well-formed-but-unknown → existing 404.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 — the aggregator (new issue, filed with this design):** guard helper + both sites (`/discuss/<ref>`, `/item/<id>`) on the matrix. The unfiled app; two of the five sites. Independent.
- **Phase 2 — the two Workers (adopted origins #2633 + #2720):** each app's helper + matrix, with the uniform 400 sharpening their "400 (or 404)" acceptance. Independent per app.
- **Phase 3 — the projector + family truth-up (adopted origin #2693), gated on Phases 1–2 for the audit only:** projector's `/subjects/` route on the contract, then a closing grep audit over `pm-stack/` + `pkgs/` proving every server-side path-segment decode is guarded, recorded here.

Phases 2–3 file no new issues: the origins keep their evidence, acceptance, `queue/queued` labels and queued triage packets; they are sub-issues of this issue and carry agent notes recording the phase structure and the settled 400.

## Alternatives (recorded in the doc)

Fix the filed issues site-by-site and file a fourth (the aggregator was already missed by three sibling filings that knew the family existed, and per-site "400 or 404" guarantees divergence — loses); a shared decode package (deployment coupling for five lines, across two deployment worlds — loses); map `URIError` → 400 in outer catches (two apps have no catch; lab-ops-hub's returns raw text; a catch-all misclassifies downstream `URIError` bugs as client errors — loses); fall back to the raw segment on decode failure (silently changes the key — confusing 404 or a wrong hit — loses); 404 for malformed (contradicts the apps' own POST behaviour: malformed is 400, well-formed miss is 404 — loses).

## Open questions (in the doc, not filed)

Query-string values (`URLSearchParams` never throws — it silently substitutes U+FFFD; a different contract, no failure evidence today); browser-side decodes in `pkgs/id/web` (a UI-state surface, already #1494); an HTML error page instead of JSON 400 for the aggregator routes (only on a shown human-facing need).

---
*agent-note:v1 — filed by the repo design architect (dedicated code job, pass 20). Design doc and central register entry (`files/potential-projects.md`, status: proposed) accompany this issue.*

## Acceptance criteria

This design epic is complete when its three phases land:
- Phase 1: the aggregator's `/discuss/<ref>` and `/item/<id>` routes answer the probe matrix — malformed percent-encodings return a JSON 400 naming the bad encoding (never a thrown `URIError` / 500), well-formed segments behave exactly as before, unknown ids keep their current behaviour — via one guard helper in the aggregator, with the matrix as tests.
- Phase 2: #2633 and #2720 land with the uniform 400 for malformed encodings (sharpening their "400 (or 404)"), each through its own app's guard helper and the shared matrix.
- Phase 3: #2693 lands on the same contract, and the closing grep audit over `pm-stack/` + `pkgs/` (every server-side path-segment `decodeURIComponent` guarded) is recorded on this issue.
- No parallel per-site issues are filed for any phase; the adopted origins' triage records this structure instead of re-filing or re-scoping them.

**Design (design-architect pass 19, 2026-10-30): pm-dispatch launch pipeline, staged.** Full design doc: `files/designs/code-pm-dispatch-launch-pipeline.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. No `user/review` — the four origin issues carry explicit acceptance, the codebase already embodies each rule locally (issue-creation warnings, the lane-ledger guard, the success-only JWKS cache), and the judgment calls are recorded in the doc. One timing call *is* flagged for Drew's attention rather than labelled: **Phase 1 should land before the `dispatch.security.cab` tunnel hostname is added** (README's remaining step), since it closes the two boundary holes below.

## Summary

pm-dispatch (#2648, merged today) launches OpenCode sessions on the laptop from authenticated HTTP calls. Four bugs filed today — #2664, #2665, #2660, #2663 — are one per stage of its launch pipeline, with one root: the pipeline's stages and failure semantics were never stated, so each stage improvised. This design states them as three rules, generalising the patterns the code already uses locally:

1. **Boundary (Rule 1):** everything the caller supplies is validated to its declared shape and scope before any side effect, and authorization binds the request's *whole effect*. `parseJwt` rejects non-plain-object header/payload decodings (→ `AuthError`, 401 — today a raw `TypeError` → 500, `auth.ts:53-67,101`, server mapping `server.ts:376-379`). `directory` resolves by rule: absent/blank → `REPO_DIRS[repo]`; otherwise an absolute path that is the repo primary (`config.ts:25-30`) or inside it, else 400 — today `optString` passes it verbatim (`validate.ts:93-98`, `server.ts:180`) and `assertCallerRepo` binds only the `repo` field (`auth.ts:190-201`), so a repo-bound OIDC caller can launch a session anywhere on the laptop. The rule applies to all caller types uniformly.
2. **Commit point (Rule 2):** the claim PATCH is the launch's commit point. After it, steps are annotations: lane ledger (already guarded, `server.ts:148-158`), issue comment and labels (unguarded today, `server.ts:161-166`) become individually guarded — failure = response warning + task note ("launch unaffected" shape), never `cancelTask`, never 502, never a `dispatch launch failed` stamp on a live session (today: `wait:true` cancels the live session's task; `wait:false` mis-stamps it, #2660). Cancel + 502 remains correct only at/before the commit point. README's flow section gains the stage/failure table.
3. **Retryable init (Rule 3):** memoized async initialization caches success only. `ensureWorker()` (`queue.ts:137-158`, the service's only `??=` promise memo) clears its memo on rejection so the next launch retries the idempotent registration — the `fetchGithubJwks` success-only-cache pattern already in `auth.ts`. Today one transient 500 wedges every launch until restart (#2663).

## Phases — adopted origins, no parallel issues filed

- **Phase 1 — boundary:** #2664 + #2665. Independent. Gate for public exposure (see top).
- **Phase 2 — commit point:** #2660, including the README stage/failure table as its truth-up. Independent in code.
- **Phase 3 — retryable init:** #2663. Independent.

Each origin is a sub-issue of this issue, keeps its own queued triage packet, and carries an agent note recording this structure — triage must not re-file, re-scope, or split them.

## Alternatives (recorded in the doc)

Fix-the-four-bugs with no stated model (improvisation already diverging inside one function — loses); per-caller directory rules (two auth models for one field; a leaked bearer becomes launch-anywhere — loses to uniform rule + a recorded extra-roots question); directory exactly equal to the primary (kills legitimate inside-tree dirs); reorder annotation before the claim (impossible — it announces the claim); `TypeError`→401 mapping at the handler (wrong layer; parse-time shape check closes the class, including the post-signature payload hole); backoff/timer retry for `ensureWorker` (call-driven retry suffices for an idempotent upsert).

## Open questions (in the doc, not filed)

Extra roots allowlist if a real outside-tree worktree consumer appears; `/v1/tasks` inheriting the directory rule if it ever gains the field; annotation-failure visibility beyond warnings/notes; JWKS success-cache staleness on key rotation (pre-existing, noted only).

---
*agent-note:v1 — filed by the repo design architect (dedicated code job, pass 19). Design doc and central register entry (`files/potential-projects.md`, status: proposed) accompany this issue.*


## Acceptance criteria

- This design epic is complete when its three adopted phases land via their origin issues — no parallel issues are filed for the phases:
  - Phase 1 (boundary): #2664 + #2665 — caller input validated to declared shape/scope before any side effect; non-object JWT header/payload decodings return 401, not a raw-TypeError 500; `directory` resolves by the stated rule uniformly for all caller types.
  - Phase 2 (commit point): #2660 — post-claim annotation failures (lane ledger, issue comment, labels) degrade to response warnings + a task note; they never cancel a live session's task, never 502, and never stamp a live session as failed; the README flow section carries the stage/failure table.
  - Phase 3 (retryable init): #2663 — `ensureWorker()` memoizes success only; a rejected registration clears the memo so the next launch retries.
- Phase 1 lands before the `dispatch.security.cab` tunnel hostname is added (the timing call flagged in the design).
- Each origin issue keeps its own queued triage packet and records this structure in an agent note; triage does not re-file, re-scope, or split them.

body:
## Finding

Two PRs in the same 2026-10-28 batch disagree about whether `codedb.snapshot` is backed up, and the daily review report now states the wrong one:

- PR #1740 added `nixos/home/laptop-untracked-review.sh`. For an untracked file over 20 MiB in the `.openclaw` repo it annotates backup coverage (current main 541578ae, `laptop-untracked-review.sh:47-51`): paths under `tmp/*` or `cache/*` are reported "NOT covered by openclaw-backup (excluded dir)", and **every other path** is reported "covered by openclaw-backup".
- PR #1767 (merged after #1740) added `codedb.snapshot` to openclaw-backup's exclusions — `nixos/home/openclaw-backup.sh:136`: `--exclude='./codedb.snapshot'` (header comment :14: "regenerable code-index snapshot — not tracked in git and not backed up").

So when the untracked `codedb.snapshot` in `~/.openclaw` exceeds 20 MiB, the daily review reports it as "covered by openclaw-backup" when the backup deliberately excludes it.

## Why it matters

The review report is the routing decision for too-big-for-git files: "covered" means the file is left untracked on the assumption the backup holds it. For `codedb.snapshot` that assumption is false. The file is regenerable, so the data-loss stakes are low — but a coverage report that affirms coverage the backup script denies undermines trust in every other line of the same report, and the next excluded path added to `openclaw-backup.sh` will silently inherit the same wrong annotation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `laptop-untracked-review.sh`'s NOT-covered case names `codedb.snapshot` alongside `tmp/*` and `cache/*` (or the coverage annotation is derived from openclaw-backup's actual exclude list instead of a hard-coded pair).
- [ ] A stubbed/fixture run of the review over a `.openclaw` tree containing a >20 MiB `codedb.snapshot` reports it as NOT covered, while a >20 MiB ordinary file still reports covered.

Phase 3 of design #2576 (aggregator ingest, fail-closed). Design doc: `files/designs/code-aggregator-ingest-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. **Gated on Phase 1** (the `validate.ts` primitives) — `status/blocked` until it lands. Independent of Phase 2.

## Scope

Put the extractor and mapper boundaries on the shared primitives from Phase 1 of #2576:

- `quota-gather-map.ts`: `entryFromResult`, `entryFromFileExport`, `entryFromTurso` range-check percents against their limit and reject negative/non-finite counts instead of publishing them as live data (#2571, #2568, #2553); the file-export adapter's window check returns the retained unparseable outcome for a null window element or non-string window name instead of throwing (#2551).
- `saas-extract.ts`: the export document is type/range-checked — negative `used`/`limit`/`billedUsd` refused, a non-string `measuredAt` cannot pass the freshness gate (#2508). Supabase addon pricing: an unpriced selected addon is unparseable, never measured $0; negative amounts refused (#2492).
- Quota extractors validate their date anchors as real calendar dates (#2470 Claude/Meta reset dates, #2383 ClinePass measured-date anchor) — an impossible date marks the entry unparseable and retains the previous read, never discards or fabricates.
- `sources/github-billing.ts`: items validated per element — one impossible date or negative amount drops that item, not the month (#2493).
- `sources/opencode.ts` / `sources/jules.ts`: wire containers validated (`data` arrays, keeper state); bad elements dropped and counted — no throw discarding the source, no fabricated `undefined`-id rows (#2543, #2531); the fleet-feed registry check in #2539's path validates its containers the same way.
- `cloudflare-export`: bucket enumeration fails closed — a 500/malformed response produces an error document, never `status: ok` with `r2Buckets: []`; pagination goes past 100 buckets (#2574).

## Named scope rule (from the design)

For each of #2383 #2470 #2492 #2508 #2551 #2553 #2568 #2571 #2493 #2531 #2539 #2543 #2574: if still open when this phase starts, this phase closes it with evidence; if already closed per-site, verify its guard uses `validate.ts` (convert if it hand-rolled) — never re-fix a landed fix.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every function named above validates via `validate.ts` primitives; malformed input yields the contract outcome for its boundary (retain / drop-and-count / refuse), never a throw, a fabricated row, or live out-of-range data.
- An impossible date in any extractor marks only its own entry unparseable; sibling pools' reads are unaffected.
- Probe-matrix tests cover each converted boundary with its issue's repro shape.
- Verification runs in CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox).

🤖 Design-architect pass 18 — agent note: phase of design #2576; the decisions are recorded there and in the design doc. Do not re-derive them in triage; flag genuine blockers on #2576 instead.

body:
# aggregator(quota-extract): ClinePass extractor's measured-date anchor is never validated — an impossible measured date or a huge "resets in" offset silently discards the pool's whole read, and a Feb-30 anchor rolls into March

## Summary

`extractClinePass` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` anchors both relative resets to the read's "Measured" timestamp: `base = Date.parse(dateTimeCDT(measured[1], measured[2]))` and `rel(d, h) = new Date(base + (Number(d) * 24 + Number(h)) * 3_600_000).toISOString()`. Nothing validates the anchor or the offsets:

- The `Measured` capture is shape-only (`(\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}) ~(\d{2}:\d{2})`). A month-13 date or a `99:99` time makes `Date.parse` return `NaN`; `new Date(NaN).toISOString()` then throws `RangeError` inside `rel`, `extractQuotaPools`' per-pool try/catch maps the throw to `raw = null`, and **the pool's entire read — including the already-matched 5-hour/weekly/monthly percentages — is silently discarded** for the shell "No current read" note.
- A Feb-30 measured date does not throw: `Date.parse` rolls it over to March 2, so both resets are computed from a phantom anchor that never existed (see probe: resets land on 2026-03-08 / 2026-03-14).
- The "resets in" offsets are unbounded `(\d+)`: `99999999999d` overflows the Date range, `rel` throws, and the whole read is discarded the same way; `200000d` (~548 years) is accepted verbatim and emitted as a `resetsAt` in the year 2574.

## Evidence (verified this run, main 5a34fa70)

Laptop probe driving the real `extractQuotaPools` (probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-29-clinepass-rel/probe.ts` on the laptop, Bun 1.4.2; the laptop copy of `quota-extract.ts`/`derive.ts` is byte-identical to main 5a34fa70 by sha256), minimal ClinePass section, `now = 2026-10-29T12:00:00Z`:

| input | ClinePass pool result |
|---|---|
| control: Measured 2026-10-25 ~04:48, resets 5d 23h / 11d 15h | windows 10/26/69%, resetsAt 2026-10-31T08:48Z / 2026-11-06T00:48Z ✅ |
| Measured **2026-13-25** ~04:48 | **windows [], "No current read" shell** ❌ |
| Measured **2026-02-30** ~04:48 | windows kept, but resetsAt **2026-03-08 / 2026-03-14** — anchored to phantom Mar 2 ❌ |
| Measured 2026-10-25 ~**99:99** | **windows [], shell** ❌ |
| weekly resets in **99999999999d** 23h | **windows [], shell** ❌ |
| weekly resets in **200000d** 23h | weekly resetsAt **2574-05-26** accepted verbatim ❌ |

File:line (main 5a34fa70):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts:182-195` — `extractClinePass`: shape-only Measured capture (:184), unvalidated `Date.parse(dateTimeCDT(...))` base (:189), unbounded `rel` arithmetic + `toISOString()` (:190).
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts:349-358` — `extractQuotaPools` per-pool try/catch maps any extractor throw to the shell pool, silently and totally.

## Why it matters

The quota view is a human-written document, and ClinePass is a dashboard-only source with no API fallback — when its read vanishes, the hub shows "No current read" with no log line and no way to tell a typo'd measured date from a genuinely missing read, and the stewardship rotation loses the pool's percentages for that cycle. The Feb-30 case is worse than a drop: it invents reset dates a week-plus away from the real ones. This is the same fail-soft contract the module header promises ("renders with its identity and a 'no current read' note instead of vanishing or inventing numbers") — the percentages were successfully read, so discarding them over a bad *reset anchor* is the failure; the reset, not the read, is what is invalid.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage pins the rule for `extractClinePass` (expected: validate the Measured capture as a real calendar date/time — e.g. the `isCalendarDate` discipline already used in derive.ts — and treat an invalid anchor or an out-of-range relative offset as `resetsAt: null` for the affected windows, keeping the matched percentage windows; a plausible bound for the offsets, e.g. ≤ 366d / ≤ 8784h, is triage's to pin).
- [ ] Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts` (the ClinePass test home): month-13 and 99:99 measured stamps and a `99999999999d` offset keep the 10/26/69% windows with `resetsAt: null`; a Feb-30 measured stamp never anchors resets in March; the existing control case (2026-10-25 ~04:48 → 2026-10-31 / 2026-11-06) is unchanged.
- [ ] No change to `extractQuotaPools`' per-pool try/catch semantics for genuinely unmatched sections (shell note still renders when no read matches at all).

Filed by new-issue-creator-code-a (lane A), run 2026-10-29 12:05 CDT. Dedup: #2196 is `monthDayTime` (Codex / OpenCode Go / Command Code reset months) — a different helper and different call sites; its fix does not touch `extractClinePass`'s base/rel code. #2197 is `dateTimeCDT`'s UTC-5-vs-CST offset — the string builder, not this validation gap. #2206/#2264/#2194 are the shape-only-date pattern in saas-extract / snapshot-records / charges-collect, different modules and consumers, filed separately by the same convention.

Follow-on from the key-recovery investigation for #2060 (deliverable: PR #2278, `doc/2026-10-29T11-28-18Z_investigation_key_recovery_hosted/`).

## Slice 1 — documented, passphrase-wrapped key export/import

The investigation's §11 lists eight buildable slices. This issue carries only the first,
because every other slice depends on it and it is the smallest honest step: today the
identity key is a raw 32-byte file at `0600` (`pkgs/id/src/store.rs:58-190`, `KEY_FILE` in
`src/lib.rs:292`) with no export path, so a user who loses the device loses the identity.

Scope:
- `id key export` / `id key import` producing a versioned envelope: format header with
  KDF id + parameters (Argon2id), AEAD ciphertext of the identity secret key.
- No server involvement: the file is the user's to store. The server never sees plaintext
  or the passphrase.
- Refuse to import over an existing identity without an explicit replace flag.
- Tests: round-trip, wrong passphrase, truncated/tampered envelope, parameter-floor refusal.

Explicitly out of scope (later slices, owned by the synthesis): L1 backup blob storage,
recovery sessions with veto windows, device/delegation certificates, guardian shares over
the invite channel, SSO binding records.

Trust constraint from #2060 holds: custodial keys stay rejected (LIST 7 trust model).

Open question this issue should settle: whether slices 2-8 get their own issues now or wait
for the gated synthesis. Sequencing is the synthesis's call, not this issue's.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `id key export` / `id key import` produce/consume a versioned envelope (KDF id + Argon2id parameters in the header, AEAD ciphertext of the identity secret)
- [ ] Tests pass: round-trip, wrong passphrase, truncated/tampered envelope, parameter-floor refusal
- [ ] Import over an existing identity refuses without an explicit replace flag
- [ ] No server involvement: plaintext and passphrase never leave the user's machine

title: codex-proxy: exec transports have no turn deadline — a hung codex exec child hangs the request forever and is never killed

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/codex-proxy
labels.description: bin/codex-proxy.mjs fleet proxy

body:
## Problem

`bin/codex-proxy.mjs`'s exec transports have no turn deadline. `runCodexOnce` (`bin/codex-proxy.mjs:803`, spawn at `:815`) returns a promise that settles only from the child's `close` handler (`:921`) or a synchronous spawn throw — there is no timer anywhere in the function. Both exec call sites await it directly: the warm-resume attempt (`:1219`) and the cold full-history run (`:1242`). If the spawned `codex exec` child hangs — alive but never finishing its turn (upstream stall, a CLI waiting on something, a wedged session resume) — the HTTP request hangs forever, the child process is never killed, and the promise never settles. The only recovery is the client giving up; even then nothing in `runCodexOnce` kills the child on client disconnect (no `res.on('close')` hook reaches it — `onSpawn` only registers the child for the caller's bookkeeping).

Every sibling path in the same file, and in the sibling proxies, is bounded:

- The app-server transport in this same file: connect timeout 10s (`:504`), JSON-RPC timeout 30s (`:635-641`).
- `bin/claude-code-proxy.mjs`: `TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 * 1000` (`:55`) applied to its spawned turns (`:455-461`), with a SIGKILL escalation 3s after the deadline (`:480`).
- `bin/muse-proxy.mjs`'s warm path: `WARM_TURN_TIMEOUT_MS = 300 * 1000` (`:300`, applied `:585-587`).

The exec fallback is precisely the path taken when the bounded app-server path has already failed — i.e. when the backend is already misbehaving — and it is the one path with no bound at all.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `b2b885b9`)

Sandbox probe with a fake `codex` binary (`$HOME/.local/bin/codex` under a scratch HOME; the fake answers `debug models` with garbage so the static catalog floor is used, and sleeps 60s for any other invocation), `CODEX_PROXY_TRANSPORT=exec`:

- Proxy log: `Spawning: .../codex exec --json --skip-git-repo-check ... -m gpt-5.6-luna ...` — the request reached `runCodexOnce`'s spawn.
- `curl -X POST /v1/chat/completions` (non-streaming): **no response after 8s** (curl killed by `timeout 8`, exit 124, 0 response bytes) while the fake child (`sleep 60`) was still running. Nothing in the proxy would have ended the request before the child's own exit at 60s — and a truly hung child never exits.

Dedup: `gh` searches for `codex-proxy exec timeout`, `runCodexOnce`, and `codex-proxy hang` (open + closed) return no covering issue. Adjacent but distinct: #2097/#2100/#2102 are the same no-timeout class in design-code-proxy, clef-proxy, and antigravity-ls-proxy (HTTP fetch / RPC paths in other files); the muse-proxy exec path has the same defect and is filed separately this run.

## Why it matters

code-queue workers and OpenCode sessions route real coding turns through this proxy. One hung `codex exec` child wedges its request indefinitely and leaks a process; repeated hangs accumulate children and stall every caller queued behind them, with no log line or error to act on. The fallback path exists for resilience — unbounded, it converts a backend stall into a permanent proxy-side hang.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `codex exec` turn that exceeds a named deadline (consistent with the house convention, e.g. claude-code-proxy's / muse-proxy's 300s turn timeout, or a `CODEX_PROXY_*` env override parsed strictly) is terminated (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after a short grace) and the request settles with an error result through the existing `done({ok:false, ...})` shape.
- [ ] The deadline applies to both `runCodexOnce` call sites (warm resume and cold run); the app-server transport's existing timeouts are unchanged.
- [ ] A client disconnect before the deadline also kills the exec child (no orphaned `codex exec` processes).
- [ ] Regression tests in `bin/codex-proxy.test.mjs` style: a fake child that never exits is killed at the deadline and the request errors; a fake child that completes normally is unaffected.
- [ ] No change to the success/failure semantics judged from `turn.failed` / exit code (#676/#680 behavior preserved for children that do exit).

body:
Implements the first layer of the owner decision on #185 (comment 6486250456, Drew, 2026-10-28).

## Model
- `tag.clear` becomes a MARKER event: anyone may post one; posting is not gated; a clear never itself deletes anything.
- The default view (the query paths most consumers use) treats a tag as cleared ONLY when the marker's poster is in an appropriate role for that tag: the tag's author, or a group admin of the group the tag belongs to.
- Markers from anyone else persist on the log and remain visible to explicit/audit queries, but are ignored by the default view.

## Acceptance
- Author-posted clear hides the tag in the default view; group-admin-posted clear hides it; any other poster's clear does not hide it in the default view but the marker is retained and queryable explicitly.
- No deletion path is reachable from tag.clear alone (deletion is the separate policy layer, filed separately).
- Tests cover all three poster roles plus the retained-marker case.

Refs #185. This closes the confirmed-at-HEAD gap (tag.clear had no author/admin gate at all): under this model the ungated post is safe by construction, because effect is role-aware at read time.

## Acceptance criteria
- Author-posted tag.clear hides the tag in the default view; group-admin-posted clear hides it; any other poster's clear does not hide it in the default view.
- Markers from non-authoritative posters persist on the log and remain visible to explicit/audit queries.
- No deletion path is reachable from tag.clear alone (deletion is the separate policy layer, #2091).
- Tests cover all three poster roles plus the retained-marker case.

body:
**No Drew direction decision needed** — origin #1935's acceptance is explicit; the judgment calls (multi-select refused to old hosts rather than flattened; `-32042` production gated on a declared, undeliverable URL question; the script hook stays a documented question) are recorded in the design doc with their reasons.

## Summary

Design originated by the repo design architect (pass 11, 2026-10-28) from origin umbrella #1935 (relocated from dezren39/nix#214) and its compare-register rows ELI-04 / ELI-09 / ELI-12 / ELI-21 in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/elicitation.md`, audited against current main `26221fcc`. Full design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-elicitation-era-edges.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

Audit verdict per row:

- **ELI-04 — OPEN.** `Question.paramsFor` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go` ~L465-507) strips `mode`/`elicitationId` per era but never rewrites `requestedSchema`: a 2025-11-25 upstream's rich enums (titled/untitled, single/multi-select, SEP-1330) reach a 2025-06-18 host verbatim, and a strict old host rejects the whole `elicitation/create`.
- **ELI-09 — LANDED (register is stale).** `Client.capabilities` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpclient/modern.go` ~L71-84) declares `elicitation.url` whenever a server-request handler is installed, in both eras; the pool installs that handler for every upstream connection (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/pool/pool.go:508`); `elicitModeDeclared` gates url questions on the negotiated revision. #1935's ELI-09 acceptance bullet is met — what remains is the register truth-up (Phase 3), not code.
- **ELI-12 — OPEN, both directions.** `-32042` appears nowhere in `internal/mcpclient` or `internal/daemon` (grep-verified): an upstream's `-32042` propagates as an opaque `rpcError` and the call fails — no URL flow, no retry. Server-side, conformance gap `elicitation-server-must-return-32042` (`internal/conformance/coverage_clientfeatures.go`) stands against the 2025-11-25 MUST.
- **ELI-21 — OPEN, deliberately NOT a phase.** `docs/elicitation.md` §5.2 designs an `onElicit` script global and marks it "NOT BUILT" itself; #1935's acceptance offers the alternative ending "or the broker-only path is documented as the deliberate design". The unsettled core is routing precedence (broker `Route` sends credential/consent questions to a human on purpose — may a script handler answer those?) plus the call-vs-script correlation `docs/protocol.md` ~L379-382 names. Recorded as an open question in the design doc with the evidence assembled; no phase filed for it.

## Proposal (recorded decisions)

- **Phase 1 — enum downgrade at the rendering seam.** In `paramsFor`, for a pre-2025-11-25 peer: titled single-select (`oneOf[{const,title}]`) → `enum`+`enumNames`; untitled/legacy shapes pass through. Multi-select has no 2025-06-18 representation (form schemas are flat primitives — no array type), and flattening would change the answer's type (`string[]`→`string`) so the upstream's own validation rejects what mcpx elicited — so a multi-select question is *not sendable to that peer* (the `Sendable` refusal pattern url mode already uses) and stays with the era-less broker. No answer back-mapping is needed for downgraded single-selects (host answers the `const`, the value in both eras).
- **Phase 2 — client-side `-32042`: complete the circuit.** On a connection negotiated at 2025-11-25, a `-32042` call error's `data.elicitations` (url-mode + `elicitationId`, per the spec MUSTs) are opened as broker URL questions through the existing `elicitViaBroker` path — full URL shown, consent, completion notification already handled (`internal/daemon/hooks.go` ~L57-68) — and on completion the original call is retried exactly once. Decline/expiry/second `-32042` surface as errors; malformed `data` passes the original error through. Era-scoped to exactly the revision that defines the code (2026 reserves it; pre-2025-11-25 doesn't have it).
- **Phase 3 — server-side `-32042` + truth-up + #1935 closure.** Produce `-32042` only when all hold: host negotiated 2025-11-25, host declared `elicitation.url`, a URL question from that call is pending, and it cannot be delivered inline; `data.elicitations` lists exactly the blocking questions with ids. Never for form, never when inline delivery works, never at 2026. An unhandled upstream `-32042` is relayed only to url-declared hosts. Plus: register rows ELI-04/09/12 updated to as-built (ELI-09 landed, with evidence), gap `elicitation-server-must-return-32042` retired or recorded partial, and completion evidence on #1935 against every acceptance bullet — closing it iff all are met, ELI-21's bullet answered by the documented-question record.

Alternatives considered and risks are in the design doc (flattening multi-select — rejected, corrupts answer type; downgrading at broker intake — rejected, era translation belongs at the era boundary; generic all-era `-32042` handling — rejected, era discipline; unbounded retry — rejected; filing `onElicit` as a phase — rejected this run, genuine open question).

## Phased breakdown

- **Phase 1:** enum downgrade for pre-2025-11-25 hosts (`internal/mcpserver/conn.go`: `paramsFor` rewrite + multi-select `Sendable` refusal). Filed as a sub-issue of this issue, triage packet enqueued.
- **Phase 2:** client-side `-32042` — broker URL questions + one retry (`internal/mcpclient` call path + `internal/daemon`). Independent of Phase 1 in code. Filed as a sub-issue, triage packet enqueued.
- **Phase 3:** server-side `-32042` production + register truth-up + #1935 closure. Gated on Phases 1–2. Filed as a sub-issue (`status/blocked`), triage packet enqueued.

Open questions stay in the design doc, not as issues: ELI-21 routing precedence + script correlation; ELI-05 defaults across the same boundary (Phase 1 triage checks the downgrade interaction); mcpx-originated URL elicitation; ELI-11's unexercised completion emitter.

Distinct from neighbours: #1753 (capability gating — its `CanElicit` shape reading is a reused seam), #1675 (broker storage/UI hygiene), #1481/#1484 (schema validation of answers), #1834 (sampling relay).

---
🤖 `agent-note:v1` — filed by the design-architect job (pass 11, developing-today/code) per the design doc above. Origin: #1935 (ex dezren39/nix#214). Audit basis: main `26221fcc`, 2026-10-28.

## Acceptance criteria
- Phases 1–3 are filed and implemented: #2078 (enum downgrade / multi-select withheld), #2079 (upstream -32042 handling + single retry), #2080 (-32042 production + register truth-up).
- Register rows ELI-04, ELI-09, ELI-12, ELI-21 in pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/elicitation.md match as-built state (ELI-09's staleness corrected).
- Umbrella #1935's acceptance is met and #1935 is closed via Phase 3 (#2080).

title: mcpx(daemon): task-store Open failure silently falls back to in-memory — durability claimed by PR #1575 can vanish with no log line

body:
## Finding

`daemon.Server.taskStore()` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/ops.go`, current main `77918e0f`) opens the durable SQLite task store and **drops the error unconditionally**:

```go
if s.paths.State != "" {
    dbPath := filepath.Join(s.paths.State, "tasks.db")
    if store, err := tasks.Open(dbPath); err == nil {
        s.tasks = store
    }
}
if s.tasks == nil {
    s.tasks = tasks.New()   // in-memory fallback, no log, no record
}
```

There is no log call anywhere in the function. The daemon has a logger and uses it for exactly this kind of degradation elsewhere (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/server.go`: `opts.Logger.Printf("elicitation disabled: %v", berr)`), but a failed task-store open is completely silent. Because creation is `sync.Once`, the fallback is also **sticky for the life of the process**: a transient failure at first use downgrades the daemon permanently, with no retry.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/1575 (merged, commits `508fb8be`, `516df392`) — "one durable task store across MCP and /v1, Phase 1 of #1554". It wired this store into the MCP surface (`internal/cli/root.go`: `a.daemonStore = srv.TaskStore()`, called eagerly at daemon startup; `internal/cli/serve.go`: `srv.TaskStore = a.daemonStore`) and **closed the conformance gap** `ext-tasks-durable-before-response` in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/spec/conformance-matrix.md` on the strength of this store ("the task store is an in-memory map; a task does not survive the daemon" → now marked tested via `TestInjectedStoreKeepsMCPTasksAcrossReopen`).
- `tasks.Open` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/tasks/tasks.go:148-166`) returns real errors: `os.MkdirAll` failure on the state dir, `initDB` schema-exec failure, and `loadTasksFromDB` query failure — i.e. an unwritable state directory or a **corrupt `tasks.db`** both reach the silent branch.
- Verified on current main `77918e0f` (2026-10-28): the function is byte-identical; no logging, no metric, no status surface records the fallback. Deduped against open + closed issues 2026-10-28: no issue covers this fallback (the silent in-memory fallback for `/v1` predates #1575; #1575 is what extended it to MCP tasks and based a conformance closure on it).

## Why it matters

When the open fails, three things go wrong at once, all invisibly:

1. Every task already persisted in `tasks.db` becomes unreachable — the daemon never opened the file, so MCP and `/v1` both report those tasks as unknown.
2. Every new task is memory-only and evaporates on daemon restart — precisely the failure the conformance matrix now says is covered.
3. Nobody can diagnose it: no log line names the path or the error, so the symptom ("tasks disappeared") has no on-box evidence trail.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A failed `tasks.Open` in `taskStore()` is logged once via the daemon logger (`s.logger`), naming the db path and the underlying error, before the in-memory fallback is installed.
- [ ] A regression test pins it: a daemon server whose `tasks.db` cannot be opened (e.g. corrupt file contents or an unusable state path) falls back **and** emits the log line; the successful-open path stays silent-or-unchanged and still returns the one shared store instance.
- [ ] The fallback remains a fallback (daemon keeps serving) — this issue asks for visibility, not a hard failure.
- [ ] Existing task-store tests keep passing (`internal/daemon/taskstore_shared_test.go`, `internal/mcpserver/tasks_shared_store_test.go`).
