title: id(didit): count_periods Week branch panics at calendar boundaries — unchecked NaiveDate arithmetic (residual of #7766)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`count_periods` in `pkgs/id/src/didit/eval.rs` (lines 395–402 on main `b64288a567`) computes the `Period::Week` branch with unchecked `chrono` date arithmetic:

```rust
let monday = today - Duration::days(i64::from(today.weekday().num_days_from_monday()));
let start = midnight(tz, monday)?;
let end = midnight(tz, monday + Duration::days(7))?;
let previous_start = midnight(tz, monday - Duration::days(7))?;
```

`NaiveDate + Duration` / `NaiveDate - Duration` **panic** on overflow (chrono implements them as `checked_add_signed(...).expect("`NaiveDate + TimeDelta` overflowed")`). For a `now` in the first or last week of the representable calendar, `monday + 7 days`, `monday - 7 days`, or the Monday offset subtraction itself runs off the end of `NaiveDate`'s range and the evaluator panics — in debug *and* release builds.

This is the residual door of #7766. That fix converted the `Period::Custom` branch to checked arithmetic with the comment that "the Day/Week branches get [OutOfRange] from the calendar" — true for `Day`, which uses `succ_opt()`/`pred_opt()` (eval.rs:388–394), but not for `Week`, which uses the panicking operators. `evaluate` is documented as a pure function that "can be replayed for any past instant" (eval.rs module docs / `didit/mod.rs`), so a calendar-boundary `now` must answer `EvalError::OutOfRange`, never panic.

The same unchecked-operator pattern survives once more in the same file: `resolve_local` (eval.rs:573) computes `naive + Duration::hours(1)` when a local time falls in a DST gap; `NaiveDateTime + Duration` panics the same way at the top of the representable range. Audit it in the same pass (a checked add that falls through to the existing UTC fallback is sufficient).

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main `b64288a567`)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-didit-week-overflow` (laptop): the Week/Day branches and their helpers copied verbatim from `eval.rs` (file md5 `592058f89673b9202523c586c80b36fc`), built against chrono 0.4.45 (the version in `pkgs/id/Cargo.lock`), run in **release** mode:

```
NaiveDate::MAX=+262142-12-31 weekday=Mon max_now=8210266833600
NaiveDate::MIN=-262143-01-01 weekday=Thu min_now=-8334601185600
control week ordinary: Ok(((1699833600, 1700438400), (1699228800, 1699833600)))
control day  ordinary: Ok(((1699920000, 1700006400), (1699833600, 1699920000)))
week now=MAX-date noon: PANIC
day  now=MAX-date noon: Err(OutOfRange)
week now=MIN-date noon: PANIC
day  now=MIN-date noon: Err(OutOfRange)
```

Same instants, same function: `Day` returns `OutOfRange`, `Week` panics at both calendar ends. Ordinary-input controls pass for both branches.

## Why it matters

- A panic in the pure evaluator aborts whatever projection/app pass called `evaluate` — the exact failure mode #7766 fixed for `Custom`, one branch over.
- The #7766 fix comment now actively misdocuments the Week branch as calendar-guarded, so the residual is likely to survive future audits that trust the comment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `count_periods` `Period::Week` uses checked date arithmetic (`checked_add_signed` / `checked_sub_signed` or `succ_opt`-style stepping) and returns `EvalError::OutOfRange` when the week's Monday, its +7d end, or its −7d previous start is unrepresentable.
- [ ] `resolve_local`'s `+ Duration::hours(1)` shift is checked or otherwise panic-free at the representable boundary.
- [ ] Regression test mirroring `custom_period_extreme_anchor_is_out_of_range_not_a_panic_or_wrapped_window`: a Week-period expectation evaluated at a `now` on `NaiveDate::MAX` and on `NaiveDate::MIN` returns `Err(EvalError::OutOfRange)` (test fails — panics — pre-fix); an ordinary Week expectation still evaluates.
- [ ] The #7766 comment in the `Custom` branch is corrected if it still claims the Week branch is calendar-guarded.
- [ ] `cargo test` for the `didit` module passes.

body:
## Problem

`didit::eval::count_periods` computes a `Period::Custom` window with unchecked `i64` arithmetic, so an expectation whose custom period carries an extreme `anchor` either panics (debug builds) or silently evaluates the wrong window (release builds), instead of returning `EvalError::OutOfRange` — the error the module already uses for instants the calendar cannot represent.

## Evidence (main `20d4b36898c0db1402101fb00808bc7049e196b7`)

`pkgs/id/src/didit/eval.rs:400-408`:

```rust
Period::Custom(custom) => {
    let length = i64::try_from(custom.length_seconds).map_err(|_| EvalError::OutOfRange)?;
    if length <= 0 {
        return Err(EvalError::OutOfRange);
    }
    let index = (now - custom.anchor).div_euclid(length);   // :405 overflow
    let start = custom.anchor + index * length;              // :406 overflow
    let end = start + length;                                // :407 overflow
    Ok(((start, end), (start - length, start)))              // :408 overflow
}
```

The input is reachable: `PeriodCustom { anchor: i64, length_seconds: u64 }` (`pkgs/id/src/didit/body.rs:321`) is decoded from a peer-supplied CBOR body, and the only validation `Period::check` applies is rejecting a zero length (`body.rs:389`). Any non-zero length with any `i64` anchor — including `i64::MIN` / near-`i64::MAX` — passes `Expectation::check` (`body.rs:559`) and reaches `evaluate()` → `count_verdicts` → `count_periods`, which runs before any calendar conversion for this branch.

Verified this run with a laptop probe (`~/git/fleet/probe-didit-custom-overflow`, the branch's arithmetic verbatim; control case correct):

- Debug (overflow checks on): `anchor = i64::MIN, length = 86400, now = 0` panics with "attempt to subtract with overflow"; `anchor = i64::MAX - 100, length = 1000, now = anchor` panics with "attempt to add with overflow".
- Release (wrapping): the first case silently returns the phantom window `(-30592, 55808)` — a 1970 window that has nothing to do with the anchor — and the second returns `end < start` (end wraps to `-9223372036854774909`), which `count_verdicts` then silently skips via its `end <= start` guard, so the expectation produces no verdict and no error.

## Why it matters

`evaluate()` is a pure function whose contract is that bad instants produce `EvalError::OutOfRange`; every sibling branch (Day/Week) goes through `local_date`/`midnight`, which enforce exactly that. The Custom branch is the one door where a crafted or corrupt expectation body — the tracker ingests expectation events from household peers — can crash the evaluating process in debug builds, or, worse, quietly fabricate/drop verdict windows in release builds with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- `count_periods` for `Period::Custom` uses checked arithmetic (`checked_sub` / `checked_mul` / `checked_add`) and returns `EvalError::OutOfRange` on any overflow, for the current window and the previous window alike.
- Regression tests in `pkgs/id/src/didit/tests.rs` (or eval tests): extreme anchors (`i64::MIN`, near `i64::MAX`) and extreme lengths produce `Err(OutOfRange)`, not a panic and not a wrapped window; ordinary custom periods keep producing the same windows as today.
- Existing didit tests pass.

labels.description: pkgs/atlas-search (Atlas search service + atlas-embed)

body:
# atlas-search + fleet-search: `parse_cursor` panics on malformed cursors instead of returning 400

## Evidence

`parse_cursor` decodes the client-supplied results-paging cursor by slicing
the string at byte offsets with no length or ASCII-hex gate:

- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs:1723-1735`
- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs:1723-1735` (byte-identical twin)

```rust
let bytes: Result<Vec<u8>, _> = (0..cursor.len())
    .step_by(2)
    .map(|i| u8::from_str_radix(&cursor[i..i + 2], 16))
    .collect();
```

The cursor arrives from the HTTP request (caller at `server.rs:1632`,
`Some(c) => parse_cursor(c)?`) in the results-paging handler. The connection
is served on a per-connection thread (`server.rs:1980`) with no
`catch_unwind` around routing, so a panic kills the thread and drops the
connection instead of producing the function's own documented
`400 "malformed cursor"` error.

Verified this run on the laptop at main `151c8e7e1c` with a probe crate
(`~/git/fleet/probe-cursor-hex`, function copied verbatim, minimal
`ServerError` stub):

- control: valid `format_cursor(42)` roundtrip → `Ok(42)`
- control: even-length non-hex `"zzzz"` → `Err(malformed cursor)`
- control: empty string → `Err(malformed cursor)`
- odd-length hex (valid cursor minus its last character) → **PANIC**
  (slice index out of range at the final pair)
- single character `"a"` → **PANIC**
- hex pair prefix + multibyte input (`"6162a\u{e9}"`) → **PANIC**
  (slice at a non-char-boundary byte offset)

This is the same ungated-hex-parser class as #7750 (fixed in #7757 for
`local_claims::hex_bytes`): the sibling parsers there carry an
`is_ascii_hexdigit` gate per #2517; `parse_cursor` in both copies has none.
`u8::from_str_radix` also accepts a leading `+`, so even where a malformed
pair does not panic it is not validated as hex before decoding.

## Why it matters

Any client (or any corrupted/proxied request) that sends an odd-length or
non-ASCII `cursor` query value crashes its connection thread with a panic
instead of receiving the designed 400. Panics on untrusted input are a
robustness/DoS surface and produce panic noise in server logs; the cursor
is explicitly documented as opaque client-held state, so malformed values
are expected input, not an internal invariant.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both copies (`atlas-search` and `fleet-search` `server.rs`) refuse a
      cursor whose length is odd or that contains any non-ASCII-hexdigit
      byte, returning `Err(bad_request("malformed cursor"))` — no panic on
      any input, including multibyte UTF-8.
- [ ] Valid cursors produced by `format_cursor` still roundtrip to the
      same offset in both copies.
- [ ] Regression tests cover at least: odd-length hex, single character,
      multibyte/non-boundary input, even-length non-hex, and the valid
      roundtrip — in both crates (or in the crate(s) where the handler
      lives, with the twin kept byte-identical in behavior).
- [ ] No other behavior of the results-paging handler changes (offset
      beyond end still returns its existing 400).

title: bin(check-opencode-metered-providers): extra arguments silently ignored — a second config path is never checked, unknown flags pass

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/check-opencode-metered-providers
labels.description: bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs metered PAYG provider guard

body:
## What

`bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs` — the guard that fails CI when a metered/PAYG provider is selected without an explicit exception (#2288) — reads only `process.argv[2]` as the config path and silently ignores every later argument:

```js
// bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs:348 (main)
const configPath = resolve(process.argv[2] ?? DEFAULT_CONFIG);
```

There is no unknown/extra-argument check anywhere in the script. A second config path, a misspelled flag, or a nonexistent second path all pass without a word, and the success line names only the first file — so an invocation that looks like it checked two configs (or a config plus an option) actually checked one.

## Verified this run (laptop, real script, main 4af4ee8354, md5 9f6353d950afd810272bd5ab60dcaf65)

Probe dir: `~/git/fleet/probe-metered-argv` on the laptop. Fixtures: `good.jsonc` (plan routes only) and `bad.jsonc` (`"model": "deepseek/deepseek-chat"` — a PAYG selection the guard exists to reject).

| Run | Observed |
|---|---|
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs bad.jsonc` (control) | exit 1, names the deepseek selection |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc` (control) | exit 0, "guard passed" |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc bad.jsonc` | **exit 0, "guard passed: …/good.jsonc" — bad.jsonc never read** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc --bogus` | **exit 0 — unknown flag silently ignored** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs good.jsonc nonexistent.jsonc` | **exit 0 — the second path is never even opened** |
| `node check-opencode-metered-providers.mjs bad.jsonc good.jsonc` (order control) | exit 1 — only the first argument is ever inspected |

## Why it matters

- This guard is the automated enforcement of the no-PAYG routing rule. A green run that silently skipped the config it was asked to check is worse than no run: the success line ("Metered-provider config guard passed: <path>") gives no hint that a second target was dropped.
- The CI invocation (`.github/workflows/opencode-config-guard.yml:28`) passes exactly one path today, so this is an operator/manual-run and future-workflow-expansion hazard, not a live CI bypass — the same extra-positional class as #7555 (confirm-charges-surfaced), in a different script with different argv code.
- Distinct from #6953 (the guard workflow's missing triggers) and #4694 (its entry-point check, fixed): neither touches argument handling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argument after the single config path (a second positional, an unknown flag, a joined `--flag=value`) fails fast with a usage error and a non-zero exit, before the config file is read.
- [ ] Zero or one positional argument keep working exactly as today: no args checks `DEFAULT_CONFIG` (`.opencode/opencode.jsonc`); one arg checks that file; the pass/fail messages and exit codes are unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.test.mjs` (subprocess-level, since `main()` is not exported) cover: extra positional naming a failing config, an unknown flag, and the two controls (single good config passes, single bad config fails).
- [ ] The existing fixture suite still passes (`node --test bin/check-opencode-metered-providers.test.mjs`).

title: id(local_claims): hex_bytes is the one pkgs/id hex parser the #2517 gate missed — it panics on misaligned multi-byte input and accepts '+'-pair spellings

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/in-progress
labels.description: Queue worker lifecycle state

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: work/self-assigned
labels.description: An agent grabbed this item directly, outside the queue

body:
## Summary

`pkgs/id/src/local_claims.rs`'s private `hex_bytes` (lines 247–257) is the one hex parser in pkgs/id that the #2517/#3457 hardening missed: it has no ASCII-hexdigit gate and decodes by slicing `&text[index..index + 2]` at byte offsets. Two consequences, both verified this run on main `4af4ee8354`:

1. **Panic instead of the designed error.** A `local-claims.jsonl` line whose `id`/`author`/`subject` field has even byte length but contains a multi-byte character at a misaligned offset panics with `byte index 2 is not a char boundary` instead of returning the function's `"{text:?} is not hex"` error. `LocalClaims::open` (local_claims.rs:69–97) is explicitly built to turn a malformed line into an `InvalidData` io error naming the file and line number; the panic escapes that handling and crashes the caller (`LocalEvents` open at local_events.rs:233) on a corrupt/hand-edited/sync-mangled claims file.
2. **Non-canonical `+` spellings accepted.** `u8::from_str_radix` accepts a leading `+`, so `"+a"` decodes as `0x0a` — exactly the dual-spelling problem #2517 fixed in `directory.rs::hex_to_array` and `directory_auth.rs::hex_bytes`, and that `invites/invitation.rs::parse_hex32` and `seitan/derive.rs::InviteId::from_hex` also gate against. Every sibling parser gates on `bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit())` first; this one does not.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/src/local_claims.rs:247-257` — ungated slicing decoder (only guard is an even-length check).
- Sibling gates for comparison: `pkgs/id/src/directory.rs:2597-2610`, `pkgs/id/src/directory_auth.rs:370-385`, `pkgs/id/src/invites/invitation.rs:124-135`, `pkgs/id/src/seitan/derive.rs:66-76`.
- Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-localclaims-hex`, exact copy of the function, main `4af4ee8354`):
  - `hex_bytes(&"0a".repeat(32))` → `Ok([10, …])` (control)
  - `hex_bytes(&"zz".repeat(32))` → `Err("… is not hex")` (control)
  - `hex_bytes(&"+a".repeat(32))` → `Ok([10, …])` (non-canonical spelling accepted)
  - `hex_bytes("€a")` (4 bytes, even) → **PANIC** `end byte index 2 is not a char boundary; it is inside '€' (bytes 0..3)`

## Why it matters

The claims file is on-disk state read at open time; robustness there is the difference between a named, line-numbered error and an unexplained crash. The missing gate is also a consistency hole in a hardening pass (#2517/#3457) that was supposed to cover the repo's hex decoders.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No input to `hash_from_hex`/`author_from_hex` can panic: decoding works on bytes (e.g. `as_bytes().chunks(2)` + `from_utf8`) or is fully gated before slicing.
- [ ] New unit tests in `local_claims.rs` cover: a `+`-pair input, a multi-byte-character input of even byte length (misaligned), and the existing valid/odd-length/non-hex cases.
- [ ] `cargo test -p id local_claims` passes.

`saas-extract.ts` caps six extracted text fields with raw UTF-16 slices. Same defect class as #7694/#7711/#7725/#7731/#7736 — in the SaaS extractor, which none of those fixes covered. #7741 (filed today for the three 240-char diagnostic caps) states the other remaining slices in `pm-stack/aggregator/src` are "dates/hex/slugs over ASCII-safe alphabets, or the event writers already tracked in #7740" — that audit missed this module: its inputs are quota-view prose and collector-export detail strings, not ASCII-safe alphabets.

## Evidence

Raw slice sites (main `752357c139ba`):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:84` — `readsOf`: dated-read text `line.slice(0, 400)` (line is quota-view prose)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:94` — `conflictsOf`: conflict line `line.slice(0, 400)`

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:1065` — `applySupabaseExport`: metric `note: parts.join(" ").slice(0, 600)` (parts include the export doc's `live.detail`)

## Verification (this run, laptop primary @ `752357c139ba`)

```
straddle conflicts[0] | len: 400 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
straddle payg.note    | len: 300 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true

straddle usageNote    | len: 600 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true

json stored contains lone escape: true
```

Every straddle case ends in a lone `\ud83d`; exact-fit controls are intact, so this is the cut, not the inputs.

## Why it matters

These fields exist to be read when reconciling subscriptions and usage: dated reads, recorded conflicts between sources, PAYG estimate notes, and live-export metric detail.  
  ```ts
  body: value.body.trim().slice(0, 20_000),
  ```

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-roadmap-events-surrogate/probe.ts` (laptop), importing the real `validateNewRoadmapAnnotation`:

# aggregator(comments): author and body caps split surrogate pairs — validateAuthor/validateNewComment raw-slice at 120/20,000, bypassing the #7694/#7711 capUnits guard

## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts` caps dashboard-comment text with raw `slice`, none of it pair-safe:

- lines 96–98 — `validateAuthor`: `id.slice(0, 120)`, `label.slice(0, 120)`, `sessionId.slice(0, 120)`
- line 132 — `validateNewComment`: `body: b.body.trim().slice(0, 20_000)`

This is the #3178 defect class that #7694 fixed for `actions.ts` `cleanText` and #7711 fixed for `markResult` via the `capUnits` helper (actions.ts:292, module-private): an astral character straddling the cap is dropped whole. The comments boundary was not audited in either fix — and it matters more here, because `validateAuthor` is the SHARED author validator: `actions.ts` (lines 154, 329) and `roadmap-annotations.ts` (lines 55, 80) both import it from `comments.ts`, so the pair-safe actions store still persists split-pair author ids/labels through this door, and roadmap annotations inherit the same defect.

The values are persisted, not just displayed: comments are written to the comments JSON store (`CommentsStore.persist`, comments.ts:259–264, `JSON.stringify` + atomic rename), so a split pair is stored as a lone `\ud83d` and any UTF-8 round-trip (file read, HTTP response) replaces it with U+FFFD.

Note on fix shape: `capUnits` cannot simply be imported from `actions.ts` — `actions.ts` imports `validateAuthor` from `comments.ts`, so that direction would create a module cycle. A local helper in `comments.ts` (or a shared helper in `validate.ts`, which `comments.ts` already imports) avoids the cycle.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ f9dfb4cfa5, real module md5 567b6272246f4fcf519fe3213b490389)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-comments-surrogate/probe.ts` (bun, imports the real `comments.ts`):

```
label straddle | len: 120   | lone high surrogate at end: true  | utf8 roundtrip changes: true
label control   | len: 120   | lone: false | roundtrip changes: false
id straddle     | len: 120   | lone: true  | roundtrip changes: true
body straddle   | ok: true   | len: 20000 | lone: true  | roundtrip changes: true
body control    | ok: true   | len: 20000 | lone: false | roundtrip changes: false
json stored label last unit: d83d
```

- Straddle cases: label/id = 119 × `x` + 😀 + tail → capped value is 120 units ending in lone `\ud83d`; comment body = 19,999 × `z` + 😀 + tail → 20,000 units ending in lone `\ud83d`.
- Controls: pair fully inside the cap (118 × `x` + 😀; 19,998 × `z` + 😀) → value intact, round-trips cleanly.
- The JSON persistence round-trip preserves the lone surrogate as `\ud83d` in the stored record.

Dedup: searches for "validateAuthor surrogate", "comments surrogate", "DashAuthor slice", and "surrogate" (open + closed) return no issue for these caps; #7694/#7711 cover `actions.ts` text fields only, #7725 covers `activity.ts` summary caps — neither touches the shared author validator or the comment body cap.

## Why it matters

- Author labels and comment bodies are operator/user text — an emoji at the wrong offset permanently corrupts the stored author identity or comment body (U+FFFD in the persisted store, and in every action/annotation record that carries the same author).
- Because `validateAuthor` is shared, this is the residual door for the two fixes that landed this morning: #7694/#7711 made action text pair-safe while the author on those same records can still be split.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four caps in `comments.ts` (author id/label/sessionId at 120, comment body at 20,000) are surrogate-pair-safe: an astral character straddling the cap is dropped whole, never split (mirroring `capUnits` semantics from #7711), without introducing a module import cycle.
- [ ] Regression tests in the aggregator suite pin the straddle case for the author label (or id) cap and the comment body cap, plus an exact-fit control (pair fully inside the cap stays intact); the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The existing aggregator test suite stays green.

# aggregator(activity): summary caps split surrogate pairs — watchdog/kaneo writers and the record-time cap raw-slice at 500, bypassing the #7694/#7711 capUnits guard

## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/activity.ts` caps activity summaries with raw `slice(0, 500)` at four sites, none of them pair-safe:

- line 120 — `watchdogDeliveries`: `summary: item.title.slice(0, 500)`
- line 196 — `kaneoChangeDeliveries` (appeared): composed summary `.slice(0, 500)`
- line 207 — `kaneoChangeDeliveries` (moved): composed summary `.slice(0, 500)`
- line 485 — the ingestion record: `summary: (d.link ? `${d.summary} — ${d.link}` : d.summary).slice(0, 500)` — a second cap applied at persist time, so even a pair fully inside a writer's 500 can be split when the ` — link` suffix pushes the boundary into it.

This is the #3178 defect class that #7694 fixed for `actions.ts` `cleanText` and #7711 fixed for `markResult` (both merged 2026-11-08) via the `capUnits` helper (actions.ts:292, not exported): an astral character straddling the cap is dropped whole. The activity writers were not audited in either fix. Summaries are persisted through `events.record` (line 478-486) into the activity stream and rendered on the board, so a split pair is stored, not just displayed: the stored summary ends in a lone high surrogate, and any UTF-8 round-trip (file write, HTTP response) replaces it with U+FFFD.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ f9dfb4cfa5, real module md5 1512d949c61186d2cdec988887197654)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-activity-surrogate/probe.ts` (bun, imports the real `activity.ts`):

```
watchdog straddle | len: 500 | last unit: 0xd83d | lone high surrogate at end: true  | utf8 roundtrip changes: true | roundtrip last: 0xfffd
watchdog control  | len: 500 | last unit: 0xde00 | lone high surrogate at end: false | utf8 roundtrip changes: false
kaneo straddle    | len: 500 | last unit: 0xd83d | lone high surrogate at end: true  | utf8 roundtrip changes: true | roundtrip last: 0xfffd
```

- Straddle case (watchdog): title = 499 × `x` + 😀 + tail → `watchdogDeliveries` summary is 500 units ending in lone `\ud83d`.
- Straddle case (kaneo): card title padded so the pair straddles the composed summary's 500 cap → same lone `\ud83d` ending.
- Control: 498 × `x` + 😀 (pair fully inside the cap) → summary intact, round-trips cleanly.

Dedup: searches for "activity surrogate", "watchdogDeliveries", and "kaneo summary" (open + closed) return no issue for these caps; #7694/#7711 cover `actions.ts` only (filed and fixed this morning; this is the residual door in the sibling module).

## Why it matters

- Watchdog titles and Kaneo card titles are operator/user text — emoji in a card title at the wrong offset permanently corrupts the stored activity record's summary (U+FFFD in the persisted stream), the same failure #7694/#7711 were filed for in `actions.ts`.
- The record-time cap (line 485) makes the writers' own caps insufficient as a fix location: the persist path must be pair-safe too.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All four summary caps in `activity.ts` (lines 120, 196, 207, 485) are surrogate-pair-safe: an astral character straddling the 500-unit cap is dropped whole, never split (mirroring `capUnits` semantics from #7711).
- [ ] Regression tests in the aggregator suite pin the straddle case for the watchdog writer, a kaneo writer, and the record-time cap, plus an exact-fit control (pair fully inside the cap stays intact); the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The existing aggregator test suite stays green.

- `note` = `"n" × 1999 + "😀" + "tail"` → stored `resultNote` is exactly 2,000 code units, last code unit `0xd83d` — same lone surrogate, same U+FFFD round-trip corruption.
- The persisted actions file literally contains the `\ud83d` escape.
- Control: `note` = `"n" × 1998 + "😀"` (exactly 2,000 code units, pair fits) is stored intact, length 2,000.

## Why it matters

This is the exact defect class fixed three times now in sibling boundaries (#3178 for pm-dispatch, #7694 for action payloads): a cap counted in UTF-16 code units silently halves an astral character, and the lone surrogate is then persisted and delivered to downstream consumers — UTF-8 encoders corrupt it to U+FFFD, and strict parsers (e.g. Rust `serde_json`) reject unpaired surrogates outright. - Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/actions.test.ts`: an astral character straddling both the `byRun` (200) and `note` (2,000) caps is stored whole-or-dropped, never halved; an exact-fit pair at the cap is kept whole; the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.

title: opencode-claimant(poll): candidate filter reads progress.stage, but the checkpoint verb writes progress.last_checkpoint.stage — ~60 recorded yields invisible per fire, stale stages offered unsafely

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

labels.name: app/fleet
labels.description: pkgs/fleet multicall binary + platform crates

body:
## Symptom

Two yield encodings disagree, and `poll.py` reads the one the checkpoint verb does not write:

| writer / reader | field |
|---|---|
| `repo-queue checkpoint` (Turso backend, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs:1759`) | `progress.last_checkpoint.stage` |
| `poll.py` `is_candidate()` (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py:123`) | `progress.stage` |

`verb_checkpoint` merges `{"last_checkpoint": {"stage": <stage>, "at": <ts>}}` into `progress`; it never writes a top-level `progress.stage`. Every recorded yield therefore lands in `last_checkpoint.stage`, while the candidate filter reads a field that holds lane work stages (`verified`, `parked`, `claimed`, `awaiting_ci`, …) and is absent on most rows.

Measured on the laptop, same snapshot, claimed opencode-lane rows with no `progress.session_id`:

| fire (UTC) | `progress.stage` ∈ {handed_off, launch_failed} | `last_checkpoint.stage` ∈ {handed_off, launch_failed} |
|---|---|---|
| 2026-11-08T12:55Z | 0 | 78 |
| 2026-11-08T13:04Z | 1 | 67 |
| 2026-11-08T13:06Z | 1 | 67 |
| 2026-11-08T13:36Z | 1 | 57 |

Across all non-terminal statuses for lane `opencode`, 541 rows carry `last_checkpoint.stage == "handed_off"` and 119 of those also carry a top-level `progress.stage == "handed_off"`; the other 339 have no `progress.stage` at all.

## Two failure directions

1. **Under-offer (the standing symptom).** A real recorded yield is invisible unless the lane happened to also write a top-level `progress.stage`, so the claimant's gate reads 0–1 candidates and ends the fire quietly — on the same snapshot in which ~60–90 tasks are genuinely handed off. This is the mechanism behind #6533.
2. **Unsafe over-offer (the dangerous direction).** A stale top-level `progress.stage == "handed_off"` keeps a task a candidate after its lane has resumed work. Task 8067 on 2026-11-08:

```json
"stage": "handed_off",           // written 2026-11-04T12:39:59Z, never updated
"stage_at": "2026-11-04T12:39:59.900381Z",
"last_checkpoint": {"stage": "verified", "at": "2026-11-08T13:00:32Z"}
```

The lane verified the task four days later; the strict filter still offers it for launch. Launching into a task whose claiming lane is mid-work is exactly the double-execution defect #4490 hardened against. On the 2026-11-08T13:36Z fire the same shape appears on tasks 10501 (`parked_awaiting_prereqs`), 10606 (`probe_lane_check`), 12787 (`pr_opened`) and 12866 (`awaiting_ci`).

## Why this matters now

`poll.py`'s docstring and `prompt.md` both describe the yield as `progress.stage == handed_off`; the database never stores it there. Until the two agree, candidate discovery is either blind (today's steady state) or unsafe (when a lane's old `progress.stage` is stale). This is independent of, and invisible behind, the `repo-queue list` table defect (#7325 / #7375): even with the transport fixed (which #7673 partially addresses), the filter compares the wrong field.

## Suggested fix (pick one, not both)

- **A. Read the recorded field.** `is_candidate()` accepts the yield from `progress.last_checkpoint.stage` (and keeps accepting `progress.stage` for rows written by older paths), then rejects any row whose live `progress.stage` names a later work stage that is not itself a yield. Update `test_poll.py`'s fixtures to the shape the verb actually writes.
- **B. Also write the top-level field.** Have `checkpoint_task` stamp `progress.stage` alongside `progress.last_checkpoint.stage`, so one field is authoritative for both writer and reader. This needs a backfill decision for the ~500 existing rows.

A is contained in the claimant and testable offline; B changes the queue contract for every consumer of `progress.stage` (the lane prompts already read it for resume), so it is the larger change.

## Acceptance

- A task whose only yield marker is `last_checkpoint.stage == "handed_off"` is a candidate.
- A task whose `last_checkpoint.stage == "verified"` (or any non-yield stage) is not a candidate even when a stale `progress.stage == "handed_off"` is present.
- Both directions pinned in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_poll.py`.

## Evidence

Found 2026-11-08 by the opencode-claimant scheduled fire (shadow mode, #3026 slice 1), while reproducing candidate discovery over the queue-broker `/list` verb. Also recorded as a comment on #6533 at 2026-11-08T13:22Z. Read-only: no task was claimed, bound, launched, prompted or deleted.

Related: #6533 (parent symptom), #7325 / #7375 (transport read), #5508 (stale ledger binding), #4490 (double-execution guard).

## Acceptance criteria

- The claimant poll filter and the checkpoint verb agree on ONE canonical yield encoding (the filter reads the field the verb writes, or the verb writes the field the filter reads — one of the two, documented in code).
- A regression test built from a checkpoint-written task row proves recorded yields (handed_off / launch_failed) are seen by the candidate filter.
- No stale stage is offered as fresh: the filter's staleness behaviour for old yield records is explicit and tested.
- On a live snapshot, the filter's yield count reconciles with the `last_checkpoint.stage` count (the ~60-per-fire discrepancy in the issue is closed).

title: Fix #7693: mcpx(source): a symlink loop entry aborts the whole @dir: resolve — ELOO

labels.name: source/dispatch
labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
Implement GitHub issue #7693 in developing-today/code: mcpx(source): a symlink loop entry aborts the whole @dir: resolve — ELOOP is neither skipped like a dangling link nor pinned like a permission error

## Problem

In mcpx's directory source walk, one symlink loop entry makes the whole `@dir:` resolve fail — while the two neighboring bad-link cases are tolerated:

- a **dangling** symlink is skipped (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go:174-180`: `os.Stat` failure is continued past only when `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)`, comment "A dangling link has no regular target to read");
- a **directory** cycle (a dir symlink pointing back to an ancestor) is skipped by the `os.SameFile` ancestor guard in the same walk (`source.go:152-157`);
- a symlink **loop** (a link to itself, or two links pointing at each other) makes `os.Stat` fail with ELOOP ("too many levels of symbolic links"), which is neither of the above: `source.go:181` returns the error and the entire directory resolution aborts with zero files read — including every healthy regular file sitting next to the loop.

A loop link, like a dangling link, has no regular target to read. The current split — tolerate a missing target and a directory cycle, but let a loop target deny the whole source — is an untested gap, not a pinned decision: the pinned cases in the shipped tests are dangling-skip (`source_test.go:245` `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), directory-cycle-safety (`source_test.go:191`), and permission-error propagation (`source_unix_test.go:73` `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget`, which pins EACCES as a returned error and must keep behaving that way). No test covers the ELOOP case.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main 8a0a1c0ceac8)

Probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-mcpx-eloop` on the laptop: the real `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go` copied verbatim (md5 `768194633188160a349eafd555defe53`, identical to the file on main) into a standalone module, driven through the exported `source.Resolve("@dir:"+root, …)`:

- control (regular.ts + dangling.ts → missing): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — matches the shipped pin;
- self-loop (regular.ts + loop.ts → loop.ts): **fails** — `reading …/loop.ts: stat …/loop.ts: too many levels of symbolic links`, zero files returned;
- pair loop (regular.ts + a.ts → b.ts, b.ts → a.ts): **fails** the same way at a.ts, zero files returned;
- control (directory back-link to the root itself): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — the ancestor guard tolerates the directory cycle.

So one stray looped link (easily produced by a bad `ln -s` pair or a tool that links a directory's contents into itself at file level) takes down every launcher/prefix/hook that reads its source from that directory, with an error that names the link but gives no way to keep the healthy remainder.

Related: closed #1727 covered non-regular files in directory sources (FIFO/socket/symlink-to-directory); this is the distinct remaining Stat-error class for file entries. The Go source lives only in this repo (`pkgs/mcpx`); dezren39/darwin-nix only wraps/launches the built mcpx, so no cross-repo set applies. Found via a pr-diff-review REVIEW-FINDING on PR #3744 that was left as decide-and-test material; verified independently this run before filing.

## Why it matters

`@dir:` sources feed mcpx launchers, prefixes, and error hooks. A single looped symlink — which the directory-cycle guard already proves the walk intends to survive at directory level — currently denies the whole source instead of just the unreadable entry. Robustness here should be uniform: an entry with no readable regular target is skipped (dangling, loop), while genuinely informative errors (permission) still surface, per the existing pin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A directory containing a self-loop symlink or a mutually-looping symlink pair, plus at least one regular file, resolves successfully and returns exactly the regular files (the loop entries skipped), for both the self-loop and pair-loop shapes.
- [ ] Regression tests for both loop shapes land in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source` (mirroring the style of `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), and fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The pinned permission behavior is unchanged: `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget` still passes — only the ELOOP class changes disposition, not EACCES or other Stat errors (or, if the fix deliberately widens/narrows which Stat errors skip, the disposition of each class is named in the PR and the affected pins updated with rationale).
- [ ] The existing source suite (`go test ./pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/...`, or the package's normal CI route) is green with the new tests.


Rules from the repo owner: (1) Deliver the finished work as a pull request in this run; put "Fixes #7693" in the PR description so the issue closes on merge. (2) Cover the whole set in the one PR: if the issue names a set (files, subcommands, cases), fix every member, and batch any directly related dependency updates into the same PR — never one PR per item or per dependency. (3) Run the relevant tests and checks before opening the PR. (4) Merging is permitted but never required: merge only when checks pass and you are reasonably certain the PR is correct and low-risk — otherwise leave it open, and state your confidence and what a human should check. (5) If you hit a genuine blocker (missing credentials, a decision only the owner can make), stop and say exactly what is needed in your final summary instead of guessing. (6) Detached-session clause: never use the `question` tool — if you hit a question, record it and the default you chose in your final summary and keep working.

body:
Implement GitHub issue #7683 in developing-today/code: ci(atlas-search): worker vitest suite (14 tests pinning #6937/#6982 + the DO cache-key oracle) run by no workflow — the #6788 cache Worker's regression suite verified nowhere

## Problem

`pkgs/atlas-search/worker/test/` — the vitest suite for the atlas-search cache Worker (the per-query Durable Object search cache from #6788: query-key canonicalisation, embedding-space validation, auth gate, embed + fan-out, DO cache hit) — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. It runs only when a human runs `npm test` in that directory by hand.

## Evidence (verified this run at main `0798a9881e`)

- Suite: 3 files, 14 tests — `test/key.test.ts` (5: `normalizeQuery` trim/NFC/case rules plus a hand-built canonical-digest oracle for the DO cache key in `src/key.ts`), `test/space.test.ts` (4: `validateEmbed` embedding-space consistency — pinned model, full width, dims/vector agreement, finiteness), `test/worker.test.ts` (5, via `cloudflare:test` SELF + fetchMock: health-open/search-gated auth, miss embeds + fans out once and the repeat is a byte-identical DO hit, the #6937 whitespace-only-query rejection on both routes, wrong-space embedding refused from the cache, the #6982 null search-service response reported as 502 not a raw TypeError).
- Hand run on the laptop in a probe copy (`~/git/fleet/probe-atlas-worker`, real worker tree copied verbatim): `npm ci` (the package ships a `package-lock.json`, unlike the github-ci Worker in #7674) then `npm test` → **3 test files / 14 tests passed**, repeated twice with the same result. The suite is green — it is simply never run by automation.
- Wiring search: `grep -rn "atlas-search/worker"` over `.github/`, root `flake.nix`, `lib/`, `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix`, `pkgs/atlas-search/default.nix`, `justfile` → **no hits**; `grep -rn "atlas-search"` over `.github/workflows/*.yml` matches only `fleet-search-parity-guard.yml`, which checks the Rust pyjson/render writers and never touches the Worker. `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix:51` sets `checks.default = atlas-search` (the Rust package) — no Worker test check. The only run instructions are manual: `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/README.md:49` (`npm test  # vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`).
- The pins are for live, recently-merged behavior: #6937 (merged 2026-11-07, whitespace-only query on GET /v1/cache/inspect) and #6982 (merged 2026-11-07, validated /v1/search response shape in `searchService`) both added their regression tests to `test/worker.test.ts` — verified by hand at merge time, verified nowhere since. `space.test.ts` is the Worker-side guard for the embedding-space consistency the #6060 series is building on (#7646/#7648, open).
- Sibling Workers show the house wiring pattern exists: `pkgs/id/hosted-worker` has `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml`; the github-ci Worker's unwired suite is filed as #7674 and the github-backup Worker's as #6085. This Worker — the one standing in front of every fleet search query, holding an indefinite result cache keyed by the digest `key.test.ts` pins — has neither a workflow nor a filing.

## Why it matters

A regression in `key.ts`'s canonical material silently changes every DO cache key (mass invalidation, or worse, cross-config serving — the exact failure `key.test.ts`'s "differs across query and across k" case guards). A regression in `validateEmbed` lets a foreign-model or truncated embedding into the cache and poisons results indefinitely (the cache has no TTL eviction policy yet, #6805). And the two most recent correctness fixes to this Worker (#6937, #6982) currently have regression protection that executes only on a human's laptop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow (house pattern, e.g. `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml` / `bin-tests.yml`: workflow_dispatch + path-gated push-to-main, main tier) runs the suite — `npm ci` + `npm test` (vitest) in `pkgs/atlas-search/worker` — and fails loudly if the suite files are missing, never a silent skip.
- [ ] The wiring demonstrably executes all 14 tests (run output reports 3 test files / 14 tests passing) on a change touching `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/**`.
- [ ] The suite passes via the wiring on main after the change lands.

Dedup (this run): title/keyword searches for `atlas` + "vitest", "atlas worker suite", "atlas-search worker" in title, and the three test filenames found no existing filing for this suite's wiring; #6879/#6937/#6982 are live-code defects in this Worker (two of them are what the suite pins), #6330 is PR-tier validation for the atlas-search **Rust** packages, #6805 is the cache eviction/invalidation follow-on, #7646/#7648 are the #6060 embedding-model slices.

body:
# aggregator(actions): cleanText caps can split a surrogate pair — a stored action field ends in a lone surrogate

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8a0a1c0cea`)

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts:289-292` — every user-supplied payload field of a dashboard action passes through:

```ts
function cleanText(v: unknown, max: number): string | undefined {
  if (typeof v !== "string") return undefined;
  const t = v.trim();
  return t === "" ? undefined : t.slice(0, max);
}
```

`slice(0, max)` counts UTF-16 code units. When an astral character (e.g. an emoji, 2 code units) straddles the cap, the stored value ends in a lone high surrogate. Call sites with caps: `reason` 2,000 (`actions.ts:336`), `text` 20,000 (`:334`), answer values 2,000 (`:376`), `optionId`/`questionId` 200 (`:349`/`:351`/`:363`/`:370`), `status` 60, `until` 64, and others (`:321`–`:450`). These values are persisted in the actions store (one JSON file, `PM_AGG_ACTIONS_FILE`) and consumed/rendered by the orchestration pass.

Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-actions-surrogate/probe.ts`, real `actions.ts` imported from the laptop primary, `validateNewAction` with verb `dismiss`):

- Input `reason` = `"x" × 1999 + "😀" + "tail"` (2,001+ code units) → validated `ok: true`; stored reason is exactly 2,000 code units and its last code unit is `0xd83d` — a lone high surrogate.
- `JSON.stringify` of the stored value ends `…\ud83d"` — the lone surrogate is carried into the persisted JSON.
- A UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip of the stored value differs from the original and ends in U+FFFD — any consumer that encodes the field to UTF-8 (file writes in other languages, GitHub bodies, Rust consumers, whose `serde_json` rejects unpaired surrogates) silently corrupts or refuses the field.
- Control: `"x" × 1998 + "😀"` (exactly 2,000 code units) is stored intact, length 2,000.

## Why it matters

This is the exact defect class fixed for pm-dispatch in #3178 (`validate.ts:319-328` keeps the cap but never leaves half a surrogate pair). The actions boundary was not given the same guard, so a dashboard user who pastes long text with an emoji at the cap boundary gets a silently corrupted reason/answer stored and delivered to consumers — and the corruption only surfaces downstream, far from the boundary that created it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cleanText` (or an equivalent shared helper) never returns a string ending in a lone high surrogate or beginning-of-cap lone low surrogate: when the cap would split a surrogate pair, the pair is dropped whole (cap becomes `max - 1` code units for that value), mirroring the #3178 fix in `pm-stack/dispatch/src/validate.ts`.
- The cap semantics otherwise stay identical: same maximum code-unit lengths, same trim/empty behaviour, non-straddling values byte-for-byte unchanged.
- Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/actions.test.ts` (or a sibling suite run by the aggregator test workflow): an astral character straddling at least the `reason` (2,000) and one small cap (e.g. `optionId` 200) boundary is stored whole-or-dropped, never halved; the new tests fail on the pre-fix code.
- Existing aggregator test suite stays green.

body:
## Problem

`.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh` — the contract test suite for `check-id-pr-checks.sh`, the flake-drift guard that gates every `pkgs/id` PR — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. The guard itself is live, but its own regression pins are verified nowhere.

## Evidence (verified this run at main `165b652488`)

- `.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh` (96 lines), header: "Contract tests for check-id-pr-checks.sh (#6881)". It pins, through the `ID_FLAKE_CHECKS_FILE` fixture hook: a well-formed list passes (including cosmetic trailing whitespace and CRLF line endings), a genuine unlisted check fails naming it, a genuine stale entry fails naming it, and a duplicated entry is reported as a duplicate, never as stale.
- Hand run on the laptop at main `165b652488`: `bash .github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh` → all 12 checks pass, ending `check-id-pr-checks.test.sh: all contract tests passed`, exit 0. The suite is green — it is simply never run.
- Wiring search: `grep -rn check-id-pr-checks.test` over `.github/workflows/`, `pkgs/id/flake.nix`, `pkgs/id/justfile`, `flake.nix` → no hits.
- The guard it tests is on the live PR path: `.github/workflows/id-check.yml:96` runs `.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.sh` in the guard job, and the workflow's `pull_request.paths` includes `.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.sh` — but not `.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh`, so even a change to the test suite itself triggers no run of it.
- Every sibling meta-suite in `.github/scripts/` IS wired: `check-workflows.test.sh` (workflow-lint.yml paths + a dedicated "Contract tests for the workflow validator" step), `check-fleet-search-parity.test.sh` (fleet-search-parity-guard.yml), `check-mcpx-fix-test.test.sh` (mcpx-fix-test-guard.yml), `check-production-line-limit.test.sh` (production-line-guard.yml), `id-bench-compare.test.sh` (id-bench.yml). This suite is the only unwired one.
- History: #6881 (closed) created this suite because the guard misdiagnosed malformed entries — duplicates read as "flake no longer defines it", whitespace/CRLF as unlisted+stale. Those exact misdiagnoses can silently return the next time the guard is edited, because nothing runs the pins.

## Why it matters

`check-id-pr-checks.sh` is the drift guard between the `pkgs/id` flake checks and `.github/scripts/id-pr-checks.txt`: a new flake check that is neither listed nor excluded fails the guard job by name instead of silently getting no PR coverage. If the guard's own parsing regresses (the #6881 failure class), id PRs either fail with misleading causes or — worse — the guard passes lists it should fail, and flake checks silently lose PR coverage. The contract suite exists precisely to pin that behavior; unwired, it is decorative.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow step runs `bash .github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh` on PRs that touch the guard or its tests (natural home: the guard job in `.github/workflows/id-check.yml`, before the guard step, following workflow-lint.yml's contract-test step pattern).
- [ ] `.github/scripts/check-id-pr-checks.test.sh` is added to `id-check.yml`'s `pull_request.paths` so a test-only change triggers the run.
- [ ] The wiring demonstrably executes the suite (its output reports "all contract tests passed"), never a silent skip.
- [ ] The suite passes on main after the wiring lands, and `check-workflows.sh` validation of the edited workflow stays green.

Dedup (this run): title/keyword search for `check-id-pr-checks.test` and the guard's wiring found no existing issue; #6881 (closed) created the suite and does not track its wiring. Sibling unwired-suite filings (#7619, #7597, #5942, …) cover different suites.

title: id(world_caps): parse_wants validates a last-wins collapse — duplicate keys bypass the version check and the 64-entry bounds (residual door of #6501/#6520)

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## Problem

`parse_wants` — the checked gate for a world program's `wants` document — parses with a bare `serde_json::from_str`, so duplicate object keys collapse last-wins before any of its checks run. It is the one program-output gate in `pkgs/id` that was not migrated to the duplicate-key-refusing helper built for exactly this class.

Evidence (main `0a27a7f19fab91b9489932a64fc03479f46bcba5`):

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:733` — `pub fn parse_wants(text: &str)`; `:738` — `let value: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(text).context("wants is not JSON")?;` Every check after this line (the `v` version check, the `MAX_WANTS_ENTRIES = 64` subscription/request counts at `:752`/`:771`, per-entry id/cap validation, args bounds) observes only the collapsed document.
- The sibling gate was migrated: `pkgs/id/src/world/mod.rs:1951-1953` — `parse_records` carries the comment "A duplicate key is a parse error (#6520): the caps below must see the document as written, never a last-wins collapse of it" and parses through `id_core::json_unique::parse_json_without_duplicate_keys` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/json_unique.rs:13`; design #6520, first landed for #6501). `pkgs/id/src/world_records.rs:274` uses the helper too. The module doc in `json_unique.rs` states the rule: "Every checked JSON gate in `pkgs/id` parses through this helper so no gate ever validates, counts, stores, or forwards a collapsed (last-wins) document."
- Callers: `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:662` and `:1209` feed program output (`plaza_wants`) through `parse_wants`. The program is sandboxed, untrusted code; its `wants` document decides which capabilities the host grants and executes.

## Verified reproduction

Probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-wants-dupkeys` (byte-identical copies of the real `world_caps.rs` and `json_unique.rs`, md5 `b1b98dcde602952c946e9213b86d0797` / `eecf91f884b0f833a019c03c8920f190` at the main commit above; controls pass):

- Control `{"v":2}` → `Err(unsupported wants version 2)`; control 65 subscriptions → `Err(wants has more than 64 subscriptions)`; control valid document → `Ok`. The gates work on documents without duplicate keys.
- `{"v":2,"v":1}` → `parse_wants = Ok` — the version gate never sees the `v:2` the document as written declares first; it validates only the collapsed `v:1`. (Reverse order `{"v":1,"v":2}` errors — the verdict depends on key order, i.e. on the collapse, not on the document.)
- `{"subscribe":[<65 entries>],"subscribe":["players"]}` → `parse_wants = Ok(subscribe=1)` — the 64-entry bound counts only the collapsed second array; the 65-entry array in the document as written is never counted.
- `{"requests":[{"id":"r1","cap":"time.now","cap":"chat.say"}]}` → `parse_wants = Ok` — inside one request object the `cap` collapses, so the capability the host acts on is not the only capability the document names; a strict reader and this gate disagree about what was requested.
- Contrast: `parse_json_without_duplicate_keys` rejects every duplicate-key text above with `duplicate JSON object key "v" / "subscribe" / "cap"`.

## Why it matters

This is the residual door of #6501/#6520 in the capability path: `parse_records` was hardened because a collapsed document lets a program publish records the caps never counted; the same program's `wants` document still gets validated, counted, and granted from a collapse. A wants document that two readers parse differently is a grant-confusion primitive — audits, logs, or a second implementation that reads the document as written (or first-wins) see different subscriptions, a different version, and different request caps than the host executes — and the entry-count bounds that exist to bound program requests can be hidden behind a duplicate key.

## Acceptance criteria

- `parse_wants` refuses any document containing a duplicate object key at any depth, in the module's existing error vocabulary (parse through `crate::json_unique::parse_json_without_duplicate_keys`, as `parse_records` does).
- Regression tests in `world_caps` cover at least: duplicate `v` in both orders, duplicate `subscribe` hiding an over-limit array, duplicate `cap` inside a request object — each must error; the existing valid/invalid single-key controls keep their current verdicts.
- Audit the sibling program-output gate `parse_surface` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_presentation.rs:435`, same bare-`from_str` + version-check shape) and either migrate it in the same change or record why it is out of scope on this issue.

body:
## What happened

A queue claim was accepted with a 45-minute lease, then silently disappeared ~15 minutes later, so every subsequent checkpoint/heartbeat/complete for that task returned `task 11049 is not claimed by repo-worker-code` and the worker had to finish through the GitHub fallback path.

Timeline (all 2026-11-08Z):

- `09:40:06` — `repo-queue claim --queue repo-health-code-pilot --worker repo-worker-code --lease-seconds 2700 --lane 9aca43b4-...` returned task **11049** with `"lease_until": "2026-11-08T10:25:06Z"` and `"lane_id": "code-z"` (the passed lane id was not stored).
- `09:40:20` — `repo-queue checkpoint 11049 --worker repo-worker-code --stage claimed` succeeded.
- `09:57` — `repo-queue checkpoint ... --stage triaged` failed: `not claimed by repo-worker-code`; `heartbeat 11049` failed the same way; `repo-queue list --status claimed --limit 500` no longer lists it.
- The task was still not claimable afterwards: a new `claim` returned a different, older-by-priority task (11972) instead of 11049.

## Why this matters

The lease the caller asked for and the lease the row reported (`10:25:06`) does not match when the claim actually died (~`09:55`, i.e. ~900 s = the helper's default `--extend-seconds`/heartbeat window). A worker that trusts the reported `lease_until` will lose its claim mid-task and, as here, be forced onto the GitHub fallback for its closing verbs — the exact "claimed-then-abandoned" shape the anti-evaporation discipline exists to prevent.

## Hypothesis

Either (a) `claim` stores `lease_until` from `--lease-seconds` but the reaper / claim validity check uses `claimed_at + 900 s`, or (b) the `leases` table row is written with the default 900 s while `tasks.lease_until` keeps 2700 s, so the two disagree.

## To check

- `agent.tasks` vs `leases` rows for task 11049 (worker `repo-worker-code`) on 2026-11-08.
- The claim RPC's `lease_seconds` handling vs `expire_leases` / `heartbeat_task` lease checks.

Note: `"lane_id": "code-z"` on the claim, despite `--lane 9aca43b4-5439-4939-9f71-323f5d32521b`, may be the same class of "requested value not honoured" defect.

## Acceptance criteria
- A claim taken with --lease-seconds 2700 remains claimed for the full lease: checkpoint, heartbeat, and complete by the claiming worker succeed at any point before lease_until.
- The lane_id passed at claim is the lane_id stored on the task row (the 2026-11-08 claim stored a different lane than the one passed).
- A regression test or broker-level check pins lease duration + lane storage, so a silent ~900s claim death recurs detectably, not silently.

title: id: implement broker / serve-proxy wire protocol per #5792 decision

labels.name: status/parked

labels.name: work/assigned

body:
## Summary

Implement the ID broker / serve-proxy wire protocol decided on #5792 (decision record: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5792#issuecomment-6719076837), as a mode of the id binary. Parent design: #5671 (its fallback ordering, trust model, and E2E boundary are unchanged and bind this work). Downstream consumer: #5798 (fleet surface for the broker role), which configures this role once it exists.

## What to build (per the #5792 decision record)

- Leg establishment: TLS 1.3 over TCP 443, through HTTP CONNECT where the egress requires a proxy; optional WebSocket binary-message adapter carrying the same frames where CONNECT is denied.
- Frame codec: 4-byte big-endian length prefix plus typed frames (OPEN, DATA, CLOSE, WINDOW_UPDATE, PING, PONG, RESUME, RESUME_ACK, ERROR); DATA payload capped at 16 KiB.
- Multiplexing: per-leg stream IDs (odd/even by initiator), broker-side stream-ID mapping between client and server legs, per-stream credit flow control (initial 64 KiB per stream, 1 MiB per connection), priority scheduling in three classes (control, interactive, bulk), and the two-connection class split (control+interactive on one connection, bulk on another).
- Keepalive: PING after 25 s idle (plus/minus 20 percent jitter), leg declared dead after 3 unanswered PINGs, broker closes legs silent for 120 s into the resume window.
- Resumption: broker-issued session token bound to the endpoint identity key, RESUME signed by that key, per-stream sequence numbers with delivered-up-to vectors, replay of exactly the unacknowledged tail, 5-minute resume window, in-memory broker state only.
- Authorization and logging per the decision invariants: authenticated broker use by default, no payload logging, metadata-only operational logs.

## Invariants (from the decision record)

The broker never holds or derives content keys and never terminates the E2E layer; control frames never queue behind DATA; credit is never exceeded (overrun closes the leg with ERROR); the broker persists nothing to disk in v1; resumption never duplicates or reorders per-stream delivery.

## Tests

Name an oracle per the repo testing doctrine: frame codec round-trip and cap enforcement via property-based tests (oracle: decode-encode identity plus the 16 KiB cap invariant); resumption via model-based tests against a simple per-stream ordered-delivery model (oracle: the model); keepalive/dead-leg timing against a fake clock. CI runs the suites per repo policy.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Frame codec, mux, flow control, keepalive, and resumption implemented in the id binary serve-proxy mode, matching the #5792 record section by section.
- [ ] Tests above pass in CI, including the no-duplicate / no-reorder resumption property.
- [ ] A broker forwards E2E ciphertext between a UDP-denied client leg and a server rendezvous leg in an end-to-end test, with the broker demonstrably unable to read payload plaintext.
- [ ] Any deviation from the #5792 decision is recorded on #5792 explicitly, not silently forked.

## Relations

Design: #5792 (decision record). Parent: #5671. Downstream: #5798. Programme: epic #2056.
Filed by queue worker task 12789 (lane code-y), 2026-11-08.

pm-dispatch(auth): the GitHub JWKS response body is shape-trusted — a malformed JWKS body escapes as a raw `TypeError`/`SyntaxError`, not an `AuthError`, so OIDC authentication returns HTTP 500 instead of 401, and a wrong-shape 200 body is cached for an hour.

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/auth.ts`:

- `:86` — `fetchGithubJwks`: `const jwks = (await res.json()) as Jwks;` — a bare cast with no validation. A non-JSON 200 body throws a raw `SyntaxError` out of `res.json()`; a null / `{}` / string body is accepted, stored in `jwksCache` (`:87`, `JWKS_TTL_MS` = 1 hour at `:82`), and returned as if valid.
- `:112` — `verifyOidcToken`: `jwks.keys.find((k) => k.kid === kid)` — assumes `keys` is an array of objects with no guard.

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts:655-659` maps `AuthError` → 401 and everything else → 500, so every malformed shape below becomes a 500.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ 9b183d7bb6)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-dispatch-auth/probe.ts` importing the real `auth.ts` (control signed token verifies OK against a well-formed JWKS):

- `null` JWKS → `TypeError` (evaluating `.keys`), not `AuthError`
- `{}` → `TypeError` (`.keys.find`)
- `"x"` (string body) → `TypeError` (`.keys.find`)
- `{keys: "x"}` → `TypeError` (`.keys.find is not a function`)
- `{keys: 42}` → `TypeError` (`.keys.find is not a function`)
- `{keys: [null]}` → `TypeError` (evaluating `k.kid`)
- `fetchGithubJwks` with a non-JSON 200 body → raw `SyntaxError`, not `AuthError`

Cache impact: because `fetchGithubJwks` caches the unvalidated body for `JWKS_TTL_MS`, one wrong-shape 200 response poisons OIDC auth for up to an hour — every subsequent OIDC request crashes the same way instead of re-fetching.

This is the residual of the sibling boundary fixes in the same service: JWT segment shapes were hardened (#2665, `parseJwt` + `isJsonObject` in this same file), the queue row bodies in #7299, the GitHub API bodies in #7101, and the OpenCode client in #7085. The JWKS body is the one remaining unvalidated external JSON body in `auth.ts`.

## Why it matters

Authentication is the dispatch service's front door. An upstream hiccup, proxy error page with a 200, or any wrong-shape JWKS payload turns a clean 401 auth failure into a 500, misleads operators/retries, and — via the cache — persists for an hour after the upstream recovers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `verifyOidcToken` throws `AuthError` (→ HTTP 401) for every malformed JWKS shape: null / non-object body, missing or non-array `keys`, and non-object key entries.
- [ ] `fetchGithubJwks` validates the body before caching it: a non-JSON or wrong-shape 200 body throws `AuthError` and is NOT stored in `jwksCache` (a later call re-fetches).
- [ ] Regression tests in `pm-stack/dispatch/test/auth.test.ts` cover the shapes above and fail pre-fix; the existing auth suite stays green.
- [ ] Control unchanged: a well-formed JWKS still verifies a valid token and returns the OIDC identity.

body:
## Turso transition grep debt: quota gatherer's Turso sink pointed at the deleted muse-platform DB for ~31 hours

The Supabase → Turso cutover (#6581, executing #5690–#5693; quota sink repointed in the 2026-11-06 Wave 3 cutover under #5690) was declared complete without ever grepping the fleet for the old database hostname. One live consumer was left pointing at it. This issue carries the full straggler list from the grep that never happened, run 2026-11-08.

### The dead sink (the symptom)

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts` wrote 17 `agent_quota_records` rows per 15-minute tick to Turso DB `muse-platform`. Journal evidence (`quota-gatherer.service`, laptop):

- Last success: **2026-11-07 00:00:24 CST** — "turso sink wrote 17 quota_records rows (source=opencode-quota)" (every tick Nov 6 19:45 → Nov 7 00:00 wrote 17).
- Every tick since: "turso sink skipped — token unresolved by name" (~31 hours at discovery; the local JSON snapshot was unaffected — fail-soft by contract).

### Diagnosis — both halves of the old target are gone, and the ledger already lives elsewhere

1. **The DB is deleted, not renamed/misconfigured.** `turso db list` (2026-11-08) shows 43 databases in group `great-star-lord`; `muse-platform` is not among them. The old host `https://muse-platform-dezren39.aws-us-east-1.turso.io` answers **502 "no route configured for host"** — the hostname is de-registered, consistent with deletion.
2. **The token name died with it.** BWS `turso.muse-platform-rw-token` no longer resolves (`fleet secrets get` rc=3; absent from the laptop BWS key list). Its value was last successfully read by the gatherer at the Nov 7 00:00 tick.
3. **The quota ledger's live home is `fleet-platform`.** `agent_quota_records` exists there (11,985 rows at check time) and `source='opencode-quota'` rows land with byte-identical ids (per-tick: 17 rows — e.g. tick `2026-11-07T05:45:03.326Z` complete through `inserted_at 05:45:16Z`, incl. `meta` = Muse Code High Usage 100%, `openai.main` 14% weekly) written **via the snapshot/outbox path into Turso directly, not via Supabase** (proof: muse-dev2's PostgREST has been 503 PGRST002 since 2026-11-06 ~19:25Z per #6619, while those batches carry `ts` = the gatherer's tick generation time). A second writer, `source='muse-subscription'` (the Muse runtime writer), is current to the minute in the same table.

So the true blocker was never "restore muse-platform": the transition moved the ledger to `fleet-platform` and retired `muse-platform`, and exactly one consumer — the gatherer's direct Turso sink — was never repointed. Its silence was masked because the ledger kept receiving the same rows through the other path.

### Fix

`gather-quota.ts` sink constants repointed to the live target (same pattern as the working `external-comms` writer):

- `TURSO_URL`: `muse-platform-dezren39…` → `https://fleet-platform-dezren39.aws-us-east-1.turso.io`
- `TURSO_TOKEN_NAME`: `turso.muse-platform-rw-token` → `turso.fleet-platform-rw-token` (already vaulted in BWS; verified resolving by name; its read-write scope on `agent_quota_records` is proven by the external-comms writer using it against that DB)
- Header/comment references updated to match (lines 67, 103, 596). No other behavior change.

PR: (link added in a comment once opened — this issue is filed first so the PR can reference it). Verification: after the fix lands in the laptop checkout, the next timer tick must log "turso sink wrote 17 quota_records rows" and a fresh `opencode-quota` batch must appear in `fleet-platform.agent_quota_records`.

### Full straggler list — the grep (2026-11-08)

Patterns: `muse-platform-dezren39.aws-us-east-1.turso.io`, `muse-platform`, `turso.muse-platform-rw-token`, plus a histogram of all `*-dezren39.aws-us-east-1.turso.io` hosts and `turso.*-token` names per tree.

**Live code (exactly one straggler — fixed by the PR above):**
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:580` — old hostname in `TURSO_URL`
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:579` + `:103` — old key name
- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:67` + `:596` — comments naming the dead DB

**Docs (historical records of the retired DB — left as written; they describe the pattern at the time):**
- `doc/fleet/queue-turso-cutover.md:36` — "muse-mirror/muse-platform pattern; BWS only" (token-pattern note from the fleet-queue creation)
- `doc/fleet/agent-events-turso.md:117` — CI-mirror secrets "point at muse-platform and are *not* reused" (records that fleet-queue deliberately did not reuse them)

**Verified clean (no hits):** `pkgs/`, `secrets/`, `.opencode/` in developing-today/code; the darwin-nix tree (`~/git/nix`); opencode config/state (`~/.config/opencode`, `~/.local/state/opencode`); `~/.config/systemd` units; the rest of `pm-stack` (host histogram: only `muse-platform` ×1 in the gatherer and `fleet-platform` ×1 in external-comms; key histogram: `turso.fleet-platform-rw-token` ×3 working, `turso.muse-platform-rw-token` ×2 both in the gatherer).

**Known residuals, stated honestly:**
- The `muse-platform` Turso DB also held other Wave-3 tables (e.g. `ci_events` per #5693's design). Nothing in the swept code trees still references its hostname, but historical rows in the deleted DB are unrecoverable from Turso; the Supabase originals and the fleet's shadow copies are the fallback record.
- `~/tools/quota-recorder.py` (the Nov 6 migration lane's recorder) no longer exists on the laptop — it was a migration-period tool; no unit references it.
- Fleet working copies of the same file under sandbox scratch dirs are stale snapshots, not consumers.

### Process gap

Cutover completion criteria for any future DB/host rename must include: a repo-wide + fleet-wide grep for the old hostname and old secret names, with every hit dispositioned (fixed / historical-doc / deleted), before the old DB or key is retired. The deletion of `muse-platform` and its BWS key happened while a live consumer still resolved both by name — the grep would have caught it in minutes.

Refs #5690 #6581 #6619

## Acceptance criteria

- Every straggler in this issue's fleet-wide old-hostname grep list is dispositioned: repointed to its live target, retired, or explicitly recorded as intentionally dead — none left silently pointing at the deleted `muse-platform` DB or its dead token name.
- The quota gatherer's sink is verified writing to the live ledger DB on consecutive ticks (the PR #7561 repoint half already merged 2026-11-08 — this criterion is the remaining-list half).
- A transition checklist item exists (in the runbook or the issue's closing comment) so the next DB cutover greps the fleet for the old hostname before being declared complete.

title: aggregator(confirm-charges-surfaced): extra positional arguments are silently ignored — a second feed path is dropped and its delivered charges are never confirmed (re-alert forever)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/confirm-charges-surfaced.ts` reads exactly one
positional argument and silently ignores everything after it:

```ts
const feedPath = process.argv[2];   // scripts/confirm-charges-surfaced.ts:11
if (!feedPath) throw new Error("usage: confirm-charges-surfaced.ts <delivered-feed>");
```

There is no other `argv` check in the file. This script is the confirmation
half of the charges pipeline: it runs after a feed is delivered
(`scripts/push-fleet-feed.sh:217` invokes it as
`bun run scripts/confirm-charges-surfaced.ts "$FEED"`) and persists the
delivered charges' keys into the surfaced-state file, which is what stops
those charges from alerting again.

## Verified evidence (laptop, main @ da4c0cc6b8, real script md5 eb26255074978317005df3bf0f88852f, probe `~/git/fleet/probe-confirm-argv`, isolated `CHARGES_SURFACED_STATE_PATH` per case)

- Control — `confirm-charges-surfaced.ts feed.json`: exit 0, state gains
  `acmeai|12.50|2026-10-30`. Correct.
- Extra argument — `confirm-charges-surfaced.ts feed.json --bogus`: exit 0,
  charges confirmed; the unknown argument is silently ignored.
- Second feed path — `confirm-charges-surfaced.ts feed.json other.json`:
  exit 0, but the second feed's charge (`otherco|99.00|2026-10-31`) is
  **never confirmed** and nothing says so. If both feeds were delivered,
  the second feed's charges re-alert forever — the exact failure mode
  #3681 fixed for malformed `chargesAttention` elements, reached here
  through argv instead.
- Flag-style — `confirm-charges-surfaced.ts --feed feed.json`: treats
  `--feed` as the path and dies with a raw ENOENT for a file named
  `--feed`, with no usage hint.

Every sibling aggregator script that takes arguments now rejects unknown /
extra / duplicate tokens with a usage error (exit 2) before any side
effect — append-usage-snapshots (#6961), compact-usage-snapshots (#6967),
backfill-usage-snapshots (#6973), generate-digest (#7097),
collect-github-billing (#7254), post-alert (#7289),
produce-charge-candidates (#7302), record-claude-launch (#7332), and
collect-fleet-feed's own `resolveOutPath` guard. This script is the
remaining unguarded one in the inventory tracked by #3353.

## Why it matters

Confirmation is a write with a suppression side effect: keys persisted
here silence future alerts for those charges. Silently dropping an
argument either confirms charges the operator did not name (extra-arg
case proceeds as if the invocation were exact) or — worse — silently
fails to confirm a delivered feed, so already-delivered charges re-alert
on every subsequent tick with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- Any invocation with more than one positional argument, or with an
  unknown/flag-like token, fails with a usage error (exit 2, message
  naming the unexpected argument) **before** the feed is read or the
  surfaced-state file is touched.
- The documented single-argument invocation behaves exactly as before
  (the #3681 suite, `test/confirm-charges-surfaced-3681.test.ts`, stays
  green unchanged).
- New regression tests run the real script as a subprocess (the #3681
  suite's pattern) covering: extra unknown argument, second feed path,
  and the single-argument control; the new tests fail against the
  pre-fix script.

Related: #3681 (same script, element validation), #3353 (argv-parser
inventory / argument-contract audit).

title: id(world/audit): IsolationInfo and PolicyInfo queries are audited as admin actions — the falsified-attribution class #4017 fixed for the other four queries

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
