labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

The structured audit log landed in #4017 (for #1063, main `2aca793a34`) records two read-only queries — `IsolationInfo` and `PolicyInfo` — as **admin** actions with outcome `accepted`, even though neither command carries any caller identity. That is the exact falsified-attribution defect #4017 itself fixed for the other four participant-readable queries.

In `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs` at `2aca793a34`:

- `WorldCommand::IsolationInfo` handler (~line 1905): calls `audit_admin_result("admin", "IsolationInfo", …, true)` and always records outcome `accepted`.
- `WorldCommand::PolicyInfo` handler (~line 1957): calls `audit_admin_result("admin", "PolicyInfo", …, true)` the same way.

By contrast, the handlers for `Metrics`, `CapsInfo`, `ExecutionProfileInfo`, and `ManifestState` in the same match deliberately emit **no** record, with comments stating the rule: these queries are readable by joined participants, the handlers carry no caller identity, and recording the read as admin "would falsify the audit actor" / "participant-readable queries are not administrative actions and stay out of the audit trail." The pinning test `participant_readable_queries_emit_no_admin_audit_record` (pkgs/id/src/world/tests.rs) covers only those four commands — `IsolationInfo` and `PolicyInfo` were missed, so the inconsistency is untested and regressable.

## Why it matters

- **The audit trail lies about who acted.** `WorldHandle::isolation()` and `WorldHandle::policy()` (pkgs/id/src/world/handle.rs:400, :483) take no authority/identity parameter — any holder of the handle can issue them, exactly like `Metrics`/`CapsInfo`. Recording them under actor `admin` manufactures admin activity that never happened, in a log whose stated purpose is replayable, trustworthy attribution of admin actions (#1063).
- **`PolicyInfo` is on a hot internal path.** The cross-world gate `WorldHub::authorize` (pkgs/id/src/world_hub.rs:302, :308) calls `policy()` twice for **every** cross-world access check, same- or cross-world reads/writes alike. Every such check now appends a spurious `admin / PolicyInfo / accepted` record, flooding the `id::audit` target with noise that drowns real admin actions and breaks the "exactly one record per admin command" invariant the audit replay test asserts.
- **Replay/review tooling cannot distinguish** a genuine admin read from an internal gate check or a participant read, undermining the refusal/provider-use dispositions #4017 added.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08, laptop, main 2aca793a34)

- Read of `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs` on current main: `IsolationInfo` and `PolicyInfo` handlers emit `audit_admin_result("admin", …, true)`; `Metrics`, `CapsInfo`, `ExecutionProfileInfo`, `ManifestState` handlers emit nothing and carry the explanatory comments quoted above.
- `git show 2aca793a34` (the #4017 landing commit) shows the same split introduced in one diff: audit calls added to the two Info handlers, no-audit comments added to the other four.
- Probe (laptop worktree `~/git/fleet/probe-audit-info`, test added to `world::tests::audit_tests` mirroring `participant_readable_queries_emit_no_admin_audit_record` but issuing `IsolationInfo` + `PolicyInfo`): a capture test in the `id::audit` target, issuing only the two identity-less queries, captured exactly two records on current main:

  ```json
  {"action":"IsolationInfo","actor":"admin","outcome":"accepted","parameters":{"isolation":"Isolated"},"schema_version":1,"world_id":"audit-test",…}
  {"action":"PolicyInfo","actor":"admin","outcome":"accepted","parameters":{"policy":"WorldPolicy { isolation: Isolated, cross_world_write: false, … }"},"schema_version":1,"world_id":"audit-test",…}
  ```

  i.e. two `admin`/`accepted` audit records for commands that carry no caller identity at all — where the four sibling queries capture zero.
- Dedup: no open or closed issue covers audit attribution for `PolicyInfo`/`IsolationInfo` (searched 2026-11-08). #1063 is the parent feature; #7370 covers only the pre-existing audit-test compile failure, a different defect.

## Fix

Remove the `audit_admin_result` calls from the `IsolationInfo` and `PolicyInfo` handlers (matching the other four queries, with the same explanatory comment), and extend `participant_readable_queries_emit_no_admin_audit_record` to issue all six commands so the whole class is pinned.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `IsolationInfo` and `PolicyInfo` commands emit no `id::audit` record, like `Metrics`/`CapsInfo`/`ExecutionProfileInfo`/`ManifestState`.
- [ ] The participant-readable-queries audit test covers all six query commands and fails if any of them emits a record.
- [ ] Genuine admin mutations (`SetIsolation`, `SetFileScope`, `UpdateCaps`, …) still emit exactly one audit record each; the audit replay test stays green.
- [ ] `cargo test -p id --lib audit_tests` green.

body:
Found 2026-11-08 by queue worker lane code-a during the code#5362 broker cutover verification (task 12731), verified against both queue-client binaries on the laptop:

**Defect.** `repo-queue list --queue <q> --status claimed` emits a human-readable table (columns: task / priority / status / age / dedupe_key / title), but both opencode-claimant consumers parse its stdout as JSON:
- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` `fetch_claimed_rows` (~line 296): `json.loads(result.stdout)` — the parse fails ("Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)"), the function warns and returns [], so every queue contributes zero candidates and zero stuck-bound rows. Fail-closed by design, but candidate discovery is silently a no-op.
- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (~line 189-200): same call, same `json.loads`, in the live-mode recovery path.

**Not a cutover regression.** During task 12731 the outputs of the hand-built `~/fleet-brokers/bin/repo-queue list` and the packaged alias `~/.local/bin/repo-queue list` were diffed byte-for-byte: identical (22 lines, same table). The mismatch exists with both binaries; the claimant mode file currently reads as the default/shadow state, so the live recovery path may not have exercised it yet.

**Fix shape (either side).** Give the queue client's `list` verb a machine-readable mode (e.g. `--json` / format env the claimant sets) emitting the row JSON the consumers already expect (a list, or `{"rows": [...]}` — poll.py accepts both), or change both consumers to parse the table. The client side is preferable: `claim`/`checkpoint` already emit JSON, so `list` is the inconsistent verb.

Acceptance: a supervised `poll.py` dry pass on the laptop completes with no "Could not poll queue" warnings and returns the real claimed-row counts for the four pilot queues; claimant tests cover the parse against a captured real `list` output fixture.

## Acceptance criteria

- `poll.py`'s candidate discovery returns the actually-claimed rows for a queue (a fire against a queue with claimed tasks yields non-zero candidates and stuck-bound rows, not silent zeros).
- `claimant.py`'s live-mode recovery path reads the same rows successfully.
- The fix is on one side of the seam, chosen and recorded: either `repo-queue list` gains a machine-readable (JSON) output the claimant uses, or both claimant consumers parse the table — the two sides cannot drift again without a test failing.
- A regression test pins the producer/consumer format contract for the claimed-rows read.

title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): launch_step ignores its mode argument — a shadow fire creates and binds a session if discovery ever returns a candidate

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` at HEAD (`b5ddb39744`) reads the mode in `main()` and then only uses it for one thing: whether to run `supervision_step()`. It is **never consulted before a launch**.

```python
# claimant.py:512-550
mode = read_mode()
if mode == "live":
    supervision_step(mode)
...
launched, skips = launch_step(mode, cap_room)   # mode is passed and ignored
```

`launch_step(mode, cap_room)` takes `mode` as a parameter and never reads it. The body goes straight from the cap check to `POST /api/session` and `repo-queue bind`.

The task packet (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/prompt.md`, §MODE) is explicit: "In shadow mode ... Never claim, bind, launch, or mutate a task in shadow mode." The living fire instruction is equally explicit that shadow is the default when `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode` is absent.

## Reproduction (verified 2026-11-08, laptop)

Patched `read_mode` → `"shadow"`, `run_poll` → one valid `handed_off` candidate, and stubbed `subprocess.run` to record argv:

```
$ python3 <stub harness invoking claimant.main()>
OpenCode claimant starting in shadow mode
Running gate step...
Running cap step...
Cap room: 36 sessions available
Running launch step...
Fire complete. Launched 1 sessions.
subprocess calls:
  curl -s -m 10 -X POST ... -d {"location": {"directory": "/home/user/git/code"}, ...} http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
  repo-queue bind 999999 --worker opencode-claimant --session-id ses_FAKE --launched-by opencode-claimant
```

`main()` returns 0 having created and bound a session **while `mode == "shadow"`**.

## Why it is invisible today

Shadow is currently safe by accident, not by design: `gate_step()` → `run_poll()` → `poll.py` → `repo-queue list`, which prints a human table (#7325), so every queue reads empty and the fire exits before `launch_step`. The moment #7325 lands — or any caller passes a candidate list, or the mode file is written `live` and later reverted while a fire is in flight — the guard that should have stopped it does not exist.

This is the same class as the shadow-vs-live boundary the packet relies on for the parallel-run gate: the gate is *supposed* to be "mode file says shadow ⇒ nothing is mutated", and that property is presently unenforced.

## Suggested acceptance

1. `launch_step` refuses to create/bind when `mode != "live"` (early return `([], [{"reason": "shadow_mode"}])`), and `main()` does not call it in shadow mode at all — belt and braces, since the packet describes shadow as read-only by construction.
2. `supervision_step`'s recovery path is likewise unreachable in shadow mode (it already returns early — pin it with a test that asserts no `subprocess.run` argv contains `bind` or `DELETE`).
3. Test that fails today: with `read_mode` → `"shadow"`, one candidate, and a recording subprocess stub, assert **zero** calls whose argv contains `bind`, `DELETE`, or a `POST` to `/api/session`.
4. Test the inverse: `read_mode` → `"live"` still launches, so the gate is not a silent kill switch.

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow), while working #3026 slice 1. Related: #7356 (launch_step's other missing steps), #7325 (the gate that currently masks this), #6257.

## Acceptance criteria

- In shadow mode, `launch_step` performs no session create, no `repo-queue bind`, and no other mutation — the mode argument is consulted before any launch action, per the packet's §MODE rule ('Never claim, bind, launch, or mutate a task in shadow mode').
- In live mode, launches proceed as today.
- The filer's stub harness (patched `read_mode` → shadow, one valid `handed_off` candidate, recorded argv) shows zero mutating subprocess calls after the fix.

title: id: implement server-side identity backup per #5033 decision (v1 envelope blob, epoch-guarded storage, download budget)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

body:
## Problem
Issue #5033 recorded the design decision (2026-11-08, task 12716) for a server-side identity backup: the blob is the #2279 v1 envelope byte-for-byte, the server holds ciphertext + metadata only, OPRF is rejected for v1 in favour of a per-identity download budget over the pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs limiter shape plus the Argon2id guessing-cost floor, storage is one epoch-guarded record per identity with signed deletion, and restore-forces-rotation is deferred to the #2380 keyset substrate with an interim restore_epoch + device-notification rule. Nothing of this exists in code: at main 9f5a92057d pkgs/id has no backup record, endpoint, or lifecycle, and the identity key is still the raw file at pkgs/id/src/lib.rs:324.

## Implementation scope (from the #5033 decision)
- Server backup record keyed by hex(SHA-256(identity public key)) holding only: envelope bytes, envelope SHA-256, blob size, upload/download timestamps, monotone upload epoch, throttle counters, restore_epoch, and a deletion tombstone (H(pub) + final epoch).
- Upload endpoint: accepts envelope bytes + Sign_identity(H(pub) || envelope_sha256 || epoch); verifies the signature against the named public key; rejects non-increasing epochs; overwrites only on a valid higher-epoch upload.
- Download endpoint: requester presents the identity public key; server enforces the download budget (10/hour, 50/day per H(pub), weighted fixed windows per pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs, plus existing per-IP/global limits, refusals with retry-after) and returns the envelope bytes. Decryption stays client-side via the existing pkgs/id/src/key_envelope.rs import path; the passphrase never leaves the device.
- Delete endpoint: signed by the identity key; deletes ciphertext + counters, leaves the tombstone; account deletion purges the tombstone.
- Restore bookkeeping: a download-for-restore increments restore_epoch and notifies bound devices before the restored key is treated as authoritative for new group epochs (interim rule from #5033 item 5). Do NOT implement a rotation flag: that representation belongs to #2380 and lands there.
- Client: backup create/upload flow reusing key_envelope.rs encryption exactly (no second format), with a weak-passphrase warning at creation (per #5033 item 3's guessing-cost analysis).

## Acceptance
- [ ] A server data dump for a backup record contains no field beyond the #5033 item-2 list (test asserts the stored field set).
- [ ] Upload with a bad signature or a stale/equal epoch is rejected; a higher-epoch signed upload replaces the blob (tests naming their oracle: the #5033 decision items 1 and 4).
- [ ] The 11th download within an hour and the 51st within a day for one H(pub) are refused with retry-after (property test over the limiter: the budget invariant holds for arbitrary interleavings).
- [ ] Restore flow recovers the identity key from passphrase + downloaded envelope using only the existing key_envelope.rs decrypt path; wrong passphrase fails locally with no server signal.
- [ ] Signed delete removes the ciphertext; replaying the pre-delete signed upload does not resurrect it.
- [ ] No rotation flag is introduced; restore_epoch increment + bound-device notification are covered by tests.

## Out of scope
OPRF/blinded unwrap (rejected for v1 on #5033, revisit only as a v2 online assist), seed-phrase restore (#2381), guardian recovery (#2382), the restore-forces-rotation flag representation (#2380).

## Sources
Design decision on #5033 (comment 6718342769); investigation doc/2026-10-29T11-28-18Z_investigation_key_recovery_hosted sections 4.2, 7, 8.4; pkgs/id/src/key_envelope.rs; pkgs/id/src/abuse.rs.

## Acceptance criteria
- The v1 backup envelope format is documented in the implementation: version field, epoch semantics, and blob layout, matching the #5033 decision items 1-4.
- A server-side identity backup can be written and restored round-trip in tests, with epoch mismatch and malformed-blob cases refused with named errors.
- No client key material is logged or persisted outside the envelope; restore requires the documented epoch/credential checks.
- Tests named per the testing doctrine (invariant/oracle stated) cover round-trip, epoch roll, and corruption cases.

title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): launch_step binds a session and never sends the prompt — every live launch creates a zero-message bound session

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (HEAD `9f5a92057d`, restored by #7290) has the correct create → verify-location → bind ordering, but **stops after bind**. Step 4d builds the worker prompt as a string and never delivers it:

```python
# claimant.py:474-489
# Step 4d: Send prompt to bound session
prompt = f"""
Execute queue task {task_id}
...
"""
# In a real implementation, this would send the prompt via the session API
# For now, we just record the successful launch
launched.append({"task_id": task_id, "session_id": session_id, ...})
```

There is no `POST` to `/api/session/<id>` (or any message endpoint) anywhere in `launch_step`. A live fire therefore **creates and binds a session that never receives a prompt**.

## Why this is urgent now

Two things changed today:

1. #7290 merged (#6865 closed 06:31:52Z), so `claimant.py` again has working supervision and a live launch path.
2. #7325 is the only remaining gate: `poll.py` cannot read the queues. Once that lands, live mode stops being a no-op and starts doing this on every launch.

A bound-but-never-prompted session is exactly the state #4758's recovery rule exists to clean up. So every launch would produce one zero-message session that supervision then has to delete and reclaim 30+ minutes later — a self-inflicted oscillating loop rather than forward progress.

## Also missing from the spec'd launch sequence (all zero-hit `grep`s in `claimant.py`)

| Spec step | Required | At HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| 4c | `checkpoint <id> --worker <worker_id> --stage launched` with session id in progress | absent |
| 4d | send the queue runbook prompt to the bound session, `--worker <worker_id>` on every verb, terminal `--execution {"lane":"opencode","session_id":"<id>"}` | **string built, never sent** |
| 4e | agent-note `agent-note:v1`, state=handed off, task id + session id | absent |
| gate | skip candidates whose issue carries `held` / `user/owned` / `do-not-merge` / `do-not-auto-edit` | absent (no label read at all) |
| gate | `attempts < max_attempts` before relaunch | absent |
| §EXECUTION | single-instance lock + bounded parallel pool | absent |

On the last row: the task prompt's EXECUTION section states `claimant.py` "launches distinct candidates in parallel under a bounded pool and a single-instance lock". Neither exists — the loop is serial with no `flock`/`O_EXCL`/`ThreadPool`. Fire cadence is 10 min and a fire can take minutes, so two overlapping fires are possible and would both walk the same candidate list; the atomic bind is what keeps exactly-once, but the lock the description relies on is not there.

## What does work

- Session create body uses the correct v2 shape (`location: {directory}`, `model: {id, providerID}`, `agent`).
- `location.directory` is verified against `PRIMARY_CLONE` before bind, with delete-on-mismatch.
- Bind happens before anything that can interleave, and a bind failure deletes the created session.
- Supervision has the zero-message delete-before-reclaim ordering.

## Suggested acceptance

1. `launch_step` `POST`s the prompt to the bound session id before recording the candidate as launched; on send failure, reconcile (read the session's messages) rather than relaunch, per the task's step 5.
2. Add `checkpoint --stage launched` and the 4e agent-note.
3. Read the issue labels and skip on any of the four hard-stop labels; skip when `attempts >= max_attempts`.
4. Add the single-instance lock and the bounded pool, or drop the claim from the task description.
5. Test that fails today: with a stub session create + bind, assert a prompt `POST` to `/api/session/ses_new1` occurs, and that a send error produces a reconciled skip rather than a second launch.

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow). Related: #7325, #6865, #4758, #4912, #5400.

## Acceptance criteria

- A live launch delivers the worker prompt to the bound session via the session API (a POST to the session's message endpoint) before the launch is recorded as successful — create → verify-location → bind → send-prompt, in that order.
- A bound session after a live fire has exactly the intended first message (verifiable via the server), never zero messages.
- If the prompt send fails, the launch is recorded as failed (and the binding is not left masquerading as a working lane).

title: id(id-core/unicode): is_format_char has no exhaustive oracle test — the boundary-sample test would miss a range-interior omission like #4070

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/unicode.rs` hand-maintains the Unicode 16 general-category Cf (format character) set behind `is_format_char` — the predicate shared by name validation and plain-text rendering, i.e. the set that keeps zero-width and bidi-control characters out of display names and rendered output. Its only test (`format_char_matches_unicode_16_range_boundaries`, unicode.rs tests) samples 32 in-set boundary codepoints and 7 out-of-set codepoints. The interiors of every multi-codepoint range (e.g. U+0601..=0604, U+13431..=1343E, U+1D174..=1D179, U+E021..=E07E) and the entire out-of-set space outside the 7 samples are untested: an edit that shrinks a range interior, drops a singleton, or widens a range would pass the suite.

This failure mode has already happened once: #4070 — `is_format_char` omitted U+061C ARABIC LETTER MARK and the omission was only caught later by review.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08, laptop, main 36e5b3eb46)

- Oracle comparison: the predicate's ranges were extracted from unicode.rs and compared against Python `unicodedata` (unidata_version 16.0.0) over all 0x110000 codepoints — the table is currently **exactly** correct: 170 Cf codepoints, 21 ranges, no missing, no extra. So this is a test-oracle gap on a correct table, not a live bug.
- The existing test checks boundaries only; no test in the crate enumerates the full codepoint space or a golden Cf list.

## Fix

Add an exhaustive oracle test for `is_format_char` in unicode.rs: a golden Unicode 16 Cf range list (generated from Unicode 16 data, named as the oracle in the test) and a scan of every `char` asserting the predicate matches the golden set exactly. This follows the house testing doctrine (every automated test names its oracle; parsers/character classes get property-style coverage).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] New test in `crates/id-core/src/unicode.rs` compares `is_format_char` against a complete golden Unicode 16 Cf list over the whole codepoint range (not samples).
- [ ] Test fails if any range in the predicate is shrunk, widened, or a singleton dropped/added (demonstrated by mutation or by construction).
- [ ] `cargo test -p id-core` green; no change to the predicate itself (it is verified correct).

title: aggregator(record-claude-launch): unknown/misspelled/joined/duplicate flags silently ignored — a typo'd --task drops the session↔task linkage, a typo'd --file writes the record to the default registry, exit 0

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/record-claude-launch.ts` — the script a Muse session (or its launcher) uses to register itself in the identity registry, the record that makes the dashboard's task ↔ session linkage work for Muse sessions — silently ignores unknown, misspelled, joined, and duplicate arguments. Every flag is probed with `indexOf` only:

- `arg()` at `record-claude-launch.ts:47-50` — `process.argv.indexOf('--' + name)`, first match wins, no scan of the remaining tokens.
- `taskRefs` at `record-claude-launch.ts:65` — a `flatMap` over exact `--task` tokens only.

The flag *values* were hardened in #3415 (a flag token refused as a value) and #6895 (empty values refused). The unknown-token half was left, exactly as it was for the sibling scripts fixed in #6961/#6967/#7097/#7254/#7289/#7302.

## Verified this run (laptop, main @ 36e5b3eb46, real script run verbatim with `bun run`, probe `~/git/fleet/probe-claude-launch-unknown-args`, script md5 `41403504aadfa51193d0de228c9c829d`)

Control (documented separated flags) exits 0 and records exactly what it names:

```
--label Control --model sonnet --status done --id claude-ctrl
-> {"id":"claude-ctrl","label":"Control","parentId":null,"status":"done","model":"sonnet"}
```

Every one of these exits 0 and appends a record, with the named intent silently dropped or redirected:

| Invocation (plus `--label X --id <id>`) | Record actually appended |
|---|---|
| `--modle sonnet` (typo) | no `model` field |
| `--stats done` (typo) | `"status":"launched"` (the default) |
| `--model=sonnet` (joined) | no `model` field |
| `--parnt sess-123` (typo) | `"parentId":null` |
| `--bogus 1 stray` (unknown + positional) | record appended, tokens ignored |
| `--label First --label Second`, `--id a --id b` (duplicates) | first value wins, second silently ignored |
| `--tas developing-today/code#123` (typo) | no `taskRefs` — the session↔task linkage the script exists to create is gone |
| `--task=developing-today/code#123` (joined) | no `taskRefs` |
| `--fil <intended.jsonl>` (typo, fake `HOME`) | record written to the **default** registry file under the fake home, not the intended file — in production the record pollutes the default registry and the collector reading the intended file never sees the session |

## Why it matters

This script's only job is faithful registration. A typo does not fail the launch — it registers a *wrong* session: unlinked to its task (`--task` typo), unparented, with the wrong status/model, or in the wrong file, all with exit 0 and a success line naming the id. The registry merge then folds/dashboards that corrupted record as truth, and there is no signal anywhere that the operator's flag was dropped.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Before any file is created, read, or appended, the script validates the whole argv against the documented flag set (`--label`, `--id`, `--parent`, `--task`, `--model`, `--status`, `--file` — all value-taking; `--task` is the only repeatable one).
- [ ] Unknown, misspelled, joined (`--flag=value`), duplicate single-value, and stray positional arguments fail with a usage error naming the offending token and exit 2, with **no** record appended to any file (including the default file).
- [ ] The documented invocations in the script header still work verbatim, including multiple `--task` flags, and the #3415/#6895 value guards keep passing.
- [ ] Regression tests in the established subprocess style (cf. `test/record-claude-launch-flag-value-3415.test.ts`, `test/record-claude-launch-empty-value-6895.test.ts`) cover typo, joined, unknown, duplicate, and stray cases and assert no file write occurred; the new tests fail on the pre-fix script.

## Prior art

Same fix shape as the merged sibling fixes: `rejectUnknownArgs()` as the first statement of the main flow, exit 2 before any I/O (post-alert #7289/PR #7295, produce-charge-candidates #7302/PR #7304, generate-digest #7097, collect-github-billing #7254).

title: opencode-claimant(poll): repo-queue list emits a table, not JSON — every queue read fails and candidate discovery is blind fleet-wide

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Symptom

Every fire of `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` prints, for all four queues:

```
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-code-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-opencode-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-openchamber-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
Warning: Could not poll queue repo-health-nix-pilot: Expecting value: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```

and reports `candidates: []`, `stuck_bound: []` for every queue.

## Cause

`fetch_claimed_rows()` (poll.py:288) runs:

```
repo-queue list --queue <queue> --status claimed
```

and then `json.loads(result.stdout)`. But `~/fleet-brokers/bin/repo-queue` `list` emits a **human-readable table**, not JSON. There is no JSON mode in the CLI either:

```
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --json
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --json
$ ... --format json   -> unrecognized argument
$ ... --output json   -> unrecognized argument
```

So `json.loads` always raises and every queue contributes zero rows.

## Impact

This is not a transient outage — the claimed set is large. At fire time 2026-11-08T05:45Z the four queues held **37 claimed tasks** (code 20+, opencode 7, openchamber 3, nix 6). The claimant cannot see any of them, so:

- **Candidate discovery is blind fleet-wide.** Any claimed, lane-`opencode`, unbound task at a recorded yield stage is invisible and never launched. The fire ends "No unbound opencode-lane candidates found" and looks healthy.
- **Supervision is blind.** `stuck_bound` (the #4758 zero-message / gone-session recovery set) is derived from the same claimed rows, so bound-but-dead sessions are never reported or recovered.
- **The fire log under-reports.```cap_room` is recorded as 0 with `skips: [{reason: no_candidates}]`** even when a direct poll shows room (23 at the time of this report). A saturated-cap reading and an unreadable-queue reading are indistinguishable in the log.

This is the "standing claimant never went live" failure mode in a new form: the process runs, exits 0, and reports nothing to do.

## Proposed fix

Either:

1. Give `repo-queue list` a JSON output mode (`--json`) that serialises the broker rows including `progress`, and have `fetch_claimed_rows()` use it; or
2. Have poll.py reach the queue-broker HTTP API directly (the same route the CLI uses) and parse the rows there.

Option 1 is smaller and keeps poll.py's "read-only by construction" property anchored on the CLI. Whichever is chosen, poll.py should also **distinguish "queue unreadable" from "queue empty"** in its output and in the claimant fire log, so a broken read can never be reported as `no_candidates`.

## Verification

```
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-opencode-pilot --status claimed
```
returns a table with 7 claimed rows; `python3 pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` should then report those rows (filtered by lane/stage) instead of `[]`.

Related: #6865 (claimant.py imports), #6868 (poll.py crash on malformed session time), #4758 (recovery rule), #3026 (slice 1).

## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related step/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

title: ci: flake checks the PR tier never runs — nix ci has no pull_request/push trigger, so deploy-list checks are unenforced on PRs

body:
## Problem

`nix ci` (`.github/workflows/nix-ci.yml`) has only `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` triggers — no `pull_request` and no `push`. The PR-tier jobs it carries (`basic: proxy port fallbacks` in the copy, `basic: NixOS host evaluation`) and the flake checks that actually exercise repo packages therefore never run on a pull request at all; the dedicated `proxy-port-fallbacks.yml` covers only the one script.

Observed on PR #6432 (merged 2026-11-08 as b908d1d2, closing #6383):

- Head `9a5bb9cb` has exactly **one** check run — CodeRabbit (neutral) — and **zero** Actions workflow runs.
- The merge produced only the `scripts-test` and `id` push runs.
- The PR's evidence line claimed `nix build --no-link .#checks.x86_64-linux.deploy-list-malformed .#checks.x86_64-linux.deploy-list` passed, but **nothing in CI ever executed that check** for the change. It landed on the PR author's own local run (or an unverified claim).
- The `nix ci` schedule run for 2026-11-07 14:53Z was still `queued` at merge time, so the nightly backstop had not covered it either.

## Why it matters

`.github/ci-policy.md` says the basic PR tier is the merge gate. For any change whose only real regression coverage is a flake check (`deploy-list-malformed`, `deploy-list`, the deploy registry checks, etc.), there is currently no gate: the merge queue validates `basic: proxy port fallbacks` only, and this class of check is not in it. A PR can claim a flake check passed and be merged without any independent execution.

## Ask

Decide and implement one of:

1. Add a `pull_request` trigger (with `paths` limited to the packages whose checks are cheap enough for the PR tier) to `nix ci`, promoting the relevant flake checks to `basic:` jobs; or
2. Add a dedicated `basic: deploy flake checks` workflow (like `proxy-port-fallbacks.yml`) on `pull_request` + `merge_group`, running `deploy-list` and `deploy-list-malformed`; and
3. Either way, make the merge-gate story explicit in `.github/ci-policy.md` so a PR body claiming a flake check passed is either backed by a check run or rejected.

## Acceptance

- A PR touching `pkgs/deploy/**` or `lib/default.nix` produces a required, `basic:`-prefixed check run that executes `deploy-list` and `deploy-list-malformed`.
- The check appears in the PR check list within the normal PR-tier latency, and `ci-policy.md` names it.

Found while triaging #6383 (queue task 12524). Related: #6376, #5766.


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

Follow these directives and areas of focus:

COMPREHENSIVE REPOSITORY & ACTIVITY AUDIT - Inspect recent commits on `main` to understand the latest velocity and architectural direction. - Review open, recently closed, and merged issues and PRs (`gh issue list --state all --limit 50`, `gh pr list --state all --limit 30`). - Review each major package, tool, and subsystem in the repository:

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts` — the producer that writes the charge candidates the daily collector matches against real money movement — has no unknown-argument rejection. Argv is probed token-by-token only:

- `argValue()` (produce-charge-candidates.ts:112-114) finds a flag via `process.argv.indexOf(flag)` and takes the next token.
- `--skip-gmail` is checked via `process.argv.includes(...)` in `main()` (:454).

Every other aggregator operator script has been given a strict `rejectUnknownArgs()` contract that exits 2 before any I/O (append-usage-snapshots #6961, compact-usage-snapshots #6967, backfill-usage-snapshots #6973, generate-digest #7097, collect-github-billing #7254, post-alert #7289, collect-fleet-feed #3352/#3509). This producer — the one that calls the Plaid and Gmail connector CLIs and writes `charges-candidates.json` — is the remaining exception.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ cf39c3aba1)

Staged mode against an empty `CHARGE_INPUTS_DIR` (any argv rejection would exit 2 with a usage error before touching the staged files):

- `bun run scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts --bogus-flag` → proceeds into staged I/O and dies with `ENOENT` on `charge-inputs-manifest.json` at produce-charge-candidates.ts:424 — the unknown flag was silently ignored, exactly like the control run with the valid `--skip-gmail`.
- By the same `indexOf`/`includes` construction (code-read, matching the sibling bugs): a typo'd `--skip-gmial` silently runs the Gmail read path the operator meant to skip; a typo'd `--strat 2024-01-01` or a joined `--start=2024-01-01` silently falls back to the default current-month period; a duplicate `--start` silently takes the first value.

## Why it matters

This script's output feeds the charges auto-matcher (admission rule #3161: a candidate exists only where money demonstrably moved). A silently wrong period or an unexpectedly-run Gmail pass produces a plausible-looking candidates file for the wrong window under a success-style run — the operator has no signal anything was mistyped. The sibling fixes established that "exit 2 before any connector call or file write" is the house contract for exactly this failure mode; the existing test file already has the harness for it (`liveHarness()` + `expectCliUsageError()` in `test/produce-charge-candidates.test.ts`, used for the date validations).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unknown, misspelled, joined (`--start=...`), duplicate, and positional arguments exit 2 with a usage error before any connector CLI call, staged-file read, or candidates-file write (in both live and staged modes; `--start`/`--end` remain accepted-and-ignored in staged mode, as documented).
- [ ] Documented forms keep working: `[--start YYYY-MM-DD] [--end YYYY-MM-DD] [--out <path>] [--skip-gmail]`, with the existing value validations (#4663, real-calendar-date, ordering) unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests added (the existing `expectCliUsageError` harness asserts exit 2, the message, no Plaid/Gmail stub calls, and no output file written) and the aggregator test suite stays green.

body:
# aggregator(produce-charge-candidates): unknown/misspelled/joined/duplicate arguments silently ignored — a typo'd `--strat` writes candidates for the wrong (default) period, a typo'd `--skip-gmal` runs the Gmail read anyway, all exit 0

## Summary

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/produce-charge-candidates.ts` probes argv token-by-token only: `argValue()` does `process.argv.indexOf(flag)` (`:112`) and the Gmail opt-out is `process.argv.includes("--skip-gmail")` (`:454`). There is no unknown-argument rejection. The value half of this script's argument contract was hardened by #3333 (trailing/flag-like values, real-calendar dates, `end >= start`), but the unknown-token half was left — the same residual pattern fixed in the sibling scripts by #6961 (append-usage-snapshots), #6967 (compact-usage-snapshots), #6973 (backfill-usage-snapshots), #7097 (generate-digest), #7254 (collect-github-billing), and #7289 (post-alert). Part of the #3352 "unknown means stop" family.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `688f44dbe0`)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-charge-unknown-args` — the real script copied verbatim (md5 `5763f90fa815740affa56238690bad88`, identical to the laptop primary at `688f44dbe0`; `src/charges-match.ts` md5-matched too), Bun, `PLAID_CLI`/`GMAIL_CLI` pointed at stubs that log their arguments, `CHARGE_CANDIDATES_PATH` pointed at a probe-local file:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| control: `--skip-gmail --start 2026-09-01 --end 2026-09-30 --out <probe>/control.json` | exit 0; period `2026-09-01..2026-09-30`; Plaid queried `--start-date 2026-09-01 --end-date 2026-09-30`; Gmail not called |
| typo'd flag: `--strat 2026-09-01 --end 2026-12-31 --skip-gmail` | exit 0; period silently became **`2026-11-01..2026-12-31`** (the default current-month start); Plaid queried for the wrong period; candidates file written for it |
| joined flag: `--start=2026-09-01 --end 2026-12-31 --skip-gmail` | exit 0; same wrong default period `2026-11-01..2026-12-31` written |
| typo'd opt-out: `--skip-gmal --start 2026-09-01 --end 2026-09-30` | exit 0; the Gmail read the operator asked to skip **ran anyway** (two `gmail +triage` calls logged) |
| duplicate flag: `--start 2026-09-01 --start 2026-10-01 --end 2026-12-31 --skip-gmail` | exit 0; first `--start` silently wins (period `2026-09-01..2026-12-31`), no complaint |
| unknown token: `--bogus` with otherwise valid flags | exit 0; silently ignored |

## Why it matters

This producer writes `charges-candidates.json`, the live input the fleet-feed collector consumes for charge matching. The dangerous direction is silent: an operator who typos the period produces — and overwrites the candidates file with — a batch for the *default* period while believing they produced the requested one, and an operator who typos the Gmail opt-out triggers the connector reads they explicitly asked to skip. Nothing in the output line looks wrong; it prints the substituted period as if it were requested. The sibling scripts were all fixed for exactly this class because a misspelled flag must be a usage error, never a silent change of behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argv token that is not a known flag (`--start`, `--end`, `--out`, `--skip-gmail`) or a known flag's value is a usage error: exit 2 with a message naming the token, before any connector call or file write (mirrors `rejectUnknownArgs()` in `post-alert.ts` / `generate-digest.ts`).
- [ ] Joined forms (`--start=2026-09-01`) and duplicated value flags are likewise usage errors, not silently ignored / first-wins.
- [ ] Known flags keep working unchanged in both modes: live mode explicit periods and staged mode (`CHARGE_INPUTS_DIR` set), where `--start`/`--end` remain accepted-but-ignored per the staged-manifest contract pinned by the existing test "staged manifest period remains authoritative over CLI period flags".
- [ ] Regression tests in `test/produce-charge-candidates.test.ts` (the existing `liveHarness`/`expectCliUsageError` harness) cover: unknown token, typo'd `--strat`, joined `--start=`, duplicate `--start`, and typo'd `--skip-gmal` — each asserting exit 2, no Plaid/Gmail stub calls, and no candidates file written or overwritten; the new tests fail on the pre-fix script.
- [ ] The existing `produce-charge-candidates` suite stays green.

title: Daily flake sync & config optimization

labels.name: source/dispatch
labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
Perform the daily configuration review for developing-today/code. Do NOT update the `opencode` or `openchamber` flake inputs — the flake-inputs-update workflow owns them.
Follow these instructions and rules:
### 1. FLAKE INPUTS — OWNED ELSEWHERE, DO NOT BUMP - The `opencode` and `openchamber` flake inputs are owned by the deterministic
  `flake-inputs-update` workflow, which bumps, validates, and merges them daily.
  Do NOT run `nix flake update` for them, do NOT change their pins in `flake.lock`,
  and do NOT open PRs that bump them. If their pins look stale, leave them — the
  owning workflow handles them the same day.
- Do NOT casually bump root `nixpkgs` (root nixpkgs is pinned deliberately per system stability policies). - Clean up any stale input overrides or unused flake dependencies in `flake.nix` (e.g. warnings about non-existent input overrides like gitignore or devshell).
### 2. CONFIGURATION & INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS - Investigate potential configuration improvements in `nixos/`, `home/`, `lib/`, and package definitions under `pkgs/`. - Check for:
  - Deprecated NixOS or Home Manager options
  - Suboptimal build phases or missing binary wrappers
  - Systemd service resilience (e.g. restart policies, socket activation)
  - Modularity and decoupling to prevent merge conflicts
- Clean up any dead code, unused flags, or documentation drift in Nix configurations.
### 3. EVALUATION & VALIDATION - Verify that all system and host configurations evaluate cleanly without errors:
  `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.nixos.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`
- Ensure git hooks, commit messages, and treefmt formatting pass cleanly.

### 4. PULL REQUEST & MERGE - If updates or improvements are present:
  - Open a clear Pull Request documenting any configuration enhancements made. Keep every related change in this one PR — never split changes into one PR per item.
  - Merge into `main` only when you are reasonably certain it is correct: all Nix evaluations and checks succeed, the PR is conflict-free, and the changes are limited to the intended bumps and fixes. Merging is permitted, never required — when any of that is uncertain, leave the PR open and explain what a human should check.

title: aggregator(post-alert): unknown/misspelled flags are silently ignored — a typo'd --severty posts a warning incident as critical, a typo'd --bodi drops the body, exit 0

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/post-alert.ts` — the one CLI every sentinel uses to post to the alert throat (#3676) — reads each flag with a bare `process.argv.indexOf` lookup (`arg()`, scripts/post-alert.ts:40-41) and never scans argv for anything else. Unknown, misspelled, joined (`--flag=value`), duplicated, and stray positional arguments are silently ignored:

- `--severity` falls back to `"critical"` when the flag is not found verbatim (scripts/post-alert.ts:55), so a typo'd flag name silently **escalates** the incident.
- An unrecognized token and its value are consumed by nothing and reported by nothing; the post proceeds with exit 0.

This is the one aggregator script left out of the settled unknown-args class: `append-usage-snapshots.ts` (#6961), `compact-usage-snapshots.ts` (#6967), `backfill-usage-snapshots.ts` (#6973), `generate-digest.ts` (#7097), and `collect-github-billing.ts` (#7254) all gained `rejectUnknownArgs()` (usage error, exit 2, before any I/O). post-alert.ts got the flag-as-value guard in #3723 but never the unknown-args scan, and it has no positional-argument contract at all.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-post-alert-unknown-args` (`probe.test.ts`): the real script run verbatim as a subprocess (current main `a23b3ce454`, md5 `de4a732f8cdf4c51e7452a30ef564198`) against a stub intake server (`Bun.serve`) and a stub `bws`, in the exact style of the shipped `test/post-alert-args-3723.test.ts`. Oracle = the captured POST body + exit code.

Control passes: `--source watch --key h1 --severity warning --title "host down" --body 503` → exit 0, posts `{"severity":"warning",...,"body":"503"}`.

With a misspelled / unknown / joined argument, the script posts anyway, exit 0:

1. **Typo'd flag name** `--severty warning` → posts `{"source":"watch","key":"h1","severity":"critical","title":"host down"}` — a warning incident silently filed as **critical** (critical incidents push immediately to subscribed browsers and escalate when unacknowledged; warnings do not — src/alerts.ts / src/render.ts alert-throat behavior).
2. **Joined form** `--severity=warning` → same result: posts `severity:"critical"`, exit 0.
3. **Unknown flag** `--bogus x` → silently ignored; the incident posts, exit 0.
4. **Typo'd optional flag** `--bodi 503` → posts `{"severity":"info","title":"host down"}` with **no `body` field at all** — the diagnostic body is silently dropped.
5. **Stray positional** `extra` after the documented flags → silently ignored; the incident posts, exit 0.

## Why it matters

post-alert is the fleet's single alert throat: every sentinel posts through it instead of inventing its own path. Its whole value is that the incident posted is the incident the caller named. A one-character typo in a sentinel's invocation today either (a) escalates a warning into a critical that pushes to browsers and pages on the ack window, training operators to ignore criticals, or (b) drops the diagnostic body that explains the incident — in both cases with exit 0, so the calling sentinel believes the alert was posted exactly as intended. The sibling scripts were fixed for precisely this failure shape; this CLI — the one whose output is an operator-facing alarm — is the remaining hole.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `post-alert.ts` rejects any argument it does not recognize — unknown/misspelled flag names, joined `--flag=value` forms, duplicated flags, and stray positional tokens — with a usage error naming the offending argument and exit 2, **before** any token is resolved or any fetch is made (the `rejectUnknownArgs()` contract of #6961/#6967/#7097/#7254). A flag's value token is consumed by its flag and is never itself scanned as an argument.
- [ ] The documented invocations are unchanged: all five flags (`--source`, `--key`, `--severity`, `--title`, `--body`) with space-separated values still post exactly the incident they name, and an omitted `--severity` still defaults to `critical` (both pinned by the existing #3723 tests, which stay green).
- [ ] New regression tests in the aggregator bun suite (extending `test/post-alert-args-3723.test.ts` or a sibling file, subprocess + stub intake/bws in the established style) cover at least: typo'd `--severty`, joined `--severity=warning`, an unknown flag, a typo'd `--bodi`, a duplicate flag, and a stray positional — each asserting exit 2, no bws call, and no captured POST — and each failing on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] No change to the intake request shape, the token resolution, or the server-side severity validation (src/alerts.ts already rejects non-enum severities; the defect is the CLI silently substituting the `critical` default for a flag the caller did write).

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for "post-alert" titles — #3723 covers the flag-as-value guard in the same `arg()` (fixed, different defect); no issue covers unknown/misspelled/joined/duplicate arguments for post-alert. The sibling fixes (#6961, #6967, #6973, #7097, #7254) each cover a different script.

# aggregator(collect-github-billing): unknown/misspelled flags are silently ignored — a typo'd `--yer` collects the current month, and a typo'd `--prnit` turns a dry run into a real outbox append

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ 1e46b89399; script md5 dc877e90d102f753d67a411f817464ff)

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-github-billing.ts` probes argv token-by-token and never rejects a token it does not recognize:

- Flag presence is `process.argv.includes(...)` and values are read via `process.argv[process.argv.indexOf(flag) + 1]` (`explicitArg` :52, resolvers :68/:75/:84/:93, `--print` check :145). Any other token is never examined.
- The flag VALUES were hardened in #3419 and #6922, but the unknown-token half was never done for this script — unlike its siblings (#6961 append-usage-snapshots, #6967 compact-usage-snapshots, #6973 backfill-usage-snapshots, #7097 generate-digest), which all reject unknown arguments before any I/O.

Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-billing-argv`, real script run in-tree with a stub `gh` on PATH logging its args and returning one valid billing item; `USAGE_SNAPSHOT_OUTBOX_PATH` redirected to the probe dir):

| Invocation | Observed |
|---|---|
| `--year 2024 --month 3 --print` (control) | exit 0, gh called with `year=2024&month=3`, 3 records printed, outbox untouched |
| `--yer 2024 --month 3 --print` (typo) | exit 0, gh called with **`year=2026&month=3`** — the typo'd flag was ignored and the CURRENT year was collected instead of 2024 |
| `--year 2024 --month 3 --prnit` (typo'd dry-run flag) | exit 0, **3 records appended to the outbox** — the operator's dry run silently became a real write |
| `--year 2024 --year 2025 --month 3 --print` (duplicate) | exit 0, gh called with `year=2024` — duplicate silently first-wins |

## Why it matters

This collector appends per-day billing snapshot records to the writers' outbox, which the fleet-feed collector drains into the snapshot store. Both failure modes are silent (exit 0):

1. A typo'd value flag (`--yer`, `--mont`, `--usr`, `--buy`) silently collects the *default* period/user instead of the requested one — the operator believes a backfill of a past month happened; it did not.
2. A typo'd `--prnit` converts a dry run into a real outbox append. The derived records are re-derivable (the store dedupes by key), so the damage is bounded — but a dry run that writes is exactly the contract `--print` exists to prevent, and in a month where the stub/real data differs the appended records are real billing data the operator never meant to publish.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argv token that is not `--year`/`--month`/`--user`/`--by` (each with its value) or `--print` is a usage error: message on stderr, exit 2, **before** any gh call or outbox write (mirror `rejectUnknownArgs` in generate-digest.ts / append-usage-snapshots.ts).
- [ ] A duplicated flag is rejected, not silently first-wins.
- [ ] Regression tests in the style of `test/collect-github-billing-args-3419.test.ts` cover: unknown flag, typo'd `--yer` (asserts zero gh calls), typo'd `--prnit` (asserts exit 2 and no outbox file created), duplicate `--year`, and a bare positional token.
- [ ] Existing `collect-github-billing-args-3419` tests still pass; valid control invocations unchanged.

# aggregator(generate-digest): unknown/misspelled flags are silently ignored — a typo'd `--knd weekly` archives a daily digest, and a typo'd `--no-delivre` delivers anyway

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ bfa5caede7; file md5-identical to origin/main 602b5d9ed6)

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/generate-digest.ts` probes argv token-by-token and never rejects a token it does not recognize:

- `arg()` (:32-33) finds `--kind` via `process.argv.indexOf(...)` only; any other `--flag` token is never examined.
- Delivery suppression is `process.argv.includes("--no-deliver")` (:77) and strict mode is `process.argv.includes("--strict-deliver")` (:120) — a misspelling simply makes the check false.
- The USAGE string (:23) documents exactly three flags (`--kind`, `--no-deliver`, `--strict-deliver`), but nothing enforces that set.

Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-digest-unknown-args/probe.test.ts`, subprocess runs of the real script with `PM_AGG_SOURCE=fixtures` and an isolated `PM_AGG_DIGESTS_DIR`, same pattern as `test/generate-digest-kind-6926.test.ts`):

| Invocation | Observed |
|---|---|
| `--kind weekly --no-deliver` (control) | exit 0, `weekly-2026-11-08.json` archived, no delivery attempt |
| `--knd weekly --no-deliver` (typo) | exit 0, **`daily-2026-11-08.json` archived** — the weekly request silently became a daily digest |
| `--bogus --no-deliver` | exit 0, daily digest archived — unknown flag ignored |
| `--kind weekly --no-delivre` (typo) | weekly archived, then the **delivery path ran anyway** (proceeded to fetch push subscriptions from Supabase; probe run exited 1 on that fetch) — the operator's do-not-deliver instruction was silently dropped |
| `--kind weekly --kind daily --no-deliver` | exit 0, weekly archived — duplicate flag silently first-wins |

## Why it matters

This script is run by systemd timers (daily/weekly digest) and by hand. Its two failure modes are both silent and one is irreversible:

1. A typo'd kind produces and archives the wrong digest under the wrong date route (`/digest/<date>` renders the archive verbatim), with exit 0 — automation and operators see success.
2. A typo'd `--no-deliver` sends Web Push notifications to every stored subscription that the operator explicitly meant to suppress. A sent push cannot be unsent.

This is the same defect class fixed per-script in #6961 (append-usage-snapshots), #6967 (compact-usage-snapshots) and #6973 (backfill-usage-snapshots) — reject unknown arguments before any I/O — and the value-guard half for this script was already fixed in #6926. The unknown-token half was left behind here.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Any argv token that is not `--kind` (with its value), `--no-deliver`, or `--strict-deliver` is a usage error: message + USAGE on stderr, exit 2, **before** any archive write or delivery attempt.
- [ ] A duplicate `--kind` is rejected (or otherwise explicitly handled), not silently first-wins.
- [ ] Regression tests in the style of `test/generate-digest-kind-6926.test.ts` cover: unknown flag, typo'd `--knd`, typo'd `--no-delivre` (asserts no delivery attempt / exit 2 / nothing archived), and the valid control invocations still pass.
- [ ] Existing `generate-digest-kind-6926` tests still pass.

# fix(pm-stack backup): pmp_links backup source resolution and offsite assertions — follow-up to merged PR #5315 (for #1744)

Bounded follow-up to unresolved review findings on merged PR #5315, filed by triage task 11960 (issue #1744) so the fix has a fresh dedupe key.

## Problem

The merged PR #5315 pmp_links archive path still has unresolved source-selection and verification gaps:

- `DATABASE_URL` handling may select the wrong entry or local database (last-assignment parsing, CR/edge-whitespace and quote handling).
- Remote/unsupported non-file URLs can silently fall through to a local default instead of failing explicitly; `file:` URL paths are not decoded before existence checks.
- Relative/default DB resolution can miss the active projector file under `PM_PROJECTOR_DIR` before falling back to the state directory.
- The upload test can pass when only one offsite destination (R2 or Drive) was called — it must require both.

This weakens the backup evidence needed for issue #1744 criterion 3 (one backup target covers the stack's data).

## Evidence

- PR #5315 is MERGED; its CodeRabbit review on commit 7c34d0ab1a has unresolved findings for: last `DATABASE_URL` assignment/parsing, file URL decoding, unsupported non-file URL fallback, `PM_PROJECTOR_DIR` default resolution, and requiring both R2 and Drive upload calls in the test.
- Files: `nixos/home/pm-dashboard-backup.sh`, `nixos/home/pm-dashboard-backup-pmp-links.test.sh` (at main edef34824f8be24a56a170e6aca3f44251c20caf when scoped).
- Issue #1744: acceptance criteria 1-2 checked; criterion 3 remains unchecked.

## Acceptance criteria

- Resolve `DATABASE_URL` using the last matching environment-file assignment; trim CR/edge whitespace plus one matching quote pair without altering interior path characters.
- Decode `file:` URL paths before existence checks; do not silently fall back to a local database for an unsupported non-file `DATABASE_URL` (fail explicitly unless remote export is implemented).
- Resolve the active relative/default projector database under `PM_PROJECTOR_DIR` before using the existing state-directory fallback.
- The with-database archive test passes only when the stub log records `copyto` calls to both R2 and Drive.
- Targeted tests pass: `nixos/home/pm-dashboard-backup-pmp-links.test.sh` and `nixos/home/pm-dashboard-backup-manifest.test.sh`.
- Out of scope: re-implementing the merged pmp_links export, migrating service data, changing issue #1744's architecture or criteria.

Refs: issue #1744, PR #5315, PR #6183, task 11960.

body:
## Background

Child of the #7079 stranded-work audit. The laptop's `~/git/fleet` is not a working clone — it is a lane scratch yard wearing a repo's name: a shell clone with 4 tracked files and no remotes, holding 1,581 top-level untracked entries, ~610,000 files, ~242 GB. Composition (measured 2026-11-07): 1,276 `probe-*` throwaway sandboxes, ~240 task dirs, 198 nested clones of the real repos, watcher-bench fixture floods (371k generated `.txt` files), and large duplicated Rust build output (~75k `target/` segments; the 25 largest files are 0.7–1 GB debug binaries duplicated across ID task checkouts). Spot-checked nested clones are clean with heads equal to their live remote tips — nothing is stranded in them. The yard is in LIVE use (new dirs created during the audit itself).

Drew's disposition rule (2026-11-07 21:31 CST): **KEEP text, scripts, and markdown.** The yard's human-authored ephemera is preserved; everything else is reappable.

## Spec — build a scratch-yard reaper for ~/git/fleet

A scheduled, janitor-pattern reaper (same operating rules as the disk janitor), run on the laptop against `~/git/fleet` only.

### KEEP — archive-first
- Every human-authored text/script/markdown file anywhere in the yard: `.md .txt .sh .py .ts .js .json .yaml .yml .toml .log` and equivalent human-authored text (lane logs, PR-body drafts, triage notes, probe scripts, docs).
- The ~92 loose root files are the known-precious set — archive ALL of them.
- Archive exactly like the disk janitor: gather into the dated archive layout (archive branch / janitor archive tree), commit ALL, push, and VERIFY the push landed before any removal of a kept file's original. Nothing kept is ever deleted before its archive copy is verified.

### REAP — only after the keep-archive verifies
- Build output and duplicated bulk: `target/` trees, `.o`/`.d`/`.rmeta`/`.rlib` artifacts, `dist/`, `node_modules/`.
- Bench fixture floods: watcher-bench `.txt` fixtures are GENERATED bulk despite the `.txt` extension — the keep rule covers human-authored text, not fixture floods. The reaper MUST use provenance/size heuristics (fixture dirs by name, per-file and per-dir caps, generated-content markers) to separate fixture bulk from authored text, and its run plan must state the heuristics it applied.
- Nested clones whose heads are verified clean AND equal to their remote tips (nothing unlanded). A nested clone with ANY unlanded state (dirty files, unpushed commits, detached work not on a remote) is archive-first, never reaped blind.

### Safety gates
- Age gate: reap only entries idle ≥ 4 hours (the janitor's rule). The yard is in live use — never touch an entry with recent mtimes, an attached live process, or a registered worktree pointing into it.
- No recursive/wildcard deletes of anything not inventoried by the run's own scan; every reap is a named entry from the run report.
- First runs are dry-run/report-only until the keep-archive path is proven end-to-end.

### Report per run
- GB reclaimed, files kept/archived (count + archive ref), entries reaped (count + GB), entries skipped (active or dirty) BY NAME.

## Acceptance
- Reaper exists as a repeatable tool + schedule on the laptop, scoped to `~/git/fleet`.
- One full run report demonstrating: keep-archive verified before reap, age gate respected, live entries untouched, GB reclaimed counted.
- The ~242 GB yard trends down without losing a single human-authored file.

## Acceptance criteria

- The reaper exists as a repeatable tool plus a schedule on the laptop, scoped to `~/git/fleet` only.
- The keep-archive (all human-authored text/scripts/markdown, including the ~92 loose root files) is committed, pushed, and the push verified BEFORE any kept file's original is removed.
- Reaping respects the safety gates: entries idle ≥ 4 hours only, no live-process or registered-worktree entries touched, no recursive/wildcard deletes — every reap is a named entry from the run's own scan.
- Bench fixture floods are separated from authored text by stated provenance/size heuristics recorded in the run report.
- One full run report demonstrates: keep-archive verified before reap, age gate respected, live entries untouched, GB reclaimed counted, entries kept/reaped/skipped (by name) listed.
- The ~242 GB yard trends down without losing a single human-authored file.

body:
# lab-ops-hub: POST /api/files returns a raw 500 for a non-multipart body and for a text 'file' field — the multipart body is never validated

## Evidence

`pkgs/lab-ops-hub/src/index.ts:378-382` (main `0d75b17aab`):

```ts
if (p === "/api/files" && req.method === "POST") {
  const form = await req.formData();              // :379 — unguarded
  const file = form.get("file") as File | null;    // :380 — bare cast
  if (!file) return json({ error: "multipart field 'file' required" }, 400);
  const buf = await file.arrayBuffer();            // :382
```

- `req.formData()` is called with no try/catch. Any body that is not
  `multipart/form-data` (or url-encoded) — a JSON body, a plain-text body, an
  empty body — makes `formData()` throw a `TypeError`, which escapes to the
  route's outer catch and is answered **500 with the raw internal error text**
  (`String(e)`), instead of the 400 client-error vocabulary every sibling
  POST route uses (`parseJsonObjectBody` in `src/lib.ts`, from #2480).
- `form.get("file")` returns a **string** when the multipart field is a text
  field, not a `File`. The bare `as File` cast hides that: a text field named
  `file` passes the `!file` guard and then crashes at :382 with
  `TypeError: file.arrayBuffer is not a function` — again a raw 500. (Had it
  survived, `file.name` / `file.type` would be `undefined` into `uploadKey`
  and the D1 bind.)

## Verified this run (laptop probe, real modules)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-labops-files` on the laptop: the real
`src/index.ts` / `src/lib.ts` / `src/html5-entities.ts` (md5-verified
identical to main `0d75b17aab`), driven through the real `fetch` handler
with stub D1/R2/Queue bindings:

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| control: multipart with a real `File` | **201**, R2 put + D1 files insert + index-file job queued |
| multipart with a **text** field named `file` | **500** `TypeError: file.arrayBuffer is not a function` |
| JSON body (not multipart) | **500** `TypeError: Content-Type was not one of "multipart/form-data" or "application/x-www-form-urlencoded".` |
| plain-text body | **500**, same raw TypeError |
| empty body | **500**, same raw TypeError |
| multipart with no `file` field | 400 `multipart field 'file' required` (existing guard works) |

## Why it matters

This is the one POST route in the hub that #2480's validation pass could not
cover (it is multipart, not JSON), and it shows both of that issue's failure
modes: a malformed client request is reported as a server fault, and the 500
body leaks the runtime's internal error text. A client uploading with the
wrong content type — the most common upload integration mistake — gets an
indistinguishable-from-a-real-outage 500 and no actionable message.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A POST /api/files whose body cannot be parsed as form data (wrong
      content type, malformed multipart, empty body) returns **400** with a
      stable error message in the route's JSON vocabulary, never a 500 and
      never raw `TypeError` text.
- [ ] A multipart `file` field that is not a file (a text/string field)
      returns **400** naming the field, before any R2/D1/Queue side effect.
- [ ] A genuine file upload is unchanged: 201 with R2 put, D1 row, and the
      `index-file` queue message, exactly as today.
- [ ] Regression coverage pins all three cases above (the string-field and
      non-multipart cases fail on the pre-fix code); the existing
      lab-ops-hub TS suite still passes.

Related: #2480 (JSON POST routes' 400 vocabulary — this route is the
multipart residual), #6975 (optional-field binding on the JSON routes;
distinct defect, distinct route).

title: pm-dispatch(opencode): auth-file and API-response JSON parsed unguarded — null/malformed state file escapes as raw Type/SyntaxError, non-string password silently coerced into the credential

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts` — the dispatch service's only client for the laptop OpenCode server — parses two JSON inputs with bare `JSON.parse` + a type cast, outside any guard, so wrong-shape or malformed input escapes as raw `TypeError`/`SyntaxError` instead of the module's own `OpenCodeError` (the error type that carries the client's 502 semantics), and a non-string password is silently coerced into the live Basic credential.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary main `0d75b17aab`, real module md5 `fd102fcacafd2a3ddb3d05dfe906c66f`)

- `authHeader()` (opencode.ts:18-27): the `try/catch` guards only `readFile` (:19-24). Line 25 is `const data = JSON.parse(raw) as { password?: string }` — outside the guard, cast-only. Line 26 checks truthiness only, never the type.
- `api()` (opencode.ts:44): `const parsed: unknown = JSON.parse(text)` on a 2xx response is likewise unguarded.
- Probe (laptop `~/git/fleet/probe-dispatch-opencode/`, real `opencode.ts` verbatim + a stub OpenCode server; `createSession` drives `authHeader` + `api`):

  | Case | Observed |
  |---|---|
  | control `{"password":"pw123"}` + `{"data":{"id":…}}` | resolves, session id returned |
  | control `{}` (no password) | `OpenCodeError: opencode auth file carries no password` (the intended vocabulary) |
  | auth file `null` | raw `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'data.password')` — not an `OpenCodeError` |
  | auth file `{not json` (truncated/mid-write state file) | raw `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error` — not an `OpenCodeError` |
  | auth file `{"password":12345}` | **request succeeds**: the number is string-coerced into the `Authorization: Basic` credential |
  | auth file `{"password":{"x":1}}` | **request succeeds**: the credential sent is the literal `[object Object]` string |
  | valid auth + HTTP 200 non-JSON body (`<html>…`, e.g. the wrong service answering on the OpenCode port) | raw `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token '<'` — not an `OpenCodeError` |

- There is no test file for this client at all: `pm-stack/dispatch/test/` covers auth/config/packet/queue/server/validate/launch_*, but no `opencode.test.ts` exists.

## Why it matters

- The auth file is the OpenCode server's own state file (`service-prod.json`, config.ts `opencodeAuthFile`), read on **every** API call. A truncated or mid-write read, a hand-edited file, or a schema drift in what the server writes turns every dispatch launch into a raw crash whose message names no file and no cause; the dispatch handler (server.ts) only special-cases Auth/Validation/Queue errors, so these surface as generic 500s / launch-failure notes instead of the client's diagnosable 502 shape.
- A non-string password never errors at the boundary at all: dispatch silently authenticates with a coerced garbage credential and the failure appears downstream as an OpenCode 401, blamed on the server rather than on the state file's shape.
- This is the same boundary-validation contract sibling dispatch modules already keep (validate.ts validates every request field; queue.ts checks the RPC row's `id` type; createSession itself validates the returned session `id` at opencode.ts:61-64) — the auth file and the 2xx body are the two unguarded doors in the same file.

## Acceptance criteria

- `authHeader()`: malformed JSON, a non-object document (null/array/scalar), and a missing, non-string, or empty `password` all throw `OpenCodeError` naming the auth file / the shape problem — never a raw `TypeError`/`SyntaxError`, and a non-string password is never coerced into a credential.
- `api()`: a 2xx response whose body is not valid JSON throws `OpenCodeError` naming the method/path — never a raw `SyntaxError`.
- A new `pm-stack/dispatch/test/opencode.test.ts` pins all of the probe cases above (valid control still resolves; `{}` control still yields the existing no-password `OpenCodeError`).
- Existing dispatch suite still passes (`bun test` in `pm-stack/dispatch`).

Found by new-issue-creator-code-b (Lane B), run 2026-11-07 20:50 CST. Dedup: searched open + closed issues for OpenCodeClient / "opencode auth" / dispatch opencode parsing — no existing issue covers this client; #3009 (orphaned session) and #3010 (body-cap units) are different defects in different files.

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpclient/handoff.go:180` — `procStat(pid)` reads `/proc/<pid>/stat` unconditionally (verified at `origin/main` 801ceb9cb16668041e85b4451443ac7d91647ffe). The file has no build constraints and there is no darwin alternative, so the process start-time / identity checks used during handoff detach (`ProcessStartTime`, and the pid-identity check at handoff.go:166-175) fail on any platform without `/proc` — including aarch64-darwin, where mcpx is deployed via dezren39/nix.

It is the only failing package (`internal/pool`, via this path) and it gates the nix mcpx package checkPhase.
- Same family as #237 item 3 (`/proc/<pid>/exe`), which PR #3288 already fixed for the daemon test package; this one is in production (non-test) code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Process start-time/identity for handoff works on aarch64-darwin via a portable source (e.g. sysctl `kern.proc` KP_EPROC / `proc_pidpath`-family equivalent), **or** returns an explicit unsupported-platform error and the affected handoff tests skip on darwin with a stated reason — no bare `/proc/...stat: no such file or directory` failures
- [ ] `internal/mcpclient` and `internal/pool` suites still pass on Linux with no regressions; `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/darwin-compile-check.sh` still passes

- The darwin takeover/upgrade support-or-refuse decision (stays on #237)
- Any other `/proc` uses in test helpers already covered by PR #3288

title: aggregator(check-contract-corpus): wrong-shape or non-JSON corpus files crash the contract gate with a raw stack instead of its FAIL report — remaining sections never run

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/check-contract-corpus.ts` is the contract gate CI runs on every pm-stack change (`.github/workflows/pm-aggregator-tests.yml:49`, `bun run scripts/check-contract-corpus.ts`). Its whole design is to accumulate `ok`/`FAIL` lines and finish with a summary (`contract check FAILED: N check(s): …`, lines 132–136) so one bad corpus file names every divergence at once.

That design only holds for values that pass the validators. The per-file sections dereference the parsed JSON with bare casts before/without a shape guard, so a wrong-shape or non-JSON corpus file crashes the script with a raw stack, aborts every remaining section, and the summary is never printed:

- `loadJson` (line 71–73) is a bare `JSON.parse(await readFile(...))` — a non-JSON corpus file dies with a raw `SyntaxError` naming no check.
- Orchestration (lines 82–86): `(orchestration as { provenance: unknown }).provenance` dereferences a `null` body.
- Projects (line 91–93): `projects.every(...)` on a non-array (the `as unknown[]` cast does not check).
- Registry (lines 95–97): `registry.every(...)` / `sanitizeRegistry(registry)` on a non-array.
- Quota (lines 99–106): `quota.pools.every(...)`, `quota.burn.every(...)`, `sanitizeQuotaView(quota)` on `null` / `{}` (no `pools`).
- Feed (lines 112–117): `feed[name]` on a `null` feed.

The publisher-file section (lines 121 ff.) already shows the intended pattern: parse failure becomes a `check(..., false, ...)` entry and the run continues. The corpus sections never got it. Residual of #6930, which guarded only this script's argv values.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ 107ac37d27)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-contract-corpus/` — real script run with `bun run scripts/check-contract-corpus.ts --corpus <dir>` against copies of the shipped corpus (`test/contract-corpus/v1/`), one file mutated at a time.

- Control (unmutated corpus): all checks `ok`, `contract check passed.`, exit 0.
- `projects.json` = `{}` → prints the `isProjectPoolSection` FAIL, then `TypeError: projects.every is not a function` at line 93, exit 1, no summary, registry/quota/feed sections never run.
- `quota.json` = `null` → `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'quota.pools')` at line 100.
- `quota.json` = `{}` → `TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'quota.pools.every')` at line 100.
- `registry.json` = `{}` → `TypeError: registry.every is not a function` at line 96.
- `feed.json` = `null` → prints the `isFleetFeed` FAIL, then `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'feed[name]')` at line 117.
- `orchestration.json` = `null` → prints the section FAIL (`not an object`), then `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'orchestration.provenance')` at line 84.
- `dns.json` = `not json{` → raw `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error` out of `loadJson` (line 72), no check line at all.

In every case the exit code is 1 — indistinguishable from a normal failed check — but the output is a stack trace that stops at the first bad file, so a corpus PR with two divergences reports only the first (and as a crash, not a finding).

## Why it matters

This script is the pre-publish/CI gate for the publisher → collector → aggregator contract (#1176). A corpus edit that changes a file's shape (exactly the class of change the corpus exists to catch) currently produces a misleading crash instead of the gate's own FAIL report, and hides every other section's result behind it. Maintainers must re-run locally file-by-file to learn what a single CI run should have listed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every corpus file is loaded defensively: a missing/non-JSON/wrong-shape file records a `FAIL` check naming the file (and the shape/parse problem) instead of throwing.
- [ ] No unguarded dereference remains on parsed corpus values: orchestration provenance access, `projects.every`, `registry.every`/`sanitizeRegistry`, `quota.pools`/`quota.burn`/`sanitizeQuotaView`, and `feed[name]` all tolerate `null`/non-object/non-array inputs.
- [ ] With one or several mutated corpus files, the run still executes every remaining section, prints the `contract check FAILED: N check(s)` summary, and exits 1 (not via an uncaught exception/stack).
- [ ] The unmutated shipped corpus still passes end-to-end (exit 0, `contract check passed.`), and the #6930 argv behavior (usage error, exit 2) is unchanged.
- [ ] A regression test in the style of `test/check-contract-corpus-args-6930.test.ts` spawns the script against mutated fixture corpora (at least: non-array projects, `null` quota, `null` feed, non-JSON file) and pins the FAIL-line + summary + exit-1 behavior; the new tests fail on the pre-fix script.
