labels.name: kind/question
labels.description: Question or design decision to resolve

body:
## The idea (Drew, 2026-10-28 — filed for consideration, not yet a build order)

Give OpenClaw a fifth ACP coding harness, agentId `muse`, alongside opencode / claude / codex / agy: an ACP adapter that drives the **Muse CLI** the way the bundled adapters drive the Claude/Codex CLIs. OpenClaw's acpx has no built-in muse agent and no bundled adapter — this is new code, sized like the other adapters.

## What already exists

- **The Muse CLI is installed and logged in on the laptop**: Muse Code 1.4.13, `~/.config/muse/auth.json` present. Drew's settled mapping (2026-10-25): the muse program's OAuth login draws on the **Muse API High Usage plan** — the SAME single Meta pool the `meta` provider uses. It never touches the assistant's own subscription.
- **Our muse-proxy (built 2026-10-21)**: an OpenAI-compatible proxy shelling to `muse exec --json` per request (codex-proxy pattern), formerly wiring an OpenCode `muse` provider on :18747. That provider was **disabled by Drew's order 2026-10-25** as a second, wasteful door into the same pool for MODEL routing — the proxy service is inactive now. An ACP harness is a different surface from a model route (it runs Muse's own agent loop, tools and session handling, rather than putting Muse models inside OpenCode's loop), but the relationship needs an explicit ruling, see questions.
- **External precedent**: pgquiles/opencode-muse bridges OpenCode to the official CLI via `muse serve` / the Muse SDK, sign-in and inference inside the CLI, subscription/plan-only. Proof the CLI route works as an agent host, from the OpenCode side.

## What an adapter would need

- ACP (stdio JSON-RPC: initialize / session-new / prompt / cancel / permissions) translated to the Muse CLI's interface — either `muse serve` (stateful, SDK protocol) or `muse exec --json` per turn (stateless; session resume semantics to design).
- Packaging in the flake like the other adapters + a per-agent command override in home/openclaw (the pattern the claude/codex/agy enablement just used) + an allowedAgents entry.
- A smoke test: ACP session spawn from OpenClaw, one real coding turn, plan usage visible in the High Usage pool readings afterwards.

## Questions to settle before building

1. **Second-door ruling**: does an ACP muse harness reopen the concern that closed the muse provider on 2026-10-25, or is the agent-loop distinction (Muse's own tools/session vs a model route) enough to make it a first-class door?
2. **Quota discipline**: harness turns would draw the High Usage pool outside the stewardship measurement gate that governs session dispatch. How are they metered/capped — and does the pool's existing plan-only rule (never PAYG) hold for harness spend?
3. **serve vs exec**: which CLI interface maps to ACP session semantics with less invention?
4. **Auth placement**: the CLI OAuth lives on the laptop today; does the harness need its own login lifecycle handling (expiry, refresh) the way the proxies learned to?

## Acceptance (if this graduates from consideration)

A short design note answering the four questions lands first; build only on Drew's go after that.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A short design note answers the four questions in the issue body (adapter shape, pool accounting, session semantics, maintenance ownership) and is linked from this issue.
- [ ] No build work starts before Drew's explicit go on that design note (this issue is a consideration, not a build order).
- [ ] If it graduates: the adapter drives the Muse CLI over ACP alongside the existing opencode/claude/codex/agy agents, with the Meta pool mapping respected (the muse program's OAuth route only; never the disabled OpenCode `muse` provider).

title: mcpx(searchpath): List reports a name as ambiguous even when a nearer entry already resolves it — the name is both listed and warned, while Find resolves it cleanly

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`searchpath.Resolved.List` and `Resolved.Find` disagree about the same resolved path. When a nearer directory provides a name unambiguously and a farther (shadowed) directory holds an overlapping `.ts`/`.js` pair for the same name, `Find` resolves the name cleanly to the nearer file — but `List` returns the name in its results **and** reports it in its ambiguity list. Nearest-wins is List's own documented rule ("the nearer occurrence of a duplicated name winning"), so a name that was won cannot also be ambiguous.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `211aa58f`)

- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/searchpath/searchpath.go:191-245` (`List`): the per-directory stem loop checks `len(hits) > 1 && !AllowOverlap` (line 233) and appends an `Ambiguity` **before** the `seen` duplicate check (line ~240), so the ambiguity branch runs for stems a nearer entry already provided. `Find` (line 146) returns at the first entry with a hit and never reaches the shadowed directory.
- Probe executed this run on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-10-28-lanea-searchpath/`, `searchpath.go` copied verbatim, sha256 `92c048ed…`; log in the goal's `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-28-laneA-searchpath/probe.log`):
  - Layout: near dir holds only `shared.ts`; far dir holds `shared.ts` + `shared.js`; extensions `[.ts, .js]`, overlap not allowed.
  - `Find("shared")` → `<near>/shared.ts`, ambiguity `nil`, error `nil`.
  - `List()` → names `[shared]`, ambiguous `[{shared [<far>/shared.js <far>/shared.ts]}]` — the same name is simultaneously listed and warned as ambiguous (probe test FAILs on current code).
- The existing test `TestListReportsEveryNameNearestWinning` covers a duplicated name with no overlap anywhere; the shadowed-overlap shape is untested.
- Honest scope note: `List` currently has no in-repo production caller (only tests call it); it is the package's exported listing API, and its two outputs contradicting each other — and contradicting `Find` — is the defect, at low priority.

## Why it matters

A consumer rendering List's output (a scripts listing with warnings) would tell the user `shared` is both available and unusable-until-they-pick-one, when running it via `Find` works with no choice needed. The ambiguity warning exists to force a deliberate pick where the outcome is genuinely undecided; a shadowed pair decides nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `List` does not report an ambiguity for a stem already provided by a nearer entry (the `seen` check governs shadowed stems), matching `Find`'s nearest-wins outcome for the same `Resolved`.
- [ ] A stem whose **nearest** occurrence is itself an overlapping pair is still reported ambiguous and omitted from the names (existing semantics preserved).
- [ ] Regression test: near `shared.ts` only + far `shared.ts`/`shared.js` → names contain `shared`, ambiguities do not; plus the near-ambiguous case above.
- [ ] Existing `internal/searchpath` tests keep passing.

## Gap (backup audit, 2026-10-27): pm-stack application databases have no backup routine at all

This is the implementation gap under the durability design in #1258 (stack state in backed-up durable storage): the aggregator state leg landed via #1459; the database leg never did.

title: id(web): adjacent lists of different types save an <!-- end list --> comment that reopens as a phantom code block

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

In the id web markdown codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), a document where a list is **immediately followed by a list of a different type** — bullet → ordered, ordered → bullet, or task → bullet with no blank line between them — is corrupted on save: the save writes a literal `<!-- end list -->` HTML comment between the lists, and reopening the saved file turns that comment into a spurious `code_block` node sitting between the lists in the document model.

#1032 fixed this for adjacent **bullet** lists (different markers) by coalescing them on save. Different-type neighbours cannot be coalesced — a bullet list and an ordered list are genuinely different lists — so the boundary case #1032 excluded is still live.

## Evidence (verified this run on main `452d69e6`; `markdown.rs` identical at `95bfedb4` where the probe copy was taken)

Probe: verbatim copy of `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` in a standalone crate (comrak 0.56), `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown` → re-parse. Log: fleet bookkeeping `probe-2026-10-27-creator-a3/out4.log` (cases also in `out3.log`).

| Input | Save output | Re-parsed PM |
|---|---|---|
| `- a\n1. b\n` | `- a\n\n<!-- end list -->\n\n1. b\n` | bullet_list, **`code_block{params:"html", htmlBlock:true}` containing `<!-- end list -->`**, ordered_list |
| `1. a\n- b\n` | `1. a\n\n<!-- end list -->\n\n- b\n` | ordered_list, **same spurious code_block**, bullet_list |
| `- a\n- b\n1. c\n2. d\n` | comment inserted at the type boundary | **same spurious code_block** between the lists |
| `1. [ ] t\n- plain\n` | `1. [ ] t\n\n<!-- end list -->\n\n- plain\n` | task_list, **same spurious code_block**, bullet_list |
| `> - a\n> 1. b\n` (inside blockquote) | `> - a\n> \n> <!-- end list -->\n> \n> 1. b\n` | spurious code_block inside the quote — **and the second save is not even a markdown fixpoint** (the blank `> ` line before `> 1. b` is dropped) |

Root cause, both directions:

- Save: `json_to_ast`'s child loop coalesces only consecutive `bullet_list` siblings (`markdown.rs:1464-1487`, the #1032 fix; its comment notes ordered/task lists are deliberately untouched). Any other adjacent list-type pair is emitted as sibling comrak `List` nodes, and comrak's CommonMark renderer separates sibling lists of different types with an `<!-- end list -->` comment.
- Parse: the comment comes back as an `HtmlBlock`, and the `NodeValue::HtmlBlock` arm (`markdown.rs:391-419`, the #982 fallback) converts it into a `code_block` with `params:"html"` / `htmlBlock:true`. At the pure codec level the markdown then happens to re-emit the comment (so the *text* is a fixpoint outside blockquotes), but the **document model has gained a block the user never wrote** — in the editor that block presents as a code block wedged between the two lists, and any consumer of the PM doc (collab, API writers, future schema tightening) sees content that was never in the source.

Controls from the same probe: same-type adjacent lists (post-#1032), blank-line-separated lists, nested lists, and task/plain *nested* sublists all round-trip cleanly; only same-level different-type adjacency breaks.

## Why it matters

Switching from bullets to numbered steps mid-document without a blank line is a common note-taking shape (a shopping list followed by numbered prep steps; an agenda followed by action items). Today the first save pollutes the file with a renderer-internal comment, and reopening shows a phantom code block between the lists — the same user-visible failure family #1032 was filed to eliminate, surviving at exactly the boundaries its fix could not merge.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All five shapes above save with **no** `<!-- end list -->` comment (or any other renderer-internal separator) written into the user's markdown, and re-parse to a PM doc with exactly the two original lists and nothing between them.
- [ ] The blockquote shape is a full markdown fixpoint across two saves.
- [ ] The chosen separation strategy is coherent with the #1032 precedent and the #982 HTML-block provenance design, with a note in the PR on what separates the lists in the saved text (e.g. a separator the parse direction provably drops, or a save-direction rewrite that avoids sibling different-type `List` nodes reaching the renderer).
- [ ] #1032 behaviour is unchanged: adjacent bullet lists still coalesce, and its regression tests keep passing; existing `web::markdown` tests keep passing.
- [ ] Regression tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover bullet→ordered, ordered→bullet, task→bullet, and the blockquote case in both save and re-parse directions.

body:
Found in the access-pattern benchmark (code#1344), 2026-10-27: POST /api/session?directory=/tmp/oc-bench-work returned a session whose location was /home/user — the query param is silently ignored; location only takes effect via the JSON body ({"location": {"directory": ...}}). The silent fallback ran a tool-enabled session in the account home directory and wrote a file there (f1.txt in /home/user) before the cause was spotted.

Fork: developing-today/opencode v2 API. Fix options, in preference order: honor ?directory= on session create for parity with the body's location; or return a 400 when an unknown/ineffective directory param is supplied. Silent fallback to the server's home is the one unacceptable behavior. Cover with a server test: create with the query param, assert the session location (or the 400).
Acceptance: no API path can produce a session in an unintended directory without an explicit, visible signal.

## Acceptance criteria
- No API path can produce a session in an unintended directory without an explicit signal: POST /api/session either honors ?directory= (parity with the body's location) or returns a 400 for the ineffective parameter.
- A server regression test covers session create with the query param and asserts the session location (or the 400).
- The silent fallback to the server's home directory is gone.

body:
## Work (Drew, 2026-10-27)

Stand up the dispatcher as a live scheduled job (`openchamber-
dispatcher`, every 30m), implementing #1187's design:

- Pull dispatchable work from the fleet queues (issues whose tasks
  are sized/routed for an OpenCode session: effort/m or /l code work
  first), pick the pool by the routing tiers (Workhorse default,
  Frontier only on evidence or for design, Fast for mechanical),
  subject to admission control: free session slots at the target
  location AND the POOL MAP measurement gate (quota read ≤60 min
  old; pool ≥85% of window → finishing work only).
- Launch the session via the OpenChamber API at the laptop location
  (paired client per #1271; until that lands, runs record the reach
  failure as data and prepare the dispatch packet instead — never a
  fake launch).
- Bind the session to its queue task (session id in task progress +
  issue comment) so the babysitter can shepherd it; hand-backs when
  saturated are a parked task with reason `executor-saturated` plus
  an issue note — never a silent backlog.
- Verify every launch by assistant-message CONTENT in the session,
  not by API acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The job exists and runs; its first three dispatches (or
      recorded reach failures, if #1271 still blocks) are visible in
      its reports with session bindings.
- [ ] Saturation produces a park + issue note, demonstrated once
      (live or synthetic).
- [ ] No session is ever launched against a pool failing the
      measurement gate; the gate read is quoted in the run report.

Extends #1187. Child of the pool & routing intelligence epic. Filed
by Muse (operator) 2026-10-27.

body:
Part of epic #1184 (PM stack coherence — ideal-system design series, 2026-10-26).

## Why
The stack lives on one laptop: aggregator-local JSON files hold the comment store and session registry, Grist/Kaneo data lives in laptop containers, and if the laptop is off or dies, the PM system of record is gone with it. The ideal stack keeps its state in backed-up durable storage, can run from a second host or the cluster, and proves recoverability with restore drills — the PM system should be at least as durable as the work it tracks.

## Design questions to answer
- State inventory: every store (comments, registry, Grist doc, Kaneo Postgres, Pad data, feed/snapshots, Project is GitHub-side) classified by owner, backup method, and acceptable loss.
- Target home: Turso/Supabase/Postgres-on-cluster vs replicated files — which store goes where, and what stays laptop-local by design?
- Failover shape: second-host warm standby, cluster deployment, or cold restore — what RTO/RPO does Drew actually need for a PM dashboard?
- Restore drills: what is restored, how often, and how is a drill result recorded so 'backed up' is a verified fact, not a hope?
- Secrets and identity in a moved stack: SOPS/Bitwarden flow per host, and how the single-URL/Access entry follows the stack.

## Acceptance
- Design note landed in repo `doc/` + implementation issues filed and linked as sub-issues of #1184; open questions needing Drew named explicitly in the design note.

## Acceptance criteria

- A design note answering every question listed under "Design questions to answer" is landed in the repo `doc/` tree and linked from this issue.
- Implementation issues are filed and linked as sub-issues of epic #1184 (developing-today/code), each with its own acceptance criteria — this design issue does not itself carry implementation work.
- Every open question that needs Drew is named explicitly in the design note (not buried in prose).
- Every state store in the inventory gets a named target home, backup method, and acceptable-loss figure; RTO/RPO targets for the PM stack are stated as numbers Drew can accept or adjust.

Part of epic #1184 (PM stack coherence — ideal-system design series, 2026-10-26).

## Why
Roadmap and Projects today show state, never trajectory: Drew can't see whether an epic lands this month, which pool walls first, or which in-flight item is quietly dying. The ideal stack forecasts from its own measurements — completion velocity per epic, per-pool burn vs reset windows, and stall-risk signals (age, blocked time, session silence) — and shows every forecast with its confidence and inputs.

## Design questions to answer
- Velocity model: what counts as throughput per epic/project (closed sub-issues, merged PRs), over what windows, and how are small-sample epics handled?
- Quota-wall prediction: per pool, projected exhaustion vs window reset using current burn and scheduled work — what data does the quota plane need to expose?
- Stall-risk score: which signals (blocked age, no-activity age, claimed-but-silent, repeated requeue) and what threshold surfaces an item, where?
- Presentation: how are ETA ranges and confidence rendered on Roadmap/Projects so a weak forecast never looks like a date commitment?
- Backtesting: how do we measure forecast accuracy against what actually happened and tune or retire bad models?

## Acceptance
- Design note landed in repo `doc/` + implementation issues filed and linked as sub-issues of #1184; open questions needing Drew named explicitly in the design note.

body:
# Path to Phase 12 — the ordered work queue

**This issue is the single ordered queue for everything that must land before Phase 12 feature work starts.** The roadmap (`planning/roadmaps/id.md`) points here; the repo queue claims work in this order (packet priorities encode the same sequence); the Phase 12 epic is #534.

## How work is picked (so nobody has to guess)
1. **Tier 1 — this list, top to bottom.** Labels: `priority/high` + `now`. Queue packets carry descending priorities matching the step numbers below, so the worker claims step 1 before step 2.
2. **Tier 2 — Phase 12** (label `next`): #807 F12.1, #556 F12.2, #835 F12.3 remainder, #1061 F12.4, #1062 F12.5, #1063 F12.6, #1064 F12.7, #1065 F12.8, #1066 F12.9, #1067 F12.10, #805 F12.11, #557 F12.12, #806 F12.13, #1068 F12.14, #558 F12.15, #559 done F12.16, #1069 F12.17, #560 F12.18. Designs run through #534 first.
3. **Tier 3 — Phase 13 + ideas** (`priority/low`): #785–#790, #1070–#1073.

## The order, and why
CI trust comes first because every validation verdict below is only as good as the test signal it reads. Validations then run in phase order — each audit produces the gap list the following work clears, and the earlier phases are the foundation the later ones extend. Journal compatibility (#227) precedes Phase 12 because worlds-as-data builds on the journal format.

- [x] Step 1 — #229 Stabilize shared-state failures in Firefox E2E CI — DONE 2026-10-26 (queue worker, PR #987, issue auto-closed on merge)
- [x] Step 2 — #241 Bulk LogSync test retries a mid-stream reset instead of explaining it (flaky CI test) — DONE 2026-10-28 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 3 — #551 F11.4 fast CI lane under 15 minutes — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 4 — #1075 Validate Phases 0–8 and the platform-completion brief (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 5 — #1076 Validate Phase 9: portable screens, Roc libraries, collaboration (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 6 — #1077 Validate Phase 10: profiles, capability ceilings, roles, fixtures (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 7 — #1078 Validate the delivered Phase 11 items (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (queue task 1259 audit complete, issue closed with the closeout table: 7 of 9 items verified by named passing tests; F11.4 regression filed as #1401, F11.5 partial tracked in #1326, F11.10 enforcement gap filed as #1438)
- [x] Step 8 — #227 Define rollback compatibility for world profile journal entries — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 9 — #553 F11.7 host metrics, Prometheus endpoint and tracing spans — DONE 2026-10-30 (PR #1715 merged; endpoint and tracing spans)
- [x] Step 10 — #539 F11.8 benchmark harness with committed baselines — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 11 — #542 F11.9 bytes-per-frame baseline table — DONE 2026-10-27 (PR #1429 merged after CI passed)
- [x] Step 12 — #555 F11.15 smaller example modules (wasm-opt -Os, strip, ≤400 KB) — DONE 2026-10-27 (PR #1453 merged after CI passed)
- [x] Step 13 — #541 F11.18 pin the Roc compiler for checked-in example modules and rebuild them in CI — DONE 2026-11-03 (PR #3883 merged)
- [x] Step 14 — #544 F11.16 replay self-check (`id world verify`) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [ ] Continuous — #534 Phase 12 design workflow (designs land ahead of each F12 item's implementation)

## Working rules for whoever picks these up
- **One issue per validation phase is deliberate**: each audit's job is to verify its phase against its plan, add the missing tests, and **file a separate issue for every gap found** — the follow-ups are the real work list, and they join this queue by label (`priority/high` + `now` while Phase 12 is blocked on them).
- **Drop rule**: any step that proves blocked, wrong, or superseded gets parked or closed with a note saying why, and the queue moves on. Never silently stall. Closing a step as superseded is always allowed; no permission needed.
- If a step's audit finds the phase is NOT actually delivered, say so plainly on that issue and file the missing work — that is the audit succeeding, not failing.

Dashboard: org Project #4, Area `id-train`, Horizon Week. Mirrored in the Grist Program roadmap ("id — Path to Phase 12").

## Finding
Evidence (live review 2026-10-26 ~22:40 CDT, laptop loopback + gh, cross-checked): Measured tonight from the laptop loopback: /projects 108,796B HTML, /sessions 100,061B, / 66,567B with 0.72s server time, /today 1.83s (it fans out to board+roadmap+attention+quota contexts incl. live Kaneo calls on every request - no caching anywhere in server.ts). On Drew's phone over tailnet these are the pages he reviews from; /api/registry.json is 162KB and /api/projects.json 127KB per poll.

## Acceptance
- /today server time <300ms on warm cache; /projects and /sessions initial HTML <40KB with full data one click away.
- No freshness regression: provenance ages still reflect source data, not cache time.
Refs: #898 (mobile-first mandate).

body:
## Finding

The Phase 10 sketch ("World directory feeds and portals": a browsable directory of worlds a node serves and knows, with names, presence counts, open/closed, and the web UI and `id world list` sharing one serializer) was not built. What exists is an inline admin-only JSON list that does not match the sketch, and the gap is untracked.

## Evidence

- `.opencode/plans/phase-9-portable-platform.md` §10 sketch: "World directory feeds and portals. A browsable directory of worlds a node serves and knows (names, presence counts, open/closed), with the web UI and `id world list` sharing one serializer."
- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:519-532`: `id world list --json` builds an inline `json!` with `name`, `open`, `default` — no presence counts, no web directory, no shared serializer.
- `pkgs/id/src/world_hub.rs:135-140`: `WorldInfo.open` means "currently loaded in memory", not "open to join".
- The command requires `--admin-token` (admin-only), so it is not a browsable directory.
- No test asserts the JSON shape beyond `test_cli_parse_world_roles_and_list_json` (parse only).
- Phase 11 plan `.opencode/plans/phase-11-foundations.md` line 84 lists "the directory feed" as still open; no issue tracks it (searches for "directory feed", "presence count", "world list json" return nothing).

## Why it matters

The directory feed is the discovery surface for worlds-as-places (Phase 10's theme). Without presence counts and a public feed it does not meet the sketch, and the Phase 12 directory-feed work has no issue to build on.

## Suggested scope (for the implementer to plan)

- Move the serializer into a shared `pub fn directory_json(&[WorldInfo])` (in `world_hub.rs` or similar) and rename `open` to `loaded` where it means in-memory.
- Decide and design presence counting and a public (non-admin) feed: who may read it, and how to count presence without opening idle worlds.
- Add a unit test of the serializer shape and an e2e check of the public feed once designed.

## Acceptance criteria

- A world directory feed exists listing the worlds a node serves and knows, with names, presence counts, and an open/closed state whose semantics mean "open to join" (not "loaded in memory").
- The web UI directory and `id world list` render from one shared serializer (no inline per-surface JSON).
- The directory is browsable without `--admin-token` (any auth boundary is deliberate and documented).
- Tests assert the feed's JSON shape beyond CLI parse-only coverage.

body:
## Problem

`main` does not compile `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds` (lib or lib-test):

```
error[E0063]: missing field `view` in initializer of `WatchCycle`
    --> crates/id-worlds/src/world_dev.rs:1389:29
```

## Cause

Two fleet PRs merged on 2026-11-11 combine badly:

- PR #8792 (merge 7a4e66ff8f, fix f86a672a40) added the `view` field to `WatchCycle` (world_dev.rs:1105) and updated the constructions it knew about — e.g. the `compile_failed` cycle just above carries `view: None`.
- PR #8793 (23c703532aa7) added a new `WatchCycle` construction in the `freshness_rescan_failed` path (world_dev.rs:~1389) written against the pre-#8792 struct, without `view`.

Each branch compiled against its own base; the combination on `main` does not. Found by lane code-b while rebasing PR #8643 onto current main for task 9301: `cargo test world::` in `pkgs/id` fails at compile time in `id-worlds`, a crate PR #8643 does not touch. The failing construction is byte-identical on `origin/main`.

## Fix

Add `view: None` to the `freshness_rescan_failed` construction — a cycle that failed the freshness rescan never reached promotion or a view, exactly like the sibling `compile_failed` cycle, which already uses `view: None`.

Filed and fixed in the same pass by lane code-b (task 9301 bookkeeping); the fix PR references this issue.

## Finding (unaddressed PR review comment)

Codex P2 on merged PR #8647 — comment https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8647#discussion_r4537028872 by chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T10:57:07Z, at `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs:1230` (at review time):

> **Reject promotion when the freshness rescan fails** — If a source is deleted, becomes unreadable, or exceeds discovery bounds while compilation is running, the freshness rescan fails. Substituting the candidate's own identity treats that failure as proof that the sources are unchanged, allowing the candidate to replace the last-good program despite the current source-discovery error. Record a failed cycle and retain the active world instead of promoting when freshness cannot be established.

## No-response evidence

- PR #8647 merged 2026-11-11T10:55:02Z; the comment was posted after merge, on the merged head.
- Fresh re-read (2026-11-11, this run): all 5 inline comments on the PR are Codex originals with no replies; no conversation reply addresses this.
- GraphQL `reviewThreads` check: this thread is unresolved.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-11, two `gh api` reads)

The file has since moved to `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_dev.rs`. In `run_dev_watch` on main (~lines 1256–1259):

```rust
let current_snapshot_id = discover_sources(dir)
    .map(|fresh| fresh.snapshot_id())
    .unwrap_or_else(|_| candidate_snapshot_id.clone());
```

A failed post-compile discovery is replaced by the candidate's own identity, so `DevSession::promote`'s stale check (`candidate_snapshot_id != current_snapshot_id`) passes by construction and the candidate can replace the last-good program while the sources are in an undiscoverable error state. Parent feature issue: #5541; no existing issue covers this (searched before filing).

## Acceptance criteria

- When the freshness rescan fails, the cycle is recorded as failed and the active world is retained (no promotion), with a regression test covering a source deleted/unreadable during compilation, **or**
- the issue is resolved by a documented decision explaining why promoting on a failed rescan is acceptable.

Filed by the pr-comment-review job (source: unaddressed PR comment; see the agent note on this issue).

body:
## Finding (unaddressed PR review comment)

Codex P1 on merged PR #8647 — comment https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8647#discussion_r4537028855 by chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T10:57:06Z, at `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs:1232` (at review time):

> **Keep the newer snapshot pending after discarding a stale build** — If the user saves snapshot C while snapshot B is compiling, this assignment marks C as already known even though only B was built. Promotion then correctly discards B as stale, but subsequent polls compare C against itself and never compile it. The running world therefore stays on the old program until another edit occurs. Keep the known identity at the last attempted snapshot, or explicitly queue C for the next build.

## No-response evidence

- PR #8647 merged 2026-11-11T10:55:02Z (merge commit 1e66da85f2); the comment was posted after merge, on the merged head.
- Fresh re-read (2026-11-11, this run): the PR has 5 inline comments, all Codex, none with `in_reply_to_id` — no reply on this thread, no conversation reply addressing it.
- GraphQL `reviewThreads` check: this thread is unresolved.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-11, two `gh api` reads)

The file has since moved to `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_dev.rs`. In `run_dev_watch` on main:

- ~line 1239: `known_snapshot_id = candidate_snapshot_id.clone();` runs before compilation ("moves first, whatever happens next").
- ~lines 1256–1262: after compilation, `current_snapshot_id` is rescanned and, when it differs from the candidate, `known_snapshot_id = current_snapshot_id.clone();`.
- `DevSession::promote` (~lines 923–937) discards the candidate as `StaleDiscarded` when `candidate_snapshot_id != current_snapshot_id`.

So when C lands while B compiles: B is discarded as stale, `known_snapshot_id` becomes C, and the next poll's `rescan_changed(dir, C)` returns `None` — C is never compiled and the old program keeps running until a further edit. Parent feature issue: #5541 (this is a specific defect in its phase-2 watch loop, not covered by any existing issue — searched open/recently-closed issues for "8647", "world dev watch snapshot", "debounce watch world" before filing).

## Acceptance criteria

- A snapshot saved while an earlier snapshot compiles is compiled and promoted on a subsequent poll (regression test: save C during B's compile; B is discarded as stale; C is then built without any further edit), **or**
- the issue is resolved by a documented decision explaining why this behaviour is acceptable.

Filed by the pr-comment-review job (source: unaddressed PR comment; see the agent note on this issue).

title: id(web): reject malformed bracketed IPv6 Host authorities

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/web/security.rs:89-97` handles any authority beginning with `[` by returning the text before the first `]`, without validating the remainder. The loopback host guard at `:189-197` then checks only that extracted value against `allowed_hosts`.

Consequently, `Host: [::1]attacker.example` is reduced to `::1` and passes the loopback allow-list, even though the authority is malformed and contains trailing host text. The same extraction also accepts malformed bracketed forms if their prefix matches an allow-listed address. Existing tests cover valid `[::1]:3000` and ordinary disallowed hosts, but not malformed bracketed authorities (`:298-330`).

This is a malformed-authority validation gap in the loopback guard. Browser exploitability is limited because browsers generally do not generate this Host value from a normal URL; the guard should nevertheless reject invalid authorities rather than allow a misleading host prefix.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add regression coverage showing malformed bracketed IPv6 Host authorities (including `[::1]attacker.example`) receive `MISDIRECTED_REQUEST` on loopback binds.
- Preserve acceptance of valid `[::1]` and `[::1]:<numeric-port>` authorities.
- Parse/validate the complete bracketed authority before extracting the host; reject unexpected trailing text and malformed bracket/port syntax.

title: Decisions page: batched decision sets — one push per set, per-item/partial submit, defer-to-orchestrator with leans (extends #8568)
body:
## Decisions page — batched sets, one push, partial submit, defer-to-orchestrator

Drew's spec (main chat, 2026-11-11 13:46 CST), building on notifications Phase 1 (#8568):

1. **One push per set.** When a set of decisions is waiting, the system sends ONE push notification for the set — not one per item.
2. **A decisions page** lists the set: groups → items → each item's questions, with each question's context and options.
3. **Per-item submit + submit-all.** Drew can update one or more items; each item has its own submit and a submitted item goes away. A "submit all filled" action submits everything filled in across the page.
4. **Partial submit.** He can answer a SUBSET of an item's questions and still submit — answered questions record immediately as rulings; unanswered ones stay open on the page.
5. **Defer to orchestrator**, per question and for the whole set, with lean flavors: plain defer, defer/skeptical (leaning no), defer/approve (leaning yes). Deferred questions/items leave the page and return to the orchestrator WITH the lean recorded.
6. **Bulk send-back**: checkbox multi-select plus an "all remaining" action, with the same three defer flavors.

## Design (extends the #8568 machinery, no forked data)

- **Source of truth stays the decisions ledger** (`pending-decisions-hourly-questions-for-drew/hidden_files/pending-questions.json`, Muse-side). The aggregator holds a working mirror for presentation only, exactly like the Phase 1 needs-drew question store.
- **Store**: new `src/decisions.ts` in pm-stack/aggregator, modeled on `src/needs-drew.ts` (serialized writes, atomic rename, first-resolution-wins). File: `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/decisions.json` (env `PM_AGG_DECISIONS_FILE`). A set = `{setId, title, token, items: [{ledgerId, title, group, links, questions: [{qid, question, context, options, resolution?}]}]}`; `qid = <ledgerId>#<1-based index>` so resolutions map back to ledger questions by index. A resolution is `{kind: "answered", optionId/optionLabel/freeText}` or `{kind: "deferred", lean: none|skeptical|approve}`.
- **Raise**: third producer extension on the existing throat intake — `POST /api/alerts` with a `decisionSet` extension (Bearer intake token, mutually exclusive with `needsDrew`/`stackHealth`; validation failure is a loud 400). Idempotent by setId. New CLI producer `scripts/raise-decision-set.ts` modeled on `scripts/post-alert.ts` (token resolved by name from BWS, never printed; the token-carrying page URL is never printed either — Drew reaches the page from the push).
- **Push**: one candidate per open set in `buildNotificationCandidates` — class `needs-drew`, objectRef `decision-set:<setId>`, breakthrough, stable state fingerprint (`{raisedAt}`) so the engine sends exactly once; at send time the payload URL becomes the token-carrying page URL (same pattern as the #8568 answer payload). No per-question pushes for set members, and no tappable answer actions — the tap opens the page. Fully-resolved sets stop candidating.
- **Page**: `GET /decisions/<setId>?t=<token>` on the board origin (https://amd-6.raptor-pumpkinseed.ts.net). Token is the only authority; a bad token renders a 403 that shows nothing about the set (same posture as `/answer/<id>`). Per question: option radios, free-text box, defer-flavor select (choosing a flavor marks the question deferred). Per-item Submit, "Submit everything I've filled in", and a bulk bar: item checkboxes + flavor + "Send back checked" / "Send back ALL remaining".
- **Submit endpoints** (token in body, no bearer — same as the Phase 1 answer endpoint): `POST /api/decisions/<setId>/submit` with per-question submissions; `POST /api/decisions/<setId>/defer` with `{lean, ledgerIds[] | allRemaining}`. Responses carry the set's remaining-open state so the page removes resolved questions/items without a reload.
- **Write-back**: `scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts` publishes a top-level `decisionResolutions` array next to the existing `answers` array: `{setId, ledgerId, qid, questionIndex, kind, optionId?, optionLabel?, freeText?, lean?, at, via}`. The dropped-thread catcher gains a **Step 2C** that applies each resolution to the ledger per question (`questions[i].resolution`), closes the item when every question is resolved (all-deferred items close as "Deferred to orchestrator in full (lean: …) — do not re-ask"), and unblocks a queue task carrying `needs_drew.ledger_id` only when the item is fully resolved. The hourly questions job then never re-presents a resolved question's item as fully open, and chat answers keep working unchanged.

## First set (loaded at ship time)

The fifteen decisions surfaced to Drew at 12:00 CST 2026-11-11 — all already ledger items (verified in the ledger, status `asked`): census-agent-sdks-investigation, census-link-system-improvements, census-quota-benchmark-tool, census-close-batch (group "Goals census"), and review-loop-2025-d1d2 (#2025), host-eval-gate-3039 (#3039), id-engine-5536-decisions (#5536), bot-autoclose-7610 (#7610), joplin-sync-target-7676 (#7676), opencode-plan-autocheck-10 (forks/opencode#10), open-knowledge-6435 (#6435), router-edge-6649-decisions (#6649), watch-cadence-7013 (#7013), gpl-uploads-5984 (#5984), release-3792 (#3792) (group "Issue rulings"). 15 items, 24 questions.

## Relation to Phase 2 (#8569)

#8569 moves the notification *relay* (Worker + DO mirror of events/subscriptions/answers) and the board's laptop-local data sources to Cloudflare homes. The decisions ledger is not one of the board's data sources and is not in #8569's migration scope; this feature therefore builds on the laptop aggregator exactly as Phase 1 did, and the DO mirror can carry `decisionResolutions` later the same way it will carry `answers`. No store here is about to move.

## Acceptance

- Raise the first set → exactly one push for the set reaches the pipeline (notification history shows one `sent` for `decision-set:<setId>`); tapping it opens the page.
- Page shows 2 groups / 15 items / 24 questions; bad token → 403 with no set content.
- Answer a subset of one item's questions + submit → those resolutions are recorded, the rest stay open on the page; fully-resolve an item → it leaves the page.
- Defer one question with each flavor across the set + bulk-defer the rest → all record with leans and leave the page.
- Next fleet-feed collection carries the resolutions; the catcher's Step 2C lands them on the ledger in its existing answered shape (per-question), and the parent chat can verify them there.

## Progress

- [ ] `src/decisions.ts` store + validation + tests
- [ ] Intake extension + submit/defer endpoints + page render + set push candidate
- [ ] Feed `decisionResolutions` publication
- [ ] `scripts/raise-decision-set.ts` producer
- [ ] Catcher Step 2C (repo copy + live job update)
- [ ] PR merged, aggregator redeployed, first set raised, push outcome read from notification history

title: fix(aggregator): roadmap annotations store defaults into the checkout on the install.sh deployment (PR #4054 x PR #4050)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/aggregator

body:
## Finding

The roadmap-annotations store still lands inside the git checkout on the
install.sh deployment path. PR #4054 added `roadmapAnnotationsFile` with a
working-directory default and fixed the state location only for the NixOS
deployment; PR #4050's install.sh — which deploys the aggregator from the
primary checkout with all runtime state under
`~/.local/state/pm-aggregator` — never picked the variable up, and it is
still missing on current main. The first roadmap annotation posted against
an install.sh deployment therefore creates
`pm-stack/aggregator/roadmap-annotations.json` inside the checkout — the
exact failure PR #4054's Nix fix says blocks pm-git-sync.

## Evidence

- PR #4054 (merged, merge commit `b56c85475422adc7e77f52a940f2db7c40c2af08`):
  adds `roadmapAnnotationsFile` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/config.ts` with
  default `join(process.cwd(), "roadmap-annotations.json")`, and sets
  `PM_AGG_ROADMAP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE=${aggState}/roadmap-annotations.json`
  only in `nixos/services/pm-stack/default.nix`, with the comment: "the
  first annotation would otherwise create roadmap-annotations.json inside
  this checkout and block pm-git-sync the same way (Codex P1 on PR #4054)".
  `RoadmapAnnotationsStore.persist()` (new
  `pm-stack/aggregator/src/roadmap-annotations.ts`) does
  `mkdir(dirname(file))` + `writeFile` on the first `add()`, so the file
  really is created at the configured/default path.
- PR #4050 (merged, merge commit `3deda7785543e5d640f5c568f21589a1f5e23da1`):
  rewrote `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` to deploy from
  `~/git/code/pm-stack/aggregator` with runtime data under
  `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator`; the `.env` it renders sets
  `PM_AGG_FEED_FILE`, `PM_AGG_COMMENTS_FILE`, `PM_AGG_ACTIONS_FILE`,
  `PM_AGG_REGISTRY_FILE`, `PM_AGG_SNAPSHOTS_DIR`,
  `PM_AGG_QUOTA_CURRENT_FILE`, and `PM_AGG_COVERAGE_SNAPSHOT_FILE` — no
  roadmap-annotations entry.
- Verified on current main `703f0d6b6211d5ac4ae73a0b3a836d967243afbd`
  (2026-11-11, contents API + code search, two independent reads):
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/config.ts:159` —
    `roadmapAnnotationsFile: s(env.PM_AGG_ROADMAP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE, join(process.cwd(), "roadmap-annotations.json"))`
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` (env block, lines 105–116) still has
    no `PM_AGG_ROADMAP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE` (later additions covered
    `PM_AGG_EVENTS_FILE` / `PM_AGG_ACTIVITY_FILE`; roadmap was missed).
  - Code search for `PM_AGG_ROADMAP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE` returns only
    `config.ts`, `nixos/services/pm-stack/default.nix:234`, and
    `test/slice3.test.ts` — nothing on the install.sh path.
  - `pm-stack/systemd/pm-aggregator.service` (the unit install.sh
    installs): `WorkingDirectory=%h/git/code/pm-stack/aggregator`,
    `EnvironmentFile=%h/.local/state/pm-aggregator/.env`, and its only
    inline state-path override is `PM_AGG_DIGESTS_DIR`. So under this
    deployment `process.cwd()` is the checkout and no source sets the
    roadmap path.
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/test/install-rehearsal.sh` asserts each rendered
    `PM_AGG_*` state path in `.env` (lines 101–107 on main) but has no
    roadmap assertion, so the gap is untested.
- Related observation for triage: `viewsFile` (`config.ts:161`) has the
  same cwd default and is likewise absent from the install.sh list;
  `freshnessFile` was already moved to a state-dir default (#5389).
  Triage may scope views in or split it — the filed defect is roadmap
  annotations.
- Dedupe (2026-11-11): searches for "roadmap-annotations install",
  `PM_AGG_ROADMAP_ANNOTATIONS_FILE`, and "roadmap annotations checkout"
  return no open issue; only the closed feature issue #1284 matches.

## Why it matters

Two supported deployments of the same service diverge: NixOS keeps
annotations in the state dir, install.sh writes them into the primary
checkout as an untracked runtime file. That dirties the checkout the
service itself runs from and recreates the pm-git-sync blockage PR #4054
already identified and fixed for the other path — it just has not fired
yet because it waits for the first annotation on an install.sh deployment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] On an install.sh deployment, the roadmap annotations store resolves
      under `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator` (via the rendered `.env`, the
      shipped unit, or a state-dir config default in the #5389 pattern —
      triage picks one and keeps both deployments consistent).
- [ ] `pm-stack/aggregator/test/install-rehearsal.sh` asserts the roadmap
      annotations path the same way it asserts the other `PM_AGG_*`
      state paths.
- [ ] Posting an annotation (`POST /api/roadmap/annotations`) against an
      install.sh-style deployment leaves the checkout clean: no
      `roadmap-annotations.json` created under `pm-stack/aggregator/`.
- [ ] The NixOS deployment's annotations path is unchanged.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #4054 and PR #4050
(developing-today/code).

title: quota-gatherer: opendesign-renewal fails on every tick — "Cannot find package 'yaml'" in the OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR checkout (no node_modules)
body:
## Defect
Every quota-gatherer tick logs `opendesign-renewal failed-soft` because the openchamber lib checkout the gatherer imports from has no `node_modules`, so `import yaml from 'yaml'` cannot resolve. The renewal door never runs, so OpenDesign session renewal is silently dead while the tick itself reports ok (the failure is soft).

## Evidence (laptop, checked 2026-11-11 ~19:02Z)
- Error, verbatim, on every tick: `quota-gatherer: opendesign-renewal failed-soft: Cannot find package 'yaml' imported from /home/user/git/openchamber-quota-lib/packages/web/server/lib/opencode/shared.js`
- `journalctl --user -u quota-gatherer.service --since -3h` contains 28 occurrences; earliest in the last 2 days is Nov 09 13:15Z, so it has failed since at least then.
- `/home/user/git/openchamber-quota-lib/node_modules/yaml` does not exist. `shared.js:4` has `import yaml from 'yaml'`, and `yaml ^2.8.1` is declared in the checkout's `package.json:161` and `packages/web/package.json:55`. The dependency is declared but not installed.
- The unit pins `OPENCHAMBER_LIB_DIR=/home/user/git/openchamber-quota-lib/packages/web/server/lib`, with ExecStart `bun run /home/user/git/code/pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts`.
- Seen by 3 separate quota-gatherer-guardian sessions on 2026-11-11 (ses_e5e3417142affeVv2jXFe4kxS3, ses_e5e3404c729ffeGJ53TVRa3Bjg, ses_e5e343bb26cffeRT8srs2P65pJ). The first called it "code-side and out of my scope; I have not filed it".
- Related but distinct: #5721 (closed) was a stale lib checkout parked on a queue branch, and #6120/#8102 cover renewal policy. None mention the missing `yaml` package, and a search of open and closed issues by the error string found nothing.

## Fix direction
Install the lib checkout's dependencies (`bun install` in `openchamber-quota-lib`) and keep that step in whatever provisions or refreshes the checkout. Alternatively, make the gatherer fail loudly (heartbeat ok:false, or a counter) when a soft door fails N ticks in a row, so a dead door cannot hide behind a healthy tick.

## Acceptance
After the next gatherer tick, `journalctl --user -u quota-gatherer.service --since -30m | grep "Cannot find package 'yaml'"` returns nothing and the opendesign-renewal door logs a real outcome instead of `failed-soft`.

title: perf(id): fuzz campaign recompiles the sandbox for every case — compile once and instantiate per case (PR #8635 review finding)

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

The fuzz campaign recompiles the identical Wasm module for every case: each iteration calls `DevScratchWorld::launch()`, which invokes `Sandbox::compile()` and creates a fresh Wasmtime engine and compiled module. A passing campaign therefore pays full native compilation 32 times with the default CLI budget and up to 10,000 times with the maximum budget, for an otherwise bounded input campaign.

Codex raised this on PR #8635 (feat(id): deterministic fuzz for id world dev (#5541 phase 4)):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635#discussion_r4536494875 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs:844`

Essence of the comment: compile the sandbox once before the loop and create a fresh guest/store for each case through `Sandbox::instantiate(&self, seed)`, which already isolates instance state.

## No-response evidence

- PR #8635 merged at 2026-11-11T10:00:58Z (merge commit b369657b7f3e); the Codex comments were posted at 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z on the merged head 724cf673e9, and no reply of any kind follows them (fresh `gh api` re-read 2026-11-11T18:03Z: the PR has exactly 3 inline comments, all Codex, none with `in_reply_to_id`).
- GraphQL `reviewThreads` check (2026-11-11): all 3 threads on PR #8635 are unresolved.
- No open or closed issue covers this finding (searched `world_dev` / fuzz / sandbox recompile / PR #8635 on 2026-11-11: only the parent implementation issue #5541, which does not mention this defect).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`)

`pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs` on main:

- `fuzz_candidate` (~line 1601): `let world = DevScratchWorld::launch(module, seed).await?;` sits inside the `for case in 0..budget` loop.
- `DevScratchWorld::launch` (~lines 274–276): `let runner = Sandbox::compile(module, SandboxLimits::default())?; let guest = runner.instantiate(seed)?;` — compilation is inseparable from launch today.
- `pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs` on main: `Sandbox::compile` (line 141) and `Sandbox::instantiate(&self, seed)` (line 228) already exist as separate operations, so a compile-once / instantiate-per-case split is available.

## Acceptance criteria

- A campaign compiles the candidate module once; each case gets a fresh isolated guest/store via the already-compiled sandbox, and campaign results (pass/failure, counterexample) are unchanged — covered by the existing fuzz campaign tests passing.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why per-case recompilation is intentional.

title: fix(id): fuzz numeric invariants compare through f64 — integers above 2^53 lose precision and violated invariants can pass (PR #8635 review finding)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

The fuzz campaign's numeric invariants convert record values through `f64`, silently losing integer precision above 2^53 — so a violated `numeric_order` or `numeric_bounds` invariant can pass. `Records` stores `serde_json::Value`, which preserves these integers exactly; the loss happens only in the campaign's comparison helper.

Codex raised this on PR #8635 (feat(id): deterministic fuzz for id world dev (#5541 phase 4)):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635#discussion_r4536494862 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs:625`

Essence of the comment: with `first = 9007199254740993` and `second = 9007199254740992`, `numeric_order` sees equal values after conversion although `first > second`; a numeric maximum of 9007199254740992 similarly fails to reject the larger integer. Preserve integer precision during comparisons, or explicitly reject values and bounds that cannot be checked exactly rather than reporting success.

## No-response evidence

- PR #8635 merged at 2026-11-11T10:00:58Z (merge commit b369657b7f3e); the Codex comments were posted at 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z on the merged head 724cf673e9, and no reply of any kind follows them (fresh `gh api` re-read 2026-11-11T18:03Z: the PR has exactly 3 inline comments, all Codex, none with `in_reply_to_id`).
- GraphQL `reviewThreads` check (2026-11-11): all 3 threads on PR #8635 are unresolved.
- No open or closed issue covers this finding (searched `world_dev` / fuzz / `numeric_order` / f64 precision / PR #8635 on 2026-11-11: only the parent implementation issue #5541, which does not mention this defect).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`, two reads)

`pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs` on main:

- `fn numeric(...)` (~lines 1378–1387) returns `value.as_f64()` — a `serde_json` integer above 2^53 is rounded at this conversion.
- `FuzzInvariant::NumericOrder` (~lines 1366–1375) compares the two `f64` results with `a > b`; `NumericBounds` (~lines 1351–1365) compares against `min`/`max: Option<f64>`. Equal-after-rounding values therefore pass both checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- Numeric invariant comparisons are exact for integer record values (e.g. compare as `i64`/`u64`/`serde_json::Number` before any float conversion), or values/bounds that cannot be represented exactly are rejected as a campaign error rather than reported as passing — with regression tests at the 2^53 boundary (9007199254740993 vs 9007199254740992).
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why inexact comparison is acceptable for declared invariants.

title: fix(id): fuzz campaign checks invariants before post-input guest processing completes — a trapping plaza_wants can pass no_trap (PR #8635 review finding)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

The deterministic fuzz campaign added by PR #8635 checks invariants immediately after each input's reply, but the actor runs post-input guest processing (`after_change`, which calls the program's `plaza_wants`) only after the input reply has already been sent. A guest that traps in that post-input processing is marked unhealthy inside the actor, but that failure never reaches the campaign — so a campaign declaring `no_trap` can report a pass for a candidate whose post-input guest processing trapped after the final generated input.

Codex raised this on PR #8635 (feat(id): deterministic fuzz for id world dev (#5541 phase 4)):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8635#discussion_r4536494851 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs:862`

Essence of the comment: `WorldActor::handle` sends the successful input response before `run` invokes `after_change`; that subsequent guest call can mark the program unhealthy without returning its error to the campaign, and reading the published records does not expose the failure. Await completion of post-input processing and propagate its guest errors before checking invariants or finishing the case.

## No-response evidence

- PR #8635 merged at 2026-11-11T10:00:58Z (merge commit b369657b7f3e); the Codex comments were posted at 2026-11-11T10:02:35Z on the merged head 724cf673e9, and no reply of any kind follows them (fresh `gh api` re-read 2026-11-11T18:03Z: the PR has exactly 3 inline comments, all Codex, none with `in_reply_to_id`).
- GraphQL `reviewThreads` check (2026-11-11): all 3 threads on PR #8635 are unresolved.
- No open or closed issue covers this finding (searched `world_dev` / fuzz / invariant / `after_change` / `plaza_wants` / PR #8635 on 2026-11-11: only the parent implementation issue #5541, which does not mention this defect).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`, two reads)

- `pkgs/id/src/world_dev.rs` on main, `fuzz_candidate` (~lines 1601–1635): each step does `world.input(input).await`, then immediately `world.records()` and `invariant.check(&records)` — there is no wait for, or query of, post-input processing health. The `no_trap` invariant's `check()` is unconditionally `Ok(())`, so the campaign's only trap signal is the input call itself.
- `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs` on main: the run loop calls `self.after_change().await` at line 552, after `handle(command)` returns; `handle`'s Input arm sends the reply at line 2101 (`reply.send(result)`), before that `after_change` runs.
- `after_change` (~lines 1145–1175) returns `()`: when `program.wants()` errors it sets `program_healthy = false` and only logs — the error cannot propagate to the input caller or the campaign, and `records()` does not expose the health flag.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fuzz case whose guest traps in post-input processing (`plaza_wants` / `after_change`) after an input is reported as a `no_trap` failure (or an equivalent campaign failure naming the post-input trap), with a regression test reproducing that shape.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why post-input traps are out of scope for the campaign's `no_trap` declaration.

title: id(block-list): surface failed lookups separately from unblocked

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Evidence

BlockList::is_blocked returns only bool (pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/block_list.rs:61-64), so callers cannot distinguish an unblocked entry from a failed lookup. The underlying EventStore::active_block/is_blocked operations are fallible and document storage errors and StoreError::Corrupt (pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/event_store/mod.rs:135-170). However, both concrete BlockList implementations erase failures: EventStore uses unwrap_or(false) at lines 369-374, while SharedEventStore also maps storage errors and poisoned-lock errors to false at pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/store_traits.rs:390-400.

Enforcement consumers treat false as a successful allow decision. For example, AbuseEvaluator::open_connection_inner refuses only when the peer/IP predicate is true (pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/abuse.rs:1141-1152), and PullGate::admits proceeds when both block predicates are false and policy admits (pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/pull_policy.rs:102-130). A corrupt block row or transient read/lock failure therefore makes the check indeterminate but indistinguishable from “not blocked”; the caller gets no diagnostic to surface to the operator.

The current fail-open behavior is explicitly documented and may be a deliberate availability choice. This issue is about making lookup failure observable and the enforcement policy explicit, not unilaterally changing it to fail-closed. Related history: closed #2245 implemented the operator block list but does not track error visibility.

## Suggested fix

Preserve a distinguishable error/indeterminate outcome at the block-list boundary (or provide an equivalent structured reporting hook). Let each enforcement seam explicitly apply its documented fail-open/fail-closed policy, and report the failed check to the operator without leaking storage details to remote peers.

## Acceptance criteria

- Successful active, absent, and expired-block lookups retain their existing semantics.
- Injected storage/decode errors and poisoned-lock failures are distinguishable from an ordinary unblocked result and produce an operator-visible diagnostic.
- Enforcement callers explicitly choose what to do with an indeterminate result; no caller silently treats it as an ordinary successful “not blocked” check.
- Tests cover the error oracle and the chosen per-surface policy; the default availability behavior is documented.

title: id(boundary): validate declaration ID when deserializing

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/boundary.rs:256-262`, `BoundaryDeclaration` derives `Deserialize` for both `id` and `body`. The checked constructor at lines 290-302 validates the body and computes its content-addressed ID, but derived deserialization bypasses that constructor. A declaration can therefore be deserialized with a body that does not match its supplied ID (or with a body that fails constructor validation).

`effective()` at lines 444-459 checks enabled/enforcement state but does not recompute or validate the ID before using the body. This contradicts the module's stated invariant (lines 19-23): every body change produces a new ID and declarations are immutable. Consumers that rely on the ID as the declaration's stable content identity can accept changed boundary contents under an unchanged ID.

This is a source-traced integrity gap; no runtime consumer/storage path is claimed by this issue.

## Suggested fix

Use a custom deserializer (or an equivalent validated wire type) that validates the body and verifies the supplied ID equals the ID recomputed from that body. Keep the accepted serialization format explicit.

## Acceptance criteria

- A valid declaration created with `new()` round-trips through serde with the same ID and body.
- Deserialization rejects a body changed while retaining the old ID, and rejects an ID that does not match an unchanged body.
- Deserialization rejects bodies that `new()` would reject.
- Tests name the invariant oracle: every accepted declaration's ID equals the canonical hash of its body.

Related: #7782 implemented the declaration model and is closed; #5683 is the broader open framework issue. Neither tracks the deserialization-integrity check specifically.

title: id(world): reject malformed complete journal lines without reading the remaining file

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/src/world_store.rs:164-203`, `FileJournal::open` reads a line with `BufRead::read_until`. If parsing fails, it unconditionally calls `reader.read_to_end(&mut rest)` before checking `complete`. For a newline-terminated malformed line, `complete` is already true and the code will always report corruption, yet it reads and allocates the entire remaining journal first. An early malformed line followed by a large journal can exhaust memory or return an unrelated I/O error instead of promptly reporting its corruption offset. This is verified by code inspection; no runtime reproduction was performed.

An unterminated line read by `read_until` has already reached EOF under normal `BufRead` semantics; preserve the existing torn-tail handling rather than assuming malformed complete lines are safe to truncate.

## Acceptance criteria

- Report a malformed newline-terminated line as corruption without reading or allocating the rest of the journal; preserve the path and byte-offset diagnostic.
- Preserve recovery of an unterminated final entry and do not silently discard complete corrupt entries.
- Add regression tests with a bounded-read oracle (for example, a test reader that fails if the remainder is consumed) and cases for complete corruption and torn tails.

Related broader resource-exhaustion tracking: #560; this identifies a concrete journal recovery path.

title: fix(aggregator): /api/roadmap.json view filtering drops items linked from kept rows — HTML twin keeps them via keptRefs (PR #4013)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

With a saved view applied, `/api/roadmap.json` drops items that the HTML `/roadmap` page keeps: items linked from a kept roadmap row are included in the HTML response even when the item itself fails the view filter, but the JSON handler filters items by the view alone. A kept row in the JSON response can therefore reference items that are absent from its own `items[]`, so API consumers cannot resolve those rows' links/badges — the JSON twin does not reproduce the page it mirrors.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4013 (merged 2026-11-02, merge commit c5f880113c43b0db5bd93c3d22142c71b333f8d1) — "feat(aggregator): saved views — named per-person filter sets, shareable URLs, persistent default (#1276)". Its body states `/board`, `/roadmap`, `/api/board.json` and `/api/roadmap.json` all resolve a view and filter consistently.
- Verified on current main 8c17d5cdfa015f74de1ad140700a0ae4ea3cb2fa, two independent reads of `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts`:
  - HTML `/roadmap` (:1864-1873): comment "Codex P2, PR #4013: items linked from a KEPT row keep their metadata (links/badges in roadmapCard) even when they fail the item filter themselves — same rule the board handler applies", then `keptRefs` is built from every kept row's links and `keptItems` keeps an item when `keptRefs.has(ref) || itemMatchesView(...)`.
  - JSON `/api/roadmap.json` (:2278-2280): `keptItems = [...items.values()].filter((it) => itemMatchesView(ghItemLike(it, poolByRef.get(it.ref)), resolved.filters))` — no `keptRefs` union.
  - The board JSON twin was later fixed to restrict shipped items to the selected cards' closure (`boardJsonViewBody`, server.ts:2244-2251); the roadmap JSON twin was not given the equivalent treatment.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-11 ("roadmap.json view", "keptRefs", "api/roadmap") returned no covering issue. The sibling board-fragment gap from the same PR was filed and fixed as #8521 (CLOSED) — this is the remaining roadmap-JSON twin, not a duplicate of it. Parent #1276 is closed.

## Why it matters

Saved views are a parameter set over the existing pages *and their `/api/*.json` twins* (PR #4013's own framing). A consumer of `/api/roadmap.json?view=…` receives rows whose linked items are silently missing, so link/badge resolution fails downstream with no error — exactly the inconsistency the in-code Codex P2 comment records as the intended rule for the HTML path.

## Acceptance criteria

- `/api/roadmap.json` with a resolved view keeps every item linked from a kept row (the `keptRefs` union), matching the HTML `/roadmap` handler.
- A test pins the parity: a view that filters out a linked item but keeps its row returns that item in both the HTML and JSON responses.
- The unfiltered (no-view) JSON response is unchanged.

title: id(web/markdown): strip_leading_blank_quote_lines deletes a literal blank line at the start of a top-level fenced code block on save (residual of #1002 / PR #4816)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Bug

`strip_leading_blank_quote_lines` (pkgs/id/src/web/markdown/markdown_serialization.rs, the #1002 save-path stripper) has no fenced-code-block state. On save, it deletes a literal blank line from the start of a **top-level fenced code block** whose first content lines look like quote lines.

Verified end-to-end on origin/main f44b8207d2 (laptop probe binary calling `markdown_to_prosemirror` → `prosemirror_to_markdown`):

- IN: `"```\n> \n> text\n```\n"` → OUT: `"```\n> text\n```\n"` — the code block's first line (`> `) is gone.
- IN: `"```rust\n> \n> text\n```\n"` → OUT: `"```rust\n> text\n```\n"` — same loss.
- Controls round-trip fine: quoted fence `"> ```rust\n> code\n> ```\n"`, `"> paragraph\n"`.

Mechanism: the fence opener line is neither a blank quote line nor quote content, so the scan sets `at_quote_start = true`; the next line (`> `, blank quote) is then treated as the start of a quote run, and the lookahead sees `> text` (quote content) and strips the blank — even though both lines are literal code content inside the fence.

## Origin

This is the unresolved CodeRabbit **Major** finding on PR #4816 (discussion r4452869637, https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4816#discussion_r4452869637), which merged for #1002 without the finding being dispositioned. It was flagged again by task 6565's park reason; this filing is that investigation's result (task 6565, lane code-a, 2026-11-11). The neighbouring `restore_github_alert_markers` in the same file already tracks fences (FenceTracker in markdown_scan.rs) for exactly this reason.

## Fix shape

Track fenced-block state in `strip_leading_blank_quote_lines` (reuse `FenceTracker` + `split_quote_prefix`, as `restore_github_alert_markers` does): never strip lines inside a fence, at any quote depth. Add round-trip regression tests: top-level backtick/tilde fences whose first content lines are `> ` + `> text`, plus the existing #1002 controls (fence/table/rule-first quotes still strip their leading blanks).

Acceptance: the probe cases above round-trip byte-identically; the existing web::markdown tests (incl. `test_blockquote_leading_block_round_trips_without_extra_blank_lines`) pass.

title: fix(coord-mirror): chunk the Supabase->Turso catch-up fetch/apply so a run can complete (195k-event backlog)

labels.name: kind/infrastructure
labels.description: Infrastructure / host-portability work

body:
## Problem

The Supabase → Turso coord-mirror (`~/tools/supabase-mirror/sync_agent_to_turso.py`, laptop) cannot complete a run from its current watermark. Evidence from task 14894 (2026-11-11, lane code-c):

- `state.json` watermark: `last_event_id 20842`, `last_run_utc 2026-10-28T16:21:38Z`.
- Backlog measured live via the script's own Management-API route: `agent.workers` 34 rows, `agent.tasks` 8,505 rows, `agent.events WHERE id > 20842` **195,484 rows**, `agent.checkpoints` 2 rows. Count queries answer in 2–8 s — the API is healthy.
- The script fetches each table in ONE unbounded Management-API query (the events fetch's curl ran for minutes per attempt; `mgmt_sql` retries 4× with no curl timeout), builds a single `sync.sql` (102 MB, ~204k statements), and `~/tools/turso-exec.py` sends ALL statements as ONE libSQL pipeline HTTP request. That request showed no completion after 31 minutes (connection live, 0% CPU client-side) and was killed; the run never advanced `state.json`.

Daily incremental runs (one day of events) were never the problem — the one-shot catch-up shape is. The daily timer is now installed (task 14894; flake declaration merged in PR #8631), but until a sync completes once, the watermark stays at 2026-10-28 and every timer run retries the same monster catch-up (the service's 30-minute `TimeoutStartSec` will kill it mid-apply).

## Fix (transport shape only — mirror semantics unchanged)

1. Paginate the `agent.events` fetch (e.g. `WHERE id > $cursor ORDER BY id LIMIT $page`, advancing the cursor) instead of one unbounded query; keep the other tables as-is or paginate tasks the same way if needed.
2. Chunk the Turso apply: send the generated statements to Turso in bounded pipeline batches (e.g. 500–1000 statements per request, in the original order) instead of one 102 MB request. The statement set, order, and idempotency properties (upserts + `INSERT OR IGNORE`) stay exactly as they are.
3. Add a curl `--max-time` (or equivalent) to `mgmt_sql` so a stalled fetch fails into the existing retry instead of hanging a run forever.
4. Run one full catch-up sync to completion and verify `state.json` advances past event 20842 with a current `last_run_utc`; then confirm a second (incremental) run completes quickly.

## Acceptance

- One catch-up run of `sync_agent_to_turso.py` completes end-to-end (exit 0, JSON summary printed) and `~/tools/supabase-mirror/state.json` advances.
- A follow-on incremental run also completes, in minutes not hours.
- The daily `supabase-turso-coord-mirror.timer` run fits inside its 30-minute service timeout.
- Evidence posted on program issue #1723; queue task 14894 is dep-blocked on this fix and auto-releases for final verification when it lands.

## Origin

Follow-on from the disposition of Dependabot PR #5602 (queue task 13401, lane code-b, 2026-11-11). That PR bumped protobufjs 7.5.4 → 7.6.6 in `/.opencode` by updating opencode-mem, but it touched only `package.json` + `package-lock.json`. This repo keeps two lockfiles in step for `.opencode` (on current main both pin opencode-mem 2.13.0 / protobufjs 7.5.4), and bun is the operative runtime for the OpenCode server — so the PR as authored would not have changed what the server installs, and would have left the lockfiles divergent.

It also cannot be repaired mechanically: resolving the PR head's `package.json` with bun (`bun install`, 2026-11-11, task 13401) selects **opencode-mem 2.42.0**, while the PR's npm lockfile pins **2.40.1** — the two ecosystems resolve the same range to different versions, and the opencode-mem jump itself (2.13 → 2.40+) is a plugin behavior change across many releases that deserves a deliberate evaluation, not a lockfile patch. PR #5602 was closed on that record.

## Scope

- Evaluate opencode-mem 2.13.0 → current (2.42.0 at filing) for the fleet's OpenCode setup: release notes across the range, config/API changes affecting `.opencode` and the memory setup, and the protobufjs line it carries (target: protobufjs ≥ 7.6.6, the bugfix-backport line PR #5602 was carrying).
- If the evaluation is favorable: land the upgrade as one change that updates `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, AND `bun.lock` consistently (pin the exact opencode-mem version in both lockfiles), with a plugin-load smoke recorded (the server itself is restarted only through the fleet's normal deploy path — do not restart Drew's live OpenCode server from this task).
- If the evaluation is unfavorable: record the verdict and the blocking change on this issue, and take the protobufjs bump alone if it is separable.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A recorded evaluation verdict for the opencode-mem range (favorable/unfavorable + the material changes), on this issue.
- [ ] Either: one merged PR with all three `.opencode` manifests consistent at the same opencode-mem version and protobufjs ≥ 7.6.6, plus a recorded plugin-load smoke; or: the separable protobufjs-only bump landed the same consistent way.
