body:
## Finding

The Cost Explorer band lane charts added by PR #3972 ship with no behavioural test. The only test coverage is source-string matching in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/aa.test.ts` (:714-725 on current main): the assertions check that the emitted page *contains* the renderer's source text — `expect(html).toContain("function bandLaneChart")`, `toContain('class="xpl-band-lanes"')`, the `bandLaneChart("Lowest price within each speed target", "cost", …)` call-site text, and `toContain("g6Lanes.push")`. None of them execute `bandLaneChart` against data. The assertions would still pass if the function returned `""`, mis-scaled every point, or plotted nothing — and the a11y suite's only script-level check compiles the explorer script with `new Function(source)` (a syntax check). The chart's actual logic — axis range computed from all band `members` while only near-leader `choices` are plotted, log vs linear scaling, the `lo === hi` widening, leader detection and point placement — is untested in every direction.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3972 (merged 2026-11-02, merge commit 2cb205582f3b70d27c2e96beae3f7b65682aa5fe) — "feat(aggregator): add Cost Explorer band lane charts" (refs #1400).
- Verified on current main 1a06801491b0b0efab3b4edf967573c8603a6dc3, two independent reads:
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/test/aa.test.ts:714-725` — the lane-chart assertions are the `toContain` source-string checks quoted above; a code search for `bandLaneChart` across the repo's tests returns only this file.
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts` `bandLaneChart` (in the explorer script): values are collected from `b.members`, points are plotted from `b.choices`; log scale for non-score metrics, `lo === hi` widening branches, leader vs near-leader styling — none of it exercised by any test.
  - `test/a11y-1215.test.ts:137` compiles the script via `new Function(source)` — parse-only.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-11 ("lane chart test", "bandLaneChart") returned no covering issue; parent #1400 remains open for the broader parity follow-ups and does not track this test gap.

## Why it matters

The lane charts are the visual half of the band comparisons — the tables' numbers are tested, the chart that re-plots them is not. A scaling or leader-detection regression would ship silently because the string-match tests pin the function's *presence*, not its *behaviour*; they also break on harmless refactors (renaming the function) while passing real breakage, the worst combination a test can have.

## Acceptance criteria

- A test executes `bandLaneChart` (directly, or by evaluating the emitted explorer script in a harness) against known band data and asserts on the rendered output: number of plotted points, leader point identity/styling, and axis behaviour for a log-scale metric.
- The `lo === hi` single-value widening case is covered.
- The members-range vs choices-points relationship is pinned by an assertion (whichever behaviour is intended), so a future change to either set is a deliberate test change.
- The existing source-string assertions for the lane chart are removed or demoted in favour of the behavioural ones.

body:
## Finding

The Project #4 audit snapshot rejects itself whenever a multi-page export over-delivers. In `pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts`, `fetchProjectSnapshot` deliberately tolerates overlapping pages — the shortfall-only check at :361-364 throws only when fewer nodes arrive than the board total, with the comment "overlapping pages can over-deliver nodes". But the audit is then built by `parseProjectAudit(firstPage, auditItems, …)` (:367) from those same raw nodes, duplicates included: `distribution()` counts every node it is given, so each distribution sums to `auditItems.length`. The feed-side gate `isProjectAudit` (:318-320) requires `distributionTotal(counts.status/area/repo) === totalItems` exactly. An over-delivered export therefore produces an audit whose distributions sum to *more* than `totalItems`, `projectAuditFromFeed` (`src/feed.ts:525-526`) returns `null`, and the snapshot surfaces as absent — the watchdog's "projects absent" card, whose remediation text points at the collector's Project read and token scope, not at the export that actually happened.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3995 (merged 2026-11-07, merge commit 5243d05933) — "pm-stack: publish auditable Project #4 snapshot (#1218)".
- Verified on current main 1a06801491b0b0efab3b4edf967573c8603a6dc3, two independent reads of `pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts`:
  - :356 `auditItems.push(...nodes…)` — no deduplication by item id across pages.
  - :361-364 shortfall-only completeness check; over-delivery is explicitly accepted.
  - :367 the audit is parsed from the un-deduplicated `auditItems`.
  - `distribution()` (same file) counts every node; `fieldValue` falls back to `"(unset)"`, so every node contributes exactly 1 to each of the status/area/repo distributions — each total therefore equals `auditItems.length`.
  - :318-320 `isProjectAudit` requires all three distribution totals to equal `totalItems` (the first page's board `totalCount`).
- `src/feed.ts:525-526`: `projectAuditFromFeed` returns the audit only when `isProjectAudit` passes, else `null`; `src/watchdog.ts:224-233` renders a null audit as "Project #4 audit is absent" with collector/token remediation.
- Over-delivery is not exotic: it occurs when the board mutates mid-export (items added shift later pages so a node repeats) — Project #4 is written continuously by the orchestrator, and the collector re-exports every ~5 minutes. A totalCount read from the first page can also drift against later pages for the same reason.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-11 ("projectAudit distribution", "overlapping pages project audit", "Project #4 snapshot audit absent") returned no covering issue. Related context only: Project #4 reconciliation trouble is tracked at #1408; this issue does not claim to be its cause.

## Why it matters

The audit snapshot exists so Project #4's state is auditable from the feed (#1218). As written, the exports most likely to occur while the board is actively changing — exactly when an audit matters — are the ones the gate discards, and the failure presents as "no snapshot / check the token", sending diagnosis in the wrong direction. Fetch-side tolerance and feed-side strictness contradict each other; one of them has to give.

## Acceptance criteria

- Exactly one consistent resolution, e.g.: deduplicate `auditItems` by item id before `parseProjectAudit` (and judge completeness against the deduplicated count), or relax `isProjectAudit` to accept distribution totals that are >= the item count with the discrepancy surfaced — the chosen behaviour is stated in the code where the two sides meet.
- A test reproduces an overlapping-pages export (a node delivered on two pages) and shows the resulting audit surviving `projectAuditFromFeed` (or being rejected with a diagnosis that names the overlap, not absence).
- The watchdog "absent" remediation is not reachable for an export that was fetched successfully.

body:
## Finding

The dashboard comments queue renders a failed GitHub comment's age from the wrong clock: `dashCommentHtml` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts` prints `` `posting failed ${relTime(c.createdAt)}` `` — the time since the comment was **created**, not since it **failed**. No failure timestamp is ever stored: `CommentsStore.markGithubResult` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts` transitions a comment to `githubState = "failed"` and sets `githubError` only, and repeat failures refresh the error text (per #1210, "last error means the newest report") with no accompanying time. A comment that sat pending for days before failing — or failed again yesterday after an earlier failure — displays as "posting failed <age of the comment>", which misstates how long the failure has been waiting on a manual repost.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3987 (merged 2026-11-01, merge commit 2f8ab785034ec05c979f1388e631da70b3235793, commit cac2674fb2) — "feat(aggregator): comments queue view, kind-aware badge counts, honest failure copy (#1210)".
- Verified on current main d398bc577a9c06bc1daba3b38b6cfe1bc3d0b01f, two independent reads of `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts`:
  - :600 `` `posting failed ${relTime(c.createdAt)} — no automatic retry exists; a fleet poster must post it by hand…` `` in `dashCommentHtml`'s `githubState === "failed"` branch.
  - :676 `relTime(iso)` computes `Date.now() - Date.parse(iso)` — a relative age of whatever timestamp it is handed; it is handed `createdAt`.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts` `markGithubResult` (read on main): the failure branches set `c.githubState = "failed"` and `c.githubError = result.error` and persist — no timestamp field is written on either the first failure or a repeat failure. `pm-stack/aggregator/src/model.ts:1190` carries `githubError?: string` and no failure-time field exists on `DashComment`.
- The semantics are pinned by a test: `pm-stack/aggregator/test/comments-queue-1210.test.ts:101` expects `/posting failed (just now|\d+[mhd] ago)/` against a freshly created fixture, so the test passes precisely because creation and failure coincide in the fixture.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-11 ("posting failed", "failedAt comments", "comment failure age createdAt") returned no issue covering this; parent issue #1210 is closed.

## Why it matters

The comments queue is the fleet's manual-recovery surface for GitHub comments that failed to post — the copy itself says a fleet poster must post it by hand. The displayed age is the triage signal for how stale that failure is. Anchoring it to creation time overstates the age of long-pending comments and understates repeat failures, so operators cannot tell a failure that happened minutes ago from one that has been waiting since the comment was written.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failure timestamp (e.g. `githubFailedAt`) is recorded on `DashComment` when `markGithubResult` transitions a comment to `failed`, refreshed on repeat failures alongside `githubError`, and cleared when the comment posts.
- The failed branch of `dashCommentHtml` renders the age from that timestamp (falling back to `createdAt` for pre-existing records that lack it).
- A test pins the distinction: a comment created well before its failure renders the failure's age, not the comment's age.

Parent design: #8575 (one door, one home per fact — fleet tool state unification). Slice 1 of 7. Approved by Drew 2026-11-11: implement in full.

## Work

Audit the current fleet queue database schema (the fleet-queue Turso store) table by table, field by field. Classify every stored fact as exactly one of:

- **Coordination** — claims, leases, heartbeats, checkpoints, lane registry, merge-order lists. Ephemeral; passes the wipe test (wiping it tonight loses only in-flight leases).
- **Durable truth** — anything whose loss would lose what was decided or done (task outcomes, parked/blocked reasons that matter, attempt history treated as record). These must move to GitHub or become derived, rebuildable cache.
- **GitHub mirror cache** — copies of GitHub facts (issues, labels, PR state). Rebuildable from GitHub at any time; never authoritative.

## Acceptance

- A written audit (doc in repo, linked from #8575) listing every table and field with its class and the evidence for the class.
- For every durable-truth item: the named new home (GitHub artifact) or the derivation that rebuilds it.

- No schema changes in this slice — audit and plan only.

body:
## Phase 1 — the stack speaks for itself (no platform move)

Design: `pm-stack-notifications-design-2026-11-11.md` (goal keep-the-four-repos-healthy, files/). Parent design context: #1254 (closed — PWA + push design), #3676 (closed — alert throat), #1226 (closed — needs-drew census), #8097 (queue/lane record where the 268-task audit landed).

### What recon established (2026-11-11, wire-verified)

The push machinery from #1254/#3676 EXISTS and works: `POST /api/alerts` throat (Bearer intake) → Supabase `alerts` store → in-aggregator engine tick (60s) → Web Push (VAPID, `src/push.ts`, `/sw.js`). Drew's phone holds the one live subscription (Android Chrome / FCM, subscribed 2026-11-01; pushes delivered 2026-11-01 self-test and 2026-11-09 globalping criticals). Drew got no pushes on 2026-11-11 because of four specific gaps — this phase closes all four:

1. **His subscription predates the classes.** `NOTIFICATION_CLASS_DEFAULTS` turns needs-drew / quota-wall / quota-near-wall / stack-health / blocked-age ON for new rows, but `classEnabled()` preserves old rows: for the 2026-11-01 subscription every class except `incident` is effectively OFF. The candidates are derived every tick (`buildNotificationCandidates`) and filtered out for his only subscription.
2. **Queue escalations never enter the stack.** The aggregator's needs-drew census reads GitHub labels (`user/review`, `user/escalated`) via the fleet feed. The 268 "waiting on Drew" tasks from the 2026-11-11 audit live in the fleet-queue Turso DB; the broker / `repo-queue` block path has NO emission into the throat or the feed.
3. **Nobody posts stack-down.** The only incident source that has ever posted is `globalping-watch` (public endpoints only). The board's own ~dozen 503 episodes on 2026-11-11 produced zero incidents — the aggregator cannot report itself, and no on-host sentinel watches it or its siblings.
4. **`stack-health` is a class with no producer.** Watchdog diagnoses exist (`src/watchdog.ts`, needs-orchestrator tier items) but nothing turns them into notification candidates/incidents.

### Work

- [ ] Broker / `repo-queue` block-with-escalation path POSTs a `needs-drew` event to the throat (`POST /api/alerts`, intake token) at block time, carrying: ledger id, the question, the option list, issue links. The task row records the ledger id so an answer can unblock it mechanically.
- [ ] Subscription class backfill: subscriptions created before a class existed get the reviewed defaults for that class (or a one-tap "apply reviewed defaults" on `/alerts/preferences`). Drew's existing phone subscription must end with needs-drew + quota-wall + stack-health ON without re-subscribing.
- [ ] Independent stack-health sentinel: a tiny systemd user unit (NOT inside the aggregator) probing loopback health of aggregator :4870, projector :7801, Kaneo :5173, dispatch :4879, OpenCode :13420, queue broker :4801 every ~30s, POSTing stack-health incidents to the throat on transitions. Honest limit: it cannot report the aggregator itself being dead to the throat — that case is Phase 2's dead-man's switch.
- [ ] `stack-health` candidate producer in the aggregator from the watchdog diagnoses.
- [ ] Answerable choices v1: a needs-drew push carries the question; ≤2 options ride as notification actions, more options deep-link to an answer page on the board listing every option as a tap target. Answer endpoint `POST /api/needs-drew/:ledgerId/answer` (per-question token from the push payload, single-question scope) writes an answers outbox in aggregator state; the fleet-feed collector carries answers into `fleet-feed.json`; the dropped-thread catcher applies them to `pending-questions.json` (status answered + answer text) and unblocks the originating queue task.

### Acceptance (Drew's terms)

- Block a queue task as escalated-to-Drew → a push with the question and answer choices reaches Drew's phone in under a minute, no cron involved anywhere in the path.
- Tap an answer on the phone → the ledger shows the item answered and the blocked task unblocks, without Drew opening this chat.
- Kill the projector → a stack-health push arrives in under a minute.
- A sole-door pool hits a quota wall → a quota-wall push arrives in under a minute (proving the already-built candidate path end to end, live).

body:
## Decision this issue implements (recorded on #1300)

Drew answered the #1300 Phase-2 fleet vector-store question (pending-questions ledger item `fleet-vector-store-1300`, corrected 2026-11-10 18:18 CST): **"Integrate into Atlas"** — fleet/agent memory integrates INTO Atlas; ensure everything is queryable across all agents/corpora. NOT local-only silos, NOT a separate new store.

Phase 1 of #1300 is landed and verified (memory-lancedb owns `plugins.slots.memory` for the laptop OpenClaw gateway, stable local embedding endpoint on fixed loopback port 18791 — `home/openclaw/default.nix`; live store/recall proof recorded under issue #6167 on 2026-11-11). This issue is the remaining work: the Atlas integration itself.

## Scope

- Design first (record on this issue or in a linked `doc/` record): how OpenClaw's memory-lancedb content and the other fleet corpora named in #1300 Phase 2 (zettelkasten/Emanote notes, repo docs, prior research reports) become queryable through Atlas, across agents (OpenClaw, OpenCode sessions, OpenChamber, Muse lanes) — one integration into Atlas, no new standalone vector store, no per-agent silos.
- Decide the access pattern inside that design (MCP server vs per-tool native access) with the reasoning recorded.
- Respect the external-content zone policy track: bulk external-content ingestion into any corpus this integration exposes gates on issue #6052's ratification (currently deferred by Drew behind the #6066 networking epic) and the #6024 licensing gate; this issue's own/fleet corpora are not blocked by that gate.
- Implementation slices filed as their own issues once the design lands, in the fleet's usual pattern.

## Acceptance

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

body:
Implementation follow-on for the design issue #5790 (versioning for a monorepo whose apps deploy individually). The design and policy questions are settled: triage findings are recorded on #5790 (2026-11-05, task 10193) and Drew ruled on 2026-11-06, with a refinement the same day. This issue is the build step the triage held back until those rulings landed.

Ruled policy (from #5790, Drew 2026-11-06, as refined):
1. Tag prefix: the short app name for ALL apps, one naming policy. App names used in tags and deploys must be unique across apps; if a short name would collide, fix the app name, not the policy.
2. Builds deployed from main without a tagged release are prereleases (alpha/beta-style prerelease versioning); deploying one does not make it a release. Releases are tag builds only.
3. First tags: each app starts at 0.1.0. Stay in 0.x: minor for feature releases, patch for fixes, no major-version increments until a separate 1.0 decision.
4. Repo tags: cut repo/v<date>.<minor>.<patch> at every release point (not every commit, not every deploy). A repo prerelease tag on deploys from main is also fine; it does not make the deploy a release.

Current state (triage evidence, 2026-11-05, main 04f78696ab): fleet packages/workspaces still carry hard-coded 0.1.0 versions and binaries embed only FLEET_SOURCE_REV, so no derivation exists yet.

Scope of this step:
- Implement derived versions for the fleet apps in pkgs/fleet: derive the version from the app's latest tag plus commits since (per the #5790 survey), falling back to 0.1.0-dev form before the first tag.
- Embed/report the derived version through the same channel that currently reports FLEET_SOURCE_REV, so --version and deployed-state checks (#5760) can consume it.
- Document the tag + release procedure (per-app tags, repo tags at release points) where the fleet release tooling lives.
Out of scope: cutting the first real release tags (a release-point decision), any 1.0 move, and the #5760 drift-check work itself.

title: docs(id): Notion importer design has no data-source model — multi-source databases cannot be mapped (PR #8416 review finding)

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

The Notion importer design's database mapping (§2.2) treats a Notion database as a single schema — but since Notion API version `2025-09-03`, a database is a container of independently identified **data sources**: schemas, row queries, and relation targets are scoped by `data_source_id`. A database with multiple data sources cannot be faithfully mapped by the design as written, and database reads/queries fail when a second source is added even on older pinned versions.

Codex raised this on PR #8416 (docs(id): design: Notion importer for the knowledge layer, for issue #6436):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8416
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8416#discussion_r4533073012 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T02:06:56Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md:80`

Essence of the comment: for a Notion database containing multiple data sources, the proposed single-schema database mapping cannot faithfully identify the row schemas and relation targets. Since API version `2025-09-03`, databases are containers of independently identified data sources; schemas, row queries, and relation targets use `data_source_id`. Pinning an older version does not avoid this: Notion documents that database reads and queries fail when a second source is added. Include data-source discovery and identity in the inventory/manifest, scope schema claims and relation identities to their source, and add a multi-source database fixture.

## No-response evidence

- The comment is the only review finding on PR #8416; there are no replies to it, and PR #8416 merged (updated 2026-11-11T02:06:59Z) with the item unaddressed.
- GraphQL reviewThreads check (2026-11-11): the thread containing comment 4533073012 is unresolved.
- No open or closed issue covers this residual (searched Notion / data_source / #6436 on 2026-11-11: the implementation issues #6513 and #8419 do not mention data sources; the design issue #6436 is closed).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`)

`doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md` on main contains **no occurrence of `data_source`** at all:

- Line 79 (§2.2): a database maps to "One logical note … + schema provenance claims" — one schema per database, recorded on the database note.
- Line 80: rows map to notes with a typed reference to the database note; relation identity (§2.2, relation row) is "database + property" — neither is scoped to a data source.
- §1.2 / inventory and the §6 manifest describe page/database/block UUID identity only; there is no data-source discovery step and no multi-source database fixture in the test corpus (§ "Databases" fixture lists property types, relations, rollups, linked views — no multi-source case).

An implementation following this design (issues #6513 / #8419) will omit or conflate data from any Notion database that has more than one data source.

## Acceptance criteria

- The design is amended: inventory/manifest records data-source discovery and identity (`data_source_id`) per database; §2.2 schema claims and relation identities are scoped to their data source; the test corpus gains a multi-source database fixture.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue (e.g. multi-source databases are explicitly out of scope, with the limitation and its failure mode stated in the design).

title: docs(id): licensing Policy 4 code exception matches the uploader, not the author — third-party code gets the group exception (PR #8402 review finding)

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

The licensing-policy design's Policy 4 exception — "I only accept MIT or CC0 unless it's code written by these groups or admins" — is expressed as group-scoped policies that §4.3 matches against the **uploader**, not the code's **author**. A group member uploading third-party Apache-2.0 or MPL code therefore receives the exception even though they did not write the code.

Codex raised this on PR #8402 (doc(id): licensing policy — ToS grant, account defaults, admin policies, for issue #5984):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8402
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8402#discussion_r4532952428 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T01:48:47Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `doc/2026-11-11_design_id5984_licensing_policy.md:201`

Essence of the comment: for a worldsmith uploading third-party Apache-2.0 or MPL code, the group policy admits the artifact because §4.3 matches principal scopes against the uploader, not the author. That contradicts Policy 4's stated exception for code "written by" those groups: §1.1's licensed route permits third-party uploads, so uploader membership does not establish authorship. Add an authorship/provenance condition to express the requested restriction rather than granting the exception to every code artifact a group member uploads.

## No-response evidence

- The comment was posted at 2026-11-11T01:48:47Z in Codex's re-review of commit df8b97edbb; PR #8402 merged at 2026-11-11T01:48:50Z with no reply to this thread (the three earlier Codex findings on the PR were each answered by dezren39 with "Fixed in df8b97edbb" replies — this one was not).
- GraphQL reviewThreads check (2026-11-11): the thread containing comment 4532952428 is unresolved, with no reply comments.
- No open or closed issue covers this residual (searched licensing / authorship / #5984 on 2026-11-11: only the parent design issue #5984, whose merged doc is the artifact carrying the defect).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`)

`doc/2026-11-11_design_id5984_licensing_policy.md` on main is unchanged on the relevant points:

- Line 146 (§4.3 step 2): scope matching is defined as "policies whose kind scope matches the artifact's kind and whose principal scope contains **the uploader**".
- Lines 193–209 (Policy 4): the exception is two group-scoped `ceiling 2` policies for `worldsmiths` / `admins`, and the prose at line 209 restates the intent as "code written by those principals" — while the worked example is "a worldsmith **uploading** Apache-2.0 code".
- The word "author" appears nowhere in the policy language as a matching condition (only in unrelated ToS / policy-conversation prose): there is no authorship or provenance condition an implementation could apply.

An implementation following this design grants the MIT/CC0 exception to any code a group member uploads, including third-party code they did not write — broader than the admin policy it claims to express.

## Acceptance criteria

- The policy language gains an authorship/provenance condition (or an equivalent mechanism) so the Policy 4 exception can be restricted to code actually written by the named groups/admins, and §4.4 Policy 4 is re-expressed using it; or Policy 4's stated intent is corrected to "code uploaded by these groups" with the widening made explicit.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why uploader-matching is the intended semantics.

## Finding (from PR review)

The licensing-policy design's §6.1 self-hosting guidance says an admin can allow NC (noncommercial) content with a "one-line removal of the shipped deny" — but removing the NC deny alone still refuses every NC upload, because the shipped/default policy retains a ladder ceiling of 2 while the consumed license taxonomy assigns NC entries levels 3–4.

Codex raised this on PR #8402 (doc(id): licensing policy — ToS grant, account defaults, admin policies, for issue #5984):

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8402
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8402#discussion_r4532952420 (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-11T01:48:47Z, P2)
- File:line at review time: `doc/2026-11-11_design_id5984_licensing_policy.md:226`

Essence of the comment: for a self-hosted server using the shipped defaults, removing the NC deny alone still refuses every NC upload: §5 retains a ceiling of 2, while the consumed taxonomy (`doc/2026-11-10_design_id5977_license_taxonomy.md`, §§2.5–2.6) assigns NC entries levels 3–4. Under §4.3 those artifacts therefore fail the remaining ceiling test. Document the additional ceiling adjustment or explicit NC allow needed so an admin following this guidance can actually enable NC distribution.

## No-response evidence

- The comment was posted at 2026-11-11T01:48:47Z in Codex's re-review of commit df8b97edbb; PR #8402 merged at 2026-11-11T01:48:50Z with no reply to this thread (the three earlier Codex findings on the PR were each answered by dezren39 with "Fixed in df8b97edbb" replies — this one, and the authorship finding filed separately, were not).
- GraphQL reviewThreads check (2026-11-11): the thread containing comment 4532952420 is unresolved, with no reply comments.
- No open or closed issue covers this residual (searched licensing / NC / ceiling / #5984 on 2026-11-11: only the parent design issue #5984, whose merged doc is the artifact carrying the defect).

## Still-live evidence (current main, read 2026-11-11 via `gh api`)

`doc/2026-11-11_design_id5984_licensing_policy.md` on main is unchanged on the relevant points:

- Line 226 (§6.1): "an admin running a genuinely non-commercial community server may allow NC with a one-line removal of the shipped deny."
- §4.3 step 0 / §5: the shipped NC deny is a top-level hard deny, and the default policy (§4.2, line ~133) is `ceiling 2` — so after removing the deny, an NC artifact at taxonomy level 3–4 still fails the ceiling test in the deciding policy.

An admin following §6.1 literally ends up with a server that still refuses all NC uploads, with no hint that a ceiling raise or an explicit NC `allow` is also required.

## Acceptance criteria

- §6.1 (and any other place repeating the "one-line removal" claim) documents the full change needed to admit NC uploads: removing the shipped deny **plus** raising the deciding policy's ceiling to cover NC levels (or adding an explicit NC allow), or the guidance is corrected to state that removal alone is insufficient.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why the current guidance is considered sufficient.

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review)

PR #4013 (merged, merge commit `c5f880113c43b0db5bd93c3d22142c71b333f8d1`, head `ae661bc5db33`) implemented saved views (#1276): a view is, in `src/views.ts`' own words, "a parameter set over the existing pages — the same items the Board / Projects / Roadmap pages and their /api/*.json twins render". The PR applied view filtering (`resolveView`) to `/board`, `/roadmap`, `/program`, `/api/projects.json`, `/api/board.json`, and `/api/roadmap.json` — including follow-up fixes (recorded as Codex P2s in the PR itself) that extended coverage to twins that were initially missed, e.g. the `/program` HTML page reached via the `/projects` redirect, and preserving view parameters in roadmap grain links.

**The Board's fragment twin was missed and still is:**

- In the PR diff, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts`'s `/frag/board` handler is untouched context — it renders `boardRender()` output with no `resolveView` call.
- Verified on current main (`84111174eff7a029e7478357b0209d4780421e2e`, read twice via `gh api` contents): `src/server.ts:1647-1651` — the `/frag/board` handler still calls `boardRender()` and `renderBoardBody(board, items, counts, act)` with no view resolution, while `/board` at `src/server.ts:1620` resolves and filters. `/frag/board` is a live, monitored fragment: `src/freshness-delivery.ts:91` registers `board: { id: "board-main", path: "/frag/board" }`.
- The fragment's own embedded refresh URL is `@get('/frag/board')` with no `view` / `viewer` / `vf.*` parameters, so even a handler-side fix needs the parameter propagation the same PR used for roadmap grain links and the `/projects` redirect.

## Why it matters

A viewer using a saved view (shareable `vf.*` URL or their persistent default) gets the filtered Board on a full `/board` load, but the Datastar fragment path (#1444 pattern) silently serves the **full unfiltered board** — no error, no indication the view was dropped. That is the same silent wrong-data class this PR's own P2 fixes treated as in-scope for every other twin.

## Acceptance criteria

- `GET /frag/board` applies `resolveView` with the same filtering rule as `/board` (including the linked-items `keptRefs` rule), for explicit `vf.*` params, a `view` id, and the `viewer` default.
- Fragment refresh/load URLs that a view-filtered page emits preserve the view parameters (`view` / `viewer` / `vf.*`), following the roadmap-grain-link pattern from PR #4013.
- Regression tests: for the same view, `/board` (HTML) and `/frag/board` return the same card set; an unfiltered request renders exactly as before.
- No change to view storage, verbs, or filter semantics.

title: id(libsql): decode chunked HTTP bodies as bytes before UTF-8 conversion

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/foreign_libsql.rs:833-849` converts the entire raw HTTP response using `String::from_utf8_lossy` before removing chunk framing. `dechunk` then interprets the HTTP chunk size (a byte count) as a Rust string slice boundary at lines 856-873. The production transport calls this parser at line 765.

A valid chunked response can split the UTF-8 bytes of `é` across two one-byte chunks: `1\r\n\xc3\r\n1\r\n\xa9\r\n0\r\n\r\n`. The lossy conversion replaces each incomplete byte sequence with a multi-byte replacement character; slicing it at byte 1 panics. Even where it does not panic, converting before reassembly can corrupt valid UTF-8. A remote response can therefore interrupt the operation rather than returning its data or a transport error.

## Acceptance criteria

- Parse and validate chunk framing using byte slices, concatenate chunk payload bytes, and only then decode the assembled body according to the transport contract.
- Valid UTF-8 split across chunk boundaries round-trips without corruption or panic; cover this with a regression test.
- Malformed or truncated framing returns a transport error rather than panicking, with focused tests.
- Preserve correct handling of ordinary chunked and non-chunked responses.

title: queue-capture-6450: probe FileNotFoundError (local fleet exec failure) falsely reported as queue-backend failure window
body:
## Problem

The `queue-capture-6450` standing capture (arm (a) for #6450) produced three false `FAILURE_CAPTURED …-probe.md` (PARTIAL) captures on 2026-11-10 — 06:47Z, 23:04Z, and 2026-11-11 01:58Z — while the queue backend was healthy. All other runs that day probed fine.

Trigger in all three: the capture's own health probe raised `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/home/hatch/tools/fleet'`.

## Root cause

Design flaw in `capture.py` (goal workspace `keep-the-four-repos-healthy/hidden_files/queue-capture-6450/capture.py`): *any* exception from `probe_health()` was treated as a failed probe = a queue-backend failure window, earning a capture.

But an `OSError` at exec time means `fleet` could not be run **locally at all** — it is not backend evidence:

- `~/tools/fleet` exists persistently (verified 2026-11-10 evening, multiple independent reads) and `fleet queue health` runs clean (rc 0, no 57014/PGRST002).
- `fleet` is a Nix-linked ELF whose interpreter is `/nix/store/…/lib/ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`. Verified with a minimal ELF test: a missing PT_INTERP produces exactly this Python error — `FileNotFoundError` naming the *binary*, not the interpreter. `/nix` is a symlink recreated by `~/tools/nix-ensure.sh` after sandbox recycles, so a run straddling a recycle/init race can transiently lose the interpreter (which exact path was missing at those three moments is unverified — the classification bug is proven regardless).

## Fix (landed + verified 2026-11-10)

In `capture.py` leg 3:

- `OSError` from the probe now runs one bounded self-heal (`~/tools/nix-ensure.sh`, idempotent) and one retry.
- If fleet still cannot exec locally, the run records a `health probe` **leg failure only** (`health_failed=False`) — a routine `OK … leg_failures=…` line, no capture. Real backend failures (non-zero exit, 57014/PGRST002 in output, timeouts) still earn captures unchanged.

Verification:

- Isolated run with `QUEUE_CAPTURE_FLEET=/nonexistent/fleet`: `OK … events_drained=0 health_failed=False leg_failures=health probe: FileNotFoundError…`, zero capture files (old code would have written a probe capture).
- Real run immediately after: `OK snapshot … events_drained=0 health_failed=False`, exit 0, no leg failures.

title: id(web): creating an existing filename silently replaces its content with an empty blob

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

body:
## Problem and evidence

`POST /api/new` can silently replace an existing named file with empty content. On the current default-branch version of `pkgs/id/src/web/routes/file_handlers.rs` (blob `f5652004ae6e2b9c4bd97994291354c6fe808512`), `new_file_handler` checks only for an empty name (lines 203–211), creates empty bytes or `{}` based on file type (213–225), and unconditionally calls `state.store.tags().set(tag, hash)` for the requested name (236–240). It does not check for an existing tag or archive the displaced content. It then updates metadata (243 onward).

Code-path reproduction (verified by inspection; not yet exercised against a running server): create a nonempty `existing.txt`, then send `POST /api/new` with JSON `{"name":"existing.txt"}`. The named tag is set to the empty blob, so subsequent reads by that name no longer resolve to the original content. Content-addressed storage may retain the old blob temporarily, but the handler does not preserve a named archive or return the old hash.

## Why it matters

A repeated create, including concurrent clients racing to choose the same filename, can silently lose the accessible version of a user document. Metadata changes can additionally misrepresent the original file.

## Acceptance criteria

- Creating a name already in use returns a conflict and leaves its content, name binding and metadata unchanged.
- Concurrent creates, and a create racing with another write to the same name, cannot replace existing content; implement an atomic claim or equivalent shared synchronization rather than a check-then-set race.
- Regression tests exercise the actual handler/store with an existing nonempty file and concurrent same-name requests, and verify the original binding and metadata remain intact; a new unique name still succeeds.
- Account for existing file-operation/name-validation contracts (see #4766) without silently turning create into an overwrite.

Searched open and closed issues for `/api/new`, `new_file_handler`, and id file overwrite; #7837 addresses client response shape, not this server-side data loss. #4766 addresses canonical/archive name ownership, not collision-safe web creation.

title: fix(id): restore Committed-arm sequence succession must be checked_add, not saturating_add (#4001 audit)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Gap found by the #4001 closing audit (task 5934, lane code-h, 2026-11-11)

`pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs`, in `WorldCore::restore_inner`'s `JournalEntry::Committed` arm (line 941 at origin/main `45638b86`):

```rust
ensure!(
    event.sequence == core.sequence.saturating_add(1),
    "journal sequence jumps from {} to {}",
    ...
);
```

This is a succession predicate in an admission (restore) path using `saturating_add`. Design #4000 decision 2: succession predicates must be `checked_add` — saturation loses, because at `core.sequence == u64::MAX` the saturated successor is `MAX` itself, so an event with sequence `MAX` satisfies the "advance by one" check without advancing; repeated `MAX` events would each pass the same check during replay.

Every sibling succession predicate in the same file already uses `checked_add` (transfer epoch succession ~line 270, checkpoint-part sequence ~line 1017, and lines ~672, ~1493, ~1832, ~1965). This is the one remaining plain-saturating succession predicate the crate-wide grep disposition in the #4001 audit found.

### Fix

- Change the predicate to `core.sequence.checked_add(1) == Some(event.sequence)` (shape of line 1017).
- Add a regression test mirroring `restore_checkpoint_sequence_does_not_wrap_at_u64_max` (world/tests.rs) for the Committed arm: a journal whose committed event sequence would need to advance past `u64::MAX` is refused.

### Evidence / provenance

- Audit posted on design #4000 by task 5934 (lane code-h, 2026-11-11): full reconstruction-entry-point inventory + plain-arithmetic grep disposition at origin/main `45638b86`.
- Filed as a named follow-up per #4001 acceptance ("fixed here (small) or filed as a named follow-up — never left as a comment-only finding"); the fix itself was not landed under the audit task because pkgs/id test builds exceed the audit shift's remaining lease.

title: fix(fleet-queue): outbox marker search is a POST that always 404s and a failed lookup counts as 'absent' — every uncertain entry is re-created

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: area/infra
labels.description: Infrastructure, deployment, and operations

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The creation-outbox drainer's marker reconciliation (`GhCreator::find_by_marker`, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:2589-2608`) can never find anything, and a failed lookup is indistinguishable from "proven absent". Every `uncertain` entry (ambiguous create, failed read-back, expired lease after a drainer crash) is therefore re-created, which is the duplicate-in-the-crash-window failure the outbox exists to prevent (#3706).

## Evidence (verified on origin/main fb97fae771, gh 2.102.0, laptop)

1. The search call is `gh api search/issues -f q=...` (client.rs:2593-2598). `gh api` switches to **POST** when any `-f` field is present, and `/search/issues` has no POST route:

```
$ gh api search/issues -f 'q=repo:dezren39/fleet-outbox-trial-3706 fleet-outbox:ob-1794350127-ac5b929eacf5' --include | head -1
HTTP/2.0 404 Not Found          (exit 1)
$ gh api search/issues -f 'q=repo:developing-today/code fleet-outbox'      # public repo: same 404
$ gh api search/issues --method GET -f 'q=repo:dezren39/fleet-outbox-trial-3706 fleet-outbox:ob-1794350127-ac5b929eacf5' --jq .total_count
2                               # issues #6 and #7, the trial-2 pair
```

2. `gh_json` (client.rs:2430-2436) maps any non-zero exit to `None` and discards stderr; `find_by_marker` `?`-propagates it, so a 404, a 403/429, or a network error all return `None`. The drain loop (client.rs:2636-2656) reads `None` as "Marker search proves absence: fall through and re-create". The lookup fails open on the duplicate-protection path.

3. Consequence for #8331: its live trial 2 attributed the duplicate (#7 after #6) to GitHub search indexing lag. The search leg cannot succeed at all with this argv, so the duplicate happens on every reconcile regardless of index freshness. The marker search is healthy with a GET (above). Adding a REST list-scan fallback, as #8331 proposes, would hide this dead call rather than repair it, and the error-as-absence behaviour would remain.

4. No test can see it: `GhCreator` is hard-wired to `Command::new("gh")` (client.rs:2420) with no seam, and nothing references `GhCreator`, `find_by_marker` or `read_back` outside `src/client.rs`. The 13 `creation_outbox` tests (pass on main) use `FakeCreator`, whose `find_by_marker` scans in-memory bodies, so the "kill/restart reconciles by marker" trial passes while the production leg is dead.

## Acceptance criteria

- The marker search is issued as a GET (`--method GET`, or a query string) and returns the landed object for a marker in an issue or PR body.
- The lookup returns a three-way result: found / checked-and-absent / could-not-check. "Could not check" (any non-2xx, transport error, unparseable JSON) leaves the entry `uncertain` with backoff and never re-creates; the stderr class is recorded in `last_error_class`.
- `GhCreator` gets a seam (a `gh` binary override or injected runner) and tests that assert the search argv is a GET, that a 404/403 yields "could not check", and that a landed marker is found.
- Relationship: this is the mechanism under #8331. #8331's strongly-consistent second source is still needed for index lag; this issue is the broken call and the fail-open handling. Related: #3706, #8363 (comment kinds).

Filed by improvement-issue-creator; filed only, not enqueued.

title: aggregator(collector): registry section outcome masks an unreadable launch-records file as absent

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

The fleet-feed collector's `registry` section outcome — added by PR #3943 so every collector section reports ok/error/skipped — cannot distinguish "no launch-records file yet" from "launch-records file present but unreadable/corrupt". The read is wrapped in a catch-all that swallows every error, and the section is then marked `ok` or `skipped` purely from whether other sources populated the registry.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3943 (merged, merge commit a10865f623) — "feat(aggregator): report collector section outcomes" (closes #1178).
- Verified on current main f2134568e19465494e6f65d885bb46562dae9d7f, two independent reads of `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts`:
  - :923-928 — `try { const jsonl = await readFile(launchRecordsPath, "utf8"); registry.push(...parseLaunchRecords(jsonl)); } catch { /* no launch records yet */ }` followed by `markSection("registry", registry.length ? "ok" : "skipped")`. A permission error, a corrupt file, or a `parseLaunchRecords` throw all land in the same silent catch as ENOENT.
- Contrast in the same file, same reporting system: the DNS register logs "collector: DNS register unreadable; section omitted" (:977); the orchestration section reports a structural-check failure as an error (:995); the projects section marks a zero-item read `error` (:1033, #3979). The registry block is the one section whose failure class is invisible.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-10 ("launch records registry collector section") returned no issue covering this; #1178 is closed.

## Why it matters

The section-outcome report exists so a silently-empty section is visible as a failure instead of a healthy-looking blank. For the registry, a broken launch-records file (bad permissions after a machine migration, a truncated write) reports exactly like the normal no-sessions-yet state, so Muse launch sessions can vanish from the registry with no signal anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- The launch-records read distinguishes ENOENT (absent — keep the current ok/skipped outcome, no error noise) from any other read/parse failure.
- A non-ENOENT failure is surfaced the way sibling sections surface theirs: a `console.error` with the sanitized error (`sanitizeCollectionError`) and a registry outcome that does not claim `ok` for the launch-records source (e.g. mark the section `error` when the registry would otherwise be empty, or record the failure in the section detail).
- A collector test covers both cases: missing file → unchanged outcome; unreadable/corrupt file → visible failure.

title: aggregator(queue-view): next-up priority tier is dead — no addNext call site passes a priority

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

The queue visibility page's next-up ordering has a priority tier that can never fire. `buildQueueView` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/queue-view.ts` sorts next-up candidates by `horizonRank || priorityRank || sequence`, and `PRIORITY_ORDER` (:80) maps urgent/critical/high/normal/low to ranks — but no caller ever passes a priority, so every candidate's `priorityRank` is the constant `2` and the tier is dead.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3959 (merged 2026-11-02, merge commit 5de0661d2a) — "feat(aggregator): add queue visibility page (#1160)".
- Verified on current main f2134568e19465494e6f65d885bb46562dae9d7f, two independent reads of `pm-stack/aggregator/src/queue-view.ts`:
  - :80 `const PRIORITY_ORDER: Record<string, number> = { urgent: 0, critical: 0, high: 1, normal: 2, medium: 2, low: 3 };`
  - :329 `const addNext = (args, horizon?, priority?) => { ... }` with :334 `priorityRank: PRIORITY_ORDER[norm(priority)] ?? 2`.
  - All three call sites pass only `(args, horizon)`: orchestration loop :341, Project pool loop :363, board loop :380. The third argument is never supplied anywhere in the file.
  - :395 sort: `a.horizonRank - b.horizonRank || a.priorityRank - b.priorityRank || a.sequence - b.sequence` — the middle term is always `2 - 2 = 0`.
- Dedupe: issue search 2026-11-10 ("queue-view priority next-up", "queue visibility priority") returned no issue covering this; source issue #1160 is closed.

## Why it matters

The next-up list is the fleet's "what gets picked up next" surface. Its ordering silently ignores priority: an urgent queued item ranks purely by horizon and insertion sequence, while the code (and anyone reading it) believes priority breaks ties. Either the ordering is wrong, or the dead parameter/table misleads every future change to this file.

## Acceptance criteria

- Decide the intended behaviour and implement exactly one of:
  - Wire a real priority source into the three `addNext` call sites (from the orchestration task, Project pool item, or board item, wherever the data actually lives), with a test showing two same-horizon candidates ordered by priority; or
  - Remove the `priority` parameter, the `priorityRank` field, and `PRIORITY_ORDER` so the sort is honestly horizon-then-sequence.
- A test pins the chosen ordering behaviour for same-horizon candidates.

title: quota gatherer: folded codex rows misfiled under openai.main (phantom 5h series) + drewrypope measurement dead (token_expired / refresh_token_reused) — fleet blind on openai.main post-$200 upgrade
body:
The quota gatherer files every folded `codex` credential row under `openai.main`, and the drewrypope account's measurement credentials died on 2026-11-10 — the fleet is currently blind on its biggest door, holding it on a retained pre-upgrade reading.

## Defect 1 — misfiled account (aggregator, fix in flight)

The fork's codex quota provider folds all OpenAI instance credentials into its per-credential answer under provider id `codex` (`foldInstanceCredentials`, fork `packages/ai/src/quota/index.ts`). The aggregator's `serviceIdFor("codex")` returns `openai.main` unconditionally (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts`), so all three accounts' rows publish under main's service id.

Evidence (quota-current.json, generatedAt 2026-11-10T21:21:48Z):
- Row `providerId=codex`, providerName **"OpenAI Alternate (Student - popesdrew)"**, cred_17514…, `serviceId: "openai.main"`, weekly **65%**, resets **2026-11-16T17:45:12Z** — alternate's numbers under main's id. Read as main, it fakes a 100→65 reset with a moved label.
- The same credential's dedicated row (`providerId=openai.alternate`) is correctly filed — the mislabel is specific to the folded codex rows.

Impact: any consumer reading the misfiled row concludes main reset to 65% and could release the quota plant early against a walled door. The Turso sink also keys rows by serviceId (`${serviceId}:${tickAt}`, INSERT OR IGNORE), so the three codex rows collide on one id per tick.

## Defect 2 — phantom openai.main 5h series (same root)

Snapshot records collapse per serviceId|window with the max-pct rule (#1624). Main's own entry reports no 5h window; the only `openai.main|5h` candidate was alternate's misfiled codex row. Result: `usage-2026-11.jsonl` carries an `openai.main` 5h series duplicating `openai.alternate` 5h tick-for-tick (2026-11-09/10: 12, 74, 100, 0, 1, 44, 100, 0, 6, 70, 100 … with alternate's resetsAt), and on 2026-11-04 `openai.main|weekly` published 100 carrying alternate's reset label (2026-11-09T17:04:02Z) while main's own read was ~17. This is the dual-source contamination the 2026-11-10 per-point lane hit (cf. #2490).

## Defect 3 — measurement dead on the drewrypope account; auto-fix precondition broken

Last good measurement: 2026-11-10T21:15:13Z (weekly 100%, resets Fri 2026-11-13T14:28:52Z — the OLD $100 tier). From the 21:21:48Z tick onward, consecutive ticks (21:21, 21:30, 21:45) fail for both drewrypope credentials (`openai.main` cred_oKXp…, `_openai` cred_3EG9…) with "Session expired — please re-authenticate with OpenAI"; the dedicated entries are #1268-retained from 21:15:13Z.

Provider verdicts (read directly, 2026-11-10 ~21:3xZ):
- wham/usage for both credentials: HTTP 401, error code **`token_expired`** — despite JWT exps of 2026-11-19 / 2026-11-20. The invalidation is server-side.
- Refresh with main's stored refresh token: HTTP 401, code **`refresh_token_reused`** — "Your refresh token has already been used to generate a new access token." The token family was consumed by a refresh/sign-in outside the credential store; the store's copies are stranded. The laptop Muse auth file holds the byte-identical pair (hash match), so the designated external refresher (CodexSync, credential stamped `externalRefresh`) is stranded too.
- openai.alternate (different account) measures fine throughout (weekly 65%).
- Both stored tokens still carry plan_type `prolite`; Drew upgraded the account to the $200 plan on 2026-11-10, so no fleet-held token reflects the new tier, and no fresh post-upgrade reading exists.

The quota path never refreshes: fork `codex.ts` `fetchQuotaForEntry` uses the stored access token as-is. A rotated/revoked measurement credential therefore stays dead in the record until the serving path rewrites the row — and here the serving path's refresher is dead too. Recovery requires **one fresh sign-in for the drewrypope ChatGPT account** (browser step), after which CodexSync re-seeds the credential and the gatherer measures the $200 tier.

Why it matters beyond blindness: Drew's rule (2026-11-10) "when quota drops it should auto fix" — the #1978 release path can only fire on a FRESH below-full reading. A dead measurement path silently disables auto-fix while looking exactly like a wall: the plant is currently holding the Terra door on the retained 100% reading from the old tier, and if the $200 bucket has room, that hold is wrong but undisprovable from the record.

## Fix

- Aggregator (this issue's PR): folded codex rows file under their own pool via a label-derived `codexPoolServiceId` (mirrors `goPoolServiceId`); the heartbeat now surfaces a partially-failed run's first error (finalizeRun previously reported the codex run as `ok` with no error while two of its three credentials were failing).
- Recovery (needs Drew): fresh sign-in for the drewrypope ChatGPT account; then verify consecutive ok ticks + the $200 tier's actual windows.
- Follow-on: a measurement failure on a held leg should raise a loud attention item, not sit retained-quiet; and the quota read path should participate in the self-renewal design (#8102, #2490).

Acceptance: (i) fresh ticks show three correctly attributed OpenAI-family entries; (ii) no new `openai.main|5h` snapshot records sourced from alternate's row; (iii) after re-auth, openai.main measures ok on consecutive ticks with the $200 tier's windows, and the release path is watched for auto-lift.

title: fix(quota-plane): Meta portal-session lapse surfaces as 'no-data' error instead of a distinct lapsed state

body:
## Problem
The Meta quota read depends on a live portal (dev.meta.ai) browser session on the hub. When that session lapses — or the portal returns the active-but-no-usage shape — the gatherer leg fails as `no-data: provider reported ok but no window data` and the Meta pool drops to a generic error state (observed by the pool-quota steward, 2026-11-08T12:49Z, 240th run, on issue #3347's thread). A lapsed session is not a provider failure: it has a known remedy (re-auth on the hub) and the last good windows should stay visible as aging data, not vanish behind an error badge.

## Context
- Predecessor chain: #3347 (both Meta routes dead, Oct/Nov) → file-export route retired by PR #5040 → portal fetcher restored under #6079 (closed 2026-11-05, session restored by hand). The session dependency is now the standing failure mode.
- Template: the OpenCode Go lapse handling that landed in PR #7898 (issue #1161) — a distinct `lapsed` state end to end (gatherer classification, current-file validators, pool overlay) instead of error.

## Acceptance
- [ ] A Meta read whose failure is a lapsed/invalid portal session is classified distinctly from a provider error (state or reason), with the re-auth remedy named in the pool note.
- [ ] While lapsed, the pool keeps its last good windows visible (stale semantics) instead of dropping to a bare error.
- [ ] Gatherer + aggregator tests cover: lapsed session, ok-but-no-usage shape, and recovery on the next good read.

title: fix(queue): broker-owned dependency blocking — typed deps, automated recheck, max TTL
body:
# fix(queue): broker-owned dependency blocking — typed deps, automated recheck, max TTL

## Drew's order (2026-11-10, verbatim)

"Also implement a method to mark things blocked by pull requests, other tasks, or CI completion, with a max DTL to recheck and an automated system within the broker to check PR status and other task status automatically. That's so that's not a concern for each item that claims a task. It's just blocked until a certain issue closes or a task completes, and then it becomes available and can be picked up on the next claim. Everything has some sort of max TTL of some number of days or hours ahead, so if something breaks, it gets rechecked and doesn't just sit forever because of an open PR." ("max DTL" = max TTL.)

## Problem today

Dependency gating is manual and per-claim: a lane claims an item, discovers a gate (open PR, parent issue, unfinished task, CI still running), verifies it fresh on GitHub, parks/blocks with a prose note — and the next claim re-verifies the same gate from scratch. Hundreds of blocked tasks and dozens of gate-parked tasks get re-checked shift after shift (tasks gated on #3901/#3801/#3418 for weeks).

## Design

**Structured block records.** `fleet queue block` gains typed dependency flags; deps are stored structurally on the task row (new additive columns on `tasks`, same migration pattern as #8187/#8210): `blocked_deps` (JSON array), `dep_next_recheck_at`, `dep_blocked_until`, `dep_recheck_seconds`. Each dep: `{kind: pr|issue|task|ci, repo, number|task_id|run_id, state, last_checked_at, last_observed, recorded_by, recorded_at, reason}`. CLI: `--blocked-by-pr owner/repo#N`, `--blocked-by-issue owner/repo#N`, `--blocked-by-task ID`, `--blocked-by-ci RUN_ID`, `--dep-recheck-seconds N`, `--dep-max-ttl-seconds N`. A block with NO deps keeps today's free-text behavior exactly — escalations to Drew are not deps and never auto-clear.

**Max TTL + recheck.** Recheck interval default 900s (15 min), caller range 300–3600s. Max TTL default 259200s (3 days), broker ceiling 604800s (7 days), floor 60s. At TTL expiry with the dep still open, the block expires: task returns to the claimable pool, audit event says the block timed out. A dep whose reference is BROKEN (PR/issue/run not found, task id unknown) is released at its next recheck with the reason in the event — a typo'd gate is not a life sentence.

**Broker-side automated rechecker.** New `/dep-recheck` path + state machine in `turso_queue.rs`, driven by the existing sweep: `fleet-queue-expire.timer` already POSTs `/sweep {"expire":true}` to the broker every minute, and verb_sweep gains the dep-recheck step on that path — no new service, no lane involvement, runs while no lane is awake. Per pass: only tasks whose `dep_next_recheck_at` has arrived are examined; identical GitHub refs across tasks are fetched once per pass.
- task dep: cleared when the dep task is `done`; `cancelled`/`failed` also release the dependent, with the dep outcome named in the event (the dependent's lane re-evaluates instead of waiting forever).
- issue dep: cleared when the issue is CLOSED.
- pr dep: cleared when the PR is MERGED or CLOSED.
- ci dep: cleared when the run is completed, any conclusion (a failed run must not hold the dependent hostage; the claiming lane evaluates the result).
GitHub reads happen inside the broker process: a `DepProbe` trait in turso_queue, production impl in queue_broker.rs resolving the `github.developing-today-code-automation` secret by name through the broker's existing secrets Resolver, calling api.github.com. A FAILED check (rate limit, token down — cf. #7930) is neither clearance nor expiry: it reschedules, and only the max TTL releases the task.

**Claim interaction.** Dep-blocked tasks keep status `blocked`, which every pick branch already excludes — lanes never see them and never re-verify gates. `wake` on a dep-blocked task forces an immediate recheck of that task (unblocks only if the recheck clears it). New `/unblock` verb + CLI: manual override by a lane/monitor, event names who overrode and discards the dep record.

**Audit.** Events: `blocked` (now carrying the deps array), `dep_cleared` (per dep, with observed evidence), `dep_unblocked` (all deps clear → queued), `dep_ttl_expired`, `dep_broken`, `dep_unblock_override`. No-change rechecks write no per-task event (counted in the sweep summary) — no poll spam.

**Labels.** The broker does not write GitHub labels (it has no label surface today). Auto-unblock returns the task to `queued` with the event as the record; the next claiming lane syncs `queue/*`/`status/*` labels at claim time per §9, and the runbook gains a line for exactly this. Failure mode, accepted: between auto-unblock and the next claim, GitHub labels lag the queue — queue state leads, labels follow, same as park expiry today.

**Health.** Per-queue health gains `dep_blocked` (blocked rows carrying deps) distinct from plain `blocked`. The dep record rides on the task row, so list output shows it; #8200 (show/history verb) is still open — when it lands it reads the same columns.

## Sequencing

Fourth in the current broker-change queue. Ahead: #8210 send/transfer (merged, PR #8214 lineage), #8217 batch claim (merged PR #8244), #8234 sink status (merged PR #8263 — status set is now queued/claimed/parked/handed_off/blocked/done/cancelled/failed). Both predecessors are on main, so this builds directly on the post-cleanup status set: dep-blocking reuses status `blocked` (no new status — blocked was already the claim-excluded home for gates; what changes is that the block becomes data the broker can act on). Links: #8187, #8210, #8217, #8234, #8200, #8191, #8192.

## Acceptance (live receipts)

- Task blocked by an OPEN PR is not claimable; a second task blocked by an already-MERGED PR is cleared by the rechecker with no lane touching it; events shown.
- Task B blocked by task A; A completes; B becomes claimable and is claimed.
- Task blocked by a still-open PR with a minutes-long max TTL returns to the pool at expiry with the timeout event.
- Task blocked on a completed CI run clears at first recheck.
- Health shows dep_blocked distinct from plain blocked; an escalation block (no deps) never auto-clears.

title: fleet-search: main build broken - server.rs initializers missing new atlas-core fields
body: Found during the #8217 deploy (2026-11-10): `cargo build -p fleet` fails on current main in crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs - 3 x E0063. atlas-core added `SearchOptions.parameters: SearchParametersV1` and `BranchQuery.{shard_top_k, global_top_k}`; the server initializers were not updated (server.rs:618 SearchOptions, server.rs:808/814 BranchQuery). fleet-search has no other SearchOptions construction site. Fix: parameters: SearchParametersV1::default() (the wire SearchRequest carries no parameters field; SearchOptions::default does the same) and copy shard_top_k/global_top_k from the incoming BranchQuery in the executor, mirroring atlas-core shards/scan.rs. Blocks any fleet binary deploy from main, including the queue broker.

title: Prod service started by its own unit runs a stale binary (3497ea2) baked into the runtime config snapshot — unit ExecStart ignored
body:
# Prod service, when actually started by its systemd unit, runs a stale binary baked into the runtime config snapshot — unit ExecStart binary is ignored

Found 2026-11-10 ~15:03 CST during the code#8086 / code#8255 / code#8261 takeover.

## Wire facts (laptop, host amd)

- The home-manager user unit `opencode.service` (generation 555) has `ExecStart=/nix/store/zzzhr7mzf1h5yhfy1nnqx2d3m53yk828-opencode-2.0.30+fafff70-wrapped/bin/opencode serve --service --hostname 127.0.0.1 --port 13420` — verified in the unit file itself.
- After a verified-clean takeover (port confirmed FREE, then `systemctl --user start opencode.service`, unit active, MainPID's parent = systemd 1459), the process that bound port 13420 and registered itself was **`/nix/store/ydgi99xfsncbwrpvqlc30dnb0grrv57p-opencode-2.0.30+3497ea2/bin/.opencode-wrapped`** (service-prod.json version `2.0.30+3497ea2`, registration id dbabcfed) — NOT the unit's fafff70 binary. The same 3497ea2 build also won an earlier systemd-detached registration at 21:00Z ("managed service registration replaced; shutting down" in the server log).
- The unit sets `Environment=OPENCODE_CONFIG=%h/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc` — a **runtime config snapshot** in the state dir. That snapshot (or the service machinery reading it) evidently carries its own binary reference: in service mode the starter hands off to the snapshot's pinned build instead of running its own image. `/run/current-system/sw/bin/opencode` currently resolves to c43145b (generation 554's pin), so the layers disagree three ways at once: unit ExecStart = fafff70, system profile = c43145b, snapshot service = 3497ea2.
- No process in the fleet is actually the unit's binary: every "successful switch" (generations 554, 555) changed the unit file and nothing else (see code#8255 for the incumbent-defer mechanism and code#8261 for the shadow supervisor that held the port in between).

## Impact

- Deploying a new opencode build to the fleet requires updating THREE pins (flake pin → generation, system profile, runtime config snapshot) and nothing in the switch procedure says so; two of the three were silently stale. Until the snapshot is regenerated from the current pin, the gathered-quota plant (fork #2252) and the feed-stamp fix (fork #2254) do not run in production, and the cline-pass bench lapses ~2026-11-11 with no pre-attempt hold behind it.

## Fix shape (for the owning lane)

1. Find what writes `~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc` and what consumes its binary pin in service mode; make the snapshot regenerate from the deployed pin on every switch (or stop carrying a binary pin — the unit's ExecStart should be the single source of truth).
2. Switch proof must read the REGISTERED service's version + the port owner's exe path, never the unit file.
3. Add the snapshot refresh to the generation-switch checklist/runbook wherever the other two pins are bumped.

Evidence gathered during the code#8086 follow-up lane, 2026-11-10.

title: Shadow supervisor (pid 1059342, stale system profile) respawns prod OpenCode service within seconds of any stop — port version decided by rebind race
body:
# A user-session supervisor respawns the prod OpenCode service from the stale system profile within seconds of any stop

Found 2026-11-10 ~14:56 CST during the code#8086 / code#8255 takeover attempts.

## Wire facts (laptop, host amd)

- The actor: pid 1059342, `/run/current-system/sw/bin/opencode` (a client process, running since Sun Nov 8 15:55:50, ~208 session sockets). `/run/current-system/sw/bin/opencode` resolves to the **8ed9d6c** build (fork main 2026-11-08) — the NixOS **system** profile, which no generation switch in this lane touched (user has no passwordless sudo; switches were user-level home-manager activations).
- Behavior, three times in a row: the registered prod service on port 13420 is stopped (management-client stop, clean) → **within ~3 seconds a new `serve --service` child of pid 1059342 binds the port**, running whatever binary the supervisor's own process image carries:
  - 14:47:42Z-ish: respawned 8ed9d6c (pid 2506140) after the first incumbent died.
  - 14:49:52Z: an ff9858a instance (pid 2517083, child of a *different* stale client, pid 3377477) won the race once.
  - 14:53:00Z: pid 2533216 (ff9858a) held the port; after the next stop, 14:56Z: pid 2551341 (**8ed9d6c** again, registered id 49a4345f) — i.e. the prize goes to whichever stale client happens to win the rebind race; the outcome is nondeterministic across stops.
- The supervisor process 1059342's parent (pid 1059341) is a **laptop-agent exec shell** whose command line is an unrelated heredoc (`cat > /tmp/lane-v-13422-note.md`) — i.e. this supervisor is a detached side effect of a Nov 8 fleet lane's tooling, not a managed unit. No systemd unit owns it.
- Consequence: `opencode service stop` + `systemctl --user start opencode.service` can never install a new binary — the unit's starter defers to the incumbent (code#8255), and the incumbent is always a stale-build respawn. The systemd unit has been dead while the port stayed served by this shadow supervision tree, which is why the watchdog (port-based) never alerted.

## Impact

- The fleet's prod server version is decided by a rebind race among stale client processes, not by any deployment. Generation switches 554 and 555 both landed their unit files correctly and changed nothing on the port.
- Any future switch will silently fail the same way until this supervision tree is retired or repointed.

## Fix shape (for the owning lane)

1. Identify the launching tool (the Nov 8 lane behind pid 1059341/1059342) and retire the shadow supervisor: prod service ownership belongs to the systemd user unit alone.
2. If a client-side supervisor is by design, it must exec the CURRENT generation's binary (resolve through the unit or a stable gcrooted path at respawn time, never its own process image).
3. After retirement, verify: stop the service, confirm the port stays free for >60s, start the unit, confirm the registered pid's exe is the current generation's wrapped path.

Evidence gathered during the code#8086 follow-up lane, 2026-11-10.

title: pm-dispatch sessions never advance after a prod OpenCode service restart — attempts freeze while service stays up
body:
# pm-dispatch sessions never advance after a prod OpenCode service restart — warm-up fails silently forever

Found 2026-11-10 ~14:52 CST during the code#8086 / code#8255 service takeover.

## Wire facts (laptop, host amd)

- At 2026-11-10T20:49:52Z the prod service on port 13420 changed hands (old pid 2506140, 8ed9d6c → new pid 2517083, ff9858a) via a management-client stop + supervisor restart.
- Since that moment, **zero new `route_attempt` rows** have been written (last attempt 20:51:07Z from the outgoing instance; check at 20:53Z: newest attempt still 1794343867260 while wall clock was 1794343918245 — a >8-minute and growing gap; the fleet normally writes attempts continuously).
- The new instance is up and healthy at the HTTP layer: it accepted client connections (pm-dispatch, pm-stack and the supervisor processes all hold ESTABLISHED connections to 13420 within seconds of the restart) and `service status` answers.
- Yet no session advances: pm-dispatch (systemd user unit, active/running) holds a connection but produces no new attempts. Warm-up failures of exactly this shape were already visible in the server log before the restart (`failed to warm session ... rate limit` warnings from the outgoing instance at 20:42Z), suggesting sessions were already fragile around restarts.
- Contributing shape seen in the log: **multiple competing `serve --service` starters** (two extra 8ed9d6c "cli starting" lines at 20:49:54Z alongside the winning ff9858a start) — every supervising layer tries to ensure the service, and session-owning layers appear to keep handles to whichever instance they warmed against.

## Impact

- A routine service restart — which every generation switch performs — silently freezes all dispatched fleet sessions: no attempts, no errors in the route tables, nothing for the quota/route telemetry to show. The fleet minder census (session states) is the only surface that would catch it.
- This blocked the code#8086 feed-stamp deployment: the only way found to move the port to the new binary also froze session advancement (state at filing: port on ff9858a, attempts frozen at 20:51:07Z).

## Fix shape (for the owning lane)

1. After any prod service restart, pm-dispatch must re-warm / re-bind its sessions against the new instance (or the instance must replay warm-up for known sessions on boot).
2. Add a liveness check that compares "service up" against "attempts advancing" and alerts/restarts the dispatch layer when they diverge for more than a few minutes.
3. Reduce competing starters: exactly one layer should own ensuring the prod service (see code#8255).

Evidence gathered during the code#8086 follow-up lane, 2026-11-10.

title: Fleet prod OpenCode service is not the systemd unit's binary — unit restarts exit 0 without binding (incumbent defer)
body:
# Fleet prod OpenCode service is not the systemd unit's binary — unit restarts exit 0 without binding

Found 2026-11-10 ~14:48 CST during the code#8086 generation-555 switch (fork pin fafff70).

## What is true on the wire (all verified on the laptop, host amd)

- The systemd **user** unit `opencode.service` (home-manager managed) points at the current generation's wrapped binary and its ExecStartPre (env-key materialize) succeeds, but a `systemctl --user restart` starts the new binary, which **exits 0 after ~1.4s without binding port 13420 and without writing `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`**. Unit shows `inactive (dead)`, MainPID 0. Restart=on-failure does not retry (exit 0).
- Port 13420 is instead held by pid 2374724, binary `/nix/store/dbi4bx5zd06x172m82534xpwq4ddfdsc-opencode-2.0.30+8ed9d6c/bin/.opencode-wrapped` — fork main as of **2026-11-08** (generation 548's build). Its parent chain: pid 1059342 `/run/current-system/sw/bin/opencode` (started Sun Nov 8 15:55:50) → parent pid 1059341 → **laptop-agent.service** (the resident fleet execution agent, code#5343). So the production server was (re)launched by laptop-agent tooling on Nov 8 under the then-current system profile, and that instance has owned the port since 2026-11-10 14:32:17 CST (its own start; service-prod.json id ee5fd03f, version 2.0.30+8ed9d6c).
- That 8ed9d6c instance is healthy and serving the fleet: it holds the live `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` (fd + fresh WAL writes), route_attempt rows advancing in real time. It predates BOTH the #2252 plant (c43145b) and the feed-stamp fix (fafff70).
- The managed-service code path explains the unit's exit: `packages/cli/src/server-process.ts` — in service mode, `Service.incumbent(...)` checks whether a registered service already answers at the URL; **if an incumbent exists, the new process returns silently (exit 0) without registering or binding**. `ServiceRegistration.register` only runs in `onListen`, i.e. only for the process that actually binds.
- Consequence for the previous switch: generation 554's activation (2026-11-10 17:30:44Z) restarted the unit, the c43145b binary likewise deferred to the incumbent, and the recorded "running server 2.0.30+c43145b pid 1487125" was a transient process, not the port owner. The port owner before 14:32 CST today is unidentified; pid 1487125 no longer exists. A full process sweep at 14:47 CST shows **no c43145b and no fafff70 opencode process running** (only 8ed9d6c ×3 incl. children, ff9858a ×1, 4b2fc8a cockpit daemon, two stale 1add729).
- The watchdog (`opencode-watchdog.service`, code#7780) sees the port serving and the unit state does not trip it, so nothing alerts: the fleet has been running a two-generations-old server while generations 554/555 reported switched.

## Impact

- Every generation switch since the laptop-agent instance took the port has been a no-op for the actual fleet server. Route/telemetry evidence gathered "post-switch" in that window describes the 8ed9d6c binary (which contains fork #1978's release and per-model skips, but NOT #2252's gathered plant and NOT the feed-stamp fix).
- The cline-pass credential bench lapses ~2026-11-11; the gathered plant (the only pre-attempt hold for that leg once the bench lapses) is not in the running binary until the port actually changes hands.

## Fix shape (for the owning lane)

1. Make the switch procedure verify the PORT OWNER's binary path + service-prod.json version/pid after restart, not the unit's ExecStart or a transient pid.
2. Decide the takeover path: gracefully stop the incumbent (its registration shutdown hook) or kill the laptop-agent-spawned instance, then start the unit so the new binary binds and registers. Sessions in flight on the incumbent are the consideration — pick a natural break or accept the restart the unit restart already implies.
3. Stop laptop-agent tooling from launching a competing `--service` instance (or make it launch through the unit), so the port cannot silently revert to a stale binary again.
4. Consider making the incumbent-defer path log loudly / exit non-zero when the incumbent's version differs from the starter's, so a version-mismatched defer can never pass as a successful switch.

Evidence gathered during code#8086 follow-up lane, 2026-11-10.

title: test(id): planted-bug check for the tag observed-remove fold (#1421)
body:
