title: fix(queue): handoff sink gets its own status (handed_off) and the fake expiry timer is deleted
body:
## Drew's order (2026-11-10, verbatim)

"Clean it up: sink gets its own status, drop the fake timer"

## Problem

The status `parked` covers two unlike things:

1. **Genuine broker-owned timed waits** — `wait_kind` + `ready_condition` + `not_before` with broker floors (triage 6h, CI/capacity 1h, #8184/#8185). The item is waiting on something real, and releases by timer or `wake`.
2. **The handoff sink** — parked rows recorded as opencode handoffs (`PARKED_HANDOFF_SQL`: `status='parked' AND progress.lane='opencode' AND progress.session_id IS NULL AND stage IN ('handed_off','launch_failed')`). These are not waiting on time at all; they are recorded handoffs nobody has collected yet.

The overlap is what made the old handoff loop hard to see, and it still produces nonsense bookkeeping: `expire_leases` returns an expired claim on a sink-shaped row to `parked` **and stamps a fresh `not_before = now+1200s` with a `{"kind":"time"}` ready_condition** — a fake timer, because the sink branch of the default pick ignores `not_before` entirely. Either the timer matters (then the sink is a wait) or it doesn't (then stop stamping it).

## Fix

Give the sink its own status: **`handed_off`**.

Name choice: `handed_off` is already the vocabulary of this state everywhere else — the checkpoint stage, the park classification, the audit events. As a status it reads as the state the task is in ("recorded handoff, not yet collected"), invents no second vocabulary, and leaves `parked` meaning exactly one thing: a genuine timed wait. (`awaiting_collection` was the alternative; rejected — longer, and a new term for a concept the fleet already calls a handoff.)

### Scope

- **Park / handoff recording:** a recorded opencode handoff lands in status `handed_off`, not `parked`.
- **Predicates:** `PARKED_HANDOFF_SQL`, `is_parked_handoff`, `handoff_shape` match the new status (keeping the session-unbound condition; dropping what the status makes redundant).
- **Default pick:** the timed-park branch no longer needs the NOT-sink exclusion (a sink row can't be `parked` by construction); the sink branch picks from `handed_off`. Claim UPDATE's parked case (+0 attempts) treats `handed_off` like `parked` for attempt purposes.
- **Claimant discovery** (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/`): collects from the new status instead of parked handoffs.
- **`expire_leases` sink return:** returns to `handed_off` with `not_before = NULL` and **no** time ready_condition — the fake timer is deleted. Binding cleared as today; attempts untouched; `lease_expired` event records the new return target.
- **By-id claim:** `handed_off` rows stay claimable by id; genuine wait-parks stay excluded.
- **Wake verb:** stays parked-only; a `handed_off` row is already claimable, so wake refuses it explicitly (help + test).
- **Health:** new status is its own count bucket; `parked` in health output means genuine waits only.
- **List verb / client / CLI help:** status enumerations updated.
- **Labels (§9):** checked — label sync stays coarse (`queue/parked` covers the wait family); the status split is a broker/queue distinction, recorded on this issue; no label change unless a consumer is found that needs one.

### #8192 disposition — folded in

#8192: broker reads stage as `COALESCE(progress.stage, last_checkpoint.stage)` while claimant poll prefers `last_checkpoint.stage`; rows whose top-level stage was overwritten after the `handed_off` checkpoint are stranded in the gap. Once sink membership is a **status**, neither the broker predicate nor the claimant needs to reconstruct it from stage at all — the stage-source disagreement stops mattering for sink membership, and the migration classifier (below) uses the union reading (either stage source says `handed_off`/`launch_failed`, lane opencode, unbound) so stranded rows like task 10995 are collected into the new status instead of left behind. #8192 closes with credit when this lands.

### #8191 disposition — reframed

#8191 (parked handoffs re-served to lanes ignoring `not_before`): the re-serves were the #8189 sink-drain working as designed (the sink branch deliberately ignores `not_before`) combined with lanes running the pre-#8187 re-handoff choreography. This change doesn't change who may collect a sink row, but it removes the ambiguity that made the report possible: a row in `handed_off` is visibly a sink row, a genuine wait-park can never be mistaken for one, and a lane that parks a collected item as a real wait puts it in `parked` where its timer is honored. Disposition comment to be posted on #8191 at landing.

### Migration

After deploy, one auditable backend operation (event recorded, like the #8187 `queue_reset` event) moves existing sink-shaped `parked` rows to `handed_off`, per queue, with before/after counts. Genuine wait-parks must not move — proven by sampling a live CI/triage wait row before and after.

### Sequencing

Lands **third**, behind #8210 (send/transfer — merged, PR #8223) and #8217 (batch claim + dispatch — in flight). No edits to `turso_queue.rs` or `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` until #8217 merges; this change rebases on final main.

### Acceptance

- Before/after `fleet queue health` for repo-health-code-pilot: `parked` drops to genuine waits only; new `handed_off` bucket holds the sink count.
- One live sink row collected after migration (claimant bind or lane flip-to-direct) from the new status.
- One forced lease expiry on a claimed sink row returns it to `handed_off` with `not_before` NULL — no fake timer.
- The sampled genuine wait row unmoved.
- Fleet-queue suite + claimant suites green, incl. updated #8184/#8185/#8187 regression tests and new tests for the above.

Refs #8187, #8185, #8192, #8191, #8210, #8217.

title: feat(modal): first Modal workload — benchmark + Atlas internal re-embed on L4 (from #6069)

body:
Implementation follow-up for #6069 (design(modal): best use of Modal credits). Filed by task 13205 (triage-doctrine re-queue) after re-verifying #6069 on 2026-11-10: the design is real and current, the allocation is recorded on #6069, and the linked follow-ups cover the GPU-after-credits survey (#6072, closed) and the embedding cost ledger (#6058, closed), with spend tracking in #1111 (open). The missing piece is the first actual Modal workload itself — this issue is that workload.

## Scope (first workload only, per the #6069 design)
1. Benchmark first (~$1 cap): validate arctic-embed-m-v2.0 throughput on one Modal L4 against the design's planning numbers (15k pess / 30k expected / 60k opt tok/s; local baseline 1,529 tok/s). Record measured tok/s and $/M tokens on this issue before any bulk run.
2. If the benchmark holds: run the full Atlas internal re-embed (55.05M tokens, measured) on L4 — design estimate 31-61 min, ~$0.60-$1.15 all-in. Output is 768-dim, dimension-identical to the live index (no migration).
3. Record spend against the $130 total ($30/mo recurring + $100 one-time grant, one-time grant expires ~Oct 2027) in the embedding cost ledger (#6058) / quota tracking (#1111).

## Hard guardrails (from #6069, binding)
- Secret-tier text NEVER goes to Modal. Internal tier only; secret tier stays on the local embedder.
- No always-on GPU, no new vendor accounts, no OCI, no Mac.
- Stop and report on this issue if the benchmark misses the pessimistic bound by >2x or projected spend for the re-embed exceeds $5.

## Acceptance
- Benchmark numbers posted on this issue.
- Re-embed completed (or a recorded verdict why not, with benchmark evidence) and the resulting index verified dimension-identical / query-parity spot-checked against the live index.
- Spend recorded in the ledger with the running total against $130.

title: feat(queue): batch claim (--count N) + per-item dedicated sub-task dispatch
body:
# feat(queue): batch claim (--count N) + per-item dedicated sub-task dispatch

## Drew's orders (verbatim, 2026-11-10)

- "why does it pull multiple items can it hand off each item to a dedicated sub task? can claim take a number of items to claim?"
- Approval: "Build batch claim + per-item dedicated sub-tasks"
- Platform limitation rule: "if something has to be it could be limited to muse or oc but better be good reason" — a task may be limited to one platform family only with a good reason recorded on it; default is open to either platform.

## Builds on

- #8187 (single-session redesign, closed): claim pick is one atomic pick, ORDER BY priority ASC (nulls last), created_at ASC, LIMIT 1; assignment decided after claim, default direct, opencode only with a recorded reason; platform is a mark, never a filter; events table is the append-only audit trail.
- #8210 (IN FLIGHT — dependency): Muse→opencode push: claim-by-id transfer verb (--from-session) + one-call send with notes and worktree. THIS issue lands second: no work on turso_queue.rs claim paths or launch_one.py until #8210's PR is merged to main; this build rebases cleanly on top of it and reuses its launcher/transfer mechanism (no third launcher).
- #6533 (claimant binding history).

## What to build

### 1. Batch claim: `fleet queue claim --count N`

- Runs the existing atomic pick N times: same eligibility (queued-due under attempts cap, expired timed parks, parked recorded-handoff sink with no not_before gate), same priority/age order, same per-claim audit events and marks (platform/lane/model/session).
- Hard cap: N ≤ BATCH_CLAIM_MAX = 5 (named constant; reasoning: a dispatcher can launch+verify ~5 dedicated sessions inside one touch without leases ageing; larger batches recreate the claimed-and-idle pile this design forbids).
- Partial success is normal: fewer eligible than N returns what exists; zero eligible returns the usual no-task verdict.
- Per-item attempts/lease semantics unchanged (queued +1, parked +0; each item its own lease).

### 2. Dispatch pairing — no idle holding

A batch claim is only legitimate paired with immediate dispatch in the same touch (a `--dispatch` mode on claim or a sibling dispatch verb — design call recorded here when made):

- Each claimed item goes to a DEDICATED sub-task session within the same operation: an opencode session launched+bound via the claimant machinery (reuse launch_one / the #8210 send-path launcher), or a Muse sub-session via the #8210 transfer mechanism.
- Each item carries: the dispatch reason (batch dispatch is the lane's stated mode, recorded once per batch on each item's lane_assigned/claim event), the lane's notes, and its worktree dir (worktrees only, one per item, never the main checkout, no two sub-tasks share a worktree).
- Platform limitation: if a task carries a recorded platform limitation + reason, batch pick/dispatch must respect it (never dispatch it to the limited-out platform); the batch machinery never creates a limitation without a reason.

### 3. Supervision + failure

- The dispatching lane verifies every item bound (session_id present) before its touch ends; the batch operation reports per-item outcomes (bound session id, or released-with-reason).
- Any item that fails to launch/bind returns to the pool immediately (release to queued / flip to direct for serial work by the lane) — never left claimed-idle.

### 4. Runbook

Lane instructions gain a dispatch mode: a lane MAY batch-claim up to the cap for part of a bundle, dispatch each item, supervise completions/heartbeats, and work serially itself whatever comes back. Serial single-session work stays the default mode; dispatch is an allowed stated mode, not a replacement.

### 5. Tests

- Broker: --count order preserved across the batch, partial batch, cap enforcement, per-item events/marks, recorded platform limitation respected by the pick.
- Dispatch: claimant-suite-style tests for launch+bind per item and failure-returns-to-pool.
- Full fleet-queue suite + claimant suites green.

## Live acceptance (receipts required)

- One real batch claim of ≥3 items; pick order across the batch matches priority/age.
- Each item bound to its own dedicated session (distinct session ids, distinct worktrees), verified from live queue state + the sessions themselves.
- One forced bind failure: the item returns to the pool immediately, not held.
- A platform-limited item (limitation + reason recorded) excluded from the wrong platform's batch; an unlimited item flows to either platform.

## Deploy

Like #8189: both broker binaries (~/.local/bin/fleet + libexec copy), old binary kept as .bak, queue-broker.service restart, health smoke test.

title: aggregator(aa-explorer): cached historical AA batches freeze the v_current_prices overlay — version switching silently switches token rates

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: app/aggregator
labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #7564 (the #3302 AA dataset-version switcher) caches one payload per ainventory
import batch. Each cached section carries the batch-bound measurements **and**
`prices` from `v_current_prices` plus the price-derived rates in `catalog`
(`aaSectionFromSupabase` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts`, ~lines 1127–1156).

`v_current_prices` is a current-price overlay, not a historical price snapshot — the
`/aa` page says so explicitly ("Token prices remain the current `v_current_prices`
overlay, not a historical price snapshot"). But once a payload is cached, that
snapshot of prices is frozen at build time. When token prices change and the collector
rebuilds only the latest batch, every previously cached historical batch keeps serving
its old `prices`/`catalog` rates. Switching dataset versions therefore also switches
token rates, while the page states they are a current overlay.

## Evidence

- Raised as Codex review finding 4 on PR #7564 (2026-11-08), acknowledged in
  https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7564#issuecomment-6777757505 and
  deliberately deferred out of that PR.
- Cache skip path: `scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts` skips a batch when
  `cacheMeta.get(row.importBatch)?.cached` is true, i.e. whenever the config
  fingerprint is unchanged — prices are not part of that key.
- The read path just returns `parsed.section` (`src/sources/live.ts`, historical
  branch), so the frozen prices are what render.

## Fix direction

Keep the batch-bound payload and the batch-independent overlay separate:

1. Cache only batch-bound data (`sources`, `rankings`, `thresholds`, `configs`,
   `testRuns`, `cai`, coverage) per batch.
2. Refresh `prices` from `v_current_prices` each tick (the collector already queries
   them for the latest payload) and re-derive the `catalog` rates on read/build for
   every served batch, latest and historical.
3. If a re-overlay is impossible (e.g. the price query failed), mark the section
   `stale` with a reason rather than silently showing old rates.

## Acceptance

- A test that builds two cached batches with differing `prices` payloads, refreshes
  prices once, and asserts both the latest and the historical section report the new
  rates.
- `/aa?batch=…` renders the same rates as `/aa` for the price overlay, with no change
  to the batch-bound figures.

title: feat(queue): Muse→opencode push — claim-by-id transfer verb (--from-session) + one-call send with notes and worktree
body:
# feat(queue): Muse→opencode push — claim-by-id transfer verb (--from-session) + one-call send with notes and worktree

Drew's orders, 2026-11-10 (verbatim):

> "can we make it so a muse session can send to 99encode and it automatically claims the item and takes any notes from the muse agent on what to do and the worktree dir is provided?" ("99encode" = opencode)

> "a verb to claim a specific task not just get the next one, possibly from a session so I can have opencode claim a task from muse sesid and that task is passed on without needing any stops"

Builds on #8187 (single-session by default; opencode routing only with a recorded reason; launch-on-handoff, PRs #8189/#8190). The claimant-never-launches history is #6533. The original by-id claim gap was #7735; PR #8066 (2026-11-09) added by-id claim for a queued row or a parked recorded handoff — what is missing is the **session-to-session transfer** case: a task currently CLAIMED by a Muse session passing directly to an opencode session, holder→claimer, in one operation.

## Part 1 — broker: claim-by-id transfer

Extend `claim` (claim_repo_task) with a transfer mode:

- New request fields: `from_session` (CLI `--from-session <ses_id>`) naming the session passing the task. With `task_id` + `from_session` present, the claim is a transfer, not a pick/by-id claim.
- The task passes holder→claimer in ONE conditional UPDATE: never through queued or parked, no release-and-reclaim gap, no intermediate state another lane can grab or a park can strand. Attempts are NOT incremented (a transfer is not a new attempt).
- The claim binds the claiming session in the same operation: `--session-id` on the transfer claim sets the bound session (progress.session_id + lane ledger session_id), the same marks a separate `bind` would record.
- The `claimed` audit event records the transfer: `transfer: true`, `by_id: true`, `from_session`, the new `session_id`, `previous_worker`, `previous_lane_id`, plus the standard #8187 marks (task, queue/pool, platform, lane, model).
- Guards:
  - Only the current holder can give a held task away: `from_session` must match a holder session mark on the task — the session recorded on the task's latest `claimed` event, the bound `progress.session_id`, or a `progress.from_session` the holder checkpointed. A random session cannot poach a claimed task by id.
  - Status must be `claimed` with a live lease. Terminal states refuse; genuine broker wait-parks (CI/dependency) stay excluded exactly as by-id claim excludes them today (a parked row is not a transfer source).
  - If the row is already bound to a different session than both parties, refuse.
  - A failed/refused transfer mutates nothing: the original claim is untouched (all checks run before the single conditional UPDATE, which re-checks status + holder worker).
- Callable from a session: the claimant machinery itself invokes it (worker `opencode-claimant`), with its session identity recorded like any claim.

Also in the broker: `lane` verb gap found while building this — an EXISTING direct ledger row cannot flip to opencode (`verb_lane`'s existing-row path only flips opencode→direct). A Muse lane that claimed a task (default direct ledger row) and then decides to send it has no way to record the opencode assignment. Add the symmetric flip: existing direct row + `--opencode-reason` + no bound session → opencode, reason recorded, `lane_assigned` event with `reassignment: true`. A session-bound row never flips, either direction.

## Part 2 — the one-call send (claimant tooling)

New `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/send_to_opencode.py`, reusing launch_one.py / claimant.py internals (no parallel launcher):

```
python3 -I send_to_opencode.py --queue <queue> --task <id> \
  --worker <sender worker> --from-session <muse ses id> \
  --reason "<stated pass-off reason>" \
  (--notes "<text>" | --notes-file <path>) \
  [--worktree <existing worktree dir>]
```

1. Refuses without a non-empty `--reason` (#8187: pass-off needs a stated reason; no reason → the sender works it direct) and without sender notes.
2. Verifies the sender currently holds the task's claim; refuses hard-stop labels (held / user/owned / do-not-merge / do-not-auto-edit) live via gh, like launch_one.
3. Records the opencode assignment WITH the reason (`repo-queue lane <task> --opencode-reason <reason>`).
4. Worktree: uses the sender-provided dir (validated as a real git worktree of the target repo — never the primary checkout itself), or creates one per existing convention (`~/.local/share/opencode/tmp/opencode/queue-<task>-...`, branch `queue/<task>-...`) when none is given. The sender's notes are also written into the worktree as a notes file.
5. Creates the opencode session IN that worktree through claimant.py's verified transport; verifies the session's location is the worktree; a mismatch deletes the session.
6. Transfers the claim with the Part 1 verb (`claim --task <id> --from-session <muse ses> --session-id <new ses> --worker opencode-claimant --platform openchamber`), binding the new session atomically. Verifies the returned row: worker is the claimant, bound session matches.
7. Checkpoints `launched` as the claimant, sends the execution prompt — launch_one's standard prompt PLUS a SENDER NOTES section carrying the Muse agent's notes verbatim and the worktree path — and posts the agent note on the issue/PR.
8. Failure semantics: any failure before the transfer completes deletes the created session and flips the assignment back to direct (`--exclusion-reason`), so the Muse sender keeps the item — never claimed-and-unlaunched. A session that bound but whose prompt failed stays bound (claimant.py's standing rule; supervision owns it) and the send reports that explicitly.

## Runbook

Update the lane runbook (§1b) and claimant prompt docs: the one-call send exists, when to use it (stated reason required; Muse lanes record their session id on claim with `--session-id` so they can pass tasks), and that a failed send means the sender keeps the item.

## Acceptance (live proof required)

- Broker + client tests: transfer happy path (marks + event fields, attempts unchanged), wrong `--from-session` refused with the original claim untouched, terminal/wait-park refusals, direct→opencode lane flip with reason, bound-row flip refusal. fleet-queue suite green; claimant suites green.
- One real queued task, held by a real Muse session claim (with `--session-id`), sent via the tool with real notes and a real worktree. Proof from live state: lane ledger row = opencode with the reason; the task's event history shows the direct transfer (claimed-by-Muse → transfer claimed event with from_session + bound session) with NO queued/parked event in between; the launched session's first prompt (read back from the server) contains the sender's notes and the worktree path; the session is working in that worktree.

title: fix(aggregator): PR #3992's null census rows are dropped by isRepoCensus — failed base counts (and their stale counts) never reach the coverage report

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Finding (from PR diff review)

PR #3992 (`feat(pm): report stale open issues per repository`, merged, commit 1134e4be7397041b019e1a65bc698903ad403858) changed the coverage collector so a repo whose base census fails is **no longer omitted** — it now always pushes a census row, with the failed counts as `null`:

- `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/collect-fleet-feed.ts` (PR #3992 diff): on base-census failure, `openIssues` / `gateNow` / `gateNext` stay `null` and the row is still pushed (`rows.push({ repo, openIssues, gateNow, gateNext, staleOpenIssues, … })`).
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/coverage.ts`: the `RepoCensus` type was widened to `openIssues: number | null` (same for `gateNow`/`gateNext`) — PR body: "Missing or failed counts remain unavailable rather than zero."

But the structural gate that feed rows must pass was **not** widened:

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/coverage.ts`, `isRepoCensus` (verified unchanged on current main, 2026-11-10): still requires `Number.isInteger(r.openIssues)`, `Number.isInteger(r.gateNow)`, `Number.isInteger(r.gateNext)`.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/feed.ts`: census rows are loaded with `raw.filter(isRepoCensus)` — so every null-count row is silently dropped.

## Why it matters

The exact partial-failure case PR #3992 set out to surface ("unavailable, not zero") never reaches `computeCoverage` or the coverage report:

1. A repo whose base census fails disappears from the report entirely instead of showing its counts as unavailable.
2. Worse, the stale-issue query runs **before** the base census in the collector loop, so a successfully collected `staleOpenIssues` count for that repo is discarded together with the row — the new >90-day stale count (the PR's headline feature) is lost precisely when a sibling query had a transient failure.
3. The PR's tests do not cover this: its `isRepoCensus` test row uses `openIssues: 100` (integer), and no test feeds a null-count row through the feed gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `isRepoCensus` accepts a census row whose `openIssues`/`gateNow`/`gateNext` are `null` (unavailable), while still rejecting negative, fractional, or gate-count-above-total rows when counts are present.
- [ ] A collector row with a failed base census but a successful stale count reaches `computeCoverage` and renders as unavailable base counts **with** its stale count and collection timestamp intact.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the null-count row through `isRepoCensus` and the feed reader, mirroring PR #3992's collector failure shape.
- [ ] Verify against current main before fixing (triage): if the gate was widened by a later PR, close this with that evidence instead.

title: fix(queue): parked-handoff stage source mismatch — broker reads progress.stage, claimant poll reads last_checkpoint.stage
body:
# fix(queue): parked-handoff stage source mismatch — broker reads progress.stage, claimant poll reads last_checkpoint.stage

Found during #8187 acceptance (2026-11-10T19:12Z), task 10995 (repo-health-code-pilot, issue #5538):

- Row state: status=parked, progress.lane='opencode', session_id null, progress.stage='awaiting_triage', progress.last_checkpoint.stage='handed_off' (at 2026-11-10T18:51:16Z).
- Broker: PARKED_HANDOFF_SQL (turso_queue.rs) computes stage as COALESCE(progress.stage, progress.last_checkpoint.stage) — top-level stage wins — so the row is NOT a parked handoff: by-id claim returns 'no claimable task', and the #8189 default-pick sink branch (same SQL) cannot serve it to a lane either.
- Claimant: poll.py normalize_row lifts stage from progress.last_checkpoint.stage (the #7706 fix), so the same row IS a launch candidate in the claimant's view.

The two components disagree about the same row's stage: the claimant can see work the broker will not release. Any row whose top-level progress.stage was overwritten after its handed_off checkpoint (e.g. by a later awaiting_triage park) is stranded in the gap.

Fix direction: one stage source of truth — make the broker's handoff predicate read the stage the same way poll.py does (last_checkpoint.stage preferred), or stop writing a divergent top-level progress.stage on park. Add a regression test with a row carrying stage='awaiting_triage' + last_checkpoint.stage='handed_off' proving by-id claim and the pick sink branch both take it.

Refs #8187, #7706.

title: fix(queue): parked opencode handoffs are re-served to lanes — task 14654 claimed 8x in one shift despite parks (#8184 residual)
body:
## Problem

The broker re-serves a parked, recorded opencode handoff to claiming lanes — the behavior #8184 (closed 2026-11-10T18:29Z) was meant to end ("the broker never serves a parked recorded handoff to a lane again; the claimant collects it through its own pick").

## Evidence — task 14654 (issue #8182), lane code-e shift 2026-11-10

- Task 14654 created 2026-11-10T18:37Z; lane row 6010 assigned `opencode`; `session_id` still null at 19:25Z — the claimant has never bound a session to it.
- Lane code-e claimed task 14654 **8 times in one shift** (18:54Z–19:25Z). Every handling followed the runbook handoff: checkpoint `handed_off` with the Rule 4 reason, then park.
- Parks did not exclude it: delays of 1200s and 3600s, with and without a fresh `{"kind":"time"}` ready-condition, were all followed by re-serve — the last ones **instantly**, ignoring `not_before` (e.g. park at ~19:04Z set `not_before` 20:04:02Z; the very next claim returned task 14654 again).
- Park records `wait_kind: "timer"` — the handoff park is not being classified as a handoff wait.
- What does work from #8184: attempts stayed 1/4 across all 8 cycles (no attempt burn on handoff cycles).
- Same shift, same pattern at lower frequency: tasks 5804 (issue #3404) and 5867 (issue #3904) were also re-served before their park `not_before` times; task 14654 is simply the deterministic case.

## Impact

Each lane shift burns its bundle slots re-handing the same handoff tasks instead of reaching other queued work (399 queued at shift start), and the claimant still never picks the task up — the underlying fix work (here, the power-guard release() fix for #8182) stalls while the queue looks busy.

## Suggested checks

1. Is the handoff classification keyed on something the park verb does not set (hence `wait_kind: "timer"`)? Compare a CI park (records `wait_kind: ci`) with a handoff park after a `handed_off` checkpoint.
2. Does claim eligibility actually filter parked handoff-sink tasks for lanes, or only for the claimant pick path?
3. Why has the claimant not bound task 14654 in ~50 minutes (lane row 6010, session_id null) — failed launches returning it to the sink would also explain the instant re-serves.

Filed by lane code-e (repo-queue-worker-shift-e) from live shift evidence; task 14654 checkpoints carry the per-cycle notes.

title: fix(queue): single-session by default — launch-on-handoff, lane works, inline triage (reverses #8097 Rule 3)
body:
# fix(queue): single-session by default — launch-on-handoff, lane works, inline triage (reverses #8097 Rule 3)

Drew's order, 2026-11-10 (verbatim): "handoff shouldn't be a pause, launch the session and then it immediate takes that item. fix lane should fix unless triage is needed and even if triage needed just handle it and run it. stop handing off over and over without reason. there should be issues that only need 1 session to resolve not this Rube Goldberg bullshit that's not needed unless there's a reason"

## What this reverses / builds on
- Reverses #8097 Rule 3 (triage separation): fix lanes no longer refuse untriaged items. A lane that claims an untriaged item triages it inline (kind/priority/effort labels, triage agent note, backlog entry) and does the fix in the SAME session.
- Supersedes the section 1b handoff chore (#3026 assignment): a handoff that parks and waits for the claimant poller is the defect. #6533 is the standing symptom (claimant never launches; executed_lane/session_id stay null across claim-handed_off-park cycles).
- Builds on #8184/#8185 (broker-owned waits): claim-time exclusion of parked handoffs, wait TTL floors, wake verb, +0-attempt handoff sink all stay. External waits (CI, real dependency gates) still use broker waits.

## Design
1. Single session by default. One session claims an item, triages inline if needed, fixes it, and runs it to a terminal state. Multi-session flow only with a stated reason: real external wait (#8184 broker waits), a platform/capability the session genuinely lacks, a hard stop (held/user-owned labels, user/escalated).
2. Lane works by default. Claim-time lane assignment no longer routes the bulk of tasks to opencode away from the claiming lane. The claiming Muse lane is the default executor; non-direct routing survives only under a narrow, explicit rule.
3. Handoff = immediate launch. Where an item is genuinely routed to another execution session, the handoff triggers that session's launch and the handing-off lane verifies a bound session exists before ending its touch. If launch fails or nothing binds in a short bounded wait, the assignment falls back to direct and the SAME lane works the item. No code path ends in "handed off and parked, nobody launched".
4. Inline triage. Runbook section 1c rewritten: lanes triage claimed untriaged items inline and proceed; a triage-kind packet completes as triaged only when its fix genuinely belongs to a separate follow-on task. The awaiting_triage lane park path is removed (broker triage wait remains for not-yet-claimed feeder tickets).
5. Triage-step job is retired or narrowed to pre-queue sweeping of feeder-filed GitHub tickets that have no queue task yet.

## Acceptance
- One real untriaged queued item: a single lane session triages it inline and carries it to a terminal fix state (or stated-reason block); task event history shows one session.
- One real opencode-routed item: worked direct by the claiming lane, OR claimant session bound and running before the lane's touch ends (bound session id as evidence). No parked-handoff terminal state.
- Broker/claimant regression tests pass; fleet-queue suite stays green.
- A subsequent ordinary lane shift shows zero awaiting_triage parks and zero unlaunched handoffs.

title: feat(queue): triage step wakes broker-held triage waits on completion (#8184 follow-up)
body:
Follow-up to #8184 (broker-owned waits, PR #8185, deployed 2026-11-10).

The broker now holds awaiting-triage parks as `wait_kind = triage` with a 6h TTL floor, and releases them instantly via `fleet queue wake <task_id>`. The floor is only the backstop: the fast path needs the **triage step** to wake each item it finishes triaging.

## Ask

In the triage-step job's instructions/tooling: after an item's triage completes (fix packet emitted, `status/needs-triage` removed), call:

```bash
fleet queue wake <TASK_ID> --worker <triage-step worker id> --reason "triaged: <packet note ref>"
```

for the queue task that carried the item (the fix-kind or triage-kind packet parked with progress stage `awaiting_triage`). If the task id is not at hand, the parked row is findable via `fleet queue list` filtered to parked + the issue number.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Triage-step instructions name the wake call as the completion step for broker-held items.
- [ ] One live verification: an item parked as a triage wait returns to `queued` within a minute of its triage completing, without waiting out the 6h floor.
- [ ] If the triage step cannot know the task id in some path, note the path here instead of guessing.

body:
## Finding (unaddressed PR review comment)

On PR #8025 (`fix(power-guard): detect dead systemd-inhibit child, re-engage loudly`, for issue #6534), CodeRabbit raised a stability finding that was never fixed or replied to:

> **Keep sampling while a stalled child is reaped.** If `systemd-inhibit` does not exit promptly, `release()` can block the loop for about 10 seconds. This delays the next sample or the confirmed sleep command. Handle stalled reaping without blocking sampling, and confirm inhibitor release before issuing sleep.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025#discussion_r4511572429 (comment id 4511572429)
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-09T10:10:56Z
- Location: `nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`, `Inhibitor._reap()` / `release()` (lines 153–175 at PR head)

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-10) and has no replies — the CodeRabbit comment is the only comment in the thread.
- PR #8025's head is unchanged since the comment: the only commit is `2a6abfda8194eb944894b5fc647778f82aa977f5` (2026-11-09T10:04:21Z, before the comment). No fix commit followed.
- The PR is still open and the comment is more than 24 hours old, so the open-PR grace rule is expired.
- No existing issue covers this (searched open/recently-closed issues for power-guard / inhibitor / release on 2026-11-10; issue #6534 covers dead-child detection, not reap blocking).

## Still-live evidence (PR head `2a6abfda81`, read 2026-11-10)

`nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`:

- `_reap()` (lines 153–175) waits synchronously: `proc.wait(timeout=5)`, and on timeout escalates to `kill()` and waits another 5 seconds — up to ~10 seconds of blocking in the caller.
- `release()` calls `_reap()` synchronously (line 253), and `main()` calls `release()` inline in the sampling loop — both on the recovery path (line 292) and, critically, on the confirmed-sleep path (lines 310–312), where the sleep command is only issued after `release()` returns. A stalled child therefore delays an already-confirmed emergency sleep by up to ~10 seconds on a critical battery, and delays every other sample while reaping.

Note the interaction with the companion finding from the same review (release forgetting a still-running child): the fix must keep sampling/reaping from blocking the loop **without** dropping the requirement that inhibitor release is confirmed before the sleep command is issued.

## Acceptance criteria

- Reaping a stalled `systemd-inhibit` child no longer blocks the sampling loop for the full double-wait; sampling continues while reaping is pending, **and** the confirmed-sleep path still does not issue the sleep command until inhibitor release is confirmed; **or** the current behavior is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.
- The existing timeout and kill-escalation safeguards are preserved.
- Regression coverage: a fake child that ignores terminate/kill exercises the non-blocking reap path in `test_power_guard.py`.

title: pm-git-sync: projector redeploy restarts without ensuring node_modules — catch-up pull crash-looped pm-projector on missing @libsql/client

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
Found 2026-11-10 during the pm-git-sync repair (see #8170). When the sync finally pulled 436 commits and restarted pm-projector.service, the projector crash-looped:

    error: Cannot find module @libsql/client from /home/user/git/code/pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts

Cause: the checkout had NO pm-stack/projector/node_modules at all, and the sync only runs the projector dependency step (scripts/setup-deps.sh) when pm-stack/projector/package.json changed in the pulled range. It had not changed, so the restart went ahead with deps absent. Same shape exists for the aggregator: bun install only runs when its package.json/bun.lock changed.

Manual recovery done at the time: ran setup-deps.sh (exit 0), then moved the generated node_modules OUT of the tree (to ~/git/code-dirt-rescue-2026-11-10/projector-node_modules-generated-2026-11-10/) because an untracked node_modules in the primary clone makes the sync fail its own clean-tree check — the two designs currently fight each other, which is presumably how the deps went missing in the first place.

Fix direction: before restarting a PM service, ensure its dependency tree exists (run the dep step when node_modules is missing, not only when inputs changed); and decide where generated deps live so the sync clean-tree check tolerates them (gitignore the node_modules paths, or provision deps outside the checkout). Acceptance: from a checkout with projector node_modules deleted, one sync run leaves pm-projector active and the tree still passes the sync clean check.

# Quota refresh: newestMeasurement counts the terminal "lapsed" state against its own contract (PR #7898 review finding)

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7898 (fix(quota-plane): lapsed OpenCode Go workspace renders as lapsed, not error (#1161)), Copilot review comment [4508796654](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7898#discussion_r4508796654) (Copilot, 2026-11-09T01:59:26Z, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-refresh.ts:36`):

> The docstring says "Newest non-error provider/pool measurement", but the helper now treats `"lapsed"` as eligible (i.e., it's not filtered like `"error"`). Since `"lapsed"` is a terminal non-measurement state (windows cleared), counting it as a "measurement" could be misleading for consumers of `newestMeasurement` (e.g., if it's used to decide whether the view is stale and should auto-refresh). Recommendation: either (a) explicitly exclude `"lapsed"` here, or (b) update the function comment (and any related naming/usage) to reflect that terminal states can advance the "newest" timestamp.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-10 by this run: the thread containing comment 4508796654 has `isResolved: false`).
- PR #7898 head is unchanged at `e572e55ce340e79f4d49cad0f4aebd7fea55dc7d` since the comment (last commit 2026-11-09T01:54:23Z, before the comment); no fix commit followed it. The finding is past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs (comment 2026-11-09T01:59:26Z).
- Issue search (open and closed) by PR number, file path, and keywords (`newestMeasurement lapsed`, `lapsed quota-refresh`, `7898`) found no existing issue covering this finding.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw read at head `e572e55ce3` agrees:
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-refresh.ts:32`: docstring "Newest non-error provider/pool measurement in the view".
- Lines 35-36: the `add()` helper's state type includes `"lapsed"` and it returns early only for `"error"` — a lapsed pool/credential/provider timestamp therefore advances the newest-measurement value.
- `isQuotaStale()` (same file) decides staleness/auto-refresh off `newestMeasurement()`, so a terminal lapse timestamp can make a view with no fresh measurements read as not stale.

## Acceptance criteria
- Either `newestMeasurement()` explicitly excludes the `"lapsed"` state, or the docstring/naming is updated to state that terminal states advance the newest timestamp AND that choice is pinned by a test — so the helper's contract and `isQuotaStale()`'s refresh decision are unambiguous.

title: Queue/lane design rules: no by-id blocking by default, optional platform selector, triage separate from fixes

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

body:
Drew's design rules for the queue/lane machinery, dictated 2026-11-09 20:22 CST after tonight's by-id claim fixes and lane-UUID registrations. These govern how lanes, the broker/claimant, and queue items are shaped.

## Rule 1 — No blocking by ID by default
Lanes must not need to block or claim by task ID in the regular queue flow. ID-targeted claims stay available for specific cases (e.g., reviving one specific parked handoff, as done tonight for task 11214), but they are the exception tool, never the default mechanism a lane depends on to get work.

## Rule 2 — No platform required; coarse selector allowed
A work item must not need a platform set on it. Provide an optional coarse selector — "use OpenChamber" or "use Muse" — that constrains which family may take the item without naming a specific lane. Default (no selector): either family's lanes may take it.

## Rule 3 — Triage is a separate step from fix work
Muse lanes work their own fixes. Triage is its own task/step, not something mixed ad hoc into fix work: a lane picking up a batch of tickets (Drew's example: 5) triages the ones that need triage as that separate step, and works fixes for the ones already triaged. (Batch size read as illustrative pending Drew's confirmation.)

## Acceptance
- The claimant/broker default flow demonstrably claims and launches regular queue work with no ID-targeted claims involved.
- The queue item schema shows platform/selector optional, with the two coarse values working end-to-end.
- Lane/sweep definitions show triage as a distinct step from fix work in the Muse lanes' flow.

# World actor: replication oversized-entry journal scan is awaited inside handle, suspending all command processing

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7890 (fix(id): recover legacy oversized checkpoints during replication), Codex review comment [4508585836](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7890#discussion_r4508585836) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-09T01:04:14Z, `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:2048`):

> Scan the journal without suspending the world actor. For any journal larger than 256 KiB, every replication connection now waits for a full journal scan inside `WorldActor::handle`. Although `spawn_blocking` moves the I/O off the executor thread, `WorldActor::run` serially awaits `handle`, so the world cannot process other commands, ticks, or schedules until the scan finishes. This also affects healthy journals with no oversized entries, and journals for programs that cannot snapshot can grow without bound. Previously, the initial journal read happened in `serve_stream` after the actor resumed. Move the probe outside the actor's command-processing wait, retaining a serialized actor operation for any required compaction.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-10: the single thread containing comment 4508585836 has `isResolved: false`).
- PR #7890 head is unchanged at `820f22c9b1ce1e790b2d30a211fa1170f98e5041` since the comment; no fix commit followed it. The finding is past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs (comment 2026-11-09T01:04:14Z; grace expired 2026-11-10T01:04:14Z).
- Issue search (open and closed) by PR number, file path, and keywords found no existing issue covering this finding.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw read at head `820f22c9b1` agrees:
- `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:2038-2049` (in `WorldCommand::ReplicationFeed` handling inside `handle`): when `snapshot_source.byte_len > MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES` (256 KiB), the actor awaits `tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || probe.first_oversized_entry())` inline before replying — so the serial command loop waits for the full journal scan on every replication connection, including for healthy journals with no oversized entries.

## Acceptance criteria
- The oversized-entry probe/scan no longer blocks the world actor's serial command processing (e.g. the probe runs outside the actor's command-processing wait, as the pre-change `serve_stream` placement did), while any required compaction remains a serialized actor operation.
- A test or documented measurement shows other commands/ticks continue to be processed while a >256 KiB journal scan is in flight.
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

title: fix(pm-dispatch): validate GitHub API response shapes at the boundary (#7101)
body:
Closes #7101. Queue task 12768 (lane code-w).

## Problem
`pm-stack/dispatch/src/github.ts` shape-trusted every GitHub API response body via bare casts: installation `{}` minted against `/app/installations/undefined/access_tokens`, token `{}` was sent as `Bearer undefined`, create `{}` returned a phantom `{number: undefined, url: undefined}` as success, lookup `{}` fabricated an issue state (rejected by #3007 attach verification as "is undefined, not open"), and null bodies escaped as raw TypeErrors — the create one then duplicated the tracking issue via the gh fallback.

## Fix
- All four `res.json()` bodies (installation lookup, access-token mint, issue create, issue lookup — app route and the gh-route parse in `getIssue`) are validated before use: JSON object body; installation `id` a positive integer; `token` a non-empty string with a parseable `expires_at`; create/lookup `number` an integer, `state`/`html_url` strings.
- Violations raise `GitHubError` (new `MalformedBodyError` subclass) naming the endpoint and the malformed field — never a raw TypeError/SyntaxError, never a coerced/undefined value.
- A malformed 2xx **create** body does NOT trigger the gh fallback create (the issue may already exist server-side); it surfaces as an explicit error. Malformed installation/token replies still fall back to gh with the malformed-body reason preserved in the combined error.
- No behavior change for well-formed responses or definitive HTTP failures (404 lookup still returns null).

## Tests (oracle: the #7101 acceptance)
New `pm-stack/dispatch/test/github.test.ts`, stubbed fetch in the `attach_verify.test.ts` style; the repo slug is a nonexistent one so the gh fallback fails deterministically and can never create a real issue in any environment.
- Post-fix: **12/12 pass**; full dispatch suite **169/169 pass**.
- Pre-fix (src change stashed): **9 fail** — the new tests are real regressions.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` in the bare worktree fails identically on the unpatched tree (missing `bun` type definitions; no node_modules in the worktree) — pre-existing environment gap, not this change.

Incident note: an early test draft's fake-gh PATH shim was not honored by `Bun.spawn`, so the real gh fallback created ten fixture issues (#8075–#8084, title "t"); all ten were closed as not planned with an explanation in the same shift, and the test was redesigned (nonexistent slug) so this cannot recur.

## Symptom

2026-11-09 evening: the fleet went to zero active sessions. Fleet-minder census: 60 live sessions failed on quota — 30× Mistral Vibe 402 (budget exhausted), 29× CommandCode 429 (weekly limit, resets Tue 2026-11-10T06:52:52Z). Two minder failover-prompt kicks went ACTIVE, then re-failed in ~90 s on the same walled head. Workhorse route decisions returned `no-candidates` ~2,500 times in 2 h.

## Diagnosis (verified on the wire, 2026-11-10T00:15–00:50Z)

This was **not** the cured #7991 auth wall (zero auth errors). Every member of the workhorse route is genuinely at its plan limit at the same time — each verified from the provider's own error and the fresh quota record (generatedAt 2026-11-10T00:15:01Z):

- Flash pool: OpenCode Go 429 "Go usage limit exceeded", retry-after ≈ 6 d (weekly → Nov 16); ClinePass quota-gated → Nov 13; OpenDesign quota-gated → Nov 14; CommandCode weekly → Nov 10 06:52Z (retry-after honored by its bench); Mistral Vibe 402 budget exhausted.
- Luna: openai.main weekly 100% → Nov 13; openai.alternate 5h 100% → 04:26Z.
- Spark (Meta): 429 "Subscription quota exhausted", retry-after 518610 s → Nov 16.
- Antigravity Gemini: 429 "Individual quota reached", weekly 100% → Nov 13 23:43Z.

The minder's named "candidates with headroom" audited:

- `_claude` — NOT a candidate. Its quota read is a stale 2026-11-07 snapshot (the heartbeat errors); the credential is blanked and its leaves sit on auth benches. The "7d 61%" figure is frozen data.
- Antigravity **Claude** — REAL headroom (per-model weekly 63%, 5h 14%, live successes all evening) but seated only in the deliberate tiers — **not in workhorse**. That gap is the routing defect: when every pooled leg walled together, workhorse had no relief leg outside the exhausted pools, so correct `no-candidates` decisions stalled the fleet.

## Fix landed

- Config: `_antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5#high` seated as the fourth member of `workhorse-weighted` (direct leaf, weight 10 — the pattern of the Gemini leaf Drew seated in this stage 2026-11-07; Drew's 2026-10-31 Antigravity removal was from the primary path, over Gemini-bucket burn).
- PR #8073 merged: `5ba883519395606e1888e36638498ad4298051f4`.
- Live: same edit applied to the running config; standing server restarted under `opencode.service` (old detached pid 3423803 → unit pid 1681035, build 2.0.30+07b0352).

## Live proof

In the window 2026-11-10T00:40:02–00:40:22Z, real fleet sessions (quota-gatherer guardian, a queue-lane session, the fleet conductor, +3 more) drew the new leg: route_decision records show `workhorse-weighted` → `_antigravity/claude-sonnet-5-5` (drawn, then sticky), with **30 successful attempts** and real output tokens (488–1,411 per traced session). Three fresh hand-launched proof sessions afterwards correctly received `no-candidates` — with the new leaf present in the candidate set and excluded by the same credential-cooldown as every other leg (see below).

## The remaining state: total plan exhaustion (not a routing defect)

At 00:40:20Z the Antigravity Claude bucket also hit "Individual quota reached" (429) — the post-restart step burst burned its remaining headroom in ~20 s. Since 00:40:23Z there have been **zero successful attempts on any route or provider** in the fleet. Every pool is at 100% simultaneously (the pools-run-to-100% doctrine + a day of pent-up demand released by the #7991 cure and the claimant fix).

Reopening schedule (UTC): openai.alternate 5h → **Nov 10 04:26Z** (weekly 32%, first real capacity); CommandCode → **Nov 10 06:52Z**; ClinePass + Luna main → Nov 13; Antigravity aggregate → Nov 13 23:43Z; OpenDesign → Nov 14; Go + Spark → Nov 16; Vibe → Dec 1.

## Follow-ups

1. Verify fleet recovery at the 04:26Z and 06:52Z resets (sessions should land via openai-plan/Luna-alternate, then the Flash pool's CommandCode leg).
2. The in-flight generation switch carries fork PR #2216 (`failureCapMs` 120 s cap on ordinary-failure benches); the running build predates it — the ~24 h benches seen tonight are quota benches (by design), but ordinary-failure exiles shorten once it deploys.

body:
## Problem

`demotedPairs()` in `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:339` is the route proxy's only leg-health gate (`applyDemotion(candidates, demotedPairs())` at line 936). It demotes a `(provider, model)` pair after ≥3 failures in 4 hours **only when the failure carries quota detail or `error_tag = 'RateLimit'`** — the SQL filter at line 347 is literally:

```sql
AND (quota IS NOT NULL OR error_tag = 'RateLimit')
```

A leg failing **every** attempt with `provider.auth` is therefore never demoted, never excluded and never reordered: it stays first-choice for new sessions and is handed out indefinitely. Today that leg is `openai.main/gpt-6-luna`.

## Evidence (2026-11-09, laptop `route_usage`, window 09:18Z–12:18Z)

| leaf | requests | failed | tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `openai.main/gpt-6-luna` | 3070 | **3070 (100%)** | 0 |
| `openai.alternate/gpt-6-luna` | 4 | 4 (100%) | 0 |
| `_muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | 3389 | 1589 (47%) | 95.3M |
| `opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 1021 | 93 (9%) | 39.0M |
| `opencode-go.popesdrew/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 283 | 31 (11%) | 10.4M |

Pool accounting from the same readout: `workhorse-weighted` **offered** `openai-plan/gpt-6-luna` **4706 times** and **chose it 3074**, while the healthy leaves above sat in the same pool and served normally. 234 sessions carried at least one of those 3070 failures.

Session-level consequence (OpenChamber attention feed): the entire **06:00, 06:20 and 06:30 CST waves** died at message 3 with the verbatim error `Provided authentication token is expired. Please try signing in again.` — including the fleet conductor, the main-CI fix trigger, the quota gatherer guardian, the builder's advocate and 8+ code lanes. That is ~40% of new workhorse sessions lost for the day, and the work each of them had claimed evaporated with them.

## Why this is not #3325 and not #5558

- **#3325** (and its parked fix task 8932 / open PR #5558) is about a session **falling through** to a live leg after a pre-content stream error. Necessary, but orthogonal: with perfect fall-through the dead leg is still first-choice for every new session and every session still burns its first attempt on it.
- **#5295** (closed) added the *quota-only* known-exhausted seating gate — same doctrine, same blind spot.
- This issue is the **demotion predicate** itself: a leg that fails 100% of attempts for any non-quota reason is not treated as unhealthy, so `route_usage`' offered-count for a dead leaf grows without bound.

Distinct code site (`demotedPairs()` filter), distinct acceptance (below).

## Acceptance criteria

- A `(provider, model)` pair with a **100% failure run** (≥ threshold attempts, zero successes) inside the demotion window is demoted/excluded from candidacy **regardless of error class** — at minimum for `provider.auth` — until it records one success. Verified in `route_usage`: the dead leaf's *offered* count stops growing while it is failing (today it was 4706 in 3h).
- Existing quota/`RateLimit` demotion behaviour is unchanged; its tests still pass.
- A session whose first attempt lands on an auth-failing leg completes a turn on a fallback leg instead of terminating at message 3 (transcript or `route_attempt` ledger evidence).

## Out of scope

- Re-signing-in / refreshing the provider credential itself — that is #7991 and is Drew's action.
- Pool weights, burn order or model choices for healthy leaves; any paid-route or PAYG switch.

## Pointers

- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:338-347` (`demotedPairs`), `:936` (call site)
- `bin/opencode-route-proxy.test.mjs` (existing demotion tests to extend)
- Triage of #3325, task 14387, lane code-f — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3325#issuecomment-6739954243
- Recurrence evidence on #3325 (auth leg, three waves lost) — https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/3325#issuecomment-6739882519

## Finding

PR #3837 added the `openai.alternate` quota pool so the alternate ChatGPT account (popesdrew) is never merged into the main account's pool. Its dated-read extractor is explicitly built for a future `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` section in the stewardship quota view. But the main pool's heading pattern also matches that future heading, so the moment such a section is added — if it appears before the main `### ChatGPT` section, which is the natural order if sections are ever alphabetised or the main section is renamed — the main pool silently reads the alternate account's windows. That is exactly the cross-account misattribution #3837 set out to prevent.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3837 (https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3837), commits `e69a41121`, `f90ab84d7`; merged 2026-11-01T17:00:07Z.
- Current main `a7404a879c60f942359314a45d612c398379528f`, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts`:
  - `:557` — main pool (`openai.main`) spec: `heading: /^### ChatGPT/` — unanchored, so it matches `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` as well as `### ChatGPT`. (Compare `:549`, Claude's anchored `/^### Claude$/`.)
  - `:565` — alternate pool spec: `heading: /^### ChatGPT \(Alternate\)/`.
  - `:203` — `sectionOf(doc, pattern)` returns the FIRST section whose heading matches the pattern.
  - `:256` — `extractChatGptAlternate`, whose comment states it "exists so a future `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` section is picked up".
- Probe (verbatim `quota-extract.ts` from current main; only the type-only/`poolState`/`parseIsoDate` imports stubbed), run twice with identical results — probe files: `hidden_files/pr-review-b-evidence/code-3837-heading-probe/` in the goal workspace:
  - View with the Alternate section first (`7-day 42% used`) and the main section second (`7-day 11% used`): `openai.main` windows = `[{7-day, 42}]` — the alternate account's read on the main pool. `openai.alternate` correctly = `[{5-hour, 33}, {7-day, 42}]`.
  - Control, main section first: `openai.main` = `[{7-day, 11}]`, `openai.alternate` correct. So the misattribution is purely heading-order dependent.
- The tests added by #3837 (`pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts`, `quota-current.test.ts`) cover the alternate pool only in the no-dated-section case (shell + gatherer overlay); no test exercises a quota view that actually contains a `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` section, in either order.

Not a duplicate of #1626 (closed; OpenCode Go reset pairing by section position) or #7813 (open; page substituting fallback windows for a fresh read) — different mechanism.

## Why it matters

/quota is the fleet's pool-attribution surface: routing and burn decisions are made from these windows, and the two ChatGPT accounts have separate allowances. A dated Alternate section is the documented next step for this pool; adding it in the wrong order would silently swap the main pool's displayed usage to the other account's, with no error anywhere.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The main ChatGPT pool's heading pattern can no longer match the `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` heading (e.g. anchored/negative match, or section selection that excludes the alternate heading).
- [ ] A regression test feeds `extractQuotaPools` a quota view containing BOTH a `### ChatGPT` section and a `### ChatGPT (Alternate)` section, in both orders, and asserts each pool carries only its own windows.
- [ ] Existing quota tests still pass (`bun test` for `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts` and `quota-current.test.ts`).

title: id(world): device.info can never succeed in production — no spawn path supplies a DeviceManifest, so every real request is refused unknown_cap

body:
# id(world): device.info can never succeed in production — no spawn path supplies a DeviceManifest, so every real request is refused unknown_cap

## Summary

`device.info` (#2338, implemented in PR #7941, merged 2026-11-09 as
commit 8fb21e4b55) is registered in the provider catalog with
`DefaultCeiling::Included` and is served by the world actor from a cached
`device_manifest` field — but **no production code path can ever populate
that field**. The only `WorldActor` construction outside tests,
`WorldHandle::spawn_inner`, hardcodes `device_manifest: None`, and none of
the public spawn entry points (`spawn`, `spawn_with_program`,
`spawn_durable`, `spawn_read_only`) accepts a manifest. The field is
`pub(crate)` and is only ever assigned `Some(...)` inside the actor's own
unit tests, by direct field mutation. The result: in every deployed
world, a granted `device.info` request is refused with `unknown_cap` —
the exact refusal meant for "the host cannot describe itself" — even
though the host was never given a way to describe itself. The feature
shipped dead: its tests pass because they bypass the only construction
path real callers have.

## Evidence (verified on main @ aa01b61853, 2026-11-09)

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:459` — `device.info` is in
  the provider registry (v1, Request kind, Join scope,
  `DefaultCeiling::Included`), with `DeviceManifest::from_json` /
  `requested_version` validation in the same file.
- `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:885` — dispatch: `"device.info" =>
  self.execute_device_info(&request.args)`; `actor.rs:912-917` —
  `execute_device_info` validates the requested version, then
  `let Some(manifest) = &self.device_manifest else { return
  Err(CapError::unknown()) }`.
- `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:360` — the field:
  `pub(crate) device_manifest: Option<DeviceManifest>`, documented as
  "enumerated once by the adapter boundary and cached here".
- `pkgs/id/src/world/handle.rs:75-131` — `spawn_inner` is the sole
  production constructor (both `spawn_durable` at :47 and
  `spawn_read_only` at :66 funnel into it, and `spawn` /
  `spawn_with_program` chain through `spawn_durable`); it hardcodes
  `device_manifest: None` at :131 and its signature
  `(core, program, journal, read_only, presence)` has no manifest
  parameter.
- Exhaustive check (`git grep` on origin/main aa01b61853): only two
  `WorldActor { ... }` literals exist in `pkgs/id` — `handle.rs:108`
  (production, `None`) and `actor.rs` `for_test` (:2477, also `None`).
  The only `device_manifest = Some(...)` assignments in the tree are
  `actor.rs:2393` and `actor.rs:2409`, inside `device_info_tests`.
  Production callers (`commands/serve.rs:900`, `web/home.rs:313`,
  `web/routes.rs`, `web/world_ws.rs`, `sandbox.rs`, `replica.rs`) all go
  through the manifest-less spawn functions.
- #2338's own scope required "Per-device caching by the adapter; a
  program must never be able to make the device re-enumerate for free" —
  no adapter-side supply exists anywhere in the tree to cache from.

## Why it matters

`device.info` is the root of the capability-adaptation model (#2027
taxonomy §3.1): every other interface capability is conditional on a
program being able to ask what device it is rendering on. As shipped, a
program that follows the documented example in the `world_caps` module
header gets `unknown_cap` on every host, forever — indistinguishable
from a host that genuinely cannot describe itself, so programs will
code against a refusal that is actually a missing wire. The gap is
invisible to the test suite because the tests construct the actor
in-crate and set the field directly, a path no real caller can take.
Until a spawn path accepts a manifest, the catalog entry, the manifest
types, and the version negotiation are unreachable code.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A public spawn path (e.g. a `spawn_*` variant or builder on
  `WorldHandle`) accepts an `Option<DeviceManifest>` (validated via
  `DeviceManifest::from_json` where it crosses a wire boundary) and
  threads it through `spawn_inner` into the actor, replacing the
  hardcoded `None`.
- [ ] At least one production caller supplies a real manifest for its
  host (e.g. the web/serve host describing itself), so `device.info`
  returns that manifest end-to-end in a served world — not only in
  actor unit tests.
- [ ] A test drives `device.info` through the public `WorldHandle`
  spawn path (not direct field mutation) and asserts the supplied
  manifest comes back in the result event; the existing
  unknown-cap-when-`None` and unsupported-version tests stay green.
- [ ] No-enumeration-per-request is preserved: the manifest is supplied
  once at spawn, and repeated `device.info` requests serve the cached
  copy.

body:
## Finding

Merged PR #3855 capped the board's Done strip at 100 rendered cards and added a `?done=all` escape hatch — but it wired `showAllDone` only into the full-page `/board` route. The board page's own live-refresh fragment, `/frag/board`, still renders the capped strip unconditionally and cannot receive the flag, so a fragment refresh silently reverts a "show all" view back to 100 cards.

## Evidence

- PR #3855 (merged 2026-11-01T17:06:51Z, merge commit 3c3c585c07be, head 829e2053bba2): `renderBoardBody`/`renderBoard` gained `renderOpts?: { showAllDone?: boolean }`, and `src/server.ts` passes it only in the `/board` handler (`url.searchParams.get("done") === "all"`). The `/frag/board` handler appears in the same diff hunk as unchanged context — it was not updated.
- Verified on current main this run (2026-11-08, main dedfa6f54c76): `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts` `/frag/board` handler (line ~1450) calls `renderBoardBody(board, items, counts, act)` with no render options, and its wrapper hard-codes the refresh URLs with no query string: `data-on-load="@get('/frag/board')" data-on-dashrefresh__window="@get('/frag/board')"`.
- The full-page route on current main (line ~1423) does pass `showAllDone: url.searchParams.get("done") === "all"`, and `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts` (lines ~1470, ~1500-1509) only renders the full strip when that flag is set.
- Dashboard actions dispatch a `dashrefresh` window event (see `__dashAfter` in `render.ts`, added context in PR #3842's diff), so any dashboard action taken while viewing `/board?done=all` triggers the fragment swap and loses the show-all state — the strip's summary flips back to "showing the 100 most recent" with no user action asking for that.

## Why it matters

The `?done=all` view is the only way to see the full Done record on the board (the PR's stated purpose for the link). As shipped, that view is unstable: the page's own refresh machinery undoes it. Low severity — no data loss, the full-page link still works until the next refresh — but it is a real, reproducible inconsistency introduced by the PR that added the feature.

## Acceptance criteria

- Viewing `/board?done=all` and triggering a dashboard refresh (or any `dashrefresh`) keeps the full Done strip rendered (fragment route carries/forwards the `done=all` state, or the fragment wrapper preserves the current query).
- The capped default is unchanged: `/board` and `/frag/board` with no `done` parameter still render at most 100 done cards with the "show all N" link.
- A regression test in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/author-picker-1179.test.ts` (or a sibling) pins the fragment path's show-all behavior alongside the existing full-page tests from PR #3855.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #3855 in its 2026-11-08 21:24 CST batch (PRs #3839–#3865). Deduped this run: issue searches for `showAllDone` and "done strip" returned only PR #3855 itself.

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Defect

`gh-post`'s App route (leg 2 of the rate-limit ladder, #6129) could never
create an issue whose title contains a space — which is effectively every
real title. The failure was silent: gh-post fell through to the outbox leg,
so posts still landed, just never via the App.

## Root cause

In `~/tools/gh-post` (hatch-personal), `laptop_paperwork()` shipped the
fleet-paperwork arguments to the laptop by joining them into one shell
string with no quoting:

```python
r = run([LAPTOP_SSH, "python3 " + PAPERWORK + " " + " ".join(remote_args)])
```

The laptop shell split the title on spaces: fleet-paperwork's argparse
received the title's first word as `--title` and the remaining words as
positional arguments, and died with:

```
fleet-paperwork: error: unrecognized arguments: event-driven trigger from fleet into Muse ho…
```

The comment leg was unaffected in practice (all its arguments are single
tokens: subcommand, repo, issue number, a `/tmp` path). The create leg's
`--title` was the only multi-word argument in the system.

## Evidence

2026-11-08, filing two design issues via gh-post: both user-route attempts
hit the secondary rate limit, both App-route attempts failed with the
argparse error above, both issues queued in the action outbox instead
(OB-2026-11-09-115, OB-2026-11-09-116).

## Fix — already applied locally (2026-11-08)

`laptop_paperwork()` now quotes each argument:

```python
r = run([LAPTOP_SSH, "python3 " + PAPERWORK + " " + " ".join(shlex.quote(a) for a in remote_args)])
```

Verified on the laptop two ways with a multi-word title: an argparse
`--help` pass parses cleanly, and a `create --dry-run` passes the title
intact and proceeds to the installation lookup — where it now fails only
on the separate, already-filed #7930 (installations pagination), not on
parsing.

## What this issue tracks

- The defect record (the fix lives in hatch-personal's `~/tools/gh-post`,
  committed there; this repo owns fleet-paperwork and the #6129 design).
- Hardening worth doing: a regression check for gh-post's App leg using a
  spaced title, and/or replacing the shell-string transport with an argv
  transport so quoting bugs of this class cannot recur.

body:
# id(world): parse_wants accepts a non-object `args` — a scalar/array args collapses to no arguments, silently widening records.read to every record

## Summary

A capability request in a `wants` document declares its arguments as a JSON
object (or `null`/absent). `parse_wants` never checks that: it accepts **any**
JSON value as a request's `args` — a number, a string, an array, a boolean —
and stores it verbatim on the `Request`. Every downstream handler reads its
fields with `args.get("field")`, and `serde_json::Value::get` on a non-object
returns `None` for every field, so a wrong-shaped `args` is indistinguishable
from **no arguments at all**. For `records.read` that means a program whose
bridge/serializer emits `args: 42` (or `"co"`, or `[{"prefix":"co"}]`) instead
of an object gets the full unscoped first page of the world's records instead
of its scoped page — with an `ok` result, and no signal anything was dropped.

## Evidence (verified on main @ 13eb408fe5)

`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs`:

- The `Request` struct documents the contract: `/// Arguments (a JSON object,
  or null)` (line ~656).
- `parse_wants` (lines ~801–805) takes the entry's `args` as
  `entry.get("args").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null)` and checks only its
  serialized size against `MAX_ARGS_BYTES`. It validates the entry's `id` and
  `cap` as strings, the `subscribe`/`requests` lists as arrays, and rejects
  duplicate keys (#7621) — but never checks that `args` is an object or null.
- Every provider manifest with arguments declares
  `ArgumentSchema::JsonObject(&[...])` (e.g. `RECORDS_READ_ARGUMENTS`,
  lines ~264–276): the schema is a *fields-of-an-object* schema.

`pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs`:

- Handlers read fields off `request.args` (`args.get("prefix")`,
  `args.get("count")`, …). On a non-object `Value`, `.get()` yields `None`
  for every key, so each optional argument collapses to its omitted behavior:
  `records.read` (lines ~924–925) → no prefix filter, no cursor;
  `chat.history` (lines ~885–888) → the default count of 16. (Caps with
  required arguments, e.g. `chat.say`/`schedule.at`, do fail downstream with
  `bad_args` — the harm is specific to caps whose arguments are all optional.)

Reproduction (probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-wants-args-20261108`,
worktree at origin/main 13eb408fe5; two tests added to
`pkgs/id/src/world/tests.rs` in the probe only):

- `probe_parse_wants_accepts_non_object_args`: `parse_wants` returns `Ok`
  with the value preserved verbatim for `args` = `42`, `"co"`,
  `[{"prefix":"co"}]`, and `true`. Controls: object args and absent args
  parse as documented.
- `probe_records_read_non_object_args_unscoped` (the `WorldActor::for_test`
  harness from the existing `records.read` tests; the program publishes
  `count=1`, `other=2`, `zebra=3`; `records.read` + `chat.history` granted):
  - Control: `args {"prefix":"co"}` → ok, records = `[count]`.
  - `args 42` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]` — the full page.
  - `args "co"` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]`.
  - `args [{"prefix":"co"}]` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]`.
  - `args true` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]`.
  - `chat.history` with `args "2"` → ok (accepted, default behavior).

Existing tests pin per-field types inside an object args (#7899, #7892) but
nothing pins the shape of `args` itself.

## Why it matters

This is the layer above #7899/#7892: those cover a wrong-typed *field inside*
an object args; this covers `args` itself being the wrong JSON type, which
bypasses every field check at once because no field is ever read. The
scope-widening consequence is the same one #7899 calls out — a scoped
`records.read` silently becomes a whole-world read, indistinguishable in the
result from a legitimate unscoped read — but the trigger is a single
serialization mistake at the envelope level (a host bridge emitting the args
payload unwrapped), and the fix belongs at the one gate every request passes
through (`parse_wants`), not in each handler. `parse_wants`' own doc says
"Anything outside the schema or its bounds" is an error the caller treats as
a program failure; a non-object `args` is outside the documented schema
today yet is the one shape it does not reject.

Related but distinct: #7899 (non-string `prefix`/`after` *fields* of
`records.read`), #7892 (`chat.history` `count` field type). A fixer may
reasonably land all three in one pass; this issue is only the
`parse_wants`-level args-shape gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `parse_wants` rejects a request whose `args` is present and is neither a JSON object nor `null` (at least number, string, array, and boolean cases), with an error that names the problem, consistent with its other schema refusals.
- [ ] Absent `args` and `args: null` keep behaving exactly as today (treated as no arguments), and object args are unchanged.
- [ ] A `records.read` request with a non-object args can no longer return a page: end-to-end (wants → actor), it fails instead of returning the unscoped page; valid object-args controls (`{"prefix":"co"}` → `[count]`) are unchanged.
- [ ] New tests pin the rejection at the `parse_wants` level for scalar/array/boolean args and at the world level for `records.read`, alongside the valid controls.
- [ ] The existing world/world_caps suites stay green.
