# id(web/world): upload/compile socket `error`, `module_installed` and `compiled` fields shape-trusted — non-string message/module_hash/diagnostics render coerced ('[object Object]', 'a,b') and a bogus installed frame still clears the admin token

## Summary

The two admin WebSocket handlers in `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` — the wasm module-upload socket and the Roc-compile socket — validate the frame envelope and `chunk_bytes`, but trust the *fields* of the `error`, `module_installed` and `compiled` frames. A wrong-shape frame from the host (deploy skew, a buggy/future server, a middlebox) is not rejected: its non-string `message`, `module_hash` and `diagnostics` are rendered as their coerced string form, and a `module_installed`/`compiled` frame with a bogus hash still reports success in green and clears the admin token input.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ origin/main 0f9e47131f; world.ts byte-identical to the probe copy)

`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts`:

- Upload socket handler (:617-675): after `isRecord` + string-`type` check, `const frame = parsed as WorldFrame;` (:631). `error` case (:632-635): `setStatus(frame.message ?? "Module install failed", "error")` — `message` unchecked. `module_installed` case (:668-673): `` setStatus(`World program installed: ${frame.module_hash ?? "ok"}`, "good") ``, log line with the same value, and `admin.value = ""` — `module_hash` unchecked, success side effects unconditional.
- Compile socket handler (:750-776): same cast (:764). `error` case (:765-768): status + log from unchecked `frame.message`. `compiled` case (:769-775): status + log from unchecked `frame.module_hash`, and `if (frame.diagnostics) appendLine(log, frame.diagnostics)` — `diagnostics` unchecked; success also clears `admin.value`.
- Sibling in the same handlers *is* validated: `upload_ready`'s `chunk_bytes` must be an integer in 1..6144 (:639-651) or the socket closes with an invalid-size status. The session socket's `receive()` likewise validates snapshot/event fields (`isWorldSnapshot`/`isWorldEvent`) and rejects bad frames via `rejectFrame()`.
- Declared contract (world.ts :39-44): `chunk_bytes?: number; module_hash?: string; diagnostics?: string; message?: string` — all string fields, none enforced in these two handlers.

Reproduction (probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-world-upload-20261108`, real `world.ts` driven through the same FakeWebSocket harness as `world-records.test.ts`; probe copy byte-identical to main; 6/6 probe tests pass — the malformed cases assert the current wrong behavior — and baseline `world-records.test.ts` is 6/6 green):

- Control: install `{type:"error", message:"bad module"}` → status `bad module`. ✔
- Install `{type:"error", message:{forged:true}}` → status `[object Object]`.
- Install `{type:"module_installed", module_hash:{forged:true}}` → status `World program installed: [object Object]`, log `program installed [object Object]`, admin token cleared.
- Install `{type:"module_installed", module_hash:12345}` → status `World program installed: 12345`.
- Compile `{type:"error", message:["a","b"]}` → status `a,b`, log `compile error: a,b`.
- Compile `{type:"compiled", module_hash:{forged:true}, diagnostics:{diag:1}}` → status `Roc program installed: [object Object]`, diagnostics appended to the log as `[object Object]`.

## Dedup / scope boundaries

- #5034 (closed) covered these same handlers at the *frame* level (non-object frames, non-integer `chunk_bytes`) — both fixed, and the chunk validation is the sibling pattern above. It did not cover the per-field types of `error`/`module_installed`/`compiled`.
- #7924 (open) covers the *session* socket's `receive()` fields (`invite`/`view`/`error`). These upload/compile sockets are separate handlers with separate sockets; #7924's fix does not touch them.
- #6620 (closed) was the Rust `world_net` client's `compiled` reply — a different consumer in a different language.

## Why it matters

These are the admin paths that install a world program. A host that answers with a wrong-shape success frame makes the page claim a program was installed under a hash that is literally `[object Object]` (or `12345`), clears the admin token as if the install completed, and logs the same fiction — the operator has no signal anything went wrong, and the real error text (when the frame is an `error`) is replaced by coerced garbage instead of the host's message or a clean invalid-response status. The handlers already have the invalid-response path ("Host returned an invalid upload/compile response" + close); the field checks belong on the same path.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In both handlers, an `error` frame whose `message` is present and not a string, a `module_installed`/`compiled` frame whose `module_hash` is present and not a string, and a `compiled` frame whose `diagnostics` is present and not a string take the existing invalid-response path (invalid upload/compile response status, socket closed) — no coerced rendering, no success status, and the admin token is NOT cleared.
- [ ] Well-formed frames behave exactly as today: string `message` renders as the error status, string `module_hash` renders in the success status/log and clears the admin token, string `diagnostics` is appended to the log.
- [ ] Web tests cover the malformed field cases for both sockets (object/array `message`, object/numeric `module_hash`, object `diagnostics`) plus the well-formed controls; the existing world web suites still pass.

title: fleet-stalling: scheduled lane waves lose every route candidate to the 10s first-output deadline — 81 sessions dead in 8h

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## What is broken, in plain words

Fleet sessions are being killed by the OpenCode client's 10-second first-output deadline. When a scheduled lane wave seats ~10 sessions inside a minute onto the same few workhorse doors, the doors queue past 10s, **every candidate in the route trips the deadline in the same turn**, and the turn ends `failed` instead of waiting out the route cooldown and retrying a live leg. The session is lost mid-task: a lane that was checkpointing, sweeping, or binding a queue task simply stops.

## Evidence (laptop server 127.0.0.1:13420, opencode.db, window 2026-11-08T18:10Z–2026-11-09T02:10Z)

**81 sessions ended `failed` with the identical error** `provider.transport` / `"No response output within 10000ms"`:

| hour (UTC) | deaths |
|---|---|
| 17 | 18 |
| 18 | 30 |
| 19 | 7 |
| 20 | 26 |

Named sessions (verbatim `idle.outcome` rows):

- `ses_e5e41f73dc2ffeXtjBHfPlEsgd` — Queue lane (scheduled) - code 20:00, died 20:08 mid-checkpoint; last text: `repo-queue: primary queue store failed on /checkpoint (exit 5): checkpoint_task: task 14030 is not claimed by repo-worker-code`
- `ses_e5e41f6c26cffed2YLdfEQyJBz` — Queue lane (scheduled) - code 20:00, died 20:09 immediately after blocking task 14029
- `ses_e5e42091170ffef0WR74Z0IPyW` — Fleet conductor 19:40, died 20:12 mid-sweep (it was polling post-nudge session activity)
- `ses_e5e41fa5585ffeFA3Q6M5XsU9J` — explore subagent under task 13835, died 20:00 ("No response output within 10000ms")

**The route does fail over — and still runs out.** `route_attempt` for `ses_e5e42091170ffef0WR74Z0IPyW` (4 consecutive timeout rows, then the turn ends):

```
1794190242512  opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash  timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190255506  opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash  timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190271205  opencode-go.popesdrew/deepseek-v4.1-flash             timeout  Transport  Timeout
1794190294012  opencode-go.drewrypope/deepseek-v4.1-flash            timeout  Transport  Timeout
```

**The deadline is being hit at a real rate, and the legs routinely exceed it.** 8h `route_attempt` totals:

| provider/model | success | Transport/Timeout |
|---|---|---|
| openai.main/gpt-6-luna | 19,757 | 1,166 |
| opencode-go.developing-today-0/deepseek-v4.1-flash | 2,085 | 407 |
| _muse/muse-spark-1.3-contributor | 1,464 | 158 |
| _vibe/deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017 | 4,194 | 217 |

Observed first-token maxima in the last 2h: gpt-6-luna **15,738 ms**, deepseek-v4.1-flash **10,185 ms**, muse-spark **10,428 ms** — i.e. these legs cross a 10 s deadline as a matter of course, and a burst pushes every door over it at once.

**The waves are the trigger.** Ten scheduled code lanes started between 20:00:01 and 20:00:52 local on the same `opencode-route/workhorse` chain (`workhorse-ordered` → `deepseek-flash-plan` → `workhorse-weighted`); 26 sessions died in the 20:00 hour.

## Why this is not #4370 or #3325

- #4370 (closed completed 2026-11-08T10:51Z) was closed on the verdict that per-leg shedding was "superseded" because `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` was retired. That premise is false at main today: `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs` is tracked, `f61b2af25e` ("fix(route-proxy): timeout each leaf first response") is an ancestor of `origin/main`, and the death class returned at 81/8h after the closure.
- #3325 (open) is the quota-exhausted-leg class (429 / muse-spark). This is the first-output-deadline class, which reaches the session as `provider.transport`, not `provider.rate-limit`.

## Acceptance test (one line)

Replaying a 10-session scheduled lane wave on `opencode-route/workhorse`, **zero sessions end with `provider.transport: No response output within 10000ms`** — either the deadline is sized above the observed leg p99 (or disabled for this chain), or a turn whose candidates all trip it retries after the route cooldown and completes, shown by a `route_attempt` timeout row set followed by a success row in the same turn.

## Pointers for the fix

- Client: `packages/core/src/session/runner/step.ts` builds the synthetic `TransportError` for the deadline (code `Timeout`) and `packages/core/src/model-route.ts` defaults `firstTokenTimeoutMs` to 10_000. The fork may need to retry after cooldown when the last candidate times out.
- Config: `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` sets no `health.firstTokenTimeoutMs` on the workhorse chain, so the 10 s default applies to every leg.
- Concurrency: the scheduled lane wave starts ~10 sessions inside a minute on the same three DeepSeek doors (see also #6533, claimant cap 36 saturated).

body:
# id(web/world): session-WS `invite`, `view` and `error` frames shape-trusted — a non-string invite capability is persisted as '[object Object]', non-string view/error text renders coerced

## Summary

On the world page, three of the remaining session-WebSocket frame handlers in
`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` `receive()` trust the frame's shape, unlike their
sibling handlers in the same switch. A wrong-shape frame from the server
(stale/buggy host, middlebox, or a future server change) is not rejected: a
non-string invite capability is adopted, coerced, and **persisted to
sessionStorage as the session capability**, and non-string `view` data /
`error` messages are rendered as their coerced string form
(`'[object Object]'`) instead of the frame being rejected.

## Evidence (verified on main @ 30bd3a1398; world.ts unchanged from a97c23c7df)

`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts`:

- The frame is accepted with a bare cast — `const frame = parsed as WorldFrame;`
  (receive(), ~line 199) — with the declared contract `invite?: { capability?: string; … }`,
  `data?: string`, `view_revision?: number`, `message?: string` (~lines 24–44).
- Sibling cases validate before use: `snapshot` is checked with
  `isWorldSnapshot`, `event` with `isWorldEvent`, and the `records` case was
  filed separately as #7908; failures go to `rejectFrame()`. The upload
  socket in the same file validates `chunk_bytes` (integer, 1..6144) before use.
- The `invite` case (~lines 297–305) has no equivalent guard:
  `const invite = frame.invite ?? frame; if (invite.capability) { showCapability(invite.capability); … }`
  — any truthy value is passed to `showCapability` (~lines 180–185), which does
  `capability.value = value; sessionStorage.setItem(storageKey, value);` and
  unhides the invite output. An object capability is stored as the literal
  string `'[object Object]'`, a numeric one as `'12345'`, and the status still
  reports “Invite ready to share” — the bogus value is then the capability the
  page rehydrates from sessionStorage and offers to copy/share.
- The `view` case (~lines 237–266): the `surface` path is guarded by
  `renderWorldSurface`, and the `patch` path checks
  `typeof frame.view_revision === "number"`, but the fallback
  `if (frame.data !== undefined) { view.textContent = frame.data; renderedViewRevision = frame.view_revision ?? null; }`
  accepts any type: an object `data` renders as `'[object Object]'`, and a
  non-number `view_revision` is stored verbatim as the rendered revision,
  after which patch base-revision comparisons can never match it.
- The `error` case (~lines 306–310): `setStatus(frame.message ?? "World request failed", "error")`
  and the log line accept any type; an object message is displayed as
  `'[object Object]'` instead of a real error or a rejected frame.

Reproduction (probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-world-frames-20261108`,
real `world.ts` driven through the same FakeWebSocket harness as
`world-records.test.ts`; probe copy byte-identical to main; 6/6 probe tests
pass — the malformed cases assert the current wrong behavior — and the
baseline `world-records.test.ts` suite is 6/6 green):

- Control: `{type:"invite", invite:{capability:"cap-valid-123", display_name:"bob"}}`
  → sessionStorage stores `cap-valid-123`, status “Invite ready to share”. ✔
- `{type:"invite", invite:{capability:{forged:true}, display_name:"bob"}}`
  → sessionStorage stores `'[object Object]'`, status still “Invite ready to share”.
- `{type:"invite", invite:{capability:12345, display_name:"bob"}}`
  → sessionStorage stores `'12345'`, status still “Invite ready to share”.
- `{type:"view", data:{not:"text"}, view_revision:"7"}` → the world view
  renders `'[object Object]'` (and the string revision is stored).
- `{type:"error", message:{code:42}}` → the status line shows `'[object Object]'`.
- Control: `{type:"error", message:"world is full"}` → shown verbatim. ✔

Existing tests do not cover this: the world suites
(`world-records.test.ts`, `world-rejoin.test.ts`, `world-surface.test.ts`, …)
deliver only well-shaped invite/view/error frames, if any.

## Why it matters

The invite capability is a credential-like value: it is persisted in
sessionStorage, rehydrated on the next load, pre-fills the capability field
the user joins with, and is what the copy button shares. A single
wrong-shape frame silently replaces a valid capability with
`'[object Object]'` / a coerced number and reports success — the user then
joins (or shares an invite) with a capability the server never issued, and
the failure surfaces later, elsewhere, with no trace back to the bad frame.
The `view`/`error` coercions are the same defect class at display severity:
bogus rendered state and useless error text instead of the house pattern —
validate, and `rejectFrame()` on a mismatch — that the snapshot/event cases
in the same switch already follow.

Related but distinct: #7908 covers the session-WS `records` frame in the
same `receive()`; #7833/#7831 cover the **REST** `/api/world/host-view` and
`/api/world/invite` HTTP responses in the same file (different functions and
transport — this issue is the WebSocket `invite` frame, not the HTTP invite
response). A fixer may reasonably handle them in one pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An `invite` frame whose effective `capability` (nested `invite` object or top-level) is present but not a string is rejected (e.g. via the existing `rejectFrame()` path): nothing is written to sessionStorage or the capability field, the invite output is not shown, and “Invite ready to share” is not reported. A missing capability stays a no-op as today.
- [ ] A `view` frame whose `data` is present but not a string is rejected the same way and does not change the rendered view; a non-number `view_revision` is never stored as the rendered revision.
- [ ] An `error` frame whose `message` is present but not a string is rejected (or falls back to the default message) — a coerced `'[object Object]'` is never displayed as the status or log line.
- [ ] Well-formed frames behave exactly as today: valid invite capabilities are stored and reported, string view data renders, string error messages show verbatim, and the existing world suites stay green.
- [ ] New tests deliver object/numeric invite capabilities, object view `data`, a string `view_revision`, and an object error `message`, and pin the rejection.

## Problem

`pkgs/id/examples/roc-text-counter` (added today in 5a485537ed, #3181) is missing from the one enumeration that actually rebuilds the Roc examples, so its checked-in `text-counter.wasm` is never rebuilt by CI and no check notices if `main.roc` and the wasm drift apart.

## Evidence (origin/main a97c23c7df)

- `pkgs/id/scripts/rebuild-roc-examples.sh:5-13` — the rebuild list has 7 entries (lounge, roc-chat, roc-counter, roc-grid, roc-screen, territory, apps/tic-tac-toe/program). `examples/roc-text-counter` is not one of them.
- `pkgs/id/flake.nix:382-398` — the `roc-examples` flake check (in the PR check list, `.github/scripts/id-pr-checks.txt:43`, run by id-check.yml) rebuilds the examples in its `beforeCheck` via exactly that script, then runs the sandbox lib tests and `cargo test --test toolchain_pin`. Whatever the script omits, the check never builds.
- `pkgs/id/tests/toolchain_pin.rs:13-22` — `ROC_EXAMPLE_BUILDS` has 8 entries and *does* include `examples/roc-text-counter/build.sh` (the #3181 commit updated this list). The two enumerations of "the Roc examples" in the same repo now disagree, and the pin test only checks toolchain version strings in each build.sh — it never runs the build.
- The checked-in artifact is load-bearing: `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:1638` does `include_bytes!("../../examples/roc-text-counter/text-counter.wasm")` for the new browser-websocket e2e tests, and `pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs:2456` + `:2631-2638` measure its FUEL_BUDGETS baselines against the checked-in module. Both suites exercise whatever wasm happens to be committed, fresh or stale.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` — the `id.roc.examples` row lists only `pkgs/id/examples/roc-world/**` as its paths and the registry has 0 mentions of `roc-text-counter`, so the registry does not flag the gap either.
- Dedup: no open issue covers this. #7904 is the Rust analog (plaza-sdk/rust-counter run by no venue at all); #3883/#541 are the closed historical pin-and-rebuild work. This example *has* a venue — the venue's list is incomplete.

## Why it matters

The roc-examples check exists so a pinned-toolchain change or a source edit that breaks an example build fails on the PR that causes it (#541/#3883). For roc-text-counter that protection is illusory: edit `main.roc`, forget to rebuild by hand, and every test stays green while shipping a wasm that no longer matches the source — the same stale-artifact failure mode as #7904, one directory over. The toolchain_pin/rebuild-list disagreement also guarantees the next new example repeats the mistake, because there are two lists to update and only one of them was.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pkgs/id/scripts/rebuild-roc-examples.sh` includes `examples/roc-text-counter`, and the `roc-examples` flake check rebuilds `text-counter.wasm` from `main.roc` with the pinned toolchain.
- [ ] The rebuild list and `ROC_EXAMPLE_BUILDS` in `pkgs/id/tests/toolchain_pin.rs` cover the same set of examples (or one derives from the other / a test asserts they agree), so a future example cannot land in one list only.
- [ ] The `id.roc.examples` row in `.github/test-suite-registry.json` names the example paths it actually covers, including `pkgs/id/examples/roc-text-counter/**`.
- [ ] Verification: the roc-examples check (or a local run of the rebuild script in the pinned shell) builds text-counter alongside the other seven, and the sandbox + world_ws suites pass against the rebuilt module.

# id(web/world): session-WS `records` frame is shape-trusted — a string `records` renders per-character entries, a non-string `next_after` is echoed back as the pagination cursor

## Summary

On the world page, the session WebSocket's `records` frame handler in
`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` trusts the frame's shape, unlike its sibling
handlers in the same `receive()` switch. A wrong-shape frame from the
server (stale/buggy host, middlebox, or a future server change) is not
rejected: its payload is merged and rendered as if it were the world's
records, and a malformed pagination cursor is sent straight back to the
server as the next page request.

## Evidence (verified on main @ 1f5ac11276)

`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts`:

- The frame is accepted with a bare cast — line 199: `const frame = parsed as WorldFrame;` — and the declared contract is `records?: Record<string, unknown>` / `next_after?: string | null` (lines 37–38).
- Sibling cases validate before use: `snapshot` is checked with `isWorldSnapshot` (line 203) and `event` with `isWorldEvent` (line 223); failures go to `rejectFrame()` (line 176).
- The `records` case (line 267) has no equivalent guard:
  - line 272: `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(frame.records ?? {}))` — `Object.entries` on a **string** yields per-character entries, on an **array** per-index entries, on a **number/boolean** nothing at all.
  - line 275: `recordsAfter = frame.next_after ?? null;` — any non-null value, whatever its type, becomes the cursor, and lines 286–293 send it back verbatim as `after` in the next `records` request.

Reproduction (probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-records-ws-frame-20261108`,
real `world.ts` driven through the same FakeWebSocket harness as
`world-records.test.ts`; probe copy byte-identical to main, 6/6 tests pass —
the BUG cases assert the current wrong behavior):

- Control: `{type:"records", records:{a1:1}, next_after:null}` renders `{a1: 1}` and terminates the fetch. ✔
- `records: "abc"` → renders `{"0":"a","1":"b","2":"c"}` — per-character junk presented as world records.
- `records: [10, 20]` → renders `{"0":10,"1":20}`.
- `records: 42` → the fetch silently completes rendering `{}` — the world's records look empty.
- `next_after: 123` → the client sends the follow-up page request with `after: 123` (a number, not a string).
- `next_after: {k: 1}` → the client sends `after: {"k": 1}` verbatim.

Existing tests do not cover this: `pkgs/id/web/src/world-records.test.ts`
covers the #1458 pagination coalescing and the #2953 `__proto__`
define-semantics, but every delivered frame has a well-shaped `records`
object and a string/null `next_after`. The baseline suite is green
(6/6 in the probe).

## Why it matters

The records panel is how a participant reads the world's published
state. A single wrong-shape frame currently (a) fabricates records that
do not exist (per-character/per-index entries), (b) silently reports an
empty world for scalar payloads, and (c) corrupts the pagination
protocol by echoing a non-string cursor the server never issued —
against a server that treats an unknown cursor as a first page, that
also re-merges page one and can keep the fetch alive past the page the
server meant to end it on. The snapshot/event cases in the same switch
already show the house pattern: validate, and `rejectFrame()` on a
mismatch instead of rendering it.

Related but distinct: #7833 covers the **REST** `/api/world/host-view`
path in the same file (`refreshHostView`, a different function and
transport); this issue is the session-WebSocket `records` frame in
`receive()`. A fixer may reasonably handle both in one pass. The
Rust-side cursor-shape fixes (#6615, #6778, #6600) and open #6578 cover
server-side readers, not this browser handler.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A `records` frame whose `records` is not a plain object (string, array, number, boolean) is rejected (e.g. via the existing `rejectFrame()` path) and does not change the rendered records or the fetch state.
- [ ] A `records` frame whose `next_after` is neither a string nor null/undefined is rejected the same way; a non-string cursor is never sent back to the server as `after`.
- [ ] Well-formed frames behave exactly as today: the #1458 coalescing/refetch behavior and the #2953 define-semantics key handling in `world-records.test.ts` stay green.
- [ ] New tests in `world-records.test.ts` (or a sibling suite) deliver string/array/numeric `records` and numeric/object `next_after` frames and pin the rejection.

body:
## Symptom
The fleet monitor's run-start digest (`monitor-digest.py`, used by repo-fleet-monitor per code#2154) flags 134 developing-today/code issues under `queue_queued_missing_task` — issues labelled `queue/queued` that the digest believes have no live queue task. Direct checks show sampled flagged issues DO have live tasks, so the flag list is unusable: the monitor's Duty 1 safety net cannot trust it and spends its bounded run re-verifying instead of reconciling.

## Evidence
- Fleet monitor run 2026-11-08 18:12 CST (run_id f52bdf5a-f312-4fe7-87fe-479ecf51b784): "Digest defect: queue_queued_missing_task over-flags 134 code items; sample of 3 all had live tasks via dedupe hit, indicating unhealthy join logic."
- Digest on disk (`hidden_files/monitor-digest.json`, generated 2026-11-09T00:12:32Z): `flags."developing-today/code".queue_queued_missing_task` has 134 entries (first entries: issues 788, 941); the same flag is 0 for opencode, openchamber, and nix.
- Code inspection (2026-11-09, dropped-thread-catcher): in `monitor-digest.py`, `live_by_issue` is built only from the digest's fetched `tasks` list, and `queue_queued_missing_task` = labelled `queue/queued` issues whose number is not in `live_by_issue`. If the task fetch is windowed/paginated differently from the label pull (label pull limit 500 per label), every issue whose live task falls outside the task fetch window is falsely flagged.

## Scope
- Fix the join in `monitor-digest.py` so `queue_queued_missing_task` only contains issues with genuinely no live (queued/claimed/parked) task in the corresponding pilot queue — e.g. fetch tasks keyed by dedupe/issue for the labelled set, or page the task fetch until it covers the labelled set.
- Do not change the flag's name or the digest's output shape; other duties consume them.
- Out of scope: the 133-item claim-evaporation backlog and any label repairs (the monitor's normal duties).

## Acceptance check
- A regenerated digest's `queue_queued_missing_task` list for developing-today/code, spot-checked on at least 5 flagged issues via direct dedupe/task lookup, contains only issues with no live task; and the count drops from 134 to the true number (expected near zero).
- The next repo-fleet-monitor run reports the flag as trustworthy (no "over-flags / wasn't trusted" note).

## Refs
- Filed by dropped-thread-catcher, 2026-11-08 run (catch fingerprint: monitor-digest-missing-task-overflag).
- Monitor implementation: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2154
- Source report: repo-fleet-monitor run 2026-11-08 18:12 CST, Fleet Monitor chat.

## Acceptance criteria
- monitor-digest.py's queue_queued_missing_task flag agrees with the fleet-queue database: an issue is flagged only when no task in any live status (queued/claimed/parked/blocked) carries its dedupe key in the repo's pilot queue.
- A regenerated digest's flag count for developing-today/code drops to the true-missing set (this run's verified sample: 1 true missing in 7 flagged), and the previously false-flagged issues (#1002, #1155, #1166, #1421, #1915) no longer appear.
- The fix lands via PR referencing this issue.

title: id(world): records.read prefix/after shape-trusted — a non-string prefix silently widens a scoped read to every record, a non-string after silently restarts pagination

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`records.read` declares its arguments in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:264-276` (at origin/main `d2c2a05b5e`): optional `prefix` and `after`, both `ArgumentType::String`. But `parse_wants` only bounds the serialized `args` size (`world_caps.rs:798-805`) — it never validates argument values against that schema — and the handler in `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:924-925` reads both fields with `.and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str)`:

```rust
let prefix = args.get("prefix").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str);
let after = args.get("after").and_then(serde_json::Value::as_str);
```

A supplied non-string value therefore collapses to `None` — exactly the same as omitting the argument. The sibling handlers in the same match do not do this: `chat.say` (`actor.rs:965`), `schedule.at` (`actor.rs:997-1001`), and `schedule.cancel` (`actor.rs:1031`) all reject a wrong-typed required argument with `CapError::bad_args()`. And #7892 covers the same silent-default pattern for `chat.history`'s `count`. `records.read`'s two string arguments are the unfiled remainder.

## Verified behavior (laptop probe, origin/main d2c2a05b5e)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-records-shape-20261108` (laptop worktree at origin/main; in-module test reusing the `WorldActor::for_test` + result-capture pattern of `records_read_pages_fit_the_result_event_that_delivers_them`, `pkgs/id/src/world/tests.rs`). The program publishes records `count=1`, `other=2`, `zebra=3`; `records.read` granted. Probe test `probe_records_read_shape_trusted_prefix_after`: **1 passed**.

Controls — valid string arguments scope the page exactly as documented:

1. `{"prefix": "co"}` → ok, records = `[count]`.
2. `{"after": "count"}` → ok, records = `[other, zebra]`.

Malformed — every one returns **ok with the full unscoped page** instead of `bad_args`:

3. `{"prefix": 123}` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]` — the prefix filter silently disappears.
4. `{"prefix": null}` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]`.
5. `{"after": 123}` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]` — pagination silently restarts from the beginning.
6. `{"after": {"x": 1}}` → ok, records = `[count, other, zebra]`.

## Why it matters

For `prefix` this is a scope-widening silent failure, not just a hidden typo: a program that asks for one prefix subtree (e.g. because it is only meant to see that subtree, or to keep the page byte-bounded) receives **every published record** in the world, key-ordered from the start, up to the page byte cap. A serialization mismatch in a guest program (a number-typed config value, a null from a host bridge) silently escalates a scoped read into a whole-world read and the caller cannot tell — the result is indistinguishable from a legitimately unscoped read. For `after`, a mistyped cursor silently restarts pagination, so a paging loop can repeat the first page forever instead of erroring. The declared argument contract (`world_caps.rs`) says these are strings; the handler should enforce it the way its sibling handlers already do.

## Acceptance criteria

- A supplied non-string `prefix` or `after` (at least number, `null`, object, array, and boolean cases) is rejected with `bad_args`, rather than treated as omitted.
- An omitted `prefix`/`after` still returns the unscoped / from-the-start page, exactly as today.
- Valid string `prefix`/`after` behavior is unchanged, including the byte-bounded page and `next_after` contract (#4888).
- Add a world-level regression test exercising malformed `prefix`/`after` through the request path (the `WorldActor::for_test` pattern used by the existing `records.read` tests), plus the valid-string controls.

## Evidence

- Code: `pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:924-925` (`prefix`/`after` read via `as_str`, `None` = omitted) at origin/main `d2c2a05b5e30af0f663625348995d591c79ebd5e`; schema `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:264-276`; `parse_wants` size-only check `world_caps.rs:798-805`. Contrast `actor.rs:965`, `actor.rs:997-1001`, `actor.rs:1031` (sibling handlers reject wrong types with `bad_args`).
- Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-records-shape-20261108/pkgs/id/src/world/tests.rs` test `probe_records_read_shape_trusted_prefix_after` (laptop, @d2c2a05b5e): controls scoped correctly; all four malformed cases returned ok with the full `[count, other, zebra]` page. `cargo test --lib probe_records_read_shape_trusted_prefix_after` → 1 passed.
- Dedup: #7892 covers `chat.history` `count` only (different cap, different argument, numeric default) — title/keyword searches for `records.read` + prefix/bad_args/malformed return no filing for these arguments; #4888 (closed) covered page-size vs result-event cap, not argument types.

title: id(web/collab): INIT doc content entries unchecked — one unknown node/mark or non-string text silently discards the whole document and opens an empty editor

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` `handleMessage` validates the INIT frame's doc only at the top level (collab.ts:305-314 at origin/main `69aa168d5d`): the doc must be a non-array object with `type === "doc"`, and `content`, *if present*, must be an array. The content **entries** are never checked. The doc is passed to `initEditor` (editor.ts:659-666), where `Node.fromJSON` throws on the first bad entry and the catch falls back to an **empty doc**:

```ts
doc = Node.fromJSON(editorSchema, initialDoc);
} catch (err) {
  console.error("[editor] Failed to parse initial doc JSON, using empty doc:", err);
  doc = editorSchema.topNodeType.createAndFill() ?? editorSchema.node("doc");
}
```

So a single malformed entry silently discards the **entire** document: the editor opens empty, `onEditorReady` fires, the session proceeds as if the file were empty — no frame drop, no error status, no reconnect/resync. The realistic trigger is version skew: a newer server (or a peer's newer client via the server) emits a node or mark type this client predates, and every older client opens the file as empty — one edit plus autosave away from overwriting the real content with the empty state. This is the doc-content sibling of #7859 (INIT *mode* field, same empty-editor outcome via the raw schema); #2824 hardened INIT version/doc-type only, and no filing covers doc content entries.

## Verified behavior (laptop probe, origin/main 69aa168d5d)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-creator-a-20261108/pkgs/id/web/src/probe-initdoc.test.ts` (real `initCollab` + FakeWebSocket harness, msgpackr-packed INIT frames, mode `"rich"`; 5/5 probe tests run, existing collab+editor suites 146/146 green as control):

1. **Control:** valid rich doc `{type:"doc", content:[{type:"paragraph", content:[{type:"text", text:"hello rich"}]}]}` → editor text is `hello rich`.
2. **One unknown node type discards everything:** content = a valid paragraph (`good paragraph`) plus `{type:"future_node_from_newer_server", …}` → editor ready with text `""`, doc `doc(paragraph)` (empty). The valid paragraph is lost too.
3. **Non-string text:** a text node with `text: 12345` → editor ready, text `""`.
4. **Numeric content entry:** `content: [42]` → editor ready, text `""`.
5. **Unknown mark type:** a text node with `marks: [{type:"future_mark"}]` → editor ready, text `""`.

In every malformed case `onEditorReady` fired and the session continued (no drop/reconnect), so the user is shown an apparently-empty file with a live save path.

## Why it matters

INIT is the one frame that defines what the user believes the file contains. A whole-document silent discard is a data-loss footgun (empty view + autosave) and makes client/server version skew — inevitable as node/mark types evolve — destructive instead of degrading. The frame boundary is where the rest of this file already validates (#2824); content entries are the unvalidated remainder of that same frame.

## Acceptance criteria

- INIT handling validates doc content entries deeply enough that a doc `Node.fromJSON` cannot parse is **rejected at the frame boundary** (log + drop, session/socket intact, no editor initialized from it), mirroring the malformed-INIT drop path — OR `initEditor`'s parse failure on a server-supplied doc surfaces as a visible error/resync instead of a silent empty editor. Either way: a non-empty server doc must never present as an empty editable file.
- The fix must not change behavior for valid docs in any content mode (rich/markdown/plain/raw), including docs with no `content` field.
- Regression tests in collab.test.ts / editor.test.ts style for each probed case: unknown node type, unknown mark type, non-string text, numeric content entry — plus the valid-doc control.
- Existing pkgs/id web vitest suite + typecheck green.

## Evidence

- Code: `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts:305-314` (INIT doc validation stops at `type`/`Array.isArray(content)`), `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:659-666` (`Node.fromJSON` catch → empty doc) at origin/main `69aa168d5da3aa0265f95ffdedeeed2fb4da1ce3`.
- Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-creator-a-20261108/pkgs/id/web/src/probe-initdoc.test.ts` (laptop, @69aa168d5d): all four malformed cases → editor ready with `textContent === ""`; control renders `hello rich`; collab.test.ts + editor.test.ts 146/146 as control.
- Dedup: #2824 (closed) covered INIT version + doc object/type; #7859 covers the INIT mode field; #7854 covers AUTH_OK/NEW_VERSION; #7873 covers UPDATE/CURSOR. Doc content entries are unfiled.

body:
## Summary

`infra/yard-reaper/tests/test_yard_reaper.py` — the 17-test suite pinning the yard-reaper's whole-entry classification and deletion-safety gates — is run by no workflow, flake check, just recipe, or registry entry. The reaper itself runs **hourly with `--apply`** from its systemd timer (`infra/yard-reaper/systemd/yard-reaper.timer`: `OnCalendar=hourly`; service `ExecStart=%h/.local/bin/yard-reaper --apply`), moving whole entries of `~/git/fleet` to trash. The tool that deletes runs on a timer; the tests that pin when it must NOT delete run nowhere.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, origin/main @ 69aa168d5da3aa0265f95ffdedeeed2fb4da1ce3)

- Suite: `infra/yard-reaper/tests/test_yard_reaper.py`, 17 tests. Its docstring names the oracle: Drew's disposition rule (2026-11-07, #7093) — KEEP text/scripts/markdown; a whole entry is reaped only when preservation is proven (clone clean + HEAD == live remote tip, or scratch tree with zero keep-set files) and every liveness gate (claimed task/issue, process cwd, 4h idle) is clear.
- Venue search on origin/main: `git grep yard` over `.github/workflows/*`, `.github/test-suite-registry.json`, `flake.nix`, `lib/*`, and `justfile` returns nothing; a repo-wide grep for `test_yard_reaper` / `yard-reaper/tests` outside `infra/yard-reaper/` itself returns nothing. The suite is also absent from the #6185 test-suite registry (0 mentions of `yard-reaper`), so it fails registry conditions 1–3 (registered / real venue / proven run) as written in `.github/ci-policy.md`.
- The suite passes today: extracted `infra/yard-reaper` from origin/main on the laptop (`~/git/fleet/probe-yard-reaper`) and ran `python3 -m unittest discover -s infra/yard-reaper/tests -p 'test_*.py'` → `Ran 17 tests in 0.851s — OK`. It is green and hermetic (stdlib unittest, temp dirs, mocked liveness reads); only the wiring is missing.
- The risk is live, not hypothetical: the tool landed today (d22e81a80a, 2026-11-08) and needed three fixes the same day, including `72df40fbf7 fix(yard-reaper): apply loop NameError on its first real run + apply-path regression tests` — the regression tests that commit added are precisely the ones no venue executes. Two classification fixes followed/preceded it the same day (42a49ff3c4 worktree registration from every primary; 35a1f7122d package caches / vendored trees are bulk, not keep-set).

## Why it matters

The yard-reaper is a deletion tool operating on the fleet's scratch yard, where probe crates, lane worktrees, and unpushed scratch live. Its keep-set and liveness gates are the only thing standing between an hourly timer and moving a still-needed entry to trash. A classification regression (a keep-set suffix dropped, a liveness gate inverted, a bulk-subtree rule widened) would pass every existing check, merge, and then act within the hour. Sibling deletion tools got this exact filing when their suites were unwired (#5952 cargo-target-janitor, whose engine this tool widens per its README); the yard-reaper is the wider, newer tool and has no equivalent coverage.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `test_yard_reaper.py` runs in a real venue: an enabled workflow job (e.g. scripts-test / an infra-tests workflow, path-gated on `infra/yard-reaper/**`) or a flake check that actually runs, naming the suite file explicitly and asserting it exists first (per the #6185 coverage contract in `.github/ci-policy.md`).
- [ ] A registry entry in `.github/test-suite-registry.json` names the suite, its venue, and its invocation.
- [ ] The venue is proven by an observed successful run on a PR or push touching `infra/yard-reaper/**` (a dispatch-only or disabled venue does not count).
- [ ] The suite still passes unmodified (17 tests, verified green on main this run) — this is wiring only, no test or reaper behaviour changes.

Relates to: #7093 (the tool), #5952 (same gap for the cargo-target-janitor it widens), #5992 (same pattern, t3code), #6185/#6187 (coverage contract / venue-reality audit).

title: id(web/collab): UPDATE and CURSOR frame fields shape-trusted — a malformed UPDATE tears the session down (close 4001 + reconnect) instead of being dropped, and a malformed CURSOR is stored verbatim as a phantom cursor

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` `handleMessage` validates the INIT frame's version/document fields before use (the #2824 hardening), but the UPDATE and CURSOR family handlers still cast frame fields unchecked:

- UPDATE (collab.ts:375-376): `const steps = msg[1] as unknown[]; const clientIDs = msg[2] as number[];` — the only guard is truthiness + `steps.length > 0` (collab.ts:378).
- CURSOR (collab.ts:417-421): `clientID`, `head`, `anchor`, `name`, `idleSecs` are all cast and passed straight to `updateCursor` / `markCursorFresh`.
- CURSOR_REMOVE (collab.ts:473): `clientID` cast unchecked.

## Verified behavior (laptop probe, origin/main e5a4fdcbcb)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-collab-frames` (real `initCollab` + FakeWebSocket harness from collab.test.ts, msgpackr-packed frames; existing collab suite 24/24 passes as control):

1. **A malformed UPDATE tears the session down instead of being dropped.** Delivering `[2, "not-an-array", [1]]` or `[2, [123], [999]]` after a valid INIT makes `steps.map(...)` / `Step.fromJSON` throw inside the step-apply `try`, whose catch (collab.ts:398-408) treats it as desync: `currentWs.close(4001, "Step apply failure")` + `scheduleReconnect()`. Observed: `closeCalls=[{code:4001, reason:"Step apply failure"}]` and new sockets on timer advance. One bad frame from a buggy/malicious peer or a version-skewed server therefore forces a full disconnect + editor destroy/re-init on the next INIT; a stream of them is a reconnect churn loop. Malformed INIT frames, by contrast, are logged and dropped with the session intact.
2. **A malformed CURSOR is stored verbatim as a phantom cursor.** Delivering `[4, 4242, {x:1}, "abc", {evil:1}, "zzz"]` stores, in the cursor plugin state, a cursor with `head=[object Object]`, `anchor="abc"`, `name=[object Object]` — it persists alongside later valid cursors. Downstream, `createCursorDecorations` clamps with `Math.min(cursor.head, docSize)` (cursors.ts:523-524), which is `NaN` for these values, so the phantom cursor feeds NaN positions into decoration/coords code instead of being rejected at the frame boundary.
3. Inconsistent handling: `[2, [], "not-an-array"]` (bad clientIDs, empty steps) is silently ignored, while the cases in (1) disconnect — the frame contract is whatever each expression happens to do with a wrong type.

## Why it matters

The collab socket is a trust boundary: frames arrive from the server relaying other clients' traffic. Every other hardened handler in this file drops malformed input at the boundary; UPDATE/CURSOR instead either amplify one bad frame into a session teardown (availability) or admit unvalidated values into ProseMirror plugin state (correctness/rendering). This is the remaining unhardened surface of the same frame-shape family as #2824 (INIT), #7859 (INIT mode) and #7854 (AUTH_OK/NEW_VERSION).

## Acceptance criteria

- UPDATE: drop (log + return, no close/reconnect) when `steps` is not an array, `clientIDs` is not an array, their lengths differ, or any step fails `Step.fromJSON` parsing *as a shape error* — genuine apply/desync failures of well-shaped steps keep the existing reconnect path.
- CURSOR / CURSOR_REMOVE: drop when `clientID` is not a string/number, `head`/`anchor` are not finite numbers, or `name` is present and not a string/null; `idleSecs` ignored unless a finite number.
- Tests in collab.test.ts style: each malformed frame above is dropped with the editor/session intact (no `close(4001)`, no new socket, no cursor stored), and a following valid frame still applies; valid UPDATE/CURSOR controls keep working (existing suite green).

## Evidence

- Code: `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts:375-421, 473` at origin/main `e5a4fdcbcb3f90b6552009420d900151454d9103`.
- Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-collab-frames/src/probe-frames.test.ts` + `probe2.test.ts` (7+1 tests, all observations above reproduced; collab.test.ts 24/24 as control).

Observed 2026-11-09 by queue lane code-b (task 13753 completion verification):

`fleet queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status done --limit 2000` and `--limit 8000` return **zero rows** (exit OK, empty output), while `--limit 5` and `--limit 100` return rows normally. The done list is also sorted oldest/priority-first, so recent completions cannot be located with any working limit either — a worker verifying a just-completed task gets "not claimed" verdicts from checkpoint/complete but cannot confirm `status=done` from `list`.

Impact: completion verification during a shift required a redundant `complete` call to elicit the verdict. A silent empty result on a large `--limit` is worse than an error: it reads as "task does not exist".

Ask: either honor large limits, or clamp with a visible notice; and consider a `--task <id>` / recent-first ordering option for single-task verification.


## Acceptance criteria
- `fleet queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status done --limit 2000` returns rows (or clamps the limit with a visible notice on stderr/output) — a large limit never silently returns zero rows when matching tasks exist.
- A worker can verify a single recent completion directly (e.g. a `--task <id>` lookup or recent-first ordering option), without a redundant `complete` call.
- Small limits (5, 100) keep behaving exactly as today.
- The fix ships with a regression check covering an over-large `--limit` against a non-empty result set.

# id(web/collab): INIT frame mode shape-trusted — a non-string or unknown mode is adopted verbatim, and a falsy mode silently opens a rich doc in the raw schema as an empty editor

## Summary

`handleMessage` in `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` validates the INIT frame's
version and doc (#2824: version must be a safe non-negative integer, doc must
be a `doc` object) — but the frame's fourth field, the content mode, is still
read with an unchecked cast (collab.ts:316 on origin/main `df780d3c3b`):

```ts
const mode = ((msg[3] as string) || "raw") as ContentMode;
documentMode = mode;
...
editorInstance = initEditor(container, docRecord, version, mode, sendCursor, filename);
```

Any value is adopted as the editor's `ContentMode` (`"rich" | "markdown" |
"plain" | "raw" | "media" | "binary"`, editor.ts:41) and drives schema
selection (`getSchema`: only `"raw"` gets the raw schema, editor.ts:476-478),
toolbar/editable decisions, and the mode stored on the editor instance. Two
failure classes result:

- **Truthy wrong shapes are adopted verbatim.** A numeric, object, or
  unknown-string mode becomes the session's mode: `initEditor` is called with
  it, `instance.mode` returns it, and every mode comparison downstream
  silently takes the "not raw / no toolbar" branch for a document that may
  be raw text.
- **Falsy wrong shapes coerce to `"raw"`.** A mode of `0` / `false` (deploy
  skew, a future server contract change) hits the `|| "raw"` fallback, so a
  rich/markdown document is parsed with the raw schema (doc = `code_block+`
  only). `Node.fromJSON` throws (`RangeError: Unknown node type:
  paragraph`), `initEditor` catches it and falls back to an **empty doc** —
  the editor opens showing nothing for a non-empty file, one
  save/autosave away from overwriting the real content with the empty state.

This is the INIT sibling of #7854 (AUTH_OK / NEW_VERSION frame fields):
that filing covers the token and hash fields; the INIT mode field was not
covered by #2824 (version/doc only) or by #7854.

## Verified behavior (this run)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-initmode` (laptop) — a detached worktree at
origin/main `df780d3c3b` (collab.ts md5 `d4ecdd5034a0219d3a88424940a73b05`,
identical to `git show origin/main:pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts`) plus
`src/probe-initmode.test.ts`, which drives the **real** `initCollab`
through the same FakeWebSocket harness as `collab.test.ts`, frames packed
with the repo's MessagePack config. All 6 probe tests pass; the editor
instance is captured via `onEditorReady`:

| INIT frame | Observed |
|---|---|
| `[0, 0, rawDoc(code_block "hello raw"), "raw"]` (control) | `instance.mode === "raw"`, doc text `"hello raw"` ✅ |
| `[0, 0, richDoc(paragraph "hello rich"), "markdown"]` (control) | `instance.mode === "markdown"`, doc text `"hello rich"` ✅ |
| `[0, 0, rawDoc, 123]` | `instance.mode === 123` (number, adopted verbatim); schema selection takes the non-raw branch |
| `[0, 0, richDoc, {type:"doc"}]` | `instance.mode === {"type":"doc"}` (object, adopted verbatim) |
| `[0, 0, rawDoc, "bogus"]` | `instance.mode === "bogus"`; `hasToolbar` false, non-raw schema for a raw doc |
| `[0, 0, richDoc, 0]` | mode coerced to `"raw"`; `Node.fromJSON` throws `RangeError: Unknown node type: paragraph`; editor initialized with an **empty doc** (`doc(code_block)`, text `""`) — the sent content silently vanishes |

## Why it matters

- The empty-editor case is a data-loss footgun: the user sees an empty
  document for a file that has content, and any edit + save from that
  state posts the empty/wrong-schema doc back.
- Wrong-schema initialization (bogus/number/object modes) silently changes
  how the document is parsed, edited, and serialized for the whole session,
  with no error anywhere — the same silent-corruption shape as #7854.
- The fix pattern is already established in this function: #2824 drops INIT
  frames with an invalid version or doc; the mode field simply never got
  the same treatment.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The INIT mode is validated at the frame boundary in `collab.ts`: it must be one of the `ContentMode` union values (`"rich"`, `"markdown"`, `"plain"`, `"raw"`, `"media"`, `"binary"`). A missing mode may keep the `"raw"` default only when the field is absent/`undefined`.
- [ ] An INIT frame with a present-but-invalid mode (non-string, or a string outside the union) is dropped with a diagnosable `console.error`, like the invalid version/doc cases — the editor is never initialized with an adopted-verbatim or coerced mode.
- [ ] A rich/markdown document can never be silently opened as an empty raw-schema editor because of a wrong-typed mode field.
- [ ] Regression tests cover mode `123`, mode `{...}`, mode `"bogus"`, and mode `0`/`false` with a rich doc, plus the `"raw"` and `"markdown"` controls (a test in `collab.test.ts` style, driving `initCollab` through the fake-socket harness).
- [ ] pkgs/id web vitest suite + typecheck green.

## Scope notes

- Fix belongs at the INIT boundary in `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` (a small `isContentMode` guard next to the existing version/doc validation is fine); server contract unchanged.
- Out of scope: AUTH_OK / NEW_VERSION fields (#7854), the version/doc INIT validation (#2824, done), UPDATE/CURSOR field tolerance (noted in #2824's probe as tolerated — cursor positions are clamped in `cursors.ts`).

body:
## Finding

PR #3785 added strict argument validation to the id-mail deploy script (#3281): only `deploy.mjs [--dry-run]` is accepted, anything else aborts with exit 2 before any config/bws/wrangler work. The guard is correct and fails closed, but two residuals shipped with it and are still on main:

1. **The duplicate case is mislabeled.** With `--dry-run --dry-run`, `unknownArgs` is empty (every arg IS `--dry-run`), so the error falls back to reporting all args as unrecognized: `unrecognized argument(s): --dry-run --dry-run` — naming the one recognized argument as unrecognized. The exit code is right; the message teaches the operator the wrong fact about a script whose whole guard exists because a typo'd flag once entered the real deploy sequence.
2. **The claimed cases are unpinned.** The PR body says an `extra-positional` case was verified, but the committed `deploy.test.mjs` pins only `--dry-run`, `--dry-rnu`, `--bogus-flag`, and no-args. No test covers a stray positional, a duplicate `--dry-run`, or `--dry-run` + bogus flag — the exact shapes an operator typo produces. (Related: #6082 already tracks that this test file is run by no workflow; this issue is about the missing cases and the message, not the CI wiring.)

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3785 `fix(id-mail): deploy.mjs strict arg validation — unknown args abort before any external call (#3281)`, commits `ac09e82a7566ca61286cfb779fc288a7119ff135`, `c0c5a85f8f34b826c65d8e6833fb118115d74e35`; merge `9bfaa0d27ff744232b0c1a7106f87d1b6ae8bc92` (verified an ancestor of main by the compare API).
- Current main (verified 2026-11-08, two independent reads via the contents API at ref=main): `nixos/services/id-mail/worker/deploy.mjs` —
  - `const unknownArgs = args.filter((arg) => arg !== "--dry-run");`
  - `if (args.length > 1 || unknownArgs.length > 0) { const offenders = unknownArgs.length > 0 ? unknownArgs : args; console.error(\`unrecognized argument(s): ${offenders.join(" ")}\nusage: deploy.mjs [--dry-run]\`); process.exit(2); }`
  - The `offenders = args` fallback is reachable only when `unknownArgs` is empty and `args.length > 1`, i.e. exactly the duplicate `--dry-run` case.
- Current main `nixos/services/id-mail/worker/deploy.test.mjs` test list: `--dry-run validates only`, `--dry-rnu (typo) aborts`, `--bogus-flag aborts`, two config-validation tests (#6947), `no args runs the real deploy sequence`. No positional, duplicate, or mixed case.

## Why it matters

This script retires and redeploys the live id-mail Worker and resets its secrets; #3281 exists because unrecognized arguments were silently treated as a request for the real deploy. The guard's error message is the operator's only signal at the moment of a typo — a message that calls the valid flag "unrecognized" invites the operator to retry variations against a destructive script. The unpinned shapes are the ones most likely to regress silently, because the file already has a history of argument-handling surprises (#3252/#3264 class in sibling deploy scripts).

## Acceptance criteria

- `deploy.test.mjs` gains cases pinning, each with exit 2 and zero external calls (the existing stub harness): a stray positional (e.g. `deploy.mjs deploy`), duplicate `--dry-run --dry-run`, and `--dry-run --bogus-flag`.
- The duplicate case's error message no longer labels `--dry-run` as unrecognized (e.g. a distinct "duplicate argument" wording, or listing only genuinely unknown offenders plus a separate duplicate note); the typo/unknown-flag messages are unchanged.
- All pre-existing deploy.test.mjs cases keep passing.

Filed by pr-diff-review-b (LANE B PR diff review, run 2026-11-08 17:18 CST) from PR #3785. Not #6082 (CI wiring of the same test file) and not #3281 (the original silent-ignore bug, closed by #3785).

body:
# id(web/collab): AUTH_OK and NEW_VERSION frame fields shape-trusted — a non-string refreshed token is persisted as the session identity, a non-string hash becomes '[object Object]'

## Summary

`handleMessage` in `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts` validates the INIT frame's
fields (#2824 fix: version must be a safe non-negative integer, doc must be a
`doc` object) — but the other server frames are still read with unchecked
casts, and two of them flow into persistent / saved state:

- `MSG.AUTH_OK` (collab.ts:494-510): `const refreshedToken = msg[3] as string | null | undefined;`
  followed by `if (refreshedToken) { currentToken = refreshedToken; onTokenRefresh(refreshedToken); }`
  — any truthy value is adopted, with no string check. In `main.ts`,
  `handleTokenRefresh` (main.ts:124-127) passes it straight to
  `saveIdentity()`, which writes it to `localStorage` via `setItem` — and Web
  Storage coerces non-strings with `String(value)`. A numeric token persists
  as `"12345"`; an object token persists as the literal `"[object Object]"`,
  **overwriting the previously valid stored token**, and `currentToken` makes
  every reconnect re-send the bogus value in the AUTH frame.
- `MSG.NEW_VERSION` (collab.ts:483-492): `const hash = msg[1] as string;`
  passed unchecked to `onNewVersion`, whose `main.ts` callback (main.ts:1033)
  does `editorContainer.dataset.hash = hash;` — a non-string hash becomes the
  literal `"[object Object]"` (or `"undefined"`), and the next save posts that
  as the document hash (main.ts:1092 reads `dataset.hash` for the save body),
  breaking the archive-the-previous-version contract the callback exists to
  maintain.

This is the WebSocket sibling of #7839 (identity HTTP responses): that
filing's fix packet explicitly scoped out "WebSocket AUTH_OK token refresh
handling", so this path is currently tracked nowhere. #2824 covered the
frame-shape boundary for non-array frames and INIT only; its probe noted the
UPDATE/CURSOR tolerance and did not cover AUTH_OK / NEW_VERSION.

## Verified evidence (laptop, origin/main @4f7a26807c)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-collab-authok` on the laptop — a detached worktree
at origin/main (collab.ts md5 `d4ecdd5034a0219d3a88424940a73b05`, verified
identical to `git show origin/main:pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts`) plus
`src/probe-authok.test.ts`, which drives the **real** `initCollab` through
the same FakeWebSocket harness as `collab.test.ts`, frames packed with the
repo's own `msgpackr` config. vitest run: probe 5/5 pass; existing
`collab.test.ts` 24/24 pass as baseline.

| Frame delivered (after a valid INIT where noted) | Result |
| --- | --- |
| AUTH_OK `[9, "client-1", "alice", "NEW_TOKEN_B"]` (control) | `onTokenRefresh("NEW_TOKEN_B")`; reconnect AUTH frame `[8, "NEW_TOKEN_B"]` — correct |
| AUTH_OK `[9, "client-1", "alice", 12345]` | `onTokenRefresh` receives the **number** `12345`; after a drop, the reconnect AUTH frame is `[8, 12345]` — the bogus token is adopted verbatim as the session credential (and `handleTokenRefresh` would persist `"12345"` to localStorage) |
| AUTH_OK `[9, "client-1", "alice", {token: "nested"}]` | `onTokenRefresh` receives the object; `String(value)` is `"[object Object]"` — what `saveIdentity`'s `setItem` would persist over the valid stored token |
| NEW_VERSION `[7, {x: 1}, "notes.md"]` | `onNewVersion` receives the object as `hash`; `String(hash)` is `"[object Object]"` — what the main.ts callback writes into `dataset.hash` |
| NEW_VERSION `[7, "abc123hash", "notes.md"]` (control) | `onNewVersion("abc123hash", "notes.md")` — correct |

## Why it matters

The AUTH_OK path is the credential-refresh path for long-lived sessions
(#1463): it exists so a refreshed token replaces the old one everywhere,
including localStorage. Shape-trusting it means one malformed frame from a
buggy, partially deployed, or compromised serving node permanently poisons
the client's stored identity — the same persisted-credential sink as #7839,
reached over the socket instead of HTTP — and the poisoned value is then
re-presented on every reconnect. The NEW_VERSION leg corrupts the hash the
next save relies on to archive the previous version. Both fail silently:
nothing logs an error, and the status still reads "connected".

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In `collab.ts`, validate AUTH_OK fields before adopting them: a
      refreshed token is adopted (written to `currentToken` and passed to
      `onTokenRefresh`) only when it is a non-empty string; anything else is
      logged and dropped, leaving the current token and the stored identity
      untouched.
- [ ] Validate NEW_VERSION fields: `onNewVersion` fires only when `hash`
      (and `name`) are strings; anything else is logged and dropped, leaving
      `dataset.hash` untouched.
- [ ] Regression tests (vitest, in `collab.test.ts` style, named oracle: the

# id(web/main): /api/identity/me, /api/identity/register and /api/identity/name responses shape-trusted — a wrong-shape 200 persists a fake 'undefined' / '[object Object]' identity in localStorage

## Summary

The client identity flow in `pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts` uses the JSON bodies of
all three identity endpoints with no shape validation:

- `ensureIdentity()` — `const data = await resp.json();` for
  `/api/identity/me` (main.ts:148) and `/api/identity/register` (main.ts:185)
- `updateDisplayName()` — `const data = await resp.json();` for
  `/api/identity/name` (main.ts:215)

`data.token`, `data.client_id` and `data.name` flow straight into
`saveIdentity()` (main.ts:91), which writes them to `localStorage` via
`setItem` — and Web Storage coerces non-string values with `String(value)`.
A wrong-shape 200 therefore does not just fail one request: it **persists a
corrupt identity that survives reloads** and overwrites a previously valid
stored token.

## Verified evidence (laptop, origin/main @1aea9b5f75)

Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-identity-shape` on the laptop — main.ts lines
63–224 extracted byte-verbatim (diff-checked against
`git show origin/main:pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts`, md5 f182df7ec224deda5298b8023c84da3f),
run under Bun with a spec-faithful localStorage stub (setItem coerces via
`String()`) and a stubbed `fetch`. Controls pass: a well-formed register
body registers and stores correctly, and a well-formed `/me` body rotates
the stored token.

Wrong-shape results:

| Scenario | Result |
| --- | --- |
| register `{}` | fake success: identity `{token: undefined, clientId: undefined}` returned; localStorage stores the literal strings `"undefined"` / `"undefined"`; `getStoredIdentity()` on the next load rehydrates `{token: "undefined", clientId: "undefined"}` |
| register `"abc"` | same fake success + `"undefined"` credentials persisted |
| register `{token: 123, client_id: {x: 1}}` | persists token `"123"` and client_id `"[object Object]"` |
| register `null` | raw `TypeError` on `data.token`, caught and logged as a generic registration error (returns null) |
| /me `{token: {evil: 1}}` with a valid stored identity | **overwrites the good stored token** with the literal string `"[object Object]"` |
| /me `{token: 12345}` | numeric token accepted and persisted as `"12345"` |
| /me `null` | raw `TypeError`, caught by the network-error branch and misreported as an identity-check failure (stored identity returned optimistically) |
| /name `{name: 123}` | `updateDisplayName` returns `123` as the name and persists `"123"` |

## Why it matters

Identity is the credential layer for the whole web UI. A single malformed
200 — from a proxy, a partial deploy, a different server version, or a
compromised/misbehaving endpoint — permanently poisons the stored identity
until localStorage is manually cleared: the client then presents token
`"undefined"` / `"[object Object]"` on every subsequent load, and the /me
path can destroy an otherwise valid token in place. This is the same
validate-where-you-read-it gap as #7811/#7823/#7831/#7837, but worse than
the display-only cases because the bad value is **persisted as a
credential**.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Parse all three identity responses through a validating parser
      (e.g. in `identity-refresh.ts`, alongside `identityNeedsRefresh`):
      the body must be a plain object; `token`/`client_id`, when required
      or present, must be non-empty strings; `name` must be a string or
      null. Anything else is a failed validation/register/name update —
      never a persisted value.
- [ ] A wrong-shape `/me` 200 must not overwrite, coerce, or clear the
      stored identity; a wrong-shape register 200 must not call
      `saveIdentity` at all.
- [ ] Regression tests (vitest, named oracle: the validated-parser
      contract) covering at least: `{}`, `null`, a bare string, a numeric
      token, and an object token/client_id for register and /me, plus a
      non-string `name` for /name — each asserting localStorage is
      unchanged / no identity is returned.
- [ ] Existing web suites stay green (in particular `identity-refresh`,
      `world`, `image-browser`, `image-upload` suites).

Found by the fleet issue creator (Lane B); sibling pattern of
#7811/#7823/#7831/#7837 — different module, endpoints, and a persisted
credential sink, so filed separately.

# id(web/main): /api/identity/register and /api/identity/me responses shape-trusted — a wrong-shape 200 persists token/clientId 'undefined' to localStorage as the session identity

## Summary

`ensureIdentity()` in `pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts` uses the JSON bodies of
`GET /api/identity/me` (`:146`) and `POST /api/identity/register` (`:176`)
without any runtime shape validation — the bodies are untyped
`await resp.json()` results whose fields are read directly:

- Register (`:186-195`): `identity = { token: data.token, clientId: data.client_id, name: data.name || null }`,
  then `saveIdentity(identity.token, identity.clientId, identity.name)`
  writes both values to `localStorage`.
- Me (`:148-165`): `if (data.token) … saveIdentity(…)` is guarded for the
  token, but `const serverName = data.name || null; if (serverName !== stored.name) updateStoredName(serverName)`
  treats a missing `name` field as "the server cleared your name".

The server contract (`pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:4047`,
`IdentityResponse`) requires `client_id: String` and (on register) a
token; the client never checks either.

## Verified behavior (this run)

Probe: real `main.ts` from origin/main `1f5ac11276`, driven under
vitest/happy-dom on the Explorer (non-program) surface — fresh `init()`
per case via module reset, stub `fetch` for `/api/identity/*`, observables
are the `localStorage` identity keys. Probe:
`~/git/fleet/probe-main-shape/` on the laptop (`probe-identity.log` +
`src/main-identity-probe.test.ts` in the snapshot). Controls pass:
a valid register body stores `tok-1`/`cid-1`/`Guest`; a valid me body
refreshes the token and name.

Wrong-shape 200 bodies:

| Endpoint | Body | Observed localStorage after init |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/identity/register` | `{}` | `id_identity_token = "undefined"`, `id_identity_client_id = "undefined"` (literal strings, persisted) |
| `/api/identity/register` | `"abc"` | same — token and clientId both `"undefined"` |
| `/api/identity/register` | `{ token: 123, client_id: 456 }` | token `"123"`, clientId `"456"` (silent coercion) |
| `/api/identity/register` | `null` | raw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'token')` at `main.ts:187`; identity is `null` for the session |
| `/api/identity/me` | `{}` (stored name `Old Name`) | stored display name silently wiped (`id_identity_name` removed); token unchanged |

## Why it matters

The persisted `"undefined"` strings are truthy, so
`getStoredIdentity()` (`main.ts:83-92`) returns them as a real stored
identity on every later load: the bogus token is sent back for validation
(`?token=<redacted> and — within the session that registered — is handed to
the collab connection as the client's identity token
(`currentIdentity?.token`). The client runs as a fake identity instead of
failing closed and retrying registration cleanly. This is the same
persist-a-fake-credential class as the world invite bug (#7831), on the
identity every Explorer session depends on. The me-`{}` case separately
destroys user data (the stored display name) on a malformed response.

Related code pointer (code-read, not probed): `updateDisplayName()`
(`main.ts:206-220`) reads `data.name || null` from
`POST /api/identity/name` the same way and calls
`updateStoredName(updatedName)` — a `{}` 200 would likewise clear the
stored name; the fix should cover it with the same guard.

## Acceptance criteria

- Register: the body is validated before `saveIdentity` is called — a
  non-null object with non-empty string `token` and `client_id`
  (name `string | null`); a wrong-shape 200 registers nothing, writes
  nothing to `localStorage`, and leaves the session identity `null`
  (the existing failure path).
- Me: a wrong-shape 200 (non-object, or a `name` field that is present
  but not a string) never wipes the stored display name and never
  overwrites the stored token; a token refresh is applied only when
  `token` is a non-empty string.
- `updateDisplayName` applies the same discipline to
  `/api/identity/name` (no name wipe on a wrong-shape 200).
- Regression tests in the web suite drive the real init/identity flow
  (or an extracted validation helper used by it) with at least `{}`,
  `null`, a string body, and numeric-field bodies, plus valid controls;
  the wrong-shape cases fail pre-fix.
- `bun run test` and `bun run typecheck` in `pkgs/id/web` pass (or any
  pre-existing failures are shown identical on clean main).

Related: #7837 (same file, file-operation responses — different
endpoints and failure modes, independent fix), #7831 (world invite
persists a fake capability, same class).

# id(web/main): /api/save, /api/new, /api/rename and /api/copy responses shape-trusted — a wrong-shape 200 reports save success with dataset.hash 'undefined' or navigates to /edit/undefined

## Summary

The four file-operation handlers in `pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts` cast their
`fetch` JSON responses with bare `as` casts and use the fields without any
runtime shape validation. A 200 response whose body is the wrong shape
(proxy error page parsed as JSON, a partial deploy, a server-side change)
is therefore treated as success, with the bad values flowing into
persistent UI state and navigation:

- `main.ts:1135` — `POST /api/save`:
  `const result = (await response.json()) as { hash: string; name: string; archive_name: string | null }`,
  then `editorContainer.dataset.hash = result.hash` (`:1139`) and the
  handler returns `{ ok: true }`.
- `main.ts:1172` — `POST /api/new`:
  `as { hash: string; name: string }`, then navigates to
  `/edit/${encodeURIComponent(result.name)}` (`:1179`).
- `main.ts:1285` — `POST /api/rename`:
  `as { name: string; hash: string; archived_original: string | null; archived_replaced: string | null }`,
  sets the button to `renamed!`, then navigates to `/edit/<result.name>` (`:1298`).
- `main.ts:1353` — `POST /api/copy`:
  `as { name: string; hash: string }`, sets the button to `copied!`, then
  navigates to `/edit/<result.name>` (`:1364`).

The WebSocket frames and other responses in this codebase are guarded
(e.g. the world page's `isWorldSnapshot`/`isWorldEvent` guards), and the
sibling home/image/world HTTP responses were fixed the same way this one
should be — these four casts are the remaining unguarded door in the
editor shell. This verifies the unverified lead recorded by creator lane A
on 2026-11-08 (22:33Z backlog entry).

## Verified behavior (this run)

Probe: real `main.ts` from origin/main `1f5ac11276`, driven under
vitest/happy-dom using the program-surface harness pattern from
`world-program-main.test.ts` (real `init()`, real ProseMirror collab
editor state for save, stub `fetch` keyed by URL, fetch-call log as the
navigation observable). Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-main-shape/` on the
laptop (`probe.log` + `src/main-shape-probe.test.ts` in the snapshot).
Controls pass for all four endpoints (valid body → `dataset.hash`
updated / navigation to the real `/edit/<name>` / success button text).

Wrong-shape 200 bodies:

| Endpoint | Body | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/save` | `{}` | returns `{ ok: true }` (fake success) and sets `editorContainer.dataset.hash = "undefined"` — the next save posts `doc_id: "undefined"` |
| `/api/save` | `{ hash: 123, … }` | returns `{ ok: true }`, `dataset.hash = "123"` (silent coercion) |
| `/api/save` | `null` | raw `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'hash')` at `main.ts:1139`, surfaced only as a generic save failure |
| `/api/new` | `{}` or `"abc"` | navigates to `/edit/undefined` |
| `/api/new` | `null` | raw `TypeError` at `main.ts:1179` in the console; the UI silently does nothing |
| `/api/rename` | `{}` | button shows `renamed!` (fake success) and navigates to `/edit/undefined` |
| `/api/rename` | `null` | raw `TypeError` at `main.ts:1298`; button shows generic `error!` |
| `/api/copy` | `{}` | button shows `copied!` (fake success) and navigates to `/edit/undefined` |
| `/api/copy` | `null` | raw `TypeError` at `main.ts:1364`; button shows generic `error!` |

## Why it matters

Save is the editor's core write path: a single wrong-shape 200 both lies
to the user (the file appears saved) and corrupts the in-page state —
`dataset.hash` becomes the literal string `"undefined"`, so every
subsequent save in that session targets a nonexistent document. Create /
rename / copy navigate the user to `/edit/undefined`, a document that
does not exist, after announcing success (`renamed!` / `copied!`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Each of the four responses is validated at runtime before any field is
  used: a non-null object whose `name` (and `hash` for save) are
  non-empty strings; archive fields on rename are `string | null`.
- On a wrong-shape 200, no state is mutated: `dataset.hash` unchanged,
  no navigation, no success button text; the failure is reported through
  the same channel as a non-OK response (save returns `{ ok: false }`,
  rename/copy show `error!`, create logs/shows a create failure).
- Regression tests in the web suite (vitest) drive the real handlers (or
  an extracted response-validation helper used by them) with at least
  `{}`, `null`, a string body, and a numeric-`hash` body per endpoint,
  plus the valid-body controls; the wrong-shape cases fail pre-fix.
- `bun run test` and `bun run typecheck` in `pkgs/id/web` pass (or any
  pre-existing failures are shown to be identical on clean main).

Related: #7831 / #7833 (world host-view/invite, same class), #7823
(image-upload), #7812 (image-browser), #7811 (home feed) — different
modules/endpoints, independent fixes.
