## Problem

id(web/world): the world page shape-trusts both of its HTTP responses — a wrong-shape 200 from `/api/world/host-view` or `/api/world/invite` surfaces raw engine TypeErrors, renders bogus records, or persists a fake invite capability while reporting success.

`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` (origin/main 8728f5c3bf, md5 2c4c46aab13c1bf9be119c0c6f373a5b):

- `:433` — host view: `const result = (await response.json()) as { snapshot?; view?; surface?; records_sequence; records; next_after }` is a bare cast. `result.records` is consumed by `Object.entries(result.records)` (:444) and `result.records_sequence` is read at :441 with no validation. The same file's WebSocket path validates every frame (`isWorldSnapshot`/`isWorldEvent`, :156-175) — the HTTP path validates nothing.
- `:566` — invite: `const result = (await response.json()) as { capability: string; display_name: string }` is a bare cast, and `result.capability` goes straight to `showCapability` (:181-185), which assigns it to the capability input and persists it via `sessionStorage.setItem(storageKey, value)`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, git-archive snapshot of origin/main 8728f5c3bf)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-world-shape/probe.ts` (bun, minimal DOM stub, stub fetch, the real `world.ts` imported from the snapshot; the page's real click handlers driven end to end):

Invite (`POST /api/world/invite`):
- control `{capability: "cap-abc-123", display_name: "guest"}`: OK — capability + sessionStorage = `cap-abc-123`, status "Invite created…"
- `{}`: **fake success** — status "Invite created. Copy it or join this browser.", capability input = `"undefined"`, sessionStorage persists the string `"undefined"` (so the bogus capability survives reload and a later Join sends it as the token)
- `"abc"`: same fake success, `"undefined"` persisted
- `null`: status shows the raw TypeError `null is not an object (evaluating 'result.capability')`
- `{capability: 123}`: status success, capability/sessionStorage = `"123"` (non-string silently coerced)

Host view (`GET /api/world/host-view`):
- control (valid snapshot/view/records page): OK — status "Read-only host view", records rendered
- `null`: status shows the raw TypeError `null is not an object (evaluating 'result.records_sequence')`
- `{}`, `{records: null, …}`, `[]`: status shows the raw TypeError `Object.entries requires that input parameter not be null or undefined`
- `{records: "abc", records_sequence: 1, next_after: null}`: **silently renders bogus records** — records view shows `{"0": "a", "1": "b", "2": "c"}` (per-character entries of the string) with the "Read-only host view" success status

## Why it matters

The invite path is the worst case: a malformed 200 (deploy skew, an error envelope returned with 200, a future server field change) tells the host an invite was created and stores the literal string `undefined` as the guest capability in sessionStorage — the host shares/joins with a credential that was never minted, and the poisoned value persists across reloads. The host view is the admin's read-only window into a world; rendering per-character garbage records as a successful read, or raw engine errors instead of the designed "Host view unavailable" message, breaks the fail-closed discipline the same file already applies to its WebSocket frames and that the sibling pages adopted in #7811/#7812/#7823.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The invite response is validated at the fetch boundary: a non-object body, or a missing/non-string/empty `capability`, fails through the existing error path ("Invite failed" vocabulary) — `showCapability` is never called, nothing is written to sessionStorage, and no success status is shown. `display_name` falls back gracefully when absent/wrong-typed.
- [ ] The host-view response is validated per page before any state is touched: body must be an object, `records` must be a plain object, `records_sequence` a finite number, `next_after` a string or null, and `snapshot` (when present) must satisfy the existing `isWorldSnapshot` guard — a malformed page shows "Host view unavailable" (or the existing designed error vocabulary), never a raw TypeError, and never renders partial/bogus records.
- [ ] Regression tests cover the malformed cases above for both endpoints (null, {}, array, string body, wrong-typed `capability`/`records`) plus the well-formed controls.
- [ ] pkgs/id web suite + typecheck green.

Related: #7811 / #7812 / #7823 (same shape-trust class in sibling id web pages; #7823 fixed by PR #7827 with a `parseUploadResponse` boundary validator — the same pattern applies here). The WebSocket frame paths in this file are already guarded and are out of scope.

# ci(atlas-search): the Rust crate test suites (77 tests — atlas-core parity/stage/shards, atlas-search cli_parity, atlas-embed gate_a) run by no workflow or flake check

## Evidence (verified this run, origin/main @ `c05f2add75`, clean git-archive snapshot)

The suites (all in `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/`):

- `atlas-core/tests/parity.rs` (461 lines), `atlas-core/tests/stage.rs` (204 lines), `atlas-core/tests/shards.rs`
- `atlas-search/tests/cli_parity.rs` (461 lines, plus a `golden/` fixture dir)
- `atlas-embed/tests/gate_a.rs` (246 lines)

No venue runs them:

- The repo's own test-suite registry (`.github/test-suite-registry.json`, row `atlas-search.rust`) records exactly this: status `uncovered`, reason "Flake checks.default exists, but no workflow invocation was confirmed; Phase 2 follow-up must be filed." Its Phase 2 pointer is #6185, which is now CLOSED — and no follow-up for this row was ever filed (cf. sibling rows that did get theirs: auto-format → #7664, meta-exporter → #6344).
- `grep "cargo test" .github/workflows/*.yml` has no atlas-search hit. The nearest workflow, `fleet-search-parity-guard.yml`, runs two bash scripts (a source-file identity guard, #5920) — it never compiles or runs the Rust tests.
- `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix:51` sets `checks.default = atlas-search;` — the package build, not `cargo test`. There is no justfile in `pkgs/atlas-search`, and the root `justfile`, `flake.nix`, and `lib/default.nix` contain no atlas-search test reference.

Hand verification (laptop, origin/main snapshot, 2026-11-08): the suites are healthy and worth wiring —

- `cargo test -p atlas-core -p atlas-proto` → 68 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p atlas-search --test cli_parity` → 8 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p atlas-embed --test gate_a` → 1 passed, 1 ignored, 0 failed

Dedup: title search for atlas-search tests returns only #7683 — the Worker vitest suite (TypeScript, `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/`), a different suite that this issue does not cover. #6185 (closed) is the registry contract itself; its per-row follow-ups are filed individually.

## Why it matters

`parity.rs` and `cli_parity.rs` are the behavioral half of the atlas-search ↔ fleet-search byte-parity contract (#5433): the bash parity guard proves two source files are identical, but only these tests prove the writers actually render byte-identical envelopes and that atlas-core staging/sharding behaves. Today a regression in any of that passes every CI check in the repo and is found only when someone happens to run `cargo test` by hand in `pkgs/atlas-search` — the exact failure mode #6185's contract was written to end.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A venue runs the atlas-search Rust suites on PR and/or main tiers: `cargo test` covering atlas-core, atlas-proto, atlas-search (incl. `cli_parity`), and atlas-embed (`gate_a`) — e.g. a real test check in `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix` invoked by an active workflow, or a dedicated workflow job.
- [ ] The venue's green run is observed and linked in the closing comment (a check that was never triggered does not count).
- [ ] The registry row `atlas-search.rust` in `.github/test-suite-registry.json` is updated to `mapped` (or its status corrected) in the same change.
- [ ] The one `#[ignore]`d gate_a test is either run by the venue or its ignore reason is documented in the PR.

# ci(goreleaser): the goreleaser workflow can never cut a release — its tag-push trigger was removed, it is disabled_manually, and its non-snapshot release branch is dead code

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ `a6ad4bc9af`)

`.github/workflows/goreleaser.yml`:

- The `on:` block (lines 3–6) is only `workflow_dispatch:`. The pre-sweep trigger was `push: tags: ["*"]` — removed by the Nov 4 sweep commit `5a94833ea3` ("ci: remove push/pull_request triggers (dispatch/schedule only)"), verified via `git show 5a94833ea3 -- .github/workflows/goreleaser.yml`.
- The GoReleaser step itself still contracts the old venue (lines 86–88): the comment says "Tag pushes cut the real release; manual dispatch runs a snapshot build instead", and the args expression is `github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'release --snapshot --clean' || 'release --clean'`. With dispatch as the only possible event, the non-snapshot `release --clean` branch can never execute — it is dead code, and a real tag push today triggers nothing at all.
- The concurrency group (line ~13) also still keys on `github.event_name == 'push'`, another unreachable branch.
- Actions API: workflow id 75152347 state is `disabled_manually`, so even the surviving snapshot/dispatch path does not run until the workflow is re-enabled. Newest run is 2026-10-21 (workflow_dispatch, success) — before the sweep.
- `.github/ci-policy.md:223` still names goreleaser as the standing example of the tag-trigger exception to the push/pull_request dedup rule: "push restricted to branches: [main] (plus tags where already applicable, e.g. goreleaser)" — policy assumes the tag trigger exists; the workflow no longer has it.
- The release target is live code, not a retired package: `.goreleaser.yaml` at repo root builds `pkgs/graph` (the workflow's setup-go step, line 78, points at `pkgs/graph/go.mod`, the fix from closed #344, whose title is literally "goreleaser workflow fails in setup on the next tag push"). The next tag push was expected — it now silently publishes nothing.
- Sibling ruling: closed #344 and the mcpx-release filing #7807 establish that a release workflow whose tag trigger is gone is a defect, not a settled dispatch-only policy. #6187 (venue-reality audit) explicitly scopes itself to *test* venues and says non-test disabled workflows "(goreleaser, mcpx-release, id-bench, etc.) are inventoried for the record only; their dispositions are not this design's to make" — so #6187 does not cover this disposition.

Dedup: searched open + closed for "goreleaser workflow", "goreleaser tag trigger disabled". #344 (closed) was the go-version-file setup failure, a different defect already fixed. #1881 is the mcpx release design, not this workflow. #405/#394 (closed) are action-pin bumps. No open issue tracks the goreleaser tag-trigger loss.

## Why it matters

This is the repo's only GoReleaser release path for pkgs/graph. Anyone pushing a version tag (the repo carries v1.x tags and #344 was fixed precisely in anticipation of "the next tag push") gets silence: no release, no failure, no artifact — the worst failure mode for a release pipeline, discovered only when a user asks where the release went. The workflow file also misleads reviewers: its comments and args expression describe a tag-driven release venue that does not exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disposition decided and implemented: restore the `push: tags: ["*"]` trigger so tag pushes run `release --clean`, or — if tag releases are deliberately retired — remove the dead non-snapshot branch, the push-keyed concurrency disjunct, and the "tag pushes cut the real release" comment, and name the replacement release mechanism.
- [ ] Workflow re-enabled (no longer `disabled_manually`) if the tag venue is restored.
- [ ] Verification observed and linked in the closing comment: a dispatch snapshot run green after re-enablement, plus (on the next real tag) a non-snapshot release run — or, for the retire disposition, a grep-clean workflow with no unreachable event branches.
- [ ] ci-policy.md:223 and the workflow agree about whether goreleaser is a tag-triggered workflow.

# ci(mcpx-release): release workflow lost its mcpx/v* tag trigger in the Nov 4 sweep and is disabled_manually — tagging a release now silently publishes nothing

## Evidence (verified this run, main `a9483c30d1`)

**Header vs. triggers.** `.github/workflows/mcpx-release.yml`'s header (lines 3–17) defines the release contract: it "Cuts an mcpx release from the monorepo (decision 0005 …; #1881)", producing binaries + checksums (channel 1), exercising the curl|sh installer (channel 2), and building the container image (channel 3), "publishing the image to GHCR on a tag". Because mcpx lives in a monorepo, "tags are `mcpx/vX.Y.Z`, and this workflow triggers on exactly that prefix." The `on:` block (:21–27) is now only `workflow_dispatch:` — the Nov 4 sweep commit `5a94833ea3` ("ci: remove push/pull_request triggers (dispatch/schedule only)") deleted exactly:

```diff
 on:
-  push:
-    tags:
-      - "mcpx/v*"
   workflow_dispatch:
```

A sweep whose stated scope was test/CI triggers removed a *release* trigger. The publish machinery is still in the file and now unreachable: the steps/jobs at :251 and :295 are conditioned on `github.event_name == 'push'`, an event this workflow can no longer receive.

**Enablement.** Actions API: workflow state `disabled_manually` — so even the header's fallback proof path ("A manual run (workflow_dispatch) is a snapshot … That run is the proof the release path works, and it is how a person checks a change before tagging") cannot be run. Newest runs: 2026-10-30T19:12:42Z (push, failure) and 2026-10-30T12:15:52Z (workflow_dispatch, success). The only `mcpx/v*` tag on the remote is `mcpx/v0.1.0`.

**Why it matters.** The failure mode is silent at the worst possible moment: the next person who tags `mcpx/v0.2.0` will get no workflow run, no release, no GHCR image, and no error — the tag simply sits there. The version-agreement guard the header describes ("A tag that disagrees with [pkgs/mcpx/VERSION] is refused before anything is built") also never fires. Unlike the dead test venues (e.g. #7794/#7795), nothing else watches this path: no other workflow builds or publishes mcpx releases.

**Dedup.** #1881 is the release-artifacts/install-channels feature tracker this workflow implements — it does not track the trigger/enablement loss. #1865/#1907 are docs release-stamping items. #6187 is the gated venue-reality audit and executes no dispositions. Sibling Nov 4 sweep venue losses filed separately: #7794 (mcpx.yml), #7795 (mcpx-test.yml), #7801 (mcpx-conformance), #7803 (mcpx-tier2-containers).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disposition recorded on this issue: restore the `push: tags: ["mcpx/v*"]` trigger + re-enable, or an explicit decision that mcpx releases move to a different, named mechanism (with the header updated to match).
- [ ] If restored: `on:` contains the tag trigger again and the workflow state is `active`.
- [ ] A `workflow_dispatch` snapshot run on current main completes, exercising the build path (all three channels in snapshot mode) — the header's own proof the release path works.
- [ ] The push-conditioned publish steps (:251, :295) are reachable again, or removed with the mechanism change.
- [ ] Workflow header comment matches the actual triggers and enablement.

# ci(mcpx-docs): the mcpx docs workflow can never do what its own header and job conditions promise — dispatch-only triggers, disabled_manually, and dead PR/push-conditioned steps

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ `6115bef007ba`)

`.github/workflows/mcpx-docs.yml`:

- Header (lines 7–11) promises: "Pull requests build .#mcpx-docs and upload the rendered site as an ordinary build artifact… Pushes to main and manual dispatches deploy the same build to Pages."
- The `on:` block (lines 24–25) is only `workflow_dispatch:` — the push/pull_request triggers were removed by the Nov 4 sweep commit `5a94833ea3` ("ci: remove push/pull_request triggers (dispatch/schedule only)"), and no schedule was added in their place.
- Two steps/jobs are conditioned on events that can now never occur, i.e. dead code inside the workflow itself:
  - Build job: "Upload site artifact (PR builds only)" has `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` — unreachable.
  - Deploy job: `if: github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch')` — the `push` disjunct is unreachable; only a manual dispatch on main can deploy.
- Actions API: workflow state is `disabled_manually`, so even the surviving dispatch path does not run until the workflow is re-enabled. Newest run is 2026-11-03 (push, cancelled); the last successful deploy run was 2026-11-02.
- The book kept changing after the venue died: e.g. `30c2611fd5` "docs(mcpx): show codemode:false opt-out…" (#7075) and the #6116 operator-docs merge `3f3b33dccc` landed after 2026-11-03, none of it built, artifact-checked, or deployed. The published Pages site is therefore stale relative to main, and a docs change that breaks `nix build .#mcpx-docs` would be caught nowhere.
- ci-policy.md:251 still lists mcpx-docs.yml among the workflows whose build/check is "authoritative" after the Magic Nix Cache step — a build that never runs.

Dedup: searched open + closed for "mcpx-docs.yml", "mcpx docs workflow dispatch-only", and the Pages deploy. #1941 (closed) built this workflow; #1890/#1943 track the site platform/subdomain, not the trigger loss. The generic venue audits #6187 and #7089 do not name mcpx-docs in their bodies (checked this run) — this is the specific, separately-fixable consequence for the docs site, in the same family as #7794 (mcpx.yml) and #7716 (cf-container-hello), which were filed individually. Not a duplicate of #7794: different workflow, different jobs (book build + Pages deploy, not tests), different fix surface.

## Why it matters

The mcpx book is the project's public documentation site (#1941, Approach C). Since 2026-11-03 it has had zero automated verification and zero deploys: merged docs changes silently never reach the site, and a broken docs build would only be discovered by a human remembering to dispatch a workflow that is currently disabled anyway. The workflow file also misleads reviewers — its header and its PR/push-conditioned steps describe a venue that does not exist.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disposition decided and implemented: restore `pull_request` (build + artifact, no deploy) and `push` to main (deploy) triggers matching the header, or — if dispatch-only is the intended end state — rewrite the header, remove/condition the dead PR/push steps honestly, and name the replacement deploy mechanism.
- [ ] Workflow re-enabled (no longer `disabled_manually`) if any automatic venue is restored.
- [ ] A green run from the restored automatic venue is observed and linked in the closing comment (a PR build artifact run, or a push-to-main deploy run that updates the Pages site).
- [ ] The deployed Pages site reflects current main docs (e.g. the #7075 codemode page change is present).

```
-export const OPERATION_FINGERPRINT = "0ac07ddbbc06f9c28a106e4e26d701a31e6cfaa37b17646b7911f165acb0af2e"
+export const OPERATION_FINGERPRINT = "d790442820a73745cf631b628d8cad6b1ee57177f8c480c15bb3031c2074b5eb"
```

The emitted `OPS` table is unchanged, so a daemon-table input to the fingerprint (op metadata the table does not print) changed in some merged PR without the regeneration landing — unidentifiable from the artifact alone, which is exactly what this guard exists to catch. It cannot catch it in CI: the test's venues are mcpx.yml's `basic: test` job and mcpx-test.yml's unit leg, both dead (filed as #7794 and #7795 this run).

## Evidence (verified this run, main `d222177982`)

**In-file triggers vs. promises.** `.github/workflows/mcpx-test.yml`'s whole `on:` block is `workflow_dispatch:`. Its header (lines 3–36) says the opposite: the serial `go test ./...` in mcpx.yml "is complemented here by a sharded suite that **also runs on PRs**", with init generating an e2e matrix from the test names in the tree, unit and lint as their own legs, and ci-ok aggregating everything. `.github/ci-policy.md` line 176 assigns "mcpx test (#1998)": PR tier = "init + unit + lint + 6 static e2e shards + ci-ok (PR tier, non-draft PRs)", main tier = "same full sharded suite on push to main". Neither tier can occur.

**Enablement.** Actions API: `disabled_manually`. Newest runs: 2026-11-03T01:59:50Z (`workflow_dispatch`, cancelled) and 2026-11-02T21:40:05Z (push, failure). No completed run since, while `pkgs/mcpx` merged dozens of changes (e.g. #1954, #7041, #4354, #7558 below).

**The machinery is healthy — it is the venue that is dead.** The init leg's exact command, run by hand on the laptop at `d222177982`:

```
python3 pkgs/mcpx/scripts/ci/e2e-shard-packer.py \
  --tests-dir pkgs/mcpx/internal/e2e \
  --timings pkgs/mcpx/scripts/ci/e2e-timings.json \
  --target-seconds 170 --max-shards 6
→ e2e tests: 360 in 6 shards … exit 0
```

The packer's coverage self-check (every `func Test` in internal/e2e dealt exactly once) passes; 360 e2e tests are being dealt to shards that never run.

**A merged change depends on this venue.** `ad374773aa` (#7558) "mcpx: clear all golangci findings and make the lint leg blocking" — the lint leg it made blocking is `basic: mcpx-test lint` in this workflow (gofmt + `go vet ./...`). A blocking leg in a workflow that cannot trigger blocks nothing. The unit leg also carries the affected-test selector regressions (`test_affected_untracked.py`) and the non-e2e `go test` package set; the plugin-ts leg carries the pinned plugin lint/type-check (#5151).

**The unit leg is already red on main — the dead venue is masking real failures.** The unit leg's exact command (`go test` over `go list ./...` minus `internal/e2e`), run by hand on the laptop at `d222177982`, exits 1 with four failing packages: `internal/api` (TestPluginOpsAreGenerated — ops.gen.ts stale; filed separately this run), `internal/conformance` (TestMatrix stale doc; TestMessagesClient extension declarations; TestStatefulServer `expiresAt` frames rejected by the strict 2025-11-25 schema; TestUtilitiesServer completion not advertised), `internal/settings` (four guard tests: undeclared env read `MCPX_ADAPTER_DECLARATION_SHA256` at routes_settings.go:950, undeclared ScriptEnv setters, `proto.*` settings without effect probes, environment.md stale), and `internal/config` (TestServerKeysAnotherHostWritesAreRecordedNotRefused — possibly the host-config hermeticity class of #7686; flagged, not adjudicated here). The settings and conformance failures are the family tracked by #2716, which has been open while its only CI venue is dead. Everything else in the leg passed (including internal/cli 89s, internal/daemon 87s).

**Dedup.** #6906 and #6822 are defects *inside* the packer (shard assignment; crash shapes) — they assume the venue runs. #6092 covers the v2 plugin bun suite's venue, not this one. #6929/#6953 are the sibling Nov 4 sweep filings for other workflows. #6187 is the gated venue audit and executes no dispositions.

# ci(mcpx): mcpx.yml lost its push/pull_request triggers in the Nov 4 sweep and is disabled_manually — the `basic: test` job, plugin-sync guard, and nightly stress never run, though ci-policy assigns mcpx PR + main tiers

## Evidence (verified this run, main `d222177982`)

**In-file triggers.** `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml`'s whole `on:` block is:

```yaml
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "23 3 * * *"   # nightly full-suite stress (#1973)
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs: { budget_seconds: … }
```

There is no `push` and no `pull_request`. Yet the jobs are written for exactly those events:

- `plugin-sync` job: `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (its comment: "The workflow-level pull_request paths include pkgs/mcpx/** and .opencode/plugin/**") — can never fire.
- `test` job (`basic: test`): `if: github.event_name == 'push'`, with the comment "Original coverage was push-only; the pull_request/schedule triggers above exist for the flake-policy jobs (#1973)" — the triggers it names do not exist.
- The concurrency comment describes push-run and PR-run grouping in detail for runs that cannot occur; the vendorhash-repair bot job and the `budget` job likewise key off push/PR events.
- The header comment still presents this as the workflow that "Builds mcpx on every change to it".

**Enablement.** The Actions API reports `mcpx.yml` as `disabled_manually`, so even the in-file nightly schedule cannot fire. Newest run of any kind: 2026-11-02T21:40:05Z (push, failure, `b0495938d9`). Nothing since — while `pkgs/mcpx` kept merging, e.g. `f5f591cd9a` (defaults before broker validation), `a95ea04973` (#1954 form-answer validation), `4fe0262b97` (#7041 task grace expiry), `ad374773aa` (#7558 golangci cleanup), `45649657e4` (#4354 bounded body reads).

**Policy disagreement.** `.github/ci-policy.md` names `mcpx` in the merge-required workflow list (lines 38–39) and its tier table (line 175) assigns mcpx "unchanged path-gated PR checks" plus "push to main". The file delivers neither. This is the same Nov 4 sweep pattern already filed per-venue for the sibling guards: #6929 (mcpx-fix-test-guard) and #6953 (opencode-config-guard); #6981 covers mcpx-nixbuild, not this workflow. The #6187 venue audit is gated on a #6185 ruling and executes no dispositions.

**What the dead `test` job carries** (mcpx.yml, from line ~110): the plugin-sync `diff -r` guard, the darwin compile gate (#1988), `go mod tidy -diff`, the Python contract suites (`scripts/test_gotest_report.py`, `scripts/test_conformance_record.py`), and the serial `go test ./...` suite with `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=deno,bun,node,python3`.

**Demonstrated consequence.** The plugin-sync guard lives only in this workflow (grep: `.github/workflows/*.yml`, `flake.nix`, `justfile` — no other site). Because it never runs, the dogfood `.opencode/plugin` copy drifted a third time — filed as #7791 (daemon.ts pre-#3490, biome.json missing; history #314, #2795).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disposition recorded on this issue: restore triggers + re-enable, or fold the carried checks into named active venues.
- [ ] If restored: `on:` carries path-gated `pull_request` and `push` to main consistent with ci-policy line 175, the workflow state is `active`, and the schedule leg stays.
- [ ] A run on current main executes the `test` job end to end (plugin-sync diff, darwin gate, tidy check, Python contract suites, `go test ./...` all actually run); failures it surfaces are fixed or filed and linked.
- [ ] The plugin-sync guard verifiably runs for a PR touching `pkgs/mcpx/**` or `.opencode/plugin/**` (or its new venue is named and shown running).
- [ ] Workflow header comments match the actual triggers and enablement.

Implementation step 4 of the design in #5683 (design record: `doc/2026-11-08_design_id5683.md` §5, PR #7781).

## Scope

Sanctions boundaries as **data, not code**:

- `ListVersion { id, source, effective_from, effective_to, entries, signature }`; decisions log the list version applied so past decisions are reproducible.
- Operator-supplied lists; a shipped list is a labelled starting point, not legal advice. No external feed fetching (design §11).
- Declared scope of interaction (signup, login, world membership, blobs, federation transit, relay transit) — an empty enforcement list means *not covered* and must be stated.
- **Grandfathering:** an entry appearing flags existing subjects for review rather than cutting them off; an entry removed clears them. Both logged.
- Exception records for false positives (name collisions, dual citizens, residents vs citizens, travellers) and an appeal path in the user-facing message.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Property test: adding a list entry never removes existing access without a recorded review flag.
- [ ] A deny on a sanctions boundary always names an appeal path.
- [ ] Decisions reference the exact list version applied.

Design: `doc/2026-11-08_design_id5683.md` §5. Parent: #5683.

Implementation step 3 of the design in #5683 (design record: `doc/2026-11-08_design_id5683.md` §4, PR #7781).

## Scope

Public IP as weak evidence:

- Derive country/region verdicts, boundary verdicts (`VerdictOnly`), and — only when a scope explicitly enables it with a stated retention window — the raw IP.
- Short default retention (connection lifetime plus a bounded window).
- Explicit X-Forwarded-For trust configuration, **off by default**; an untrusted header is ignored, not believed.
- Contradiction handling: declaration admits + IP contradicts → `warn` by default; never deny existing access on IP alone.

## Hard constraints

- **No weak signal removes access a subject already has** (design §3.4).
- Relay/bridge paths: the visible IP is the relay's — IP evidence is structurally unavailable there and must be treated as unknown, not as the user's address.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Property test: IP-derived evidence alone never yields a deny that removes existing access.
- [ ] Untrusted X-Forwarded-For is ignored (test).

Implementation step 2 of the design in #5683 (design record: `doc/2026-11-08_design_id5683.md` §2.3, §2.4, §7, PR #7781).

## Scope

The `BoundaryDeclaration` record and its invariants:

- Content-addressed id; every change is a new monotone version (no in-place edits of a live declaration).
- `enabled` is true only by explicit admin/user action — the only default is `false`.
- Reject at declaration time: `enabled: true` with empty `enforcement` (a boundary nobody enforces is a false promise).
- Four failure behaviours only: `deny` / `warn` / `step-up` / `quarantine`.
- Composability: intersection of server ∧ world ∧ user preference; a user preference can never widen a parent scope.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A declaration with `enabled: true` and no enforcement point is rejected with a named error.
- [ ] Property test: `effective(server, world, user)` is a subset of `server` for all inputs (narrowing only).
- [ ] A conflict yields a deny naming the denying scope, never a silent merge.

title: opencode.service stays down: restart attempt exits 0 and systemd never retries

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## What happened (2026-11-08, laptop `amd`)

The standing OpenCode server (`opencode.service`, user unit, build 2.0.30+8ed9d6c, generation 548 pin) went down and stayed down for ~15 minutes until a human-path manual `systemctl --user start` restored it.

Timeline (all CST, from `journalctl --user -u opencode.service`):

- 12:53:05 — main process pid 2563072 exited with code 130 (SIGINT-style shutdown) after 11h37m uptime. Not OOM (no SIGKILL), not a systemd stop (would be SIGTERM), no NixOS switch (generation 548 untouched since 01:16), no sudo command in the journal at that minute. The sender of the SIGINT is not identifiable from the journal.
- 12:53:06 — systemd `Restart=on-failure` restarted the unit once (restart counter 1). The replacement process (pid 3770810) exited with status 0/SUCCESS after 731ms, producing no log output at all (no "server listening" line).
- Because the exit was "clean", systemd made no further restart attempt. Port 13420 had no listener and `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` was absent from then on.
- ~13:00 — a further process on a newer build (2.0.30+ae632cd, pid 3802432, per session-minder observation) wrote the service file, then exited and removed it. Also not a recovery.
- 13:01:26 — pm-aggregator reported "OpenCode server unreachable; attention empty"; the 13:01 collector wrote 0 sessions.
- 13:08:47 — manual `systemctl --user start opencode.service` with the unchanged unit/binary succeeded immediately: pid 3842555, listening on 127.0.0.1:13420, `/api/info` reports 2.0.30+8ed9d6c, sessions list normally. The 13:11 collector wrote 60 sessions again.

## The defect

Whatever made the first restart attempt exit 0 instantly, the unit's restart policy turns a transient failure into a standing outage:

1. `Restart=on-failure` does not retry a process that exits 0 — and this binary can apparently exit 0 without serving (silent, sub-second).
2. There is no second-chance mechanism (no `RestartSec` loop, no watchdog, no StartLimit burst configured to catch it) and nothing alerted on "unit inactive + port dark" — the fleet noticed via the session minder, not via the service's own supervision.

## Suggested fixes (either or both)

- Change the unit to `Restart=always` (with a sane `RestartSec`), or keep `on-failure` and add a watchdog timer that checks the port/service file and restarts + alerts when the unit is inactive.
- Investigate why a fresh `serve --service` invocation can exit 0 in <1s with no log output when the standing server has just died (singleton handoff? service-file state? DB lock?) — that behavior is the trigger; the restart policy is why it became an outage.

## Notes

- Two stale `serve --service` processes from Nov 06 (build 2.0.30+1add729, pids 331379/331557) are still running on ports 13498/13499. They did not block the successful 13:08 start, but their role in the restart attempt's instant exit is unproven either way.
- `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` is 21.4 GB — noted in passing, not part of this incident.


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related step/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

body:
## What

`.github/workflows/repo-universe-tests.yml` — the workflow that runs the scripts/fleet/repo-universe regression suites (`test_generate.py` + `test_check_issues.py`) — declares one trigger policy in its header and implements another:

- Header (`.github/workflows/repo-universe-tests.yml:21`): "Trigger policy matches the house pattern since 5a94833ea3: **dispatch/schedule only**, no push/pull_request triggers."
- Actual trigger block: `on:` contains **only `workflow_dispatch:` — there is no `schedule:` trigger at all**.

So nothing automatic ever runs the suites. The workflow is `active` in the Actions API (not disabled), but a dispatch-only workflow runs only when a human remembers to dispatch it. (Sibling instance for a different workflow/suite: the github-backup-tests workflow has the identical header-vs-trigger mismatch — filed separately this run, since the suites, owners, and fixes are independent.)

## Verified this run (laptop, main a565493a34)

- Actions API: workflow state `active`; newest run is **2026-11-05T04:29:59Z** (`workflow_dispatch`, success). No run of any kind since.
- Merged repo-universe changes since that last run — every one a validation/gate fix of exactly the kind these suites pin:
  - `67674b9774` fix(repo-universe): validate full_name/html_url/fork fields at the entry gate (#6814)
  - `03c31fb331` fix(repo-universe): validate issue fields in check_issues (#6757)
  - `835048ed55` fix(repo-universe): name wrong-shape enumeration entries instead of crashing (#6716)
  - `d44e3b883c` fix(repo-universe): require --forks-org-json in offline mode (#6612)
  - `6fa0aa40a9` fix(repo-universe): wrong-shape fetch/state JSON becomes per-repo ERRORs (#6652)
  - `af06baabb0` repo-universe: enumerate developing-today-forks org alongside developing-today (#5615)
- Hand run on the laptop, exactly as the workflow runs it (`python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/fleet/repo-universe -p 'test_*.py'`): **36 tests, OK**. The suite has also grown since the workflow header was written (header says 16 tests; 36 now), so the unverified surface is larger than the header describes. The production systemd timer runs `check_issues.py` itself but never its tests (per the workflow header), so a generator/checker regression surfaces as a corrupt inventory or a wrong delta report, not as a red test.

## Why it matters

- The header comment is the record a future maintainer (or an audit like #7089/#7091) reads to learn the intended venue; it says a schedule exists. It does not, so the suites' coverage is illusory: six validation fixes merged after 2026-11-05 have had no CI verification at all.
- This is the same failure shape as #7715/#7716/#7663 (suites whose only venue silently stopped exercising them while the code kept changing), except here the workflow is not even disabled — it is simply never triggered, which makes the gap easier to miss.

## Distinct from

- #5945 (closed): the original "run by no workflow" filing that created this workflow. The workflow now exists; this issue is that its stated schedule does not.
- #7089/#7091: the ci-policy agreement audits — this filing is the concrete verified instance for this workflow's header-vs-trigger mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The workflow's implemented triggers match its stated policy: either a real `schedule:` trigger is added (with a cadence named in the header), or the header is corrected to dispatch-only **and** another automatic venue (e.g. path-gated push-to-main) runs the suites — a comment-only fix that leaves the suites unexercised does not close this.
- [ ] A run triggered by the new automatic venue is observed green on current main (link the run in the closing comment).
- [ ] The header's test count (16) is corrected to the suite's actual size, or the count is removed so it cannot go stale again.
- [ ] The registry row for these suites in `.github/test-suite-registry.json` reflects the real venue/trigger after the fix.

(One transient `test_fetch_mirrors.py` failure appeared in a first sequential run and did not reproduce standalone or on the repeat — not claimed as a suite failure; it does underline that the suite currently gets no regular exercise.)

## Why it matters

- The header comment is the record a future maintainer (or an audit like #7089/#7091) reads to learn the intended venue; it says a schedule exists. It does not, so the suite's coverage is illusory: regressions in clone/reconcile/drain/deploy safety code merged after 2026-11-05 have had no CI verification at all.
- This is the same failure shape as #7715/#7716/#7663 (suites whose only venue silently stopped exercising them while the code kept changing), except here the workflow is not even disabled — it is simply never triggered, which makes the gap easier to miss.

## Distinct from

- #6085: the github-backup **Worker** vitest suite (`worker/test/index.test.mjs`) run by no workflow — a different suite; this issue is the Python regression suite whose workflow exists but never fires.
- #7089/#7091: the ci-policy agreement audits — this filing is the concrete verified instance for this workflow's header-vs-trigger mismatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The workflow's implemented triggers match its stated policy: either a real `schedule:` trigger is added (with a cadence named in the header), or the header is corrected to dispatch-only **and** another automatic venue (e.g. path-gated push-to-main) runs the suite — a comment-only fix that leaves the suite unexercised does not close this.
- [ ] A run triggered by the new automatic venue is observed green on current main (link the run in the closing comment).
- [ ] The registry row for this suite in `.github/test-suite-registry.json` reflects the real venue/trigger after the fix.

body:
## Summary

The zero-message verification in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (prompt.md step 1a, the #4758 / design #4912 recovery rule) calls an endpoint the v2 server does not have:

```
claimant.py:253  GET http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/<id>/messages
```

The live server serves the **singular** `/message` (returning `{"data": [...], "cursor": ...}`). `/messages` is a **404 with an empty body** — verified on `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/message   -> 200  data[50], cursor
GET /api/session/ses_e5e441ca753ffdMse0Sd5IZ977/messages  -> 404  (empty body)
```

`poll.py` and the fire probe already use the singular form (`fire-probe.py` `session_messages()`); only `claimant.py` — and the stub in `test/test_claimant.py:75`, which pins the wrong path — use `/messages`.

## Why this is fail-open, not merely inert

The block at `claimant.py:250-265` is:

```python
messages_response = subprocess.run(["curl", "-s", "-m", "5",
    f"http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/{session_id}/messages"], ...)
if messages_response.returncode == 0:
    message_count = len(json.loads(messages_response.stdout or "[]"))
    if message_count == 0:
        recovery_candidates.append(...)
```

`curl -s` exits **0** on a 404, and the 404 body is empty, so:

1. `returncode == 0` → true,
2. `stdout or "[]"` → `"[]"` (the `or` was written for a timeout producing empty output),
3. `message_count == 0` → **every** stuck-bound row passes the zero-message gate.

The session GET immediately above it has the same shape (`claimant.py:217-231`): an unauthenticated `curl -s` returns a 401 `{"_tag": ...}` body, which is parsed and has no `id`, so the session is treated as **gone**. Chained together in live mode, the step-1 path is:

session GET → 401 body, no `id` → "gone" → attempts remain → messages read → 404 empty body → "0 messages" → recovery candidate → `DELETE` (401, `returncode == 0`, recorded as success — #7367) → `bind --launched-by opencode-claimant-recovery:zero-message-deleted` clears both bindings.

That is precisely the ordering the packet's step 1b forbids: an un-deleted session holding messages, with its binding cleared, leaving the task launchable for a second session while the first may still be alive. Today the only thing preventing it is that `supervision_step`'s candidate list comes from `repo-queue list` parsed as JSON, which fails (#7325), so the list is empty. The safety is incidental, not structural.

## Not covered by the open issues

- **#7367** (open) covers the missing Basic-auth header and "returncode is not a success test" for the delete. It does not cover the wrong path: with auth fixed, `/messages` still 404s and the empty-body `or "[]"` still reads as zero messages.
- **#7356** (open) covers `launch_step` never sending the prompt.
- **#4758** is closed against the rule's design, not against this implementation.

## Fix direction

1. One transport helper (per #7367) with a **path** constant, using `GET /api/session/<id>/message` and reading `data` from the envelope.
2. Treat an empty body, a non-2xx status, or a body that is not a message list as **unknown**, never as zero: the step-1a rule already says "if the message read is unavailable/incomplete, treat the state as unknown … leave it bound and stop". The current `stdout or "[]"` inverts that.
3. `test/test_claimant.py:75` must stub the singular path, and the fail-closed test should assert that a 404/empty messages read emits **no** `bind` argv and leaves the binding intact (it currently stubs an empty-body-free `"[]"`, so it cannot fail).

## Acceptance

- With the stub transport returning 404 + empty body for the messages read (and a live session object for the per-id GET), no recovery `bind` is emitted and no `DELETE` is issued.
- With the stub returning `{"data": [ ... 50 messages ... ]}`, no recovery candidate is produced.
- With the stub returning `{"data": []}` and every other stuck-bound fact true, the DELETE and atomic recovery `bind` are emitted, in that order.
- `grep -rn '/messages' pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` returns nothing outside the retired implementation docs (README.md:96, IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKLIST.md:206 also name the wrong path).

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow, `#3026` slice 1). Shadow report: `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/shadow-fire-20261108T161653Z.json`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The zero-message gate in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` queries the endpoint the v2 server actually serves (singular `/message`), matching `poll.py` and `fire-probe.py`.
- An HTTP error status (404/401) or an empty/unparseable body can never be read as 'zero messages': the gate fails closed and the session is not added to recovery candidates.
- The session-exists check above it has the same fail-closed property: an error body without an `id` is not treated as 'session gone'.
- The stub in `test/test_claimant.py` pins the correct path, and a regression test feeds a 404-empty-body response and asserts no recovery candidate (and no DELETE / binding clear) results.

# ci(mod-tidy): the Go Mod Tidy workflow never runs — dispatch-only in-file and disabled_manually, while ci-policy still assigns it PR + main tiers

## Summary

`.github/workflows/mod-tidy.yml` (job `basic: Go module tidy`, the tidy guard for
`pkgs/graph/go.mod`/`go.sum`) cannot run at all:

- In-file it declares exactly one trigger, `workflow_dispatch`
  (`.github/workflows/mod-tidy.yml:4`).
- The Actions API reports the workflow `disabled_manually`, so even a manual
  dispatch cannot run it until it is re-enabled.
- Its newest run is 2026-10-30T08:23:29Z (push, success) — nothing since.

Meanwhile `.github/ci-policy.md:175` (tier-assignment table) still assigns
mod-tidy "unchanged path-gated PR checks (already PR-tier weight)" in the PR
tier and "push to main" in the main tier. Neither tier can ever fire.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08 on laptop primary at 3762e65642)

- `.github/workflows/mod-tidy.yml:4` — `on:` contains only `workflow_dispatch:`.
- The workflow body still carries steps for the events it can no longer
  receive: "Verify tidy changes are committed" gated
  `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` (mod-tidy.yml:32) and "Commit tidy
  changes on main" gated `if: github.event_name == 'push'` (mod-tidy.yml:41).
  Both are dead code under the current trigger set.
- Actions API: `GET /repos/developing-today/code/actions/workflows/mod-tidy.yml`
  → `state: "disabled_manually"`; runs list newest-first starts at
  2026-10-30T08:23:29Z (push/success), then 2026-10-29 — no runs in November.
- Trigger history: 285e425b77 ("ci: no PR triggers") removed the PR trigger and
  ff989c8bfa ("fix(ci): disable push triggers on auto-format and mod-tidy
  maintenance workflows") removed the push trigger. The deliberate-disable
  commit makes restore-vs-retire a real decision, not an accident to silently
  revert — but the policy table was never updated to match either way.
- Unlike the test-suite venues, mod-tidy appears nowhere in
  `.github/test-suite-registry.json` (it is a tidy guard, not a test suite), so
  the #6187 venue-reality audit does not dispose of it. Sibling filings for the
  same Nov-4-sweep pattern: #6929 (mcpx fix-test guard), #6953
  (opencode-config-guard), #6959 (production-line-guard), #6981 (go-module
  builds), #7715 (lab-ops-hub — the other un-disposed member of the same
  ci-policy.md:175 row).

## Why it matters

`pkgs/graph`'s go.mod/go.sum tidiness is currently verified by nothing. The
repo has been bitten by exactly this drift before (#347: go.mod/go.sum not
tidy, recorded-indirect mismatch; #349: modules with no tidy guard drift
silently). The guard's two behaviors — fail a PR that leaves tidy changes
uncommitted, and auto-commit tidy fixes on main — are both unreachable, and
the dead event-gated steps make the file read as if they still work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A disposition is chosen and recorded on this issue: restore, retire, or
      fold the tidy check into another workflow that actually runs.
- [ ] If restore: triggers match the ci-policy tier assignment (path-gated
      `pull_request` + `push` to main), the workflow is re-enabled
      (`disabled_manually` cleared), and an observed run exists.
- [ ] If retire or fold in: `.github/workflows/mod-tidy.yml` and the
      ci-policy.md:175 row are updated in the same change so policy and
      reality agree, and the replacement venue (if any) is named.
- [ ] Either way, ci-policy.md no longer assigns tiers to a workflow that
      cannot run.

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.description: Package/app: aggregator (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Summary

The event log's writers cap `actor`/`summary` with raw UTF-16 slices at exactly the lengths `validateStreamEvent` enforces (200 / 500). The validator checks length only, so when an astral character straddles a writer's cap, the event validates, is appended, and a lone high surrogate is persisted into the append-only, hash-chained event log (#1739/#3322). Same defect class as #7694/#7711/#7725/#7731 — at the event log's writer boundary, which none of those fixes covered.

## Evidence

Raw slice sites (main `722fbe8aa2`):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:1065` — session-registry event: `` summary: `session ${r.label} (${r.agentLabel}) merged into the registry`.slice(0, 500) `` (label/agentLabel are source data)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:1630` — orchestration action event: `summary: action.summary.slice(0, 500)` (summary comes from the orchestration feed)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/sources/live.ts:1643` — tier-change event: `` summary: `tier ${prev} → ${tier} (run ${section.runId})`.slice(0, 500) ``
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:1248` — action-result event: `actor: updated.appliedByRun ?? body.byRun.slice(0, 200)` (the `appliedByRun` branch is pair-safe after #7711; the fallback raw-slices the request's `byRun`)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:1254` — action-result event: constructed summary `` (... + note).slice(0, 500) `` (note is caller-supplied)

The receiving side does not re-guard: `validateStreamEvent` (`events.ts:160-171`) rejects only `length > 200` / `length > 500`; a 200/500-unit string ending in a lone surrogate passes. `EventsStore.record` (`events.ts:795`) validates through it, and the summary is folded into the hash chain (`events.ts:308`).

## Verification (this run, laptop primary @ `722fbe8aa2`)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-roadmap-events-surrogate/probe.ts` (laptop), importing the real `validateStreamEvent` and `EventsStore`:

- Writer-shaped summary `("x"×499 + 😀 + "y"×50).slice(0, 500)` (the `live.ts:1630` expression shape) → `validateStreamEvent` returns `ok`; value length 500, **last code unit `0xd83d` (lone high surrogate)**; UTF-8 round-trip contains U+FFFD.
- Writer-shaped actor `("r"×199 + 😀 + "z"×10).slice(0, 200)` (the `server.ts:1248` fallback shape) → same: `ok`, lone `0xd83d` at the tail.
- Recording the summary event through a real `EventsStore` persists it: the events JSON file on disk contains the escaped lone surrogate `\ud83d`.

## Why it matters

The event log is the cross-stack audit stream: append-only, hash-chained, rendered in the UI and searched (`events.ts:390`). A corrupted summary is not a transient display glitch — it is written into the durable record (and its hash), and every UTF-8 read-back renders U+FFFD. Orchestration summaries and session labels are feed data, so a straddling emoji at the boundary is a matter of time, not imagination.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No event writer can emit an `actor` or `summary` ending in a lone surrogate: pair-safe caps at the five sites above, or an equivalent guard at the `recordStreamEvent`/`validateStreamEvent` boundary — triage picks the placement (per-site mirrors the #7694-family pattern; a boundary guard covers future writers).
- [ ] Regression tests: straddling pair at the 500-unit summary cap and at the 200-unit actor cap (fail pre-fix), exact-fit pair at each cap (stays intact), under-cap values unchanged.
- [ ] Existing events test suite (`pm-stack/aggregator/test/events.test.ts`) passes; hash-chain integrity check stays green for newly written events.

title: fleet(queue): claim verb cannot target a specific task — monitor Duty 1B PR binding has no claim path for a queued task

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: source/fleet-monitor
labels.description: Filed or driven by the fleet monitor / operator reconciliation

labels.name: app/fleet
labels.description: pkgs/fleet multicall binary + platform crates

body:
## Problem

The fleet monitor's Duty 1B (PR↔queue binding, protocol §9) requires claiming a SPECIFIC queued task as worker `repo-fleet-monitor`, checkpointing the PR binding, and parking it as the PR's shepherd. The current `fleet queue claim` verb cannot do this:

- `fleet queue claim --queue <q> --worker <w>` claims the queue's next-up task, whatever it is — there is no way to name the task to claim.
- `fleet queue claim 12866 --queue repo-health-code-pilot --worker repo-fleet-monitor` → `repo-queue: claim: unexpected extra argument "12866"`.
- `fleet queue claim --task 12866 ...` → `repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --task`.
- `fleet queue bind` exists but requires `--session-id` (the dispatcher-session claim/bind of #1337); a monitor run has no dispatcher session to bind.

## Evidence (repo-fleet-monitor run 2026-11-08 08:12 CST)

Three verified PR↔task bindings could not be bound through the queue verbs: task 12866 ↔ PR #7615 (issue #5895), task 12631 ↔ PR #7564 (issue #3302), opencode task 12710 ↔ PR #2032 (issue #1678). All three were bound by agent note only, after the monitor's dead-in-queue cap repairs made the tasks claimable and lanes claimed them. Two monitor probes of the claim verb also claimed unrelated tasks (shadow task 8685; code task 12502, triage #6280) — both parked/released immediately; a claim verb that fires on next-up with no target is a footgun for any reconciliation tooling.

Related: #6463 (lease expiry strands tasks at cap), #7068 / #6985 (claim races), #7598 (claim returns foreign-lane tasks), #6420 (repo-queue duration flags).

## Acceptance criteria

- `fleet queue claim` gains a task-targeting form (e.g. `--task <id>` or positional id) that atomically claims exactly that task if it is queued/claimable, and fails cleanly (no claim) when it is not.
- The targeted form composes with `--queue`, `--worker`, `--lane`, and `--lease-seconds` and returns the same task JSON as the next-up form.
- A regression test proves a targeted claim never returns a different task than the one named.
- The monitor's Duty 1B binding (claim → checkpoint `pr_opened` → park `pr-bound-shepherd`) can be executed end-to-end against a named queued task using only the fleet CLI.

— filed by the fleet monitor (repo-fleet-monitor), 2026-11-08 08:12 CST run.

title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): gate-exit logs a hardcoded cap_room 0 — idle fires read as cap-saturated

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/human
labels.description: Filed directly by a human

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Symptom

Every `claimant.py` fire that ends at the gate writes a **false** `cap_room: 0` into the fire log:

```
{"timestamp": "2026-11-08T14:20:19Z", "mode": "shadow", "candidates_seen": [], "sessions_launched": [], "cap_room": 0, "skips": [{"reason": "no_candidates"}]}
```

But `poll.py`, run seconds later against the same server, reports real headroom:

```
cap: 36  concurrency_cap: 36  live_root: 9094  active_root: 4  cap_room: 32
```

## Cause

`claimant.py:533` hardcodes `0` in the gate-exit path:

```python
if not has_candidates:
    print("No unbound opencode-lane candidates found. Exiting.")
    log_fire(mode, [], [], 0, [{"reason": "no_candidates"}])
    return 0
```

`cap_step()` is never reached — it runs *after* the gate — so the value logged is a placeholder, not a measurement.

## Why it matters

`cap_room` in `fires.jsonl` is the field an operator reads to answer "was this fire idle because the fleet was full, or because nothing was eligible?" With the gate-exit path writing `0`, every candidate-less fire is indistinguishable from a saturated one.

This is not hypothetical confusion: the fire log shows `cap_room: 0` for the 14:05, 14:10, 14:15 and 14:20 fires on 2026-11-08 while the true cap_room was ~31-32. A reader would conclude the fleet was pinned at the 36 cap; it was at 4 active roots.

It also masks #7325. A blind-discovery fire and a genuinely-empty-queue fire both log `no_candidates` with `cap_room: 0`, so the log cannot distinguish "nothing to do" from "I could not read the queues."

## Suggested fix

- In the gate-exit path, log `null` (unknown) rather than `0`, since the cap was not measured on that path.
- Optionally run `cap_step()` before the gate so every fire log carries a measured cap count, and record `candidates_seen` as unknown-vs-empty.

## Environment

- `claimant.py` at HEAD `f9dfb4cfa5`
- Laptop OpenCode server `http://127.0.0.1:13420`
- Shadow mode (no `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode`)

## Acceptance criteria

- A gate-exit fire (no candidates) logs `cap_room` as null/unknown — never a hardcoded 0 — in `fires.jsonl`.
- If the optional measured path is chosen instead, the logged value comes from `cap_step()` run on that fire, and reconciles with a `poll.py` reading taken at the same time.
- A regression test or fixture fire proves an idle fire's log line cannot be mistaken for a saturated one.

title: id(waiting): WaitingPool duplicate guard misses the handed-out state — a key taken by take_ready can be inserted and handed out again before arrived

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Summary

`WaitingPool` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/waiting.rs` promises that a duplicate is ignored — "`insert` docs: an event whose key is already held, has arrived, or is ready is a duplicate, and it is ignored" — and #2001 added the `ready_keys` index precisely so the guard can see the ready state, with #4730 making `arrived` drop a ready-queue copy. One state is still invisible to the guard: **handed out**. `take_ready()` clears `ready_keys` (`take_ready`, waiting.rs), so a key that has been handed to the caller but not yet marked `arrived` is in no index at all — not `by_key`, not `ready_keys`, not `arrived`. Re-inserting the same key in that window (a duplicate delivery arriving while the caller is applying the first copy, before its `arrived(key)` call) passes every guard check and is handed out a second time by the next `take_ready()`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe against current main 73294b076e)

Probe crate `~/git/fleet/probe-waiting-ready` on the laptop, path-depending on `crates/id-core`, `WaitingPool<u32, &str>` with default limits:

1. `pool.arrived(10, 0)` — dependency present.
2. `pool.insert(author, 1, [10], "first", 0)` → `Ok(())`; `pool.take_ready()` → `["first"]`.
3. `pool.insert(author, 1, [10], "second", 0)` → `Ok(())` (the duplicate is accepted); `pool.take_ready()` → `["second"]` — **key 1 handed out twice before `arrived(1)` was ever called.**
4. No-deps form behaves the same: `insert(author, 7, [], "first", 0)`, `take_ready()` → `["first"]`, `insert(author, 7, [], "second", 0)` → `Ok(())`, `take_ready()` → `["second"]`.
5. Control: after `pool.arrived(1, 0)`, a re-insert of key 1 IS ignored (`take_ready()` → `[]`) — the guard works once arrival is recorded; only the handed-out window is unguarded.

Code points (main 73294b076e):

- `crates/id-core/src/waiting.rs` — `take_ready` does `self.ready_keys.clear()` and drains `ready`, recording the handed-out keys nowhere.
- `insert` / `park` / `restore` duplicate guards check only `arrived`, `by_key`, and `ready_keys`.
- The module's own caller loop (waiting.rs module docs, steps 1–2) is: insert → `take_ready` → apply each event → call `arrived` for its key. Duplicate deliveries are the pool's stated reason to exist (sync re-sends unacknowledged events), and a caller applying a batch interleaves exactly in the unguarded window.
- `release()` doc (#1730 store path) shows the same shape was considered for the store's path; the standalone `insert`/`arrived` protocol has no equivalent handed-out tracking.

## Why it matters

The pool's contract — the thing #2001, #3911, and #4730 each extended — is "a key is handed out once until it arrives". The handed-out state is the one remaining hole in that contract: a caller that trusts it applies/decides the same event twice. Today's in-tree impact is bounded (the event store's `drain` in `src/event_store/ingest.rs` re-checks duplicates via its applied table, and the store path uses `restore`/`release`, not `insert`), but `waiting` is a public `id-core` module and the standalone protocol is the documented interface for the future group-sync initiator (see `sync_method.rs`: "a production group-sync initiator … does not exist yet") — the hole will be inherited by the first caller that relies on the contract as written.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A regression test in `crates/id-core/src/waiting.rs` (deps-arrived form and no-deps form): insert a ready event, `take_ready()`, re-insert the same key before `arrived(key)` — the second insert is ignored and the second `take_ready()` is empty.
- [ ] The fix records handed-out keys until `arrived`/`release` settles them (or an equivalent mechanism), without breaking the #1730 store path: `release` must also settle a handed-out key, and restoring a handed-out key must not hold a second copy (#3911 guards still hold).
- [ ] Existing waiting-pool tests still pass, including #2001's ready-duplicate test and #4730's arrived-drops-ready-copy test; the bounded-memory story is stated (handed-out keys are released by `arrived`/`release`, so the set cannot grow past what a caller has taken and not yet settled).
- [ ] `insert`'s rustdoc duplicate list names the handed-out state, so the contract and the guard agree.

Relates to: #2001 (ready-queue duplicate guard), #4730 (arrived drops ready copy), #3911 (restore guards), #1730 (store release path).

title: mcpx(source): a symlink loop entry aborts the whole @dir: resolve — ELOOP is neither skipped like a dangling link nor pinned like a permission error

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

In mcpx's directory source walk, one symlink loop entry makes the whole `@dir:` resolve fail — while the two neighboring bad-link cases are tolerated:

- a **dangling** symlink is skipped (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go:174-180`: `os.Stat` failure is continued past only when `errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist)`, comment "A dangling link has no regular target to read");
- a **directory** cycle (a dir symlink pointing back to an ancestor) is skipped by the `os.SameFile` ancestor guard in the same walk (`source.go:152-157`);
- a symlink **loop** (a link to itself, or two links pointing at each other) makes `os.Stat` fail with ELOOP ("too many levels of symbolic links"), which is neither of the above: `source.go:181` returns the error and the entire directory resolution aborts with zero files read — including every healthy regular file sitting next to the loop.

A loop link, like a dangling link, has no regular target to read. The current split — tolerate a missing target and a directory cycle, but let a loop target deny the whole source — is an untested gap, not a pinned decision: the pinned cases in the shipped tests are dangling-skip (`source_test.go:245` `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), directory-cycle-safety (`source_test.go:191`), and permission-error propagation (`source_unix_test.go:73` `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget`, which pins EACCES as a returned error and must keep behaving that way). No test covers the ELOOP case.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop, main 8a0a1c0ceac8)

Probe at `~/git/fleet/probe-mcpx-eloop` on the laptop: the real `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/source.go` copied verbatim (md5 `768194633188160a349eafd555defe53`, identical to the file on main) into a standalone module, driven through the exported `source.Resolve("@dir:"+root, …)`:

- control (regular.ts + dangling.ts → missing): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — matches the shipped pin;
- self-loop (regular.ts + loop.ts → loop.ts): **fails** — `reading …/loop.ts: stat …/loop.ts: too many levels of symbolic links`, zero files returned;
- pair loop (regular.ts + a.ts → b.ts, b.ts → a.ts): **fails** the same way at a.ts, zero files returned;
- control (directory back-link to the root itself): resolves OK, files = [regular.ts] — the ancestor guard tolerates the directory cycle.

So one stray looped link (easily produced by a bad `ln -s` pair or a tool that links a directory's contents into itself at file level) takes down every launcher/prefix/hook that reads its source from that directory, with an error that names the link but gives no way to keep the healthy remainder.

Related: closed #1727 covered non-regular files in directory sources (FIFO/socket/symlink-to-directory); this is the distinct remaining Stat-error class for file entries. The Go source lives only in this repo (`pkgs/mcpx`); dezren39/darwin-nix only wraps/launches the built mcpx, so no cross-repo set applies. Found via a pr-diff-review REVIEW-FINDING on PR #3744 that was left as decide-and-test material; verified independently this run before filing.

## Why it matters

`@dir:` sources feed mcpx launchers, prefixes, and error hooks. A single looped symlink — which the directory-cycle guard already proves the walk intends to survive at directory level — currently denies the whole source instead of just the unreadable entry. Robustness here should be uniform: an entry with no readable regular target is skipped (dangling, loop), while genuinely informative errors (permission) still surface, per the existing pin.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A directory containing a self-loop symlink or a mutually-looping symlink pair, plus at least one regular file, resolves successfully and returns exactly the regular files (the loop entries skipped), for both the self-loop and pair-loop shapes.
- [ ] Regression tests for both loop shapes land in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/source` (mirroring the style of `TestDirectorySkipsDanglingLinkAndFollowsLinkOutsideRoot`), and fail on the pre-fix code.
- [ ] The pinned permission behavior is unchanged: `TestDirectoryReportsInaccessibleSymlinkTarget` still passes — only the ELOOP class changes disposition, not EACCES or other Stat errors (or, if the fix deliberately widens/narrows which Stat errors skip, the disposition of each class is named in the PR and the affected pins updated with rationale).
- [ ] The existing source suite (`go test ./pkgs/mcpx/internal/source/...`, or the package's normal CI route) is green with the new tests.

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/atlas-search/worker/test/` — the vitest suite for the atlas-search cache Worker (the per-query Durable Object search cache from #6788: query-key canonicalisation, embedding-space validation, auth gate, embed + fan-out, DO cache hit) — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. It runs only when a human runs `npm test` in that directory by hand.

## Evidence (verified this run at main `0798a9881e`)

- Suite: 3 files, 14 tests — `test/key.test.ts` (5: `normalizeQuery` trim/NFC/case rules plus a hand-built canonical-digest oracle for the DO cache key in `src/key.ts`), `test/space.test.ts` (4: `validateEmbed` embedding-space consistency — pinned model, full width, dims/vector agreement, finiteness), `test/worker.test.ts` (5, via `cloudflare:test` SELF + fetchMock: health-open/search-gated auth, miss embeds + fans out once and the repeat is a byte-identical DO hit, the #6937 whitespace-only-query rejection on both routes, wrong-space embedding refused from the cache, the #6982 null search-service response reported as 502 not a raw TypeError).
- Hand run on the laptop in a probe copy (`~/git/fleet/probe-atlas-worker`, real worker tree copied verbatim): `npm ci` (the package ships a `package-lock.json`, unlike the github-ci Worker in #7674) then `npm test` → **3 test files / 14 tests passed**, repeated twice with the same result. The suite is green — it is simply never run by automation.
- Wiring search: `grep -rn "atlas-search/worker"` over `.github/`, root `flake.nix`, `lib/`, `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix`, `pkgs/atlas-search/default.nix`, `justfile` → **no hits**; `grep -rn "atlas-search"` over `.github/workflows/*.yml` matches only `fleet-search-parity-guard.yml`, which checks the Rust pyjson/render writers and never touches the Worker. `pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix:51` sets `checks.default = atlas-search` (the Rust package) — no Worker test check. The only run instructions are manual: `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/README.md:49` (`npm test  # vitest + @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`).
- The pins are for live, recently-merged behavior: #6937 (merged 2026-11-07, whitespace-only query on GET /v1/cache/inspect) and #6982 (merged 2026-11-07, validated /v1/search response shape in `searchService`) both added their regression tests to `test/worker.test.ts` — verified by hand at merge time, verified nowhere since. `space.test.ts` is the Worker-side guard for the embedding-space consistency the #6060 series is building on (#7646/#7648, open).
- Sibling Workers show the house wiring pattern exists: `pkgs/id/hosted-worker` has `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml`; the github-ci Worker's unwired suite is filed as #7674 and the github-backup Worker's as #6085. This Worker — the one standing in front of every fleet search query, holding an indefinite result cache keyed by the digest `key.test.ts` pins — has neither a workflow nor a filing.

## Why it matters

A regression in `key.ts`'s canonical material silently changes every DO cache key (mass invalidation, or worse, cross-config serving — the exact failure `key.test.ts`'s "differs across query and across k" case guards). A regression in `validateEmbed` lets a foreign-model or truncated embedding into the cache and poisons results indefinitely (the cache has no TTL eviction policy yet, #6805). And the two most recent correctness fixes to this Worker (#6937, #6982) currently have regression protection that executes only on a human's laptop.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow (house pattern, e.g. `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml` / `bin-tests.yml`: workflow_dispatch + path-gated push-to-main, main tier) runs the suite — `npm ci` + `npm test` (vitest) in `pkgs/atlas-search/worker` — and fails loudly if the suite files are missing, never a silent skip.
- [ ] The wiring demonstrably executes all 14 tests (run output reports 3 test files / 14 tests passing) on a change touching `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/**`.
- [ ] The suite passes via the wiring on main after the change lands.

Dedup (this run): title/keyword searches for `atlas` + "vitest", "atlas worker suite", "atlas-search worker" in title, and the three test filenames found no existing filing for this suite's wiring; #6879/#6937/#6982 are live-code defects in this Worker (two of them are what the suite pins), #6330 is PR-tier validation for the atlas-search **Rust** packages, #6805 is the cache eviction/invalidation follow-on, #7646/#7648 are the #6060 embedding-model slices.

## Problem

`.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` runs test suites for three pm-stack areas that its own trigger paths never match, so changes to those areas get no automatic test signal at all — on pull requests or on pushes to main:

| Suite the workflow runs | Step | Trigger path present? |
|---|---|---|
| pm-dispatch bun suite (10 files, incl. #4917 launch-failure/orphan-compensation pins) | `Test dispatch` (:65-73), working-directory `pm-stack/dispatch` | **No** — `pm-stack/dispatch/**` is in neither the push nor the pull_request path list |
| Grist Python suite (`test_update_choice_options.py`, discovered `test_*.py`) | `Test claimant and grist Python suites` (:85-105) | **No** — `pm-stack/grist/**` absent |
| Script smokes (`seed-smoke.test.sh`, `deploy-install-smoke.test.sh`) | `Test seed and deploy/install scripts` (:74-78) | **No** — `pm-stack/scripts/**` absent |

The push and pull_request path lists (workflow :5-25) name only `pm-stack/external-comms/**`, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/**`, `pm-stack/opencode-usage-export/**`, `pm-stack/cloudflare-export/**`, `pm-stack/supabase-export/**`, and the workflow file itself.

No other workflow fills the gap: `grep -rn "pm-stack/dispatch" .github/workflows/` hits only pm-stack-tests.yml's own step, `grep -rln "grist" .github/workflows/` hits only pm-stack-tests.yml, and `pm-dispatch-smoke.yml` is a dispatch-only manual smoke of the dispatch *service's* ci-fix mode, not a test run. The wiring PRs that added these steps (#6090 for dispatch, #5951 for grist) added the steps but not the matching trigger paths — the same step-without-trigger shape as #6929/#6953, inside an otherwise-active workflow.

## Verified this run (laptop primary @ 8c84644124)

- Workflow read end to end: steps at :43 (aggregator), :51 (projector), :65 (dispatch), :74 (scripts), :85 (claimant+grist), :112 (external-comms), :134/:138/:142 (quota exporters) vs path lists at :5-25 — dispatch, grist, and scripts appear only as steps, never as paths.
- The suites are real and green where they run: grist discovery ran on the laptop this run (`Ran 15 tests, OK`); `seed-smoke.test.sh` passes; the dispatch suite was verified at 131 pass when #6090 wired the step.
- The workflow itself is active and firing for its listed paths (runs today on push/pull_request, e.g. 2026-11-08T12:06Z), so this is not the disabled/dispatch-only class — the trigger list simply does not cover three of its own suites. (Its current red-on-main state is the separate issue #7680.)
- Out of scope deliberately: `pm-stack/aggregator/**` and `pm-stack/projector/**` are also absent from these paths, but those suites have their own workflow (pm-aggregator-tests.yml), whose dispatch-only state is blocked under Drew's runner-strategy ruling on #6126 — this issue does not propose changing that.

## Why it matters

Dispatch is the fleet's work-intake service; its bun suite pins the launch-failure compensation and orphan-cleanup behavior that #4917's orphan flood motivated. A dispatch-only PR today merges with zero dispatch test signal, and a dispatch-only push to main runs nothing either — the suite #6090 wired is decorative for exactly the changes it exists to guard. Same for the grist choice-options suite and the deploy/install script smokes (whose current breakage, #7680, is precisely the kind of drift per-area triggers exist to catch at PR time).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pm-stack/dispatch/**`, `pm-stack/grist/**`, and `pm-stack/scripts/**` are added to both the push and pull_request path lists of pm-stack-tests.yml (or an equivalent trigger shape that fires the workflow for changes in those trees).
- [ ] Evidence on the fixing PR: a dispatch-only (or grist-only / scripts-only) change triggers a pm-stack-tests run — e.g. the PR's own run, since the PR touches the workflow and one of the three trees, or a documented `gh workflow run` path-filter check.
- [ ] No other workflow's triggers change; aggregator/projector coverage stays as #6126 has it.
- [ ] The workflow still passes `bash .github/scripts/check-workflows.test.sh` (workflow-lint) after the edit.

Related: #6090 (dispatch step wiring), #5951 (grist step wiring), #6126 (aggregator workflow blocked, separate), #7680 (this workflow currently red on main for an unrelated step failure), #5993 (the other two pm-stack script suites remain unwired).
