body:
## Problem

The `pm-stack tests` workflow has failed every completed run since 2026-11-04 (last success 2026-11-04T19:24Z at a5dfe4f3; ~25 completed runs on 2026-11-05/06/07 all `failure`). The failing step is always the same one — **Test seed and deploy/install scripts** — and inside it only `pm-stack/scripts/deploy-install-smoke.test.sh`, which fails the same 4 checks deterministically in CI and on the laptop. `seed-smoke.test.sh` in the same step passes, so the step is not environment-broken in general.

## Verified this run (laptop primary @ 8c84644124, origin/main)

```
$ bash pm-stack/scripts/deploy-install-smoke.test.sh   # exit 1, twice, identical
cp: cannot stat '/tmp/opencode/deploy-install-smoke.XXX/aggregator-home/git/code/pm-stack/aggregator/../systemd/pm-aggregator.service': No such file or directory
FAIL - aggregator install smoke completes using temporary HOME and stubs
FAIL - aggregator copies package and unit files only under temporary HOME
FAIL - aggregator health-version gate accepts the stubbed matching version
FAIL - ready-for-agent install smoke completes using temporary HOME and stubs
deploy-install-smoke.test.sh: 4 check(s) failed
```

CI says the same: `gh run view 42390617495 --log-failed` shows the identical `cp: cannot stat '.../aggregator/../systemd/pm-aggregator.service'` line, the same 4 FAILs, and `ready-src/install.sh: line 192: ./apply-config.sh: No such file or directory`. Control: `bash pm-stack/scripts/seed-smoke.test.sh` passes on the same tree.

## Root causes (two fixture/install drifts, one per failing half)

1. **Aggregator unit path resolves through a symlink.** `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh:30` sets `UNIT_SRC="$SRC/../systemd/pm-aggregator.service"` and `:126` copies it. The smoke fixture links the aggregator package into the fake checkout (`deploy-install-smoke.test.sh:321`: `ln -s "$AGG_SRC" "$AGG_EXPECTED_SRC"`) and creates the unit at the *logical* sibling path (`:319`, `$AGG_HOME/git/code/pm-stack/systemd/pm-aggregator.service`). Path resolution of `symlink/../` goes through the symlink *target's* parent, so the copy looks in `$TMP/systemd/…`, where nothing exists. The install's own guard at `install.sh:72` already treats a missing unit as `unit:absent` for hashing, but the copy at `:126` is unconditional when the destination is not symlink-managed. (Distinct from closed #5396, which was the *destination* unit being a home-manager symlink; that skip exists at `install.sh:123-127`.)
2. **Ready-for-agent fixture predates #1203.** `pm-stack/ready-for-agent/install.sh:192` runs `./apply-config.sh` unconditionally on the verified-serving path (added by #1203, commit dcea7fa213). The smoke fixture copies only `install.sh` into the fake deploy root (`deploy-install-smoke.test.sh:359`) plus its systemd unit — no `apply-config.sh`, no stub — so the success path always dies at line 192. This is the same root cause as open #5368, which tracks it for the sibling harness `pm-stack/ready-for-agent/test-install.sh`; the smoke fixture in `pm-stack/scripts/` has the identical gap and is not named there.

## Why it matters

`pm-stack-tests` is the only CI venue for the aggregator/projector/dispatch bun suites, the claimant/grist Python suites, and the quota-exporter suites. It has been red on main for four days, so none of those suites' results mean anything right now — a real regression in any of them is invisible inside a permanently-failing workflow, and every PR run inherits a known-red step that trains everyone to ignore it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash pm-stack/scripts/deploy-install-smoke.test.sh` exits 0 on current main: all aggregator and ready-for-agent checks pass.
- [ ] The aggregator fix keeps the #1150/#5396 behavior pinned: install from the real primary checkout still copies `pm-stack/systemd/pm-aggregator.service`, and the symlink-managed destination skip still applies. Whether the fix lands in `install.sh` (resolve the unit against the checkout root, not through a possibly-symlinked package dir) or in the fixture (materialize the package instead of symlinking it), the smoke must still exercise the real `install.sh`.
- [ ] The ready-for-agent smoke case provides `apply-config.sh` the way #5368 requires for `test-install.sh` (real script + config with dependencies stubbed, or a recording stub) and asserts it was invoked — deleting or skipping the call in `install.sh` does not count.
- [ ] A `pm-stack tests` run on main completes with conclusion `success` (all steps, not just this one).

Related: #5368 (same apply-config root cause, sibling harness), #5396 (closed; destination-symlink unit skip), #5993 (the other two pm-stack script suites are unwired), #6126 (pm-aggregator-tests dispatch-only, blocked separately).

## Problem

`pkgs/github-ci/worker/test/` — the vitest suite for the github-ci webhook Worker (the #5693 receiver: workflow_run → Turso `ci_events`, plus the fleet push/PR/issues sink into agent events / repo snapshots) — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. The package does not even ship a `package-lock.json`, so the suite cannot be reproduced with `npm ci` either; it runs only when a human does an ad-hoc `npm install` by hand.

## Evidence (verified this run at main `ca698a867a`)

- Suite: 4 files, 22 tests — `test/policy.test.ts` (4: fleet-repo set, skip rules, dedupe-key format, payload retention), `test/turso.test.ts` (7: the #6949 Turso pipeline-envelope pins), `test/sink.test.ts` (4: the #6925 public broker-route pins), `test/worker.test.ts` (7: HMAC 401, ping, ci_events insert, the #6949 results-less-200 delivery failure, skip/ignore rules, push → snapshot + sink event).
- Hand run on the laptop in a probe copy (`~/git/fleet/probe-ghci-tests`, real worker tree copied verbatim): after `npm install`, `npx vitest run` → **22/22 passed** (repeated 3× full-suite, plus the two heaviest files standalone). The suite is green — it is simply never run. (One cold first run right after install showed 2 spurious failures; it did not reproduce in any later run and is not claimed as a finding.)
- `npm ci` is impossible: `pkgs/github-ci/worker/` contains `package.json`, `vitest.config.ts`, `wrangler.toml`, `src/`, `test/` — and **no `package-lock.json`** (sibling Workers `pkgs/atlas-search/worker` and `pkgs/pkarr-worker` both ship one). `npm ci` errors out for lack of a lockfile.
- Wiring search: `grep -rn "github-ci"` over `.github/workflows/*.yml` (outside name/comment lines), plus `grep -rn "pkgs/github-ci"` over `flake.nix`, `lib/default.nix`, `justfile` → **no hits**. No workflow mentions the package at all.
- The pins are for live, recently-merged behavior: #6949 (merged fix: Turso envelope validation — `turso.test.ts` is its regression suite, and `worker.test.ts` carries the end-to-end "results-less 200 fails the delivery" case), #6925 (broker route, `sink.test.ts`), and the HMAC gate that #6936 (open) is about. A regression in any of these would currently be caught by nothing.
- Sibling Workers' suites show the house wiring pattern exists: `pkgs/id/hosted-worker` has `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml` (#6095); the github-backup Worker's suite got its own filing (#6085, open). This package — the one writing CI events and fleet snapshots — has neither a workflow nor a filing.

## Why it matters

This Worker is on the fleet's observability path: it decides which workflow runs land in `ci_events`, advances `agent_repo_snapshots`, and appends sink events. Its policy rules (which repos count as fleet, which runs are stored, the dedupe key format shared with the Edge Function) are exactly the kind of contract that drifts silently. The regression suites for its two most recent correctness fixes (#6949, #6925) exist and pass — unwired and lockfile-less, they protect nothing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A committed `package-lock.json` for `pkgs/github-ci/worker` makes `npm ci` work from a clean checkout.
- [ ] A workflow (house pattern, e.g. `id-hosted-worker-tests.yml` / `bin-tests.yml`: dispatch + path-gated push-to-main, main tier) runs the suite — `npm ci` + `npm test` (vitest) in `pkgs/github-ci/worker` — and fails loudly if the suite files are missing, never a silent skip.
- [ ] The wiring demonstrably executes all 22 tests (run output reports 4 test files / 22 tests passing), on a change touching `pkgs/github-ci/**`.
- [ ] The suite passes via the wiring on main after the change lands.

Dedup (this run): title/keyword searches for `github-ci` + "run by no workflow", the four test filenames, and "github-ci worker suite" found no existing filing for this suite's wiring; #6085 is the github-**backup** Worker (different package), #6093 is pkarr-worker's lockfile defect, #6936/#6945/#6946 are live-code defects in this Worker, not its test wiring.

## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test/test_claimant.py` (168 lines, 4 tests: "Offline tests for claimant ordering and fail-closed behavior") is run by no workflow, flake check, or just recipe — and it no longer runs at all against the current claimant. It is a Slice-1 artifact (landed in bfa5caede7, "slice1 artifacts / branch disposition 2026-11-07") written against a claimant API that the live implementation does not have:

- The suite patches `claimant._POLL` (test/test_claimant.py:147), `claimant._current_bound_row` (:148), `claimant.prepare_candidate` / `claimant.launch_one`, `claimant._verify_candidate_is_current`, `claimant._github_issue_labels`, `claimant._load_runbook`, and `claimant._post_launch_note` — none of these exist in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` on main (ca698a867a). The live claimant exposes `launch_step(mode, cap_room)` (claimant.py:351) and `supervision_step(mode)` (:177) and loads poll via `_load_poll_module()` / `_poll_module` (:134), not a `_POLL` constant.
- The suite's supervision test calls `claimant.supervision_step(data, "live")` with a data argument; the live signature is `supervision_step(mode: str)`.

## Verified this run (laptop, main ca698a867a)

```
$ python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test/test_claimant.py
ERROR: test_create_failure_checkpoints_without_binding
ERROR: test_held_issue_label_prevents_preflight
ERROR: test_session_is_bound_before_checkpoint_and_prompt
ERROR: test_zero_message_delete_precedes_atomic_recovery
  (AttributeError: module 'claimant' does not have the attribute '_POLL', and siblings)
Ran 4 tests — FAILED (errors=4)
```

Control: the wired live suites pass on the same tree — `python3 -m unittest pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_claimant.py pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_poll.py` → Ran 53 tests, OK. Wiring check: `grep -rn "test/test_claimant" .github/workflows/ flake.nix justfile` → no hits; pm-stack-tests.yml wires only the top-level `test_claimant.py` + `test_poll.py` (#5951).

## Why it matters

- A broken suite in the tree is a false alarm generator: anyone running unittest discovery over `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` (the natural thing to do) gets 4 errors and cannot tell whether the live claimant regressed — the exact confusion the live suite's header (#6865 negative control) was written to prevent.
- Two of its pins have no live counterpart and are safety-relevant: held-label preflight (`test_held_issue_label_prevents_preflight` — a candidate whose issue carries `do-not-merge` must never be prepared/launched; no `held`/label check exists in live claimant.py or poll.py) and the bind → checkpoint → prompt ordering with the route password kept out of the prompt. The live suite covers bind/recovery for gone sessions, but not the held-label gate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Disposition decided and recorded on this issue: port the still-relevant pins to the live claimant API, or retire the Slice-1 suite.
- [ ] If porting: the held-label preflight and bind-before-checkpoint-before-prompt / password-not-in-prompt pins exist as tests against `launch_step`/`supervision_step` (or the held check is implemented in the live claimant/poll path if it is genuinely missing there), and the ported suite is wired in pm-stack-tests.yml alongside the existing claimant suites with the house file-exists assertion.
- [ ] If retiring: `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test/test_claimant.py` is deleted and the deletion PR names which pins were judged superseded and where each surviving behavior is pinned instead.
- [ ] Either way: `python3 -m unittest discover -s pm-stack/opencode-claimant -t .` (or the documented equivalent) runs with zero errors from stale suites, and the wired claimant suites stay green (53 tests at filing time).

Related: #5951 (wired the live Python suites), #6091 (claimant install.test.mjs unwired), #6865 / #6990 (live claimant restoration the Slice-1 API did not survive).

## Problem

`pkgs/identity/provider/core-static-test.sh` (150 lines) — the regression suite for the #6180 security fix that confines the identity provider's static-file handler to its static root — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. The confinement contract for a path that serves files next to a `.env` secret is verified nowhere in automation.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop primary @ main ca698a867a)

- `pkgs/identity/provider/core-static-test.sh:2-13` — header: "Regression test for issue #6180: the identity provider's static-file handler must confine every /static/... request to the static root", exercising `resolve_static_path` directly and through the handler against a fixture tree with a marker `.env` two levels above `static/` and a symlink escape (`static/escape.txt -> <tmp>/.env`).
- The code under test is live: `pkgs/identity/provider/core.sh:392` defines `resolve_static_path`, and `core.sh:437` calls it in `writeHttpResponse` to resolve the served `FILE_PATH`.
- Hand run on the laptop at ca698a867a: `bash pkgs/identity/provider/core-static-test.sh` → exit 0, "all checks passed": `/static/../../.env` gets 403 without the marker; encoded traversal gets 403; symlink escape gets 403; a normal asset returns 200 with its expected bytes; a missing asset returns 404; and a property check of 398 generated paths agrees with the confinement oracle (0 mismatches).
- Wiring search: `git grep core-static-test.sh` over the whole repo returns no references outside the file itself; no workflow, flake check, or recipe runs it.

## Why it matters

#6180 was a security fix: an unconfined `/static/...` handler can be walked (or symlinked) out of the static root to the provider's `.env`, which holds live secrets (the fixture's marker is `TURSO_AUTH_TOKEN`). The fix shipped with exactly the right regression suite — direct helper checks, handler checks, and a 398-case property against a confinement oracle — but because nothing runs it, a future refactor of `core.sh`'s path handling can silently reopen the traversal and no check would fail.

## Acceptance criteria

- Package changes merged since 2026-11-03 with zero workflow runs (git log): #7001 token-response shape validation (`d20de1fd34`), PR #6726 frame/size bounds (two Codex P1 rounds), #6590 decompression bound, #6602 listing-loop bounds, #6531 repair_dump fix, #6233 Range-request memory bound.

## Why it matters

cold-store-reaper verifies sha256s, enforces budget stops, and produces the only portable Turso exports (workflow header). Its last pre-workflow PRs "all shipped unexecuted test changes" (#1427's rationale) — that is again the standing state, now with a workflow present that makes it look covered.

body:
## Problem

`nix build .#fleet` (and therefore `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel`, which includes the fleet package) fails on current main (`df0e415c91`, verified 2026-11-08 in a clean worktree by task 13007):

```
error: couldn't read `/build/source/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/../../../schema/atlas_stage_v1.sql`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
error: couldn't read `/build/source/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/../../../schema/stage_registry_v1.sql`: No such file or directory (os error 2)
error: could not compile `atlas-core` (lib) due to 2 previous errors
error: Cannot build '...-fleet-0.1.0.drv': builder failed with exit code 101
```

## Root cause

- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/stage.rs:45` does `include_str!("../../../schema/atlas_stage_v1.sql")` and line 49 does the same for `stage_registry_v1.sql`. Both files exist at `pkgs/atlas-search/schema/`.
- `pkgs/fleet/default.nix` builds the fleet binary from a `lib.fileset.toSource` union (`fleetSrc`) containing only `pkgs/fleet`, `../atlas-search/Cargo.toml`, and `../atlas-search/crates` — `../atlas-search/schema` is NOT in the fileset, so the `.sql` files are absent from the Nix build source. Local cargo builds from the full tree pass; only the Nix build fails.

## Fix

Add `../atlas-search/schema` to the `fleetSrc` fileset union in `pkgs/fleet/default.nix`.

## Acceptance

- `nix build .#fleet` succeeds on main.
- `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` gets past the fleet-0.1.0 dependency (green, or any remaining failure is a different, separately filed defect).
- Found by: task 13007 (#2727 verification) — the toplevel failure is pre-existing on clean main and unrelated to #2727 (its nodejs_24 build passes).

## Acceptance criteria
- nix build .#fleet succeeds on current main (and the toplevel build that includes the fleet package gets past the atlas-core compile).
- The fleetSrc fileset in pkgs/fleet/default.nix includes pkgs/atlas-search/schema, so both include_str! .sql files are present in the build source.
- No other include_str! path in the fleet build's dependency set is missing from the fileset (checked, not assumed).

- Run by hand on the laptop at main 0a27a7f19f: `bash pkgs/id/scripts/build-sh-test.sh` → **"build-sh tests passed", exit 0**. The suite is green; it is simply never executed by automation.

## Defect

`pkgs/id`'s own test suite fails deterministically at current main: two world-schedule tests panic in `WorldCore::restore` with

```
journal event at sequence 1 uses participant 1 before it was issued
```

Failing tests (both in `src/world/tests.rs`, module `world::tests::schedule_tests`):

- `a_fire_the_program_refuses_stays_pending_in_the_journal` (panics at tests.rs:7140 — the `WorldCore::restore(..., entries).unwrap()`)
- `replay_reproduces_the_pending_and_fired_sets` (panics at tests.rs:7232, same call)

## Evidence (2026-11-08, laptop `amd`)

- **Package check phase (nix sandbox)**, main as of this morning: `test result: FAILED. 2995 passed; 2 failed` on the first attempt (drv `2rngdkgnyvpz...`), then `3000 passed; 2 failed` on a later main (drv `yvdsgkaq6f...`). The same two tests, both times.
- **Bare worktree retry of the first failing drv succeeded once** (`ID_EXIT=0`) — under the full 16-thread sandbox run at machine load ~16. That single pass does not reproduce.
- **Local runs at main `0a27a7f19f`** (dev toolchain, `cargo test --offline --lib world::tests::schedule_tests::`): FAILED in 3/3 runs at `--test-threads=16`, and FAILED in 3/3 runs at `--test-threads=1` (19 passed, 2 failed, finished in 0.01–0.10s). Deterministic in this environment, independent of test parallelism.
- The tests' journal is synthetic (`Recorded::for_world` seeds `JournalEntry::Created`, then the actor's own appends: capability issuance for participant "ann", then `ScheduleSet`). Restore validates participant issuance in journal order and rejects the stream at sequence 1. Nothing time- or load-dependent is visible in the test setup up to the restore call.

## Impact

`pkgs/id` has `doCheck = true`, so the failing check phase blocks the `id` package build, which blocks `unit-id-primary.service` → `system-units` → `etc` → **the whole NixOS toplevel**: `nixos-rebuild switch` on `amd` cannot complete while this stands (observed twice on 2026-11-08, switch attempts for #6765). Every deploy to the laptop is gated on this until fixed — this is fleet-stalling, not a test nit.

## Notes for whoever picks this up

- Recent `pkgs/id` change in the area: PR #7611 (`id(replication): refuse snapshot header-version downgrades`, merged 2026-11-08T09:48:09Z) touched only `src/world/replication.rs`. Whether the stricter issuance validation arrived there or the tests rotted against an older change is the first question — the two green-field data points are: tests assert the error string "before it was issued" exists elsewhere in the suite (tests.rs:2152/2170/2183), so the rule is intentional somewhere; these two schedule tests may predate it.
- The one bare-drv pass vs deterministic local failures discrepancy is worth understanding (sandbox profile `ci-check` vs dev profile is the visible difference).
- Filed from the #6765 deploy lane, which this blocks; that lane's change (ONNX Runtime pin) is merged and verified independently — do not conflate the two.

## Acceptance criteria
- Both named tests (a_fire_the_program_refuses_stays_pending_in_the_journal and replay_reproduces_the_pending_and_fired_sets in pkgs/id src/world/tests.rs schedule_tests) pass deterministically across repeated runs at --test-threads=16 and at 1.
- WorldCore::restore no longer rejects a journal whose early events reference a participant the journal itself issues later in sequence - or the tests' journal construction is corrected, with the verdict (code bug vs test bug) recorded on the issue.
- The full pkgs/id suite is green (0 failed) in the package check phase.

body:
## Problem

`nix run .#format` (treefmt) — the formatter the scheduled **auto-format** workflow runs on `main` (`.github/workflows/auto-format.yml`, the one-repo PoC tracked by #2015) — aborts on `pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css`. Biome refuses the file because it contains Tailwind v4 directives (`@source`, `@plugin "daisyui" { … }`) and Biome's CSS parser has Tailwind-directive parsing **disabled** (`biome.json` has no `css.parser.tailwindDirectives`).

Because treefmt treats a formatter error as fatal, the whole pass exits 1 and **nothing is committed** — so the auto-format pass is a no-op stuck loop: it reformats `app.css` every run, then throws the result away when the `ui.css` error aborts the run. This is the failure seen in the scheduled runs on 2026-11-05/06/07 (`42438417218` at the time of writing still sitting in `queued`; `42360613068`, `42311315333`, `42210543931` … all `failure`).

## Evidence (reproduced on current `main`, `5ab0c06928`)

```
$ nix run .#format -- pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css
…
pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css:12:2 parse ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  × Tailwind-specific syntax is disabled.
     12 │ @source "./";
  i Enable `tailwindDirectives` in the css parser options, or remove this if you are not using Tailwind CSS.
pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css:13:2 parse ━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
  × Tailwind-specific syntax is disabled.
     13 │ @plugin "daisyui" {
Found 2 errors.
Error: failed to finalise formatting: formatting failures detected
```

The same error is what fails the scheduled workflow (log of run `42360613068`, step "Format changed files with treefmt and commit any fixes"). The file is authored as Tailwind v4 + DaisyUI v5 on purpose (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css` header, Phase C #6153) and is built by `bun run build:css` (`tailwindcss -i src/ui.css -o src/assets/app.css`), so removing the directives is not an option.

## Verified minimal fix

Add the parser option Biome itself points at:

```json
"css": {
  "formatter": { "enabled": true, "indentStyle": "space", "indentWidth": 2 },
  "linter": { "enabled": true },
  "parser": { "tailwindDirectives": true }
}
```

With that one key, `nix run .#format -- pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css pm-stack/aggregator/src/assets/app.css biome.json` exits 0 and is idempotent (second run: `formatted 0 files (0 changed)`). Biome's own hint names this exact option, and the equivalent CLI flag `--css-parse-tailwind-directives=true` makes plain `biome format` succeed, confirming it is the correct lever (treefmt cannot pass per-file flags, so the config key is the fix).

## Open question for the fix (design, not blocking)

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/assets/app.css` is a **generated** artifact (`bun run build:css` output, committed per the file header and deployed without a build step). Once the pass stops aborting, treefmt will commit Biome's reformat of both files (~3,000 lines of mechanical churn). Decide whether to keep letting Biome format the generated `app.css` (status-quo intent) or add it to `treefmt.toml` `[global] excludes` / format it inside the build, so regeneration does not fight the formatter.

## Acceptance

- `nix run .#format -- pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css` exits 0 (no parse error) and a second run reports `0 changed`.
- A scheduled `auto-format` run on `main` completes successfully and commits (or verifies clean) rather than failing on the `ui.css` parse error.
- The generated-`app.css` question above is resolved with the choice recorded.

Related: #2015 (format auto-fix PoC), #5230 (push-race retry), #6153 (Tailwind/DaisyUI aggregator UI).

## Acceptance criteria

- `nix run .#format` (treefmt) completes on a tree containing `pm-stack/aggregator/src/ui.css` without the Tailwind-directives parse abort.
- The scheduled auto-format workflow (`.github/workflows/auto-format.yml`) goes green on main and commits real formatting output again (it is currently a no-op stuck loop: format, abort, discard).
- `ui.css` keeps its Tailwind v4 / DaisyUI directives (removing them is not an option — the file is authored that way on purpose, Phase C #6153), and `bun run build:css` output is unchanged.

body:
## Summary

`scripts/tests/test_hardware_doc_init.py` — the 9-test regression suite for the #6890 hardware-doc-init branch-routing fix (landed via PR #7035) — is run by no workflow, flake check, or justfile recipe. The pins verify only when a human remembers to run the suite by hand, so the branch-routing contract can silently regress again.

## Evidence (verified 2026-11-08, main 35390d33ac)

- The suite: `scripts/tests/test_hardware_doc_init.py` (9 tests; oracle stated in its docstring: fixture git repositories; the script promises an existing, clean, behind checkout is fast-forwarded and every unsafe state warns and is left byte-identical). Tests: absent target cloned, behind checkout fast-forwarded, no-upstream / detached / dirty / diverged / unpushed states warn and stay untouched, non-repo target errors, up-to-date reports up-to-date.
- Run by hand on the laptop at main 35390d33ac: `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_hardware_doc_init.py'` → **9 tests, OK** (1.1s). The suite is green; it is simply never executed by automation.
- Wiring check: `grep -rn hardware .github/workflows/` → no hits for this suite. `scripts-test.yml` names exactly three Python suites (`test_update_nixpkgs_inputs.py` #603, `test_worker_preflight.py` #4862, `test_bitwarden_load_secrets.py` #5650) plus the power-guard discover and the sops shell suite — this suite is not among them. `research-workflow.yml` runs `test_*workflow*.py` + `test_plan_check.py`, which do not match this file. No flake check or justfile recipe mentions it either.
- The script it pins is live: `scripts/hardware-doc-init.sh` "also runs automatically in the devshell" (`.agents/skills/hardware-device-research/SKILL.md:37`), so a routing regression reaches real checkouts with no test signal.

## Why it matters

#6890 was exactly the failure mode this suite exists to catch: the update block was unreachable (a condition requiring `$TARGET/.git` to both exist and not exist), so a clean, behind checkout was adopted as-is with no fetch, warning, or update — silently. The fix and its fixture-oracle suite landed, but with no CI wiring the same class of routing break can return unnoticed, in a script that runs automatically in the devshell.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A workflow step (the natural home is `scripts-test.yml`, alongside the other three named Python suites) runs `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests -p 'test_hardware_doc_init.py'` on the same triggers as the sibling suites.
- [ ] The step is verified to actually execute the suite (a run reports "Ran 9 tests"), not silently match zero files.
- [ ] The suite passes on main after the wiring lands.

## Notes

- Same verified-nowhere class as #5935 / #6082 / #6092 / #6093, but a distinct suite and script; not a duplicate of the #6890 fix (closed) — this is only about the missing CI wiring for its regression tests.
- Filed by new-issue-creator-code-b, 2026-11-08 run.

body:
## Implementation: Turso/libsql HTTP adapter v1 (from the #5806 decision record)

Parent contract: #5672 Part B (foreign data-store adapters) and B3. Design decision record: #5806 (recorded 2026-11-08, task 12805) — this issue implements exactly that record; it does not re-decide it.

### Scope (v1)
- Raw libsql HTTP protocol client (v2 pipeline, JSON) inside pkgs/id — no libsql crate, no new SQLite-family dependency (the shipped-build guard test `test_the_lock_has_no_sqlite_with_logsync_wired` must stay green).
- Read-only, live pass-through querying of a remote Turso/libsql database as an ID foreign data source, addressed by a local alias (`id://foreign/libsql/<alias>`) resolved from local config to {url, credential reference}.
- Typed value mapping and validation exactly as specified in the #5806 record, including the named lossy corners (no silent coercion; type-mismatch is an error).
- Grant/existence-privacy enforcement: predicates pushed into the remote query; query shapes that cannot be enforced without leaking are refused, not degraded. Not-found and not-granted are indistinguishable to the caller.
- Credential handling: token obtained via the configured credential reference at call time; never stored in ID data, payloads, or logs.

### Out of scope (v1)
- Writes / appends to the foreign store (refused explicitly; a follow-on design may revisit, per #5672 non-goals).
- Materialized caching into redb (follow-on; the record names the conditions under which it may be added).
- Public-Turso exposure mechanics (design ticket 4 under #5672 owns discovery, limits, unpublish).

### Acceptance
- Adapter queries a remote libsql database over HTTP with the record's type mapping; lossy-corner tests cover u64 > i64::MAX, f64 precision, non-UTF8 bytes, NULL vs empty, and bool encoding.
- No SQLite-family dependency enters the shipped graph (guard test passes unmodified); FUEL_BUDGETS untouched.
- Error/timeout behavior matches the record (bounded retries for reads only, circuit breaker, auth failure is fatal and non-retried).
- Tests name their oracle per the testing doctrine (reference mapping table from the record).

title: id(web/markdown): #3740's alert-marker restore unescapes markers in blockquotes that start with a fence or HTML block — quote_has_content is never marked on the fence/HTML path

body:
## Finding

PR #3740's save-side `restore_github_alert_markers` only unescapes a GitHub alert marker when it is the first content of its blockquote — its own doc comment: "Markers elsewhere remain ordinary escaped text." The tracking has a hole for one first-block shape: when a blockquote's first block is a fenced code block or an HTML block, no line on that path ever marks `quote_has_content`, so the quote still counts as "empty" when a later paragraph begins. A standalone escaped marker line there (`\[\!NOTE\]` with a hard break — authored literal text, not an alert) is then unescaped and its hard-break backslash is stripped, silently rewriting authored text on save. The parse side got this right (`preserve_github_alert_marker_breaks` requires the first child to be a Paragraph), and the nested-quote first-block case is handled (content lines mark ancestors) — fence/HTML-first is the unhandled sibling.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3740 (merged, merge commit `bf26382e60c00db923a57915128d382af4e109be`) — "Fix #1376: preserve GitHub alert blockquotes". #1376 is CLOSED; deduped: searches for the function name / fence-first case returned no covering issue.
- Current main `2aca793a345a88b2f11a815fc190da4df07e0ee0`, `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`, `restore_github_alert_markers` at `:4254`:
  - The fence-interior branch, the HTML-interior branch, and the fence/HTML opening-line branches all `continue` without touching `quote_has_content` — verified by reading the function top to bottom: `quote_has_content` is written only in the depth-0 reset, the guard reset, and the final marker/content branch.
  - `quote_is_empty` is computed as `!quote_has_content[..=depth].iter().any(...)`, so after a fence-first blockquote the later marker line still sees an "empty" quote and is unescaped (with the hard-break suffix stripped).
- Trace (this run, on the main code): input lines `> ``` `, `> code`, `> ``` `, `>`, `> \[\!NOTE\]\`, `> Body.` — the three fence lines pass through the fence branches unmarked; the marker line then satisfies `quote_is_empty` and is rewritten to `> [!NOTE]`, losing the authored escape and the hard break.
- PR #3740's tests pin the neighbouring cases — marker text inside a fence stays verbatim (`test_alert_marker_text_inside_code_fence_is_untouched`), and a nested quote as first block does not make an alert (`test_nested_first_block_does_not_make_alert`) — but no test has a fence or HTML block as the quote's first block followed by a literal marker line.

## Why it matters

This is the same silent-rewriting class #3740 was written to eliminate, in the one first-block configuration its tests do not cover: a document that quotes a code sample and then writes a literal `[!NOTE]`-looking line loses the escape (and a hard break) on the first save, so the text no longer round-trips as authored.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A blockquote whose first block is a fence or an HTML block counts as having content: a later standalone escaped marker line in it stays escaped, hard break intact.
- [ ] Genuine alerts (marker as the quote's first content) still restore, and the existing #3740 fixpoint tests still pass.
- [ ] A regression test pins the fence-first (and ideally HTML-first) blockquote with a following literal marker line as a save fixpoint.

body:
## Finding

PR #3737 extracted the Cost Explorer computations into `aa-explorer-computations.js` so that, in its own words, "the browser and tests now execute the same implementations". For three of the nine functions that is not true on current main: `logEdges`, `scoreEdges`, and `bandIndex` were copied into the shared module and imported by the page script, but their original inline definitions inside the script's IIFE were never removed. The inline definitions shadow the module imports for every call site inside the IIFE, so the browser runs the untested inline copies of the banding functions while the Bun tests exercise the module copies. Today the copies are identical, so nothing renders wrong yet — but any future fix to the module's banding code (the code under test) will silently not reach the browser, and a fix to the inline copies will not be tested.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3737 (merged, merge commit `adfa050a8094cae558135bccb1d74431e4afff8d`) — "test(aggregator): cover Cost Explorer client computations". Deduped: searches for the module name / shadowing returned no covering issue.
- Current main `2aca793a345a88b2f11a815fc190da4df07e0ee0`, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts`:
  - `:3940` the emitted page script imports all nine from the module: `import { applyInequalityFilters, bandIndex, computeRecommendations, logEdges, normName, paretoSet, pctRank, projectTask, scoreEdges } from "/assets/aa-explorer-computations.js";`
  - `:4960` `function logEdges(vals, n)`, `:4969` `function scoreEdges(rows, n)`, `:4977` `function bandIndex(v, edges)` — identical definitions still declared inside the IIFE, shadowing the imports.
  - In-IIFE call sites use the shadowed names: `:5083-5085` (`logEdges`/`scoreEdges` for the band comparisons), `:5092` and `:5154` (`bandIndex`).
  - The other six functions have no inline twin and genuinely run from the module.
- Verified this run: the inline bodies at `:4960-4983` and the module's `aa-explorer-computations.js` exports are currently byte-for-byte equivalent in logic — this is a latent divergence, not a live numeric bug.
- The guard test does not catch it: `pm-stack/aggregator/test/aa.test.ts:783` ("/aa loads the same browser computation module imported by Bun tests") asserts the page contains the module import and that the asset serves `computeRecommendations`/`projectTask`; it never checks for inline redefinitions.
- Secondary: the server-side import of the same module in `render.ts` (`:45-55`) has no call site in `render.ts` outside the emitted script string.

## Why it matters

The entire point of #3737 was one implementation under test. For the three banding functions — the ones that decide band edges and membership for the comparison shortlists — the guarantee is illusory, and the failure mode is silent: the first edit that lands in only one copy splits shipped behaviour from tested behaviour with every test green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The inline `logEdges`/`scoreEdges`/`bandIndex` definitions are removed from the emitted script, so all nine computations run from the shared module in the browser (or, if a local copy is genuinely needed, it is no longer claimed/tested as shared).
- [ ] A regression test fails if the emitted page script redefines any name it imports from `aa-explorer-computations.js`.
- [ ] The existing aa / aa-explorer-computations suites still pass.

title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): every OpenCode server call is unauthenticated — session create always 401s, and the delete gate trusts curl's exit status

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` reaches the laptop OpenCode server with HTTP Basic auth read from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` (`_server_get`). `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` reaches the **same server on the same port with plain `curl -s` and no auth at all** — every one of its six server calls (session create, per-id get, messages, delete ×3).

Verified against `http://127.0.0.1:13420` on 2026-11-08:

```
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{}' http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session
401
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:13420/api/session/nope
401
  body: {"_tag":"UnauthorizedError","message":"Authentication required"}
$ curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null ...   # curl exit status
0                                 # <- 401 is still a "successful" curl
```

## Consequences in the live path

1. **Session creation cannot succeed.** `POST /api/session` returns `{"_tag":"UnauthorizedError",...}` with no `id`. `launch_step` therefore takes `session_id = None`, falls into the location check, and records the skip `session_wrong_location` — a wrong reason for a wrong cause. Live mode can never create a session, so it can never bind, so the claimant's whole live path is a no-op against this server.
2. **`returncode == 0` is not a success test for the delete.** `supervision_step` gates its delete on `delete_result.returncode == 0`. A 401 satisfies that. Today the zero-message gate happens to block it (`len(json.loads('{"_tag":...,"message":...}')) == 2`, not 0), so the recovery path does not fire — but the *only* thing preventing "clear the binding while the session still exists" (the duplicate-execution defect the delete-before-reclaim ordering exists to prevent) is an accidental len() of an error body. That is exactly the fail-open shape the packet's step 1b forbids.
3. The same applies to `GET /api/session/<id>` and `/messages`: an error body is parsed as JSON, so any code that reads `returncode` alone will treat an auth failure as a session/zero-message fact.

Note the correct credentialed path already exists in this repo: `pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts` sends the Basic header on the same v2 API.

## Suggested acceptance

1. One transport helper in `claimant.py` (Basic auth from the same auth file `poll.py` uses, honouring `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE`), used by every server call; no bare `curl` without the header.
2. Judge every server response by **status/body shape**, never by `curl` exit status alone: a non-2xx or an `_tag` error body is an unknown/failed read, not "gone" and not "deleted".
3. Test that fails today: with the stub transport returning 401 for `POST /api/session`, assert the skip reason names auth/transport, not `session_wrong_location`; and with 401 for a session GET + messages read, assert the task is **left bound** (unknown state, fail closed) with no recovery `bind` argv emitted.
4. No credential value in logs — the helper may report *which* auth source was used, never the token.

Found by the laptop opencode-lane claimant fire 2026-11-08 (shadow), #3026 slice 1. Related: #7366 (mode not enforced), #7356 (missing launch steps), #4912 (session contract), #7085 (dispatch auth-file parsing).

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `claimant.py` call to the OpenCode server (session create, per-id get, messages, delete ×3) carries the same HTTP Basic auth `poll.py` reads from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` — no unauthenticated `curl -s` remains in the claimant.
- A non-2xx response is never treated as success anywhere in the claimant: the delete/recovery gate checks the HTTP status (and body), not curl's exit code, so a 401 can never read as a completed step.
- A live-mode fire against the laptop server (127.0.0.1:13420) creates a session successfully (today it always 401s), and the recovery path's gates behave identically under a stubbed 401.

title: repo-queue(client): a list response over 32 KiB comes back chunked — the client does not de-chunk, parses Null, and silently prints "(no tasks)" for a 178-row queue

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: meta/enriched
labels.description: Intake review done: acceptance criteria, links, and normalized labels added

body:
## Symptom

`repo-queue list` silently reports an **empty queue** when its response exceeds 32 KiB, with exit code 0:

```
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --limit 97 | tail -n +3 | grep -c '^task '
97
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --limit 98
(no tasks)
$ echo $?
0
```

The same queue holds **178 claimed rows** at the time of writing (verified by talking to the broker directly). The threshold is not the row count, it is the byte size of the response: the largest plain-bodied reply I could get was 32 602 bytes (`--limit 97`, non-rich); every reply from 33 053 bytes up came back chunked.

`/health` is unaffected for the same queue, and `--limit` up to the 500 maximum is accepted without complaint.

## Cause

`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/queue_broker.rs` serves `/list` through `tiny_http`, which switches from `Content-Length` to `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` once the body passes ~32 KiB:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK | Content-Length: 32602        # --limit 97
HTTP/1.1 200 OK | Transfer-Encoding: chunked   # --limit 98
```

The client's direct-broker transport (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:120-130`) reads to EOF and then does:

```rust
let split = raw.windows(4).position(|w| w == b"\r\n\r\n")...;
let resp_body: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&raw[split + 4..]).unwrap_or(Value::Null);
```

It never de-chunks. So `serde_json` sees `2000\r\n{"ok":true,...` and fails; `unwrap_or(Value::Null)` turns that failure into `Null`; `cmd_list` (client.rs:1121-1129) does `resp.get("rows")...unwrap_or_default()` → empty vec → prints `(no tasks)` and returns 0.

Nothing logs, warns or exits non-zero: a truncated/chunked read is indistinguishable from an empty queue.

## Impact

- **Any queue large enough to exceed 32 KiB per page reads as empty.** For `repo-health-code-pilot` that is `--limit` ≥ 98 with `rich`, or ≥ 98 without. Raising the limit to see more rows makes the result *worse*: exactly the pages that would carry the census return nothing.
- **This is a second, independent cause of the `poll.py` blindness in #7325.** Even after #7325 gives `list` a JSON mode and `fetch_claimed_rows()` parses it, a `--limit` that makes the response large enough will still yield zero rows — and #7325's proposed fix is to raise the limit.
- **Independent truncation in `poll.py` today:** `fetch_claimed_rows()` passes no `--limit`, and the CLI/broker default is 20 (`LIST_LIMIT_DEFAULT`). `repo-health-code-pilot` holds 158 claimed `opencode`-lane rows; only the first 20 by `(priority, created_at)` are ever read, so a `handed_off` candidate sorting past row 20 is invisible no matter what the JSON mode does.

## Proposed fix

- Decode `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` in `direct_roundtrip` (and any other hand-rolled HTTP parse in this client), and **fail closed** — non-zero exit with a message — when a 200 body cannot be parsed, instead of `unwrap_or(Value::Null)`. A silent empty list is the worst possible outcome for a queue reader.
- Have `poll.py` request an explicit high `--limit` (500) so a large claimed set is read whole, and treat "row count == requested limit" as possibly-truncated rather than proven complete (the same escalating-limit rule `poll.py` already applies to the OpenCode session list).
- Consider making `/list` always send `Content-Length`, since the broker materialises the whole body anyway.

## Verification

```
$ python3 - <<'PY'   # direct broker read, de-chunked
# limit=98 -> 98 rows; limit=500 -> 189 rows
PY
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --limit 200 | tail -n +3 | grep -c '^task '
# expected: 178 (currently 0)
```

Related: #7325 (poll.py table-vs-JSON, the first cause of the same blindness), #7349 (`list`/`health` reject `--worker`), #6865 (claimant.py imports), #3026 (slice 1).

## Acceptance criteria

- `repo-queue list` returns the true rows for a response over 32 KiB (chunked transfer encoding) — e.g. `--queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --limit 98` and above print the claimed rows instead of `(no tasks)`, with the row count matching a direct broker read.
- A malformed or unparseable response can never print `(no tasks)` with exit code 0: parse failure is a loud non-zero error.
- A regression test covers a >32 KiB list response end to end.

title: repo-queue: `list` and `health` reject `--worker`, which the opencode-claimant packet mandates on every verb

body:
## Symptom

The opencode-claimant packet mandates `--worker opencode-claimant` on **every** `repo-queue` verb it uses. The deployed binary rejects that flag on two of the verbs the claimant's read path depends on:

```
$ repo-queue health --queue repo-health-code-pilot --worker opencode-claimant
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --worker

$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --worker opencode-claimant
repo-queue: unrecognized argument: --worker
```

Verbs that accept it (probed 2026-11-08): `bind`, `checkpoint`, `heartbeat`, `claim`, `fail`, `complete`, `park`, `block`, `lane`.
Verbs that reject it: `list`, `health`.

## Impact

- `poll.py`'s `fetch_claimed_rows()` does **not** pass `--worker`, so it is unaffected today — but any attempt to bring the read path into line with the packet (as #7325's fix will touch) fails at the CLI.
- The packet's own contract ("pass `--worker opencode-claimant` on every verb you use") is unsatisfiable as written for the read verbs, so a fire that follows the packet literally aborts on its first `health` call.
- Note the failure mode is at least loud (`unrecognized argument`) rather than silently ignored — unlike #3278.

## Proposed fix

Either accept (and ignore, or use for attribution) `--worker` on `list` and `health`, or amend the claimant packet to scope `--worker` to the mutating verbs only. The former keeps the packet uniform and matches every other verb.

## Verification

```
$ repo-queue list --queue repo-health-code-pilot --status claimed --worker opencode-claimant
# should return the table, not an error
```

Related: #7325 (poll.py table-vs-JSON), #6865 (claimant.py imports), #3026 (slice 1).

body:
## Defect

`bin/sync-models.mjs` silently skips a provider whose section is absent from the runtime overlay, and reports the run as up-to-date — so a provider rename leaves the model catalog orphaned under the old id forever, with a green daily service.

## What happened (2026-11-07)

- The provider rename (opencode#1823: `antigravity-direct` -> `_antigravity`, `claude-code` -> `_claude`, etc.) updated the tracked config and this script's target list (`for (const targetProvider of ['_antigravity'])`).
- The runtime overlay (`~/.local/state/opencode/opencode-runtime.jsonc`, code#4544) still keyed the Antigravity catalog `"antigravity-direct"`. The base config's `_antigravity` block carries no inline models by design ("maintained by sync-models in the runtime overlay").
- The sync loop guards `if (!config.provider[targetProvider]) continue;` — with no `_antigravity` key in the overlay, the Antigravity sync no-ops. The run summary printed "0 models added, 0 updated, 0 removed — All providers are already up-to-date!" and the service exited success (verified 2026-11-07 22:58 CST run).
- Consequence: merged config gave `_antigravity` zero models, so route leaf `_antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash` resolved to no models after route transforms and route `gemini-flash-plan` was never built. Every pinned turn failed `provider.no-route`; zero route_attempts and zero route_decisions for ~27h (last success 2026-11-07T01:52:52Z) despite the Gemini weekly window sitting at 4% used.

## Repair applied (instance)

Renamed the overlay provider key `"antigravity-direct"` -> `"_antigravity"` (single key, models unchanged), restarted opencode + openclaw-gateway. First post-fix attempt: 2026-11-08T05:00:17Z `_antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash` success; `gemini-flash-plan` decisions (drawn) resumed. With the key present, the deployed sync-models (which already targets `_antigravity`) maintains the catalog again.

## Fix wanted

1. When a target provider is absent from the overlay but a catalog exists under a known legacy/alias id, migrate the key (or at minimum log loudly and exit non-zero) — never report up-to-date.
2. Consider creating the target section when the upstream discovery returned models for it, instead of requiring the section to pre-exist.
3. The summary should distinguish "provider skipped (section absent)" from "provider in sync".

Related: fork gate defect developing-today-forks/opencode#1974 (the same door was also held by a provider-wide quota skip; separate mechanism, removed the same night).

title: pm-dispatch(queue): PostgREST row bodies shape-trusted — null/non-JSON 200 escapes as raw TypeError/SyntaxError, string body resolves as a phantom TaskRow

body:
## Problem

pm-dispatch's Supabase queue client (`pm-stack/dispatch/src/queue.ts`) shape-trusts PostgREST response bodies in its three row-reading methods. Wrong-shape 200 bodies either escape the module's `QueueError` boundary as raw errors or are silently returned as phantom task rows:

- `patchTask` (queue.ts:109): `const rows = text.trim() ? (JSON.parse(text) as TaskRow[]) : []` — a bare cast, no array check.
- `getTask` (queue.ts:114-122): `const rows = (await res.json()) as TaskRow[]` — same bare cast.
- `findByDedupeKey` (queue.ts:131-139): same bare cast via `res.json()`.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ cf39c3aba1)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-dispatch-queue` (laptop) imports the real `queue.ts` and stubs `fetch` with a 200 response:

| Body | patchTask | getTask | findByDedupeKey |
|---|---|---|---|
| control `[{id:7,...}]` | resolves row 7 | resolves row 7 | resolves row 7 |
| `null` | raw `TypeError: null is not an object (evaluating 'rows[0]')` | raw `TypeError` | raw `TypeError` |
| `"x"` (JSON string) | **resolves `"x"` as a TaskRow** | **resolves `"x"`** | **resolves `"x"`** |
| `{...}` (object) | QueueError "matched no row" | resolves `null` | resolves `null` |
| `not json{` | raw `SyntaxError: JSON Parse error` | raw `SyntaxError` | raw `SyntaxError` |

## Why it matters

- `findByDedupeKey` is the `findExisting` callback for `enqueueDispatchTask` (server.ts:499), whose contract is documented at server.ts:369-372: "Lookup failures must resolve to null (unknown), never throw." A 200 with a null or non-JSON body violates that contract and kills the whole `POST /v1/tasks` / `POST /v1/sessions` request with a raw TypeError/SyntaxError instead of degrading to "no known existing row" (the terminal-status check in `isPreExistingTaskRow`, server.ts:330, is the designed backstop).
- A string body resolves as a phantom `TaskRow`: `isPreExistingTaskRow` then reads `.status`/`.id` off a string (both `undefined`), silently misclassifying pre-existing-row detection — the exact #2677/#4661 logic this module exists to get right.
- `patchTask` is on the session-launch path (server.ts:138/:160, launch_annotations.ts:53): a raw SyntaxError/TypeError there escapes the `QueueError` (HTTP 502) vocabulary callers handle, so a malformed PostgREST 200 surfaces as an unhandled 500-class crash instead of a queue error.
- Sibling modules have already been hardened for this exact pattern (dispatch github.ts in #7101, opencode.ts in #7085); `queue.ts` is the remaining unguarded response reader in dispatch. Its shipped tests (`test/queue.test.ts`) cover only the `ensureWorker` memo — none of the row readers.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `patchTask`, `getTask`, and `findByDedupeKey` validate that a parsed 200 body is an array (and that the first element, when present, is a plain object with a numeric `id`) before treating it as a `TaskRow`.
- [ ] Null, scalar, object, and non-JSON 200 bodies produce the module's own vocabulary: `QueueError` for `patchTask`; `null` ("unknown") for `getTask`/`findByDedupeKey` lookup failures — never a raw `TypeError`/`SyntaxError`, and never a phantom non-object row.
- [ ] New regression tests in `pm-stack/dispatch/test/queue.test.ts` (stub-fetch style, mirroring the existing file) cover null / string / object / non-JSON bodies for all three methods; the control array body still resolves the row.
- [ ] Existing dispatch test suite stays green.

# id(tag): PR #3756 — the only fix for #1735 — is conflicting, partially superseded by merged PR #3763, and untouched since 2026-11-01; shepherd it or supersede it

## Finding

PR #3756 ("fix(id): escape synced fields in TSV renderers", closes #1735) is a stale-but-needed PR whose scope has been half-landed by another PR: its `id list` / `id find` hunks were implemented and merged by PR #3763 (for issue #1742) using the canonical `plain_field`/`tsv_row` helpers, while its unique remainder — the `id tag` rendering for still-open issue #1735 — was never landed. The PR no longer merges, its own helper diverges from the rendering contract that is now canonical on main, and it has had no movement since the day it was opened.

## Evidence

- PR #3756: OPEN, single commit, head `6f22d4719e23`, base `dad9ddd1725c` (the PR #3754 merge), last updated 2026-11-01T16:17Z. Live check this run: `mergeable: CONFLICTING` / `mergeStateStatus: DIRTY`; compare API shows main ~3507 commits ahead of its head (head 1 commit ahead).
- Partially superseded: PR #3763 MERGED 2026-11-01T16:13Z (merge `dee3cb93d25e`, verified ancestor of current main) covers the same list.rs sites (3) and the same helpers.rs find renderers (`print_match_cli` / `print_matches_cli` / `print_match_repl`) that PR #3756 touches, via `commands::text::plain_field` and the new `tsv_row`. Issue #1742 is CLOSED.
- Still needed: issue #1735 ("id(tag): meta-tag TSV output renders subject/key/value raw…") is OPEN. On current main, `pkgs/id/src/commands/tag.rs` still prints raw: `print_tag_line` (lines 379–384) interpolates subject/key unescaped and `format_value` (line ~110) returns value text with no escaping; the `tag set:` lines (255–256) print subject/key raw. No `display_text_field` exists on main (code search: no hits).
- Helper divergence: PR #3756's new `helpers::display_text_field` quotes a field when it contains ANY whitespace (a plain space in "two words" gets JSON-quoted) and does not treat category-Cf format characters as structure-breaking (a bidi override such as U+202E passes through raw). The canonical `plain_field` on current main (`pkgs/id/src/commands/text.rs`) quotes only on Cc controls, Cf format characters, and U+2028/U+2029, and escapes Cf as `\uXXXX`; that module's contract states every plain renderer accounts for both classes and no surface re-derives the character set. Landing PR #3756 as-is would install a second, weaker, incompatible TSV escaper beside it.
- The blocker PR #3756's body cites no longer exists: its tests were blocked by the pre-existing #3751 compile break (the displaced `Command` derive); that break was fixed on main by merged PR #3754, so a rebase today compiles past it.

## Why it matters

#1735 is a live row/column-forging bug in `id tag` output (a newline in a synced tag value forges rows, a tab forges columns) and PR #3756 is its only fix. Left rotting, it either gets re-implemented from scratch — duplicating work and risking the divergent helper landing anyway — or the tag surface stays forgeable after its list/find siblings were fixed. The salvageable core is small: the tag.rs application sites and their tests, re-based onto `plain_field`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] PR #3756 is rebased on current main with only its tag scope kept: `print_tag_line` / `format_tag_line`, `format_value`, and the `tag set:` lines in `pkgs/id/src/commands/tag.rs` render subject/key/value through `plain_field` (or an equivalent single shared helper), with PR #3756's per-field LF/TAB/CR renderer tests ported to pin it — OR PR #3756 is closed with a note on issue #1735 naming the superseding PR/plan (salvage-diff first, per the lifecycle protocol).
- [ ] The list.rs and helpers.rs find-renderer hunks of PR #3756 are dropped, not landed: those sites already render through `plain_field`/`tsv_row` on main (PR #3763), and no second TSV escaper (`display_text_field`) is added.
- [ ] On merge, issue #1735 closes via the PR; a stored tag field containing LF/TAB/CR or a Cf character renders as one row with the real tab delimiters only.

title: pm-dispatch(github): GitHub API response bodies are shape-trusted — a token-less access-token reply is sent as Bearer undefined, a wrong-shape create reply is returned as a successful issue, and a null create body falls back to a duplicate gh create

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/github.ts` — the GitHub App client every pm-dispatch session/task launch uses to create its tracking issue, verify attach targets, comment, and label — reads every GitHub API response body through a bare TypeScript cast and never validates the shape. A wrong-shape **200/201** from the API (or any intermediary that answers 2xx with an unexpected body) is silently trusted:

- `github.ts:104-105` — the installation lookup: `const data = (await res.json()) as { id: number }; installationId = data.id;`
- `github.ts:110-112` — the access-token mint: `const data = (await res.json()) as { token: string; expires_at: string };` the token is cached and returned unvalidated.
- `github.ts:183-184` — issue creation: `const data = (await res.json()) as { number: number; html_url: string }; return { number: data.number, url: data.html_url };`
- `github.ts:230-241` — issue lookup (`getIssue`): the same cast for `{ number, state, html_url, pull_request? }`.

This is the dispatch sibling of the projector GitHub client fixed in #6954 ("a token-less access-token reply is returned as a valid app token") and of the dispatch OpenCode client fixed in #7085 — this module was never given the same boundary. `test/attach_verify.test.ts` exercises `getIssue` only with well-formed bodies and a 404; no test feeds the client a wrong-shape 2xx.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Probe on the laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-dispatch-github` (`probe.ts`, `probe2.ts`): the real `src/github.ts` copied verbatim (md5 `90762430977c01650312e325510c915a` on both sides, current main `bfa5caede7622a9e3dee01beeec110e2c5fde2bf`), `fetch` stubbed in the style of `test/attach_verify.test.ts`, and a fake `gh` first in PATH so the CLI fallback is deterministic. Control cases pass: a well-formed installation/token/create sequence returns `{ number: 123, url: "…/issues/123" }`, and a well-formed lookup returns the issue.

With a wrong-shape 2xx, the client does **not** raise a boundary error:

1. **Installation `{}`** → the token mint is POSTed to `/app/installations/undefined/access_tokens` (the undefined id used verbatim) and the flow "succeeds".
2. **Access-token `{}`** → issue creation proceeds with the header `Authorization: Bearer undefined` and is reported as success (the probe stub records `authIsUndefined: true` on the create call). A numeric token (`{ token: 123, … }`) is likewise coerced and sent as `Bearer 123`. A bad `expires_at` is cached as `expiresAt: NaN`.
3. **Create-issue `{}`** → `createIssue` returns `{}` — i.e. `{ number: undefined, url: undefined }` — **as a success**. Downstream (`src/server.ts`) that phantom ref feeds `canonicalDedupeKey(kind, repo, issue.number)`, the agent-note `comment(repo, issue.number, …)` and `addLabels(repo, issue.number, …)` calls, and the 201 response's `issue_number` — all against an issue that was never identified.
4. **Create-issue `{ number: "abc", html_url: 42 }`** → returned verbatim as `{ number: "abc", url: 42 }`.
5. **Lookup `{}`** → `getIssue` returns a non-null info with `number`/`state`/`url` all `undefined` (only `isPullRequest: false` survives serialization). The #3007 attach verification then rejects the target with `issue #<n> … is undefined, not open` — a live, open issue refused on a fabricated state.
6. **JSON `null` bodies** (installation, token, create, lookup) → a raw `TypeError` (`null is not an object (evaluating 'data.token')` / `'data.number'` / `'(await res.json()).id'`) escapes the parse site, is caught only by the generic app-route fallback, and is misreported as a dual-route failure ("issue create failed via app (…) and via gh (…)"). For **issue creation this is worse than a confusing error**: the app POST may already have created the issue server-side before its body failed to parse, and the fallback then creates a **second** tracking issue via `gh`.

## Why it matters

pm-dispatch is the fleet's launch door: every dispatched session/task anchors its queue packet, dedupe key, agent-note comment, and labels to the issue identity this client returns. A single malformed 2xx can (a) send a literal `Bearer undefined` credential, (b) anchor a real queue task to a phantom `undefined` issue, (c) reject a valid attach target as "undefined, not open", or (d) duplicate the tracking issue across the app and `gh` routes. The failure mode is silent or misattributed in every case — nothing in the response tells the operator the GitHub reply itself was malformed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every `res.json()` body in `pm-stack/dispatch/src/github.ts` (installation lookup, access-token mint, issue create, issue lookup) is validated before use: the body must be a JSON object; `id` a positive integer; `token` a non-empty string with a parseable `expires_at`; create/lookup `number` an integer, `state` and `html_url` strings. Violations raise `GitHubError` naming the endpoint and the malformed field — never a raw `TypeError`/`SyntaxError`, never a silently coerced or `undefined` value.
- [ ] A malformed **2xx create-issue** body does not trigger the `gh` fallback create (the issue may already exist server-side); it surfaces as an explicit error. Malformed installation/token replies may still fall back to `gh` (no side effect has happened yet), with the malformed-body reason preserved in the combined error.
- [ ] New regression tests (new `test/github.test.ts` or extending `test/attach_verify.test.ts`, stubbed `fetch` in the existing style) cover at least: installation `{}`, token `{}`, token numeric, create `{}`, create wrong-typed fields, lookup `{}`, and a `null` body — each failing on the pre-fix code — while the well-formed control cases and the existing dispatch suite stay green.
- [ ] No behavior change for well-formed responses or for definitive HTTP failures (404 lookup still returns `null`; non-2xx still raises/falls back as today).

Dedup: searched open + closed issues for `installationToken`, "dispatch github shape", and pm-dispatch GitHub-client titles — no hits. #6954 covers `pm-stack/projector/src/github.ts`, not this client; #7085 covers `pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts`, not this module.

## Branch hygiene is broken in three places at once — forensics 2026-11-07

Full forensics: ~/workspace/scratch/branch-hygiene-forensics-2026-11-07.md (live-verified 2026-11-07 ~21:40 CST; related: closure audit #7079, smart janitor #6884, branch-cleanup failure history #1615).

### The numbers (live tonight)
- code: **1,698** remote branches = **1,309 `archive/janitor-*`** (77%) + 308 `queue/*` + ~81 others. Of the 1,000 most recent merged PRs (Nov 2-8): **0** head branches survive — `delete_branch_on_merge=true` works there.
- opencode 321 / openchamber 221 / darwin-nix 46: `delete_branch_on_merge=false` in all three; surviving merged-PR heads in samples: opencode 23/890, openchamber 18/834, darwin-nix 22/729.

### Defect 1 — the GitHub Action auditor deletes ~nothing (all 4 repos, every run)
`branch-cleanup.yml` is active, LIVE (`BRANCH_CLEANUP_LIVE=true`), runs daily on schedule, and has reported **`0 candidates` in every run examined** (2026-11-05 runs x3 repos, 2026-11-06 code, today's runs x4). Cause chain:
- (a) The Action's 14-day inactivity gate reads the **newest commit date on the branch**, but the fleet's merge style keeps topping merged lanes' trees up: branch names like `queue/1193-547-*` (Oct-era tasks) carry commits dated Nov 5-7. Today's run in opencode: 321 fetched, 311 skipped (295 "SKIP active", 16 open-PR heads), 0 deletions. Old merged branches never age past the gate.
- (b) Its candidate test is `git merge-base --is-ancestor` (SHA ancestry); squash/rebase-style landings never qualify even if they did age out. The Muse cron sweep uses the stronger standard (merged-PR check) and deletes 70-100/day.
- (c) code's copy has `timeout-minutes: 5` while its fetch alone names 403 refs — today's scheduled run sat `queued` 14h+ and a manual dispatch was cancelled. Raise to match opencode's 30.
The Action currently provides false assurance: green runs, zero effect.

### Defect 2 — `delete_branch_on_merge=false` in 3 of 4 repos
opencode, openchamber, darwin-nix (and both fleet repos). Known since the 2026-10-27 settings audit (code=true; others=false, recorded as "a root cause of branch pileup") but never flipped. **Drew's word needed** — it changes repo behavior fleet-wide. One setting per repo ends the merged-PR-head class permanently in those repos.

### Defect 3 — unhandled registry escalation never fired
The Muse `branch-cleanup-sweep` cron (daily 07:12 CT) deletes merged branches fine (73 today) but its registry of unmerged/no-PR branches holds **209 entries, oldest first-seen 2026-11-01 — 6 days old today, crossing the job's own >7-day "name to Drew" threshold tomorrow (Sun 2026-11-08)**. The escalation is only a line in the cron's own chat report; there is no tracking issue. This issue is that escalation, filed before the threshold technically trips. The Nov-2 disposition precedent applies: merge in sound work via PR, close dead/superseded with tip SHAs recorded, keep+flag only true judgment calls.

### Fix list
1. Fix `branch-cleanup.yml` in all four repos: base the inactivity clock on the PR/merge date (or drop the date gate for PR-verified merged branches), accept merged-PR evidence as a candidate test (not just SHA ancestry), raise code's timeout to 30, keep the 50/run cap and the fail-closed open-PR read.
2. Drew decision: flip `delete_branch_on_merge` on opencode/openchamber/darwin-nix (+ fleet repos) — recommended yes.
3. Disposition the 209-entry unhandled registry (merge-in-or-close per the Nov-2 precedent).

Labels: queue/queued, source/creator, task/triage, status/needs-triage, priority/normal.

## Acceptance criteria

- `branch-cleanup.yml` in all four repos bases its inactivity clock on PR/merge evidence (not the newest commit date on the branch) and accepts merged-PR evidence as a candidate test, not only SHA ancestry; code's timeout is raised to 30 minutes; the 50/run cap and the fail-closed open-PR read are kept.
- A run of the fixed auditor on at least one repo deletes a non-zero number of verified merged branches (no more perpetual `0 candidates` while merged branches pile up).
- Drew's decision on flipping `delete_branch_on_merge` for opencode / openchamber / darwin-nix is recorded on this issue (the flip itself, if approved, is verified per repo settings).
- The 209-entry unhandled branch registry is dispositioned per the Nov-2 precedent (merge sound work via PR, close dead/superseded with tip SHAs recorded, keep+flag only true judgment calls), with the disposition recorded.

body:
# Agreement checker — fail when ci-policy's tiers and a workflow's triggers disagree (Phase 1)

Phase 1 of the ci-policy agreement design (design issue filed pass 70, 2026-11-07, title "Policy, triggers, enablement must agree — one agreement contract for ci-policy's guard and build workflows"; design doc `files/designs/code-ci-policy-agreement.md` in the `keep-the-four-repos-healthy` goal workspace). This phase is NOT gated on Drew's ruling recorded at the top of the design issue — the checker enforces agreement under any ruling.

## Scope

- Write the tier→trigger mapping into `.github/ci-policy.md`: a basic/PR-tier guard is satisfied by `merge_group` plus its path gate where one existed; a main-tier assignment requires `push: branches: [main]` (path gates as before) or a named main-tier venue running the same check; a `workflow_dispatch:`-only trigger block satisfies no tier.
- Add the missing ci-policy tier-table row for `production-line-guard.yml` (it currently has none — its absence is invisible from the policy side, #6959).
- A checker script under `.github/scripts/` (house style: pure bash, contract tests beside it, per the existing guard scripts) that parses every workflow ci-policy names in a section or tier-table row, compares its `on:` block against the mapping for its assigned tiers, and fails naming the workflow and the missing leg (tier, trigger, or — where the tree can see it — a policy row naming a workflow file that does not exist).
- Wire the checker into `workflow-lint.yml` (active; fires on `pull_request` + `merge_group` over `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/actions/**` and the checker files), so a future trigger sweep cannot land without the check firing in the same change.
- The known disagreements at filing (Phases 2–3 of the design: #6929, #6953, #6959, #6981) land as explicit waiver entries in the checker naming their phase issue and disposition state — the checker is green on main with the disagreement set explicit, never silently exempted. A waiver with no live phase issue fails the checker.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The tier→trigger mapping and the production-line-guard row are in `.github/ci-policy.md`.
- [ ] The checker exists on main, runs in workflow-lint, and passes on the current tree with exactly the Phase 2–3 waivers.
- [ ] Probe evidence posted on this issue: on a scratch branch, remove a tier-required trigger from an in-scope workflow and show the checker fails naming it; add a ci-policy row for a nonexistent workflow and show it fails again.
- [ ] The design issue is commented with the landing state.

Do not re-arm or retire any workflow in this phase — that is Phases 2–3. Do not extend the checker to test suites (that registry is #6185's, design #6186/#6188) or to workflows ci-policy does not name.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

On merged PR #6874 (which fixed #6873 for literal root values), CodeRabbit raised one inline comment with two **Minor** bypass variants of the new `workflow_docs` root guard. Neither was replied to or fixed, and both are still live on current main:

> 1. **Report root-resolving paths in the profile diagnostic.** When either profile sets `workflow_docs` to `docs/..`, validation lets it through. The command can then report a generic path error without the profile file or field. Reject root-resolving values in `load_profile` with the existing profile diagnostic.
> 2. **Reject symlinks that resolve to the repository root.** If either profile names a symlink to its repository root, this guard accepts it. On a fresh mirror, a target symlink can make `--write` place workflow files at the repository root. Resolve `workflow_docs` against its repository and reject the root in both profiles.

## Evidence

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6874 (merged)
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/6874#discussion_r4501614425 — coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-07T12:00:02Z, `scripts/sync_research_workflow.py:54`
- No-response evidence: the thread has no replies and is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-08); Codex reported no findings on this PR, and no fix commit followed the CodeRabbit comment before merge.
- Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-08 via `gh api` reads):
  - `load_profile` (`scripts/sync_research_workflow.py:49-59`) rejects only values with no path parts; the regression test `test_workflow_docs_must_not_name_the_repository_root` covers only `""`, `"."`, `"./"`. A value of `docs/..` passes `load_profile` and only fails later inside `inside()` with the generic "path must be a repository-relative path" error — no profile file or field named.
  - `inside()` (lines 33–39) rejects a resolved path only when it is not relative to the repo root; a symlink resolving exactly to the root passes (`is_relative_to` includes equality), so a `workflow_docs` symlink to the root is treated as a valid docs directory. The existing symlink test covers only a symlink escaping the checkout, not one resolving to the root itself.
- Related: #6873 (closed) covered the literal root values that PR #6874 fixed; these resolved/symlink variants were raised after that fix and are not covered by any open or closed issue (dedupe searched 2026-11-08).

## Acceptance criteria

- `load_profile` rejects any `workflow_docs` value that resolves to the repository root — including `docs/..`-style root-resolving paths and a symlink to the root — in both profiles, using the existing profile diagnostic that names the profile file and field.
- Regression tests cover `docs/..` and symlink-to-root for both the source and target profiles.
- Or resolve this issue by a documented decision explaining why a resolved-root `workflow_docs` is safe.

## Slice 3 of issue #2072 — queue/PM integration views (requirements 1 + 3)

Filed by queue task 12027 (triage of the #2072 remainder, Lane A, 2026-11-07), following the sequencing recorded in the design-triage on #2072 (task 4722, 2026-11-02) and the routing pattern of slices 1–2 (each slice filed only after the previous lands).

**State of the tracker when filed:**
- Slice 0 (design) — done (comment on #2072, 2026-11-02).
- Slice 1 (OpenCode usage exporter) — landed, PR #4680 merged 2026-11-03.
- Slice 2 (GitHub webhook ingestion + hot list) — landed: this slice's predecessor issue #5204 CLOSED 2026-11-04, PR #5327 merged (append-only hot list + consumer checkpoints on main). Slice 3's stated dependency — "needs slice 2 event stream" — is now satisfied.
- Slice 4/7 territory partially advanced elsewhere: issue #4822 (spend-attribution projection) is CLOSED. Slices 5, 6, 7 remain unfiled per the sequencing (they file when their turn comes; slice 3 is next).

## Scope (from #2072 requirements 1 and 3)

1. **The PM stack and the queue must be available TO the external systems** — delegated systems can read queue state and report outcomes into the PM stack through a supported surface, so their work lands in the shared record as it happens instead of being reconstructed later.
2. **One integrated PM + queue view** where the owner can see, in one place:
   - what is queued, and in what order;
   - what has been picked up, and by which system;
   - stats, metrics, graphs and trends over token usage, model selection, plan quotas, and all scheduled jobs.
3. Consume the slice 2 hot-list/event stream (#5204, PR #5327) rather than building a competing ingestion path (the same instruction issue #3321 carries).

## Acceptance

- An external/delegated system can read current queue state (queued order, claimed-by) and submit an outcome report through the integrated surface, verified end-to-end with a real delegated session.
- The integrated view answers, for a given window: what is queued, what was picked up and by which system — joining PM and queue records without hand reconstruction.
- Usage/quota/job trend data reachable from the same view (linking the existing aggregator/projector stores is enough; new collectors are out of scope).
- Design/spec recorded on this issue before implementation, per the tracker's design-first shape (the treatment slices 1 and 2 received from their triage tasks).

## Out of scope

- Attribution rollups per job/model/session (slice 4), session-ID assignment + OpenClaw/Codex mapping (slice 5), quality linkage (slice 6), projections + accuracy tracking (slice 7) — later slices of #2072, filed in turn.
- New ingestion (slice 2, landed) or new quota collectors (existing gatherers stand).
