body:
# pm-stack(aggregator): an unparseable coverage-snapshot anchorAt silently disables weekly rotation forever — the bad anchor is re-persisted verbatim on every panel read

## Evidence

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/coverage.ts` at origin/main `a90fb771b`:

- `CoverageSnapshotStore.read()` (lines 224–232) validates only that the parsed file is an object with a `current` whose `repos` is an array. `anchorAt` is never checked — any string is accepted.
- `nextCoverageSnapshot` (lines 199–211) measures the rotation age from that anchor:

```ts
const anchor = stored.anchorAt ?? stored.current.generatedAt;
const age = now.getTime() - new Date(anchor).getTime();
if (Number.isFinite(age) && age >= COVERAGE_WEEK_MS) {
  return { baseline: stored.weekly ?? stored.current, current, weekly: current, anchorAt: now.toISOString() };
}
return { baseline: stored.baseline, current, weekly: stored.weekly ?? stored.current, anchorAt: anchor };
```

  For an unparseable anchor, `new Date(anchor).getTime()` is `NaN`, so `age` is `NaN`, the `Number.isFinite` guard (correctly) refuses to rotate — and the fallthrough return hands the **same bad anchor back**, so the next call fails the same way, forever.
- `coverageSnapshot()` in `server.ts` (lines 131–147) runs this on every /projects panel read and persists the result when it changes; `current` refreshes on changed reads, so the poisoned snapshot — bad anchor included — is written back to disk repeatedly. Nothing logs, quarantines, or heals it.

## Verified (laptop probe, this run)

Probe script in a throwaway worktree at origin/main `a90fb771b` (`pm-stack/aggregator/probe-covanchor.ts`, importing the real `src/coverage.ts`; worktree removed after the run). Stored snapshot: baseline generated 2026-10-01, weekly/current generated 2026-10-20; `now` = 2030-01-01, then a second pass at 2031-01-01:

```
control valid old anchor: rotated=true  baseline.generatedAt=2026-10-20 anchorAt=2030-01-01
control +1y:              baseline.generatedAt=2030-01-01 anchorAt=2031-01-01
garbage anchor "not-a-date": rotated=false baseline.generatedAt=2026-10-01 anchorAt=not-a-date
garbage anchor +1y:          baseline.generatedAt=2026-10-01 anchorAt=not-a-date   (never rotates)
store.read() with garbage anchorAt: NON-NULL anchorAt=not-a-date                     (accepted as a good snapshot)
```

Secondary observation: an impossible ISO anchor (`2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z`) is rolled by the JS Date parser to 2026-03-01/02, so rotation is measured from a day that never existed — the same class of stamp the aggregator's `isIsoDate` gates reject elsewhere.

## Why it matters

The coverage panel's week-over-week delta is only meaningful if the weekly rotation actually fires: rotation promotes the frozen `weekly` report to `baseline`. With an unparseable anchor the baseline freezes at whatever it was when the anchor went bad, while `current` keeps refreshing — so the panel silently presents a delta against a baseline that is weeks, months, or years old as if it were last week's. There is no crash and no log line; the only recovery is deleting the snapshot file by hand. The store's own contract is "corrupt reads as absent" (class comment, coverage.ts), and the file format already anticipates drift (optional `weekly`/`anchorAt` fields with documented fallbacks for older files) — this is exactly the drift case that contract exists for.

## Distinct from #4140

#4140 (open) covers `read()` accepting malformed `baseline`/`weekly` **report shapes**, which then crash `diffCoverage` on /projects; its acceptance criteria validate the three report objects and their rows. `anchorAt` is not a report, appears nowhere in #4140's criteria or test list, and its failure mode is the opposite shape: no crash, no NaN — a silent, permanent stall of the rotation clock. A fix for #4140 as specified would not catch a string `anchorAt` that simply isn't a date.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A stored snapshot whose `anchorAt` is present but not a parseable, real calendar date no longer stalls rotation: either `CoverageSnapshotStore.read()` treats such a file as absent (per its "corrupt reads as absent" contract), or `nextCoverageSnapshot` falls back to `stored.current.generatedAt` — the same fallback already documented for files written before `anchorAt` existed — when the anchor does not parse.
- [ ] Impossible calendar anchors (e.g. `2026-02-30`) are treated the same as unparseable ones, not rolled to a neighbouring real day.
- [ ] Well-formed files, including pre-`anchorAt` files relying on the `current.generatedAt` fallback, behave exactly as today (the control case above still rotates on schedule).
- [ ] Tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/coverage.test.ts`: a snapshot with `anchorAt: "not-a-date"` rotates (or reads as absent) at a `now` more than a week past the current report; the impossible-date anchor case is covered; the existing rotation and concurrent-write tests still pass.
- [ ] Existing aggregator tests still pass.

body:
## Finding

`ServerConfig` is fully built and parsed — and nothing in production ever loads it. The config half of #798 landed in PR #1801 (merged 39e8410b, 2026-10-29): a `[policy]` table with `freshness_window_seconds` + `pull_policy`, `[budgets]`, typed accessors, and startup-failing parse errors. Since then the remainder of #798 (consumption by `id serve` / sync sessions) has stayed blocked, and a fresh check at main `3b8d3215d808` (2026-11-03T20:15Z, task 2657 resume) shows why: there is still no production consumption point to wire the config *into*. This issue is that missing integration work, split out of #798 so the block has a name.

## Evidence (fresh, main `3b8d3215d808`)

- `ServerConfig::load` (`pkgs/id/src/server_config/mod.rs:178`) has **no caller** outside `server_config`'s own tests (`parse.rs`). Code search for `server_config::` hits only `server_config/{mod,parse,provision}.rs` and a doc mention in `pull_policy.rs`.
- `id serve` (`pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs`, 3038 lines) has **no server-config flag and never references `server_config`**; its `resolve_config` is the unrelated CLI bootstrap/topic defaults.
- The only production `PullGate` construction is `event_sync::open_gate()` — hard-coded `PullPolicy::Open` over a `NoWorlds` membership stub — called at `serve.rs:1256` for the node's own event-store sync. `event_sync.rs` documents why: "there is no world whose membership this store belongs to." Every `PullPolicy::Members` gate in the tree is in tests (`log_sync.rs`, `event_store/sync.rs`, `pull_policy.rs`). `pull_policy.rs:22-23` still states it plainly: "`id serve` does not read it yet, and no session builds a gate from config."
- The freshness consumer does not exist in production either: `seitan::admit` (the only caller of the `Freshness` window) is referenced only by `seitan`'s own tests and a design spike under `doc/`. `Freshness` is constructed in production nowhere outside `server_config::freshness()` itself, which nothing calls.
- `Provisioned::apply` (startup provisioning from the same config) likewise has no production caller — the whole file is dead at runtime, not just the `[policy]` table.

## Scope

- `id serve` learns to load a server config (path flag in the existing CLI style; absent = today's behaviour, code defaults everywhere) and fails startup on a parse error, matching `ServerConfig::parse`'s contract.
- Serve builds its sync pull gate(s) from `config.pull_policy()`; where a gate's store has no world membership (the `event_sync` own-store case), the design must say what `members` means there — refuse-all, refuse-startup-with-a-clear-error, or a membership source — and not silently serve open.
- The invite-admission path that consumes `config.freshness()` is wired where seitan admission is actually served, or that consumer is built as part of this work.
- Startup provisioning (`Provisioned::apply`) runs from the loaded config.
- Once landed, #798's remainder closes: pull policy + freshness consumed from config, and `doc/2026-10-14T_platform_completion/acceptance-brief.md` line 76 checked off.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `id serve` with a config file naming `pull_policy = "members"` demonstrably refuses a non-member pull in a test, and with no config file behaves exactly as today
- [ ] A malformed config file fails `id serve` startup with the parse error named
- [ ] The configured freshness window reaches the seitan admission check that serve runs (test at the configured value, not the 5-minute default)
- [ ] #798's remaining acceptance items are verified against this change and #798 is closed or its remainder re-scoped

## Out of scope

- Changes to the `[policy]`/`[budgets]` parse surface itself (landed, PR #1801)
- Blob gating (`blob_gate` already requires membership independently)

body:
Follow-up from the design note in [#4962](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4962) (`doc/2026-11-03T14-55-00Z_design_id4630_oversized_replication_entries.md`), covering the one residual case the checkpoint-splitting fix ([#4966](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/4966)) does not reach for [#4630](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/4630).

## Problem

#4966 stops the writer from ever *producing* a `Checkpoint` entry over 192 KiB. But a journal compacted by an older binary can already hold one oversized `Checkpoint` on disk, and re-compaction is not automatic at open: `WorldCore::checkpoint_due` (`pkgs/id/src/world/core.rs`) requires `since_checkpoint >= checkpoint_every`, which is 0 after restore. So a restored legacy world with an oversized checkpoint keeps failing `split_entry_payload` forever — `send_snapshot` (`pkgs/id/src/world_replication_net.rs:206-243`) returns `PayloadTooLarge` before the first frame, with no indication of which entry or which bound was violated, and no path to recovery other than writing `checkpoint_every` new events.

## Required change

At feed-build time (before `split_entry_payload`), detect an entry exceeding `MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES`:

1. If the world has an active program and compaction is legal, re-compact immediately (a one-shot forced checkpoint), so the legacy oversized entry is replaced by bounded parts from #4966. Reuse the existing compaction path; do not invent a second writer.
2. Otherwise (no active program, or compaction refused by the open-presence limit), return an actionable error naming the offending entry's ordinal, its encoded size, and the bound — instead of the bare `PayloadTooLarge` from the split step. The message must say that the journal needs compaction once the world can be checkpointed.

Do not raise `MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES` and do not add continuation frames: both were rejected/deferred in the design note.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A synthetic legacy journal image containing one `Checkpoint` entry > 256 KiB, opened with an active program, is force-compacted at feed build and then replicates end-to-end (`split_entry_payload` → `send_snapshot` frames → `ReplicationTracker::accept`) with a matching cursor.
- [ ] The same journal with no active program (compaction illegal) returns an error that names the entry ordinal, its size, and `MAX_REPLICATION_PAYLOAD_BYTES`, and is distinguishable from a malformed payload.
- [ ] A journal with no oversized entry takes the unchanged fast path (no forced compaction, no extra serialization pass) — asserted by behavior, not timing.
- [ ] `cargo test -p id --lib world::replication` and the `world_store` replication feed tests pass.
- [ ] Module doc in `pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs` states the legacy-journal path next to the per-entry guarantee.

## Out of scope

- Splitting checkpoints at write time (#4966).
- Re-compacting journals that merely *want* it by policy — this is only the oversized-entry escape hatch.

body:
Design (fleet design architect, pass 44): **the claimant judges and drives sessions per-id under the v2 contract, and every bound state has a named next step.** Full design doc: `files/designs/code-claimant-session-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

## Problem

The opencode-claimant (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` — `poll.py` + `prompt.md`, #3026 slice 1) talks to the OpenCode v2 server through three seams whose contract was never stated, and each has now filed:

1. **Judging from a list page** — #4757: `poll.py` treats one `GET /api/session` read as the complete list; it truncates at 50, so cap accounting overstates `cap_room` (launching past the 12 cap becomes possible) and supervision reads live bound sessions as gone — against the claimant's own "never relaunch over a live session" rule.
2. **Creating under the wrong contract** — #4870: `prompt.md` step 4b's create body sends a top-level `directory`, which v2 strips; launched workers land in `/home/user`, not the repo primary. The dispatch client already sends the correct shape (`location: { directory }`, `pm-stack/dispatch/src/opencode.ts:52-58`).
3. **A bound state with no next step** — #4758: a bound session that is alive with zero messages (task 6722, resend already spent, lease expired) is reachable by no rule: not a candidate (bound), not gone (answers per-id), resend exhausted. Claimed forever.

## Recorded decisions

1. **Per-id judging.** Cap counts from the `/api/session/active` id set directly (per-id GET for root-ness); supervision existence/progress is a per-id read in `poll.py` and in `prompt.md` steps 1 + 5. Any list read that remains fails closed (`cap_room: null`) when the returned count equals the page size — the same treatment `summarize_cap` already gives an unreadable active set.
2. **Verify before bind.** Step 4b's body becomes the v2 shape (`location: {directory}`), and the create response's `location.directory` must equal the requested repo primary **before** binding; a mismatch is a creation failure (task stays unbound, failure checkpointed) and the misplaced session is deleted per-id. Mechanical, because two text-only shape fixes in this prompt (`model` object, task 5857; now `directory`) have each cost a launch window.
3. **Every bound state has one disposition** (table in the design doc). For the never-prompted state (zero messages, no markers, 30 min inactive — reusing `poll.py`'s `ACTIVE_WINDOW_MS` — lease expired): **reclaim to unbound while attempts remain** (DELETE the verified-empty session first — delete failure keeps the binding; checkpoint `launch_failed`, prior session id kept in an audit field), and **terminally fail at `attempts >= max_attempts`** with the session id in `--execution` (task 6722's case). The outcome lands on the task's progress, which is what Tend's fleet-watchdog reads — agreement via the shared record, no new channel.

Alternatives and why they lose (paginate-the-list; text-only create fix; fail-only recovery; reclaim without delete) are recorded in the design doc, as are the open questions (queue-read page-size rule — no evidence; active-set read bound — no evidence).

## Phases (adopted origins — do not re-file or split)

- **Phase 1 = #4757** — per-id judging: cap + supervision.
- **Phase 2 = #4870** — v2 create shape + verify-before-bind (independent).
- **Phase 3 = #4758** — never-prompted recovery as decided above (independent).
- **Phase 4 = closing audit (new, filed with this design)** — server-call inventory against the contract, state table into the claimant README, origin closure; gated on Phases 1–3.

Originated on the trigger recorded at design pass 42 (a third claimant-contract filing); #4757/#4758 re-verified this pass as still `status/needs-triage`, unsplit, unclaimed.

title: queue: Supabase PostgREST hangs on authenticated requests — repo-health queues unreadable from ~11:25Z 2026-11-03

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: kind/infrastructure
labels.description: Infrastructure / host-portability work

body:
## What

From ~11:25Z on 2026-11-03 the repo-health queue database (Supabase project backing the four `repo-health-*-pilot` queues) has stopped answering authenticated PostgREST requests. The helper and `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` both fail closed, so the opencode execution lane cannot claim, bind, launch or checkpoint.

## Characterisation (read-only probes, 11:30–11:42Z)

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `GET /rest/v1/` with no key | 401 in 0.2s |
| `GET /rest/v1/` with a **bogus** apikey | 401 "Invalid API key" in 0.1s |
| `GET /rest/v1/` with the **real** service-role apikey | accepted, then **hangs, 0 bytes** (12/20/30/45/60s attempts) |
| `GET /rest/v1/repo_queue_health` with the real key | same hang |
| `GET /rest/v1/tasks?queue=eq.…` with the real key | same hang |
| `GET /storage/v1/status` | 200 in 0.15s |
| `bws` credential fetch | ok, ~3s |

So credentials, egress, DNS and the Supabase gateway are healthy; the request hangs after the key check, i.e. PostgREST/Postgres behind it, not a claimant or helper defect. The queue was fully readable at the 11:14:37Z claimant fire (79 candidates), so onset is 11:14–11:25Z.

Corroboration: `pm-aggregator` logged HTTP 544 for the same backing project (tick failures 05:25–05:36 local = 11:25–11:36Z).

## Impact

- Two claimant fires (11:37:15Z and 11:41:38Z) both launched nothing. `cap_room` was **not** the constraint (8 room); the unreadable queue was.
- Supervision (read-only, via `GET /api/session/<id>`) still ran on both fires: all 15 bound sessions verified present — 14 `outcome=succeeded` + idle, 1 dormant-but-bound (task 6722, see #4758).
- **Unverified this outage:** whether those 14 terminal sessions' *tasks* were moved to a terminal state. Poll.py/the helper could not read task rows, so the claimant cannot distinguish "worker forgot to record" from "recorded, DB unreadable".

## Why nothing was launched anyway

Launching would require the step-4a re-verify (still claimed / lane `opencode` / unbound / stage `handed_off`) and `bind` immediately after session creation. With the DB down, a created session could not be bound — exactly the Oct 28 duplicate-PR defect — so the fire failed closed rather than create unbound sessions.

## Suggested follow-up

- Confirm whether the project paused / hit connection exhaustion, and whether the service-role path alone is affected (the gateway answers, storage answers).
- Once readable, sweep the 14 bound tasks above for terminal-state recording.
- Consider making `poll.py`'s exit-4 path emit a distinguishable "queue unreadable" marker in the fire log (today it is `candidates_seen: null` plus a free-text skip reason), so consecutive-fires-of-outage can be counted mechanically.

This is an incident record, not a work request for the claimant lane.

body:
Part of epic #1184; implementation follow-up of design issue #1259 (spend rollups). Design note: `doc/spend-rollups-design-1259.md`.

## Scope
Attach real PAYG dollar charges to pools/services in the spend rollups, extending the existing charges pipeline — `pm-stack/aggregator/src/charges-collect.ts` / `charges-match.ts` / `charges-catalog.ts` (#1057, Plaid + Gmail charge candidates matched to services) — instead of building a second money path.

## Rules (per the design note)
- Only matched, real charges enter the dollars column. Unmatched charges stay visible in the existing unmatched-charge surfacing; they are never force-attributed to a project/epic.
- A charge attributes to a project/epic only through the pool/service it matched AND attributed session activity for that pool in the charge period; otherwise it lands at stack level as "unattributed dollars" — shown, not hidden.
- Dollars are never converted to or from tokens or share-of-window, in either direction, anywhere in this slice.
- OpenCode's per-session `cost` field is a list-price estimate: it is excluded from the dollars column entirely (drill-down labelling is the rendering slice's job).

## Acceptance criteria
- Tests: matched charge with in-period attributed activity → project/epic dollars; matched charge without → stack-level unattributed dollars; unmatched charge → absent from rollups, still surfaced as unmatched.
- Reconciliation: rollup dollars for a period equal the charges pipeline's matched totals for that period.
- No code path in the PR reads a per-session `cost` value into a dollars total (guarded by a test on the rollup writer inputs).

## Checks
- `bun test` and `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `pm-stack/aggregator` pass (CI on the PR).

body:
Part of epic #1184; implementation follow-up of design issue #1259 (spend rollups). Design note: `doc/spend-rollups-design-1259.md`. Depends on the attribution projection slice of #1259.

## Scope
Persist weekly and monthly spend rollups per project and per epic from the snapshot history, in the existing append-only snapshot store pattern (`pm-stack/aggregator/src/snapshots.ts`): one rollup record per (window, scope, unit) with full unit separation.

## Rules (per the design note)
- Three unit families are stored and rendered as **distinct measures, never merged**: tokens per pool; PAYG dollars (real charges only); plan-pool share-of-window (percent of a pool window consumed).
- A week/month counts only if the source was available for the whole window; partial windows are labelled partial, never read as zero spend.
- Rollups are immutable once written for an `attributionVersion`. When attribution rules change, history is **restated** as a new version alongside the old, with the version labelled in output — raw events are never edited and old rollups are never silently overwritten.
- Backfill horizon: from the start of retained snapshot history; the rollup record names its coverage start so a short history cannot masquerade as a long one.

## Acceptance criteria
- Rollup writer + reader with tests: complete window, partial window, restatement under a new attribution version, and coverage-start labelling.
- Reconciliation test: rollup totals equal projection totals for the same window/version.
- No merged cross-unit figure exists anywhere in the stored schema (schema review + a test that rejects a synthetic merged field).

## Checks
- `bun test` and `bunx tsc --noEmit` in `pm-stack/aggregator` pass (CI on the PR).

title: id(discovery): resolve_config pairs a CLI topic/secret with the public default for the other half under --no-default-topic

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Problem

`id_core::discovery::resolve_config` resolves the gossip topic and the topic secret **independently**, so with `--no-default-topic` and exactly one of `--topic` / `--topic-secret` given, the result pairs a CLI-provided value with the public network's hardcoded default for the other half:

- `--no-default-topic --topic my-private-net` (no secret) → topic `my-private-net`, secret = `DEFAULT_TOPIC_SECRET` (the public, in-source secret `id-public-discovery-v1`).
- `--no-default-topic --topic-secret my-private-secret` (no topic) → topic = `DEFAULT_TOPIC` (`id-peer-discovery-v1`, the public topic), secret = the CLI secret.

That contradicts `resolve_config`'s own documented cascade (step 7, `crates/id-core/src/discovery.rs:231-232`): "If `no_default_topic` is `true`, drop the default topic and secret (keep only CLI-provided values; if none, fall back to hardcoded constants to avoid empty values)". The per-field fallback at `discovery.rs:275-278` (topic) and `discovery.rs:294-295` (secret) fires even when the *other* half was CLI-provided, so "skip the defaults" silently reintroduces one default.

Topic and secret are consumed as a pair at both call sites — `TopicId::new(config.topic)` together with `RecordPublisher::new(..., config.topic_secret, ...)` in `pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs` (~1239-1248) and `pkgs/id/src/commands/peers.rs` (~430-438) — and the secret is what encrypts the topic's DHT bootstrap records (`DEFAULT_TOPIC_SECRET` doc, `discovery.rs:57-65`: nodes with the same secret discover each other; the default is public knowledge). A "private" topic paired with the public secret is discoverable by anyone who knows the topic name; a private secret paired with the public topic name puts the node's records on the public topic under a secret nobody else shares.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe at origin/main f28aa79e3)

Probe test `crates/id-core/tests/probe_resolve_pair.rs` in a detached laptop worktree (`~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-laneB-scan4`), run with `cargo test -p id-core --test probe_resolve_pair`:

- `resolve_config(&[], Some("my-private-net"), None, false, false, true)` printed `topic="my-private-net"` and `secret_is_public_default=true` (secret bytes equal `DEFAULT_TOPIC_SECRET`).
- `resolve_config(&[], None, Some("my-private-secret"), false, false, true)` printed `topic="id-peer-discovery-v1"` and `secret_is_cli=true`.

Both assertions of pair-consistency failed, as expected from reading the two independent fallback chains.

## Acceptance criteria

- With `no_default_topic = true` and exactly one of `cli_topic` / `cli_topic_secret` provided, `resolve_config` never pairs it with the public hardcoded default for the other half: either the pair falls back together (both hardcoded) only when *neither* is provided, or resolution refuses/names the missing half — one behaviour, documented in the step-7 cascade text and matched by the code.
- New unit tests cover both single-sided cases under `no_default_topic`, plus the existing both-provided and neither-provided cases (`test_resolve_config_no_default_topic*` keep passing or are updated to the documented behaviour).
- The non-`no_default_topic` cascade (conf pair, per-field CLI override) is unchanged.

Found by new-issue-creator lane B (code) while scanning id-core modules not covered by lane A's recent passes (discovery.rs was not in its scan lists).

title: Phase 4 (audit) of #4706 — closing state-and-route inventory + contract statement for the OpenClaw ACP adapter

body:
Phase 4 (closing audit) of design #4706 — *a prompt's state dies with the prompt: one server contract and one lifecycle for the OpenClaw ACP adapter* (`bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs`). Design doc: `files/designs/code-acp-adapter-prompt-lifecycle.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace.

**Gated on Phases 1–3 of #4706 landing** (Phase 1 = #4614, the v2 server contract; Phase 2 = #4616 + #4618, scoped prompt state and the one terminal cleanup; Phase 3 = #4617, reconnect reconciliation). Do not start the audit before they land.

## Scope

Produce the closing inventory for the adapter: every module-level state container and every serve route in `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs`, dispositioned against the design contract — *conforms* / *named exception, with the reason* / *gap, filed as a named follow-up issue*. Rewrite the file's header mapping comment so it states the v2 contract and the prompt-lifecycle rules (scoped state, cancellation only for in-flight prompts, one terminal cleanup, lost continuity is terminal) instead of the v1 mapping it states today. The inventory is the deliverable; fixing a confirmed gap inside this issue is out of scope beyond a single-site slip (file it instead).

## Required dispositions

- **(a) `sessions` map lifetime** — entries are added at `session/new` and never removed; there is no session-close path. Disposition: is process-lifetime acceptable (the adapter exits with its ACP client), or does the shared standing server accumulate sessions it should be told to delete (the v2 `DELETE /api/session/:id` exists — see design Phase 1)? Answer from the acpx launch model, with evidence.
- **(b) `pendingClientRequests` cleanup** — a permission request the ACP client never answers stays in the map forever and the permission reply is never posted. Disposition: bounded by what, and does the serve side's own permission expiry make that safe?
- **(c) Permission flow's v2 shape** — if Phase 1 (#4614) did not land the permission-reply route's v2 form, disposition it here with evidence from the pinned server.
- **(d) `partTextSent` keying after Phase 2** — confirm the landed scoping matches design decision 2 ((session, part), removed only for the finishing session), and disposition any part-id collision risk across sessions that remains.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The header comment in `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs` states the v2 contract and the four lifecycle rules from #4706, and no v1 route shape is documented as current.
- [ ] The inventory is posted on this issue: one row per module-level state container (`sessions`, `pendingPrompts`, `cancelledSessions`, `partTextSent`, `pendingClientRequests`, plus any found) and per serve route the adapter calls, each with its disposition and evidence (file:line).
- [ ] Required dispositions (a)–(d) are each answered on this issue with evidence.
- [ ] Any confirmed gap is filed as a named follow-up issue and linked here — not fixed inside the audit beyond a single-site slip.
- [ ] Evidence is posted on #4706 summarising the inventory outcome.
- [ ] The adapter's existing tests pass (CI or laptop per repo rules — no builds on the sandbox).

## Related

Design #4706; phases #4614 (Phase 1), #4616 + #4618 (Phase 2), #4617 (Phase 3); feature origin #1243.

title: openclaw ACP adapter: pending prompts are never reconciled when the SSE event stream reconnects (#3997)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: source/design-architect
labels.description: Filed by the repo design architect job

labels.name: source/pr-comment-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-comment-review job

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

If the SSE event stream drops during an active prompt and the server completes that prompt before reconnection, the prompt's final `session.idle` event is lost and the ACP request hangs forever. Codex (P2, PR #3997):

> This reconnect path neither resolves or rejects pending prompts nor queries their current status, and `session/prompt` has no other completion mechanism. The ACP request therefore remains pending indefinitely, with subsequent prompts rejected as already in flight even after the stream reconnects. Reconcile pending sessions after reconnecting, or explicitly fail their outstanding requests when event continuity is lost.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #3997 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3997 (merged 2026-11-02 as-is)
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/3997#discussion_r4437436115 — chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-01T21:31:18Z, `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs:189`
- No-response evidence: the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads`, checked 2026-11-02), the comment has no replies, and PR #3997 contains a single commit (8e67215808, 2026-11-01T21:26:51Z) that predates the comment — no fix followed it before merge.
- Still live on current main (verified by raw read 2026-11-02): `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs:185-190` — the event-stream loop logs "reconnecting" and retries after 1s; nothing reconciles, resolves, or rejects entries in `pendingPrompts` on reconnect.

## Acceptance criteria

- After an event-stream reconnect, pending prompts are reconciled against the server's current session state (resolved/rejected accordingly) or explicitly failed when event continuity was lost.
- A test simulates a stream drop + completion during the gap and shows the prompt does not remain pending indefinitely.
- Or the finding is resolved by a documented decision on this issue.

body:
Design doc: `files/designs/code-id-replication-admission.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audit at origin/main `73c0ec7466291b164b00f2fb3c911c2769997de2` — every defect below re-verified present at the cited sites this pass (2026-11-02).

## Summary

`ReplicationTracker::accept` (`pkgs/id/src/world/replication.rs`) is the receiver-side trust boundary for world-journal replication (F12.13, #806, PR #4447): whatever it accepts, the durable receiver and spectator phases treat as a verified, restorable journal. The module's own rule, recorded when the PR #4447 follow-up closed the undecodable-entry hole, is that *a verified cursor never covers data the restore path cannot read*. That rule has been enforced leg by leg for the payload — entries must decode (`chain_payload`), and the payload's own journal header must be exactly one `Created` header for this world at the envelope's version (`validate_payload_journal_header`, #4486, landed today). The envelope's own `header_version` field is still held to neither of the two contracts `WorldCore::restore` and the journal writer jointly state:

- **Range** (#4471) — restore accepts a header version only in `JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION` (1..=3, `world/core.rs:217`). `accept` checks only the upper bound (`replication.rs:712`), so a signed snapshot with `header_version = 0` rebases the tracker onto a chain no binary can restore, and `ReplicationTracker::new` performs no range check either (a v0 tracker accepts v0 tails). The origin's laptop probe: v0 snapshot accepted, `header_version()` becomes 0; MAX+1 refused as control.
- **Monotonicity** (#4487) — journal header versions only ever move forward (the writer bumps the header *before* appending an entry kind an older binary cannot read, `world/mod.rs:915-946`; there is no downgrade path). Tail and Terminal frames enforce this (`HeaderVersionChanged` on any change); the Snapshot arm does not — it checks only that `cursor_before` is the chain base *for the snapshot's own version* and assigns `self.header_version = envelope.header_version` unconditionally (`replication.rs:739-752`). The origin's probe: v1 tail → v2 bump snapshot → v1 tail refused → v1 snapshot accepted → v1 tail accepted. The guard is defeated by inserting one snapshot frame.

Both are one unstated contract with two clauses: **the envelope's header version is admitted only if the chain it names could exist** — in the restore range, and never behind the chain the tracker already holds.

## The contract

> **A frame is admitted only if its header version names a chain that could exist: inside the restore range `JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION`, and — for a snapshot, the one frame kind allowed to change the chain's version — never lower than the version of the chain the tracker already holds.**

Recorded decisions (full reasoning, alternatives and risks in the design doc):

1. **The range check lives in `accept`, for every kind, before any state changes** — `header_version` outside `JOURNAL_VERSION..=MAX_JOURNAL_VERSION` is refused with the existing `UnsupportedJournalVersion` variant, now applied to both ends. Snapshot, Tail and Terminal alike: a v0 Terminal against a v0 tracker is the same hole as a v0 Snapshot.
2. **Construction is made inert, not redesigned** — #4471 offers two endings for `ReplicationTracker::new`; this design records the second. With decision 1 in `accept`, an out-of-range session version makes the tracker inert: every frame kind carries its own `header_version` and is range-checked on the envelope, and tails/terminals must additionally equal the tracker's version, which no in-range frame can do against an out-of-range tracker. `new`'s doc states this explicitly. A fallible constructor would ripple to every session bootstrap for a state that cannot arise from a real journal header — the session version comes from the local journal, whose header restore already range-checks.
3. **Snapshot monotonicity gets its own error** — a snapshot whose `header_version` is lower than the tracker's current `header_version` is refused with a dedicated variant (`HeaderVersionRegressed`), leaving cursor and header version untouched. Reusing `HeaderVersionChanged` loses: that variant's doc names the tail/terminal fact (any change on a frame kind that may not change version), while a snapshot regression is a different diagnosis — the one frame kind that *may* move the version moved it the one way journals never move — and the durable receiver's logging will want to tell a downgrading writer bug from a merely desynchronised peer.
4. **Equal and higher stay accepted** — same-version snapshots remain the compaction rebase; higher in-range snapshots remain the header-bump rebase (both covered by existing tests). Only the lower direction is refused; no legitimate writer state is excluded, because no code path in the repo ever lowers a journal's header version.

## Phased breakdown

Phases adopt the two open origins as sub-issues (no parallels); #4486 is the landed third leg, cited as the embodiment, not a phase. Phase 3 is a new closing-audit issue, gated on Phases 1–2.

- **Phase 1 — the restore range at the envelope** (adopted: #4471). Decisions 1–2: range-check every kind in `accept`; `new`'s inert-tracker doc. (#4471 is currently `status/parked` with a holder — its agent note under this design records the phase structure; the design does not reassign it.)
- **Phase 2 — snapshot monotonicity** (adopted: #4487). Decisions 3–4: refuse a lower-version snapshot with `HeaderVersionRegressed`, state untouched. Independent of Phase 1 in logic; textually adjacent in `accept` (whichever lands second rebases a small diff — noted, not gated).
- **Phase 3 — closing admission inventory + contract statement** (new issue, gated on Phases 1–2): the contract statement lands in the `replication.rs` module doc, and every precondition `WorldCore::restore` demands of a journal is dispositioned against a check in `accept` (holds at accept / holds at restore only, with the reason that is safe / gap filed as a named follow-up). Required dispositions: (a) entry-kind version gating — whether a signed in-range snapshot may carry an entry kind that requires a higher header version (`header_version_for_entry`) on a lower header, and what restore makes of it; (b) the session-bootstrap version source — where `ReplicationTracker::new`'s `header_version` argument comes from in the serve wiring, and whether decision 2's inert-tracker reasoning holds at that call site, including whether a new session may legitimately start below a previous session's version; (c) Terminal frames carrying an out-of-range version against a tracker set by a pre-fix snapshot (expected covered by Phase 1 — confirm, don't assume); (d) any `accept` caller that pre-validates versions itself — disposition each as removed, delegated to `accept`, or named exception.

## Open questions (in the design doc, not filed)

Whether the durable receiver (#806 phase 3) should persist a regression refusal as writer-misconduct evidence or merely log it; whether a future protocol revision wants an explicit reset/rebase frame kind for disaster recovery (snapshot regression is recorded as *not* that mechanism); the session-restart version question, assigned to Phase 3's disposition (b) to answer from the actual bootstrap code.

## Related

- Origins adopted as phases: #4471 (Phase 1), #4487 (Phase 2).
- Landed sibling leg, cited not adopted: #4486 (payload's own journal header, closed 2026-11-02) and the PR #4447 decode leg in `chain_payload`.
- Sibling designs in the same crate: #2898 / #4000 (journal reconstruction is admission — the restore side of this same rule), #3231 (signed-artifact receipt), #4502 (gossip admission). This design is the replication-receipt gate; it does not re-audit the journal seams #2898/#4000 own.
- Feature epic: #806 (F12.13 replication; phases 2–5 build on this contract).

## Acceptance criteria

- Every acceptance leg named in the design audit is either implemented with tests or explicitly dispositioned on this issue: a verified cursor never covers journal data the restore path cannot read (headers, chain payload, and each leg the audit enumerates).
- Regression tests reproduce each audited defect against the pre-fix code and pass after the fix.
- The design doc (`files/designs/code-id-replication-admission.md` in the goal workspace) and this issue agree at landing; any leg deferred is filed as a linked follow-up issue, not dropped.

body:
## Problem

PR #4449's sibling PR #4432 (issue #3187, Phase 2 of design #3231) bounds `home_declared` `world_id` in `SignedArtifact::parsed()` (max 64 bytes, no whitespace-only, no control/format characters) and refuses duplicate endpoints. Local history is covered: replay of an existing log uses a lenient path (`parsed_for_replay`), so a world whose log already holds an over-bound declaration still reopens (pinned by the PR's `a_legacy_home_declaration_still_replays` test).

The **peer-pull path is not covered** (CodeRabbit Major on PR #4432, verified 2026-11-02): `Directory::receive_artifact` (`pkgs/id/src/directory.rs:1380`) calls the strict `artifact.parsed()?`, and the refusal ends the page in `apply_page` / the pull in `pull_within`. A peer whose signed chain contains a pre-upgrade declaration with an over-bound `world_id` therefore cannot be pulled past that entry — later artifacts from that account never apply. The declaration is signed and cannot be rewritten.

## What is needed

A design decision, under design #3231's one-receipt-contract (the #3232 Phase 3 audit may be the right venue):

- Choose a **trusted cutoff** that marks pre-upgrade chain state for the receive path (candidates: per-account chain position/seq at upgrade time, a protocol/version marker, an explicit allowlist of known legacy artifact hashes) and name its authoritative source.
- Peer provenance alone is not a validation boundary, and the local replay path (`parsed_for_replay`) must not simply be reused for pulled artifacts.
- The strict bound keeps applying to genuinely new receipts either way.

Until that cutoff exists, PR #4432's strict-receipt behavior is the conservative default and its merge is held on this question (queue task 5758 parked with this issue as the resume condition).

## Links
- PR #4432 (held) · issue #3187 · design issue #3231 · audit issue #3232 · queue task 5758

## Acceptance criteria

- A peer pull over a journal containing pre-upgrade home_declared entries completes (entries are migrated, skipped with a recorded reason, or surfaced as a typed error — not a halt of the whole pull).
- Regression coverage exercises a pre-upgrade home_declared entry through the pull path.
- Behavior for genuinely corrupt entries remains a hard error (the #3187 strictness is not silently dropped).

title: Consolidate muse-dev2 Supabase tables: merge workbook-era duplicates, retire deprecated views

body:
## Why

On 2026-11-02 Drew ordered Supabase-only for the model/plan data: every Drive workbook was audited, the one gap was ingested, and the Drive files were renamed DEPRECATED (see the ainventory Maintenance_Log entry "Supabase-only consolidation", 2026-11-02). What remains is the table sprawl the workbook era left inside muse-dev2 itself: several overlapping stores hold the same facts, and reads keep landing in the wrong one. Concrete proof, same day: the AA Intelligence Index v5 load (2026-10-31) lives ONLY in `ainventory.sheet_rows` Rankings rows, while `measurement_events` and `benchmark_results` hold no v5 at all — a direct question about v5 data was first answered "we don't have it" because the event log was checked instead of the sheet mirror.

## Scope

**ainventory (first):**
- [ ] Decide the canonical store for benchmark facts. Three layers overlap today: `sheet_rows` (JSON-cell workbook mirror), `benchmark_results` (typed, workbook-era, frozen at the 2026-10-26 import), `measurement_events` (append-only event log, holds II v4.3.2 + CAI only). The 2026-10-26 design (#1248) names the event log as the target shape.
- [ ] Backfill the canonical store from Rankings AA|v5 + AA|v4.3.2 rows (incl. the 2026-11-02 source-44 rows: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 keying, cost/time fills) so no dataset exists only as sheet cells.
- [ ] Retire `benchmark_results` as a table — drop it or rebuild it as a view over the canonical store.
- [ ] Retire the deprecated alias view `v_latest_workbook_batch` (marked DEPRECATED 2026-11-02; use `v_latest_import_batch`). Consumers to migrate/audit first: the coding-plan-watch job (switched 2026-11-02), `ainventory_append.py`, the pm-aggregator AA collector/explorer (#3294, #3302 touch this surface).
- [ ] Data hygiene inside the sheet mirror: duplicate variant keys for the same model+effort (Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol each appear twice per effort — `|reasoning|` and `|yes|` key forms); the two `model_value_data` sources (ids 42 + 43) — keep both for provenance, dedupe at read time or via the canonical store.

**Other schemas:**
- [ ] automation / engineering / finance / home / research all carry the same workbook-era `sheet_rows` + `ingest_batches` + `sources` clone shape. Decide per domain: converge on the typed `events` shape their append helpers already write, or formally keep the mirror — no silent third state.
- [ ] `agent.mirror_*` tables: verify each mirror still has a live consumer; drop or document the ones nothing reads.

## Constraints

- No history loss: merges preserve provenance (source ids, import batches, snapshot dates, estimated-vs-measured flags such as the Rankings `|estimated` rows).
- No DROP before a consumer audit + readback verification of the replacement path (pm-aggregator collector, quota gatherer, coding-plan-watch, pool-intelligence all read this data).
- One schema/domain at a time, each step verified by readback before the next.
- Finish by updating `~/hatch-personal/workspace/supabase/ARCHITECTURE.md` so the documented shape matches reality.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Exactly one canonical read path per dataset, named in ARCHITECTURE.md.
- [ ] No live job, view, or doc references `v_latest_workbook_batch` or describes Drive workbooks as a data source.
- [ ] v5 benchmark data is queryable from the canonical store (not only from sheet cells).

Related: #1248 (the event-log design this executes), #3142 (pm stack into Supabase — adjacent, not this), #3294 / #3302 (AA explorer consumers).

1. **Contract statement landed**: the contract from #4375 (error bodies are excerpts at `defaults.HTTPErrorBodyLimit`; a buffered success body is refused past its named cap, never silently truncated; a retained copy is truncated while the delivered stream is not; every outbound call carries a deadline as well as a byte bound) is written into `internal/defaults/defaults.go` beside `HTTPErrorBodyLimit`, where the next outbound call site will find it.
2. **Read inventory**: every `resp.Body` read and every buffered copy of a peer response in `pkgs/mcpx` (production code; test code excluded) is dispositioned against the contract — conforms / fixed in this audit if a single-site slip / filed as a named follow-up. The inventory is recorded on #4375 or in the defaults doc comment beside the contract statement.
3. **Required dispositions** (each recorded on #4375 with its reason):
   - **Remote embeddings error read** (`internal/catalog/embeddings.go:101`, unfiled at design time): decision 1 of #4375 applies (excerpt at `HTTPErrorBodyLimit`). Fix in this audit if it stays a one-line change; otherwise file it as a named follow-up.
   - **`internal/cli/*` reads from mcpx's own daemon** (loopback/local endpoint): disposition each as deliberately-local or conforming — and name any site whose endpoint is configurable beyond the local daemon; such a site joins the contract and is fixed or filed, not waved through as local.
   - **Decoder-streamed success paths** (embeddings `Decode`, cli `Decode`, the mcpclient JSON decoder path): streaming, but the decoded value itself is unbounded — record the disposition per path (the per-message / decoded-value bound questions are open questions on #4375; this audit records, it does not silently expand the contract).
   - **Stdin / file `io.ReadAll` sites**: out of scope — they are not peer bytes. Record that ruling so they are not re-audited as contract violations.
4. **Closing evidence on #4375**: all three origins (#4354, #4282, #2114) closed or verified already-fixed, the contract statement landed, and the inventory complete.

## Acceptance criteria

- The contract statement is present in `internal/defaults/defaults.go` beside `HTTPErrorBodyLimit` and matches #4375's four decisions.
- The read inventory covers every production `resp.Body` read / buffered peer-response copy in `pkgs/mcpx`, each with a disposition and a reason or a follow-up link.
- All four required dispositions are recorded on #4375.
- No behaviour change beyond a single-site slip fix (the embeddings excerpt, if it qualifies); anything larger is filed as a named follow-up, not fixed inside the audit.

body:
Follow-up to #1833 / PR #4052 (Codex P2 thread 4437715494).

## Context
PR #4052 caps server WebSocket messages at MAX_FRAME_BYTES (1 MiB). The client-side guard added in that PR (pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts `send()`) never sends an over-cap message: the socket survives and local edits are preserved, but an edit whose packed STEPS message exceeds 1 MiB (e.g. a single paste over 1 MiB) cannot sync — the connection reports the error status and the unconfirmed steps stay local until the user shrinks them (e.g. undo).

## Ask
Split oversized sendable step batches in `handleEditorChange` / the send path so large pastes sync in multiple in-cap messages:
- Chunk by packed size (measure with msgpackr as `send()` does today), each chunk within MAX_FRAME_BYTES with margin.
- Preserve the prosemirror-collab authority protocol: chunk N+1 must be based on the version advanced by chunk N (use the ACK [3, version] / UPDATE flow — do not fire chunks concurrently against the same base version, and do not resend steps already in flight on a later editor:change).
- A single step that alone exceeds the cap needs an explicit outcome (visible rejection that preserves local state is acceptable there).

## Acceptance
- A paste over 1 MiB syncs to a second client intact, in order, with no disconnect.
- No message the client sends ever exceeds MAX_FRAME_BYTES.
- Existing collab tests pass; new tests cover multi-chunk ordering and the single-oversized-step outcome.

## Acceptance criteria
- A paste over 1 MiB syncs to a second client intact, in order, with no disconnect.
- No message the client sends ever exceeds MAX_FRAME_BYTES (1 MiB).
- Chunking preserves the prosemirror-collab authority protocol: chunk N+1 is based on the version advanced by chunk N (ACK/UPDATE flow), chunks are not fired concurrently against the same base version, and steps already in flight are not resent on a later editor:change.
- A single step that alone exceeds the cap gets an explicit, visible outcome that preserves local state.
- Existing collab tests pass; new tests cover multi-chunk ordering and the single-oversized-step outcome.

body:
## Problem

`routeForTool` in `bin/codedb-bridge.mjs` rejects only a hand-named set of arguments (`project` on every tool; `regex`/`scope`/`compact` on search/outline). **Any other argument key — including a typo of a supported one — is silently dropped on every tool**, which breaks the module's own stated contract (header comment, citing #3352): "arguments the daemon cannot honour are rejected by name, never silently ignored."

The advertised `inputSchema` for each tool lists an exact property set, but nothing enforces it: a caller that sends `max_result` (typo), `case_sensitive: true`, a `path` filter on search, `depth` on tree/deps, or `since` on hot gets a successful result computed **without** that argument — the worst silent-third-path shape, because the caller believes the argument took effect.

## Evidence (main `a0e6d1d3`, file md5 `df5e54371d04828465c680e9e96727d3`, identical on sandbox clone and laptop clone)

- `routeForTool` (codedb-bridge.mjs:155-194): the only rejection helpers are `rejectProject` and `rejectTrue(key)` for named keys; there is no allowlist check against the tool's schema properties. Unknown keys are never inspected.
- `sliceData` (codedb-bridge.mjs:196-203) only ever reads `max_results`/`limit` from the mapped slice — a typo'd key never reaches it, so no error is possible downstream.

Verified this run on the laptop (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-bridgeargs/`, verbatim bridge module @a0e6d1d3) — every one of these was **ACCEPTED with the extra argument silently dropped**:

- `codedb_search {query, max_result: 5}` (typo) → route `/explore/search?q=x`, no slice
- `codedb_search {query, case_sensitive: true}` → accepted, plain substring route
- `codedb_search {query, path: "src/"}` → accepted, no path filter applied
- `codedb_tree {depth: 2}` and `codedb_tree {max_results: 3}` → accepted (tree's schema has **no** properties)
- `codedb_hot {since: "2026-01-01"}` → accepted
- `codedb_outline {path, max_results: 2}`, `codedb_deps {path, depth: 1}`, `codedb_symbol {name, limit: 5}` → accepted

End-to-end through `createHandler` with a stub daemon returning 5 results: `codedb_search {query: "x", max_result: 2}` returned **all 5 results, `isError` unset** — the caller's limit silently never happened.

Controls: the named rejections do fire — `codedb_search {regex: true}` and `codedb_tree {project}` both throw by name, confirming the gap is specifically the never-named keys.

## Distinct from

- Issue #4197: the *named* codedb options (`regex`/`scope`/`compact`, `limit`/`max_results`) being silently ignored on the *wrong* tools. This issue is the remaining general case: keys that are in **no** tool's schema (typos and invented options) are silently dropped on **every** tool, including codedb_search and codedb_tree, the tools #4197 treats as reference-correct for their named arguments. A per-tool key allowlist closes both, but #4197's fix as scoped (extend the named rejections per tool) does not.
- Issue #4191 (no daemon fetch timeout) and issue #4198 (daemon URL validation, fixed) — unrelated seams of the same file.

## Why it matters

The bridge is the shared per-session front door to codedb for every MCP client in the fleet (#4120). MCP clients — including LLM callers — routinely invent or mistype arguments; today each such call silently returns an unfiltered/unlimited result set instead of an error naming the argument, so the caller reasons from data it believes was filtered or bounded. That is exactly the failure the bridge's #3352 contract was written to prevent, and the named-argument rejections already in the file show the intended behaviour — the allowlist is simply missing.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `routeForTool` rejects, by name, any argument key outside the called tool's accepted set (its advertised `inputSchema` properties plus the explicitly handled rejection keys `project`/`regex`/`scope`/`compact` where they apply, and `body` on codedb_symbol), with an error in the existing style naming the argument and the tool.
- [ ] A typo'd argument (`max_result` on codedb_search, `limit` on codedb_symbol, any key on codedb_tree) produces an `isError` tool result naming the key — verified end-to-end through `createHandler`, not only at `routeForTool`.
- [ ] All currently accepted valid calls behave identically: the existing `bin/codedb-bridge.test.mjs` cases pass unchanged, and the named #3352 rejections keep their current messages.
- [ ] New tests in `bin/codedb-bridge.test.mjs` pin the allowlist for every advertised tool (at least one never-named key per tool, plus the search typo case end-to-end).

body:
## Summary

`isAaSection` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts:1092) — the structural gate the live source applies to the feed's AA section before `/aa` renders it (src/sources/live.ts:1110) — still checks several fields shallower than their consumers dereference them. #2415 deepened the gate for `thresholds`, `sources`, and `testRuns[].snapshotDate`; the same class remains for:

- `configs` — checked only as `Array.isArray(s.configs)` (aa.ts:1109). `renderAa` passes it to `aaConfigsTable` (render.ts:5513), which dereferences `c.modelName` on every entry (render.ts:5340): a `[null]` entry throws.
- `testRuns[].modelVariantKey` — entries are checked only for `snapshotDate` (aa.ts:1113-1120). `aaTimingsTable` calls `variantLabel(r.modelVariantKey)`, which does `modelVariantKey.split("|")` (render.ts:5321-5330): an entry without it throws. (The #2415 test's own "complete section" fixture — `testRuns: [{ testRunKey, snapshotDate }]` — crashes `renderAa` for exactly this reason.)
- `coverage` (optional) — never checked. `renderAa` reads `cov.catalogNotPooledMeasured.length` and passes the four arrays to `aaNameList` (render.ts:5396-5402): `coverage: {}` or a non-array field throws.
- `catalog` (optional) — never checked. `renderAa` calls `catalog.map((e) => e.provider)`, `catalog.filter(...)` (render.ts:5406-5410): `catalog: {}` or a `[null]` entry throws.
- `cai` (optional) — never checked. `renderAa` calls `aaCaiPoints(s.cai)` (render.ts:5415) and `aaCaiTable(s.cai)` (render.ts:5514), both of which `.map` over rows and dereference row fields: a non-array `cai` or a `[null]` row throws.

## Verified this run

Laptop probe (verbatim aggregator `src/` from f2006aaa, md5-matched aa.ts 826aad6c / render.ts 2d99393c; probe dir `probe-2026-11-01-laneB-aagate/` on the laptop) — a complete minimal section renders fine (control), and every variant below passes `isAaSection` (`gate=true`) while `renderAa` throws `TypeError`:

- `configs=[null]` → `c.modelName` on null
- `testRuns=[{testRunKey, snapshotDate}]` (no `modelVariantKey`) → `modelVariantKey.split` on undefined
- `coverage={}` → `cov.catalogNotPooledMeasured.length` on undefined
- `coverage.catalogNotPooledMeasured="x"` → `names.map is not a function` in aaNameList
- `cai="x"` → `rows.map is not a function` in aaCaiPoints
- `cai=[null]` → `r.version` on null
- `catalog=[null]` → `e.provider` on null
- `catalog={}` → `catalog.map is not a function`

## Why it matters

The gate's contract (per #2415) is that a section it accepts renders, and a malformed section degrades to the not-collected banner instead of throwing in the request path. The feed is a shared document with more than one producer (#3852), so a drifted optional field currently turns `/aa` into a 500 rather than a degraded page — the exact failure #2415 fixed for the fields it covered.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isAaSection` checks `configs` entries (object with string `modelName`), `testRuns[].modelVariantKey` (string), and — when present — `coverage` (object whose four name lists are string arrays), `catalog` (array of objects with a string `provider` — gate at the depth renderAa dereferences: `provider`, `disabled`, `routes`, `aaScore`), and `cai` (array of row objects) at the depth their consumers dereference them.
- A section failing any of these reads as absent/degraded, never throws in `renderAa`.
- New gate tests in the style of test/aa-gate-2415.test.ts covering each variant above, plus a render-fine control with all optional fields present and well-formed.
- Collector-built sections (aaSectionFromRaw output) still pass the gate unchanged.

Related: #2415 (same gate, thresholds/sources), #3441 (generatedAt depth), #2576 (umbrella validation contract — this is a concrete instance).

## Finding

`pkgs/mcpx/package.nix` still excludes the `examples` package from the nix build's `checkPhase`, even though the failure that justified the exclusion has been fixed and the condition the exclusion itself names has been met.

## Evidence

- PR #3088 (merged 2026-10-31) commit `52e23167d` added `"examples"` to `checkExclude` as an interim measure, and its body states: "That failure is tracked as #2896; this exclusion should be removed when it lands."
- The in-place comment on current main (`pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:158-164`, verified on main `d9636237`) says the same: "Interim exclusion so the package builds again; remove it when the #2896 fix lands."
- The #2896 fix has landed: PR #2943 ("fix(mcpx): run e2e/examples harnesses with policy.write=allow (#2896)") merged 2026-11-01T16:49:31Z and closed #2896 as COMPLETED. On current main, `pkgs/mcpx/examples/examples_test.go:167` sets `MCPX_POLICY_WRITE=allow`.
- The exclusion is still present on current main: `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:164` — `"examples"`.
- Dedupe: #2686 tracks the `checkPhase` exclusions for `internal/e2e` and `internal/settings` only — its body and comments never mention `examples`, and its acceptance criteria do not cover removing this exclusion. No other open or closed issue found tracking it (searched "TestExamples nix", "examples checkExclude", "2896").

## Why it matters

`TestExamples` is the only coverage proving the shipped examples actually run against the daemon. With the package excluded, the nix build — the artifact that ships in the home-manager generation — silently skips that coverage, and the interim exclusion has outlived the condition its own comment set for removal.

## Acceptance criteria

- `"examples"` is removed from `checkExclude` in `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix` (the other exclusions are untouched — they are #2686's scope).
- `nix build .#mcpx` passes with `TestExamples` actually running in the checkPhase (build log shows the examples package in the tested list).
- If a sandbox-specific failure appears that is distinct from the fixed #2896 confirmation failure, record the evidence on this issue and re-justify any remaining exclusion in place instead of silently keeping it.

body:
## Phase 4 (audit) of design #4113 — closing kind-by-gate inventory for pkgs/id boards

Parent design: #4113 ("one signed set, one meaning — BoardGraph's gates hold at insert, projection and replication"). Design doc: `files/designs/code-id-boardgraph-one-signed-set.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audit baseline: origin/main `d9636237`.

**Gated on Phases 1–3 of the design**: Phase 1 = #3963 + #4109 (insert gates: `embed_ref` validation; second-first `BoardListing` refused), Phase 2 = #4003 + #3964 (projection determinism: active-only attestation edges; deterministic Rules resolution), Phase 3 = #4081 (fork record in the fork board's replication set + closure). Do not start the inventory before all three land.

## Scope

A kind-by-gate inventory for `pkgs/id/src/boards.rs`: for **every** `BoardObject` variant (Board, Rules, Forum, Thread, Post, Attachment, Membership, RoleAttestation, ModerationAction, BoardFork, Supersede, Theme, BoardListing, Tombstone), disposition each of the design's five gates, with the code site or test that proves it:

1. **Shape** — `validate_shape` constrains every field that carries a rule (bounds, uniqueness inside the object, text rules).
2. **References at insert** — every reference field the object carries is validated by `validate_links` (existence + board scope via `require_scoped` / `require_board`, kind checked where a kind rule exists). List each variant's reference fields explicitly; a field with no validation is a finding, not an oversight to leave silent.
3. **Chain / resolution posture** — one of: chain head unique at insert (listings) / competing versions resolved by a stated deterministic rule (rules) / not versioned, with the reason.
4. **Projection effect** — the variant's effect in `compose_view` (and `latest_listings` where relevant) under the active-records rule: a record contributes edges/effects only while itself active, or the deliberate exception with its reason (cf. the `has_role` existence-based acceptance note — deliberate, documented divergences are dispositions, not findings).
5. **Replication membership + closure** — the variant's `board_ref()` posture and whether `board_object_set`'s closure pulls in everything `validate_links` needs for a fresh graph to accept it (the Board/Theme/BoardFork dependency pattern).

Record the inventory as a table in the `boards.rs` module header doc (the checklist the next object kind is reviewed against), and post a summary on design #4113.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The inventory table is in the `boards.rs` module header doc, covering every variant × the five gates above, each cell dispositioned (holds / fixed here / filed follow-up / deliberately different with reason).
- [ ] A summary with any findings is posted on design #4113.
- [ ] Any confirmed same-shape gap (an unvalidated reference field, an undispositioned versioned kind, a variant missing from its board's replication set) is either fixed under this issue — only if small and within one variant — or filed as a named follow-up issue linked from #4113. Never left as a comment-only finding.
- [ ] No behaviour changes beyond the dispositions taken; existing boards tests still pass (CI).

🤖 Filed by the design architect (pass 35, 2026-11-01) as Phase 4 (audit) of design #4113.

body:
## Summary

`BoardGraph::insert` accepts a **second "first" listing** for the same
(board, host): a `BoardListing` with `version == 1` and
`supersedes == None` is admitted even when a listing for that host already
exists. The documented listing contract (`pkgs/id/src/boards.rs`, the
`BoardListing` doc comment) is: "the first listing is version 1, and every
later listing supersedes the previous one and advances the version by
exactly one." A later listing that supersedes nothing breaks that chain:
two competing version-1 listings for one host then coexist, and
`latest_listings` resolves the tie by **greater content hash** — so whether
the host counts as listed or withdrawn depends on hash luck, not on the
signed version sequence.

## Evidence (verified this run, current main `d9636237`)

`BoardListing` link validation, `pkgs/id/src/boards.rs:763-790`
(`BoardGraph::validate_links`): when `supersedes` is `Some`, the arm checks
same board scope, same host, same author, and
`version == previous.version + 1`. When `supersedes` is `None`, the whole
check is only:

```rust
} else {
    ensure!(
        value.version == 1,
        "the first listing for a host starts at version 1"
    );
}
```

It never checks whether a listing for this (board, host) already exists.

Laptop probe (verbatim `boards.rs` from main, md5
`e142727a25d638136a27ac9ecfb7c3f9`, harness reused from the lane-B boards
probes; probe dir `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-listingfirst/` on the
laptop):

```
v1 publish (supersedes=None): OK; active=true
second v1 (supersedes=None, listed=false): ACCEPTED hash=04beb284fb508a6a39cd522ac9178a95d878638ee294a084b6a849d131699959
latest_listings now: version=1 listed=true (tie at v1 broken by content hash)
active_listings contains host: true
control v2 supersedes v1: OK; active=false
control first listing for host2: OK; active2=true
```

So the board creator can sign a withdrawal-shaped v1 that supersedes
nothing; in this run it lost the hash tie-break and the publish stayed
active, but with different body bytes the same construction wins the tie
and the host reads as withdrawn — with no v2 anywhere. Publication state
for a (board, host) pair must be a function of the signed version chain
only.

The existing test `listing_publish_and_withdraw_follow_signed_versions`
(boards.rs:2491) covers foreign signer, first-version-must-be-1, version
skips, and the proper v2 withdrawal — but never a second `supersedes: None`
listing for an already-listed host.

## Why it matters

Listings are the federation discovery mechanism from #3806: hosts decide
what to replicate and serve from `active_listings`. A duplicate "first"
listing makes that decision hash-dependent and identical graphs can be
built where the same signed set yields listed/unlisted by content-hash
ordering rather than by the version rules the module documents and
enforces everywhere else (same-host, +1 version, supersedes required).
It also gives a confused or malicious board creator a way to mint an
untethered withdrawal that no chain audit can order against the publish.

## Acceptance criteria

- Inserting a `BoardListing` with `supersedes == None` for a (board, host)
  that already has any listing in the graph is rejected, with an error
  naming the rule (e.g. "the first listing for a host starts at version 1"
  is no longer sufficient — the rejection must be because one exists).
- The legitimate first listing for a host (any host, supersedes None,
  version 1) is still accepted; the proper supersede chain (v2 over v1,
  same host/author, +1) is unchanged.
- Replication convergence is preserved: in `replicate_board_from`, a
  listing set exported from a valid source graph still converges
  (listings whose supersedes target is present insert in dependency
  order; a first listing never becomes un-insertable because a later
  version arrived first — later versions cannot insert before their
  supersedes target exists, so this ordering already holds).
- New test coverage in the boards test module: second-first listing
  rejected for both `listed: true` and `listed: false` second copies;
  first listings for two different hosts on one board both accepted.
- Existing boards tests pass (`listing_publish_and_withdraw_follow_signed_versions`,
  `two_hosts_converge_via_replication`, and the rest of the module).

## Distinct from

- #3964 (Rules revision numbers not unique per board — same shape, different
  object kind; Rules carry no supersedes chain, listings do).
- #3963 (Post `embed_ref` never validated), #4081 (BoardFork absent from
  replication sets), #4003 (compose_view superseded-attestation edges).
- The same-version signed *fork* that `latest_listings` documents
  (two listings at one version) arises through the supersedes chain;
  this issue is only about the untethered `supersedes: None` case.

body:
## Summary
`RateAuthorisation::validate` in the new `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` (PR #3888, main `c3fda1c4`) checks exactly two things — issuer == event author and `rate_den != 0` (currency.rs:170-180). Every other internally inconsistent body folds as `Live`: the fold's only validity gate is this function (currency.rs:313-320), so a signed authorisation that can never legitimately convert — or that misprices every conversion — is indistinguishable from a good one for every consumer of the fold.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop probe)
Probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneB-currency/` on the laptop — verbatim `validate` from currency.rs (reference copy sha256 `8f68982526219dff920586495a076d2c1a33f87fe3b6716a74e561ea821b9493` @ `c3fda1c4`). All of these return `Ok(())`:

```
validate(min>max) -> Ok(())                                   min_amount 10000, max_amount 1
validate(expires_at==not_before (empty window)) -> Ok(())     2000 / 2000
validate(expires_at<not_before) -> Ok(())                     2000 / 3000
validate(fee_bps 99999 (>100%)) -> Ok(())                     fee is 999.99%
validate(empty ledgers) -> Ok(())                             source_ledger "" and dest_ledger ""
validate(source==dest ledger) -> Ok(())                       ABC -> ABC
validate(rate_num 0 (zero rate)) -> Ok(())                    every conversion yields 0
validate(total_cap 0) -> Ok(())                               cap permits nothing
validate(empty allowlist (allows nobody)) -> Ok(())           AuthorisedCallers::Allowlist([])
test validate_accepts_internally_inconsistent_bodies ... ok
```

(Sanity: the two documented checks do fire — `rate_den = 0` returns `ZeroRateDenominator`.)

## Why it matters
`validate` is the library-level contract the fold, and later the Phase 2 gateway checks (#3801: window, min/max, remaining volume at submission), rely on. A body with `min_amount > max_amount`, an empty/inverted validity window, or `fee_bps > 10000` can never be caught downstream as "invalid" — the gateway's live-state checks would evaluate a nonsense window and nonsense bounds as if they were policy, and different consumers can disagree about shapes like a zero rate or a same-ledger "conversion". The field docs in this same file state the invariants in prose ("Rate denominator; non-zero in a valid authorisation", "Mandatory expiry", "Optional fee in basis points") — `rate_den` is the only one enforced.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `validate` rejects, with named `ValidateError` variants: `min_amount > max_amount`; `expires_at <= not_before`; `fee_bps > Some(10000)`; empty `source_ledger` or `dest_ledger`; `source_ledger == dest_ledger`.
- [ ] Shapes that are arguably legitimate-but-dead (zero `rate_num`, zero `total_cap`, empty allowlist) are either rejected with named variants or explicitly documented as valid in the field docs — one stated rule, tested either way.
- [ ] Tests cover each rejected shape; existing currency tests still pass; the fold ignores the newly invalid bodies (covered by the existing fold-filter test pattern).

Distinct from: #3801 (gateway submission-time checks against accounts/tiers — it assumes a valid folded object), #4069 (duplicate-version fold tie-break, same file, different defect), #4063 (app_manifest parser validation, different module).

## Phase 3 (audit) of design #4000 — closing reconstruction-admission inventory (pkgs/id)

Parent design: #4000 ("reconstruction is admission, continued — carried state, checked succession, and every restore's guards"), the follow-on to #2898. Design doc: `files/designs/code-id-restore-admission-followon.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audit baseline: origin/main `83709fac`.

**Gated on Phases 1, 2 and 3a of the design**: Phase 1 = #3942 (checkpoint-carried handoff validation), Phase 2 = #3736 + #3961 (checked succession in restore), Phase 3a = #3911 (WaitingPool restore guards + explicit proof-park route). Do not start the inventory before all three land.

## Scope

(a) **Reconstruction-entry-point inventory for `pkgs/id`**: enumerate every entry point that rebuilds state from durable or carried input — at minimum `WorldCore::restore` (every journal arm, and every field a `Checkpoint` carries: events, schedules, execution profile, caps ceiling, transfers, snapshot), `WaitingPool::restore` (id-core), the sandbox snapshot restore (`sandbox.rs`), `world_store::restore_program`, and the directory/petname persistence restores — and disposition each on the design issue as: validates with the live rules / fixed under this issue (only if a same-shape gap is confirmed *and* small) / filed as a named follow-up / deliberately different with the reason recorded. Where a surface is also in #2898 Phase 3's named scope (sandbox snapshot, `restore_program`, petname/directory), cite that phase's outcome rather than re-auditing it.

(b) **Plain-arithmetic grep disposition**: grep `pkgs/id/src` and `pkgs/id/crates` for plain arithmetic (`+ 1`, `- 1` and compound forms) inside predicates that decide admission (restore, receipt, and live guards alike), record the pattern and site list on the design issue, and disposition each site with design #4000's decision 2 applied: succession predicates must be `checked_add` (saturation loses — `MAX → MAX` would pass an advance check); counters that may legitimately sit at a cap may stay saturating, with the reason recorded per site. At audit baseline the `core.rs` inventory is exactly two sites (`core.rs:368`, `core.rs:476`), both covered by Phase 2 — this audit is the crate-wide proof, not a re-fix of those two.

(c) **Transfers-bound disposition**: #3942 notes a checkpoint's `transfers` list is installed with no bound, and design #4000 deliberately records no cap value. Record on the design issue whether an existing journal limit (retained events, entry/size limits, the standalone path's practical bounds) already bounds the list in practice, or file a named follow-up proposing the bound — do not invent a cap inside this audit.

(d) **Cross-note on #2898**: post the note recording that #4000's follow-on phases have landed and that the two designs cite one rule, citing the landed phase PRs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The inventory in (a) is posted on design #4000 with a disposition and reason per entry point; any confirmed same-shape gap is either fixed here (small) or filed as a named follow-up issue — never left as a comment-only finding.
- [ ] The grep disposition in (b) is posted on #4000 with its pattern and site list; no plain-arithmetic succession predicate in an admission path remains undispositioned.
- [ ] The disposition in (c) is recorded on #4000.
- [ ] The cross-note in (d) is posted on #2898.
- [ ] No behaviour changes beyond the dispositions taken in (a)/(b); existing tests still pass (CI).

🤖 Filed by the design architect (pass 34, 2026-11-01) as Phase 3 (audit) of design #4000.
