body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#132 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #97

## Summary

Map every mcpx feature to the integration tests that exercise it, list the features with none, and then make the map enforce itself: a guard, in the style of `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket`, that fails CI when a new op, command or setting ships without an integration test. The opencode plugin is part of the inventory. It was item 6 in the brief and is folded in here because its first step is small: run the test file that already exists.

This is a **review** (audit what exists) followed by a **design** (the guard). Closing the gaps it finds is follow-up implement work. File that work as one issue per feature group, not per op.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - a general goal is to ensure all features have one or more integration tests
>     - the mcp servers can be specialized mocks but the app entrypoint or binary is used and config is passed in or config path set to appropriate test
>     - for both binary && app entrypoint (consider binary a superset)

For this issue, "integration test" means what the two child bullets say: the real binary or an app entrypoint (#133) drives mcpx, mock MCP servers are allowed, and config is passed in. A unit test of `internal/<pkg>` does not count, however thorough it is.

## Current state (written on d0b7e01; counts re-checked at 05c78b2)

### Surfaces, and whether a guard can enumerate them

| Surface | Declared in | Enumerable by a test today? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CLI commands | `handlers` map literal inside `main()`, `cmd/mcpx/main.go:119-162`: 42 names including the aliases `list`/`namespaces` and `logs` | **No.** It is a local variable in `main`. A guard needs it exported, which the `cli.Run` refactor in #133 does as a side effect |
| `/v1` ops | `api.Ops()`, `internal/api/ops*.go`: 53 distinct paths | Yes |
| MCP tools at `/mcp` | the same ops table. `internal/api/parity_test.go:87` `TestEveryNonStreamingOpIsReachableAsAnMCPTool` | Yes |
| `mcpx serve --transport stdio` | `app.CmdServe` | One e2e test: `internal/e2e/proto_test.go:289` `TestAStdioClientIsAskedOnTheWire` |
| Settings | `internal/settings` registry, about 149 `Path:` entries at d0b7e01; 152 at 05c78b2 after #171 (`registry.go` 57, `wire.go` 45, `consumer.go` 15, `exec.go` 13, `plugin.go` 10, `proto.go` 9) | Yes |
| Plugin | `plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts`, `mcpx-tui.tsx`, `mcpx/daemon.ts` | No registry. The surface is the opencode hooks (`shell.env`, tools, and so on) |

### Gaps found by a cheap grep

Method: search `internal/e2e/*.go` for the literal command name as the first argument of `e.run`/`e.try`/`e.runStdin`, and for the literal `/v1` path prefix. The grep can mislead in both directions. A mention does not prove a test, and a missing literal does not prove missing coverage, because the CLI reaches `/v1` routes indirectly. The inventory has to go feature by feature. This list only says where to look first.

- **CLI commands never invoked by e2e:** `adapter`, `api`, `completion`, `daemon`, `help`, `init`, `man`, `openapi`, `registry`, `scripts`, plus the aliases `namespaces` and `logs`. Some are partly covered elsewhere. `internal/adapter`, `internal/openapi` and `internal/registry` have unit tests. `package.nix` `postInstall` runs `man` and `completion`, but nothing checks their output.
- **`/v1` paths with no literal in e2e (26 of 53):** `/v1/ask`, `/v1/ask/{id}`, `/v1/ask/{id}/abandon`, `/v1/ask/{id}/answers`, `/v1/client.ts`, `/v1/elicit`, `/v1/elicit/{id}`, `/v1/elicit/{id}/{action}`, `/v1/globals.d.ts`, `/v1/intent`, `/v1/namespaces`, `/v1/prompt`, `/v1/prompts`, `/v1/recipes`, `/v1/recipes/{name}`, `/v1/recipes/{name}/run`, `/v1/refresh`, `/v1/resource`, `/v1/resource-templates`, `/v1/resources`, `/v1/restart`, `/v1/search`, `/v1/session/release`, `/v1/shutdown`, `/v1/status`, `/v1/types`. Several of these are reached through the CLI (`mcpx elicit`, `mcpx status`, `mcpx prompt`). All non-streaming ones are hit by the route guard, but that guard only asserts "not 404 and not 5xx" (`internal/e2e/v1ops_test.go:350-357`). It proves the route is **served**, not that it is **correct**.

### Feature by feature (starter table; the review completes it)

| Feature | e2e evidence today | Gap to audit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Launchers with `@placeholders` (#7) | `e2e_test.go` (19 mentions of `launcher`) | depth |
| Recipes, `mcpx prompt`, `POST /v1/intent` | `consumer_test.go:92-196` through the CLI | `/v1/intent` is never called directly |
| Artifacts and ExecOptions (#40) | `exec_test.go:22-494` (11 tests) | none obvious |
| Elicitation broker | `proto_test.go`, `consumer_test.go:248-331`, `e2e_test.go` | `seedElicitation` (`e2e_test.go:2367-2381` at 05c78b2) shells out to `python3` for sqlite3. That is a hidden environment dependency (#134) |
| Sampling passthrough | `proto_test.go:287-353` (stdio client asked `sampling/createMessage`) | HTTP `/mcp` sampling path |
| Tasks | `v1ops_test.go` | cancel/result edge cases |
| `mcpx api --spec` (OpenAPI to tools) | **none** | the whole feature |
| CLI to MCP adapters (`paths.adapters`) | **none** | the whole feature |
| Registry search/add | search against the stub (#65) | the `registry` CLI; add |
| Live server add/remove | `settings_test.go:111,139` | remove |
| Content-addressed exec workdirs | no literal `workdir` in e2e | reuse, invalidation |
| Connection ladder, inline mode, named endpoint | `e2e_test.go:2383-2468` (05c78b2) | remote success path (#134) |
| Every runtime | `runtime_test.go:13,45` | these **skip** when a runtime is missing (`runtime_test.go:17-18`), so a runner without bun is silently green (#134) |
| Plugin | `plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts`: 21 `bun:test` cases at 05c78b2 of the discovery ladder against fake daemons (`Bun.serve({unix})`) | **still not run by CI** (no `bun test` step in `.github/workflows/`). `mcpx-session.ts` and `mcpx-tui.tsx` have no tests |

### The existing "every X has Y" guards (the model)

| Guard | What it enumerates | What it asserts |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` (`v1ops_test.go:287`) | `api.Ops()` | each route is served (not 404/5xx) |
| `TestEveryDaemonRouteIsDeclared`, `TestEveryDeclaredOpHasARoute`, `TestEveryNonStreamingOpIsReachableAsAnMCPTool` (`api/parity_test.go:54,73,87`) | ops and the mux | declaration and route/tool parity |
| `TestEverySettingIsReachableOverV1` (`settings_test.go:173`) | settings registry | each setting can be read over `/v1` |
| `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` (`e2e_test.go:2877` at 05c78b2, after #74/#75) | exec flags | each flag changes behaviour |
| `TestEverySettingIsReadSomewhere`, `TestNoHandRolledSettingEnv`, `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:73,145,209`, #171) | settings registry, `MCPX_*` reads, plugin reads | each setting is read by some code; no undeclared env read |
| `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault` (`defaults/guard_test.go:92`) | package sources | no duplicate defaults |

None of them asserts that a feature **has a behavioural test**. They assert reachability or parity. That is the gap this issue closes. The "declared but never read" audit and guard landed in #171 (rows above). It covers "every setting is read" and should not be duplicated here; the stronger form -- reading a setting can change an observable outcome through an ordinary caller -- is #129's (#181 collision 15).

## Approaches

### A -- a hand-maintained inventory table in docs (least recommended)
Put the table above in `docs/testing.md` and ask contributors to update it. It costs nothing and helps humans. It also starts going stale the day it is written. Nothing fails when someone adds an op and skips the table, and the history (#74: flags accepted and ignored, found by accident) shows that unenforced lists do not hold. Use it only as the output of the review, not as the mechanism.

### B -- a static name guard
A Go test enumerates `api.Ops()`, the command table and the settings registry, then greps the e2e sources for each name. Any name that never appears fails, unless it is on an exemption list with a reason. It is cheap, runs in milliseconds, needs no daemon, and can run in every shard. The weakness: a mention is not a test. A name in a comment or an unrelated string satisfies it, so it measures presence, not behaviour, and it pushes people toward adding the literal rather than the test. Aliases and paths with parameters need special-casing.

### C -- a runtime coverage ledger (recommended)
The e2e harness records what each test actually **exercised**. `e.run`/`e.try` log the resolved command (after alias and global-flag handling). The socket/TCP client logs the op. The daemon already records every request in its log store (`/v1/log`), so op coverage can also be read back from each env's state dir before cleanup. A `TestMain` in `internal/e2e` writes the ledger. A guard then compares it against the three registries and fails on any entry that was neither exercised nor exempted. The exemption list is a checked-in file with one reason per entry, like the route guard's inline skip list (`v1ops_test.go:294-298`).

Recommended because it measures what actually ran, so gaming it takes a real call. It extends naturally to "every setting was set by some test" and to the plugin's hooks. And it composes with #133: line coverage from a `-cover` binary is complementary evidence, not a replacement, because a covered line is not an asserted behaviour.

Costs:
- It needs the full e2e run. Under sharding (#95) each shard writes a partial ledger, and a final job merges them and runs the guard. The CI tree owns that job; this issue defines the ledger format (JSON lines: `{test, kind: cli|op|mcp|setting, name}`).
- The command table must be enumerable (see above).
- Tests that call `/mcp` must go through a harness helper so the ledger sees them.

Take B's static check as a cheap per-shard pre-check if the merged job comes later. Do not treat it as the end state.

### The plugin (folded item 6)
1. **Run `daemon.test.ts` in CI.** It runs as `bun test plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.test.ts` (the file's header comment). It needs only bun. The CI tree (#95) owns where the step goes; it is under a second of work.
2. **A plugin harness against the real daemon** (#47/#48 need this). Load the plugin module with a stub opencode `PluginInput`, point it at an isolated e2e-style daemon (#138), and assert on the hooks. `shell.env` should inject `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT` (`mcpx-session.ts:696`), a tool call should reach `fakemcp`, and the TUI should load. Write it against #48's harness-free core API once that exists, so the #47 v2 rewrite reuses the same harness and does not get its own. Before #48, a thin harness over the v1 plugin is acceptable, on the understanding it will be rewritten.

## Open questions

- What is a "feature" for the guard: an op, a command, a setting, or also named behaviours (the ladder rungs, inline mode, profiles, aliases)? Proposal: the three enumerable registries, plus a hand list of behaviour features in the same exemption/manifest file so they at least appear.
- Does reaching a command only through its alias count?
- Per setting: is `TestEverySettingIsReachableOverV1` enough, or must each setting have a test proving it changes behaviour, as `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` does for exec flags? The second is #129's guard (#181 collision 15, building on #171's `consumed_test.go`), so decide it there, with #99 (guard-per-bug-class policy).
- Should ops that have no CLI command (#76) be flagged by the inventory as a separate class?
- Plugin tests are bun-only (`Bun.serve`). That is fine for opencode, which runs on bun. Does #48's harness-free core need a node/deno run too?
- Should the behaviour-feature list become a real registry (a `features.json` the man page and the book also read), rather than a hand list inside the exemption file? It would pay for itself in the docs tree (#96) (from #160).
- One exemption file, or one per registry? One is easier to review; per-registry is easier to own (from #160).

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (review S; ledger and guard M; closing the gaps is separate implement work) · **Impact** high
**Depends on / related**: #133 (exported command table, harness runner), #138 (isolation, needed before the plugin harness), #95 (merged-ledger job, bun step), #99 (guard policy), #93 (tests that randomise take the run seed), #47, #48, #76, #74 (closed, fixed in #75 -- the precedent), #171 (merged: the declared-but-never-read guard), #129 (the behaviour-changing guard, #181 collision 15), #137 (whether real-software-only coverage counts).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- A feature↔integration-test inventory exists (on this issue or in the docs tree and linked here) covering CLI commands/ops, settings, and the opencode plugin, naming the features with no integration test.
- A guard in the style of `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` fails CI when a new op, command, or setting ships without an integration test, or the guard's design is pinned here with a follow-up implementation issue filed.
- Gaps the inventory finds are filed as follow-up issues, one per feature group (not per op), and linked here.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links or inventory output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#307 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Not now; recorded so it is designed once rather than patched case by case.

## The problem
mcpx serves every MCP revision at once (2024-11-05 through 2026-07-28). Most differences are resolved by the version the peer states (header, `_meta`, `initialize`). Some are not: two revisions require incompatible behaviour and nothing on the wire says which the peer expects -- `docs/spec/revision-conflicts.md` lists them (HTTP 404 meaning "session gone" vs "method not found", disconnect-as-cancel SHOULD NOT vs MUST, `-32002` vs `-32602` for a missing resource, request-ID reuse, logging without a requested level). Today each is decided ad hoc in code.

## Proposal (spitballed by the user)
- **Default: newest wins.** Unresolvable conflicts pick the later revision unless configured otherwise; each case still gets considered rather than assumed.
- **A precedence setting**: an ordered list of revision dates, e.g. `["2027-xx-xx", "2025-11-25", "2026-07-28", "2024-11-05"]` -- "I care about 27, then 25, then 26 ...". Order is the precedence; no numbers needed. Unlisted revisions fall after, newest first.
- **`--mcp-spec <date>`** (and env/config equivalent): shorthand that puts one revision at the top of that list.
- **Version predicates** called wherever behaviour depends on the revision, usable in a `switch` or an if-chain: `atOrAfter(d)`, `before(d)`, `only(d1, d2, ...)`, `between(a, b)` (order-insensitive: the set of revisions between the two dates). These replace string comparisons like `version >= "2026-07-28"` scattered through `internal/mcpserver`.
- **A conflict resolver**: where the peer's version cannot settle it, ask the precedence list which revision's rule applies -- and **implement both behaviours**, so the user's choice is real.
- The conformance runs should pass under the default; where a test needs another order, set `--mcp-spec` for that run.

Related: `docs/spec/revision-conflicts.md`, `internal/mcpserver/revisions.go` (already has a feature table keyed by revision), `docs/in-name-only.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- A precedence setting (ordered revision list) exists in config, with `--mcp-spec <date>` and env/config equivalents putting one revision on top; unlisted revisions fall after, newest first; default is newest-wins.
- Version predicates (`atOrAfter`, `before`, `only`, `between`) replace scattered string version comparisons in `internal/mcpserver`.
- Every conflict in `docs/spec/revision-conflicts.md` resolves through the precedence list with both behaviours implemented where the peer's version cannot settle it.
- Conformance runs pass under the default order, and at least one run under a non-default `--mcp-spec` order is demonstrated.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#129 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #99

## Summary

When a bug is one instance of a **class** -- a declaration and its use live apart, and the same shape has shipped before -- the fix adds a **guard test** that fails for *every* member of the class, present and future, not just the instance found. mcpx already has more of these than the strategy doc lists; this issue inventories them, finds where the existing ones leak, picks how guards are written, and lists the guards worth adding next. It also sets the rule for when a bug "is a class". It **owns #181 collision 15**: a setting must be able to *change behaviour*, not merely be read. That guard is due before or with #172.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - agents should make at least 1 simple, new test for every bug observed from any source, when cheap to do so-- aggresively test many permutations. 

(Guards are the per-class extension of "at least 1 simple, new test for every bug": the per-instance policy is #128.)

## Current state: guards that exist at 05c78b2

There are about twenty-five, not three. The ones that matter here, by mechanism:

| Guard | Class it closes | Mechanism | Tier |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:2877`, from #74/#75) | a flag accepted and ignored | **hand table** + runtime probe (with vs without) | e2e |
| `TestEveryDeclaredRouteAnswersOverTheSocket` (`internal/e2e/v1ops_test.go:287`) | a declared `/v1` op that 404s | registry enumeration (`api.Ops()`) + runtime probe | e2e |
| `TestEveryDaemonRouteIsDeclared`, `TestEveryDeclaredOpHasARoute`, `TestEveryNonStreamingOpIsReachableAsAnMCPTool` (`internal/api/parity_test.go:54,73,87`) | route/op/MCP-tool drift | source scan of `internal/daemon/*.go` + registry enumeration | unit |
| `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault` (`internal/defaults/guard_test.go:92`) | a constant outside `defaults.json` | **regex source scan** with a reasoned allowlist and an `outOfScope` list | unit |
| `TestEverySettingIsReachableFromAllThreeSurfaces`, `TestEveryDefaultSurvivesItsOwnValidator`, `TestEverySettingSaysWhoReadsIt` (`internal/settings/registry_test.go:27,41,287`) | settings registry consistency | registry enumeration | unit |
| `TestEverySettingIsReadSomewhere`, `TestNoHandRolledSettingEnv`, `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting` (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:73,145,209`, from #171) | a setting declared and never read; a registry-owned variable read by hand; the plugin honouring an undeclared variable | registry enumeration + **regex source scan** for a `Set` accessor call outside the settings package (`accessorRead`/`readViaHelper`, `:54,60`), one-entry allowlist with a reason (`paths.config`, `:66`) | unit |
| `TestTheDocumentationListsEverySetting` (`internal/settings/docs_test.go:19`) | docs drift | registry vs `docs/configuration.md` | unit |
| `TestEverySettingIsReachableOverV1` (`internal/e2e/settings_test.go:173`), `TestEverySettingTheSchemaAdvertisesActuallyWorks` (`e2e_test.go:1879`) | registry vs served surfaces | runtime probe | e2e |
| Nine effect tests in `internal/e2e/unread_test.go:48-184` (from #171), e.g. `TestPoolDefaultsAreReachableFromTheEnvironment`, `TestScriptEnvIsReachableFromTheEnvironment` | a wired setting that changes nothing | **hand-picked** runtime probes: set the value as a user would, assert an observable change | e2e |
| `TestNoOrphanProcessesAfterStop` (`e2e_test.go:534`) | MCP children surviving `stop` | runtime probe | e2e |
| `TestEnvCleanupStopsTheDaemonItStarted` (`e2e_test.go:2630`, from #182) | a test env's daemon surviving its cleanup (#52) | runtime probe; falsified by reverting the fix | e2e |
| `TestEveryTuiViewProducesRowsFromRealData`, `TestEveryConsoleMethodIsCoveredAndNameIsKept`, `TestEveryModernRequestCarriesVersionAndCapabilities`, ... | various | mixed | mixed |

The "declared but never read" audit landed as #171. Its inverse ("read but never declared", 44 `MCPX_*` variables) is #172 and is in flight. `TestEverySettingSaysWhoReadsIt` checks only that a setting *declares* a scope; `TestEverySettingIsReadSomewhere` checks that something reads it. **Nothing checks that reading it can change anything** (leak 5 below).

### Where the existing guards leak

1. **`TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` does not enumerate the flags.** It has four rows (`--export`, `--launcher`, `--prefix`, `--typecheck`) and a comment "Add a row when you add a flag". The exec/run flag set has 23 flags (`internal/cli/commands.go:435-481`), including three that #75 fixed (`--no-launcher`, `--allow-repeat`, `--no-capture-console`) with no row. A new flag with no row passes. The class is not closed; it relies on memory, the thing the guard exists to replace. Its *probe* half is the model to copy: each row asserts the outcome with the flag and its absence without, and that half caught #75's own first `--typecheck` assertion, which matched output present either way.
2. **Regex source scanning misses spellings.** PR #56: `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault` matched `"5 * time.Minute"` while gofmt writes `5*time.Minute` in call arguments, so nine live constants were invisible to it. A guard that silently passes is worse than none; it was found by accident.
3. **Allowlists are one-way doors.** `outOfScope` in `guard_test.go` still exempts seven whole packages and one file (`guard_test.go:86-90`) "owned by work happening in parallel"; nothing makes it shrink.
4. **Nothing fails when a test reaches the network** (#65 fixed the one instance via `MCPX_REGISTRY_URL`, `e2e_test.go:57`). #52 is fixed (#182): cleanup is `stop --all` with the error logged, not discarded (`e2e_test.go:71-85`), and `TestEnvCleanupStopsTheDaemonItStarted` checks one env's daemon dies. Still unguarded: a daemon started outside `newEnv`, and `testsupport`'s `mcpx-bin-*`/`mcpx-fake-*` dirs, which are never removed (`internal/testsupport/build.go:27,57`).
5. **`consumed_test.go` proves a setting is read, not that reading it matters.** `registry.pageSize` is read (`internal/cli/registry.go:265`, `internal/daemon/ops.go:285`) but consulted only inside `if limit <= 0` (`internal/registry/registry.go:154-155`). Every ordinary caller passes a positive limit: `--limit` defaults to 20 (`internal/cli/registry.go:26`), and the daemon falls back to `registry.limit` (`internal/daemon/ops.go:275-276`). So it passed #171's sweep while inert (#179). The scan sees a read; it cannot see that the read is unreachable. `unread_test.go` has the right shape, a with/without probe, but covers nine hand-picked settings out of 149. This is #181 collision 15, owned here (next section).
6. **A guard's name can overclaim.** `TestEverySettingIsReachableFromAllThreeSurfaces` (`internal/settings/registry_test.go:27-39`) checks that a flag name exists, that the variable is `MCPX_`-prefixed and that the setting is documented. That is name shape, not reachability. The e2e `TestEverySettingIsReachableOverV1` is the one that probes.
7. **An allowlist entry's reason is prose nothing checks, and one is false.** `consumed_test.go:67-70` exempts `paths.config` as "read by config.SearchPath from `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` directly" (repeated in `docs/declared-but-unread.md:93-96`). Nothing reads `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG`; the search path reads `MCPX_CONFIG` (`internal/config/config.go:549`). The exemption hid a setting that is dead on all three channels (#5). An allowlist reason that names a mechanism should be a mechanism a test can check (the variable is read somewhere, the function exists), or say "declared, not read" plainly.

## Owns #181 collision 15: a setting must be able to change behaviour

**Owns #181 collision 15:** the stronger settings guard. Every registry setting must be able to change an observable outcome through an ordinary caller, not merely be read. #179 (`registry.pageSize`) is the instance; this issue owns the class.

- **Model:** #75's exec flag table (`e2e_test.go:2877`) asserts, per row, the outcome with the flag and its absence without. #171's `unread_test.go` already does the same for nine settings by hand (set the value the way a user would, as an env var or config key and not a Go field, then assert a change).
- **Shape (Approach C below, applied to `settings.Registry()`):** a unit-speed completeness test fails when a setting has neither an effect probe nor an exemption with a reason. Exemptions ratchet down (e.g. plugin-scoped settings the Go side cannot observe, and `paths.config`, #5). The e2e probes set a non-default value through an ordinary caller and assert a with/without difference. A negative test plants an inert setting, read only behind an unreachable branch as `registry.pageSize` is, and expects the guard to fail.
- **Timing:** apply it **before or with #172** (in flight), which will move up to 44 more `MCPX_*` variables into the registry (its recommended option declares the inbound ones and allowlists the outbound). Each should arrive with a probe row or a reasoned exemption, not be audited afterwards. Of the whole tree, this is the one part of #99 that is time-sensitive.
- **Scale:** 149 settings at 05c78b2 (unique `Path:` entries in `internal/settings/*.go`), with more to come from #172. A probe per setting in e2e is too slow for every PR. Keep the completeness half at unit speed (T3 in #127). Group probes by surface, so that one daemon checks many settings. #124's `settings.precedence` generator can supply the non-default values.

## When a bug "is a class"

Add a guard (in the fix PR, or file `testing` + `implement` and link it) when any of these holds:
- the same shape has shipped before (#74 was the third "accepted and ignored");
- the bug is drift between a declaration and its use (registry vs reader, op table vs route, flag vs options struct, docs vs code);
- the fix edits a table, registry or allowlist;
- the bug depended on the environment the test ran in (network, OS, leftover processes).

## Approaches: how guards are written

### A -- source scanning with regexes (least recommended)
Walk `.go` files and match text, as `TestNoPackageRedeclaresADefault`, `daemonRoutes` and #171's `consumed_test.go` do. Quick to write and needs no registry. Risks: formatting changes the text (the gofmt miss above), comments and strings produce false hits, renames produce false passes, a match proves a call exists but not that it is reachable (leak 5), and failures read as "line 212 matched a pattern" rather than "setting X is never read". Keep only where nothing better exists, and if so parse with `go/parser`/`go/ast` (or `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages` for type info) rather than regexes.

### B -- enumerate the registry (reflection over data)
Iterate `settings.Registry()`, `api.Ops()`, `flag.FlagSet.VisitAll`, the command table, and assert properties per entry. Unit-speed, exact, cannot be fooled by spelling -- most of the table above is this. Limitation: it proves declarations are *consistent*, not that they *work*; a registry entry nothing reads passes every B guard, and so does one that is read but cannot matter (`registry.pageSize`).

### C -- enumerate, require a probe per entry, prove the guard can fail (recommended)
1. **Enumerate** the registry (B) as the source of truth.
2. **Completeness:** a unit test fails when an entry has neither a probe row nor an exemption *with a reason* (the `allowed` map style in `guard_test.go`). Fixes leak 1: a new flag without a row fails in milliseconds, locally, at T1/T3 of #127.
3. **Probe:** each row proves an observable effect in both directions (the #75 with/without pattern); probes that need the binary live in e2e and run in CI.
4. **Ratchet:** exemption lists may only shrink -- a test pins their length, or CI compares it to `main`.
5. **Negative test:** every guard's checker is a function with its own test that feeds it a planted violation and expects a failure (fixes leak 2's lesson: a guard that cannot fail is not tested).
6. Use AST scanning (not regex) only for classes with no registry. (#171's "declared but never read" guard used a regex scan, which is enough to find a read but, as leak 5 shows, not to prove it matters; step 3's probe is what closes that.)

Recommended because it closes the gap the current exec guard has (enumeration), keeps the cheap half (completeness) in unit time so agents actually run it, and makes the guards themselves falsifiable.

## Candidate new guards

| Guard | Class | Mechanism (per C) | Owner / coordination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Every setting can change an observable outcome** | read but inert (#179, `registry.pageSize`) | `settings.Registry()` vs a probe table; completeness at unit speed; with/without probes in e2e; ratcheted exemptions; planted-inert negative test | **here -- #181 collision 15; first implement task, before or with #172** |
| Every exec/run flag has a row or an exemption | accepted and ignored (#74) | `VisitAll` over the exec flag set vs the table | here |
| Every command's flags, not just exec | same, other commands | command table enumeration; rows per command | here |
| ~~Every setting in the registry is read by something~~ | declared, never read | **done in #171** (`consumed_test.go`, regex scan for a `Set` accessor read) | superseded by the row above for "read but inert" |
| No two concurrent runs share a generated path | #69, #70, #73 (three instances in three PRs) | property over the runner's naming function (a content hash of every input that changes the program), plus a concurrent e2e probe per artifact kind | here; candidate |
| Every flag mcpx passes to a runtime has the effect it is passed for | an inert subprocess flag (#108) | An acceptance check ("the runtime exits 0 with this argv") would **not** have caught #108: Node 24 accepts `--experimental-strip-types` and it is simply inert. Use a **pinned capability matrix** instead: real argv against a fixture per TypeScript construct per runtime, failing when the matrix *changes*, so an inert flag shows up as the Node column losing its `enum` rows. Keep the cheap exit-0 check as a first half, since it still catches a typo or an upgrade that drops a flag. Deno's permission flags (`--allow-*`, `--no-check`) are the same exposure: no test file mentions them | here; #108 (in flight) owns the fix, #100 the runtime matrix |
| Every documented capability exists | a documented capability that does not exist (#102, #106) | Split the ask. Mechanical where a registry is behind it: #102's tool list vs the generated client, #106's CLI vs `/v1/exec` resolution; those should not wait. Prose gets a marker table, which is probably #132's feature inventory with one more column (build it once). Prose-linting is rejected outright: there is no honest mechanism for it | here + #132 (#97) |
| Every CLI flag has non-empty usage and appears in `mcpx --help`/`mcpx man` | undocumented knob | enumerate flag sets vs generated man (`package.nix:88-89` builds it from the binary) | docs tree for the book; here for the test |
| Every `/v1` op has a CLI command, or a listed exemption | CLI parity (#76) | `api.Ops()` vs command table; exemption list starts as #76's table and ratchets down | #76 |
| Every feature has an integration test | untested feature | reads #97's inventory file, checks each named test exists (`go test -list`) | **#97 owns the inventory**; this issue owns only the rule that a guard reads it |
| No test reaches the network | #65 | see sub-choice below | here + #95 |
| No test leaves a process (or temp dir) behind | #52 (fixed in #182 per env) | `TestMain` in `internal/e2e`: after `m.Run()`, find processes whose argv contains this run's temp prefix, kill them and fail; remove `mcpx-bin-*`/`mcpx-fake-*`. #182 already stopped discarding the `stop` error and added the per-env test | here (suite-wide backstop) |
| Quarantined tests have an issue link and an unexpired date | permanent quarantine | scan for the quarantine helper | #130 |

### Sub-choice: enforcing "no network"

- **Env only (weakest):** set `HTTP_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY` to a dead port (`http://127.0.0.1:9`) in `newEnv` and a unit `TestMain`. Catches Go HTTP clients that honour proxy env (including the spawned `mcpx` binary); misses raw dials and anything in `NO_PROXY`.
- **In-process dialer guard:** replace `http.DefaultTransport`'s `DialContext` in `TestMain` to refuse non-loopback. Precise for unit tests; cannot reach the `mcpx` subprocess or the JS runtimes.
- **No network in the CI test step (recommended, plus the env layer locally):** run tests in a network namespace (`unshare -rn` / `systemd-run --property=PrivateNetwork=yes` / a container with `--network none`) after `go mod download`. Catches everything, including deno/bun/node. Linux-only, so it lives in CI (#95); macOS keeps the env layer.

## Tasks

- [ ] Implement: **settings effect guard (#181 collision 15)** -- completeness over `settings.Registry()`, probes grouped by surface, a planted-inert negative test. Before or with #172.
- [ ] Implement: enumerate the exec/run flag set in `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` (completeness + exemptions), rows for the #75 flags.
- [ ] Implement: negative tests for existing checker-style guards (`defaults`, `parity`, `consumed`).
- [ ] Implement: no-network (env layer now; namespace via #95).
- [ ] Implement: process/temp-dir sweep `TestMain` (#52 itself is fixed by #182; this is the suite-wide backstop and the temp-dir cleanup).
- [ ] Decide which other candidates become issues.

## Open questions

- Should the completeness half of an e2e guard be a separate unit test (runs at T1), or stay inside the e2e test (runs only in CI)? Proposed: separate.
- ~~Does the "declared but never read" audit produce a registry-level guard (B/C) or an AST scan (A with `go/ast`)?~~ Answered by #171: a regex scan (A's mechanism, `consumed_test.go:54,60`) over registry enumeration. The effect guard above is the C half it lacks.
- Which settings cannot be probed from Go at all (plugin-scoped ones read only by TypeScript, `paths.config`)? Do they get a TypeScript-side probe in the plugin's `bun test`, which CI does not run yet (#141)?
- Where do exemption lists live: in the test file (current style) or in a data file several guards share?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (policy S; each guard S-M) · **Impact** high
**Depends on / related**: #74, #75, #76, #65, #52 (closed, fixed in #182), #56 (the defaults-guard miss), #69/#70/#73 (the shared-path class), #97 (integration inventory), #95 (no-network CI step), #93 (generators for probe inputs); #171 (merged: the read guard), #172 (in flight: its inverse; lands with or after the effect guard), #179 (in flight: the `registry.pageSize` instance), #181 (collision 15, owned here); siblings #127 (T3 guards list), #128, #130, #131.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- The existing guard tests are inventoried on this issue, with where each leaks (class members it cannot catch) named.
- The rule for when a bug "is a class" is recorded, and the house style for writing guards is pinned.
- The #181 collision-15 guard — a setting must be able to change behaviour, not merely be read — is landed, or scheduled before/with #172 as the body requires.
- The guards worth adding next are listed, with follow-up issues filed for any not landed here.
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links or guard output as applicable) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

title: mcpx: tool views and composed tool sets — rename/pin/hide, cross-server namespaces, script-backed tools, and generators that emit declarations

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#114 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #176

## Summary

Four related asks: compose new tools out of existing ones, add tools to a server that does not have them, turn an arbitrary executable into a server by generating its spec, and make a restricted renamed view of a server. The user's framing is "generate" for all four — a model produces them.

The finding of this issue is that **three of the four are better as declared, deterministic features, with generation as an optional author-time convenience on top**, and that mcpx is roughly 70% of the way there already: `aliasOf` + tool filtering + `prelude` (aliases, `docs/story.md` §"Profiles and aliases"), `internal/adapter` (CLI programs as servers), `internal/openapi` + `mcpx api --spec` (OpenAPI documents as servers). What is missing is small and specific: pinned arguments, tool renaming, cross-server composition, and script-backed tools.

The distinction that matters: a **generated artefact is a file a human reviews and checks in**; a **runtime behaviour is a thing that must be correct every time**. Generation belongs to the first and never to the second.

## Original notes

> - mcp-owned opencode api support
>   - generate OpenAPI.fromSpec for a binary or script or any executable/whatever and add it as an mcp, save the openapi json for reuse by hash or similarity
>   - generate new mcp commands out of existing 1 or more
>   - generate new mcp commands that trigger its own prompts/scripts/binaries
>   - generate new x_commands for an mcp and add them into the given mcp
>     - doesn't have to just be merging transforming filtering limiting existing
>     - can extract the creds pull the api and add endpoints from sdk missing in mcp using the sdk descriptions 
>   - please make an alias for the tailscaleMcp except it should not require auth it should accept the creds i already used to connect to it and the only skill it should provide is listTailnet and listHostnames

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

**Aliases already do most of the tailscale request.** From `docs/story.md` §"Profiles and aliases" and `internal/config/config.go:148-152`:

```jsonc
"tailscale-peek": {
  "aliasOf": "tailscale",
  "mcpx": {
    "tools": ["list_devices", "list_tailnets"],
    "description": "read-only view of the same tailnet"
  }
}
```

An alias is "a second *view* — its own namespace, tool subset, prelude and description — over the same command". Tool filtering is **not** part of pool identity, "because filtering is presentation", so the alias shares the target's running process and therefore its already-established credentials — which is precisely the note's "it should accept the creds i already used to connect to it". Filtering is applied by `visibleTools` (`internal/daemon/registry.go:183`) against `Resolved.Tools`/`ExcludeTools`. Alias chains are rejected.

What the alias mechanism **cannot** do, and the note asks for:

| gap | detail |
| --- | --- |
| **rename a tool** | the note wants `listTailnet` and `listHostnames`; the view exposes whatever the server named them. `Tools`/`ExcludeTools` select, never rename. |
| **pin or default an argument** | no way to say "this view always passes `readonly: true`" or "drop the `tailnet` parameter from the schema and always send `-`". `docs/proposals.md` §"Per-instance argument templating" proposes templating **argv**, not tool arguments — different layer. (An *adapter* parameter already has a `Default`, `internal/adapter/adapter.go:86-87`; a view over an MCP server has nothing.) |
| **compose across servers** | a view is over exactly one target. |
| **add a tool that the server does not have** | nothing can inject a tool into a namespace. |
| **narrow a schema** | no way to remove or constrain a property in the exposed `inputSchema`. |

**Executables as servers already exists, declaratively.** `internal/adapter` turns a command-line program into a server from a JSON declaration — `paths.adapters`, `Spec{Name, Command, Args, Env, Dir, Description, Instructions, Timeout, Tools[]}`, each `ToolSpec{Name, Args, Params[], Stdin, JSON, Timeout}` with `Param{Name, Type, Required, Flag, Repeat, Default, Enum}`. Its tests encode the sharp edges: a boolean becomes the flag's presence not `--loud true`, a repeated flag is sent once per value, a missing required parameter is refused before the process starts. Its package doc states the boundary explicitly: *"This is deliberately not a general shell escape. A tool here is a named subcommand with declared parameters, so a model cannot invent a command line, and what is reachable is exactly what somebody wrote down."* Two limits at 05c78b2: adapter tools are loose MCP tools, not namespaces — absent from `mcpx ls`, the generated TypeScript and scripts (#83, #102) — and `mcpx adapter` today offers only `list`, `check` and `call` (`internal/cli/adapter.go`).

**OpenAPI documents as servers already exists.** `internal/openapi` + `APISpec{Name, Spec, BaseURL, Include, Exclude, Methods, IncludeDeprecated, Headers, Description}` + `paths.apis` + `mcpx api tools|call --spec <path-or-url>`. Headers expand `${VAR}` from the environment "so a declaration can be checked in and a token cannot" (`internal/cli/openapi_tools.go:64-68`).

**Scripts as reusable units already exist.** Recipes (#41): a script on the search path declaring `@param` holes in a header comment, matched by a deterministic scorer, runnable via `POST /v1/recipes/{name}/run`. What a recipe is *not* is a tool: it does not appear in `tools/list`, has no `inputSchema`, and is not callable as `namespace.tool`.

**MCP tools are generated from the ops table** (`internal/api/ops*.go`), and `GET /v1/openapi.json` is generated from the same declarations — the precedent that one declaration should drive every surface.

## Approaches

### Approach A — least recommended: a model generates tools at runtime

`mcpx` is asked for a tool it does not have; a model composes one on the fly from the catalogue and it becomes callable.

Why not:

- **A tool is an interface, and an interface that changes shape is not one.** MCP clients cache `tools/list`; `2026-07-28` adds `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` specifically to make that caching reliable, and asks servers to return tools in deterministic order for prompt-cache hits. A catalogue that varies run to run breaks all of it.
- **It defeats the reason mcpx exists.** The pitch is that tool schemas stay out of the model's context. Generating a tool requires sending schemas to a model — on a path that was supposed to avoid exactly that.
- **`internal/adapter`'s stated boundary is the thing being given up.** "A model cannot invent a command line" is the property that makes adapters safe. Runtime generation is that property removed, reintroduced as a feature.
- **Unreviewable and unversionable.** Nobody can diff it, check it in, or say why it changed.

### Approach B — middle: extend views to be real transforms, declared in config

Generalise `aliasOf` from "a filtered view of one server" to a declared **tool view** that can rename, pin, narrow, and compose:

```jsonc
"tailscale-peek": {
  "aliasOf": "tailscale",
  "mcpx": {
    "description": "read-only tailnet listing",
    "toolViews": {
      "listTailnet":   { "from": "list_tailnets" },
      "listHostnames": { "from": "list_devices",
                         "pin": { "fields": ["hostname"] },
                         "hide": ["tailnet"],
                         "description": "hostnames on the current tailnet" }
    }
  }
}
```

- `from` renames; `pin` supplies fixed arguments the caller cannot set; `hide` removes pinned properties from the exposed `inputSchema` so the tool looks like what it is; `description` overrides. Selection (`tools`/`excludeTools`) stays as it is and a `toolViews` map implies the allowlist.
- **Composition across servers** needs one more thing: a view whose `from` is a fully-qualified `server.tool` rather than a bare name, and a server entry with no `aliasOf` at all — a *virtual* namespace assembled from several targets. `Registry.views` is already `map[string]*config.Resolved` keyed independently of pools (`internal/daemon/registry.go:41-45`, "pools may be shared between names; views never are"), so this is a natural extension rather than a new concept. **Namespaces and collision rules are #83's (#181 collision 4).** #83's tool-source interface defines what a namespace is and what happens when two sources claim one name; virtual namespaces, views and script-backed tools here are built on those rules and do not define their own. The shapes in this section are input to #83.
- **Sequencing two tools into one** ("out of existing 1 or more" where more than one must *run*) is not a schema transform — it is a script. Which is the next item.
- **Script-backed tools** are the highest-value missing piece and the smallest: let a config declare a script as a tool.

  ```jsonc
  "ops": { "scripts": { "staleIssues": { "file": "close-stale.ts", "description": "...", "params": "auto" } } }
  ```

  The script's `@param` header already declares its holes with types — the same header recipes use — so `inputSchema` generates from it with no new authoring format. This single feature covers **"generate new mcp commands that trigger its own prompts/scripts/binaries"** entirely: a script can call several tools, shell out, run a prompt, or invoke a binary, and it appears as one ordinary tool. It also promotes recipes from a side channel to first-class, which they should be. This is the same feature as #83's first ship step ("recipes as tools, since the schemas already exist"), so it lands as a #83 tool source; the config spelling above is a proposal for that, not a second mechanism.
- **Scope and profiles apply unchanged**, so a view can be `default: false` and pulled in by `--profile`.

This is deterministic, diffable, reviewable, testable, cacheable, and it is what the runtime should be built on regardless of whether anything ever generates it. It also answers the tailscale request exactly and completely.

The cost is authoring: someone has to write the JSON, and for the SDK-mining case ("extract the creds pull the api and add endpoints from sdk missing in mcp using the sdk descriptions") that is a lot of JSON. Which is where generation earns its place — but as an author-time tool, not a runtime.

### Approach C — recommended: B as the runtime, plus generators that *emit declarations*

Build Approach B. Then add generators whose only output is a file in one of the formats mcpx already consumes — an adapter `Spec`, an `APISpec`, an OpenAPI document, or a `toolViews` block. The generator is a `mcpx` subcommand a human runs; the daemon at runtime reads only declarations, exactly as it does today.

```
mcpx adapter generate <binary>       # --help scraping + a model -> adapter Spec JSON (beside today's list/check/call)
mcpx api generate <binary|script>    # -> an OpenAPI document
mcpx view generate <server> "<ask>"  # -> a toolViews block
```

Each prints to stdout or writes to a path, is reviewed, and is checked in. The runtime is unchanged and cannot be surprised.

**`OpenAPI.fromSpec` for an arbitrary executable, concretely.** The deterministic first pass is substantial and should come first: run `--help`, `help`, `-h`, `--help=full`; parse the common conventions (a usage line, an indented flag block, subcommand tables); many modern CLIs also expose `--json`/`completion` output, and Cobra/clap/argparse produce highly regular help text. That gets a usable adapter `Spec` for a large fraction of programs with no model at all, and a model's job becomes filling in descriptions and types the help text left ambiguous — which is exactly the job a model is good at and the one where being wrong costs a bad description, not a wrong command line.

On the note's "save the openapi json for reuse by hash or similarity": **hash, yes; similarity, no.** Cache on the binary's content hash plus its `--version` output. A content hash is exact and a stale entry is impossible. Similarity matching on binaries ("this looks like a tool I have a spec for") would hand one program another program's command-line interface, which fails by constructing a plausible, wrong invocation — the worst failure mode available. If a similarity notion is wanted at all it should surface as a suggestion to a human ("this looks like `rg` 14.x, reuse that spec?"), never as an automatic resolution. Note also that the natural intermediate here is the **adapter `Spec`**, not OpenAPI: a local executable is not an HTTP service, and `internal/adapter` already models argv, flags, stdin and JSON output, which OpenAPI does not. Generate the adapter spec; generate OpenAPI only for things that really are HTTP services.

**Adding endpoints an MCP server omits, from its SDK.** This is the most ambitious item and the most valuable when it lands, because the common complaint about vendor MCP servers is that they expose a fraction of their own API. The route with the best ratio: many vendors publish an **OpenAPI document** for the service the MCP server wraps, and mcpx can already turn one of those into tools (`mcpx api --spec`). So the deterministic path is: point `APISpec` at the vendor's published document, `Include` the operations the MCP server lacks, expand the auth header from the environment — and merge that into the same namespace with a virtual view. No model, no SDK parsing, no credential extraction. Mining an SDK's source for undocumented endpoints is a much larger and much more fragile project, and should only be considered where no document exists. **"Extract the creds" is out of scope here** — reusing a credential means naming an environment variable in the declaration, which `APISpec.Headers` already supports with `${VAR}` expansion; anything that reads a credential out of a running server's process is a security design and deferred.

**On the nested "doesn't have to just be merging transforming filtering limiting existing"** — agreed, and that is what script-backed tools are for. Once a script can be a tool, "new" has no ceiling: a tool can call three servers, run a binary, transform the result and return something none of its inputs could produce. The declarative view layer handles the cheap 80% (rename, pin, hide, select, compose schemas) and scripts handle everything else, which is a cleaner split than trying to make a declarative transform language Turing-complete.

Recommended because the runtime stays declarative and reviewable, because every generated artefact lands in a format that already has a loader and a test suite, because the highest-value single feature (script-backed tools) needs no model at all, and because it answers the user's concrete request — the tailscale alias — today, in config, with one small addition to a mechanism that already exists.

### What the tailscale request needs, specifically

| requirement | status |
| --- | --- |
| a second namespace over the same server | **exists** (`aliasOf`) |
| reuse the credentials already in use | **exists** — the alias shares the pool, hence the process, hence its auth; also `Headers` `${VAR}` expansion for the HTTP case |
| expose only two skills | **exists** (`mcpx.tools` allowlist) |
| name them `listTailnet` and `listHostnames` | **missing** — needs `toolViews.from` |
| "should not require auth" | ambiguous: reusing the target's session is what the alias does; genuinely removing an auth requirement is deferred |

So this is roughly a one-field change away from working. Worth doing first, on its own, as proof the view layer is the right shape.

## Open questions

- Do renamed tools break anything that assumes a tool name is the server's name? `codegen.ToolFuncName`, `catalog-history.json` keying, diagnostics, and `internal/diagnose`'s namespace filter all key on names — the view's name must be what the caller sees and the target's name what history records, and those must not be confused.
- Should `pin` be invisible or merely defaulted? Invisible (`hide`) is what the tailscale case wants; defaulted-but-overridable is friendlier. Probably both, as separate fields.
- Virtual namespaces and profiles: does a virtual view belong to the profiles of its targets, or declare its own?
- Where do generated declarations live by default — `paths.adapters`/`paths.apis` targets, a state directory, or stdout only? Stdout only is safest; a `--write` flag is the convenience.
- Does a script-backed tool run through `POST /v1/exec` with the caller's `ExecOptions`, or with fixed options from its declaration? Fixed, probably, or a tool's behaviour depends on who called it.
- Should `tools/list` mark a view-derived tool as such in `_meta`, so a client can tell it is not the server's own?
- How does a script-backed tool declare `destructiveHint`/`readOnlyHint`? It must, or the confirmation policy has nothing to work with.
- Is there a path to contributing generated adapter specs back — a shared repository of specs by binary hash? Useful, and a distribution question rather than a code one.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** L overall; the tailscale-unblocking `toolViews.from`/`pin`/`hide` is **S–M**, script-backed tools **M**, virtual cross-server namespaces **M–L**, spec generation **L** · **Impact** high — it turns mcpx from a router into a place where a personal tool surface is *composed*, and script-backed tools alone make recipes first-class.

**Depends on / related**: #83 (owns namespaces, collision rules and the tool-source interface this builds on — #181 collision 4; its step 1 is script-backed tools and its step 5 generated declarations), #102 (an adapted binary is not script-callable — in flight), #7 (launcher placeholders — same `@` substitution family), #41 (closed, fixed in #58: recipes and their `@param` headers are the input format for script-backed tools), #40 (closed, fixed in #57: artifacts, for generator output), #5 (config chain — views must layer), #76/#77 (ops table and protocol; `_meta` marking and annotation plumbing), `docs/proposals.md` §"Protocol adapters, including OpenAPI" and §"Per-instance argument templating". Siblings: #110 (generators' model), #115 (the tailscale/Dropbox/Drive/Outlook servers this would view), #111 (shared schema-validation code).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#159 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #96

## Summary

Found while designing the generated reference (#144, #145) and the level-2 pages (#146 - #149): the sources the docs
would be generated from, and some of the hand-written docs, are incomplete or wrong. A generator will publish these
faithfully, so they must be fixed first or the generated reference is precisely wrong. Grouped here because they are
one class: "a single source that is not single, or a document that says something the code does not do". This is an
architect-added issue; none of it is in the user's notes, and each item is cheap to confirm.

## Original notes

Architect-added; it serves these lines (quoted in #144 too):

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 'ok i just installed this thing what even is it' layer
>         - a page or section in a page for
>           - env vars
>           - cli arguments
>           - cli commands
>           - /v1

## Current state (each checked on main `d0b7e01`; every item re-checked at `05c78b2` on 2026-09-30)

Status at `05c78b2`: items 1-6, 8, 10-12 and 14-17 are still true. Item 7 is partly fixed and its count is owned by
#172. Item 9 is mostly fixed by #171. Item 13 was wrong and is struck below. Items 18 and 19 are new and were found
in this pass. Line numbers are re-cited at `05c78b2`.

### Code: sources of truth that are not

1. **`Commands()` is not the one list.** The `Command` type's doc comment (`internal/cli/manual.go:12-17`) says help,
   the man page and the command table cannot disagree because they share `Commands()` (`manual.go:33`, 32 entries).
   The dispatch map in `cmd/mcpx/main.go:119-162` (42 keys: 39 commands plus the aliases `list`, `namespaces` and
   `logs`) also dispatches `serve`, `openapi`, `adapter`, `registry`, `api`, `man`, `completion` and the `logs`
   alias. None of them is in `Commands()`, so they are missing from `mcpx help <cmd>`, the man page and shell
   completion. `mcpx help` with no argument prints hand-written text (`internal/cli/root.go:549-611`), not
   `Commands()`. *Still true at `05c78b2`.*
2. **`mcpx init` writes a starter config that silently does the wrong thing.** It emits `"mode": "shared"` /
   `"mode": "session"` (`starterConfig`, `internal/cli/commands.go:1379-1407`, with `mode` at `:1390` and `:1400`).
   The server struct has `sharing` and `scope` (`internal/config/config.go:93-94`) and no `mode`, and the loader's
   `json.Unmarshal` (`config.go:695`) drops unknown fields. The chrome-devtools example
   therefore gets one shared browser, not the per-run browser its comment promises. The quick start (#157) must not
   tell anyone to run `mcpx init` until this is fixed. *Still true at `05c78b2`.* The same stale model is also taught
   by the top-level `mcpx help` text: its CONCURRENCY block (`internal/cli/root.go:597-604`) says "Each server declares
   a mode in its config" and lists `shared`/`pooled`/`session`. `pooled` is not a sharing value at all (the only
   values are `shared` and `exclusive`, `config.go:33,36`). Fix both together.
   A third place says the opposite of the code: `docs/proposals.md:45-50` claims "the retired `mode` key is now a hard
   error carrying a migration hint rather than a silent default". Nothing in `internal/config` mentions `mode`; the
   key is dropped silently. Either make the claim true (reject `mode` with the hint, which also fixes `init`'s output
   loudly) or correct the sentence.
3. **`mcpx openapi` publishes a stale document** describing the removed `serve --transport http` server (`/health`,
   `/openapi.json`, port 8787; `internal/cli/openapi.go:45,52,98`, while `internal/cli/serve.go:360-376` rejects every
   transport but stdio). There are three OpenAPI documents (`mcpx openapi`, `mcpx schema --format openapi`,
   `GET /v1/openapi.json`) and they describe different things; only the last is the daemon API. *Still true.*
4. **`GET /v1/openapi.json` includes the running daemon's configured tools** (`internal/daemon/ops.go:498-535`:
   `handleOpenAPI` merges `toolPaths()`, built from the live catalogue), so a docs build that fetches it
   publishes the builder's configuration. The docs need the static ops-table part only (see #144). *Still true.*
5. **The man page is not reproducible**: it stamps today's date (`internal/cli/manual.go:335`). Use the commit or
   release date (`SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` convention). *Still true.*
6. **Acronyms derive unreadable names**: `daemon.leaseTTL` -> `--daemon-lease-t-t-l` / `MCPX_DAEMON_LEASE_T_T_L`
   (`docs/configuration.md:216`), likewise `proto.askTTL`, `proto.stateTTL`, and the user-facing `proto.serveMCP`
   (`:403`, `:409`, `:407`; derived by `dashed`, `internal/settings/schema.go:227-243`).
   Fix the derivation (treat a run of capitals as one word) and keep the old spelling as an alias. *Still true.*
7. **Environment variables outside the registry.** *Partly fixed; the count belongs to #172.*
   - ~~about 49 `MCPX_*` names read by non-test code are not in the settings table (e.g. `MCPX_FORMAT`, read
     directly by `mcpx daemon`, `internal/cli/root.go:95-101`)~~
   - **Fixed in #171:** `mcpx daemon` no longer reads `MCPX_FORMAT` or `MCPX_LOG_LEVEL` by hand. It reads
     `logging.format` and `logging.level` from the resolved settings (`internal/cli/root.go:131-146`), and
     `MCPX_FORMAT` is now read nowhere. `TestNoHandRolledSettingEnv` (`internal/settings/consumed_test.go:145`) fails
     if a registry-owned variable is read with `os.Getenv`.
   - **Still open, owned by #172 (#181 collision 17):** variables that no setting declares. #172 counts 44 undeclared
     of 64 referenced (at `8001f23`). This issue's "about 49" used a different allowlist and is withdrawn in favour of
     #172's count. #172 defines the allowlist once.
   - A page generated from the registry alone would be incomplete. Either register them or generate a second list
     from a declared allowlist, with a test that no `os.Getenv("MCPX_...")` escapes both. That is #172's Approach C.
8. **130 per-command flags are declared by hand** and appear only in Go's `-h`, not in help, the man page or
   completion. *Still true.* Measured at `05c78b2` over non-test `internal/cli/*.go`: 118 `x := fs.String/Bool/Int/
   Duration(...)` plus 12 `fs.Var(...)` = 130 declarations. The "118" in #181 and in the integration-pass comment
   left out the 12 `fs.Var` flags (`--prefix`, `--env`, `--allow-repeat`, `--log-source`, ...).
9. **Plugin options have two sources that disagree.** *Mostly fixed in #171; one gap remains.*
   - ~~9 `plugin.*` settings in the registry, 13 options in `plugin/opencode/README.md`; six README options are not
     registered and two registered ones are not in the README.~~
   - **Fixed in #171:** `plugin.remember` and `plugin.annotate` were registered, `plugin.skills` was deleted, and
     `plugin.discoveryRetry` is now read (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:196`). The four README options that are
     not settings (`endpoint`, `socket`, `daemonTools`, `headless`) are allowlisted with a reason each
     (`pluginEnvAllowed`, `internal/settings/consumed_test.go:188-200`), and `TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting`
     (`:209`) fails on any other undeclared variable the plugin reads.
   - **Still open:** the README's options table (`plugin/opencode/README.md:79-93`) is a second, hand-written list
     that nothing reads. It already omits `discoveryRetry`. Registry: 10 `plugin.*` settings; README: 13 options.

### Documents that say something false

10. `docs/configuration.md:151-153` claims `mcpx config --schema` "prints the same thing" as its table; its output has
    no scope or hot columns (`Describe` and `JSON`, `internal/settings/file.go:175-208`, `:219-252`). The table has no
    generator in the tree (it arrived in 32f49b9 without one). *Still true.* #171 shows the cost: its two new rows,
    `plugin.remember` and `plugin.annotate`, were appended by hand after `plugin.tools` (`configuration.md:354-355`),
    out of the table's alphabetical order.
11. `docs/parity.md` is stale: **27** of the 60 ops have no row (the 33 rows in `## /v1 operations`, `:29-63`, are all
    valid; the count "26" was a miscount, see #180), and no test reads the file. The missing 27 are whole feature
    families: `artifact_delete`, `artifact_get`, `artifact_put`, `artifacts_list`, `ask_abandon`, `ask_answers`,
    `ask_begin`, `ask_poll`, `call_path`, `catalog_history`, `diagnose`, `exec`, `intent`, `protocol`, `recipe_get`,
    `recipe_run`, `recipe_save`, `recipes_list`, `resolve`, `servers_add`, `servers_list`, `servers_remove`,
    `settings_get`, `settings_list`, `settings_set`, `settings_unset`, `tool_invoke`. The parity test checks
    routes/ops/tools, not the document. Routes are registered by hand and found by regex
    (`internal/api/parity_test.go:21`) -- the ops table generates OpenAPI and MCP tools, not routes. *Still true.*
    Ownership (#181 collision 18): **#145** owns the drift check, which must fail on an absent row and not only on a
    wrong one, because today the file's `## Known gaps` cannot be told apart from rows that are simply missing. The
    page's content belongs to whoever regenerates it (#76, #144). SURFACES owns `docs/parity.md` while #76 is in
    flight, so this issue does not propose edits to it beyond this item.
12. Dependency claims: `docs/dependencies.md:8` ("One."), `docs/story.md` "Nix packaging" (`:2394`,
    `vendorHash = null`, one dependency), `ASSESSMENT.md:17` ("dependency-free Go") and `OPENCODE-V2.md:139` ("no
    dependencies") are all false. `go.mod:5-11` requires bubbletea, bubbles, lipgloss, yaml.v3 and
    modernc.org/sqlite (5 direct and 29 indirect modules), and `package.nix:54` pins a vendorHash. *Still true.*
13. ~~`docs/opencode-plugin.md` section 6 says the plugin sets `MCPX_SESSION`; the code sets `MCPX_SESSION_ID`.~~
    **Struck (2026-09-30): the framing was wrong, and acting on it would break every generated client (#181
    collision 16, owned here).** `MCPX_SESSION` is not a misspelling of `MCPX_SESSION_ID`. They are two variables
    with different owners:
    - `MCPX_SESSION` is set by mcpx for the scripts it runs (`internal/cli/commands.go:672`,
      `internal/execsvc/execsvc.go:575`, `internal/daemon/consumer.go:536`). The generated client reads it
      (`internal/codegen/emit.go:253`: `const SESSION = env("MCPX_SESSION") || DEFAULT_SESSION;`), and
      `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go` asserts it.
    - `MCPX_SESSION_ID` and `MCPX_CALL_ID` are set by the opencode plugin
      (`plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts:670,677`).
    - `MCPX_CALL` exists nowhere.

    **Nothing in the code should be renamed.** What remains is a one-line doc fix: `docs/opencode-plugin.md:406`
    says the plugin "Sets `MCPX_SESSION`, `MCPX_CALL` and friends". It should name what the plugin actually sets,
    `MCPX_SESSION_ID` and `MCPX_CALL_ID`.
14. `OPENCODE-V2.md`'s body still contradicts its own 2026-09-29 correction block (`:3`): "TypeScript is rejected"
    (`:121`) and "if you stay on opencode v1 ... none of v2's Code Mode is available" (`:222`). `ASSESSMENT.md:278-279`
    points at a `nix/darwin-module.nix` `services.mcpx` that does not exist anywhere in the repo. Size figures in both
    (3,500 lines / 84 tests; 4.2k LOC) are historical; main has 44,916 non-test Go lines at `05c78b2`. These two are
    dated records: correct in place with a dated note rather than rewriting history (see #153). *Still true.*
15. `docs/story.md`'s `## Proposed` (`:2419`) still lists "OpenAPI documents as tools" (`:2562`) although
    "Specifications as tools" (`:1685`) is `standard`, and "Service installation" (`:2498`) still asks for
    `mcpx completions` (`:2508`), shipped as `mcpx completion`. story.md also says adapted binaries are callable from
    a script; they are not (#102). *Still true.* New at `05c78b2`: `docs/story.md:582` says "`MCPX_FORMAT` and
    `MCPX_LOG_LEVEL` set defaults". Since #171 nothing reads `MCPX_FORMAT` (item 7). The variable is
    `MCPX_LOGGING_FORMAT`, and `MCPX_LOG_LEVEL` survives only as an alias of `logging.level`
    (`internal/settings/registry.go:99`). story.md is left to the final docs pass.
16. The version is hard-coded **four** times: `package.nix:19`, `package.nix:61`, the fallback in
    `cmd/mcpx/main.go:18`, and `ARG VERSION=0.1.0` in `Containerfile:40` (added by #182). #158 replaces this with
    the tag. *Still true.*
17. Upstream `transport: "sse"` is accepted (`internal/api/ops_settings.go:100`), but only a Streamable HTTP client
    exists (it handles SSE-framed replies; `internal/pool/pool.go:368-380` builds stdio or `mcpclient.NewHTTP`); no
    legacy HTTP+SSE client was found. Either implement it or document "sse" as an alias with that caveat.
    *Still true.*

### Found in the 2026-09-30 pass (at `05c78b2`)

18. `docs/protocol.md` §2.2 (`:96-110`) still lists `logging` as declared for 2025-03-26 through 2025-11-25, and says
    push-dependent capabilities are declared "when a notifier is behind them". Since #171, mcpx declares no `logging`
    capability and gates `subscribe`/`listChanged` on whether the *connection* can push
    (`internal/mcpserver/server.go:1389-1420`). HTTP connections cannot push. `docs/protocol.md` belongs to PROTOCOL
    (in flight). #145 step 6 generates this table from the code, which ends this kind of drift.
19. `paths.config`'s allowlist reason is false. `internal/settings/consumed_test.go:67-70` and
    `docs/declared-but-unread.md:93-96` say it is "read by config.SearchPath from `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG` directly".
    Nothing reads `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG`: `SearchPathFrom` reads `MCPX_CONFIG` (`internal/config/config.go:549`). Yet
    `docs/configuration.md:336` advertises `--paths-config` / `MCPX_PATHS_CONFIG`, so a generated env-var page would
    publish a variable that does nothing. #5 owns `paths.config`. Until it lands, the allowlist reason and the docs row
    should say "declared, not read".
20. `docs/proposals.md` describes remote daemons as unbuilt: `:767` says `--server example.com:8008` "would let the CLI
    drive a remote daemon" and names authentication as the blocker; `:938` says "optionally binding beyond loopback"
    as a proposal. Both ship: `daemon.endpoint` (client scope, "a daemon somewhere else, instead of the local socket")
    and `daemon.address` (daemon scope, default `127.0.0.1`) at `internal/settings/registry.go:350,365`. The
    proposals need a "shipped as `daemon.endpoint` / `daemon.address`" status line, the way `:45` has one (found by
    reconciling #162 into #134).
21. `docs/dependencies.md:73-76` says script clients use loopback TCP "because `fetch()` over a unix socket is not
    portable across the three runtimes". The generated client uses the unix socket on Deno and Bun and TCP only on
    Node (`internal/codegen/emit.go:256-300`), and the e2e suite asserts exactly that
    (`internal/e2e/e2e_test.go:2470-2492`, "via unix" for deno and bun, "via tcp" for node).

## Approaches

No real design choice for most items; they are fixes. The one choice is how to stop the class recurring:

- **A -- fix each item by hand.** Cheapest now, and the same drift returns within two releases; this is how items
  1, 9, 10 and 11 happened.
- **B -- fix, and add a presence test per list** (every dispatched command is in `Commands()`; every `MCPX_*` read is
  registered or allowlisted; every op has a parity.md row). Catches omissions, not wrong descriptions. Two of these
  tests now have owners: the `MCPX_*` one is #172's, and the parity-row one is #145's. #171 already added the plugin
  direction (`TestThePluginReadsNoUndeclaredSetting`).
- **C -- recommended: fix, add the presence tests from B, and make the lists single-sourced** where the code allows
  (dispatch built from `Commands()`; per-command flags declared in `Commands()`; the plugin README table generated
  from the registry plus `pluginEnvAllowed`; parity.md generated per #145). Then the generated reference in #145 is
  correct by construction, and B's tests guard what cannot be single-sourced.

## Open questions

- Should `mcpx init` be fixed or removed in favour of documented examples? Either way, the `mcpx help`
  CONCURRENCY block (item 2) goes with it.
- Should `mcpx openapi` be deleted, or become an alias for the `/v1` document?
- Split this into per-item bugs if they will be fixed by different people; kept together here because they block
  the same thing. Items already owned elsewhere: 7 (count and allowlist) -> #172, 11 (drift check) -> #145 and
  (content) #76/#144, 16 -> #158, 18 -> PROTOCOL / #145 step 6, 19 -> #5.

## Ease · Impact · Related

Ease: M (items are small; C's single-sourcing is the bulk) · Impact: high (blocks an accurate reference) ·
Depends on / related: #144, #145, #146, #147, #148, #157, #153, #172 (owns the `MCPX_*` count and allowlist, #181
collision 17), #5 (item 19), #158 (item 16), #180 (the re-verification this pass used), #177 (class tracker:
a promise and a behaviour that disagree), #74 (closed, fixed in #75; the same class: flags accepted and ignored), #76, #102 (docs
promise a feature that does not work).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.
