body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#83 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #173

## Summary

"Turn anything into an MCP server" is already most of what mcpx does — it is the premise of `paths.adapters` and `paths.apis` — but the coverage is uneven and the results are second-class. A command-line program can become tools; a shell script, a Python script or a bare binary cannot, except by writing an adapter declaration by hand. And what adapters and OpenAPI produce are loose MCP tools, not namespaces: they are absent from `mcpx ls`, from the generated TypeScript, and from scripts.

This issue asks for two things. One: extend "anything becomes a server" to scripts of any language, to bare binaries with no declaration, and to plugins. Two: make everything produced that way a **first-class namespace**, registerable from configuration *and* live, so a declaration, a plugin and an upstream MCP server are indistinguishable once loaded.

## Original notes

> - support adding bash/js/ts/py scripts as mcp
> - support embedding/config/dynamic-add "mcp" for any plugin above
> - support embedding/config/dynamic-add any binary as mcp
> - binary mcp

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

**Command-line programs → tools: shipped.** `internal/adapter/adapter.go` takes a declaration — `name`, `command`, `args`, `env`, `dir`, `timeout`, and a list of `tools`, each a fixed-arg subcommand with typed `params` (string/number/integer/boolean/array, flag or positional, `repeat`, `default`, `enum`, plus `stdin` for a parameter written to stdin and `json` to parse the output). Declarations are loaded from `paths.adapters` (`internal/settings/registry.go:292`, `internal/cli/adapter.go:22`). `mcpx adapter check` reports whether the binaries exist, and `mcpx doctor` includes the same check (`internal/cli/doctor.go:230-244`). Two deliberate details are recorded in `docs/story.md:1626-1630`: a boolean parameter becomes the flag's *presence*, and a non-zero exit is a *result*, not an error.

**OpenAPI → tools: shipped.** `paths.apis` and `mcpx api --spec <path-or-url>` (`internal/cli/openapi_tools.go`).

**Saved scripts already carry a tool schema.** A recipe is a script on the scripts search path that declares its holes in a header comment: `// @param repo:string  which repository`, with types `string`/`number`/`boolean`/`json`, defaults, and optional markers (`internal/recipes/recipes.go`). That is a JSON Schema in all but spelling. Recipes are reachable as `GET /v1/recipes`, `GET /v1/recipes/{name}`, `POST /v1/recipes/{name}` and `POST /v1/recipes/{name}/run` (`internal/api/ops_consumer.go:42-95`), and through `mcpx prompt` / `POST /v1/intent` matching. **They are not individual MCP tools.** An agent cannot see `close_stale_issues(repo, days)` in `tools/list`; it can only see the recipe machinery.

**Live add exists, for servers only.** `POST /v1/servers` writes the entry to a config file and reloads, so the server is callable immediately and still there after a restart; `DELETE /v1/servers/{name}` removes it (`internal/api/ops_settings.go:82,111`). There is no equivalent for an adapter, an API spec or a recipe-as-tool.

**The second-class problem, precisely.** Adapter tools and OpenAPI operations are attached as `mcpserver.Extra` when the MCP server is constructed (`internal/cli/serve.go:328-346` at 05c78b2; `WithExtras` at `:346`). That gets them into `tools/list` over `/mcp` and `mcpx serve --transport stdio`, and nowhere else: not into the pool, not into `mcpx ls` or `mcpx catalog`, not into the codegen, and therefore not callable as `gitx.log()` from a script. `docs/story.md:1619-1620` says an adapted program "is callable from a script" — and so does the adapter package's own doc comment ("appearing in `mcpx ls`, callable from a script", `internal/adapter/adapter.go:8-10`); against the code as it stands neither is true, and this issue should fix the code rather than the sentence. The narrower defect (fix or retract the claim, and guard that `tools/list` and the generated client agree) is #102, in flight; this issue is the design it belongs to. Extras are also computed once at MCP-server construction, so there is no live add/remove path for them at all.

**No Python or shell runtime anywhere.** `internal/runner/runner.go:73` resolves `deno`, `bun`, `node` only. Python 3.14.7 and uv 0.9.28 are installed on this machine but mcpx has no notion of them.

## Approaches

### Approach A — least recommended: a generic "run this command as a tool" escape hatch

`{ "name": "sh", "command": "bash", "tools": [{ "name": "run", "params": [{"name": "script"}] }] }` — one tool that takes a string and runs it. Or its more honest spelling, a `shell` server type.

Two lines of config and it covers every bullet in the notes, which is why it is tempting. It is wrong for a reason the adapter package already wrote down (`internal/adapter/adapter.go:12-14`): "This is deliberately not a general shell escape. A tool here is a named subcommand with declared parameters, so a model cannot invent a command line, and what is reachable is exactly what somebody wrote down." A generic runner discards every property that makes the adapter useful: no schema, so no typed client and nothing for an agent to reason about; no `mcpx doctor` check, because there is nothing to check; no namespace, no descriptions, no `mcpx catalog` entry with any information in it. The agent ends up writing shell, badly, with mcpx as a very slow `bash -c`.

Note also that mcpx already has a *better* general escape hatch: `mcpx exec` runs TypeScript with typed clients for everything, preflight diagnostics, artifacts and content-addressed workdirs. A shell escape is a worse version of a feature that shipped.

### Approach B — middle: extend the adapter declaration to cover scripts and bare binaries

Keep the declaration model and widen what it can point at:

- **Scripts.** An adapter whose `command` is a script file works today if the file is executable. What is missing is a `runtime` field, so `{ "command": "./tools/report.py", "runtime": "python" }` resolves `uv run` / `python3` / `bun` / `deno` / `bash` without the author hard-coding an interpreter path. This is a small, self-contained addition and the natural home for the notes' `bash/js/ts/py` list. It must be its own resolver, not `script.runtime` (`internal/settings/registry.go:176`), which is about the JS runtime that executes mcpx-generated scripts and means something different.
- **Bare binaries with no declaration.** For a program that already emits a machine-readable interface there is no reason to write one by hand. Three real sources, in descending order of how often they exist: a program that ships an OpenAPI or JSON Schema document (feed it to the existing `paths.apis` path); a program with a `--help` that a *generation* step — run once, by a human, possibly with a model — turns into a declaration file the user then edits and commits; and the degenerate case, one tool per binary taking an argv array, which is Approach A wearing a hat and should be opt-in and loud.

  The important design point: generation produces a **file the user keeps**, not a runtime inference. A declaration inferred fresh on every daemon start makes a tool surface that changes when someone upgrades a CLI, and an agent's context changing because `jq` got a new flag is a bug that will take a day to find.
- **Scripts-as-tools from recipes.** A recipe already declares typed parameters; publishing each one as an MCP tool is mostly plumbing (`internal/recipes/recipes.go` → a JSON Schema → an `Extra` or a namespace). This is the highest value-per-line item in the whole issue: the schemas exist, the runner exists, the search path exists.

All correct and all incremental. B's limit is that it leaves everything in the `Extra` path, so all of it stays absent from `mcpx ls`, the codegen and scripts, and none of it can be added live.

### Approach C — recommended: one internal notion of a *tool source*, with declaration, plugin and upstream server as three implementations

Adopt the interface `docs/proposals.md:427-429` already proposes — "something that can list tools with JSON Schemas and call one" — and make **every** producer implement it: an MCP server (today's default), a CLI adapter declaration, an OpenAPI document, a recipe, a plugin (sibling issue), and a script or binary through B's widened declaration. Then do the part that makes it matter: register them through the *same* path as servers, not as `Extra`s.

What that buys, in one list:

| property | today, for an adapter | with a tool source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| in `tools/list` over `/mcp` | yes | yes |
| in `mcpx ls` / `mcpx catalog` / `mcpx search` | no | yes |
| in the generated TypeScript, callable from a script | no | yes |
| namespaced, with `mcpx.namespace`/description | partly | yes |
| live add/remove | no | yes, one path |
| pooled, idle-reaped, `sharing`/`scope` | n/a | where it applies |
| preflight diagnostics find calls to it (`internal/diagnose`) | no | yes |

And the three ways to add one collapse into one mechanism seen from three angles, which is what the notes' "embedding/config/dynamic-add" triplet is asking for:

- **config** — a declaration on `paths.adapters` / `paths.apis` / `paths.plugins` / the scripts search path, or a `servers` entry. Declarative, reviewable, in git.
- **dynamic-add** — the existing `POST /v1/servers` generalised: a body that may carry a `kind` (`server` | `adapter` | `api` | `script` | `plugin`) and the corresponding fields, writing to the right file and reloading, exactly as it does now for servers. Prefer extending that operation over minting `/v1/adapters`, `/v1/scripts`, `/v1/plugins`: it already does the hard parts — choose a scope, write the file, reload, keep other instances alive — and one table entry in `internal/api/ops*.go` means one CLI command, one MCP tool and one OpenAPI operation rather than four of each. A new endpoint is justified only if the bodies turn out to have nothing in common, which they mostly do not.
- **embedding** — the daemon holding its own in-process tool source rather than spawning anything: recipes and `/v1` op tools are already this. Covered further in the embedding sibling issue.

Recommended because it is the smallest set of concepts that covers every bullet, it retires the "adapter tools are invisible to scripts" gap rather than widening it, and it is the interface the project already wrote down as the right shape and deferred. Do it now precisely because plugins are about to be the fourth producer: adding a fourth `Extra` list is how this ends up with four half-integrated surfaces.

Ship order that keeps every step useful on its own: (1) recipes as tools, since the schemas already exist; (2) the tool-source interface with adapters and OpenAPI moved onto it, which is where the `mcpx ls`/codegen win lands; (3) `runtime` on a declaration, for bash/js/ts/py; (4) generalised live add; (5) generated declarations for bare binaries.

## Open questions

- Namespacing collisions: an adapter named `git`, a plugin named `git` and an upstream server named `git`. Today adapters flatten to `name_tool` and servers namespace properly. One rule, and a loud error on collision.
  **Owns #181 collision 4:** the tool-source interface defines namespaces and collision rules for every producer. #114's tool views, cross-server namespaces and script-backed tools are built on these rules and do not define their own; #80's plugins are a namespace under them.
- Does a CLI adapter belong in the *pool*? It has no long-lived process — every call is a fresh `exec`. It needs to be a namespace without being a pooled server, which is the main piece of real design work in C.
- Is a recipe-as-tool automatic for every recipe, or opt-in per recipe? Automatic is friendlier and can flood `tools/list` in a repo with fifty scripts. Probably a declaration marker, defaulting to on, with a budget in `mcpx catalog`.
- For bare binaries: is `--help` parsing worth it at all, given how irregular help output is? A one-shot, model-assisted generation into a file the user edits is defensible; a runtime parser is not.
- Should a generated declaration record the binary's version, so an upgrade produces a visible "this declaration was written against jq 1.7" warning rather than silent drift?
- `mcpx adapter check` generalises to `mcpx source check` — is that worth the rename, and what does it do for a plugin (start it and `tools/list`?) versus a binary (does it exist?)?
- `stdin`, `json`, boolean-as-presence and non-zero-exit-as-result are adapter-specific semantics. Which of them survive into the general interface, and which stay adapter-local?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease:** M for recipes-as-tools and a declaration `runtime`; L for the tool-source interface and generalised live add; XL for all of it including generated declarations. **Impact:** high — this is the feature mcpx is *for*, and the `Extra` gap currently caps it.

**Depends on / related:** #80 (a plugin is the fourth tool source, and the reason to unify now), #84 (mcpx as its own upstream, in-process sources), #102 (in flight: the documented-but-false "callable from a script" claim; slice 2 here delivers the capability), #114 (builds on this issue's namespace and collision rules, collision 4), #7 (placeholders/`@param` spelling is shared with recipes), #6, #76 (`/v1` operations without CLI commands — the same parity discipline applies to any new registration verb), #79 (codegen and catalog cost when the tool count grows), #105/#106 (a declaration `runtime` for Python and shebangs is the same resolution problem), #5.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#155 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #92

## Summary

Design the mcpx home page: the first stop of the 30-second layer (home -> overview -> quick start -> close
the tab). It carries the pitch (why you would install it), a short video, a small intro block, one static
TypeScript example, the download link, two copy-button install commands and a copy-button agent prompt
that rotates among four phrasings. Nothing like it exists: `docs/landing.md` is a PR landing checklist, not
a landing page, and the only first-screen prose is the top of `docs/story.md`, which is a long walk, not a
skim.

The design constraint for every choice below is note line 8: someone "skimming while doing 3 different
things will accidentally learn". So: one screen of hero, no reading required to get the three claims, every
command copyable, nothing on the page that is not real.

This issue also flags a defect in the notes: the system-wide install form `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)` does
not do what it looks like it does (see "System-wide install command").

## Original notes

> - documentation
>   - make a book using whatever is the most common and simple modern choice
>     - specialized agent markdown all pages
>       - home page has install prompt built into the bot version
>     - 3 main things, not book sections jsut like levels of detail-
>       - the 30 seconds look at home page click the overview page, click the quick start page, ctrl+w should be simple enough that even this person skimming while doing 3 different things will accidentally learn
>         - why you would install it
>           - code mode
>             - makes shareable, reusable scripts
>           - reclaim context, use less tokens
>             - smarter, cheaper
>           - tame mcp
>             - one mcp config
>             - share endpoint with your tailnet
>             - corral your scripts, apis, and binaries
>         - how to install it
>           - home page has
>             - short flex video
>             - simple intro
>               - short 1-4 sentence paragraph
>               - surrounded by small title/small here-blocks/bigger word lines
>               - code block example
>                 - static syntax-highlighted typescript
>                 - exec real editable example click button remote
>                 - wasm, local mcp, daemon/cli-client
>             - download link
>             - per-user `curl <short> | sh` [copy-button]
>               - ~system-wide `sudo $(curl <short> | sh)` [copy-button]
>             - <`subitem[rand(this.len)]`> [copy-button]
>               - `hey please one-shot setup mcpx right now`
>               - `hey install this mcpx thing and comment out all my mcp config`
>               - `replace mcp with mcpx codemode`
>               - `guided install mcpx now plz`

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

- **No home page, no site.** `dezren39/nix` has no Pages site; the generator is #117, deploy #118,
  the short domain behind `<short>` #119.
- **No installer and no download.** No tags, no GitHub releases, no install script; version hard-coded
  `0.1.0` (`pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:19`, `:61`, the default in `cmd/mcpx/main.go:18`, and
  `Containerfile:40`). The only install path today is the flake output (`flake.nix:385`, app at `:494`);
  since #182 a `pkgs/mcpx/Containerfile` builds a local image, but none is published. Channels are designed
  in #158.
- **Pitch material exists, scattered.** `docs/story.md` above `<!-- table-of-contents-marker -->`
  (story.md:1-296) has the numbers the pitch needs: `mcpx ls` "Seven namespaces, 43 tools, 171 tokens";
  27 Chrome tools and "not one byte of their schemas is in the agent's context"; "about 4,600 tokens total"
  for the whole task, "and left behind a script that costs nothing to run again". `package.nix` `meta`
  has a two-paragraph description. `AGENTS.md` opens with the three framing lines.
- **Each "why" bullet maps to a shipped feature** (all `status: standard` in story.md unless noted):

  | Note | What backs the claim today | Ref |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | code mode -> shareable, reusable scripts | named scripts on a search path (`.mcpx/scripts/<name>.ts`, then `~/.config/mcpx/scripts/`), `mcpx run <name>`, generated typed client | story.md "Named scripts" (:641), AGENTS.md "Scripts" |
  | reclaim context -> smarter, cheaper | `ls`/`search`/`types <ns>` pull schemas on demand; the story's token counts | story.md:142, :274, "Zero-context discovery" (:298) |
  | one mcp config | mcpx reads the standard `mcpServers` object ("an existing config can be pasted in unchanged", `internal/cli/commands.go` `starterConfig`); one daemon serves CLI, plugin, `/v1`, `/mcp` | story.md "One daemon per config" (:728) |
  | share endpoint with your tailnet | `mcpx daemon --address <ip> --port 8899` on one host, `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT=http://host:8899` on clients (`daemon.address`, `daemon.port`, `daemon.endpoint`; `internal/settings/registry.go:343-375`). Nothing tailnet-specific; binding beyond loopback prints a one-time warning because the API is unauthenticated (`internal/cli/root.go:198-202`) | story.md "One daemon, many clients" (:2092) |
  | corral scripts | the named-script search path above; recipes (`mcpx recipes`) | story.md :641, docs/consumer.md |
  | corral APIs | `mcpx api tools --spec <url>` / `mcpx api call <op> --spec <url>` turn an OpenAPI document into tools | story.md "Specifications as tools" (:1685) |
  | corral binaries | `paths.adapters` declarations turn a CLI into MCP tools; `mcpx adapter check` | story.md "Command-line programs as servers" (:1593) |

  **Caveat for the last two rows (#102):** adapter tools and OpenAPI operations are attached as
  `mcpserver.Extra` and reach `tools/list` over `/mcp` and `mcpx serve` only. They are not in `mcpx ls`, the
  generated client or scripts, although story.md says an adapted binary "is callable from a script". The
  home page may say "OpenAPI specs and CLI programs become MCP tools"; it must not say "call them from your
  scripts" until #102 / #83 land.

  Two story.md inconsistencies the pitch must not inherit: "OpenAPI documents as tools" is still listed
  under `## Proposed` with `status: proposed` (story.md:2562) although "Specifications as tools" (:1685) is
  `standard`; and "Service installation" (:2498) still asks for `mcpx completions bash|zsh|fish`, which has
  shipped as `mcpx completion` (`cmd/mcpx/main.go:144`, used by `package.nix` postInstall). Reported for
  the compendium (#150); the home page should claim only `standard` features.
- **The name is crowded.** At least six unrelated GitHub projects are called mcpx (lydakis/mcpx with its own
  Homebrew tap, kwonye/mcpx published as `@kwonye/mcpx`, Codestz/mcpx, arcadeai-labs/mcpx, lwsinclair/mcpx,
  thiagomendes/mcpx), and the unscoped npm name `mcpx` is a `0.0.1-security` placeholder (`npm view mcpx`).
  This decides the agent-prompt design below.

## Page anatomy (proposed, top to bottom)

| # | Block | Content | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Intro | eyebrow + display lines + chips + 1-4 sentence paragraph | "Intro" below |
| 2 | Video | 10-20 s loop | "Video" below |
| 3 | Install | per-user command, system-wide command, download link, each with a copy button | "Install commands" below |
| 4 | Agent prompt | one of four prompts, copy button | "Rotating prompt" below |
| 5 | Example | static highlighted TypeScript, "run it" affordance | the runnable part is #156 |
| 6 | Why | three short columns: code mode / reclaim context / tame MCP | "Why copy" below |
| 7 | Next | two large links: Overview, Quick start (and a small "now what") | #157 |

Order is a judgement call: install and prompt sit above the fold because the notes' 30-second reader may
never scroll. An alternative puts "Why" at #2 and the video at #6; see Open questions.

### Intro: "small title / small here-blocks / bigger word lines"

This is an **interpretation** of note line 34, to be confirmed:

- **small title**: an eyebrow (kicker) line above the headline in small caps, e.g. `MCP, in code mode`.
- **small here-blocks**: small inline chips or badges beside or under the headline, each a two- or three-word
  fact: `one config`, `fewer tokens`, `scripts you keep`. Read as "little blocks that say *here is X*".
- **bigger word lines**: two or three large display lines that carry the pitch on their own for someone who
  reads nothing else, e.g. `Tame MCP.` / `Reclaim your context.` / `Keep the scripts.`
- **the paragraph** (1-4 sentences) sits under them in body size. Draft, from `package.nix` `meta` and
  AGENTS.md: "mcpx puts every MCP server on your machine behind one command. Agents discover tools when they
  need them and call them from TypeScript, so tool schemas and intermediate results stay out of the context
  window. What the agent writes is a script you can run again."

### Why copy

Three columns, each a display line plus one sentence plus one link into the overview (#157):

1. **Code mode.** Agents write TypeScript against a typed client instead of making one tool call per turn;
   the result is a script in `.mcpx/scripts/` anyone can rerun (`mcpx run shot-flow`).
2. **Reclaim context.** Schemas load on demand: the story's whole task cost about 4,600 tokens, most of it
   one deliberate `mcpx types`. Numbers must be the story's, re-measured per release (docs/release-runbook.md
   "Per-release" step 2). "Smarter" is a claim, not a measurement; phrase it as "fewer tool schemas
   competing for attention" and link the evidence page in the compendium (#153) rather than asserting it.
3. **Tame MCP.** One `mcpServers` config for every harness; one daemon other machines on your tailnet can
   point at; OpenAPI documents and CLI programs become MCP tools too (served over MCP; not yet callable from
   scripts, #102). Copy for the tailnet line must not promise
   more than exists: today it is `daemon.address`/`daemon.port` plus `daemon.endpoint`, nothing
   Tailscale-aware, so write "point your other machines at one daemon (over Tailscale, WireGuard, a VPN)"
   and link the remote-daemon page in level 2 (#146).

### Static TypeScript example

- Source: an excerpt of the story's two-screenshot script (story.md:196-234), not new code. Proposed excerpt
  (about 12 lines; lines elided with `// …`): the `tools.chrome_devtools` binding, `new_page`, the snapshot ->
  `uid` -> `click` sequence with its comment "click needs that, not a selector", and the final
  `console.log`. It shows the three things the pitch claims: typed calls, image bytes that never reach the
  model, one printed line.
- **Warning:** that script is Deno-specific. It calls `Deno.mkdir` and `Deno.writeFile`; the generated
  client's Deno shim for Bun/Node covers only `Deno.args`, `Deno.env.get`, `Deno.inspect` and
  `Deno.readTextFile(Sync)` (`internal/codegen/emit.go:348-390`). Either the excerpt avoids those calls, or
  the page labels it "Deno", or the script is changed to `node:fs` (which Deno and Bun both support).
- The snippet must be included from a real file that CI runs, not pasted into the page, so it cannot rot.
  Needs an include directive in the generator (#117). Docs checks run in CI; see the testing trackers under #91 (CI pipeline #95, integration/environments #97)
  (the lead will link it).
- Highlight at build time (Shiki, or the generator's own highlighter), not client-side highlight.js, so the
  page renders with JavaScript off and the agent twin (#120) gets the same code fence.
- A "run it" button belongs to #156; this issue reserves the slot and a copy button that copies an
  `mcpx run`/`mcpx exec` command.

### Download link

A single "Download" link to the latest GitHub release for the reader's platform needs releases first
(#158). Do not detect architecture from the User-Agent: macOS browsers report Intel on Apple Silicon.
Link to the release page (or a per-OS list) and let `install.sh` detect with `uname`. Until releases exist,
the link goes to the install page's nix section (#157).

### Install commands and copy buttons

- **Per-user:** `curl -fsSL <short> | sh`. The flags matter and should be on the page as written: `-f` makes
  an HTTP error fail instead of piping an HTML error page into `sh`; `-sS` hides progress but keeps errors;
  `-L` follows the redirect a short URL will almost certainly be. The script itself must wrap its body in a
  function called on the last line so a truncated download runs nothing. Installs to `~/.local/bin`
  (#158).
- **"Read it first" variant**, one click away (a disclosure under the command, not a separate page):
  `curl -fsSL <short> -o install-mcpx.sh && less install-mcpx.sh && sh install-mcpx.sh`.
- **System-wide:** see the next section. The note's `~` in "~system-wide" is read as "roughly / the
  alternative"; not a path.

### System-wide install command: the notes' form is wrong

`sudo $(curl <short> | sh)` runs `curl <short> | sh` **unprivileged** in a command substitution, captures
the installer's **stdout**, word-splits and glob-expands it, and executes the result as a command under
`sudo`. Every progress line the installer prints becomes argv. It only works if the script is designed to
print exactly one command and nothing else, and even then quoting is lost to word splitting. It is not an
established pattern and it will surprise anyone who reads it.

| | Command | Runs as root | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | `sudo $(curl <short> \| sh)` | whatever the script prints | least recommended: fragile (stdout is code), unusual, unreviewable; only viable if the script has a dedicated "print the install command" mode, and then it is a worse `--system` |
| B | `curl -fsSL <short> \| sudo sh` | the whole installer, including the download | the common pattern; simple; but runs the network fetch, archive extraction and checksum as root when only the final copy needs it |
| C | `curl -fsSL <short> \| sh -s -- --system` | only the copy into `/usr/local/bin` (the script calls `sudo install -m 0755 ...` itself, or `doas`) | **recommended**: least privilege, one script with one flag, the same command shape as per-user, and the script can explain what it is about to escalate for |

Recommend C, with B shown under "other ways" for environments without `sudo` in the script's path (running
as root already, containers). `--system` is designed in #158. The install page (#157) shows the same two
forms, substituted from the same source, and never the notes' form.

### Rotating prompt `<`subitem[rand(this.len)]`>`

- The four prompts, **verbatim**, not reworded:
  `hey please one-shot setup mcpx right now` · `hey install this mcpx thing and comment out all my mcp config`
  · `replace mcp with mcpx codemode` · `guided install mcpx now plz`.
- **Random choice client-side.** All four are in the HTML; a few lines of inline script pick one per page
  view (`Math.floor(Math.random() * items.length)`) and hide the rest. No-JS fallback: the first one shows
  (or all four as a list). No server-side randomness: the site is static (#118) and a CDN would cache one
  choice anyway. Optional: clicking the prompt cycles to the next.
- **The copy payload must carry a URL.** Given the crowded name (Current state), an agent that has never
  heard of this mcpx and is told "setup mcpx" will search and install one of the other six. So the copied
  text is the prompt plus a line with the site's agent entry point, e.g.
  `hey please one-shot setup mcpx right now` + newline + `https://<short>/llms.txt`. The URL is **visible**
  under the prompt in small text: copying text the reader did not see is a pattern used by clipboard
  attacks and should not be normalised on an install page. This does not reword the prompts; it appends a
  pointer.
- **What the URL must lead to** (#120, the bot home page with the install prompt built in, note line 6):
  an agent-facing install procedure that handles each prompt's intent:
  - "one-shot setup": detect OS, install per-user, run `mcpx doctor`, add the harness integration
    (AGENTS.md / the opencode plugin), verify with `mcpx ls`.
  - "comment out all my mcp config": mcpx reads the same `mcpServers` object, and its config search path
    already includes `.mcp.json` at every directory level (`internal/config/config.go:561`), which is Claude
    Code's project file name. There is **no importer** for other hosts' files (opencode, Cursor, Claude
    Desktop: no reference to their paths in `internal/`), so the agent moves those entries by hand into
    `~/.config/mcpx/config.json` or `.mcpx.json`, then comments them out of the harness config. The
    procedure must say to back up first, and must warn that commenting out a project `.mcp.json` hides
    those servers from mcpx too, so they move to `.mcpx.json` before they are commented out.
  - "replace mcp with mcpx codemode": the same, plus AGENTS.md or the plugin, so the agent stops calling MCP
    tools directly (AGENTS.md "Do not" list).
  - "guided install": interactive; the agent asks before each step. `mcpx prompt` (from #41) is not usable
    for this on first install: it needs a sampling answerer and configured recipes, neither of which exists
    yet on a fresh machine (`internal/cli/manual.go` `prompt` Detail). The agent is the guide.

### Quick start and now what

Two large links to #157's overview and quick start, and one smaller "now what" into level 2 (#94).
Nothing else in the footer area competes with them.

## Approaches: the short flex video

| | Tool | Reproducible | Size | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A | screen recording (QuickTime, OBS) | no | large | least recommended |
| B | asciinema `.cast` + player | partially | tiny | text, not video |
| C | charmbracelet VHS `.tape` rendered in CI | yes | small | **recommended** |

- **A, screen recording.** Easiest the first time and wrong every time after: the CLI output changes, the
  recording shows stale columns and tokens, and re-recording is manual. Large files, a real desktop
  (notifications, fonts) in frame, and nothing checks it.
- **B, asciinema.** Records a real terminal as a text `.cast` (kilobytes), renders with the asciinema player
  (JS), text is selectable, and `agg` converts to GIF. Honest and small. But a recording is still captured
  once by hand unless driven by a script, the player needs JS (no-JS fallback is nothing), and it plays
  like a terminal, not a hero video.
- **C, VHS (recommended).** A `.tape` file in the repo (`Type "mcpx ls"`, `Enter`, `Sleep 2s`, ...) renders
  to webm/mp4/gif with deterministic timing, fonts and size (`Output hero.webm`), and runs in CI through
  `charmbracelet/vhs-action`. Re-render per release so the video never shows stale output; because it runs
  the real binary against a fixture config, it doubles as a smoke test. The tape's commands are the agent
  twin's transcript (#120). Cost: VHS needs `ttyd` and `ffmpeg` in CI (both in nixpkgs), and the demo
  needs fixture MCP servers that behave identically every run.

Embed rules regardless of tool:

- `<video muted loop playsinline preload="metadata" poster="hero.png">` with a webm (VP9/AV1) source and an
  mp4 (H.264) fallback. Not a GIF: typically several times larger for the same clip.
- **prefers-reduced-motion:** the `autoplay` attribute cannot be disabled from CSS. Omit `autoplay` and
  start playback from a few lines of script only when
  `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)').matches`; otherwise show the poster with controls.
  With JS off the poster and controls show. Pause when scrolled out of view (IntersectionObserver).
- Budget: 10-20 s, at most ~1 MB for the webm, 1280x720 or smaller, captions not needed if every frame is
  terminal text, but `aria-label` describing the sequence.
- Content: what the video shows is open (below). The story's two-screenshot flow is the strongest flex but
  needs Chrome in CI.

## Where the home page comes from (constraints on #117, not a second decision)

#117 owns the generator choice and currently recommends mdBook for the book plus **one hand-written
`index.html`** for the home page, because mdBook renders `index.md` as chapter one with a sidebar and has
no hero layout. Everything in this issue fits that shape. What the home page needs from it:

- **One source for two outputs.** The hand-written page and its agent twin (`index.md`, #120) drift
  unless one is generated from the other. Prefer a small build step that renders `index.html` from a
  markdown-plus-front-matter source (prompts, commands, paragraph), so copy edits happen once.
- **Include a file region into a code block**, for the example and the install commands, so the page shows
  the same bytes CI runs.
- **Build-time highlighting** for the example (mdBook's own pages use client-side highlight.js; the home
  page need not).
- **Copy buttons on arbitrary blocks**, small inline JS, a `<video>` element, all working or degrading
  cleanly with JS off.
- **The `<short>` values substituted at build** from one place (#119), not typed into the page.
- Shared CSS with the book or a deliberately different look is #117's open question 4; the 30-second
  path crosses from the home page into book pages, so at minimum header, fonts and colours should match.

## Open questions

- Is the "small title / small here-blocks / bigger word lines" interpretation right?
- Hero order: install above the fold (proposed) or "why" first?
- Video content: the story's browser flow (needs Chrome in CI) or a fixture-only flow (`ls` -> `search` ->
  `exec` printing one line)? Is 10-20 s right?
- Should the example be the story excerpt (Deno-specific today) or a runtime-neutral script?
- Copy payload: prompt + `llms.txt` URL (proposed), or prompt + the human install page URL?
- Should the page show a runtime prerequisite (deno, bun or node 22.6+ on `PATH`; `mcpx doctor` fails
  without one, `internal/cli/doctor.go:47-60`)? Releases outside nix do not bundle a runtime (#158); the
  container image ships bun.
- Does #79's `script.typecheck` default change what the example's "run it" command prints on first run?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease**: M (design and copy; the template work is small once #117 is chosen; the VHS pipeline is
another S-M). **Impact**: high (the page most people will ever see).
**Depends on / related**: #117 (generator constraints above), #118, #119 (`<short>`),
#120 (copy payload target, bot home page), #156 (the run button), #157 (overview, quick start,
install page), #158 (download link, `install.sh`, `--system`), #150/#153 (story.md status
inconsistencies; evidence for "smarter"), #146 (remote daemon page), #41 (closed, fixed in #58: `mcpx prompt`, not a first-run
guide), #44 (closed, fixed in #53: plugin without the binary), #48 (other harnesses the prompts may land in), #79 (typecheck
default), #94 (level 2), #102 and #83 (adapter and OpenAPI tools are not in the script client).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

body:
## Phase 3 of #1834 — reviewable sampling in `mcpx elicit` + truth-up + nix#256 evidence

Design: #1834 (mcpx sampling trust boundary). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-sampling-trust-boundary.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Origin: dezren39/nix#256. **Gated on Phase 2 of #1834** (the rendering shows the validated shapes, and the truth-up needs both earlier phases' as-built state).

### Problem

A person cannot review a sampling request, because the prompt is not shown. Sampling questions are broker rows whose `Message` is the request's system prompt (or "`<server>` asks for a model completion") and whose `Schema` field carries the full `CreateMessageRequest` — but `renderQuestion` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/elicit.go`) renders `Schema` as a JSON Schema: `describeSchema` looks for `properties`, a sampling request has none, so the messages render as nothing and the answer example offered is `'{}'`. `elicit.Route` (`internal/elicit/elicit.go` ~L502-503) also sends every Sample question to the agent audience unconditionally. Gaps: `sampling-app-review-ui`, `sampling-app-view-edit-prompts`, `sampling-app-review-responses`, `sampling-client-user-approval-controls` in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/conformance/coverage_clientfeatures.go`.

### Scope — the existing surface learns sampling (no new UI)

- `renderQuestion` for a Sample question renders it as sampling: requesting server, system prompt, and the message list (role + content per message, text verbatim) — not via `describeSchema`. `mcpx elicit show` gives the full request JSON.
- The answer example for a Sample question is a real `CreateMessageResult` skeleton (`role`/`model`/`content`/`stopReason`), not `'{}'`.
- CLI help/docs for Sample questions state the review story plainly: a pending question can be inspected and answered/overridden by a person through list/show/answer; answered results are recorded on the broker row and visible via `mcpx elicit result <id>`. Do NOT claim a pre-delivery staging state exists — building one is an open question on #1834, not part of this phase.
- Existing approval controls (audience routing, policy, decline) stay as they are; no new gate is invented.

### Truth-up

- `pkgs/mcpx/docs/spec/conformance-matrix.md` rows for all seven scoped `#256` gaps updated to as-built — retired, or explicitly partial per row where the as-built state only partially meets the row (the review rows in particular: claim only what the rendering/routing changes actually deliver).
- Compare-register sampling rows touched by this design (SMP-05, SMP-06, SMP-10 in `pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/sampling.md`) updated to as-built.
- Completion evidence comment on dezren39/nix#256 against each of its four acceptance bullets with the landing PRs; close nix#256 if and only if every bullet is met, naming any that is not.

Out of scope: validation or error-code changes (Phases 1–2), a pre-delivery staging hold, sampling rate limits (nix#257), elicitation rendering (that is #1675 Phase 3's ground — reuse its patterns, don't redo it).

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=design-architect state=filed at=2026-10-28T21:34:31Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- `mcpx elicit list/show` on a pending sampling question displays the server, system prompt and actual messages; the offered answer skeleton is a valid `CreateMessageResult` shape.
- Matrix rows for the seven scoped gaps and register rows SMP-05/SMP-06/SMP-10 match the code as built (partials stated as partials).
- dezren39/nix#256 carries completion evidence against each acceptance bullet and is closed if and only if all are met.

body:
## Design: mcpx sampling trust boundary — reviewable, validated, and honestly error-coded

**Design doc:** `files/designs/code-mcpx-sampling-trust-boundary.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (developing-today/code design architect, pass 10, 2026-10-28).
**Origin:** [dezren39/nix#256](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/issues/256) — sampling relay: human review, validation of results, error mapping (8 conformance rows). This design scopes only its remainder (audit below); no Drew direction decision is needed — nix#256's acceptance is explicit and its scope is conformance-only (sampling is deprecated in 2026-07-28; standing instruction is keep-working, add-nothing-new).

### Problem

mcpx has no model, so sampling is a relay with a trust decision inside it: an upstream asks for a completion, something answering for the user produces one, and mcpx hands it back as if the user had spoken. Verified on main `528886eb`:

1. **A person cannot review a sampling request — the prompt is not shown.** `sampleViaBroker` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/hooks.go` ~L198-214) stores the request's *system prompt* as the broker question's Message (fallback: "`<server>` asks for a model completion") and the full request in the question's Schema field. But `mcpx elicit`'s `renderQuestion` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/elicit.go`) renders Schema as a JSON Schema: `describeSchema` looks for `properties`, a sampling request has none, so the messages — the actual prompt — render as nothing and the answer example offered is `'{}'`. Routing never offers a person the question either: `elicit.Route` (`internal/elicit/elicit.go` ~L502-503) sends every Sample question to the agent audience unconditionally. Denial exists (decline is conformance-tested), but the spec's review rows have no surface. Gaps: `sampling-app-review-ui`, `sampling-app-view-edit-prompts`, `sampling-app-review-responses`, `sampling-client-user-approval-controls`.
2. **Nothing validates sampling messages or results, either direction.** `sampleViaBroker` unmarshals only `maxTokens`/`systemPrompt`; `messages` is never inspected — tool-result messages with non-`tool_result` content, or a `tool_result` id no earlier `tool_use` issued, pass through (register SMP-06 pairing). On return, the only checks are JSON-object / not-null (~L226-236); a missing `role`/`model` is then *silently filled in* ("unknown") instead of judged, and the result is never checked against its request (`stopReason: "toolUse"` / `tool_use` content against a tools-less request; era content shape per SMP-05). `Client.answer` validates nothing either. Gaps: `sampling-both-validate-message-content` (client + server rows).
3. **Every sampling failure is `-32603`.** The 2025-11-25 sampling error table assigns: user rejected → `-1`; tool result missing / tool results mixed with other content → `-32602`. mcpx produces neither: a decline becomes `errors.New("the sampling request was " + action)`, an expired wait becomes the raw `Await` error, and `Client.answer`'s handler wrap (`internal/mcpclient/modern.go` ~L296-303) flattens every handler error to `-32603`. An upstream cannot tell "the user said no" from "mcpx broke". Gap: `sampling-client-errors-user-rejected-and-tool-shape`.

### Already in place (not this design's work)

- Denial: broker decline/cancel of a sampling question works and is tested (`sampling-human-in-loop-can-deny`).
- The broker substrate is shared and sufficient: sampling questions are ordinary broker rows (`Mode: Sample`), listed/shown/answered by the existing `mcpx elicit` commands — the review gap is rendering + routing, not a missing store or UI.
- Typed-error precedent exists (`rpcError`/`codeInvalidParams` in mcpclient; fault classification in mcpserver); the broker already refuses null Sample answers with the question left open.
- Neighbours are distinct: #1753 gates which sampling *fields may cross* (its Phase 2 adds a request-shape `-32602` before the handler — this design's `-32602`s are content errors decided by validation, and compose with it); #1481 is schema validation of tool/elicitation payloads; #1675 is broker storage hygiene + review-first *elicitation*; the sampling rate limit is nix#257's.

### The design (decisions recorded in the doc)

- **One choke point, one validator.** All sampling validation lives in one helper used by the broker path (`sampleViaBroker`, in and out) — where legacy wire requests and modern `input_required` answers already converge — not copied into mcpclient/mcpserver separately.
- **Errors first (Phase 1).** Decline/cancel of a sampling answer → `-1` ("user rejected", action named). Expiry/no-answerer stays `-32603` with an explicit expired message — nobody chose, so it is not a rejection. Tool-shape violations → `-32602` (raised by Phase 2's checks through Phase 1's typed error). `Client.answer`'s wrap preserves a typed error's code.
- **Validation judges, doesn't repair (Phase 2).** Request side, on open: messages decode per era (content single before 2025-11-25, single-or-array from 2025-11-25); tool-result messages hold only `tool_result` blocks, each id paired with a preceding `tool_use` — violations get `-32602` *before* a question opens. Result side, on answer: result must carry `role` and `model` and era-legal content, and `toolUse`/`tool_use` is valid only against a tools-carrying request — and the silent `role`/`model` fill-in is **removed** (it manufactures fields the answerer never supplied). A bad answer is refused at the broker step with the question left open where it arrived through the broker. Model-hint mismatch is *not* a failure (hints are expressly ignorable).
- **Review on the existing surface (Phase 3).** No new UI: `mcpx elicit` renders a Sample question as sampling (server, system prompt, message list; full JSON on `show`; a real `CreateMessageResult` answer skeleton instead of `'{}'`). Review-before-delivery takes the honest form this architecture has — inspect/override while pending, results recorded and visible via `result` — stated plainly in CLI help; a genuine pre-delivery staging hold for agent answers is an open question in the doc, not a phase.

### Phases (sub-issues of this issue)

- **Phase 1** — typed sampling errors (`-1` rejection, `-32602` tool-shape type, expiry stays `-32603` labelled). Independent.
- **Phase 2** — message + result validation at the broker (request pairing/era shape; result-vs-request; fill-in removed). Independent in code; its `-32602` raising uses Phase 1's typed error (triage settles the seam if Phase 1 hasn't landed — not hard-gated).
- **Phase 3** — reviewable sampling in `mcpx elicit` + conformance-matrix/register truth-up + nix#256 completion evidence. Gated on Phase 2.

### Open questions (kept in the design doc, NOT filed)

- Genuine pre-delivery staging of agent sampling answers (a latency-contract change; only on evidence inspect-while-pending is insufficient).
- Era threading to the broker: if the upstream's era can't reach `sampleViaBroker` without new plumbing, union-shape acceptance vs plumbing for a deprecated feature is Phase 2 triage's recorded call.
- Whether a validated-bad request should also be recorded (count/log naming the server) for chronic-malformation visibility.
- Sampling as a client-hosted task (2025-11-25 only): untouched; would inherit the validator if it ever becomes real.

### Acceptance (design level)

- Phases 1–3 landed. A person can read a pending sampling request's actual messages in `mcpx elicit` and answer with a well-formed skeleton; a malformed request is refused `-32602` before any question opens; a malformed or request-mismatched result never reaches the upstream and missing `role`/`model` is refused, not filled; a decline reaches the upstream as `-1` and an expiry as `-32603` naming expiry.
- The seven scoped `#256` conformance gaps retired or explicitly recorded partial in the matrix; dezren39/nix#256 carries completion evidence against each acceptance bullet and is closed iff all are met.

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=design-architect state=filed at=2026-10-28T21:34:31Z -->

## Acceptance criteria

- Phases 1–3 (sub-issues of this design) have landed: typed sampling errors, broker message+result validation, and reviewable sampling in `mcpx elicit` with matrix/register truth-up.
- A declined sampling request reaches the upstream as `-1`; tool-shape violations as `-32602`; an expired wait as `-32603` naming expiry — no sampling failure is flattened into an unlabelled internal error.
- Sampling requests are validated before a broker question opens (era content shape; tool-result pairing per SMP-06) and results are validated against their request before relay (role/model present, era-legal content, toolUse only against a tools-carrying request); the silent `role`/`model` fill-in is gone.
- `mcpx elicit` renders a Sample question's server, system prompt and messages, and offers a real `CreateMessageResult` answer skeleton.
- The seven scoped dezren39/nix#256 conformance gaps are retired or explicitly recorded partial, and dezren39/nix#256 carries completion evidence against each of its acceptance bullets, closed if and only if all are met.

body:
## Problem

The envelope outbox (`pkgs/id/src/envelope_outbox.rs`) never forgets a finished delivery:

- `Outbox.entries` (`envelope_outbox.rs:121`) is a `BTreeMap<String, Entry>` holding every payload ever queued. The only removal anywhere in the module is the `Withdrawn` arm of `apply` (`envelope_outbox.rs:322`), and `withdraw` itself refuses any entry that has been attempted or finished — so a `Delivered` / `Refused` / `GaveUp` entry can never leave the map for the life of the process.
- The on-disk journal has the same shape: `commit` (`envelope_outbox.rs:278`) only appends one JSON line per queue/attempt/finish, and `open` (`envelope_outbox.rs:130`) only ever truncates a torn final line (`set_len`, :160). No compaction or pruning exists anywhere in the crate (verified by searching `src/` for the outbox file's writers: `commit`/`open` are the only ones).
- The cost is paid on every restart and every directory view: `open` replays and re-parses every line ever written, and `deliveries()` (`pkgs/id/src/directory_view.rs:432`) iterates all entries and clones a `DeliveryView` for each one the viewer may see. The view's own doc promises only envelopes "still in, or **recently left**, the outbox" (`directory_view.rs:86`) — the implementation has no recency bound at all, so a long-lived server's directory view grows linearly with its entire delivery history, forever.

This is a queue, not a journal of record: the directory log is where history lives. Nothing else in the crate reads finished outbox entries except `deliveries()` and `entry()` status lookups.

## Evidence (verified this run, main `8c6bdc09`)

- Line trace of `envelope_outbox.rs` (whole file): `apply` arms are `Queued`, `QueuedArtifact`, `Attempted`, `Finished`, `Withdrawn`; only `Withdrawn` removes, and `withdraw()` (same file) errors unless `attempts == 0 && finish.is_none()`.
- `grep` over `pkgs/id/src` for compaction/pruning of the outbox (`set_len`, `remove`, rewrite): the only hits are the torn-tail truncation in `open` and the `Withdrawn` removal above.
- `deliveries()` at `directory_view.rs:432-448` filters by viewer only — no age, count, or finish-time bound — while its field doc at :86 says "recently left".

Distinct from #1620 (torn-tail acceptance in the same file) and from #1713 (SaveRateLimiter map growth in `web/`) — this is the outbox store itself, its journal file, and its directory view.

## Why it matters

A world server runs for months and flushes its outbox on a timer (`world_hub.rs` `spawn_outbox_flush`). Every friend envelope and artifact push adds permanent in-memory entries (including full payload clones), permanent journal lines, restart replay time, and directory-view response size. Growth is slow but strictly unbounded and invisible until the file and the view are large.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A retention rule is pinned and documented at `Outbox` (e.g. finished entries kept for a bounded age or bounded count, still long enough for `deliveries()` to honestly show "recently left" ones).
- [ ] Finished entries past the bound are dropped from the in-memory map, and the journal is compacted (rewritten without the dropped history) at a safe point, e.g. on `open` after replay.
- [ ] `deliveries()` output is bounded by the same rule; a test with an old finished entry and a recent finished entry shows only the recent one.
- [ ] Existing outbox tests keep passing (`envelope_outbox` + `envelope_net` flush tests), including torn-tail handling (#1620's area must not regress: compaction must keep the crash-torn-tail rule working).
- [ ] A restart test: after compaction, reopening the file yields the same due/pending set as before.

body:
## Bug: a heading containing a hard break is corrupted on save — break becomes a literal backslash and the rest of the heading splits into a new paragraph

Found in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` (the markdown ⇄ ProseMirror codec), verified this run on main `95bfedb4` with a standalone probe crate carrying a verbatim copy of `src/web/markdown.rs` (comrak 0.56; probe logs in the goal workspace `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-27-creator-a2/out3.log` cases `setext-hardbreak-backslash` / `setext-hardbreak-spaces`, PM-side case `heading-hardbreak` in `out2.log`).

### Reproduction (pure markdown in, no editor tricks needed)

A setext heading is a multi-line paragraph, so it can contain a hard break:

```markdown
Title\
more here
=====
```

(or the same with two trailing spaces after `Title` instead of the backslash.)

1. Parse direction: `markdown_to_prosemirror` produces one heading node whose inline content is `text "Title"`, `hard_break`, `text "more here"` — the parse-side `NodeValue::LineBreak` arm (`markdown.rs:295`) emits `hard_break` regardless of the containing block, and placement validation (`markdown.rs:979`: `"paragraph" | "heading" => child == Placement::Inline`) accepts it, since `hard_break` is inline.
2. Save direction: the `hard_break` arm (`markdown.rs:1385`) builds a comrak `NodeValue::LineBreak` inside the `Heading` node built at `markdown.rs:1141`, and `format_commonmark` renders it as a backslash + newline *inside* the ATX heading line:

   ```
   # Title\
   more here
   ```

3. Re-parsing that saved file yields a **different document**: a heading whose text is `Title\` (a literal backslash character has been added to the user's text) followed by a new plain paragraph `more here`. The heading the user had is split in two and gains a stray `\`.

The same PM doc built directly in the editor (e.g. convert a paragraph containing a hard break into a heading — `heading` in `richSchema` is `inline*` content, `pkgs/id/web/src/editor.ts:46`) corrupts identically.

### Why this is a codec bug, not just a renderer quirk

A direct comrak parse → `format_commonmark` control renders the same bytes (probe `out4.log`, DIRECT cases) — comrak's renderer cannot spell a line break inside an ATX heading either. But the codec's contract is ProseMirror fidelity (cf. #1031, #1370), and here the **PM document itself** changes across one open → save cycle. The codec already solves exactly this shape of problem for table cells: #1017's `append_table_cell_child` (`markdown.rs:~1560`) degrades a hard/soft break to a single space because "a table cell is single-line content in markdown". A heading is single-line content in markdown for the same reason, and gets no such degradation.

### Suggested fix direction (triage decides)

Degrade `LineBreak` children of a `Heading` to a space in the save direction (mirroring #1017's table-cell handling), or equivalently normalize them in the parse direction, so a heading with a hard break saves as `# Title more here` and re-opens as the same single heading. Rejecting with a `ConversionError` would be worse than the space degradation (it would make the whole document unsavable).

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Title\` + newline + `more here` + `=====` (and the two-trailing-spaces variant) round-trips to a single heading containing `Title more here` (or an equivalent single-line spelling) — no literal backslash added, no paragraph split.
- [ ] A hand-built PM heading containing a `hard_break` saves without corrupting on re-parse; output is a fixpoint.
- [ ] Hard breaks in paragraphs still save as hard breaks (existing behaviour unchanged).
- [ ] Regression test in `web::markdown` tests next to the #1017 table-cell tests; existing codec tests still pass.

## Roadmap: vector memory for OpenClaw — and possibly the fleet

Drew approved enabling **memory-lancedb** for the laptop OpenClaw (2026-10-26), and raised the open design question this issue tracks: does vector memory stay an OpenClaw-only store, or do we eventually incorporate our own vector store as an additional data source the agent can use more broadly?

### Phase 1 (do now, small)
- Enable the `memory-lancedb` runtime plugin in `plugins.slots.memory` for the laptop gateway, with a local embedding endpoint (the fleet already runs local llama.cpp embedding servers for OpenCode; check for a stable endpoint or stand one up — avoid per-instance dynamic ports).
- Verify the official npm package name before wiring (two candidates surfaced in research: `@openclaw/memory-lancedb` vs a third-party scope; the nix-openclaw catalog entry `memoryLancedb` is the authority for what the module builds).
- Confirm recall quality improves over the current degraded state (gateway logs vector-recall fallback warnings today).

### Phase 2 (decide later, this issue)
- Should OpenCode sessions, OpenChamber, and other fleet agents share one vector store (e.g. the same LanceDB, or a served store) instead of each keeping their own?
- Data sources worth indexing beyond chat memory: the zettelkasten/Emanote notes, repo docs, prior research reports.
- Access pattern: MCP server vs per-tool native stores.

### Notes
- Oh My OpenClaw's "Graphiti memory" was reviewed and not adopted (no such config exists in its reference; its persona/model-routing defaults also clash with fleet quota discipline). Cherry-picks only.
- Keep phase 1 reversible: memory slot swap is one config line.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Phase 1: memory-lancedb is enabled for the laptop OpenClaw gateway (plugins.slots.memory) using the verified official package (the nix-openclaw catalog entry memoryLancedb is the authority) and a stable local embedding endpoint — no per-instance dynamic ports. *(Verified 2026-11-11, task 11932: `home/openclaw/default.nix` — `slots.memory = "memory-lancedb"`, dedicated `openclaw-embedding` service on fixed loopback port 18791; PR #4451, PR #6151.)*

- [x] The fleet question is answered on this issue with a recorded decision: OpenClaw-only store, or a fleet vector store as an additional agent data source — with the follow-up implementation issue filed if the fleet option is chosen. *(Decision recorded 2026-11-11, task 11932: Drew — "Integrate into Atlas" (ledger `fleet-vector-store-1300`, corrected 2026-11-10). Follow-up implementation issue: #8567.)*

Today Sonnet and Opus enter the pools ONLY through Antigravity's Claude quota (sonnet-plan and opus-plan each have a single antigravity-ls leaf). Antigravity's quota is a flexible multi-model resource — spending it on Claude is its least differentiated use. The Claude plan, by contrast, can only ever buy Claude models, and the claude-code proxy provider is currently wired for Haiku 5.5 only (full thinking-budget variant ladder).

Evaluate:
1. Whether the Claude Code CLI proxy can serve claude-sonnet-5-5 / claude-opus-5-5 (model availability through the subscription, rate/usage accounting).

3. If no: record why in the provider-quota registry and close.

Why it matters: pool economics (Drew, 2026-10-26) — each plan's quota is best spent on what only it can buy; Claude caution applies to burning shared/flexible quotas on Claude when a Claude-only quota sits Haiku-only.

# Network fabric

## Purpose
A documented, declarative network design sized for the cluster: fast east-west between nodes, scarce egress managed deliberately.

## Scope
Switching and addressing plan replacing the torn-down v1.9 test layout (doc/talos-addresses.md is historical only). Confirm the exact high-speed NIC spec on core machines and the switch gear between them (needed to sanity-check LINSTOR/DRBD replication traffic). Management network for BMC/KVM. Edge: 2 Gbps symmetric Brightspeed fiber; egress strategy (tunnels to Cloudflare/Turso/Tailscale, compression) documented as design constraints. Existing notes: doc/network-topology.md, doc/inventory/routing-and-switching.md.

## Execution mode
Hybrid: design and config online; cabling, switch install, and link verification physical.

## Dependencies
Depends on epic 1 (NIC inventory). Gates epic 6 bootstrap.

## Acceptance
Addressing + VLAN/segmentation plan committed; NIC/switch facts verified against hardware; management network reachable for every first-node machine.

## Structure

Part of the basement cluster program. Project home: `planning/roadmaps/basement-cluster.md` in this repo. body:
## Bug

In the id web editor's markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), **link reference definitions that are not used by a link in the document are silently deleted on save**:

```markdown
body text

[unused]: https://example.com
```

loads and saves as just:

```markdown
body text
```

The extreme case is total: a document consisting only of reference definitions (a shared "link library" page, or a draft whose links are added later)

```markdown
[a]: https://a.com
[b]: https://b.com
```

loads as an empty document and saves as an **empty file**.

Definitions that *are* used survive in substance — full (`[one][r]`), collapsed (`[text][]`) and shortcut (`[ref]`) references all round-trip, with the reference inlined as `[text](url)` and the definition consumed. So the loss is specifically: any definition whose label no link in the current document references.

## Verified repro (this run, main 3b9d1592)

Standalone verbatim-codec probe (evidence log: goal `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1415/out4.log`):

- `unused-ref-def`: `"body text\n\n[unused]: https://example.com\n"` → PM is a single paragraph `body text` (the definition appears nowhere) → save returns `"body text\n"`.
- `ref-def-only-doc`: `"[a]: https://a.com\n[b]: https://b.com\n"` → PM is the empty-document placeholder paragraph → save returns `""` (empty file).
- Controls (same log): `shortcut-ref`, `collapsed-ref`, `multi-ref-same` — used definitions round-trip correctly as inlined links.

## Why it happens / why it matters

The ProseMirror schema the codec targets has no node for a reference definition, and comrak resolves definitions during parsing without surfacing unused ones as AST nodes — so the parse direction has nowhere to put them and they vanish before the editor ever sees the document. Keeping a block of reference definitions at the foot of a note for later use is a standard markdown authoring pattern; opening such a file in the id web editor and saving (even with no edit) destroys that block with no warning. Same silent-loss-on-save family as #996 (empty links), in a distinct mechanism.

## Suggested direction (triage to decide)

The fix needs a deliberate design choice, e.g.: (a) preserve unused definitions verbatim — the parse direction would need a source pre-scan for reference definitions, diff them against the labels comrak actually consumed, and carry the leftovers (e.g. as a trailing raw block the editor displays but does not eat); (b) represent definitions in the PM doc (a dedicated node) — cleaner but touches the editor schema; or (c) if neither is acceptable, document the limitation where the codec's schema is described (module doc comment at the top of markdown.rs) so the loss is at least a known, stated behaviour instead of a silent one. Doing nothing silently is the only unacceptable outcome.

## Acceptance criteria

- A document with an unused reference definition no longer loses it silently on a load/save round trip — either the definition survives (verbatim or in an equivalent reference form), or the limitation is explicitly documented in the codec module docs and this issue is closed citing that documentation.
- Used references (full, collapsed, shortcut, multiple links sharing one definition) keep round-tripping exactly as today.
- A definitions-only document does not save as an empty file under the chosen fix (or is covered by the documented limitation).
- Existing `web::markdown` tests pass.

body:
## Bug

In the id web editor's markdown ↔ ProseMirror codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), saving a document whose **blockquote starts with a non-paragraph block** (a fenced code block, a table, or a thematic break) inserts **two stray blank lines** — `> ` lines — at the top of the quote, before that first block:

Input:

```markdown
> ```rust
> let x = 1;
> ```
```

After one load/save round trip:

```markdown
> 
> 
> ```rust
> let x = 1;
> ```
```

The ProseMirror document is correct throughout (the blockquote contains exactly one `code_block`, no empty paragraphs) and the output is a stable fixpoint — the two lines appear on the first save and stay. But every affected file gets polluted on save, the quote renders with a gap at the top in other renderers, and the diff noise obscures real edits.

## Verified repro (this run, main 3b9d1592)

Standalone verbatim-codec probe crate (evidence log: goal `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-1415/out3.log`, probe source is current `markdown.rs` verbatim):

- `markdown_to_prosemirror("> ```rust\n> let x = 1;\n> ```\n")` → `{"type":"blockquote","content":[{"type":"code_block","attrs":{"params":"rust"}, …}]}` — correct, no empty paragraphs.
- `prosemirror_to_markdown` of that document → `"> \n> \n> ```rust\n> let x = 1;\n> ```\n"` — two leading blank quote lines.
- Same pattern for a table as first block (`> | a |…` → two leading `> ` lines) and a thematic break first (`> ---\n> text` → two leading `> ` lines, plus the normal separator before `text`).
- Controls that save cleanly: blockquote starting with a paragraph, a heading, or a list; a blockquote where the same code block is *not* first (`> intro` + fence) saves with exactly the one normal separator line.
- Control isolating the layer: comrak's own parse → `format_commonmark` render of the original input produces the same two blank lines, so the quirk is in the comrak CommonMark renderer behaviour the codec's save direction relies on (`prosemirror_to_markdown`, markdown.rs:868-874, serializes a hand-built AST with `format_commonmark`) — the codec inherits it on every save even though its own AST is correct.

Not #954: that issue is no-info code blocks being rewritten as indented blocks (document-level). This one is about leading blank lines inside a blockquote, affects info-string fences, tables and thematic breaks, and also appears when the block is not first in the file but first in the quote.

## Why it matters

Silent file pollution on save, in the same codec family as #982/#954/#981 but a distinct mechanism: quoted code snippets, quoted tables and quoted rules are common in notes/docs, and the first save of any such file rewrites its top-of-quote for no reason.

## Suggested fix

In the save direction, stop the two spurious separator lines from reaching the file — e.g. investigate whether the hand-built AST is missing something the renderer keys on for a blockquote's first child (in which case fix `json_to_ast`'s `blockquote`/`code_block` construction), or post-process the serialized output to collapse a blockquote's leading blank `> ` lines (only at quote start — blank separators *between* blocks in a quote are required and must be kept, cf. the `> intro` + fence control). If the behaviour turns out to be unfixable without forking the renderer, record that and close with the rationale rather than leaving it untracked.

## Acceptance criteria

- Round-trip tests: blockquote starting with (a) a fenced code block with an info string, (b) a table, (c) a thematic break followed by text — each saves byte-identical to its input (no leading `> ` lines).
- Regression controls unchanged: blockquote starting with paragraph/heading/list, and paragraph-then-fence inside a quote (exactly one separator blank line), still round-trip as today.
- Existing `web::markdown` tests pass.

body:
## Problem

In the id web editor's markdown codec (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs`), a fenced code block **without an info string** is rewritten as an indented (4-space) code block on save. The user's chosen fence form is destroyed on every open→save, even when nothing else changed. An empty fenced block additionally gains a spurious blank line.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Round-trip probe on main `a2eef6f7` (standalone crate compiling the verbatim `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` against comrak 0.56.0 + serde_json; full logs in the goal's `hidden_files/probe-2026-10-26-0312/out.log` and `out3.log`):

| Input | Saved output |
|---|---|
| ` ``` ` block with blank lines, no info (`` ```\nline1\n\n\nline2\n``` ``) | indented block: `    line1\n    \n    \n    line2` |
| ` ```` ` block containing a ``` line (no info) | indented block: `    ```\n    inner` |
| fenced block (no info) inside a list item | rewritten to a 6-space indented block inside the item |
| fenced block (no info) inside a blockquote | rewritten to indented form (`>     code line`) |
| empty fenced block (` ```\n``` `) | ` ```\n\n``` ` — a blank content line appears |
| ` ```rust ` block with blanks (control, has info) | stays fenced, unchanged ✓ |

The rewritten forms are currently stable fixpoints (a second round-trip does not degrade them further), so this is a fidelity/diff-noise bug rather than progressive corruption — but the rewrite is unconditional: merely opening and saving a note reformats every info-less fenced block in it.

## Root cause (to confirm in triage)

`json_to_ast` builds every `code_block` as `fenced: true, fence_length: 3` (`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:885-890`), yet comrak's `format_commonmark` renderer still emits the indented form for these blocks — the cases above suggest it does so whenever there is no info string (the `rust`-info control stays fenced). Separately, the literal is always built as `format!("{content}\n")` (:890), so an empty block's literal is a single `"\n"`, which renders as the spurious blank line. The existing round-trip test (`test_roundtrip_code_block`) only covers an info-carrying block, so neither behavior is pinned.

## Why it matters

- Silent reformatting on save pollutes diffs in synced/vault notes and erodes trust in the editor's other (correct) round-trips.
- Indented code is context-fragile once the user edits the saved file by hand or in another tool: it cannot interrupt a paragraph, is invisible as a block, and is the form most likely to be mangled by other markdown tooling.
- Info-less fences are the common case for plain shell/output snippets.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fenced code block without an info string round-trips open→save still fenced (byte-identical modulo the file's trailing newline), including blocks with blank lines, blocks containing ``` lines, and blocks nested in list items and blockquotes.
- An empty fenced block round-trips with no spurious blank line added.
- Info-carrying blocks and all existing codec tests are unchanged; new unit tests in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` cover the info-less and empty cases.
- Saved output is a stable fixpoint on a second round-trip.

body:
## Finding

The aggregator dashboard's new comment API accepts a **self-asserted author identity**: `validateAuthor` checks only the shape (`kind` is `drew`/`muse`/`agent`, non-empty `id`/`label`), never that the identity exists in the session registry — even though PR #920's body advertises "Unambiguous authorship: drew / muse / agent identities **from the registry**". Any client that can reach the server can post a comment as Drew, and downstream consumers act on that attribution.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #920 (dashboard slice 3, #906), 2026-10-25; verified on current main (`92d0c6ee`).

## Evidence

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts:41-55` — `validateAuthor(a)`: returns an author for any object with `kind ∈ {drew, muse, agent}` and non-empty string `id`/`label` (truncated to 120 chars). No registry lookup, no credential, no session binding.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:131-136` — `POST /api/comments` stores whatever `validateNewComment` returns; the registry (`identitiesFromRecords`, used to build the comment *form* options in `commentFormOpts`) is never consulted on the write path.
- The package's own tests prove the point: `pm-stack/aggregator/test/slice3.test.ts` posts with a bare literal `const author = { kind: "drew", id: "drew", label: "Drew" }` and it is accepted.
- Why the attribution is load-bearing (comments.ts header, lines 12-25): kind `message` comments are "the orchestrator's queue input" — triaged and acted on as instructions; kind `github` comments are posted to GitHub by a fleet poster with the attribution line "— posted by Drew via the PM dashboard". A forged `drew` author therefore flows into agent instructions and into GitHub comments carrying Drew's name.
- The trust-model comment (comments.ts:9-11) notes the server binds loopback + tailnet and writes are unauthenticated "like every other fleet-internal surface" — but other surfaces do not mint *Drew-attributed instructions and GitHub posts*. Agent sessions themselves run on the tailnet, so a confused or compromised agent (not just a person) can impersonate Drew to the orchestrator.

## Why it matters

This fleet treats Drew's word as the highest authority. A comment box that lets any tailnet client speak *as Drew* — into the orchestrator's input queue and onto GitHub under his name — is an authority-confusion surface that contradicts the PR's stated design ("identities from the registry", "unambiguous authorship").

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Triage verdict on the intended trust boundary: either (a) the write path validates the author against the registry / a per-identity credential, so `kind: "drew"` cannot be self-asserted by an arbitrary client, or (b) the design is consciously accepted and the code/PR claims are corrected (comments.ts header and docs stop claiming registry-backed unambiguous authorship, and github-kind posts are not attributed to Drew unless the author was verified).
- [ ] If (a): a test posts an unregistered/forged `drew` author and is rejected, while registry identities still post.
- [ ] If (b): the orchestrator's consumption contract in comments.ts documents that message-kind comments are unauthenticated input, not Drew instructions.

— filed by the pr-diff-review job (PR #920); triage via the repo-health queue pilot.

body:
`handled_requests` lives in memory only (`pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:208`) and starts empty after a reopen. So every capability request still listed in the guest's `wants` runs again on the first pass after a restart. With no acting participant, it runs as permitted (`actor_permits`). For a non-idempotent provider (`chat.say` today; F12.5 `kv`, `http.fetch` and `notify`), a restart can repeat a side effect with world authority. The comment near `actor.rs:400` calls delivery at-least-once, but the restart case is not documented or tested.

Proposed: write down the restart semantics and add a test. Consider journaling handled request ids, or refusing un-attributed re-execution after a reopen. The F13.7 design refuses with `actor_denied`, reason `restarted`.

Found while writing the F13.7 design (#789).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The restart semantics for capability requests still listed in a guest's `wants` after a world reopen are written down in the code/docs
- [ ] A test covers the reopen case: a non-idempotent request (e.g. `chat.say`) is not silently re-executed unattributed, or its at-least-once re-execution is explicitly asserted as intended
- [ ] If the chosen semantics refuse re-execution, the refusal uses the documented code (`actor_denied`, reason `restarted`, per the F13.7 design)
