body:
`pkgs/mcpx` (at 6081a86a) builds and runs on aarch64-darwin, but its daemon handover features do not work there, and the test suite fails without exclusions. Found while vendoring it verbatim into the nix-darwin config (dezren39 `~/.config/nix`, `pkgs/mcpx`), where it runs as a launchd agent.

## What fails on darwin

1. **`internal/daemon/takeover_test.go` does not compile**: `syscall.SOCK_CLOEXEC` is Linux-only (the `unixPair` helper, line 24). Because `handoff_conns_test.go` uses `unixPair`, the whole `internal/daemon` test package fails to build.
2. **Every takeover/upgrade/handoff test fails at runtime** (`takeover: EOF`, or the successor never takes over), across `internal/daemon`, `internal/e2e`, `internal/mcpclient` and `internal/pool`:
   - daemon: TestAnIdleConnectionSurvivesATakeoverInProcess, TestACallInFlightAtTheHandoverIsAnsweredByTheOldDaemon, TestKeepAliveCallersLoseNoCallsAcrossATakeover, TestCallsIssuedDuringATakeoverNeverFail, TestAClientLeaseSurvivesADaemonTakeover, TestHandoffRecordsTheIdentityAPoolWasMadeWith, TestRegistryHandoffKeepsTheChildAcrossTheSuccessor, TestRegistryHandoffThatIsNotCommittedRestoresTheChild
   - e2e: TestAnIdleKeepAliveConnectionSurvivesATakeover, TestACallInFlightAtATakeoverIsAnsweredAndItsConnectionMovesOn, TestKeepAliveCallersLoseNoCallsAcrossARealTakeover, TestTakeoverKeepsTheChildAndTheListener, TestTakeoverRestartsAChangedServerAndKeepsTheRest, TestTakeoverLosesNoCallsWhileAClientKeepsCalling, TestClientLeaseSurvivesDaemonTakeover, TestUpgradeKeepsTheChildAndHandsMainPIDToTheSuccessor
   - mcpclient: TestDetachedChildKeepsItsPipesAndAdoptionResumesThem, TestHandoffDoesNotSplitAFrameAcrossTheTwoProcesses, TestClientHandoffCommitsOnlyWhenActivated
   - pool: TestDetachRefusesWhileACallIsInFlight
3. **`TestExecChangeRestartsThatPoolAndNoOther`** passes functionally (the pool restarts) but verifies the new executable via `/proc/<pid>/exe`, which darwin lacks.

Everything else (adapter, api, cli, config, conformance, catalog, preflight, secrets, scripting, ...) passes on darwin.

## Why it matters beyond tests

`mcpx upgrade` relies on the successor staying in the unit's cgroup and claiming `MAINPID` via `NOTIFY_SOCKET`. launchd has neither, so on macOS the only safe deploy is a plain restart (which ends every MCP child). The nix-darwin config does that today and skips the tests above (`flake.nix`, `mcpxDarwinSkip`).

## Asks

- Make the test helpers portable (no `SOCK_CLOEXEC`; `os.Executable`/`proc_pidpath` instead of `/proc/<pid>/exe`), or build-tag the Linux-only tests.
- Decide whether takeover is supported on darwin at all. If yes, find what breaks it (fd passing over the unix socket looks like the common factor); if not, have `mcpx upgrade` refuse cleanly on darwin and document a launchd story (e.g. `launchctl kickstart -k` with children adopted on restart).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `internal/daemon` test package compiles on aarch64-darwin (no unguarded Linux-only constants such as `syscall.SOCK_CLOEXEC` in test helpers, or darwin equivalents/build tags in their place)
- [ ] Takeover/upgrade/handoff tests on darwin either pass, or the unsupported feature returns an explicit error and the tests skip with a stated reason — no bare `takeover: EOF` failures
- [ ] The same suites still pass on Linux with no regressions
- [ ] The fix is carried to the mcpx copy dezren39/nix consumes (cross-repo set rule — tracked from this issue, no duplicate filing)

title: fix(id/web): SaveRateLimiter::acquire is not atomic — a save completing between its check and its reservation re-opens the cooldown (PR #4193 follow-up)

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4193 (merged, commit 06ea8c8328) fixed the #2466 check/record race by adding `SaveRateLimiter::acquire`, but the acquire path itself is not atomic, and its design note claims it is:

- The design doc merged in the same PR (`doc/2026-11-02T07-00-00Z_design_save_reservations/2026-11-02T07-00-00Z_design_save_reservations.md`, decision 1) says `acquire` "combines the existing cooldown check with an in-flight reservation, **taken atomically** under the in-flight lock".
- The code — unchanged on current main at `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/lib.rs:156-166` (the file moved in the crate split; line numbers are current main) — does:

```rust
pub async fn acquire(&self, name: &str) -> Result<SavePermit, Duration> {
    self.check(name).await?;                       // (1) cooldown check, tokio mutex on last_save
    let mut flight = self.in_flight.lock()          // (2) reservation, a *different* std mutex
        .unwrap_or_else(|poisoned| poisoned.into_inner());
    if !flight.insert(name.to_owned()) { return Err(self.cooldown); }
    ...
}
```

`check` (1) and the reservation insert (2) are separated by an await on a different lock, so on the multi-threaded tokio runtime the web server runs on, this interleaving is possible:

1. Save A holds the permit and is finishing: `SavePermit::complete()` calls `record()` (writes `last_save[name] = now`), then Drop removes `name` from `in_flight`.
2. Save B calls `acquire(name)` and its `check` reads `last_save` *before* A's `record()` lands — it passes.
3. B's insert runs *after* A's Drop removed the name — it succeeds.

B is admitted inside the cooldown A just recorded. This does **not** recreate the original #2466 overlap (B can only insert after A released the reservation, i.e. after A finished, so saves never run concurrently) — what it re-opens is the cooldown guarantee that `acquire` exists to enforce atomically: a client retrying at exactly the completion moment bypasses the 5 s rate limit the 429 contract promises.

Second, smaller defect in the same lifecycle: `SavePermit::drop` (current main, `lib.rs:206-208`) releases the reservation with `if let Ok(mut flight) = ...lock()`, while `acquire` explicitly recovers a poisoned lock with `into_inner()`. If the `in_flight` mutex is ever poisoned, Drop silently leaves the name in the set, and every later `acquire` (which recovers the guard and sees the name still present) refuses that filename forever — a permanently wedged save for that file, with no error anywhere.

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4193 (merge commit 06ea8c8328, verified an ancestor of current main ed926a977e63 — compare `behind_by=0`)
- Source PR's parent issue: #2466 (CLOSED)
- Current main: `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/lib.rs` — `acquire` at line 156 (`self.check(name).await?` at 157, in-flight lock at ~159-161), `complete` at ~199-204 (`record` then Drop release), `Drop for SavePermit` at line 206 (`if let Ok` at 207). Read twice this run (code search + raw contents), identical.
- Dedupe (2026-11-13): issue searches for `SaveRateLimiter acquire`, `save limiter in-flight`, `acquire re-check cooldown`, `in_flight poisoned save` returned only PR #4193 / issue #2466 themselves — no open or closed issue covers this residual.

## Why it matters

The whole point of #4193 over the old check/record split was that the cooldown + in-flight decision is one atomic step. As merged (and still on main) it is two steps with a completion window between them, so the rate-limit guarantee has a race at exactly the busiest moment (a save just completed, a retry already waiting). The poisoned-Drop asymmetry is a latent permanent wedge for a filename if the lock is ever poisoned — and `acquire`'s own poison recovery shows poisoning was contemplated on one path but not the other.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `acquire` re-validates the cooldown after taking the in-flight reservation (or otherwise makes check + reserve atomic with respect to `record` + release), so a save that records while another `acquire` is between check and insert causes that acquire to be refused with the cooldown error, and the refused acquire leaves no reservation behind.
- [ ] A deterministic regression test orchestrates the completion-during-acquire interleaving (not a sleep/timing loop) and fails before the fix / passes after; the existing limiter tests (refuses second in-flight, concurrent acquires admit exactly one, dropped permit releases without recording, completed permit records) still pass.
- [ ] `SavePermit::drop` recovers a poisoned `in_flight` lock the same way `acquire` does (`into_inner`), with a test or a reasoned note if a poison test is impractical.
- [ ] The design doc's "taken atomically" wording matches the implementation after the fix.

## Shadow note

Stage A shadow verdicts are closed (window ended 2026-11-13, summary on #2313), so no shadow verdict section is attached to this filing.

body:
## Finding

PR #4154 added a non-trivial client-side behavior layer to the aggregator /aa page — viewBox zoom math with focal-point anchoring, pan clamping, per-chart zoom state that must survive (or deliberately drop across) redraws, deferred pointer capture so plain clicks still select points, and a 400 ms click-suppression window after a pan — but its tests never execute any of that behavior. The two tests the PR added (still the only coverage on current main) assert that the rendered HTML *contains strings* (`function enhanceCharts()`, `data-zbound`, `setPointerCapture(drag.id)`, …) and that the emitted script parses. A regression that breaks the zoom math, the clamping, or the click suppression — while keeping those strings present — passes the suite unchanged.

## Evidence

- PR: #4154 https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4154 (MERGED, head `88920b4a06c600707672877366023b04805ca35e`, merge `fddd4ad68c21c1465fe7b86529dca6fa424f02f2`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare behind=0)
- Behavior under test, on main `ef16105eebb6d865960cde9f6bc1094b355000ee`, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts`: `clampChartView` :4479, `zoomChart` :4484 (16× zoom floor, aspect-preserving resize, focal anchoring, zoom-out-to-base clearing state), `panChart` :4499, `resetChart` :4509, click suppression via `data-zsuppress` :4587-4592.
- Only coverage, `pm-stack/aggregator/test/aa.test.ts:867` (`describe("aa chart expand + zoom/pan (#3298)")`): two tests, both `toContain` string assertions over `renderAa(...)` output plus a `new Function(script)` parse check. No DOM, no invocation of `zoomChart`/`panChart`/`clampChartView`, no assertion on any resulting `viewBox`.
- This is not a hypothetical style point: the PR's own history shows this layer needed three Codex-driven behavior fixes (deferred pointer capture, per-chart wrapper for band scatters, re-enhancement after recommendation-only redraws) — all behavior, all still guarded only by the presence of a string.
- Dedupe: all-state searches for `zoom/pan` and `chart zoom test` returned only #3298 (the feature request, CLOSED by #4154), #4154 itself, and unrelated CI-failure issues — no test-coverage issue exists.

## Why it matters

The /aa explorer is the AA comparison surface Drew reads; zoom/pan is now the primary way to inspect dense frontier charts. The zoom/pan state machine is exactly the kind of code that regresses silently (a redraw resetting `applied`, an aspect change on the scores chart, a clamp inversion when a view is taller than wide) — and the current tests would stay green through every one of those regressions, giving false confidence in the page's most interactive code.

## Acceptance criteria

- Executable tests drive the enhancer's pure behavior: at minimum `zoomChart` focal anchoring and the 16× floor, zoom-out-to-base clearing `cur`, `panChart` clamping at the base viewBox edges, and `resetChart` restoring the base viewBox — asserting the resulting `viewBox` values, not string presence.
- The click-suppression contract is pinned by a test: a click within the suppression window after a moved drag is swallowed; an ordinary click without a drag still reaches point selection.
- Tests run under the aggregator's existing `bun test` suite (a minimal DOM stub or extracting the pure viewBox helpers for direct import are both acceptable); the existing string-presence tests may stay but no longer count as the behavior coverage.

body:
## Finding

PR #4151 added per-record load validation to the aggregator's `ActionsStore` and `CommentsStore`, but the validators are purely per-record: a store file carrying **two individually valid rows with the same `id`** loads silently — no quarantine, no diagnostics — and both rows stay in the active store. Every id-addressed consumer then sees only the first row (`find`), while counts include both. This is the same cross-row class the sibling `ViewsStore` was later found to have and had fixed as its own issue (#4301, fixed by PR #4536's `crossRowInvariantError`); the two stores #4151 touched never got the cross-row check.

## Evidence

- PR: #4151 https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4151 (MERGED, head `46c5e6d330568c6400d094710d93884c8afda3f4`, merge `15af52b2dbbb044a30a4ffd99cd8f5975799bef0`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare behind=0)
- Verified on main `ef16105eebb6d865960cde9f6bc1094b355000ee`:
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/comments.ts`: `commentRecordProblem` at :88 validates one record at a time; validated rows are assigned wholesale at :294 with no cross-row pass. `markGithubResult` at :397-399 resolves an id with `this.comments.find((x) => x.id === id)` — first match only.
  - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts`: `actionRecordProblem` at :141, wholesale assignment at :653; `markResultTransition` at :791-796 likewise uses `find`.
  - Precedent in the same codebase: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/views.ts:115` `crossRowInvariantError` rejects duplicate view ids (plus duplicate per-owner names and second defaults) on load.
- Probe (current-main sources of both stores, run under bun in the review scratch dir): a comments file with two valid rows sharing id `c-dup` loaded **2** rows, `counts()` reported 2 for the object, and no `.corrupt-*` archive or diagnostics file was created; an actions file with two valid rows sharing id `a-dup` loaded **2** rows, with `pendingCounts()` counting the `new` copy while the `applied` copy is unreachable by id.
- Dedupe: all-state searches for `duplicate id aggregator`, `cross-row store`, and `duplicate actions store id` returned only the views-specific #4301 (CLOSED) and its fix #4536 — no issue covers the actions/comments stores.

## Why it matters

These files are the dashboard's audit history. #4151's whole point was that a malformed row must not silently distort the store: it archives the original bytes and rewrites only validated rows. A duplicate id is a malformed *store* that survives that treatment untouched — one of the two records becomes permanently shadowed for every id-addressed operation (result marking, triage transitions) while still inflating per-object counts, and the next persist rewrites both rows as if nothing were wrong, so the corruption is preserved rather than quarantined.

## Acceptance criteria

- Loading an actions or comments file whose rows contain a duplicate `id` follows the #4151 contract: the original bytes are archived with a diagnostics entry naming the duplicate row index/id, and the active store does not retain two rows under one id (whole-file quarantine or later-row rejection — either is acceptable if it matches the views precedent's spirit and is tested).
- Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/store-corrupt.test.ts` cover duplicate-id files for **both** stores, alongside the existing per-record malformed cases.
- Valid files (unique ids) load exactly as today, including legacy rows without optional fields.

title: fix(id): PresenceTable capacity eviction defeats the replay watermark — future-stamped heartbeat can be replayed back to life past receipt-based expiry

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4160's `PresenceTable` capacity eviction selects its victim by **effective stamp** only. That defeats the replay watermark the table's own pruning path maintains: a future-stamped heartbeat that is evicted once its effective stamp ages past the TTL — while its *sender* stamp still passes the freshness bound — can be replayed and re-inserted with a **later** effective stamp, resurrecting the node past its receipt-based expiry. `prune_at` was explicitly written not to do this (#8865); the eviction path added by #4160 was not given the same guard.

Worked timeline (current main, `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/chat_presence.rs`; `PRESENCE_TTL_SECS = 75` at :110, `MAX_FUTURE_SKEW_SECS = 10` at :124):

1. At receipt time `T`, a heartbeat stamped `T+10` (inside the skew allowance) is accepted; its effective stamp is clamped to `T` (:395).
2. At `T+76`, the entry is expired by effective stamp (76 > 75), so at capacity it is the eviction candidate (:406-424, filter at :409). Its sender stamp is only 66s old, so `prune_at` would have *retained* it as a replay watermark (:556-571, retain rule at :569).
3. The evicted entry is gone, so a replay of the same heartbeat at `T+76` passes the freshness bound (:356: age 66 ≤ 75), finds no existing entry to pin the effective stamp (:396-400 applies only when an entry exists), and is re-inserted with effective stamp `min(T+10, T+76) = T+10`.
4. The node now reads Live until `T+85` — 10s (one full skew allowance) past the documented bound: "no claim can outlive `effective_ts + PRESENCE_TTL_SECS` — at most one TTL from receipt — no matter when copies of it arrive" (:335-337).

## Evidence

- PR: #4160 https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4160 (MERGED, head `6b99c3a175d2eb603efd73fdf7bbbeda3e47efbf`, merge `ccdfacd24537f74b851e6ecef978bb9c945d728c`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare behind=0)
- Verified on main `ef16105eebb6d865960cde9f6bc1094b355000ee`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/chat_presence.rs`: eviction filter :406-424 (effective stamp only); `prune_at` watermark rationale :556-571; freshness bound :356-360; effective-stamp pinning for existing entries :395-400; invariant statement :335-337.
- #4160's own tests (`node_count_bound_evicts_oldest_expired_entry_at_capacity`, now at :1230) use a past-stamped victim (age 80 at eviction) whose replay would fail the freshness bound anyway — the future-stamped victim case is not covered.
- Dedupe: all-state searches for `PresenceTable eviction`, `presence eviction replay`, and `PresenceTable` returned only #4004 (the bound request, CLOSED by #4160), #4160 itself, and the #4502 design umbrella — none covers eviction-vs-watermark interaction. Source-traced from the three code sites above; no runtime repro (the window needs a full 1,000-entry table plus a replay inside the skew-extended window).

## Why it matters

The effective-stamp machinery (#8865) exists precisely so replayed gossip cannot extend a node's claimed liveness past one TTL from receipt. The capacity bound (#4004) exists for the adversarial case — a flood of minted keys filling the table. Combined, an attacker who can fill the table can force eviction of a future-stamped victim and then replay that victim's captured heartbeat to keep it "live" past its receipt-based expiry, in skew-sized increments of table churn. Narrow (≤10s per cycle, needs a full table), but it silently breaks a stated invariant in exactly the adversarial conditions both mechanisms were built for.

## Acceptance criteria

- Capacity eviction never removes an entry whose sender stamp still passes the freshness bound (the `prune_at` watermark rule), OR a replayed heartbeat can never gain a later effective stamp than its first acceptance earned — one of the two, with the invariant at :335-337 holding under both prune and eviction.
- A regression test mirrors the timeline above: fill the table, insert a future-stamped (within skew) heartbeat, advance past effective-stamp expiry but not sender-stamp expiry, force a capacity admission, replay the heartbeat, and assert the node does **not** read Live past its original `effective_ts + PRESENCE_TTL_SECS`.
- Existing presence tests still pass, including `node_count_bound_*` and the #8865 replay/skew tests.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**mcpx adapter import's bash completion parser promotes every `subcommands`/`commands` word list in the file to top-level tools, losing the enclosing command context — for the installed git completion, `_git_bisect()`'s list (`start bad good skip reset …`) generates a top-level `start` tool whose fixed arguments are just `["start"]` instead of `["bisect", "start"]`, and because the nonempty completion parse wins the source ladder, ordinary git imports emit unusable tools instead of falling back to another source.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9161, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import_parse.go:271` at review:

> "Preserve command context when extracting bash subcommands. When a bash completion contains command lists inside nested-command handlers, this branch promotes every list to top-level tools. In the installed `/usr/share/bash-completion/completions/git:1448–1453`, `_git_bisect()` declares `local subcommands="start bad good skip reset visualize replay log run"`; the parser therefore generates a `start` tool whose fixed arguments are just `["start"]`, omitting `bisect`. The inspected `git start --help` confirms the result: "'start' is not a git command." Because this nonempty completion wins the source ladder, ordinary Git imports can emit unusable tools instead of falling back to another source. Preserve the enclosing command path or reject lists whose context cannot be established."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9161 "feat(mcpx): adapter import generates declarations from completions, man and --help (#1962)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161#discussion_r4558765530 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T01:52:25Z, file `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import_parse.go:271`

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is **unresolved** (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13) and the Codex comment is the thread's only comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer. (The author's five "Fixed in commit 07cacdd5b9" replies on this PR answer the *first* Codex round; this second-round comment was never answered.)
- PR #9161 was merged after this comment with the context-free list extraction unchanged; no follow-up commit on main has fixed it (verified by fresh read of `adapter_import_parse.go` on main, 2026-11-13).

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**mcpx adapter import marks every parsed positional operand as required, discarding usage-derived optionality — so for a binary whose positional is optional (e.g. argparse `add_argument('item', nargs='?', default='default-item')`, shown as `[item]` in usage), the generated declaration's `buildArgs()` rejects calls that omit the operand even though the binary accepts them and applies its default.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9161, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import.go:332` at review:

> "Preserve optionality of parsed positional operands. For help describing optional positional operands, marking every parsed positional as required prevents valid invocations. For example, argparse's `add_argument('item', nargs='?', default='default-item')` produces usage containing `[item]` and an ordinary `item` row under `positional arguments:`. The parser retains that row without its optionality, and this declaration makes `buildArgs()` reject calls omitting `item`, even though the binary accepts them and uses its default. Preserve usage-derived optionality, or avoid requiring operands whose required status has not been established; the subcommand branch has the same problem."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9161 "feat(mcpx): adapter import generates declarations from completions, man and --help (#1962)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161 (merged)

**mcpx adapter import appends its positional catch-all parameter named `args` unconditionally in both generation branches — when the imported help already declares a positional named `args` or a flag `--args`, the generated declaration carries two `args` parameters: `Spec.Validate()` accepts the duplicates, `Schema()` overwrites the earlier schema, and `buildArgs()` renders both entries from the same input, so positional operands are passed twice or a flag value also becomes an unintended trailing operand.**

Consequently, positional operands are passed twice, or a flag value also becomes an unintended trailing operand. This affects both generation branches; choose a catch-all name that does not collide with parsed parameters, or reuse an existing variadic positional."

## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**mcpx adapter import infers an integer parameter type whenever the value placeholder merely *contains* the substring `int` (or `num`/`count`) — so a string option like `--endpoint ENDPOINT` is generated as an integer-only parameter, and valid string values are rejected by argument validation before the adapter ever runs.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9161, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import.go:260` at review:

> "Infer integer types from complete placeholders, not substrings. For string-valued options whose placeholders happen to contain `int`, this heuristic generates an integer-only schema. For example, inspected argparse help for `add_argument('--endpoint')` prints `--endpoint ENDPOINT`, and argparse accepts a URL as its value, but `ENDPOINT` contains `int` and therefore produces an integer parameter here. `ToolSpec.Schema()` publishes that incorrect type, and `mcpclient.validateToolArgs()` rejects a valid string endpoint before invoking the adapter; generated TypeScript clients also expose it as a number. Match explicit numeric type names rather than arbitrary substrings, retaining string as the fallback when the source does not establish a numeric type."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9161 "feat(mcpx): adapter import generates declarations from completions, man and --help (#1962)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161#discussion_r4558765537 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T01:52:25Z, file `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import.go:260`

- No existing issue covers this finding (searched open and closed issues for PR #9161 and adapter-import keywords on 2026-11-13; only the parent feature issue #1962 and an unrelated salvage issue #9172 matched — neither covers this defect).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**`page_items` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch-test` returns an empty vector for any page body that has no array field — including a malformed page whose array field is `null` or absent — so `fetch_all_pages` treats the malformed page as an empty final page, returns `Ok`, and `append_page` rewrites `total_count` to the partial length: the listing ends silently short, against this crate's own "never truncate silently" rule.**

CodeRabbit (Minor, Data Integrity & Integration) in its review on PR #9149, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch-test/src/lib.rs:421`:

> "Reject malformed pages instead of treating them as an empty final page. `page_items` returns an empty vector for any body that has no array. This includes an object whose array field is `null` or absent. `fetch_all_pages` then treats that page like an empty final page, returns `Ok`, and `append_page` rewrites `total_count` to the partial length. The listing ends without an error and reports a short count. This conflicts with the stated rule to never truncate silently. Distinguish a missing or non-array field from a real empty array. A legitimate `[]` or `"workflow_runs": []` must keep ending the walk. A missing or non-array page must return an error that names the listing. Add a test with a second page of `{"workflow_runs": null}` that expects `Err`."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9149 "docs: land the #6622 pagination contract statement in the Phase 1-3 systems (#6623)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9149 (merged)
- Review: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9149#pullrequestreview-5884444344 — reviewer `coderabbitai[bot]`, state COMMENTED, 2026-11-13T00:54:36Z, file `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch-test/src/lib.rs:421` (outside-diff comment, so no inline thread exists)

## No-response evidence

- The finding was raised in a review body; PR #9149 has no inline comment replying to it and no conversation comment addressing it (full comment set re-read 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job: 0 inline, 1 review, 2 conversation comments — the conversation comments are the Codex no-findings summary and the CodeRabbit review-stack entry).
- PR #9149 merged minutes after the review with the page-reading path unchanged; no follow-up commit on main has added the malformed-page distinction (verified by fresh read of `lib.rs` on main, 2026-11-13).
- No existing issue covers this specific defect (searched open and closed issues for PR #9149, `page_items`, and malformed-page keywords on 2026-11-13; the #6622 contract issue and its closed Phase 4 inventory #6623 state the rule but do not track this live violation of it, and open issue #9150 covers a different defect — two page loops with no page bound).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-dispatch-test/src/lib.rs` on main: `page_items` (line 410) returns `Vec::new()` whenever the body is neither a bare array nor an object containing an array value — a `{"workflow_runs": null}` page yields the empty vec.
- `fetch_all_pages` (line 460) stops the walk when a page's item count is below `PAGE_SIZE` and returns `Ok(merged)`; `append_page` (line 428) rewrites an object body's `total_count` to the merged (partial) length. A malformed second page therefore produces a silent short count presented as exact.

## Acceptance criteria

- `page_items` / the page-reading path used by `fetch_all_pages` distinguishes a real empty array (ends the walk) from a missing or non-array listing field (returns an error naming the listing).
- A regression test covers a second page of `{"workflow_runs": null}` expecting `Err`, and a real empty array page still terminates the walk normally.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why treating malformed pages as final pages is acceptable here despite the never-truncate-silently rule.

## Defect: queue broker POST /list ignores the task/dedupe filters

Observed 2026-11-13T10:28–10:40Z from the laptop against the configured broker (`~/.config/repo-queue/broker-url`), during the #9106 delivery-publisher run (task 15354).

The non-rich `POST /list` route honors `queue`, `limit`, and `offset`, but silently ignores `task` and `dedupe_key` filters:

- `{"queue":"repo-health-code-pilot","task":15882,"limit":1,"offset":0}` → returns task **1111** (the queue's first row), not 15882.
- `{"queue":"repo-health-code-pilot","task_id":15882,...}` and `{"id":15882,...}` → same wrong row.
- `{"queue":"code","task":15882,...}` → returns task 15339 (that queue's first row).
- `{"task":15882,"limit":1,"offset":0}` (no queue) → `rows: []`, although task 15882 exists (verified via `fleet queue lane 15882`: lane record present, enqueued 2026-11-13T10:28Z by the #9106 publisher, dedupe `repo-health:v1:triage:developing-today/code:issue:9418`).
- `{"dedupe_key":"repo-health:v1:triage:developing-today/code:issue:9418","limit":1}` → `rows: []`.

Impact: the approved #9106 delivery publisher (`doc/2026-11-13T03-40-00Z_design_id-atlas-summit/delivery-publish/publish.py`, `queue_readback`) verifies every enqueue with exactly this filter — a verification the mill verified as working at approval time earlier on 2026-11-13. It now fail-closed-refuses after the first slice: issue #9418 filed and task 15882 enqueued, coverage unverified, remaining 126 of 127 issues unpublished until readback works again. Any other consumer verifying queue writes via /list task filtering is equally blind.

Ask: restore exact task/dedupe filtering on the non-rich /list route (or publish the route's current contract and a supported exact-task read). Acceptance: the first query above returns exactly task 15882's row; the no-queue task query returns it too; dedupe_key query returns the matching row.

title: Map existing ID stores to explicit port boundaries

## Problem and goal
Establish a source-accurate seam map that keeps blob, event, world, and sync stores distinct and gives port design an explicit ownership baseline.

Filed by fleet-minder run322 (2026-11-13T03:xx-06:00) under priorities brief line 1 (fleet-stalling breakage).

### Which check failed
OpenChamber/OpenCode lanes launch on schedule, but every session launched since ~09:00Z fails on its first model call. This meets the fleet-minder broken-launcher definition: "sessions start but their models never answer."

### Evidence
- Attention census 2026-11-13T09:10Z: 84 sessions — 60 errored/failed, 2 in-motion (both the 03:10 batch, verified failed minutes later), 0 verified working at end of run.

  - Challenge Summit ses_e5e2d678c0cffedHj8JD7QI3gD also failed `provider.rate-limit` on `_claude/claude-fable-5-2`.

title: id: implement Residency step 3 — native sync and hosted bridge checks (#5529)
body:
Implementation step 3 of the residency design (#3398, `doc/2026-11-01_design_id3398.md` §7) for epic issue #5529.

**Scope:** pkgs/id — preflight and receive-side residency policy checks for native sync and the production bridge seam; outbox enqueue and retry coverage.

**Depends on:** step 1 (merged, PR #5629: `residency` evaluator in id-core) and step 2 (task 9596 / PR #9391: `residency_inventory` deployment admission). Start only after step 2 is merged.

**Acceptance (design §3 rows + §7 step 3):**
- Native sync evaluates residency policy on both sides before event bytes are sent or ingested for scoped worlds; a valid join capability does not override a denial.
- Bridge sync for scoped content stays disabled until every store and hop in the session has evidence; missing/expired evidence sends and stores zero protected events; a relay cannot turn a denial into an allow.
- Outbox enqueue and retry re-evaluate policy (a retry after evidence expiry denies).
- Negative tests for this step's §3 rows pass, asserting both the refusal and the absence of disallowed side effects.
- Preserve signed-event ingest semantics; the bridge does not become a trust authority.

Filed by queue task 9596 (lane code-a) as the ordered follow-on split the design's §7 requires. Sibling steps: step 4 and step 5 issues filed in the same pass.

title: Decisions page: per-item submit unreachable on multi-question (v2) items + submitted items vanish with no way back

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

body:
**Bug (Drew, live, 2026-11-13 02:07 CST):** "the per item submit is gone" on the decisions pages, reported while steering the blocked-review category sets (decisions-2026-11-13-blocked-*).

**Root cause:** not a missing button in code — a layout/scale failure. The renderer emits exactly one "Submit this item" button per item, after its last question. v1 sets carry 1 question per item, so a button sits within ~a screen of every question (verified: design-blocked, 11 items, buttons every ~800px). The v2 category sets pack 7–17 questions into ONE item, so the page's only per-item submit sits at 6,015px of a 6,845px page — ~7 viewport heights below the first question (CDP-measured on the live-shaped page). For the person answering question 1 of 16, per-item submit effectively does not exist. Second half of the same report: a fully-submitted item was removed from the DOM/page outright (applyOpenState `card.remove()`; server render returned ""), so a submitted item could never be re-checked on the page — Drew's ruling: submitted items hide by default, with a way to bring them back.

**Fix:**
- Multi-question items render "Submit this item" at the TOP of the card (under the title, before the first question) as well as at the bottom; both buttons carry the same data-submit-item wiring. Single-question items are byte-identical to before.
- Fully-resolved items now render as submitted cards, hidden by default (`display:none`), behind a "Show submitted items (N)" toggle at the top of the page; all-submitted group labels hide with them. The live flow converts a just-emptied card to the same hidden submitted state (with a recorded-note) instead of deleting it, and the toggle count tracks both server-rendered and in-session submissions. The recorded resolution lines stay inside the card for review — the page has no undo, so re-checking has to be possible.

**Verification:** CDP-driven on a faithful fixture instance before deploy (v2: top button at 421px above first question at 481px; submit → card hidden, toggle count 1, toggle re-shows; v1 open set unchanged 11/11; v1 fully-resolved set: 43 submitted cards, 0 visible, toggle reveals all 43). New `test/decisions-page.test.ts` boots the real server and asserts placement + submitted rendering + the submit round-trip; decisions suites 76/76 green. Live verification after the pm-aggregator restart is noted in the closing comment.

title: pm-stack(lineage-manifest): board taxonomy names Type instead of canonical Kind — epics placed without Kind=Epic lose dashboard membership (from PR #8980)

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**The lineage manifest's board taxonomy names a `Type` field instead of the canonical Project `Kind` field, and its board follow-up omits setting `Kind=Epic` — following it can leave newly placed epics without dashboard epic membership, because the aggregator only recognises epic ancestors via `Kind=Epic`.**

Codex (P2) on PR #8980, `pm-stack/lineage-manifest-2026-11-12.md` (line 23 at review):

> "Use the canonical Kind field for epic board placement. When completing board placement for the new epics, this taxonomy names `Type` instead of the canonical `Kind` field, and the follow-up instructions likewise omit setting `Kind=Epic`. This is operationally significant: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts:188-191` reads `Kind`, and `resolveEpicRefs` at lines 205-212 recognizes epic ancestors only when that value is `Epic`; an `epic` label or a separate `Type` value does not substitute for it. Following this manifest can therefore leave the newly linked children without dashboard epic membership even after board access is restored. Align the taxonomy and placement instructions with `pm-stack/README.md` and `planning/templates/epic-intake.md`, which require setting `Kind=Epic` on the epic's Project item."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #8980 "pm-stack: lineage manifest 2026-11-12 — epic/board/label register" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8980
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8980#discussion_r4555029431 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-12T19:04:51Z, file `pm-stack/lineage-manifest-2026-11-12.md:23`
- Canonical source on main: `pm-stack/README.md:99` — "Project `Kind=Epic` is canonical. The aggregator reads this field…"

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is **unresolved** (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13) and the Codex comment is the thread's only comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer.
- PR #8980 was merged with the manifest unchanged on this point; no follow-up commit on main has corrected the taxonomy (verified by a fresh read of the file on main, 2026-11-13).
- No existing issue covers this finding (searched open and closed issues for the PR number and `Kind=Epic` board-placement keywords on 2026-11-13; matches were unrelated epic issues only).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

- `pm-stack/lineage-manifest-2026-11-12.md:21-24` on main still describes Project #4 as having "Area/Status/Horizon/Type fields", and the board follow-up at lines 44-48 still only requires Area to be set — it never mentions setting `Kind=Epic` on epic items.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/projects.ts` on main still parses `kind: singleSelect(item, "Kind")`, and `resolveEpicRefs` still returns an epic reference only when an ancestor's `kind === "Epic"` — a `Type` value or an `epic` label does not substitute.

## Acceptance criteria

- The manifest's taxonomy and board follow-up instructions are aligned to the canonical field: Project #4 fields named as Area/Status/Horizon/Kind, and epic board placement explicitly sets `Kind=Epic` on each epic's Project item (per `pm-stack/README.md` and the epic-intake template).
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why `Type` is correct for this board despite the aggregator reading `Kind`.

---
Filed by the pr-comment-review job from an unaddressed PR review comment (source: PR #8980). This issue deliberately does not reply to or resolve the source review thread.

title: fix(mcpx docs): keep protocol generated regions compatible with treefmt

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation (area)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On current GitHub `main` at `936424f5d73a4c29aff149335486fbd587c0a927`, the focused drift guard reproduces the CI failure:

```text
cd pkgs/mcpx
go test ./internal/refdoc -run TestCommittedRegionsAreCurrent -count=1
--- FAIL: TestCommittedRegionsAreCurrent
    internal/refdoc/regions_test.go:119: docs/protocol.md generated regions are stale
```

The same test failure appears in the `mcpx nix build` main run [43348422142](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43348422142) at `8d0921ba60` (the treefmt auto-format commit); the failing Nix checkPhase runs the Go package tests. `regions_test.go` compares the committed `protocol-features` and `protocol-capabilities` marker regions byte-for-byte with `ProtocolFeaturesTable()` and `ProtocolCapabilitiesTable()` from `internal/cli/manual_md.go`. The committed tables have formatter-style column padding while the generated-region check rejects that representation, so formatting and the generated-doc contract disagree and main's package check is red.

The focused test was also run against a clean worktree at current main and still fails. Related generated-reference issues #1846, #4909, and #4982 are CLOSED; fresh all-state searches for `protocol-capabilities`, stale generated regions, and generated `protocol.md` found no open tracker. No matching open PR was found.

## Why it matters

The generated-reference drift check is itself incompatible with the repository formatter on a committed generated region. This leaves the current main check failing and makes future `treefmt` runs able to reintroduce the same failure after documentation is regenerated.

## Acceptance criteria

- Choose one stable formatting contract: make the generator emit the formatter's canonical table form, or prevent formatting from rewriting generated regions while preserving normal formatting for surrounding prose.
- Regenerate/format `pkgs/mcpx/docs/protocol.md` so `go test ./internal/refdoc -run TestCommittedRegionsAreCurrent -count=1` passes on current code.
- Add or adjust a regression check demonstrating that the repository formatter followed by the generated-region check remains green.
- The relevant `mcpx` Nix package check passes.

title: perf(id/web): avoid reserializing all records on every host-view page

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` (`8b4cc5f5aa8e90f0bfc3f9267945c1226e29ab06`), `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:106-114` computes `records_revision` by serializing the complete `Records` map into a new `Vec<u8>` and hashing it. `host_view_handler` calls `world.records()` and recomputes this revision on every request, before filtering records by the `after` cursor (`world_ws.rs:153-167`). The host-view client fetches these pages sequentially.

The data is bounded, but not to a page: `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/mod.rs:2150-2190` permits 4,096 records with values up to 8 KiB each, while `pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/world_caps.rs:740-744` caps each served page at 768 KiB. A valid near-limit records set can therefore be roughly 33 MiB. Paging such a set can serialize and hash that entire map dozens of times, allocating a full-size temporary buffer each time; per-page slicing also serializes values again. This makes a legitimate large host view disproportionately expensive in CPU and transient memory.

The existing page-count/advance fix tracked by #9043 and PR #9051 addresses a client loop, not the repeated full-map work in the server handler.

## Why it matters

A world owner opening a large host view can trigger repeated full-map serialization for each bounded page. This can make the admin view slow and create avoidable memory pressure in the serving process, even though each response is capped.

## Acceptance criteria

- Preserve cross-page snapshot/revision consistency without serializing and allocating the entire records map anew for every page.
- Keep the 768 KiB page limit and existing behavior when records change during paging.
- Add a regression test for a multi-page records set that pins bounded revision work (use a structural/counting oracle rather than a timing threshold) and verifies page consistency/change detection.

title: fleet gh: sandbox binary lagged current build — no token rotation on heavy project calls
body:
## Defect (observed 2026-11-12, board-gap lane)

In the sandbox, `fleet gh project item-list` (org Project #4, developing-today) returned the personal token's GraphQL rate-limit error twice with no failover, while the laptop fleet build rotated correctly. The lane finished with light targeted GraphQL queries instead, and flagged it as a suspected sandbox-shim limitation.

## Root cause (diagnosed same day)

Stale sandbox binary — candidate cause (1) of three checked:

- At observation time the sandbox `~/tools/fleet` was an earlier build than the laptop's. (This morning's recorded state: sandbox fleet source rev `d4ecd0195d4b`, no `gh` domain at all; the laptop carried the post-#9014 build.)
- Ruled out: (2) a token-pinning shim — sandbox `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN` are unset in the environment and the trace shows the serving leg changing per attempt; (3) a gh.rs classifier gap on current code — the current build fails over on exactly this GraphQL error shape (proof below).

## Fix

The sandbox binary was replaced at 2026-11-12T22:14:04Z with a build of the PR #9054 merge (`743966553e78`, "feat/fleet-gh-apps-tiers", merged 22:10:59Z — 18 commits ahead of, and 0 behind, the #9014 merge `febd7fa921`). `fleet version` in the sandbox now reports source rev `743966553e`, and `fleet capabilities` shows the `gh` domain `available`.

## Verification (sandbox, `FLEET_GH_TRACE=1`, no token values printed)

1. The exact heavy call that failed before:
   `fleet gh project item-list 4 --owner developing-today --format json --limit 1400`
   → `attempt 1 under personal` → `personal failed (rate limit); failing over` → `attempt 2 under app:developing-today` → exit 0, `totalCount 1229`, 1229 items returned.
2. Manufactured failover: `FLEET_GH_ORDER=app:dezren39,app:developing-today fleet gh project view 4 --owner developing-today`
   → user-installation leg failed → org installation served the call, exit 0.
3. Light call sanity: `fleet gh api user` returns `dezren39` under the personal leg.

## Durability note

Nothing yet guarantees the sandbox binary tracks current main the way the laptop's install flow does; the sandbox lagged through both the #9014 and #9054 landings today and was only refreshed incidentally. If sandbox fleet freshness matters, it wants an explicit refresh/check step (e.g. in the sandbox init tooling) rather than relying on a lane noticing. Recorded here as the follow-up; this issue closes on the verified fix above.

title: fix(pm-stack): stack sentinel flaps on single probe timeouts — paging Drew for load spikes
body:
## Problem

Drew is being paged by PM-stack "front-end fails" that are not failures. The stack sentinel (`pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/stack-sentinel.ts`) flips a service to `down` on a **single failed probe** and posts the transition to the alert throat; the aggregator's notification engine then pages on the resulting stack-health candidate whenever the 6h cooldown has lapsed.

Diagnosis (2026-11-12, live laptop state):

- `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/notifications.jsonl`: 433 notification events today, 30 sent. `service:projector` alone: **118 events, 4 sent**; `service:opencode` flapped the same way.
- `pm-projector.service` **never crashed** — active (running) since 2026-11-10, same PID. What fails is the probe: `probe failed: The operation timed out` (3s probe timeout) while the laptop sits at load average 8–10 under the fleet burn. One slow probe → `down`; next round answers → `recovered`; repeat.
- The projector itself is fine; the health signal cries wolf under load.

## Fix

Flap damping in the sentinel:

- A service flips to `down` (for state + notification purposes) only after **3 consecutive failed probes** at the 30s cadence (~90s of continuous failure). A single failed probe never flips state and never posts.
- Probe timeouts for the 3s probes (projector, kaneo, dispatch, opencode, queue-broker) raised to **10s** so a slow-but-alive service under load answers in time (aggregator's /board probe already uses 15s).
- A recovery transition is only ever posted after the corresponding `down` was actually posted (the `postedState` bookkeeping already guarantees this; the damping keeps it true — a blip that never became a posted down produces no recovery).
- The first-sighting baseline is amended to match: a failed first probe now starts the failure streak instead of posting an immediate down (a genuinely down service is still declared after 3 probes, ~90s after sentinel start).
- Existing notification cooldown + dedupe stay untouched.

`health:fleet-feed` also sent 4 pushes today but is a **different mechanism** — a 5-minute feed-staleness window in `src/health.ts`, not a single-probe flip — and is deliberately out of scope here.

Ordered by Drew, main chat 2026-11-12: "Tune the health check so load spikes stop paging me." Follow-up to #8568 (Phase 1, closed).

title: queue: per-task session binding history + model timeline — session_id join to raw opencode data (extends #8176)

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

body:
# Queue: per-task session binding history + model timeline (extends #8176)

Drew's order, main chat 2026-11-12 ~15:45–15:49 CST:

> "allow marking model over time as transitions occur, or include session ID in stamp and we can join the raw opencode data to a task that way. allow multiple stamps and sessions etc and tracking changes over time"
>
> "we need to get the session and be able to see which exact model resolved. maybe it's not stored in the queue related tables. or near the end the most used model can get recorded while closing out for convenience but the most important is session id link to opencode data, then we can get exact models over time, even if one session handles multiple tasks we can look at that session from item start to stop, ensure that detailed status gets set over time."

## Finding first: is the task↔session binding stored today? (verified 2026-11-12, live fleet-queue DB)

Partially — and not on the volume paths:

- `repo_task_lane_ledger.session_id`: 599 of 6,087 ledger rows carry one. One row per task (task_id UNIQUE) — current binding only, overwritten, no history, no window.
- `tasks.progress.session_id`: 493 tasks carry it. It is set only by the /bind verb and by transfer claims. **Pick claims and by-id claims that name a session never set it** — the session lands only in the `claimed` event's detail.
- `events`: 1,025 `lane_session_bound` events (the /bind path) and `session_binding_cleared` events on every clear path (park/release/fail/expire/re-claim all funnel through `on_binding_cleared`). So a bound/unbound history exists for bind-path tasks only.
- `claimed` events carrying a session_id: **11 of 43,621**. Until today's #8176 fix the volume claim surfaces never even named a session.

So the binding is real but narrow: bind/transfer tasks are joinable; ordinary session claims are not recorded as bindings at all.

## Why the session link is the product (demonstrated on live data)

Task 14440's claim stamp reads `opencode-route / workhorse` — a route name, a hint. Its bound session `ses_e5e37addeb0ffeumu1UPO2bI8G` in the OpenCode server's `route_attempt` table (`~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`, indexed on (session_id, time_started)) shows what actually served: **27 calls, all `_openai / gpt-6.1-terra` variant `low`**, 2026-11-11 01:56:30Z → ~02:03Z, inside the task's bound window. Exact models over time come from that join — session_id + the task's window in the session — never from stamp guesswork. One session can serve several tasks; each task slices the session's attempts by its own bound→unbound window.

## Design

Storage follows the codebase's own doctrine: the `events` table is the append-only audit log (see `audit_marks` in turso_queue.rs). New records ride it; the task row keeps the latest-stamp columns for cheap reads.

1. **Binding history (core).** New event kinds `session_bound` / `session_unbound` (detail: session_id, trigger, via; the events row's created_at is the window edge). Written by the broker at every point a binding is set or cleared:
   - set: pick claim naming a session, by-id claim naming a session (claim_by_id learns the session parameter), transfer claim, /bind. These paths also set `progress.session_id` where they don't today (pick, by-id), so every later event's audit marks carry the session.
   - cleared: the existing `on_binding_cleared` funnel (park/release/fail/expire/re-claim/revalidate) additionally writes `session_unbound`; /complete and /cancel write a record-only `session_unbound` (trigger complete/cancel) when a binding is open.
   - The legacy `lane_session_bound` / `session_binding_cleared` events stay untouched for their existing consumers; the timeline reader treats them as the same pair for pre-change history.
2. **Stamp history.** New event kind `model_stamp` (detail: session_id, provider, model, variant, trigger ∈ claim|transfer|bind). The broker writes it inside `stamp_claim_model`, which also gains a `tasks.claim_session_id` column (additive, ensure_schema pattern; SCHEMA + TASK_COLS updated) so the row's claim_* set is the complete latest stamp. A stamp with no known session stays session-less; no model or session is ever fabricated (#8176 honesty rule).
3. **Read path.** New broker verb `/events-list` {task_id, kind?, limit?} (events_task index) and a CLI `fleet queue timeline <task-id>` that renders bound/unbound windows + stamps in order, collapses duplicate writes of the same (kind, session, model, trigger) within 120s (a pre-switch CLI append and the post-switch broker write can both land for one bind), and — on the laptop — enriches each window with the exact model segments from `route_attempt` for that session+window. Interim read (works today): `SELECT id, kind, detail, created_at FROM events WHERE task_id = <id> AND kind IN ('model_stamp','session_bound','session_unbound','lane_session_bound','session_binding_cleared') ORDER BY id;`
4. **Close-out convenience field.** `fleet queue complete` gains an optional `--queue`; when the task's row can be fetched (rich list, which also gains `claimed_at`) and its progress names a session, the CLI computes the dominant (provider, model, variant) by call count from `route_attempt` over [claimed_at, now] for that session and merges `dominant_model` into the result JSON (an explicit caller value wins). Fail-soft at every step: any miss completes the task without the summary.
5. **Live-now activation (no broker restart).** The broker changes merge and activate at the coordinated switch (standing boundary: no broker restart until the deployed binary contains both 6a792f60 (#8548) and aba44429 (#8561)). Everything the CLI can do against the current broker goes live via the rebuilt CLI swap (~/.local/bin/fleet, the #9025 pattern): after a successful claim/bind/release/park/fail/cancel, the CLI appends the same `model_stamp` / `session_bound` / `session_unbound` records through the existing `/events-append` verb — for claims, only when the claim response row lacks the `claim_session_id` key (the capability signal that the broker is pre-switch and did not write them itself).

## Detailed status over time (point 5 of Drew's note)

Window edges are only as good as recorded transitions. Verified today: claim/park/release/fail/complete/cancel/expire all write timestamped events, and tasks carry claimed_at/completed_at columns. The set-side gap this issue fixes (pick/by-id claims not recording the session binding) was the main hole; progress JSON itself does not timestamp every stage transition (checkpoints are timestamped via their events, not inside progress) — noted here, not changed.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A task claimed under session A then transferred to session B shows, read back from the DB: two bindings with windows, two model_stamp records with session ids, claim_session_id = B on the row.
- [ ] `fleet queue timeline <id>` renders that history; the route_attempt join for one window shows the exact resolved model sequence.
- [ ] An organic model_stamp/session_bound pair from live traffic after the CLI swap.
- [ ] fleet-queue tests green (new oracles named per behavior); no broker restart taken.

state: filed

Found by the #6623 closing pagination inventory (2026-11-12, origin/main 338c6cf03f):

`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/fallback.rs` — `fetch_markers` reads issue comments with `for page in 1..=10` at `per_page=100` (line ~575), breaking on a short page. The loop is volume-bounded (rule 2 of the #6622 contract), but if the 10th page is still full the function returns the markers it has with **no error and no notice**: claim/lease markers past the first 1,000 comments are silently dropped, so the fallback queue can read a live claim as absent — the completeness axis (rule 3: truncation is never silent) in the one fleet list read the closing inventory found still violating it.

Fix: when the bound is reached on a full page, fail (or surface an explicit truncation notice the caller cannot ignore) rather than returning a partial marker set as complete — the cargo-target-janitor liveness reads (`MAX_PR_PAGES` + `SafetyError`) are the in-repo precedent.

Acceptance: a >1,000-comment issue's marker read errors or reports truncation explicitly; reads under the bound are unchanged; a test pins the full-10th-page case.

<!-- agent-note:v1 -->
state: filed
source-task: 15331
parent: #6623 (closing pagination inventory of design #6622)

Found by the #6623 closing pagination inventory (2026-11-12, origin/main 338c6cf03f):

`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` — the read-only host view fetches record pages in a `do { ... after = result.next_after } while (after !== null)` loop (lines ~492-522). The cursor's TYPE is validated (`pkgs/id/web/src/world-http.ts:70-71` throws when `next_after` is present and not a string), and the in-repo sender is pinned to string-or-null — but the loop itself carries **no page-count bound and no advance check**: a repeating or self-equal cursor from a buggy or compromised host makes the browser fetch pages forever. That is the one pkgs/id page consumer the #6622 contract's rule 2 (volume bounded, breach is an error naming the listing) does not reach.

Fix: give the loop a named page bound (and/or an advance check consistent with `world_net.rs` `record_pages`), breaching which surfaces the existing host-view error state ("World records changed while paging; refresh" is the neighbouring precedent) instead of looping.

Acceptance: host-view paging terminates with a visible error on a non-advancing cursor or after the named page bound; normal multi-page host views are unchanged; a test pins the repeating-cursor case.

title: Scheduled Suggestions — developing-today/code

labels.name: source/dispatch
labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
You are a code-review agent running as a dispatched session in this
repository. Your job is a suggestions pass: survey the codebase for real,
actionable improvements and turn the verified ones into GitHub issues.

## Dispatch context — read this first

- You are running in this repository's LAPTOP CHECKOUT (the repo's primary
  checkout on the owner's laptop). Work there; do not clone the repo
  elsewhere.
- A tracking issue and a queue task were ALREADY created for this run by
  the dispatcher, and this session is already claimed against them. Do
  NOT create another tracking issue for this run, and do not dispatch
  further tasks.
- There is NO plan-approval step. Proceed directly; do not stop to ask
  for approval of a plan.

## What to review

Survey the codebase across these five areas:

- **Cleanup** — dead code, duplicated logic, obsolete files or config,
  leftover scaffolding.
- **Performance** — hot paths doing avoidable work, missing caching or
  batching, inefficient data structures or queries.
- **Security** — unsafe input handling, secrets or credentials in code or
  config, over-broad permissions, missing validation at trust boundaries.
- **Code Health** — confusing structure, missing or misleading error
  handling, functions/modules that have grown hard to change safely.
- **Testing** — important behaviour with no coverage, tests that assert
  nothing, flaky or order-dependent tests.

## Verify before you file — no speculative filings

Every candidate finding MUST be verified against the actual code before
it becomes an issue:

- Read the code at the location you cite. Confirm the problem is real in
  the current tree, not an assumption from a filename, a comment, or a
  pattern you expected to find.
- Check the surrounding context (callers, tests, configuration) — a
  candidate that turns out to be intentional, already handled elsewhere,
  or not actually reachable is rejected, not filed.
- Search the repo's OPEN issues before filing. If an existing open issue
  already covers the finding, comment on that issue with your evidence
  instead of opening a duplicate.

## Filing

- Per real, verified finding, file ONE issue in this repo with
  `gh issue create` from the laptop checkout. Each issue must include:
  - the canonical component label for its area; use `app/pm-stack` for
    PM-stack / aggregator issues in this repo. `app/aggregator` is a legacy
    alias and must not be used for new filings.
  - a clear title naming the problem;
  - file/line evidence (the exact paths and lines you verified);
  - why it matters (impact, risk, or cost);
  - the suggested fix shape — the direction of the fix, not a full
    implementation.
- CAP: at most **5 filings per pass** (new issues plus evidence comments
  on existing issues). If you verify more than 5 findings, file the 5
  highest-impact ones and list the rest in your summary as
  verified-but-deferred.
- Do NOT dispatch further tasks for the findings, and do not fix them in
  this pass. The issues are the record; the fleet's normal lanes pick
  work up from them.

## Finish

End with a short summary — as your session output, and as a comment on
this run's tracking issue if you can identify it — covering:

- **Filed** — each issue you opened or commented on, with its number and
  one line on the finding.
- **Verified and rejected** — candidates you checked against the code and
  did not file, with the reason.
- **Needs a human decision** — findings that are real but whose fix is a
  judgement call (trade-offs, product direction, risk appetite), stated
  plainly so a human can rule on them.

title: id: design: Joplin continuous sync target / plugin bridge (from #5678)

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: kind/design
labels.description: A design proposal (design-architect): multi-step, phased, decision-bearing

labels.name: epic/id-program
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Summary

Design-only follow-on under the knowledge-layer programme. Investigate whether the ID knowledge layer could support continuous two-way synchronization with Joplin through an ID-hosted Joplin-compatible sync target, a Joplin-side plugin bridge, or another bounded adapter. This issue follows the deferred decision in [#7676](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/7676), builds on the one-shot importer design in [#5848](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5848), and belongs to programme [#5678](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/5678).

**Do not decide build/no-build in this design task.** Drew's 2026-11-11 ruling deferred the sync-target question to the orchestrator with the guided pick “Overturn — scope a design task,” and said we can design it and decide later. The build/no-build decision is explicitly after this design lands. Do not re-ask Drew. Keep #5848's one-shot import plus idempotent re-import as the v1 baseline; do not silently reverse or expand it.

## Design question and boundaries

Compare, at minimum:
1. Keep one-shot import, idempotent re-import, and the designed export path; make no continuous-sync addition.
2. An ID-hosted Joplin-compatible sync target/backend.
3. A Joplin-side plugin/extension bridge that communicates with ID through a supported interface.
4. Any materially different adapter that evidence shows is viable (state why it is distinct).

For each option, describe trust boundaries and components, what state it owns, identity and lifecycle mapping, supported Joplin client/version surfaces, failure/recovery behavior, and where source-of-truth authority resides. Keep the design bounded to Joplin↔ID knowledge-layer continuity; no implementation, general sync redesign, or product build/no-build decision.

## Required analysis

- **#5848 manifest/import design:** assess whether its source-vault identity and Joplin-ID↔ID-note/resource mapping can support ongoing synchronization, and what additional cursors, tombstones, field provenance, version mapping, or migration state would be needed. Preserve stable ID identity, append-only events, idempotency, and explicit reporting; distinguish re-import from continuous sync.
- **#2048 multi-head/conflict semantics:** explain concrete concurrent-edit cases (including deletion/restore, metadata/tags, links, attachments/resources, and offline clients). Do not introduce last-writer-wins or flatten concurrent ID heads silently. Specify user-visible conflict/merge behavior or mark the conflict an architectural blocker. Address the existing #5848 §7 export rule without changing #2048 decisions silently.
- **Joplin protocol/API and churn:** verify the current supported extension/plugin and synchronization surfaces from primary Joplin sources. Assess protocol/version compatibility, client interoperability, locking/transactions, item serialization, deletion propagation, resource handling, E2EE boundaries, upgrade cadence, and the cost/owner of ongoing compatibility maintenance. Separate documented facts from assumptions.
- **Migration and operations:** explain how an existing #5848 one-shot import/manifest transitions to and from each option without duplicate identities or data loss; include rollback/disable behavior, backup/recovery, observability, support burden, test-corpus needs, and a practical maintenance-cost estimate with stated assumptions.
- **Alternatives and decision boundary:** provide a comparison table, evidence-backed feasibility assessment, and design recommendation/conditions. Record which product decision remains for after the design and what evidence the decision-maker should weigh; do not make that decision here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A linked design record compares all required alternatives and covers the four required analysis areas above.
- Claims about Joplin APIs/protocols and compatibility are backed by dated primary-source references; unknowns are clearly labeled with a verification plan, not presented as facts.
- The design states explicit invariants and failure/conflict cases, including how it preserves #2048 multi-head semantics and how it interoperates with the #5848 import manifest.
- Migration, maintenance/ownership, rollback, and test/evidence costs are described with assumptions; protocol maintenance has an explicit owner requirement rather than an implied “forever” obligation.
- Hard blockers and ordering/dependencies are stated. At minimum, treat #2048 as settled, #5848's one-shot design as baseline, and coordinate with the #5838 multi-device sync design and #5844 attachment/media decisions where their boundaries intersect; record conflicts instead of silently changing those decisions.
- The deliverable remains design-only. It does not choose build/no-build, implement a target/plugin, enable a scheduled job, or change #5848's v1 scope. The post-design build/no-build decision is explicitly left pending.

## Evidence expected

Joplin's current official documentation/source for plugin APIs and synchronization protocol/version behavior; the landed #2048 and #5848 design records; relevant #5838/#5844 records; and a migration/cost analysis grounded in those interfaces. Include a small scenario matrix or test-corpus proposal with decidable expected outcomes for conflict, retry/recovery, deletion, and manifest migration.

## Relations

Follow-on to #7676; design baseline #5848; programme #5678. Related boundaries: #2048, #5838, and #5844. Build/no-build is deferred until this design lands.

title: aggregator(quota-extract): monthDayTime accepts out-of-range minutes — 'Oct 30, 18:99 UTC' becomes a fabricated 19:39 resetsAt instead of null

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: priority/normal

body:
## Finding

`monthDayTime` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` (line 39 on current main `a5318f8798b1`) validates the month and the day-of-month, but never validates the time-of-day it captures. Its UTC round-trip check (`isRequestedDate`) compares only `getUTCMonth()` and `getUTCDate()`, so an out-of-range **minute** that does not push the constructed date across midnight is silently normalized by `Date.UTC` into a different, fabricated reset time instead of returning `null`.

Hours 24–99 happen to return `null` only as a side effect (they always roll the date forward a day, tripping the day check). Minutes 60–99 roll forward only one hour, so they usually pass.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4135 (merged, merge commit `4f7147ce54d2883f0a05c0a6dfb8193f2cc58b0a`, commit `bfc1e0bfd2d5242b7be1051db6e24ae9e20d49c2`), which fixed issue #2196. Its stated contract: unknown month or out-of-range day returns `null` so the window keeps its percentage and no reset date is invented. Its regression tests cover `Oct 39` and `Foo 30`, but no out-of-range time.
- All three callers capture the time with the same shape, so the malformed values reach the function: Codex `resets (\w{3}) (\d{1,2}), (\d{2}:\d{2}) UTC` (quota-extract.ts:240), OpenCode Go `monthly reset … (\d{2}:\d{2}) UTC` (:316), Command Code `period ends … (\d{2}:\d{2}) UTC` (:436).
- Node probe of the verbatim `monthDayTime` from current main (TypeScript types stripped only; `now = 2026-10-26T00:00:00Z`; probe saved by the filing job):

  ```text
  Oct 30 18:01 -> 2026-10-30T18:01:00.000Z   (valid, control)
  Oct 30 18:59 -> 2026-10-30T18:59:00.000Z   (valid, control)
  Oct 30 18:99 -> 2026-10-30T19:39:00.000Z   (INVALID minute, fabricated)
  Oct 30 00:90 -> 2026-10-30T01:30:00.000Z   (INVALID minute, fabricated)
  Oct 30 18:60 -> 2026-10-30T19:00:00.000Z   (INVALID minute, fabricated)
  Oct 30 23:99 -> null                        (only because it crosses midnight)
  Oct 30 24:00 -> null                        (only via the day-roll side effect)
  Oct 39 18:01 -> null                        (the #4135 day case, correct)
  Foo 30 18:01 -> null                        (the #4135 month case, correct)
  ```

- Still present on current main: the function body on `a5318f8798b1` is byte-identical in behavior to the PR #4135 version (read via the contents API during the filing run).
- Dedupe: `gh search issues` for `monthDayTime` returns only closed #2196 and closed #2470 (Claude/Meta reset *dates* — a different validation path, already landed); no open issue and no open PR tracks the time-of-day component.

## Why it matters

The aggregator's whole validation discipline in this area (issues #2196, #2383, #2470, and the sibling guards merged the same day in PRs #4136/#4142) is: a malformed provider read keeps its percentage and gets `resetsAt: null` — never an invented date. A dashboard line with a corrupted time (e.g. `resets Oct 30, 18:99 UTC`) currently produces a confident, wrong reset time on the quota card instead, which is exactly the failure mode #2196 was filed to eliminate for dates.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `monthDayTime` returns `null` for any out-of-range time-of-day component (hour > 23 or minute > 59), for all three call sites (Codex, OpenCode Go, Command Code), while the window's percentage/other fields are preserved.
- [ ] Valid times, month-case normalization, unknown-month `null`, out-of-range-day `null`, and the >30-days-past roll-forward behavior from #4135 keep working unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/quota.test.ts` pin at least: minute 60, minute 99 not crossing midnight (e.g. `18:99`), hour 24, and a valid boundary time (`23:59`), across the existing three-consumer test matrix or an equivalent direct cover.
- [ ] No other extractor's behavior changes.

title: feat(mcpx-tests): MCPX_TEST_BINARY override for the binary suite (#1980)
body:
## What

Implements the binary-override piece of #1980 (approach B / stage-2 increment): `testsupport.MCPXBinary` previously always ran a fresh `go build ./cmd/mcpx`, so the e2e suite could only ever test a plain build — never the artifact users install (the nix wrapper's PATH pinning, the ldflags version, the generated man page and completions).

- `MCPX_TEST_BINARY=/path/to/mcpx` now points the binary suite at a prebuilt binary (nix `result/bin/mcpx`, or the binary from the shipped container image); nothing is built in that mode.
- The override is validated up front by `resolveMCPXOverride`: a set-but-missing / directory / non-executable value fails the suite loudly naming the variable, instead of silently falling back to a fresh build and testing the wrong artifact.
- Unset behaviour is byte-for-byte the old path.

## Tests (oracle: filesystem state planted per case)

- New `internal/testsupport/build_test.go`: unset → no override; executable file → returned; relative path → absolutized; missing → error naming `MCPX_TEST_BINARY`; directory → error; non-executable → error. 6/6 pass; full `testsupport` package passes; `go vet` + `gofmt` clean.
- End-to-end smoke on the laptop: built `./cmd/mcpx` once, then `MCPX_TEST_BINARY=<that binary> go test ./internal/e2e/ -run TestTypesRejectsUnknownNamespace` PASS (11.5s); with `MCPX_TEST_BINARY=/tmp/does-not-exist-mcpx` the same test FAILs at `build mcpx: MCPX_TEST_BINARY: stat ...: no such file or directory` — the loud failure working as designed.

## Scope

Refs #1980 — this is one stage, not the whole issue. Remaining on #1980: stage-2 environment threading for in-process parallelism, the dual-runner harness, the `-cover` build + GOCOVERDIR wiring (its CI artifact home is an open question belonging to #95/#99), and the scriptable mock replacing fixed-behaviour fakemcp. Stage 1 (`cli.Run`, PR #2714) is already on main.
