body:
## Summary

`validateNewAction` (pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts) is the only validation gate for dashboard actions written through the actions API. For the two date fields it checks nothing but `Number.isNaN(Date.parse(x))`:

- `payload.until` — actions.ts:229-232 (`payload.until must be an ISO date/time`)
- `payload.proposalUpdatedAt` — actions.ts:292-296 (same pattern)

V8's `Date.parse` does not refuse impossible calendar days — it normalizes them. Verified on the laptop (node v24 / bun, same engine family as the aggregator runtime):

```
Date.parse("2026-02-30")            = 1772409600000 = 2026-03-02T00:00:00.000Z
Date.parse("2026-02-29")            = finite (2026-03-01; 2026 is not a leap year)
Date.parse("2026-04-31T00:00:00Z")  = finite (2026-05-01)
Date.parse("2026-13-01")            = NaN (only the month range is checked)
```

So the check catches a bad month and garbage, but an impossible day passes, and the string is stored **verbatim** (`payload.until = until`, actions.ts:231).

## Verified repro (this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-actionuntil/probe.ts` (bun, importing the real `validateNewAction` from `src/actions.ts` and `cardState` from `src/card-state.ts`; laptop clone `~/git/code` at main `e6577a96`, all five involved files md5-identical to origin/main):

```
validate until=2026-02-28 -> OK (stored as "2026-02-28")
validate until=2026-02-29 -> OK (stored as "2026-02-29")   ← 2026 has no Feb 29
validate until=2026-02-30 -> OK (stored as "2026-02-30")   ← impossible day
validate until=2026-04-31 -> OK (stored as "2026-04-31")   ← April has 30 days
validate until=2026-13-01 -> ERR payload.until must be an ISO date/time
validate until=not-a-date -> ERR payload.until must be an ISO date/time

cardState at 2026-03-01T12:00Z with until=2026-02-28 -> suppressed: null     (control: snooze over)
cardState at 2026-03-01T12:00Z with until=2026-02-30 -> suppressed: "snoozed" (still hidden on Mar 1)
```

The consumer side is `cardState` (src/card-state.ts:75): `Date.parse(snooze.payload.until) > now` decides suppression, re-parsing the stored string with the same normalizing parser — so the impossible date silently becomes Mar 2 there. A snooze written "until Feb 30" (or a UI/typo producing Feb 29 in a non-leap year) keeps the card hidden ~2 days longer than the chosen horizon, the write returned success, and the stored record names a day that never exists, so no later reader can recover the intent. `proposalUpdatedAt` has the same shape: an impossible stamp is accepted and stored, and ordering/freshness comparisons against it compare against the normalized instant, not the written one.

## Why it matters

- This is the write-path gate for user-facing dashboard actions; a wrong-but-plausible date is exactly the input a strict validator exists to catch, and the failure mode is silent (success response, wrong behavior days later).
- The codebase already has the strict primitives and the precedent: `validate.ts` `parseIsoDate`/`isIsoDate` (real-calendar-date check, #2264/#2577) are used by `feed.ts` and `snapshot-records.ts` (`freshestDate`: "an impossible date like 2026-02-30 … must not win"). `actions.ts` is the remaining Date.parse-only gate on this surface.
- Sibling snapshot-gate findings (#3379, #3365) cover the snapshot pipeline; this is the distinct actions/card-state path — the persisted action log and live card suppression, not snapshot history.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `validateNewAction` refuses a `payload.until` or `payload.proposalUpdatedAt` whose calendar day does not exist (e.g. `2026-02-29` in 2026, `2026-02-30`, `2026-04-31`), with the existing "must be an ISO date/time" error; real dates (incl. `2024-02-29`) still pass, as do full ISO datetimes for real days.
- [ ] The validation uses a real-calendar check consistent with `validate.ts` (`parseIsoDate` semantics for the date part), not `Date.parse` alone.
- [ ] Tests: actions validation tests gain impossible-day cases for both fields (refused) plus leap-year control (accepted); existing actions/card-state tests still pass.
- [ ] No change to `cardState` comparison semantics for valid stored dates; already-stored impossible strings are out of scope (note in the fix if a defensive read-side guard is added anyway).

Filed by new-issue-creator-code-a (lane A), run 2026-11-01. Evidence probe: `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-01-laneA-actionuntil/` on the laptop.

body:
## Problem

PR #2886 (#2080) returns `-32042` to a 2025-11-25 host while the broker **keeps** the pending URL questions and the original ask call stays alive (triage-settled design on #2080: no Abandon; the host completes the elicitations out of band and retries, mirroring the spec flow and the client-side flow of #2079).

Codex review on #2886 (P1, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/ask.go`) points out the asymmetry this creates in mcpx's suspended-call architecture:

- When the out-of-band flow completes, `OnElicitationComplete` (`internal/daemon/hooks.go`) answers the broker question, so the **original** upstream invocation resumes and can complete the operation.
- The host's retry after `-32042` reaches `beginAsk`, which calls `Ask.Begin` again — there is no `requestState` or other retry correlation in the 2025-11-25 error — so the retry starts a **second** upstream invocation.
- For a non-idempotent operation, both executions can run.

A spec-shaped `-32042` server has ended its invocation when it returns the error; mcpx has not, so the spec's retry model does not by itself prevent double execution here.

## Scope / acceptance

- Decide and implement a correlation or prevention mechanism, e.g. join-on-retry in the daemon asker (a retry whose method+params match a live/completed ask with answered URL questions reattaches to that call instead of `Begin`-ing a new one), or another mechanism that preserves the settled "broker keeps the questions" behaviour.
- A test proving: host retries after out-of-band completion → the upstream operation executes exactly once (or the retry is answered from the original call's outcome).
- Non-idempotent pass-through calls are the case that must be safe; document what a host that retries *before* completion gets.

## Origin

Codex P1 finding 4429651482 on PR #2886, dispositioned there as: real, but a design-level change beyond #2080's triage-settled scope (settled triggers + no-Abandon). Tracked here so the merge of #2886 does not silently ship it.

## Acceptance criteria

- A host retry after a `-32042` response whose out-of-band elicitations have completed does NOT start a second upstream invocation: it reattaches to (or is answered from) the original call, so a non-idempotent operation executes exactly once — proven by a test.
- A retry that arrives before completion has documented, tested behaviour (no silent double execution).
- The settled #2080 behaviour is preserved: the broker keeps the pending questions and no Abandon is introduced.
- CI green on the PR that implements this, including the new exactly-once test.

body:
Phase 1 of design #2434 (mcpx error honesty, finished). Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-error-honesty.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. The decisions are recorded on #2434; this phase implements its first slice.

## Scope

One structured error carriage through the gateway, so a peer's error reaches the client as that peer's error, and mcpx's own errors are recognisably mcpx's:

- The daemon `/v1` call reply gains a structured upstream-error field (code, message, data), populated whenever the pool/client layer holds a real JSON-RPC error from the upstream. Today the failure is flattened to text (`internal/daemon/routes_proto.go` `ToolFailure` path) and `internal/cli/serve_ask.go` (~L225-255) rebuilds an `UpstreamError` by guessing at that text, with one structured special case (-32021, serve_ask.go:241).
- The gateway/MCP path consumes the structured field and relays it verbatim via the existing `UpstreamError` mechanism (`internal/mcpserver/capability.go`). The text-reconstruction heuristics are deleted for any reply carrying the structured field; they remain only as fallback for replies that don't (older daemon / non-JSON-RPC failure). The daemon batch path's text-only `isError` surfacing is in scope where it carries the same replies.
- mcpx's OWN locally-minted errors (its -32602 name checks, -32603 internal failures, policy refusals) go through one minting helper that stamps `error.data` with the origin marker `"mcpx": {"origin": "local"}` (merged into any existing data). Peer errors are relayed untouched and never gain the marker.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A pass-through upstream error and the same error via the gateway (`mcpx_call`) reach the client with identical code, message and data — pinned by a parity test
- [ ] An upstream -32021 relayed through the gateway keeps its `data.requiredCapabilities` intact without the serve_ask special case
- [ ] Every error mcpx mints itself on the MCP surface carries the origin marker in `data`; no relayed peer error carries it
- [ ] Replies without the structured field (older daemon shape) still surface as before via the text fallback
- [ ] Tests run via CI per fleet policy (no builds on the sandbox)

Out of scope: the dispatch gate (Phase 2), -32021 production (Phase 3), any change to which errors mcpx mints — only their carriage and marking.

## Acceptance criteria

- Daemon `/v1` call replies carry a structured upstream-error field (code, message, data) whenever the pool/client layer holds a real JSON-RPC error from upstream.
- The gateway/MCP path relays that structured error verbatim via the existing `UpstreamError` mechanism; the text-reconstruction heuristics are deleted for replies carrying the field and remain only as fallback for replies without it.
- Tests cover the structured relay end-to-end, the no-field fallback path, and the existing -32021 special case behaving identically through the structured path.

body:
Follow-up from the capability taxonomy v0 investigation (#2027, record: `doc/2026-10-29T14-05-00Z_investigation_capability_taxonomy/`, PR #2337).

## Goal
`loc.*` capabilities — `loc.position` (one-shot) and `loc.watch` (subscription with an interval floor) — with an accuracy ceiling, and the consent seam they exercise.

## Scope
- Reading carries `{lat, lon, accuracy_m, fix_age_ms, source}`; `source` ∈ `gnss | network | ip | caller_supplied`, never silently degraded.
- Precision ceiling: the device's `outside_ceiling` + `precision_ceiling` reason. An imprecise fix must be refusable rather than plausible-looking.
- Sensor caps are **not wildcard-grantable** — refine the existing grant ledger so `*` never reaches `loc.*`.
- Consent: `cap_denied` + `consent_required` / `os_permission_denied`; withdrawal arrives as `{"cap":"loc.watch","event":"revoked","reason":"consent_withdrawn"}` and closes the stream.
- `no_fix` on `failed` when there is no sky view.

## Acceptance
- Both names in CATALOG with providers; tests for precision-ceiling refusal, wildcard-not-reaching, and an open `loc.watch` receiving a revocation event.
- Documented interval floor and battery note for long watches.
- Per-platform: browser geolocation, phone tiers, ESP32 GNSS.

## Out of scope
Geofencing, trail history, reverse geocoding, any persistent location store.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] loc.position and loc.watch are in CATALOG with providers; readings carry {lat, lon, accuracy_m, fix_age_ms, source} with source in gnss|network|ip|caller_supplied, never silently degraded
- [ ] Tests cover: precision-ceiling refusal (outside_ceiling + precision_ceiling), wildcard grants never reaching loc.* in the grant ledger, and an open loc.watch receiving the consent_withdrawn revocation event and closing
- [ ] Consent refusals use cap_denied + consent_required / os_permission_denied; no_fix on failed when there is no sky view
- [ ] Documented interval floor and battery note for long watches; per-platform notes (browser geolocation, phone tiers, ESP32 GNSS)

body:
Follow-up from the capability taxonomy v0 investigation (#2027, record: `doc/2026-10-29T14-05-00Z_investigation_capability_taxonomy/`, PR #2337).

## Goal
`form.*` capability plus a `Form` `WorldSurface` variant: structured input (`text`, `choice`, `number`, `date`, `confirm` fields + actions) that each device renders with its own trusted widgets — never program-supplied HTML/CSS/validation code.

## Scope
- Caps `form.present`, `form.result`, `form.cancel`. A presented form answers later as an event (`form.result` `{form_id, action, values}`), because the human may answer after the request's connection is gone.
- Bounds: field set and payload share `MAX_ARGS_BYTES`; the response obeys `MAX_EVENT_BYTES`.
- Closed field set with declared minimal device requirements, because a rotary-encoder ESP32 can only do choice-from-list and number. `text_entry:"none"` in the device manifest gates what a device may be asked for.
- Validation is the program's job on the result; a rejected value is `bad_args` + `field_invalid`, re-presented — no server-side retry loop.

## Acceptance
- Catalog names added; `kind: form` parses with a validated field/action model; a test asserts oversize forms are refused and a result event validates.
- Text projection of a form (lines + numbered actions) exists per #2027's text-only rule.
- No HTML/CSS/escapes reachable from a form document.

## Out of scope
Layout engine, focus model, multi-form composition, styling beyond semantic tokens.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Catalog names form.present / form.result / form.cancel added; `kind: form` parses with a validated closed field/action model (text, choice, number, date, confirm)
- [ ] A test asserts oversize forms are refused (field set + payload share MAX_ARGS_BYTES; responses obey MAX_EVENT_BYTES) and a result event ({form_id, action, values}) validates
- [ ] Text projection of a form (lines + numbered actions) exists per the #2339 text-only rule; device gating via the #2338 manifest (e.g. text_entry:"none") is honoured
- [ ] No HTML/CSS/escapes reachable from a form document; rejected values surface as bad_args + field_invalid with re-presentation, no server-side retry loop

body:
Implements §5.1–§5.2 and §7.2 of the #2025 review-loop design (`files/review-loop-design-2025.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace, linked from #2025).

**Scope**
- Add `second_pass` to the `repo-task/v1` packet kind enum (`pr_shepherd | triage | small_fix | ci_investigation` today — verified 2026-10-29).
- Add the `review` payload block (verdict, verdict_note_url, artifact, pass, pass_cap, gap_list, goal_context_refs, producer, route_floor); `gap_list` and `verdict_note_url` required for kind `second_pass`.
- Validation rejects a `second_pass` packet with `pass > pass_cap` — the termination cap is enforced in the enqueue code path, not by reviewer restraint.
- New deterministic dedupe family: `repo-health:v1:second-pass:<repo>:<issue>:pass-<n>` (one live packet per artifact+pass by construction).
- Queue result outcome `superseded_by_second_pass` / `second_pass_complete` recognised in result validation if it validates outcomes.

**Acceptance**
- [x] `repo-queue.py validate` accepts a well-formed `second_pass` packet and rejects: missing gap_list, missing verdict_note_url, pass > pass_cap
- [x] A second enqueue for the same (issue, pass) collides on the dedupe key
- [x] Existing kinds validate exactly as before (regression: run the current packet corpus through validate)

body:
Implementation follow-on from the #2140 triage (queue task 3169, 2026-10-29). Parent design: #2140 (snapshot schema + supervision gating recorded there); fleet epic: #2055; conductor: #2153.

Two parts, independently landable — do Part 1 now; Part 2 is gated and must not be half-started.

**Part 1 — per-lane handoff snapshots (no gate).**
1. Add a snapshot step to every queue-lane shift body (all `repo-queue-worker-shift*` jobs, all four pilot queues): at exit, after the signal refresh, the lane writes `hidden_files/lane-handoff-<queue>-<lane>.json` with the schema from #2140 (generated_at, queue health counts, worked list with terminal states + PR links, in-flight claims with PR/CI pointers, infra notes with first-seen times, next-task leads). Overwrite in place; one file per lane, no history accumulation.
2. Add the read step: a shift reads its own lane's snapshot after the Step 0 gate, treats every entry older than one cadence or contradicted by a fresh check as a lead only, and re-verifies consequential facts (claims, CI, labels) exactly as today — the snapshot replaces *search*, never *verification*.
3. Measure: daily token check-in reports per-lane input/run for the two weeks after landing vs the 6–13M check-in #5 range; success = median shift input/run down with tasks/shift held or rising.

**Part 2 — supervision mode (GATED, do not start until both hold).**
Gate: (a) the session conductor (#2153) is cut over, and (b) session↔task binding is recorded on queue tasks (a claimed task names its OpenCode session id in progress). When both hold, file the activation as a fresh follow-on from #2140: lanes batch-supervise 15–20 dispatched sessions per shift (checkpoints, stall nudges via the conductor's ladder, hand-backs) instead of executing tasks directly, and only then evaluate the 40m → 2h cadence change — a rate change, which needs Drew's explicit word even then, with before/after tokens-per-completed-task from the daily check-in as the evidence pack.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Snapshot write + read steps present in all lane shift bodies; schema matches #2140
- [ ] One evidenced handoff: a shift starts from the previous shift's snapshot and its report names what the snapshot saved vs re-verified
- [ ] Two-week input/run comparison posted on #2140 (Part 1 success test)
- [ ] Part 2 gate state recorded on #2140 (binding present or not); no supervision-mode or cadence change made under this issue

Parent: #93

## Summary

The simple, explicitly requested issue: **review all existing tests, set up the fuzz framework, and write its policies** -- i.e. execute #121-#124 in the smallest useful slice. Three deliverables: an inventory of the 735 tests (at 05c78b2; which become generators, which hide time/randomness/ports, which are flake-prone), the seed helper + wrapper + first generator landed, and the policy text handed to #99.

## Original notes

> - testing
>   - agents should make at least 1 simple, new test for every bug observed from any source, when cheap to do so-- aggresively test many permutations. 
>     - you can absolutely rely on fuzzing anywhere you can fit it and you should whenever you can-- but you _must_ use a single seed per-run to generate all inputs. (this could eventually be discussed with careful consideration.) it should be appended into a test tracking structured file in the repo and it can be committed. ideally main branch commit's seed or pr merge seed should make it back into file eventually. to prevent churn, maybe ci appends the seed into a gha var (race/overwrite risk?), or attached as artifact to each workflow in init job before tests begin-- a collector job can scoop them up sometime later. once a day/week/on-release/every-100-commits. im thinking touch tests/seeds/<seed> or uv has a seed generate job. anyways ci it should end up in that dir, then as an artifact if gha and main branch, then passed into the test matrix. if uv test without arg- warn, generate and write it yourself pass it to all tests, if some other testing method there should not be a static seed, throw for empty or setup should make the seed. avoid changing how seed generates data. im not sure if a convenient uuid with time, v7?, is valid, but as long as its enough entropy whatever works. either put nothing in their or compact json, consider seeds/v1/id/<first 2 char>/<seed><--symlink: seeds/yyyy/mm/dd/<seed> avoiding conflicts is important.
>       - think a hack job of antithesis/tigerbeetle. this is the primary testing method is throw insane amount of variations. if something is found outside this system and a test that could have had missed it, make a different generator that uses the same seed and makes an infinite amount of things matching the offensive shape.
>         - make a simple issue for reviewing all tests, setting up framework and policies for the fuzz.

## Current state (initial inventory from `rg`, re-counted at 05c78b2 -- the review deepens it)

| Package | Tests | Generator candidates | Hidden time / randomness / ports |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `internal/e2e` | 209 | `exec.flagset` (from the `TestEveryExecFlagChangesSomething` table, `e2e_test.go:2877`), `api.v1request` (`v1ops_test.go:287`) | `time.Sleep`/`time.Now` polling loops in `e2e_test.go`, `v1ops_test.go:420-429`, `consumer_test.go:286-358` (60 s/30 s waits), `proto_test.go:411-426`. Daemon leaks are fixed (#182: `stop --all` cleanup, 60 s idle exit, guarded by `TestEnvCleanupStopsTheDaemonItStarted`, `e2e_test.go:2630`); `testsupport` still never removes its `mcpx-bin-*`/`mcpx-fake-*` temp dirs (`internal/testsupport/build.go:27,57`) |
| `internal/config` | 66 | `config.layers` (merge/scope: `merge_test.go:42-157` are hand-picked layer stacks) | none seen |
| `internal/mcpserver` | 45 | request shapes | `server_test.go:621-632` polls with 2 s deadlines and 20 ms sleeps |
| `internal/codegen` | 42 | `codegen.jsonschema` (`codegen_test.go:16-50` is one schema per test) | none |
| `internal/logging` | 35 | redaction inputs (`redact_test.go` table) | `file_test.go:45-138` build timestamps from `time.Now().Truncate(time.Hour)` -- check for hour/day-boundary sensitivity |
| `internal/settings` | 28 | `settings.precedence` (`registry_test.go` already iterates the registry) | env reads |
| `internal/launcher` | 25 | `launcher.template` (`define_test.go`, `template_test.go`) | none |
| `internal/pool` | 21 | -- | `pool_test.go:423-424` sleeps 50 ms then `ReapIdle(time.Now())`: timing-dependent; `ReapIdle` already takes `now` as a parameter, so a fixed clock is a one-line change |
| others (22 packages) | 264 | parsers: `openapi`, `searchpath`, `artifacts/name`, `diagnose` | `tasks_test.go:16` sleep, `elicit`, `mcpclient/modern_test.go` |

Totals: 9 test files call `time.Sleep`, 14 call `time.Now`; at least 9 files use `[]struct` tables (37 match a looser table/range pattern); no `t.Parallel()` anywhere; network use is unix sockets and `httptest` (`daemon/routes_resolve_test.go`, `openapi`, `registry`), plus the stub registry in e2e after #65.

## Plan (small steps; each a PR)

1. **Inventory**: finish the table above for every package as a checklist in this issue (or `docs/testing/inventory.md` if #99 picks a docs home). Per test file: *generator candidate* / *hidden time* / *hidden randomness* (production code mints ids with `crypto/rand` in `pool`, `tasks`, `elicit`, `artifacts`, `mcpserver`, `logging/trace`, so outputs differ per run; flag any test that asserts on them) / *flake-prone* (sleep-then-assert) / *fine*. No rewrites in this step.
2. **Seed helper + wrapper** (#121 option C): `internal/testsupport/seed` (`Rand(t, gen)`, failure reproduce line, CI fail-closed), the wrapper recipe, `.gitignore` for `.cache/test-seed/`. Unit-test the helper itself (derivation is stable: golden root/stream for a test-vector id).
3. **Registry + first generator** (#123 option C, #124): `internal/testsupport/gen` with `Source`, `bytesSource`, golden-output guard, and **one** generator. Proposed first: `launcher.template` or `codegen.jsonschema` -- pure functions, fast, rich shapes. Plus its `Fuzz*` twin with a small seed corpus.
4. **CI init job** (#121 section 7): mint + artifact + `MCPX_TEST_SEED` on the test step; coordinate the edit with #95 (who owns the workflow).
5. **Policy text** handed to #99 (which owns where it lives and the per-bug-test policy): the rules below.
6. Fix the two cheapest flake-prone spots found in step 1 (e.g. `pool_test.go:423` with a fixed `now`), as proof the inventory pays.

Deferred to follow-ups: remaining generators from #124, the collector (#122), soak fuzzing (#95).

## Proposed policy text (for #99 to place)

- Every random input in a test comes from `seed.Rand(t, ...)`. No `math/rand` top-level functions, no `time.Now().UnixNano()` seeds, no `crypto/rand` for test data. (A guard test can `rg` for these in `_test.go`.)
- Never hard-code a run seed. Test vectors inside generator golden tests are the only fixed keys.
- Run tests through the wrapper; in CI a missing seed is a failure.
- A failing seeded test is reported with its seed and reproduce command; do not re-run to green without recording the seed (#122 keeps failing seeds).
- Changing a generator's output means bumping its version.
- When a bug escapes, add the regression test and answer "which generator could have caught this?" (#124 escape loop).

## Approaches

No real three-way choice: the user asked for one simple issue that executes the designs. The one judgement call is order -- **inventory first** (read-only, cheap, informs which generator goes first) vs **helper first** (unblocks everyone). Proposed: helper and inventory in parallel, since neither depends on the other; first generator after both.

## Open questions

- Inventory as an issue checklist (cheap, dies with the issue) or a committed doc (maintained, discoverable)? Defer to #99's decision on where testing docs live.
- First generator: `launcher.template` (smallest) or `codegen.jsonschema` (highest yield, needs one `deno check`)?
- Guard test banning unseeded randomness in `_test.go`: now, or once the first generators exist?

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** S-M (inventory S, helper S, registry + first generator S-M) · **Impact** high (turns the design into something every later test uses)
**Depends on / related:** #121, #122, #123, #124, #126; #99 (policy home, per-bug test, flake policy), #95 (CI init job), #52 (closed, fixed in #182; the leftover temp dirs are a #129 guard candidate), #65, #35.

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria

- An inventory of the existing tests (735 at 05c78b2) is recorded: which become generators, which hide time/randomness/ports, and which are flake-prone.
- The fuzz framework's first slice is landed via PR: the seed helper, the wrapper, and the first generator.
- The fuzz policy text is written and handed to #99 (linked here).
- The work described in the Summary/Scope above is delivered via a branch + PR (no direct push to main); verification runs in GitHub Actions CI, not on the sandbox.
- Evidence (CI links and the inventory location) is recorded on this issue before it is closed.

## Summary

Where opencode's and Cloudflare's code modes are ahead of mcpx on script ergonomics: every result is typed `any` although `outputSchema` is parsed; stdout is returned whole with no cap; a snippet's value must be printed or emitted (the final expression is not the result); failures are an `error` string plus exit code rather than typed kinds; in-script `search()` has a limit and no offset; and search does not cover saved scripts.

Found while writing the comparison register (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/`) and checked against the code at `05c78b2`. Each row below links its register entry, which carries the value, effort, risk, the specification text and every source.

## Register rows

| row | difference | mcpx @ 05c78b2 | effort |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [CODE-44](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-44-return-types-generated-from-a-tools-outputschema) | Return types generated from a tool's `outputSchema` | ✗ — parses `outputSchema`; every result typed `any` | S |
| [CODE-16](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-16-cap-on-the-size-of-returned-output) | Cap on the size of returned output | ✗ — stdout returned whole; only stderr is bounded | S |
| [CODE-19](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-19-final-top-level-expression-becomes-the-result) | Final top-level expression becomes the result | ✗ — result is stdout, `emit()` or a default export | M |
| [CODE-30](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-30-failures-reported-as-typed-kinds) | Failures reported as typed kinds | ✗ — `error` string, `exitCode`, `timedOut` only | M |
| [CODE-35](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-35-in-program-search-pages-its-results) | In-program search pages its results | ✗ — `search(query, limit = 20)`, no offset | S |
| [CODE-36](https://github.com/dezren39/nix/blob/main/pkgs/mcpx/docs/compare/register/code-mode.md#code-36-in-program-search-also-finds-saved-snippets) | In-program search also finds saved snippets | ✗ — in-script `search()` covers tools only | M |

## What to do

Each is independent. Typed results from `outputSchema` and an output cap (a setting) are the two with the most value.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M · **Impact** med · **Related**: #79 (typecheck default), #109 (search), #175

## Acceptance criteria

- Tool results in mcpx exec scripts are typed from the tool's `outputSchema` instead of `any` (CODE-44).
- Returned stdout is capped at a documented size with a visible truncation marker (CODE-16).
- A snippet's final expression is its result — no `print`/emit required (CODE-19).
- Failures surface as typed error kinds, not only an `error` string plus exit code.
- In-script `search()` supports offset paging and covers saved scripts.
- Tests cover each behavior above.

Relocated from dezren39/nix#109 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #176

## Summary

`mcpx search` is substring scoring. It fails on typos and on any query whose words share no substring with a tool name or description — which is most of how a person asks for something. "Natural language processing search" is the ask; the useful reading of it is a staged ladder where each rung is cheap, deterministic and independently shippable, and only the last rung needs a model or an index.

## Original notes

> - better natural language processing search

## Current state (what mcpx does today, with file refs)

`Registry.Search` (`internal/daemon/registry.go:392`, cited at 05c78b2) lowercases the query, splits it on whitespace and scores every tool with `rank` (`:423`):

| match | score |
| --- | --- |
| tool name equals the term | 100 |
| tool name has the term as a prefix | 60 |
| tool name contains the term | 40 |
| the `ns.func` path contains it | 30 |
| the namespace contains it | 20 |
| the description contains it | 10 |

Every term must match; when all-terms returns nothing the whole query is retried any-term (`:402-407`), which is what makes `mcpx search screenshot click` return both tools rather than neither. Results are sorted by score then function name, `InputSchema` is nulled out to keep the payload small (`:454`), and `-n` caps at `search.limit` (default 20). Documented in `docs/story.md` §Search.

Three other rankers already exist and are deliberately not this one:

- **`mcpx catalog`** ranks by *cost* (`len(line)/4`), not relevance, and `--bias <query>` promotes signatures matching a query ahead of the cost order (`docs/ideas.md` §Catalogue, items 9–10). That is the only place a query already bends a non-relevance ranking.
- **Recipe matching** (`internal/recipes`, from #41) scores a free-text request against a recipe's name, summary, placeholder names and the tools it calls, and refuses to choose when the leader is not ahead by `recipes.matchMargin` (`docs/consumer.md` §3). No model, no embedding, no index — that was the point of it.
- **`GET /v1/registry/search`** (`internal/registry/registry.go:153`) searches the *public* registry for servers that are not configured yet. Different corpus, different question — and the registry matches server *names* only, as a substring (`:147-150`), so a sentence finds nothing there.

`docs/proposals.md` §"Better tool search" already proposes tags → typo tolerance → concept similarity, in that order, and recommends stopping after typos to reassess. This issue agrees with that ordering and fills in what "concept similarity" would actually cost.

## Approaches

### Approach A — least recommended: embedding search over the tool catalogue

Embed every tool's name + description at catalog load, embed the query, rank by cosine similarity. This is what "NLP search" sounds like it means and it is the worst first move here.

- It needs a model. Either a local one (a download, a runtime dependency, a per-platform build problem in a Go binary that currently has none) or a remote one (an API key, latency on every search, and a network dependency on a command whose whole value is that it is instant). mcpx's stated position is that it has no model of its own and `docs/consumer.md` §"The concerns from the issue" says the configured-provider option "was not built and should not be" — see #110 for why that position is now worth revisiting, but it is still a heavy thing to take on *for search*.
- It needs a cache keyed on the catalog fingerprint, and `internal/codegen`'s fingerprinting plus the `cacheVersion` trap already documented in `docs/consumer.md` §"Bugs found on the way" says cache invalidation here is a live source of silent wrongness.
- It is non-deterministic across model versions. The same query returning a different tool after an upgrade is a support burden for a command people use in scripts.
- The corpus is tiny. A typical mcpx catalogue is tens to low hundreds of tools with one-line descriptions. Embeddings earn their keep on large corpora of prose; here the recall problem is vocabulary, not semantics.

### Approach B — middle: lexical NLP, no model

Everything a classical IR pipeline does that needs no learned parameters, applied to the existing scorer:

1. **Tags.** `"tags": ["browser", "visual"]` on a server entry in `config.Server`/`Extras` (`internal/config/config.go:90-128`, beside the existing `description`, `prelude`, `tools`, `excludeTools`), matched at a score between name-prefix and name-contains, plus `mcpx search --tag browser` as an exact filter. This is the only rung that lets a config author *fix* a bad match without touching the upstream server, which makes it the highest-value one regardless of what else lands. Tags should also feed `mcpx ls` and `catalog --bias`.
2. **Stemming and normalisation.** Split `take_screenshot` and `takeScreenshot` into `take` + `screenshot` so the term `screenshots` matches, and fold a light English suffix stemmer (Porter, or a hand-written -s/-es/-ing/-ed rule set, which is ~30 lines and covers the tool-name vocabulary) over both sides. Today `screenshots` scores zero against `take_screenshot` on the name and only hits the description if the word happens to be there.
3. **Typo tolerance.** Levenshtein ≤ 2 against tool and namespace *names only*, applied after exact scoring returns nothing, scored below every exact tier. Names are short and few — this is microseconds over a few hundred strings with no index. **The matcher itself is #186's (#181 collision 6):** mcpx already has two near-miss implementations that disagree on transpositions (`internal/diagnose/diagnose.go:417-455`, `internal/launcher/template.go:341-381`), and #111's rung 1 needs a third. #186 defines the distance, the normalisation (including step 2's word-splitting) and the threshold once; this issue calls it and owns only where a typo match ranks. The Levenshtein ≤ 2 figure here is input to #186, not a separate definition.
4. **A synonym table.** A small curated map shipped in `internal/defaults` (`screenshot`/`capture`/`image`, `query`/`search`/`find`, `issue`/`ticket`, `delete`/`remove`/`rm`), overridable from config so a user can add their own vocabulary. This is the honest, cheap version of "concept similarity": it buys most of the recall for none of the dependency, and it is inspectable, which an embedding is not.
5. **Field weighting and phrase scoring.** IDF-ish weighting so a term appearing in half the catalogue (`get`, `list`) contributes less than a rare one, and a bonus for terms appearing adjacent in the description. BM25 over name/description/tags is roughly 100 lines and removes the need for the hand-tuned constant table entirely.
6. **A better fallback than all-terms/any-term.** The current binary fallback throws away the information that three of four terms matched. Score partial matches with a per-term coverage multiplier instead, so a tool matching 3/4 terms outranks one matching 1/4 without needing a second pass.

All of it is deterministic, dependency-free, testable with table tests, and works the same in `search`, `catalog --bias` and recipe matching — which matters, because three rankers drifting apart is how "why did it find that" becomes unanswerable.

The risk is that steps 4–5 are tuning, and tuning without a corpus of real queries is guessing. Ship a `mcpx search --explain` that prints the per-term, per-field score breakdown first, so a bad result is diagnosable rather than mysterious.

### Approach C — recommended: B as a staged ladder, plus one AI rung that is explicitly *not* on the hot path

Do Approach B, in the order `--explain` → tags → normalisation/stemming → typo tolerance → synonyms → BM25, reassessing after typo tolerance exactly as `docs/proposals.md` recommends. Most "I could not find the tool" reports are vocabulary problems and tags plus synonyms fix vocabulary directly.

Then add one model-backed rung, deliberately shaped so it cannot become a dependency:

- **It is a separate command/parameter, not a mode of `search`.** `mcpx search` stays instant and deterministic forever. The model-backed path is reached by asking for it (`--semantic`, or `POST /v1/intent` which already exists and already does exactly this job — it ranks the catalogue for a request and returns candidates).
- **It reuses the AI layer rather than owning a model.** Whatever #110 lands — sampling through the broker, a configured provider, or the opencode v2 plugin's `ctx.generate.text` — search calls *that*, with the same off-by-default posture `prompt.sample: never` already has.
- **The right model job here is query expansion, not ranking.** Ask for synonyms and likely tool-name fragments for the query, then run the *deterministic* scorer over the expansion. That keeps ranking explainable, keeps the result cacheable by query string, makes the model failure mode "no expansion, normal search" rather than "no results", and lets a successful expansion be written back into the synonym table — which is how rung 4 gets curated for free instead of by hand.
- **Offline embeddings stay an option, not a default.** If a corpus ever gets large enough (hundreds of servers, or searching the public registry rather than the local catalogue), `mcpx search --index` building a persisted embedding index over the *registry* corpus is a reasonable later step. The local catalogue is not that corpus.

Recommended because it delivers the user's actual complaint — search does not understand how I ask — in increments that each work on their own, with no new runtime dependency, and because it keeps the one property `mcpx search` has that a semantic search does not: the same query gives the same answer, every time, for free.

One correction to the framing: "natural language processing" for a catalogue of a few hundred short identifiers is mostly *tokenisation and vocabulary*, not semantics. The word-splitting and synonym rungs are where the wins are; the embedding rung is the smallest win per unit of cost, which is the opposite of the order it is usually attempted in.

## Open questions

- Should tags live on the server entry only, or per-tool? Per-tool needs a map in `Extras` and gives config authors a way to tag a tool the server named badly, which is the common case.
- Should `--explain` be a flag or a `plumbing` output mode? The settings registry already has a `plumbing` concept (`internal/settings`).
- Does recipe matching adopt the same scorer, or stay separate? One scorer is better; recipe matching has a margin rule (`recipes.matchMargin`) that tool search does not want.
- Should `mcpx search` also search the public registry when the local catalogue returns nothing ("you do not have a tool for this, but this server exists")? That bridges to #115 and risks a network call on a local command — probably a flag.
- Is there a corpus of real failed queries anywhere? `/v1/log` records calls; it does not obviously record searches. Logging query + whether the caller then called a tool from the results would give a relevance signal for free.

## Ease · Impact · Related

**Ease** M (S for tags + typos alone; M for the full lexical ladder; L if the semantic rung is included) · **Impact** high — search is the entry point to zero-context discovery, and a miss there costs an agent a full catalogue load.

**Depends on / related**: `docs/proposals.md` §"Better tool search", `docs/ideas.md` items 9–12, #186 (owns the near-miss matcher step 3 calls — #181 collision 6), #41 (closed, fixed in #58: recipe matching, `/v1/intent` — the semantic rung reuses both), #79 (faster CLI/exec — search must stay instant), #110 (the only place a model may come from), #111 (rung 1 shares #186's matcher), #115 (a search miss is its feedback record).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

body:
Relocated from dezren39/nix#93 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): mcpx's single source lives in developing-today/code (pkgs/mcpx); re-home tracked at #309. Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

Parent: #91

## Purpose

Randomised testing for mcpx, under one rule taken from the notes and treated as non-negotiable: **one seed per run generates every input**. A run that fails can then be replayed exactly from a single value, and a failure that cannot be replayed is a bug in this tree rather than a fact of life.

This is the branch #91 says must land **first**. Every other testing tree can be built in any order and repaired later; the mapping from a seed to the data it produces cannot. Change it after seeds exist and every recorded seed silently stops reproducing what it recorded, with nothing failing to tell you. So the format, the derivation and the engine are decided here before the first randomised test is written.

Starting point, re-checked at 05c78b2: **there is nothing**. 735 `func Test*` across 64 files and not one `Fuzz*`, `Benchmark*`, `testing/quick`, `rapid`, `math/rand` or `t.Parallel()` in the tree. That is an advantage -- there is no existing randomness to migrate and no recorded seed to invalidate.

Two of these children exist because the user asked for them by name:

- **#125** -- "make a simple issue for reviewing all tests, setting up framework and policies for the fuzz."
- **#126** -- "we aren't shooting for deterministic execution to start, maybe we should but no ... separate simple issue for considering both those things." It is explicitly **not a plan**; it is a record of an aspiration, kept so that the option is not lost and not mistaken for a proposal.

What this tracker does **not** own: when an agent is obliged to write a randomised test, and the rule that every bug gets a test -- those are policy, and belong to #99. The CI job graph that the seed's `init` job plugs into belongs to #95 (#135). The feature inventory those generators aim at belongs to #97.

## Children

- [ ] #121 mcpx testing: one seed per run -- format (UUIDv7), derivation, and how it reaches every test
- [ ] #122 mcpx testing: seed store layout and collector (file per seed, artifact + scheduled collector)
- [ ] #123 mcpx testing: choose the generator engine for one run-wide seed (native fuzz, testing/quick, rapid, hand-rolled)
- [ ] #124 mcpx testing: bug-shape generators -- registry, versioning, budget, first shapes
- [ ] #125 mcpx testing: review all tests, set up the fuzz framework and its policies
- [ ] #126 mcpx testing: deterministic execution as a long-term aspiration (retrofit vs Rust rewrite)

## Proposed order

1. **#121 and #123 together.** The seed's format and derivation, and the engine that consumes it, are one decision viewed from two sides -- Go runs one test process per package, so how a single run-wide value reaches every generator depends on what the generator is. Settle both before writing any randomised test.
2. **#125.** Audit the 735 existing tests and stand up the helper and the corpus layout the earlier two decided. This is what turns the design into something the next test can use.
3. **#122.** The seed store and its collector. Needs #121's format, and needs #95's `init` job (#135) to exist before the artifact path is real. The collector's commits must not re-trigger `mcpx.yml` (its `push.paths` covers `pkgs/mcpx/**`; see #122 step 6).
4. **#124.** Bug-shape generators, once there is an engine and a framework to hang them on. This is the ongoing work: each escaped bug adds a generator for its shape.
5. **#126.** Any time, or never. It gates nothing.

**Hard ordering constraint:** nothing in #95, #97 or #99 may introduce a randomised test before #121 and #123 are decided.

## Children -- ease and impact

| # | Title | Kind | Ease | Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| #121 | one seed per run -- format, derivation, delivery | design | S (~150 lines helper + wrapper; ~20 lines of CI) | **high** -- every randomised test depends on it |
| #122 | seed store layout and collector | design | M (~80-line collector workflow, record schema, guard test) | med -- logs reproduce for 90 days without it; the store is what makes seeds durable |
| #123 | choose the generator engine | research | S (the research is the deliverable; gates #124/#125) | **high** -- fixes the shape of every generator |
| #124 | bug-shape generators -- registry, versioning, budget | design | M (registry + guard S; each generator S-M) | **high** -- the notes call this the primary testing method |
| #125 | review all tests, set up the framework and policies | review + implement | S-M (inventory S, helper S, registry + first generator S-M) | **high** -- turns the design into something every later test uses |
| #126 | deterministic execution / Rust -- **not a plan** | research | S to record; C incremental S per seam; B L-XL; A XL, not planned | low now, med long-term |

## Warnings carried by this tracker

- **A sixth direct Go dependency is not free.** `pkgs/mcpx/package.nix:36-53` opens with a comment headed "Five direct Go dependencies." that names and defends each, and states everything else is standard library. A test-only library still lands in `go.mod`'s direct block, changes `vendorHash` (`package.nix:54`), and becomes a Renovate bump that the existing repair step in `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml` has to service. Adopting `pgregory.net/rapid` means editing "Five" to "Six" with a paragraph as good as the one sqlite got. #123 weighs this explicitly.
- **Go's native fuzzing mutator is not seedable**, so "one seed per run" and `go test -fuzz` are not the same mechanism and cannot be made the same by wishing. #123 has the detail.
- **`-shuffle` interacts with ordering, not with membership.** A shuffled run and a seeded run are different kinds of reproducibility; #130 and #139 both touch this.
- **The seed variable is an undeclared `MCPX_*` read.** #172 (in flight) is about to ban `os.Getenv("MCPX_*")` outside the settings package except for an allowlist. `MCPX_TEST_SEED` (#121) needs an entry there, or the test helpers need to be out of that guard's scope.
- **Not every escaped bug has an input shape** (#124's escape loop, from its addendum): #65 needs a hermeticity guard and #35 an environment axis, not a generator. Classify first, so that a generator that cannot reach the bug is not counted as coverage.

## Related

#91 (parent), #95 (the `init` job that mints the seed; #135), #97 (what the generators aim at), #99 (when an agent must write one; #129 for bugs that need a guard, not a generator), #127 (do not run the full suite to find out; since #182 fixed #52 the reason is time), #172 (seed variable vs the undeclared-`MCPX_*` guard), #65, #35, #74/#75, #102, #106, #108 (the escaped bugs that motivate generators).

Security/auth deferred; see tracker.

## Acceptance criteria
- A fuzz/property test suite for mcpx exists in the repo, runs in CI with exactly one recorded seed per run, and a failing seed reproduces the failure deterministically.
- Coverage targets from the issue are met or explicitly re-scoped with the reason recorded on this issue.

Relocated from dezren39/nix#976 on 2026-10-28 (placement audit): laptop backup coverage gap; the fix is written in the laptop-backups modules whose canonical home is code after the #1043/#1740 relocation (same evidence as #1026). Original body below; issue references inside it are historical (dezren39/nix numbering).

## Gap (backup audit, 2026-10-27): laptop non-git data has no routine backup

Verified on the laptop (amd-6) on 2026-10-27:

- The only routine backup mechanisms on the laptop are two systemd user timers created recently, and **neither has ever fired**: `dashboard-backup.timer` (daily 04:30, first run 2026-10-28) and `repo-archive-backup.timer` (daily 05:15, first run 2026-10-28). The restic 3-backend pattern (local + R2 + Google Drive) built for `~/repo-archive` is good — it just covers exactly one tree, and is unproven.
- Everything else non-git on the laptop is single-copy on the laptop disk: docker volumes for pm-stack/Grist/Pad (filed separately in developing-today/code), `~/atlas` (8.3 GB incl. the v3 embedding DBs), `~/.local/state/opencode`, `~/secrets/*.sops.yaml` (one .bak sibling from 2026-10-24), and `~/backups` itself (the dashboard archives land there; their off-machine leg is a sandbox cron that has also never run yet).
- There is no full-system backup: the Backblaze personal backup for this laptop is still a drafting goal (~$3.48/mo, awaiting Drew), not a running system.
- Git clones are the healthy exception: fleet primaries are pushed to GitHub; at audit time `~/git/code` and `~/code` each had 4 dirty files (known quota-gatherer WIP) — small, named exposure only.

### Acceptance
- The laptop's non-git state set (at minimum: `~/.local/state`, `~/backups`, docker volume data or its dumps, `~/atlas` canonical copies) is covered by a routine backup with an off-machine leg, reusing the existing restic pattern rather than a new tool.
- The coverage survives the in-flight NixOS migration: services being authored as NixOS modules should declare their state dirs so the backup set follows the services, not hand-maintained paths.
- First scheduled runs are verified, and a freshness check exists so a stopped backup gets named.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An inventory exists on this issue (or a linked doc) of the laptop's non-git data classes (app databases, browser profiles, SSH keys, password vaults, at minimum) with a backup decision for each.
- [ ] Every class decided "back up" has a restic (or equivalent) routine covering it that runs on a schedule without manual steps, and its snapshots are visible in the timer/repository listing.
- [ ] At least one restore from the new routine is performed and recorded (a backup that has never been restored does not count).
- [ ] Classes decided "do not back up" are named with the reason, so the gap is a decision, not an oversight.

body:
## Finding

PR #1242 ("OpenClaw secrets via sops-nix (bws mirror)", commit 259363f5) is MERGED, but its change is **not on main** and nothing consumes it:

- #1242's base was the feature branch `feat/openclaw-summarize`, not `main`. Its merge commit 53ebc06e is verified NOT an ancestor of `origin/main` (checked 2026-10-27, main at a120b9a9), and `nixos/hosts/amd-openclaw-secrets.nix` does not exist on main.
- The stranded branch is otherwise clean: `git diff origin/main...origin/feat/openclaw-summarize --stat` is exactly #1242's change — 3 files (`nixos/hosts/amd-openclaw-secrets.nix` +22, `nixos/hosts/default.nix` +1, `secrets/sops/common/bws.yaml` re-sync). The branch tip IS the #1242 merge (2026-10-27 01:25 CDT) and there is no open PR from it to main. (The later "rescued" PR #1490 preserved only unrelated uncommitted gateway/QUOTAS edits from that worktree — not this change.)
- The follow-up #1242's body explicitly promised and deliberately excluded — "A tiny follow-up then points home/openclaw wrapper environment paths from ~/.secrets/openclaw/* to /run/secrets/openclaw/*" — has not happened either: on current main, `home/openclaw/default.nix:21` and its `environment` block (line ~80) still read the gateway token from `~/.secrets/openclaw/gateway-token`, no file on main references `/run/secrets/openclaw`, and no issue tracks the follow-up (searched: "openclaw sops", "openclaw-summarize", "1242"; general git-hygiene issue #1371 does not name this branch or PR).

## Why it matters

The sops-nix declarations for `openclaw/gateway-token`, `openclaw/slack-bot-token`, and `openclaw/slack-app-token` are dead config sitting on an unmerged branch: a system activation from main will never materialize `/run/secrets/openclaw/*`, and the gateway keeps depending on manually created `~/.secrets/openclaw/*` files — exactly the unmanaged state #1242 set out to replace. Because the PR shows as "merged", the work looks done; it is not.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Land #1242's change on main (PR from `feat/openclaw-summarize` — its diff to main is only the 3 files above — or an equivalent cherry-pick), with CI green.
- [ ] Repoint the `home/openclaw` wrapper environment paths from `~/.secrets/openclaw/*` to `/run/secrets/openclaw/*` for the gateway token (and wire the Slack bot/app tokens the same way if the gateway config consumes them), per #1242's stated sequencing: only after the sops secrets materialize on activation.
- [ ] Verify an activation on amd materializes `/run/secrets/openclaw/{gateway-token,slack-bot-token,slack-app-token}` (owner user, mode 0400) and the gateway starts reading the token from the new path.
- [ ] Delete or retire the stranded `feat/openclaw-summarize` branch once its change is on main.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #1242 (batch watermark 1074→1242, developing-today/code).

body:
Design doc: `files/designs/code-mcpx-tasks-one-store.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Register: central potential-projects list, same workspace (`files/potential-projects.md`).

**Framing (recorded by the design architect):** no `user/review` — the roadmap row sits at `proposed` and states the intent, SEP-2663 dictates the wire shapes, and the one-store rule is the codebase's own stated design (`internal/tasks/tasks.go` header: "Two stores would be two sets of expiry bugs"). This design completes recorded intent; it does not open a new direction. Two judgment calls are recorded in the design doc: the `/v1` operator surface keeps its unscoped view of the shared store, and the client phase is `required`-only.

## Summary

dezren39/nix#209 charged that mcpx advertises the 2026 tasks extension and the 2025-11-25 core `tasks` capability while implementing only the legacy shape, with tasks unbound, split across two stores, and unusable as a client. Most of that charge has since been answered in code (audit in the design doc: era-gated advertisement, flat `Task` + `ttlMs`/`pollIntervalMs`, `DetailedTask`, `tasks/update` + `inputRequests`, per-era cancel semantics, `related-task`, requestor binding, -32021 refusals, `notifications/tasks`). Two structural items remain — the two halves of the same complaint that **tasks are not one thing in mcpx yet**:

1. **Two store instances (nix#209 TASK-27, TASK-20).** One store *type* (`internal/tasks.Store`), two live instances: the MCP server lazily creates a private in-memory store (`internal/mcpserver/tasks.go` `tasks()` → `tasks.New()`; field at `internal/mcpserver/server.go:273-274`, no injection seam), while the daemon's `/v1` creates a separate SQLite-backed store at `<state>/tasks.db` (`internal/daemon/ops.go:436-453`, also used by `routes_proto.go`, `routes_exec.go`, `input_required.go`). A task started over MCP is invisible to `/v1` and vice versa, and every MCP task dies with the process. The conformance register says it plainly (`internal/conformance/coverage_stateful.go:112`, gap `ext-tasks-durable-before-response`): "the task store is an in-memory map; a task does not survive the daemon."
2. **The client cannot execute a task-required call (nix#209 TOOL-21 client half, CAP-26 client direction).** `mcpclient` carries `execution.taskSupport` raw (`internal/mcpclient/client.go:171-174`) but never reads it, never declares the tasks extension upstream, and `CallTool` (`client.go:1164`, called from `internal/pool/pool.go:1051`) is a plain `tools/call`. An upstream tool declared `taskSupport: "required"` cannot be called the way its server demands — and downstream, mcpx's own working server-side task machinery starts tasks whose body is exactly this call, so the failure surfaces inside mcpx's tasks.

A third, lesser item: the conformance register (`docs/compare/register/tasks.md`, CAP rows in `capabilities.md`) still marks landed behaviour ✗ — nix#209 cannot honestly close until it tells the truth.

**Proposal:**

- **One store, injected.** `mcpserver.Server` gains a task-store seam; the daemon constructs its store once and hands it in where the server is built (`internal/cli/serve.go:474`, `App.MCPServer()` — which already wires `Notify`, `Passthrough`, `Timing`). Standalone embeddings (`internal/cli/adapter.go:195`, `openapi.go:90`) keep a private in-memory store: no second surface, no state dir. MCP ownership/visibility semantics unchanged (owner map stays in `mcpserver`); `/v1` keeps its operator view; one `PollInterval` source (settings, at construction — today the two stores read different settings); restart story is the store's existing one (`tasks.Open` reloads rows and reaps a non-terminal row to `Failed` — "daemon restarted before task completion", `internal/tasks/tasks.go:243-249`).
- **A client that can run a task-required call.** `mcpclient` executes `taskSupport: "required"` calls as upstream tasks, per upstream era (`Client.Era`): legacy — `params.task`, poll `tasks/get`, outcome via `tasks/result`; modern — declare `extensions["io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks"]` at initialize, flat `Task` result, poll `tasks/get` (`DetailedTask` inlines the outcome). Honour poll interval and TTL; context cancellation sends `tasks/cancel`. `"optional"` stays a plain call; an upstream task parking in `input_required` returns a distinct named error (relaying is an open question, below).
- **Register truth-up + origin closure.** Rows rewritten to as-built with evidence, landed Gap entries retired, roadmap row updated, completion evidence posted on dezren39/nix#209 and the origin issue closed from this repo (the set handling recorded for nix#254 in design #1481 — no duplicate filed).

Alternatives (argued in the design doc): merge the other way (/v1 proxies the in-memory store — throws away durability); keep two stores and synchronise them (the exact expiry-bug duplication the package header warns against, plus sync bugs); stop advertising tasks on MCP until unified (punishes a working, conforming surface); mark `required` tools uncallable (silently shrinks the gateway's catalogue); task-augment `optional` tools too (changes pooled-call latency fleet-wide for no correctness gain).

Risks: semantic leakage across the merge (`/v1`-started tasks carry no MCP owner — legacy MCP list requires an owner match so they stay invisible; Phase 1 tests pin it); the PollInterval unification silently changing one surface's cadence if the wrong setting wins; polling cost for fast `required` tools (bounded by the upstream's own poll interval); non-conforming legacy upstreams (a malformed task response must be a call error, never a hang — pinned by test).

## Phased breakdown

- **Phase 1 — one durable store across MCP and /v1.** Store seam on `mcpserver.Server`, daemon constructs once and injects, single PollInterval source, cross-surface + visibility + restart-durability tests, conformance gap `ext-tasks-durable-before-response` retired. Filed as a sub-issue of this issue.
- **Phase 2 — client task execution for `taskSupport: "required"`.** Per-era augmentation, polling, cancel propagation, fault surfacing in `mcpclient`; modern initialize declares the extension; fake-upstream tests for both eras. Independent of Phase 1. Filed as a sub-issue of this issue.
- **Phase 3 — register truth-up + nix#209 closure.** Register rows to as-built, Gap retirements, roadmap row, origin closure with evidence. Gated on Phases 1–2. Filed as a sub-issue of this issue.

### Open questions (NOT filed; stay as questions)

- Operational limits (gaps `tasks-rate-limit`, `tasks-resource-limits`): per-requestor concurrency cap, maximum TTL, tasks/* rate limit — policy values, not just mechanism.
- Cooperative cancel (gap `ext-tasks-cancel-cooperative`): let work reach its own terminal status instead of forcing `cancelled`?
- Task audit logging (gap `tasks-audit`): tie creation/completion/retrieval into the lifecycle-event stream?
- Failed-task `statusMessage` for isError results (gap `tasks-failed-status-message`); documenting id-only reachability of unbound modern tasks (gap `tasks-document-unbound`).
- Task ID entropy (nix#209 TASK-23): `NewID` is 64 random bits (`internal/tasks/tasks.go:344-348`) and modern tasks are unbound by design — raise to 128?
- Client input relay: answer an upstream task's `inputRequests` by relaying to the downstream client and replying via `tasks/update`? (Phase 2 returns a named error instead.)
- `tasks/get`-implies-list asymmetry (gap `tasks-get-implies-list`): document or change?

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Phases 1–3 are filed as sub-issues of this design (done at filing time) and land.
- [ ] One `tasks.Store` instance serves MCP and `/v1` in the daemon; MCP tasks survive a daemon restart to the store's existing semantics; gap `ext-tasks-durable-before-response` is retired.
- [ ] A pooled call to an upstream `taskSupport: "required"` tool completes through the upstream's task machinery in both eras (legacy `params.task` + `tasks/result`; modern extension + `DetailedTask` polling).
- [ ] `docs/compare/register/` tells the truth about tasks, and dezren39/nix#209 is closed with evidence from this repo.
- [ ] A completion note is posted on this issue; the open questions above remain recorded here as questions, not silently dropped.

## Gap found by the #1078 Phase 11 claimed-done audit (slice 5, coverage gaps)

**F11.10 (large-module split, #808) has no regression-catching automation for its exit criterion.**

Exit criterion (`.opencode/plans/phase-11-foundations.md`): "No file over 2,500 lines of production code; full suite passes unchanged; diff shows moves only."

Verified on current main `95cd41f0` (2026-10-27, #1078 audit slice 5):

- The criterion **holds today**: scanning all `.rs` files under `pkgs/` + `apps/` (production lines = lines before the first `#[cfg(test)]`), the largest production source file is `pkgs/id/src/cli.rs` at 2,200 prod lines, then `web/routes.rs` at 2,141 — no `src/` file is over 2,500.
- But **nothing enforces it**: `git grep` for `2500` / `2,500` across `pkgs/id` and `.github` finds no check (only crash-corpus data rows); the fast-lane check list (`.github/scripts/id-pr-checks.txt`, 26 checks) contains no file-size check; no test, lint, or flake check counts lines. The audit's verification was a one-off manual scan (slices 2 and 5 of #1078) — the next 2,500-line file would land silently and F11.10 would regress exactly the way F11.4 did (#1401).
- (For the record: the largest `.rs` file overall is the integration test `pkgs/id/tests/cli_integration.rs` at 4,312 lines — test code, outside the criterion's "production code" wording; splitting it is optional and not what this issue requires.)

## Acceptance criteria

- An automated check runs in the fast lane (a flake check added to `.github/scripts/id-pr-checks.txt`, or an equivalent test) that fails when any production `.rs` file under `pkgs/id/src` (and any other tree the F11.10 criterion is read to cover) exceeds 2,500 production lines, naming the offending file.
- The check passes on current main and is demonstrated to fail on a synthetic over-limit file (or an equivalent unit test of the checker).
- The check is named in the F11.10 row of the Phase 11 records so the next audit finds enforcement, not just a manual scan.

body:
## Problem

`project-reconcile.sh` (org Project #4 "Developing Today" sync, orchestrator is single writer per #910 Stage 4) computes ALL proposals over the full ~200-item Project before writing anything. The proposal computation does not finish inside the run's time budget, so passes die with **0 Project writes**:

- 2026-10-27 07:41Z pass — ended incomplete at 540s timeout mid-list; which MOVE writes completed is unverified.
- 2026-10-27 08:12Z pass — exit 124 at 240s, 0 writes (report: `reconcile-2026-10-27-0812.txt`, header + KEEP lines only).
- 2026-10-27 08:43Z pass — interrupted during proposal computation, 0 writes (`reconcile-2026-10-27-0843.txt`, header only).
- 2026-10-27 11:14Z pass — dry-run timed out at 240s after proposing on only ~20 of 200 items; `--apply` not attempted because it would time out identically.

Four consecutive incomplete passes. The Project board drifts behind actual issue/PR states until this lands.

## What works today

The bounded inline pass (2026-10-27 06:23Z) applied 14 updates successfully by working a bounded slice instead of the whole list. The very first Stage 4 pass (2026-10-26) also completed when the Project had 27 items — the approach does not scale to 200.

## Fix

Make the bounded pass the standard path in `project-reconcile.sh`:

- Process items in bounded batches (e.g. oldest / most-blocked first, within the existing ~25-update cap), writing each batch before computing the next.
- A pass that hits its time budget must leave the writes it completed applied and reported — never all-or-nothing.
- The run report must state exactly which writes completed, so the next pass can resume instead of re-deriving state.
- Keep the existing rules unchanged: label-gated auto-add (now/next/epic), status sync signals, single-writer discipline, no new Project fields.

## Acceptance

- A full pass over the ~200-item Project completes within the orchestration run's budget, or completes a bounded batch with applied writes and a precise resume point.
- Two consecutive orchestration passes run with no incomplete-reconcile flag in the run log.

body:
## The gap (found in fleet review, 2026-10-27)

The babysitter (`openchamber-babysitter`, every 20m) watches OpenCode/OpenChamber sessions: verdicts, stall detection, nudges. But the fleet's *other* working sessions — the cron agent runs themselves (lane shifts, producers, monitor, steward, dispatcher) — have no real-time watcher at all.

What covers them today: the fleet monitor's hourly reconciliation, which finds claim evaporation after the fact (labels repaired, handoffs posted), and the lane gate/lock discipline. On 2026-10-26 that meant evaporation on the opencode/openchamber queues was discovered up to an hour late — task 1149 (#530) burned multiple attempts before its final one died at 7/7 — and several shift reports never arrived in chat at all (now tracked as the certification problem, #1131). Detection latency, not detection absence, is the gap.

## Scope (assess, then build or formally accept)

- Assess a lightweight run-watch for cron executions: a run sitting in its execute phase far beyond its job family's p90 duration (baselines exist in run history) gets flagged within ~20 minutes — e.g. a small periodic check over scheduler run state, or a heartbeat convention lane runs touch at checkpoint time that a watcher can staleness-test.
- The watcher's output should be the same shape as the monitor's repairs (flag + evidence), just faster; intervention stays with the existing owners (monitor repairs, lanes re-claim).
- Alternatively, if the assessment shows the hourly bound is acceptable — e.g. because migration 0012 + lane discipline made evaporation cheap and rare — record that reasoning here with the evaporation census numbers that support it, and close this as a documented acceptance.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An assessment exists (comment on this issue) with run-duration baselines per job family and the observed detection latencies for the 2026-10-26 evaporation cases.
- [ ] Either a run-watch mechanism is built and demonstrated flagging a stale run inside ~20 min, or the hourly bound is explicitly accepted with the supporting numbers recorded.
- [ ] The decision is reflected in the babysitter/monitor instruction files (who watches what, at what latency).

body:
## Finding

PR #1022 (merged, merge commit 76672b97df023607d8469d462f21420604fe92d5) preserves spaced link/image destinations by swapping each one for a deterministic placeholder before rendering and restoring it afterwards with a global string replace over the whole rendered document:

`pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` (current main):
- `:1100-1103` — placeholder is `format!("idweb-spaced-destination-{}-placeholder", substitutions.len())`, derived only from the substitution index; nothing checks whether that token already occurs in the document.
- `:1070-1072` — restoration is `output = output.replace(&placeholder, &format!("<{raw}>"))`, which replaces EVERY occurrence in the rendered markdown, not just the destination the renderer emitted.

## Why it matters

If the document's own text (or a code block, or another non-spaced destination) literally contains `idweb-spaced-destination-0-placeholder` and the document also has a spaced link/image destination, the save direction rewrites the document's own text into `<the spaced destination>` — silent content corruption on save, in the same codec family as the %20 mutation #1022 set out to fix. The token is fixed and guessable, so the collision does not require exotic input for anyone documenting this codec. The tests added by #1022 cover destinations, titles, and editor hrefs, but not a document that already contains the placeholder token. Verified still present on current main (2026-10-27).

## Evidence

- PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/1022 — `fix(id-web): preserve spaced link/image destinations in angle form on save (#1019)`
- `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:1081` `substitute_spaced_destinations` — no scan of existing document text/URLs before choosing tokens
- `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs:1070-1072` — global `str::replace` restoration
- Dedup: #1019 (closed) was the %20 rewrite itself; no open or closed issue mentions the placeholder collision.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Placeholder tokens are chosen so they cannot collide with content already in the document (e.g. scan the AST's text/literal/url content and keep extending/randomizing the token until it is absent), OR restoration is scoped to the rendered destination positions instead of a global replace.
- [ ] Regression test: a document containing the literal current token text plus a spaced link destination round-trips with the literal text unchanged and the destination in `<...>` angle form.
- [ ] Existing #1019 tests (spaced link, spaced image, title, editor href) still pass and round-trips remain fixpoints.

body:
Found during the 2026-10-25 NixOS switch (generation 504, built from main @45c817e0).

**Symptom 1 — declarative commandcode-proxy unit crash-loops (stopped manually after 59 restarts):**
```
commandcode-proxy.service: Unable to locate executable '/nix/store/3gy9alpqrmkvyvjz8x34fwh1knq3dycl-bin/commandcode-proxy-start.sh': No such file or directory
Main process exited, status=203/EXEC
```
The `-bin` store copy contains only **16 files** — exactly the bin/ tree of the old main (e18acea8 era). It is missing every bin file added Oct 24–25: commandcode-proxy.mjs/.test.mjs/-start.sh, claude-code-proxy.*, muse-proxy-start.sh, proxy-relay.mjs, proxy-supervise.*. The ExecStart in home/common/default.nix is `${../../bin}/commandcode-proxy-start.sh`, and the file IS in the repo (100755, verified via git ls-tree) and in the flake source export (25 files in bin/).

**Symptom 2 — OpenChamber's managed opencode is still 2.0.30+e7baa0d** after the switch, even after killing it so OpenChamber respawns it (new port, same old store path), while /run/current-system (gen 504) ships 2.0.30+954ff7c.

**Deterministic, not a switch-time race:** building `nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` from a clean checkout of current main (and from ~/code) reproduces the running toplevel bit-for-bit (2lrvq0pi…), stale -bin included. So somewhere in the eval graph the home layer (home/common and friends) is sourced from a tree that predates the Oct 24–25 bin additions, even though lib.from-root resolves to inputs.self.outPath and the flake source export itself is complete.

**Impact:** low right now — the proxy-supervisor's transient fps-commandcode-proxy unit serves :18748 (HTTP 200 verified), and the background opencode service (which does serve the new build + the opencode-go-* instances) is unaffected. But the declarative unit cannot take over until this is fixed, and the managed server will not pick up new opencode builds.

**Pointers for whoever digs in:** check how home-manager.users.user is assembled for amd (nixos/hosts/amd-krdp.nix, nixos/home/default.nix) and whether any input or module list pins a second copy of this repo at an old rev; compare `nix flake metadata` source bin/ (25 files) against the -bin path baked into the built unit (16 files).

## Acceptance criteria

- The root cause of the stale home-layer source tree is identified and named (which input/module pins the pre-Oct-24 tree), not just worked around.
- A clean-checkout build of `nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` produces a `-bin` store copy containing the full current `bin/` tree (including commandcode-proxy-start.sh and claude-code-proxy.*).
- After a switch, the declarative `commandcode-proxy` unit starts without 203/EXEC and serves on its registered port.
- OpenChamber's managed opencode picks up the current build after a switch/respawn (version/rev matches the system profile).

body:
Follow-up to #863 (which made the `desktop-commander` entry portable).

The same portability wart remains for two other entries in the tracked project config `.mcpx.json`:

- `codedb`: `command: "/home/user/bin/codedb"`
- `fff`: `command: "/home/user/.local/bin/fff-mcp"`

These absolute paths only resolve on machines whose home is `/home/user`. Because mcpx **project scope overrides user scope**, a machine with a different home directory cannot shadow them with working user-level entries — the broken project entries win and the servers fail to start.

Observed on the Muse sandbox (home `/home/hatch`), merged project view via `mcpx status`:

- `server "codedb": start /home/user/bin/codedb: fork/exec ...`
- `server "fff": start /home/user/.local/bin/fff-mcp: fork/exec ...`

Possible directions (not prescribed): portable `npx`-style commands like the rest of the file where a published package exists, a PATH-relative command name, or an env-substituted path if mcpx config supports it. Any change should keep the laptop (home `/home/user`) working unchanged in behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `codedb` and `fff` entries in the tracked `.mcpx.json` no longer hard-code `/home/user` absolute paths; they resolve on machines with a different home directory (verified on the Muse sandbox, home `/home/hatch`, via `mcpx status` with no fork/exec errors for these servers).
- Behavior on the laptop (home `/home/user`) is unchanged: both servers still start and respond.
- The chosen mechanism (PATH-relative name, published package command, or env substitution) matches the portability approach already used for the `desktop-commander` entry in #863.

## What and why

Route builder and moderator authority through the session frames. Today the install and revoke frames do not carry a builder or moderator actor. Phase 12 (PR #801, F12.3) added the `BUILDER`/`MODERATOR` scope bits, `invite --role builder|moderator`, and the journal-only audit entries `BuilderInstalled` and `Revoked { by }`. But every caller passes `by: None`, so in practice a builder cannot install and a moderator cannot revoke over the wire, and the audit entries never appear. PR #801 lists "F12.3 install/revoke frame wiring" as remaining, and no issue tracks it.

## Source

- [Phase 14 plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/.opencode/plans/phase-14-close-out.md): F14.6 (PR #834)
- [Phase 12 plan](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/.opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md): F12.3
- PR #801 body, "Remaining Phase 12": "F12.3 install/revoke frame wiring"
- Epic #534, D1-021

## Current status

**Partial.** `pkgs/id/src/world/handle.rs:489` (`revoke` → `revoke_by(participant_id, None)`) and `:648` (`install_program` → `install_program_by(..., None, ...)`) are the only callers of the `_by` variants outside tests. `world/actor.rs:1192-1195` journals `BuilderInstalled` only when an actor is passed. The session code in `world_session/` never passes one.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The install-module frame accepts a participant holding `BUILDER` and passes the actor to `install_program_by`
- [ ] The revoke frame accepts a participant holding `MODERATOR` and passes the actor to `revoke_by`
- [ ] Over a real session (not the handle API), a builder installs, a moderator revokes, and a plain guest is refused for both with the documented F11.13 code
- [ ] Each use is journaled with its actor (`BuilderInstalled`, `Revoked { by }`)
- [ ] Builder still receives no network, file, or process authority (test)

## Size

M

## Prerequisites

- #227: F11.12 journal format version (Phase 14 F14.1). `BuilderInstalled` is a new entry type, and it must be covered by the version contract before it is produced in practice.
