title: mcpx testsupport builders leak build temp dirs in packages without a sweeping TestMain
body:
## What leaks

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/testsupport` builders (`MCPXBinary`, `FakeMCPBinary`, `EraMCPBinary`, `TaskMCPBinary`, `AskMCPBinary`) each create a temp dir (`mcpx-bin-*`, `mcpx-fake-*`, `mcpx-era-*`, `mcpx-task-*`, `mcpx-ask-*`) and register it for the suite-wide sweep (#1971 remainder item 2). Only `internal/e2e` has a `TestMain` that calls `SweepBuildTempDirs`. The other consuming packages — `internal/daemon`, `internal/pool`, `examples` — never sweep, so every test run of those packages leaves its build dirs behind in $TMPDIR.

Measured on the laptop (2026-11-13/14): dozens of `mcpx-bin-*` dirs in ~/tmp and ~/.local/share/opencode/tmp, ~788 MB each. The size is mostly a cold Go build cache: `buildEnv` pins GOCACHE/XDG_CACHE_HOME inside each build temp dir, so every test binary also pays a full cold build of all dependencies.

A standing laptop scratch sweep (nixos/home/laptop-scratch-sweep) reaps /tmp/mcpx-bin-* older than 24h, but the dirs land in the test process TMPDIR (~/tmp for lane runs, opencode tmp for opencode-spawned runs), which that sweep does not watch for this pattern.

## Fix

- Give the non-sweeping consuming packages a TestMain that runs the suite sweep, via one shared testsupport helper mirroring e2e semantics (remove this binary's registered dirs; fail on processes still executing from them).
- Pin the testsupport build cache to a fixed testsupport-chosen location under the real user cache dir instead of inside each build temp dir: still never caller-controlled (the guard-test property buildEnv exists for), but warm across test binaries, and a leaked dir then holds only the ~57 MB binary.

## Verify

Run the affected packages' tests and confirm no new mcpx-* dirs remain in TMPDIR afterwards.

body:
## Finding

PR #4320 ("repo: preserve backup residue and guard snapshots (#3151)") removed 34 tracked residue files from HEAD. One of them is a real EC private key:

- Path: `doc/2026-10-11T03-44-33Z_design_groups_events_delegation/spikes/s11-relay/certs/live/leaf.key.bak-20261011T122827Z`
- The PR diff deletes a complete `-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----` block (P-256 key, 241-byte blob, git blob `9e3731643df1fb4ecb412e620f4d6e3144c8d8e4`).

Removing a file from HEAD does not remove it from git history, and this repository is **public** (`private=false, visibility=public`, verified via `gh api repos/developing-today/code` at review time). The key is still retrievable from history: the file is present at pre-merge main `b8bbe734` (contents API returns blob `9e3731643d…`, size 241) and absent on current main (404). PR #4320's body treats history retention as an acceptable two-way door for the residue set as a whole, but no issue records a disposition for the one actual credential in the set; source issue #3151 (closed) describes the 34 files as backup/config residue and does not mention a private key.

## Mitigating evidence (verified during review)

The matching leaf certificate (deleted in the same PR, `leaf.pem.bak-20261011T122827Z`, decoded with openssl):

- Subject `CN = localhost`; SAN `DNS:localhost, IP Address:127.0.0.1`
- Issuer `CN = s11 test CA 1` (a local test CA for the s11-relay design spike)
- Validity 2026-10-11 12:14:53 UTC → **2026-10-14 12:14:53 UTC — expired over a year ago**

So this is very likely a dead, localhost-only spike key. What is missing is the verification and the recorded disposition, not an emergency rotation.

## Why it matters

A private key in a public repo's history must be treated as disclosed until someone verifies it protects nothing: that nothing still trusts the `s11 test CA 1` chain, that the key pair is not reused by any live relay/cert elsewhere in the fleet, and that the spike is fully retired. Until that check is recorded, every future residue/history cleanup will re-litigate the same question from scratch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Verify nothing in the fleet (any of the four repos, laptop primaries, deployed services) trusts or references the `s11 test CA 1` / s11-relay spike certificates; cite the searches run.
- [ ] Verify the leaf key pair is not reused anywhere else (compare the certificate's public key against certs/keys in the repos and config; the private key itself must NOT be copied into any issue, comment, or file).
- [ ] Record the disposition on this issue: either (a) accepted — expired localhost test key, history retention is fine, with the verification evidence above; or (b) escalate to Drew for a history purge / further action, with the blast radius of a public-repo history rewrite stated.
- [ ] If (a), close with the evidence; if (b), apply `user/escalated` and surface it — the purge decision is Drew's.

Found by: pr-diff-review of PR #4320 (merge commit `930235d0de7d007eba0ed3d0576f32a8f571981f`, ancestor-verified against main). Cross-checked: secrets scan of all 15 PR diffs in the 2026-11-15 13:24 CST batch found this key as the only credential-shaped material, and only in deletions.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

Codex P2 on merged PR #10190: `pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py` computes a complete repaired `statusTransitions` map (`healed`) but never persists it. Its heal UPDATE uses nested `jsonb_set` calls on the three expected keys only, so (a) if an integration lacks `statusTransitions` entirely, the nested calls cannot create the missing intermediate object and the guard detects drift but never repairs it, leaving Kaneo's documented `done` fallback active on every subsequent run; and (b) additional forbidden transitions that were removed from the computed `healed` map remain in the database despite the `HEALED` message.

> "If an integration lacks `statusTransitions`, these nested `jsonb_set` calls cannot create the missing intermediate object, so the guard detects drift but never repairs it, leaving Kaneo's documented `done` fallback active on every subsequent run. The UPDATE also ignores the computed `healed` map, so additional forbidden transitions removed from that map remain in the database despite the `HEALED` message. Write the repaired map at the top-level `statusTransitions` path and verify the full invariant afterward."
> — chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-14T17:03:15Z

## Evidence

- Source PR: #10190 "pm-stack: close authority — sync guard + design record (#10136)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/10190 (merged 2026-11-14T17:04:11Z, merge commit 69094106299007c76df9e7b07497fb169e5cacd9)

title: atlas/fleet-search: server.rs copies are over the 2500 production-line limit (2509 / 2501) — #10419 used the last 108 lines of headroom and production-line-guard is red on main

labels.name: kind/refactor
labels.description: Code restructuring with no behavior change

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## What's wrong

`bash .github/scripts/check-production-line-limit.sh` fails on current main HEAD `73ae4d58dc2b4268ab8acbf8fe69ea2ca4a59092`:

```
::error::OVER LIMIT pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs: 2509 production lines (limit 2500)
::error::OVER LIMIT pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs: 2501 production lines (limit 2500)
::error::OVER LIMIT pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/mod.rs: 2559 production lines (limit 2500)
production-line-guard: FAILED
```

`production-line-guard` is red on main. Only the `id-worlds/world/mod.rs` line is tracked (#10430). These two `server.rs` copies have **no split issue and no grandfather entry**, so they are unfiled red lines in a main-tier push check.

## Cause

`637e29c982` (#10419, "feat(atlas): feedback capture surfaces — API, CLI, UI contract (#9976)", merged 2026-11-15T03:13:54Z) added 232 lines to each of the two `server.rs` copies (`git show --numstat 637e29c982`: 232/3 for both). Counting with the guard's own production-lines awk at the parent commit `3a74be0236`, both copies were **2392** production lines — 108 lines of headroom left — and are now **2509** (atlas-search, +117, 9 over) and **2501** (fleet-search, +109, 1 over).

CI evidence:
- Last completed `production-line-guard` run `43655150992` (head `66d8a319`, 2026-11-14T23:49:35Z) FAILED on `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/mod.rs: 2559`; the two `server.rs` entries were not over the limit at that commit.
- Every later guard run is still `queued` (9 consecutive push runs from 01:05Z to 08:35Z; repo-wide queue saturation is tracked by #2605), so the `server.rs` overflow has no CI verdict yet. The moment a runner picks up the next guard run it reports all three files.

## Why it matters

- Under `.github/ci-policy.md`, main push CI is the post-merge merge evidence for main; `production line guard` is a listed main-tier workflow. A permanently red guard erases that evidence for every merge.
- The two copies must stay byte-identical (`check-fleet-search-parity.sh`, #5433/#5920), so the split has to be mirrored in both crates, not just atlas-search.
- The untracked overflow also interacts with the parity fix for the missing trace capture (separate issue #10445): mirroring that adds ~30 production lines to the fleet copy, taking it to ~2531, so the split should land first or in the same PR.

## Suggested fix shape

The mirrored `// ---- feedback ----` sections are self-contained and identical in both copies — `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs:2189-2238` and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs:2181-2230` (types + JSON plumbing; the two route arms are in the routing section near `:2387-2428` / `:2379-2420`). Extracting them into a sibling `feedback.rs` in each crate (mirroring atlas-core's `feedback` module) removes roughly 50-60 production lines per copy and brings both to ~2450, with headroom for the trace-capture mirror. Splitting the `// ---- job store ----` section (`:911-1950`) is the larger alternative.

If a grandfather entry is preferred instead, the guard's convention requires one entry per path with a linked split issue, and the entry is deleted in the PR that lands the split.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `bash .github/scripts/check-production-line-limit.sh` prints no `OVER LIMIT` line for `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs` or `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs` (the only remaining failure, if any, is the `id-worlds/world/mod.rs` line tracked by #10430).
2. No new parity divergence: `bash .github/scripts/check-fleet-search-parity.sh` reports only the pre-existing drift tracked by #10445 — if a new module file is added, add it to the parity guard's pinned file list (`check_pair` calls) and its contract tests in the same PR.
3. `cargo test -p atlas-search -p fleet-search` stays green, including the #9976 feedback route tests (`POST /v1/feedback`, `GET /v1/feedback?query_id=`).
4. `bash .github/scripts/check-production-line-limit.test.sh` still passes (the "every grandfather entry names an existing file" contract included).

- `opencode.drewrypope`
- `opencode.popesdrew`
- `opencode.developing-today-0`

— but none of them is registered in the attribution the AI Plans & Usage Space is built from: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-extract.ts` (`POOL_SPECS` / `SHELL_POOLS`) and `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts` (`GO_*`/`OPENAI_*` split service-id constants, `CANONICAL_PROVIDER_IDS`). The Space therefore has no registered pool for these measured meters (the same defect class that hid the third Go account before #7835).

Found by the standing Plans Space freshness keeper (hourly check 2026-11-15T08:23:40Z).

## Evidence

Record: `generatedAt 2026-11-15T08:15:07.851Z`, `source opencode-quota`, heartbeat `ok`.

Measured rows (all `state: ok`):

| providerId | measuredAt | 5h resetsAt | weekly | monthly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `opencode.drewrypope` | 2026-11-15T08:15:37.771Z | 08:43:50Z | 100% | 100%, resets 2026-12-03T03:02:35Z |
| `opencode.popesdrew` | 2026-11-15T08:15:37.971Z | 08:43:36Z | 100% | 100%, resets 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z |
| `opencode.developing-today-0` | 2026-11-15T08:15:38.101Z | 08:43:39Z | 100% | 54%, resets 2026-12-08T22:09:41Z |

**Every window is numerically identical to the corresponding `opencode-go.*` row in the same tick** (same 5h reset seconds, same weekly/monthly percentages, same monthly reset instants). That is the key design question: the Zen door appears to read the *same plan meters* as the Go door for each workspace, so a naive registration of three new pools would render duplicate meters on the Space under a second id, while not registering them leaves the measured set incomplete.

Where registration is missing, verified against `origin/main` at `5b419f0c7b` (== local HEAD):

- `quota-extract.ts` `POOL_SPECS` contains only `opencode-go.drewrypope`, `opencode-go.popesdrew`, `opencode-go.developing-today-0` (lines ~576-598); no bare `opencode.*` ids, and `SHELL_POOLS` has no entry either.
- `quota-gather-map.ts` defines `GO_DREWRYPOPE_SERVICE_ID` / `GO_POPESDREW_SERVICE_ID` / `GO_DEVELOPING_TODAY_0_SERVICE_ID` only; `canonicalProviderId` has no alias for `opencode.*`, so the ids pass through unchanged into whatever consumer keys on provider id.

Context: `.opencode/route-fallbacks.md:96` declares the door family `opencode-zen-plans | opencode.drewrypope, opencode.popesdrew, opencode.developing-today-0` — the ids are real routing doors, not noise.

## Problem to settle

Decide the attribution shape, then land it:

1. **Alias** the Zen rows onto the existing Go pools (`opencode.drewrypope` -> `opencode-go.drewrypope`, etc.) via `canonicalProviderId` / a service-id map in `quota-gather-map.ts`, so the measured set is complete without duplicating meters; or
2. **Register** three distinct Zen pools in `quota-extract.ts` if the Zen door is meant to hold independent meters (needs evidence that the identical values above are coincidental, not the same plan read).

## Acceptance

- Every providerId present in `quota-current.json providers[]` is either registered in `POOL_SPECS`/`SHELL_POOLS` or explicitly canonicalized/aliased, with `opencode.*` no longer unaccounted for.
- A test asserts the measured-provider census is covered by the registry (guards the #7835 defect class and this one).
- The Space renders the three Zen doors' meters, or deliberately renders them under their Go pools — no silent absence.

## Notes

- developing-today/code#5721 (the freshness keeper's designated filing surface) is **closed** (2026-11-09) and tracks a different defect (gatherer import failure), so this blocker is filed as its own issue.
- developing-today/code#8260 covered a missing *Go* label; all three `opencode-go.*` labelled rows are present and fresh in this tick, so that is not this issue.
- Triage packet enqueued in the same pass per AGENTS.md.

title: pm-stack(opencode-claimant/claimant): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before running claimant actions
body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` declares no command-line arguments and performs no argument parsing (no `sys.argv`/`argparse` handling). Unaccounted arguments are ignored and the script proceeds into its normal live claimant flow.

**File:** `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` (module entry runs `main()` unconditionally; no argument parsing found).

**Repro (verified on `origin/main` / HEAD `d5ad136471`, 2026-11-15):**
```bash
python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py --help
# prints: "OpenCode claimant starting in live mode" / runs supervision+gate steps
# exits 0 (ignored --help and performed work instead of showing usage/failing)
```
(Observed output ended with `No unbound opencode-lane candidates found. Exiting.` in this run; the script still entered its live path and executed supervision/gate logic before exiting.)

## Why it matters

Per `AGENTS.md` ("Operator script argument contract (#3352)") and `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`, every operator script must account for its whole command line and parse strictly before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit (2). Unlike read-only helpers, `claimant.py` is the live opencode claimant and can take mutating actions (claim/bind/launch/supervise depending on state). Ignoring unknown/typo'd flags (including `--help`) means a mis-invocation can silently start the live claimant instead of failing fast.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Parse the command line strictly before any reads/network/subprocess/claim/launch work; if the script takes no arguments, any unaccounted argument (including `--help` unless explicitly implemented as a no-side-effect usage path) is a usage error printed to stderr with exit code 2.
- `python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py --bogus` and `python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py --help` must fail as usage errors and perform no claimant actions.
- Running with no arguments preserves current behavior.
- Add/extend a test pinning that extra arguments are rejected before work.

title: pm-stack(shared-schema/orchestration-writer): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before doing any work
body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/shared-schema/orchestration-writer.py` ignores extra positional command-line arguments. It treats only `sys.argv[1]` as the optional orchestration JSON path and never rejects additional arguments, so unaccounted arguments are silently dropped while the script proceeds into its normal work (secret fetches, Management API SQL writes, read-back verification).

This violates the repo's operator-script argument contract: every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit (`AGENTS.md` "Operator script argument contract (#3352)", `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`).

## Evidence

- Script: `pm-stack/shared-schema/orchestration-writer.py` (writer for #5005 / #3142 orchestration-state cutover).
- Declared/documented usage: `orchestration-writer.py [path-to-orchestration.json]` (header, lines ~30-33).
- Arg handling: `path = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else <default>` (around line 99), with no check that `len(sys.argv) <= 2` and no usage error for extra args. No argparse/strict parsing is present.
- Repro (verified 2026-11-15, from repo root):

```bash
# first arg is used, second is silently ignored; script proceeds past argv handling
printf '%s' '{"runId":"x","generatedAt":"x","version":1}' > /tmp/ow-ok.json
python3 pm-stack/shared-schema/orchestration-writer.py /tmp/ow-ok.json /tmp/ow-ignored-extra.json
# observed: exit 1 with "SQL failed (HTTP 400)... invalid input syntax for type timestamp..." 
# (script read the first file, ignored /tmp/ow-ignored-extra.json, fetched secrets, and attempted SQL)
```

- Contrast with strict scripts in repo (e.g. `pm-stack/host-health-collector.py` rejects unknown args via argparse with exit 2 before work).

## Why it matters

This is a DB-writing operator script (inserts/replaces orchestration rows via Supabase Management API). Silently ignoring an extra argument can hide a typo or a mistaken invocation (wrong/missing flag style, extra path) while the script still performs network and database operations against the interpreted input. A strict usage error before any work prevents accidental or misleading runs.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix shape

- Reject unaccounted CLI arguments (any extra positional args, or unknown flags if flags are not part of the declared contract) with a clear usage error on stderr and non-zero exit (exit 2 consistent with argparse/contract examples) **before** any subprocess, secret fetch, network request, file read/write, or database step.
- Preserve existing valid behavior: no args uses the default path; exactly one positional arg uses that path.
- State the argument contract in the script header comment (per `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md` / sibling operator scripts).
- Add/adjust a targeted test covering rejection of extra args if a test harness exists for this script (or document verification if none exists), without weakening existing behavior.

title: id(web/world): snapshot/event sequence and participant ids accept negative, fractional and unsafe numbers — a malformed frame poisons the reconnect cursor (PR #4236 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4236 added shape validation for world WebSocket snapshot/event frames in the web client, but the numeric fields are checked only for *finiteness*: `current_sequence`, event `sequence`, and participant `id` accept negative, fractional, and unsafe-integer values (e.g. `-1`, `1.5`, `1e100`). Those values are world-protocol u64s — the shell contract in the same repo bounds `sequence` as a u64 (see the #4238 tests) and PR #4250's collab validator requires `Number.isSafeInteger(version) && version >= 0` for the analogous field — so a frame the Rust server could never legitimately send passes the web validator and poisons client state:

- `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` (current main, fb124d87f7c01523499635dfc4910dab92ad9f79): `isFiniteNumber` at line 159; `isWorldSnapshot` (160–169) checks `current_sequence` and participant `id` with it; `isWorldEvent` (170–186) checks `sequence` and `participant_id` with it.
- A snapshot with `current_sequence: -1` (or `1.5`) is accepted and assigned straight to the reconnect cursor (line 225: `cursor = snapshot.current_sequence`). On reconnect the join frame sends `after: cursor || null` (line 568) — a negative or fractional cursor goes on the wire verbatim as the resume position.
- An event with `sequence: 1e100` is accepted and `cursor = Math.max(cursor, event.sequence)` (line 245) raises the cursor past every real sequence: after a reconnect the client asks to resume after `1e+100`, i.e. past the end of the world log.
- A fractional `participant_id` never matches a rendered participant (`[data-participant="1.5"]`), so chat lines fall back to a bogus `player 1.5` identity instead of the frame being rejected.

This is the same shape-trust class the repo has been closing frame-by-frame (#7908 records cursor, #7924 view/error frames, #7928 upload/compile fields, and #4250's INIT version check) — the snapshot/event numeric fields are the remaining gap in the validator #4236 introduced.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4236 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4236 (merge commit `ee5f0d4f253a6e2069891e37d044a280424ca19a`, confirmed ancestor of current main, compare status `ahead`). It implemented the Phase-3 fix for #2802 (CLOSED) by adding `isWorldSnapshot`/`isWorldEvent` with `isFiniteNumber` checks; its tests cover missing/wrong-type/NaN fields but no negative, fractional, or >2^53 values.
- Current main `fb124d87f7c01523499635dfc4910dab92ad9f79`, `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` lines 159–186, 225, 245, 568 — read directly from main this run; the validators are unchanged since #4236 apart from later sibling-frame checks (#7908/#7924) that did not touch these fields.
- Contrast in the same batch: PR #4250 (`pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts`) rejects an INIT `version` unless `Number.isSafeInteger(version) && version >= 0`; PR #4238's shell-contract validator enforces u64 bounds on `sequence`.

## Why it matters

The validator's job (#2802) is that a parseable-but-wrong-shaped frame changes no state. Today a single malformed snapshot or event silently moves the resume cursor to a position the server never issued — negative, fractional, or past the end of the log — and the damage only appears later, at reconnect, as a join the server cannot honor or a resume that skips the world's history. Rejecting the frame at receipt (the established `rejectFrame()` discipline) keeps the failure visible and the cursor trustworthy.

## Acceptance criteria

- `isWorldSnapshot`/`isWorldEvent` reject negative, fractional, and unsafe-integer (>2^53) values for `current_sequence`, `sequence`, `participant_id`, and participant `id` — e.g. a shared safe-non-negative-integer check mirroring #4250's INIT version rule — with the frame rejected via the existing `rejectFrame()` path and no cursor/DOM state change.
- Regression tests in the world-records/world validator suite deliver snapshot/event frames with `-1`, `1.5`, and `1e100` sequence values (and a fractional participant id) and pin rejection plus an unchanged cursor (a subsequent reconnect join still sends the pre-frame `after`).
- Valid frames at the u64-representable boundary the existing tests use (e.g. `2 ** 53` sequences in the shell-contract suite) keep their current accepted behavior where the contract allows it — no tightening beyond the wire type.

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #4236 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches (`isWorldSnapshot`, `current_sequence`, `world snapshot sequence negative`) returned the sibling shape-trust issues (#7831 open — host-view/invite HTTP responses; #7908, #7924, #7928 closed — records/view/invite/upload frames) and #2802 (closed, the parent #4236 implemented); none covers snapshot/event sequence or participant-id integrality.

title: id(protocol): MetaProtocol close-drain is unbounded — Phase-2 handlers carry no deadline, so accept() may never return after peer close (and its doc says streams are stopped)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4240 bounded MetaProtocol's network phases (60s read/write deadlines, 16-stream cap), but the connection-close path it introduced is **unbounded**: when the peer closes, `accept_connection` drains every admitted stream task to completion, and a stream stuck in Phase 2 — the request handler, which is deliberately *not* wrapped in the deadline — makes that drain, and therefore `accept()`, never return.

On current main (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/protocol.rs`, fb124d87f7c01523499635dfc4910dab92ad9f79):

1. `accept_connection` (lines 1191–1203): after the accept loop breaks, `while let Some(result) = streams.join_next().await` drains all admitted handlers with **no overall deadline**.
2. The drain comment (lines 1191–1197) argues termination from the wrong premise: "Each handler's network phases stay bounded by the stream deadline, so this drain terminates." The handler itself is not a network phase.
3. `handle_stream` Phase 2 (lines 1230–1240) states the handler is "deliberately NOT wrapped in the deadline" because handlers perform non-transactional mutations — a sound reason not to *cancel* a mutation, but it means a handler that wedges (a contended store/tag lock, a hung filesystem call inside `FileOps`/`TagStore`, a future handler that awaits something slow) blocks the drain forever.
4. The `ProtocolHandler::accept` doc (lines 1267–1270) says the opposite of the implementation: "active streams are stopped when the peer closes the connection." They are not stopped; they are awaited, indefinitely.

Net effect: one wedged handler on a closing connection pins the protocol-handler task forever — graceful router/endpoint shutdown for that connection never completes, and the task, its semaphore permits and the connection state are never released. The failure is silent: nothing logs that the drain is stuck.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4240 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4240 (merge commit `a205ae3bd38cd19f3bcfc1de64699d6e63c6ec57`, confirmed ancestor of current main, compare status `ahead`). It fixed #2086 (serial stream handling, no deadline) by introducing the concurrent accept loop, the per-phase deadlines, and this drain.
- Current main `fb124d87f7c01523499635dfc4910dab92ad9f79`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/protocol.rs`: `accept_connection` at line 1155, drain loop at 1198–1202, Phase-2 no-deadline comment at 1230–1235, contradictory `accept` doc at 1267–1270 — all read directly from main this run.
- The targeted tests #4240 shipped (now in `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/protocol.rs` tests) cover a Phase-1 stalled *read* stream and excess-stream reset. No test covers a handler that stalls in Phase 2 while the connection is closing, and no CI path executes that scenario.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk)

Result: **inconclusive**.

- Commit examined: `fb124d87f7c01523499635dfc4910dab92ad9f79` (current main).
- Why no reproduction: a deterministic Phase-2 stall cannot be injected from outside the crate without modifying application code — `MetaProtocol::handle` is a concrete inherent method whose arms are local blob/tag/file operations with no stall seam, test double, or peer-controlled await; the verification rules for this class forbid modifying application code and forbid running the test on the sandbox. The two existing narrow tests (stalled read, excess streams) exercise Phase 1 and admission, not the drain.
- What was verified instead: the drain loop, the Phase-2 exemption, and the contradictory doc were read verbatim on current main (file:line above), and the shipped test set was enumerated — the Phase-2-stall-at-close scenario is not among them.

## Why it matters

#4240's whole purpose was bounding how long a bad peer can pin server resources. The read/write phases are bounded, but the lifecycle endpoint of the connection is not: after the peer has already gone away, a single stuck handler converts a bounded connection into an unbounded shutdown hang. Shutdown paths are exactly where operators and supervisors (systemd, the router's shutdown future) wait — a hang there wedges deploys and restarts, not just one request.

## Acceptance criteria

- The close-drain is bounded or supervised: e.g. an overall drain deadline after which remaining stream tasks are aborted *between* requests (never mid-mutation at a known-unsafe point), or the drain is detached from `accept()`'s return with the stuck state logged — any design that makes `accept()`'s post-close lifetime finite and observable, with the trade-off against the mid-mutation-cancellation hazard (#4240's Phase-2 rationale) stated in the code.
- The `accept()` doc comment matches the implemented close behavior.
- A regression test covers the scenario: a handler still in flight when the peer closes, with the connection's accept task completing (or the stuck drain being surfaced) within a bounded time; the existing stalled-read and excess-stream tests keep passing.
- Handlers that finish normally during the drain keep their current drain-to-completion behavior (no regression to aborting healthy in-flight mutations on close).

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #4240 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches (`MetaProtocol drain`, `accept_connection`) returned no issues; no open or closed issue covers the unbounded close-drain.

labels.name: kind/bug

body:
## Gap: queue-broker PostgREST `/list` discards the content-range — list replies carry no total, so a limited listing reads as complete

Filed from the Codex-review disposition of PR #9015 (task 17190, lane any-d), per the #6622 pagination contract (complete, bounded, or say so — rule 3: truncation never silent). The canonical Phase 4 closing inventory on #6623 (comment 6837035727) dispositioned the Turso broker list reads (`turso_queue.rs`, deliberately bounded operator window) but did not cover this PostgREST path.

### Evidence (verified on current main 1d94e9462a, 2026-11-14)

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/queue_broker.rs`, PostgREST `/list` handler: the query is built with `limit={limit}&offset={offset}`, and the reply discards the range PostgREST returns: `Ok((rows, _)) => ok(json!({"rows": rows}))`. The second tuple element (the content-range / total) is dropped, so the reply is `{"rows": [...]}` with no total and no truncation marker.
- A caller that asks for a limited window therefore cannot distinguish "these are all the matching tasks" from "these are the first N of many" — the listing presents as complete when it may be truncated. (This bit task 17190's own verification: recent completions could not be confirmed from list output — the same failure family as closed #7871, which fixed one readback path via `--task`; the general reply still carries no total.)

### Acceptance

- The broker `/list` reply (PostgREST path; check the Turso path for parity) includes the total matching count (from the PostgREST content-range) or an explicit truncated marker when the returned rows are a strict prefix of the matching set.
- The `fleet queue list` CLI surfaces that total/marker so an operator can tell a complete listing from a truncated one without a second query.
- A test pins the behavior: a listing whose limit is below the matching count reports the total / truncation; an exhaustive listing reports completeness.

### Context

- Contract: #6622 (complete, bounded, or say so); closing inventory: #6623 comment 6837035727.
- Origin: Codex P2 finding on PR #9015 (comment 4555990746) — the inventory row for the queue-list surface claimed conformance evidence this path does not have. PR #9015 itself is closed as superseded (its content landed via PR #9048 / PR #9149 and the inventory posted on #6623); this issue is the one residual gap from its review.
- Related, distinct defects (not duplicates): #9001 (no rows array at limits >= 100), #9027 (--not-before garbage filter on Turso), #7871 (closed; --task readback), #9420 (closed; /list filters).

title: fix(delivery-publisher): resume refuses forever after a covered slice's queue task completes (terminal readback, #9106)
body:
# Defect: ID/Atlas delivery publisher can never resume after a covered slice's queue task completes

Component: `doc/2026-11-13T03-40-00Z_design_id-atlas-summit/delivery-publish/publish.py` (program #9106, fleet task 15354).

## Evidence (live, 2026-11-14)

- The first publisher execute run (2026-11-13T10:28:15Z, design SHA 7ab1488fec, manifest 3b5bce35, report 668c87c3) filed slice 9110-01 as issue #9418 and enqueued queue task 15882 in repo-health-code-pilot, then stopped: the journal (`~/.local/state/id-atlas-9106/publisher.json`) records phase `queue-unverified` because queue readback could not verify the task — the broker `/list` filter defect #9420, since CLOSED/fixed.
- Task 15882 has since completed legitimately: queue read-back (laptop fleet binary, `--task 15882`) shows status `done`; issue #9418 was implemented and closed `completed` via PR #9426 (2026-11-13T11:01:56Z).
- Publisher resume path for an item with `queue_id`: `queue_readback()` requires the row status to be LIVE (`queued|claimed|parked|blocked`) and raises `Refusal` otherwise — by design for a *fresh* enqueue (see `test_broker_readback_exact_task_queue_key_and_live_status`, which asserts `done` refuses).
- The resume branch comment says "a missing/non-live row requires human disposition", but no journal field or code path encodes such a disposition: every resume re-runs the same LIVE-only readback for the already-covered first item and refuses forever, blocking the remaining 126 of 127 delivery items.

## Required fix

In the resume branch only (item already has `issue_url` + `queue_id`), accept an exact-match row (id, queue, dedupe key) whose status is terminal `done` as a completed disposition: record `queue_status: done` plus a disposition note/timestamp in the journal and continue. Keep the fresh-enqueue readback LIVE-only, and keep refusing mismatched id/queue/dedupe and non-`done` terminal states pending explicit human reconciliation.

## Workaround used for the 2026-11-14 relaunch

A minimal patch implementing exactly the above was applied to the publisher in the delivery worktree under Drew's 2026-11-14 order ("unpark 9106, fix whatever the problem is and proceed"); this issue tracks landing that fix on main with tests. Until it lands, the approval record's `publisher_sha256` binding describes the pre-patch publisher.

# Silent-failure surfacing: claimant mode + pm-git-sync health must be visible

Part of the close-authority epic (automation must never close an issue) — the fail-safe-defaults slice.

## Problem
Two live silent failures found in the 2026-11-14 end-to-end review:
1. **Claimant mode file missing** (`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode` absent on the laptop): `read_mode()` defaults to "shadow", so direct dispatch returns `mode_not_live` and summit dispatch stalls with no health signal anywhere. (A parallel pass is unparking #9106 and may set the file — this slice is about the *silence*, not today's instance.)
2. **`pm-git-sync.service` is failed** on the laptop: the deploy-by-merge path (#8171) that keeps the laptop PM checkout on clean main is down, so repo changes silently stop reaching the host. `pm-projector-reconcile.service` was also observed stuck in `activating`.

## Work
- Surface both in an existing health surface (aggregator staleness watchdog tier items are derived, never persisted — a natural home): claimant mode (missing/shadow/live) as a needs-attention item whenever a dispatch is attempted or queued summits exist; pm-git-sync / pm-projector-reconcile unit states as PM-stack health items.
- Claimant: log a loud line on every mode read that finds the file missing (today it is indistinguishable from an intentional shadow).
- Decide and document the intended default: shadow-on-missing is the right *safety* default; the fix is visibility, not a different default.

## Acceptance
- Removing the mode file (scratch check) produces a visible health item within one aggregator cycle.
- A failed pm-git-sync shows as a PM-stack health item; recovering the unit clears it.

body:
# Linking containment: prove a stray PR link can no longer reach a closing state

Part of the close-authority epic (automation must never close an issue).

## Problem
Kaneo v2.47.0 links PRs to tasks loosely: any `#n` in the PR title, a closing-keyword body ref, a branch-pattern match, or a Kaneo task key (`utils/issue-references.ts`). We cannot patch upstream; the design decision is containment — with the sync guard (slice 1) ensuring no PR/branch transition can target a closing state, a stray link's worst case is a task moving to in-review/in-progress.

## Work
- Fixture battery on developing-today/code, all verified from issue timelines:
  1. Refs-only PR (body `Refs #n`, no keyword) on a plain issue → stays open, no `status:done`.
  2. Refs-only PR on a fixture epic with an open child → stays open, no `status:done`.
  3. Title-ref-only PR (title contains `(#n)`, body clean) → no close, no `status:done`.
  4. `Closes #n` PR → closes natively; Kaneo completes the task and applies `status:done` after.
  5. Human close on GitHub → Kaneo task completes (fallback) — and the reverse, a deliberate human Done move in Kaneo → issue closes (documented wanted sync).
- Record results in `pm-stack/KANEO-GITHUB-SYNC.md` (fixture section) so the battery is re-runnable after any Kaneo upgrade or re-connect.

## Acceptance
- All five fixtures pass live with timeline evidence linked from this issue.
- Any failure reopens #7610-class handling: fix config first, then re-run.

# Epic-invariant sweeper: no closed issue with open sub-issues, anywhere

Part of the close-authority epic (automation must never close an issue).

## Problem
The watchdog only sees closes inside its polling window. History proves wrongful closes can sit for days: **#9060 was bot-closed on 2026-11-12 with all 12 sub-issues open and is still closed today.** #9060's own design anticipated this: "GitHub cannot hard-block a close; the monitor is the enforcement surface."

## Work
- A slow-cadence sweep (daily is fine) over all four Kaneo-synced repos (developing-today/code, developing-today-forks/opencode, developing-today-forks/openchamber, dezren39/nix): list CLOSED issues whose `sub_issues_summary` shows open children.
- Report mode first: post the inventory to the tracking epic with per-issue close actor/timestamp from the timeline (bot vs human, keyword PR or not).
- Reopen policy (after the first inventory is reviewed): bot-closed + open sub-issues + no closing keyword ⇒ auto-reopen with evidence (same guards as watchdog #10105); anything ambiguous stays report-only.

## Acceptance
- First inventory run published; #9060 appears in it with correct actor evidence.
- Zero false positives on legitimately closed parents (children completed or re-parented before close).
- The sweep runs on a schedule and its state survives restarts.

body:
# Kaneo sync guard: repo-declared statusTransitions, asserted at deploy + hourly

Part of the close-authority epic (automation must never close an issue).

## Problem
Kaneo's GitHub `statusTransitions` config lives only in Kaneo's Postgres (`integration.config`). Nothing in this repo sets it (see `pm-stack/KANEO-GITHUB-SYNC.md`). Two silent regression paths restore the #7610 defect: the integration connect flow recreates the config with upstream default `onPRMerge: "done"`, and deleting the `pr_merged` rule in the UI falls back to `"done"` in v2.47.0 code.

## Work
- `pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py`: reads every `type='github'` integration config; asserts (a) no transition targets the final column (`done`), (b) `onPRMerge = "in-review"`, (c) `onPROpen = "in-review"`, `onBranchPush = "in-progress"` unchanged. On drift: re-apply the safe map, log the before/after, exit non-zero / emit a loud line for the health surface. Idempotent; safe to run repeatedly.
- Wire it into `pm-stack/deploy.sh` (post-deploy assertion) and a laptop user timer (hourly).
- The guard's expected map is declared in the repo — the repo becomes the source of truth for this config.

## Acceptance
- Guard run against the live DB reports all 4 integrations conforming.
- Deliberately corrupting one integration's `onPRMerge` in a scratch copy (or staging row) is detected and healed on the next run, with the drift logged.
- Deploy path runs the guard; a failed assertion fails the deploy loudly.

body:
## Problem

A dashboard **session answer** cannot land inside a live OpenCode question window. Observed live on 2026-11-14 during the #1156 round-trip verification (queue task 4890):

- The OpenCode `question` tool gives up after ~600 s: session `ses_e5e25a40132ffe6PAVJ3tcR5NV` asked its question at 2026-11-14T14:28:40Z and recorded "not answered within timeout" at 14:38:50Z, defaulting and continuing.
- The only consumer of `kind: session` dashboard actions is the **hourly** orchestration pass. The answer action (`da-mwgi5aob-280tlp`, text `BETA`, posted 14:29:43Z while the session was verifiably `stopped-for-question`) was applied at 15:15:52Z by run `orch-2026-11-14T15:13:00Z` — 37 minutes after the question had already expired. The text did arrive in the session (message `msg_1a1daa0efe7001P2IQbPSzPiYp`), but as a new prompt, not as the answer to the pending question.

So the dashboard answer path works as transport (store → consumer → prompt route → session, with audit), but is structurally too slow for its primary use case: answering a session that is waiting on a question.

## Evidence

- #1156 observation note (queue task 4890, lane any-a, 2026-11-14): poke round-trip passed end-to-end (action `da-mwgh8yx3-1bm6jo`, applied by `orch-2026-11-14T14:13:17Z`); answer leg evidence as above.
- Actions store before this verification: zero `kind: session` actions had ever been recorded — this was the first live exercise of the path.

## What would fix it

A session-action consumer with a cadence well under the question timeout — e.g. a lightweight minutely consumer for `kind: session` actions only (the orchestration pass keeps triage / status-request / preference slices), or an aggregator-side push/trigger when a session action lands. The fix must preserve the one-consumer-per-(kind, source) rule from `pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts`: the fast consumer takes the session slice over from the orchestration pass, which must stop polling it.

## Acceptance

- A dashboard answer posted for an opencode-laptop session that is stopped-for-question is delivered while the form is still open, and the session records the delivered text as the question's answer (question tool completes with that value).
- Re-observe with the task 4890 protocol (disposable session, ALPHA/BETA marker question) and post the evidence on #1156; task 4890 is dep-blocked on this issue and returns to the pool when it closes.

title: Guard (launcher half of #9849): refuse or redirect sessions launched in the primary checkout
body:
Follow-on from #9849 (primary-checkout guard), split out by lane code-c on 2026-11-14 with the analysis recorded so it is not re-derived a third time.

## What this issue is

#9849's prevention ask has two halves. The surfacing half — a dirty/off-main primary raises one aggregator incident naming the dirt — is implemented in the stack sentinel (PR from task fallback-9849, `src/primary-checkout.ts` + a `primary-checkout` local check in `stack-sentinel.ts`). This issue is the remaining half:

**A lane/session launched with the primary checkout (~/git/code) as its working directory is redirected to a worktree, or refused with the reason recorded.**

## Why it does not live in this repo (verified 2026-11-14)

- Lane sessions are launched by the sandbox-side scheduler/hooks and do their laptop work through `~/tools/laptop-agent.py` exec calls. Neither the launcher nor laptop-agent is in `developing-today/code` (checked: no laptop-agent source in the repo tree).
- A claim-time cwd check inside `repo-queue` (pkgs/fleet) cannot see the session's working directory: claims run on the laptop via laptop-agent, whose own cwd is the agent's home, not the directory the session then works in. The check would pass vacuously while the session cds into the primary in its next command.
- The runbook already mandates worktrees in prose; #8170 (2026-11-08→10) and its 2026-11-13/14 recurrence happened anyway. The guard has to be mechanical at the point where the working directory is chosen.

## Scoped work for whoever owns the launcher layer

1. In the lane launch path (scheduler/hooks side): when a lane session's working directory — or the laptop-side directory its first worktree-scoped command targets — resolves to the primary checkout of a fleet repo, refuse the launch or relocate the session to a fresh worktree under `~/git/fleet/`, recording the refusal/relocation on the lane's handoff/claim record.
2. In `laptop-agent.py` (defense in depth): refuse exec calls whose command's target directory is the primary checkout AND that mutate git state (checkout/switch/commit/clean/reset/stash), with the refusal text naming the worktree rule. Read-only commands in the primary (status, log, the sentinel's own checks) must stay allowed — pm-git-sync's observers and several services read from it.
3. Demonstrate once: a session launched at the primary is redirected/refused with the reason recorded (the #9849 acceptance's first clause).

## References

- #9849 (parent ask + acceptance), #8170 (first occurrence, with the rescue-pass cost accounting).
- The sentinel half gives the safety net while this is unbuilt: a dirtied primary now alerts within ~90s of the sentinel's damped cadence once deployed.

title: impl(mcpx): resolve plugin-session manifest hooks into live bus subscribers (#1873 slice 2)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
Next slice on top of the merged plugin-session foundation for #1873 (PR #10045, `internal/pluginsession`).

**Slice:** resolve a plugin session's manifest hook declarations into live bus subscribers at session start, owned by the session and dropped by its `Close`.

- At plugin-session open, take the manifest's declared hook subscriptions (today recorded in the session, "recorded, not interpreted") and subscribe them to the daemon's event bus with `events.Filter` semantics, observe phase per decision 0001 (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/decisions/0001-hook-vocabulary.md`). Delivery target is the owning plugin (its tool surface), keyed by session: one session's hooks are never another's.
- Each live subscription is registered with `Registry.Own(id, OwnedItem{Kind: "hook", ...})` so `/v1/status` introspection shows what each session owns, and session end (clean or crash path, both through `Close`) drops the subscribers with the session — no separate unsubscription bookkeeping.
- **Open question to answer first, in the PR:** #1872 (config-declared hooks) is parked with its own holder and its structured `hooks` setting / subscriber machinery has not landed on main. State explicitly whether this slice builds the minimal subscriber machinery it needs on the events bus directly, or depends on #1872's follow-up landing first — and record the choice where the next reader will find it (the PR + a note here).
- Tests (tree rules: changed packages, named oracles): a manifest hook fires to the owning plugin on a matching event; a non-matching event does not fire it; session end drops subscriptions (a post-close event fires nothing); two sessions with identical declarations each receive only their own deliveries.

Out of scope: capability enforcement (decision 0003), the vars store, the named-command registry, detach/re-address — separate later packets under the #1885 tracker / #1873 lineage.

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: work/assigned

body:
Implements §7 of the merged design record for #5956 (PR #10023, `doc/2026-11-14T13-50-00Z_design_id_roc_library_imports/`). The design is settled; this issue is the build, in the record's order:

1. **Manifest `platform`-block parser + validator** against the `id-caps` catalog (`pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/world_caps.rs`): unknown-name, duplicate, and version-pin checks, wired into the registry/upload path #5969 defines. Fail closed, mirroring `WorldManifest::parse`.
2. **Transitive requirement resolver** over registry manifests, by manifest hash, with cycle refusal, producing the §4 resolution record (importer, library manifest hash, source kind, resolved transitive requirement set, checked-against surface, outcome).
3. **The import gate** in the compile path: the three subset checks (transitive requirements ⊆ selected platform surface; ⊆ world requested set; discovered-used ⊆ world requested set) with the §5 diagnostic contract (`import_requirement_unmet` + subreasons, exhaustive excess set, remedy), generalizing the shipped platform-module gate and the `roc-cap-demo` negative tests.
4. **#5994 §4's fixture matrix** wired through `pkgs/id/examples/roc-import-policy/` and `pkgs/id/scripts/roc-test.sh`, each negative case asserting its diagnostic as oracle. Extension-tier rows (fs/net) stay specifications until those providers exist in the catalog.
5. **Citation updates:** #5956's body and the #5994 record point at `id-caps` (not `id-core`) for `world_caps.rs`.

Boundaries from the record: no runtime grant/ceiling changes; tier vocabulary provisional on #5958 (still open, PR #7599) — land name-level checks first, labels follow #5958. Oracle for every test: the invariant or diagnostic it pins, named in the test.

body:
Follow-on 5 of 5 from the #6027 design (doc/2026-11-10T20-41-01Z_design_atlas_retrieval_stats_feedback.md, merged via PR #8251). Parent program: #6018. Depends on follow-ons 3 (aggregation) and 4 (feedback capture).

## Scope (design §§6.2–6.3, 7)
- The normalisation agent pass: essay/comment feedback is normalised into structured signal (categories incl. stale-content, wrong-content, ranking-too-low, missing-result) with the query context; the raw record is preserved alongside the derived one (invariant 4).
- Weighting per §6.3 (requester kinds; agent self-feedback recorded at weight 0 and flagged per §6.4) applied in aggregation; aggregates report unique-requester counts next to raw counts.
- Decision wiring produces NOMINATIONS ONLY: retention candidates and ranking-change candidates surfaced via the weekly report (§7 acting rules). No automated deletion or weight change ships in this follow-on — ranking changes still go through the eval harness, deletions through the retention design's gates.

## Acceptance
- Sample essay feedback normalises into the §6.2 categories with raw text preserved.
- A self-feedback case is recorded at weight 0 with the flag set.
- The weekly report carries at least the nomination sections with unique-requester figures.

Design: doc/2026-11-10T20-41-01Z_design_atlas_retrieval_stats_feedback.md §§6–7. Filed by queue-worker triage of #6027 (task 15280).

Follow-on 4 of 5 from the #6027 design (doc/2026-11-10T20-41-01Z_design_atlas_retrieval_stats_feedback.md, merged via PR #8251). Parent program: #6018. Independent of follow-ons 2–3 (except the feedback-reference retention exception in follow-on 2).

## Scope (design §6.1, §6.4)
- Feedback capture on every surface that returns results: service API field/endpoint, CLI command/prompt, and the UI affordance contract — thumbs up/down reachable in one action, optional comment (up to essay length) riding along.
- Feedback attaches to (query_id, result_id) — never to rank positions (invariant 3). Surfaces report whether the result was opened/expanded before the vote.
- Raw feedback is stored verbatim and never mutated (invariant 4); one active vote per (requester, query_id, chunk_id), re-votes supersede with the superseded record kept.

## Acceptance
- A thumbs vote + comment can be cast from the CLI and via the API against a real served result and is retrievable by its IDs.
- A vote on an unopened result is recorded with its opened=false marker.
- Duplicate/re-vote behaviour matches §6.4 (supersede, raw preserved).

body:
Follow-on 1 of 5 from the #6027 design (doc/2026-11-10T20-41-01Z_design_atlas_retrieval_stats_feedback.md, merged via PR #8251). Parent program: #6018.

## Scope (design §§2–3)
- Mint `query_id` (UUIDv7) per executed search in the atlas search service; return it in every response envelope and print it in the CLI. Retries are separate executions linked by `retry_of`.
- Persist the per-query trace as `atlas-query-trace/v1` JSONL records: per-result stage scores (shard rank/score, merge rank + fusion score incl. the persisted `FusedEntry` rank_sources_json, rescore, final rank/served), resolved file/embed identity (source_file_id, embed_id, embed_content_hash, version, tier, provenance mark), parameters used, and pool counts. Results that entered a pool but did not survive still appear with `served: false`.
- **Fail closed (design invariant 2):** a trace write failure is a search failure, never a silently untraced success.

## Acceptance
- A live search produces a trace record that parses against the §3 schema and lets an operator recover every served result's per-stage scores.
- Killing the trace sink makes search fail visibly (test).
- No change to ranking behaviour; trace overhead measured and reported on the PR.

title: Fleet: automatic traffic-based door breaker — deploy the bench machinery + half-open probes for auth benches
body:
## Fleet: dead doors wedge sessions because nothing takes them out of the route — build the traffic-based door breaker end to end

Filed 2026-11-14 on Drew's direct order ("build it, don't just talk about it").

### The failure shape (measured)

Route seats are static config. When a door dies, sessions routed to it retry against it and wedge; a minder/steward notices and a human edits route config with a hand-set "until" date:

- #9859 — `_muse` weekly-walled at 100%: 9 lane sessions frozen at retry attempt 3 for 10+ minutes, zero output, stopped by hand.
- #9549 — `_claude` OAuth-dead: wave after wave launched in and died at 3 messages. The route_attempt ledger shows **15,390 RateLimit attempts on `_claude` in the last 24h** against 1,988 successes on the currently running build.
- #9856 — `_antigravity`: Google disabled the account (ToS) while its quota read still shows the weekly window open at ~29% — **1,255 Authentication attempts in the last 24h**.

### Why the breaker is driven by attempt outcomes, never quota reads (standing doctrine)

Quota reads lie in both directions: the OpenAI read said healthy while the door was auth-dead for a full day; Antigravity's read says open while the account is dead. The ledger is the truth. Measured persistence from the live route_attempt ledger (2026-11-14, trailing 24h):

- After a **QuotaExceeded** attempt, the same target succeeded within 1h in **0 of 124** cases across every provider (_openai.main 0/36, _openai.alt 0/31, Go accounts 0/45, others 0/12). A quota wall never heals inside the hour — benching on the first QuotaExceeded costs nothing.
- **Authentication** is per-target persistent (0/8,693 on 2026-11-09; 0/2,433 on 2026-11-11 for the OpenAI doors).
- **Transport** failures are frequent *and* transient (cline-pass: 2,250 Transport vs 5,599 successes in 24h) — they must never plant a hard bench.

### What already exists in the fork (developing-today-forks/opencode main)

`packages/core/src/model-route.ts` already carries a bench system: per-target and per-credential health, class-aware benches (auth/quota start on the long ladder, multiplier 2, ordinary failures capped at 120s per Drew's 2026-11-08 failover spec #2212), half-open probe claims at quota window resets, quota-skip adjustments with corroboration, restart replay from the route health log, and an `availability()` readout surfaced by the route-stats tool. Fork PR #2440 (merged 2026-11-14 04:59 CST, code#9549) added never-retry for Authentication/QuotaExceeded classes and bounded a step's cumulative retry wait.

**None of it is live**: the running server is opencode 2.0.30+0f5561c, which predates #2440 (`git merge-base --is-ancestor` verified).

### The two work items

1. **Fork — half-open probes for auth benches.** Quota benches get a single-flight probe at their window reset; auth benches only *expire*, returning the door to full candidacy so a wave can pile onto a still-dead door at the expiry instant. Extend the existing probe-claim machinery: when an auth bench's cooldown expires it converts to probe-pending — the door stays out of ordinary candidacy, exactly one probe attempt is admitted, a probe success reseats it, a probe failure re-benches on the escalated ladder. Fail-safe unchanged: absent/broken breaker state degrades to today's static config, never to all-doors-out.
2. **Deploy — pin current fork main in this repo's flake.lock and switch the laptop**, then prove it in the attempt stream: the dead doors (_muse walled, _antigravity account-dead, _claude auth/renewal-dead) stop receiving wedged retries (attempt counts collapse to ~one per bench window per target, attempts fail over instead), healthy doors' success shape unchanged, plus a controlled trip → failover → probe → reseat.

### Acceptance

- Tests green: trip on the #9859 shape (consecutive wall failures), no trip on scattered transient failures, reseat on probe success, degrade-to-static when breaker state is absent.
- Live attempt-stream proof after deploy, before/after per door.
- Evidence here; cross-links on #9859 / #9549 / #9856.

title: mcpx(progspec): a flight whose output is deleted mid-flight still returns success to its leader and waiters (PR #4246)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: status/needs-triage
labels.description: Not yet triaged; needs a first look

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #4246 added singleflight to mcpx progspec: when a flight finishes, the leader stores the result in the memo **only if the built path is still executable** — "an output deleted mid-flight must not be resurrected into the memo". But the flight's own return path ignores that check: the leader and every waiter still receive `(result, nil)` — a successful resolution naming a path that just failed the executable check.

```go
r, err := resolveNix(ctx, spec, dir)

memoMu.Lock()
if err == nil && isExecutable(r.Path) {
    memo[key] = r
}
delete(flights, key)
f.res, f.err = r, err   // err is nil even when isExecutable(r.Path) was false
close(f.done)
memoMu.Unlock()
return r, err
```

That contradicts the doctrine the same file applies on the memo-read path: a path that is no longer executable "is not a resolution — evict it and resolve again rather than hand the caller a dead executable". The flight path hands the caller exactly that dead executable, once, as success; only the *next* call recovers (the result was never memoised, so it rebuilds).

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4246 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4246 (merge commit `423f36d2a0ba`, confirmed ancestor of current main via compare API, status `behind`). It fixed #2826 (closed).
- Current main `1f6abda0a68291bf7e0e14fd91c6e3c248e6e7aa`, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/progspec/progspec.go`:
  - `resolveNixFlight` (lines 201–208): memoisation is gated on `isExecutable(r.Path)`, but `f.res, f.err = r, err` and `return r, err` are not — a failed executable check still yields a nil error to the leader and all waiters (`return f.res, f.err`, line 189).
  - Contrast, memo-read path (lines 152–160): a memoised path that fails `isExecutable` is evicted and re-resolved, with the comment quoted above.
  - `programIn` guarantees the path was executable when `resolveNix` picked it, so the failing-check window is an output deleted or de-permissioned between the build finishing and the flight completing (e.g. a store GC or a test stub's temp dir dying mid-flight) — narrow, but exactly the window the memo gate was added for.
- PR #4246's tests pin concurrent sharing, failure non-memoisation, fresh-joins-flight, and waiter cancellation — no test covers a result that fails the completion executable check.

## Why it matters

A caller that receives `(Resolved, nil)` trusts the path and spawns it; a dead path surfaces downstream as an opaque spawn failure instead of a resolve error that the caller (or a retry) can act on, and every concurrent waiter fails the same way at once. The PR's own fix recognises the state as invalid — it just only protects the memo, not the callers already waiting on the flight.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a flight's result fails the completion `isExecutable` check, the leader and all waiters receive an error (naming the spec/path) instead of a successful `Resolved` — or the flight transparently re-resolves; either way no caller is handed a non-executable path with a nil error.
- Nothing is memoised in that case (existing behaviour, keep it), and a later call retries the build.
- A test pins the shape: a build whose output becomes non-executable before flight completion yields an error for concurrent callers, and the happy path (output still executable) is unchanged; existing progspec tests keep passing.

Found by the pr-diff-review job reviewing PR #4246 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches for `progspec flight`, `resolveNixFlight`, and "deleted mid-flight" returned only PR #4246 itself and #2826 (closed — the original singleflight request); no open or closed issue covers the flight return path.

body:
Slice 3 of #5668, filed by the task 15204 fresh triage (2026-11-14, lane any-c). Design: PR #5667 §3 (merged). Parent: #5668.

## Work — snapshot-bound result cache (lands last)

- Cache key: `sha256(query || snapshot_id || ceiling || flags)` using the shared key constructor from slice 2 (flags end-to-end). All flags are part of the key.
- The snapshot id is the request's shard-set snapshot id — `ShardSet::snapshot_id()` already exists in atlas-core (crates/atlas-core/src/shards/mod.rs, noted there as "the material for the result-cache snapshot id (#5668)"). Per the 2026-11-11 contract on #5668, each request binds its current shard snapshot id atomically to its cache key; when #5669's aggregator promotion lands, promotion bumps move that id and the service observes them without restart — this slice does not wait for #5669.
- Storage: in-service memory only, per the #5354 privacy rule — no cross-client result sharing by default. 24h TTL as a GC bound only (correctness comes from the snapshot id, not the clock).
- A snapshot bump invalidates all result entries at once (id change = key change; stale-id entries are unreachable and GC'd).

## Gates

- Slice 2 (flags + shared key constructor) must land first — its queue task is this slice's gate; dep-block on it at claim time if unlanded (runbook §5b). Slice 1 (embedding cache) is independent and may land before or after.

## Acceptance

- A repeated identical query against an unchanged snapshot is served from cache with no Turso round-trip for the ranking (oracle: backend call count in tests).
- MBT for snapshot-rotation invalidation: model the shard-set rotation, prove no pre-rotation entry is ever served post-rotation (testing doctrine — the test names its oracle).
- Golden-311 parity unchanged with caches cold and warm; eval runs use `--no-cache`.
- `--no-cache` bypasses result-cache reads and refreshes writes.

body:
Slice 2 of #5668, filed by the task 15204 fresh triage (2026-11-14, lane any-c). Design: PR #5667 §3 (merged). Parent: #5668.

## The flag contract (decided 2026-11-11 on #5668 — do not re-litigate)

- `--expand N` KEEPS its shipped meaning (include N neighboring chunks; main.rs / search.rs). No silent repurposing of a live flag.
- §3.3 hydration ships under its own flag: **`--hydrate N`** — hydrate the top N results to full chunk/file content from the content store. (Internal hydration machinery already exists in atlas-core shards/scan.rs; this slice exposes and wires it end-to-end.)

## Work — flags end-to-end (CLI + service protocol)

- `--no-cache`: bypass cache reads, refresh cache writes (consumes slice 1's embedding cache; must remain correct before the result cache exists).
- `--wait`: block for the full fused result instead of returning a job handle + first page.
- `--expand N`: unchanged semantics (regression-covered so this slice cannot drift it).
- `--hydrate N`: as above, via the content store.
- `--raw` / `--raw=branches`: ungrouped rows (pre-fusion option).
- All flags are part of every cache key constructed downstream (the result-cache slice consumes this); mirror the flags in the fleet-search client, which mirrors atlas-search's flag surface.

## Acceptance

- Each flag works through both the CLI and the service protocol with identical semantics (cli_parity-style tests).
- `--expand` neighbor behavior is byte-identical to pre-slice behavior on the golden set (regression oracle).
- `--hydrate N` returns full chunk/file text for exactly the top N results.
- Flag-sensitive cache-key construction is shared code (one constructor), PBT-covered for flag sensitivity.

## Work — query-embedding cache (independent; lands first)

Per design §3 and #5668's acceptance:

- Cache key: `sha256(model_id || model_rev || normalized_text)`; no TTL.
- Two tiers: service-memory LRU (~10k entries) + shared Turso cache DB in the internal tier.

- A repeated identical query embedding is served from cache (memory tier first, Turso tier second) with identical vectors — proven by tests that count embedding-provider calls (oracle: provider call count stays 1 across repeats).

- Golden-311 parity unchanged with the cache cold and warm.
- No behavior change when the Turso cache DB is unreachable (search proceeds, cache write dropped).

body:
Split from #1239 by the task 15180 fresh triage (2026-11-14, lane any-c). Parent: #1239 (dashboard: full id platform coverage).

## Why this exists

Task 8045 (the original P1 small_fix for #1239) was blocked as packet_defect on 2026-11-04 because the aggregator had no queue read source and no safe read-only queue API existed: "Specify a safe read-only queue endpoint/credential, issue-to-task join key, complete/partial-read semantics, source timestamps and queue freshness threshold... Do not reuse the dispatch service-role credential."

That premise is now retired. The queue runs on the Turso backend behind the fleet queue-broker (code#6741), which exposes read surfaces the coverage reconciliation already uses (code#7016): `/list` (rich rows: status, attempts, max_attempts, lane, worker, lease, progress) and `/health` counts, plus `/coverage`. The broker is laptop-local (100.99.113.103:4801, token file ~/.config/queue-broker/token) — the same host and access model the aggregator already runs under (loopback + tailnet only, #898).

## Work

Add a read-only fleet-queue collector to pm-stack/aggregator:

- A sources/ collector that calls the queue-broker's read verbs only (`/health`, `/list`) with the broker token read from its file; NO write verbs, NO dispatch service-role credential, NO direct Turso credential in the aggregator.
- Config: broker URL + token file path via the aggregator's existing config pattern; a fixture/offline mode for tests (mirror sources/fixtures.ts).
- Output shape: per-queue counts (queued/claimed/parked/blocked/done, oldest queued age) + task rows (id, queue, status, issue join via dedupe_key / payload issue number, worker/lane, updated_at), each payload carrying its source timestamp.
- Freshness semantics per #1239's rules: if the broker read fails or the payload is older than the aggregator's feed stale threshold, the collector reports the source as stale/unavailable (the panels must show a stale-source warning, never silently old data).
- Issue-to-task join key: dedupe_key (`repo-health:v1:<kind>:<repo>:issue:<n>`) with payload.issue.number as the corroborating field; document the join in the collector header.

## Acceptance

- Collector returns live queue data from the laptop broker in a local run, with source timestamps on the payload.
- Tests: fixture-backed unit tests cover the row projection, the dedupe-key join, and the stale/unavailable path (broker error -> stale marker, no throw-away-the-page failure).
- No write path: the collector module imports no enqueue/claim/complete client surface (grep-verifiable).
- This unblocks the Queue & fleet panel and the queue half of the Path to Phase 12 panel for #1239; those packets name this issue's task as their gate.

title: ci(pm-stack): opencode-claimant launch/send/dispatch Python suites (51 tests) run nowhere — pm-stack-tests.yml invokes only test_poll.py/test_claimant.py

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

labels.name: epic/pm-stack
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/` carries three Python test modules that no CI venue invokes:

- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_launch_one.py` — 26 tests (`TestLaunchOne*`)
- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_send_to_opencode.py` — 14 tests (`TestSendToOpenCode*`)
- `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_dispatch_batch.py` — 11 tests (`TestDispatchBatch*`)

Total **51 tests**, all passing on current main.

- `.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` is the pm-stack venue. Its Python step invokes only `test_poll.py`, `test_claimant.py`, `test/test_claimant.py`, and `grist/test_update_choice_options.py` — **none** of the three files above.
- A repo-wide search finds **no** reference to `test_launch_one`, `test_send_to_opencode`, or `test_dispatch_batch` in `.github/`, `scripts/`, `justfile`, or any `*.nix` file.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` has no entry for these three files: `opencode-claimant.install` covers only `test/install.test.mjs`, and `pm-stack.claimant.poll` covers only `test_poll.py`.

Verified this run on `origin/main` at `668f8de210` (clean checkout, HEAD == origin/main):

```
$ cd pm-stack/opencode-claimant && python3 -m unittest test_launch_one test_send_to_opencode test_dispatch_batch
Ran 51 tests in 0.081s
OK
```

## Why it matters

These suites cover the claimant's launch-one path, the `send_to_opencode` task dispatch (including the #9103 code-stream whitelist handling), and the dispatch-batch orchestration — the core of the fleet's task launch pipeline. Because nothing runs them, a regression in any of these (including the recent code-stream fix) passes CI silently. This is the same class the fleet has already fixed per suite: #9860 (decision-events-worker), #8026 (watchdog-state), #6090/#6091 (dispatch + claimant install).

## Suggested fix shape

Follow the guarded-step pattern already in `pm-stack-tests.yml` (see the "Test claimant and grist Python suites" step):

- Add a step that asserts each of the three files exists (fail the job if not, so a green run can never be a silently skipped suite), then runs `python3 -m unittest` on each.
- Add `.github/test-suite-registry.json` rows recording the venue for each (or one combined row), mirroring the existing `pm-stack.claimant.poll` entry.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A CI step runs `test_launch_one.py`, `test_send_to_opencode.py`, and `test_dispatch_batch.py`, and fails if any file is missing or any test fails.
- [ ] `.github/test-suite-registry.json` records the suite's venue.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: #9103 is a behavioral bug in `send_to_opencode`; #9532/#9529 are main-run failures about the already-wired suites. None tracks wiring for these three files.
