body: You are "Palette" 🎨 - a UX-focused agent who adds small touches of delight and accessibility to the user interface. Your mission is to find and implement ONE micro-UX improvement that makes the interface more intuitive, accessible, or pleasant to use. ## Sample Commands You Can Use (these are illustrative, you should first figure out what this repo needs first) **Run tests:** `pnpm test` (runs vitest suite) **Lint code:** `pnpm lint` (checks TypeScript and ESLint) **Format code:** `pnpm format` (auto-formats with Prettier) **Build:** `pnpm build` (production build - use to verify) Again, these commands are not specific to this repo. Spend some time figuring out what the associated commands are to this repo. ## UX Coding Standards **Good UX Code:** ```tsx // ✅ GOOD: Accessible button with ARIA label // ✅ GOOD: Form with proper labels ``` **Bad UX Code:** ```tsx // ❌ BAD: No ARIA label, no disabled state, no loading // ❌ BAD: Input without label ``` ## Boundaries ✅ **Always do:** - Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` based on this repo before creating PR - Add ARIA labels to icon-only buttons - Use existing classes (don't add custom CSS) - Ensure keyboard accessibility (focus states, tab order) - Keep changes under 50 lines ⚠️ **Ask first:** - Major design changes that affect multiple pages - Adding new design tokens or colors - Changing core layout patterns 🚫 **Never do:** - Use npm or yarn (only pnpm) - Make complete page redesigns - Add new dependencies for UI components - Make controversial design changes without mockups - Change backend logic or performance code PALETTE'S PHILOSOPHY: - Users notice the little things - Accessibility is not optional - Every interaction should feel smooth - Good UX is invisible - it just works PALETTE'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY: Before starting, read .Jules/palette.md (create if missing). Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL UX/accessibility learnings. ⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover: - An accessibility issue pattern specific to this app's components - A UX enhancement that was surprisingly well/poorly received - A rejected UX change with important design constraints - A surprising user behavior pattern in this app - A reusable UX pattern for this design system ❌ DO NOT journal routine work like: - "Added ARIA label to button" - Generic accessibility guidelines - UX improvements without learnings Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title] **Learning:** [UX/a11y insight] **Action:** [How to apply next time]` PALETTE'S DAILY PROCESS: 1. 🔍 OBSERVE - Look for UX opportunities: ACCESSIBILITY CHECKS: - Missing ARIA labels, roles, or descriptions - Insufficient color contrast (text, buttons, links) - Missing keyboard navigation support (tab order, focus states) - Images without alt text - Forms without proper labels or error associations - Missing focus indicators on interactive elements - Screen reader unfriendly content - Missing skip-to-content links INTERACTION IMPROVEMENTS: - Missing loading states for async operations - No feedback on button clicks or form submissions - Missing disabled states with explanations - No progress indicators for multi-step processes - Missing empty states with helpful guidance - No confirmation for destructive actions - Missing success/error toast notifications VISUAL POLISH: - Inconsistent spacing or alignment - Missing hover states on interactive elements - No visual feedback on drag/drop operations - Missing transitions for state changes - Inconsistent icon usage - Poor responsive behavior on mobile HELPFUL ADDITIONS: - Missing tooltips for icon-only buttons - No placeholder text in inputs - Missing helper text for complex forms - No character count for limited inputs - Missing "required" indicators on form fields - No inline validation feedback - Missing breadcrumbs for navigation 2. 🎯 SELECT - Choose your daily enhancement: Pick the BEST opportunity that: - Has immediate, visible impact on user experience - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines - Improves accessibility or usability - Follows existing design patterns - Makes users say "oh, that's helpful!" 3. 🖌️ PAINT - Implement with care: - Write semantic, accessible HTML - Use existing design system components/styles - Add appropriate ARIA attributes - Ensure keyboard accessibility - Test with screen reader in mind - Follow existing animation/transition patterns - Keep performance in mind (no jank) 4. ✅ VERIFY - Test the experience: - Run format and lint checks - Test keyboard navigation - Verify color contrast (if applicable) - Check responsive behavior - Run existing tests - Add a simple test if appropriate 5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your enhancement: Create a PR with: - Title: "🎨 Palette: [UX improvement]" - Description with: * 💡 What: The UX enhancement added * 🎯 Why: The user problem it solves * 📸 Before/After: Screenshots if visual change * ♿ Accessibility: Any a11y improvements made - body:
Second occurrence under identical conditions (first: 2026-11-13 reconcile; recurrence: code#8170, closed 2026-11-14).

Problem: lane sessions keep doing work directly in the laptop primary checkout (~/git/code) instead of a worktree. The dirt then blocks deploys that run from the primary, and each rescue costs a full preservation + per-hunk accounting pass. In both occurrences the dirt turned out to be stale-base copies of work that had already landed on main — pure waste and deploy risk, no unique work either time.

Prevention ask (from code#8170's body, still unimplemented at its close):
- A lane/session that starts working in the primary checkout gets stopped or redirected to a worktree (claimant/launcher-level check: session directory scope == primary path -> refuse or relocate).
- A main-holding worktree or a dirty primary raises an alert through the aggregator before it blocks a deploy (pm-git-sync already observes the state every ~30s; a dirty-primary condition is a cheap signal to surface).

Acceptance: a session launched with the primary as its directory is redirected to a worktree (or refused with the reason recorded), and a deliberately dirtied primary produces one alert incident naming the dirt — demonstrated once each.

title: codedb-bridge: parseDaemonUrl errors echo the raw CODEDB_DAEMON_URL — userinfo/query rejections print embedded credentials and tokens to stderr (PR #4199)

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.name: app/codedb-bridge
labels.description: bin/codedb-bridge.mjs — stdio MCP bridge to the shared codedb daemon

body:
## Finding

PR #4199 made `parseDaemonUrl` in `bin/codedb-bridge.mjs` reject a `CODEDB_DAEMON_URL` carrying a query string, fragment, or userinfo instead of silently stripping them (fixing #4198). But every error `parseDaemonUrl` throws interpolates the **raw URL value**, and the new branches additionally interpolate the sensitive components themselves — so the rejection prints the very secrets it is protecting into the error message:

- The userinfo branch fires exactly when the URL embeds credentials, and its message includes `CODEDB_DAEMON_URL="${value}"` — the full raw URL, password included.
- The query branch includes both `${value}` and `(query "${url.search}")` — a query such as `?token=secret` (the shape used in PR #4199's own test fixture) is printed verbatim, twice.

The caller prints the message to stderr and exits (`console.error(err.message); process.exit(1)`), and codedb-bridge runs as a stdio MCP server — stderr is captured into MCP host/client logs, so an embedded daemon password or token lands in log files that outlive the process.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4199 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4199 (merge commit `cc5effd832a1d2587f61c6301c83f69643e86716`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare status `behind`). The pre-existing throws already interpolated `${value}`; #4199 added three new throws on the credential/token-bearing shapes.
- Current main `60f92edfee0a70b6891a6d7da72593087924ccdc`, `bin/codedb-bridge.mjs`:
  - `parseDaemonUrl` throws interpolating `${value}` at lines 54 (invalid URL), 58 (non-origin), 63 (query, also `"${url.search}"`), 68 (fragment, also `"${url.hash}"`), and ~73 (userinfo).
  - Caller at lines 352–355: `daemonUrl = parseDaemonUrl(process.env.CODEDB_DAEMON_URL)` inside a try whose catch does `console.error(err.message); process.exit(1)`.
- PR #4199's test (`bin/codedb-bridge.test.mjs`) asserts the throws match `/CODEDB_DAEMON_URL.*query/` etc., but never asserts what the messages must **not** contain; its fixtures include `http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:7719/` and `http://127.0.0.1:7719/?token=secret`, both of which appear verbatim in the thrown messages today.

## Why it matters

The triage decision on #4198 was "reject, do not honour" because credentials in this URL would otherwise be silently dropped. Echoing them into stderr defeats the other half of that protection: an operator who pasted a credential-bearing URL gets a startup failure whose log line contains the password/token in cleartext, in a log stream (MCP host logs) that is routinely shared for debugging. Error messages for secret-bearing input should name the offending component, never its value.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `parseDaemonUrl` error message contains the URL's password, userinfo, query value, or fragment value; messages name the component only (e.g. "must not carry userinfo (embedded credentials)"), with the raw `${value}` interpolation removed or redacted in all branches of `parseDaemonUrl` (including the pre-existing invalid-URL and non-origin branches).
- Tests assert the negative: for inputs like `http://user:pass@127.0.0.1:7719/` and `http://127.0.0.1:7719/?token=secret`, the thrown message matches the component name and does **not** contain `pass` or `secret`.
- Rejection behavior is otherwise unchanged: query/fragment/userinfo still throw, valid origins still parse, and the existing #4198 tests keep passing.

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #4199 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches (`codedb-bridge`, `CODEDB_DAEMON_URL`) returned #4198 (closed — the silent-strip bug this PR fixed), #4191 (closed — fetch timeout), and unrelated items; no issue covers credential echo in the validation errors.

title: mcpx(mcpserver): JSON-null root capability declarations still count as declared — {"sampling":null} passes CanSample, {"roots":null} passes the roots/list gate (PR #4194 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4194 (fixing #2474) taught mcpx's sub-capability gates to ignore JSON `null` declarations, and added an explicit root check to `CanElicit` — but two root gates still use the presence-only `Peer.Declared`, so a JSON-null **root** capability declaration still counts as declared:

- `CanSample()` is `return p.Declared("sampling")` — a client sending `{"sampling": null}` is treated as having declared sampling.
- The `roots/list` branch of `Question.Sendable` is `return p.Declared("roots")` — a client sending `{"roots": null}` is treated as having declared roots.

`Peer.Declared` (conn.go) is a bare map-presence check (`_, ok := p.Caps[name]`). #2474's own `declaredValue` comment names exactly this failure: a presence check counts a null declaration as declared. The elicitation root gate was fixed with `declaredValue(p.Caps["elicitation"])`; the sampling and roots root gates were not.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4194 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4194 (merge commit `bc20bb283c8d863fdb4fce2342c911e7f2b158e9`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare status `behind`). It converted `DeclaredExtension`, the `CanElicit` root/form/url branches, and `samplingSub` (tools/context) to `declaredValue`, but left `CanSample` and the `roots/list` Sendable branch on `Declared`.
- Current main `60f92edfee0a70b6891a6d7da72593087924ccdc`, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/mcpserver/conn.go`:
  - `Peer.Declared` — presence-only (lines 243–246).
  - `CanSample` — `return p.Declared("sampling")` (line 303).
  - `Question.Sendable` — `case "sampling/createMessage": return p.CanSample() && (...)` (lines 595–601); `case "roots/list": return p.Declared("roots")` (lines 602–603).
  - Contrast: `CanElicit` root gate — `if !declaredValue(p.Caps["elicitation"]) { return false }` (line 273), the pattern #4194 established.
  - `AnswersInline()` (line ~400) is `p.CanElicit("form") || p.CanSample()`, so the sampling-null hole also flips `AnswersInline` (used by ask.go to decide a question may be answered inline).
- Existing #2474 tests pin null for elicitation root/form/url, sampling **sub**-capabilities (`{"sampling":{"tools":null,"context":null}}`), and extension entries — no test pins a null sampling **root** or a null roots declaration.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk)

Result: **reproduced**.

- Commit tested: `60f92edfee0a70b6891a6d7da72593087924ccdc` (current main, detached worktree on the laptop, removed after the run).
- Command: `go test ./internal/mcpserver/ -run TestProbeNullRootCaps -count=1 -v` in `pkgs/mcpx` (one-off probe test in package `mcpserver_test`, saved as `probe_nullroot_test.go` in the review evidence; not committed).
- Environment: laptop (host `amd`) via the fleet laptop SSH route; the narrow package test only — no full suite, no CI changes, no application-code changes.
- Result: 1 test, PASS (probe logs the gate outcomes). Observed behavior:
  - `{"sampling":null}` peer → `CanSample=true`, `AnswersInline=true`, a plain `sampling/createMessage` question `Sendable=true` (while `CanSampleTools=false`, correctly).
  - `{"roots":null}` peer → `Declared("roots")=true`, `roots/list` question `Sendable=true`.
  - Controls: `{"elicitation":null}` → `CanElicit("form")=false` (the #4194 fix); empty caps `{}` → `CanSample=false`, both questions not sendable.

## Why it matters

This is the exact invariant #2474 was filed and closed for — "a client is never sent something it did not declare" (`TestAClientIsNeverSentSomethingItDidNotDeclare`). A host that serializes an unset sampling or roots capability as JSON `null` (the shape #2474 documents real clients produce) will be sent a `sampling/createMessage` or `roots/list` request it never agreed to, instead of the question staying with the broker. The fix that closed #2474 is incomplete at the two remaining presence-only root gates.

## Acceptance criteria

- `CanSample()` returns `false` for a `{"sampling": null}` declaration (root value checked with `declaredValue`, mirroring the `CanElicit` root gate), while `{"sampling": {}}` still returns `true`.
- The `roots/list` branch of `Question.Sendable` returns `false` for `{"roots": null}`, while `{"roots": {}}` / `{"roots": {"listChanged": true}}` still return `true`.
- New tests in the #2474 style pin: null sampling root grants no plain sampling question and no `AnswersInline`; null roots grants no `roots/list`; non-null empty-object declarations for both still count as declared.
- No behavior change for elicitation, sampling sub-capability, or extension gates (existing #2474 tests keep passing).

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #4194 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches (`sampling null capability`, `CanSample`, `declaredValue`, `roots null declared`) returned only #2474 (closed — elicitation + sub-capabilities) and unrelated items; no open or closed issue covers the sampling/roots root gates.

title: Productionize the OpenClaw comment loop: zero-token pre-filter watcher, gateway resilience, real quota_left

labels.name: kind/chore
labels.description: Routine maintenance, housekeeping, dependency hygiene

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: area/infra
labels.description: Infrastructure, deployment, and operations

labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Productionize the OpenClaw comment loop (follow-up to pilot #1190)

Pilot #1190 (task 15863, lane code-d, 2026-11-14) proved the comment loop works with the pinned `pilot-loop:v1` format, and killed the naive watcher design on cost. Production work, in order:

1. **Zero-token pre-filter watcher.** Replace the every-2-minute LLM poll (measured 39k-81k total tokens per idle poll, ~1.2-2.4M tokens/hour idle) with an OpenClaw cron **command payload** (shell) that polls the designated issue for a new unanswered `pilot-loop:v1` round and only wakes an agent turn when one appears. Idle cost must be ~0 tokens.
2. **Gateway resilience.** On 2026-11-14 the `openclaw-gateway.service` was found inactive (port 18789 refusing) despite being linked; the pilot lane started it manually. Give the gateway a restart/watchdog story (Restart policy, health check + auto-restart, or a documented start step in the watcher pre-filter) so the loop does not silently die with the gateway.
3. **A quota source for `quota_left`.** The pilot SESSION-REPORT could only answer `unknown` for quota_left. Wire the watcher turn to a real quota read (fleet provider-quota registry / route status) so the babysitter field is substantive.
4. **Turn timeout floor.** The first pilot watcher turn died at the 150s cron timeout in phase `model-call-started` (route opencode-route/workhorse cold start). Production watcher turns need a >=600s timeout or a warm route.

Acceptance: a status-request round on a designated issue is answered end-to-end by the production watcher with an idle-hour token cost of ~0, a SESSION-REPORT whose quota_left is a real value, and the gateway-down case is detected and recovered (or surfaced) without a human starting the service.

Source: pilot report on issue #1190 (task 15863 completion comment, 2026-11-14).

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed — prepared by pr-comment-review 2026-11-13 07:54 CST run; held in backlog over the per-run filing cap)

**mcpx adapter import normalizes a completion file's program name (dots become dashes, e.g. `toolbox.v2` → `toolbox-v2`) before passing it to the completion parser, whose fish command filter compares `complete -c <name>` against the normalized name — so every line of a valid `toolbox.v2.fish` is discarded and the import fails as empty; for bash/zsh the normalized name is also stored as the executable command.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9161, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import.go:479` at review:

> "Keep the completion command separate from the adapter name. For a completion file whose program name contains a dot, such as `toolbox.v2.fish`, this normalization changes the name to `toolbox-v2` before it is passed to `parseCompletion()`. `parseFishCompletion()` then discards every `complete -c toolbox.v2 ...` line because its command filter compares against the normalized name, so a valid completion file fails import as empty. For bash and zsh, generation instead stores the normalized name as the executable command. Retain the original program name for parsing and execution, and sanitize only the adapter namespace."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9161 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161#discussion_r4558765519 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T01:52:25Z

## No-response evidence

- Thread unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13), no replies; PR merged after the comment.

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13)

- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import.go` on main: `buildCompletionFileImport` computes `name = adapterName(completionName(base, shell))` (dots → dashes) and passes that same `name` to `parseCompletion(...)` and as the spec command; `parseFishCompletion` in `adapter_import_parse.go` skips any line whose `-c` value differs from that name.

## Acceptance criteria

- The original program name is retained for completion parsing and for the generated spec's command; only the adapter namespace name is sanitized.
- Regression test imports a `toolbox.v2.fish` fixture and asserts a non-empty declaration.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on the filed issue.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed — prepared by pr-comment-review 2026-11-13 07:54 CST run; held in backlog over the per-run filing cap)

**mcpx adapter import's fish tokenizer ignores escapes inside single quotes, so a description containing an escaped apostrophe (e.g. fd's `--ignore-file` described as `'Add a custom ignore-file in \'.gitignore\' format' -r -F`) closes and reopens the quote and swallows the following `-r -F` option metadata into the description — the generated parameter becomes boolean and renders only `--ignore-file`, losing its required value.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9161, `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import_parse.go:45` at review:

> "Honor escaped apostrophes inside fish single quotes. When a fish description contains an escaped apostrophe, ignoring escapes inside single quotes can consume the option metadata following the description. The installed `/usr/share/fish/completions/fd.fish:15` describes `--ignore-file` using `'Add a custom ignore-file in \'.gitignore\' format' -r -F`; this tokenizer incorrectly closes and reopens quotes, swallowing `-r -F` into the description. The resulting parameter is boolean and renders only `--ignore-file`, whereas the inspected `fdfind --help` explicitly documents `--ignore-file <path>`. Handle fish's escaped apostrophes and backslashes inside single-quoted strings so required-value markers remain separate tokens."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9161 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9161#discussion_r4558765532 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T01:52:25Z

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13)

- `pkgs/mcpx/internal/cli/adapter_import_parse.go` on main: `fishTokens` handles backslash escapes only inside double quotes; inside single quotes a backslash is written literally and the following `'` closes the quote, exactly as flagged.

## Acceptance criteria

- `fishTokens` honors fish's escaped apostrophes/backslashes inside single-quoted strings; `-r -F` after such a description tokenizes as separate option metadata.

This violates the operator-script contract in `AGENTS.md`, which requires every unaccounted-for argument to produce a non-zero usage error. title: pm-aggregator: /program + /board stall ~8.2s and /program 503s when the projector is slow — briefs latest-comments fan-out is uncached with an 8s abort cliff
body:
Distinct defect in the #5082 surface family, root-caused 2026-11-13 (follow-up lane to #9594, which covers the separate post-restart boot stall).

## Symptom

Pool-quota-steward runs 376 and 377 (2026-11-14T04:21Z / 05:20Z, #5082 comments 6871649763 / 6872326046): `/program` returned **503 on pass 1** in both runs (11.38s / 11.57s), recovering on pass 2; `/board` pass 1 was 9.84s / 10.21s and `/api/overview.json` 7.21s / 7.24s in the same passes. Run 369 had earlier measured `/api/program.json` at 17.83s on pass 1.

## Measured root cause (2026-11-13 evening, laptop, live service)

Reproduced with a timed probe loop over the steward surface set (15s cadence, 23:34–23:45 CST): from 23:37:34 to ~23:40:27, `/board` and `/program` — and only those two surfaces — repeatedly took **8.11–8.55s** per hit, then decayed (6.44s, 2.79s) back to ~0.3s. `/api/program.json` stayed at 0.04s throughout; `/`, `/today`, `/quota`, `/frag/overview` never stalled.

- The two stalling surfaces are exactly the ones whose handlers call `briefCommentsFor` → `source.latestComments(refs)` on **every request, uncached** (server.ts; used by boardRender, attentionRender, the roadmap handler, and the /program handler). `/api/program.json` does not read comments and never stalled.
- `projectorLatestComments` (src/sources/live.ts) fans out one projector `GET /comments?refs=<ref>&limit=1` per ref in batches of 16. Every fetch carries `AbortSignal.timeout(8000)` (getJson). When the projector is slow, each batch resolves at the 8s abort, the whole call returns null, and the page pays ~8.2s before the fail-soft fallback — the measured stall to within measurement noise.
- The projector was slow because `POST /reconcile` runs `reconcileRepos` **inline in the projector process** (pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts), triggered every 15 min by pm-projector-reconcile.timer. The 23:30 CST run was still active 13+ min later; a direct projector `/comments` hit inside the window measured **11.2s** (vs 0.0006s warm). Steward passes at ~:20 land ~5 min after each :15 reconcile start, while the sweep is in an apply-heavy phase.
- `/program` converts the stall into a 503 because it is a bounded dashboard route: assembly past the 10s deadline serves the last-good response only if it is ≤5 min old, and an hourly visitor's last-good is always older — so the timeout path returns the hard 503 (184 B body, as measured).

## Fix (aggregator side, this lane)

1. Per-ref stale-while-revalidate cache for latest comments in the live source: fresh entries serve from cache; expired entries serve stale immediately and refresh single-flight in the background; only never-seen refs pay a projector read on the request path. A failed refresh keeps the stale value (the TodayCache contract the rest of the stack already uses, #1179/#5082).
2. Boot warm-up also primes the briefs comments for the program pool refs, so the first post-restart `/program` and `/board` do not pay the fan-out either (companion to the #9594 boot prime in PR #9596).
3. `/api/program.json` joins `BOUNDED_DASHBOARD_PATHS`: run 369's 17.83s unbounded wait becomes a deadline-bounded stale-or-503 response like its HTML twin.

The projector-side inline reconcile (a >13 min sweep occupying the read process every 15 min) is the environmental trigger; it is recorded here as context, not fixed in this lane.

Refs #5082 (closed family track — stays closed), #9594 (sibling boot defect, same PR).

title: ci(id): biome-check fails on main — pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.test.ts is unformatted (#9339)

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Summary
`nix flake check (biome-check)` fails on current main (`f667b108b5`): `biome format` wants to reflow one line in `pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.test.ts`.

## Evidence
Run the check's exact command in `pkgs/id` on current main:
```
biome format --files-ignore-unknown=true web/src/image-browser.test.ts
```
⇒ `Found 1 error`:
```diff
393    │ -     ["missing field", { images: [{ hash: "abc123", name: "cat.png", url: "/blob/abc123?filename=cat.png" }], next_cursor: null }],
       │ +     [
       │ +       "missing field",
       │ +       { images: [{ hash: "abc123", name: "cat.png", url: "/blob/abc123?filename=cat.png" }], next_cursor: null },
       │ +     ],
```
A whole-tree run of the biome-check command reports exactly this one error (100 files checked). The line was introduced by `25d3e8ada4` (PR #9339, "perf(id/web): paginate image browser listing").

## Why it matters
`biome-check` is part of the main-tier `id` workflow's flake check matrix; main CI stays red until the file is formatted.

## Fix
Run `biome format --write` on `pkgs/id/web/src/image-browser.test.ts` (a pure reflow, no semantic change).

*Filed by the OpenChamber issue-sweep task; fixed in the same pass, so no triage packet is queued.*

title: fix(id-worlds): world actor discards self.persist(...) errors on revocation and capability grants

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence
In `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor.rs`, `self.persist(...)` returns `Result<()>`, but its return value is discarded with `let _ = self.persist(...)` after mutating in-memory state:

- `actor.rs:2484-2498`: `self.core.revoke_tree(participant_id)` mutates in-memory state, then `let _ = self.persist(JournalEntry::Revoked { participant_id, by });` drops any disk/I/O error, and `audit_admin_result(..., true)` + `reply.send(was_active)` report success to the caller.
- `actor.rs:1364` and `actor.rs:1552`: `let _ = self.persist(JournalEntry::CapsGranted { granted });` similarly drops persistence errors while arming subscriptions or allowing capability execution.

## Why it matters
If journal persistence fails (e.g., disk full or I/O error), a revoked participant appears revoked in-memory and to the caller, but will be active again on restart or replica recovery. Similarly, capability grants can take effect in-memory without being durably recorded.

## Acceptance criteria
- Handle or propagate `self.persist(...)` errors in `actor.rs` for `Revoked` and `CapsGranted` instead of discarding them with `let _ =`.
- Do not report success (or commit/broadcast the in-memory state change) if journal persistence fails.
- Add unit tests covering `self.persist(...)` failure on revocation and capability grant.

## Summary
`pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/Cargo.toml` omits the `[lints.rust]` and `[lints.clippy]` tables (`unwrap_used = "deny"`, `expect_used = "deny"`, `panic = "deny"`, etc.) that every other extracted `pkgs/id` crate carries.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` `d4f6a03c5d`)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/Cargo.toml` ends at `[dev-dependencies]` (line 57) with no `[lints` section.
- Every sibling crate (`id-caps`, `id-core`, `id-directory`, `id-events`, `id-groups`, `id-native-shell`, `id-store`, `id-sync`, `id-web`, `id-worlds`) and `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml:216+` define `[lints.rust]` and `[lints.clippy]`.
- Extracted in commit `e4af08ffc0` ("id: extract id-cli crate; facade becomes re-exports + main.rs (split step 7b, #4411)"), `id-cli` holds ~36.7k lines of CLI, `serve`, and REPL code.

## Why it matters
`just clippy-lint` (`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`) no longer enforces `unwrap_used`/`expect_used`/`panic` denial on `id-cli`, allowing panicking calls to be added to production CLI/server paths unchecked.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Copy `[lints.rust]` and `[lints.clippy]` from `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` (or `crates/id-web/Cargo.toml`) into `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/Cargo.toml`.

body:
## Summary
All 5 `#[cfg(feature = "sandbox")]` tests in `id-web` (`world_ws.rs`) are silently compiled out because `id-web/Cargo.toml` defines no `sandbox` feature. In addition, 4 of those tests still use pre-split relative paths to `pkgs/id/examples/`, so enabling `sandbox` will immediately fail to compile/run until those paths are updated.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` `d4f6a03c5d`)
1. **Missing feature:** `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/Cargo.toml:18-19` defines only `default = []` (no `sandbox` feature, and `id-worlds` is a dev-dependency without `sandbox` forwarded).
2. **Compiled-out tests & helpers:** `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/world_ws.rs` gates 3 helpers (`:1412, :1431, :1455`) and 5 `#[tokio::test]` functions (`:1647, :1726, :1815, :1894, :1984`) on `#[cfg(feature = "sandbox")]`.
3. **Stale paths from crate split (`9d3f035666`):**
   - `world_ws.rs:1661`: `include_bytes!("../../examples/roc-counter/counter.wasm")` (resolves to `pkgs/id/crates/examples/...`, missing; needs `../../../examples/...`)
   - `world_ws.rs:1829`: `include_bytes!("../../examples/roc-text-counter/text-counter.wasm")` (missing; needs `../../../examples/...`)
   - `world_ws.rs:1745, :1754, :1913, :1922`: `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/examples/roc-world")` (resolves to `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/examples/roc-world`, missing; needs `/../../examples/roc-world`).

## Why it matters
The 5 WebSocket+Roc sandbox tests (`browser_websocket_can_upload_and_run_a_roc_module`, etc.) are silently skipped even under `--all-features`, leaving browser-to-Roc world execution untested in `id-web`.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Declare `sandbox = ["id-worlds/sandbox"]` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/Cargo.toml` (and forward `"id-web?/sandbox"` from `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` if appropriate).
2. Update the `include_bytes!` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` paths in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/world_ws.rs` (`:1661, :1745, :1754, :1829, :1913, :1922`) to point to `pkgs/id/examples/`.
3. Verify `cargo test -p id-web --features sandbox` compiles and runs all 5 `world_ws` sandbox tests.

body:
## Summary
The `web_router_security` integration test in `id-web` is silently compiled out (0 tests run) because it still carries `#![cfg(feature = "web")]` from before the crate split, while `id-web` has no `web` feature.

## Evidence (verified on `origin/main` `d4f6a03c5d`)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/tests/web_router_security.rs:3`:
  ```rust
  #![cfg(feature = "web")]
  ```
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/Cargo.toml:18-19`:
  ```toml
  [features]
  default = []
  ```
- Commit `9d3f035666` ("id: extract id-web crate (split step 6c, #4409)") moved `tests/web_router_security.rs` from `pkgs/id/tests/` (where `web` was a facade feature) into `crates/id-web/tests/`, leaving the crate-level `#![cfg(feature = "web")]` in place.
- As a result, `cargo test -p id-web --all-features` compiles the integration test binary as an empty stub and skips `every_public_router_constructor_enforces_its_security_policy` (`web_router_security.rs:130`).

## Why it matters
`every_public_router_constructor_enforces_its_security_policy` is the regression guard proving every public web router constructor enforces `WebSecurity`. Silently skipping it leaves router security policy regressions undetected in CI.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. Remove `#![cfg(feature = "web")]` from `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/tests/web_router_security.rs:3`.
2. Verify `cargo test -p id-web --test web_router_security` compiles and runs `every_public_router_constructor_enforces_its_security_policy` (non-zero test count).

title: fix(id): residency sync gate denies every scoped session under a default Policy::new — required planes are not filtered to the path's planes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## What

`SyncResidency::admit_send` and `admit_receive` pass the local scope's **entire** `Policy` to `residency::evaluate`, but supply hops for only two planes — Storage (the store) and Transport (the session transport):

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/residency_sync.rs:99-118` — both call `evaluate(&self.scope, &Self::hops(...), ...)` with two hops.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/residency.rs:229-233` — `evaluate` adds `DenyReason::PlaneUnknown(p)` for **every** `policy.required` plane that has no hop.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/residency.rs:104-111` — `Policy::new` (the documented constructor) sets `required` to **all four** planes. Nothing on the builder (`allow`, `trust_evidence_source`) removes a plane from `required`, and there is no builder method to set `required` at all.

So a scope policy built the documented way (`Policy::new([...]).allow(Storage, ...).allow(Transport, ...).trust_evidence_source(...)`) leaves `required = {Storage, Processing, Transport, Metadata}`, and the sync gate unconditionally denies with `PlaneUnknown(Processing)` + `PlaneUnknown(Metadata)` — **even when the store and transport evidence is current, trusted, and in-policy**.

This is the same path/plane-matching question step 2 already solved: `residency_inventory::admit` clones the policy and narrows it to the planes the path evaluates before calling `evaluate`:

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/residency_inventory.rs:200-201` — `policy.required.retain(|p| planes.contains(p));`

`residency_sync` omits that step, so the two step-2/step-3 modules interpret the same `Policy.required` differently. Design §3 scopes native sync to only the planes it touches — "current evidence for the receiving store and applicable controlled transport" (`pkgs/id/doc/2026-11-01_design_id3398.md:99`, native-sync row), not processing or metadata.

The module's own test masks the defect: `scoped()` hand-narrows `policy.required` to `[Storage, Transport]`, with a comment that the `Policy::new` default "would demand evidence this path never produces" (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/residency_sync.rs:169-181`). The production/documented constructor is the one that breaks.

## Reproduced

Added a unit test to `residency_sync::tests` that builds the scope policy with `Policy::new` + plane allows (leaving `required` at its default) and asserts a fully-evidenced scoped session is admitted:

```rust
let policy = Policy::new(["operator-ca".to_string()])
    .allow(Plane::Storage, &["eu"], &["local-store", "peer-store"])
    .allow(Plane::Transport, &["eu"], &["relay-eu"])
    .trust_evidence_source(Plane::Storage, "provider-control-plane")
    .trust_evidence_source(Plane::Transport, "provider-control-plane");
assert_eq!(policy.required.len(), 4);
let gate = residency(Scope::Scoped(policy)); // local+peer evidence current and in-policy
assert!(gate.admit_session(NOW).is_allow());
```

Result (fresh `origin/main` `d4f6a03c5d`, `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` reusing the prebuilt tree):

```
test residency_sync::tests::probe_default_policy_required_set_does_not_deny_scoped_sync ... FAILED
default Policy::new denied a fully-evidenced scoped sync: Deny([PlaneUnknown(Processing), PlaneUnknown(Metadata)])
test result: FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed
```

The existing six tests still pass because each builds its scope through `scoped()`, which narrows `required` first. Probe file reverted; no tree changes left.

## Why it matters

Once a caller wires the gate (`EventSyncProtocol::with_residency` / `sync_with_peer_checked`, both added in the same change), passing the operator's normal scope policy turns the residency gate into an **unconditional deny for all scoped content** — scoped native sync becomes impossible while appearing "fail-closed". A gate that denies a correctly-evidenced, in-policy path is a false denial, not a safety property. This is presently latent (`with_residency` / `sync_with_peer_checked` have no callers yet), but step 4/5 of #5529 will wire it, and the failure is silent (a `debug!` log line) and indistinguishable from a genuine evidence failure.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Mirror `residency_inventory::admit`: in `admit_send` and `admit_receive`, clone the scope's policy and `policy.required.retain(|p| planes.contains(p))` over the planes the sync path evaluates (`[Plane::Storage, Plane::Transport]`) before calling `evaluate`. A shared private helper keeps the two functions consistent.
- A unit test that builds the scope with `Policy::new` + plane allows (default `required`, **no** manual narrowing) and asserts `admit_session` allows when the store and transport evidence is current, trusted, and in-policy; and still denies when that evidence is missing/expired/revoked/out-of-policy (the existing negative cases).
- Keep the existing negative coverage (`missing_receiver_evidence_refuses_the_send`, `expired_evidence_refuses`, `revoked_evidence_refuses`, `out_of_policy_transport_refuses_the_receive`) green.

Filed by the improvement-issue creator (lane b) after a fresh source review of `developing-today/code`; verified by reading `residency_sync.rs`, `residency.rs` and `residency_inventory.rs` and by running the focused `id-events` lib test above.

title: pm-stack: decision-events Worker read-back pagination skips events sharing a timestamp (PR #9341 Codex P2)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

labels.name: source/pr-comment-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-comment-review job

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

PR #9341 (merged, `feat(pm-stack): decision-set event pipeline — Turso sync + Cloudflare Worker/D1/DO (#9335)`) adds the decision-events Worker's read-back endpoint. Codex's P2 finding: **the pagination cursor is the last returned event's timestamp alone, so events sharing that timestamp are skipped**. With three events at the same `ts` and `limit=2`, the third event is unreachable through pagination, even though the query already orders by `(ts, event_id)`.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341#discussion_r4560023676
- Reviewer: `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T05:34:08Z (P2)
- Flagged location: `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/src/index.ts:195`

> "When a page ends within a group of events sharing the same timestamp, requesting the next page with `after` equal to the last returned timestamp skips all remaining events in that group. For example, three events with identical `ts` values and `limit=2` make the third event unreachable through pagination. The ordering already uses `(ts, event_id)`; expose and apply that same composite cursor so bounded read-back does not omit events."

## No-response evidence

- The review thread contains only the Codex comment — no replies (verified 2026-11-14 via the PR comments API and a GraphQL `reviewThreads` read: `isResolved=false`, 1 comment).
- PR #9341's only commit after the comment is `66940fb15f` (2026-11-13T05:40:26Z), a merge of `origin/main` into the branch — it does not touch the flagged logic. The PR merged at 2026-11-13T05:45:31Z (merge commit `aad1d3602a`) with the finding unaddressed; the only later main commit touching these files is a treefmt style pass (`d451641c31`).
- Dedupe: open/closed issue searches by comment id, file path, and keywords (fan-out, pagination cursor, outbox-dir, webhook acknowledgement) found no issue covering this finding; parent issue #9335 is closed and does not track it.

## Still-live evidence (verified 2026-11-14 on current `main`)

- `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/src/index.ts:189-197` (`handleGetEvents`): `after` is read as a bare timestamp and the query is `... WHERE set_id = ? AND ts > ? ORDER BY ts, event_id LIMIT ?` — there is no `event_id` component to the cursor, so a page boundary inside a same-`ts` group drops the rest of the group.

## Acceptance criteria

- Read-back pagination uses a composite `(ts, event_id)` cursor (exposed and applied), so paging through a set returns every event exactly once, including groups sharing a timestamp.
- A regression test pages through at least three events with identical `ts` at a small limit and receives all of them.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue that this omission is accepted, with the reasoning recorded.

## Defect: laptop-agent broker — no singleton across two implementations + silent CONNECT-pool wedge (two fleet-blind episodes, 2026-11-13)

Lineage: broker built under #5343 (laptop-agent design, closed). This issue is the broker-reliability defect record; #5343's scope (the daemon design) does not cover it.

All times CST (UTC−6); Z = UTC. Sandbox↔laptop traffic rides the session proxy (HTTP CONNECT) to the laptop tailnet IP 100.99.113.103; the broker listens on the unix socket `~/.cache/laptop-agent/broker.sock` and pools CONNECT tunnels to the laptop agent on :4799.

### Episode 1 — duplicate brokers + ensure churn (~16:43–17:27 CST)

- `~/.cache/laptop-agent/broker.log` shows interleaved starts of **two implementations on the same socket path** all afternoon: the Python broker (`laptop-agent broker on .../broker.sock`, untimestamped lines) and the Rust fleet proxy (`fleet proxy serve start implementation=fleet-proxy version=0.1.0 pool_size=50`, pids 31923 @22:43:42Z, 39880 @22:55:22Z, 42268 @22:59:29Z), plus repeated tracebacks from `laptop-agent-broker.py` main(): `OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use`.
- Two Python broker processes ended up LISTENing on the socket simultaneously. Diagnosis at the time isolated the fault to the broker layer: a broker-bypass health call to the laptop succeeded while brokered calls failed.
- Fix applied ~17:27 CST: killed both brokers; a single broker (pid 19044) respawned; round-trip verified in 0.9s.

### Episode 2 — single broker, silently wedged pool (from ~17:36 CST; fleet blind from ~17:48 CST)

- The broker that held the socket from 23:36:01Z (pid 25276, Python) was the **sole** listener (verified via `ss -xlpn`: one listener, fd 3; `broker.pid` matched) — this is **not** the duplicate condition.
- It was nonetheless dead in place: **2 threads, zero outbound TCP tunnels** (a healthy broker holds a keep-alive pool), and **broker.log received no writes after its start** (log mtime 23:36:02Z) — a ≥20-minute total silence during the wedge.
- Clients hung, not errored: `laptop-agent.py health` blocked inside `tunnel_socket()` at `sock.recv(1)` for the full client timeout (live repro 17:57 CST: 25.0s, `CallTimeout`). Observed failures: the 17:48 CST activity-refresh probe ("laptop-agent: proxy closed during CONNECT"), a direct probe at 17:54 CST (25.4s), and the 17:57 CST repro. A fleet worker's own note from the window reads "tunnel down since ~23:37Z", corroborating onset within a minute of this broker's start.
- The log also contains an earlier uncaught `BlockingIOError: [Errno 11] Resource temporarily unavailable` traceback in the broker's `read_msg` (laptop-agent-broker.py lines 216/238) — a plausible handler-thread-killing mechanism for the silent wedge.
- The fleet queue was already in GitHub-comments fallback mode by 23:56Z ("queue backend is down"), i.e. the blind spot propagated beyond quota/supervision.

### Remediation attempt — restart does not restore service (17:58 CST → 19:46 CST)

- 23:58Z: killed pid 25276; a fresh Python broker (pid 40681) auto-respawned and failed identically (24.8s, "proxy closed during CONNECT"). A broker-bypass direct CONNECT health call also failed (8.4s) — by then the refusal had moved to / was also present in the shared CONNECT leg.
- The sandbox VM recycled ~00:05–00:15Z. Post-recycle, a Python broker (pid 2704, 01:11:49Z) briefly owned the socket, after which **`fleet proxy serve` (pid 7861, started 01:18:01Z) took over the same socket path** — and `broker.pid` did not match the actual socket owner.
- The fleet proxy fails fast and explicitly (better posture): `HTTP 502: broker: tunnel recovery for port 4799 still in flight; failing fast`, then `HTTP 502: broker: tunnel to 100.99.113.103:4799: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 11)` — but its tunnel recovery cannot complete.
- Raw CONNECT probe at 01:43Z (bypassing all broker code): the session proxy **hung ≥15s with no response** to `CONNECT 100.99.113.103:4799` and **closed instantly with an empty response** to `CONNECT 100.99.113.103:22`, while general HTTPS egress through the same proxy answered GitHub in 1.4s. So at the tail of episode 2 the proxy↔DERP↔laptop leg itself refuses/hangs CONNECTs to the laptop on both ports.
- As of 19:46 CST (01:46Z) `laptop-agent.py health` still fails; the documented sandbox-side restart has been applied (wedged broker killed; successors respawned) but service is **not** restored, because the current blocker is upstream of any broker process.

### Layer evidence summary

- Sandbox egress: healthy (GitHub via the same proxy, 1.4s).
- Laptop: healthy during episode 1 diagnosis (broker-bypass health call succeeded); unreachable by any sandbox path during episode 2's tail (both ports, raw CONNECT).
- Broker layer: at fault in episode 1 (duplicates) and at onset of episode 2 (silent single-broker wedge); not the current blocker at the tail of episode 2.

### Acceptance

1. **Singleton across implementations.** Exactly one process may own `broker.sock`, whether the Python broker or `fleet proxy serve` provides it. Concurrent ensure/start invocations from both implementations converge on one owner (no Errno 98 churn, no silent takeover); `broker.pid` always names the socket owner (checkable against `ss`). Backed by a regression test or a documented invariant. (Two auto-started implementations racing for one socket path is the root architectural smell — pick one owner for the path, or partition the paths.)
2. **Wedged-pool self-detection.** A broker whose tunnel pool is empty/dead and cannot complete a CONNECT within a bounded time must log loudly, rebuild the pool or respawn, and fail clients **fast** (<5s) with an explicit error — never accept a client connection and hang it for 25s+ in silence. The Python broker logged nothing for the entire episode-2 wedge; fleet proxy's fail-fast 502s are the behavioral floor.
3. **Handler robustness.** Uncaught `BlockingIOError` in the request path (`read_msg`) must not silently kill request handling.
4. **Log observability.** Every broker log line carries a timestamp (Python broker lines currently have none), and tunnel death/recovery events are logged as they happen, so the next episode is diagnosable from the log alone.

### Fleet impact

Quota refresh and summit supervision were blind from ~17:48 CST until at least 19:46 CST (episode 2), on top of the episode-1 window earlier in the afternoon. Restart-alone is proven insufficient as the runbook fix: it cured episode 1 and did nothing for episode 2.

> "This test still passes if the score comparison is reversed, the tool tie-breaker is removed, or `count` always equals zero. These changes would break ordering or pagination. Add a behavioral test that executes the generated `search()`. Use matches with different scores and tied scores across namespaces and tools. Check consecutive pages, a final partial page, an offset beyond the results, and negative or fractional pagination values."

## No-response evidence

- No reply, fix, or follow-up addressed this review item: the PR's two Codex P2 findings were both fixed in `bbe9dacb6a` with replies on their threads, but the CodeRabbit test item received no reply and no behavioral test was added before merge (verified 2026-11-13 from the PR's inline comments, reviews, and conversation comments).

title: pm-aggregator: first /program hit after restart stalls ~26s — boot warm-up saturates the event loop and never warms the program assembly
body:
Follow-up to #5082 (closed): a distinct defect in the same surface family, first flagged as a watch item on #5082 (comment 6865079577) and re-sighted by pool-quota-steward run 369 (/api/program.json 17.83s first pass, 0.06s second; #5082 comment 6865203340).

Measured root cause (2026-11-13, laptop, live service):
- First /api/program.json after a service restart: 26.44s and 26.48s on two controlled restarts; every later hit ~0.03s. A 150ms poll through a restart shows exactly one 26.48s response (the first on the new process), then 0.03-0.06s throughout.
- The program legs themselves are fast in a clean process: items 0.02s, projects 0.01s, roadmap 0.29s, orchestration 0.02s, coverageCensus 0.03s (programRefs = 8).
- Warm TTL-expiry first pass is 0.023s — the TodayCache SWR conversion from #9589 works; expiry is not the stall.
- The stall is event-loop queueing at boot: the first buildQuotaAnalytics is fully synchronous and measures 12.23s in a clean process (second build 0.00s), and the boot warm-up ran it plus three cold context assemblies on the single Bun event loop. Any request arriving in that window queues behind it.
- /program was the visible victim because programSources was the one major assembly the boot warm-up did NOT warm, so its first post-restart request always landed cold, inside/behind that backlog. Deploy restarts are frequent (three today), so first-pass-after-restart is the recurring shape of both sightings.

Fix (this lane): prime the aggregates cache at boot through the existing day-sliced SWR refresh (primeAttemptAggregates in analytics-store.ts) instead of the synchronous build, and warm programSources() alongside board/overview/today in server.ts. Request-path semantics unchanged: a /quota request landing before the prime settles still pays the synchronous cold build on its own path, as today.

Acceptance: >=5 cache-expiry cycles with first-pass /program and /api/program.json each cycle, a 6-way concurrent cold burst after restart, and a closing sweep of all aggregator surfaces in today's healthy ranges.

body:
## amd toplevel does not evaluate — rust-overlay has no stable 1.99.1 for the pinned rev

Found 2026-11-13 by lane code-d (task 15847) while switching the #1029 telegram fix: after the memory-wiki evaluation blocker is removed, `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` still fails:

```
error: Stable 1.99.1 is not available
… while evaluating the attribute 'stable."1.99.1"'
  at «github:oxalica/rust-overlay/4ca2963243427cb86bd6b4d9ca6010db0162a619»/lib/rust-bin.nix:115
… while evaluating the option `home-manager.users.backup.xdg.configFile."systemd/user/opencode.service".source'
… while evaluating derivation 'opencode.service'
```

So the backup home user's generated `opencode.service` pulls a Rust toolchain pinned at 1.99.1 through the pinned rust-overlay (rev 4ca29632…), whose stable manifest set does not contain 1.99.1. The 1.99.0 → 1.99.1 pin bump landed today (PR #7205, task 13513 — verified for cargo builds, which use a different toolchain source); this nix-eval consumer was not covered.

Impact: the amd NixOS configuration cannot be switched at all until this evaluates again — it blocks, among other things, the live activation of the merged #1029 telegram fix (PR #9423) and its `openclaw channels status --probe` acceptance probe (task 15847 is dep-blocked on this issue).

Fix shapes (owner's pick):
- bump the rust-overlay input (flake.lock) to a rev whose stable manifests include 1.99.1, or
- pin this consumer to a stable version the locked overlay carries (e.g. 1.99.0), or
- move the pin to the overlay's versioned manifest name if 1.99.1 exists under a different channel key.

Acceptance: `nix build .#nixosConfigurations.amd.config.system.build.toplevel` evaluates and builds on the laptop; a switch succeeds.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**The queue client's claim-stamp session lookup ignores the existing `OPENCODE_URL` and `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE` connection overrides used by the claimant tooling: it reads a different URL variable and always loads the production credential file, so it can contact a different server or authenticate with the wrong credentials — and its fail-soft return then silently leaves claims unstamped despite the configured server being available.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9025, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:1428` at review:

> "Honor the existing OpenCode connection overrides. When the claimant tooling is configured with `OPENCODE_URL` or `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE`, this lookup ignores both overrides: it reads a different URL variable and always loads the production credential file. `claimant.py` and `poll.py` use those existing overrides for their session operations, so the new queue-client lookup can contact a different server or authenticate with the wrong credentials. Its fail-soft return then silently leaves claims unstamped despite the configured server being available. Resolve the URL and credential file consistently with those callers."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9025 "fix(queue): make the #8176 claim-model stamp land on the real claim paths" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9025 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9025#discussion_r4556253578 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-12T20:58:11Z, file `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:1428`

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is **unresolved** (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13) and the Codex comment is the thread's only comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer.
- PR #9025 was merged with this lookup unchanged; no follow-up commit on main has aligned it with the claimant overrides (verified by a fresh read of `client.rs` on main, 2026-11-13).
- No existing issue covers this finding (searched open and closed issues for PR #9025 and `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE` claim-stamp keywords on 2026-11-13; no matches).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` on main, `derive_claim_model_stamp` (around line 1427): reads `std::env::var("OPENCODE_SERVER_URL")` (default `http://127.0.0.1:13420`) — not `OPENCODE_URL`.
- The same function (around lines 1431-1434) always reads `{home}/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` for the password — it never consults `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE`.
- By contrast, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py:53-55` and `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py:136-138` on main both resolve `OPENCODE_URL` (same default) and `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE` — the inconsistency the comment describes is present verbatim.

## Acceptance criteria

- The queue client's stamp lookup resolves the server URL and credential file consistently with `claimant.py`/`poll.py`: `OPENCODE_URL` and `OPENCODE_AUTH_FILE` are honored (with any existing variable kept only as a documented fallback).
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why the queue client must use a separate URL variable and the production credential file.

---
Filed by the pr-comment-review job from an unaddressed PR review comment (source: PR #9025). This issue deliberately does not reply to or resolve the source review thread.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**The #8176 claim-model stamp derives from the session's `model` field — for routed sessions that is the configured route alias (e.g. `opencode-route/workhorse`), not the provider/model/effort that actually served the claim — so routed claims permanently record the route alias and lose serving-leaf attribution.**

Codex (P2) on PR #9025, `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:1358` at review:

> "Derive the stamp from the serving leaf rather than the route. For routed sessions such as `opencode-route/workhorse`, the session's `model` identifies the configured route, not the provider/model/effort that actually served the claim. Reading this field therefore permanently records the route alias and loses the serving-leaf attribution required by `doc/fleet/queue-turso-cutover.md` and `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/prompt.md`, which explicitly distinguishes `route_usage.lastServing` from the declared route. The new Python collection stamps have the same problem because they record the future session's route before it has served anything. Use the actual serving-leaf readout when available and leave the claim unstamped otherwise."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #9025 "fix(queue): make the #8176 claim-model stamp land on the real claim paths" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9025 (merged)
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9025#discussion_r4556253567 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-12T20:58:11Z, file `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs:1358`

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is **unresolved** (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13) and the Codex comment is the thread's only comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer.
- PR #9025 was merged with this derivation unchanged; no follow-up commit on main has switched the stamp to the serving-leaf readout (verified by a fresh read of `client.rs` on main, 2026-11-13).
- No existing issue covers this finding (searched open and closed issues for PR #9025 and claim-stamp/serving-leaf keywords on 2026-11-13; only the parent issue #8176 and unrelated items matched — #8176 does not cover the route-alias defect).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

- `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs` on main: `session_model_stamp` (around lines 1349-1377) reads only the session record's `model` field (`providerID` + `id`, optional `variant`). There is no code read of `route_usage` / `lastServing` anywhere in the file — those names appear only in comments (around lines 1305-1306 and 2304-2305) asserting the stamp names the serving leaf.
- `derive_claim_model_stamp` therefore stamps the declared/route model for routed sessions, exactly as the comment describes.

## Acceptance criteria

- The claim stamp is derived from the actual serving-leaf readout (`route_usage.lastServing`) when available, and the claim is left unstamped otherwise — routed sessions no longer record the route alias as their serving model.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why the session `model` field is an acceptable serving-leaf source for routed sessions.

title: id: implement Residency step 4 — federation, relays and metadata (#5529)
body:
Implementation step 4 of the residency design (#3398, `doc/2026-11-01_design_id3398.md` §7) for epic issue #5529.

**Scope:** pkgs/id — route policy for replicated projections and world participation (federation), approved relay selection, and discovery/observability metadata destinations.

**Depends on:** step 3 (native sync and hosted bridge checks for #5529) — start only after the step-3 implementation is merged.

**Acceptance (design §3 rows + §7 step 4):**
- Jurisdiction partitioning is the default for federation; a cross-boundary shared world requires an explicit world-level policy and participant consent/disclosure.
- A valid capability plus a destination outside the allowed set is denied and creates no replica.
- Scoped routes use only approved, attested relays (relays are transport, never residency evidence); an unknown/unapproved relay or forbidden metadata destination never receives protected bytes or identifiers; changing to direct mode alone does not satisfy a strict transport requirement.
- Discovery, logs, traces and metrics have explicit metadata destinations; tests cover forbidden relay metadata, direct-route limits and telemetry egress.

Filed by queue task 9596 (lane code-a) as the ordered follow-on split the design's §7 requires.

body:
## Evidence
On current `origin/main` (`a0f3a529d3e167df0f614a598dc0c9f7aa532b0c`), the tag broadcast ring is capped at 256 events (`pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/tags.rs:402-403, 711`). In `pkgs/id/src/web/tags_ws.rs:237-258`, a `RecvError::Lagged(n)` is only logged and the WebSocket continues with newer events; the skipped events are never replayed and no resync is signaled to the client.

The browser uses incoming tag events to refresh the file list and the current file's tags (`pkgs/id/web/src/main.ts:706-733`), but its open handler only resets reconnect attempts (`:701-704`). A burst or slow WebSocket consumer that falls more than 256 events behind can therefore miss changes and keep a stale view until some unrelated later refresh. Existing WebSocket coverage verifies normal delivery and inbound frame limits (`pkgs/id/src/web/tags_ws.rs:643-704`), but not broadcast overflow/lag recovery.

This is source-traced; no runtime overflow reproduction was run.

## Acceptance criteria
- Do not silently continue after dropping tag events. Make loss trigger a reliable client refresh/resync (or close the connection with reconnect behavior that performs a full refresh).
- Add a deterministic regression that drives the receiver past the broadcast capacity and verifies the selected recovery path and that the client refreshes current state.
- Preserve normal tag-event delivery and disconnect behavior.

body:
On current main, building the `id` lib without the `sandbox` feature fails:

```
error[E0433]: cannot find `sandbox` in the crate root
    --> pkgs/id/src/boards.rs:1528:30
1528 |         let sandbox = crate::sandbox::Sandbox::compile(
note: found an item that was configured out
    --> pkgs/id/src/lib.rs:287:20
286 | #[cfg(feature = "sandbox")]
287 | pub use id_worlds::sandbox;
```

`BoardGraph::replay_game_lineage` (from the #6161 save-point work, refactored in #8902) uses `crate::sandbox` unconditionally, but `boards` is an unconditional module and `crate::sandbox` only exists under the `sandbox` feature. The default build (`default = ["sandbox", "world"]`) never sees this; the consumer that does is `id-native-shell` (F13.6, #788), which builds `id` with `default-features = false, features = ["world"]` — so `cargo test -p id-native-shell` was broken on main even though no native-shell code changed.

Fix (rides PR #7197, the PR whose named tests this unblocks): gate the one function with `#[cfg(feature = "sandbox")]`. Its only callers are boards tests, which run under the default sandbox-on build. Commit 74edbfbca2 on PR #7197.

If PR #7197 stalls, cherry-pick that commit independently — the regression is on main, not in the PR. Found by lane code-d, task 9341, 2026-11-12.

## Evidence
On fresh `origin/main` (`878f08222d5d8684eaa94f29f655da0dcbbacd6d`), `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1370-1381` converts a failed `tag_store.list_all()` into an empty metadata set with `unwrap_or_default()`. The same function returns `files` (still empty) when `store.tags().list()` fails at `:1438-1440`. During stream consumption, `while let Some(Ok(tag_info))` at `:1441` also stops at the first stream error and returns the partial list without reporting the failure.

## Impact
The file-list page/API can present an empty or incomplete result as a successful response during a storage/tag-store outage. Users may mistake a backend failure for missing files or missing metadata, and monitoring/callers cannot distinguish the failure from a genuinely empty store. This is source-traced; no injected store-failure runtime repro was run.

## Acceptance criteria
- Propagate or explicitly report metadata/tag-list/stream errors instead of silently returning an empty or partial successful list.
- Add deterministic tests for failures from `list_all`, `tags().list()`, and mid-stream tag iteration, asserting the chosen error response/behavior.
- Preserve the valid empty-store response and normal file-list behavior.

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/web/routes/file_handlers.rs:642-691` implements `images_list_handler` by listing every blob tag (`:647-655`), then awaiting a `content-type` metadata lookup for each non-internal tag (`:664-669`). For every image it also awaits `blob_size` individually (`:683-688`), and returns the complete image list in one JSON array (`:691`). Thus loading the image browser does work serially proportional to all stored tags and returns an unbounded result, even when only a small subset of the store contains images.

This is a source-verified scaling gap; I did not run a large-store benchmark. Existing image-browser issues such as #7812 concern response-shape validation, not listing cost. The broader virtual-filesystem/index design in #9100 may inform a durable index, but it does not track making this current endpoint bounded and avoiding per-tag serial round trips.

## Why it matters

As stores accumulate files, opening the image browser can incur repeated sequential metadata/blob lookups across unrelated tags, and response size grows with every image. Latency and memory use therefore grow with the store rather than the requested page.

## Acceptance criteria

- Avoid serial per-tag metadata and blob-status lookups; use an indexed/batched query or bounded concurrency.
- Bound the response for large image collections (for example, pagination), while preserving or deliberately migrating the existing client contract.
- Add deterministic coverage with many mixed internal/non-image/image tags for filtering, ordering and page boundaries, and assert the lookup strategy does not perform serial database round trips per tag.
- Keep image entries’ existing fields and URL semantics unless the client contract is intentionally migrated.

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` (`a0bf8e4ec86ff115e4b791127fb563bb361659bd`), `pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/store.rs:154-169` creates the final key path with `create_new(true)` and writes the 32-byte secret directly to it. The path becomes visible at `open()` before `write_all()` completes. `read_key_after_creation_race` (`:133-145`) retries a short file for one second, then returns `invalid key length`; it does not remove or repair that file.

If the creating process is interrupted or the write fails after file creation, there is no writer left to finish it. Future `load_or_create_keypair` calls keep failing on that residue, preventing startup with the identity until someone manually removes the key file. The existing partial-write test (`:525-567`) covers only a concurrent writer that eventually finishes; it does not cover a failed/interrupted creator. This is source-traced; no process-kill repro was run.

## Suggested fix

Publish a fully written key atomically while preserving `create_new` winner semantics and owner-only permissions, or otherwise provide safe recovery for an incomplete file without replacing a valid winner or silently rotating an existing identity.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed/interrupted first write cannot leave a partial file at the final key path that permanently blocks later startup.
- Concurrent first-run callers still converge on the same on-disk identity; neither caller overwrites the winner.
- New files remain owner-only on Unix, and pre-existing malformed key files are still rejected rather than silently replaced.
- Add deterministic regression coverage for a write failure/interruption and retain the existing concurrent/partial-writer tests.

## Problem

`pkgs/id`'s web facade (`src/web/`, feature `web`) does not compile at main ec536c5e22 — it still calls into `id-worlds` items that the #4408 crate split left `pub(crate)` or private:

- `cargo check -p id --lib --features web` (from `pkgs/id/`) fails with 5 errors, including:
  - `WorldHandle::host_view` is `pub(crate)` in `crates/id-worlds/src/world/handle.rs` (~line 1185) but is called from `src/web/world_ws.rs` host_view_handler.
  - `crate::world_session::MAX_RECORDS_PAGE_BYTES` is a `pub(crate)` alias in `crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/mod.rs` but is used by the host-view paging loop in `src/web/world_ws.rs`.
  - `WorldService.world` field is private (a `world()` method exists) where `src/web/world_ws.rs` accesses the field.
  - `crate::world_session::encode_hex` is `pub(crate)` in id-worlds but imported by world_ws tests.
- The lib *test* target additionally fails (9 errors): `crate::world_hub::testing::MemoryOpener` is `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate)` inside id-worlds, so it can never be visible to the `id` package's tests; `crate::fileops::{claim_archive_name, snapshot_provenance_tags}` unresolved from `src/web/routes.rs`; `directory_view::level_name` private from `src/web/explore.rs`.
- `--all-features` check fails too (same class), while default features (`sandbox`, `world`) check clean — which is why this survives: no CI job builds the `web` feature (id-check.yml runs default / no-default / no-world configs only).

## Impact

Any change to `src/web/world_ws.rs` (e.g. #9104) cannot be compile- or test-verified locally in the web configuration until this is fixed; the host-view / world bridge surface is effectively unbuildable from the facade crate.

## Suggested fix

Decide the intended visibility contract between the facade and id-worlds (promote the needed items to `pub` with docs, or move the web bridge into id-worlds), restore `cargo check -p id --lib --features web` and the lib test target under that feature set, and add a CI job that builds the `web` feature so it cannot silently rot again.

Found by lane code-c during task 15343 (#9104), 2026-11-13. All errors reproduce on clean main with the task's diff stashed.

body:
## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/send_to_opencode.py` cannot send a task that lives in the one-queue stream `code`:

- Its `--queue` argparse `choices` are restricted to the four pilot queue names (`repo-health-code-pilot`, `repo-health-nix-pilot`, `repo-health-openchamber-pilot`, `repo-health-opencode-pilot`).
- `launch_one.REPOS` has no `code` entry, so `send()` raises `KeyError: 'code'` at `primary = REPOS[queue_name][1]` even when the module is driven programmatically.
- `poll.fetch_claimed_rows(queue)` is keyed by the same names, while the one-queue broker (live since 2026-11-11, #8097/#8438) serves tasks whose stream is `code` (e.g. task 15341, claimed unfiltered by a Muse lane).

The #8210 transfer verb itself (`fleet queue claim --task <id> --queue code --from-session ... --session-id ...`) is stream-agnostic and works — only the claimant-side tooling whitelist is stale.

## Evidence (2026-11-12, lane any-b shift)

- Stock CLI dry-run for task 15341 with `--queue repo-health-code-pilot` failed verify_claim: "task 15341 is not claimed (by anyone) in repo-health-code-pilot" — the task is claimed in stream `code` (`fleet queue list --queue code --status claimed` shows it).
- Workaround used for task 15341: a driver importing `send_to_opencode` and registering `REPOS["code"] = ("developing-today/code", "/home/user/git/code")` on the module's own sibling copy of `launch_one` completed the send successfully (summit session bound, prompt delivered). Note the trap: `send_to_opencode` loads its own sibling copy of `launch_one` via `_load_sibling`, so patching a separately imported `launch_one` module does not take effect.

## Fix sketch

- Derive the queue/stream set from the broker (or accept any stream name) instead of the hardcoded pilot list; add a `code` stream entry mapping to developing-today/code + `/home/user/git/code`, or resolve repo/primary from the task packet's `repo` field.
- Add a regression test: send (dry-run) for a claimed task in stream `code` passes verify_claim.
- Check `launch_one.py` and `dispatch_batch.py` for the same whitelist assumption.

title: fix(id): avoid orphaned identities when registration is cancelled

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

On fresh `origin/main` (`21531e2372574bdae2483ff4bd6e527710afcc42`), `pkgs/id/src/web/identity.rs:300-318` explains that the registration critical section is deliberately detached so persistence and in-memory admission accounting finish even when the request future is cancelled. The spawned task at `:325-348` persists the record and inserts it into `clients`. Only after awaiting that task does the caller create the name watcher (`:356-362`) and sign/return the token (`:365-366`).

If the `/api/identity/register` request is cancelled while the spawned task is running, the task can still finish the database write and insert the identity, while the cancelled caller never reaches watcher creation or token issuance. That leaves a registered identity that no client received a token for. Persistent stores reload/count it on restart, so repeated disconnected registrations can consume the configured identity capacity without producing usable identities. This is a source-traced cancellation interleaving; no timing-dependent runtime repro was run.

The existing detached-task rationale prevents persisted records from being under-counted, but does not cover the post-commit cancellation window or reclaim/complete the user-visible registration result.

## Why it matters

A client disconnect or cancellation at the wrong point can permanently consume one of the bounded identity slots while losing the only token that could authenticate that identity. Repeated occurrences can exhaust the 10,000-entry default admission capacity.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and implement cancellation semantics so a cancelled registration cannot leave an unreachable identity consuming persistent or in-memory capacity (or make the completed registration result recoverable/idempotent).
- Ensure watcher creation and persisted identity state cannot diverge when cancellation races with registration completion.
- Add a deterministic regression test that pauses registration after the detached persistence/insertion begins, cancels the caller, resumes the operation, and asserts the chosen no-orphan/recovery contract, including reopen behavior for the persistent-store path.
- Preserve the current concurrent-registration capacity guarantee and verify it with existing tests.

title: fix(id/backup): prevent device binding from bypassing pending restore notifications

labels.name: kind/bug
