- quota-analytics.json: pool state = error; the 5h projection reports samples: 0, insufficient-history (fewer than two same-period readings spanning 10 minutes), while the 7d projection still says walled.

So the analytics layer treats 'no extractor samples' as an error state for the pool, overriding the fresh walled state from quota.json. Effect: the walled count in the Live Status headline understates reality by one for every uninstrumented-but-walled pool.

Fix direction: for pools whose extraction is intentional/uninstrumented, analytics should carry the pool state from quota.json (walled/healthy by its windows) instead of error. Reserve error for instrumented pools whose readings actually fail or go stale.

title: fleet(queue): max_attempts split-copy quarantine — one source of truth + blocked-row re-validation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Defect

Every queue task carries `max_attempts` in TWO copies: the tasks-row column and `payload.max_attempts`. The claim guard (#5444, `claim_guard_reason` → `validate_packet`) requires the two copies to AGREE and quarantines the task when they differ.

Drew's #8973 order (2026-11-12) raised max_attempts to 1000. The creation-default alignment (commit `d67e7bfbf`, 2026-11-14) updated the ROW copy to 1000 on live tasks while packet payload copies kept their old values (3/4/6). The guard then quarantined tasks at claim for a pure bookkeeping split: 311 on 2026-11-14, 23 on 2026-11-15, 114 more on 2026-11-16 — 449 of the 655 blocked tasks in the 2026-11-16 blocked-pile audit trace to this one defect (audit root cause #1, the "#8973 alignment accident"; evidence: goals/keep-the-four-repos-healthy blocked-audit-2026-11-16).

Second half of the defect: 99 blocked rows had BOTH copies already at 1000 yet sat blocked forever — nothing ever re-validates a blocked row, so a quarantine whose cause has been repaired (or whose recorded error no longer reproduces) never clears. The dep rechecker (#8276) only touches dep-blocked rows; a classic quarantine block has no deps and no recheck schedule.

## Fix (in flight this pass — direct implementation, PR follows in the same pass)

1. **One source of truth.** `validate_packet` stops requiring the two copies to agree: the packet/row copy is authoritative; the payload copy is range-checked only. `task_from_packet` normalizes the stored payload copy to the selected row value at enqueue, so new tasks are born aligned. Legacy split rows can never quarantine again.
2. **Blocked-row re-validation.** The broker sweep (which already carries the dep rechecker) gains a quarantine recheck: a blocked, dep-free row whose recorded error is a claim-path quarantine is re-run through the claim guard; if the error no longer reproduces, the row is requeued automatically with an auditable event. A `/quarantine-recheck` verb + CLI mirror the `/dep-recheck` shape for manual triggering.
3. Regression tests reproducing the two-copy mismatch (packet 1000 / payload 3) at both the validator and the claim guard, plus the recheck release/keep decisions.

Data repair for the live pile (copy alignment + requeue of quarantine-only rows) ran ahead of the code fix from the audit directory's repair ledger.

Cross-references: #8973 (the order that raised the value), #5444 (the claim guard), #6448 (the validation contract whose agreement rule this amends — the agreement invariant made sense when both copies were written once at creation; the #8973 bulk row update broke the premise), #9609 (the earlier ceiling half of the same accident).

title: pm-stack(dispatch): readJsonBody buffers the entire body before enforcing its 256 KiB cap

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts:65-76` (verified on origin/main):

```ts
async function readJsonBody(req: Request): Promise<unknown> {
  const text = await req.text();            // :66 — unbounded buffer
  if (new TextEncoder().encode(text).length > MAX_BODY_BYTES) throw ...
```

`MAX_BODY_BYTES = 256*1024` (`:55`) is checked only **after** `req.text()` has materialised the whole body. A 100 MiB POST is fully buffered before it is rejected. Used by `POST` intake paths (`:198`, `:420` — session/task creation). The path is authenticated (GitHub Actions OIDC or static bearer, `:16-17`, binds loopback + laptop tailnet) so this is robustness, not an unauthenticated DoS — but one misbehaving/buggy client can still OOM or stall the intake.

## Why it matters

The repo already has the bounded pattern to copy: streaming `reader.read()` + `byteLength > cap → cancel` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/request-body.ts:13-27`, and `readBoundedBody(req.body, 10_000_000)` in `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts:257` / `webhook.ts:7-29` (landed via #10638). Dispatch is the remaining intake that buffers first and checks second.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

Check the `content-length` header first, then bounded streaming read with early `reader.cancel()` and `413/400 "body: too large"` — never `await req.text()` on an unbounded stream. Add a test posting > 256 KiB and asserting rejection without full buffering (mirror the projector `write-bounds.test.ts` approach).

Deduped: `gh search issues` for dispatch body limits returns nothing; the sibling projector bounds (#10595/#10601/#10635, all fixed via #10602/#10638) are a different service; no open PR touches dispatch `server.ts`. Verified against origin/main `81d10205bf` (read-only worktree).

title: id(core): decode_canonical trusts attacker-declared array/map lengths and has no nesting bound, violating its never-panic contract

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/canonical_cbor.rs` (verified on origin/main):

- Contract (`:51-52`): "Typed profile errors. Every rejection of a signed encoding is one of these — never a panic, never a silent coercion."
- Array (`:279-286`) and map (`:287-309`) arms: `let len = self.argument(additional)?` takes a u64 straight from the input bytes (additional-27 accepts any u64 > u32::MAX in shortest form), then `Vec::with_capacity(len as usize)` allocates **before** the loop discovers the input is truncated. A ~10-byte input (`0x9B <8-byte huge length>`) triggers a multi-GB allocation attempt — `capacity overflow` panic or allocator abort, both violating the never-panic contract (an abort is uncatchable in-process).
- Byte/text strings are safe (`take()` bounds-checks against the slice, `:198-206`) — only the array/map preallocation is exposed.
- No depth bound: `value()` recurses per array element (`:283`) and map key/value (`:293,307`). Nesting is bounded only by input length (`0x81` x N nests N deep, ~2 bytes/level), so a few KB of input overflows the thread stack — again dodging the typed-error contract.
- No test coverage: `crates/id-core/tests/canonical_cbor_vectors.rs` has no giant-length, capacity, depth, or nesting test.

## Why it matters

This module's stated purpose is decoding signed records from the network; it explicitly promises panic-freedom. Today the only in-tree callers are the vector tests (no production caller yet — confirmed by grep), so this is the cheap moment to harden it: land the guards **before** the first network caller arrives rather than after a DoS.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Before allocating, bound the declared count by what the input can possibly contain (each item consumes >= 1 byte): `if len > (bytes.len() - pos) as u64 { return Err(CborError::UnexpectedEof) }`, then `with_capacity` is safe.
- Add a `MAX_NESTING_DEPTH` (e.g. 64-128, threaded through `Reader` or as a recursion parameter) returning a new `CborError::TooDeeplyNested`.
- Regression tests: giant declared length (`0x9B…`) -> `UnexpectedEof`, deep nesting (`0x81` x N) -> `TooDeeplyNested`, both asserting no panic/abort.

Deduped: `gh search issues` for canonical CBOR in this repo returns only the currency/profile design issues (#2319, #10176) and closed codec issues (#3358, #5363) — no tracker for this decoder hardening; no open PR touches `canonical_cbor.rs`. Verified against origin/main `81d10205bf` (read-only worktree).

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/crates/id-directory/src/directory_auth.rs`:

- `open_session` (`:161-174`) inserts one `SessionRecord` per call after only an expired-entry `retain` — no limit constant, no refusal path. `SESSION_TTL_MS` is 12h (`:23`), and `principal()` (`:177-185`) only removes the single token looked up, so every unexpired entry survives until the next `open_session`.
- The same struct hard-caps its siblings: pending email codes (`CODE_PENDING_LIMIT` 4096 + `CODE_PENDING_PER_ACCOUNT` 16, `:31-36`, enforced `:235-251`, introduced in #5749) and signed-request replay nonces (`SIGNED_NONCE_LIMIT` 4096 + per-key sub-limit, `:38-45`, enforced `:373-383`), each refusing with `Refusal::RateLimited`.
- Reachability: `DirectoryAction::OpenSession` (`directory_view.rs:1195-1202`) mints a session for any resolved account/admin viewer — one valid credential yields unlimited 12-hour entries.

## Why it matters

One authenticated caller can grow `sessions` without bound (memory exhaustion / degraded `retain` scans on every open). The crate already decided this class of map must be bounded (#5749); sessions are the odd one out.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

Mirror the code/nonce pattern: a global `SESSION_LIMIT` plus a per-principal sub-limit, checked after the expired-entry sweep in `open_session`, refusing with `Refusal::RateLimited`. Add cap tests analogous to `pending_codes_are_capped_globally…` (`:786`) and the nonce cap tests (`:1063` region); the existing session test (`a_session_lasts_its_ttl_and_closes_on_request`, `:519-528`) covers TTL + close only.

Deduped: `gh search issues` for session caps in this repo returns only unrelated claimant/queue items; no open PR touches `directory_auth.rs`. Verified against origin/main `81d10205bf` (read-only worktree).

title: projector: POST /links and POST /hot/checkpoints accept unbounded JSON bodies (bare req.json) while webhook intake is capped at 10MB

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/needs-triage

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts` on `origin/main` (`f2b4512ad8`):

- Webhook intake is bounded — `server.ts:257`:
  `body = await readBoundedBody(req.body, 10_000_000)` → `413 { error: "body_too_large" }` on overflow (`webhook.ts:7-29`).
- Authenticated writes are NOT bounded — both use bare `req.json()` with no `Content-Length` / size guard:
  - `POST /links`: `server.ts:365` (`body = await req.json()` → `400 invalid_json` only on parse failure)
  - `POST /hot/checkpoints`: `server.ts:454` (same shape)

Both routes require the bearer token, so this is authenticated-only, but one credential (or one compromised caller) can force the process to buffer an arbitrarily large JSON body before validation even runs. `POST /links` then stores the `note` string verbatim, so a multi-MB note also becomes persistent row bloat.

## Repro (runtime semantics + code paths)

- `Request.json()` buffers the whole body: a 12 MB JSON payload parses fine (`req.json() accepted bytes: 12582923`), while the webhook-style `readBoundedBody(stream, 10_000_000)` rejects the same size with `body_limit` (node probe, verbatim logic from `webhook.ts`).
- Code-path read: `server.ts:257` (bounded) vs `server.ts:365` and `server.ts:454` (unbounded). No `readBoundedBody`, no length check, and no limit on `note`/`consumer` string lengths before the store call.

## Why it matters

The webhook path already establishes the discipline (10 MB cap → 413). The two authenticated write paths bypass it entirely, so the server's memory ceiling for a single request is whatever the caller sends. Same class as the fixed read-side caps (`MAX_REFS` #10595, `parseLimit` #1547, links cap #10601) — the write side was left open.

## Suggested fix / acceptance

- Route both `POST /links` and `POST /hot/checkpoints` through `readBoundedBody` with the same (or a stated) cap, returning `413 { error: "body_too_large" }` on overflow, then `JSON.parse` → existing `400 invalid_json` handling.
- Bound the stored/compared string fields (`note`, `consumer`, `subject`) to a stated max (e.g. reject or truncate with a 400) so a 12 MB note cannot become a 12 MB row.
- Acceptance: a >cap `POST /links` and `POST /hot/checkpoints` each return 413 without reaching the store; existing `400 invalid_json` / `401 unauthorized` behavior unchanged; unit test pins the cap for both routes alongside the webhook 413 case.

## Dedupe

- Open search `projector links body`, `hot checkpoints`, `body_too_large`: only adjacent #10540 (unstructured 500s on read/reconcile) and #9850 (health stalls) — neither covers write-path body bounds.
- Closed search `projector bounded body`: #1547 (read limit validation), #2693 (subjects percent-encoding) — different routes.
- No open PR touching `server.ts:365/:454` (`gh pr list --search "projector body"` empty).

title: fix(pm-dispatch): launch-failure note says a session 'may still be live' even when its cleanup succeeded — and the cleanup-success path has no test

labels.name: kind/bug

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

Merged PR #4350 made dispatch clean up orphaned OpenCode sessions after a failed launch: `handleLaunchFailure` cancels the queue task, DELETEs the created session, then posts a note on the issue. The note is composed *after* the cleanup outcome is known, but both of its session wordings lead with the same hedge:

- cleanup succeeded: `OpenCode session <id> may still be live; session cleanup succeeded.`
- cleanup failed: `OpenCode session <id> may still be live; session cleanup failed: <error>`

When the DELETE succeeded, "may still be live" is simply wrong — the session was deleted by the handler itself moments earlier. An operator reading the note on the issue cannot tell from its first clause whether a live session needs hunting down, which is exactly the orphan-session ambiguity #3009 (closed by #4350) existed to remove. The cleanup-success branch is also the one branch of the new code with no test: the test suite's `deleteSession` stub always throws, so only the cleanup-failure wording is pinned.

## Evidence

- PR #4350 (MERGED, merge commit `dff881b8b1c2b64cd637c9a46f1f5080f684233b`, commit `076822dd9`), closes #3009: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4350
- Still on current main (`91df8555386eb8347ce4f0842c396be42e44cfa4`): `pm-stack/dispatch/src/launch_failure.ts:127` — `` `OpenCode session ${sessionId} may still be live; session cleanup succeeded.` `` (cleanup-failure twin at :128). The note is built at :123-128, after `deleteSession` has run at :106-115 (cancel → delete → note order), so the outcome is known when the wording is chosen.
- The cancel *reason* (`launch_failure.ts:102`, written before the DELETE runs) legitimately says "may still be live" — at that point it is true. Only the post-cleanup issue note misreports.
- Test gap on main: `pm-stack/dispatch/test/launch_failure.test.ts` — the shared failure harness's `deleteSession` stub (line ~104) always throws `delete failed`; the only session-note assertion (line ~165) pins "session cleanup failed: delete failed". No test exercises a successful `deleteSession`, so the success wording is unpinned. PR #4350's own evidence lists the same five cases (prompt/claim failures, ordering, cleanup failure, original-error preservation) — no cleanup-success case.

## Why it matters

The issue note is the operator's record of whether a failed dispatch left a live OpenCode session behind. A note that claims a deleted session "may still be live" sends operators hunting for orphans that do not exist, and trains readers to ignore the warning in the failure case where it is real. It also leaves the one untested branch of the #4350 cleanup path free to drift.

## Acceptance criteria

- When session cleanup succeeds, the issue note states the session was deleted (or otherwise drops the "may still be live" claim for that branch); the "may still be live" wording remains only where cleanup failed or no deletion callback was available.
- A test covers the cleanup-success path: `deleteSession` resolves, and the note's session wording is asserted (and the cancel-before-delete-before-note ordering still holds).
- Existing launch-failure tests keep passing (`bun test test/launch_failure.test.ts`).

## Shadow verdict (PoC)

Stage A window already closed (summary on developing-today/code#2313) — no shadow verdict recorded.

title: fix(id): hard_delete_handler skips canonical-name validation that soft-delete/restore enforce
body:
## Defect

`hard_delete_handler` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:1311`) takes `Json(req)` immutable and passes `req.name` straight to `FileOps::delete`, skipping the `canonical_web_name` trim+validate step that `delete_handler` (:1216), `restore_handler` (:1266), `save_handler` (:49) and the other route at :252 all enforce:

```rust
// delete_handler — validates
Json(mut req): Json<DeleteRequest>,
...
if let Err(response) = canonical_web_name(&mut req.name) { return response; }

// hard_delete_handler — does not
Json(req): Json<DeleteRequest>,
...
match ops.delete(&req.name).await {
```

The ops layer does not backstop it either: `FileOps::delete` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs:638`) only rejects `trim().is_empty()`, never calls `validate_name` (:275) — while sibling entry point `put` (:388) and rename/copy via `validate_target` (:462, :581) do.

## Impact

- A hard-delete request for `" notes/x "`, `"a//b"`, `"a/../b"`, or a reserved archive name bypasses the canonical-name rule closed everywhere else by #10549/#10573/#10585. Depending on tag-store semantics it either 404s inconsistently (soft-delete of the same padded name would have been trimmed+validated first) or, worse, deletes under a non-canonical key while soft-delete/restore disagree on what that key means.
- This is the destructive endpoint: it removes the blob tag, all archive tags, and all metadata tags. It should be the *most* validated, not the least.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hard_delete_handler` runs `canonical_web_name(&mut req.name)` like `delete_handler`/`restore_handler` (trim + reject with the same 4xx body).
- [ ] Defense in depth: `FileOps::delete` calls `Self::validate_name(name)?` instead of only the empty check, so direct ops callers get the same rule.
- [ ] Test: padded (`" x "`), empty-component (`"a//b"`), dot-dot, and reserved archive names are rejected by hard-delete; canonical names still hard-delete (metadata + archives removed).

## Dedupe

title: id(web): `just test` is red on a clean checkout — `test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest` requires a built `web/dist` manifest

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: kind/test
labels.description: Test coverage, test infrastructure, or test-only fixes

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`just test` / `just test-unit` / `just test-rust` fail on a clean checkout, before any change is made, on a test that has nothing to do with the change:

```
id-web  crates/id-web/src/lib.rs:1141  tests::test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest
  main_js should be hashed (name.hash.js): /assets/main.js
```

The test is not detecting a bug in the code — it is asserting that the *build artifact* (`pkgs/id/web/dist/manifest.json`) exists. On a clean checkout `pkgs/id/web/dist/` contains only the tracked placeholder `.gitkeep`, so there is no manifest and no hashed filenames, and the assertion fails deterministically.

## Evidence (origin/main `4974e7a8af9e`)

1. Assets are embedded from `web/dist` at compile time, and the directory is empty on a clean checkout:

   - `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/assets.rs:24` — `#[folder = "../../web/dist"]`
   - `pkgs/id/web/dist/.gitkeep` is the only tracked file in that directory (`git ls-tree origin/main -- pkgs/id/web/dist`), so `Assets::get("manifest.json")` is `None`.

2. `load_asset_urls()` documents and implements exactly that fallback, returning the **unhashed** defaults:

   - `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/lib.rs:509-525` — `let Some(manifest_data) = Assets::get("manifest.json") else { ... return AssetUrls::default(); }`
   - `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/templates.rs:28-33` — `Default` gives `main_js: "/assets/main.js"`, `styles_css: "/assets/styles.css"`.

3. The test then asserts the opposite — that the URLs must be hashed:

   - `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/lib.rs:1141-1160` — `assert!(js_dots >= 2, "main_js should be hashed (name.hash.js): {}", urls.main_js)`; `/assets/main.js` has one dot, so the assertion fails with its own diagnostic.

4. The failure contradicts the design intent that a clean checkout can run `cargo test`. `pkgs/id/build.rs:27-30` says a missing/empty dev `web/dist` is deliberately tolerated (“a dummy dist lets `cargo check` / `cargo test` compile on a clean checkout where the frontend has not been built”) and only *release* builds require real assets (`:31-41`).

5. The documented dev recipes never build the frontend first, so they inherit the failure:

   - `pkgs/id/justfile:227-228` — `test-rust: cargo nextest run --all-features`
   - `pkgs/id/justfile:239` — `test: test-rust test-web-unit test-web-typecheck`
   - `pkgs/id/justfile:293-294` — `test-unit: cargo nextest run --all-features --lib`
   - `pkgs/id/AGENTS.md:109` lists `just test` as “All fast tests”, with no built-assets prerequisite.

6. Observed twice, independently, already tolerated as noise:

   - issue-sweep run 2026-11-16T04:43Z (backlog, item 1): `cargo test -p id-web --lib` → “676 passed + 1 pre-existing env failure (`test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest`, needs built web assets)”.
   - That lane recorded it as an accepted environment failure rather than a defect, which is exactly the tolerance this issue asks to remove.

`crates/id-web` is in the workspace `default-members` (`pkgs/id/Cargo.toml:38-50`), so every `cargo nextest run --all-features` hits this test; the nix test venues pass only because their shared derivation runs `(cd web && bun run build)` before `just <check>` (`pkgs/id/flake.nix:180-240`), which is precisely why nothing catches this locally.

## Repro

```bash
git clone https://github.com/developing-today/code && cd code/pkgs/id
ls -A web/dist          # .gitkeep only
just test-unit          # or: cargo test -p id-web --lib test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest
# => FAIL id-web ... test_load_asset_urls_from_manifest
#    main_js should be hashed (name.hash.js): /assets/main.js
```

No `web/dist` build, no bun, no network: the failure is deterministic and requires nothing but a fresh clone.

## Why it matters

- Every fresh clone, worktree, and contributor's first `just test` is red before touching anything, and the failure is in a crate unrelated to the change being tested — the classic path to “known red test” blindness where a real `id-web` regression hides behind the expected one.
- It also breaks the fast local loop the recipes exist for: `just test-unit` is advertised as “unit tests only (fast)”, yet it depends on a Bun frontend build that those recipes do not run.
- The test does not verify what it looks like it verifies. It asserts that a build artifact exists, not that `load_asset_urls` maps a manifest to URLs correctly; the transformation itself (`main.js` → `main.<hash>.js`) has no direct coverage.

## Fix shape

Preferred: make the test independent of the build tree.

- Extract the pure mapping so it can be tested directly, e.g. `fn asset_urls_from_manifest(manifest: &serde_json::Value) -> AssetUrls` (or from `&str`), with `load_asset_urls()` reduced to `Assets::get("manifest.json")` → parse → `asset_urls_from_manifest`.
- Test the mapping with an inline fixture manifest (`{"main.js":"main.deadbeef.js","styles.css":"styles.deadbeef.css"}`) and assert the `/assets/` prefix and hashed name; test the documented fallback separately (absent/invalid manifest → `AssetUrls::default()`), and keep the “compiles with an empty `web/dist`” property asserted.
- Optionally keep one build-artifact assertion for the release variant in a check that actually builds the frontend, rather than in the unit suite.

Acceptable alternative, if the extraction is not wanted: have `just test*` recipes depend on the web build (e.g. `test-unit: web`), but that reintroduces the Bun dependency into the “fast” loop, so the extraction is preferred.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `cargo test -p id-web --lib` (and `just test-unit` / `just test-rust`) passes on a clean clone with an empty `pkgs/id/web/dist` (only `.gitkeep`), with no Bun build.
- [ ] A manifest-to-URLs mapping test exists that covers the hashed-name transformation and the `/assets/` prefix from a fixture manifest.
- [ ] The missing-manifest fallback remains covered (defaults returned, no panic), matching `load_asset_urls`' documented behaviour and `pkgs/id/build.rs`'s clean-checkout intent.
- [ ] Nothing in the release build path is weakened: a release build without real frontend assets still fails as `pkgs/id/build.rs:31-41` requires.

## Related

- #9616 (open) — the release web-asset guard counts `web/dist/.gitkeep` as “built”, so a `.gitkeep`-only tree can ship a 404 web UI. Same placeholder file, different code path (release guard, not tests); this issue does not supersede it.
- #10590 (merged) — the run whose comment first recorded this failure as a “pre-existing env failure”.

title: mcpx(pool): detach→restore rollback permanently loses the stdio exec watch — `watching` is never reset, so executable changes go undetected until a daemon restart

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Defect

A pool that survives a takeover rollback (`Detach` → `Restore`) can lose its
stdio exec watch permanently: the watch goroutine exits while the pool is
closed, but `watching` is never cleared, so `watchExecLocked` refuses to start
it again for the rest of the pool's life. After that, an executable that is
re-pointed / re-installed / rewritten is never noticed and the pool keeps
serving the stale binary until the daemon restarts.

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/pool/execwatch.go:36-58`:

```go
func (p *Pool) watchExecLocked() {
	if p.watching || p.execEvery <= 0 || !p.cfg.Stdio() {
		return
	}
	p.watching = true
	go p.watchExec(p.execEvery)
}

func (p *Pool) watchExec(every time.Duration) {
	...
		case <-t.C:
			if p.isClosed() {
				return        // goroutine exits; p.watching stays true
			}
```

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/pool/handoff.go:68-95` (`Detach`) sets `p.closed = true`;
`handoff.go:154-176` (`Restore`/`restore`) clears it again (`p.closed = false`,
`p.instances = p.parked`, `cond.Broadcast()`) and never touches `watching` and
never calls `watchExecLocked`. `watching` is only written at
`execwatch.go:40`.

## Trigger

`Detach` is the old side of a daemon takeover, and rollback onto the old
daemon is an expected path: `daemon/takeover.go:298` (`ho.Restore()` when the
successor stalls or the child hand-off fails), `daemon/registry_handoff.go:48`
and `:69`. The pool stays `closed` for up to `daemon.takeoverTimeout` (15s,
`internal/defaults/defaults.json:233`) while the successor is waited on, and
the exec watch ticks every `limits.execCheckInterval` (30s,
`defaults.json:237`). Whenever a tick lands inside the closed window, the
watcher exits and nothing restarts it after `Restore`.

## Verified

Probe test against `origin/main` (ddeba2db50) in a throwaway copy of
`pkgs/mcpx`, no tracked file changed:

- `setExecWatch(t, 20ms, …)`, pool over a symlinked wrapper, one call to start
  a child, then `Detach` → sleep `5 * execTick` → `Restore` → re-point the link
  at a different program. Result: **FAIL — the change was never detected, the
  child pid never changed** (6.77s).
- Control, identical repoint with no `Detach`/`Restore`: **PASS**, the child is
  replaced (3.06s).
- Short closed window (`execTick/4`, no tick inside it): **PASS**, the watcher
  survives — confirming the mechanism is the `isClosed()` early return during
  the handoff, not the repoint logic.

This is a silent liveness regression on a recovery path: the daemon looks
healthy and serves the restored children, but stops noticing executable
changes for those pools.

## Acceptance criteria

- After a `Detach` → `Restore` rollback, a stdio pool with `execEvery > 0`
  still has a running exec watch; an executable change after the rollback
  replaces the child.
- Regression test in `internal/pool` covering detach → hold across a tick →
  restore → repoint → child replaced (the probe above is a starting point;
  `handoff_exec_test.go` and `execwatch_test.go` already have the helpers:
  `setExecWatch`, `writeExecWrapper`, `servedPID`, `awaitReplacement`).

## Suggested fix shape

Make the watch state rollback-safe: clear `watching` when the watch goroutine
exits (deferred, under `p.mu`), and/or have `restore` re-arm the watch
(`watchExecLocked` after reopening when instances remain). Keep the existing
"only started once the pool has a live child" behaviour for a fresh pool.

title: id(id-native-shell): run_session retains every durable event for the whole session — unbounded memory growth in a long-lived shell, and nothing reads it

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Defect

`id-native-shell`'s live session keeps every durable host event for the whole
session lifetime, with no bound and no consumer, so memory grows with total
world activity since the last snapshot.

`pkgs/id/crates/id-native-shell/src/session.rs:110-141`:

```rust
pub struct SessionState {
    snapshot: Option<Value>,
    events: Vec<Value>,
    ...
}
...
            "snapshot" => {
                self.snapshot = Some(frame["snapshot"].clone());
                self.events.clear();
                Ok(ServerUpdate::Snapshot)
            }
            "event" => {
                self.events.push(frame["event"].clone());
                Ok(ServerUpdate::Event)
            }
```

`events.clear()` runs only on a `snapshot` frame. `run_session`
(`session.rs:245-253`) folds every host frame into the shared `SessionState`
for the entire session, and returns the accumulated state on exit
(`session.rs:291`). `events()` (`session.rs:169-174`) hands out a `&[Value]` —
there is no drain, cap, or byte budget.

## Why this is unbounded in practice

The host emits `snapshot` only at three points: on join
(`pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/mod.rs:1718`), on a lagged
broadcast receiver (`mod.rs:1859`), and on `ProgramInstalled`
(`mod.rs:1808`). The steady state is `event` frames plus coalesced `view`
frames — no periodic snapshot. A client that keeps up never lags, so between
join and program install `events` grows without limit.

The running binary does not read it. `id-native-shell/src/main.rs` drains only
views (`drain_session_views`); `events()` is consumed solely by tests
(`session.rs:339,365`, `tests/live_session.rs:186,194`). So the process
retains a full duplicate of the world's durable event stream for its own
lifetime and never looks at it.

## Impact

`id-native-shell` is the reference live client intended to stay connected and
present an ongoing world (step 2 of #788, PRs #10526/#10536 merged). On an
active world (chat/input/system events at steady rate) a multi-hour session
accumulates every payload — unbounded peak RSS driven by remote activity, not
by caller choice, and a plausible OOM for the shell process.

## Acceptance criteria

- `SessionState` retention of durable events is bounded on the receive path
  (e.g. fixed count/byte budget keeping a tail, or a drain API the consumer
  uses), enforced in `apply_server_frame`/the reader loop, not at read time.
- The bound is covered by a test that feeds more than the budget of `event`
  frames without an intervening `snapshot` and asserts retention stays within
  the budget.
- Either `events()` semantics are documented as bounded (and the tests updated)
  or the running binary explicitly drains what it retains.

improvement-issue creator. No fix attempted here.

body:
## Failure

Main-branch run [43807605419](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43807605419) (push, head `bcb467ece6`, workflow `pm-stack tests`) failed job `aggregator + projector + dispatch + python suites + quota exporters` at step **Test dispatch** — 203 pass / 4 fail:

```
(fail) OpenCodeClient auth file boundary (#7085) > control: a valid auth file resolves and sends the password verbatim
(fail) OpenCodeClient response body boundary (#7085) > a non-JSON 200 body is an OpenCodeError, not a raw SyntaxError
(fail) OpenCodeClient.getSession (#5555) > returns the session object on 200 (envelope unwrapped)
(fail) OpenCodeClient.getSession (#5555) > returns null on 404 — the session does not exist
error: opencode GET /api/session/ses_ok unreachable: unexpected network fetch in test: http://127.0.0.1:45791/api/session/ses_ok
```

## It is a flake, and the defect is test isolation

A manual `workflow_dispatch` of the same workflow on the **same head** `bcb467ece6` is green: run [43808691940](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43808691940) (dispatched 2026-11-16T05:12Z, success). The dispatch suite also passed on `ec68de7f` (run 43792350594) with an identical `pm-stack/dispatch` tree — no dispatch source changed between them.

Root cause: `pm-stack/dispatch/test/server.test.ts` installs a global fetch override **at module scope** and never restores it:

```ts
// pm-stack/dispatch/test/server.test.ts:16-25
const realFetch = globalThis.fetch;
globalThis.fetch = (async (input: unknown) => {
  if (String(input) === JWKS_URL) { ... }
  throw new Error(`unexpected network fetch in test: ${String(input)}`);
}) as typeof fetch;
```

`realFetch` is captured but never restored. Bun executes the dispatch suite's 12 test files in one process, so once `server.test.ts` has been loaded, every later file that performs a real local-HTTP request (`opencode.test.ts` drives `127.0.0.1:<port>/api/session*`) throws that guard. Whether the suite is red depends purely on file execution order — which is why the same tree goes green and red.

Sibling files already do this correctly (`attach_verify.test.ts:148/171/181`, `auth.test.ts:246/259`, `github.test.ts:67`, `queue.test.ts:124` restore `realFetch` in their cleanup hooks). `server.test.ts` is the only module-scope stubbing file that never restores.

## Fix

- Restore `globalThis.fetch = realFetch` in `server.test.ts` (an `afterAll`, plus per-test `beforeEach`/`afterEach` scoping for the stub) so no state escapes the file.
- Audit the suite for any other module-scope global mutation that is not restored.
- Add a guard test that fails when a global fetch override survives a test file (e.g. a small test that asserts `globalThis.fetch` identity before/after walking the suite), so a future leak cannot silently return.

## Related

- Superseded tracker: #9529 (same workflow, older `claimant install bun suite` / systemd-gatherer failure; that step is green now).
- Earlier rounds on this workflow: #10469, #8737, #7680, #6452 (all closed).

title: pm-aggregator tests: browser acceptance (MOB-00) red on main — fragments never load (data-on-load is not a Datastar v1 attribute)

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/ci-watch
labels.description: Filed by main-ci watch

body:
## Failure `developing-today/code` · workflow **pm-aggregator tests** · branch `main` · run [43804024455](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43804024455) (`workflow_dispatch`, head `3fb67243f5bfa3c3bff06eba9f18e7800516344c`, created 2026-11-16T04:25:35Z). Two jobs failed: | Job | Step | Failure | |---|---|---| | [browser acceptance (MOB-00)](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43804024455/job/133090529192) | Run browser acceptance (MOB-00 contract test) | `expect(locator).toBeVisible()` — element(s) not found | | [aggregator tests and typecheck](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43804024455/job/133090529543) | Run aggregator tests | 1/2746: `a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test` (5000ms) | The browser job is the consistent breakage: the preceding run [43803736802](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/43803736802) (head `1fbf3927`) fails the same assertion, and the job has failed in every run that contained it since it was added (~2026-11-13). The hook timeout is a one-off flake (see last section). ## Browser failure ``` Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed Locator: locator('#queue-main article.card').filter({ hasText: 'Dispatch trial: doc/README.md starting point (#762)' }).first() Expected: visible Timeout: 10000ms Error: element(s) not found at test/browser/mobile-work-view.spec.ts:66:22 ``` The retained `error-context.md` page snapshot from the failed run still shows `text: Loading queue…` under `heading "Queue visibility"` — i.e. the queue shell never hydrated. The trace network log for the run contains `/queue`, `/assets/datastar.js`, `/assets/freshness-client.js`, `/freshness/stream` — and **no request to `/frag/queue` at all**. ## Root cause The fragment containers are bootstrapped with `data-on-load`: - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/render.ts:1740, 3572, 3832, 3909, 4109` (board, attention, today, queue, overview shells) - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:2536, 2567, 2612, 2636` (`/frag/*` responses) - `pm-stack/aggregator/src/freshness-delivery.ts:102` `data-on-load` is **not a Datastar v1 attribute**; the vendored bundle is Datastar v1.0.0 (`src/assets/datastar.js:1`), where event listeners are `data-on:` and one-shot initialization is `data-init`. `load` also does not fire on a `div`, so even as an event name it would never trigger. The attribute comes from the v0.21-era migration plan (`.opencode/plans/htmx-to-datastar-migration.md:323` uses `data-on-load__interval`), and the bun tests only assert the string is rendered (`test/boot.test.ts:144`, `test/frag-watchdog-1503.test.ts:34`). Consequence: the initial fragment fetch never happens. A page only hydrates when the freshness client dispatches `dashrefresh` (`data-on:dashrefresh__window`), i.e. when the SSE stream delivers a `freshness`/`reset` notice. On a quiet stream the page shows `Loading queue…` forever. ## Reproduction (local, deterministic) ``` cd pm-stack/aggregator PM_AGG_SOURCE=fixtures PM_AGG_DEV=1 PM_AGG_PORT=4797 PM_AGG_FRESHNESS_PORT=4897 bun run src/server.ts ``` - `curl /frag/queue` → 200 with 11 `article class="card"` and the expected title; `curl /queue` → skeleton only. So the data/fragment side is fine. - Load `/queue` in a browser and **block `/freshness/stream`**: `/frag/queue` is never requested and `#queue-main` keeps `
Loading queue…
` for 11+s (observed). This is exactly the CI trace. - Load `/queue` with the stream live: `/frag/queue` is requested only after the client's `reset` handler fires (`/api/freshness-events.json?after=0` first), ~1.6s in. - The MOB-00 spec passes locally with the same server when the stream happens to deliver a notice (system Chromium, `playwright test` with an `executablePath` override). That is why this only shows up as a CI failure: the check is asserting first-paint hydration, and first paint currently depends on a freshness event. ## Suggested fix - Put the initial fetch on the **shell placeholder** with `data-init="@get('/frag/...')"` and keep `data-on:dashrefresh__window="@get('/frag/...')"` for refresh. - Do **not** add an immediate re-fetch trigger to the `/frag/*` response wrapper itself: `ssePatch` uses `mode outer`, so a `data-init` in the response would re-initialize on every patch and loop. - Update the tests that pin `data-on-load` (`test/boot.test.ts:144`, `test/frag-watchdog-1503.test.ts:34`) and, if useful, add a browser assertion that the queue fragment is requested without any freshness event (the MOB-00 spec already covers the outcome; making the stream unavailable in the harness would make the regression deterministic). ## Verification This workflow is dispatch-only by design (Drew's 2026-11-05 ruling, #6126) — do not add push/PR triggers. Verification is a `workflow_dispatch` run of `pm-aggregator tests` where `browser acceptance (MOB-00)` is green and `aggregator tests and typecheck` passes, plus `cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test` locally. ## Secondary: aggregator hook timeout `aggregator tests and typecheck` failed once with `(fail) (unnamed) [5000.10ms] ^ a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test` (2745 pass / 1 fail, Bun v1.4.4). The same commit's sibling run passed this job. Treat as a separate flake to identify while in the suite (which hook/file owns the unnamed timeout), not as the reason main is red.

body:
## Summary

`pkgs/id/scripts/prod-lines-check.sh` keys both its grandfather allowances and its module-gated test-only exemptions on paths relative to `pkgs/id` in the **pre-crate-split** layout (`src/cli.rs`, `src/directory.rs`, `src/web/routes.rs`, `src/web/markdown.rs`, `src/encryption/tests.rs`, `src/world_session/tests.rs`). Since the crate split (`crates/*/src/...`, id-cli extraction e4af08ffc0 2026-11-13, step 7b of #4411) no row can ever match, so the guard reports files that its own header declares out of scope, ignores an explicit allowance, and cannot go green on main regardless of the split work in #8590/#8592/#8593.

## Evidence

Reproduced on origin/main `3fb67243f5`:

```
$ cd pkgs/id && bash scripts/prod-lines-check.sh
::error file=crates/id-cli/src/cli/tests.rs::crates/id-cli/src/cli/tests.rs has 2869 production lines (limit 2500) — split the module per F11.10 (#1411)
::error file=crates/id-cli/src/commands/serve.rs::... 3084 ...
::error file=crates/id-directory/src/directory.rs::... 2536 ...
::error file=crates/id-groups/src/encryption/tests.rs::... 2850 ...
::error file=crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor.rs::... 3870 ...
::error file=crates/id-worlds/src/world/core.rs::... 3168 ...
::error file=crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/tests.rs::... 3599 ...
prod-lines-check: 334 production files scanned (limit 2500), largest crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor.rs at 3870 lines, 0 test-only skips, 0 grandfathered
prod-lines-check: 7 file(s) over the limit
exit=1
```

Tables and scan root: `grandfather_allowance` at `scripts/prod-lines-check.sh:38-73`, `test_only_reason` at `:78-89`, `root` at `:32-33`, scan at `:140` (rel paths are therefore `crates/<crate>/src/...` today).

Four of the seven reported violations are false positives by the guard's own documented scope (header `:8-13`: "Test-only files stay out of scope … module-gated test modules in TEST_ONLY below"):

1. `crates/id-directory/src/directory.rs` — **2536** production lines, under its own **2610** allowance (`:48-53`), but the row matches only `src/directory.rs`, which no longer exists. A file that was explicitly grandfathered is now reported as "split the module".
2. `crates/id-groups/src/encryption/tests.rs` — 2850; parent `crates/id-groups/src/encryption/mod.rs:40-42` declares `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. The row at `:80` is keyed `src/encryption/tests.rs`.
3. `crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/tests.rs` — 3599; parent `crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/mod.rs:44-47` declares `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. The row at `:84` is keyed `src/world_session/tests.rs`.
4. `crates/id-cli/src/cli/tests.rs` — 2869; parent `crates/id-cli/src/cli/mod.rs:1664-1666` declares `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. No `test_only_reason` row exists for this successor at all.

The other three are genuine over-limit production files and are already tracked, though their issues still carry pre-split paths: `crates/id-cli/src/commands/serve.rs` 3084 (#8590), `crates/id-worlds/src/world/actor.rs` 3870 (#8592), `crates/id-worlds/src/world/core.rs` 3168 (#8593).

## Why it matters

- The `id` basic tier is red on main and on every merge: failing job `basic: nix flake check (prod-lines-check)` 133026221059 in run 43778616728, and the main-broken chain keeps filing per-commit breakage for it (#10596, #10597, #10599 open now, each dispatching a critical triage/fix task). Those dispatches are chasing splits of *test* files and of a file that is under its allowance.
- The ratchet invariant ("allowance is a ceiling that must only shrink: any growth fails") is silently unenforced: because no row matches, growth in `crates/id-directory/src/directory.rs` past 2610 would be reported as a plain 2500 violation rather than as allowance growth, and the old `src/cli.rs` allowance no longer guards anything. The obsolete rows for `src/web/routes.rs` (now 2096 production lines) and `src/web/markdown.rs` (now 1196) should be deleted rather than migrated.
- Even after #8590/#8592/#8593 land, the guard still fails on the four false positives above, so CI cannot return to green.
- Root cause of the missed regression: `scripts/prod-lines-check-test.sh:81-100` builds every fixture in the pre-split `$tmp/src/...` layout, so the self-test exercises exactly the paths that still work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Grandfather/test-only lookups resolve in the post-split layout. Suggested shape: normalize to a crate-relative `src/...` form (strip a leading `crates/<crate>/`) before matching, or key rows by `*/src/<rest>`, so moving a file between `pkgs/id/src` and `pkgs/id/crates/*/src` does not change the verdict.
- [ ] On current main, `cd pkgs/id && bash scripts/prod-lines-check.sh` reports `crates/id-directory/src/directory.rs` as grandfathered at 2536 ≤ 2610, skips the three module-gated test modules, and fails only on files still tracked by #8590/#8592/#8593 (i.e. exits 0 once those land).
- [ ] Migrate the `src/directory.rs` row to the crate path; drop the obsolete `src/cli.rs`, `src/web/routes.rs`, `src/web/markdown.rs` rows with a reason.
- [ ] `scripts/prod-lines-check-test.sh` gains crate-layout fixtures: a module-gated test module under `crates/x/src/...` is skipped; a grandfathered file under `crates/x/src/...` passes at/below its allowance and fails when it grows past it.
- [ ] Plain 2500-limit behavior for non-exempt files is unchanged; do not weaken the check to get green — it is the F11.10 ratchet (#1438, #1411).

title: projector: GET /links returns the whole pmp_links table with no limit
body:
## Summary
`GET /links` with no `subject`/`ref` filter returns every row in `pmp_links` in one response, with no `limit` parameter and no cap in the store query. Every sibling list endpoint is bounded (`/items`, `/comments`, `/hot` all go through `parseLimit` with documented maxima); `/links` is the outlier. Like #10595 (uncapped `refs` bypass on `/items`/`/comments`), the read path is unauthenticated, so one request can force a full-table scan + full-table serialization.

## Evidence (origin/main `3fb67243`)
- `pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts:328-335`: `GET /links` reads optional `subject`/`ref` and calls `store.getLinks` directly — no `parseLimit`, no max, no default. POST (`:336`) and DELETE (`:357` area) require `bearerAuthorized`; GET does not.
- `pm-stack/projector/src/store.ts:535-552`: `getLinks` builds `WHERE …` only from the two optional filters and runs `SELECT * FROM pmp_links ${where} ORDER BY created_at DESC` with no `LIMIT` placeholder. Empty opts produce a bare full-table select.
- Contrast: `/items` (`server.ts:306`), `/comments` (`:315`), `/hot` (`:399`) all clamp via `parseLimit(raw, default, max)` (`:91-106`, digit-only, `MAX_ITEMS_LIMIT=1000`/`MAX_COMMENTS_LIMIT=1000`); `getComments` binds `LIMIT ?` (`store.ts:437-441`), `listItems` binds `LIMIT ?` (`:278-282`). `getLinks` has neither.
- Residual: `/subjects/:subject` (`server.ts:379+` → `store.getSubject` `store.ts:646-658`) fans out through the same unbounded `getLinks({subject})` plus unbounded `getItems(refs)`, so a subject with many links inherits the same blowup. Fixing `getLinks` (or capping at the route) covers both.

## Impact
- Availability: a single unauthenticated `GET /links` on a large projection forces SQLite to materialize and the handler to JSON-serialize the entire link table (grows with every reconciled repo × issue × link).
- Inconsistency: the pagination contract every other read endpoint honors (`limit` capped, digit-only per #1547/#2971) silently does not apply here; clients cannot page links at all.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `GET /links` accepts the same `limit` semantics as the sibling reads (digit-only `parseLimit`, documented default + max) and passes the bound to the store.
- [ ] `store.getLinks` enforces the bound in SQL (`LIMIT ?`) for all three shapes: unfiltered, subject-filtered, and ref-filtered.
- [ ] Unfiltered full-table read is either paged (cursor/offset + `next_cursor`) or explicitly rejected/redirected to a filtered/paged form — no silent unbounded path remains, including via `/subjects/:subject` fan-out if that route keeps using `getLinks`/`getItems`.
- [ ] Regression test: unfiltered `GET /links` over N > max rows returns at most max rows (and a paging signal if paging is chosen); filtered reads honor the same cap.
- [ ] Related: cross-link #10595 (refs bypass) and #10540 (unstructured 500s); distinct endpoint and fix site (links route + `getLinks` query), not a duplicate.

title: pool-quota steward: step-6 page-truth check counts provider rows, not distinct pool service IDs — false regression filings after #10444 Zen aliasing
body:
## Problem

The pool-quota steward's step-6 page-truth check counts quota **provider rows** in the read against rendered **pools** on `/api/quota.json`. Since PR #10444 (merged 2026-11-15, closing #10443) the three OpenCode Zen door rows (`opencode.drewrypope`, `opencode.popesdrew`, `opencode.developing-today-0`) are deliberately aliased onto the `opencode-go.<workspace>` pools — they read the same plan meters, so rendering them as separate pools would double-count. The naive row-vs-pool count therefore reports a false "19 read vs 16 rendered" regression and filed #10574, which a queue checker task (task 17405) then had to disposition by hand.

## Fix

In the steward's step-6 comparison (pool-quota-steward instruction / compare step):

- Compare rendered pool coverage against **distinct pool service IDs** in the read, not raw provider rows.
- Treat provider rows whose `serviceId` is shared with another row (the Zen -> `opencode-go.*` aliasing) as covered when that service ID renders as a pool.
- Keep a separate regression check for genuinely divergent readings between aliased rows (different windows/resets for the same service ID), which is the real failure mode worth filing.

## Evidence

- #10574 disposition (lane code-b, task 17405): live `/api/quota.json` verified 2026-11-16T02:2xZ — the three `opencode-go.*` pools render, and the gatherer section carries the three Zen provider rows in `ok` state filed under the `opencode-go.*` service IDs, exactly as #10444 designed.
- The on-issue cross-check comment on #10574 (2026-11-16T00:59Z) reached the same conclusion: deliberate #10444 aliasing, not three missing meters.

title: update-locatedb fails on watcher-bench manydirs fixture (too many open files) and trips switch failure reporting

## Problem

`update-locatedb.service` (timer, plocate updatedb) fails scanning the laptop tree:

```
Nov 15 20:02:41 amd updatedb[705868]: /home/user/git/fleet/watcher-bench-195/fixtures/manydirs/d130877: Too many open files
Nov 15 20:02:41 amd updatedb[705868]: Hint: Try `ulimit -n 262144 or similar (current limit is 131072).`
```

The watcher-bench fixture tree (`~/git/fleet/watcher-bench-195/fixtures/manydirs`) holds an extreme number of directories; updatedb exhausts its 131072 fd limit partway through and exits 1 after ~2m42s / 3G read.

## Why it matters beyond the index

On 2026-11-15 this timer failure landed in the middle of the gen-558 `nixos-rebuild switch`: switch-to-configuration counted the coincidentally-failed unit and exited status 4, so the switch reported failure even though the generation set, activated, and installed its boot entry correctly. A noisy index job should not be able to make a healthy switch look broken.

## Fix options

- Add the bench fixture path (or `~/git/fleet` generally) to updatedb's prunepaths in the NixOS config, and/or
- Raise the unit's LimitNOFILE.

Pruning is the better fix: the fixture tree has no locate value.

## Acceptance

- `update-locatedb.service` completes successfully on amd.
- A switch run no longer risks a false failure from this unit.

title: id(web): upload handler stores non-canonical multipart filenames verbatim when the extension matches
body:
## Evidence (origin/main)

`reconcile_upload_filename` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes.rs:1077-1095`) returns the caller's multipart filename **verbatim** whenever its extension already agrees with the validated content type (`:1088-1090`):

```rust
if current.as_deref().is_some_and(|c| acceptable.contains(&c)) {
    return name.to_owned();
}
```

Only the mismatch branch canonicalizes (via `file_stem`, which drops directory components, `:1091-1094` — the comment at `:1092-1093` even claims upload names are plain file names, but the early return above it does not enforce that).

The upload path then stores that name unchecked:

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:453-454` — only rejects blank-after-trim filenames, then calls `reconcile_upload_filename`.
- `file_handlers.rs:388-407` (`uniquify_upload_name`) — returns the intended name verbatim when free or already naming the same blob.
- `file_handlers.rs:551-552` — `state.store.tags().set(Tag::from(filename), hash)` stores it as-is, plus filename-keyed metadata tags below.

`FileOps::validate_name` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs:275-296`) — documented as "the single canonical-name rule for every FileOps entry point" — rejects exactly these shapes (`..` components, rooted names, leading/trailing padding), but the upload path never calls it.

## Repro (code-level, verified against the function)

With validated type `image/png`:

| multipart `filename` | stored tag name | `validate_name` says |
|---|---|---|
| `../../x.png` | `../../x.png` verbatim | `InvalidName` (`..` components) |
| `/abs.png` | `/abs.png` verbatim | `InvalidName` (rooted) |
| ` foo.png` (leading space) | ` foo.png` verbatim | `InvalidName` (padding) |
| `evil.html` | `evil.png` (mismatch branch, fine) | ok |

(Any HTTP client can set an arbitrary multipart `filename`; browsers sending basenames does not constrain the server-side contract.)

## Why it matters

- Stored tag names that no forgiving surface can re-specify identically (CLI/REPL trim before calling in): padded twins (` foo.png` vs `foo.png`) and path-shaped names (`../../x.png`, `/abs.png`) enter the blob-tag and metadata-tag namespaces, defeating the canonical-name invariant every FileOps entry point enforces.
- Path-shaped stored names are a latent traversal input for any current or future consumer that joins a tag name onto a filesystem path (export/backup/sync flows).

## Sibling cluster (not duplicates)

- #10549 (save/new JSON handlers bypass validation) and #10573 (delete/restore JSON handlers bypass validation) cover different handlers with a different fix site. This issue covers the multipart upload path; fix site is `reconcile_upload_filename` in `routes.rs` (or a `validate_name` gate in `upload_handler`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] An upload whose multipart filename carries `..` components, a rooted path, or leading/trailing padding is rejected (400) or normalized to the canonical plain file name before any tag/metadata write — no non-canonical name is stored.
- [ ] The mismatch branch keeps its type-reconciliation behavior (`evil.html` + PNG bytes -> `evil.png`).
- [ ] Regression tests pin the verbatim-passthrough cases above (matching extension + `..`/rooted/padded name) alongside the existing `reconcile_upload_filename_matches_validated_type` cases.

title: fleet-secrets test misses Response.transport field — amd system build broken on main
body:
## Problem

`nixos-rebuild build --flake .#amd` fails on current main (1e08635e71, 2026-11-15): the fleet package build dies compiling fleet-secrets' lib test.

```
error[E0063]: missing field `transport` in initializer of `fleet_proxy_proto::Response`
    --> crates/fleet-secrets/src/lib.rs:1464:28
     |
1464 |                 let resp = Response { status, body };
     |                            ^^^^^^^^ missing `transport`
error: could not compile `fleet-secrets` (lib test) due to 1 previous error
```

## Cause

Cross-PR breakage: the fleet-proxy transport work (code#10356) added `transport: Option<String>` to `fleet_proxy_proto::Response`, and the fleet-secrets retry work (#10578) added a scripted-broker test helper that constructs `Response { status, body }` without the new field. Each passed its own checks; together on main the test target no longer compiles, so `fleet-0.1.0` fails and every dependent (etc, home-manager generation, the amd toplevel) fails with it. This blocks the amd switch Drew ordered on 2026-11-15.

## Fix

Add `transport: None` to the test helper's `Response` initializer (matching fleet-proxy-proto's own test usage). One line, test code only.

## Acceptance

- `cargo test -p fleet-secrets --lib` compiles and passes.
- `nixos-rebuild build --flake .#amd` succeeds on main and the switch lands.

title: fleet-secrets: bws fallback has no token of its own; broker exchange has no timeout or retry — a 16s broker restart degrades whole consumer runs
body:
## Problem

On 2026-11-15 ~18:00 CT a switch restarted the laptop's user units; the secrets-broker was down 16s (18:00:02→18:00:18) and its tunnel with it. A consumer run (the left-on-the-ground sweep) called `fleet secrets get` inside that window, got 502/503, and degraded its whole run — the `bws` fallback inside the verb never rescued it. Diagnosis found two client-side defects in `fleet-secrets`:

1. **The `bws` fallback has no credential of its own.** `BwsSource` ran `bws` with the ambient environment only. Non-interactive callers (cron workers, scheduled sweeps) run with `BWS_ACCESS_TOKEN` unset or **set-but-empty** (reproduced live in the sandbox: the variable is present with length 0, and `bws` dies with "Missing access token"). The broker server resolves its token properly — env if non-empty, else the on-disk machine-account token files (`~/.config/bitwarden/access-token`, `~/.config/bws/access-token`) — the client fallback never did. Proven: with the socket pointed at a dead path, `fleet secrets get` exits 3 with both sources failed; with the token loaded from the file, the same call resolves via `bws` in ~1.6s.

2. **No timeout anywhere on the broker exchange.** `BrokerSource`/`DirectBrokerSource` set no read/write timeouts. Proven live: against a session-broker socket that accepts and never answers, `fleet secrets get` blocks indefinitely (had to be killed by an external `timeout 10`, rc 124). In that failure shape neither fallback nor any retry could ever engage.

## Fix (Drew's ruling, 2026-11-15: the retry goes in the binary)

In `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-secrets`:

- Broker legs retry `Unavailable` outcomes (transport errors and 502/503-class statuses) with capped exponential backoff + jitter under one budget constant (`BROKER_RETRY_BUDGET` = 120s, initial 2s, max 15s). A broker 404 is definitive and never retries — a missing name stays a fast answer. Exactly one broker leg in the default chain owns the budget (the direct leg on the laptop; the session-broker leg on the sandbox).
- Every broker attempt is time-bounded (`BROKER_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT` = 10s read/write), so an accept-but-silent peer fails the attempt instead of wedging the caller.
- The `bws` fallback resolves its token the way the broker does (non-empty env, else the token files) and hands it to the `bws` child explicitly (`BwsTokenRunner`); when no token resolves it removes the variable, so a stale empty ambient value cannot masquerade as a credential.
- Invariants preserved: never exit 0 with an empty value; no negative caching; errors stay value-free.

Tests: 12 new in fleet-secrets (503/502-then-recovers over a scripted socket, 404 single-attempt under the full budget, silent-peer attempt timeout, chain fall-through to bws after retries are spent, retry-loop semantics, token lookup + runner env control). Workspace suite: 683 passed / 0 failed locally.

Deploy: one build from merged main flipped to both installs (laptop `~/.local/bin/fleet`, sandbox `~/tools/fleet`) per `pkgs/fleet/README.md`; revs recorded on #5760.

title: id(web): delete/restore file handlers bypass FileOps canonical name validation
body:
## Problem

The web file-management handlers `delete_handler` and `restore_handler` (soft-delete / restore) accept `req.name` and operate on it with only an emptiness check (`req.name.trim().is_empty()`), then use the original, unvalidated `req.name` as the tag/metadata key. They never apply the canonical name validation that `FileOps` enforces for every FileOps entry point (`FileOps::validate_name`). This lets the web API soft-delete/restore under names that the CLI/REPL/meta protocol reject, diverging behavior across entry points and allowing padded, rooted, `..`-containing, or reserved archive-shaped names to enter the tag namespace via the web surface.

This is the delete/restore sibling of the already-tracked save/new gap (#10549); `hard_delete_handler` delegates to `FileOps::delete` (which at least emptiness-checks), and `rename`/`copy` go through `FileOps`, but the soft-delete and restore paths bypass `FileOps` entirely.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:1167-1215` (`delete_handler`): rejects only when `req.name.trim().is_empty()` (line ~1173), then looks up `state.store.tags().get(&req.name)` and calls `state.tag_store.set_singleton(..., req.name.as_bytes(), b"deleted", ...)` using the original untrimmed `req.name` — no `FileOps::validate_name` (or equivalent) check before the side effect.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:1218-1262` (`restore_handler`): same emptiness-only check (line ~1224), then `state.store.tags().get(&req.name)` and `state.tag_store.del_by_key(..., req.name.as_bytes(), b"deleted")` on the original untrimmed name — no canonical validation.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs:267-296` (`FileOps::validate_name`): documents "The single canonical-name rule for every FileOps entry point" and rejects names that are not exactly trimmed (`name != name.trim()`), rooted / `\`-prefixed / Windows drive-prefixed, containing empty/`.`/`..` path components, or matching the reserved archive-tag shape (`is_archive_tag_name` -> `ReservedArchiveName`). `FileOps::put/rename/copy` all validate via this rule.
- Contrast: `hard_delete_handler` (`file_handlers.rs:1268+`) delegates to `FileOps::delete` (`fileops.rs:638+`), and rename/copy handlers route through `FileOps`; only soft delete + restore operate on the raw tag store with the canonical rule absent.

Concrete bypass examples under current code:
- A name with leading/trailing whitespace (e.g. `" notes.md"`) passes the emptiness check but is used verbatim as the tag key, while `FileOps::validate_name` rejects it (not exactly trimmed).
- Reserved archive-shaped names (e.g. `doc.md.archive.1234567890`, matched by `is_archive_tag_name`) would be rejected as `ReservedArchiveName` by FileOps but can receive a `deleted` tag / have it removed through the web handlers.
- Names containing `..` components or other shapes forbidden by the canonical rule are not rejected by delete/restore, unlike FileOps-backed paths, and the `deleted` tag then lives under a non-canonical key.

## Why it matters

- Breaks the "single canonical-name rule for every FileOps entry point" invariant: web soft-deleted/restored files may be keyed under names other surfaces reject, diverging tag/metadata semantics across surfaces.
- The `deleted` marker is stored under the raw, possibly non-canonical name, so a padded or reserved-shaped name can carry (or lose) a `deleted` tag that FileOps-backed tooling cannot address consistently, reintroducing name/namespace confusion the FileOps validation was meant to prevent (related prior fixes: #4102, #4720 addressed FileOps-side name/archive rules; #10549 tracks the save/new sibling).

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Apply the canonical name rule to web soft-delete/restore paths: validate `req.name` in `delete_handler` and `restore_handler` with `FileOps::validate_name` (or the same semantics, after any intended forgiving normalization such as trimming is applied consistently and the stored name is the normalized one) before the existence lookup and before any tag write (`set_singleton`/`del_by_key`).
- [ ] Reject `EmptyName`, `InvalidName` (untrimmed, rooted/drive-prefixed, empty/`.`/`..` components), and `ReservedArchiveName` with clear 4xx responses (and preserve existing behavior for valid names).
- [ ] Keep behavior consistent with `hard_delete_handler`/FileOps paths (same error mapping style) where applicable.
- [ ] Consider the same validation for other web entry points that accept user-controlled file names outside FileOps (e.g. upload naming, rename/copy request prechecks) for consistency, if not already covered.
- [ ] Add regression tests covering: delete and restore reject reserved archive-shaped names; reject names with `..`/invalid path components; reject untrimmed/whitespace-padded names (or normalize-then-validate consistently); valid ordinary names still soft-delete/restore successfully.

## Related

- #10549 (save/new file handlers sibling gap)
- Epic #4766 (canonical name / archive namespace)

title: pkgs/id(tests): planted-bug-check.sh ignores unaccounted CLI arguments before mutating/running suites
body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh` documents a no-argument invocation but does not parse or reject CLI arguments before performing work. When invoked with extra arguments it proceeds into its normal flow (dirty-tree checks, baseline cargo test run, patch/apply/restore cycle).

- Script: `pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh:11` documents usage as `pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh` / `just planted-bug-check`; there is no argument parsing/`$#` validation before work begins (git status checks and restoration setup at `:37-46`, baseline suite execution at `:59-64`).
- Invoked as an operator/dev check: `pkgs/id/justfile:234-235` (`planted-bug-check` recipe runs `bash tests/planted-bug-check.sh`), also recorded in `pkgs/id/just-recipes.json` and referenced in `pkgs/id/tests/README.md`.
- Observed behavior: invoking `bash pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh --help` from `pkgs/id/` did not fail fast; it entered the script's execution path and began running (had to be interrupted/terminated in this session before completion because it proceeds to cargo test suites). This indicates unaccounted arguments are ignored rather than rejected before work.

## Why it matters

Per the operator-script argument contract in `AGENTS.md` / #3352, every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess/file-mutating work; anything unaccounted for must be a usage error with a non-zero exit. `planted-bug-check.sh` mutates/restores tracked source files and runs expensive test suites; ignoring unexpected arguments can trigger heavy, stateful work on a mistyped invocation (e.g. `--help`/wrong flags) instead of failing safely.

(Related but distinct: #8037 tracks that `planted-bug-check.sh` runs nowhere in CI/flake/check-all; this issue is about strict argument handling regardless of where it runs.)

## Acceptance criteria

- `pkgs/id/tests/planted-bug-check.sh` rejects any unaccounted CLI arguments (including extra positional args and options such as `--help` unless explicitly supported and documented) before performing dirty-tree checks, git restore/trap setup side effects beyond safe parsing, patch application, or running cargo test suites, exiting non-zero with a clear usage/error message.
- The documented contract (usage/header comment) states the accepted invocation (no arguments, unless a supported flag is intentionally added and documented).
- Existing valid invocations (`bash tests/planted-bug-check.sh`, `just planted-bug-check`) continue to work unchanged.
- Add/update coverage (script-level check or documented test hook) showing unaccounted arguments are rejected before work.

## Suggested fix shape

Add a strict preflight argument check at the very top of the script (before `MUTATED_FILES`/dirty checks/trap/baseline), e.g. reject when `$# -ne 0` with usage to stderr and a non-zero exit; update the usage/header to reflect the contract.

- `pkgs/id/scripts/test-shard-sandbox-test.sh` rejects any unaccounted CLI arguments (including extra positional args and options such as `--help` unless explicitly supported and documented) before creating temp fixtures or running checks, exiting non-zero with a clear usage/error message.

title: laptop-autocommit-openclaw death spiral: 131MB live sqlite tracked in git, push can never succeed, ~10 cores burned every minute

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/parked
labels.description: Deliberately paused with a recorded resume condition

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

labels.name: queue/parked
labels.description: Queue task is parked (waiting on CI, time, or an event)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Symptom

The laptop (16 cores) sits at sustained load ~25–28. `laptop-autocommit-openclaw.service` fires every minute and each run consumes 8–13 CPU-minutes in ~62 s of wall clock with a 9–17 GB memory peak, then fails: `autocommit: PUSH FAILED in /home/user/.openclaw (N commit(s) unpushed)` — N grows by one every minute (2205 at 12:55 CST → 2406 at 16:23 CST on 2026-11-15). The `.git/objects/pack/` dir is littered with `tmp_pack_*` garbage from killed pack runs (151 garbage files, 556 MB).

This permanent load is the amplifier behind the PM aggregator page flaps tracked in #9850: with the box saturated, aggregator assemblies starve. It contributed to the 2026-11-14 attention.json flaps and to the post-#10466-deploy /board 503 on 2026-11-15 16:16 CST (cold caches after the 16:12 switch restart + a /board assembly that blew the 10 s deadline under load ~26, with no last-good cache to serve stale from).

## Evidence (2026-11-15, laptop, live reads)

- `journalctl --user -u laptop-autocommit-openclaw`: every minute `Consumed 8min–13min CPU time over ~1min wall, 9.5–16.9G memory peak`, followed by `PUSH FAILED ... unpushed` with the count incrementing by 1 per run.
- Repo state: `git count-objects -vH` → 8603 loose objects, **6.19 GiB loose**; `@{u}..HEAD` = **2406 commits ahead**, never draining.
- Largest tracked file: `agents/main/agent/openclaw-agent.sqlite` = **137,469,952 bytes (131 MiB)** — a live SQLite DB rewritten continuously, re-hashed and re-stored as a fresh loose blob by `git add -u` every minute. Second: `state/openclaw.sqlite` 8.2 MB, same churn pattern.
- The push can never succeed: the 131 MiB blob exceeds GitHub's 100 MB per-file hard limit, and the script's `timeout 60 git push` kills pack-objects mid-compression every run — pack threads on all 16 cores for 60 s, every minute, forever. A death spiral: each failed run adds one more commit and one more ~131 MB blob to the next attempt.
- The other three autocommit units are healthy (hatch-personal: 1.4–3.6 s CPU/run) — this is specific to the `.openclaw` repo contents, not the script's other deployments.

## Scope

- `~/.openclaw` checkout of dezren39/openclaw-personal on the laptop, and `laptop-autocommit-openclaw.{service,timer}`.
- NOT in scope: the aggregator/projector code (#9850 / PR #10466 covers that side; its reconcile + attention fixes verified live 2026-11-15 16:15 CST — a full pass now takes ~16 s / 58 rows vs 22–35 min / ~11.5k rows before).

## Fix applied (ops, this pass)

1. Stopped `laptop-autocommit-openclaw.timer` to stop the bleed.
2. Backup coverage check: the daily `openclaw-backup` job already archives all of `~/.openclaw` (sqlite DBs snapshotted transaction-consistently) to local + R2 + Drive with 30-day retention — untracking the live DBs from git loses no backup coverage; they never reached GitHub anyway.
3. Preserved the local tip under `refs/backup/pre-squash-2026-11-15`, untracked both live sqlite DBs (`git rm --cached`) + added them to `.gitignore`, squashed the 2406 unpushed autocommits into a single commit on top of `@{u}` (tree = current tracked state minus the DBs; no blob >100 MB), pushed, restarted the timer.

## Acceptance

- `laptop-autocommit-openclaw` runs complete in seconds, push succeeds, `@{u}..HEAD` returns to 0 after each cycle.
- Laptop load average returns to normal (well under core count) with the timer running.
- Aggregator probes (/board, /api/attention.json, /api/quota.json) sustain 200s with no timeout/503 over a 15-minute window under the restored timer.

## Follow-ups worth considering

- A guard in `pkgs/laptop-autocommit`: refuse (loudly, once) to commit a tracked file over ~95 MB instead of spiralling — defense in depth for every autocommit deployment.
- `git gc` on the `.openclaw` repo to reclaim the ~6.2 GB of unreachable loose objects once the fix verifies.

Refs: #9850 (aggregator stalls — this was a contributing load source), #1723 (autocommit program, closed).
