title: id(web): save/new file handlers bypass FileOps canonical name validation
body:
## Problem

The web file-management handlers `save_handler` and `new_file_handler` accept and persist `req.name` without applying the canonical name validation that `FileOps` enforces for every FileOps entry point. This lets the web API create/save names that the CLI/REPL/meta protocol reject, diverging behavior across entry points and bypassing the reserved archive namespace and path-shape invariants.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:12-206` (`save_handler`): takes `Json(req): Json<SaveRequest>` and uses `req.name` throughout (rate limiting/reservation, save, publish filename tag, archive, blob tag `Tag::from(req.name.clone())`, metadata keys, collab notification, response) with no `FileOps::validate_name` (or equivalent) check.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs:212-260+` (`new_file_handler`): only rejects when `req.name.trim().is_empty()` (line ~218) but then operates on the original `req.name` (existence lookup, mode detection, tag set, metadata writes), again without canonical validation.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs:267-296` (`FileOps::validate_name`): documents "The single canonical-name rule for every FileOps entry point" and rejects names that are not exactly trimmed (`name != name.trim()`), rooted / `\`-prefixed / Windows drive-prefixed, containing empty/`.`/`..` path components, or matching the reserved archive-tag shape (`is_archive_tag_name` -> `ReservedArchiveName`). `FileOps::put/rename/copy` all validate via this rule; rename/copy also reject `SameName`.

Concrete bypass examples under current code:
- A name with leading/trailing whitespace (e.g. `" notes.md"`) passes `new_file_handler`'s emptiness check but is stored verbatim, while `FileOps::validate_name` rejects it (not exactly trimmed).
- Reserved archive-shaped names (e.g. `doc.md.archive.1234567890`, accepted by `is_archive_tag_name`) would be rejected as `ReservedArchiveName` by FileOps but can be saved/created through the web handlers.
- Names containing `..` components or other shapes forbidden by the canonical rule are not rejected by save/new web handlers, unlike FileOps-backed paths.

`save_handler` also archives via `archive_original_tag` / `claim_archive_name` and manipulates tags/metadata directly rather than through a single FileOps operation, so invalid/reserved names can enter the same tag/metadata/archive namespace FileOps treats as governed.

## Why it matters

- Breaks the "single canonical-name rule for every FileOps entry point" invariant: web-created files may be impossible to manage consistently via FileOps/CLI/REPL/meta or may collide with the reserved archive namespace and archive bookkeeping.
- Creates cross-surface behavior drift (web accepts names other surfaces reject), which makes name-based operations and metadata/archive semantics harder to reason about and can reintroduce name/namespace confusion the FileOps validation was meant to prevent (related prior fixes: #4102, #4720 addressed FileOps-side name/archive rules).

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- [ ] Apply the canonical name rule to web save/create paths: validate `req.name` in `save_handler` and `new_file_handler` with `FileOps::validate_name` (or the same semantics, after any intended forgiving normalization such as trimming is applied consistently and the stored name is the normalized one) before rate-limiting side effects/tag writes/metadata/publish/archive work.
- [ ] Reject `EmptyName`, `InvalidName` (untrimmed, rooted/drive-prefixed, empty/`.`/`..` components), and `ReservedArchiveName` with clear 4xx responses (and preserve existing behavior for valid names).
- [ ] Consider the same validation for other web entry points that accept user-controlled file names outside FileOps (e.g. upload naming, rename/copy request prechecks) for consistency, if not already covered.
- [ ] Add regression tests covering: save and new reject reserved archive-shaped names; reject names with `..`/invalid path components; reject untrimmed/whitespace-padded names (or normalize-then-validate consistently); valid ordinary names still save/create successfully.

title: fix(bin): openchamber-start.sh ignores unaccounted CLI arguments before reading state and exec
body:
## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`87e0133554`, 2026-11-15), [`bin/openchamber-start.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/87e0133554/bin/openchamber-start.sh) declares/uses only a single positional argument (the OpenChamber serve script path, passed by the home-manager unit shim):

- `serve="$1"` (line 23)
- empty check: `if [ -z "$serve" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` (lines 24-27)
- it then reads the standing OpenCode server state/password from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`, exports credentials, and `exec "$serve"` (lines 29-41)

There is no `$#`/extra-argument validation, so any additional positional arguments after the required serve script are silently ignored before sensitive startup work.

### Repro (safe, no service started)

Using a throwaway executable that exits immediately as the serve script argument:

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp /home/user/.local/share/opencode/tmp/opencode/oc-serve.XXXXXX.sh)
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$tmp" && chmod +x "$tmp"
bash bin/openchamber-start.sh "$tmp" extra-bogus-arg; echo "rc=$?"
rm -f "$tmp"
```

Observed on this host (with `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` readable): exit code `0` and the dummy serve script was exec'd, proving `extra-bogus-arg` was ignored and the script proceeded through state/password handling and exec.

## Why it matters

`bin/openchamber-start.sh` is an operator/startup wrapper that reads a local password/state file and exports `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` before attaching/starting OpenChamber. Ignoring unaccounted CLI arguments violates the operator-script argument contract (#3352): a mis-invocation (extra/typoed argument, wrong argument order, or stale caller assumptions) is silently accepted instead of failing fast, which can lead to starting the service under unintended assumptions.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bin/openchamber-start.sh` rejects any unaccounted CLI arguments (including extra positional arguments after the required serve-script argument) before reading state, exporting credentials, or exec'ing the serve script.
- [ ] Rejection prints a clear usage/error to stderr and exits non-zero (usage-error exit code consistent with repo operator-script conventions).
- [ ] Existing valid invocation with exactly the expected serve-script argument preserves current behavior.
- [ ] Add/update a regression test (or test harness coverage, as appropriate for this wrapper) covering: missing argument, valid single argument path, and extra/unaccounted argument rejection.

## Suggested fix shape

Validate the full command line up front (e.g. require exactly 1 argument, or explicit `--`/option parsing if expanded later) and emit `usage: openchamber-start.sh <serve-script>` on violation; keep the current state-file/password checks and exec behavior unchanged for valid input.

title: projector: read/reconcile routes return unstructured 500s on store or runtime failures

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

Most `pm-stack/projector` HTTP routes let store, git, or reconcile exceptions propagate out of `handleRequest`, so a runtime failure becomes an unhandled fetch rejection and a framework-default 500 response with no JSON error body. This is inconsistent with the service's own `/health` and `/github/webhook` paths, which catch failures and return structured JSON responses.

## Evidence

`pm-stack/projector/src/server.ts`:

- `GET /health` (`/api/health`) catches probe failures and returns `503` JSON: `L280-294` (`try { ... } catch (e) { return jsonResponse(503, { ok: false, error: ... }) }`).
- `POST /github/webhook` validates input, guards apply/publish, records outcomes, and returns structured 4xx/5xx JSON on failures: `L297-358`.
- Other routes do not guard store/runtime calls:
  - `GET /items`: `L305-322` calls `store.getItems` / `store.listItems` without try/catch.
  - `GET /comments`: `L325-340` calls `store.getCommentsForSubject` / `store.getComments` without try/catch.
  - `GET /links`: `L346-351` calls `store.getLinks` without try/catch.
  - `DELETE /links`: `L395-399` calls `store.deleteLink` without try/catch (POST's `upsertLink` is separately guarded at `L384-388`).
  - `GET /subjects/*`: `L418-431` calls `store.getSubject` without try/catch.
  - `GET /hot`: `L444-456` calls `store.hotHighWater` / `store.listHotEvents` without try/catch.
  - `GET /hot/checkpoints`: `L458-463` calls `store.getConsumerCheckpoint` without try/catch.
  - `POST /reconcile`: `L500-504` calls `reconcileRepos(...)` without try/catch.

`serve()` returns `handleRequest(...)` directly (`L603-615`), so thrown/rejected errors are not normalized into the service's `jsonResponse` shape.

## Why it matters

Projector is an internal API consumed by other PM-stack components and operational tooling. DB contention/corruption, bad state, or reconcile failures can produce opaque/non-JSON 500s that are harder for clients and monitors to interpret than a consistent `{ "error": ... }` response.

## Suggested fix shape

Add a consistent error boundary for route handlers (or a top-level catch around `handleRequest`/`serve` fetch) that logs the failure and returns a structured JSON 5xx (e.g. `jsonResponse(500, { error: ... })`), while preserving existing specific status codes where already intentional. Keep the webhook's current semantics where appropriate.

title: aggregator: /api/sw-probe accumulates unbounded in-memory script URLs

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Problem

`POST /api/sw-probe` accepts client-reported service-worker script URLs and stores every unique foreign/evicted URL string forever in process memory, with no cap on entry count or key length. `GET /api/sw-probe` returns the full accumulated maps. The endpoint is unauthenticated.

## Evidence

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/push.ts:110-123` — `recordSwProbe` appends any string from `report.registrations`/`report.evicted` into module-level `probe.foreignSeen` / `probe.evictedSeen` maps without bounds:
  - `if (typeof r === "string" && isForeignSwScript(r)) { probe.foreignSeen[r] = (probe.foreignSeen[r] ?? 0) + 1; }`
  - evicted strings are stored similarly with no foreign-script filter.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/push.ts:126-133` — `swProbeSummary()` returns copies of both full maps, so response size grows with accumulated state.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:3409-3415` — `/api/sw-probe` POST reads a JSON body and records it with no authentication gate in that route; GET exposes the running summary.

Request bodies are bounded by `readJsonBody` (100KB), but repeated requests can add many distinct entries over time, growing memory and the GET payload without limit.

## Why it matters

Unbounded input-driven in-memory growth is a resource-exhaustion risk (memory/response bloat) for the long-lived aggregator process. Because the probe is observational, accumulation beyond what is useful provides no operational value.

## Suggested fix shape

Bound the probe state: enforce a maximum number of tracked script URLs and/or maximum key length, drop/ignore entries beyond the cap (or keep only aggregate counts/top-N), and consider bounding the evicted map the same way. Optionally add lightweight input validation (e.g. only accept plausible URL/script-path strings) while keeping the endpoint fail-soft.

title: pkgs/id(scripts): just-recipes-check.sh ignores unaccounted CLI arguments before running checks
body:
## Problem
`pkgs/id/scripts/just-recipes-check.sh` accepts and ignores unaccounted positional CLI arguments, then proceeds with its normal work (subprocesses and file reads/writes in a temp dir) instead of failing fast with a usage error.

This violates the operator-script argument contract (#3352): every operator script must declare its whole command line and reject anything unaccounted for with a non-zero exit **before** any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step.

## Evidence
- Script: `pkgs/id/scripts/just-recipes-check.sh` (HEAD 87e0133554). It declares no positional arguments and has no `$#`/arg validation; it immediately does work (`cd` to pkgs/id, `mktemp`, `just --dump --dump-format json`, `jq` projections, `diff`).
- Verified repro from `pkgs/id` on 87e0133554:
  - `bash scripts/just-recipes-check.sh extra-arg-test` exited 0 and printed `✓ just-recipes.json matches the justfile` after running the check, showing the extra argument was ignored and work was performed.

## Why it matters
Unaccounted arguments are silently accepted, so typos or misuse (e.g. a mistaken path/flag) do not stop execution. That can hide operator error and makes the script's CLI contract ambiguous.

## Acceptance criteria
- `pkgs/id/scripts/just-recipes-check.sh` rejects any unaccounted positional arguments with a clear usage/error on stderr and a non-zero exit (exit 2, consistent with sibling pkgs/id scripts) **before** performing `cd`/temp-dir/subprocess/check work.
- Normal invocation with no arguments behaves as before.
- `--help`/`-h` behavior, if added or already present, also rejects trailing unaccounted arguments per contract.
- A regression test covers rejection of extra arguments (and preserves the no-arg success path where applicable).

## Suggested fix shape
- Add an explicit argument contract (e.g. `usage()` + `if (($# != 0)); then ... exit 2; fi`, and optional `--help` handling that also rejects extra args) near the top, before `cd`, `mktemp`, or any `just`/`jq`/`diff` work.
- Follow the strict pattern used by other covered pkgs/id operator scripts (e.g. `build.sh`, `test-shard-sandbox.sh`).

title: pm-stack(aggregator): install.sh ignores unaccounted CLI arguments while performing install/deploy work
body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` is an operator install/deploy script for the laptop aggregator, but it never declares or enforces a CLI argument contract. Any unaccounted positional arguments are silently ignored while the script proceeds to validate the checkout, render/install deployment inputs, run `bun install`, migrate state, and (re)start/verify `pm-aggregator.service`.

## Evidence

- Script: `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh`
- Usage comment declares no arguments: "Usage (on the laptop):  bash install.sh" (around line 16-20 in the header block).
- The script begins real work immediately with `set -euo pipefail`, `cd "$(dirname "$0")"`, path validation, state/env setup, change detection, dependency install, env rendering, migration, systemd install/restart, and health checks (`:1-220+`), but contains no `$#`/`$1`/`$@` validation, `getopts`, `case`, or `shift` handling to reject extra arguments.
- Result: `bash pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh unexpected` is accepted and the full operator flow runs as if invoked correctly.

## Why it matters

Per the repo's operator-script argument contract (#3352), operator scripts must declare their whole command line and reject anything unaccounted for before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step. Accepting stray arguments risks running a heavyweight install/restart with a mistaken invocation (for example a typo'd flag or an argument meant for a different script) without a usage error.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` explicitly rejects any unaccounted CLI arguments with a clear usage message and non-zero exit before performing validation side effects beyond argument parsing (and before dependency install, env rendering, migration, systemd operations, or network/health checks).
- `bash pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` (no args) continues to behave as today when run from the expected checkout.
- `bash pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh --help` and/or an unexpected argument path fails fast with usage and non-zero status.
- Add/update a targeted test or shell check covering the argument-rejection path if an appropriate harness exists for this script.

title: pkgs/id(scripts): rebuild-roc-examples.sh ignores unaccounted CLI arguments before rebuild work

## Problem
`pkgs/id/scripts/rebuild-roc-examples.sh` does not enforce the operator-script argument contract before doing rebuild work.

The script declares no positional arguments and performs no CLI parsing/validation (`pkgs/id/scripts/rebuild-roc-examples.sh:1-19`). It immediately changes into the pkgs/id root and rebuilds a fixed set of Roc examples by running `bash ./build.sh` in each example directory (`:5-18`), so any unaccounted positional arguments are silently ignored while expensive rebuild work runs.

Per the repo operator-script argument contract (#3352), operator scripts must declare their whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess/file/build work; anything unaccounted for must be a usage error with non-zero exit.

## Evidence
- HEAD: `87e0133554` (`origin/main`)
- File: `pkgs/id/scripts/rebuild-roc-examples.sh` (19 lines)
- No `$#` check, no `getopts`, no usage/arg rejection; work begins unconditionally.

## Why it matters
This is a pkgs/id (standing-priority) maintenance script that triggers multiple example rebuilds. Ignoring extra arguments hides typos/misuse and can waste time doing unintended rebuilds instead of failing fast.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix shape
- Document that the script takes no positional arguments.
- Reject any unaccounted arguments before `cd`/rebuild work, with a usage message to stderr and non-zero exit.
- Preserve current behavior when invoked with no arguments.
- Add a regression test (or extend existing script tests) asserting extra args are rejected without performing rebuild side effects.

title: pkgs/id: build.sh and scripts/build.sh ignore unaccounted CLI arguments before build work

## Problem
`pkgs/id/build.sh` and `pkgs/id/scripts/build.sh` (identical files) do not enforce the operator-script argument contract before doing build work.

Both scripts document a fixed interface:

- `pkgs/id/build.sh:2-5` — `Usage: build.sh [variant] [profile]` with `variant` in `{lib,web,assets}` and `profile` in `{debug,release}`
- `pkgs/id/scripts/build.sh:2-5` — same usage

They read and validate only the first two positional arguments (`pkgs/id/build.sh:23-37`, `pkgs/id/scripts/build.sh:23-37`), then proceed into frontend/Rust build logic (`pkgs/id/build.sh:54+`, `pkgs/id/scripts/build.sh:54+`) without rejecting extra positional arguments. Any additional arguments (for example a typoed third arg or `--help` passed positionally in an unexpected form) are silently ignored while the script may perform real build work.

Per the repo operator-script argument contract (#3352), operator scripts must declare their whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess/file/build work; anything unaccounted for must be a usage error with non-zero exit.

## Evidence
- HEAD: `87e0133554` (`origin/main`)
- Files: `pkgs/id/build.sh`, `pkgs/id/scripts/build.sh` (byte-identical, 170 lines each)
- No `$#` / extra-arg rejection; only `$1`/`$2` are consumed and validated.

## Why it matters
`pkgs/id` build scripts are core developer/operator entrypoints (standing-priority area). Silent acceptance of unaccounted arguments can hide typos/misuse and cause unexpected build behavior instead of failing fast.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix shape
- Declare the full accepted CLI (at most 2 positional args: `[variant] [profile]`) in header comments and usage text.
- Reject any unaccounted positional arguments before frontend/Rust build work begins, emitting a usage error to stderr and exiting non-zero.
- Preserve existing valid behavior for 0, 1, or 2 valid arguments.
- Add/update a regression test covering rejection of extra args (and that valid invocations still behave as before), consistent with existing script tests in `pkgs/id/scripts/*-test.sh`.

title: pm-stack(pad/deploy): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before render/restart/deploy work
body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/pad/deploy.sh` is an operator script (renders SOPS-backed `.env`, pulls/recreates the Pad container, waits for health) and declares its command line as `[deploy|render|restart]`:

- `pm-stack/pad/deploy.sh:69-95` dispatches only on `${1:-deploy}` and rejects unknown commands, but never checks for extra arguments after a recognized command.
- `render` (lines 70-72) runs `render` and exits success even when extra args are present (e.g. `./deploy.sh render --oops`).
- `restart` (lines 73-75) runs `docker compose restart` and ignores extra args.
- `deploy` (lines 76-90) renders, pulls, force-recreates, and runs the health gate loop while ignoring extra args.

Repro (static): invoking any recognized subcommand with trailing arguments performs the full operation instead of failing with usage, so typos/extra flags are silently accepted.

## Why it matters

Per `AGENTS.md` "Operator script argument contract (#3352)" / `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`, every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for must be a usage error with non-zero exit. Accepting unaccounted arguments here can trigger unintended deploy/restart/render work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pm-stack/pad/deploy.sh` rejects any argument beyond the single optional subcommand it declares (`deploy|render|restart`) with a usage error to stderr and non-zero exit (2), before rendering, running docker compose, or performing health checks.
- Valid invocations (`./deploy.sh`, `./deploy.sh deploy`, `./deploy.sh render`, `./deploy.sh restart`) preserve existing behavior.
- Add/update coverage (or a documented check) showing extra args are rejected and valid forms still work.

## Suggested fix

Add an argument-count/position check after parsing the subcommand (e.g. `[[ $# -le 1 ]] || { usage >&2; exit 2; }`) or enforce per-branch arity, matching the strict pattern used by covered siblings (see recent pm-stack arg-contract fixes such as #10441/#10442).

## Why it matters

You are "Bolt" ⚡ - a performance-obsessed agent who makes the codebase faster, one optimization at a time.

Your mission is to identify and implement ONE small performance improvement that makes the application measurably faster or more efficient.


## Boundaries

✅ **Always do:**
- Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` (or associated equivalents) before creating PR
- Add comments explaining the optimization
- Measure and document expected performance impact

⚠️ **Ask first:**
- Adding any new dependencies
- Making architectural changes

🚫 **Never do:**
- Modify package.json or tsconfig.json without instruction
- Make breaking changes
- Optimize prematurely without actual bottleneck
- Sacrifice code readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S PHILOSOPHY:
- Speed is a feature
- Every millisecond counts
- Measure first, optimize second
- Don't sacrifice readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY:
Before starting, read .jules/bolt.md (create if missing).

Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL learnings that will help you avoid mistakes or make better decisions.

⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover:
- A performance bottleneck specific to this codebase's architecture
- An optimization that surprisingly DIDN'T work (and why)
- A rejected change with a valuable lesson
- A codebase-specific performance pattern or anti-pattern
- A surprising edge case in how this app handles performance

❌ DO NOT journal routine work like:
- "Optimized component X today" (unless there's a learning)
- Generic React performance tips
- Successful optimizations without surprises

Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title]
**Learning:** [Insight]
**Action:** [How to apply next time]`

BOLT'S DAILY PROCESS:

1. 🔍 PROFILE - Hunt for performance opportunities:

  FRONTEND PERFORMANCE:
  - Unnecessary re-renders in React/Vue/Angular components
  - Missing memoization for expensive computations
  - Large bundle sizes (opportunities for code splitting)
  - Unoptimized images (missing lazy loading, wrong formats)
  - Missing virtualization for long lists
  - Synchronous operations blocking the main thread
  - Missing debouncing/throttling on frequent events
  - Unused CSS or JavaScript being loaded
  - Missing resource preloading for critical assets
  - Inefficient DOM manipulations

  BACKEND PERFORMANCE:
  - N+1 query problems in database calls
  - Missing database indexes on frequently queried fields
  - Expensive operations without caching
  - Synchronous operations that could be async
  - Missing pagination on large data sets
  - Inefficient algorithms (O(n²) that could be O(n))
  - Missing connection pooling
  - Repeated API calls that could be batched
  - Large payloads that could be compressed

  GENERAL OPTIMIZATIONS:
  - Missing caching for expensive operations
  - Redundant calculations in loops
  - Inefficient data structures for the use case
  - Missing early returns in conditional logic
  - Unnecessary deep cloning or copying
  - Missing lazy initialization
  - Inefficient string concatenation in loops
  - Missing request/response compression

2. ⚡ SELECT - Choose your daily boost:
  Pick the BEST opportunity that:
  - Has measurable performance impact (faster load, less memory, fewer requests)
  - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines
  - Doesn't sacrifice code readability significantly
  - Has low risk of introducing bugs
  - Follows existing patterns

3. 🔧 OPTIMIZE - Implement with precision:
  - Write clean, understandable optimized code
  - Add comments explaining the optimization
  - Preserve existing functionality exactly
  - Consider edge cases
  - Ensure the optimization is safe
  - Add performance metrics in comments if possible

4. ✅ VERIFY - Measure the impact:
  - Run format and lint checks
  - Run the full test suite
  - Verify the optimization works as expected
  - Add benchmark comments if possible
  - Ensure no functionality is broken

5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your speed boost:
  Create a PR with:
  - Title: "⚡ Bolt: [performance improvement]"
  - Description with:
    * 💡 What: The optimization implemented
    * 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
    * 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement (e.g., "Reduces re-renders by ~50%")
    * 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
  - Reference any related performance issues

BOLT'S FAVORITE OPTIMIZATIONS:
⚡ Add React.memo() to prevent unnecessary re-renders
⚡ Add database index on frequently queried field
⚡ Cache expensive API call results
⚡ Add lazy loading to images below the fold
⚡ Debounce search input to reduce API calls
⚡ Replace O(n²) nested loop with O(n) hash map lookup
⚡ Add pagination to large data fetch
⚡ Memoize expensive calculation with useMemo/computed
⚡ Add early return to skip unnecessary processing
⚡ Batch multiple API calls into single request
⚡ Add virtualization to long list rendering
⚡ Move expensive operation outside of render loop
⚡ Add code splitting for large route components
⚡ Replace large library with smaller alternative

BOLT AVOIDS (not worth the complexity):
❌ Micro-optimizations with no measurable impact
❌ Premature optimization of cold paths
❌ Optimizations that make code unreadable
❌ Large architectural changes
❌ Optimizations that require extensive testing
❌ Changes to critical algorithms without thorough testing

Remember: You're Bolt, making things lightning fast. But speed without correctness is useless. Measure, optimize, verify. If you can't find a clear performance win today, wait for tomorrow's opportunity.

title: atlas/fleet-search: #9973 trace capture was never mirrored into the fleet-search copy — `fleet serve search` writes no atlas-query-trace records and omits query_id (parity guard red on main)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

body:
## What's wrong

`bash .github/scripts/check-fleet-search-parity.sh` fails on current main HEAD `73ae4d58dc2b4268ab8acbf8fe69ea2ca4a59092` (exit 1) with two divergences between the atlas-search originals and their fleet-search copies:

```
::error::check-fleet-search-parity: render.rs diverged ...
@@ -97,9 +97,6 @@
         if let Some(qid) = out.get("query_id") {
             lines.push(format!("query_id: {}", py_str(Some(qid))));
         }
::error::check-fleet-search-parity: server.rs diverged ...
-use JsonlTraceSink ... TraceContext ... run_search_with_executor_traced,
+run_search_with_executor(
```

- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs:671-687` builds `JsonlTraceSink::new(JsonlTraceSink::default_dir())` and `TraceContext::new("service-api", "agent", "atlas-service")` and calls `run_search_with_executor_traced(...)`. The fleet copy `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs:668-676` calls plain `run_search_with_executor(...)` — the whole crate has **zero** references to `JsonlTraceSink`/`TraceContext`/`run_search_with_executor_traced` (`grep -rn` over `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/` returns nothing).
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/render.rs:104-106` prints a `query_id:` line in human output; `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/render.rs` (~:101-106) prints no such line.

The drift was introduced by `135e87dc50` (feat(atlas): query-trace capture — atlas-query-trace/v1, fail-closed, #9973), which touched only the atlas-search copies. The #8306 parity restoration (`edbcf08789`) fixed the previous drift; this one is new.

## Why it matters

- `#5604` rehomed the atlas service as `fleet serve search`, and the #5433/#5920 contract says the service must behave identically under either name. Today the deployed fleet surface silently produces **no `atlas-query-trace/v1` records at all**, so the trace consumers in atlas-core (`trace_stats.rs`, `trace_ingest.rs`) see nothing from the deployed role.
- #9973 designed trace capture as **fail-closed**: a trace write failure is a search failure, never a silently untraced success. On the fleet surface tracing is not attempted, so the invariant is simply absent there — the opposite failure mode.
- Operator-visible output diverges too: `atlas-search` prints `query_id:` for the same search that `fleet serve search` prints without it, which breaks result correlation between the two surfaces.
- Nothing catches it automatically: `fleet-search-parity-guard` is manual-only under `.github/ci-policy.md` (`| fleet-search-parity-guard | none | yes |`), and #10419's merge message already recorded the guard red at its base `ff161a7297` — i.e. the drift has been sitting undetected since `135e87dc50`.

## Dedupe

No open issue and no open PR tracks this. #8306 (CLOSED) covered the earlier parameter drift; #9973 (CLOSED) scoped trace capture to atlas-search; #8573 is about flaky atlas tests, unrelated.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `bash .github/scripts/check-fleet-search-parity.sh` exits 0 on the PR head (no drift reported for `render.rs` or `server.rs`).
2. `server.rs` copies match: same imports, same `run_search_with_executor_traced` call with the trace sink and a `TraceContext`. Decide and record one of: keep the `"atlas-service"` context string in both copies (byte parity, simplest), or extend the guard's normalizer to pin a `fleet-search` variant — in which case the guard, its pinned header text and `check-fleet-search-parity.test.sh` change in the same PR.
3. `render.rs` copies both render `query_id:` when the envelope carries one.
4. A fleet-side test proves `fleet serve search` writes a parseable `atlas-query-trace/v1` record for a live search (temp trace dir), and that a failing trace sink fails the search (#9973 fail-closed invariant).
5. `bash .github/scripts/check-fleet-search-parity.test.sh` still passes.
6. Coordination with the line limit: mirroring this adds ~30 production lines to `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search/src/server.rs`, which is already 1 production line over the 2500 limit (separate linked issue), so the split should land first or in the same PR.

title: pm-stack(deploy): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before render/restart/deploy work
body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/deploy.sh` is an operator script that declares a single optional subcommand (`deploy` default, `render`, or `restart`), but it ignores any additional positional arguments after a recognized subcommand and proceeds with its normal work.

## Evidence

- Script: [`pm-stack/deploy.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pm-stack/deploy.sh)
- Contract: root `AGENTS.md` → "Operator script argument contract (#3352)" and [`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md): every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit.
- Source: the script dispatches only on `${1:-deploy}` (`case` at `:102-130`) and never validates `$#` or rejects extra positional arguments. For a recognized subcommand, extra args are silently ignored:
  - `./deploy.sh render unexpected-arg` takes the `render` branch and runs `render()` (`:103-105`), which decrypts secrets via `sops --decrypt` and writes `.env`, `tunnel.token`, and `tunnel.env` (mode 600) before exiting (`:40-99`).
  - `./deploy.sh restart unexpected-arg` takes the `restart` branch and runs `docker compose restart` (`:106-108`).
  - `./deploy.sh deploy unexpected-arg` takes the `deploy` branch and performs the full deploy (render, pull, recreate, health wait, sync-guard subprocess/network checks) (`:109-130`).
  Unknown subcommands are correctly rejected (`:131-134`), but unaccounted extra arguments alongside a valid subcommand are not.

## Why it matters

Silently ignoring extra arguments makes typos, stale invocations, or future interface changes do the wrong thing without feedback. This script decrypts secrets, writes credential/token env files, restarts containers, and performs deploy/health/guard work; argument mistakes should fail fast before any of that work.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Declare the script's full command-line contract (at most one positional argument: `deploy`/`render`/`restart`, default `deploy`) and reject any unaccounted extra positional arguments with a clear usage message to stderr and a non-zero exit, before any subprocess, secret decryption, file write, network, or deploy step.
- Preserve existing behavior for valid invocations: no args, `deploy`, `render`, and `restart`.
- Add/update regression coverage asserting that extra positional arguments (e.g. `./deploy.sh render unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh restart unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh deploy unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh unexpected-arg extra`) are rejected with non-zero exit and do not start render/restart/deploy side effects in a controlled fixture.

## Summary

`pm-stack/grist/seed.sh` is an operator script (run on the host after deploy/bootstrap to seed the Grist roadmap document) that declares no command-line arguments, but it never rejects unaccounted positional arguments and proceeds with its normal work when extras are supplied.

## Evidence

- Script: [`pm-stack/grist/seed.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pm-stack/grist/seed.sh)
- Contract: root `AGENTS.md` → "Operator script argument contract (#3352)" and [`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md): every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit.
- Source: the script takes no positional parameters and performs no `$#`/argument validation. It immediately proceeds into work: `cd "$(dirname "$0")"`, a `bun` availability check and `bun run validate-roadmap-seed.ts` subprocess (`:13-17`), decrypts secrets via `sops --decrypt` (`:22`), and makes Grist API calls / may create workspace, document, table, and seed rows (`api` helper and subsequent logic, `:27+`). Any extra argument (e.g. `./seed.sh unexpected-arg`) is silently ignored before these subprocess, secret-access, network, and state-changing steps.

## Why it matters

Silently ignoring extra arguments makes typos, stale invocations, or future interface changes do the wrong thing without feedback. This script can decrypt secrets, talk to the Grist API, and create/seed roadmap data; argument mistakes should fail fast before any of that work.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Declare the script's full command-line contract (no positional arguments) and reject any unaccounted arguments with a clear usage message to stderr and a non-zero exit, before any subprocess, secret decryption, network, or API/file work (including the early `bun run validate-roadmap-seed.ts`).
- Preserve existing behavior for valid invocations with no positional arguments and existing environment-variable handling (`PM_STACK_SECRETS`, `SOPS_AGE_KEY_FILE`).
- Add/update regression coverage (a shell/script test exercising the entrypoint with an extra positional argument in a controlled fixture or with side-effecting steps stubbed/guarded) asserting that an extra argument is rejected with non-zero exit and that no seed/decrypt/network work is started.

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/grist/deploy.sh` is an operator script that declares a single optional subcommand (`deploy` default, `render`, or `restart`), but it ignores any additional positional arguments after a recognized subcommand and proceeds with its normal work.

## Evidence

- Script: [`pm-stack/grist/deploy.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/pm-stack/grist/deploy.sh)
- Contract: root `AGENTS.md` → "Operator script argument contract (#3352)" and [`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md): every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit.
- Source: the script dispatches only on `${1:-deploy}` (`case` at `:87-114`) and never validates `$#` or rejects extra positional arguments. For a recognized subcommand, extra args are silently ignored:
  - `./deploy.sh render unexpected-arg` takes the `render` branch and runs `render()` (`:88-90`), which decrypts secrets via `sops --decrypt` and writes `.env` (mode 600) before exiting (`:38-85`).
  - `./deploy.sh restart unexpected-arg` takes the `restart` branch and runs `docker compose restart` (`:91-93`).
  - `./deploy.sh deploy unexpected-arg` takes the `deploy` branch and performs the full deploy (render, pull, recreate, health wait/subprocess/network checks) (`:94-110`).
  Unknown subcommands are correctly rejected (`:111-114`), but unaccounted extra arguments alongside a valid subcommand are not.

## Why it matters

Silently ignoring extra arguments makes typos, stale invocations, or future interface changes do the wrong thing without feedback. This script decrypts secrets, writes the Grist env file, restarts containers, and performs deploy/health work; argument mistakes should fail fast before any of that work.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Declare the script's full command-line contract (at most one positional argument: `deploy`/`render`/`restart`, default `deploy`) and reject any unaccounted extra positional arguments with a clear usage message to stderr and a non-zero exit, before any subprocess, secret decryption, file write, network, or deploy step.
- Preserve existing behavior for valid invocations: no args, `deploy`, `render`, and `restart`.
- Add/update regression coverage asserting that extra positional arguments (e.g. `./deploy.sh render unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh restart unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh deploy unexpected-arg`, `./deploy.sh unexpected-arg extra`) are rejected with non-zero exit and do not start render/restart/deploy side effects in a controlled fixture.

title: scripts(hardware-doc-init): reject unaccounted CLI arguments per operator-script contract
body:
## Summary

`scripts/hardware-doc-init.sh` is an operator script that performs filesystem and git work (locates the repo/worktree, adopts or clones `hardware-doc`, may fetch/fast-forward it, and creates/updates `doc/hardware` and archive symlinks). It declares no positional command-line arguments, but it never rejects unaccounted arguments and proceeds with its normal work when extras are supplied.

## Evidence

- Script: [`scripts/hardware-doc-init.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/scripts/hardware-doc-init.sh)
- Contract: root `AGENTS.md` → "Operator script argument contract (#3352)" and [`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md): every operator script must declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit.
- Source: the script reads only environment variables (`HARDWARE_DOC_URL`, `HARDWARE_DOC_DIR_NAME`) and resolves repo/worktree paths; there is no `$#`/positional-argument validation. It then runs git/filesystem operations and can clone, fetch, fast-forward, and create symlinks.
- Repro (safe, isolated temp layout; `hardware-doc` exists as a clean local git repo with no upstream so the update path warns and does not fetch/merge, but the script still performs work and creates the symlink):

```sh
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
mkdir -p "$tmp/repo/.git" "$tmp/repo/doc" "$tmp/hardware-doc"
git -C "$tmp/repo" init -q && git -C "$tmp/repo" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.com -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --allow-empty -qm init
git -C "$tmp/hardware-doc" init -q && git -C "$tmp/hardware-doc" -c user.name=t -c user.email=t@example.com -c commit.gpgsign=false commit --allow-empty -qm init
cd "$tmp/repo"
bash /path/to/scripts/hardware-doc-init.sh unexpected-arg
echo "RC=$?"
readlink doc/hardware
```

Observed:
- prints normal status lines including `! branch 'main' has no upstream — not updating`
- creates `doc/hardware -> ../../hardware-doc`
- exits `0` (`RC=0`) despite the unaccounted positional argument `unexpected-arg`

## Why it matters

Silently ignoring extra arguments makes typos, stale invocations, or future interface changes do the wrong thing without feedback. This script can clone a repository, run git fetch/merge operations, and create/replace symlinks in the worktree; argument mistakes should fail fast before any of that work.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Declare the script's full command-line contract (no positional arguments) and reject any unaccounted arguments with a clear usage message to stderr and a non-zero exit, before resolving paths or performing git/filesystem work.
- Preserve existing behavior for valid invocations with no positional arguments and existing `HARDWARE_DOC_URL` / `HARDWARE_DOC_DIR_NAME` environment-variable handling.
- Add/update regression coverage (e.g. in `scripts/tests/test_hardware_doc_init.py`) asserting that an extra positional argument is rejected with non-zero exit and does not cause side effects (no clone/fetch/merge/symlink changes) in a controlled fixture.

title: pm-stack(opencode-claimant/poll): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before reading broker/ledger/server state
body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` declares no command-line arguments and performs no argument parsing (`main()` takes no parameters, and the script contains no `sys.argv`/`argparse` handling). Unaccounted arguments are ignored and the script proceeds to do its normal read work.

**File:** `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py:1-120,520-551` (module docstring states read-only discovery; `main()` builds/fetches queue, lane-ledger, and OpenCode server state and prints JSON; `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())`).

**Repro (verified on `origin/main` / HEAD `d5ad136471`, 2026-11-15):**
```bash
python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --bogus
# exits 0 and prints the full JSON discovery payload after performing reads

python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --help
# exits 0 and prints the full JSON discovery payload (no help/usage; work performed)
```

## Why it matters

Per `AGENTS.md` ("Operator script argument contract (#3352)") and `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`, every operator script must account for its whole command line and parse strictly before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit (2). `poll.py` is a `pm-stack` operator script that reads queue-broker state, lane-ledger state, and OpenCode server session state; ignoring unknown/typo'd flags (including `--help`) means a mis-invocation can silently do real reads instead of failing fast.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Parse the command line strictly before any reads/network/subprocess work; `poll.py` takes no positional or option arguments, so any unaccounted argument (including `--help` unless explicitly implemented as a no-side-effect usage path) is a usage error printed to stderr with exit code 2.
- `python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --bogus` and `python3 -I pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py --help` must fail as usage errors and perform no broker/ledger/server reads.
- Running with no arguments preserves current behavior and output.
- Add/extend a test (e.g. alongside existing `scripts`/pm-stack claimant tests) pinning that extra arguments are rejected before work.

title: scripts(worker-preflight): reject unaccounted CLI arguments per operator-script contract
body:
## Summary

`scripts/worker-preflight.sh` is an operator script invoked at the start of worker tasks (see root `AGENTS.md`, "Worker Git preflight"). It takes no arguments, but it does not declare or enforce that contract: extra positional arguments are silently ignored and the script proceeds as if invoked correctly.

## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`e77ed212644298222326837e36c5771d3a05d0e2` at time of check), in `/home/user/git/code`:

```bash
$ bash scripts/worker-preflight.sh extra-arg
worker-preflight: clean (/home/user/git/code; no local refs/heads/origin/main)
$ echo $?
0
```

`scripts/worker-preflight.sh` (24 lines) performs its checks and exits 0/1/2 based on repo state, but never validates `$#`. Any stray or misspelled argument is accepted without notice.

## Why it matters

`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md` and root `AGENTS.md` ("Operator script argument contract #3352") require every operator script to declare its whole command line and parse strictly against that declaration before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step; anything unaccounted for is a usage error with a non-zero exit. Worker preflight is a guardrail script workers run before relying on Git names — silently accepting unexpected arguments weakens that contract and can hide invocation mistakes.

## Suggested fix / acceptance criteria

- Reject any unaccounted argument(s) with a clear usage error on stderr and exit code 2 (usage error), before performing preflight checks or emitting the success/clean message.
- Document the accepted command line in the script header comment (no arguments).
- Preserve existing behavior and exit codes for valid invocations: exit 0 when clean, exit 1 when `refs/heads/origin/main` shadows the remote-tracking ref, exit 2 when not in a Git worktree or ref verification cannot be completed.
- Add/adjust a small regression check (shell test or existing test harness convention for `scripts/worker-preflight.sh`, if present) asserting that an extra argument is rejected with non-zero/usage status and does not print the clean success message.

## References

- `scripts/worker-preflight.sh`
- `AGENTS.md` — "Worker Git preflight", "Operator script argument contract (#3352)"
- `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`

title: pm-stack(kaneo-sync-guard): reject unaccounted CLI arguments before running guard
body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py` is an operator script that runs `docker exec`/`psql` subprocesses and can heal Kaneo `statusTransitions` drift in Postgres, but it ignores any command-line arguments and proceeds with its normal work. This violates the operator script argument contract (unexpected/typo'd args must be rejected as a usage error before any subprocess, network, file write, lock, or deploy step).

## Evidence

- Script: `pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py`
  - Declared usage takes no arguments: docstring shows `python3 pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py` (`pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py:19`).
  - `main()` does not inspect `sys.argv` and performs guard work immediately (`pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py:67-121`), then `if __name__ == "__main__": sys.exit(main())` (`pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py:124-125`).
- Current callers pass no arguments: `pm-stack/deploy.sh:104`, `pm-stack/systemd/pm-kaneo-sync-guard.service:7` (`ExecStart=/bin/sh -lc 'python3 /home/user/pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py'`).
- Repro on `main` (HEAD observed in this run: `637e29c982`, 2026-11-15):
  - `python3 pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py unexpected-arg` exits `0` after running the guard and printing conforming integration results.
  - `python3 pm-stack/kaneo-sync-guard.py --help` also exits `0` and runs the guard instead of showing usage/rejecting the argument.

In the observed repro there was no drift to heal, but the script still executed its `psql` reads/subprocesses before any argument validation could reject the invocation.

## Why it matters

A typo, stray positional, or forgotten flag is silently treated as a normal run of a guard that can mutate integration config when drift is present. That defeats the strict argument contract for operator scripts and makes accidental misuse harder to detect.

## Acceptance criteria / suggested fix

- Parse/validate the full command line before any subprocess or DB access.
- Reject any unaccounted argument (unknown flag, stray positional, typo) with a usage error naming the offending argument and a non-zero exit (exit code `2` is appropriate here, matching the script's existing usage/error convention).
- Either declare and implement `-h`/`--help` explicitly or reject it the same way as any other unexpected argument (but do not run the guard first).
- Add/update a focused test or script contract check covering `unexpected-arg` and `--help` behavior so a future regression fails closed.

## References

- Operator script argument contract: `doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md` / root `AGENTS.md` ("Operator script argument contract (#3352)").
- Related component: close-authority guard #10137 / #10136.

title: ci(pm-stack): scheduled-history collector test (19 checks) runs nowhere and pm-stack-tests paths omit pm-stack/scheduled-history/**

labels.name: kind/ci
labels.description: CI/CD pipelines, workflows, and build automation

body:
## Summary

`pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py` is a 19-check regression suite for the scheduled-history reconciler/collector (`pm-stack/scheduled-history/collect.py`, added for #2174 / Gap 1). It passes locally on current `main`, but no CI workflow, flake check, or test-suite registry entry runs it, and changes under `pm-stack/scheduled-history/**` are not covered by the `pm-stack-tests` workflow path filters.

## Evidence

- Suite: `pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py` (19 checks, script-style suite; prints `19/19 checks passed` on success).
- Implementation/readme: `pm-stack/scheduled-history/collect.py`, `pm-stack/scheduled-history/README.md` (documents `python3 test_collect.py`).
- Local verification on `developing-today/code` @ `e77ed21264b8` (2026-11-15):
  - `python3 -m unittest pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py` → `Ran 0 tests in 0.000s` / `NO TESTS RAN` (not unittest-discoverable)
  - `python3 pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py` → exits 0 with `19/19 checks passed`
- CI wiring:
  - `.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` path filters include `pm-stack/scripts/**`, `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/**`, etc. but do **not** include `pm-stack/scheduled-history/**`.
  - `pm-stack-tests.yml` job steps run aggregator/projector/dispatch suites and specific script/python suites, but never invoke `pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py`.
  - `rg -n "scheduled-history|test_collect" .github nixos` returns no matches (no workflow/flake reference).
- Dedupe: `gh issue list -R developing-today/code --state all --search "scheduled-history OR test_collect"` returns no issue tracking this test/wiring (checked 2026-11-15).

## Why it matters

The scheduled-history collector is the durable per-run/outcome/token dataset for OpenChamber scheduled tasks (#2174). Without CI coverage, regressions in reconciliation/finalization/enrichment/windowing can land unnoticed, and edits under `pm-stack/scheduled-history/` currently won't even trigger the pm-stack test workflow.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CI runs `pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py` (e.g. `python3 pm-stack/scheduled-history/test_collect.py`) and fails the job on failure/non-zero exit.
- [ ] `.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` (or an equivalent appropriate workflow) includes `pm-stack/scheduled-history/**` in its path filters so changes to the collector/tests trigger the run.
- [ ] The wiring is documented/registered consistently with repo conventions if applicable (e.g. `.github/test-suite-registry.json` entry when suites of this kind are tracked there).
- [ ] A run demonstrates the 19 checks pass in CI on current `main`.

title: Server build lags the root lock opencode pin by 7 fork commits (4bcf07a running, aa0c8be locked)
body:
Found during the 2026-11-14 switch verification (code#10322).

The root flake.lock pins the opencode fork at aa0c8be805 (merge of fork PR #2449, the ratelimit bench-granularity series), and flake.nix declares openchamber.inputs.opencode.follows = "opencode" with a comment recording the intent that the committed lock be the single statement of the fork rev for CLI and server (the generation-530 incident).

The running server, however, is opencode-2.0.30+4bcf07a (process exe /nix/store/cnrh9acvp...-opencode-2.0.30+4bcf07a, started at switch activation 2026-11-15T00:14Z). 4bcf07a (fork PR #2441) is an ancestor of aa0c8be and DOES contain the retry fix (fork PR #2440, d9d67a78) — verified by merge-base — but NOT the 7 bench-granularity commits on top (feb2dc36, 86f04fde, b9d5013e, faa78115, 084d06ad, 5c62dfca, d4b4757a).

home/common/default.nix:131 defines the cascade package as inputs.openchamber.inputs.opencode.packages.opencode, and services.opencode.package points at the wrapped cascade. Suspect: the home configuration for amd is evaluated through a second input graph (dezren39-nix/flake.lock pins openchamber cd93d950, whose own opencode pin is older), so the root locks follows does not reach the server package. The /run/current-system CLI stamps yet another rev (c43145b, in the -wrapped package name).

Ask: make the server package provably build from the root lock opencode pin on every switch — one statement of the fork rev, verified by a post-switch check that compares the running servers source rev against flake.lock (a version-stamp comparison is not sufficient evidence; the fork package stamp may lag its source, which is part of the confusion here). Acceptance: after a switch, a check command shows running-server source rev == root flake.lock opencode rev.

title: pkgs/compiz: glibmm attribute removed from pinned nixpkgs — package no longer evaluates

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/compiz` no longer evaluates against the repo's pinned nixpkgs: the `glibmm` attribute has been removed from nixpkgs (replaced by explicit-ABI `glibmm_*` attributes), and `pkgs/compiz/default.nix` still takes `glibmm` in its callPackage argument set (line 8) and `buildInputs` (line 55).

## Evidence (2026-11-14, queue task 17198 shepherd pass on PR #8927)

Control-verified pre-existing on clean main (737e5434f5) — not caused by PR #8927, whose compiz change is only the `xorg.libXcursor` → `libxcursor` rename:

```
$ nix eval --impure --expr 'let f = builtins.getFlake (toString ./.); pkgs = f.inputs.nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux; custom = import ./pkgs { inherit pkgs; }; in custom.compiz.drvPath'
error: 'glibmm' attribute has been removed from nixpkgs. Use a 'glibmm_*' attribute with an explicit ABI version instead.
```

Same failure on main and on the PR branch. The amd NixOS toplevel does NOT reference compiz (it is only in the `pkgs/default.nix` overlay set), so system builds are unaffected; anything instantiating the custom package set's `compiz` (or evaluating the whole set) breaks.

## Fix shape

Pick the ABI variant compiz actually links (compiz 0.9.x uses glibmm 2.4 → `glibmm_2_4` if present in the pin), update the argument + buildInputs in `pkgs/compiz/default.nix`, and re-run the eval above until it returns a drvPath. Check the same removal pattern for other args in that file while there (e.g. `libwnck3` still exists in the pin — it evaluated past argument binding to the glibmm failure).

Found by lane any-a during the PR #8927 shepherd pass; that PR lands its own (unrelated) compiz rename without touching this breakage.

title: id(directory_mail): SmtpSink continuation-line cap (MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES) has no test that can reach it (PR #4267)

labels.name: kind/test
labels.description: Test coverage, test infrastructure, or test-only fixes

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Finding

PR #4267 (fix for #1899) added three bounds to SmtpSink's SMTP reply reader in `directory_mail.rs`: a total deadline, a per-line byte cap (`MAX_REPLY_LINE_BYTES`, 8192), and a per-reply continuation-line cap (`MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES`, 100). The deadline and the line cap each got a dedicated fake-relay regression test. The continuation cap got none — and the tests that look closest cannot reach it:

- `a_trickling_reply_fails_at_the_total_deadline` uses a relay that sends one `250-` continuation line every 50 ms and a 300 ms send timeout, so the send fails at the deadline after ~6 continuation lines — the counter never approaches 100.
- The byte-trickle and over-long-line tests exercise the deadline and the line cap, not the continuation count.

So the `continuations <= MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES` refusal can be deleted or broken (off-by-one, counter reset per line, cap raised) and every test in the suite stays green. The bound is part of the #1899 hardening: without it, a relay that answers promptly but endlessly with continuation lines is bounded only by the 10 s total deadline, not by the documented 100-line reply bound.

## Evidence

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4267 (merge commit c2b908b986de, ancestor-verified against current main 8b522c14816566c66e94dab2d3e804f35b59e034).
- On current main the code lives at `pkgs/id/crates/id-directory/src/directory_mail.rs` (moved in the id crate restructure): the cap constant at line 224, the counting/refusal in `expect` at lines 358–376 (`continuations += 1; ensure!(continuations <= MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES, ...)`).
- The same file's tests (lines ~866–985) contain exactly the three PR #4267 regressions — trickling reply (300 ms timeout, 50 ms trickle), byte-trickling line, over-long line — and no test that sends more than 100 continuation lines inside the deadline. Verified by reading the file on main twice (contents API + targeted greps for `continuation`/`CONTINUATION`).
- Dedupe: issue searches for `MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES`, "SMTP reply continuation", and "directory_mail continuation test" return only closed #1899 (the parent fix) — no open or closed issue covers this test gap.

## Why it matters

#1899's fix was a hardening change against a hostile or broken relay. Two of its three bounds are pinned by tests; the third is a three-line `ensure!` that a future refactor of `expect`/`read_reply_line` can silently drop. A prompt endless-continuation relay is exactly the case the deadline tests do not cover at the cap boundary, so the regression would ship unnoticed.

## Acceptance criteria

- A fake-relay test in the `directory_mail` test module sends more than `MAX_REPLY_CONTINUATION_LINES` continuation lines promptly (well inside the send deadline) and asserts the send fails with the continuation-cap error ("more than 100 continuation lines"), not the deadline error.
- A control at or under the cap (e.g. a reply with a handful of continuation lines followed by a final line) still succeeds, pinning that the cap counts continuations per reply.
- Existing directory_mail tests keep passing.

title: Monthly backup generations not kept

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
Found by the 2026-11-14 whole-PM-stack backup/DR audit (verdict issue filed same day).

**The ruling (Drew, 2026-11-03 on #1258, Q3/Q6):** off-machine retention = **daily generations kept 30 days, plus monthly generations kept 12 months**; #1218 Project exports retained off-machine for 1 year.

**Observed (2026-11-14):** no routine implements the monthly tier.
- `pm-dashboard-backup` / `pm-stack-backup` / `dashboard-backup` prune their dated dirs at **30 days** (local, and the same 30-day retention on the R2 + Drive legs) — grep for `monthly|keep-monthly|12 month` across `nixos/home/*.sh` and `~/tools/*backup*.sh` returns nothing.
- restic jobs (`repo-archive-backup`, `laptop-state-backup`) use keep-last 7 / keep-daily 7 / keep-weekly 4 — no monthly-12 either.
- Supabase dumps in R2 carry a config note: "Retention is informational for now: pruning is a deliberate manual step" (90 days noted, nothing enforced).
- #1218 is CLOSED (Project export built), but no off-machine copy of a Project export with a 1-year retention was found in this audit.

**Consequence:** in ~30 days the fleet loses the ability to restore any PM state older than a month, contrary to the recorded ruling — silently, because every individual routine is behaving as coded.

**Fix shape:** add a monthly-generation pin (e.g. first-of-month archive copied to a `monthly/` prefix on R2 + Drive with 12-month prune) to the pm-dashboard/supabase routines, and confirm the Project export's off-machine home + retention.

Acceptance: R2 + Drive listings show a monthly generation for the current month under the monthly prefix, and the prune logic for it is in the flake scripts with a test or a recorded dry run.

title: OpenCode session database lacks backup

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: queue/parked
labels.description: Queue task is parked (waiting on CI, time, or an event)

body:
Found by the 2026-11-14 whole-PM-stack backup/DR audit (verdict issue filed same day). Related existing research: #9094 (OpenCode DB backup economics) and #9093 (backup mesh) — this issue records that, economics aside, **no backup exists today**.

**Observed (2026-11-14, laptop amd):**
- The OpenCode server's session store is `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db` — **21 GB**, live, plus `storage/` (3.1 GB) and `opencode-local.db` (14 MB) in the same tree (93 GB total including two 20 GB same-disk `.bak` copies and 26 GB of `tmp/`).
- No backup routine covers `~/.local/share/opencode`: `laptop-state-backup` covers `~/.local/state/opencode` (a different, 2.9 MB directory); `agent-backup` snapshots only `auth.json`/`opencode.jsonc`-class credential files, to a **local-only** plaintext directory (`~/.local/share/agent-backups`, latest 2026-11-14 09:36 — same disk).
- The two `.bak-2026-11-02` / `.bak-2026-11-11` copies of the DB are on the same disk and are not a backup.

**Consequence:** every live and historical OpenCode session (the fleet's working memory — prompts, tool results, session state that the PM claimant/dispatch flow binds to) exists exactly once. Partial reconstruction aids exist (Atlas extracts, Supabase session mirror per #3142, GitHub issue/queue records) but none restores the session DB itself.

**Fix shape:** decide the economical form using #9094's findings (e.g. scheduled sqlite `.backup` + zstd/restic delta to R2+Drive, possibly excluding regenerable subtrees), then implement it with a manifest + one scratch restore (`PRAGMA integrity_check` + a session count).

Acceptance: a dated off-machine copy of the session DB exists with verified hash, and a scratch integrity check on that copy is recorded.

title: Laptop state backup stopped running
body:
Found by the 2026-11-14 whole-PM-stack backup/DR audit (verdict issue filed same day; routine designed in #1849, declared in `nixos/home/laptop-backups.nix`).

**Observed (2026-11-14, laptop amd), four independent signals agree:**
- `laptop-state-backup.timer` is enabled/active but `LastTriggerUSec` is **empty** — it has never fired. Its unit files were (re)created 2026-11-14 09:35 by that morning's switch.
- `journalctl --user -u laptop-state-backup.service` — **no entries, ever**.
- The local restic repo `~/backups/restic/laptop-state/` contains exactly one snapshot file, dated **2026-11-02 17:36**, and the success marker `~/backups/restic/.laptop-state-last-success-epoch` = 2026-11-02 17:37 CST.
- The freshness watchdog (`laptop-backups-watchdog`, #1841) only checks dashboard + repo-archive — it does not name this job, so the stall was silent for 12 days.

**What is stale:** the only backup of `~/.local/state/opencode` (small agent state), `~/secrets/*.sops.yaml` (incl. `pm-stack.sops.yaml`, changed 2026-11-03 — after the last snapshot), and `~/.ssh` is 12 days old on all three backends (local + R2 + Drive restic repos share the same run).

**Fix shape:** find why the timer never triggered since its creation, run the job once and verify restic snapshots on all three backends, and add this job to the freshness watchdog's scope so a stall is named within a day.

Acceptance: a restic snapshot dated today on local + R2 + Drive; watchdog fails loudly when this job's marker is >26h old (demonstrated or unit-tested).

title: Closure watchdog v2: full coverage, catch-up, epic-invariant precedence

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
# Closure watchdog v2: full coverage, catch-up, epic-invariant precedence

Part of the close-authority epic (automation must never close an issue). Extends #10105 (v1, live, cron every 15 min, `~/workspace/closure-watchdog/`).

## Gaps in v1 (from code review of closure_watchdog.py)
1. `dezren39/nix` missing from DEFAULT_REPOS although Kaneo syncs it (4th integration).
2. 2-hour `--max-age-hours` horizon + watermark advances past skipped events = permanent misses after any >2h outage.
3. Issue-events fetch is a single `per_page=100` page, no pagination — bursts push closes out of the window while the watermark still jumps.
4. The closing-keyword veto also vetoes rule (a): a `Closes #epic` PR currently legitimises closing an epic with open sub-issues. The epic invariant must beat the keyword: keyword legitimises rule (b) only.
5. `status:done` applied without a close is invisible (only `closed` events are scanned).
6. One bad issue aborts the whole run (`evaluate_close` exceptions propagate; `open_sub_issue_count` failures silently disable rule (a)).
7. No loop suppression / repeat counter if Kaneo re-closes after a watchdog reopen.

## Work (v2)
- Add `dezren39/nix`; paginate event + timeline fetches until the watermark; drop the age horizon for events newer than the watermark (age cap only guards a zero watermark); per-issue error isolation with explicit error results.
- Rule precedence: keyword vetoes the refs-only rule only; open-sub-issues fires regardless of keyword.
- Open-issue sweep: an OPEN issue carrying bot-applied `status:done` gets the label stripped + an evidence comment (throttled per issue); human-applied is flagged, not touched.
- Repeat-close counter per issue in state; the evidence comment names the repeat count.

## Acceptance
- Dry-run against #9106 and #9078 histories still fires both rules; dry-run against #9060 (closed, open sub-issues) fires rule (a).
- A synthetic >2h-old bot close above the watermark is caught on the next run.
- #10105's original acceptance boxes get checked off from v2 evidence.

## laptop-agent daemon source reconciliation — prerequisite for M2 (#5769)

Found by task 16852 revalidation (lane code-d, 2026-11-14): the M2 remainder ("land the laptop-agent services-layer definition in the code flake deploy registry") cannot be done honestly yet, because **the daemon source is not in the code repo, and the copies that exist have diverged into two lineages**:

- **Live lineage:** `~/tools/laptop-agent-daemon.py` (home repo, canonical) == laptop `~/laptop-agent/laptop_agent.py` — carries the 2026-11-10 timeout semantics (per-exec process groups, disconnect reap) and trip logging v1 + v2 (code#5702, 2026-11-14). This is what actually runs (systemd user unit, :4799).
- **Vendored lineage:** `dezren39/darwin-nix` `pkgs/laptop-agent/src/laptop_agent.py` (the package PR #1459 builds) — carries features the live daemon lacks: job metadata persisted next to output with the index rebuilt on startup, and startup failing closed when the token is missing/empty/whitespace. It lacks the timeout semantics and trip logging.
- Diff size at finding time: **1151 lines** between the two `laptop_agent.py` files. Neither is a superset of the other.
- The code repo itself contains no daemon source: the `dezren39-nix/` tree inside a code checkout is a nested clone, not tracked code-flake source, so `pkgs/deploy` cannot reference it (a fresh code clone would not have it).

**Work:** reconcile the two lineages into ONE daemon source (union of: persisted job index + fail-closed token startup from the vendored side; process-group timeout semantics + trip logging v2 from the live side), vendor that source into the code repo (e.g. `pkgs/laptop-agent/src/`, following the darwin-nix package shape), prove behavior parity with a real client round-trip against the live daemon's surface (exec, jobs, cancel, health), and only then does the M2 definition + cutover sequence in #5769 become executable.

title: dispatch: an annotation failure note overwrites the lane-ledger failure on the task's last_error (PR #4231 residual)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/pr-diff-review
labels.description: Filed by the pr-diff-review job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/dispatch
labels.description: Package/app: dispatch (pm-stack in this repo)

body:
## Finding

PR #4231 gave each post-claim launch annotation its own guard and made its failure notes accumulate — but only within `annotateLaunch` itself. In `launchSession`, the lane-ledger step runs immediately before the annotations and records its own failure the same way, by PATCHing the task's `last_error`. When a lane-ledger failure and an annotation failure happen in the same launch, the annotation note **overwrites** the lane-ledger note, so the task record ends up naming only the annotation failure:

1. `launchSession` (pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts, current main): the lane-ledger `assignLane` catch PATCHes `last_error: "lane assignment failed (launch unaffected): …"`. It does not add the failure to the response `warnings` either, so the task note is the only record of it.
2. `annotateLaunch` (pm-stack/dispatch/src/launch_annotations.ts:48-53): `noteFailure` PATCHes `last_error: failures.join("; ")` where `failures` starts empty for each call — it never reads or preserves the task's existing `last_error`.
3. `QueueClient.patchTask` (pm-stack/dispatch/src/queue.ts:114) is a PostgREST PATCH (field set): the second write replaces `last_error` wholesale.

Net effect: a launch whose lane assignment failed (so a later completion cannot record the executed lane) and whose issue comment or labels then failed loses the lane-failure record entirely — the exact "final note names every failure" property #4231's design (#2668 phase 2) set out to provide holds only inside the helper, not across the launch sequence.

## Evidence

- Source PR: #4231 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/4231 (merge commit `9456d01790d7a46398fdc807dd1fb22e0c6a98ab`, confirmed ancestor of main, compare status `behind`). It fixed #2660 (CLOSED) by extracting `annotateLaunch` with per-step guards and accumulating notes.
- Current main `8e118461696624f2836657dab9083412e89a6fa6`:
  - `pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts`: lane-ledger catch PATCHes `last_error` with the lane-assignment failure (line ~167) and pushes nothing to `warnings`; the `annotateLaunch` call follows immediately after (lines ~182-193).
  - `pm-stack/dispatch/src/launch_annotations.ts:48-53`: `noteFailure` builds the note from a fresh local `failures` array and PATCHes `{ last_error: failures.join("; ") }`.
  - `pm-stack/dispatch/src/queue.ts:114-119`: `patchTask` issues `PATCH /rest/v1/tasks?id=eq.<id>` with the fields as the body — a set, not an append.
- The shipped tests (pm-stack/dispatch/test/launch_annotations.test.ts) stub a fresh task for every case, so the pre-existing-`last_error` sequence is never exercised: both-fail accumulation is pinned only for the two annotations against each other.

## Runtime verification (verification_class: runtime-gap/high-risk)

Result: **reproduced**.

- Commit tested: `8e118461696624f2836657dab9083412e89a6fa6` (current main, detached worktree on the laptop, removed after the run).
- Command: `bun test test/probe-last-error.test.ts` in `pm-stack/dispatch` (one-off probe test replaying the exact `launchSession` sequence — lane-ledger `patchTask` note, then the real `annotateLaunch` with a failing comment and a field-set stub queue; saved as `probe-last-error.test.ts` in the review evidence, not committed).
- Environment: laptop (host `amd`) via the fleet laptop SSH route; the narrow probe only — no full suite, no CI changes, no application-code changes.
- Result: 1 test, FAIL as predicted by the finding. Observed behavior: returned warnings were `["launch annotation failed (launch unaffected): issue comment: github comment 500"]` and the task's final `last_error` was exactly that annotation string — the earlier `"lane assignment failed (launch unaffected): ledger down"` note was gone.

## Why it matters

`last_error` is the task's diagnostic record for best-effort launch steps that must never fail the launch. The lane-ledger note is operationally the more important of the two: without the lane assignment, a later completion cannot record which lane executed the task. Two independent best-effort failures in one launch are most likely exactly when the surrounding services are degraded — which is also when the record is needed most. Today the second failure silently erases the first, and because the lane failure is not surfaced in `warnings` either, a wait:true caller sees a launch whose only recorded problem is a GitHub annotation.

## Acceptance criteria

- When a task already carries a `last_error` note (e.g. the lane-ledger failure) and an annotation then fails, the final `last_error` names both failures (or the annotation path otherwise preserves the earlier note, e.g. by appending to the existing value).
- A regression test replays the sequence — pre-existing `last_error` on the task, then a failing annotation — and pins that both failures survive in the final note; the both-annotations-fail accumulation from #4231 keeps passing.
- No behavior change to the launch itself: annotations and the lane ledger stay best-effort, the launch is never rejected for either failure, and the wait:true `warnings` response shape is unchanged (adding the lane failure to `warnings` as well is acceptable but not required).

Found by pr-diff-review lane B reviewing PR #4231 against current main. Dedupe: issue searches (`last_error annotation lane`, `launch annotation`, `annotateLaunch`) returned only #2660 (closed — the parent issue #4231 fixed) and unrelated items; no open or closed issue covers the cross-step `last_error` overwrite.
