title: fix(id): pkgs/id library fails to compile — currency::gateway::sign_request ignores Result from directory_auth::sign_request

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Evidence

File: `pkgs/id/src/currency/gateway.rs`, function `sign_request` (around lines 432-441):

```rust
pub fn sign_request(
    key: &ed25519_dalek::SigningKey,
    request: &CurrencyRequest,
    at: u64,
    nonce: &str,
) -> Result<(Signed, Vec<u8>), GatewayError> {
    let body = request.body()?;
    let signed =
        directory_auth::sign_request(key, REQUEST_METHOD, REQUEST_TARGET, &body, at, nonce);
    Ok((signed, body))
}
```

`directory_auth::sign_request` (in `pkgs/id/crates/id-directory/src/directory_auth.rs`) returns
`Result<Signed>` (anyhow), failing on an empty / over-long / non-domain nonce. The
gateway code binds that result directly to `signed: Signed` and returns
`Ok((signed, body))`, so the whole `id` library crate fails to type-check:

```
error[E0308]: mismatched types
  --> src/currency/gateway.rs:441:9
   |
441 |     Ok((signed, body))
   |         ^^^^^^ expected `Signed`, found `Result<Signed, Error>`
```

Verified locally with `cargo check` on the current (clean) checkout: the only error is
this one, and handling the `Result` (propagating it as `GatewayError::Envelope`, since
a bad nonce is the only failure mode) makes the library compile (`Finished dev profile`).

## Why it matters

`currency` is declared unconditionally in `pkgs/id/src/lib.rs` (`pub mod currency;`),
while `directory_auth` is gated behind the `world` feature. With the default feature
set (`default = ["sandbox", "world"]`) the module is reachable, so the crate cannot
be built at all, which blocks any downstream consumer (id-cli, id-web, tests) that
compiles the `id` library. The defect went untracked because the recent id sweeps
compiled per-crate tests that do not pull in this module.

## Acceptance criteria

- `cargo check -p id` (default features) succeeds.
- `sign_request` propagates a bad-nonce failure from `directory_auth::sign_request`
  as a typed `GatewayError` instead of failing to compile; `GatewayError::Envelope`
  is the natural mapping (the same variant `verify_envelope` uses for a rejected
  envelope).
- Add a regression test exercising a non-domain nonce (empty / over-long / invalid
  character) returning `Err(GatewayError::Envelope)`.

## Suggested fix shape

```rust
let signed = directory_auth::sign_request(key, REQUEST_METHOD, REQUEST_TARGET, &body, at, nonce)
    .map_err(|_| GatewayError::Envelope)?;
```

Building the home generation from current main (`f2df19ed`, pin PR #9970) succeeds, but `./activate` aborts in its checks: these files exist on disk, are not the current generation's to replace, and would be clobbered:

**2. `pm-git-sync.service` is in `failed` state.**
The primary checkout `~/git/code` sat at `8dc31f0add` while origin/main had moved through #9967/#9969/#9970 — the sync that keeps the primary current and redeploys PM services on subtree changes is down, so merged config changes do not propagate on their own.

## Phase 2 of epic #1384 — takeover becomes attach for supervised instances

Parent design: #1384 (adopted by Drew 2026-10-27: per-instance mcpx supervisor replaces the stdio takeover handoff). Phase 1 (#1385, supervised stdio transport behind a flag) closed 2026-10-28, so the socket protocol this phase depends on now exists as built.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

PR #9340 (merged, `id: move seed_phrase, key_envelope and key-file consts to id-core (split step 7a, #4411)`) tracks `pkgs/id/web/dist/.gitkeep` so the `web/dist` folder exists in source copies (the PR's own Nix record explains: rust-embed in id-web generates no `get` when the folder is absent). Codex's P2 finding: **the release asset guard in `pkgs/id/build.rs` counts any directory entry as proof that frontend assets were built — and `.gitkeep` is now always such an entry**. On a clean checkout a release build with the `web` feature therefore passes the guard without running Bun and can ship a binary whose static assets all return 404, defeating the documented requirement that web assets be built first.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9340
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9340#discussion_r4560045474
- Reviewer: `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T05:37:38Z (P2)
- Flagged location: `pkgs/id/web/dist/.gitkeep:1`; the guard is `pkgs/id/build.rs:7-12`

> "On a clean checkout, this placeholder is the only entry in `web/dist`, but `pkgs/id/build.rs:7–10` considers any directory entry proof that frontend assets exist. Consequently, a release build with the `web` feature now passes the guard without running Bun and can ship a binary whose static assets all return 404. Update the guard alongside this placeholder to ignore `.gitkeep` or require an actual build artifact, preserving the documented requirement that web assets be built first."

## No-response evidence

- The review thread contains only the Codex comment — no replies (verified 2026-11-14 via the PR comments API and a GraphQL `reviewThreads` read: `isResolved=false`, 1 comment). The PR author's conversation comment (2026-11-13T05:54:42Z) explains why `.gitkeep` was added for the Nix/rust-embed compile, but does not address the release-guard concern and is not a thread reply.
- No commit followed the comment: PR #9340's head is `f88a8ebeaf` (2026-11-13T05:35:14Z, predates the comment); it merged at 2026-11-13T05:54:46Z (merge commit `4f29145756`). No later main commit touches `pkgs/id/build.rs`.
- Dedupe: open/closed issue searches by comment id, `dist_has_assets`, and ".gitkeep / web/dist" found no issue covering this finding (#4411, the parent split-step issue, is closed and does not track it).

## Still-live evidence (verified 2026-11-14 on current `main`)

- `pkgs/id/build.rs:7-12`: `dist_has_assets` returns `entries.next().is_some()` — the first entry of any kind, including `.gitkeep`, counts as assets; the release branch (lines 28-38) asserts on exactly this function.
- `pkgs/id/web/dist/` on `main` contains exactly one entry: `.gitkeep` ("Placeholder so the web/dist directory exists in source copies…") — so on a clean checkout the release guard passes with no built assets present.

## Acceptance criteria

- The release guard ignores `.gitkeep` (or requires an actual build artifact, e.g. `index.html`), so a release `web` build on a clean checkout fails with the existing "build them first" message until the frontend is built.
- The dev-build convenience and the Nix/rust-embed reason for tracking the placeholder are preserved.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue that this behavior is accepted, with the reasoning recorded.

PR #9341 (merged, `feat(pm-stack): decision-set event pipeline — Turso sync + Cloudflare Worker/D1/DO (#9335)`) adds the `sync-decision-events.ts` operator script. Codex's P2 finding: **a failure to read the explicitly requested `--outbox-dir` is silently converted into an empty directory**. The script then continues with the default outbox and can exit successfully with zero pending events while leaving the requested source completely unsynchronized. Propagate directory-read failures or report them and return a non-zero exit status so operators can distinguish a broken source from an empty outbox."

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

PR #9341 (merged, `feat(pm-stack): decision-set event pipeline — Turso sync + Cloudflare Worker/D1/DO (#9335)`) adds the decision-event sync leg. Codex's P2 finding: **the sync client acknowledges every pending event after a webhook batch, without checking how many the Worker actually accepted** — and the two sides validate timestamps differently, so a real event shape crosses the gap: an outbox event with `ts: "2026-11-12"` passes the aggregator's `isIsoDate` validation but is rejected by the Worker's timestamp validator, which requires a `T`. The Worker returns HTTP 200 with the event in its per-event `errors`; the client marks it acknowledged anyway, so it is never stored in D1 and never retried — silent event loss.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341#discussion_r4560023666
- Reviewer: `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T05:34:08Z (P2)
- Flagged location: `pm-stack/aggregator/src/decision-events.ts:310` at review time; the sync code now lives at `pm-stack/aggregator/src/decision-events-sync.ts` (renamed in the same PR's reconciliation with Track A)

> "The Worker returns HTTP 200 even when individual events fail validation, but this client checks only `inserted` and then `syncDecisionEvents` marks every pending event acknowledged. This occurs with the current implementations: an outbox event with `ts: \"2026-11-12\"` passes the aggregator's `isIsoDate` validation but is rejected by the Worker's timestamp validator, which requires `T`. The event is consequently never stored in D1 and never retried. Check the response's acceptance count and per-event errors before advancing acknowledgment state, and align the two validators."

## No-response evidence

- The review thread contains only the Codex comment — no replies (verified 2026-11-14 via the PR comments API and a GraphQL `reviewThreads` read: `isResolved=false`, 1 comment).
- PR #9341's only commit after the comment is `66940fb15f` (2026-11-13T05:40:26Z), a merge of `origin/main` into the branch — it does not touch the flagged logic. The PR merged at 2026-11-13T05:45:31Z (merge commit `aad1d3602a`) with the finding unaddressed; the only later main commit touching these files is a treefmt style pass (`d451641c31`).
- Dedupe: open/closed issue searches by comment id, file path, and keywords (fan-out, pagination cursor, outbox-dir, webhook acknowledgement) found no issue covering this finding; parent issue #9335 is closed and does not track it.

## Still-live evidence (verified 2026-11-14 on current `main`)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/decision-events-sync.ts:344-347` (`postDecisionEventsWebhook`): on HTTP 200 it checks only that `out.inserted` is a number — `accepted` and `errors` are never compared against the batch.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/decision-events-sync.ts:462` (`syncDecisionEvents`): `markAcked(opts.state, leg, pending)` acknowledges **all** pending events for the leg, regardless of per-event rejection.
- Validator mismatch intact: aggregator `validateDecisionEvent` (line 164) uses `isIsoDate` from `src/validate.ts`, which accepts a date-only string; the Worker's `isIsoTimestamp` in `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/src/events.ts` returns false when the value contains no `T`.

## Acceptance criteria

- The webhook leg advances acknowledgment only for events the Worker accepted (compare `accepted`/`errors`, or ack per-event), and rejected events stay pending with the rejection surfaced in the leg report.
- The aggregator and Worker timestamp validators accept the same shapes (or the mismatch is otherwise closed), with a test using a date-only `ts` event.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue that this loss mode is accepted, with the reasoning recorded.

body:
## Finding (from PR review)

PR #9341 (merged, `feat(pm-stack): decision-set event pipeline — Turso sync + Cloudflare Worker/D1/DO (#9335)`) adds the decision-events Worker. Codex's P1 finding: **pending Durable Object fan-out is lost permanently when ingest fails after the D1 batch commits**. The Worker fans out only events whose D1 `INSERT OR IGNORE` reported changes; if the Durable Object ingest then fails (non-OK response), the handler still returns HTTP 200, the sync client acknowledges the events, and on any retry the D1 inserts report zero changes — so the events are never fanned out to subscribers or the per-set coordination state.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341
- Review comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/9341#discussion_r4560023660
- Reviewer: `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-13T05:34:08Z (P1)
- Flagged location: `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/src/index.ts:170`

> "If the Durable Object ingest fails after the D1 batch commits, these events can never reach the object on retry: their next inserts report zero changes, so `insertedEvents` excludes them permanently. A non-OK ingest response is also converted into an HTTP 200 webhook response, causing the sync client to acknowledge the events despite the failed fan-out. Persist pending fan-out separately and retry it, with event-ID deduplication at the Durable Object, so transient failures do not permanently lose subscriber notifications and coordination state."

## No-response evidence

- The review thread contains only the Codex comment — no replies (verified 2026-11-14 via the PR comments API and a GraphQL `reviewThreads` read: `isResolved=false`, 1 comment).
- PR #9341's only commit after the comment is `66940fb15f` (2026-11-13T05:40:26Z), a merge of `origin/main` into the branch — it does not touch the flagged logic. The PR merged at 2026-11-13T05:45:31Z (merge commit `aad1d3602a`) with the finding unaddressed; the only later main commit touching these files is a treefmt style pass (`d451641c31`).
- Dedupe: open/closed issue searches by comment id, file path, and keywords (fan-out, pagination cursor, outbox-dir, webhook acknowledgement) found no issue covering this finding; parent issue #9335 is closed and does not track it.

## Still-live evidence (verified 2026-11-14 on current `main`)

- `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/src/index.ts:160-186`: the D1 batch runs first; `insertedEvents` is built only from rows with `meta.changes > 0` (lines 161-167); the fan-out loop (line 170) iterates only `insertedEvents`; a non-OK ingest is recorded as `{ error: ... }` in the `fanout` map (line 177) and the handler still returns `Response.json({...})` with HTTP 200 (lines 180-186). A retry therefore excludes the already-stored events from fan-out forever.
- The Durable Object `/ingest` handler (lines 91-96) increments `state.fannedOut` and overwrites last-event fields for every event it receives, with no event-ID deduplication — so a retry mechanism also needs the dedup the reviewer asked for.

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed Durable Object ingest no longer loses fan-out: pending fan-out is persisted/retried (or the webhook returns a non-200 the sync client will not acknowledge), and the Durable Object deduplicates by event ID.
- A regression test covers: D1 commit succeeds, DO ingest fails, retry delivers the events exactly once.
- Or: a documented decision on this issue that this loss mode is accepted, with the reasoning recorded.

body:
## Fleet-stall: claim path quarantines tasks the fleet itself enqueued

**Scale (fresh DB read, 2026-11-13 ~23:10Z): 279 tasks at `status=blocked` with `last_error` starting `quarantined by claim path: packet failed validation (#5444)`.**

By queue: repo-health-code-pilot 208, repo-health-opencode-pilot 34, repo-health-openchamber-pilot 12, repo-health-dezren39-pilot 6, repo-health-zettel-pilot 6, repo-health-code-pilot 6, code 4, finance 1, ops 1, repo-health-code-shadow 1. Created 2026-10-22 → 2026-11-13; new rows still landing (latest `2026-11-13T22:06:36Z`).

### Shape split

- **270 rows: `packet.max_attempts: must be an integer between 1 and 100`** — every one of these rows carries `max_attempts=1000`.
- **9 rows: `payload.schema: must be 'repo-task/v1'` / missing `payload.problem` etc.** — producer packets omitting required `repo-task/v1` fields.

### Root conflict

Two standing fleet decisions now contradict each other:

1. **#8973 (Drew order 2026-11-12):** "attempts were reset to 0 and max_attempts raised to 1000 on all 693 non-terminal tasks"; new tasks to default to 1000.
2. **The #6448 validation contract (live in the claim path):** `packet.max_attempts` and `payload.max_attempts` must be integers 1–100 —
   - `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/validate.rs:744` (`packet.max_attempts: must be an integer between 1 and 100`),
   - `validate.rs:181` (`payload.max_attempts: ... between 1 and 100`).
   - Enforced at claim by `claim_guard_reason` (`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs:2245,2252`), which stamps `quarantined by claim path: packet failed validation (#5444)` and blocks the row.

So the bulk #8973 update armed ~693 rows that detonate into `blocked` the first time any lane tries to claim them. 279 have detonated; the rest (including currently-`queued` rows) detonate on next claim. Related but distinct: #2937 (attempts=max_attempts unclaimable), #6423 (max_attempts<=0, closed), #9028 (one PostgREST producer bypass), #9029 (bounds-table reconcile).

### Named casualties

- Task 16147 (`repo-health-opencode-pilot`, lane any-b) — the **fix follow-on for the fleet-stalling #1806 route-failover trap** — is quarantined (`max_attempts=1000`). The trap's fix cannot be claimed.
- Task 15155 (`repo-health-code-pilot`, lane any-d) — the **fix for #8973 itself** — is quarantined (payload missing schema/problem). Self-referential: the order's own fix task is blocked by the conflict.
- Task 16120 (`repo-health-opencode-pilot`, lane any-d, the live #2405 main-CI fix task) — quarantined while a session is adopting its PR.
- Task 12126 (`repo-health-code-pilot`, **currently `queued`**, lane code-k, bound to #7064 id/many-worlds) carries `max_attempts=1000` — a live landmine: the next claim attempt quarantines it.

### Recommended direction (triage decides; do not contradict the standing order)

Either (a) raise the validator bound to admit the ordered 1000 default (reconcile with #9029's bounds table, keep enqueue/claim oracle agreement), or (b) get Drew's revised word and clamp producers back under 100. Whichever wins, also: repair the 279 quarantined rows (re-validate and release, not mass-delete), fix producer packets that omit `repo-task/v1` schema/kind/problem (the 9-row shape), and add a creation-time or enqueue-time rejection so a bad packet can never be born `queued` again.

### Acceptance

- `validate_packet` and every producer default agree on `max_attempts` range; the agreed bound is written in one place with a test.
- All 279 currently-quarantined rows re-validated: conforming rows released back to `queued` (attempts preserved), and any row that cannot conform is re-scoped or failed with reason, never silently left `blocked`.
- A conforming enqueue through each producer path claims clean on first attempt (prove with a live claim, not a unit test alone).
- Task 12126 (or its successor) claims without quarantine.

title: pm-stack(aggregator): install.sh aborts copying quota-gatherer.service over the home-manager /nix/store symlink

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: status/parked
labels.description: Deliberately paused with a recorded resume condition

labels.name: queue/parked
labels.description: Queue task is parked (waiting on CI, time, or an event)

body:
Found during the #5082 deploy (2026-11-13): `pm-stack/aggregator/install.sh` aborts partway on this host when it tries to install `quota-gatherer.service`:

```
cp: cannot create regular file '/home/user/.config/systemd/user/quota-gatherer.service': Read-only file system
```

`~/.config/systemd/user/quota-gatherer.service` is a home-manager symlink into `/nix/store/...` (the unit is NixOS/home-manager managed — its own description says "NixOS; runs from ~/git/code checkout, #1151"), so a plain `cp` over it can never succeed here. The aggregator's own steps (env render, pm-aggregator unit, restart, /api/health version gate) complete BEFORE this step, so the deploy itself worked — but install.sh exits non-zero, which makes every aggregator deploy look failed and trains operators to ignore its exit code.

The quota-gatherer itself is unaffected: it is a timer-driven oneshot (~15 min cadence) and its ticks run fine (12:30Z and 12:35Z ticks on 2026-11-13, 16/16 providers ok).

Suggested fix: install.sh should skip (or use `cp --remove-destination` only for files it owns) units that are symlinks into /nix/store, i.e. detect home-manager-managed units and leave them to the NixOS switch — the same split the pm-aggregator unit already lives with.

title: test(id): proptest regression seeds are orphaned — the crate split moved the tests, not the seeds

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: effort/s

body:
## Evidence

On current `main` (`ef16105eebb6d865960cde9f6bc1094b355000ee`):

- `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt:7` holds the saved counterexample
  `cc fce84d0aae919263e375639bc286c07c2c3b98fae4f575aefda2312697c3b8d8 # shrinks to sizes = [38802, 39929, 60569, 51657, 62725, 5764]`
  for the paging property `pages_fit_the_budget_and_neither_lose_nor_repeat_an_artifact`
  (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/artifact.rs:2217-2225`).
- `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/friendship.txt:7` holds
  `cc 8f1c16e287e31eaee32015dce22c133194284dda35ff888ce7e180a0592df0bc # shrinks to script = [...], cap = 1`
  saved for `the_cap_is_never_exceeded(script, cap)` when the test lived in
  `pkgs/id/src/friendship.rs` (added by `b3315bfab5`). The equivalent property
  today is `prop_no_group_is_ever_over_its_cap_and_a_friendship_is_active_only_when_both_are_present`
  (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/groups/tests.rs:2029`), which no longer takes a `cap` parameter.

proptest 1.12's default `FileFailurePersistence::SourceParallel("proptest-regressions")`
resolves the seed path by walking up from the test's source file to the directory that
contains `lib.rs`/`main.rs`, then reading `proptest-regressions/<path relative to that dir>.txt`
beside that directory's parent. Both tests now live in sub-crates whose `src/lib.rs` exists
(`crates/id-sync/src/lib.rs`, `crates/id-events/src/lib.rs`), so proptest looks for:

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt`
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/proptest-regressions/groups/tests.txt`

Neither exists on `main` (`gh api repos/developing-today/code/contents/pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt?ref=main` → HTTP 404), so both root seed files are never read.

**History.** `proptest-regressions/artifact.txt` was added by `dd64470859` ("pull pages capped by
bytes") while the test was `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs` — the correct location then. The crate split
moved the file to `crates/id-sync/src/artifact.rs` in `da4f4a0bd6` ("pkgs/id crate split step 3c
… #4406") without moving the seed. The friendship tests moved to id-events in `f89b565629`
(step 2b-1, #4405); `friendship.txt` stayed behind. `da4f4a0bd6`'s stat lists only
`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/*` additions and the shrunken `pkgs/id/src/artifact.rs` — no
`proptest-regressions/` move.

**Reproduced on the built test binaries** (`target/debug/deps/id_sync-*`, `id_events-*`; the
unparsable-line warning is proptest's own, emitted only for a file it actually reads):

- Appending `THIS_IS_NOT_A_SEED_LINE` to `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt`, then running
  `artifact::tests::pages_fit_the_budget_and_neither_lose_nor_repeat_an_artifact` → **no warning**; the file is not read.
- Creating `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt` with a junk line → proptest prints
  `proptest: /home/user/git/code/pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt:2: unparsable line, ignoring`.
- Same pair for `friendship.txt` vs `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/proptest-regressions/groups/tests.txt`
  (`groups::tests::prop_no_group_is_ever_over_its_cap_and_a_friendship_is_active_only_when_both_are_present`).

## Why it matters

The `artifact` seed is the exact counterexample from the byte-budget paging fix ("pull pages capped
by bytes", `dd64470859`). Because it is no longer replayed, a regression of that paging bug passes
CI while the repo still looks like it carries the saved case. Any future failure in these tests writes
its new seed to `crates/<crate>/proptest-regressions/…` (proptest creates the directory), silently
diverging from the root `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/` that reviewers read as canonical. This is dead
regression coverage: exactly the class of guard the paging fix was meant to keep alive.

## Acceptance criteria

- Move the seeds to the paths proptest resolves for their tests:
  - `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt` → `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/proptest-regressions/artifact.txt`
  - `pkgs/id/proptest-regressions/friendship.txt` → `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/proptest-regressions/groups/tests.txt`,
    or delete it and say why (its original property no longer exists).
- Demonstrate the artifact seed is actually loaded: with it in place, a run that induces the byte-budget
  overflow must fail the property (or assert directly that the seed line is read).
- Add a guard so a seed cannot silently land where proptest never reads it — e.g. a check that every
  checked-in `proptest-regressions/**/*.txt` sits at the path proptest resolves for the test it names,
  or set `failure_persistence: FileFailurePersistence::Direct(...)` explicitly in the affected tests.

Affected repo(s): `developing-today/code` only.

title: fleet-stalling: main-broken watcher files duplicate issues per failing run and spawns duplicate fix sessions

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: epic/main-broken
labels.description: Epic: main-broken - all issues of this effort carry it

body:
## Defect
One failing main CI run is filed more than once, and each filing starts its own fix session. Sessions then find that another watcher already owns the breakage and stop, so the work is wasted and the queue carries duplicates.

## Evidence (fleet census, 2026-11-13 05:55–06:02)
- Run 43392267205 (fleet-rust-tests): #9523 (closed), #9528 (open), #9531 (closed) are three filings for one run.
- Fix sessions started for near-identical breakage in the same window (main-CI fix triggers): ses_e5e2b3e515effe (#9525 dependabot-wrangler), ses_e5e2b3e6f6affe (#9526 production-line-guard), ses_e5e2b3e5b04ffe (#9529 pm-stack), ses_e5e2b3e4713ffe (#2394/#2393 opencode test), ses_e5e2b3e6601ffe (#9528 fleet-rust-tests). Each was told by the conductor: "another watcher already filed and is working this same breakage" and stopped, after creating a local worktree and in some cases an empty pushed branch (origin/fix/9525-dependabot-wrangler, origin/fix/9523-fleet-rust-tests).
- Search for an existing issue on this (duplicate watcher / per-run dedupe) found none.

## Acceptance test
For one failing main run id, exactly one open main-broken issue exists (the watcher searches open and closed issues for the run id before filing and comments instead of filing), and exactly one fix session is dispatched per open issue. A test replays two watcher firings for the same run id and asserts one issue and one dispatch.

Filed by the builder's advocate, 2026-11-13. Ledger: advocate-ledger.md.

- **Owned files:** existing `pm-stack/aggregator/src/actions.ts`, `src/server.ts`, new `pm-stack/aggregator/src/work-action-contract.ts` and `test/work-action-contract.test.ts`; common Fleet `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/work/contracts.rs` and `operations.rs` seam under #8581 ownership. Do not add an independent router or `fleet-gh` crate.
- **Failing test / oracle:** `work_action_stale_version_conflicts_without_effect` in `pm-stack/aggregator/test/work-action-contract.test.ts`; stale work version or actor-role revocation between preview/apply must fail before any consumer effect, while same operation key returns the original receipt.
- **Done/oracle:** model-based state-transition test: draft→previewed→accepted→running→pending_sync/partial/conflict/uncertain/rejected→verified_complete; expected-work-version oracle compares against authoritative fixture; fake downstream consumes only validated operations and count asserts one effect per idempotency key. Existing action store remains a request ledger, not authority for the applied fact. Command: `cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test test/actions.test.ts test/work-action-contract.test.ts`.
- **Edges:** hard MOB-01 and authority contract from #9180/#9200; #8581 Fleet verb contract and `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet/src/gh.rs` (existing binary module; no `fleet-gh` crate) are soft caller seams. #8575/#8579 authority audit must be reconciled before assigning persistent fields. `fleet-queue/src/work/contracts.rs`, `operations.rs`, `authority.rs` and adjacent modules in `architecture.md` are proposed internal modules, not V1. Any `fleet/src/main.rs`, `fleet-registry` or shared route registration is one later integration slice after domain contracts settle, not parallel edits by each MOB slice.

Parent integration adds native parent/blocker edges in a later pass after the command map, requirements IDs, and acyclic graph are verified.

## Starting failing test, oracle, and done check

- **First failing test:** `test_experiment_replays_same_fixture_and_rejects_bad_contract`
- **Oracle:** The source slice’s stated reference model, golden fixture, or invariant; compare expected and observed state explicitly. No mock-only claim of deployed/live behavior.
- **Done command:** `seeded inputs, generator versions, oracle and output schema are pinned; repeated run produces byte-stable machine result. Property/model tests cover negative cases; no production code is used as its own oracle. Run only named offline test command in the filed issue, with exact test listing check. -`
- Tests must first be listed by exact name in the owning target (`-- --list`); assert the test exists before execution. A zero-test filter passing is not acceptance.

## Acceptance and negative cases

seeded inputs, generator versions, oracle and output schema are pinned; repeated run produces byte-stable machine result. Property/model tests cover negative cases; no production code is used as its own oracle. Run only named offline test command in the filed issue, with exact test listing check. -

Negative coverage: invalid Unicode/duplicate JSON key/lossy ID/unknown major schema, incomplete graph/page and unverified remote effect fail closed. Disable runner by removing CI invocation; no DB/production side effect exists. -

## Compatibility, migration, and runtime gates

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.
- QTI remains unlocated/unverified; #9241 is the existing provenance-recovery issue. #3424/#8575/#8579/#8602 are candidates/constraints, not presumed equivalents. Any overlapping persisted field/schema change waits for the QTI crosswalk and named current owner.
- Runtime gates: implementation starts only after the document PR is merged, the exact curated requirement IDs are integrated, and this issue's granular prerequisite edges are resolved. Schema/migration, production rollout, telemetry, authenticated remote writes, deployed behavior, and live acceptance each require their own explicit evidence and approval. Normal triage does not inherit urgency 450/Do Now.
- Projection rows being rebuildable/disposable does not authorize deleting the PM PostgREST database or unrelated tables. Preserve unique human-authored `pmp_links`/link writes and all unrelated tables; follow the existing backup/restore requirements before any future migration or cleanup.
- Compatibility: Additive and reversible only after existing owner/schema review; retain prior data and behavior; no silent fallback or dual authority.
- Rollback: Disable only the new capability; preserve pending intents, artifacts, existing state, and remote effects. No broad reset, destructive cleanup, or deletion of history.

### CEN-05 — Offline reference model and experiment runner

- **Tier:** crucial, implementation-independent. **Goal:** run deterministic test-only/reference conformance and priority/exploration/lifecycle models using immutable synthetic fixtures; no production reads/writes.
- **Owns:** new proposed `validation/experiment.py`, `validation/fixtures/` and `validation/test_experiment.py`; this runner emits machine-readable result artifacts only. Exact run arguments and fixture schema become part of its strict CLI contract.

Property/model tests cover negative cases; no production code is used as its own oracle. Run only named offline test command in the filed issue, with exact test listing check.
- **Negative / rollback:** invalid Unicode/duplicate JSON key/lossy ID/unknown major schema, incomplete graph/page and unverified remote effect fail closed. Disable runner by removing CI invocation; no DB/production side effect exists.
- **Operator-script contract:** parser declares the full invocation and validates all flags/values before reading fixtures or writing result artifacts; unknown arguments are usage errors; no subprocess/network/production target is part of this experiment runner.

- Preserve the current queue/status/identity/Project-writer/Fleet `gh` compatibility surfaces. Do not silently change existing spellings or normalize ratified `expedite=15` / `next-up=25`; those remain distinct from `do_now`.

body:
You are "Bolt" ⚡ - a performance-obsessed agent who makes the codebase faster, one optimization at a time.

Your mission is to identify and implement ONE small performance improvement that makes the application measurably faster or more efficient.


## Boundaries

✅ **Always do:**
- Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` (or associated equivalents) before creating PR
- Add comments explaining the optimization
- Measure and document expected performance impact

⚠️ **Ask first:**
- Adding any new dependencies
- Making architectural changes

🚫 **Never do:**
- Modify package.json or tsconfig.json without instruction
- Make breaking changes
- Optimize prematurely without actual bottleneck
- Sacrifice code readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S PHILOSOPHY:
- Speed is a feature
- Every millisecond counts
- Measure first, optimize second
- Don't sacrifice readability for micro-optimizations

BOLT'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY:
Before starting, read .jules/bolt.md (create if missing).

Your journal is NOT a log - only add entries for CRITICAL learnings that will help you avoid mistakes or make better decisions.

⚠️ ONLY add journal entries when you discover:
- A performance bottleneck specific to this codebase's architecture
- An optimization that surprisingly DIDN'T work (and why)
- A rejected change with a valuable lesson
- A codebase-specific performance pattern or anti-pattern
- A surprising edge case in how this app handles performance

❌ DO NOT journal routine work like:
- "Optimized component X today" (unless there's a learning)
- Generic React performance tips
- Successful optimizations without surprises

Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title]
**Learning:** [Insight]
**Action:** [How to apply next time]`

BOLT'S DAILY PROCESS:

1. 🔍 PROFILE - Hunt for performance opportunities:

  FRONTEND PERFORMANCE:
  - Unnecessary re-renders in React/Vue/Angular components
  - Missing memoization for expensive computations
  - Large bundle sizes (opportunities for code splitting)
  - Unoptimized images (missing lazy loading, wrong formats)
  - Missing virtualization for long lists
  - Synchronous operations blocking the main thread
  - Missing debouncing/throttling on frequent events
  - Unused CSS or JavaScript being loaded
  - Missing resource preloading for critical assets
  - Inefficient DOM manipulations

  BACKEND PERFORMANCE:
  - N+1 query problems in database calls
  - Missing database indexes on frequently queried fields
  - Expensive operations without caching
  - Synchronous operations that could be async
  - Missing pagination on large data sets
  - Inefficient algorithms (O(n²) that could be O(n))
  - Missing connection pooling
  - Repeated API calls that could be batched
  - Large payloads that could be compressed

  GENERAL OPTIMIZATIONS:
  - Missing caching for expensive operations
  - Redundant calculations in loops
  - Inefficient data structures for the use case
  - Missing early returns in conditional logic
  - Unnecessary deep cloning or copying
  - Missing lazy initialization
  - Inefficient string concatenation in loops
  - Missing request/response compression

2. ⚡ SELECT - Choose your daily boost:
  Pick the BEST opportunity that:
  - Has measurable performance impact (faster load, less memory, fewer requests)
  - Can be implemented cleanly in < 50 lines
  - Doesn't sacrifice code readability significantly
  - Has low risk of introducing bugs
  - Follows existing patterns

3. 🔧 OPTIMIZE - Implement with precision:
  - Write clean, understandable optimized code
  - Add comments explaining the optimization
  - Preserve existing functionality exactly
  - Consider edge cases
  - Ensure the optimization is safe
  - Add performance metrics in comments if possible

4. ✅ VERIFY - Measure the impact:
  - Run format and lint checks
  - Run the full test suite
  - Verify the optimization works as expected
  - Add benchmark comments if possible
  - Ensure no functionality is broken

5. 🎁 PRESENT - Share your speed boost:
  Create a PR with:
  - Title: "⚡ Bolt: [performance improvement]"
  - Description with:
    * 💡 What: The optimization implemented
    * 🎯 Why: The performance problem it solves
    * 📊 Impact: Expected performance improvement (e.g., "Reduces re-renders by ~50%")
    * 🔬 Measurement: How to verify the improvement
  - Reference any related performance issues

BOLT'S FAVORITE OPTIMIZATIONS:
⚡ Add React.memo() to prevent unnecessary re-renders
⚡ Add database index on frequently queried field
⚡ Cache expensive API call results
⚡ Add lazy loading to images below the fold
⚡ Debounce search input to reduce API calls
⚡ Replace O(n²) nested loop with O(n) hash map lookup
⚡ Add pagination to large data fetch
⚡ Memoize expensive calculation with useMemo/computed
⚡ Add early return to skip unnecessary processing
⚡ Batch multiple API calls into single request
⚡ Add virtualization to long list rendering
⚡ Move expensive operation outside of render loop
⚡ Add code splitting for large route components
⚡ Replace large library with smaller alternative

BOLT AVOIDS (not worth the complexity):
❌ Micro-optimizations with no measurable impact
❌ Premature optimization of cold paths
❌ Optimizations that make code unreadable
❌ Large architectural changes
❌ Optimizations that require extensive testing
❌ Changes to critical algorithms without thorough testing

Remember: You're Bolt, making things lightning fast. But speed without correctness is useless. Measure, optimize, verify. If you can't find a clear performance win today, wait for tomorrow's opportunity.

If no suitable performance optimization can be identified, stop and do not create a PR.---

title: Blocked-until: condition-gated blocked items (registry + daily checker) — stop re-validating unchanged blockers
body:
**What:** Blocked fleet items are no longer re-validated from scratch by every watcher. An item is registered ONCE with a test and custom on-fire instructions; the daily blocked-until-checker is the only thing that touches it until its condition fires.

**Why (Drew, 2026-11-13):** the queue-hygiene sweep (4h) and the dropped-thread catcher (hourly) were re-checking the same unchanged gates dozens of times — e.g. two #7297 tasks released then re-held three times, PR/issue dependency gates re-verified every sweep run with identical results. Drew ordered: leave an item blocked without any checks until a condition occurs; custom instructions per item; re-check all items on a routine daily interval; store all tests and results; conditions may be custom functions with access to tools and state.

**Built 2026-11-13 (live):**
- Registry: `~/workspace/goals/keep-the-four-repos-healthy/hidden_files/blocked-until/registry.json` — items carry queue task ids, linked issue, a test spec, and on-fire instructions. Test kinds: pr-merged, pr-closed, issue-closed, date-after, ledger-answered, quota-below, custom.
- Custom functions: files under `blocked-until/functions/`, executed with the entry JSON + the item's full stored test history on stdin; they may use any fleet tool (gh via laptop, Turso queue, secrets by name) and blocked-until state; they print `{"fired": bool, "evidence": "..."}`. Instructions-text customs are executed by the checker agent itself under the same contract.
- Results: `blocked-until/results.jsonl` — append-only, one line per test run (fired or not) and per registration. Nothing is deleted.
- Checker: cron `blocked-until-checker`, daily — tests all waiting items, acts on fired ones per their instructions (default: release tasks + sync issue labels + evidence comment), and runs a registration sweep over remaining blocked/parked tasks whose blocker names a checkable gate.
- Registry gate added to BOTH churn sources: `queue-hygiene-sweep` and `dropped-thread-catcher` now skip registered tasks/items entirely (no release, no validation, no re-listing).
- Seeded with 10 items: PR gates (opencode#233, code#8998), issue gates (code#1063, #3801, #3804), the dead dependency PR code#3917 (closed unmerged — report-only), the code#1342 quota gate (reset Sun Nov 15 18:00 CT + fresh read <100%), the two ping-pong guards (#7297 fallback pair, code#171 park), and a notify-only expedite watch on PR #7179.

**Acceptance:** a registered item shows zero validation/release activity from the sweep and catcher across a full day while its condition is unmet; when a seeded PR merges or issue closes, the checker releases the task within one daily run and the firing test + evidence are in results.jsonl.

**Never:** darwin-nix items are never registered (Drew hold); the expedite set is never changed by this system (watch entries are notify-only); packet defects are not registered (they need work, not waiting).

body:
# serve_tests world-module web/iroh presentation test fails: forged join is not refused with "join denied"

Found during the pkgs/id crate split (step 6c, #4409) — NOT a split regression.

## What

`cargo test -p id --features web,ssh --test cli_integration serve_tests::test_world_module_shared_over_iroh_and_web_presentations` fails at `tests/cli_integration.rs:2800`:

```
assertion failed: String::from_utf8_lossy(&forged.stdout).contains("join denied")
```

The test serves a world module over both iroh and web presentations, joins legitimately, then attempts a forged join, which the world session layer should refuse by sending the frame error `join denied` (`crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/mod.rs`, `send_error(..., "join denied")`). The forged client's stdout does not contain it.

## Why it went unnoticed

This test only runs in the `web,ssh` feature configuration ("suite B"), which did not compile on main from step 5 of the crate split (#4408) until step 6c (#4409) repaired the web seam visibility. The Nix package checks skip `serve_tests` entirely (`checkFlags = ["--skip", "serve_tests"]` in pkgs/id/flake.nix, because they need networking the sandbox lacks). So no lane has executed this test in that window.

## Proof it predates the 6c extraction

A/B: pristine main at `0e68fb4a` (the step-6b merge) plus ONLY the mechanical visibility widenings needed to make suite B compile, with the web layer in its original `src/web` layout, fails the same test in the same way (4.1s, same assertion). The 6c diff does not touch the join/session logic; its id-worlds changes are visibility keywords and the `test-utils` feature gate.

## Observed environment notes

- Server stderr during the test shows one warning: `serve: app discovery failed error=apps: No such file or directory (os error 2)` — possibly related (the test environment has no apps directory), possibly benign.
- The id-worlds unit tests asserting the same `join denied` refusal (`crates/id-worlds/src/world_session/tests.rs`) pass.

## Acceptance

- The test passes under `cargo test -p id --features web,ssh`, or is shown to be environment-bound and is gated with the same explicitness the Nix checks use, with the reason recorded here.

body:
## Finding (from PR review, never addressed)

**Section-risk pool membership drops the leaf model, so split Antigravity pools are joined by door only — a healthy `_antigravity.claude-gpt` pool suppresses the `speed` section failure/risk notification even when every pool actually serving `speed` is walled or pending wall.**

Codex (P2) on PR #8889, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts` (line 848 at review):

> "Preserve the leaf model when joining split quota pools. For the configured `speed` section, the only Antigravity leaf is `gemini-flash-plan` → `_antigravity/gemini-3.8-flash` (`.opencode/opencode.jsonc:2463,3337-3341`), but dropping the model here causes `poolServesDoor` to include both Antigravity pools. The gatherer's `antigravityPoolForModel` explicitly attributes Gemini models only to `_antigravity.gemini`. Consequently, a healthy `_antigravity.claude-gpt` pool suppresses the failure/risk notification even when every pool actually serving `speed` is walled or pending wall. Preserve the model identity and apply the gatherer's split-pool attribution when deriving membership."

## Evidence

- Source PR: #8889 "feat(pm-stack): section-risk notification class (#8882)" — https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8889
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8889#discussion_r4548028848 — reviewer `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`, 2026-11-12T08:26:54Z, file `pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts:848`
- Codex review summary on the PR records `has_unresolved_findings: true` for the reviewed commit `16c71c15f5`.

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is **unresolved** (GraphQL `reviewThreads` re-read 2026-11-13) and the Codex comment is the thread's only comment — no reply from the author or any maintainer.
- PR #8889 contains a single commit, the reviewed commit `16c71c15f533ff4990c2baada8e39e697071108b`, and was merged at 2026-11-12T08:27:00Z — seconds after the review — with no fix commit.
- No existing issue covers this finding (searched open and closed issues for `poolServesDoor`, `antigravityPoolForModel`, and the PR number on 2026-11-13; only the parent feature issue #8882, closed, matches the topic).

## Still live on current main (verified 2026-11-13 by the pr-comment-review job)

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/aa.ts` — `sectionPoolIdsFromConfig` still derives doors as `leaf.split("/")[0]`, discarding the model (line ~847), and `poolServesDoor` (line ~816) still treats any pool under the door with a dot suffix as serving it, so both `_antigravity.gemini` and `_antigravity.claude-gpt` count for the `_antigravity` door. The only commit touching `aa.ts` since the merge is a treefmt auto-format pass.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-gather-map.ts:234-238` — `antigravityPoolForModel` still attributes Gemini models only to the Gemini pool (`model.startsWith("gemini") ? ANTIGRAVITY_GEMINI_SERVICE_ID : ANTIGRAVITY_CLAUDE_GPT_SERVICE_ID`), confirming the attribution mismatch.
- `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` — the `speed` section still reaches exactly one Antigravity leaf, via `opencode-route/gemini-hydrogen-plan#high` → `_antigravity/gemini-4-hydrogen` (the Flash seat was renamed to Hydrogen on 2026-11-12; the door/model pattern the finding is about is unchanged).

## Acceptance criteria

- Section pool membership preserves leaf model identity and applies the gatherer's split-pool attribution (e.g. a Gemini leaf maps only to `_antigravity.gemini`), so a healthy unrelated split pool cannot suppress a section-risk notification; regression tests cover the split-pool case.
- Or: resolve by a documented decision on this issue explaining why door-level membership is acceptable.

title: fleet-paperwork: two GitHub page loops have no page bound (#6622 contract rule 2)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Gap found by the #6623 closing pagination inventory (Phase 4 of #6622)

The pagination contract (#6622, rule 2) requires every page loop to carry a page-count or accumulated-result bound whose breach is an error naming the listing. Two GitHub page loops in `infra/fleet-paperwork/fleet_paperwork.py` follow pages with `while True` and no page bound:

- `AppClient.installations()` (fleet_paperwork.py:262-283): pages `/app/installations?per_page=100&page=N`, stopping only at a short/empty page.
- `AppClient.assert_repo_in_scope()` (fleet_paperwork.py:312-339): pages `/installation/repositories?per_page=100&page=N`, stopping when the accumulated count reaches the response's `total_count` or a page is empty.

Both terminate against GitHub's real API (finite listings; a page past the end is empty/short, and the second is also bounded by the server's own `total_count`), so this is a contract-conformance gap, not a live hang: a fresh-full-page stream (buggy or hostile endpoint, or a proxy fault) loops unbounded, accumulating results, instead of ending in a diagnosable error naming the listing — the exact shape #6602/#6572 bounded in cold-store-reaper and github-backup.

The third page loop in the same file, the issue-search scan (fleet_paperwork.py:403), is already capped (`for page in range(1, 11)`, the Search API's 1000-result ceiling) and conforms.

## Fix shape

Add a generous named page bound to both loops (sized off the legitimate maximum: installations and per-installation repositories for the orgs the App serves), whose breach dies with an error naming the listing — mirroring `MAX_QUEUE_PAGES` in github-backup's drain_queue.py and `MAX_PAGES` in fleet-dispatch-test's `fetch_all_pages`. Add a test with a fake transport that always returns full pages, asserting the bound fires (the probe matrix on #6622 includes the fresh-token stream past the bound).

Filed by the #6623 closing inventory per its acceptance rule: a gap is filed as its own issue, never fixed silently inside the inventory.

body:
## Problem

PR #8513 (for #7950) taught `.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` to verify push branch filters for the main tier, covering #7950's enumerated cases (branches list must include main, branches-ignore containing main, tags-only push, bare push). Review rounds on that PR (Codex rounds 15-17, CodeRabbit) identified further YAML constructs the checker's hand-rolled filter parser does not handle. They are dispositioned out of PR #8513 by reply and tracked here as parser hardening.

## Findings to harden

1. Quoted-scalar tokenisation: `branches: ['release main']` — the quoted scalar is preserved by the tokenizer but re-split on whitespace downstream in `add_tokens()`, so a single pattern is treated as two (Codex, PR #8513 comment 4541379042).
2. Anchored mapping alias as a whole trigger: `push: *gate` where `&gate` holds only `paths:` — distinguish a resolved paths-only anchor from an unknown alias (CodeRabbit, PR #8513 comment 4541386299).
3. Sequence aliases as filter values: `branches: &m [...]` reused via `branches-ignore: *m` must resolve before pattern matching (CodeRabbit, PR #8513 comment 4541386315).
4. Inline alias values: `push: {branches-ignore: *excluded}` — the trailing `}` is glued to the alias name and defeats the exact alias matcher (Codex, PR #8513 comment 4556891702).
5. Multiline flow-mapping anchors declared on a non-push event are stored truncated (continuation collection only runs inside the push branch) (Codex, PR #8513 comment 4556891713).
6. Quote characters inside plain scalars: `branches: [ma'in]` — an embedded apostrophe in an unquoted plain scalar wrongly starts quoted mode and rewrites the pattern to `main` (Codex, PR #8513 comment 4556891717).
7. Block-scalar filter entries: a `branches-ignore:` item written as `- |-` with indented `main` must be decoded before matching (Codex, PR #8513 comment 4556891725).

## Why this is separate from #7950

Verified 2026-11-12 (task 14311): no workflow in this repo uses anchors, aliases, block scalars, or space-containing quoted patterns in a push trigger filter — every push branch filter in `.github/workflows/` is a plain `branches: [main]`, block scalars appear only in `run:`/`prompt:` step bodies, and the checker returns OK on the real tree with the recorded waiver set unchanged. None of the seven constructs can change a verdict the checker produces today; they are robustness gaps against future workflow shapes, not live mis-certifications like #7950.

## Acceptance

- Each construct above parses to the verdict real YAML semantics give, with contract tests in `check-ci-policy-agreement.test.sh` (the generated representation/pattern oracle extended to cover them).
- Existing contract suite and real-tree OK verdict unchanged; waiver set unchanged.

# pm-stack/dispatch is a direct PostgREST producer that bypasses the packet validator and the queue broker (Phase 4 disposition (b) of #6449)

## Finding

Design #6448 decision 2 left the SQL layer unchanged because every evidenced path into the queue passed through the validator or the broker. The Phase 4 inventory searched the repo and the claimant for direct producers and found one:

- `pm-stack/dispatch/src/queue.ts` — `QueueClient.rpc()` POSTs directly to `${baseUrl}/rest/v1/rpc/${name}` with the service-role key. `enqueue()` calls `enqueue_repo_task` / `enqueue_repo_task_fleet` forwarding `p_title`, `p_body`, `p_payload`, `p_dedupe_key`, `p_priority`, and `p_max_attempts` taken from `packet.payload.max_attempts` — with NO `validate_packet` pass: an unvalidated `max_attempts`, `priority`, `not_before`-class value, or mistyped payload field reaches the RPC exactly as the pre-#6448 gap allowed.
- The same client also PATCHes task rows directly (`patchTask`, `rest/v1/tasks?id=eq.<id>`) to "assign immediately" — a claim-equivalent write that bypasses `claim_repo_task`'s eligibility predicate entirely.
- It is wired live in code: `pm-stack/dispatch/src/server.ts` constructs `QueueClient` whenever a Supabase service-role key is configured (`server.ts:51`) and enqueues through it (`server.ts:241`, `server.ts:503`); `launch_annotations.ts:53` uses `patchTask`.

The opencode claimant (`pm-stack/opencode-claimant`) was searched too: it has no Supabase/PostgREST/direct-RPC path — it reads and writes through the broker. No other direct producer was found in the repo (searches for the RPC names, `rest/v1/rpc`, `rest/v1/tasks` outside `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue`).

## What this reopens

Per #6449 disposition (b): only a found direct producer reopens the SQL-guard question, and it is filed, not fixed in Phase 4. The open questions for this follow-up:

1. Is pm-dispatch still deployed with a service-role key against a live queue store? The live queue backend is now Turso (the broker's PostgREST path is the legacy backend); if the dispatch server still runs against the old Supabase project, determine whether that store is live, read, or a zombie.
2. If it is live: route its enqueue through the broker (or run `validate_packet` semantics before the RPC) and replace the claim-PATCH with a broker claim path; if the SQL layer becomes the only guard for a live path, the migration-guard question from #6448 decision 2 is back on the table with this evidence.
3. If it is retired: remove or quarantine the client so the next audit does not have to re-derive its liveness.

## Evidence

Audit at code origin/main d7ad9d05ef, recorded in full on #6449 by task 15303. File:line — `queue.ts` `rpc()` (~:72), `enqueue()` (~:92), `patchTask()` (~:115); `server.ts:51,241,503`.

title: list --not-before: garbage filter value silently narrows the listing on the Turso backend (Phase 4 disposition (a) of #6449)
body:
agent-note:v1 — filed by queue task 15303 (lane any-c) as a required follow-up of the Phase 4 closing inventory on #6449 (design #6448). Not folded into that phase's diff, per its acceptance criteria.

# list --not-before: a garbage filter value silently narrows the listing on the Turso backend (Phase 4 disposition (a) of #6449)

## Finding

The `list` command's `--not-before` filter flag is validated at NO layer:

- Client: `cmd_list` forwards it raw — `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs`, the `/list` body built in `cmd_list` carries `"not_before": args.get("not-before")` with no `validate_not_before_flag` call. (The park verb's `--not-before` IS validated, via `validate_not_before_flag` in `cmd_park` — the list verb was missed.)
- Broker: `validate_request_not_before` in `queue_broker.rs` gates only `/park` and `/revive`; `/list` is not covered on either backend.
- PostgREST backend (`queue_broker.rs` `/list`): the value is interpolated into `not_before.lte.<value>` — a garbage value fails loudly as a timestamptz comparison error there.
- Turso backend (`turso_queue.rs` `verb_list`): the comparison is TEXT — `not_before <= ?` over stored RFC 3339 strings. A garbage value that sorts before every timestamp (e.g. `0`, `!`) makes the predicate false for every row that carries a `not_before`, so those rows silently vanish from the listing with exit 0; a value that sorts after (e.g. `banana`) silently disables the filter. No error either way.

That is the #6419 shape — a filter value producing a misleading listing with a success exit — in milder form: rows with a NULL `not_before` still list, so the listing is silently narrowed, never provably empty for a whole queue.

## Fix direction (not prescribed in detail)

Apply the existing #6426 rule to the filter: `validate_not_before_flag` in `cmd_list` (client, exit 2 naming the flag) and add `/list` to the broker's `validate_request_not_before` gate, so non-CLI callers get the same rejection. Add tests mirroring the park `--not-before` tests for both backends.

## Evidence

Audit at code origin/main d7ad9d05ef, recorded in full on #6449 by task 15303.

title: fleet fallback: fetch_markers silently truncates at its 10-page cap (#6622 Phase 4 gap)
body:
## Gap — found by the #6622 Phase 4 closing pagination inventory (#6623)

`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/fallback.rs` `fetch_markers` pages issue comments at `per_page=100` for `page in 1..=10` and breaks on a short page. The volume bound exists (10 pages / 1000 comments — contract rule 2 satisfied), but when the loop ends by hitting the cap rather than a short page, it returns the accumulated markers **as if complete**: no error, no marker of truncation.

That matters because the markers are the fallback queue's claim/lease state (the function's own doc: "The marker's own embedded `ts` is authoritative"). Comments are returned chronologically, so on an issue with more than 1000 comments the *newest* markers — the live claim and heartbeat markers the lease math reads — are exactly the ones silently missing. The read feeds a safety decision (who owns this issue), which under the contract (#6622 rule 3) must fail closed or say so, never present a truncated read as the set. Contrast the same contract's operator-drain disposition (#6615: a visible truncation notice) and the janitor's fail-closed full-page rule (#6618).

## Fix shape

When the loop exits by exhausting the page cap with a full last page, fail closed with an error naming the issue (or return the truncation explicitly for the caller to surface) — never return the partial marker set as complete. A test with a stubbed >10-page comment stream pins it. Bound value (10 pages) is unchanged unless the fixer re-sizes it.

Filed by the Phase 4 inventory (task 14524, lane code-b). No fix is attempted inside the inventory, per #6623's acceptance.

Add a named page bound (and/or accumulated-row bound) to `listResource`, sized generously above the largest legitimate reconcile listing across the four repos, whose breach throws an error naming the resource path. body:
## Problem

`basic: workflow lint` fails on current main in the "Contract tests for the ci-policy agreement checker (#7089)" step: `.github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.test.sh` exits 1 with no output at its first ("ok") fixture case.

## Evidence

- Fails on unrelated PRs today: dependabot actions/checkout-7 PR run 43204032501 (2026-11-12T10:51Z) and PR #8944 run 43259308384 (2026-11-12T16:31Z) — both in the agreement contract-test step, in ~0.1s, with no assertion output.
- Reproduced locally on clean main (7f6876e6): `bash .github/scripts/check-ci-policy-agreement.test.sh` exits 1 silently; `bash -x` shows it dies at the first `check-ci-policy-agreement.sh $TMP/ok` invocation.
- The checker itself passes on the real tree (`check-ci-policy-agreement.sh` → OK, 10 workflows).

## Root cause (read from the tree)

The #7089 re-arm (commit 82377fa1ed, 2026-11-11) emptied the checker's WAIVERS array, but the contract test's fixtures still encode the waiver-era world:

- the "ok" fixture gives `opencode-config-guard.yml` no `push` trigger and expects a `WAIVED opencode-config-guard.yml: main tier` line (test line ~61);
- the "ok" fixture gives `production-line-guard.yml` only `workflow_dispatch` and the stale-waiver case (test lines ~78-83) expects a `STALE WAIVER` outcome.

With no waivers recorded, the "ok" fixture itself disagrees (opencode-config-guard main tier requires `push`), so the checker exits 1 and `set -e` ends the test before any assertion prints.

## Fix shape

body:
## Problem

`nixos-rebuild build --flake ~/git/code#amd` fails at current main (`ed8864602a`, 2026-11-12), so the amd host cannot be switched. The running system is generation 554, built 2026-11-10 11:30 — every merged NixOS/home-manager change since then is undeployable via the normal switch route until this is fixed.

## Evidence

Build error (2026-11-12, task 15129 deploy step for #8933):

```
user profile: programs.openclaw.instances.default.runtimePlugins contains unsupported ids: memory-wiki.
Supported ids in this build: acpx, amazon-bedrock, …, memory-lancedb, meta, … (no memory-wiki)
Source/install specs such as npm:... or clawhub:... belong in programs.openclaw.runtimePluginSources.
Maintainers can inspect unsupported-plugin diagnostics in nix/generated/openclaw-runtime-plugins/report.json.
Command 'nix … build … nixosConfigurations."amd".config.system.build.toplevel' returned non-zero exit status 1.
```

- The config side comes from the memory-wiki enablement tracked on #6167 §2 ("Enable in home/openclaw (runtimePlugins + entry)"); the pinned OpenClaw build in this flake does not list `memory-wiki` among its supported runtime plugin ids, so the module's assertion rejects the whole system build.
- Lazy evaluation still works for unrelated attributes (e.g. individual `systemd.user.services` definitions evaluate fine), which is why this only surfaces on a full build/switch.
- Consequence already incurred: the merged #8933 tunnel hardening (PR #8935) could not deploy via `nixos-rebuild switch` and was deployed surgically (generated unit files installed directly) on 2026-11-12; the next full switch will need this fixed first regardless.

## Related

- #6156 (main's HM generation evaluation breakage — §1 of #6167 says the activation queue waits on it)
- #6167 §2 (memory-wiki: evaluate + likely enable — the intent behind the config entry)

## Acceptance

- `nixos-rebuild build --flake ~/git/code#amd` succeeds at main.
- The disposition of the `memory-wiki` entry is explicit and recorded here: either the OpenClaw pin is bumped to a build that supports the id (with #6167's post-activation proofs), the id moves to `runtimePluginSources` as the diagnostic suggests, or the entry is removed until a supporting pin lands — the one that matches #6167's intent, chosen by whoever picks this up with the evidence in `nix/generated/openclaw-runtime-plugins/report.json`.
- After the fix, `nixos-rebuild switch` lands cleanly on amd and the generation advances past 554.

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/structured_logging.rs` documents `ID_LOG_FILE` as a second destination whose events are appended (lines 18–20). `SharedFileWriter::open` opens the path with `create(true).append(true)` and has no size/retention limit or rotation handling (lines 302–312). The existing writer test verifies writes through clones continue accumulating in the same file (lines 500–513). Logging is initialized for the long-running `id` process in `pkgs/id/src/main.rs` (lines 273–283).

As configured, the file can grow for the lifetime of the process and eventually exhaust disk space. I verified this by source inspection; I did not run a runtime test.

## Suggested fix

Choose and document a supported operational contract: either provide configurable bounded rotation/retention for `ID_LOG_FILE`, or explicitly support external rotation and ensure the writer safely reopens a rotated file rather than continuing to write an unlinked inode. Keep the default behavior and compatibility intentional.

## Acceptance criteria

- The `ID_LOG_FILE` retention/rotation contract is documented, including the default behavior and operator configuration.
- If rotation is implemented, it has deterministic tests for the size/retention boundary, existing-file startup, and writes from cloned writers across rotation; no event is interleaved or silently lost.
- If external rotation is the supported approach, add a regression test demonstrating the writer follows the rotated path (or clearly document any required process signal/restart) and add an operator-facing example.

Related prior feature: #1791 introduced structured logging and append-mode file output; that issue is closed and did not specify retention/rotation.

title: id(envelope): Envelope::signed accepts a from that can never verify — refuse a sender/key mismatch at sign time (gap from #6488)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Gap found by the Phase 4 sign-surface inventory (#6488, contract #6487)

**Signer:** `Envelope::signed` — `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/envelope.rs:77`
`pub fn signed(key: &SigningKey, kind: EnvelopeKind, from: &str, to: &str, audience: &str, request: Option<&str>, at: u64) -> Result<Self>`

**Receipt rule it does not mirror:** `Envelope::verify` (`envelope.rs:110`) derives the verifying key from the envelope's own `from` field and checks the signature against it. An envelope whose `from` is not the hex of the signing key's verifying key can therefore never verify — it is dead on arrival at every receiver.

**Why it is decidable at the seam:** the rule is class (b) signer-relative under the #6487 contract — it compares one of the signer's own inputs (`from`) against the key it already holds. Nothing receiver-side is needed to decide it.

**Why production is not affected today:** both production callers pass a `from` that a prior authentication step has already bound to the key — `Directory::prepare_request_friend` and `Directory::prepare_accept_friend` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/directory.rs:1409` and `:1464`) pass the ID returned by `Directory::authenticate`, which itself ensures the ID equals the key's hex (`directory.rs:1819`). The gap is in the public helper itself: any other caller can mint an unverifiable envelope with no error.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `Envelope::signed` refuses a `from` that is not the signing key's verifying-key hex, with an error naming the rule — or takes the sender from the key itself so the mismatch is unrepresentable.
- [ ] Existing callers (`prepare_request_friend`, `prepare_accept_friend`, test helpers) keep working unchanged in behaviour; their envelopes verify exactly as before.
- [ ] A new test shows a mismatched `from` is refused at sign time; the existing envelope/directory suites stay green.
- [ ] Receipt behaviour (`Envelope::verify` and the directory's envelope acceptance policy) is unchanged.

Filed from the #6488 Phase 4 inventory (task 15067, lane code-a). Do not fix inside #6488 — that phase is inventory and documentation only.

title: id(backup): sign_upload signs envelopes every store refuses — mirror validate_envelope at sign time (gap from #6488)

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Gap found by the Phase 4 sign-surface inventory (#6488, contract #6487)

**Signer:** `sign_upload` — `pkgs/id/src/backup.rs:129`
`pub fn sign_upload(signing_key: &SigningKey, envelope: &[u8], epoch: u64) -> [u8; 64]`

**Receipt rule it does not mirror:** `BackupStore::upload` (`pkgs/id/src/backup.rs:558`) unconditionally calls `validate_envelope(envelope)?` (`pkgs/id/src/backup.rs:475`) before it verifies the signature — a malformed envelope (bad magic, unsupported KDF, out-of-range KDF parameters, truncated header) is refused at receipt no matter who signed it.

**Why it is decidable at the seam:** the rule is class (a) intrinsic under the #6487 contract — it depends only on the `envelope` bytes the signer already holds. `validate_envelope` is a private function in the same module (`backup.rs:475`), so the signer could call it today; the blocker is the shape, not the information: `sign_upload` is infallible (`-> [u8; 64]`), so it cannot refuse without an API change (the same shape `directory_auth::sign_request` had before #6443 made it fallible).

**Effect today:** a client can produce a valid signature over an envelope every backup store will refuse — creation reports success, consumption silently ignores, the exact failure shape #6487 exists to remove. All current in-repo callers are tests in `backup.rs` itself, so the API change is contained.

**Not part of this filing:** the epoch rules at receipt (`StaleEpoch`, `Tombstoned`) are class (d) receiver-state — they depend on the store's current record, which the signer cannot know. Those stay receipt-only.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `sign_upload` refuses a malformed envelope (one `validate_envelope` rejects) before signing, with an error naming the envelope rule — or the seam is changed to a validated-envelope type that makes the same refusal structural.
- [ ] The envelope predicate stays defined once and is used by both the signer and `BackupStore::upload`, so the two cannot drift.
- [ ] Valid envelopes sign exactly as before; the existing `backup` test suite stays green, plus a new test that a malformed envelope is refused at sign time.
- [ ] Receipt behaviour is unchanged.

Filed from the #6488 Phase 4 inventory (task 15067, lane code-a). Do not fix inside #6488 — that phase is inventory and documentation only.

body:
## Drew's ask

**2026-10-05 — Drew approved both proposed fixes for the ~65s "already initialized" boot path: "yes all of it"**

- (A) Move the boot-marker check to the top of init.sh — the fast path drops from ~65s to ~3s.
- (B) Make the cron's Phase 1 trigger-style: compare /proc boot_id against the marker in milliseconds; run init.sh only on mismatch.

The analysis behind the approval (~/memory/2026-10-05.md): the expensive work — `du -sh` over nix-persist plus 4 HTTPS round trips to cache.nixos.org — runs BEFORE the marker check.

## Why this is still live

The 2026-10-05 day-file marks the approval **"NOT YET DONE, interrupted by flush. PENDING"**, and nothing later records it landing. Follow-on measurements agree: code#5717's 2026-11-04 data still shows init.sh costing **68–97s per run**, ~60s of it the same nix-persist `du` timing out. (#5717 was a different, telemetry-cost item and is closed — its closure does not record the fast-path landing.) The 60-day design audit (register X18) calls this the clearest approved-but-dropped item in the window.

## Scope

Implement (A) and (B) as approved. No redesign — the design was settled on 2026-10-05.

## Acceptance check

- The already-initialized path completes in ~3s (marker check first, no `du`, no network round trips before it).

title: id(repl): bound shell-capture output and execution time

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Evidence

On current `main` (`af726f27001d126b4fa48a4bec4e2a31c854d4d4`), `pkgs/id/src/repl/input.rs:177-189` implements `shell_capture` with `std::process::Command::output()`. This buffers all stdout and stderr in memory and waits for the command to exit; neither output size nor execution time is bounded. The REPL preprocessor calls it for `$()` (`input.rs:793-794`), backticks (`842-843`), and `|>` (`884-885`), then inserts captured output back into the command (`806-807`).

For example, `$(yes)` can grow the output buffer without limit, while `$(sleep 999)` holds the REPL until that child exits. These are consequences of the current implementation; no stress command was run.

## Why it matters

A long-running or output-heavy substitution can make an interactive REPL appear hung or exhaust its process memory, without a way for the preprocessor to bound resource use or report which limit was reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and document a maximum captured output size and an execution deadline for shell substitutions.
- When a limit is reached, stop and reap the child process and return a clear, distinguishable error rather than returning truncated output as success.
- Apply the same policy to `$()`, backticks, and `|>` (or explicitly document any intentional difference).
- Add deterministic tests for output-limit and timeout behavior that verify the REPL returns promptly and does not retain unbounded output.

## Evidence

On current `main` (`27018e7f41e2e9446b87c028eaeeb09c9519ff60`), `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/event_store/chat.rs:173-204` first checks that `reader` belongs to the requested `group`, then builds the requested group's timeline and applies its non-`Full` history policy using `join_event(...)`.

`join_event` at `chat.rs:211-235` receives no requested group. It considers every applied `Create` listing the reader and every applied `Add` naming the reader, across the entire resolved event store. The resolver retains the action's group (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/event_store/resolve.rs:202-207`); creates identify their group by their own event ID (`resolve.rs:378-414`), but the selector does not use either scope. It chooses the candidate with the smallest causal past.

`pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/chat.rs:433-462` defines `FromJoin` (and currently `Recent`/`Causal`) visibility as records causally following that selected event. Consequently, when one reader is a member of multiple groups, an applied membership action in another group can be selected as the join for this group's timeline. A target-group record causally after that foreign action but before the reader's actual target-group join can then be included under a non-full history policy. The roster check remains in force: this is excess pre-join history for a current member, not access for a non-member. Default policy is `Full`, so the exposure requires a non-full history policy.

## Why it matters

A membership event in one group must not define when a member becomes eligible to see history in a different group. The current global selection can reveal target-group messages from before that member joined that target group.

## Acceptance criteria

- Select the history boundary only from the requested group's membership events: an `Add` must match the event's group, and a `Create` must match the requested group ID.
- Add a regression test with the same reader in two groups and a non-full history policy, where a foreign-group membership event precedes a target-group message but the reader's target-group join follows it; the earlier target-group message must remain hidden.
- Keep the current roster check and verify that legitimate target-group join/history behavior remains covered, including the full-history control.
- Run the focused `id-events`/`id-store` chat tests.

## Deduplication

Searched all-state issues for `FromJoin`, `join_event`, and cross-group chat history, including #3950 (chat membership/history implementation, closed) and #1573 (zero-length `Recent` policy, closed). No issue tracks cross-group join selection. No open PR found for `chat_timeline` or `join_event`.

body:
## Finding

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/test_slice1.sh` is described as a test, but unconditionally writes `live` to the user state mode file and runs the production claimant (`lines 72–78`). The claimant reads that same file in `claimant.py:166–177`; in live mode its `launch_step` proceeds past the shadow-only branch and can create sessions/bind tasks (`claimant.py:587–627`). The test only removes the mode file afterward (`test_slice1.sh:83`), so it can both perform real queue/session mutations and delete a pre-existing mode setting.

## Impact

Running this test on a developer laptop or CI host with access to the live queue can launch work or mutate task state. It is also not hermetic: it changes `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/mode`, and the cleanup does not restore an existing value.

## Suggested fix

Refactor the test to use isolated temporary state and injected/mock queue/session dependencies. Keep any live-mode smoke check behind an explicit opt-in that cannot be enabled by the ordinary test target; preserve and restore any user state if a manual live check remains.
