body:
Follow-up to PR #7775 (vendoring the Atlas Python reference for #5670). The vendored `pkgs/atlas-search/eval/eval3.py` is byte-faithful to the production reference (source SHA-256 recorded in `pkgs/atlas-search/eval/README.md`), so these three real bugs — all flagged by Codex review on PR #7775 — were deliberately NOT fixed inside the vendoring PR; they belong in this in-repo fix change now that the reference lives in the repo:

1. **Truncate query embeddings alongside document embeddings** (Codex P2, eval3.py `embed_queries` / `load_matrix`): `--trunc 384` truncates document embeddings in `load_matrix`, but `embed_queries` returns full-dimensional query embeddings, so `M @ Q[qi]` raises a dimension-mismatch error for e.g. a 768-dim model before scoring. Apply the same truncation + renormalization to query embeddings, including cached ones.
2. **Validate query and model identity before reusing cached embeddings** (Codex P2, eval3.py qcache check): a reused `--qcache` is accepted on row count alone; changing the model or changing/reordering queries with the same count silently scores the wrong vectors under the new model's name. Store and validate the ordered query texts + model/framework identity alongside the cache.
3. **Bound per-category recall@10 to ten ranks** (Codex P2, eval3.py per-category counter): when `--k` exceeds 10, the category counter counts gold matches beyond rank 10 while labeling them `recall@10`, overstating category performance vs the overall counter (which checks `rank <= 10`). Apply the same ten-rank cutoff.

Acceptance: all three fixed in `pkgs/atlas-search/eval/eval3.py` with the eval README's provenance note updated to record that the in-repo copy now diverges from the laptop source by these fixes; `python3 -I -m py_compile pkgs/atlas-search/eval/eval3.py` passes; fixture generation (`pkgs/atlas-search/fixtures/gen_core_fixtures.py`) still passes.

Filed by queue worker lane code-c, task 14987 (stale-PR resolution for PR #7775 / issue #8733).

body:
Found 2026-11-11 during the code#8653 fix (evidence there).

## What happened
The standing OpenCode server (opencode.service, user unit written 2026-11-10 18:54) had ExecStart pointing at /nix/store/72ghrggn…-opencode-2.0.30+01148f7-wrapped/bin/opencode. That store path no longer exists — it was garbage-collected while the server process (started 04:22Z, 11h17m uptime) was still running from it. The service looked healthy until the first restart today (15:39Z), when every start attempt failed with status 203/EXEC ("Unable to locate executable") and the unit hit its start limit. The fleet's central session server was down until restored by hand.

## Stopgap in place
~/.config/systemd/user/opencode.service.d/zz-8653-binary-restore.conf overrides ExecStart to the generation-548 build (+8ed9d6c, present in the store). Health check /global/health returns 200; sessions are serving. The coordinated switch must render the unit against its own new build AND remove this drop-in (a leftover drop-in would silently pin the old binary after the switch).

## Fix wanted
The standing server's binary must be GC-protected for as long as its unit references it: a gcroot (or profile reference) covering the unit's ExecStart path, rendered/updated with the unit itself, so a store GC can never strand a running service again. Audit the other standing user services for the same exposure while in here.

Family: code#8264 (stale binary baked into a runtime config snapshot), code#883 (unit 203/EXEC from a stale bin tree) — same class, different mechanism.

body:
## Symptom
The quota gatherer's Claude (Anthropic) leg fails the whole tick when Anthropic's usage endpoint returns HTTP 429 ("Rate limited. Retrying soon.") instead of backing off and retrying. The provider's row in quota-current.json goes stale for hours, and the stale row is then misread downstream as a credential/session failure.

## Evidence
- Usage & quota report chat, 2026-11-11 06:20 CST run: Claude gather leg rate-limited, row retained ~1h old.
- Same chat, 2026-11-11 08:20 CST run: read reported as failing "session expired", retained row ~3h old, crossing the stale threshold — the assistant told Drew the Monday-night sign-in had died again and offered to re-run the login.
- Same chat, 2026-11-11 ~09:16-09:20 CST correction (verified on the laptop): `claude auth status` says logged in, credentials file freshly rewritten at 09:16 with valid tokens; the actual tick error is "Rate limited. Retrying soon." The "session expired" wording was the stale-token window before the CLI refreshed itself. The assistant's own conclusion: "The durable fix belongs in the gatherer leg — back off and retry instead of failing the tick." It then asked Drew whether to file it — no issue was filed.
- Pool quota steward run 312 (2026-11-11 06:17 CST) likewise reported Claude unmeasured / credential expired at 05:25 CST under code#6120's lane, showing the stale read propagating into steward judgments.

## Scope
- The Anthropic/Claude leg of the quota gatherer (pm-stack aggregator/gatherer, laptop): on a 429 from the usage endpoint, back off and retry within the tick (bounded retries with jitter), instead of failing the tick and retaining the old row.
- A retained row caused by rate limiting must be distinguishable from a credential/session failure in the gatherer output (error kind recorded), so downstream reports do not claim "session expired" for a 429.
- Out of scope: the _claude credential renewal itself (code#6120 / code#8102), and the pm-core consolidation (code#8570) — this fix should land in the current gatherer and carry over.

## Acceptance check
- With the usage endpoint returning 429 then 200, one gatherer tick completes with a fresh Claude row (no retained/stale row) and the tick log shows the retry.
- With the endpoint persistently 429, the tick records the failure kind as rate-limited (not session-expired), and the usage report wording matches that kind.
- No regression: other provider legs' tick behavior unchanged.

## Refs
- Usage & quota report chat (hourly), runs 2026-11-11 06:20 / 08:20 / 09:20 CST.
- Related: code#6120 (provider credential renewal), code#8102 (_claude pair expiry), code#8570 (pm-core consolidation).
- Filed by the dropped-thread catcher, 2026-11-11: the fix was identified in chat and left as an unanswered question to Drew; under the standing file-the-issue rule it gets an issue and a queue route now.

title: fix(coord-mirror): coord_tasks dedupe_key UNIQUE collisions silently drop mirrored tasks

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

labels.name: kind/infrastructure
labels.description: Infrastructure / host-portability work

labels.name: epic/fleet-orchestration
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Problem

The Supabase → Turso coord-mirror's `coord_tasks` upserts fail on a second, unhandled conflict: the upsert in `sync_agent_to_turso.py` (laptop `~/tools/supabase-mirror/`, hatch-personal) is `INSERT INTO coord_tasks (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE ...`, but the mirror table also carries a UNIQUE index on `dedupe_key`. Whenever a task's `dedupe_key` matches a DIFFERENT task's already-mirrored row, the statement aborts with `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT: UNIQUE constraint failed: coord_tasks.dedupe_key` and that task never mirrors (the surviving row keeps the older task's data under that key).

Measured during the code#8636 catch-up (2026-11-11, queue task 14960): one 1000-statement task batch had **70** such failures, all this constraint. `agent.tasks` contains many same-`dedupe_key` rows across different ids (historical duplicates), so this is not a corner case.

## Why it was invisible

`turso-exec.py` prints per-statement ERROR lines but exits 0, and the sync's original error check never matched them — past "successful" syncs silently dropped these tasks. Since the code#8636 round-2 change, the sync counts them per batch and reports `apply_errors` in its JSON summary, so the loss is at least measured.

## Fix shapes to decide

- Drop the UNIQUE index on `coord_tasks.dedupe_key` in the mirror (the mirror is a read model of `agent.tasks`, whose own uniqueness story is the queue's, not the mirror's), or
- Make the upsert dedupe-aware (e.g. conflict handling that also covers `dedupe_key`), accepting that two source tasks would then share one mirror row — a semantics decision, or
- Pre-dedupe in the sync (last writer wins per `dedupe_key`, named in the summary).

Any of these is a mirror-semantics change — deliberately out of scope for code#8636 (transport only). This issue owns the decision + fix + a `--full` re-sync to backfill the dropped tasks.

Refs: code#8636, code#1723.

labels.name: epic/fleet-orchestration

body:
## Problem: bare `fleet queue claim` is a footgun that keeps firing

Running `fleet queue claim` with no arguments (e.g. while probing the CLI's usage) claims the queue's top task under a default identity. It has now fired **five times**, each time self-caught and released within minutes with the task verified back to `queued`, no work done:

- Tasks 10945, 12706, 14884 (2026-11-10, main-chat probing)
- Task 11421 / issue #7012 (2026-11-11, workflow re-arm lane probing CLI usage; disclosed on #7089)
- Task 5865 (2026-11-11, notifications Phase 1 lane probing CLI usage; released within the minute, read back queued @30)

## Why it matters

Each firing steals the top task from its rightful lane until a human notices. Five catches in two days means the sixth will eventually not be caught in time — the task sits claimed under a dead identity while its real work stalls.

## Fix (acceptance)

- `fleet queue claim` with no explicit task id and no explicit filter/limit arguments refuses with a usage error (a bare claim is never a meaningful intent), OR requires an explicit `--confirm-bare` style flag.
- Directed claims (`--task <id>`) and filtered claims are unaffected.
- A regression test covers the refusal.
- The worker runbooks' probing guidance updated if they document usage probing.

Parent design: #8575 (one door, one home per fact — fleet tool state unification). Slice 4 of 7. Approved by Drew 2026-11-11: implement in full.

## Work

Merge-intent queue and local PR stack:

1. When GitHub writes are unavailable (or as the standing discipline, where a lane chooses it), finished work stacks locally: each new branch is based on the previous branch's tip rather than on main, and the intended merge order is recorded as a list in the coordination database.
2. A replay command walks the stack bottom-up when GitHub is writable: push the branch, open the PR, merge it, rebase the next branch onto the new main, continue. Merge intents and outcome agent notes recorded during the outage replay in the same pass.
3. Conflict ownership: a conflict surfacing at replay belongs to the lane/session that authored the change; the replay records whose it is and routes it back to that owner instead of resolving it anonymously.

## Acceptance

- A live drill: with GitHub writes artificially blocked, two items are worked and stacked; on unblock, one replay lands both in the recorded order with correct issue closures and outcome notes.
- The stack state (branches, order, owners) is fully visible from the database alone while GitHub is down.
- A forced conflict at replay is routed to its authoring lane with the context needed to resolve it.

`pkgs/mcpx/internal/conformance` suites `TestStatefulServer` and `TestMessagesClient` FAIL on current main — reproduced 2026-11-11 by queue lane code-b (task 14860) while baseline-checking PR #8512:

body:
# Fix: turso_client pipeline chunks lose the session (rde_incoming vanishes mid-load)

Found by Codex review on PR #8544 (migration of the runtime-db-export machinery to `pkgs/agent-backup/`, #5976), comment 4534316362. The defect is pre-existing in the hatch original (`tools/runtime-db-export/turso_client.py`) — the migrated copy is verbatim, so both copies carry it.

## Problem

When a history-enabled spec such as `spec_m3.json` loads a 100-row page, `load_rows.py` creates and populates the temporary `rde_incoming` table using more than 100 statements. The chunking loop in `turso_client.py` splits those statements into separate `_pipeline` calls, each appending `close` without preserving a session baton. Subsequent staging inserts and the history archive then run on a connection where `rde_incoming` does not exist, so normal paged exports can fail.

## Fix direction (per the finding)

Preserve the same session across chunks, or keep the staging, archive, and merge operations together in one pipeline/session.

## Scope notes

- Fix in the canonical code copy (`pkgs/agent-backup/turso_client.py`) and mirror to the hatch original (or supersede it), so the copies do not diverge silently.
- Needs a test that exercises a history-enabled load whose statement count crosses the chunk boundary, with the oracle: staging table persists across all chunks and the archive/merge steps see the staged rows.

# F02 — permission noninterference reference-model fixture pack

**Tier/status:** crucial; fixture work ready after this design merges, integration conditional. Parent [#6020](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6020), programme [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018); [design on main](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4.md). Evidence: [baseline V1-D08/D12](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/01-baseline-inventory.md), [architecture](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/06-architecture-directives.md).

## Scope

Build a standalone test-only state machine modeling authorized physical selection, retrieval, resolution/hydration, cache and current-epoch revocation. Its fixture inputs are identities, caller authorization, content visibility, retained snapshot, cache entries and rights transitions. Its public projection contains only observable permitted results, ranks, counts, errors and metadata. This is not #6021's live classification scan, #8479 remediation, #6228 manifest implementation, or a production access-control mechanism.

## Failing-first steps and oracle

1. Create paired worlds with identical permitted objects but differing forbidden objects, source paths and content; write failing noninterference assertions that the low-privilege observable projection is identical, including counts, errors and metadata.
2. Build an independent reference model selecting authorized physical inputs before ranking, then authorizing resolution, hydration and every cached replay against **current** rights. Generate sequences of read, cache, reclassify/revoke and replay; check every result against the model. Seed cached formerly allowed content, revoked historical snapshot, and mixed-rights byte-identical occurrences.
3. Include deliberately insecure selection-after-ranking and stale-cache mutations that assertions reject. Restrict timing/side-channel claims to modeled observable values; don't assert constant-time execution.

**Hard prerequisites:** merged design and local fixtures only. **Soft ordering:** #3125 occurrence work, #6805 cache policy, #6228/#6993 manifest, #6021/#8479 remediation. Future integration requires verified live enforcement at each relevant serving boundary; tests alone do not prove deployed security.

**Existing candidate seams:** `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/search.rs`, `filters.rs`, `tests/`; `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/src/server.rs` and fleet counterpart exist. Prefer a new isolated `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/tests/permission_model.rs` for this slice, without changing production APIs. Future proposed done command: `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/atlas-search/Cargo.toml -p atlas-core --test permission_model`. No live corpus, credentials, network, or external costs.

**Risks:** manifest labels are not authorization, ranking can leak hidden membership, and historical access is not present access. Fixture passes are not a certification of runtime, other surfaces, or side channels.

## Design merge gate

The reviewed design is in [PR #8519](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8519). This tracker is filed now to preserve the independently buildable slice while the design PR waits on the unrelated basic-tier baseline defect #8306. **Do not start implementation until #8519 is merged.** The main-branch source links become available at that merge; this issue does not authorize production integration.

# F03 — citation and occurrence resolution conformance fixtures

**Tier/status:** recommended; independently ready after design merge; live adapter conditional. Parent [#6020](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6020), programme [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018); [design on main](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4.md). Evidence: [baseline V1-D04/D05](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/01-baseline-inventory.md), [lineage analysis](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/03-provenance-lineage.md), [architecture](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/06-architecture-directives.md).

## Scope and distinction

Build an offline, test-only conformance corpus plus reference resolver. Each synthetic record has a content ID, distinct occurrence ID, version, source coordinates, retained bytes/hash, coverage flag and rights; a request includes caller and current authorization. Output is an authorized source/version citation with an exact byte range or a properly scoped unavailable/not-found response. Completeness is only within the enumerated ingested, retained, permitted snapshot. Never reveal forbidden occurrence counts or paths.

This does **not** implement #3125's occurrence registry, backfill, CAS, storage, MCP tools or live resolution; #6035 owns span design and #6062 owns graph publication. #6266 is an independently scoped product. This fixture is an adapter-conformance oracle, not a new response wire protocol or production schema.

## Failing-first steps and oracle

1. Hand-author expected results for same bytes at multiple locations/rights, pinned historical version, source rename, missing coverage, deleted bytes and changed permissions. Begin with deliberately incorrect aliasing and stale-replay implementations and assert conformance rejects them.
2. Implement a simple independent reference projection over explicit fixture records. Model/property tests generate occurrences and ensure each successful citation resolves to the *exact retained bytes* at its specified version/range; byte-identical IDs cannot merge occurrence authority. Current revocation makes old citations unavailable; a hidden insertion never changes visible counts or metadata.
3. Supply a test-local adapter interface and a small deliberately correct fake; compare fake and hand-authored expected results. Avoid importing F02's test helper so either slice can ship separately. F02 checks whole-pipeline noninterference; this issue checks occurrence identity and citation fidelity.

**Hard prerequisites:** merged design and test-local fixture only. **Soft ordering:** #3125, #6035, #6062 and #6054 deletion design; real adapter needs registry and current authorization/deletion behavior, and is explicitly out of scope.

**Candidate seam:** verified `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/types.rs` and existing `tests/`; add isolated `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/tests/citation_conformance.rs` without modifying production types. Proposed future command: `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/atlas-search/Cargo.toml -p atlas-core --test citation_conformance`. No live corpus, credentials, network, or external cost.

**Risks:** a hash verifies bytes, not source truth; unavailable content cannot be regenerated as historical evidence. A test fake is not evidence the registry or resolver is deployed.

## Design merge gate

The reviewed design is in [PR #8519](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8519). This tracker is filed now to preserve the independently buildable slice while the design PR waits on the unrelated basic-tier baseline defect #8306. **Do not start implementation until #8519 is merged.** The main-branch source links become available at that merge; this issue does not authorize production integration.

body:
# F01 — synthetic missing-versus-buried diagnostic fixture and runner seam

**Tier/status:** recommended; fixture work ready after this design merges. No runtime integration is implied. Parent [#6020](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6020), programme [#6018](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/6018); [design on main](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4.md). Evidence: [baseline](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/01-baseline-inventory.md), [diagnostic research](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/04-feedback-retrieval.md), [architecture](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/main/doc/2026-11-11T03-45-00Z_design_atlas_v2_v4/research/06-architecture-directives.md).

## Problem and boundary

The existing #5741 `atlas-eval` scores supplied rankings against qrels; it does not enumerate a corpus or determine which pipeline stage lost a known target. #6046 owns a feedback-derived golden-set builder/gate; #8062 owns its missing fresh-ranking seam. This slice does neither: it tests diagnostic reasoning on a closed synthetic world, with no claim of real-corpus absence.

## Deliverable and minimal interface

Create an offline fixture pack and a test-local runner accepting a synthetic snapshot ID, independently enumerated eligible documents, coverage completeness, target ID and relevance, indexed IDs, generated ordered candidate IDs, served cutoff, context-included IDs, per-stage completion/error state and answer-support flag. Return stage and coverage confidence independently; unknown and intentionally excluded may not be presented as globally absent. A timeout/error is not an empty successful candidate set, and a served hit omitted from context is not an answer-support failure. No production API, trace schema, corpus loader or model is required. Fixed in-memory supplied runs are not #8062's live baseline/candidate generation.

## Steps and oracle

1. Write failing example fixtures: incomplete coverage, fully enumerated absent, stored but unindexed, indexed but not a candidate, candidate below cutoff, served but omitted by context packing, context delivered but unsupported, served supported, stage timeout/error, and policy excluded. Explain a forbidden target only with ordinary not-found shape.
2. Write a small reference decision procedure independent from the runner under test; use generated finite corpora and compare the runner's stage/coverage tuple to the exhaustive-set oracle. A positive control explicitly includes the target; a negative control requires complete enumeration. Mutation tests or explicit deliberately wrong stage outcomes must demonstrate the assertions detect failures.
3. Make the runner pass; add deterministic replay and malformed-input checks. Keep unsupported-answer judgments distinct from retrieval.

**Hard prerequisites:** only this design and a locally runnable test environment. **Soft ordering:** coordinate #6046/#8062 and #8245; no trace persistence or golden-set gate is needed for fixtures. Future production adapters are separate, conditional on current snapshot, authorization and trace contracts.

**Candidate seam:** verified existing `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/eval.rs` and `tests/`; prefer new isolated `tests/diagnostic_fixture.rs` instead of changing `EvalData` or shared evaluator. Proposed future done command, not yet an existing test: `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/atlas-search/Cargo.toml -p atlas-core --test diagnostic_fixture`. No network, live corpus, credentials, or external cost.

**Risks:** an implementation that compares a function to itself proves nothing; maintain separate expected fixture data and reference procedure. Never equate unjudged with irrelevant or an incomplete snapshot with absence. This is not a production search-quality or authorization certification.

## Design merge gate

The reviewed design is in [PR #8519](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8519). This tracker is filed now to preserve the independently buildable slice while the design PR waits on the unrelated basic-tier baseline defect #8306. **Do not start implementation until #8519 is merged.** The main-branch source links become available at that merge; this issue does not authorize production integration.

title: id(web): stale saves replace the current filename without archiving its version

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/high
labels.description: Important and time-sensitive

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/m
labels.description: Medium: expected under 1 day of work

body:
## Evidence

On default-branch commit `853f57178247b40e0240a3cd2b6582d87f82a3ed`, `pkgs/id/src/web/routes/file_handlers.rs:93-102` calls `archive_original_tag` with the client-supplied `doc_id`, ignores its `None` result, and then sets the filename tag to the new blob. The helper at `file_handlers.rs:1219-1234` returns `None` when the current filename points to a different hash. Existing handler test `pkgs/id/src/web/routes.rs:1711-1718,1727-1732,1767-1771` sends a fixed nonmatching hash and expects both same-name saves to succeed, without checking the displaced filename binding or archive.

Code-path scenario (not runtime-reproduced): clients A and B open H0; A saves H1; after the save cooldown, B saves an edit based on H0. The archive helper does not archive H1 because it does not match H0, but the handler replaces the filename with B’s H2 and reports success. The signed event for H1 may remain in history; permanent deletion is not established. This differs from #8407, which concerns `/api/new` rather than stale saves.

## Why it matters

A stale editor can silently supersede another client’s more recent edit, without the expected named archive for the displaced version, making recovery and conflict awareness difficult.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define and enforce a safe stale-save policy: reject with an actionable conflict while preserving the current version, or explicitly preserve the displaced current version and communicate the conflict.
- Make the check and update safe against concurrent saves; a check-then-set alone is insufficient.
- Add handler/store regression tests for two clients starting from the same hash, concurrent same-name saves, and a normal matching save; assert responses, current binding, and archive/history behavior.
- Account for archive/store failures without reporting an unqualified success that loses the named recovery path.

title: id(web): distinct colon-containing tags collide in home feed aggregation

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/src/web/home.rs:90-98`, the home feed builds a tag identity using `format!("{key}:{value}")`, then uses that rendered label as the deduplication key. Thus key `a:b` with value `c` and key `a` with value `b:c` both become `a:b:c`. Colon-containing keys are valid: `pkgs/id/src/tags.rs:2817-2818` tests one.

The collision merges distinct tags within a document, reducing its reported tag count, and across documents in `home.rs:109-119`, inflating popular-tag occurrences and changing rankings. The count is documented at `home.rs:45` as the number of documents carrying the exact tag. This is confirmed by code inspection; no runtime reproduction was run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Aggregate and deduplicate using the actual tag identity, not an ambiguous rendered label; display distinct tags unambiguously.
- Count each exact tag at most once per document and preserve distinct tags with colons in either key or value.
- Add regression tests for collisions within one document and across documents, including occurrence counts and ranking; preserve ordinary labels where compatible.

title: id(world): concurrent journal handles can acknowledge appends to a replaced inode

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/src/world_store.rs:147-158` opens a journal without exclusive ownership, so two `FileJournal` handles may open the same path. `compact` writes a sibling file and renames it over that path (`:356-392`), then replaces only its own writer descriptor (`:394-399`). The other handle still points to the old inode; its `append` can succeed (`:271-290`) while a subsequent reopen reads the replacement and cannot see the acknowledged entry. `append_transaction` also invokes compaction (`:328-353`); simultaneous compactions share the same temporary path (`:361`). This conclusion is from code inspection, not a reproduced integration test.

One deterministic regression scenario: open handles A and B on the same journal, compact using A, append a supported entry using B, drop both, then reopen and check that every acknowledged entry survives. Alternatively, if multiple handles are unsupported, opening B must fail clearly before it can write. Note that a lock on the journal inode alone does not protect ownership across the rename; a stable per-world lock or equivalent ownership protocol is needed.

## Why it matters

Two processes, or two independently opened handles in one process, can silently lose successfully acknowledged world history. Existing distributed spill lease design #2819 addresses a different multi-node protocol and does not establish local file ownership.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Enforce a documented single-writer invariant across handles and processes, or safely coordinate all appends and rewrites.
- [ ] Regression coverage for the open/open/compact/append/reopen sequence and competing compactions; no acknowledged entry disappears.
- [ ] Ownership remains valid across replacement, failure, and release, with a clear error for an unsupported second writer.

title: claim_by_id platform-limit block unreachable dead code (G7)

labels.name: epic/fleet-orchestration
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Defect: the #8217 platform-limit enforcement inside `claim_by_id` is unreachable

Found during the one-queue gap analysis (code#8097, PR #8438).

On current main, the platform-limit block inside `claim_by_id`
(`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs`) sits after a
`return Ok(None)` inside the claim-guard block, so it never runs —
rustc emits an `unreachable expression` warning at that block. The
pick path and the transfer path enforce
`repo_task_lane_ledger.platform_limit` live; the by-id path does
not, despite the source-shape test
`claim_by_id_enforces_platform_limit_like_the_pick_8217` asserting
the enforcement code is present (it is present, just dead).

Impact: a task with a recorded platform limitation (with reason)
can be claimed by id by an ineligible family. Claim-by-id is an
explicit special case under the #8097 rules, so this is a narrow
path — but the enforcement was designed (#8217) and is believed to
be live, and it is not.

Fix: move the ledger platform-limit block out of the claim-guard
block so it executes on the by-id path (before the claim proceeds),
matching the pick path's semantics. PR #8438's new
`task_requirements_unmet` check in `claim_by_id` was placed in
reachable code (after `by_id_claimable`) and covers payload
`requires`; the ledger block needs the same treatment. Add a test
that exercises the by-id path against a limited task with an
ineligible claimer (behavior, not source shape).

Recorded in the one-queue gap analysis (G7) filed on #8097.

body:
## Evidence

On main `f731530172adef9c3f7fd28302cdeccd8d2374fc`, `pkgs/id/src/web/security.rs:151-169` copies the request URI path verbatim into `clean_bootstrap_target`, and lines 248-261 emit that value as the `Location` of a 303 on successful query-token bootstrap. A request target `//evil.example/path?token=<valid-token>` with an allowed Host and no existing token cookie therefore can produce `Location: //evil.example/path`; a browser interprets this network-path reference as navigation to `evil.example`, not a same-origin path. The removed token is not shown to be disclosed. This contradicts the same-origin contract documented in the function and closed #5746.

This is verified by code inspection; confirm the end-to-end route and request-target behavior with a regression test. Exploitation requires a valid bootstrap token and a client that sends the double-slash request target.

## Acceptance criteria

- Bootstrap redirects cannot navigate off-origin for paths beginning with multiple slashes or other browser-normalized authority forms, while still stripping the token.
- Add a middleware/HTTP regression test with a double-slash request target, and preserve ordinary paths and non-token query parameters.
- Cover relevant browser URL normalization edge cases or explicitly constrain the redirect target to a safe same-origin form.

title: id(sanctions): bind decisions to the declared active list and its matches

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix

body:
## Evidence

At main `99d8b9ac6d7709b00fe9dc96641bd4da621d89d8`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/sanctions.rs:243-245` declares that a boundary reads the list named by `list_id`; `ListVersion::is_active_at` defines its effective window at lines 152-163. However, `evaluate` (lines 350-386) accepts any `ListVersion` and arbitrary caller-supplied `SubjectMatch` values without checking the list identity, activity, or match provenance. For example, a boundary for list A evaluated with list B and a strong match from B returns `Deny` and records B. A match from another version can likewise be recorded against a list that does not contain it. `cleared_by_removal` (lines 395-411) similarly accepts an unrelated or inactive list and can record a `Cleared` decision against it. Neither function receives evaluation time.

This risks enforcing the wrong operator policy or clearing a restriction incorrectly, with an audit record that cannot reproduce the asserted match. These are model API hazards, not a claim that production currently invokes this path. The design requires a referenced, versioned list and effective dates (`doc/2026-11-08_design_id5683.md:361-375`).

## Acceptance criteria

- Bind evaluation and removal decisions to the boundary’s declared list and the version valid at the decision time; reject invalid inputs explicitly rather than silently allowing or clearing.
- Bind matches to the evaluated list/version (for example compute them inside a checked evaluation API, or use an appropriately validated typed result); document the trust boundary.
- Add tests for unrelated list IDs, future/expired versions, stale or foreign matches, and valid boundary/effective-window edges. Preserve grandfathering and weak-match guarantees.
- Coordinate with #8201, which owns the signed store and activation lifecycle; its reconciliation comment treats the evaluation core as already delivered.

body:
## Problem
fleet-place (repo-queue placement dispatch, PR #8325 for #5413) correlates a workflow dispatch with the Actions run it created by snapshot exclusion: it records the workflow run ids that exist before submitting, then attaches the earliest run that appears after. That fixes attaching an earlier run, but two dispatches POSTed in the same instant whose runs appear in the same poll window cannot be proven apart (Codex P1 finding on PR #8325, thread r4531401135, dispositioned with this residual).

## Fix
Carry a unique dispatch identifier through the workflow and match on it:
- Add a `dispatch_id` workflow_dispatch input to `.github/workflows/org-run.yml` (developing-today/code) and to fleet-run.yml (dezren39/fleet), and surface it via `run-name:` (e.g. `run-name: org-run ${{ inputs.dispatch_id }}`) so the runs list API returns it as the run display title.
- In `dispatch_workflow` (pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/placement.rs), generate the fp_ handle (or a dispatch nonce) before dispatch, pass it as the `dispatch_id` input when the workflow supports it, and prefer a run whose display title carries the id; keep snapshot exclusion as the fallback for workflows without the input.

## Acceptance
- A dispatch can be correlated to exactly its own run even when another dispatch of the same workflow lands in the same poll window, proven by a test with interleaved runs.
- Workflows without the input keep working via the snapshot fallback.

## Follow-on from PR #5949 review (CodeRabbit minor, heavy lift — deferred by lane code-o, task 14767)

`collect_link_reference_definitions` in `pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs` applies its `indent > 3` indented-code skip to the RAW line. A link reference definition nested inside a list item can be indented four or more columns from the line start while sitting at a relative indent of 0–3 from the item's content column:

```
- item

    [unused]: /keep
```

(relative indent 2 from the `- ` content column, after the blank line ends the item paragraph). The raw-indent check skips the line before collection, so the unused definition is dropped on save.

## Fix shape

The scanner currently tracks fences, HTML blocks, footnote blocks, and block-start eligibility, but no list-container context. Evaluate the indentation relative to the enclosing container's content column (the recorded container prefix machinery — `container_signature` / `strip_container_levels` — is the natural base) before applying the indented-code skip, with regression tests covering: list-nested definition collected; a genuinely indented code line inside a list item still NOT collected; the no-blank-line paragraph-continuation case staying paragraph text.

Deferred from PR #5949 because it is a structural scanner change in a file with a long history of edge-case regressions, and the PR's own Codex gate findings were the merge blockers in scope.

body:
# Fix: outbox reconcile must not trust GitHub search absence (live trial 2 duplicate)

Found by the live trials for the creation outbox pilot (#3706, task 14666, 2026-11-10) against scratch repo dezren39/fleet-outbox-trial-3706.

## What happened
Trial 2 (kill/restart): entry ob-1794350127-ac5b929eacf5 was claimed by a drainer that "landed its create then died" (issue #6 on the scratch repo, created manually with the entry's marker, exactly as a crashed drainer's landed create would look). After the 120s lease expired, a fresh drain claimed the row as `uncertain` (correct) and ran `find_by_marker` — which searches via the GitHub search API. The search returned nothing for an issue created ~2.5 minutes earlier (search indexing lag), the drainer treated that as proven absence, and re-created: duplicate issue #7 with the same marker. The row resolved done against #7.

## Defect
`find_by_marker` (pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs) uses GitHub search as its only source. Search is eventually consistent; "not in the index yet" is indistinguishable from "does not exist", so the reconcile path can duplicate precisely in the crash window it exists to protect (a create that landed seconds-to-minutes before the restart).

## Fix direction
Before concluding absence, the reconcile must check a strongly consistent source: list the repo's recent issues via the REST list endpoint (issues list is not search-indexed) and scan bodies for the marker — at minimum the most recent N issues / issues created since the entry's lease start. Only if BOTH search and the list scan find nothing may the drainer re-create. Add an oracle test: marker present in list results but absent from search results reconciles, never duplicates.

## Evidence
- Scratch repo: dezren39/fleet-outbox-trial-3706 issues #6 and #7 (same title, same marker `<!-- fleet-outbox:ob-1794350127-ac5b929eacf5 -->`); #7 closed as the trial duplicate.
- Trial record: comment on #3706 by task 14666 (2026-11-10).
- The producer flip (new-issue-creator-code-a) stays blocked on this fix: a drainer that can duplicate in the crash window must not be the fleet's creation path yet.

body:
Filed by the #4707 closing audit of design #4706 (task 12695, lane code-n, 2026-11-10). Evidence at origin/main 9b65fa2ec8, `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs`.

## Gap

`pendingClientRequests` (:206) holds one entry per outbound `session/request_permission` (`requestClient`, :224-232); an entry is deleted only when the ACP client's response arrives (dispatch, response branch). The adapter sets no timeout anywhere on that wait.

If the client never answers:
- the map entry leaks for the adapter's process lifetime (bounded only by process exit and by the number of unanswered asks — small, but unbounded within a long-lived process), and
- `handlePermissionAsked` (:446ff) awaits forever, so the permission reply is never posted to the serve. No evidence in this repo shows the pinned serve expiring an unanswered `permission.asked` on its own clock, so the serve-side tool call the permission gates stays blocked until the session is interrupted or deleted.

## Fix shape (named, not designed here)

Give the client request a bounded wait in the adapter: on expiry, resolve the permission flow through the path `handlePermissionAsked` already uses for a failed client request — post `{decision: "reject"}` to `POST /api/session/:id/permission/:permId/reply` — and delete the `pendingClientRequests` entry. The timeout value is the implementer's call, recorded on the PR; it should be generous enough for a human approver and finite.

body:
## Problem

Found by the #4376 closing audit of the #4375 response-read contract (2026-11-10, lane code-b, task 13050). Two buffered reads of a fetched OpenAPI document in pkgs/mcpx/internal/openapi/openapi.go (lines 157 and 690) cap the read with `io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 32<<20))` — bounded, but silently truncating: contract decision 2 (#4375) requires a buffered success body to be *refused* past its named cap, never silently truncated (the cap+1-and-refuse pattern the provider paths use with ProviderResponseBodyLimit). A truncated spec parses as a shorter document or fails downstream with a misleading error, instead of failing the fetch at the cap.

The source is an operator-configured URL, so this is a peer read under the contract, not a local file path (the os.ReadFile branch beside line 157 is out of scope — not peer bytes).

## Fix shape

Apply the cap+1 refuse pattern at both sites with the cap named in internal/defaults (or recorded as a defaults constant), so an over-cap spec fails the fetch with a clear "exceeds N bytes" error. Behaviour change is deliberately *not* inside the #4376 audit (its acceptance allows only the single-site embeddings slip fix); this issue is the named follow-up the audit files.

Related: #4375 (contract), #4376 (audit).

title: queue: by-id claim drops the --session-id mark (claimed event + progress record null)

labels.name: epic/fleet-orchestration
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
Found during the #8210 live acceptance (2026-11-10): a by-id claim (`repo-queue claim --task <id> --session-id <ses>`) records `session_id: null` on its `claimed` event and does not stamp the claimer's session into the task progress, even though `--session-id` was passed. Verified live on task 14440: event 162950 (by-id claim by repo-worker-code / lane code-m with `--session-id bfa19dac-…`) carries `"session_id":null`.

Cause (read in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs`, `verb_claim`): the effective session mark is forced to `None` on the by-id path (`session_mark = if by_id.is_some() { None } else { … }`) — presumably so a sink re-claim never rebinds an already-bound session, but it also drops the claimer mark entirely, which cuts against #8187's rule that who is looking at an item is always marked (marks are observability, never filters).

The #8210 transfer path compensates for the send flow (the sender checkpoints `progress.from_session` before transferring, and the transfer claim records full marks), so this is not blocking the send — but a plain by-id claim should still record WHO claimed it.

Fix shape: on a by-id claim, record the requested `--session-id` as the claimer mark on the `claimed` event (and in progress when no session is bound), while still never rebinding a row that already has a bound session. Regression test alongside the #8066/#8210 claim tests.

Links: #8210 (found there), #8187 (marking rule), #8066 (by-id claim origin).

title: quota: no labelled opencode-go.popesdrew row — the account's Console measurement publishes as the unlabelled opencode-go aggregate

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Symptom

The quota gatherer's record (`~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/quota-current.json`, 15-minute ticks) carries labelled per-account rows for two of the three OpenCode Go accounts — `opencode-go.drewrypope` and `opencode-go.developing-today-0` — plus ONE unlabelled `opencode-go` row. There is no labelled `opencode-go.popesdrew` row, so that account's windows cannot be read or steered per-account. The three Go accounts are seated 1:1:1 in the deepseek-flash-plan tier of workhorse-ordered, so per-account steering matters.

Census 2026-11-10 (quota-current.json generatedAt 2026-11-10T20:30:08Z, all rows fresh-measured in that tick):

- `opencode-go.drewrypope` — 5h 0% / weekly 100% / monthly 100% (monthly resets 2026-12-03T03:02:35Z)
- `opencode-go.developing-today-0` — 5h 0% / weekly 100% / monthly 54% (monthly resets 2026-12-08T22:09:41Z)
- `opencode-go` (unlabelled, no credentialId) — weekly 100% / monthly 100%, credits_balance $0.00, resets 2026-11-16T00:00Z / 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z

## Root cause (wire-verified on the laptop, 2026-11-10)

The unlabelled row IS popesdrew's measurement, unattributed:

- popesdrew is enrolled as a **Console OAuth device sign-in** (credential `cred_bh5LJo8s26zwYccj8tDnC3LP1x`, org `org_01M6H7986JGCDR5H81QXPFJW2J`, popesdrew@gmail.com, token expiry 2026-12-03T17:42:29Z) stored under its **own instance integration** `opencode-go.popesdrew`. The other two accounts hold API-key credentials under their instance integrations. The same Console sign-in also exists as the shared `opencode` integration's active row.
- The gatherer's single source is the opencode fork's quota subcommand (`opencode quota --json`, fork `packages/ai/src/quota`). Its base per-credential walk for `opencode-go` reads only the credential aliases `opencode` + `opencode-go` — so it measures popesdrew's account **through the shared `opencode` row** and emits it as the bare, unlabelled `opencode-go` result. Proof the numbers are popesdrew's: a direct Console status call with that credential returns week used 3,006,253,692 / 3,000,000,000 micro-cents (100%, resets 2026-11-16T00:00Z), month 6,006,253,692 / 6,000,000,000 (100%, resets 2026-12-03T17:35:51Z — exactly the unlabelled row's reset), billing balance 0 ($0.00 — exactly the unlabelled row's balance), fiveHour meter present but idle (used 0, resetsAt null — the Console parser drops a meter with no reset, which is why the unlabelled row has no 5h window while the API-key rows do).
- The instance path never rescues it: `opencode-go` did not set `foldInstanceCredentials` (only Codex did), so configured instances were never folded into the base answer; and the row-usability verdict re-keys an instance row under the base id (`opencode-go`), where a Console sign-in reads as neither Console credential (that lookup keys on the shared `opencode` integration) nor API key — so the instance is judged unusable, excluded from the configured listing, and an explicit ask for `opencode-go.popesdrew` answers `Not configured` (verified live).

## Fix

In the opencode fork's quota module (the gatherer's single source), with the OpenChamber quota lib (the same module's original home, still used by OpenChamber surfaces) mirrored:

1. `opencode-go` provider sets `foldInstanceCredentials: true` — configured Go instances fold into the base answer, one labelled row per account, the pattern Codex already uses for openai.main / openai.alternate.
2. The provider gains an `isCredentialUsable` hook that judges a row on its own shape (Console sign-in under the Console key, or an API key present) instead of the dispatcher's base-id re-keying, which cannot see an instance-stored Console row.
3. The listing's instance-usability verdict consults the same hook the fetch path uses, so listing and fetch agree (previously the listing re-implemented the verdict without the hook).

Tests: fork `packages/ai/test/quota.test.ts` gains a describe block covering the fold, the instance ask, and the listing (212 pass, typecheck clean); OpenChamber lib `index.test.js` gains the mirror coverage (46 pass) and `opencode-go.test.js` stays green (45 pass).

Related: #5324 (the route-level sibling symptom — the popesdrew pool drawing zero), #2490 (quota read-path unification), #1161 (the Go console per-workspace adapter this builds on), #8102 (popesdrew self-renewal stays UNPROVEN — its Console token expires 2026-12-03).

## Proof

Posted as a comment on this issue after deploy: a fresh gatherer tick's quota-current.json with three labelled opencode-go rows and popesdrew's numbers quoted.

body:
Follow-on from task 12126 profiling (issue #7064, #557 remainder). Profiling verdict recorded on issue #7064: the many_worlds ack path is capped by per-append fdatasync — `FileJournal::append` (pkgs/id/src/world_store.rs) does write_all + sync_data inline in the world actor's persist() (pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs), unit cost 5.18 ms median sequential (repo bench journal_append_fsync), and concurrent fdatasync across 100 journal files on ext4 aggregates only ~0.85–1.5k syncs/s — below the 2,000/s offered load, so queueing delay, not service time, dominates p99 (5,650 ms vs 50 ms target).

## Scope

Implement ack batching (group commit) for world inputs so one sync_data covers a batch of queued inputs per world, preserving durability-before-ack for every command:

- Journal: add `append_batch(&[JournalEntry])` to the WorldJournal trait (default = per-entry append loop); FileJournal override = one concatenated write_all + one sync_data, falling back to per-entry append when any entry requires a header version bump.
- Actor: when the command loop receives an unsigned Input, drain already-queued unsigned Inputs (bounded, e.g. 64; stop at the first non-Input and hold it for the next loop iteration), stage them in order, persist the batch once, then commit and reply in order.

## Invariants the implementation must respect (found in profiling, do not rediscover)

- `prepare_input` assigns sequence = core.sequence + 1 without advancing it: batch staging must assign sequences explicitly in order (a prepare-at-sequence variant) or commits fail "prepared world event is stale".
- `ensure_uses_left` is checked at prepare time but `spend` happens at commit: a batch from one participant must account for staged spends, or it over-admits past the uses limit.
- program.update runs before persist today; a mid-batch program rejection marks the program unhealthy and later inputs must see today's exact error semantics — stage in order, stop at the first failure, commit the staged prefix, and route the failed + remaining inputs through the single-command path.
- append_transaction is NOT the batch primitive: it rewrites the whole journal via compact (O(journal size)) and exists for builder-install atomicity.

## Acceptance

- cargo test -p id --lib green (world actor + journal tests, plus new batch tests: batch of N inputs = N events, one sync; mid-batch program rejection semantics unchanged).
- Full world_bench run on the reference laptop recorded in pkgs/id/benches/baseline.txt + BASELINES.md showing the many_worlds p99 movement vs the 5,650.792 ms line; issue #557 stays open until a recorded run shows target_met=true.

# Home-resolution contract: disposition the Python `expanduser` / `Path.home()` surface against #5762

Follow-up from the Phase 4 closing inventory audit (issue #5763, design issue #5762, contract in `files/designs/code-home-resolution-contract.md`, goal workspace keep-the-four-repos-healthy).

## Why this is filed separately

The Phase 4 audit (#5763) fixed the same-shape sites in-phase (invented substitute directories). The Python surface is a different shape and a different set of deploy units:

- `os.path.expanduser("~")` and `Path.home()` on POSIX use `$HOME` when set and otherwise the **pwd (passwd) entry**; `Path.home()` raises only when the passwd lookup also fails. Passwd resolution is the fallback the #5762 contract **declined as the default**, so these sites do not conform — but none of them invents a root/CWD/literal-`~`/hardcoded directory either.
- The ~35 sites span unrelated operator tooling (infra/ janitors and reapers, pm-stack/opencode-claimant, pkgs/cold-store-reaper, pkgs/deploy, scripts/, lib/, nixos/) — each with its own runtime context (systemd units, cron, manual operator runs). Dispositioning them needs per-tool judgment about whether HOME is guaranteed by the unit, which is a sweep of its own.

## Inventory (origin/main 7dc4aefa23, from the #5763 audit)

- infra/cargo-target-janitor/bin/cargo_target_janitor.py:517,805,806,808,813 (`Path.home()`)

body:
## Summary

Implement the rendezvous decision record for UDP-denied clients: `doc/2026-11-10_rendezvous_discovery_udp_denied_design.md` (PR #8213, from issue #5793 / task 12886, parent #5671).

## Scope

- **Advertisement type in `pkgs/id`:** `TransportAdvertisement` v1 — subject identity fingerprint, transports[] (kind/endpoint/priority/broker identity), issued_at/expires_at (TTL ≤ 24h), strictly increasing sequence, Ed25519 signature over the domain-separated canonical encoding (`id-transport-advertisement/v1` || canonical JSON).
- **Sign/serve:** server-side minting on transport change and per TTL; the `.well-known/id-transport-advertisement` HTTPS handler serving the current signed ad byte-for-byte.
- **Fetch/verify/cache client:** pinned-identity signature verification, highest-sequence-wins across substrates, last-known-good cache with degraded-past-expiry semantics and background revalidation, fetch order per the record (cache → well-known HTTPS → Workers rendezvous by subject hash → DNS bootstrap hints).
- **Sequence durability:** the sequence counter persists beside the identity key and never regresses across restarts.

## Acceptance

- Hostile-substrate test: a substrate serving forged, altered, or replayed (older-sequence) ads fails closed — the client never acts on them (record invariant 2/3).
- Disagreement test: two substrates returning different valid ads resolve to the highest sequence regardless of fetch order.
- Expired-ad test: past-expiry ad is used only as flagged-degraded last-known-good, with revalidation attempted.
- Round-trip test: an ad minted by the server verifies and selects transports in the parent #5671 fallback order.

## Out of scope

- The Cloudflare Workers rendezvous component itself (its own #5671 decomposition ticket) — this issue implements only the client fetch against its blob interface and the self-hosted `.well-known` substrate.
- Broker protocol/framing, CONNECT traversal, latency budgets (sibling #5671 decomposition tickets).

## Links

- Decision record: doc/2026-11-10_rendezvous_discovery_udp_denied_design.md (PR #8213)
- Design ticket: #5793 · Parent: #5671 · Programme: #2056

body:
## Finding (unaddressed PR review comment)

On PR #8025 (`fix(power-guard): detect dead systemd-inhibit child, re-engage loudly`, for issue #6534), CodeRabbit raised a **Major** stability finding that was never fixed or replied to:

> **Keep the child until release is confirmed.** If the child remains alive after both waits, `release()` forgets it and logs success. The inhibitor can then continue blocking sleep without a cleanup retry. Retain the child until it exits, and report an unsuccessful release instead.

- Source PR: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025
- Comment: https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/8025#discussion_r4511572439 (comment id 4511572439)
- Reviewer: coderabbitai[bot], 2026-11-09T10:10:56Z
- Location: `nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`, `Inhibitor.release()` (lines 233–254 at PR head)

## No-response evidence

- The review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` checked 2026-11-10) and has no replies — the CodeRabbit comment is the only comment in the thread.
- PR #8025's head is unchanged since the comment: the only commit is `2a6abfda8194eb944894b5fc647778f82aa977f5` (2026-11-09T10:04:21Z, before the comment). No fix commit followed.
- The PR is still open and the comment is more than 24 hours old, so the open-PR grace rule is expired.
- No existing issue covers this: issue #6534 is the parent dead-child-detection issue that PR #8025 addresses; the release-path defect below is distinct. Searched open/recently-closed issues for power-guard / inhibitor / release on 2026-11-10.

## Still-live evidence (PR head `2a6abfda81`, read 2026-11-10)

`nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py`:

- Line 233–234: `release()` copies `self.proc` to a local and immediately sets `self.proc = None` — the child is forgotten up front.
- Lines 253–254: after `terminate()`, `rc = self._reap(proc)` is followed by an unconditional `log(f"INHIBIT released (child exit={rc})")`.
- `_reap()` (lines 153–175) returns `proc.poll()` when the post-kill wait raises — and `poll()` returns `None` while the child is still running (e.g. stuck in uninterruptible sleep, where even SIGKILL stays pending). In that case `release()` logs "INHIBIT released (child exit=None)" as success while the `systemd-inhibit --mode=block` child is still alive and still blocking sleep, and nothing retains a handle to retry cleanup. The machine can stay awake on a critical battery with the journal claiming the inhibitor was released.

## Acceptance criteria

- `release()` retains the child handle until the child's exit is confirmed (`poll()`/`_reap()` shows a real exit), and clears it / logs successful release only after that confirmation; **or** the current behavior is resolved by a documented decision recorded on this issue.
- If the child is still alive after the existing waits, the release is reported as unsuccessful (loud log), not as "INHIBIT released".
- Regression coverage: a fake child whose `poll()` still returns `None` after terminate + kill + waits exercises the retained-handle / unsuccessful-release path (the PR #8025 review also noted the inhibitor failure paths in `test_power_guard.py` lack such cases).

body:
## Symptom

The opencode-claimant fire at 2026-11-10T14:14Z and again at 14:52Z reached step 4 with
`cap_room` 30/36 and 90+ eligible unbound `handed_off` candidates — and launched **nothing**,
because the Workhorse route's serving leaf rejected every new session on the provider's own
membership ceiling:

```
[code=tier_limit_exceeded] membership concurrency limit exceeded: 11/10 resets 2026-11-10T15:12:00Z
```

Claimant.py has no gate for that. Its four steps (supervision, gate, cap, launch) know about
*undirected* candidates and the *fleet* root-session cap of 36; they know nothing about the
provider's concurrency ceiling, which is 10 on this plan and is already exceeded while the fleet
root count sits at 6–9. So the packet answers "there is room" and the provider answers "there is
not", once per launch.

## Why this is damage, not just a no-op

A launch against the wall is not free:

- **It burns the shared membership rpm.** The same window hit `membership rpm limit exceeded:
  101/100` at 14:40:51Z — the claimant's own burst is what crossed it.
- **It consumes a task attempt and takes a lease on a dead session.** The 13:40:21Z fire launched
  31 sessions; all 31 are `failed`. The 14:39:33Z fire launched 26; 25 of 26 died on their first
  assistant step. Those tasks now carry the attempt and a lease they cannot use, and each
  contributes 4–15 messages to the "terminal outcome recorded" supervision rows, which hide the
  fact that the execution never started.
- **It masks the real blocker.** A `failed` worker session looks like worker-shaped failure in the
  task record; the actual cause is a route-wide capacity wall.

Measured this fire (same server, same route, workers created and prompted exactly as step 4 does):

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| 14:37Z, 8 sessions × 1 prompt | 2 / 8 first steps died on `tier_limit_exceeded` |
| 14:48Z, 4 sessions × 1 prompt | 3 / 4 died |
| 14:51Z, 4 sessions × 1 prompt | 0 / 4 (intermittent, wall not lifted) |
| 14:39Z fire, 26 launches | 25 / 26 worker sessions died |

## What is missing

Step 3 (CAP) counts fleet roots and stops only at 36. Step 4 has no provider-capacity check, so
`launch_step` is willing to create and prompt a worker session whose only possible outcome is the
provider's 400.

## Proposed gate (packet change)

Add a provider-capacity gate between steps 3 and 4, in the same fail-closed spirit as `cap_step`:

1. Before the first launch, and after any launch that returns a `tier_limit_exceeded` body, stop
   launching for the rest of the fire.
2. Record the provider's error **verbatim** in the fire-log line under a `provider_wall` key, with
   the route and serving leaf, so the record distinguishes "no candidates" from "nowhere to run
   them".
3. Do **not** consume an attempt when the worker session's first assistant step dies on
   `tier_limit_exceeded`: the launch never became work. (Today the task pays an attempt for it.)

Until that gate exists, the claimant's fire-time behaviour on a walled route is documented in the
fire log: candidates and cap are reported, launches are zero, and the verbatim provider error is
carried in the same line.

## Related

- #8039 — no single-instance lock or bounded pool; several claimant fires were live at once during
  this window, which multiplies the same provider pressure.
- #8038 — slice-1 fire implementation diverges from the packet spec (audit fields among them).
- #8086 — Workhorse route: every leg quota-walled at once (closed; this is the per-plan membership
  ceiling, a narrower wall).
- #5016 — the fleet cap accounting problem.

body:
# id: DEVICE_OPS hardening follow-ups from PR #8144 review (sync delivery, ingest atomicity, expiry cleanup, upgrade recovery)

Source: CodeRabbit review of PR #8144 (task 14249, issue #5656). The PR's packet acceptance is met and verified by targeted tests; the four findings below are adjacent hardening the review surfaced. Each was dispositioned as follow-up work at merge time rather than expanding PR #8144.

1. **Range sync does not deliver device-operation bodies** (PR #8144 thread 4522516137, ingest.rs ~291-308). A fresh peer receiving an Admin-device grant through range sync stores only the header and never populates DEVICE_OPS, so its default view can retain a claim a directly-ingesting peer hides. Sync must deliver the committed device-operation body and run it through the receiving peer's ingest flow.
2. **DEVICE_OPS rows leak when held events expire** (thread 4522516148, ingest.rs ~309). A stream of signed device events with missing dependencies can repeatedly fill and expire the waiting pool; each expiry leaves a DEVICE_OPS row, growing disk use beyond the waiting-pool limit. Delete the row when a held event expires or is dropped; keep rows for stored events and for held events that are released.
3. **Device operation is not written in the ingest transaction** (thread 4522516157, ingest.rs ~313-338). If the process stops or the second write fails after ingest_event commits, the device operation is lost: a missing grant blocks an authorized clear, a missing revocation can let a revoked device hide another author's claim. Write the device operation in the ingest transaction before resolution, including duplicate and waiting paths.
4. **Upgraded stores have no DEVICE_OPS rows for pre-change grants** (thread 4522516168, mod.rs ~668-675). Admin-device clears can leave claims visible until the original bodies are supplied again. Provide a recovery path from verified grant/revocation bodies, or explicitly report when recovery is not possible.

Acceptance: each item either lands with tests covering the named scenario, or is closed with evidence the scenario cannot occur.

body:
## Problem

Follow-on from #2937 (acceptance 4, verified open at current main 2026-11-10, HEAD 9d7f54fda6):

A `fleet queue claim` that finds nothing returns only `{"task": null}` with exit 5 (the #5486 contract in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/client.rs`, `claim_output` / `NO_CLAIM_EXIT`). That is distinguishable from success, but it names no reason: a worker whose gate saw queued work cannot tell whether the queue is empty, every queued row is at its attempt cap, rows are not yet due (`not_before`), or rows were quarantined by the claim guard.

Health already computes the discriminating counts (`at_cap_queued`, #6528), so the data exists - the claim path just does not surface it at the moment it matters.

## Scoped fix

- Broker `/claim` handler: when the claim returns no row, attach per-queue counts to the response envelope: `queued`, `at_cap_queued`, `queued_not_yet_due`, `parked_due`.
- Client `claim_output`: print those counts to stderr as the no-claim diagnostic, while keeping the stdout contract unchanged (`{"task": null}`, exit 5) and its existing unit tests green.
- Add a unit test: null row + counts envelope produces the diagnostic naming the at-cap count.

## Acceptance

- [ ] `fleet queue claim` against a queue whose queued rows are all at cap prints a diagnostic naming the attempt cap as the reason (stderr is fine).
- [ ] Existing claim output contract tests (#5486 / #5444) still pass; `cargo test -p fleet-queue` green.

Found by: lane code-m, task 14479, findings on #2937 (2026-11-10).

body:
## Problem

The atlas-search Rust gate added by #6330 surfaced a flaky test in CI: `cli_shard_fanout_matches_python_vector_results` failed on run 42513932438 with

```
thread 'cli_shard_fanout_matches_python_vector_results' panicked at crates/atlas-search/tests/cli_parity.rs:382:9:
case vector_default: exit Some(2), stderr: atlas-search: ATLAS_SEARCH_QVEC_FILE: bad JSON vector in /tmp/atlas-cli-qvec-5050.json: EOF while parsing a value at line 1 column 0
```

## Cause

`qvec_file()` in `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-search/tests/cli_parity.rs` names its temp file with only `std::process::id()`:

```rust
let p = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("atlas-cli-qvec-{}.json", std::process::id()));
std::fs::write(&p, serde_json::to_string(&exp["qvec_raw"]).unwrap()).expect("write qvec");
```

Every test in the binary shares that one path (cargo runs tests in parallel threads), and `run_bin()` rewrites it for each child process. Two tests writing/reading concurrently leave a truncated file for the other's child, which then fails with `EOF while parsing a value`.

## Fix

Give each call its own path (pid + atomic counter, or a `tempfile::NamedTempFile` kept alive for the call), and/or write via a temp file + rename. Test-only change.

## Why separate

#6330 scopes itself to CI wiring and explicitly excludes changes to `pkgs/atlas-search` Rust sources; this is a pre-existing test race the new gate exposed, not a defect in the workflow.

Discovered while finishing PR #6591 (issue #6330), 2026-11-10.

body:
# mcpx e2e shard-packer tests keep NamedTemporaryFile open while reopening its path — fails on Windows

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7897 (mcpx(ci): guard malformed e2e timing seeds), Copilot review comments [4508758212](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7897#discussion_r4508758212), [4508758233](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7897#discussion_r4508758233), [4508758244](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7897#discussion_r4508758244), [4508758252](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7897#discussion_r4508758252), and [4508758267](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7897#discussion_r4508758267) (Copilot, 2026-11-09T01:50:15Z–01:50:16Z, `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/tests/test_e2e_shard_packer.py:33,65,89,100,136`) — one finding repeated at five call sites:

> `NamedTemporaryFile` is kept open while `load_weights()` (and the subprocess in the CLI test) tries to open the same path. This is a known portability issue on Windows (file locking can cause PermissionError / open failures). Consider writing to a temp path that is closed before reading (e.g., `TemporaryDirectory()` + `open()`), or using `NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)` and explicitly closing it before calling `load_weights()` / running the subprocess (with a `finally` cleanup).

## No-response evidence
- No replies in any of the five comment threads; all five review threads are unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-10: threads for comments 4508758212, 4508758233, 4508758244, 4508758252, and 4508758267 each have `isResolved: false`).
- PR #7897 head is unchanged at `dc84f22fcf9978483f0607956a2cfc4dbf6f3631` since the comments; no fix commit followed them. The finding is past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs (comments 2026-11-09T01:50:15Z; grace expired 2026-11-10T01:50:15Z).
- Issue search (open and closed) by PR number, file path, and keywords found no existing issue covering this finding.
- The PR's other review finding (Codex, CI-venue wiring) was responded to by dezren39 and is already tracked by issue #7795 — it is not part of this filing.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw read at head `dc84f22fcf` agrees — the pattern is present verbatim at every flagged site in `pkgs/mcpx/scripts/tests/test_e2e_shard_packer.py`:
- Lines 30–33 (`load_seed` helper): `with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w", suffix=".json") as seed:` … `return packer.load_weights(seed.name, …)` inside the `with` block.
- Lines 62–65, 86–89, and 97–100: the same open-while-reopening pattern in three more tests.
- Lines 122–139 (CLI test): `with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode="w+", suffix=".out") as output:` is passed as `--github-output` to a subprocess and then read/seeked while still open.

## Acceptance criteria
- No test in `test_e2e_shard_packer.py` reopens (directly or via subprocess) a path whose `NamedTemporaryFile` is still open: write-close-read via a temp directory/path, or `delete=False` + explicit close with cleanup, at all five sites (including the CLI output file).
- The shard-packer test suite still passes.
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

Filed by the pr-comment-review job (run 2026-11-09 19:54 CST) under the queue cutover: labels applied at filing, standard agent note posted after filing, and a repo-task/v1 triage packet (kind: triage, priority 30) enqueued on repo-health-code-pilot.

# Android client design: a consumer-specific grant denial suspends the provider capability for everyone

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7826 (docs(id): design native Android client (#5780)), Codex review comment [4508024010](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7826#discussion_r4508024010) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T22:16:30Z, `doc/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client/2026-11-08T22-06-00Z_design_id_android_client.md:125`):

> Keep consumer grant denials scoped to the invocation. When one consumer has an expired, revoked, or missing ID grant, this rule suspends the provider capability in discovery even if other consumers still have valid grants and the Android permission remains available. That turns a consumer-specific authorization failure into unavailability for authorized consumers. The consumed #5903 decision distinguishes these cases: D3(2) denies the individual invocation, while D3(3) suspends dependent capabilities on Android permission revocation. Restrict capability-wide suspension to provider/platform availability changes and keep consumer grant failures scoped to the affected authorization.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-10: the single thread containing comment 4508024010 has `isResolved: false`).
- PR #7826 head is unchanged at `2150c436a90c54e34ea71e71e360a1fc270db96e` since the comment; no fix commit followed it. The finding is past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs (comment 2026-11-08T22:16:30Z).
- Issue search (open and closed) by PR number, file path, and keywords found no existing issue covering this finding.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw read at head `2150c436a9` agrees:
- Design doc line 125 (§5.1): "Denial or revocation by either gate stops the invocation and suspends the affected provider capability in discovery" — a per-consumer ID-grant denial still triggers capability-wide suspension in discovery.
- Line 131 (§5.2) separately and correctly scopes suspension to Android permission revocation / provider shutdown, showing the design already distinguishes the platform case the #5903 D3(3) rule covers — line 125 does not make the same distinction for the ID-grant gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- The design record scopes consumer ID-grant denials (expired, revoked, or missing grant for one consumer) to the affected invocation/authorization, and restricts capability-wide suspension in discovery to provider/platform availability changes (Android permission revocation, provider shutdown, leaving the declared execution envelope), consistent with #5903 D3(2)/D3(3).
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

body:
## Symptom

The `stale-pr-warden` scheduled job still reads the fleet queue from the frozen Supabase copy (`agent.tasks` via the old schema name) for its queue read-back / dedupe checks. The fleet queue migrated to Turso (`fleet-queue` database) on 2026-11-06, and the Supabase copy froze at that migration (last completion 2026-11-06 18:06 UTC). The warden's writes go through the `fleet queue` client (which reads Turso), but its read side still speaks the old schema — so its dedupe/read-back checks run against a queue state that is days stale and growing staler.

## Evidence

- Daily token usage check-in fix run, 2026-11-09 (Reports chat, completed 23:26Z): the sibling sweep that repointed `daily-token-usage-checkin` from Supabase to Turso reported verbatim: "`stale-pr-warden` still names `agent.tasks` for its queue read-back/dedupe checks (its writes go through the `fleet queue` client, but the read side still speaks the old schema name)" — and recorded it as "listed, not changed (out of scope)" / "flagged but left alone".
- The same fix proved the Turso source live: `fleet-queue` Turso database, 9,271 done rows, freshest completion 2026-11-09T22:16:57Z, versus the Supabase copy frozen 2026-11-06 18:06 UTC.
- Catcher search 2026-11-09T23:45Z: no existing issue covers the stale-pr-warden Supabase read (GitHub search for "stale-pr-warden supabase" in this repo returned no results).

## Scope

- Repoint `stale-pr-warden`'s queue read-back / dedupe reads from Supabase `agent.tasks` to the Turso `fleet-queue` `tasks` table, using the same pattern the 2026-11-09 daily-token-usage-checkin fix used (repo copy first, then `cron.update`, read-back proof).
- Do not change the warden's schedule, scope, or write path.

## Acceptance check

- The job's live definition (cron read-back) names the Turso `fleet-queue` source for its queue reads and contains no `agent.tasks` queue read.
- One warden run completes its queue read-back/dedupe step against Turso data (a completion timestamp newer than 2026-11-06 18:06 UTC is visible in its read path).

## Refs

- Dropped-thread catcher run 2026-11-09T23:31Z (this catch: the defect was flagged in the Reports chat 2026-11-09 and explicitly left alone as out of scope for that fix).
- Sibling fix: `daily-token-usage-checkin` repointed to Turso 2026-11-09, committed on origin as 2523d5144256ad5d445fc41fa9311b45ae00847a.

# id DoS catalogue: deadline scenarios cannot fit the fixed 30s attack profile (SSH inactivity timeout is 10 minutes)

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7738 (docs(id): record DoS scenario catalogue for #5892), Codex review comment [4506648822](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7738#discussion_r4506648822) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T15:00:03Z, `doc/2026-11-08_decision_id5892_dos_scenario_catalogue.md:84`):

Ending the fixture within 60 seconds cannot observe that timeout, while closing the attacking clients after 30 seconds tests client cleanup instead of server expiry. Explicitly exempt deadline-bound scenarios from the fixed attack duration, or specify a supported clock/deadline override so this assertion can actually be exercised.
