# Atlas golden-set design: master schema omits `runs`, but EvalData requires saved rankings

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7656 (docs(atlas): golden-set builder + eval gate design record (#6046)), Codex review comment [4506026826](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7656#discussion_r4506026826) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T11:23:52Z, `doc/2026-11-08T10-45-00Z_design_atlas_golden_set_eval_gate/2026-11-08T10-45-00Z_design_atlas_golden_set_eval_gate.md:97`):

> Specify how fresh baseline and candidate rankings enter evaluation. The proposed master schema contains no `runs`, so stripping provenance and remapping queries/qrels cannot produce the promised consumable evaluation input. `EvalData` requires saved rankings in `runs` (`pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/eval.rs`), and the harness explicitly scores supplied rankings without executing retrieval. As specified, compilation would either produce an input rejected for missing `runs` or require an unspecified external input before the gate could measure any retrieval change. Define how baseline and candidate rankings are generated and supplied to compilation so the gate evaluates the changed retrieval behavior rather than absent or stale rankings.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-09: the single thread containing comment 4506026826 has `isResolved: false`).
- PR #7656 head is unchanged at `11c0128c00c3c1dc6011c4760c6e5d3763c882a5` since the comment; no fix commit followed it. The Codex review summary on the PR records `has_unresolved_findings: true`. The finding is past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw reads at head `11c0128c00` agree:
- `pkgs/atlas-search/crates/atlas-core/src/eval.rs:246-254`: `pub struct EvalData` includes `pub runs: Vec<Run>`; `evaluate()` (line 565+) scores the supplied runs and the module never executes retrieval.
- The design doc's master schema example (section 3.1) contains queries with `qrels` but no `runs`, and the compilation step (section 3.2) only maps `doc_id` and query fields — it never generates or supplies `runs`.

## Acceptance criteria
- The design record specifies how fresh baseline and candidate rankings are generated and supplied to compilation so the emitted `atlas-eval/v1` input contains the `runs` that `EvalData` requires, OR the compilation contract is changed so the gate executes retrieval itself.
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

# Atlas source-mark grammar: token ranges exclude ASCII letters, rejecting the spec's own examples

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7629 (docs(atlas): source-mark grammar spec for composite provenance marks, #6044), Codex review comment [4505856173](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7629#discussion_r4505856173) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T10:18:21Z, `doc/2026-11-08T10-17-00Z_design_source_mark_grammar/2026-11-08T10-17-00Z_design_source_mark_grammar.md:67`):

> Include ASCII letters in the token character ranges. For host marks such as the documented `system@atlas-laptop@…` and `chat@ses_…@…` examples, these character ranges exclude every uppercase and lowercase ASCII letter (`0x41–0x5A` and `0x61–0x7A`). A parser implementing §3 therefore rejects all the named host-mark examples. Define the token character set to include letters while excluding the `@`, `:`, and `#` delimiters required by V3.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-09).
- PR #7629 head is unchanged at `aac41eefd44cec7480e1e7dca4263802ba1b7678` since the comment; no fix commit followed it. Past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Raw read of the spec at head `aac41eefd4`: §2 examples include `system@atlas-laptop@2026-11-04T12:00:00Z:…` and `chat@ses_2b2eab662ffeRZGv4MoA62kl6A@…` (letters throughout), while the §3 EBNF `token-char` ranges still omit the ASCII letter ranges — a parser built to §3 rejects the §2 examples.

## Acceptance criteria
- The token character set includes ASCII letters while still excluding the `@`, `:`, `#` delimiters, OR the examples are changed to marks the grammar accepts — spec and examples must agree.
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

# Aggregator: /api/board.json limits the done strip before applying view filters

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7753 (fix(aggregator): bound /api/board.json to the board the page shows, #5082), Codex review comment [4506893015](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7753#discussion_r4506893015) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T16:19:04Z, `pm-stack/aggregator/src/server.ts:1900`):

> Apply view filters before limiting the done strip. When a view's matching done cards fall outside the newest 100 cards globally, this truncation removes them before the view filter runs. For example, `/api/board.json?repo=owner/repo` can return no done cards even though `/board?repo=owner/repo` displays recent completions: the HTML handler filters the board first and lets `renderBoardBody` cap the filtered result. Filter the policy-eligible board using the full item lookup before applying the strip limit, then restrict the returned items to the selected cards.

# Currency gateway: registration `cap` cannot round-trip large values through CBOR

## Finding (from PR review)
On PR #7650 (feat(id): add currency gateway request envelope, #2319), Codex review comment [4506000711](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/7650#discussion_r4506000711) (chatgpt-codex-connector[bot], 2026-11-08T11:13:36Z, `pkgs/id/src/currency/gateway.rs:243`):

> Encode the registration cap with the fixed-width u128 adapter. For a registration whose cap exceeds `u64::MAX`, this bare `u128` cannot round-trip through the gateway's CBOR protocol: CBOR integers stop at `u64`, and `check_value` explicitly rejects the tags needed for larger integers. Unlike `client_request_id` and the amount fields, `cap` omits `#[serde(with = "u128_bytes")]`, so otherwise valid large-cap registrations cannot be signed and decoded successfully. Apply the same fixed-width adapter here and cover registration in the full-width round-trip test.

## No-response evidence
- No replies in the comment thread; the review thread is unresolved (GraphQL `reviewThreads` verified 2026-11-09).
- PR #7650 head is unchanged at `abef5c07e7bcd45b92210dd659f6480f717ec7e5` since the comment; no fix commit followed it. The finding is now past the 24-hour grace period for open PRs.

## Still-live evidence (current PR head)
Two independent raw reads of `pkgs/id/src/currency/gateway.rs` at head `abef5c07e7` agree: line 243 is a bare `pub cap: u128,` (doc: "Finite v1 supply cap, in minor units") with no `u128_bytes` serde adapter.

## Acceptance criteria
- `cap` uses the same fixed-width `u128_bytes` adapter as the other u128 fields, OR the cap is explicitly bounded to u64 range with a documented, enforced validation error.
- The full-width round-trip test covers registration with a cap above `u64::MAX`.
- Resolving by a documented decision on this issue is also acceptable.

title: opencode-claimant: fire log cannot distinguish a failed queue read from an empty queue, or say why a bind failed

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Problem

Two fire-log gaps in `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` make a fire's outcome
impossible to reconstruct after the fact. Both were hit live on 2026-11-09.

### 1. A failed queue read is logged as "no candidates"

`gate_step()` runs `poll.py` and looks at `candidates`. `poll.fetch_claimed_rows()`
returns `[]` on any broker failure (it prints a warning to stderr). `run_poll()`
captures stderr and only checks the exit code, so a transient broker read failure is
indistinguishable from a genuinely empty queue, and the fire logs:

```json
{"reason": "no_candidates"}
```

Observed: the 12:17:51Z fire logged `no_candidates` while `poll.py` run minutes
before and after returned four `handed_off` candidates for the same queue
(`13723`, `13748`, `13813`, `14120`). Nothing launched either way (cap_room was 0),
but the log states a fact that was not established.

### 2. `bind_failed` discards the error, so a repeat failure is undiagnosable

In `launch_step()` a failed bind deletes the freshly created session and records
only `{"reason": "bind_failed"}`. `bind_result.stderr` — which is where
`bind_repo_task_lane_session` says exactly which precondition failed (task not
claimed with a live lease / no lane ledger row / already bound to session X /
task does not exist) — is dropped.

Observed: task `8750` hit `bind_failed` at the 10:06:00Z fire **and** again at the
12:29:18Z fire. Each attempt created and deleted a session, and the log cannot say
whether the lease had lapsed, or the ledger still held an old session id. The same
happened to `13932` at 10:06:00Z.

## Why it matters

- The fire log is the claimant's only audit trail and the thing the next reader
  (human or agent) reasons from. Saying "no candidates" when the queue could not be
  read is a false statement about the fleet.
- A bind loop burns one session creation + one DELETE per fire, forever, with no
  recorded cause; the fixing move differs per cause (reclaim with the atomic
  compare-and-clear for a stale ledger binding vs. wait/let the lane re-claim for a
  lapsed lease).

## Suggested fix

- `poll.py`: report per-queue read success (e.g. `queues[q]["read_ok"]`), and have
  `gate_step()` log `queue_read_failed` skips when a queue could not be read rather
  than concluding "no candidates".
- `claimant.py`: put the bind error text in the skip record
  (`{"reason": "bind_failed", "error": <first line of stderr>}`), truncated and
  credential-free.

Not blocking: both are logging-only; launch safety is unchanged.

Found while running the opencode lane claimant on the laptop (#3026 slice 1).

title: opencode-claimant(claimant.py): no single-instance lock or bounded pool — a live fire overlapped another fire 11 s apart

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: epic/opencode-platform
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## What

The claimant packet and the deployed `claimant.py` disagree about concurrency control:

- Packet: "claimant.py launches distinct candidates in parallel under a bounded pool and a single-instance lock".
- Deployed `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/claimant.py` at `origin/main` `9fbddc76c6`: a sequential `for candidate in unbound_opencode:` loop, no file lock, no pool (`grep -n 'flock\|lock\|ThreadPool\|max_workers'` → nothing). `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/claimant.lock` exists on disk and is never used by the code.

## Evidence from the 2026-11-09T12:22Z fire (live)

`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/fires.jsonl`, five consecutive fires in six minutes from more than one entry point:

| line | timestamp (UTC) | cap_room | launched | wrapper `fire-run-live-*.out` present |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 423 | 2026-11-09T12:16:53Z | 0 | 0 | yes (12:16:51) |
| 424 | 2026-11-09T12:17:51Z | 0 | 0 | no |
| 425 | 2026-11-09T12:20:39Z | 0 | 0 | no |
| 426 | 2026-11-09T12:22:28Z | 0 | 0 | yes (12:22:26, this fire) |
| 427 | 2026-11-09T12:22:39Z | 0 | 0 | no |

Line 426 and line 427 are 11 s apart: two invocations overlapped. The entries with no wrapper output are ad-hoc session runs of the same script; the ones with output are the `*/10`-minute OpenChamber scheduled task (`f1b4a33b-14d5-4a69-9ad6-d221e42e3ac9`).

## Why it matters

`cap_step()` computes `cap_room = 36 - active_roots` once, and `launch_step()` then decrements its own local copy. Two overlapping fires each start from the same `cap_room`; the atomic `bind` keeps the *same* task from being double-bound, but nothing stops two fires from spending the same free slots (active roots above 36 — the exact condition the cap exists to prevent) or from racing one candidate, where the loser wastes a create→bind-fail→delete cycle (the recurring `bind_failed` skips already seen in lines 420/421).

Both overlapping fires saw `cap_room 0` this time, so nothing was harmed. A 47 s launching fire (line 421) overlaps a scheduled fire easily.

## Proposal

1. `flock` (LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) on `~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/claimant.lock` around the whole fire; a second fire exits early with a distinguishable fire-log reason (`already_running`), not `no_candidates`.
2. Either a bounded `ThreadPoolExecutor` as the packet describes, or — simpler and matching the observed wave behaviour — keep the sequential loop and record the packet change. Whichever lands, packet and code must state the same thing.
3. While in there: pass the discovered candidate list to `log_fire` so `candidates_seen` is real (currently hardcoded `[]` on every fire — related to #7732).

## Scope note

Slice 1 of #3026 (claim/bind/launch/record). Fail-closed both times: no session was created, bound or deleted while this defect was live.

body:
## Problem

The root `just-recipes.json` — the file `lib/default.nix` reads to generate `nix run .#<recipe>` apps — has no drift guard. A recipe added to `root.just` without running `just just-recipes` silently gets no nix app, and a changed doc/parameter silently keeps the old description. The `pkgs/id` copy of this exact file has a guard (`just-recipes-drift`, from #2729); the root copy does not.

## Evidence (verified on origin/main `d71ad6057e`, laptop worktree)

- Consumer: `lib/default.nix:641-653` — `justRecipes = builtins.fromJSON (builtins.readFile ../just-recipes.json)`, then `publicRecipes` filters private/`default`; the comment above it says: "To add a new nix app: add a recipe to root.just, run `just lockfiles`, and the app appears automatically". Nothing enforces the second step.
- Guard gap: repo-wide grep for `just --dump` returns exactly one hit — `pkgs/id/scripts/just-recipes-check.sh:13`, which `cd`s to `pkgs/id` and certifies only the `pkgs/id` file. No script, workflow step, or flake check touches the root file. (`id-check.yml` runs one job per check in `.github/scripts/id-pr-checks.txt`, whose `just-recipes-drift` entry maps to the pkgs/id script.)
- Recurrence, not hypothetical: 6 commits changed `root.just` without touching `just-recipes.json` (`7c2c8191ff`, `ac91b09acd`, `076da3a68e`, `19597b5262`, `051d8e19a7`, `30623a69f7`). `7c2c8191ff` ("add rebuild recipe") states it explicitly: "just-recipes.json intentionally NOT regenerated here: regeneration embeds the generating checkout absolute path (source field) and the committed file is already stale" — i.e. past drift was worked around by skipping regeneration, which is exactly what a guard would have caught at review time.
- Current state is clean (verified this run: `just --dump --dump-format json` at the root, projected to recipe presence/doc/parameters/dependencies/private + alias targets exactly as the id guard does → 35 recipes, zero diff). So this is a missing-guard filing, not live drift.

## Why it matters

The failure mode is silent omission: `nix run .#<new-recipe>` fails with "no such app" (or an old doc string renders) while `just <new-recipe>` works, so the author who added the recipe never sees the break. #2729 already proved this shape bites on the pkgs/id copy (`crash-gate-sampled`'s doc went stale on main).

## Suggested fix shape (triage call)

- A root variant of `pkgs/id/scripts/just-recipes-check.sh`: anchor to the repo root, `just --dump --dump-format json`, project out `source` (absolute path, per the `7c2c8191ff` note) and recipe bodies (just-version serialization drift, per the id script's `#2729` comment), diff the semantic projection.
- Wire it where it runs: either a `scripts-test.yml`-style explicit step (following the `test_check_provider_retirement_gate.py` pattern from #7789) or the check-each mechanism — but note the root regeneration recipe also runs `biome format --write` (`root.just:102-104`), so the guard must compare against the formatted output or normalize first.
- Dedupe: #2729 (CLOSED — delivered the pkgs/id guard only), #6957 (CLOSED — that guard's CWD anchoring), #3566 (CLOSED — preserved branch). Nothing tracks the root file.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A check exists that fails when root `just-recipes.json`'s semantic projection (recipes + alias targets) differs from `just --dump` of the root justfile.
- [ ] The check runs in CI (workflow step or flake check), not just as documentation.
- [ ] The `source`/formatting normalization is pinned by a test, so the guard itself does not false-positive across machines or just versions.

README documents only the manual `python3 -I ...` invocation.
- No workflow references `queue-reconcile` or `test_check_coverage`; `check_coverage` appears nowhere in `.github/test-suite-registry.json`; on-disk-vs-registry diff confirms the file is unregistered.

Suggested shape: run it in scripts-test.yml alongside the other `scripts/tests` unittest discovers (or a fleet workflow), plus a registry row; the #6188 ratchet then guards the file.

body:

Evidence (verified this run at origin/main 1e0860e43d, clean worktree):
- `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/v2/picker.test.ts` (9 tests) added in 884ad6fbf5 (2026-11-08 17:15 CST) — AFTER the registry contract f9dfb4cfa5 (same day 08:03). Header invocation: `bun test plugin/opencode/v2/picker.test.ts`.
- Registry row `mcpx.plugin.v2` names exactly 5 files (permission/sampling/tool-filter/tools/v2) with venue null; `picker` appears nowhere in `.github/test-suite-registry.json`. No workflow references `plugin/opencode/v2/` (mcpx.yml only invokes `bun test plugin/opencode/mcpx/`, the v1 dir).

- Dedupe: open-issue search for `picker` finds only #6092 (the 61-test/5-file v2 suite — this file is the 6th, added later), #2841 (parent feature), #1858. Nothing tracks this file.

Why it matters: the 9 tests pin the #2841 item-3 picker contract — a selection counts only when applyChoice ran with the picked target, and every failure path (bad index, no permission domain, rejected assert) must leave applyChoice uncalled. A regression in `picker.ts` that changes the selected daemon (or applies a cancelled pick) is currently caught nowhere.

Suggested shape: name `picker.test.ts` in the `mcpx.plugin.v2` registry row (or widen to the v2 dir) and give the v2 suite a venue — ideally together with #6092's wiring, with the #6188 ratchet covering the row so a 7th file cannot slip the same way.

Acceptance criteria:
- [ ] `mcpx.plugin.v2` registry row names `picker.test.ts` (or equivalent coverage of the file).

body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts` (12 tests, ~72k assertions: PBT invariants + MBT ladder model + acceptance fixtures + disk round-trip) is the only verification of `pm-stack/exporters/src/watchdog-state.ts` — the decision layer of the quota watchdog core (failure classes + repair ladder), landed 2026-11-08 in #6032 (now merged; #6032 CLOSED 2026-11-09).

It runs nowhere:

- No workflow step invokes it. `grep -rn "watchdog-state" --exclude-dir=.git .` hits only the test's own import, and `pm-stack/exporters/README.md` (which documents the manual invocation `cd pm-stack/aggregator && bun test ../exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts` — proof the authors know bare `bun test` doesn't reach it).
- `pm-stack/exporters/` has no `package.json`; the root `package.json` has no workspaces/scripts, so no aggregate `bun test` reaches it. `bun test` in `pm-stack/aggregator` scans only that directory.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` has no entry for it (`quota-exporters` covers only the three other exporter suites: opencode-usage, cloudflare, supabase).
- `pm-stack-tests.yml` trigger paths (`push` + `pull_request`) list `external-comms`, `opencode-claimant`, `opencode-usage-export`, `cloudflare-export`, `supabase-export` — `pm-stack/exporters/**` is absent, so even a wired-up step would never fire on changes to the watchdog.

Verified on origin/main `c2283a57` in a clean worktree. Suite passes on the laptop:

```
bun test ../exporters/test/watchdog-state.test.ts  (from pm-stack/aggregator)
12 pass, 0 fail, 71766 expect() calls
```

## Why it matters

This is the same already-fixed class: #6084 (three quota-exporter suites ran nowhere → wired into pm-stack-tests.yml), #6344 (meta-exporter suite runs nowhere), #7681 (pm-stack-tests triggers omit dispatch/grist/scripts). The watchdog decision layer drives repair escalation; a regression here passes CI silently — exactly the failure mode #6084 fixed for the sibling exporters.

## Suggested fix shape

Follow the #6090/#5951/#6217 pattern already in `pm-stack-tests.yml`: a step asserting `test/watchdog-state.test.ts` exists, then `bun test` on the explicit path (the README's invocation), plus `pm-stack/exporters/**` in the workflow's `push`/`pull_request` paths, plus a registry venue entry. Small, mechanical, precedent-covered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A CI job runs `watchdog-state.test.ts` on every PR touching `pm-stack/exporters/**` and fails if the file is missing or any test fails.
- [ ] `pm-stack-tests.yml` (or another workflow) lists `pm-stack/exporters/**` in its trigger paths.
- [ ] `.github/test-suite-registry.json` records the suite's venue.

body:
Found by queue lane code-l (task 14224 bookkeeping correction, 2026-11-09) while verifying the #7686 fix: this config test fails on the laptop on clean main, pre-existing and unrelated to #7686.

## Evidence

- Command: `go test ./internal/config/ -count=1 -run TestServerKeysAnotherHostWritesAreRecordedNotRefused` (pkgs/mcpx, Go 1.26 on the laptop)
- Result on clean pre-fix main `c2283a5721`: FAIL — `config_test.go:212: a merged load lost the ignored key: []`
- Result on merged main `e4e867473f98` (includes PR #8006): identical FAIL. The #7686 change touches only `internal/testsupport/gen/registry_test.go`, a different package's test file, so it cannot cause this.
- The full `internal/config` package run fails with this as the failing test; `internal/testsupport/gen` passes in both TMPDIR modes.

## Likely shape (not yet root-caused)

The test isolates `HOME`/`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` to a temp dir and loads from a nested `proj/` dir — the same isolation shape #7686 just fixed in the gen property test. Its own comment (config_test.go, above the test) already names the risk: "a stale key in a real ~/.mcpx.json would fail this test on that machine and nowhere else." `config.SearchPathFrom` walks up from the working directory past the isolated root, so host config files on the ancestor path (real home when TMPDIR lives under it, plus `/etc/mcpx/config.json`) enter the chain on a developer machine but not in CI.

## Acceptance

- `TestServerKeysAnotherHostWritesAreRecordedNotRefused` passes on a machine whose real mcpx config exists (laptop), and still passes in CI.
- The leak path is named in the fix, as in #7686.

title: fleet(outbox): prepared-entry backlog grows faster than the 10-per-run drain — 535 waiting, notes land hours late or drop superseded

labels.name: epic/fleet-orchestration
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
## Symptom
The fleet action outbox (hidden_files/action-outbox.md, protocol of 2026-10-28) is growing far faster than the action-outbox-processor drains it. Prepared entries awaiting posting: 243 at ~2026-11-08 21:50 CST, ~632 pending reported by the processor at 2026-11-09 00:12 CST, and 535 entries at status "prepared" verified by direct count in action-outbox.md at 2026-11-09 06:47Z. The processor drains 10 entries per 30-minute run (20/hour), so even with zero new inflow the current backlog needs ~27 hours to clear; with current inflow it never clears.

## Evidence
- Outbox processor chat report, 2026-11-09 00:12 CST run: "Heads-up on volume: ~632 prepared entries still remain pending, up from 243 a few runs ago — producers are adding to the outbox much faster than the 10-per-run drain."
- Direct verification by dropped-thread-catcher, 2026-11-09T06:47Z: `grep -c '^- status: prepared' action-outbox.md` = 535 (672 OB entries total in the file).
- Inflow driver, from the pending entries themselves: lane notes are prepared "without a live attempt" because the gh user-token route is verified blocked by the GitHub secondary rate limit (HTTP 403) and the developing.today App route is verified down (fleet_paperwork: no installation for owner 'developing-today' — that failure is tracked on #7930). Every lane handoff/park note therefore lands in the outbox instead of posting directly.
- Consequence: agent notes that carry handoff, park, and blocked evidence for queue tasks are delayed by hours to days; some are dropped as superseded before they ever post, so issue timelines lose the record the outbox protocol exists to preserve.

## Scope
- The drain side: action-outbox-processor's per-run batch (currently 10) and any safe way to raise effective throughput without tripping the GitHub secondary rate limit harder (e.g. adaptive batch sized to recent limit headroom, prioritising notes whose tasks are still active over stale handoffs).
- The inflow side: producer behaviour while both posting routes are degraded — dedupe/supersede at prepare time (a note whose task already has a newer posted note should not be queued), and expiry for notes whose task reached a terminal state.
- Out of scope: fixing the App-route installation lookup itself (#7930 owns it) and changing the processor's 30-minute cadence.

## Acceptance check
- Prepared-entry count in action-outbox.md trends down across consecutive processor runs and reaches a small steady-state (tens, not hundreds) while lane work continues.
- No prepared entry waits more than 2 hours to post or be dropped-as-superseded with the reason recorded.
- The processor's per-run report states inflow, drained, dropped, and remaining counts so the trend is visible without a manual count.

## Refs
- Filed by dropped-thread-catcher, 2026-11-09 run (chat evidence: Action outbox processor chat, 2026-11-09 00:12 CST run).
- Related: #7930 (App route down — inflow driver), #3706 (creation outbox design), action-outbox protocol (2026-10-28, Drew's directive).

body:
Follow-up from the #3068 Phase 3 closing audit (evidence: doc/2026-11-09_audit_3068-phase3-closing.md, on PR for #3069). The audit inventoried every parse-then-dereference boundary in bin/, scripts/, pkgs/, and pm-stack's non-aggregator handlers. The sites below are boundaries the #3068 phases missed and the same rule covers — validate the shape you deref, at the boundary, before any side effect; absence is not emptiness. Each item is its own small fix; do them as separate small PRs, in roughly this risk order:

1. bin/sync-models.mjs:127 — models.dev response read as `(await res.json()).response?.models || {}`: absence-as-emptiness (corollary 3). A shape drift reads as "zero models" instead of an error.
2. pkgs/id/web response casts: src/main.ts (8 .json() sites, several `as {…}` casts), src/world.ts:433,566, src/home.ts:105 — first-party server responses dereferenced by cast with no shape parser (contrast image-browser.ts / image-upload.ts in the same package, which use named parsers — the compliant pattern).
3. pm-stack/dispatch: src/github.ts casts ({id}, {token, expires_at}, {number, html_url}), src/queue.ts:119,136 TaskRow[] casts, src/auth.ts:109 response deref.
4. pm-stack/projector/src/github.ts:191 — generic helper returns `(await res.json()) as T` (contrast its own unknown-first sites in the same file); src/server.ts:252,346 inbound req.json() bodies.
5. pkgs/atlas-search/worker: inbound casts src/index.ts:75, src/cache_do.ts:82; response casts src/index.ts:92,113.
6. pkgs/cold-store-reaper/worker/src/index.js:108 inbound request.json() job deref; :159 resp.json() payload (dist/worker.js is the built copy).
7. pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts:463,476,537 — `(await res.json()) as T` / `as Resolution` on daemon responses.
8. bin/codedb-bridge.mjs:250 response parse raced then dereferenced; bin/provider-catalog-sync.mjs:525 res.json() returned to dereferencing callers.
9. Exporter scripts returning API responses unvalidated to dereferencing callers: pm-stack/meta-exporter (:195, :330), pm-stack/supabase-export, pm-stack/opencode-usage-export. (cloudflare-export's GraphQL errors shape is excluded — already fixed under #2608.)
10. pm-stack/opencode-claimant (claimant.py, poll.py): queue-broker responses parsed and acted on (session launches) without a shape check. Loopback, token-authed, first-party — lowest risk in this list, same rule.

Acceptance: each numbered item either lands a boundary shape check in the surface's own error vocabulary, or is dispositioned on this issue with the one-line reason it is not a trust boundary. Reference the probe matrix from the contract statement (aggregator README, "Parsed-shape contract (#3068)"): null, array, scalar, {}, each relied-on field wrong-typed.

body:
Follow-up filed from the Phase 3 closing audit of design #4592 (issue #4593, task 14247), at origin/main .

## Gap

 () never checks that each payload entry's required journal version is at or below the frame's .  (replication.rs:379) proves only that every line decodes as a .

 demands the opposite:  () refuses any entry whose  () exceeds the journal header version — e.g. an  entry (requires version 2, or 4 with a persisted budget) under a version-1 header.

So a signed, in-range snapshot can carry an entry kind its header version does not admit. The verified cursor advances over it, the durable receiver commits it, and the replica then refuses its own journal at the next restore — the same brick-at-next-open shape Phase 1 of #4592 closed for version-0 envelopes (see the comment at replication.rs:740-744). Restore refuses the journal whole, so no impossible world state is ever applied; the defect is admission, not application.

A real writer can never produce this frame (the writer bumps the header before appending such an entry,  contract on ), so this is a writer-bug / forged-stream hole of exactly the class #4471, #4486 and #4487 closed leg by leg.

## Fix shape (for the implementing task, not this audit)

In , before chaining a Snapshot/Tail payload, refuse any entry whose  exceeds , with a typed  (a dedicated variant or -adjacent — implementer's call, recorded on the PR). Add regression tests mirroring : an in-range snapshot and tail carrying an over-version entry are refused with tracker state untouched.

## Sibling observation from the same inventory

Checkpoint-parts ordering (parts immediately followed by their , enforced in ) is likewise restore-only. It is NOT part of this fix: parts and their checkpoint can span frame boundaries, so a per-frame  check cannot decide it. Triage may split it into a receiver/commit-path check if wanted.

## Links

- Audit: issue #4593 (full inventory + dispositions (a)–(d))
- Design: issue #4592; contract statement landed in the  module doc by the #4593 PR

body:
## Confirmed behavior

`chat.history` declares `count` as an optional unsigned integer in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/world_caps.rs:258-263`. However, `parse_wants` only bounds the serialized `args` size (`world_caps.rs:798-805`); it does not validate the argument against that schema. The handler then reads `count` with `as_u64().unwrap_or(16)` (`pkgs/id/src/world/actor.rs:880-888`).

For example, this request is accepted and silently uses the default 16 instead of reporting invalid arguments:

```json
{"v":1,"requests":[{"id":"h","cap":"chat.history","args":{"count":"2"}}]}
```

The same fallback applies to other non-unsigned values such as negative numbers, fractions, `null`, and objects. The existing test `chat_history_defaults_and_clamps_and_records_read_rejects_an_oversized_first_record` (`pkgs/id/tests/world/tests.rs:1782-1832`) verifies the omitted-count default and oversized-count clamp, but not malformed supplied values.

This is distinct from #796 / PR #4681: that proving test covers the default, clamp, and oversized `records.read` behavior, not wrong-typed `chat.history.count` values. No open PR for this behavior was found.

## Why it matters

A caller typo or serialization mismatch is silently turned into a successful request for 16 lines. The declared argument contract is therefore not enforced, making client errors harder to detect and potentially returning more history than requested.

## Acceptance criteria

- A supplied non-unsigned `chat.history.count` (at least string, negative, fractional, `null`, and object cases) is rejected with `bad_args`, rather than treated as omitted.
- An omitted `count` still returns the documented default of 16.
- Valid unsigned counts still work, and values above `MAX_CHAT_HISTORY_LINES` still clamp as they do today.
- Add a world-level regression test exercising malformed input through the request path.

title: meta-exporter: restore the #2789 plain-decimal gate lost in the #6333 re-home (#3005 grammar drift)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Summary

The #2789 plain-decimal embodiment in meta-exporter's `parseSubscriptionQuota` has **drifted**: the exporter re-home in #6333 (commit b4cf60a2db, 2026-11-05) restored `pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs` with the pre-#2789 bare coercion, and the #3005 grammar gate has been absent since. Found by the #3005 closing inventory audit (issue #3006, task 4350, 2026-11-09).

## Evidence (fresh at origin/main 69aa168d5d, 2026-11-09)

- #2789's fix (commit 934b902621, PR #2864) added the `DECIMAL = /^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$/` gate inside `parseSubscriptionQuota`'s `num()`, plus empty-string reset tolerance and guarded `as_of` handling.
- The console-scrape exporter was then retired in 1d0944333f (superseded by #5040), and the re-home b4cf60a2db (#6333) brought the file back with `const num = (v) => (typeof v === "string" || typeof v === "number" ? Number(v) : NaN);` — the exact pre-#2789 line.
- Current `meta-quota-export.mjs:83` is that bare `num()`: a string field of `""` reads as a measured 0, `"0x10"` as 16, `"1e2"` as 100, subject only to finite/non-negative checks.
- Current knock-ons of the lost gate: `consoleAsOf` is computed as `Number.isFinite(num(q.as_of)) ? iso(num(q.as_of)) : null`, so an empty `as_of` again produces the 1970 epoch instead of null; `resetField` no longer treats an empty/whitespace reset string as absent.
- `pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.test.mjs` contains no decimal-spelling probes (no `0x10` / `1e2` / padded cases) — the shared probe matrix from the #3005 design does not run for this app.

## What to do

Restore the #2789 ruling in `parseSubscriptionQuota` in the #3005 recorded form:

- Field form only for string fields (`/^[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$/` as landed, or the design's per-gate narrowing); non-decimal spellings fail closed with the exporter's existing `ExportError("unparseable", 6, …)` outcome.
- Empty/whitespace reset strings treated as absent (zero-usage window tolerated with `resetAt: null`; window with usage fails closed), as #2789 landed.
- `as_of`: absent/empty stays `null`; any other non-decimal spelling fails closed — never the 1970 epoch.
- Reinstate the probe-matrix tests for this app (plain, grouped-field refusal, empty, padded, hex, scientific, trailing-junk cases).
- Note: `parsePaygBalance`'s grouped prose capture (line ~157, `[\d,]+` + strip) is grammar-conformant and is not part of this drift.

## Links

- Design: issue #3005 (recorded grammar); closing audit: issue #3006
- Original fix: issue #2789, commit 934b902621
- Drift introduced: #6333, commit b4cf60a2db

title: id(web/world): /api/world/host-view and /api/world/invite responses shape-trusted — a wrong-shape 200 shows raw TypeErrors or stores a fake 'undefined' capability

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low

labels.name: app/id

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The world page (`pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts`) shape-trusts both of its HTTP
responses with bare casts, while the WebSocket frames in the same file are
carefully guarded (`isWorldSnapshot` / `isWorldEvent` / `isRecord`):

- **Host view:** `world.ts:433` — `const result = (await response.json()) as { … records_sequence: number; records: Record<string, unknown>; next_after: string | null }`, then `world.ts:445` runs `Object.entries(result.records)` unguarded.
- **Invite:** `world.ts:566` — `const result = (await response.json()) as { capability: string; display_name: string }`, then `world.ts:567` calls `showCapability(result.capability)`, which writes the value into the capability input and persists it to `sessionStorage` (`world.ts:181-185`).

A wrong-shape 200 (deploy skew, a future contract change, a proxy error page
served as JSON) therefore fails in two bad ways instead of through the
handlers' own error vocabulary ("Host view unavailable" / "Invite failed").

## Verified (this run, laptop, origin/main 8728f5c3bf)

Probe `~/git/fleet/probe-world-shape` — a vitest/happy-dom test against the
real `world.ts` from a clean `git archive` snapshot, using the same page
harness as `world-rejoin.test.ts` (real template markup, stubbed `fetch`).
Controls pass: a well-formed host-view payload renders "Read-only host view"
with its records; a well-formed invite stores `cap-123`.

Malformed payloads, observed:

| Case | Host view (`/api/world/host-view`) | Invite (`/api/world/invite`) |
|---|---|---|
| `null` | status = raw `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'records_sequence')` | status = raw `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'capability')` |
| `{}` | status = raw `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` | **fake success** "Invite created…" — capability input and `sessionStorage` both persist the literal string `"undefined"` |
| `"abc"` | raw `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` | fake success, `"undefined"` persisted |
| `[]` | raw `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` | fake success, `"undefined"` persisted |
| `{records_sequence:0, records:null, next_after:null}` / records missing | raw `Cannot convert undefined or null to object` | — |
| `{capability:123, display_name:"ada"}` | — | fake success, capability coerced and persisted as `"123"` |
| `{capability:"cap-x"}` (no `display_name`) | — | success, log line reads "Invite created for undefined" |

The invite case is the worse one: the persisted `"undefined"` capability is
read back on the next page load (`world.ts:125`) and used as the join
credential, so one wrong-shape response poisons the browser's stored
credential while telling the user the invite was created. The host-view case
surfaces a raw engine `TypeError` as the status line instead of the handler's
own "Host view unavailable".

## Server contracts (what validation should enforce)

- `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:90-97` — `HostViewResponse { snapshot: Option<…>, view: Option<String>, surface: Option<…>, records_sequence: u64, records: Records, next_after: Option<String> }`: `records_sequence` (number) and `records` (object) are required; `next_after` is a string or null.
- `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:533` `invite_handler` returns the invite JSON; the server-side test at `world_ws.rs:1218` pins `capability` as a non-empty string. The client contract is `{ capability: string, display_name: string }`.

## Why it matters

Same class as #7811 (home feed), #7812 (image-browser), and #7823 (upload,
fixed by validating at the fetch boundary): a malformed 200 must fail closed
through the existing error path. Here it additionally corrupts persistent
state — the stored capability — with a fake success message on top.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Malformed `/api/world/host-view` 200 payloads (null / non-object body, missing or wrong-typed `records` or `records_sequence`, wrong-typed `next_after`) surface as "Host view unavailable" (or an equally clear host-view error), never as a raw `TypeError` status, and never render partial records.
- [ ] Malformed `/api/world/invite` 200 payloads (null / non-object body, missing, empty, or non-string `capability` or `display_name`) surface as an invite failure; `showCapability` is never called, the invite output stays hidden, and nothing is written to `sessionStorage`.
- [ ] Well-formed payloads behave exactly as today (existing world tests unchanged and green, including the host-view and rejoin suites).
- [ ] New regression tests in the web suite (e.g. alongside `world-rejoin.test.ts` / a new `world*.test.ts`) cover the malformed cases above and fail pre-fix.
- [ ] Web suite + typecheck green.

Scope: `pkgs/id/web/src/world.ts` response validation at the two fetch
boundaries only. Do not change the Rust handlers or the WebSocket frame
handling (already guarded). Sibling HTTP shape-trust items in other modules
(#7811, #7812) are separate issues.

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=design-architect state=filed at=2026-11-08 -->
🤖 **Agent note** · design-architect pass 74 — design filed this pass

**Design doc:** `files/designs/code-claimant-seam-contract.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace. Audit at origin/main `b64288a567fa1710abea0866dd3e43cd7f7fab61`.

## Summary

Design #4912 stated the opencode-claimant's contract with the OpenCode server for its Slice-1 surfaces (`poll.py` + `prompt.md`). The claimant has since grown a second implementation (`claimant.py`) and works through three seams whose contract was never stated — the queue it reads, the server transport it shells out through, and its own actuation and fire log. Eight filings are one defect: **the claimant acts on reads it never verified, in shapes the writers never produced, and records measurements it never took.**

- **Queue seam:** `repo-queue list` emits a human table while the claimant parses JSON, so discovery is blind (#7325, #7375); and the checkpoint verb writes the yield at `progress.last_checkpoint.stage` while `is_candidate()` reads `progress.stage` — ~60–78 real yields invisible per fire in one direction, and a stale top-level `handed_off` offering a task whose lane is mid-work in the other (#7706, the double-execution shape #4490 hardened against).
- **Server seam:** every `claimant.py` server call is an unauthenticated `curl -s` whose exit code is treated as success (#7367); the zero-message gate guarding #4912's recovery calls a plural `/messages` path the v2 server 404s with an empty body, and `stdout or "[]"` reads that as **zero messages** — every stuck-bound row passes the gate that protects live sessions from deletion, and only the queue read failing first (#7325) prevents the chained DELETE + binding clear today (#7760).
- **Actuation seam:** `launch_step` binds a session and never sends the prompt (#7356), ignores its mode argument so a shadow fire creates and binds (#7366), and gate-exit fires log a hardcoded `cap_room: 0` although `cap_step()` never ran (#7732).

This design originates on the trigger recorded at passes 71–73 (a further claimant interface filing): three landed in one window (#7706, #7732, #7760). #4916 (parked) scopes only `poll.py`/`prompt.md` server calls plus a `limit=500` question — none of the eight legs is in its scope.

## The contract

**The claimant acts only on a verified read.** A read is verified when it arrived through the seam's one transport, in the shape the writer actually produces, with its status checked. Anything else is UNKNOWN — and unknown never authorizes a side effect (launch, delete, unbind) and is never recorded as a measurement.

## Decisions recorded (the architect's pins)

1. **Queue channel:** the claimant reads queue state through ONE channel — the repo-queue CLI's JSON output (the CLI grows a stable JSON mode; the human table stays for humans). Direct broker HTTP from the claimant loses: queue selection, auth and de-chunking are the CLI's contract, and the filed traps (#7355, #7358) live there. A failed/non-JSON read is discovery-UNKNOWN, not zero candidates.
2. **Yield field:** #7706's option A — the yield of record is `progress.last_checkpoint.stage`; `progress.stage` stays accepted for older rows, and a row whose live `progress.stage` names a later non-yield work stage is rejected (stale direction). Option B (checkpoint also stamps the top-level field) loses: it changes the queue contract for every consumer and needs a ~500-row backfill to fix a one-reader defect.
3. **Server transport:** one authenticated helper for every server call; success = HTTP 2xx AND the body parses into the expected envelope (`{"data": [...]}` for message reads, singular `/message` path as a constant). A subprocess exit code is never a verdict — reads or DELETE. *Zero messages* is a 200 with an empty `data` list; *gone* is a 404 from the per-id GET through the same helper; empty body / non-2xx / wrong shape is UNKNOWN. This states at the transport what prompt.md step 1a already rules, completing #4912's recovery rule.
4. **Actuation:** a launch is create → prompt → bind (a failed prompt send leaves no binding); mode is checked at the actuation helper, not per call site (shadow = no create/bind/prompt/delete); the fire log records only measured values (`cap_room` is `cap_step()`'s value or `null`; `candidates_seen` distinguishes unknown from empty).

## Phases (sub-issues of this issue)

- **Phase 1 — #7325 + #7375 + #7706 (ADOPTED):** queue seam — CLI JSON channel + yield from `last_checkpoint.stage` with the stale-direction rejection.
- **Phase 2 — #7367 + #7760 (ADOPTED, independent):** server seam — one authenticated transport, status + shape verdicts, unknown-never-zero/gone, test stub corrected to the writer's shapes.
- **Phase 3 — #7356 + #7366 + #7732 (ADOPTED, independent):** actuation seam — create → prompt → bind, mode gate at the helper, measured-only fire log. Coordination: its create/delete calls use Phase 2's transport helper when it exists; if Phase 3 lands first it introduces the helper for its own calls rather than a private curl shape.
- **Phase 4 — NEW (closing audit, filed with this design):** seam + stub-shape inventory over `poll.py`, `claimant.py`, and `prompt.md`'s queue reads; README contract statement; required dispositions — (a) repo-queue verb trio #7349/#7355/#7358 dependency per verb, (b) #7735 claim targeting (queue-side, not a phase), (c) the #4916 boundary (its inventory owns `poll.py`/`prompt.md` OpenCode calls; this one owns `claimant.py` + both queue seams), (d) #6533 discovery tracker closure/re-scope on Phase 1 evidence.

## Open questions (recorded in the design doc, not phased)

Deprecating `progress.stage` as a yield source entirely (queue-side, long-term form of #7706's B); generating `prompt.md`'s prose steps from `claimant.py`'s constants (the drift class behind the wrong path); a queue-health read as the discovery-unknown signal.

**For triage:** do NOT re-file or split the phases — they are the sub-issues of this issue, with the decisions recorded here and in the design doc.

## Acceptance criteria

- The seam contract (design doc linked in the body) states one rule for all three seams — queue reads, server transport, actuation/fire log: the claimant acts only on a verified read, in the shape the writer actually produces, and logs only measurements it actually took.
- Each of the eight linked filings (#7325, #7375, #7706, #7367, #7760 and siblings) maps to a named contract clause, so a reader can trace filing → clause → implementation.
- Implementation follow-on issues exist and are linked for every clause that is not already fixed, per the native-relations rule (a design with no implementation link is not finished work).
- A claimant fire after the contract lands shows no action taken on an unverified, mis-shaped, or unmeasured read in any of the three seams.

body:
## Symptom

`repo-queue claim` with no `--queue` silently claims from `repo-health-code-shadow`, the **shadow** queue. In a session with no `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` set:

```
$ repo-queue claim --worker opencode-claimant
{ "id": 10744, "queue": "repo-health-code-shadow", "title": "Fix #6366: per-unit ..." }
```

`repo-queue list` / `health` inherit the same default, so a bare read also looks at the shadow queue and reports a healthy, nearly-empty view while the four pilot queues hold 180+ claims.

## Why it matters

This is the same trap that `enqueue` was explicitly hardened against — `resolve_enqueue_queue` (client.rs:938-961) resolves flag → packet → env and **fails loudly** rather than defaulting, with the comment:

> `enqueue` queue resolution (#7016, the shadow-default trap): ... There is deliberately NO built-in default for enqueue: with none of the three the enqueue fails loudly instead of silently landing in the shadow queue — the failure that misrouted ~291 tasks on 2026-11-07.

`claim` never got that treatment: `opt_queue` (client.rs:781) falls back to `DEFAULT_QUEUE = "repo-health-code-shadow"` (client.rs:26).

## Evidence it is already happening fleet-wide

Four rows in `repo-health-code-shadow` carry progress notes written by scheduled lanes that made exactly this mistake:

| task | progress.note |
|---|---|
| 8675 | "Accidental no-argument claim selected a task from repo-health-code-shadow instead of the requested repo-health-code-pilot. No task work performed..." |
| 8685 | "park immediately: this claim came from repo-health-code-shadow, not the requested pilot queue" |
| 9431 | "release accidental bare-claim probe immediately; no task work started" |
| 10744 | "park immediately; accidental claim came from invoking repo-queue claim without queue/lane flags" |

Each of those burned a shared claim + lease on a shadow task, and each then needed a manual park to release it. Two of them were re-claimed by the same trap more than once (8685 at attempts 2/4, 10744 at 4/4).

## Impact on this consumer

The opencode-claimant packet mandates `--worker opencode-claimant` on every verb. A fire that follows the packet but runs `claim` from the wrong working context mutates the shadow queue instead of the pilot queues — and because the claim is a write, the claimant's "discover, do not mutate" shadow-mode rule is violated silently.

## Proposed fix

Give `claim` (and, for consistency, `list`/`health`) the same resolution `enqueue` uses: `--queue` flag → `REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE` → **error naming the flag**, with the shadow queue reachable only by passing it explicitly. Alternatively keep a default for `list`/`health` (harmless reads) but make `claim` — the write that burns a lease and allocates work — require an explicit queue.

## Verification

```
$ repo-queue claim --worker opencode-claimant
repo-queue: claim: no queue resolved — pass --queue or set REPO_QUEUE_DEFAULT_QUEUE
$ repo-queue claim --worker opencode-claimant --queue repo-health-code-shadow
# proceeds explicitly
```

Related: #7016 (the shadow-default trap for enqueue), #7325 / #7355 (the claimant's own read path), #3026 (slice 1).

## Acceptance criteria

- `repo-queue claim`, `list`, and `health` with no `--queue` and no env/packet queue fail loudly with a clear error — they never silently operate on `repo-health-code-shadow` (the `enqueue` / `resolve_enqueue_queue` treatment from #7016, applied to every verb).
- With `--queue` (or the env/packet resolution) supplied, all three verbs behave exactly as today.
- A regression test pins the no-default behaviour for claim, list, and health.

# Closing agreement audit — every ci-policy-named workflow against all three legs (Phase 4)

Phase 4 of the ci-policy agreement design (design issue filed pass 70, 2026-11-07, title "Policy, triggers, enablement must agree — one agreement contract for ci-policy's guard and build workflows"; design doc `files/designs/code-ci-policy-agreement.md` in the `keep-the-four-repos-healthy` goal workspace). GATED on Phases 1–3 of the design (the agreement checker; adopted origins #6929 + #6953; adopted origins #6959 + #6981) — keep `status/blocked` until they land.

## Scope

- Inventory every workflow `.github/ci-policy.md` names (sections + tier table) against all three legs of the contract: the tier the policy assigns, the triggers the workflow declares, and the venue's Actions enablement state (API read, evidenced on this issue). Every row ends in agreement or in a recorded disposition (re-arm / fold / retire) with its issue.
- Land the contract statement in `.github/ci-policy.md` beside the tier table: the three-leg agreement rule, the tier→trigger mapping's home, and the disposition vocabulary — one paragraph, pointing at the checker.

**Decision for Drew (one line):** the seven guard/build workflows below are dark in three different modes while ci-policy still promises their tiers — re-arm them (merge_group for the two basic-tier guards per the sibling precedent; re-enable + restore for the build set) under this design's agreement checker, or accept dispatch-only for them too and strike their tier promises from ci-policy? Phases 1 and 4 do not wait for the ruling; the re-arm/re-enable executions in Phases 2–3 do.

# Policy, triggers, enablement must agree — one agreement contract for ci-policy's guard and build workflows

Design doc: `files/designs/code-ci-policy-agreement.md` in the `keep-the-four-repos-healthy` goal workspace. Filed by the design architect (pass 70, 2026-11-07), audit at origin/main 08dd577848. This pass originates on pass 69's recorded trigger: a third policy-listed guard found dead since the 2026-11-04 sweep (#6959, after #6929 + #6953) — a fourth filing (#6981, covering four build workflows) arrived in the same window.

## Problem

`.github/ci-policy.md` states which CI checks run at which tier. One commit (5a94833ea3, 2026-11-04) rewrote the trigger reality of ~25 workflows; nobody compared policy against reality afterwards, so the divergence surfaced by hand audit, one workflow at a time. Test suites got design #6185 and Drew's dispatch-only ruling (2026-11-05). The guard/build workflows ci-policy names got neither — #6187 inventories non-test disabled workflows "for the record only; their dispositions are not this design's to make", and #6981's body makes the same point for its set. This design takes that remainder.

## Current state (verified this pass)

Seven ci-policy-promised workflows, three failure modes:

1. **Dispatch-only, venue active, check unreachable** — #6929 (mcpx-fix-test-guard: `workflow_dispatch:` only; the enforcement step is `pull_request`-gated, so even a dispatch never runs the #1969 guard; policy still assigns PR + main tiers) and #6959 (production-line-guard: dispatch-only, venue active, and main already fails it — directory.rs 2,610 production lines vs the 2,500 limit, ungrandfathered; this workflow has no ci-policy tier row at all).
2. **Merge-group only, venue disabled** — #6953 (opencode-config-guard: kept `merge_group:`, but Actions state is `disabled_manually`, zero runs since 2026-11-03; policy claims pull requests + merge groups + pushes to main). The only CI check between the canonical OpenCode config and a metered/PAYG provider selection.
3. **Dispatch-only AND disabled — cannot run at all** — #6981 (go-modules-build, identity-build, map-build, mcpx-nixbuild: all `workflow_dispatch:`-only at HEAD, all `disabled_manually` per the Actions API this pass, no completed run since 2026-11-03; policy assigns a class-3 PR tier + always-on main tier).

Conforming siblings prove the intended shape: workflow-lint (active, pull_request + merge_group) and fleet-search-parity-guard (active, merge_group) both run.

## The contract

For every workflow ci-policy names, three records must agree: the assigned tier, the declared triggers, and the Actions enablement state. Any disagreement is a defect with exactly one recorded disposition — re-arm, fold, or retire — never a persisting default. Agreement is checked in the tree (a script in workflow-lint, the active venue that fires on exactly the paths a trigger sweep touches) and enablement is audited from the API on #6187's recurring cadence, extended to this non-test set.

Recorded decisions (full reasoning in the design doc): the tier→trigger mapping is pinned (a basic-tier guard is satisfied by merge_group + its path gate; a main tier requires push-to-main or a named equivalent venue; dispatch-only satisfies no tier); the two basic guards re-arm via merge_group, not restored pull_request triggers (sibling precedent; no new PR-tier runner load — #6929's either/or, pinned); #6959's directory.rs follows the guard's own split-or-grandfather convention; #6981 is dispositioned per workflow.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 (NEW, filed with this design):** the agreement checker — tier→trigger mapping written into ci-policy, production-line guard's missing row added, checker script + contract tests under `.github/scripts/`, wired into workflow-lint; the Phase 2–3 disagreements land as explicit waivers naming their phase issues so the checker is green with the set explicit.
- **Phase 2 (ADOPTED):** #6929 + #6953 — the basic-tier guards brought into agreement, each closing with a completed run on main as proof; #6953's venue re-enable executes when Drew rules above.
- **Phase 3 (ADOPTED):** #6959 + #6981 — production-line guard dispositioned (directory.rs split-or-grandfathered) and one disposition per build workflow, executed under the same ruling gate.
- **Phase 4 (NEW, gated on Phases 1–3):** closing inventory of every ci-policy-named workflow against all three legs + contract statement in ci-policy + four required dispositions (checker venue coverage; #6187 audit output naming the non-test set; #6960's guard file-selection sibling; any workflow filed dark after this design).

Open questions stay in the design doc (step-level `if:` reachability; nightly-tier mapping; schedule-triggered operations workflows).


## Acceptance criteria
- The problem described above is confirmed against current main (reproduced or traced to the named code path), or the issue is closed with that evidence.
- A fix/implementation addressing the described behaviour is merged via PR referencing this issue, with tests naming their oracle where the change has meaningful invariants.
- Related/sibling issues from the same filing batch are cross-linked and any dependency is recorded as a native blocked-by relation.

body:
Split from issue #1940 (PLG-38 remainder), filed by triage task 12006 (lane code-x, 2026-11-08).

## Problem
A host abort does not cancel an in-flight `mcpx_exec`. Verified at origin/main 13ebeccaff12d7f242cc6e29f86f5fcc55fc32fc:
- `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx-session.ts`: `mcpx_exec` execute() calls `c.exec(args.source, context?.sessionID)` — the execution context abort signal is never passed.
- `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx/daemon.ts` (line 579): `async exec(source: string, session?: string)` has no signal parameter.
- The generated client already supports it: `CallOptions.signal` in `pkgs/mcpx/plugin/opencode/mcpx/ops.gen.ts`.
- The CLI fallback path (`viaCLI(["exec", args.source])`) likewise has no cancellation input.

## Acceptance criteria
- The host execution-context abort signal is threaded through the daemon exec path (mcpx-session.ts → daemon.ts exec → generated client CallOptions.signal) and through the CLI fallback path, so aborting the host tool call cancels the in-flight `mcpx_exec`.
- Tests cover abort on both the daemon path and the CLI fallback path; existing plugin tests still pass.
- Session forwarding from issue #1910 (closed, PR #2569 merged) is preserved.

body:
## Recorded decision: DIY backup `api` transport deliberately omits the Supabase platform schemas

Filed by Lane E (2026-11-07) while killing the backup schema-list trap at the source (#5695 / #6619), so the partial list is a recorded decision rather than a silent gap a future audit can misread.

### Facts (verified against the actual 2026-11-06T10:47:11Z pgdump, parsed directly)

The dump contains 16 schemas with COPY tables. The backup config `schemas` list (now 12) covers every fleet-owned schema: public, agent, ci, ideas, ainventory, engineering, automation, finance, home, research, alerts, cron.

The four schemas NOT in the list are Supabase platform schemas. In the dump, every user-facing table in them is empty; the only nonzero tables are platform bookkeeping:

| schema | nonzero tables in dump | user tables |
|---|---|---|
| auth | auth.schema_migrations (82) | all 0 rows (users, sessions, identities, ...) |
| storage | storage.migrations (80) | all 0 rows (buckets, objects, ...) |
| realtime | realtime.schema_migrations (91) | subscription 0 rows |
| vault | (vault.secrets 0) | 0 rows |

### Semantics (the part that was misread before)

- The `pgdump` transport ignores the `schemas` list entirely (`pg_dump` runs with no `--schema` flag; full-database dumps) — platform schemas ARE in every pgdump backup regardless of the list.
- The `api` transport (sandbox) filters its DDL/row/sequence exports by the list, so api-transport backups do not carry these four schemas. That is deliberate: they are platform-managed, hold no fleet data, and are left behind at decommission per the migration program disposition.

### Decision

Keep the exclusion. If a future change ever needs api-transport coverage of a platform schema, amend the list and this record in the same pass — do not infer coverage from the list for pgdump backups, and do not treat the api list as the backup-coverage statement for the fleet.

## Acceptance criteria
- This recorded decision stays the reference for backup schema coverage: the `api` transport list (12 fleet-owned schemas) deliberately excludes the Supabase platform schemas auth/storage/realtime/vault.
- Any future change that needs api-transport coverage of a platform schema amends the list and this record in the same pass.
- No code change is required by this issue itself; it closes when the decision record is acknowledged in the backup/migration documentation it informs.

body:
## Context

Incident: #3372 — the laptop's single 3.3T NVMe partition hit 99% (free space oscillating 39–88G within an hour on 2026-11-06). One of the largest consumers is `~/git/fleet`: 604G across 1,600+ per-task directories. Those directories are git worktrees **of the inner repos** — fleet itself is not a repo; do not make a worktree of fleet, worktree the inner repos.

The 2026-11-06 janitor pass (strict guardrails) could only remove 12 verified worktrees / 8.04 GiB: of 1,178 dirs older than 48h, 1,051 (115.1 GiB) were dirty with uncommitted work and 72 (24.0 GiB) held unpushed-only commits. Drew ruled archive-first on that residue (2026-11-07), and the same day set the standing policy below. One-off manual janitor passes do not scale — this issue asks for a recurring, policy-driven janitor.

## Policy (Drew, 2026-11-07)

1. **Reproducible build artifacts are auto-deletable.** Old `target/` dirs and equivalent reproducible build-artifact dirs may be deleted automatically, without archiving — they can always be rebuilt.
2. **Aging worktrees: auto-commit, auto-push, then remove.** For a worktree past the age threshold: commit ALL changes, push to an archive branch, verify the push landed, and only then remove the worktree. Nothing with unpushed state is ever removed before its archive push verifies.
3. **Our own branches are in scope.** The fleet's own branches are part of cleanup too — stale fleet branches get the same archive/cleanup treatment, not an exemption.
4. **Stop the accumulation at the source (structural fix).** Lanes should `git worktree remove` their worktree at task end, so residue stops accumulating in the first place. The janitor is the backstop, not the primary mechanism.

## Ask

Design and implement a recurring, policy-driven janitor for laptop disk/worktree hygiene:

- **Schedule + thresholds:** a recurring run with explicit age/size thresholds for (a) build-artifact dirs (`target/` and equivalents) and (b) worktrees eligible for archive-and-remove.
- **Guardrails (hard requirements):**
  - Verified push before removal — an archive branch push must be confirmed on the remote (sha readback) before its worktree is removed.
  - Deletes are named, one by one — no recursive/wildcard deletes on shared trees (standing delete guardrail).
  - Non-git files go to recoverable trash, never hard delete.
  - A manifest/report per run: what was archived (branch + sha), what was removed, what was skipped and why, and free space before/after.
  - **Never-touch list:** primary clones, any worktree younger than 48h, and anything whose unpushed state failed archive verification.
- **Lane hygiene:** the `git worktree remove` at task end (policy point 4) wired into lane/worker completion paths so the janitor's input shrinks over time.

## Links

- Incident: #3372 (policy rulings recorded there 2026-11-07)
- Drew's archive-first ruling on the current ~139 GB residue: #3372, 2026-11-07

## Acceptance criteria
- A recurring janitor run exists on the laptop with explicit age/size thresholds for (a) reproducible build-artifact dirs (`target/` and equivalents) and (b) worktrees eligible for archive-and-remove, and its schedule is recorded on this issue.
- Build-artifact dirs past threshold are removed without archiving; every removal is named one by one (no recursive/wildcard deletes on shared trees) and non-git files go to recoverable trash.
- No worktree is removed before its archive push verifies: for each archived worktree the manifest records the archive branch and the remotely read-back sha.
- The never-touch list is enforced and tested: primary clones, worktrees younger than 48h, and anything whose unpushed state failed archive verification are never removed.
- Each run emits a manifest/report: what was archived (branch + sha), what was removed, what was skipped and why, and free space before/after.
- Lane/worker completion paths call `git worktree remove` at task end (policy point 4), so janitor input measurably shrinks over successive runs.

body:
## Bug: `POST /v1/search` crashes on a JSON `null` body — the 400 envelope is unreachable for it

`pkgs/atlas-search/worker/src/index.ts` (the #6788 Worker, merged 2026-11-06 in PR #6800), verified at origin/main `8a5cd8ea75`:

```ts
let body: { query?: unknown; k?: unknown };
try {
  body = (await req.json()) as typeof body;      // :74-78 — only the parse is guarded
} catch {
  return errorJson(400, "bad_request", "body must be JSON");
}
if (typeof body.query !== "string") {            // :79 — dereferences body
  return errorJson(400, "bad_request", "query must be a string");
}
```

`null` is valid JSON, so `req.json()` succeeds and returns `null`; the very next line dereferences it. The `TypeError` escapes the `fetch` handler entirely, so the client gets the platform's unhandled-exception 500 instead of this route's own `{error:{code:"bad_request",...}}` 400 envelope — the one malformed-body shape the gate's error contract does not cover.

### Verified this run (laptop, handler logic reproduced verbatim in node)

| body | result |
|---|---|
| `null` | **THROWS `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'query')`** |
| `5` | 400 `bad_request` |
| `"str"` | 400 `bad_request` |
| `[]` | 400 `bad_request` |
| `{}` | 400 `bad_request` |
| `{"query":1}` | 400 `bad_request` |

Every other non-object shape is handled; only `null` (the one value whose property access throws rather than boxing to `undefined`) escapes. The existing suite (`pkgs/atlas-search/worker/test/worker.test.ts`) has no null-body case — its malformed-input coverage is the unauthorized and non-JSON paths.

### Why it matters

This Worker is the gated inbound surface for cross-database search (#6788). Its routes deliberately return a uniform JSON error envelope (`errorJson`) so clients can distinguish their own bad input (400) from upstream failure (502, via `SpaceError`/`ServiceError`). A crash-on-input breaks that contract: monitoring and clients see a 500-class platform error for a client bug, and the throw happens *after* the gate check, so any authenticated caller can produce unhandled exceptions at will with a one-word body.

### Fix shape

Validate the parsed body is a non-null object before dereferencing — e.g. extend the parse guard: `if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null) return errorJson(400, "bad_request", "body must be a JSON object")` immediately after the `try` (arrays may keep flowing to the existing `query must be a string` 400, or be rejected by the same check — either is consistent as long as it is a 400 envelope, never a throw).

### Acceptance criteria

- `POST /v1/search` with body `null` returns HTTP 400 with the standard `{error:{code:"bad_request",...}}` envelope; no exception escapes the handler.
- A regression test in `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/test/worker.test.ts` covers the `null` body (and, cheaply, the other primitive bodies `5` / `"str"` / `[]` asserting the same 400 envelope).
- All existing worker tests still pass (`npm test` in `pkgs/atlas-search/worker`) and `npm run typecheck` is clean.
- No behavior change for well-formed requests: miss/hit flow, `clampK`, and the inspect route are untouched.

PR #6427 (open, "fix(id): render footnote references in plain-text saves") adds footnote-reference rendering to `extract_plain_text`: every non-empty string label is preserved verbatim inside `[^...]`, without changing surrounding text. Codex flagged that this precise serializer invariant is covered only by fixed examples, while the root `AGENTS.md` testing doctrine requires property tests for meaningful serializer invariants and says example-based tests do not replace them.

body:
## Problem

The laptop's `/home` filesystem (3.3T nvme, shared by every fleet worktree and cargo target) hit 100% full during the 2026-11-06 evening shifts (observed 2026-11-07 ~05:05-05:15Z by lane code-y):

- `df -h /home`: 3.2T used, 9.0G avail, 100% — later 0 bytes avail mid-build.
- A `cargo test` for pkgs/id in a fresh fleet worktree died at the final lib-test compile with `No space left on device (os error 28)`; plain file writes to laptop /tmp failed the same way.
- One fresh pkgs/id worktree target alone is ~4.3GB; with 26 code lanes plus opencode/openchamber/nix lanes building in parallel worktrees under ~/git/fleet, targets accumulate faster than worktree cleanup reclaims them (worktrees are removed at task end, but an in-flight set plus the primary clones' targets fills the disk).

## Impact

Worker shifts cannot compile or test Rust changes on the laptop (the designated execution surface), and scratch/script transfers to the laptop fail. Lanes fall back to partial verification or stall.

## Suggested directions (triage decides)

- A scheduled janitor for stale fleet worktree target dirs (the cargo-target-janitor work in #6790 is adjacent — queue-claim offset pagination over the live set suggests it already reasons about which targets are live).
- A shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR per repo with lane-safe locking, or sccache-only artifacts with per-worktree target caps.
- A disk-headroom alert (fleet monitor) before 100%: warn at e.g. 95% with the largest target dirs named.

Filed by repo-worker-code lane code-y (fallback shift, issue #6779 work blocked at the test step; that issue's PR discloses the partial verification).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Fleet worktree/cargo-target growth on the laptop is bounded by an enforced cleanup or quota mechanism, so /home does not reach 100% during normal parallel lane operation.
- [ ] The cargo-target-janitor runs successfully on its cadence (its silent hourly failure is fixed or superseded) and reclaims stale targets.
- [ ] A build that would previously have died with ENOSPC instead completes or fails with an actionable disk-headroom signal (see the alert follow-up, issue #6813).

body:
## Problem

The laptop secrets broker serves a STALE secret value long after the
secret is rotated in Bitwarden Secrets Manager. `fleet secrets get`
(broker-first) keeps returning the pre-rotation value, so a rotation
appears to succeed while every broker consumer keeps using the dead
credential.

## Observed (2026-11-06, during the runtime-db-export Turso repoint, #5691)

- BWS secret `turso.muse-mirror-rw-token` rotated via `bws secret edit`;
  verified by direct `bws secret get`: new value sha256 fingerprint
  `6320fec2` (len 348).
- `fleet secrets get turso.muse-mirror-rw-token` returned the OLD value
  (fingerprint `a0542dc2`) at +20s after the edit, and STILL at +10 min:
  the repointed loader's live probe at ~22:05 CST had its broker-supplied
  token rejected by Turso (`auth role not found`) and only succeeded via
  a direct-BWS fallback.
- The old token was not merely stale but WRONG for the current DB
  (minted against a superseded muse-mirror instance), so the failure
  mode was a hard auth rejection, not a soft staleness.

## Impact

Any consumer resolving rotated secrets through the broker silently uses
dead credentials after a rotation (DB tokens, API keys). Rotation
runbooks that verify via BWS directly will report success while broker
consumers keep failing.

## Expected

- The broker reflects BWS edits within its documented TTL (bounded,
  minutes at most), or `fleet secrets get` documents that it may serve
  cached values and exposes the value's age/source.
- Regression check: rotate a canary secret in BWS, assert
  `fleet secrets get` returns the new value within the TTL.

Related: #5860 (secrets-broker vault-refresh loop defects — TTL=0 spin).
Workaround in place: `~/tools/runtime-db-export/turso_client.py` falls
back to a direct BWS read when the DB rejects the broker-supplied token.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After a secret is edited/rotated in Bitwarden Secrets Manager, `fleet secrets get <name>` returns the NEW value within a bounded, documented TTL (minutes at most) — no indefinite staleness.
- [ ] A regression check exists: rotate a canary secret in BWS, then assert the broker-served value matches the direct-BWS value within the TTL.
- [ ] If a cached value is ever served, its age/source is knowable (documented behavior or exposed metadata), so a rotation runbook can tell whether it is verifying the broker or BWS.
- [ ] The stale-value failure mode from the 2026-11-06 observation (broker token rejected by Turso at +10 min after rotation) no longer reproduces.

body:
## Summary

The `bws freshness` workflow's credential-free fixture tests (`lib/bws-to-sops-check.test.sh`, the contract tests for `lib/bws-to-sops.sh --check`) run only on `schedule` and `workflow_dispatch` — there is no `pull_request` (or `push`) trigger, and no other workflow runs that test script. A PR that breaks the `--check` contract can therefore merge with the fixture suite never having run, and the breakage is first seen by the nightly scheduled run on main.

## Evidence (verified this run, laptop @ 4e92da9311)

- `.github/workflows/bws-freshness.yml:25-28`: the entire `on:` block is `workflow_dispatch:` plus `schedule: - cron: "23 6 * * *"`. No `pull_request`, `merge_group`, or `push`.
- `.github/workflows/bws-freshness.yml:38-45`: the `fixture-tests` job ("full (main tier): bws freshness fixture tests") runs `bash lib/bws-to-sops-check.test.sh` — and its header comment (:8-9) says the job "needs no credentials and always runs", which the trigger set contradicts: on a PR it does not run at all.
- Repo-wide grep over `.github/` (this run): `bws-to-sops-check` appears only in `bws-freshness.yml` (:45 run line and :8 comment). No PR-tier workflow covers it.
- Probe (laptop, `~/git/fleet/probe-bws-freshness/probe_bws.py`, run against the real workflow file @ 4e92da9311): the pre-`jobs:` block contains neither `pull_request` nor `push` — machine-checked, not just eyeballed.
- Contrast with the CI tier policy (`.github/ci-policy.md`): class-2/3 changes get "affected unit tests" in the PR tier, and sibling static guards (e.g. the OpenCode metered-provider config guard, fleet-search parity guard) explicitly "run on pull requests, merge groups, and pushes to main". This suite — pure stubbed fixtures, ~seconds, no credentials — is exactly the kind of check the PR tier exists for, and its own job name already brands it main-tier-only.
- The defect class is live, not hypothetical: #6631 (merged PR #6401 left `--check` silently skipped when combined with `--dry-run`) is precisely a `--check`-contract regression that a PR-time fixture run is meant to catch before merge.

## Why it matters

`--check` is the freshness oracle for the BWS -> SOPS mirror (#5451): if its contract regresses on a PR, the nightly job either fails on main (teaching everyone to ignore it — the exact failure the workflow header at :20-23 worries about) or, worse, silently passes drift. Running the fixtures only after merge converts a cheap pre-merge signal into a main-breakage report.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The fixture tests run before merge for changes that can affect them: add a `pull_request` trigger (path-filtered to at least `lib/bws-to-sops.sh`, `lib/bws-to-sops-check.test.sh`, and the workflow file itself) — following the ci-policy dedup rule so the suite does not double-run on push + PR (the scheduled/dispatch triggers stay).
- [ ] The job display name / tier prefix is updated to match the tier it now runs in per `.github/ci-policy.md` naming (`basic: ` for a PR-tier job), or the policy table gains a row explaining the exception.
- [ ] The workflow header comment (:8-9) is corrected to state when the job actually runs.
- [ ] `live-check` remains schedule/dispatch-only (it needs credentials the PR tier must not get) — only the credential-free fixture job gains the PR trigger.
- [ ] Related: #5451 (parent), #6631 (the `--check` regression this would have caught).
