body:
Standalone analysis commissioned by Drew, 2026-11-01: full comparison of DeepSeek's [dsh-superagent-prototype](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype) against our repo-health fleet — same-path check, concept mapping, adoptable ideas (fed into #3424 and #3418), and the deliberate differences we keep. Full text below; also sent to Aster for review.

# DeepSeek dsh-superagent-prototype vs. our repo-health fleet — comparison & adoptable ideas

Date: 2026-11-01. Scope: whole system, not just code#3424.
Sources read: their `docs/000-philosophy.md`, `001-domain.md`, `002-authorization.md`,
`003-execution.md`, `004-prompts.md`, `005-panel.md`, `007-architecture.md`
(006-deployment / 008-cookbook not read). Ours: goal GOAL.md, code#3424 + newest
comments, code#3418, opencode#1014 + directive comments, fleet instruction files,
standing Drew rules (merge authority, quota doctrine, decision surfacing).
Every claim about their system cites the doc it came from. Nothing posted to GitHub.

---

## 1. Their core concepts (compact)

**Philosophy / operating stance**
- Prime metric: take as little human attention as possible, give as much value as
  possible; every message, notification, question, setting, and panel element must
  earn its attention cost or be removed (000-philosophy).
- Acts only when asked, or when a written rule allows it; unrequested work starts
  in a record-only mode (000-philosophy, 002-authorization).
- Speaks only when a person must act or can use a result; confirms a request once,
  stays quiet while working (000-philosophy, 004-prompts).
- One concrete question at a time, in structured form (000-philosophy; implemented
  as the Report's structured question field, 001-domain / 003-execution).
- Stops by impact, not effort: local change → reviewable result; a change needing
  a design decision stops with a clear question (000-philosophy).
- Honest reporting: drafts marked unfinished, failures reported as failures,
  limits never bypassed to avoid asking (000-philosophy, 004-prompts).

**Domain (001-domain)**
- Source — an event stream (kind + instance config); holds its read position and
  bot identity; drops the bot's own messages before they enter the domain.
- Trigger — one immutable event; the unit of audit and idempotence (accepting it
  twice creates one Ticket).
- Thread — Triggers in time order; at most one Eval at a time; holds
  Subscriptions and Decision history.
- Eval — stateless judgement on a batch of Triggers in two layers: a deterministic
  Gate, then model Assessment. Output is a Decision: accept / stop / ignore /
  unavailable.
- Mandate — what an accept grants: Policy version, scope, strength, matched
  rules, sender identity. Immutable; wider scope = new Ticket; only a person's
  stop withdraws it; revalidated against current Policy before an ended Ticket
  resumes.
- Ticket — the unit of authorized work; open → ended → resumable by a person's
  message on its Threads; defines its own state, independent of the Executor.
- Assignment — binding of a Ticket to one Executor instance; a Ticket has several
  over time; pending → running → ended independently of the Ticket.
- Subscription — many-to-many Ticket↔Thread relation; fan-out delivers Thread
  messages to live Tickets as context with no authority check; context-only
  subscriptions lend context but no authority and do not resume.
- Correlation — relation between Threads sharing a Trigger; adds context, never
  routes.
- Channel — the write side of a Thread (acks, replies, PRs, review replies).
- Policy — versioned assessment rules + per-Source parts (allowed list, admission
  table, bot list); a Policy change notifies affected live Tickets but does not
  revoke their Mandates.
- Attention — a structured question on a Ticket waiting for a person's answer.
- Disposition — the record of where each Trigger went (filtered / evaluated /
  fanned out / handed back / answered).
- Report — the Executor's structured state report to its Ticket: progress /
  waiting / ready / blocked / failed / dropped, plus an optional question.
- Explicitly rejected concepts (001-domain "Rejected concepts"): cross-Source
  identity mapping, Eval scheduling its own delayed Triggers (waiting belongs to
  Sources), waiting/revoked Eval states, one-live-Ticket-per-Thread, Ticket state
  following the Executor session, an Executor declaring a person asked to stop,
  cancelling running Tickets on Policy change, inferring "waiting on a person"
  from free-text reports.

**Authorization (002-authorization)**
- Strength: explicit (allowed person addresses the agent, or follows up on a
  Thread with a Ticket) vs inferred (bot on the bot list, unlisted follow-up,
  admission-cell candidates). Bots can never make explicit requests or stop work.
- Admission table per Source: rows = receiving scopes, cells decide
  explicit / inferred / ignore by sender membership × addressed-or-not.
- Accept mode per Policy: `off` / `observe` (default; inferred accepts are
  recorded as "would accept" and nothing starts) / `auto`. Explicit requests
  work in every mode. Proactive accept requires ≥1 matching rule, and every
  enabled rule is judged exactly once per assessment.
- Follow-up ownership: a message on a Ticket's Thread is owned by that Ticket's
  Executor (no Eval); the Executor handles it in-scope or hands it back once,
  with a reason; only when no Ticket owns it does it go to fresh Eval. The main
  Session may act on an owned follow-up only to stop work.
- Revalidation before resume: an ended Ticket's Mandate is checked against
  today's Policy (mode, rules still enabled, sender still listed, bot still
  listed); failure = the Ticket stays ended and its waiting messages re-enter
  the intake path as unowned.
- Eval failure discipline: an expired Eval requeues twice, then records
  `unavailable`; assessment failure also records `unavailable`; Policy change
  mid-Eval records `unavailable` and requeues under the new version immediately.

**Execution (003-execution)**
- Ticket stages are derived, not stored: a precedence table (first match wins)
  computes the stage from facts — input-undelivered, has-Attention, latest
  Report ready / blocked / failed, queued, idle (waiting), working. A `person/*`
  stage means the Ticket cannot continue without a human.
- One Executor Session + one directory per Ticket (`worker-<ticket id>`);
  prepare command (typically `git worktree`) runs once before the first
  Assignment; a PR belongs to the Ticket when its branch's last segment matches
  the Ticket's short name.
- Worker slots: a Ticket holds a slot through background work; background work
  gets ≤30 min after turn end, then shell jobs are killed and the Ticket reports
  waiting with which jobs were killed. One extra slot beyond the concurrency
  limit is reserved for a person's message or a status request, and human wakes
  take priority over new launches.
- Blocked/failed hold: on a `blocked`/`failed` Report the Ticket takes no
  automatic Input (CI/bot messages are recorded, not delivered); transient
  provider/network failures (408/429/5xx, refused/reset/timeout) retry 3× with
  growing backoff before the hold; a person's message, a non-blocked Report, or
  a manual Retry ends the hold.
- Stored work: side effects are stored first, executed after (transactional
  outbox); retries with doubling backoff; a kind of work surfaces as a system
  problem only after 3 consecutive failures of an item.
- Restart recovery: interrupted Assignments restart with a recovery note ("check
  directory, git history and GitHub before repeating any outside action"),
  oldest Ticket first; read/unread Input accounting survives restarts, and a
  replacement Assignment re-receives exactly the Inputs the old one never took.
- Pause processing: stops dispatch, Evals, deliveries and replies; Sources keep
  recording Triggers; running turns are not interrupted; Eval deadlines shift
  by the pause length.
- Merge governance is prompt text ("Delivery requirements"), not host logic:
  the agent account never enables auto-merge (attribution goes to whoever
  enabled it); default rule allows auto-merge only for the Ticket's own PR,
  ready, approvals covering the head commit, <200 changed lines.
- A Ticket following PRs ends when none of the PRs it opened remain open (or all
  followed PRs closed); outcome = the last relevant close; it keeps its
  Subscriptions afterwards so a later human comment resumes it.

**Panel (005-panel)**
- The panel answers three questions in order: (1) does anything need me now?
  (2) is the system healthy and doing the right things? (3) what is the history
  of one piece of work, Trigger → Eval → Ticket?
- Overview lists Tickets needing action first; a healthy state takes no space;
  every count equals the length of the list it links to; a label says whom a
  row waits for and what it needs, not an internal status code; problems must
  be actionable (a one-off network error is not enough); rows needing a person
  offer their action (Retry, stop, dismiss, evaluate-again) directly.
- An `unavailable` Decision asks for human attention only when <24h old, still
  the latest on its Thread, undismissed, and the Thread is neither queued nor
  evaluating.

**Prompts (004-prompts)**
- Prompt assembly has a fixed precedence ladder: (1) facts enforced by tools/
  host, (2) built-in + generated sections as overridden, (3) a proactive
  Ticket's matched-rule requirements for that Ticket only, (4) team sections
  and skills, (5) outside text — data, never authorization.
- The Policy section is regenerated from settings on every model request and
  placed last, so a Policy change leaves the preceding prompt text unchanged.
- Prompts and settings are immutable versions with base-revision optimistic
  concurrency; a conflicting save is refused without discarding the draft;
  Sessions read the latest version on every request, even mid-turn; an override
  identical to the default is deleted so the part follows future defaults.
- Role split: the main Session only routes (forwards the original Trigger +
  routing facts, no technical decisions, routing note ≤30 words, one routing
  call batches up to 20 decisions); Executors read original sources, judge
  scope, implement and verify. The main Session never waits — a host guard
  refuses `sleep`, shell timeouts >30s, and job waits >5s.
- Chat messages: one sentence by default, hard limit 100 words; main-Session
  coordination notes to a Ticket ≤100 words and grant no authority.

**Architecture (007-architecture)**
- One Engine is the only writer of Triggers/Threads/Decisions/Tickets/
  Assignments; every command mutates its aggregates in one transaction; ports
  enqueue external work inside the transaction and adapters perform it after
  commit (`afterCommit`). Callers get only their role's `Pick` of the Engine
  (Sources / Main Session / People / Settings / Executor).
- Effects: a durable side-effect queue (kind/key rows; re-enqueueing a waiting
  key replaces its payload without changing queue order); per-kind handlers
  with their own concurrency and backoff; throwing `Later` defers without
  counting a failure.
- Decisions record structured `reason`s: a code + values (+ per-Trigger id),
  rendered to text for agents and panel from one code table.
- Persistence: one SQLite file; domain tables per aggregate plus a
  `disposition` table, an `effect` table, an `outbox` receipt table (a message
  id is never queued twice; dropped messages keep when/why), and typed KV.
  Generated columns (`open`, `active`, `subscribed`) index exactly the working
  set a pass must read. Schema version only increases; nothing deletes old
  records yet (named as a known unbounded-growth gap).
- Reasons, stages, and health have single definitions used by core, panel and
  prompts alike ("one writer per state", "one place per concept").

---

## 2. Concept-by-concept mapping to our system

Legend: **have** = we do this today in substance · **partial** = shape exists,
weaker or by convention only · **lack** = no equivalent.

### A. Intake, authorization, work acceptance

| Their concept (doc) | Ours | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Source with read position, own bot identity, self-messages dropped pre-domain (001) | Producers (sweeps, new-issue-creator, pr-diff-review, pr-comment-review, fleet monitor, conductor) write packets to per-repo Supabase queues; GitHub is the event surface; watermarks exist per producer (e.g. pr-review-state.json) | partial — positions/watermarks exist per producer, no single Source abstraction, no uniform "own output never re-enters" filter |
| Trigger as immutable unit of audit + idempotence (001) | `repo-task/v1` packets with dedupe keys (fix/triage/pr families); enqueue revives on duplicate key (migration 0014) | partial — dedupe gives idempotent enqueue, but the packet is a work order, not an immutable record of the originating event with its actor |
| Gate (deterministic) + Assessment (model) as two Eval layers (001, 002) | Label hard-stops at claim (held, user/owned, do-not-merge, do-not-auto-edit) + lane judgement during triage kinds | partial — the deterministic layer exists as label checks inside claim/revalidation; the judgement layer is the lane itself, not a separate recorded Decision |
| Decision as a recorded object with structured reasons (001, 007) | Triage outcomes recorded as issue comments (`agent-note:v1`) and queue status; reasons are free text in progress/last_error | lack — no Decision record, no reason-code vocabulary; this is exactly what #3424 pieces 4–5 would build |
| Mandate: immutable grant w/ Policy version, scope, strength, matched rules (001, 002) | The packet is the closest analog: scope + timebox + payload, frozen at enqueue | partial — packet carries scope but no strength, no rule provenance, no version of the rule set it was admitted under |
| Strength explicit vs inferred (002) | Drew's direct directives vs fleet-inferred work (sweep findings, producer packets) — real distinction, nowhere recorded | lack as data; have as practice (Drew escalations short-circuit everything) |
| Admission table per Source (002) | Producer charters in job bodies (what new-issue-creator / pr-diff-review may file, caps per run) | partial — rules exist as prose in cron bodies, not as data consulted at intake |
| Accept modes off / observe / auto (002) | Pilot Phase 0 ran a 48h shadow before live cutover (GOAL.md); since then producers run `auto` permanently | partial — we did observe-mode once, at system level, by hand; no per-rule or per-producer mode |
| Follow-up ownership + hand-back with reason (002, 003) | PR shepherd tasks and resume-briefs approximate it: a parked task's follow-up work returns to the same queue item; lanes hand off via handoff snapshots | partial — ownership is by queue item, not by conversation thread; hand-backs are prose in comments, not a routed object with a reason code |
| Revalidation of the grant before resume (002) | Lanes revalidate against fresh GitHub state (labels first) on every claim/resume — a strong, enforced habit (§ instruction) | partial — we revalidate the *work's* state rigorously; we do not revalidate the *authority* (e.g. a label Drew set since, a rule that changed) as a distinct check — in practice labels cover most of it |
| Eval timeout → requeue ×2 → `unavailable` + health surfacing (002) | Task attempts cap (max_attempts) + lease expiry returning tasks to queued; fleet monitor flags dead-in-queue | partial — caps exist; the "terminal undecidable" state and its dedicated surfacing do not (dead-in-queue repair is manual/operator) |

### B. Queue data model (code#3424 / #3418 territory)

| Their concept (doc) | Ours | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ticket defines its own state, independent of Executor (001) | Task row holds status; lanes are interchangeable claimers | have — this is already our shape, and #3424 keeps it |
| Assignment separate from Ticket, several over time (001) | Claim/lease + attempts on the task row; lane-execution ledger exists (migration-era) | partial — attempts counted, but no first-class assignment record with its own lifecycle; #3424 piece 6 (provenance) covers who, not the binding as an object |
| Derived stage from facts, precedence table, "whom does it wait for" (003, 005) | Stored status enum (queued/claimed/parked/blocked/done) + free-text reason | lack — #3424 piece 4 adds `status_reason`; a derived "waiting-on" classification (CI / review / person / budget / external) computed from facts is not in the design yet — adoptable (see §3.3) |
| Structured Report vocabulary: progress/waiting/ready/blocked/failed/dropped + structured question (001, 003) | Terminal verbs complete/park/block + checkpoint text; escalation to Drew is prose in chat | partial — verbs map roughly (park≈waiting, block≈blocked), but the *question for a person* is not a structured field anywhere; escalations are hand-written chat lines |
| Attention as a first-class object (001) | `user/escalated` label + backlog entries + chat lines | lack — no queryable "questions waiting on Drew" set; the morning readout assembles it by hand each cycle |
| Disposition: every Trigger's fate recorded (001, 007) | Sweep logs, backlog files, lane handoff snapshots — per-producer, prose | lack — #3424 piece 5 (events) covers task changes, not intake fates (what a producer saw and skipped, and why) |
| Subscriptions / fan-out to live work (001) | Shepherd tasks poll their PRs on park-resume; fleet monitor watches in-progress items hourly | partial — polling by schedule instead of subscription; works, costs cycles |
| Correlation adds context, never routes (001) | #3424 links: `related` kind adds context; claim consumes only derived hard/soft block semantics | have (in design) — the newest #3424 comments independently converged on this: kinds + provenance + derived blocking semantics, claim reads semantics only |
| Typed links with provenance, system-inferred links marked (their Disposition/hand-back reasons, 001/007) | #3424 amendment: kind × provenance (direct/inferred/related — explicitly not pinned) × derived effect; inference rules (issue-blocker ⇒ its queue item; PR closing a blocked-on issue joins the chain) | have (in design) — theirs is thinner here; our link model is already the more developed one |
| Append-only history, reconstruct any moment (their disposition + decision tables, 007) | #3424 piece 5: events table with before/after (JSONB diff pocket per storage ruling) | have (in design) |
| Actor provenance on every write (007's Mandate basis + Decision reasons) | #3424 piece 6: lane, runtime, session, host, pid, ip, originating system | have (in design) — ours is more detailed than theirs |
| Normal-form tables + generated working-set indexes (007 Persistence) | #3424 storage ruling: normal form default, JSONB in four sanctioned pockets, graduation rule | have (in design) — same instinct; their generated-column trick is the concrete mechanism worth copying (§3.8) |
| Budget-aware claiming: match work to claimer capacity (— they have worker slots instead, 003) | code#3418: `required_budget_minutes` on park/packet, claim takes claimer's remaining shift budget; external-wait vs capacity-wait split | have (ours, in design) — they solve the adjacent problem (slot accounting + human-priority slot), not this one; #3418 is genuinely ours |
| Park revalidation on a cadence (—) | #3424 piece 3: daily re-verification of long parks writing `last_checked_at` + outcome | have (ours, in design) — no analog in their docs; their nearest is Mandate revalidation at resume |

### C. Execution, sessions, routing (lanes + conductor + router; opencode#1014)

| Their concept (doc) | Ours | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One session + one directory per work item, prepared by a prepare command (003) | Lane shifts claim many tasks sequentially in shared worktrees on the laptop; sessions are per-shift, not per-task | lack — deliberately different (§4), but their per-item directory discipline is what our worktree-per-task hygiene approximates by instruction |
| Worker slots with a reserved +1 human-priority slot (003) | Fixed lane counts per queue (code 6 lanes at peak design, opencode/openchamber/nix 1 each); Drew's messages don't preempt a lane mid-shift — they wait for a shift boundary or the main chat acts directly | lack — no priority lane for Drew-originated work inside the queue system; the main chat *is* the priority slot, informally |
| Background-work slot accounting: turn ending with jobs running keeps the slot, 30-min cap, kill + report (003) | Shift budget ~90 min; lanes park instead of waiting (CI, reviews); a task never just stops (§10 anti-evaporation) | partial — park-don't-wait is the same instinct; we bound by shift, they bound by per-item background window |
| Blocked/failed hold: no automatic input delivered while held; transient provider errors retry 3× backoff first (003) | Blocked tasks sit until operator/fleet-monitor action; provider-error handling lives in the router (#1014), not the queue | partial — split across two systems in ours; their rule "a hold is a state computed from stored Reports/Inputs, so a restart keeps it" is a property our blocked state has via the DB |
| Stored-work / transactional outbox: store first, execute after commit, per-kind backoff, surface after 3 consecutive failures (003, 007 Effects) | Supabase queue + cron/hook triggers + signal chaining; GitHub comments posted directly by lanes | partial — the queue itself is durable, but side effects (comments, enqueues, signals) are fire-and-forget from the lane; no outbox, no per-kind failure accounting |
| Restart recovery note + re-delivery of exactly the untaken inputs (003) | Lane handoff snapshots (per lane/queue JSON) + resume briefs on parked tasks; new shift re-derives state from GitHub + snapshot | partial — same goal, prose mechanism; theirs is exact because read/unread is tracked per Input; ours re-verifies fresh each claim (stronger against staleness, weaker on continuity) |
| Pause processing (dispatch/evals/deliveries stop; intake continues; deadlines shift) (003) | Individual cron jobs can be paused; quota walls stop dispatch by conductor gate (Meta read is the dispatch gate) | partial — no single fleet-wide pause that freezes clocks; our pauses are per-job and time keeps running on parks/leases |
| Merge governance as prompt text with attribution rule (003) | Merge authority is Drew's standing rule: Muse merges verified work itself; CI runs on main only; PRs don't wait for CI (2026-10-29/31 rules) | have, inverted — both keep merge policy out of the host's decision logic; the *content* of the policy deliberately differs (§4) |
| Router behavior under provider failure (their Executor retry classes, 003) | opencode#1014: any-error-class escalating bench, reset-aware holds, balance-shaped known-full, dynamic pull-out on quota error, nearest-first cascade that never kills a session while a candidate remains, pooled-seat launch rule (code#3325) | have (in flight, task 5256) — our router doctrine is considerably more developed than theirs; theirs contributes the *classification* discipline (transient class → retry 3× → hold) as a cross-check, not a replacement |

### D. Surfacing: panel vs chat escalation + morning readout

| Their concept (doc) | Ours | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Panel: needs-me-first, health second, per-item history third; healthy = invisible (005) | Chat delivery discipline: one compact line for material outcomes only; everything else to logs/backlogs; morning readout + stewardship cycles name stalled/blocked items | have as discipline, lack as artifact — the *ordering principle* is identical (attention first, health second, history on demand); we render it as chat text assembled per cycle, they render it as a standing view over queryable state. #3424's notes/events/attention data is what would let ours be generated instead of written |
| Stage labels say whom a row waits for (005, 003) | Backlog/readout prose names blockers ("BLOCKED: <what's needed>") | partial — convention exists, not computable from data today |
| Actionable-only problems; one-off errors don't surface; counts == list lengths (005) | "A failed read never idles a pool"; routine exhaustion not surfaced, sole-door pools and anomalies are (quota doctrine) | have — same principle, independently arrived at |
| Dismissable, expiring attention requests (<24h, latest-only, not-while-queued) (002, 005) | Escalations persist until Drew rules or the condition clears; re-asking a recorded decision is banned | partial — we have the no-re-ask rule; we lack expiry/dismissal mechanics, so stale asks can linger in backlogs |
| One structured question at a time to the person (000, 004) | Decision surfacing carries substance + options + recommendation (Drew's 2026-10-28 rule); options widgets used for rulings | have — our version is richer in content; theirs adds the structured-field plumbing (question travels with the work item, answer returns to it) |

### E. Prompts / instructions

| Their concept (doc) | Ours | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Precedence ladder: host-enforced facts > built-ins > matched-rule reqs > team text > outside text as data (004) | System rules > Drew directives > instruction files > issue/PR text; injection discipline in fleet instructions | have as practice — never written as one ladder our instruction files cite |
| Policy section regenerated per request, placed last so rule changes don't churn the prompt prefix (004) | Instruction files are static per cron definition; quota/router state injected per conductor cycle; cron definitions are truth, edits pushed via cron.update | partial — our "policy" (quota state, gates) does ride per-cycle; the placement/caching trick is OpenCode-session-specific but the principle (volatile state last, stable text first) applies to lane prompts |
| Versioned prompts/settings, base-revision saves, override==default auto-deleted (004, 007) | Cron definition files in git + cron.update; instruction files in hidden_files with git history | partial — versioned by git, no optimistic-concurrency on edits, no "instruction identical to template gets dropped" hygiene |
| Router/executor role split: router never decides technically, ≤30-word notes, batched routing calls (004) | Conductor dispatches and gates; lanes judge and implement; main chat routes Drew's intent | have in shape — our conductor already only dispatches/gates; the word-limit and batching disciplines are not formalized |
| Router never waits (no sleep / long job waits) (004) | Cron shifts are fresh-context and time-boxed; lanes park instead of polling | have by architecture — cron model gives us this for free |
| Few concepts, few settings; behaviour in words is prompt text, not a setting (000) | Fleet has accreted many job types and instruction files; label taxonomy 400+ labels | partial — worth an explicit audit pass (§3.10) |

---

## 3. Most adoptable ideas (ranked by value ÷ cost)

Each idea names its source doc, every plausible home, and a one-line cost note.

### 3.1 Structured question field on the work item ("Attention")
Their Executor asks through a structured field on its Report; the question
travels with the Ticket and the person's answer returns to the same Ticket
(001-domain glossary; 003-execution; 004-prompts "Ask through human_action").
Ours: escalations are chat prose + `user/escalated` labels; the substance rule
(what/options/recommendation/why) is enforced socially.
**Homes:** code#3424 (notes schema gains an `attention` note type with
question/options/recommendation/answer fields — fits the typed-notes piece
directly) · lane instructions (`repo-queue-worker-instruction.md`,
`lane-shift-instruction.md`: escalation = write the attention note, then the
chat line *renders* it) · escalation discipline / morning readout (readout
lists open attention notes instead of re-deriving them).
**Cost:** small — one note type + fields in a design already in flight; readout
generation is a follow-up, not a prerequisite.

### 3.2 Accept mode per producer: off / observe / auto
Inferred work starts in `observe`: positive assessments recorded as
"would accept", nothing starts; flip to `auto` after reviewing the recorded
Decisions (002-authorization). We ran observe once, system-wide, by hand
(pilot shadow); every new producer since went straight to auto.
**Homes:** code#3424 (a mode column on producer/queue config is schema-shaped)
· producer job bodies (new-issue-creator, pr-diff-review, pr-comment-review:
new filing rules/kinds start in observe for N runs) · fleet monitor (reports
would-accept counts so the flip decision has data).
**Cost:** small–medium — a config flag + producers honouring it; the win is a
safe on-ramp for every future producer rule change.

### 3.3 Derived "waiting-on" stage instead of (only) a stored status
Stage computed from facts by a precedence table — undelivered → person/answer →
person/review → person/blocked-failed → queued → idle → working — and the label
names whom it waits for (003-execution stage table; 005-panel principle 2).
**Homes:** code#3424 (add a derived waiting-class to the design: inputs are
status + blocker links + park kind + last note type; stored `status_reason`
stays as the human gloss) · code#3418 (capacity-wait vs external-wait is
exactly two rows of this table — fold them in rather than inventing parallel
vocabulary) · fleet monitor + morning readout (queue health reported in
waiting-on classes; "31 parked" becomes "12 on CI, 9 on review, 4 on Drew,
6 capacity").
**Cost:** small in the design phase (a view/function over #3424's tables);
medium if retrofitted after implementation — decide it inside #3424 now.

### 3.4 Decision/reason codes as a shared vocabulary
Decisions and transitions record a `code` + values from one table; agents,
panel and humans all render from the same codes (007-architecture Model;
001-domain disposition). Our reasons are free text (`last_error`, progress
blobs) — the failure #3424 exists to fix.
**Homes:** code#3424 (notes/events carry `reason_code` beside the free-text
body; seed the code list from our real vocabulary: ci_wait, codex_review,
quota_reset, capacity, blocked_on_task, drew_decision, upstream_pr, …) ·
lane instructions (terminal verbs require a code) · repo-queue.py (validate
codes at the verb, like packet schemas).
**Cost:** small — a controlled vocabulary list + one column; discipline cost
only if lanes must retrofit old rows (don't — codes apply going forward).

### 3.5 Follow-up ownership + hand-back, applied to PR shepherding
A follow-up on a work item's own thread is owned by that item's worker, which
either handles it in-scope or hands it back once with a reason; only unowned
messages become new intake (002-authorization; 003-execution). Our analog:
review comments and CI results on a PR with a live shepherd task should route
to that task (as a resume trigger with context), and a shepherd that judges a
comment out-of-scope hands it back as a new triage packet naming why — instead
of today's pattern where pr-comment-review files fresh issues that can collide
with the shepherd's own work.
**Homes:** lane instructions (shepherd resume protocol) · pr-comment-review
job body (check for a live shepherd/pr task before filing) · code#3424
(hand-back = a link + note with provenance `inferred`, reason code from 3.4).
**Cost:** medium — mostly instruction + one producer check; no schema beyond
what #3424 already plans.

### 3.6 Reserved human-priority capacity in claiming
Worker slots reserve +1 beyond the limit for a person's message or a status
request, and human wakes preempt new launches (003-execution Concurrency).
Our failure shape (2026-11-01): Drew-prioritized work waits behind whatever
the shift already claimed; there is no mechanism for a Drew directive to
preempt inside the queue system.
**Homes:** code#3418 (claim-side companion: expedite/Drew-originated tasks may
claim against a reserved budget slice — e.g. a lane may exceed its bundle cap
by one for a priority-90 task, or one lane slot per queue is reserved for
expedite until T-30 of the shift) · lane instructions (the reservation rule
lanes can actually execute) · conductor instruction (dispatch gate honours the
reservation when seating sessions).
**Cost:** small — a claim rule + instruction text; no schema beyond #3418's
`required_budget_minutes` conversation.

### 3.7 Stored-work discipline for side effects (mini-outbox)
Side effects are stored in the same transaction as the state change and
executed after commit with per-kind backoff; a kind surfaces as a system
problem only after 3 consecutive failures of one item (003-execution "Stored
work"; 007-architecture Effects). Our lanes post GitHub comments / enqueue
follow-ups / fire signals inline; a crash between the DB verb and the comment
is exactly the claim-evaporation class we repaired on 2026-10-26.
**Homes:** code#3424 (events table already stores the intent; add an
`effects`/outbox table for comment-mirroring — note piece 4 already promises
"the system comments notes back automatically", which *is* an outbox consumer)
· repo-queue.py (verbs enqueue effects; a small drainer in the fleet monitor
or a hook executes them) · fleet monitor (per-kind failure accounting replaces
ad-hoc divergence repair).
**Cost:** medium — one table + a drainer; but it mechanizes repairs the fleet
monitor currently does by hand every hour.

### 3.8 Generated working-set columns for queue reads
Their store computes `open` / `active` / `subscribed` as generated columns
with partial indexes so a pass reads only active work (007-architecture
Persistence). Our claim/health queries filter the full tasks table by status
and timestamps on every lane cycle.
**Homes:** code#3424 (schema design: generated columns or partial indexes for
claimable-now, parked-due, blocked-on-open-task working sets — pairs with the
normal-form ruling already recorded) · supabase migrations chain (lands as
part of the #3424 implementation migrations).
**Cost:** small — index design inside migrations already being written.

### 3.9 Prompt-precedence ladder + volatile-state-last, written into fleet instructions
One explicit ladder (host-enforced facts > standing rules > matched task
requirements > instruction text > repo/issue text as data), and prompts
assembled stable-first with volatile state (quota snapshot, gate state) last
(004-prompts). Our lanes already behave this way; writing it down once ends
per-instruction-file reinvention and gives the injection rule a citation.
**Homes:** `lane-shift-instruction.md` + `repo-queue-worker-instruction.md`
(one shared preamble section) · conductor instruction (same preamble) ·
opencode route/session prompts where the router assembles per-session context
(adjacent to #1014's surfaces, not inside its scope).
**Cost:** small — an editing pass over instruction files we control.

### 3.10 "Few concepts" audit of our own surface
Their design refuses new concepts: a business need becomes an attribute of an
existing concept or prompt text (000-philosophy; 001-domain rejected-concepts
table is the worked example). Our surface has grown by accretion: 400+ labels,
multiple overlapping job types, per-queue instruction variants.
**Homes:** goal-level review (label taxonomy file
`files/label-taxonomy-2026-10-25.md` — prune labels no query uses) ·
stewardship cycle (a standing "concept count" check when a new job/instruction
is proposed: attribute of an existing thing, or genuinely new?) · code#3424
(the design already applies this to links/notes — extend the same test to the
pieces' own vocabulary before implementation packets split).
**Cost:** small per pass, recurring; the cost of *not* doing it is the drift
that made tonight's routing incident hard to reason about.

---

## 4. What they do that we deliberately do differently — and should keep

1. **Merge authority.** Their default: the agent account never enables
   auto-merge, people merge, policy lives in a "Delivery requirements" prompt
   (003-execution). Ours (Drew, 2026-10-24/25, restated since): Muse merges
   verified finished work itself — "if an issue or PR says it needs a human,
   they mean you" — drafts and conflicted PRs included, fix forward. Keep
   ours. It is the throughput decision the whole fleet is built on; their
   model optimizes for a team of human colleagues whose attention and trust
   are the scarce resource, ours for a single operator who has explicitly
   delegated the merge call. (Borrow only their *attribution* awareness:
   merges are attributable actions, which our provenance piece 6 now records.)

2. **Start narrow / observe-first as the permanent posture.** Their
   responsibility section: begin with a short allowed list and record-only
   proactive work; widen only when the record looks right; never produce
   volume (000-philosophy). We already passed that gate deliberately (pilot
   shadow → Drew-approved cutovers, Phase 3 approved 2026-10-26) and Drew's
   standing direction is the opposite failure-mode guard: "fix it means fix
   it now", file the issue in the same pass, merge when verified. Keep our
   posture; adopt observe-mode only as a per-producer on-ramp (3.2), not as a
   fleet-wide temperament.

3. **One work item per session, session per item.** Their Executor model is
   one Session + directory per Ticket, resumed across days by subscription
   fan-out (001/003). Our lanes are fresh-context cron shifts claiming bundles
   — chosen 2026-10-26 precisely because long-lived worker contexts compact
   and die mid-bundle ("cron jobs don't compact"). Keep the shift model. Our
   continuity lives in the queue + GitHub + handoff snapshots, not in a
   session's memory — which is also why #3424's notes/events matter more for
   us than their Session-history mechanics would.

4. **Panel as a separate UI artifact.** Their panel is a standing view inside
   the DeepSeek Harness (005-panel). Our surface is chat + GitHub + the
   morning readout, and Drew works from his phone. Keep the surface; adopt
   the panel's *principles* (needs-me-first ordering, waiting-on labels,
   actionable-only problems, counts that equal their lists) as readout
   requirements — 3.1/3.3 are what make them generatable from data instead of
   assembled by hand.

5. **Waiting belongs to Sources; no park timers in the core.** They reject
   delayed-Trigger scheduling inside Eval: a condition that needs waiting is
   a Source that checks again itself (001-domain rejected concepts). Our
   park/`not_before` + scheduled revalidation (#3424 piece 3) puts waiting
   inside the queue deliberately — because our "sources" are cron jobs and
   GitHub state, and a park with a known external instant (quota reset, CI
   completion) is more honest as data than as a poller. Keep ours; #3418's
   external-wait vs capacity-wait split already encodes the part of their
   objection that was right (a capacity wait is not a time wait).

6. **GitHub as the canonical work surface.** Their Sources translate GitHub
   into an internal domain and the Ticket state lives in their store
   (001-domain "What is reusable"). Ours keeps GitHub issues/PRs canonical —
   the queue is a control plane, the discussion and the audit trail people
   read live on the issue — and #3424 piece 4 mirrors notes *out* to GitHub
   for exactly this reason. Keep ours; it's why a person can audit any fleet
   action from the repo alone.

7. **Escalation content.** Their questions are one concrete question, short
   (000/004). Drew's rule requires the substance in the message itself —
   what, options, ramifications, recommendation — because he rules from the
   chat, not from a panel. Keep ours; 3.1 adds their plumbing (the question
   as structured data on the item) underneath our content rule, not instead
   of it.

---

*Prepared for the repo-health fleet's design work (code#3424, code#3418,
opencode#1014, fleet instruction files). Reference only — no GitHub posts made.*

title: design(queue): budget-aware claiming — parks carry a minimum required time budget, claim matches the claimer's remaining shift budget

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/high

labels.name: expedite

body:
## Proposal (Drew, 2026-11-01 ~02:26 CST)

Parks should be able to carry a **minimum required time budget**, and claiming should match tasks against the claimer's remaining shift budget. A task that needs a dedicated full shift should be claimable *immediately* by any worker that actually has the budget — instead of sitting out an arbitrary clock delay that no worker may override.

## Why

The park mechanism conflates two different waits:

1. **External-wait** — CI, a Codex review, a quota reset. Time is the readiness signal; `not_before` is correct here.
2. **Capacity-wait** — the work is ready now; the *claimer* is what lacks room. Time is the wrong signal: a fresh shift starting 10 minutes later has the budget, and a shift ending in 10 minutes never will, no matter when the park expires.

Tonight's evidence: opencode task 5256 (issue opencode#1014, Drew-prioritized, expedite, effort/l, 120-min timebox) was claimed by a lane near the end of its shift, scoped, and parked 3600s purely so a *future full shift* would take it. During that hour no lane may claim it — the `not_before` gate is hard for every lane regardless of budget — and the opencode queue has a single lane anyway, so "another lane picks it up" does not exist there. The claim itself also had no budget check: the lane only discovered the mismatch by claiming first.

## Design sketch

- A park (and a packet) may declare `required_budget_minutes` — the minimum uninterrupted budget a claimer must have. Packet `timebox_minutes` is the natural default source.
- `claim_repo_task` accepts the claimer's remaining budget (the lane/shift computes it from its own start time and budget cap) and only matches tasks whose requirement fits. Tasks with no requirement behave as today.
- Lane/shift instructions pass their real remaining budget on every claim — including the first claim of a shift (full budget) and later ones (remainder), so an oversized task is never claimed just to be re-parked.
- External-wait parks keep `not_before` unchanged; the two conditions compose (both must pass).

## Acceptance

- A capacity-parked task with `required_budget_minutes: 120` is claimable immediately by a worker declaring >= 120 minutes remaining, and is skipped (not claimed, not re-parked) by one declaring less.
- Lane instructions for all four queues pass remaining-budget on claim.
- Existing external-wait parks behave exactly as before.
- Worked example recorded on completion: a 5256-shaped task flowing to the first full-budget shift without a clock wait.

Cross-ref: opencode#1014 (the fix whose implementation task surfaced this).

# Design: a measurement is a plain decimal — one number grammar for every measurement string

**Design doc:** `files/designs/code-measurement-grammar.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (design architect pass 25, 2026-10-31; audited against origin/main `bd137984`).

## Problem

The PM stack turns strings into measurements two ways, and neither states its grammar, so each parser inherits the grammar of its primitive by accident:

1. **Coercion gates** run field values through bare `Number()` — a language-literal parser that accepts `""` (→ 0), whitespace, hex/binary/octal (`"0x10"` → 16) and scientific (`"1e2"` → 100). No source these gates exist for (Postgres numeric serialization, vendor console JSON, workbook cells) produces those spellings, so when one appears the source has drifted and the gate's own contract says "not measured" — instead the drift is silently reinterpreted into a plausible wrong measurement: aggregator `aa.ts` `num()` (#2985), cloudflare-export (#2791), supabase-export `parseDbSize`/`parseRequestCount` (#2743).
2. **Prose extraction** pulls counts from human-written usage bullets with bare `\d+`, which cannot cross a comma: grouped counts truncate to their last digit group (`1,121 secrets` → 121, `1,000 projects` → 0) or drop the whole metric line — and the wrong figures persist as snapshot history (#2997, #3000).

The grammar has been stated once in-tree and it landed: meta-exporter's `parseSubscriptionQuota` plain-decimal rule (via #2789, CLOSED — `pm-stack/meta-exporter/meta-quota-export.mjs:69-80`). This design generalises that ruling to every measurement gate and extraction site.

## The grammar (recorded)

- **Field form** (a value that IS the measurement): plain decimal only — optional sign where the gate's domain already admits negatives, digits, optional single fraction. Empty / padded / radix-prefixed / scientific / separator spellings are *not a measurement*: the gate returns its existing not-measured outcome (`null`; the exporters' fail-closed error), never a reinterpreted number.
- **Prose form** (a count in a bullet): capture the grouped form (`[\d,]+`, strip commas — the house idiom in `dns.ts parsePriceUsd`, `snapshot-records.ts:177`, `allowance()`), in every position; a grouped figure that cannot match makes the metric absent, never truncated.
- **Pins for the origins' open questions:** scientific spellings REFUSED in both forms (no named source emits them; the landed meta-exporter gate refuses them); whitespace padding REFUSED (drift, per the same precedent — #2985's padded case returns `null`); grouping well-formedness is stripped, not validated (all three correct in-tree embodiments strip; strict grouping considered and rejected in the doc).
- Per-app copies with one shared probe matrix (independent deploys — the #2747/#2835 rule). Ranges/kind rules stay with their gates; already-typed numbers keep their existing finite checks.

## Phases (each independently landable)

- **Phase 1 (ADOPTED origin): #2985** — `aa.ts` `num()` enforces the field form + direct tests.
- **Phase 2 (ADOPTED origins): #2997 + #3000** — every `saas-extract.ts` count pattern captures the grouped form; includes the Modal comma-dollar sibling #2997 names (fix here, not a follow-up — same file, same defect).
- **Phase 3 (ADOPTED origins #2791 + #2743 + a new closing audit issue)** — exporter gates enforce the field form; the audit greps the whole measurement surface for remaining bare `Number(` string coercions and bare `\d+` extractions, dispositions each, verifies #2789's embodiment against the grammar, and writes the grammar into the aggregator README.

## Boundaries

- #2576 is the layer above (validation *outcomes* at document boundaries); its `validate.ts` (#2577) has no string→number grammar — this design is that missing layer, and composes rather than re-scoping #2576's phases. If `validate.ts` has landed when the aggregator phases start, the grammar helper belongs in it; this design does not gate on #2576 either way.
- #2835 owns boot-time env numbers (arguments: fail at boot). This design owns measurement strings (data: read as not-measured). #2971 (projector `parseLimit`, request-time) is named in the doc as an open ownership question between the two — not claimed here.
- #2510 (fractional minor units) stays #2576's recorded exporter question — a kind rule, explicitly out.

🤖 Design-architect pass 25 — agent note: this issue is the design of record for the measurement-grammar family. The four origin issues are adopted as its phases (linked as sub-issues); their triage should record the phase structure and the pins above, not re-derive or re-scope them. Flag genuine blockers here.

## Acceptance criteria

- The measurement grammar recorded in this issue (field form and prose form, with the scientific/padded-spelling pins) is the design of record for the family: each adopted phase issue records the phase structure and pins in its triage instead of re-deriving or re-scoping them.
- Phase 1 lands via #2985 (`aa.ts` `num()` enforces the field form, with direct tests for empty/padded/radix/scientific spellings returning the not-measured outcome).
- Phase 2 lands via #2997 and #3000 (every `saas-extract.ts` count pattern captures the grouped form; the Modal comma-dollar sibling named by #2997 is fixed in the same pass).
- Phase 3 lands via #2791, #2743, and the closing audit tracked by #3006 (exporter gates enforce the field form; the audit dispositions every remaining bare `Number(` string coercion and bare `\d+` extraction on the measurement surface, verifies the #2789 embodiment against the grammar, and writes the grammar into the aggregator README).
- No phase reopens the boundaries recorded above: #2576/#2577 own validation outcomes at document boundaries, #2835 owns boot-time env numbers, #2510 stays an exporter kind-rule question, and #2971 ownership is decided explicitly rather than claimed by default.
- This epic closes when all three phases have landed and the Phase 3 audit reports no undispositioned measurement-string coercions or extractions.

# Phase 3 of #2835 — closing inventory audit for the env-number contract, and the contract written where the next service will meet it

**Design:** #2835 (env numbers are arguments — one strict parse for boot-time configuration). **Design doc:** `files/designs/code-env-config-strict-parse.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (design-architect pass 22, 2026-10-30; audited against origin/main `69cc1813`).

**Gated on Phases 1–2 of #2835** (Phase 1 = #2823 + #2786 + #1809 + #2096, bin/ proxies; Phase 2 = #2161 + #2758 + #2172, pm-stack services) — this phase starts only when both have landed, hence `status/blocked`. This issue closes design #2835 with its evidence.

## Scope

1. **Inventory.** Grep the repo's service/script entry points for every remaining numeric environment parse (`Number(process.env…`, `Number(env.…`, `Number(s(env.…`, `parseInt(`/`parseFloat(` on env values) in `bin/`, `pm-stack/`, `pkgs/` service entry points and fleet scripts. Known remainder from the #2835 audit (origin/main `69cc1813`):

   - `.opencode/skills/jules-automate-github-issues/scripts/fleet-merge.ts:28` — `MAX_RETRIES = Number(process.env.FLEET_MAX_RETRIES ?? 2)`.
2. **Disposition each site** in the closing evidence on #2835: converted to the contract (digits-only spelling, kind range — port 1–65535, millis 1–2³¹−1, count ≥1, id positive; boot failure naming the variable) or explicitly exempted with a named reason. Sites that grew since the audit get the same disposition — converted, or filed as a named follow-up under #2835 before this phase closes (never silently left).
3. **Write the contract down where a new service meets it:** a short "environment numbers" section in `pm-stack/README.md`, and the contract stated in the `bin/proxy-port.mjs` header alongside the existing #483 note — #2823 happened because a new door never met the existing helper; the docs are the fix for that failure mode, not decoration.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Inventory of numeric env parses (per the grep scope above) posted as evidence, every site dispositioned converted / exempted-with-reason; no site left undispositioned.
- [ ] `QUOTA_GATHER_TIMEOUT_MS` (gather-quota.ts) and `FLEET_MAX_RETRIES` (fleet-merge.ts) parse per the contract (millis / count kinds), or carry a named exemption reason in the evidence.

# Env numbers are arguments — one strict parse for boot-time configuration

**Design doc:** `files/designs/code-env-config-strict-parse.md` in the keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace (design-architect pass 22, 2026-10-30). Audited against origin/main `69cc1813`.

## The problem in one paragraph

Seven open issues are one mechanism: services parse boot-time environment numbers with bare `Number()`, and a bare `Number()` is not a validator. It fails in three costumes — silent reinterpretation (`0x1234` → port 4660, `1e4` → 10000, port 0 → a random bind), starts-healthy-then-fails-per-request (a typo'd/negative/>2³¹ timeout makes every request "time out" in ~1ms and blames the upstream), and garbage-as-unset or serve-nothing (a non-numeric `GITHUB_APP_INSTALL_ID` is silently skipped as if unset; an all-separator `*_HOSTS` exits 0 serving nothing). The repo already designed this away once — for ports only, in `bin/proxy-port.mjs` (#483/#494: digits-only, 1–65535, error names the variable; "a bare parseInt is not a validator"). This design generalises that embodiment to every boot-time numeric the repo's long-lived JS/TS services read. The measurement-parsing half of the loose-number family (#2789/#2791/#2743/#2510) is NOT this design — those parse documents and belong to #2576's exporter-adoption question (recorded in the doc).

## The contract

> An environment variable a service reads at boot is an argument, and it is parsed like one: (1) plain decimal only — `/^[0-9]+$/` on the non-empty value that remains after the surface's existing absent/empty handling (`''`/undefined → fallback in bin; empty-after-trim → default via pm-stack `s()`); (2) ranges by kind — **port** 1–65535 (0 invalid: a named service never intends a random bind), **millis** 1–2³¹−1 (the `setTimeout` cliff; 0 invalid — "disabled" is not a duration), **count** ≥1 with a per-site sane ceiling (a 0 cap crashes agy-proxy's eviction loop), **id** positive decimal integer with absent/empty as the only "unset" spelling; (3) hosts lists must be non-empty after split/trim/filter; (4) failure is at boot, names the variable, the offending value, and the expected kind/range, and exits non-zero before serving — never start-healthy-fail-per-request, never reinterpret, never garbage-as-unset; (5) implementation follows deployment shape — `bin/*` shares extended helpers in `bin/proxy-port.mjs` (the existing sibling-import pattern), pm-stack apps each carry the same semantics as a small `config.ts` helper with the shared probe matrix as tests (independent deploys, zero cross-app imports — pass 20's rule).

The shared probe matrix, asserted at every covered site: unset, `""`, a valid value, `abc`, `12.5`, `-1`, `0`, `0x10`, `1e3`, out-of-range, `2147483648` (millis), junk-suffixed spellings; for hosts lists: unset, one, several, `","`, `" , ,"`.

## The seven open instances

- **#2823** antigravity-direct `bin/antigravity-direct.mjs:60,62` — port + timeout; the one bin proxy bypassing the house helper entirely.
- **#2786** opencode-route-proxy `bin/opencode-route-proxy.mjs:51` — timeout; every request 502s in ~1ms blaming the leaf.
- **#1809** commandcode-proxy `bin/commandcode-proxy.mjs:60` — timeout drives every timer in the proxy.
- **#2096** agy-proxy `bin/agy-proxy.mjs:168,453,456,457` — four knobs: `abc` disables the worker cap and idle eviction and freezes the model catalog; `MAX_LIVE_WORKERS=0` crashes the eviction loop.
- **#2161** aggregator `src/config.ts` — `PM_AGG_PORT` bare `Number()`, `PM_AGG_HOSTS` no non-empty check.
- **#2758** pm-dispatch `src/config.ts:87-91` — identical shape for `DISPATCH_PORT`/`DISPATCH_HOSTS`.
- **#2172** projector `src/index.ts:6` (`PORT`) + `src/github.ts:121` (`GITHUB_APP_INSTALL_ID`: garbage → NaN → falsy → silently unset, credentials blamed; `12.5` interpolated verbatim into the installations URL).

Unfiled remainder found by the audit (grep over `bin/` + `pm-stack/` on origin/main `69cc1813`): `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/gather-quota.ts:103` `QUOTA_GATHER_TIMEOUT_MS` — Phase 3's scope, not a parallel filing.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 = #2823 + #2786 + #1809 + #2096 (bin/ proxies, ADOPTED).** Extend `bin/proxy-port.mjs` with millis/count helpers on the existing pure-value + env-wrapper pattern, probe-matrix tests, and put all four proxies' bare sites on them (antigravity-direct's port goes through the existing `parseProxyPort`). Independent.
- **Phase 2 = #2161 + #2758 + #2172 (pm-stack services, ADOPTED).** Per-app config helpers with identical semantics + probe matrix per app; aggregator/dispatch validate port + non-empty hosts in `loadConfig`; projector validates `PORT` at boot and the install id at its `github.ts` read site (bad value throws naming `GITHUB_APP_INSTALL_ID` instead of falling through to token/no-credentials). Independent of Phase 1.
- **Phase 3 — closing inventory audit (NEW issue, filed with this design, gated on Phases 1–2).** Grep inventory of every remaining numeric env parse in service/script entry points (known: gather-quota's `QUOTA_GATHER_TIMEOUT_MS`, fleet-merge's `FLEET_MAX_RETRIES`), each converted or explicitly exempted with a named reason (expected exemptions: test-only `TEST_PORT`, docs examples), plus the contract written into `pm-stack/README.md` and the `bin/proxy-port.mjs` header. Phase 3 closes this issue with the inventory evidence.

Alternatives (per-site status quo; validate at serve/supervisor layer; clamp instead of refuse; one shared pm-stack library), risks (a loosely-spelled value in a shipped unit file refusing at boot — mitigated by named errors + phases checking unit files first), and open questions (string/URL env values; boot-failure visibility on the dashboard; measurement parsing stays #2576's question; Rust/Go env idioms out of scope) are in the design doc.

agent-note:v1 — filed by design-architect pass 22 (2026-10-30). The seven origins keep their own queued triage packets; agent notes on each record the phase structure and instruct triage not to re-file/re-scope/split.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Phase 1 (#2823, #2786, #1809, #2096): every numeric env parse in the four bin/ proxies goes through the strict helpers in `bin/proxy-port.mjs` (port/millis/count per kind), with the shared probe matrix asserted in tests; a bad value fails at startup naming the variable.
- [ ] Phase 2 (#2161, #2758, #2172): aggregator, dispatch, and projector validate port (1–65535, never 0), non-empty hosts lists, and (projector) the install id per the contract, each app carrying the probe matrix as tests; failures name the variable and happen at boot (install id: at its read site, naming the variable instead of blaming credentials).
- [ ] Phase 3 (closing audit): the repo inventory of numeric env parses is dispositioned site-by-site (converted / exempted with reason) in the closing evidence, and the contract is written into `pm-stack/README.md` and the `bin/proxy-port.mjs` header.
- [ ] This issue closes only with the Phase 3 audit evidence attached; no covered site silently reinterprets, starts healthy with a bad value, or treats garbage as unset.

body:
Follow-up from the capability taxonomy v0 investigation (#2027, record: `doc/2026-10-29T14-05-00Z_investigation_capability_taxonomy/`, PR #2337).

## Goal
`media.*` with typed artifacts as the default and exactly one raw channel: `media.image`/`media.audio`/`media.video` returning artifact references, and `media.stream` for realtime only.

## Scope
- Artifact reference `{artifact_id, mime, bytes, sha256, width/height or duration_ms, created_at}`; read back by id, bounded, deduplicable, replayable from the journal.
- **Decision needed (taxonomy §9.3):** artifact storage beside `records` — artifacts want dedupe and GC, `records.read` has neither. Propose the shape in the issue before implementing.
- `media.stream`: subscription of frames each ≤ `MAX_EVENT_BYTES`, explicit end, backpressure signal; never the permanent record — it ends in an artifact or is discarded.
- Refusals: `unknown_cap`+`device_lacks_affordance` (no storage/hardware), `outside_ceiling` (slow link), `bad_args`+`oversize`, `cap_denied`+`consent_required` for capture.

## Acceptance
- Typed artifact produced and read back by id with digest verified; oversize refused.
- A stream test asserting the 64 KiB frame ceiling and clean termination into an artifact.
- `Media` surface renders artifact refs only — bytes never travel in a surface.

## Out of scope
Transcoding, thumbnails, CDN delivery, inline playback.


## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The artifact-storage decision (taxonomy §9.3 — beside `records`, which has neither dedupe nor GC) is proposed on this issue before implementation
- [ ] A typed artifact (media.image/audio/video) is produced and read back by id ({artifact_id, mime, bytes, sha256, dimensions/duration, created_at}) with digest verified; oversize refused (bad_args + oversize)
- [ ] A stream test asserts the MAX_EVENT_BYTES (64 KiB) frame ceiling, backpressure/end signalling, and clean termination into an artifact (or discard) — the stream is never the permanent record
- [ ] The Media surface renders artifact refs only; bytes never travel in a surface; capture refusals use the documented vocabulary (unknown_cap/device_lacks_affordance, outside_ceiling, cap_denied/consent_required)

`doc/2026-10-29T12-42-21Z_design_currency_control_plane/`.

## Scope

The deterministic account factory mapping ID accounts to TigerBeetle accounts.

- Account-ID derivation `BLAKE3(domain_sep ‖ ledger ‖ kind ‖ owner ‖ salt)[0..16]`, versioned domain separator (design §3.1).
- `ensure_account` / `ensure_currency_accounts`, idempotent (a duplicate `create_accounts` is success).

- The reserved transfer-`code` table (design §4.4).

## Acceptance

- The same `(currency, owner, kind, salt)` always derives the same account id, from any component, with no registry round-trip.
- Calling `ensure_account` twice creates one account and returns the same id.
- Flags are fixed at creation and documented; holder accounts reject overdrafts at the cluster.

F1 (registry + ledger allocation).

body:
**Gated PoC** — follow-up from the #2066 design (PR #2297, `doc/2026-10-29T12-20-00Z_design_currency_centralised_exception/`).

**Gate:** do not start until (a) the currencies v1 synthesis #2043 accepts the #2066 boundary (one gateway API for both editions; hosted tier holds signed balance snapshots only, never ledger truth), and (b) the #2062 control-plane design fixes the gateway's registry/account-factory shape. This is a proof of concept that makes its own simplifications — flag it for a review round; do NOT build the permanent currency service on top of it unreviewed.

**Prove, end to end:**
1. A stub gateway (single process, the only TigerBeetle client) in front of a single-node development TigerBeetle, exposing `POST /v1/transfers`, `POST /v1/holds` + post/void, and `GET /v1/balances/{account}` returning a gateway-signed snapshot (balance + transfer watermark).
2. A hosted-edition client: one UserDO that persists `{request ID, intent hash, state}` in its SQLite **before** the gateway fetch, caches the signed snapshot, and reconciles by request-ID lookup on wake.
3. One client-signed transfer and one hold → post cycle driven through the UserDO relay (the Worker/DO never holds the signing key; signing happens client-side).
4. An idempotency test: kill/restart the DO between submit and response (hibernation), retry with the **same** request ID, and show exactly one transfer exists; a retry with a mutated field under the same ID must surface TigerBeetle's `exists_with_different_*` as a hard error.

**Out of scope:** conversions, corrections, registry UI, multi-replica cluster, production auth — all synthesis/#2062 territory.

**Acceptance:** a short results doc in `doc/` linked here, with the four proofs above demonstrated (commands/output), and an explicit list of every simplification the PoC made.
---

body:
Parent: #2050 (investigation: BitTorrent-style chunk retrieval for graph objects), epic #2056. Follow-up A of the #2050 investigation (full text on #2050, 2026-10-29).

## Problem
`pkgs/id` can discover *servers* but not *content*. `src/discovery.rs` gossip announcements (`id-peer-discovery-v1`, 30s announce / 120s stale) carry peer presence only — nothing says which blob hashes a peer holds. And the blob access gate in `src/blob_gate.rs` (fetch/observe decided by membership in a world referencing the hash; observe answers size + held ranges) is **not wired into `id serve`** because its `WorldAccess` reference index (hash → worlds referencing it) "has no producer yet" (blob_gate.rs module doc).

Without a hash→holders index, multi-holder retrieval (#2050 follow-up B) has nobody to schedule from, and holder queries cannot be answered safely for private worlds.

## Scope
- Provider table in `pkgs/id`: hash → set of (EndpointId, held-ranges summary: complete / ranges / unknown, last-seen), fed by (1) world/doc sync state — peers observed Complete for a hash, the pattern iroh-docs' `ProviderNodes` uses for iroh-blobs' `ContentDiscovery` trait — and (2) gossip holder announcements on the existing discovery plane (per-world; full hash sets for small worlds, a compact summary format for large ones — choose and document the format).
- Produce the blob_gate reference index from the world graph (artifacts/documents naming a hash) and wire `blob_events` into `id serve` so fetch/observe are gated as designed. Refusals must stay indistinguishable for unknown vs forbidden hashes; observe stays off by default and world-narrowable only downward.
- A public server for a world must be able to answer holder queries for that world from its provider table (the rendezvous role in #2050 §2, channel 3).

## Acceptance criteria
- A node that holds none of a world's blob can obtain a candidate holder list for its hash from sync state, gossip announcements, or the world's public server.
- `id serve` enforces the blob gate on get/get_many/observe with the reference index populated; tests cover member-allowed, non-member-refused, and unknown-hash-indistinguishable cases.
- Holder announcements never leak holdings of a membership-gated world to non-members.
- Stale holders expire on the discovery plane's existing announce/stale cadence shape.

Not in scope: the retrieval scheduler itself (follow-up B), global/Mainline discovery (follow-up D).

body:
## What this is

Route pools landed in PR #915 (design record doc/2026-10-25T21-11-31Z_design_route-pools/): tiers scout / workhorse / specialist / summit over per-model plan pools. What is missing is the policy layer and the OpenCode-native affordances. Drew directed 2026-10-29: write the escalation policy; make sure OpenCode sessions can natively change their own model; let subsessions select route pools; and make OpenCode pool-aware — prefer managed pool routes over individual model pins, without making it a hard rule.

## 1. Escalation policy (draft for Drew's approval)

- **Workhorse is the default** for all routine work (Decision 008 stands).
- **Specialist is acceptable** when any of: the task is design or deep-reasoning work; workhorse has already failed once on the same task; the code is a critical path (auth, money, data loss); the task is reviewing specialist-tier output.
- **Summit is rare** — only when: specialist has failed on the task; OR the decision is one-shot and gates many downstream tasks; OR Drew directs it. Every summit use is logged with its reason, and the daily token check-in flags summit if it exceeds ~2% of fleet tokens.
- Escalation is one tier at a time unless the failure mode clearly skips a tier.

## 2. Native model switching in OpenCode

OpenCode's own instructions must tell sessions they may change their own model mid-session when the policy above calls for it, and how: switch, note the reason in the session record, continue. No external babysitter should be required for a session to escalate itself.

## 3. Subsessions select route pools

A subsession is spawned against a route pool (tier), not a raw model, by default. The pool resolves the actual model. A specific model may be requested when the task needs a capability only that model has.

## 4. Pool awareness, managed-first

OpenCode's instructions state the pool map (tiers + plan pools) and prefer managed pool routes over individual model pins. This is a preference, not a hard requirement: pinning a specific model stays allowed, with a reason.

## Acceptance

- Policy text (with Drew's edits) landed where OpenCode reads its instructions.
- A live session demonstrably escalates its own model per policy and logs the reason.
- A subsession demonstrably spawns on a pool route.
- Summit uses show up in the daily token check-in with reasons.

body:
Implements the design in #1721 (design note: https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/1721#issuecomment-6481531446). Owner decision 2026-10-28: **GO — build it with the design note's rulings.**

## What this builds

A first-class acpx `muse` agent for OpenClaw: an ACP adapter whose harness runs the Muse CLI as the agent, backed by `muse serve` (MSP) on the laptop. This is a harness door into the one Meta pool (the Muse API High Usage plan) via the CLI's sanctioned OAuth login — it is NOT a model route, and the OpenCode `muse` provider closure of 2026-10-25 stands untouched.

## Rulings folded in (from the design note)

- **Q1:** first-class door. The adapter sits alongside the existing acpx agents with per-agent command overrides pointing at laptop paths.
- **Q2 (build-blocking):** metering and capping are acceptance criteria, not follow-ups — plan-only by construction, a per-session usage ledger, a pre-dispatch pool check, and a per-session turn budget (below).
- **Q3:** `muse serve` is the transport (owner's smoke test: warm turns 7.2–7.8s vs exec 13.3–18.0s). `muse exec` exists only as the degraded fallback when serve fails before a response is committed.
- **Q4:** the adapter owns no credentials and no login lifecycle. Auth is solely the CLI's laptop OAuth login (`~/.config/muse/auth.json`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] acpx `muse` agent registered and selectable in OpenClaw; an ACP session on it completes a real coding turn end-to-end on the laptop.
- [ ] Plan-only by construction: the child process is spawned with `META_API_KEY` deleted from its environment; no API-key route exists anywhere in the adapter.
- [ ] Per-session usage ledger: the adapter records turns/usage per session in a durable, readable store.
- [ ] Pre-dispatch pool check: dispatch refuses to start when the freshest Meta pool reading (≤60 minutes old) shows 100%; burns over an hour re-check at least hourly.
- [ ] Per-session turn budget enforced from adapter config.
- [ ] Auth failures (expired/revoked login) surface as a terminal session error — "muse login required on laptop" — never a silent retry, route switch, or interactive login attempt by the adapter.
- [ ] CLI drift handled by probing `serve --help` / `exec --help` at startup (the `bin/muse-proxy.mjs` pattern), never by version-string checks.
- [ ] The OpenCode `muse` provider remains disabled and untouched by this work.
- [ ] Lands as a worktree branch + PR per fleet discipline (never the primary checkout).
