## mcpx nightly stress: e2e package hits the 600s test timeout (run 43707720627)

Observed in mcpx workflow run 43707720627 (2026-11-15, schedule, head 7d3dcebe), tracked by #10487: both stress jobs (ubuntu-latest and macos-latest) failed the `internal/e2e` package with `panic: test timed out after 10m0s` (600.09s / 600.12s). At the ubuntu timeout, `TestAShutdownDoesNotCutACallInFlight` was in flight.

Isolated verification (2026-11-15, task 17361): that test passes standalone on Linux in 99s (`go test ./internal/e2e -run TestAShutdownDoesNotCutACallInFlight -count=1`), but its `a_short_call` subtest alone takes 91s — it is slow and timing-sensitive, so under the nightly `-race -shuffle -repeat` load the e2e binary's cumulative time crosses the 600s go test timeout. No deterministic failure reproduced.

The deterministic failures from the same run (workflow `$f` loop, envguard classification, stale environment doc, compendium manifest, macOS socket-path/workdir test bugs) are fixed in the #10487 PR; this issue tracks only the stress-timeout isolation.

Next steps for whoever picks this up:
- Reproduce under the nightly stress flags (`-race -shuffle=<seed 7550508743126527922> -count` repeat) and identify which tests dominate the e2e binary's wall time.
- Decide: raise the e2e package timeout for the stress job, split the slowest tests, or reduce the shutdown test's real-time waits (fake clock / shorter grace).
- Do not weaken the shutdown-semantics assertions to make it faster.

body:
Found while verifying the #9850 round-2 fix (PR #10466), 2026-11-15 ~03:00 CT.

`pm-stack/aggregator/test/today-cache-1179.test.ts` fails with "a beforeEach/afterEach hook timed out for this test" (5.01 s) — and it fails identically on a pristine main checkout and on the #10466 worktree, run back to back. The box was at load ~14 at the time. The other aggregator attention suites pass on both trees.

This looks like a load-sensitive test (a 5 s hook budget against wall-clock-sensitive cache timing on a heavily loaded machine), not a product defect: the TodayCache primitive is unchanged and its behavior is exercised green by the suites that use it. But a test that fails under ordinary fleet load trains everyone to ignore red runs.

Suggested fix: make the hook work fake-timer or deadline-free (the cache takes an injectable clock in the paths that matter), or raise the hook budget with a comment tying it to load. Whoever picks this up: reproduce by running the single file while the box is under load; it passes on a quiet machine.

body:
## sigterm-witness hardening follow-ons from the PR #8786 review

Three CodeRabbit minor findings on PR #8786 were dispositioned as follow-ons (the Codex P1/P2 set and two CodeRabbit items were fixed in the PR itself, head fd6fbc5007):

1. **Forward caught signals independently of the receipt queue** (sigterm-witness.c, drain loop): when the self-pipe is full (~96–106 caught signals inside one 20 ms poll interval), the handler drops the event and increments `dropped_events`, and a dropped caught signal is never forwarded to the child. Track forwarding state separately (per-signal pending flag set in the handler, cleared + forwarded in the main loop) so receipt loss never becomes signal loss. Oracle: a burst test that fills the pipe still delivers every distinct caught signal to the child, and `dropped_events` counts only receipt loss.
2. **Make failed receipt writes observable** (sigterm-witness.c, logline): a failed/incomplete log append (full filesystem) is currently discarded silently while the signal is still forwarded. Fall back to stderr on append failure, without preventing forwarding. Oracle: unwritable log path produces a stderr diagnostic and the child still receives the signal.
3. **Reject unknown single-dash options before side effects** (argument contract decision): the strict prefix currently rejects unknown `--long` options, but a single-dash token (e.g. `-x`) is taken as the command name and fails only at exec. Decide the contract — reject dash-prefixed command tokens pre-fork (keeping `--` for explicit names), or document first-token-is-command as final — and implement + test the decision. Context: the operator-script argument contract discussion on PR #8786 and the Codex strict-parse fix.

Refs PR #8786, issue #8777.

title: ci(id): crate integration suites + build-manifest suite have no registry-named venue (ratchet follow-up to #6188)
body:
## Problem

The coverage-ratchet work on #6188 (Phase 4 of #6185) inventoried every test file inside the registry's stated boundary (pkgs/id/**, pkgs/mcpx/**) against `.github/test-suite-registry.json`. Five id-side test files are named by no registry entry:

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/tests/aliases.rs`
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/tests/web_router_security.rs`
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/tests/probe_petname_load.rs`
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-store/tests/store_traits.rs`
- `pkgs/id/web/scripts/build-manifest.test.sh`

The four crate integration suites may or may not run under the id flake package check (`pkgs/id/flake.nix` sets `doCheck = true` with a cargo test phase, and the world-snapshot-arm64 job runs a full workspace `cargo test` in a nix develop shell) — but no registry row names them and no run evidence was found either way during the #6188 pass, so the registry now carries them as `id.rust.crate-integration` (uncovered-in-fact) and `id.web.build-manifest` (uncovered) instead of letting them stay invisible. The build-manifest shell suite has no referencing workflow, package script, or flake check at all.

## Acceptance

- For each crate integration suite: prove with a recorded run whether an enabled venue executes it (name the venue and the run), or wire it into one; update the registry rows from uncovered-in-fact to mapped with the evidence.
- For `build-manifest.test.sh`: wire it into a venue (the id web area's checks or workflow-lint family) or record a waiver reason in the registry.
- The ratchet (`check-suite-registry.sh`, #6188) stays green throughout: rows are updated in the same change that changes the truth.

title: Backup bootstrap credentials not documented

labels.name: kind/docs
labels.description: Documentation improvement or addition

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: status/triaged

body:
Found by the 2026-11-14 whole-PM-stack backup/DR audit (verdict issue filed same day).

**Observed (2026-11-14):** a brand-new computer cannot bootstrap the backup/restore chain from the backups themselves. The roots of trust live outside every backup:

- **Bitwarden Secrets Manager access tokens** — the laptop's is at `~/.config/bws/access-token` (dated 2026-10-17), the sandbox's at `~/.config/bitwarden/access-token`. By design the BWS token is *not* stored in BWS (recorded 2026-10-07). No backup set includes either file, and no runbook says where a replacement comes from: a human must log into the Bitwarden account and mint a new machine-account token. That account's own credentials/recovery are Drew-held and undocumented in any restore doc.
- **Google Drive leg** — every Drive copy goes through the laptop's rclone `drive` remote; its OAuth token lives only in `~/.config/rclone/rclone.conf` on the laptop, in no backup set. A new machine needs a fresh interactive Google OAuth sign-in (Drew) before any Drive restore or backup works.
- **Restic passwords** are fine (in BWS by name: `restic.repo-archive-password`, `restic.sandbox-config-password`, `restic.platform-binaries-password`) — but reaching them needs the BWS token above, so the chain still roots in the manual Bitwarden step.
- **Sandbox side** — Muse's cron definitions themselves live in the Muse platform (copies under `~/workspace/cron.d/` + goal workspaces, covered by the sandbox home restic/git system, latest snapshot verified 2026-11-14), but re-creating the *scheduler* on a new host is a platform provisioning step, not something any backup restores. The closure-watchdog's watermark (`~/workspace/closure-watchdog/state.json`, current 2026-11-14) rides that same sandbox backup; if it were lost, the watchdog's own catchup-gap path is the safety net.

**Fix shape:** write the bootstrap page (one page, names only, no values): order = Drew signs into Bitwarden → mint BWS machine token → fetch restic/R2/Supabase secrets by name → Drew signs into Google for rclone Drive → 1Password service-account tokens come from BWS (`op muse…` names) → SOPS age key per its own gap issue. body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/decision-events-worker/` (the #9335 decision-set event pipeline: authenticated webhook → D1 store + Durable Object fan-out) carries a real test suite that no venue runs.

- `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/package.json` declares `"test": "bun test"`.
- The directory holds `test/events.test.ts` (104 lines) and `test/pagination.test.ts` (117 lines) — **14 tests, 51 `expect()` calls**.
- Runs nowhere. A repo-wide search for `decision-events-worker` finds **no** reference in `.github/**`, `justfile`, `flake.nix`, or any `*.nix` file.
- `.github/workflows/pm-stack-tests.yml` is the pm-stack venue. Its `push` path filters list `external-comms`, `opencode-claimant`, `opencode-usage-export`, `cloudflare-export`, `supabase-export`, `meta-exporter`, `dispatch`, `pad`, `grist`, `scripts` — `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/**` is **absent**, so no step could fire even if one were added. Its steps run aggregator/projector/dispatch/external-comms/claimant/grist/exporter suites; none touches this worker.
- `.github/test-suite-registry.json` has no entry for it (`grep -c decision-events .github/test-suite-registry.json` → 0; the `quota-exporters` row covers only the three other exporter suites).

Verified this run on `origin/main` at `f8a79cd224` (clean checkout, HEAD == origin/main):

```
$ cd pm-stack/decision-events-worker && bun test
bun test v1.4.4 (38afee6c8)
 14 pass
 0 fail
 51 expect() calls
Ran 14 tests across 2 files. [12.00ms]
```

It needs only bun — no wrangler or npm install is required for the suite to run.

## Why it matters

This suite is the only verification of the Worker's validation, auth, event-cursor and pagination logic, and its test titles pin the exact Codex-round findings filed as separate open issues:

- `events cursor (#9614)` and `GET /sets/<setId>/events pagination (#9614)` — the composite `(ts, event_id)` cursor skip, fixed today by PR #9645 (#9614). These are the regression pins for that fix.
- `isAuthorized accepts Bearer or X-Webhook-Secret, fails closed unset` and `timingSafeEqual` — the webhook auth path must fail closed when the secret is unset.
- Related behavior still open: #9612 (DO fan-out lost when ingest fails after the D1 commit), #9613 (sync acks events the Worker rejected), #9615 (unreadable `--outbox-dir` ignored), #9794 (kill switch returns 0 before `parseArgs`).

Because nothing runs the suite, a regression of any of these — including the auth fail-closed behavior — passes CI silently.

This is the same class the fleet has already fixed per suite: #6084 (three quota-exporter suites), #6090 (dispatch), #6091 (claimant install bun suite), #6217 (external-comms), #6344 (meta-exporter), and still-open #8026 (`pm-stack/exporters/watchdog-state.test.ts`).

## Suggested fix shape

Follow the guarded-step pattern already in `pm-stack-tests.yml` (see the dispatch step and the #6090/#6091/#6217 comments there):

- Add `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/**` to the workflow's `push` (and `pull_request`, where present) trigger paths.
- Add a step that asserts `test/*.test.ts` exists (fail the job if not, so a green run can never be a silently skipped suite), then runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile && bun test` in `pm-stack/decision-events-worker` (the dispatch step shows the exact shape).
- Add a `.github/test-suite-registry.json` row recording the venue.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A CI job runs the suite on every change touching `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/**`, and fails if the directory holds no `*.test.ts` or any test fails.
- [ ] `pm-stack-tests.yml` (or another workflow) lists `pm-stack/decision-events-worker/**` in its trigger paths.
- [ ] `.github/test-suite-registry.json` records the suite's venue.

## Notes

- Not a duplicate: #9612/#9613/#9614/#9615/#9794 are behavioral bugs in this same component; none tracks test wiring.
- The sibling wiring gaps #8026 (exporters) and #6084/#6344 (exporters) are the same class but different files.

body:
## Finding (verified 2026-11-13, Scheduled Suggestions pass on issue #8324)

`nixos/services/power-guard/power-guard.py` executes an environment-derived command string through a shell, as root:

- Line 22 (module docstring): "Runs as root in production (systemd unit from the NixOS flake)."
- Line 94: `SLEEP_CMD = os.environ.get("POWER_GUARD_SLEEP_CMD", "systemctl hybrid-sleep")`
- Line 231 (in `main()`, after a confirmed critical state): `subprocess.run(SLEEP_CMD, shell=True)`

The systemd unit in `nixos/services/power-guard/default.nix` sets no environment, so today the variable is only a test/manual hook (`test_power_guard.py` line 179 sets `POWER_GUARD_SLEEP_CMD=f"touch {self.marker}"`). The env source is therefore service/root-controlled, not remote input — this is a hardening item, not a live exploit path. It still matters:

- A root daemon should not need a shell to run a two-word command; `shell=True` turns any future wiring of this variable to a less-trusted source (a NixOS option, a drop-in, a test harness running unprivileged input) into root shell execution with no further code change.
- Shell parsing of the override is a surprise surface: quoting/metacharacters in an otherwise legitimate multi-word command change its meaning silently.

## Suggested fix shape

- Parse once at startup with `shlex.split`, validate the result is a non-empty argv, and run `subprocess.run(argv)` with no shell — mirroring the file's existing fail-closed-at-startup treatment of timing overrides (`timing_from_env`, lines 71-83).
- Update the test hook usage in `test_power_guard.py` (line 179) accordingly; `touch <marker>` still works as an argv form.
- Alternatively, if shell semantics are intentionally kept for the test hook, restrict the production default path to a fixed argv and document why the hook is trusted.

Related but distinct existing items (different defects in the same file, checked before filing): issue #8182 (release() forgets a still-running systemd-inhibit child) and issue #6534 (dead systemd-inhibit child never noticed). Neither covers the `shell=True` sleep command.

Found by: repo-worker-code-d, lane code-d, fleet queue fallback mode (queue backend down), suggestions pass for issue #8324. Evidence read from `main` via the GitHub API on 2026-11-13.

Perform the daily configuration review for developing-today/code. Do NOT update the `opencode` or `openchamber` flake inputs — the flake-inputs-update workflow owns them.
Follow these instructions and rules:

  `flake-inputs-update` workflow, which bumps, validates, and merges them daily.
  Do NOT run `nix flake update` for them, do NOT change their pins in `flake.lock`,
  and do NOT open PRs that bump them. If their pins look stale, leave them — the
  owning workflow handles them the same day.
- Do NOT casually bump root `nixpkgs` (root nixpkgs is pinned deliberately per system stability policies). - Clean up any stale input overrides or unused flake dependencies in `flake.nix` (e.g. warnings about non-existent input overrides like gitignore or devshell).
### 2. CONFIGURATION & INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS - Investigate potential configuration improvements in `nixos/`, `home/`, `lib/`, and package definitions under `pkgs/`. - Check for:
  - Deprecated NixOS or Home Manager options
  - Suboptimal build phases or missing binary wrappers
  - Systemd service resilience (e.g. restart policies, socket activation)
  - Modularity and decoupling to prevent merge conflicts
- Clean up any dead code, unused flags, or documentation drift in Nix configurations.
### 3. EVALUATION & VALIDATION - Verify that all system and host configurations evaluate cleanly without errors:
  `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.nixos.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`
- Ensure git hooks, commit messages, and treefmt formatting pass cleanly.

### 4. PULL REQUEST & MERGE - If updates or improvements are present:
  - Open a clear Pull Request documenting any configuration enhancements made. Keep every related change in this one PR — never split changes into one PR per item.

body:
## Gap

The PM stack quota "Analytics & projection" section (PR #9363) counts mcpx tool use from OpenCode session transcripts (`mcpx_discover` / `mcpx_exec` / `mcpx_project` tool parts). That only sees mcpx calls made *through an OpenCode session*. Calls made directly against the mcpx daemon (other clients, scripts, health probes with real tool calls) are invisible — the daemon keeps no durable call ledger of its own.

## Ask

Give the mcpx daemon an append-only call ledger: one record per tool execution — timestamp, server, tool name, caller identity as known (client/session), outcome, duration. JSONL beside the daemon state, rotated, is enough. The aggregator can then report total mcpx use (daemon-recorded) alongside the in-session subset instead of presenting the subset as the whole.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Every daemon tool execution appends exactly one ledger record, including errors.
- [ ] Records carry server + tool + outcome + duration; no argument payloads (avoid leaking secrets passed as tool args) — names and counts only.
- [ ] pm-aggregator analytics reads the ledger and labels mcpx counts as recorded, with the transcript-derived in-session count shown as the subset it is.

body:
## Evidence

On current `main` (`cd3ec81a6d0098850d9f69393b5486c1b19a2e66`), the collaboration broadcast loop handles `broadcast::error::RecvError::Lagged` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/collab.rs:1039-1054`: it sends a desynchronization error and stops forwarding so the client can reconnect for a fresh `Init` and catch-up. The browser client in `pkgs/id/web/src/collab.ts:531-543` treats that error as recoverable, closes the socket, and schedules reconnect.

Current coverage checks only that the desync error message encodes/decodes (`collab.rs:2079-2092`). Client tests exercise other reconnect cases, but `collab.test.ts` has no desynchronization-error/reconnect case, and there is no test driving a lagged server broadcast receiver through to a successful fresh initialization.

## Why it matters

This is the recovery path that prevents a slow collaborative-editing client from silently staying behind after the bounded broadcast channel drops updates. A regression in either half can leave collaborative documents stale or prevent recovery, while the existing codec-only assertion still passes.

## Acceptance criteria

- Add deterministic regression coverage that overflows or otherwise induces a lagged collaboration broadcast receiver and verifies the server emits the recoverable desynchronization signal.
- Verify the client responds by closing/reconnecting and accepts a fresh `Init`/catch-up state, rather than remaining connected with stale state.
- Keep ordinary in-order delivery and intentional-disconnect behavior covered and unchanged.

Found by the #2716 settings/conformance desync work (task 8673, 2026-11-13): on clean main, go test ./internal/conformance/ -run TestStatefulServer fails ~34 subtests, every one with the same frame error:

    2025-11-25 frame for tools/call does not match the schema: $.result.task.expiresAt: property not defined by this revision (strict)
    (same for tasks/get frames at $.result.expiresAt)

The task representation (pkgs/mcpx/internal/tasks/tasks.go:43, ExpiresAt *time.Time with json tag expiresAt, no omitempty) serializes expiresAt — null for nonterminal tasks, a timestamp once terminal — into 2025-11-25 task results, whose strict schema defines no such field (the revision's task shape is taskId/status/statusMessage/createdAt/lastUpdatedAt/ttl/pollInterval). Acceptance:
- go test ./internal/conformance/ -run TestStatefulServer -count=1 passes.
- Decide the owning shape per revision (drop expiresAt from the legacy representation, or render it only where a revision defines it) and say which in the PR; check the daemon /v1 task surface for the same field before changing the shared representation.
- No other conformance regressions: full ./internal/conformance/ run compared against the #2716 PR baseline.

Not part of #2716's original four conformance items (authsplit binding, matrix binding, client extensions, completion-max-100) — those are fixed on the #2716 branch; this family arrived with the tasks implementation and needs its own change.

## Problem

Issue #7787 step 6 parts 2-4 (queue task 15074) wire `boundary_surfaces::check_surface` (landed in PR #8850, merged 4267e5213b) into the live signup/login, world, and bridge/federation call sites. Fresh verification on current main shows the wiring has **no inputs to wire**:

- `grep -rn "BoundaryDeclaration|EffectiveBoundary|residency::|boundary::"` across `pkgs/id/src` and crates id-worlds / id-sync / id-groups / id-store / id-events / id-caps returns **zero** uses outside id-core. Nothing in the app constructs a declaration, an effective boundary, a residency `Policy`/`Scope`, `SubjectEvidence` claims, or an `EvidenceVerifier`.
- There is no operator configuration surface for boundaries: no config file, world record, or CLI path carries a `BoundaryDeclaration` (content-addressed, versioned) or a policy's trust roots.
- There is no evidence source: nothing issues placement `Evidence` for the account store, world blob stores, world turn hosts, or transport peers/relays, and no verifier implementation exists to check it.
- The packet's named signup/login location is also stale: `pkgs/id/src/commands/serve.rs` (4160 lines) contains no signup/login handling; the account surface is `Directory::sign_up` / `sign_up_keyed` / `authenticate` in `crates/id-worlds/src/directory.rs`, whose signatures carry no connection, claims, or policy inputs.

Wiring call sites today would mean inventing the semantics (where declarations live, who issues evidence, who verifies) inline in four live surfaces — the half-wired enforcement the #7787 park notes warned against.

## Needed (design + build, before #7787 parts 2-4)

1. **Declaration residence**: where an operator's `BoundaryDeclaration`s live and how the app loads the effective boundary per scope (server / world / account) — config file, world record, or operator CLI; versioning/supersession per `boundary.rs`.
2. **Evidence sources**: who issues placement `Evidence` for (a) the account store (storage), (b) the serving connection (transport), (c) world blob stores (storage) and turn hosts (processing), (d) federation peers/relays (transport) — and how peer-asserted claims are collected for `peer_asserted_claim`.
3. **Verifier**: the app-side `EvidenceVerifier` implementation (signature + revocation) the adapter's call sites will pass.
4. Then re-packet #7787 parts 2-4 against these inputs (queue task 15074 is blocked on this issue as a dependency).

## Acceptance

- [ ] A design note (in `doc/`, following the id design-doc pattern) decides 1-3 with named code locations.
- [ ] The plumbing lands: the app can load an enabled declaration for a scope and obtain the claims + verifier a `check_surface` call needs, with tests.
- [ ] #7787 parts 2-4 can then be wired without inventing semantics at the call site.

Parent: #5683. Blocks: #7787 parts 2-4 (queue task 15074, dep-blocked on this issue).

body:
## Drew's ask

Drew, in a direct OpenCode session on 2026-10-12 (opencode:ses_ecfab4789ffe):

> "expand how the config works to be able to set specific times to deprioritize or prioritize specific provider/model combinations and also per-provider or per-model/route pool, so that you can express… these are the peak hours and maybe choose another model if there are other options."

Scope as asked:
- Schedules by day of week + time of day + timezone + specific days of month
- Applies per provider, per model, and per route pool
- A default priority level (every model = 1) when no schedule applies
- Existing stickiness and user-override rules still apply on top of scheduled priorities

## Why this is filed now (evidence of absence)

This ask never became an issue. It surfaced only in the 2026-11-11 design-audit gap pass, which combed the OpenCode session corpus via Atlas (the Muse-side record does not contain Drew's direct OpenCode sessions):

- No matching issue found (gh searches: "peak hours schedule pool"; title scans of the opencode and openchamber forks)
- No design artifact in any scanned tree (sandbox + hatch-personal + laptop)
- No record of time-based schedules landing in the pool config in any scanned source — whether it was ever built is unverified

Register entry: F4.18 in `pm-stack/design-register-2026-11-11.md`. Tracking epic: #8805.

## Acceptance check

- [ ] First establish ground truth: does any part of the current pool/route config already support time-based priority? Record the finding on this issue.
- [ ] If absent: config can express a schedule (days of week, time window, timezone, days of month) that raises/lowers priority for a named provider, model, or route pool, with default priority 1 outside scheduled windows.
- [ ] Stickiness and user-override behavior verified to still win over scheduled priority.
- [ ] One worked example in config: a peak-hours window that deprioritizes one pool in favour of another option, demonstrated live.

body:
Follow-up from issue #6521 (Phase 4 of design #6520, closing JSON-parse inventory). The inventory in `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/JSON_PARSE_INVENTORY.md` dispositioned every production `serde_json` parse site in `pkgs/id/src` + `pkgs/id/crates` at main `160e2d6f38`. The 29 sites below are dispositioned **gate** (the parse feeds a check, a store, a forward, or a comparison) but do not yet route through the shared helper `id_core::json_unique::parse_json_without_duplicate_keys`. Per #6521's acceptance, no gate site stays a silent exception: this issue is the filed follow-up for all of them.

## Conversion pattern

Lossless form (corrected on a verified Codex finding on PR #8796): run `parse_json_without_duplicate_keys` over the raw text/bytes to validate uniqueness and discard its `Value`, then run the existing typed decode (`from_str` / `from_slice`) over the original bytes. Do NOT generally decode the helper's `Value` with `from_value`: with serde_json's default features a `Value` cannot represent integers above `u64::MAX` losslessly, and bodies in this tree carry `u128` fields (e.g. `RateAuthorisation`) that the current typed decoders support. `from_value` over the helper's `Value` is acceptable only where the target type is known to be Value-representable. Where a signature is verified over the raw bytes, verification is unchanged. Add a regression test per site or family: a duplicated key in the input is refused, naming the key.

## Sites

**Signed-object receipt — disposition (a) of #6521 (receipt takes the refusal):**
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/artifact.rs:1333` — receive_pushed: peer-pushed SignedArtifact receipt (the primary (a) gate)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/artifact.rs:1286` — pull protocol PullRequest frame
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/artifact.rs:1406` — fetched Page frame
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/attestation.rs:111` — GenesisAgreement::from_body (signed event body)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/attestation.rs:146` — ResultClaim::from_body (signed event body)
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:136` — RateAuthorisation::from_body (signed event body)
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:232` — RateRevocation::from_body (signed event body)
- `pkgs/id/src/web/identity.rs:527` — token payload decode (signature verified over exact bytes first)
- `pkgs/id/src/boards.rs:883` — BoardObject from_value over artifact.body: cannot itself refuse; closed by converting the receipt parses above, and recorded here so the coverage is explicit

**Peer frames and replies:**
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/envelope_net.rs:185` — Envelope receipt
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/envelope_net.rs:103` — exchange Reply decode
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_net.rs:1511` — recv_json_with_frame_bytes: the single inbound frame parse for the world host protocol (all world_net reply decoders consume its Value)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_replication_net.rs:126` — replication Request decode
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs:1040` — SSH session frame parse (its :1055 surface decode follows)

**Checks over supplied documents:**
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/core.rs:366` — validate_import_envelope
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication.rs:426` — chain_payload (signed payload journal lines)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication.rs:468` — validate_payload_journal_header
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication_receiver.rs:537` — validate_committed_journal
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/shell_contract.rs:306` — ShellContract::parse
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/shell_contract.rs:668` — check_transcript
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_dev.rs:1611` — parse_fuzz_decl (version/bounds checked after parse)
- `pkgs/id/src/commands/world.rs:475` — world doctor execution-profile file

**Store/forward inputs:**
- `pkgs/id/src/web/world_ws.rs:386` — directory_write_handler request body
- `pkgs/id/src/foreign_libsql.rs:1121` — libsql pipeline response rows
- `pkgs/id/src/currency_poc/intent.rs:265` — intent directory scan (foreign files; PoC)
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/directory_view.rs:1060` — publish_document content
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/directory_view.rs:1071` — receive envelope
- `pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs:144` — document content parse: the parsed value is retained and forwarded to connected clients as CollabMessage::Init (collab.rs:911-928) (added on a verified Codex finding, PR #8796)

**Embedded documents inside checked data:**
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/mod.rs:2064` — presence_change: parses the presence JSON embedded as a string in a received replica journal's System event; WorldCore::restore_inner (world/core.rs:1064-1095) uses it for a capability check and presence counts. Routing the outer journal parsers does NOT cover the embedded document — the conversion must refuse duplicates inside it (added on a verified Codex finding, PR #8796)

## Acceptance

- Each site above parses through the helper (or its family's single conversion point, for world_net) with a duplicate-key refusal regression test.
- The inventory table in `JSON_PARSE_INVENTORY.md` is updated: these rows move from gate — follow-up to gate — routed.
- No other production site changes disposition.

body:
# Implement: program fork operation with structural attribution

Implementation item from the Phase-14 Program ecosystem v1 design (#6291; design record: `doc/2026-11-11T05-01-15Z_design_id_program_ecosystem_v1/`), refining core decision D3 from the #6278 core design record (`doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/`).

## Why this is separate

The core record filed #8280 (bundle format + sideload import — it carries the lineage *field*) and #8282 (template worlds), but no issue owns the fork *operation* itself. This issue is that gap in the v1 breakdown.

## Scope

- Fork operation: given a bundle the user holds, produce a NEW bundle — the forking author's key becomes author of the fork's new version line; lineage = parent's lineage plus the parent's full identity (author key, name, version, content hash); the fork is signed with the forking author's key.
- No permission from the original author and no registry involvement; fully local file operation.
- Presentation rule: CLI surfaces present a fork with its full lineage chain and never as the original author's work.
- A fork starts pinned-only: lineage is history, not an update channel (no subscription to parent versions either way).
- Out of scope: gallery publishing/fetching (#8281 / v2 #6293), update channels (v2), template worlds (#8282).

## Acceptance

- Fork of a fork carries the full ordered ancestor chain; a lineage-mutated bundle fails signature verification.
- Fork round-trip: the forked bundle imports into a fresh world through the ordinary #8280 import path, with its install record showing the full lineage.
- Operation completes fully offline.

body:
## Problem

Codex P1 finding on PR #8529 (seitan admission path for #8487), review comment 4534012963:

When `id serve` serves a durable world, the live world uses its own `.id-worlds/<name>/directory.jsonl` (loaded by `world_store.rs`), but the seitan admit path built for #8487 checks accounts and appends `AccountVerified` in the **server-config directory journal** (`server_config_directory_path`, beside the groups log). Consequences Codex names:

- a provisioned account can be admitted successfully (invite consumed) while remaining unverified in the named world's live directory — capability authorization consults the live directory (`world/core.rs`);
- accounts created through the world's directory API are absent from the server-config directory lookup, so their admits refuse `unknown_account`.

## Why this is a follow-up, not a PR #8529 change

The recorded design for #8487 (task 14857, design comment on #8487) decision 3 scopes v1 deliberately: the membership change is directory-level, appended via `Directory::verify_account` into the server-config directory journal; "World-session membership is a separate existing mechanism (`world_session` invites) and is out of scope here." PR #8529 implements exactly that design, and its acceptance criteria (packet for task 14862) name the server directory. Rebinding admission to per-world live directories is a design change beyond that recorded scope.

## What to decide / do

1. Decide the intended binding: when the invite names a world that has a live `.id-worlds/<name>/directory.jsonl`, should admit resolve that directory for the account check + `AccountVerified` append instead of (or in addition to) the server-config journal?
2. Reconcile the account universes: accounts created via the world's directory API vs provisioning / `/api/identity/register` in the server-config directory — which one is authoritative for the `unknown_account` check?
3. Implement the decided binding with integration tests in the routes.rs seitan idiom (durable-world admit lands in the live world directory; world-created account admits without `unknown_account`).

Refs: PR #8529, issue #8487, task 14862 (lane tmp-code-b dispositioned the Codex thread with this follow-up).

body:
## Defect

A queue lane row whose recorded `session_id` belongs to a session that was **cleared** (progress `session_cleared` via `park_task`) can never be flipped to `direct`, so the task it names is unworkable by every lane:

- The broker serves the task to Muse lanes (handed_off sink, #8234 default pick) and re-serves it **immediately after every park** — the park delay is not honored (`not_before` stays null), so a lane cannot move past it by claiming.
- `fleet queue lane <task> --exclusion-reason "..."` returns the row **unchanged** (no error, `assigned_lane` stays `opencode`, `exclusion_reason` stays null) — three attempts on 2026-11-11, including the exact #8187 recovery sequence (opencode launch failed `cap_saturated`, `cap_room: 0`, then flip) that the runbook prescribes for this case.
- The recorded session is dead: cleared 2026-11-05, and no live session owns the task.

Net effect: the task loops claim → park → claim across lanes (14 attempts so far on this one), burning lane shifts, and the underlying work never starts — even though its dependency gate has since landed, so the work itself is unblocked.

## Evidence (2026-11-11, lane code-t, task 8750 / issue #3983)

- Lane row 1587: `assigned_lane: opencode`, `session_id: ses_e5e5668ee9dffew1e9HBjhjSbN`, `executed_at: 2026-11-05T02:45:01Z`, `updated_at` never changes on flip attempts.
- Task progress: `session_cleared: {via: "park_task", cleared_at: "2026-11-05T02:45:00Z", session_id: "ses_e5e5668ee9dffew1e9HBjhjSbN"}` — the broker itself cleared the binding, but the lane row still carries it.
- Parks at 1800s and 3600s were both followed by an immediate re-claim of task 8750 by the same lane (claim `attempts` unchanged, `not_before: null`).
- `launch_one.py --launch repo-health-code-pilot:8750` → `{ok: false, reason: "cap_saturated", cap_room: 0}`.

## Expected

One of:
1. The lane flip succeeds when the row's session is recorded cleared in the task progress (the session is not bound in any live sense), or
2. The flip refusal is an explicit error naming the bound session and its state (today it silently returns the unchanged row, indistinguishable from success at a glance), and a park of such a task honors its delay so lanes can move on.

## Pointers

- Task 8750 (repo-health-code-pilot), lane row 1587, issue #3983 (gate #3933 closed — the implementation itself is ready to start).
- Runbook: repo-queue-worker-instruction §1b (#8187/#8234), the bound-session park rule this defect defeats.

body:
Filed by the #4707 closing audit of design #4706 (task 12695, lane code-n, 2026-11-10). Evidence at origin/main 9b65fa2ec8, `bin/opencode-acp-adapter.mjs`.

## Gap

The adapter creates one serve session per ACP `session/new` (`sessions.set` at :627, via `POST /api/session` at :622) and never deletes any of them: there is no `DELETE /api/session/:id` call anywhere in the file, no ACP session-close handler, and nothing runs on stdin close / SIGTERM except `process.exit` (main, end of file).

The adapter-side `sessions` map (:237) dies with the adapter process — acpx launches a fresh adapter per gateway session — so adapter-side lifetime is process-lifetime and acceptable. The serve side is different: the server is the fleet's ONE standing shared `opencode serve`, so every ACP session ever created persists server-side after its adapter exits, for as long as the serve process lives, unless the serve expires idle sessions itself (no evidence in this repo that it does).

## What to settle

1. Verify from the pinned serve whether idle sessions expire server-side, and on what clock. If they do, record it on #4707 and close this as a named exception.
2. If they do not: delete serve sessions the adapter owns — on stdin close / SIGTERM, `DELETE /api/session/:id` for every id in the adapter's `sessions` map (best-effort, bounded time, never blocking exit), and disposition the crash case (adapter killed hard: sessions leak until serve restart — state whether that residual is accepted).

Design context: #4706 open question 2 named exactly this — it needed Phase 4 evidence before becoming work; this issue is that evidence landing.

body:
# Implement: signed program bundle format + sideload import

Implementation next step from the Phase-14 Program ecosystem core topic #6278; design of record: `doc/2026-11-10T21-24-00Z_design_id_program_ecosystem/` (Program ecosystem — share, fork, gallery: first-pass research + design), decisions D1–D2.

## Scope
- The program bundle format: a single-file bundle carrying the program (`.roc` / component payload), a manifest with program identity (author public key, name, version, content hash of the payload), the F12.17 signature over manifest + payload (#1069), the F12.7 ABI descriptor (#1064), and fork lineage (parent identity + parent content hash, empty for originals).
- Export: produce a bundle from an installed/authored program.
- Sideload import: import a bundle from a local file into a world with no server involved — verify signature + content hash, check the ABI descriptor against the world's host ABI, record provenance in the world's install record. Sideloading must always work (Phase-14 principle from #1240: the app must not technically need us).
- Out of scope: gallery publishing/fetching (separate issue), update channels (F12.9 #1066 governs upgrade mechanics; channel policy is v2 #6293's design).

## Acceptance
- Bundle round-trip: export → sideload import into a fresh world yields a runnable install whose recorded identity, hash, signature, and lineage match the bundle.
- Tampered payload or manifest fails verification and is refused with the failing check named.
- Import works fully offline / local-only.

body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id`'s clippy gate (`checks.x86_64-linux.clippy-lint`, recipe: `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features`) is red at HEAD with **571 deny-level lint errors** and has been red since the workspace lints table landed:

- `unwrap_used = "deny"`, `expect_used = "deny"`, `panic = "deny"` (plus `unimplemented`/`todo`/`dbg_macro`) were set in `pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` on **2026-11-02** in merge PR #4626 (`2f62ce6c90`). The tree was never brought into conformance, and because PR CI is disabled (CI runs on main only) and main-tier runs have not executed since (runner queue frozen), the red gate was invisible until the main-broken run 41815275218 executed on 2026-11-04 — this is the clippy leg of #5459.

## Evidence (measured on the laptop at origin/main 917e1a3bdb, 2026-11-06)

- `id-core`: exactly **1** error — `clippy::panic` at `crates/id-core/src/residency.rs:399` (`panic!("allowed")` in the `storage_evidence_does_not_cover_other_planes` test's let-else). The codebase's sanctioned pattern exists: `#[allow(clippy::panic)]` on the test fn (precedent: `src/store_traits.rs:1205`). One-line fix, verified shape.
- `id` (lib target): **20** errors — production-code `unwrap()`/`expect()`/`panic` sites.
- `id` (lib test target): **551** errors. The lints table's own comment states the convention: "Test modules should add: #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]" — most test modules never got the attribute.
- Error mix (lib test): unwrap Result ×241, expect Result ×188, unwrap Option ×57, expect_err ×26, expect Option ×23, panic ×15, unwrap_err ×3.
- Hottest files: `src/currency_poc/tests.rs` ~100 sites, `src/web/markdown.rs` ~50, `src/publications.rs` ~43, `src/world/handle.rs` ~36, `src/app_manifest.rs` ~33, `src/world_session/mod.rs` ~29, `src/commands/world.rs` ~28, `src/world/replication.rs` ~27 — 40+ files in total.
- Full logs from the evaluation: `nix log` of the clippy-lint derivation at that tree; summary in the dead-at-cap evaluation report (2026-11-06).

## What done looks like

- `clippy-lint` check passes on main.
- Test-module errors resolved with the conventional `#[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)]` (and `clippy::panic` where a test genuinely needs it), module by module — not a workspace-level weakening of the lints table.
- The 20 production (lib) errors fixed individually with real error handling, or a narrowly-scoped, justified allow where the operation is provably infallible.
- The `id-core` residency.rs site fixed with the one-line allow.
- Note the lints table references a planned "lints review in plan step P8.8" — if that review intends a different end-state for these lints, this issue is where that decision should be recorded instead of silently leaving the gate red.

## Context

- Parent breakage: #5459 (this is its clippy leg; the format leg was fixed in PR #6461, and test-shard-0's CI failure was runner disk exhaustion, verified green on the laptop).
- Filed from the 2026-11-06 dead-at-cap evaluation: the remediation task for #5459 (queue task 9553) burned 24 attempts on claim evaporation without the work ever being attempted, which is why this sat untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- checks.x86_64-linux.clippy-lint passes on main (cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features in pkgs/id is clean under the deny lints).
- Test-module sites are resolved with the conventional per-module #[allow(clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used)] (and clippy::panic only where a test genuinely needs it) — no workspace-level weakening of the lints table.
- The 20 production (lib) errors are fixed individually with real error handling, or carry a narrowly-scoped allow with a justification comment; the id-core residency.rs:399 site uses the sanctioned one-line allow precedent.

body:
## Problem

Markdown converted for the ID web surface copies Comrak link URLs into HTML href attributes without rejecting executable schemes. In pkgs/id/src/web/markdown.rs around lines 2985-2995, imported or collaborative Markdown can contain a link such as [open](javascript:alert(document.domain)); when rendered and clicked in the same-origin application, the javascript URL runs in the user's browser context. The collab document path reaches this renderer via pkgs/id/src/web/collab.rs:141-153.

Existing renderer tests cover safe schemes but not javascript: (markdown.rs around lines 5808-5829 and 5879-5899). The /blob active-content mitigation in #908/#919 is related precedent but does not cover these editor links.

## Required behavior

Only render URLs from an explicit safe set; neutralize executable or unknown schemes such as javascript:, data:, and vbscript:. Preserve safe http, https, mailto, and relative/internal links. Do not rely on browser sanitization.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A regression test renders a javascript: link and proves it cannot produce an executable href.
- [ ] Cases cover data:, vbscript:, protocol-relative, relative, http, https, and mailto, with a documented allowed-scheme oracle.
- [ ] Collaborative Markdown rendering uses the same sanitizer as other Markdown entry points.
- [ ] Existing safe-link behavior and formatting are unchanged.

A module can silently regrow past the limit and the split's benefit erodes unnoticed, exactly what F11.10 was meant to prevent.

## Acceptance criteria

- An automated check runs in the id fast lane (or as a test in `pkgs/id`) that fails when any production `.rs` file under `pkgs/`/`apps/` exceeds 2,500 production lines (production = lines before the first `#[cfg(test)]` module, matching the #1078 audit's measurement; test files under `tests/` are not production code — e.g. `pkgs/id/tests/cli_integration.rs` at 4,312 lines is out of scope).
- The check names the offending file(s) and their line counts on failure.
- The check passes on current main (largest production file: `cli.rs`, 2,200).
- Linked from #1078's closeout table as the F11.10 coverage gap.

Found by: #1078 slice 5 (queue task 1259, repo-worker-code). Related: #841 (status-record corrections).

title: Avoid evaluating Bitwarden secret values as shell code in drain wrapper

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: source/queue-worker
labels.description: Filed or worked by the queue/worker pilot

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: mode/online
labels.description: Fully doable remotely: design, config, code, cloud

labels.name: app/github-backup
labels.description: infra/github-backup estate mirror system

body:
## Finding

`infra/github-backup/systemd/drain-wrapper.sh:23-35` fetches the Worker URL and bearer from Bitwarden, then runs `eval` over Python output built with `repr()`:

```bash
eval "$(python3 - <<'PY'
...
print(f"export GHB_WORKER_URL={get('github-app.backup-worker-url')!r}")
print(f"export GHB_WORKER_BEARER={get('github-app.backup-worker-bearer')!r}")
PY
)"
```

Python string `repr()` is not shell escaping. A value containing both quote types can make the generated shell statement execute injected syntax. This was reproduced in an isolated wrapper harness using fabricated secret data; the command executed with the wrapper's user privileges. The existing wrapper tests (`infra/github-backup/tests/test_drain_wrapper.py`) exercise only simple values such as `https://worker.invalid` and `stub-bearer`, so they miss this boundary case.

## Impact

A malicious or accidentally malformed Bitwarden value can execute arbitrary shell commands whenever the systemd drain wrapper runs, before `drain_queue.py` starts. This affects the host account running the backup service. No real credentials or external services were used in reproduction.

## Suggested fix

Do not feed Python `repr()` output to `eval`. Pass values to the child process without shell interpretation, or emit values using a shell-specific quoting function and add regression tests containing quotes and shell metacharacters that assert no command execution and exact environment round-tripping.

Related: #12260 (scheduled suggestions pass that found this issue).

body:
## Problem

The new `pm-stack/lane-guard` CLI regression test is tied to the real date and has become permanently red. In `pm-stack/lane-guard/test_lane_guard.py::Cli.test_note_cli_requests_issue_comments`, the stub comment is timestamped `2026-11-19T17:55:00Z`, while the test's fixed `NOW` is `2026-11-19T18:00:00Z`. But the CLI path calls `note_verdict()` without passing that fixed clock (`pm-stack/lane-guard/lane_guard.py`); `note_verdict()` therefore uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc)`. Its 24-hour dedupe check suppresses only comments younger than 24 hours. Once real time passed `2026-11-20T17:55:00Z`, the stub was no longer recent, `post` became true, and the test started failing permanently.

Verified in `pm-stack-tests` run [44919018795](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/44919018795): the suite file was present and 27 tests ran; `test_note_cli_requests_issue_comments` failed with `AssertionError: 0 != 3` (expected `EXIT_STOP`, got `EXIT_GO`). Reproduced locally against the same lane-guard files: 26 pass, this test fails. The issue is the test's missing clock seam, not the dedupe behavior itself; the `note_verdict` unit tests that pass `now=NOW` remain green.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Make the CLI test deterministic by injecting/controlling the clock or deriving its stub timestamp from the controlled test time.
- [ ] Keep explicit coverage that an existing matching note inside the 24-hour window suppresses posting and yields `EXIT_STOP`.
- [ ] Run `python3 -m unittest test_lane_guard.py` from `pm-stack/lane-guard/`; all 27 tests pass regardless of the wall-clock date.
- [ ] The scheduled `pm-stack-tests` workflow passes the lane-guard step on `main`.

body:
## Summary

Two remaining `pkgs/id` state-file writers use write-to-temp + rename but do not sync the temp file before the rename or the parent directory afterward. `id-core::durable_write::write_durable` now provides that discipline for three sibling writers (merged PR #12153), but these two sites were outside #12152's explicitly listed scope. A sudden power/kernel loss can therefore leave the newly published bytes or rename non-durable even though the save returned success.

## Evidence

Verified on `origin/main` `aca6c869f28a33645c08093bc9f316bd8060c9b8`:

1. `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_records.rs:61-72`, `write_atomic`: writes `contents` with `tokio::fs::write(&tmp, ...)`, then renames, with no file or directory sync. `RecordsStore::open` uses it at :132 to persist the iroh-docs namespace ID. The file is a cache and can be recreated, but losing/replacing its durable namespace identity can break continuity with the existing records document and its replica tickets. The comment says this follows `tags::save_registry`; that sibling now uses the durable helper, so the comparison is stale.
2. `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/publications.rs:342-359`, `Registry::save`: writes JSON with `std::fs::write`, then renames, with no file or directory sync. This is the persisted publication set loaded by `id serve`; its module contract says restart restores the set, and its save comment says a crash mid-save keeps the previous set intact.
3. Correct sibling pattern: `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/durable_write.rs:8-23` writes all bytes, syncs the temp file, renames, and attempts to sync the parent directory. Its existing callers are the three sites covered by #12152 / PR #12153.

## Why it matters

Atomic rename prevents readers from seeing a partially written destination during ordinary operation, but without syncing the temp data and directory entry it does not provide the same power-loss durability as the new shared helper. The publication registry can fail to restore the last successfully saved set; the namespace cache can lose continuity with its document. This is a durability gap, not a claim about ordinary process termination.

## Dedupe

- CLOSED #12152 and MERGED #12153 cover exactly `SequenceFile::next_sequence`, `id-store::tags::save_registry`, and `ListVersionStore::save`; neither candidate file is in the PR diff or the issue acceptance criteria.
- CLOSED #1544 concerned the non-atomic `records.namespace` write; it predates this temp-and-rename helper and does not cover fsync/directory durability.
- Fresh all-state searches for `world_records`, `publications`, `write_atomic`, and `fsync power loss atomic rename` found no open issue for these sites. Open PR search for `world_records`, `publications`, or `durable_write` found no matching PR.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Both writers use `id_core::durable_write::write_durable` (or an equivalent shared helper) so the temp file is synced before rename and the parent directory is synced afterward.
- [ ] Temp paths remain sibling paths on the same filesystem and are chosen consistently with the helper's callers; errors retain useful path context.
- [ ] Persistence tests for namespace-file recovery/reuse and publication-registry save/load still pass, with focused coverage for replacement and cleanup behavior as appropriate.
- [ ] Update the `write_atomic` comment and the publication persistence docs to describe the actual durability guarantees without overstating them.

## Suggested fix

Reuse `id_core::durable_write::write_durable`; select stable sibling temp paths and preserve the existing async/sync API shape as practical. No fix was made in this audit.

title: fix(pm-aggregator): serialize concurrent prompt-store writes

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Evidence

`pm-stack/aggregator/src/prompts.ts:78-105, 123-127` implements the live `/api/prompt` POST store. `PromptsStore.load()` uses a boolean set only after an awaited read, so simultaneous first calls can all read an empty/missing file before any marks it loaded. `add()` mutates a shared in-memory array then persists using the single temp name `${path}.${process.pid}.tmp` with no write serialization.

Reproduced on `origin/main` by calling `Promise.allSettled(Array.from({length: 12}, () => store.add(validPrompt)))` against a fresh temp file: 9 calls rejected with `ENOENT` renaming the shared temp path, although all 12 prompt records were written to disk. The route converts these persistence rejections to HTTP 500 (`src/server.ts` `/api/prompt` POST), so clients retry submissions that were already accepted and can create duplicates.

The sibling `CommentsStore` already addresses this exact class: memoized load promise and serialized writes with unique temp names (`src/comments.ts:225+, 333-355`; issue #1509). No open issue found for `PromptsStore`; #9539/#10032 track the feature, not concurrent persistence failure.

## Why it matters

Concurrent prompt submissions can receive errors despite being persisted. Retrying can duplicate work once prompt execution/enqueueing is added; simultaneous first reads can also race with writes and lose in-memory records.

## Acceptance criteria

- Memoize the first load so concurrent callers share one read and cannot reset or overwrite newly added prompts.
- Serialize persistence per store and use unique temporary paths; ensure a rejected write does not poison later writes.
- Add a concurrent-add regression test (including first access to a missing file) asserting all calls settle successfully and persisted records match successful return values exactly.
- Preserve existing single-add, reload, and missing-file behavior.

body:
## Problem

A snapshot's signed `header_version` claim is never required to match the version in the snapshot payload's own `Created` journal header. This leaves a gap in the reusable signing/acceptance contract for world replication: a payload can be internally valid for one version while the signed envelope claims another supported version, then be staged and committed as though the claim were authoritative.

The in-repo network feed currently carries the writer's correct version, but offline/programmatic envelope construction is also supported. The test added in `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_store.rs:1794-1808` hand-reads the payload header specifically to populate the claim, which shows this coupling is currently caller-maintained rather than enforced.

## Evidence

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication.rs:559-600`: `validate_payload_journal_header` checks the snapshot's first `Created` entry has the expected world ID, but does not check that its version equals `envelope.header_version`.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication.rs:685-700`: sign-time `validate_envelope_local` checks only that the claimed version is in the supported range.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/replication_receiver.rs:243-264`: `DurableReceiver::open` validates the committed journal and reads its actual header version, but snapshot acceptance validates against the envelope claim rather than the payload header.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_store.rs:1794-1808`: the offline replication test manually derives `header_version` from the first payload line before constructing the snapshot.

Adjacent trackers are not duplicates: #4486 covers missing/foreign/duplicate journal headers, #4487 covers receiver-side rollback to a lower version, #6469 covers the sign-time refusal contract generally, and #10715 covers header-version monotonicity. None requires claimed snapshot version to equal the payload's `Created.version`.

## Why it matters

A signed snapshot with a supported but mismatched claim can be accepted and committed even though its journal bytes identify a different version. Subsequent replica validation or synchronization can then reject that state. The normal network path supplies the correct version today, but the public signing/receiver APIs and offline transfers should enforce the invariant rather than rely on every caller to do so.

## Acceptance criteria

- Refuse to sign a snapshot when its claimed header version differs from its payload's `Created.version`; add regression coverage.
- Refuse to accept/stage the same mismatched signed snapshot without changing receiver state; add regression coverage.
- Audit direct/offline snapshot construction paths and retain or simplify the hand-derived version in the offline test as appropriate.
- Consider whether `DurableReceiver::begin_session` also needs to guard a claimed version inconsistent with the already-committed journal; split that concern if needed.
- Preserve legitimate higher-version snapshot rebases and all existing supported-version checks.
- Run targeted `id-worlds` replication tests.

title: pm-dispatch sessions run in the primary clone and leave ~/git/code on their PR branches
body:
## What happened

On 2026-11-21 at 02:07 CST the laptop's `pm-git-sync` started failing: `~/git/code` was on `bolt/cache-notification-clock-formatters-12207`, then on `palette/add-tag-title`, with a tracked edit in `templates.rs` while the session worked.

The commits came from two pm-dispatch sessions: "Scheduled Bolt — developing-today/code" (queue task #20901, issue #12207, PR #12210) and "Scheduled Palette — developing-today/code" (PR #12211). `POST /v1/sessions` defaults `directory` to the repo's primary clone (`REPO_DIRS`), so OpenCode runs the session in `~/git/code`. That clone is the deploy checkout `pm-git-sync` keeps on clean main (#8171). The Palette branch was also cut from the Bolt branch, because both sessions shared one checkout. One session also set a repo-local `user.name = repo-worker-tmp-code-b` in `~/git/code/.git/config`.

## Fix

- pm-dispatch gives every launch into a primary clone its own detached worktree at the remote default branch (`PM_DISPATCH_WORKTREE_ROOT`, default `~/git/fleet`). It never runs a session in the primary. If the worktree can't be made, the launch fails the same way any other pre-session failure does (the task is cancelled and the issue gets a note).
- The prompt prefix names the worktree and says the primary is off limits.
- The pm-dispatch package puts `git` on its wrapper PATH.

✅ **Always do:**
- Run commands like `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` (or associated equivalents) before creating PR

⚠️ **Ask first:**

BOLT'S PHILOSOPHY:
- Speed is a feature

BOLT'S JOURNAL - CRITICAL LEARNINGS ONLY:

Format: `## YYYY-MM-DD - [Title]
**Learning:** [Insight]

BOLT'S DAILY PROCESS:

BOLT'S FAVORITE OPTIMIZATIONS:
⚡ Add React.memo() to prevent unnecessary re-renders
⚡ Add database index on frequently queried field
⚡ Cache expensive API call results

BOLT AVOIDS (not worth the complexity):

❌ Premature optimization of cold paths
❌ Optimizations that make code unreadable
❌ Large architectural changes
❌ Optimizations that require extensive testing
❌ Changes to critical algorithms without thorough testing

Remember: You're Bolt, making things lightning fast. But speed without correctness is useless. Measure, optimize, verify. If you can't find a clear performance win today, wait for tomorrow's opportunity.

title: laptop-repo-keeper pushes half-finished agent work to main (tracked-only snapshots)
body:
## What happened

On 2026-11-20 at 22:26 CST the hourly `laptop-repo-keeper` committed `repo-keeper: snapshot code 2026-11-20 22:26 CST` (623e9b53d4) in `~/git/code` and pushed it to `main`.

A lane had been building the #10032 prompt slice directly in the primary clone. The keeper's snapshot step is `git add -u`, so it took the tracked half of that work (`server.ts` and `config.ts` now import `./prompts.ts`) and left the new files (`prompts.ts`, `prompt-widget.ts`, `prompts.test.ts`) untracked. `main` then had an aggregator that cannot load: `Could not resolve: "./prompts.ts"`. The untracked files also stalled `pm-git-sync` at 22:38. PR #12161 adds the missing files.

## Why it keeps happening

1. **Tracked-only snapshots.** When new untracked files sit beside tracked edits, the edits are usually half of one change. Committing only the tracked half and pushing it to `main` ships a broken tree. Today's test `untracked-ordinary case` pins exactly that behaviour.
2. **The deploy clone gets snapshotted at all.** `~/git/code` is the deploy clone that `pm-git-sync` (#8171) keeps on clean `main`. Any edit there that the keeper snapshots goes to `main` with no PR or review.

## Fix

- Hold the snapshot (report it, commit nothing) when untracked files are present beside tracked edits.
- Never snapshot repos listed in `REPO_KEEPER_NO_SNAPSHOT`. It defaults to `~/git/code`, and the home-manager module exposes it as `services.laptop-repo-keeper.noSnapshotRepos`.
- Edits stay on disk either way. Nothing is reset or deleted, and pull and push behaviour for already-committed work is unchanged.

title: fix(id): fsync temp files before rename in SequenceFile, registry and list-store saves

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Summary

Three crash-safety helpers in `pkgs/id` use a "write a temp file, then rename it over the real file" pattern but never fsync the temp file before the rename. Several sibling `pkgs/id` writers do fsync first, so this is an inconsistent gap rather than a deliberate exception. On a power loss the rename can reach disk while the file's data does not, leaving a zero-length file at the real path. Each helper then fails when it reads that file back, which bricks the feature until someone repairs it by hand. The `SequenceFile` doc also claims a "durable" counter, which this does not deliver.

## Evidence (origin/main `e61d9d5ee1ce05d403f0678a8f86d1a4e899a3e8`)

1. `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/transport_advertisement.rs:346-351`, `SequenceFile::next_sequence`. The doc at lines 329-331 says "Issue the next sequence, durably" and cites invariant 8. The code is `std::fs::write(&tmp, next)` then `std::fs::rename(&tmp, &self.path)`, with no `sync_all`. A zero-length file makes `last_issued` (line 333-340) return `InvalidData` because `"".parse::<u64>()` fails. `AdMinter::mint_locked` (line 415) propagates that error, so every mint fails and the transport advertisement stops refreshing until the counter is repaired by hand.
2. `pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/tags.rs:1740-1754`, `save_registry`. The doc says "atomically (write to temp then rename)". The code is `tokio::fs::write(&tmp, &json)` then `tokio::fs::rename(&tmp, path)`, with no fsync. A zero-length `registry.json` makes `load_registry` (line 1727-1737) fail on every tag operation, since `serde_json::from_slice` rejects empty input.
3. `pkgs/id/crates/id-core/src/sanctions_store.rs:508-513`, `ListVersionStore::save`. The doc says "so a crash mid-write never leaves a torn snapshot". The code is `std::fs::write(&tmp, &bytes)` then `std::fs::rename(&tmp, path)`, with no fsync. A zero-length snapshot makes `load` (line 516-519) fail on `serde_json`.

Existing patterns that do this correctly, to copy from:
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/local_claims.rs:197-212`: `File::create`, write, `file.sync_all()?`, then `rename`.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_store.rs:634-646`: `file.sync_all()?`, then `rename`, then a parent-directory `sync_all`.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/identity.rs` (around line 874): a parent-directory sync after the rename.

## Why it matters

- Invariant 8 and the "durable" wording say a restart never reissues or loses state. Without the fsync, a power loss can leave the counter or the registry unreadable, and the failure is a hard error in the normal read path, not a recoverable torn tail.
- `sanctions_store` and `save_registry` document crash-safety that the code does not provide on power loss.
- The fix is the same few lines at each site, so one change set covers the family.

Not a duplicate: closed #1544 covered `records.namespace` (a different file and crate), and no open issue or PR mentions `next_sequence`, `save_registry`, or the list-store `save` fsync gap (searched all states for `SequenceFile`, `next_sequence`, `fsync`, `sync_all`, `save_registry`, `registry.json`, `power loss`, `torn write`).

## Suggested fix

Introduce or reuse one small helper in `pkgs/id` that writes a sibling temp file, `sync_all`s it, renames it over the target, then `sync_all`s the parent directory. Use it at all three sites. Optionally add a failing-load test that a zero-length counter or registry is reported as a clear error, not silently treated as zero.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `next_sequence`, `save_registry`, and `ListVersionStore::save` each fsync the temp file before the rename, and fsync the parent directory after it, with the same discipline as `local_claims.rs` `persist`.
- [ ] Existing `transport_advertisement` counter, tag registry, and sanctions snapshot tests still pass; `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml` for the touched crates passes.
- [ ] A regression test exercises the write path (for example, asserts the temp file is synced before the rename via the shared helper, or that a truncated file is reported as an error and not as sequence 0).
- [ ] The doc comments at all three sites match what the code does.

## Notes

- Found by a read-only audit of `pkgs/id` atomic-write call sites by the improvement-issue creator (lane B). No source change in that pass.

title: fix(id-web): do not bypass stale-save conflict check when tag listing fails

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`current_filename_hash` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes/file_handlers.rs`
swallows tag-store read failures:

```rust
pub(super) async fn current_filename_hash(
    store: &iroh_blobs::api::Store,
    name: &str,
) -> Option<iroh_blobs::Hash> {
    use futures_lite::StreamExt;
    let mut tags = store.tags().list().await.ok()?;
    while let Some(Ok(tag_info)) = tags.next().await {
        if tag_info.name.as_ref() == name.as_bytes() {
            return Some(tag_info.hash);
        }
    }
    None
}
```

The stale-save conflict policy (#8524) relies on this lookup to decide
whether an incoming save is based on the current version:

```rust
if let Some(current) = current_filename_hash(&state.store, &req.name).await
    && let Ok(base) = id_core::iroh_hash::parse_hash(&req.doc_id)
    && base != current
{
    // refuse with 409 stale_save_conflict
}
```

When `store.tags().list()` fails, `current_filename_hash` returns `None`
and the entire conflict check is skipped, so the save proceeds and can
silently supersede a newer version without archiving it (the very
regression #8524 was added to prevent). A transient backend read error
therefore becomes a data-loss window.

The same `.await.ok()?` swallowing also affects `get_hash_for_name` and
`get_file_name` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes.rs`, which report
"not found" on storage failure, but the conflict path is the
data-integrity-relevant one.

## Acceptance criteria

- `current_filename_hash` (and ideally `get_hash_for_name`/`get_file_name`)
  distinguishes a storage failure from "no binding" instead of collapsing
  both to `None`.
- On a storage failure the save handler surfaces the error (e.g. 503 or
  an actionable error response) rather than bypassing the conflict check
  and overwriting.
- Existing tests that call `.unwrap()` on the result are updated to the
  new return shape without weakening the conflict assertions.
- Add a regression test simulating a tag-list failure on the save path
  and asserting the save does not silently succeed.

title: fix(id-sync): surface MetaRequest::Find storage failures

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage

labels.name: source/creator

labels.name: priority/normal

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Problem

`MetaRequest::Find` on the serving node silently converts any tag-store
read failure into an empty result, conflating a storage error with "no
matching files". This mirrors the defect fixed for `Get`/`Send` in #12127
and in progress for `List` in #12141/#12143, but `Find` was left
untouched.

Evidence (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/protocol.rs`):

- Handler at ~line 1310:
  ```rust
  MetaRequest::Find { query, prefer_name } => MetaResponse::Find {
      matches: self.find(&query, prefer_name).await,
  },
  ```
- `MetaProtocol::find` (~lines 1504-1535):
  ```rust
  if let Ok(mut list) = self.store.tags().list().await {
      while let Some(Ok(item)) = list.next().await {
          ...
      }
  }
  ```
  Both the initial `list()` failure and any `list.next()` stream error are
  swallowed: the function returns whatever it accumulated (possibly empty),
  indistinguishable from a genuinely empty store.

Impact: a remote `id find` (and the REPL/web surfaces that route through
`MetaRequest::Find`) reports "no matches" during a transient backend
failure instead of an error, masking outages and making retries impossible
for callers that key off `MetaResponse::Error`.

## Acceptance criteria

- `MetaProtocol::find` (or a helper) distinguishes a failed tag-list
  setup from an empty store and propagates stream-iteration errors
  instead of truncating.
- On failure the handler returns `MetaResponse::Error` with a message
  of the form `"failed to list file tags for Find"` (consistent with
  #12143's `"failed to list file tags for List"`).
- Add unit tests mirroring #12143: setup failure becomes an operation
  error; a stream error does not yield a partial success; empty and
  successful listings remain valid.
- No change to the `FindMatch` shape or sort order on the success path.

body:
`MetaRequest::List` currently turns tag-store failures into a successful empty or incomplete `MetaResponse::List`.

## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/protocol.rs`, the `MetaRequest::List` handler silently suppresses three failure classes:

- `self.store.tags().list().await` failure is ignored by `if let Ok(...)`, leaving `items` empty.
- A stream item error ends iteration because the loop is `while let Some(Ok(item))`, returning the prefix as a successful list.
- `self.tag_store.list_all(ns).await` failure is ignored, returning the items without the requested `origin` and `uploaded_at` enrichment.

The handler then unconditionally returns `MetaResponse::List { items }`.

## Impact

A remote protocol client cannot distinguish a genuinely empty store from a failed list operation, and can accept a partial listing or silently missing metadata as complete. This hides storage failures and can cause clients to make incorrect synchronization or display decisions. This is source-confirmed; no injected storage-failure runtime reproduction was run.

## Acceptance criteria

- Surface tag-list initialization, mid-stream, and metadata-enrichment failures as explicit protocol errors instead of empty/partial successful lists.
- Add deterministic tests for all three failure paths, asserting the client receives an error rather than an empty or partial success.
- Preserve successful empty-list behavior and normal listing/enrichment behavior.

title: fix(pm-stack): require completed evidence for host-health success
body: The PM host-health collector can mistake a reset systemd success result during retry for a completed successful run. This can pair a failed exit with apparent freshness or hide a known failure. Acceptance: use completed-process evidence, preserve known prior outcomes during retry, preserve actual recovery, keep pending and missing states honest, and verify deterministically offline. Keep snapshot shape, watchdog routing and installed services unchanged.

body:
## Evidence
In `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs`, `FileOps::rename` reads each referenced archive owner with `archive_owner(...).await.ok().flatten()` (around line 585). This collapses a storage error into the same `None` used for a successful lookup with no owner. The subsequent `legacy_owned` fallback (`current_owner.is_none() && is_owned_archive_tag_name(from, archive_name)`) can then call `set_archive_owner` and replace the archive owner based only on its filename.

The error-suppression is not present in `delete`: it propagates `archive_owner(...).await?` before trusting an owner-attributed reference. So rename can convert an owner-read failure into a trusted owner back-reference. For example, a legacy-shaped archive reference on `from` can be attributed to `to` after a transient `get_by_key` failure even though the existing `archive.owner` value may name a different file. Later deletion can then trust that rewritten attribution and remove the archive. This violates the FileOps ownership contract documented at the top of the module and the intent of #8815.

All-state issue searches for `archive.owner`/rename/read failure and archive-owner legacy fallback found no duplicate. #4766/#4767 track the broader design/audit; they do not identify this error-vs-absence branch. No matching open PR was found.

## Suggested fix
Only use the legacy filename fallback when `archive_owner` succeeds and proves the owner is absent. On lookup error, log and leave the owner unchanged. Add a deterministic regression test injecting an owner-tag read failure during rename.

## Acceptance criteria
- A failed owner lookup is distinguishable from a successful lookup returning no owner.
- Rename never rewrites `archive.owner` based on the filename when the owner read failed.
- Legacy owner inference still works when the lookup succeeds and no owner tag exists.
- A regression test covers the read-error interleaving and existing archive ownership/rename/delete tests pass.

body:
## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/protocol.rs`, the `MetaRequest::Get` handler at lines 1210-1219 chains `.get(&filename).await.ok().flatten()`. A tag-store read error is therefore serialized as `MetaResponse::Get { hash: None }`, indistinguishable from a successful lookup of a missing file. The `MetaRequest::Send` handler around lines 1380-1395 uses the same `.ok().flatten()` pattern, then returns `Error { message: "not found: ..." }` on storage failure.

## Impact

Remote clients and transfer callers receive a false absence result during transient/corrupt-store failures. They may report a missing file, skip retries or take wrong recovery actions; operators also lose the actual storage error. This is source-confirmed from the server request handler; no injected runtime failure repro was run. This is distinct from the closed #9195 file-list API issue, which addressed listing/stream failures rather than these per-file protocol lookups.

## Acceptance criteria

- Propagate tag-store lookup failures as `MetaResponse::Error` with useful context for both `Get` and `Send`; preserve `None`/"not found" only for a successful lookup with no tag.
- Add deterministic tests distinguishing storage errors from missing-file responses for both operations.
- Existing successful lookup, missing-file, and transfer behavior remains unchanged.
