title: mcpx: hot embeddings.* updates must take effect — atomic embedder replacement, honest applied state, vector-cache invalidation

labels.name: app/mcpx
labels.description: Package/app: mcpx (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Context

#13575 owns the runtime behavior contract for hot `embeddings.*` updates. Triage on #13575 (confirmed fresh against origin/main 4473da0c00446173bb61ec253d79c498a604f17e) established:

- `embeddings.wasmPath` (and the whole `embeddings.*` family) is registered `Hot: true` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/settings/wire.go`), so `PUT /v1/settings/embeddings.wasmPath` stores a runtime override and answers `applied: true` (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/routes_settings.go` — the hot branch only calls `SetRuntime` + `applyPoolRuntime`, and `applyPoolRuntime` is a no-op for non-`pool.*` paths).
- The active embedder is built exactly once: `Registry.UseSettings` constructs the cascade embedder, and its only call site is daemon startup (`pkgs/mcpx/internal/daemon/server.go`). Neither the settings PUT path nor `reloadConfig` ever calls it again, so the embedder a daemon starts with is the embedder it keeps for its whole PID lifetime — the `applied: true` answer is false today.
- The persistent vector index (`<state>/embeddings.db`, `catalog.VectorIndex`) caches semantic-search tool vectors keyed by tool name only, with no record of which embedder produced them, so even a correct swap would silently mix vector spaces (all embedders are checked against the same `VectorDim`, so no dimension guard trips).
- `Registry.UseSettings` silently swallows a `NewWasmEmbedder` load error, and `WasmEmbedder.Embed` silently falls back to the local subword projection when a module has no `embed` export — both matter to what "applied" may honestly claim.

## Scope — smallest correct first slice

1. **Synthetic fixtures.** Two `embed`-exporting Wasm guest modules with known, distinct, deterministic output vectors, built and committed the way `internal/wasmtools/testdata` guests are (Zig source + compiled `.wasm` alongside). The fixtures must really export `embed` (and `allocate`); a module without `embed` silently yields subword vectors, so the tests must be able to tell wasm vectors from subword ones.
2. **Atomic replacement.** A runtime change to any `embeddings.*` setting rebuilds the cascade embedder from the live settings set and swaps `Registry`'s embedder under the registry lock; the replaced `WasmEmbedder`'s wazero runtime is closed. Afterwards, `/v1/embeddings` on the same daemon PID returns the new model's vectors for identical inputs, equal to a fresh daemon started with the new settings.
3. **Honest applied state.** A `wasmPath` that cannot be read or compiled refuses the PUT with rollback (the settings handler's existing refused/rollback machinery) instead of reporting success — the swap path must not inherit `UseSettings`' silent load-error swallow. Any `embeddings.*` setting that cannot be applied live reports `restartRequired` instead of `applied: true`. No setting may report applied without taking effect.
4. **Cache invalidation.** On embedder swap, the tool vectors cached in the persistent `VectorIndex` are invalidated — flushed, or keyed by an embedder identity recorded in the index — so semantic search never scores a new-model query vector against old-model tool vectors.
5. **Contract test.** A daemon-level test driving both fixture modules on one daemon PID per #13575's acceptance: identical inputs before/after the switch, comparison against a fresh daemon, cache state after the switch, and the reported applied state.

## Out of scope

- The e2e `EffectProbes` entry for `embeddings.wasmPath` and removal of its exemptions (the `setting embeddings.wasmPath` line in `internal/e2e/feature_coverage_exemptions.txt` and the `settings.EffectExemptions` entry / `EffectExemptionPin`). That is #8471-family closing work once this behavior exists — #13575: keep the ratchet until its corresponding named effect probe lands.
- Any change to the remote/local embedder tiers beyond what the swap requires.

## Acceptance

The five scope items land with tests green via Fleet dispatch (`go test ./...` in `pkgs/mcpx`, or at minimum the affected packages: `internal/daemon`, `internal/catalog`, `internal/settings`). #13575's acceptance is then satisfiable by the follow-on probe work under #8471.

Program #13264. Filed from the #13575 triage by lane felix.

title: fleet placement: distinguish unreadable runner load from measured idle capacity

labels.name: app/fleet
labels.description: pkgs/fleet multicall binary + platform crates

body:
## Observed dispatch

On 2026-11-23 at 18:13:37 UTC, Fleet submitted a Linux job to `fleet-personal`. The local placement receipt reported that it could not read load for that runner host because no covering token was available. Its decision text then described **0 active jobs and 40 free slots** and picked the least-loaded eligible owner. Other host reads reported HTTP 403. The invocation supplied no load, budget or surface override. The caller's seat reported revision `22ec90b9c29d`. GitHub confirms the workflow dispatch and attempt. Actual provider-wide occupancy and this owner’s available slots at selection time are unknown. [Run 45236087853, attempt 1](https://github.com/dezren39/fleet/actions/runs/45236087853/attempts/1) · [Fleet program #13272](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13272)

## Source premise

Main at `10b0db798295` initializes running and queued to zero per owner. A missing token skips both reads. A failed read records an error and contributes zero. An HTTP 200 with a missing or invalid `total_count` contributes zero too. The resulting tuple has no indication of coverage. The adapter subtracts the sum from the registry cap and exposes a numeric free-slot estimate. Selection sorts these values as measured loads. Even complete runner-host counts are a proxy for account occupancy. The relevant placement and adapter files had identical contents at the inspected seat revision and this main revision. [Collector](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/10b0db798295149bf11a5d63a12d42e2e6b0b0dc/pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/placement.rs#L910-L961) · [Capacity calculation](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/10b0db798295149bf11a5d63a12d42e2e6b0b0dc/pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/placement/adapters.rs#L488-L514) · [Selection](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/10b0db798295149bf11a5d63a12d42e2e6b0b0dc/pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/placement.rs#L1110-L1158)

## Acceptance criteria and fixture oracles

- Carry per-owner read coverage, time, source and status into the JSON and operator explanation. A successful, explicit zero from every required host/status read is a measured zero on those hosts. Missing credentials, non-200 responses, transport failure, absent or invalid counts and stale samples produce unknown or partial coverage. Preserve the known subtotal as a lower bound. Label explicit simulation overrides and the configured cap separately.
- Prefer an otherwise eligible plan-covered surface with measured headroom. An unreadable eligible surface remains an option under an explicit unknown-capacity rule. Show that rule in the dispatch receipt and preserve deterministic ordering among unknowns. If a known subtotal already reaches the cap, it proves saturation even with partial coverage. Retain repository eligibility, the macOS cap and zero-spend constraints.
- With a fake GitHub adapter, assert on the decision JSON and explanation for a fully observed zero with cap 40, missing token, 403, malformed successful reply, missing one status when the other returns 3, and an explicit override. Only complete observations or clearly marked simulations may yield numeric estimated headroom. When every otherwise eligible included surface has unknown load, dispatch can select one with a reason that names the uncertainty. Failure to read load must never authorize paid overage. No production probes or load are needed.
- Verify the operator chapter and placement reference against the output from the fixtures under DOC-01. This issue covers interpreting and reporting load. Credential changes and live placement experiments are outside its scope.

No queue item was manually enqueued during this read-only production resurvey.

title: fix(id-store): enforce the artifact byte ceiling during media stream assembly

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
## Finding

The accepted media contract fixes the artifact ceiling at 256 MiB. The public id-store MediaStream helper checks each incoming frame and the current credit window, then appends to the assembled bytes. The total artifact size is checked when the caller finishes. A caller using the reusable API therefore has no enforced artifact-sized bound on the logical bytes retained during assembly. This finding concerns the library contract; production endpoint exposure was not established.

[Source at checked main](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/cb4f687a2479c82718697139cc278bd3705200c8/pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/media.rs#L428) · [Adopted artifact-storage decision](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/2342#issuecomment-6912122685) · [Original implementation](https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/10653) · [ID program](https://github.com/developing-today/code/issues/13240)

## Acceptance

Apply the existing cumulative artifact ceiling before consuming frame credit or extending the assembly buffer. Preserve the existing frame, ended-stream and backpressure errors. Reuse the artifact oversize refusal. A boundary test with a small synthetic limit checks exact fit, rejection, unchanged bytes and credit, and subsequent finalization of the admitted prefix. Update the data-crate library chapter in the same PR.

title: C4 shared formatter: long-horizon ranges lose week information (weekday-only calendar form)
body:
Found by Codex review on PR #13529 (the duplicate of the #13408 landing, PR #13530): the shared §4 formatter (`renderPredictionRange` in `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-downtime.ts`) loses week information in long-horizon ranges.

The formatter selects the calendar form whenever earliest/latest fall on different Chicago days, and its dayparts name only the weekday ("Tuesday afternoon"). That is unambiguous for the downtime kind's short windows, but arrival predictions (C4.4, `quota-arrival.ts`) routinely span weeks. Codex's example: a vendor cadence anchored and issued at `2026-09-01T17:00:00Z` with a 28-day period and 7-day spread predicts Sep 22 → Oct 6, and the stored `rendered` is now `between Tuesday afternoon and Tuesday afternoon` — where the pre-unification arrival renderer emitted an unambiguous days-from-now string (21–35 days). Both arrival bases are affected; the stored string is what the scorer and the C6 pages show, so the ambiguity is user-visible and permanent for those records.

This is a property of the shared formatter, not of the arrival adoption itself: #13408 prescribed the unification (landed as PR #13530, methodology c4-meth:2). The fix belongs in the one formatter so every kind benefits — candidate shapes for the design owner (#9572): prefer a days form when the span exceeds a week, add week context to the calendar form for far bounds, or name the month/day for bounds more than N days out. Any change to stored renderings is methodology-visible (§6 log entry + version bump, per the #13408 precedent).

Filed by Lane AU6 from the Codex P2 finding on PR #13529; the landed implementation is PR #13530 (merge `074d39603ac7`).

title: id: implement grant expiry bound and grantor veto (#6379 F1+F2)
body:
Implementation follow-on for #6379 findings F1 + F2. **Gated on the #6379 design-core record** (threat model + decisions, lane felix, PR to be linked here when opened): do not start implementation until that record merges; the record's decision sections are the spec.

Scope, per the design of record (§7.1/§7.4 of the 2026-10-11 groups/delegation design) and the design-core record's decisions:

1. **Grant expiry (F1).** Optional signed `expires_at` bound on the grant event and a matching `id delegate` flag (`DelegateArgs`, `pkgs/id/crates/id-cli/src/cli/groups.rs`); the delegation judge (`pkgs/id/crates/id-events/src/groups/delegation.rs`) refuses a chain link whose grant has expired at the action's causal position (validity rule 5). Judged only from signed fields, so the fold stays a deterministic function of the log. `uses` bounds are out of scope (design §7.4: never a group state rule).
2. **Grantor veto (F2).** Extend the veto judge so a grant's own grantor may veto that grant (author == grant grantor, grant in the veto's causal past, same group), in addition to the existing manager veto, which is unchanged. Grants re-anchored at the group (`from == None`) have no grantor and remain manager-veto only; a transfer-reissued grant's grantor is its reissuer.

Acceptance: fold-layer tests for expiry-at-position (incl. a chain failing only after expiry, and pre-expiry positions still judging valid) and for grantor veto (own grant cut; another's grant refused; manager path unchanged); CLI flag covered by the F5 test packet's scenarios where applicable. No existing refusal is weakened.

body:
Implementation slice 2 of the Notion importer design for #6436, landed as `doc/2026-11-10_design_id6436.md` (PR #8416, amended PR #8558). Parent implementation issue: #6513. Slice 1 (manifest + inventory, #8419) has landed; this is the next slice in the design's implementation slicing.

Scope (design §2.1, §2.5, §3, §4; Implementation slicing item 2):

- Identity assignment pass: fill the manifest's page UUID → note ID map and block UUID → (note ID, block identity) map, idempotently — an assignment, once recorded, never changes on re-import (§6.1).
- Page/block core: rebuild each page's block tree from fresh block-children responses (sibling order preserved), and convert the clean classes of §2.5 (paragraph, headings, lists, to-do, quote, code, divider, bookmark) into the note revision content form, with child pages as typed references to their own notes. Every block is classified clean / degraded / unsupported; unsupported blocks are preserved verbatim, never dropped (§2.5).
- Two-pass link rewriting (§3): identity is assigned for the whole inventory before any content converts, so page links, mentions, and block links (`#<block-uuid>`) rewrite to typed references through the manifest map; a link whose target is outside the import set stays a verbatim external URL and is counted as externalised.
- Files (§4): file-bearing blocks are fetched during the run through an injected fetcher boundary; blobs are keyed by their BLAKE3-256 content hash (the model's `raw-blake3-256` profile), duplicate bytes are stored once, and the manifest records source file ↔ blob. A file that cannot be fetched degrades its page with a named missing-resource reason and never aborts the import.

Acceptance:

- Offline fixture tests over recorded block-children responses: converting the fixture pages yields the expected content trees, typed references, and manifest maps (design §8 checks 2 and 6, page/block subset).
- Re-running identity assignment and conversion over an unchanged corpus changes nothing: no new note IDs, byte-identical content (design §8 check 3, conversion level).
- No credentials persisted (§6.5): file URLs arrive only through the injected boundary at fetch time and are never recorded in the manifest or content.

Later slices: 3 databases (schema claims, relations, rollups/formulas); 4 comments + degradation classes + hybrid export matching; 5 fidelity report + incremental re-import.

body:
Perform a comprehensive daily codebase review, innovation scan, and issue/PR maintenance pass across developing-today/code.

You are acting as an unrestricted principal architect and senior systems engineer. Do not hold back: generate bold ideas, surface hidden gaps, polish proposals, and solve immediate problems opportunistically.
Follow these directives and areas of focus:
### 1. COMPREHENSIVE REPOSITORY & ACTIVITY AUDIT - Inspect recent commits on `main` to understand the latest velocity and architectural direction. - Review open, recently closed, and merged issues and PRs (`gh issue list --state all --limit 50`, `gh pr list --state all --limit 30`). - Review each major package, tool, and subsystem in the repository:
  - **`pkgs/id`**: Distributed identity, cryptographic event log, p2panda synchronization, local event store, group encryption, discovery, and capability delegation.
  - **`pkgs/mcpx`**: Model Context Protocol daemon, multi-server multiplexing, protocol compliance, session leasing, JIT secret prompt vault, and Code Mode projection.
  - **`pkgs/fleet`**: The Rust multicall fleet tools and queue client — automated multi-agent coding workflows, issue triage, and parallel agent execution (the retired packages were removed by PR #5376; audit the fleet queue automation under `pkgs/fleet` and `.github/workflows`, the dispatch actions `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-start` and `.github/actions/pm-dispatch-task`, the scheduler `.github/workflows/pm-scheduled.yml` and its repo-specific scheduled callers, and the CI-breakage automation).
  - **NixOS System Infrastructure & Web Services**: Modules, cloud functions, background daemons, and system services.

### 2. UNRESTRICTED INNOVATION & NEW FEATURE GENERATION - You are NOT restricted by what currently exists. Brainstorm things that *should* exist, would be exceptionally useful, or incorporate frontier concepts:
  - Edge architectures using Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, KV, and Queues.
  - Distributed SQLite / libSQL / Turso primitives for offline-first, syncable state.
  - Advanced autonomous coding loops, speculative tool execution, and local verification loops.
  - Cross-platform bridges, native desktop integrations, and performance optimizations.
- **Bias Toward Capture**: It is far better to create an issue to triage later than to let a valuable opportunity or insight pass.
### 3. ACTIVE ISSUE & PR MAINTENANCE - **Scope Variety**: Create single large architectural vision issues for strategic direction, or narrow, highly focused issues for targeted improvements. - **Issue Decomposition**: If an existing issue is too broad, ambiguous, or monolithic (including issues created by others), break it apart into a series of clear, modular, linked sub-issues with explicit dependencies. - **Deduplication & Consolidation**: Identify overlapping or duplicate proposals/issues and consolidate them into unified, high-quality reference issues. - **Comments & Spec Refinement**: Leave comments or edit existing issues/PRs to provide missing technical specifications, edge-case analysis, data schemas, or suggested test cases. - **Zero-Context Hand-off Standard**: Every issue you author must be self-contained, citing exact file paths, interfaces, architectural rationale, and verifiable acceptance criteria so a new agent with zero prior context can execute it.

### 4. OPPORTUNISTIC IMPLEMENTATION (QUICK-WIN PRS) - If you identify straightforward bugs, unhandled edge cases, missing test coverage, or clean opportunities to refactor code to prevent future merge conflicts:
  - You are actively encouraged to open small, focused Pull Requests implementing the fix or feature directly.
  - Ensure all added code follows repository standards, includes tests, and passes formatting/linting hooks (`treefmt`, `conform`).
  - Never introduce breaking regressions to existing stable flows.
  - **One PR per coherent set**: batch every instance of the same problem — and all related dependency updates — into a single PR, or a few PRs split by coherent group. Never one PR per item or per dependency.
  - **Prefer tracked, higher-impact work**: before inventing a new micro-fix, check the open issues and implement the highest-impact one you can complete and verify, even when it spans several files.
  - **Merging is permitted, never required**: merge your PR only when checks pass and you are reasonably certain it is correct and low-risk. Otherwise leave it open and state your confidence and what a human should check in the description.

body:
**Today.** The Worker's code is tested under bun (357 tests), and `scripts/edge-smoke.ts` runs the bundle in the real runtime (workerd) before each deploy. The smoke run has no sign-in to present, so everything behind the owner's sign-in is checked only under bun: the actions the edge does itself, once-only by name, what is held and taken back, the Machines and Platform reads. The alarm that wakes the object (notifications with nobody looking, the wake after a refusal) is not run in the real runtime at all. Bun is not the runtime: a report that hung for twenty seconds there once passed every bun test.

**What done looks like.**

- The smoke run signs its own token with a key it also serves as the issuer's (as `scripts/edge-demo.ts` does), so it can make signed-in requests of the Worker in workerd.
- It then checks, in the real runtime: an action done once under a name and answered again from the record; one held with the host down, listed by the Machines read, and taken back; the Platform read; and that an alarm set by the object fires and does its work (a short interval set by a variable for the run).
- It stays in the deploy workflow as the gate it is today.

title: id: SubscriptionStore/BoardSubscription derive Debug, printing private follower keys — contradicts the slice-1 privacy invariant
body:
Slice 1 of #7585 (commit 0dfe789276f, `pkgs/id/src/boards/subscription.rs`) stakes a privacy invariant and then derives the surface that breaks it.

**Evidence**

- `pkgs/id/src/boards/subscription.rs:14-17": "the only reads are a per-pair lookup and a per-subscriber listing, so there is no surface that enumerates who follows what."
- `pkgs/id/src/boards/subscription.rs:296-299" (test): "follower identity is visible to no one but the follower" (oracle invariant 4).
- `pkgs/id/src/boards/subscription.rs:44" and `:83": `BoardSubscription` and `SubscriptionStore` both `#[derive(..., Debug, ...)]` over `subscriber: String` (canonical Ed25519 key) keyed maps. One `{store:?}` in a log line dumps the entire follower graph: every subscriber key with every board each follows.

**Verified, not a hunch**

Added a temporary in-module probe (reverted afterwards, tree clean):

```rust
let mut store = SubscriptionStore::new();
store.follow(&viewer(), &board, 1).unwrap();
assert!(!format!("{store:?}").contains(&viewer()));
```

Result: FAILED — `store Debug leaks subscriber key` at `src/boards/subscription.rs`. The derived Debug prints the subscriber hex.

**Why it matters now**

Slice 1 has no callers yet, so nothing logs the store today — but slices 2+ (discovery/feed surfaces per #7585) will hold this store next to request logging. A single `:?}` on an error/log path then leaks who-follows-what. Redacting now is a ~10-line fix before the store grows callers.

**Acceptance**

- `SubscriptionStore` and `BoardSubscription` no longer emit subscriber keys via `Debug` (custom redacting impl or removed derive), with a regression test asserting the rendered form contains no subscriber key.
- Module docs still hold: per-pair lookup + per-subscriber listing remain the only enumeration surfaces.

Related: #7585 (epic), #5862 (design Decision 1). Follow-up to slice-1 commit 0dfe789276f.

title: Daily flake sync & config optimization

labels.name: source/dispatch
labels.description: Filed by pm-dispatch

body:
Perform the daily configuration review for developing-today/code. Do NOT update the `opencode` or `openchamber` flake inputs — the flake-inputs-update workflow owns them.
Follow these instructions and rules:
### 1. FLAKE INPUTS — OWNED ELSEWHERE, DO NOT BUMP - The `opencode` and `openchamber` flake inputs are owned by the deterministic
  `flake-inputs-update` workflow, which bumps, validates, and merges them daily.
  Do NOT run `nix flake update` for them, do NOT change their pins in `flake.lock`,
  and do NOT open PRs that bump them. If their pins look stale, leave them — the
  owning workflow handles them the same day.
- Do NOT casually bump root `nixpkgs` (root nixpkgs is pinned deliberately per system stability policies). - Clean up any stale input overrides or unused flake dependencies in `flake.nix` (e.g. warnings about non-existent input overrides like gitignore or devshell).
### 2. CONFIGURATION & INFRASTRUCTURE IMPROVEMENTS - Investigate potential configuration improvements in `nixos/`, `home/`, `lib/`, and package definitions under `pkgs/`. - Check for:
  - Deprecated NixOS or Home Manager options
  - Suboptimal build phases or missing binary wrappers
  - Systemd service resilience (e.g. restart policies, socket activation)
  - Modularity and decoupling to prevent merge conflicts
- Clean up any dead code, unused flags, or documentation drift in Nix configurations.
### 3. EVALUATION & VALIDATION - Verify that all system and host configurations evaluate cleanly without errors:
  `nix eval --raw .#nixosConfigurations.nixos.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath`
- Ensure git hooks, commit messages, and treefmt formatting pass cleanly.

### 4. PULL REQUEST & MERGE - If updates or improvements are present:
  - Open a clear Pull Request documenting any configuration enhancements made. Keep every related change in this one PR — never split changes into one PR per item.
  - Merge into `main` only when you are reasonably certain it is correct: all Nix evaluations and checks succeed, the PR is conflict-free, and the changes are limited to the intended bumps and fixes. Merging is permitted, never required — when any of that is uncertain, leave the PR open and explain what a human should check.

title: mcpx book build: generated spec tables carry unescaped placeholders; docs workflow header claims PR builds
body:
## What this is

Two book-build infrastructure disagreements found by the bookwright coverage audit of the mcpx book (PR #13413, tracking #1888). The audit fixed the book-side symptoms; both items are about the generators/config that will reintroduce them.

## 1. Generated spec tables carry unescaped placeholder tokens

The baseline `.#mcpx-docs` build emitted 19 "unclosed HTML tag" warnings. Thirteen of them sit in text generated from the MCP spec corpus or quoted from upstream sources:

- `spec/conformance-matrix.md` — `mcpx elicit result <id>` (5 occurrences of `<id>`)
- `spec/requirements.md` — `<server>`
- `spec/revision-conflicts.md` — `<server>`, `<id>`
- `protocol.md` — a quoted `"Invalid or missing client id: <uri>: <reason>"` string
- `compare/register/plugin-apis.md` — quoted TypeScript (`Array<Hooks>`, `Promise<void>`, `Array<SystemPart>`)

Bare `<token>` prose is eaten as an HTML tag by the renderer: the placeholder vanishes from the published page, not just from the log. PR #13413 escaped the committed occurrences, and the settings table's instance was fixed at its source (the `script.devshell` Short string in `internal/settings/registry.go`). But the spec chapters are regenerated from the corpus, so the next regeneration reintroduces the spec-side ones unless the generator escapes angle-bracket placeholders in quoted spec text (backticks or `<`).

Ask: the spec-corpus generator escapes placeholder tokens at generation time, so regenerated chapters are warning-free without hand edits.

## 2. mcpx-docs.yml's header describes PR builds its triggers never fire

`.github/workflows/mcpx-docs.yml` opens with "Builds run on pull requests, pushes to main, and manual dispatch" and has an "Upload built site (PR builds only)" step guarded by `if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'` — but its `on:` triggers are `push` (main) and `workflow_dispatch` only. There is no `pull_request` trigger, so the step is unreachable and the comment is wrong. (The sibling build-only workflows — `fleet-docs.yml`, `atlas-docs.yml`, `id-docs.yml` — likewise build on push-to-main + dispatch, not on PRs.)

Ask: either add the `pull_request` trigger (with the artifact upload the comment promises) or correct the header comment and remove the dead step, so the workflow file and its own documentation agree. The book's new deploying chapter (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/deploying.md`, PR #13413) describes the triggers as they actually are.

## What this is

Corrections to the mcpx programme census, found by the bookwright coverage audit of the mcpx book (PR #13413, tracking #1888) and verified against the binary built from `0d29cdad5cf` (unchanged at `1310027fd1f`). The investigation prompt (first comment on #13264) and the research files behind it state three figures that the subject itself contradicts. The prompt is a starting point other agents consume as ground truth, so the record should be corrected where they will read it.

## The corrections

1. **Settings: 241, not 252.** `mcpx config --schema --plumbing` prints 241 settings (193 public + 48 internal/plumbing), and the source registry in `internal/settings` agrees exactly (both set differences empty). The 252 figure counted `Path:` literals across the whole settings tree — 253 such literals exist, 12 of them in test files (fixtures like `mini.setting`, `x.port`), not in the registry.
2. **Commands: 75, not ~50.** `mcpx --help` declares 75 top-level commands in **six** groups. The research census captured five groups and flagged its own inspection tail as unverified; the sixth group (DAEMON OPERATIONS — the generated per-operation commands: `artifact`, `ask`, `task`, `session`, …) plus the inspection tail (`hook`, `want`, `interactions`, …) account for the difference.
3. **Effect exemptions: 5, not 8.** `EffectExemptionPin` is 5 on current main. The three settings the census listed as flag-held (`plugin.instructions`, `plugin.disabledTools`, `protoTasks.cancelGrace`) gained their e2e probes on 2026-11-23 (PRs #13345, #13370, #13361; #8473 closed). The book's new coverage chapter (`pkgs/mcpx/docs/coverage.md`, PR #13413) carries the verified numbers with the method, and the book itself never stated the old ones. title: id-worlds: JournalAdminHistory cannot be constructed outside the crate — no public constructor for current-form checkpoint fixtures
body:
## Problem

`JournalAdminHistory` (crates/id-worlds) cannot be constructed outside the `id-worlds` crate: its fields are `pub(crate)` and it has no public constructor. Any code outside `id-worlds` — benches, integration tests, downstream tooling — that needs to write a journal containing a **current-form** (split) checkpoint cannot build one:

- `WorldCore::checkpoint_entries` writes split checkpoints whose parts are joined by `admin_history: Some(..)`.
- Restore's split-parts path requires `admin_history: Some({ events, complete })`; a parts set written with `admin_history: None` is refused.
- So an external writer can only produce the **legacy** inline-checkpoint form (`admin_history: None`, single `JournalEntry::Checkpoint`), which restore supports explicitly.

Found by Lane XZ while landing #13084 (`stress_join` bench): the bench's checkpoint fixtures use the legacy inline form and disclose the limitation in the bench header. The retained window (≤ `WorldLimits::default().retained_events`) serializes under the writer's own inline bound (`MAX_CHECKPOINT_PART_BYTES`, 192 KiB), so the inline form is also the form the writer itself would choose at those sizes — but any fixture needing a current-form checkpoint (e.g. a >192 KiB retained window, or admin-history-specific restore coverage) is blocked.

## Ask

Give `JournalAdminHistory` a public construction path (a constructor or builder in `id-worlds`, re-exported through the `id` facade) so benches/tests can write current-form checkpoints, or document an intended alternative route for external checkpoint fixtures.

Refs #13084.

title: C4: quota-arrival.ts has its own renderPredictionRange without the §4 compound/calendar forms
body:
Found while landing #13357 (PR #13406): the design (§4) says `rendered` is produced by **one** formatter, but there are two `renderPredictionRange` functions with the same name:

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-downtime.ts` — the shared formatter (C4.1 downtime and C4.2 reset-duration use it). After #13357 it implements duration, day, compound, and calendar forms.
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/quota-arrival.ts` — its own copy, ms-number signature, duration and day forms only. Its header comment says "the calendar form (day names / dayparts) is not yet", and it has no compound form either.

Unifying them on the shared formatter would change arrival records' stored `rendered` strings (e.g. "between 2.5 and 5.7 days from now" → "2.5 to 5.7 days"), so it is a methodology-visible change: it needs a §6 methodology-log entry and a version bump, not a silent edit. The arrival kind's records currently name `c4-meth:1` via their own `ARRIVAL_METHODOLOGY_VERSION` constant.

Suggested slice: point the arrival builder at the shared formatter (adapting the call site from ms numbers to ISO strings), update the arrival §4-form tests to the shared renderings, bump the methodology version with a log entry. Do not close #13357's follow-up until the arrival tests pin the shared forms.

title: id: reject hosted imports with a mismatched unkeyed-export token
body:
## Summary
`ingest_import` does not bind the `VerifiedImport` token's `unkeyed_export` trust decision to the export being ingested. A token minted for a keyed export can therefore authorize ingest of an unkeyed export without the operator confirmation required by `verify_import`.

## Evidence
- `pkgs/id/src/hosted_export.rs:391-404` includes `unkeyed_export` in `VerifiedImport`.
- `pkgs/id/src/hosted_export.rs:503-513` rejects an unkeyed manifest unless `confirm_untrusted` is true.
- `pkgs/id/src/hosted_ingest.rs:269-274` checks binding ID, Iroh ID, object count, and blob count, but not `verified.unkeyed_export` against `export.manifest.unkeyed_export`.
- Reproduced on current `origin/main`: `verify_import(&unkeyed_export, false)` returns an error, but passing that export to `ingest_import` with a token from a same-shape keyed export succeeds and the object lands in the event store.

## Impact
The ingest API's typed verification token can be reused across exports that differ in the operator-confirmation trust property. A caller that verifies a keyed export can unintentionally ingest an unkeyed/service-signed export without explicit confirmation.

## Acceptance criteria
- Reject before mutating the event store when `VerifiedImport.unkeyed_export` differs from the export manifest's `unkeyed_export` value.
- Add a regression test proving a keyed-export token cannot ingest an unkeyed export, while matching keyed and explicitly confirmed unkeyed token/export pairs retain their intended behavior.

Related ongoing work: #13313 checks the CSE choice on this token path; it does not cover the unkeyed-export trust flag.

title: ci(mcpx): e2e-no-deno leg — real bun and node paths with no Deno on PATH
body:
Follow-up from #1983 (mcpx test environments), filed by lane felix 2026-11-23 after a done check against current main.

## What is missing

The `e2e-no-deno` matrix row from #1983: the real bun and node e2e paths with no Deno anywhere on `PATH` — what a user without Deno gets from `script.runtime=auto`. No current leg shows this: the host legs always install Deno (setup-deno), and the nix package wrapper suffixes Deno onto PATH, so every wrapped run resolves `auto` to Deno. A Deno-less user's `auto` behaviour is untested end to end.

## Scope

A leg in `.github/workflows/mcpx-test.yml` on ubuntu-latest:

- Install bun and node only — no setup-deno — and assert `deno` is absent from PATH in the leg, so the leg cannot pass by secretly having it.
- `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=bun,node,python3` (a missing one of those fails, per the #6904 semantics already in `internal/testsupport/require.go`).
- Run the runtime-focused e2e tests `-run`-filtered — at minimum the per-runtime tests in `internal/e2e/runtime_test.go` (the deno subtests skip via `RequireBinary`; bun and node subtests must run and pass) plus an `auto`-resolution probe: with only bun/node present, `script.runtime=auto` executes successfully. Filtered runs are exempt from the feature-coverage guard by design (`featureCoverageGuardViolations` returns nil for `-run` runs), so the leg does not need the full suite.

## Acceptance

- The leg is green in CI, with the bun and node subtests shown as run (not skipped) in the output.
- The leg fails if Deno is introduced onto the runner PATH.

## Queue coverage

Not enqueued as a pilot task in this pass: #1983 marked the row tier 1 "once #100 lands" (the `auto` runtime question, historical dezren39/nix numbering), and which existing test owns `auto`-picks-each-runtime needs confirming when this is scoped. Filed as a sequenced remainder of #1983 for Felix to scope and enqueue.

title: test(mcpx): remote-safe e2e subset — per-test needs selection + remote runner leg
body:
Follow-up from #1983 (mcpx test environments), filed by lane felix 2026-11-23 after a done check against current main.

## Where #1983's Remote section stands

Approach C (the same tests, tagged by need, and a remote runner) is only partly landed. What exists today: the `remote-smoke` leg in `.github/workflows/mcpx-test.yml` — the shipped image's daemon runs in its own container on a docker network and a client container reaches it over TCP (`status` reports running). That proves the transport. What does not exist: any run of the actual e2e assertions against a remote daemon.

## Scope

1. A per-test needs/opt-in mechanism for `internal/e2e`: a test declares `localFS`, `ownsDaemon` (restart/stop), or `perTestConfig`, or opts in as remote-safe. #1983's open question stands — opt-in is safer at first; deriving from declared needs is the later step. The selection must fail closed: a test whose needs are undeclared is not run remotely.
2. A remote runner leg (in `mcpx-test.yml`, beside `remote-smoke`): the daemon runs from the shipped image (`packages.mcpx-container`) in a separate container with `daemon.address=0.0.0.0` and a fixed port; the selected remote-safe `/v1` + MCP subset runs against it via `MCPX_DAEMON_ENDPOINT`. Per-test servers are added over `POST /v1/servers` with a per-test name suffix and removed in cleanup.
3. `TestExecOnTheDaemonRunsWhereTheDaemonIs` (`internal/e2e/exec_test.go`) is the canonical member of the subset.

## Acceptance

- The leg is green in CI with the selected subset actually executing (test count reported, not a smoke).
- CLI tests stay local; commands that name a local path are refused clearly against the remote daemon, per #1983.

## Queue coverage

Not enqueued as a pilot task in this pass: the opt-in-vs-derived decision in step 1 is a design call the parent issue left open, and the leg's shape depends on it. Filed as the sequenced remainder of #1983 for Felix to scope and enqueue.

## ID book survey disagreements: CLI help / README vs the parser source (CLI-1…CLI-14)

Found by the source survey behind the ID book (#13332; book live at https://developing-today.github.io/code/id/). In each case the book states the **source** behaviour; items are cited by number inline in most chapters shown, and the rest are recorded here from the survey. Full file:line evidence was verified against the checkout at `1ccb4a19457` (2026-11-23). The fix belongs to whichever side is wrong — usually the help text or the README, occasionally the code.

- **CLI-1** — README gives `list` an `ls` alias the parser does not have. (`id ls` fails, exit 2; the alias exists only in the REPL and on `tag list`.) — *File commands: put, get, find and kin*
- **CLI-2** — README's Cargo quick-start misdescribes `--no-default-features` (a default build already has no web UI; the flag also removes `sandbox`/`world`). — *Installation and provisioning*
- **CLI-3** — README's command table omits `walk`; its own body documents it. — *The id command line*
- **CLI-4** — Shipped binaries disagree with the source (and each other) about `serve` (`--replace-defaults`, `defaults.conf` vs `defaults.json`, `walk`, `--version`). — *Installation and provisioning*
- **CLI-5** — Serve lock filename: `serve.rs` module doc says `.id-serve-lock`; the constant is `.iroh-serve.lock`. — *Installation and provisioning*
- **CLI-6** — `serve --topic`/`--topic-secret` help presents the hardcoded constants as "the default". — *Serve and server commands*
- **CLI-7** — README's REPL example pipes output to the shell with `|`; the REPL has no such operator. — *The interactive REPL*
- **CLI-8** — README labels `id find "*.rs"` "Find files by pattern"; there is no glob/wildcard matching anywhere in the search implementation. — *File commands: put, get, find and kin*
- **CLI-9** — Top-level help says `group` can "join"; `group join` parses its ticket and then always fails (unimplemented stub). — *Groups, documents, claims and keys*
- **CLI-10** — Inconsistent feature gating: `world` parses without its feature, `match-audit` does not. — *World commands: joining and playing*
- **CLI-11** — REPL `find`/`search` default format is `union`; the clap commands default to `tag`. Neither side's help mentions the other. — *File commands: put, get, find and kin*
- **CLI-12** — REPL startup banner under-reports the REPL command set. — *The interactive REPL*
- **CLI-13** — README "Project Structure" describes the pre-split layout. — *The shape of the system*
- **CLI-14** — `id put --content`'s documented example contradicts its flag contract (the one-name requirement is missing from the `--help` summary line). — *File commands: put, get, find and kin*

title: fix(pm-aggregator): metadata-sweeper crashes when the metadata DB parent directory does not exist

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

body:
## Evidence

At fresh `origin/main` `2d69ca216237858a0b6254e0d629094e3c48788c`, `pm-stack/aggregator/scripts/metadata-sweeper.ts:338` opens the store directly:

```ts
const db = new Database(options.dryRun ? ":memory:" : options.dbPath);
```

with the default `dbPath` (`:81`) `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/pm-metadata.sqlite`. The file contains no `mkdir` (verified by grep), and unlike the server path it does not go through `openMetadataStore`.

Reproduced with bun 1.4.4 (same runtime): `new Database("/tmp/sweeper-repro/no-such-dir/pm-metadata.sqlite")` throws `SQLiteError: unable to open database file`. bun:sqlite creates the file but not its parents, so in any clean environment (fresh runner/container, new machine with no `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator`) the sweeper crashes before scanning anything — the same defect class as #13293, whose fix (commit `a1dbcf6`) only covered the server-side `openMetadataStore` in `metadata-ingestion.ts`.

## Why it matters

The sweeper is the scheduled ingestion path into the same metadata store; a clean-venue run fails outright for a reason unrelated to the repos it scans, and the failure (SQLITE_CANTOPEN) looks like a database problem rather than a missing directory. The server can now boot cleanly while its companion script cannot.

## Dedupe

- #13293 (CLOSED): server boot via `openMetadataStore` — fixed; the sweeper bypasses that function.
- All-state issue search for `CANTOPEN` returns only #13293; no open issue or open PR tracks the sweeper path.

## Acceptance criteria

- Non-dry-run sweeper creates the DB parent directory (`mkdirSync(dirname(dbPath), { recursive: true })`, `:memory:` exempt — or reuse `openMetadataStore`) before opening, mirroring `a1dbcf6`.
- Pointing `--db` (or `PM_METADATA_DB_PATH`) under a nonexistent nested directory proceeds past the DB open instead of throwing SQLITE_CANTOPEN; genuine open failures (permissions, non-directory parent) still throw.
- Dry-run behavior unchanged (still `:memory:`, still touches no file).
- Regression test covering the missing-parent case.

title: opencode-claimant hermetic suite: violation gate trips on 5 caught subprocess attempts across four modules
body:
## Finding

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/run_hermetic_tests.py` (the claimant's canonical offline suite; the Makefile `test` target) currently exits 1 even when every test passes: `Ran 226 tests ... OK`, then `Forbidden external I/O attempted: subprocess.Popen ×5` and a failing exit status. The runner's contract is deliberate — code that catches the guard's exception still attempted real I/O, so the run is not a successful offline check — but five caught attempts across four modules trip it, so the suite cannot report green end-to-end.

Per-module bisect (2026-11-23, worktree bisect harness replicating the runner's guard/env, pristine main `ba7ea99e9fe`):

- `test_claimant.py` (offline_claimant): 2 attempts
- `test_babysitter.py` (offline_babysitter): 1 attempt
- `test_nudges.py` (offline_nudges): 1 attempt
- `test/test_claimant.py` (offline_mode): 1 attempt
- `test_poll.py`, `test_prompt_constants.py`: 0

Each attempt is a production fail-open path (a subprocess spawn whose failure the code under test catches and converts to a verdict) exercised by a test that does not fake the subprocess boundary.

## Suggested disposition

Per case, one of: fake the subprocess boundary in the test (the shape used for the `TestCodeSourceFireLog` fix landed under #13254), move the test out of the offline suite if its purpose is the spawn-failure path itself, or — only with a recorded rationale — amend the guard's contract. The suite should exit 0 with an empty violation list when this is done.

Found by Lane XS during the #13254 verifier audit (2026-11-23). The two hard test *errors* that previously accompanied this (TestCodeSourceFireLog spawning real git, from #12813) are fixed under #13254 and are not part of this item; this issue covers only the remaining caught-attempt violation backlog.

title: id-currency-registry: add currency status transitions (freeze/sunset) and wire them into the gateway service
body:
## Context

The gateway service landed by the #5522 slice (`pkgs/id/src/currency/gateway_service.rs`) refuses the `freeze` and `sunset` ops by name (`ServiceError::Unsupported`). The F3 envelope authorizes both ops, but the F1 registry crate has no status-transition write: `CurrencyStatus` has `Frozen`/`Sunset` variants and no `Registry` method ever sets them, so there is nothing for the service to execute. Refusing by name was deliberate — the alternative was pretending — but the ops should work.

## Scope

1. `id-currency-registry`: add issuer-only status transitions (`freeze_currency`, `sunset_currency` or one `set_status`) with `Store` support. Decide and document repeat-transition behavior (idempotent success vs typed refusal) and whether sunset is reachable from frozen.
2. Gateway service: execute `Freeze`/`Sunset` through the same write-ahead intent path as the other mutating ops (durable intent, stored receipt, replay on retry), replacing the `Unsupported` refusal.
3. Decide where a frozen/sunset currency refuses value ops: the F3 authorization layer already has an inactive-currency refusal — wire the registry status through the service's `RegistryView` so `issue`/`transfer` on a frozen currency refuse there, and say in the module docs which layer refuses what.

## Acceptance

- Registry tests: transition happy paths, non-issuer refusal, repeat-transition behavior as documented.
- Service tests: freeze posts an intent and replays on retry; issue/transfer against a frozen currency refuse; sunset is terminal.
- The `Unsupported` arms for freeze/sunset are gone from the gateway service.

## Filing note

Filed without a pilot packet/enqueue: the prioritized shortlist is managed by the lane operator (Felix); this is a candidate for `fleet agent shortlist add` in the currencies line, after #5522's slice lands. Refs #5522, #10070 item 1 follow-on.

title: fleet-command runner surface: no cargo toolchain, and nix cannot build (nixbld group missing; /homeless-shelter purity error)
body:
Found 2026-11-23 while dispatching a Rust test run for #5756 (PR #13330) through the documented fallback (`gh workflow run fleet-command.yml --repo developing-today/fleet`).

The standard Fleet build container (ghcr.io/dezren39/fleet-build-full) cannot run a Rust build/test command today:

1. **No Rust toolchain on the surface.** `which cargo rustc rustup` finds nothing; PATH is `/home/vscode/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/local/go/bin:...` (nix, go, python3 only). The workflow's CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME caches (`.fleet/cache/{cargo,rustup}`) restore empty on a cold key, and nothing installs a toolchain into them. The runbook's example command (`cargo test --workspace`, `pkgs/fleet/doc/agents/remote-build-and-test.md`) fails with `cargo: command not found` (run 45177566734).
2. **The nix route is broken in the container.** `nix develop` against the code repo's root flake first needs `--extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes'` (acceptable), then fails: `error: the group 'nixbld' specified in 'build-users-group' does not exist` (run 45179906596). With `--option build-users-group ''` it fetches substitutes fine but fails at build time: `error: home directory '/homeless-shelter' exists; please remove it to assure purity of builds without sandboxing` (run 45183462671).

**Workaround used for PR #13330 (works, and warms the caches):** the dispatched command bootstraps the pinned toolchain via rustup into the run's CARGO_HOME/RUSTUP_HOME: `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh -s -- -y --default-toolchain 1.99.1 --profile minimal`, then `export PATH="/bin:/opt/hatch/bin:/opt/hatch-image/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin:/home/hatch/workspace/custom-skills/in-flight-reasoning-log/scripts:/opt/muse/skills/documents/scripts:/opt/muse/skills/generate_podcast/scripts:/opt/muse/skills/style-tryon/scripts"`. Run 45185203954 passed end to end with it.

**Ask:** make the standard surface run the runbook's plain cargo commands — either pre-install a rustup-managed toolchain in the build image (or restore one into the fleet-deps cache under the toolchain-file key), or fix the container's nix configuration (create the nixbld group / set build-users-group empty + sandbox off coherently) so `nix develop` works. Until then every Rust dispatch rediscovers this.

Refs: #5756, PR #13330. Runs: 45177566734 (cargo missing), 45179906596 (nixbld), 45183462671 (homeless-shelter), 45184417123 + 45185203954 (rustup bootstrap; the second is the passing one).

title: id(fileops): delete collects overflow-digit archive lookalikes the shared writer/reader rule treats as user files
body:
Found by the #4767 Phase 4 closing audit (disposition (b)), 2026-11-23, against main `5835457324d`. Filed per that audit's acceptance: confirmed gaps are named follow-ups, not fixed inside the audit.

## The divergence

The shared writer/reader archive rule is `archive_tag_timestamp` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs:188`): `{stem}.archive.{digits}` counts as an archive only when the digit suffix **fits in u64**. The writer's reservation (`validate_name`, via `is_archive_tag_name` at :197) and the web reader's classification (`classify_tag` in `pkgs/id/crates/id-web/src/routes.rs`, which calls the same function) both use it, and the test `fileops_rejects_archive_shaped_names_but_allows_lookalikes` (fileops.rs:1094) pins the consequence, citing #11790 ("one rule for writer and reader"): `a.archive.18446744073709551616` (u64::MAX + 1) is **a valid primary user file name**.

`FileOps::delete`'s two archive-collection paths use a wider, digit-only spelling with no u64 fit:

- The prefix scan (fileops.rs:715–727): any tag under `{name}.archive.` whose rest is non-empty and all ASCII digits is collected, subject to the `archive.owner` check. An ordinary user file carries no `archive.owner`, so the check reads Absent and the tag is collected.
- `is_owned_archive_tag_name` (fileops.rs:867), which decides whether a stored `archive.rename`/`archive.replace` reference is honoured: same digit-only check.

## Consequence

`put("a.archive.18446744073709551616", …)` succeeds and listings classify the file as Primary — but `delete("a")` hard-deletes it as if it were an archive of `a`. Delete disagrees with the writer, the reader, and the #11790 one-rule decision for exactly the overflow-lookalike class that decision deliberately kept as user files.

## Fix shape

Both collection predicates should apply the shared rule: a suffix counts only when the full tag name is accepted by `archive_tag_timestamp` with the expected stem (equivalently: suffix non-empty, all ASCII digits, and parses as u64). This preserves legacy recovery for every u64-fitting archive name — all FileOps-minted archive names fit by construction (`claim_archive_name` starts from a u64 timestamp) — and aligns delete with writer and reader.

## Tests

Extend the existing fileops test modules: (1) an overflow-suffix user file survives `delete` of its stem neighbour; (2) a u64::MAX-suffix archive is still collected by `delete`; (3) `is_owned_archive_tag_name` rejects an overflow-suffix reference name.

title: fix(pm-aggregator): server boot crashes in clean environments when the metadata DB directory does not exist
body:
Found during #9608's outage-queueing slice (PR #13292), verified 2026-11-23 via remote dispatch in a clean GitHub-hosted runner.

**Symptom:** `bun run src/server.ts` crashes at startup with `SQLiteError: unable to open database file (SQLITE_CANTOPEN)` at `src/server.ts` (the `openMetadataStore(metadataDbPath, ...)` call, ~line 2244): the default `PM_METADATA_DB_PATH` is `~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/pm-metadata.sqlite`, and nothing creates that parent directory before the SQLite open. On the laptop the directory exists from prior state, so boot works; in any clean environment (fresh runner, fresh container, new machine) the aggregator cannot start at all.

**Blast radius:** every boot-based aggregator test suite fails in a clean venue for this reason alone — observed in fleet-command run 45177942229 for the pre-existing `test/actions.test.ts` and `test/break-glass-route-9608.test.ts` boots, identical crash, on code paths unrelated to the change under test. The #9608 route suite works around it by pointing `PM_METADATA_DB_PATH` at its temp dir; that is a per-suite workaround, not a fix.

**Suggested fix:** create the parent directory (`mkdir(dirname(path), { recursive: true })`) before opening the metadata store — in `openMetadataStore` or at the server.ts call site — mirroring how the other state stores persist (they mkdir their file's dirname on write). Keep fail-closed behaviour for genuine open failures (permissions, corrupt DB): only the missing-directory case should self-heal.

**Acceptance:** the aggregator boots in a clean HOME with no pre-created state directory; the pre-existing boot suites (`test/actions.test.ts`, `test/break-glass-route-9608.test.ts`, `test/boot.test.ts` where venue permits) pass in a clean runner without per-suite env workarounds; a regression test or boot check covers the missing-directory case.

title: id(fileops): delete collects overflow-digit .archive. names that the shared writer/reader rule calls ordinary files

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

body:
Found by the #4767 Phase 4 closing audit (2026-11-23, against main `c1700bc77d8`). A confirmed gap, filed per that audit's acceptance — not fixed inside the audit.

**The divergence.** The shared archive-shape rule `archive_tag_timestamp` (`pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/fileops.rs`) requires the suffix after `.archive.` to parse as a u64 (#11790 unified writer and reader on this). So `validate_name` ACCEPTS `a.archive.18446744073709551616` (u64::MAX + 1) as an ordinary user file — pinned by the test `fileops_rejects_archive_shaped_names_but_allows_lookalikes` — and the web reader `classify_tag` shows it as `FileKind::Primary`.

But `FileOps::delete`'s two archive-collection paths use an unbounded all-ASCII-digit suffix check instead: the `{name}.archive.` prefix scan inside `delete`, and `is_owned_archive_tag_name`. Neither requires the suffix to fit in u64.

**Probe evidence (first-hand, 2026-11-23).** In an in-memory store, seed file `a` and the user file `a.archive.18446744073709551616`, then `delete("a")`: the outcome was `archives_removed == 1` and the overflow-suffix file was gone. Under the shared rule the expected outcome is `archives_removed == 0` with the file surviving — it is a user file, not an archive of `a`. (Probe test `delete_of_base_spares_overflow_suffix_user_file` was run in the #4767 audit worktree and failed exactly on that assertion, left: 1, right: 0.)

**Fix shape.** Make both collection checks agree with the shared rule: a collected suffix must be all digits AND parse as u64 (equivalently, the candidate must satisfy the `archive_tag_timestamp` shape relative to the owner prefix). Land the probe above as the regression test. This cannot orphan a real archive: the writer only mints suffixes from a u64 timestamp incremented from a u64 start (`claim_archive_name` / `free_archive_name`), so every FileOps-produced archive name fits u64 by construction.

**Related:** #4767 (audit that found it), #11790 (writer/reader unification), #4720 (the original reserved-namespace fix this is the residual edge of).

title: id: verify export blob refs against each envelope's actual content citations
body:
## Evidence

At fresh `origin/main` `7fecf882f614cfd6642b8a387009489a19a354ec`, `pkgs/id/src/hosted_export.rs:596-615` builds `referenced_blobs` only from each export object's caller-supplied `blob_refs`, then checks those names against carried blob hashes. It does not decode the envelope's actual document citation and prove that the named blob bytes produce that content. The envelope signature authenticates its citation, but `blob_refs` is not part of that envelope signature or the manifest's `objects_digest`.

Reproduced with a temporary integration test against current source: create a valid signed `document.put` envelope citing content A; supply unrelated bytes B as the export blob and set the object's `blob_refs` to B's SHA-256; build and sign the export normally. `verify_import` returns `Ok(VerifiedImport)`. `hosted_ingest::ingest_import` then reports the import complete, stores B under its BLAKE3 hash, and leaves the envelope's cited A unavailable. The test's final deliberate panic marked the confirmed gap; the temporary test was removed before filing.

Related production mapping exists in `pkgs/id/hosted-worker/src/export.ts`: it resolves envelope citations by BLAKE3 content to SHA-256 blob names. That producer-side check cannot protect a self-hosted importer from a hostile/tampered export. Related PR #13196 adds §6.2 refusal coverage but does not cover this binding: its changed files/test list do not validate `blob_refs` against the envelope's citations.

## Impact

A malicious or corrupt export can pass the importer's signature/integrity verification and be reported complete while silently breaking a document's content citation. The verification boundary must establish that each signed envelope citation resolves to the bytes of the carried blob before any ingest occurs.

## Acceptance criteria

- `verify_import` derives each object's content citations from its verified envelope and checks them against blob bytes (BLAKE3 citation identity → export SHA-256 blob name), rather than trusting `blob_refs` alone.
- Reject a valid signed object paired with a decoy blob, a missing cited blob, and inconsistent/extra blob references before ingest writes anything.
- Preserve the honest hosted export fixture and round-trip import tests.
- Add a regression test proving the decoy export is refused by verification and no object/blob is ingested.

title: Atlas toolchain pin disagreement: rust-toolchain.toml says 1.99.1, flake comment + CI + default.nix say 1.99.0 (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found while building the Atlas book (#13251), verified on the laptop checkout 2026-11-23.

pkgs/atlas-search/rust-toolchain.toml reads `channel = "1.99.1"` — the file the Nix build and rustup actually use (flake.nix's rust-overlay reads it; home/common/default.nix builds the laptop's atlasSearchToolchain from it).

Three other sources say 1.99.0:
- pkgs/atlas-search/flake.nix's comment describes the pin as "the pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml, channel 1.99.0) — the same rustup toolchain the step 1-4 gates ran under".
- CI installs 1.99.0 (`rustup toolchain install 1.99.0 --profile minimal`) and runs `cargo +1.99.0 test ... -p atlas-core`.
- pkgs/atlas-search/default.nix also records 1.99.0.

So CI tests a different compiler than the Nix build ships. The toolchain file itself warns that changing the channel may cause rustc to build from source, so the fix direction (bump CI + comments to 1.99.1, or set the file back to 1.99.0 once nixpkgs has it cached) is a deliberate call — but the four sources should agree, and today they do not.

The book states the file's value as what a build uses and records this disagreement (pkgs/atlas-search/book/development/building.md, getting-started/installation.md).

title: Atlas repo docs and design archive disagreements: README index, who serves, CI triggers, census freshness, endpoint table (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found by the Atlas book survey (#13251, survey D). Disagreements in the repo's own Atlas documentation and design archive. The book (pkgs/atlas-search/book/) now carries the reconciled account; these are the stale sources.

1. **doc/README.md indexes 6 Atlas records; doc/ contains 38 Atlas entries.** Most of the design archive — including the design of record, scaler revision, staging gate, classification, metadata, D1-cache and embedded-replica records — has no README entry, while one README entry (the lawyer packet) has no "atlas" in its directory name. A reader navigating by the README misses ~85% of the archive. (The book's roadmap chapter now maps all 38.)
2. **Design-of-record layout vs the package as built.** Design §4 proposes pkgs/atlas-search/ with a package-local doc/ and exactly four crates + fixtures/. The built package has docs/ (plural, three files), no package-local doc/, and substantial extra top-level surface the design tree does not show (atlas_search.py, worker/, eval/, schema/, tools/, tests/, test-vectors/, onnxruntime/).
3. **atlas_search.py points at a README that was not there; Python line count drift.** The Python header says "(see README.md in this directory)" — pkgs/atlas-search/ had no README.md (the book PR adds one, so the pointer now resolves). The design of record describes the Python as 1,177 lines (true of the hatch-personal copy); the in-repo copy is 1,629 lines. The two copies are not the same file version; "the Python reference" needs a which-copy qualifier.
4. **Who serves: design + unit name say atlas-search serve; the live ExecStart is fleet serve search** (#5604, atlasSearchServeViaFleet = true). The Worker README's deploy note ("a binary refresh of the laptop's atlas-search.service") is unit-accurate but binary-silent on this point.
5. **CI headers/names vs CI triggers (three workflows).** atlas-search-pr.yml is named for PRs but triggers on nightly schedule + dispatch only (deliberate policy; the name is the stale part). atlas-search-worker-tests.yml's header says it runs "on pushes to main that touch pkgs/atlas-search/worker/ and on dispatch"; its on: block is dispatch + nightly only. fleet-search-parity-guard.yml presents as a drift guard for a byte-parity contract but triggers on workflow_dispatch only — nothing runs it automatically, and the two server.rs copies already differ in size (151,924 vs 151,913 bytes), so "verbatim copy" in fleet-search/src/lib.rs reads as a maintained copy under parity discipline, not byte-identity.
6. **Program record names a package that does not exist.** The program investigation record describes "`pkgs/atlas-search/`, `pkgs/atlas-core` surfaces" — there is no pkgs/atlas-core; atlas-core is a crate inside pkgs/atlas-search/crates/.
7. **Two caches, opposite TTL stories, both called "the Atlas cache".** The service temp store: in-memory, 10-minute TTL / 60-minute hard cap, nothing survives restart by requirement (a security property). The Worker cache (#6805): Durable-Object-persisted, indefinite, no TTL/eviction in v1 (a cost property). Documents that do not name which store a TTL claim belongs to mislead; the book names them separately throughout.
8. **Embedding endpoint 18791 (memory design) vs in-process ONNX (everything else).** The memory-integration design routes ingestion embeddings through "the openclaw-embedding service, fixed loopback port 18791" or atlas-embed. No code, nix, or other doc in the Atlas estate references 18791; the built embedding is in-process ONNX resident in the serve process, and the service's outward embedding surface is POST /v1/embed on :18760 (#6788). The memory design's slice 2 does not describe the pipeline the service runs.
9. **Ingest: two generations described as current in different homes.** The turso-atlas README presents the collect→normalize→index→publish→access atlas-ingest.py pipeline as THE pipeline, present tense. The in-repo machinery describes per-unit staging DBs, a registry, classification-at-staging, an M6-gated promote and a five-stage batch gate; the scaler design's migration table says the aggregator path replaces direct-to-core ingest. The 2026-11-23 program record sides with the README on current practice (manual/script-driven; #5670 migration open) and with the in-repo design on target shape. The book states the generation labels once, early.
10. **Census freshness: the headline numbers are a 2026-10-31 snapshot repeated as present tense.** 18,325 / 122,124 / 107,639 appears in the design of record (2026-11-04) as current shape and is still the ground-truth line in the 2026-11-23 program record — which itself flags the store has grown (~7.3 GB monolith) without a verified recount. The design of record's "107,639 chunks in a Turso database" (monolith framing) and the program record's "monolith plus 29 topic shards" describe the same census at different physical-layout generations. The book dates the census 2026-10-31 everywhere.
11. **Design endpoint table vs the implemented route table.** Design §2's table has seven rows; the implemented server.rs dispatch adds POST /v1/embed, POST/GET /v1/feedback (+ unversioned aliases) and GET /v1/search/jobs. None contradicts the design, but an API chapter built from the design table alone would omit three live surfaces — including the one the Worker depends on.

Book chapters: pkgs/atlas-search/book/design/roadmap-and-issue-map.md (archive map), reference/service-api.md, concepts/ingest.md, operations/backup-and-census.md.

title: Atlas library internal disagreements: model spellings, sensitivity vocabularies, pad id, ORT versions, content_hash producer (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found by the Atlas book survey (#13251, survey C). Internal code/comment/schema disagreements in the Atlas library surface. The book documents the code behaviour and names each item.

1. **Three model-identity spellings for one model.** types::DEFAULT_MODEL and atlas-proto's default: `Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0`. shards::EMBEDDING_MODEL_ID (stamped into shard and staging-DB manifests, compared at discovery/fan-out): `snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0`. The Worker's EMBED_MODEL: the HF spelling. A shard stamped by the aggregator can never string-equal DEFAULT_MODEL; no code converts between the spellings.
2. **Sensitivity vocabularies collide across stores** (also survey D §7.8). Staging items.sensitivity defaults to 'internal' and uses the TIER vocabulary (public/internal/secret — also gate_records.tier CHECK, shard-manifest tier key), while publish chunks.sensitivity / session_labels.sensitivity use the LADDER vocabulary (shareable/personal/local-only/secret-bearing); staging_units.sensitivity is free TEXT with no CHECK. The tier↔ladder mapping lives in prose and in exactly two code paths (tier_sensitivity_name at promotion; TierCeiling::from_sensitivity the other way) — no schema encodes it.
3. **Pad token id: tokenizer declares 1, pipeline and crate use 0.** The shipped tokenizer's declared pad id is 1; the corpus pipeline pads with 0 and atlas-embed hard-codes PAD_ID = 0. Recorded as bit-identically inert on this fp32 graph — but the constant contradicts the tokenizer config it loads, and a future graph change voids the inertness proof.
4. **Gate A bit-identity is version-matched, but two ONNX Runtime versions are in play.** Fixtures recorded with onnxruntime 1.31.1 (venv build); the nix closure carries 1.27.1 (~1e-7 deltas). Handling (fail as NOT APPLICABLE) is agreed in fixtures/README.md and gate_a.rs — the disagreement is between pinned provenance and deployed closure: a plain cargo test environment loading 1.27.1 can produce no parity verdict either way.
5. **SearchParametersV1 carries controls the code refuses to run.** planner_enabled, spell_enabled, query_class_hint and variant != Raw are representable in the versioned contract (and included in cache-key canonical material) but validate() rejects any non-default value as "not implemented yet". The contract presents them as v1 parameters; the implementation is raw-variant-only.
6. **The chunk content_hash — the system's identity join — has no pinned producer.** Every store joins on it, the golden-set fingerprint is built from it, shard chunks.content_hash is UNIQUE — yet test-vectors/content-hash-v1.json records its producer as unavailable, with no algorithm and no known-answer vectors, and forbids interop claims until one is pinned.
7. **Turso read-only tokens: the platform API path cannot produce one.** atlas_search.py's header (verified 2026-10-31): the Platform API mint endpoint ignores read-only request bodies (returns a=rw regardless), so minting goes through the CLI (a=ro). The backend's "read-only by construction" claim rests on the CLI mint path only.
8. **atlas-core's crate doc predates the shard composition.** lib.rs frames the monolith Scan as "the current production path" with the index strategy decided at the #5356 cutover, while shards/scan.rs documents ShardedBackend already serving the vector branch from shards in the service composition (monolith retained for FTS/details). Both are true of different layers; the crate doc's framing is the stale one.
9. **classification.rs has no module doc and is not re-exported**, unlike every sibling module — despite defining ClassificationRecord / EffectiveClassification, which disclosure.rs and classify.rs build on. A discoverability gap in the library surface itself.
10. **Staging-DB invariant vs the promotion stamp.** atlas_stage_v1.sql and stage::check_stage_schema assert a staging DB's table set is EXACTLY the five v1 tables; aggregate.rs step 4 adds a sixth table (atlas_manifest) as the promotion stamp, which closes the DB to further stage_artifact writes. Deliberate and documented in aggregate.rs — but a promoted staging DB no longer satisfies the v1 schema its own DDL defines.
11. **boundary_drift_6038.py's docstring describes the pre-fix experiment.** It defines boundary_shift as "drop W0's first sentence" — the construction PR #7661's review found defective. The corrected construction is what the .md report describes and the re-run measured; the .py docstring was not brought along.

title: Atlas evaluation record disagrees with itself: RRF k, two production rows, trunc-384, stale eval README (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found by the Atlas book survey (#13251, survey C §6 + disagreements). The evaluation record disagrees with itself about what the production configuration and its numbers are. The book names which system each number belongs to; these records need reconciling at the source.

1. **RRF k: 10 (production) vs 60 (the entire Python eval lineage).** query-parameters-v1.json sets rrf_k = 10; fusion.rs tests decompose at k=10; atlas_search.py's header records the 2026-10-31 production shape at k=10, pool 100 (best row: 189 hits@10 / MRR 0.3894). But eval3.py's hybrid fuses top-30 branches at k=60, and gate5733.py / gate-5733-results.md measure the "Python reference hybrid" at k=60 with trunc-384. The gate's base retrieval is therefore NOT the production configuration it is described as reproducing.
2. **Two different "production hybrid" golden-311 rows.** atlas_search.py header: 189 hits@10 / MRR 0.3894 (pool 100, k=10). gate-5733-results.md sanity gate: recall@10 183/311, MRR 0.3640 (depth 30, k=60, trunc-384). Both are labelled production-hybrid numbers for the same golden set; neither document names the other's row.
3. **Truncation: production full-width vs eval's 384.** Rust SearchOptions.trunc defaults to 0 (full 768); the corpus was embedded prompt-free at full width. gate5733 and eval3 run the base retrieval at trunc-384. Gate numbers are 384-dim numbers, not full-width numbers.
4. **gate5733.py docstring says 60 near-exact passages; the fixture and verdict say 54.** heldout-nearexact-54.json contains 54 queries ("First 54 qualifying chunks kept"); the results record measures 54 throughout. The docstring's 60 was not updated when the set was cut.
5. **eval/README's held-out status is stale in both directions.** It says the real held-out set "is collected under #5741's test plan" and frames eval-smoke.json as the only fixture-like set — but heldout-nearexact-54.json has existed since 2026-11-17 and a full gate has run on it. Conversely its ablation framing implies SPLADE is an evaluable signal while its own "What this does not do" confirms no SPLADE encoder/postings exist — SPLADE has never been scored.
6. **Two unrelated "golden" artefacts.** overlap-report-6039.md's golden set is provisional and self-derived; the #6027 golden set it should have used "has not landed", and golden-311's qrels (chunk-id judgements against the conversation corpus) cannot serve the overlap experiment (span judgements against the repo slice). The report also records that its expectation (prose vs logs would differ) did not hold — both saturate at 10%.

title: Atlas Worker README vs code: cache key, D1 flag, gate scope, ceiling check, module map (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found by the Atlas book survey (#13251, survey B: Worker/MCP/REST source walk). Disagreements between the atlas-search Worker's README/comments and its code. The book documents the code.

1. **README's cache-key description predates KEY_SCHEMA 2.** README "Shape": key = sha256 over normalized query + fingerprint (ceiling, model revision, vector table, k). Code (key.ts): the material also contains `"v": 2` and `"context": "hosted-per-user"` (the disclosure context added by #12622 — precisely why KEY_SCHEMA bumped to 2 and all v1 entries were orphaned). A reader building a key from the README computes the wrong digest.
2. **The D1 hot cache reads as flag-gated; in code it is entirely unwired.** README: "with the flag off nothing reads or writes the cache" — implying on activates it. Code: HotCacheStore has no caller in the request path (only tests call it); with the flag on and the binding present, the Worker still never touches D1. Read-path integration is #13105.
3. **wrangler.toml's secret comment scopes the gate to /v1/* only.** "`GATE_TOKEN` — inbound bearer for /v1/*". Code + the same file's header: the gate also covers POST /mcp.
4. **README credits ceiling enforcement to the service only; the Worker also enforces it.** service.ts verifies `effective_ceiling === "personal"` after every search and refuses (502, before caching) any result reporting a different ceiling. The README's "Shape" section omits the Worker-side check.
5. **README's module map misattributes keying.** "src/index.ts — gate, normalization, keying, routing." Keying lives in key.ts (queryKey/keyMaterial), invoked for search from search.ts (executeSearch); index.ts calls queryKey directly only for inspect/purge. Normalization likewise lives in key.ts.

title: fleet search surface disagreements: serve routing, the mirroring claim, get-chunk delegation, = spelling (book survey, #13251)
body:
Found by the Atlas book survey (#13251, survey A §7). Disagreements inside the fleet search surface over Atlas.

1. **fleet search serve: help, error string, and behaviour disagree.** `fleet help search` lists serve as a domain command. cli.rs::run() contains a branch rejecting serve as "not part of the fleet search client surface". Live behaviour: `fleet search serve` starts the service (routes to fleet serve search before the client parser runs, as cli.rs's own header states). The rejection branch is unreachable for serve (still live for init/fetch-model, exit 2), and its error text incorrectly lumps serve with them.
2. **fleet search help says "mirroring atlas-search search" — it is a subset, and two validations differ.** The atlas-search search flags absent from fleet's parser are enumerated in the book (20 names verified against parse_search_args; the survey text says 21 in one place — the count itself needs pinning). --expand is validated 0..=100 by atlas-search but only >= 0 by fleet's via-service path; --hydrate is capped at 1000 by atlas-search, only >= 0 by fleet. Help also abbreviates the model default to `Snowflake arctic-embed-m-v2.0`; the parser's actual default is `Snowflake/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0`.
3. **fleet search get-chunk help understates its real surface.** The verb documents only --neighbors and --text, but parses nothing: every argument delegates verbatim, so atlas-search get-chunk's --context, --backend, --db, --vecdb, --via-service and --service-url all work through it undocumented — and a mistyped fleet-level flag fails at the artifact with atlas-search's wording, not fleet's.
4. **fleet serve search accepts --flag=value; fleet search does not.** The serve role's hand parser splits on `=`; the search client parser has no `=` handling (`--k=5` is an unknown-option usage error). The standalone clap binaries accept both spellings throughout.
