title: enroll: no provisioning path for the three broker token files on non-muse seats (secrets/queue/shell legs)
body:
## Summary

A freshly enrolled non-`muse` fleet seat has **no provisioning path at all** for the three shared broker token files its client verbs require:

| Client file (on the seat) | Server-side counterpart (laptop) | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `~/tools/secrets-broker-token` | `~/.config/secrets-broker/token` | session broker sends it as `X-Agent-Token` to the secrets-broker (port 4800); named in every `fleet secrets` broker request (`DEFAULT_SECRETS_TOKEN_FILE`, fleet-config) |
| `~/tools/queue-broker-token` | `~/.config/queue-broker/token` | session-proxy queue requests name this file (`fleet-queue` client transport, port 4801) |
| `~/tools/laptop-agent-token` | `~/tools/laptop-agent-token` (laptop) | `fleet laptop-agent` reads it directly ("token file … unreadable" when absent); also the session broker's default token (port 4799) |

Verified 2026-11-23: on the archer seat each file is 65 bytes, mode 0600, and its sha256 is **identical** to the laptop server file's sha256 (hashes compared, values never printed). They are copies of the laptop's service tokens.

## Why fresh seats never get them

- `scripts/muse/bootstrap.sh` never mentions any of the three files (grep of main @ 6ceb9067134: no hits). Its phases provision only the BWS token, the optional 1Password token, the fleet binary, and the tailnet.
- On the `muse` seat the files exist only because the **restore phase** brings back the old sandbox's `~/tools` from restic — i.e. by accident of the home backup, not by design.
- The enrollment helper skips `restore,persist,init` for non-`muse` kinds (correctly — a grok seat must not restore the Muse home), which removes the only accidental path and leaves no replacement.

## Observed consequences (grok seat, 2026-11-22)

- `fleet secrets list` → secrets-broker HTTP 502 (the local session broker synthesizes 502 when a request fails; reading the named token file is the first step of its request path). `list` has no fallback — only `get` falls through to `bws`.
- Queue leg: doctor fails, `cannot read token file ~/tools/queue-broker-token`.
- Shell leg: doctor fails, `laptop-agent-token unreadable`.
- Bridge leg knock-on: resolving `message-bridge.fleet-token` (not a BWS name; derived from the owner token when the broker answers) goes through the broken broker leg first, whose retry policy (fleet-secrets: 120 s budget, 10 s per attempt, 502 = retryable `Unavailable`) burns ~120 s per name — two names ≈ 4 minutes — before the `bws` fallback can derive the token. That is the "bridge hello hangs with no timeout" symptom, and why the grok seat's manual `fleet agent enroll` exited 0 (any one intake leg up — GitHub — is enough) while reporting `registered: false` (that field is computed at enroll time from the bridge leg only; it is not stored in `agent.json`), and why no `grok` row exists in the bridge registry (`fleet bridge agents`, verified 2026-11-23).

Also verified: Bitwarden holds **no** copy of the queue-broker or laptop-agent tokens under any name, and the BWS name `secrets-broker.token` does **not** hash-match the secrets-broker client token file — so "fetch them from BWS" is not currently a route either.

## Fix shape (needs an owner decision on the secret-distribution route)

Give the enrollment flow an explicit token-provisioning step for these three files, e.g. one of:

1. Publish the three service tokens to BWS under dedicated names and have the bootstrap token phase fetch them by name (0600) like it does other secrets — requires creating those BWS entries from the laptop's files first.
2. Transfer them over the tailnet from the laptop during enrollment (the laptop-agent port answers, but that leg itself needs the laptop-agent token — a bootstrap-order problem).

Until one lands, a new seat can only be completed by a manual, operator-side copy of the three files from the laptop (paths in the table above) to the seat's `~/tools/`, mode 0600.

## Related

- #12885 — the grok seat's 502 report (diagnosis recorded there)
- #12897 — bootstrap check-phase `--groups muse` hardcode
- #12858 — enrollment helper defects

No secret values are included in this report.

title: bootstrap.sh check phase hardcodes --groups muse on bridge hello for every enrolling kind
body:
## Summary

`scripts/muse/bootstrap.sh`'s check phase hardcodes the `muse` group on its bridge registration probe, whatever agent is actually enrolling:

```bash
# line 718 (main @ 6ceb9067134)
if fleet bridge hello --agent "$AGENT" --groups muse >/dev/null 2>&1; then
```

The header comment (line 33) bakes in the same assumption: "bridge hello as agent \"muse\" (group muse)".

## Why it is wrong

- `bootstrap.sh` is kind-agnostic: `$AGENT` comes from `$FLEET_AGENT` and the enrollment helper runs it for non-`muse` kinds too (e.g. kind `grok`, whose registry groups are `["grok"]` — `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-agent/src/kinds.rs`).
- A successful check-phase hello therefore registers/refreshes the enrolling agent in the **wrong group** (`muse`), or — as on the grok seat, 2026-11-22 — the check fails for unrelated transport reasons and the hardcode is the visible defect in the failing line.
- The bridge's registration semantics make the hardcode unnecessary: `hello` without `--groups` registers a new agent with no groups and, for an existing agent, refreshes `last_seen` **without touching its groups** (`pkgs/message-bridge/worker/src/fleet.js`, `touch()`: groups are only updated when supplied). The follow-on `fleet agent enroll --kind <kind> --name <name>` is the step that owns group assignment (kind registry groups plus `--groups` extras).

## Fix

In the check phase: pass `--groups "$FLEET_AGENT_GROUPS"` only when that variable is set and non-empty; otherwise call `fleet bridge hello --agent "$AGENT"` with no `--groups` at all. Never substitute a literal group the script cannot know is the enrolling agent's own.

## Related

- #12858 — enrollment helper defects (different script: `enroll-agent.py`)
- #12885 — the grok seat's secrets-broker 502 (separate root cause: broker token files are never provisioned for non-`muse` kinds; recorded there)

No secret values are included in this report.

title: ci(org-run): nix unusable inside fleet-build:full legs — missing nixbld group (run 45111805634); prior leg failed on nix-command flag (run 45111518413)
body:
## Failure

Two consecutive `org-run (generic dispatch runner)` legs on main failed back-to-back (~04:23Z and ~04:25Z, 2026-11-23). Newest first — only the newest needs fixing, the older one is the same dispatch retried:

- **Newest: run 45111805634** — https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/45111805634 — job `run (developing-today/code #0)`, step `Run command`: FAILED
- Older: run 45111518413 — https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/45111518413 — same job/step: FAILED (same breakage family, superseded by the retry)

## What was dispatched

Single-shot leg, manual dispatch (blank dispatch\_id), ref `codex/agent-next-05-17082-sidecar-snapshot`, HEAD 998b7097ff7e3715d8dad879643d82b447eb9dcc:

- older: `nix develop ./pkgs/id --command cargo test --manifest-path ./pkgs/id/Cargo.toml -p id-store --test sidecar_snapshot`
- newest: same with `--extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes'` added

So a lane is iterating toward running the id sidecar\_snapshot test via org-run, and the runner environment is blocking it twice in two different ways.

## Errors (verbatim from --log-failed)

Newest (45111805634), after nix finished substituting store paths:

```
warning: the group 'nixbld' specified in 'build-users-group' does not exist
error: the group 'nixbld' specified in 'build-users-group' does not exist
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

Older (45111518413):

```
error: experimental Nix feature 'nix-command' is disabled; add '--extra-experimental-features nix-command' to enable it
##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.
```

## Reading

- The older failure is a caller-side flag omission, already corrected in the retry — not a repo bug.
- The newest failure is environment-side: `ghcr.io/developing-today/fleet-build:full` (run with `--user root`) ships a nix.conf referencing `build-users-group = nixbld`, but that group does not exist in the container, so every `nix develop`/`nix build` leg dies before running anything. Any org-run leg that touches nix is broken until this is fixed — including id test dispatches, which is the fleet's standing priority work.
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/org-run.yml` (container image pin at the `container:` stanza, `Run command` step). Candidates: create the nixbld group + build users in the image (or set `build-users-group =` empty / single-user mode for container legs), or pin nix.conf accordingly. Do NOT paper over it by telling dispatchers to avoid nix.

## Done when

- A manually dispatched org-run leg running `nix develop --extra-experimental-features 'nix-command flakes' ./pkgs/id --command true` (or equivalent trivial nix command) on main goes green.
- The retry of the sidecar\_snapshot dispatch command is unblocked (its own test result is that lane's business; this issue is the runner environment).

## Context

- Filed by the main-CI watch trigger (fresh pass 2026-11-23 ~04:35Z). Watermark advanced past both runs; no live fix existed for this workflow.
- Related, not duplicates: #12235 (fleet-run.yml converge), #12752 (sandbox-seat nixbld ACLs — same symptom family on a different surface; fix here should check whether that surface needs the same treatment).

title: fix(id-config): reject malformed extension namespaces accepted by Rust but forbidden by schema
body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/crates/id-config/src/lib.rs:565-568` validates extension keys with only `contains('.') || contains('/')`. This accepts malformed names such as `"."` (and `"a b/c"`) as namespaced keys.

Reproduced on current `origin/main` (`f2866476f2ad`): a minimal otherwise-valid schema-v1 document with `"extensions":{".":true}` passes `ConfigDocument::parse(...).resolve()` and returns `Ok` retaining the key. The canonical schema `pkgs/id/config/id-config-v1.schema.json` instead requires `^[^./\\s]+([./][^./\\s]+)+$`, which rejects empty segments, whitespace, and separator-only values. The existing `cargo test --manifest-path pkgs/id/Cargo.toml -p id-config` passes, but has no crate unit tests; `pkgs/id/tests/config_invariants.rs` does not exercise malformed extension names, so the Rust/schema drift is currently undetected.

## Why it matters

Consumers using the Rust reference validator can accept and persist extension identifiers that schema-based consumers reject, undermining the crate's stated fail-closed, lockstep contract. A later schema-based read or producer can then reject a configuration already accepted by Rust.

## Acceptance criteria

- Apply the schema's namespace-key rule in the Rust validator (prefer one shared, explicit predicate matching the schema contract).
- Reject separator-only and empty-segment keys (including `"."`, `"/"`, `"a..b"`, and `"a//b"`) and keys containing whitespace (including `"a b/c"`).
- Continue accepting valid dotted/slashed namespaces such as `example.com/experiment`.
- Add regression coverage to the independent config invariant suite so the JSON Schema and Rust validator agree for valid and invalid extension keys.

title: handoff: enroll-agent pins a dead branch, restores the Muse home for every agent kind, hardcodes kind muse
body:
## Defects found by the Grok enrollment (2026-11-22, reported via Drew)

A new non-Muse agent (grok) enrolling through `scripts/muse/handoff/` hit four defects:

1. **Dead branch pin.** `enroll-agent.py` (`RAW_ROOT`), `README.md`, and `PROMPT.md` all point at `codex/muse-agent-enrollment-20261122`, which returns GitHub 404 — the branch does not exist. The helper's pinned bootstrap download cannot work as shipped.
2. **Muse home restore runs for every kind.** `enroll-agent.py` invokes `bootstrap.sh --all` unconditionally, so enrolling any agent runs the `restore` phase — a full restic restore of the Muse home (338 entries, tens of GB) onto a seat that is not a Muse and never needs it. Grok stopped it at 88/338 entries (~48G) with disk pressure. Non-Muse kinds need only tools/token/tailnet/fleet/check.
3. **Kind hardcoded.** The helper enrolls with `--kind muse` regardless of the agent being enrolled; a grok/http seat then needs a manual superseding enroll.
4. **Cloudflare 1010 on the claim.** The handoff claim POST uses the default Python urllib user agent, which Cloudflare blocks (error 1010) before the request reaches the Worker.

Also observed, unresolved at filing time: from the grok seat the secrets broker returned HTTP 502 on `fleet secrets list` and `fleet secrets get` hung, and `~/tools/queue-broker-token` / `~/tools/laptop-agent-token` were absent — but the tailnet phase never ran (enrollment stopped during restore), so these legs get retested after a restore-free resume before any broker-side defect is concluded.

Fix: helper gains `--kind` (default `muse`); non-muse kinds run the bootstrap with `--skip restore,persist,init`; the enroll call uses the requested kind; all raw URLs point at `main`; claim/download requests send an explicit user agent.

title: id-render: Stage 2 assertion half — consume the #5850 vocabulary (the #7918 remainder)
body:
## Problem

`pkgs/id/crates/id-render` implements the rendering pipeline compiler core from decision record #5855 — except Stage 2's assertion half, which was deliberately deferred under #5855 assumption A2 pending #5850. The `assert` slot is still carried opaquely through parse/validate/compose/lowering.

#5850 is now CLOSED, so the deferral's precondition is gone. This is the unblocked remainder of #7918 (whose verification record, 2026-11-22, names this slice).

## Scope

- Consume the assertion vocabulary #5850 settled, as versioned data (the crate's existing pattern: mapping tables are data modules feeding the pipeline, never pipeline branches).
- Parse + validate assertions in the `assert` slot (unknown assertion vocabulary fails validation with suggestions, per the #5849 idiom the crate already uses); compose and lowering treat assertions per #5855/#5854 rather than carrying them opaquely.
- Tests name the decision-record behaviours they verify (the crate's existing test-naming convention).
- While here: fix the stale crate docs in `lib.rs`, which still claim the crate "implements the first stages" and "#5850 is not settled."

## Acceptance

- An assertion-bearing pipeline definition parses, validates, composes, and lowers with its assertions honoured (not carried opaquely), on all three targets (web #5851, native #5852, custom-GUI #5853), with the coverage/conflict report accounting for assertions like any other assertion class.
- `cargo test -p id-render` green on the laptop, including the pre-existing 56 integration tests.
- #7918's done check passes with this landed.

title: opencode-claimant: all live fires abort at cap since primary clone left on xaltha branch (cap_unknown, nothing launches)
body:
## Incident

Every live opencode-claimant fire since ~03:02 UTC 2026-11-23 aborts at the cap step: `cap_room` null, `skips: [{reason: cap_unknown}]`, zero sessions launched, supervision skipped. Queue broker is healthy (queue\_health rows present in the fire log); this is not the backend-outage fallback case.

Fire log (`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/fires.jsonl`):

- `2026-11-23T02:57:23Z` cap\_room 36, 1 candidate (task 20708, #3321), skip sink\_claim\_failed — last good fire
- `2026-11-23T03:02:17Z` cap\_room null, 1 candidate, skip cap\_unknown
- `2026-11-23T03:06:18Z` cap\_room null, 1 candidate, skip cap\_unknown

## Root cause

The primary clone `/home/user/git/code` was checked out from `main` to `xaltha/12751-read-authority` at 2026-11-22 20:55:36 -0600 (reflog), between the last good fire and the first bad one. That branch's `pm-stack/opencode-claimant/poll.py` predates the #12225 paging fix: it escalates `GET /api/session?limit=` over (1000, 10000, 100000). The standing OpenCode server (2.0.30+9acf714, pid 1891329, up since 02:26 UTC) caps `limit` at 200 — `?limit=201` and `?limit=1000` both return HTTP 400 `Expected a value less than or equal to 200` (verified repeatedly; auth fine, default list and `/api/session/active` both OK). So `fetch_sessions()` returns None on the first read and the fire fails closed per the cap rule.

`main` already contains the fix (a9542de91c8, `SESSION_FETCH_LIMIT = 200` with cursor paging); the checked-out branch does not. The fail-closed abort itself is correct behavior — the defect is the primary clone sitting on a stale branch, which silently converts every fire into a no-op.

## Impact

- Task 20708 (#3321 aggregator remainder, handed\_off to the opencode lane) is not launching; repeated `sink_claim_failed` before, now not even attempted.
- Supervision (step 1) does not run while the cap read fails.

## Suggested remediation

1. Confirm nobody owns the `xaltha/12751-read-authority` checkout in the primary clone (tree is clean except untracked `.fleet-session-id`; it looks like a left-behind checkout, not active work — but verify before touching), then restore the primary clone to `main`.
2. Consider making the claimant independent of primary-clone branch state (pin the ref it runs from, or record the checked-out branch/commit in the fire log so the next incident names itself).

## Notes

- Filed by the scheduled opencode-claimant fire, which executed `claimant.py` per its contract and recorded the abort. No branch switch was performed by the filer: branch ownership is unknown and out of the claimant lane.
- Related: #12223 / #12225 (paging fix, on `main` but not on the checked-out branch).

title: Atlas search: vault the per-seat client tokens so seats can self-provision client.json
body:
Follow-up from the #12782 audit (Gap E), split out so #12782 could close on its discoverability scope.

## The gap

The Atlas search service's per-seat client tokens exist only in the laptop's service config (`~/.local/state/atlas-search/service.json`). The vault holds only:

- `atlas.search-worker-gate-token` — the Cloudflare worker's GATE_TOKEN (authenticates worker→gate, not a service client)
- `atlas.search-cf-worker-token` — the cf-worker service client token

The `sandbox-scripts`, `openchamber`, and `fork-server` client tokens are not vaulted anywhere, so a seat cannot self-provision `~/.config/atlas-search/client.json` from the vault after a rebuild/recovery — provisioning today is a manual copy from the laptop's service config (that is how the sandbox seat was provisioned during the #12782 audit, 2026-11-23).

## The ask

Vault each seat client token as `atlas.search-<client>-client-token` (Bitwarden Secrets Manager, per the secrets-by-name convention), so any seat can self-provision during its normal secret sync. Record the provisioning step wherever seat setup is documented.

Client identities (from the service config): drew-cli, openchamber, fork-server, sandbox-scripts, cf-worker (already vaulted).

title: fix(mcpx): install.sh masks a failed GitHub releases fetch as "no mcpx release found"

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/mcpx/scripts/install.sh:115-133` (verified on origin/main 45191b4e2e14910a0365537f22014daa1a60daf0). The script runs under `set -eu` without `pipefail` (line 40) and discovers the latest release via:

```sh
version=$(curl -fsSL "$releases_url" | awk '...') || die "could not ask GitHub for the latest mcpx release"
[ -n "$version" ] || die "no mcpx release found; set MCPX_VERSION ..."
```

Without pipefail, the pipeline's exit status is awk's; on a curl failure (network, DNS, 403/429 rate-limit) awk reads empty input and exits 0, so the `|| die "could not ask GitHub..."` branch is dead code. **Reproduced:**

```bash
MCPX_RELEASES_URL=file:///nonexistent/releases sh pkgs/mcpx/scripts/install.sh --user
# observed:
#   curl: (37) Could not open file /nonexistent/releases
#   mcpx installer: no mcpx release found; set MCPX_VERSION to a version that exists ...
#   exit=1
```

Expected: "could not ask GitHub for the latest mcpx release" (the intended fetch-failure diagnostic). Actual: the misleading "no mcpx release found", steering the user toward remediation (pick a version that exists) that cannot help.

## Why it matters

During a GitHub API outage or rate-limit window every user gets a wrong diagnosis from the supported install path. The fix is small: check curl's status separately (command substitution without the pipe, or `set -o pipefail`, or fetch to a variable/file first and die on curl's own failure).

## Acceptance criteria

- A failed releases fetch produces the "could not ask GitHub" failure (curl's own error), not "no mcpx release found".
- A successful fetch with no matching release still produces "no mcpx release found".
- Verified under `/bin/sh` (the script's shebang), not only bash.

## Dedupe

No open or closed issue/PR matches (searched mcpx install/pipfail/curl titles; #12428/#12482 are unrelated mcpx issues).

title: fix(fleet): restore-row-count-diff.sh missing option value crashes with an unbound-variable error instead of a usage error

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/low
labels.description: Nice to have; do when convenient

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`scripts/fleet/restore-row-count-diff.sh:41-56` (verified on origin/main 45191b4e2e14910a0365537f22014daa1a60daf0). The script runs under `set -euo pipefail` (line 32) and parses options as:

```bash
--manifest) manifest="$2"; shift 2 ;;
```

with no `$# -ge 2` guard. **Reproduced:**

```bash
bash scripts/fleet/restore-row-count-diff.sh --manifest
# observed: line 44: $2: unbound variable ; exit=1
```

Also, `--manifest --live /path` silently consumes `--live` as the manifest value and then reports "unknown argument: /path" — a flag accepted as a filename is a misparse the operator cannot see from the error.

## Why it matters

The operator-script argument contract (`doc/agents/operator-script-argument-contract.md`, #3352) requires the whole command line to be declared and strictly parsed before any work, with unaccounted input as a clean usage error at the script's established usage exit code. This script already uses exit 2 for its other usage errors (`unknown argument`, missing inputs, usage) — this case escapes as a raw bash error with exit 1, so automation cannot distinguish a usage mistake from a runtime failure, and the operator sees a shell internals message instead of usage.

## Acceptance criteria

- `--manifest` (or `--live`/`--inventory`) with no value prints the usage message and exits 2.
- An option value that begins with `--` is rejected as a usage error, not consumed as the value.

## Dedupe

No open or closed issue/PR matches; sibling operator scripts that follow the strict pattern were checked for comparison.

title: fix(fleet): restore-row-count-diff.sh fails open when the inventory file is unreadable — the gate can PASS with its coverage check skipped

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

`scripts/fleet/restore-row-count-diff.sh:141-149` (verified on origin/main 45191b4e2e14910a0365537f22014daa1a60daf0). The post-restore safety gate reads the source inventory in an awk END block:

```awk
while ((getline line < inventory) > 0) {
  if (line == "") continue
  if (!(line in in_manifest)) {
    fail(line ": in source inventory but MISSING from the manifest — silence is not a disposition")
  }
}
```

awk `getline < file` returns `-1` on a read error (e.g. permissions), and the `> 0` loop condition treats that as end-of-input. The existence check earlier (`[ -f "$inventory" ]`) checks existence, not readability. So an unreadable inventory silently skips the entire coverage check and the gate passes.

**Reproduced** (exit 0, `bar` never reported missing):

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp -d)
printf 'table\tlive_count\nfoo\t1\n' > "$tmp/live.tsv"
printf 'table\tsource_count\tdisposition\tallowed_delta\tnote\nfoo\t1\tload\t0\t\n' > "$tmp/manifest.tsv"
printf 'foo\nbar\n' > "$tmp/inv.txt"   # bar is in inventory, absent from manifest
chmod 000 "$tmp/inv.txt"
bash scripts/fleet/restore-row-count-diff.sh --manifest "$tmp/manifest.tsv" --live "$tmp/live.tsv" --inventory "$tmp/inv.txt"
# observed: INFO foo: live 1 == source 1  /  GATE PASSED: 0 failure(s)  /  exit=0
```

Expected: the gate fails because `bar` is in the source inventory but missing from the manifest — the script's own stated invariant is "silence is not a disposition" (line 146), yet an unreadable inventory produces exactly that silence.

## Why it matters

This is the post-restore acceptance gate for a selective restore. The same file already closes a fail-open hole for an empty live export (PR #8406, the `[ -s "$live" ]` guard with the comment "a failed export would otherwise be indistinguishable from a pass"); an unreadable inventory is the same class of hole on the coverage side — an incomplete restore can be accepted because the check that would have caught it never ran.

## Suggested fix shape

Fail closed: before the comparison, verify the inventory is readable (e.g. `[ -r "$inventory" ]` alongside `[ -f ... ]`), and/or check `getline`'s return for `-1` in the awk loop and `fail("inventory ... unreadable")` on it. Either way, an inventory that cannot be read must be a gate failure, not a skip.

## Acceptance criteria

- The repro above (inventory with `bar` missing from manifest, chmod 000) makes the gate FAIL.
- A readable, complete inventory behaves exactly as today.
- A usage/invocation error is reported as a failure, not a pass.

## Dedupe

No open or closed issue/PR matches (searched "restore-row-count-diff", "inventory", gate fail-open; #8406 is a past PR review, not a filed defect).

title: Atlas search discoverability: sandbox routing stale since #5343, --help shadowed, docs/skill silent
body:
## Atlas search is built but undiscoverable: help, docs, and sandbox-seat routing gaps

Audit 2026-11-22 (Lane BS, on Drew's order: atlas fully available as a fleet search subcommand, documented, known to all agents/sessions). The capability itself is real and verified live from both seats today — what is missing is discoverability and one stale transport assumption.

### What exists (verified)
- `fleet search` domain (pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-search, step 5 of #5433): `search` + `get-chunk`, flag surface mirroring atlas-search, server-side ceiling enforcement, named client identities (drew-cli / openchamber / fork-server / sandbox-scripts / cf-worker).
- The Atlas service is live on the laptop (127.0.0.1:18760, health ok); the Cloudflare worker surface (pkgs/atlas-search/worker) pins context `hosted-per-user`, ceiling `personal`.
- Parity proof: the same query returns identical chunk ids/scores from the laptop (standalone) and from the Muse sandbox seat (via-service).

### Gaps
1. **Sandbox via-service routing is broken on post-#5343 seats (code).** `fleet-search`'s `ensure_sandbox_forward` bootstraps the SSH control master via `~/tools/laptop-ssh.sh` — retired as an SSH transport 2026-11-04 (#5343); it is now the laptop-agent redirect and creates no master, so the `-O forward` step silently no-ops and the sandbox seat falls back to standalone. The real SSH wrapper is `~/tools/laptop-ssh-real.sh` (option-for-option identical ssh flags). Verified by hand: bootstrap via the real wrapper + forward + `fleet search` returns live results from the sandbox seat.
2. **`fleet search --help` answers with the thin registry help (code).** The client's full usage (SEARCH_USAGE) is only reachable via `fleet search search --help` or a bare invocation. The serve roles got carve-outs for exactly this (#6400, #6770); the search client did not. `fleet search get-chunk --help` is worse: it delegates `--help` to the standalone artifact as if it were a chunk argument.
3. **verbs.md §search is a 3-row table (docs).** No routing defaults, no provisioning, no ceilings/identities, no examples, no exit codes. It is the canonical fleet doc the fleet-operations skill points sessions at.
4. **No agent-facing surface names the command (broadcast).** `.agents/skills/fleet-operations/SKILL.md` never mentions search/atlas; the fleet-agent hand-out does not either. Sessions cannot use a tool they are never told about.
5. **Seat provisioning has no vault home (ops).** A sandbox seat needs `~/.config/atlas-search/client.json` with the `sandbox-scripts` client token — but no BWS secret holds that token (only the worker gate token and the cf-worker service token are vaulted: `atlas.search-worker-gate-token`, `atlas.search-cf-worker-token`). Today the token can only be copied out of the laptop's service config. Recommendation: vault the per-client service tokens under `atlas.search-<client>-client-token` names via the laptop route so seats can self-provision with `fleet secrets get`.

### Fix in flight (this issue's lane)
- fleet-search: bootstrap via `laptop-ssh-real.sh` when present (fallback to the historical name); `get-chunk --help` answered in-process with its own usage; SEARCH_USAGE gains get-chunk, provisioning, and examples.
- fleet bin: `fleet search --help` carve-out printing the client usage (the #6400/#6770 pattern).
- verbs.md §search expanded to the canonical doc; fleet-operations skill gains a short atlas-search section pointing at it.

title: fleet queue: no unblock/release verb — blocked tasks cannot be released or dep-corrected from any seat
body:
## fleet queue has no unblock/release verb — blocked tasks cannot be released from any seat

Found 2026-11-22 during the blocked-queue sweep ordered by Drew (487 blocked tasks examined across queues; record on #12280, batch comments 7090007019 / 7090007941 / 7090011449).

The queue verb set (validate, list, enqueue, claim, lane, bind, heartbeat, checkpoint, park, block, cancel, fail, complete, health, signal, fallback, verify-disposition) contains **no way to return a blocked task to claimable**, and no way to edit a blocked task's dependency record:

- `fleet queue claim --task 3809` on a blocked task → "no claimable task"
- `fleet queue block 3809` on an already-blocked task → refused: "task 3809 is not claimed by archer: it is blocked"

Consequences, all observed in the sweep:
- **5 tasks are verifiably ready** (every referenced blocker closed/merged) but cannot be released: 20094→#8220, 19782→#2339, 20060→#8037, 20678→#10706, 4995→#1241, plus 3809 (#2154) nearest-ready in its cycle group. They wait on the shepherd flow alone.
- **Bogus dep entries cannot be corrected**: e.g. task 20408 (#9509) carries a self-loop dep entry alongside real, still-open deps (#9513/#9502/#9508); the self entry is data noise no seat can remove.
- The only release valve available to a worker is `cancel`, which destroys the task even when its work is still needed.

Ask: an `unblock` (or `release`) verb for blocked tasks — worker-scoped like block/cancel, requiring a reason, ideally with an evidence/disposition check in the same shape as fix-class completion — plus a way to drop a single dep entry from a blocked task's record with the reason recorded.


Related: #9178 §2 — the unblock/release/unpark verbs asked for here are the missing half of #9178's manual-claim contract for parked / attempt-capped tasks (claim-by-ID itself already exists). Triage routing recorded on #9178 (comment 7091328709) and in the cross-link comment on this issue (7091378703).

body:
The PM console on this host (amd) has stopped taking merges. Find out why, fix it, and say what it was.

Evidence, from outside: https://pm-console-edge.developing-today.workers.dev/console/health shows hostVersion 6226e4d93599, which is main as of 2026-11-23T00:20Z. Main has had five merges that touch pm-stack/console since 02:04Z (55f0bdd8605a, 2bec21c17fae, ce26128d5cb1, 45191b4e2e14 and whatever follows). hostSeen in the same answer is fresh, so pm-console.service is up and reporting, on old code. Before 00:20Z each console merge was in service within about four minutes.

The chain is: pm-git-sync (every 30 s) keeps ~/git/code at origin/main; pm-console-redeploy.timer (every minute) runs pm-stack/console/redeploy.sh, which compares the checkout's pm-stack/console tree with ~/.local/state/pm-console/deployed, self-checks the new code, and runs install.sh, which restarts pm-console.service.

Find which link is broken:
1. Is ~/git/code at origin/main? `git -C ~/git/code status -sb`, `git -C ~/git/code log --oneline -3`, `systemctl --user status pm-git-sync.service pm-git-sync.timer`, `journalctl --user -u pm-git-sync.service -n 40`. A local commit that is not on origin (a rebuild commit that changed flake.lock is the known case, #12520), or uncommitted changes, stops the pull.
2. Is the redeploy failing or standing aside? `journalctl --user -u pm-console-redeploy.service -n 40`, `~/.local/state/pm-console/redeploy.log`, and the files `deployed` and `deploy-failed` beside it. redeploy.sh exits quietly, changing nothing, while anything under pm-stack/console in the checkout differs from HEAD (`git -C ~/git/code diff --stat HEAD -- pm-stack/console pm-stack/systemd`).

title: id-store: validate block-tree invariants when decoding content bytes
body:
## Evidence

`pkgs/id/crates/id-store/src/note_blocks.rs:282-283` implements `BlockTree::from_bytes` as `postcard::from_bytes` only. The module defines mandatory invariants in `BlockTree::check` (unique IDs, valid/nonempty NFC IDs, NFC and size-bounded text, heading levels 1..=6, and maximum nesting depth), but the decoder returns a `BlockTree` without enforcing them. `BlockTree` and its fields are public, so serialized bytes can encode trees that the module itself considers invalid; downstream code can then treat malformed content as a valid note block tree unless every caller remembers a separate check.

A focused regression test was added temporarily in the scratch worktree to serialize a tree with an empty repeated ID, invalid heading level, and oversized text, then decode it successfully; the decoded value fails `check()`. This reproduces the invariant bypass directly.

## Why it matters

The content blob is the persistence boundary for note revisions. A decoder that silently accepts invalid schema values makes correctness depend on every future reader remembering a second validation call, and allows invalid IDs/depth/text into anchor and projection code.

## Acceptance criteria

- `BlockTree::from_bytes` rejects decoded trees that fail `BlockTree::check` (or expose a clearly named unchecked decoder and make the normal decoder validated).
- Regression tests cover duplicate IDs, invalid IDs/text, invalid heading level, and excessive depth at decode time.
- Existing valid-tree round-trip remains covered.
- Any decode resource bounds needed to prevent pathological payload sizes/depth are stated and tested.

title: fleet-queue: producers never write payload.labels — #7030's label-band selection (PR #12464) is inert at enqueue

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

body:
## Problem

PR #12464 (slice 1 of #7030, merged 2026-11-22) made `task_from_packet` in `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/validate.rs` derive the stored row priority from `payload.labels`: `expedite` ⇒ 15, `next-up` ⇒ 25 (Drewry's ratified bands). The selection only fires when the packet's payload carries a `labels` array.

Verified 2026-11-23 during the #7030 live re-band: **no producer writes `payload.labels`**. Of the 70 tasks created in the fleet-queue store after PR #12464 merged, 0 carry a `labels` array. Both live tasks for the one open `expedite` issue (#12228 — triage task 21084, fix task 21092) were enqueued post-merge at their stated priority 30 with no labels present, so the band reached the store only via the manual guarded re-band recorded on #7030.

## What's needed

Packet producers (the triage-step job's enqueue path and any lane/helper that authors repo-task/v1 packets for an issue) must copy the issue's GitHub labels into `payload.labels` at enqueue time, so the ratified bands apply at the single source of truth instead of by periodic manual correction.

Alternative worth weighing in the fix: the broker already mirrors issue data in the same store (`github_mirror_issues`); enqueue-time enrichment from the mirror would put the labels on every packet regardless of producer discipline. Either way, acceptance is a readback: enqueue a task for an `expedite`-labeled issue through the normal producer path and show the stored row at priority 15 with no manual update.

Refs: #7030 (re-band record), PR #12464, the 2026-11-07 precedent comments on #7030 (6715618437 / 6715652659) for the guarded-update pattern this makes unnecessary.

labels.name: queue/queued

body:
## Problem

The babysitter's pool-state feed (#12689, merged 2026-11-22T22:10Z for #1338) is not live in production. Babysitter rounds run inside every claimant fire on the laptop and record `pool_state: "unread"` (verified rounds 16–19, 2026-11-22T23:40–23:50Z): `pool-state.json` does not exist in the claimant state dir (`~/.local/state/opencode-claimant/`) or anywhere else on the laptop.

Root cause (verified 2026-11-22 during the OpenChamber lane-scheduler audit, recorded on #2019): the laptop's quota gatherer is the Nix-store binary `pm-aggregator-0.1.0` (`quota-gatherer.service` ExecStart points into /nix/store), which predates #12689, and the unit's Environment carries no `POOL_STATE_PATH`. So the merged writer code never runs on the tick, and the babysitter's wall input stays absent: rounds verdict sessions with `pool_walled: false` by default rather than from a fresh quota projection. A walled pool would not be seen as walled by the babysitter until this is deployed.

## Fix shape

1. Redeploy the laptop aggregator from a build that includes #12689 (commit 690bbc7e999).
2. Set `POOL_STATE_PATH` in the quota-gatherer unit's environment to the claimant state dir's `pool-state.json` (or confirm the code's default lands there).
3. Verify: after one gather tick, `pool-state.json` exists and is fresh; the next babysitter round records a read pool_state (not "unread"); a stale file surfaces as state with no wall, per #12689's contract.

## Boundary

This is a deployment step, not a code change: the writer (#12689) and reader (babysitter.py `read_pool_state`) are both merged and contract-tested. Filed from the #2019 scheduler audit per Drewry's 2026-11-22 order to keep lanes constantly running via OpenChamber scheduled tasks — every other lane need audited healthy; this feed is the one production gap.

title: Fleet build fails: microsoft/onnxruntime source returns 404 (repo made private)
body:
Main's fleet build has failed since Nov 18 because the onnxruntime 1.31.1
source fetch returns 404 from `microsoft/onnxruntime`.

Verified live 2026-11-21 and re-verified 2026-11-22 ~17:53 CST:
- `https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime` → 404
- `https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/archive/refs/tags/v1.31.1.tar.gz` → 404

Cause: Microsoft made some repos private on Nov 20 while investigating
malicious content (tied to the agent-framework PyPI hijack). No return
timeline known.

Scope: only source fetches break. PyPI, NuGet and npm distributions of
onnxruntime are unaffected.

The fetch is pinned in `pkgs/atlas-search/onnxruntime/default.nix`:
`fetchFromGitHub { owner = "microsoft"; repo = "onnxruntime"; tag = "v1.31.1"; fetchSubmodules = true; hash = "sha256-wATnI1v3De6+41fGYWS2458TCUWhBECNw2kBnfajKEo="; }`.

Impact: a build on any host whose Nix store does not already hold the
onnxruntime 1.31.1 source (with submodules) fails at fetch time.

Direction (Drewry, 2026-11-22): do not wait for Microsoft. Find the
vendored/cached copy believed to exist in our estate (laptop Nix store,
sandbox store, Actions caches, R2/restic backups, repo mirrors) and
cache/vendor the source so the build resolves independently of the dead
upstream — verified against the pinned hash above, never an unverified
mirror.

## Problem

On current main, the id-worlds lib test `shell_contract::tests::the_contracts_required_fields_are_exactly_what_the_host_requires` fails:

assertion `left == right` failed: join.device_input: the contract and the host disagree about null

 right: false

at `crates/id-worlds/src/shell_contract/tests.rs:316`.

title: pm-dispatch validate.test.ts: 'fixture cleanup' test deletes its fixture and asserts nothing

labels.name: kind/test
labels.description: Test coverage, test infrastructure, or test-only fixes

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

labels.name: app/pm-stack
labels.description: pm-stack (Pad/Grist) in developing-today/code

body:
## Finding

In `pm-stack/dispatch/test/validate.test.ts`, the fixture directory is removed inside a test that asserts nothing.

- `:438` creates `base` with `mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "dispatch-3999-"))` inside `describe("session directory symlink confinement (issue #3999)")` (`:429`).
- `:516-518`:

  ```ts
  test("fixture cleanup", () => {
    rmSync(base, { recursive: true, force: true });
    expect(true).toBe(true);
  });
  ```

- The file has no `afterAll` or `afterEach` (`grep -n afterAll` returns nothing).

## Why it matters

- Order-dependent: the temp directory is removed only when this test runs. A filtered run (`bun test -t <name>`), a shard, or a `-bail` stop skips it and leaks a `dispatch-3999-*` directory in tmpdir.
- No signal: `expect(true).toBe(true)` always passes, so the test reports a pass even if the removal failed.
- Low severity, but it is the kind of test-quality drift the testing doctrine (`doc/agents/testing-doctrine.md`) asks us to avoid.

## Suggested fix shape

Move the `rmSync` into an `afterAll` in that describe block and delete the `fixture cleanup` test. If the teardown must be checked, assert `existsSync(base) === false` in `afterAll` or in a dedicated test.

title: identity: pkgs/identity/default-deploy.sh pipes an unpinned remote script into bash and nothing uses it

labels.name: kind/security
labels.description: Security issue or security hardening

labels.name: app/identity
labels.description: Package/app: identity (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/xs
labels.description: Trivial: expected under 30 minutes of work

body:
## Finding

`pkgs/identity/default-deploy.sh:3` is `curl -L default.computer | bash -s -- "$@"`. It pipes an unpinned remote script straight into bash, with no checksum and no HTTPS-only restriction. The script is not referenced anywhere in the repo: `git grep -n "default-deploy"` matches only the file itself.

Context checked:
- `pkgs/identity/deploy.sh` and `init.template.sh` do not call it.
- `pkgs/identity/README.md` does not mention it.
- The only `curl | sh` installers the repo documents are separate, and they are upstream-provided.

## Why it matters

- Security: anyone who controls `default.computer` (DNS, redirect with `-L`, or a compromised host) gets code execution on any machine that runs this file. Nothing in the repo uses it, so it adds risk with no benefit.
- Cleanup: an orphaned deploy script in a package directory misleads readers about how identity is deployed.

## Suggested fix shape

Delete `pkgs/identity/default-deploy.sh`, since nothing references it. If a caller is found, replace the pipe with download, pin to a version and SHA-256, and run with `curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -fsSL`.

title: fix(id): make http.fetch allowlist port semantics explicit and enforceable

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Problem

The `http.fetch` admin allowlist is described as matching the normalized host exactly, but URL ports are discarded during validation. As a result, listing `example.com` admits requests to `https://example.com:8443/` (and other non-default ports); redirect hops use the same host-only check. This may expose services on a host that the administrator intended to approve only for ordinary HTTP(S) traffic.

## Evidence

On `origin/main` `94f49ac7e0945e610c6b84dd155e491ae932ccce`:

- `pkgs/id/crates/id-caps/src/world_caps.rs:1405-1424` parses the URL and returns only its normalized host; the port is not retained.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/core/operations.rs:289-296` compares only that host with `http_fetch_hosts`.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/http_fetch.rs:119-126` applies the same host-only check to redirect destinations.
- `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world/tests.rs:11025-11068` tests host, scheme, credentials, and subdomains, but not ports. The design note `doc/2026-11-22_design_id1062-http-fetch-provider.md:55-62` specifies exact normalized-host matching without stating port behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

- Define the allowlist contract for ports: either host entries intentionally allow every port (document that explicitly and pin it with a test), or allowlist entries can constrain ports.
- If ports can be constrained, reject a request to an unlisted port before connecting and reject redirect hops that leave the permitted host/port set with the existing `host_not_allowed` refusal.
- Add tests for direct requests and redirects, including a control for the documented permitted case.

No change is requested to host normalization, exact-host matching, or the existing default-off capability gate.

Today's typed presentation has exactly one variant, `WorldSurface::Screen`; richer semantics cannot be claimed by a shell that only implements the screen/text view — they need a separately designed, versioned, host-validated presentation extension first (design of record: `doc/2026-11-01_design_id788.md` §7 steps 3–4, §6 conditional criteria).

## Scope — two steps, in order, separate PRs

1. **Portable rich-presentation contract.** Design and validate the minimal typed scene/audio/widget payloads in the existing optional `surface` slot of the server `view` (or propose a separately versioned alternative if that slot cannot express them). Update host validation, the machine-readable contract (`pkgs/id/contract/shell-contract.v1.json`), and conformance/fallback tests in its own PR. Any new frame kind waits for the F11.12 gate — prefer the `surface` slot, which needs none.
2. **Bevy rich-surface renderers.** Add renderers and a deterministic example world for only the payloads accepted in step 1, in `pkgs/id/crates/id-native-shell`; world input stays on the same contract frames.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The selected surface schema has explicit versions, bounds, safe fallback behavior, contract/conformance coverage, and host-side validation before the Bevy renderer consumes it
- [ ] Old shells still render `view.data` unchanged; malformed or oversized rich surfaces are refused by host validation
- [ ] A real session demonstrates each selected surface in the native shell, its transcript passes `id world contract --check`, and an older shell's text fallback remains usable
- [ ] No WIT/component-model dependency: per the #788 decision record, WIT (F12.8/#1065) governs the guest ABI only and does not change the shell contract

## Prerequisites

- #788 (F13.6) — closed complete 2026-11-22; its Bevy reference shell and the F13.1 conformance seam are the foundation here
- F11.12 journal/frame gating, only if a new frame kind is proposed

## Size

XL (two sequenced steps; step 1 is the design-bearing one)

title: id: browser reconnect resume retains its baseline; host restores viewport from the retained baseline
body:
## Problem

Browser reconnect resume is degraded end to end, on v1 today and independent of the binary transport (#12242):

1. **Browser discards its baseline but keeps the token.** `web/src/world.ts` `connect()` clears `renderedSurface`/`renderedViewRevision` while retaining the resume token (Codex P2 finding on PR #12246, world.ts:648). If the host answers the reconnect with a catch-up patch, the browser has no base to apply it to and falls back to a full view — the patch round-trip is wasted.
2. **The host does not restore the viewport on resume.** `joined()` initializes every connection's `viewport` to `None`; neither the join frame nor the resume-token lookup restores it (Codex P2 finding on PR #12246, world.ts:665). The first resumed view renders at the program's default size, so a retained baseline recorded at the browser's real viewport does not match, and views stay default-sized until the pane changes size.

## Prior work

PR #12246 (superseded by the #12242 lane-T2 implementation for the transport itself) implemented both halves: the browser retains the matching screen/revision with the token and sends the token on reconnect, and the host restores the participant-bound viewport from the retained baseline before rendering the first resumed view (its head commit 3751be8). That head's regression test — reconnect at a non-default viewport, apply a catch-up patch — was never run (no CI on the head, per the PR body), so the fix needs verification, not just porting.

## Scope

- Browser: retain token + surface + revision as one unit across reconnects; send the token on rejoin; drop all three together when the viewport actually changes.
- Host: when a join presents a resume token whose retained baseline matches, restore the session viewport from the baseline before the first `send_view`.
- No token semantics change: a token stays a cursor, not a credential; misses still get a full view; join authorization unchanged.
- Coverage: the non-default-viewport reconnect regression (from #12246) run and green, plus a browser-side test that a catch-up patch applies after reconnect without an intervening resize.

Filed from lane T2's reconciliation of PR #12246 into the #12242 slice; the transport slice deliberately did not absorb this because it changes resume behavior beyond negotiation and its only test was never executed.

title: fix(id-sync): do not hold replica lock while waiting on peer transfer

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/triage
labels.description: Queue packet kind: verify, reproduce, and route this item

labels.name: source/creator
labels.description: Filed by the new-issue-creator job

labels.name: priority/normal
labels.description: Ordinary priority (the default)

labels.name: app/id
labels.description: Package/app: id (pkgs/ or apps/ in this repo)

labels.name: effort/s
labels.description: Small: expected under 2 hours of work

body:
## Evidence

In `pkgs/id/crates/id-sync/src/federation/exchange_net.rs`, `ExchangeProtocol::session` acquires `self.replica.lock()` at line 700, writes the hello reply at 711, then waits for the remote transfer frame at lines 713–717. The same mutex guard remains live while receiving and processing the transfer and sending the reply (through line 744). The only bound on this wait is the 30-second `TIMEOUT` around the session in `accept` (lines 751–754).

A remote peer can complete a valid hello exchange and then stop sending. During that interval, the replica-wide mutex is held, so other sessions for the same `ExchangeProtocol` cannot read/update the replica and may themselves time out waiting for the lock. This turns one stalled stream into up to 30 seconds of avoidable federation unavailability.

## Why it matters

The timeout prevents indefinite lock retention, but serializing unrelated sessions behind a peer-controlled network wait makes a single slow or malicious peer able to delay legitimate synchronization.

## Acceptance criteria

- Do not hold the replica mutex across a peer-controlled read/write wait.
- Preserve the exchange invariant that both offers are computed from pre-transfer inventories and that received versions are admitted in the defined order.
- Add a regression test with one session stalled after hello and another healthy session, demonstrating that the healthy session can make progress (or is rejected promptly by a documented bounded-concurrency policy rather than waiting on the replica lock).
- Keep the per-session timeout and ensure timed-out streams release resources.

title: atlas(search): full-content payloads can carry sibling-chunk text above the served chunk's classification

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: queue/queued
labels.description: Has a queued queue task

labels.name: epic/atlas-program
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
Found during #12404 (disclosure-context enforcement at Atlas output boundaries); the strict case is handled there, this is the residual.

## What #12404 does

`--with-message` and hydration attach the FULL parent-message text to a served chunk. #12404 gates those payloads on the served chunk's own classification and withholds them entirely on `public-surface` (full-message text cannot be filtered at chunk granularity there).

## Residual

Under `fleet-internal`, `hosted-per-user`, and `local-owner`, the payload is the whole message — which spans every chunk of that message. Chunk classification is per-chunk (classification records compose per embed), so a message can mix classifications: a served `personal` chunk's message payload can carry text belonging to a `secret-bearing` sibling chunk, or to an `excluded_personal_life` sibling, across the boundary the served chunk itself passed.

Whether real corpus messages actually mix classifications is an empirical question the fix should answer first (measure: how many messages have chunks whose effective classifications differ, and by how much).

## Acceptance

- Measurement recorded on this issue: prevalence of mixed-classification messages in the corpus.
- A leak test with a mixed-classification message: the payload attached to the lower-classified chunk either contains only spans whose chunks pass the caller's grant ∩ context intersection (span-level filtering), or is withheld when any sibling chunk fails the intersection (whole-payload withholding) — the chosen rule implemented and documented in `crates/atlas-core/src/search.rs`.
- `excluded_personal_life` sibling text never crosses under any context, including `local-owner`.
- Existing atlas-core / atlas-search suites stay green.

Coordination: #12404 owns the boundary; #12408 owns the per-embed classification records the span rule would consume.

title: atlas(python): disclosure-context enforcement parity for the legacy atlas_search.py

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: New feature or capability request

labels.name: epic/atlas-program
labels.description: Reprioritization program epic (2026-11-12)

body:
Follow-up to #12404 (disclosure-context enforcement at Atlas output boundaries), deferred there with this issue as the record.

## Gap

`pkgs/atlas-search/atlas_search.py` is the legacy Python CLI the Rust port mirrors. It predates the #9096 classification model and has no disclosure-context concept:

- It applies only the caller's `--max-sensitivity` ceiling; nothing intersects a destination context.
- It does not know the `excluded_personal_life` disposition: a chunk carrying that label is served like any other content at a sufficient ceiling (the Rust boundary withheld it even before #12404's slice only in the service's chunk path; the Python serves it everywhere).
- Neighbor expansion and full-message payloads are never classification-checked.

Until the Python is retired, any output produced through it bypasses the boundary enforcement #12404 landed for the Rust paths.

## Acceptance

Either:

- The Python gains the same context semantics as the Rust boundary: a `--context` flag with the design §4 table (default `local-owner` for this local tool, matching the Rust `get-chunk` default), context ∩ ceiling applied at render for results, neighbors, and message payloads, `excluded_personal_life` never served, unknown/missing labels fail-closed — with tests mirroring `crates/atlas-core/tests/disclosure.rs`; or
- The Python is retired/deleted with the retirement recorded here and any remaining callers pointed at the Rust CLI.

Coordination: #12404 owns the context model; the Rust implementation is the reference semantics.

body:
Follow-up to #12404 (disclosure-context enforcement at Atlas output boundaries), deferred there with this issue as the record.

## Gap

The Cloudflare Worker in `pkgs/atlas-search/worker/` is the hosted search surface (#9092). It pins `CEILING = "personal"` (`worker/src/space.ts`), verifies `effective_ceiling` before caching, and keys its Durable Object result cache by ceiling (`worker/src/key.ts`, `cache_do.ts`) — but it carries no disclosure-context concept:

- Requests to the search service do not state a context. The wire field now exists (`SearchRequest.context`, atlas-proto, added by the #12404 slice) and the service resolves an unstated context to its fleet-internal default — the wrong default for a hosted per-user surface if the service default ever changes.
- The result cache key includes the ceiling but not the context. Today the surface serves exactly one context, so no cross-context serving is possible yet; the moment the surface fronts a second destination (or a caller states one), a payload filtered for one destination could be served to another from cache.

Per the #9096 design (§4, §10), this surface is the `hosted-per-user` context (ceiling `personal` — the current pin equals it, so stating it changes no behavior today).

## Acceptance

- The Worker states `context: "hosted-per-user"` on search requests it forwards.
- The Durable Object result-cache key includes the resolved context, alongside the ceiling.
- A request that states a different context (if the surface ever accepts one) can never be served a payload cached under another context; test proves the separation.
- Existing worker tests stay green.

Coordination: #9092 owns the hosted search surface; #12404 owns the context model and the service-side enforcement this builds on.

title: fleet: queue complete cannot close tasks claimed via fleet agent next (claim worker identity mismatch)
body:
Observed twice on 2026-11-22 (archer, sandbox):

1. `fleet agent next` claims a queue task (the claim subprocess runs as `fleet queue claim --worker archer --lane archer`; the task is returned with rung=queue).
2. The work is done and recorded on the GitHub issue.
3. `fleet queue complete <id> --worker archer` then fails: `complete_task: task <id> is not claimed by archer` (exit 5, GitHub fallback offered).

Instances: queue tasks 19479 (openchamber#81, PRs merged) and 18787 (code#8968, PR #12617 merged, issue closed). Both times the GitHub-side record is complete, so the practical harm today is bookkeeping: the queue store keeps the tasks as claimed/open until lease expiry instead of completed.

Worth pinning down: which worker identity the agent-next claim actually binds (a session/bridge identity rather than the agent name?), and whether `complete` should resolve the claimer the same way `next` does. If the claim binds a different identity by design, `fleet agent next` should say what it is, so the worker who did the work can close the task.

title: id: http_fetch schedule tests panic in the nix build sandbox — reqwest finds no system CA certificates
body:
## Finding (from #1372 verification, 2026-11-22)

The `id` package's lib test suite fails inside the nix build sandbox: 3 tests panic because a default reqwest client cannot load system CA certificates that do not exist in the sandbox. This fails the `id` derivation's checkPhase, which cascades to every check whose closure includes that build — including `nixos-test-driver-id-serve` / `vm-test-run-id-serve` and, by the same shape, the other NixOS VM checks — so the `id e2e nightly` cannot reach the VM tests even when everything else is green.

**Failing tests** (all in `crates/id-worlds/src/world/tests.rs`, schedule_tests):
- `world::tests::schedule_tests::http_fetch_refuses_redirects_off_the_list_and_past_the_hop_cap`
- `world::tests::schedule_tests::http_fetch_round_trip_through_the_actor`
- `world::tests::schedule_tests::http_fetches_journal_nothing_and_replay_is_unaffected`

**Panic (identical for all three):**
```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at /build/cargo-vendor-dir/reqwest-0.13.5/src/blocking/client.rs:1278:38:
Client::new(): reqwest::Error { kind: Builder, source: General("No CA certificates were loaded from the system") }
```
Suite result: `test result: FAILED. 1092 passed; 3 failed; 3 ignored` → builder exit code 101 → `error: Cannot build '...-nixos-test-driver-id-serve.drv'. Reason: 1 dependency failed.`

**Evidence:** `id e2e nightly` run [45035241965](https://github.com/developing-today/code/actions/runs/45035241965) (targeted `only_checks=nixos-serve` dispatch from PR #12582's branch, tree = current main + workflow-only changes), job log lines at 2026-11-22T15:35:53Z (failures) and 15:36:03Z (cascade). The same tests pass outside the sandbox, where system CA certificates exist — consistent with earlier green local `cargo check`/test runs and with the nightly dying pre-VM.

## Acceptance criteria
- The three `http_fetch_*` tests pass inside the nix build sandbox (e.g. the test client is built without depending on system CA roots — webpki roots / a test-local client config — or the check environment provides a cert bundle), without weakening what they assert about redirect/allowlist behavior.
- `nix build ./pkgs/id#checks.x86_64-linux.nixos-serve` reaches and runs the VM test instead of failing in the `id` dependency build.

Blocks #1372's close condition (a completed full-nightly verdict on `nixos-integration`) and #1374's equivalent readiness evidence. Filed per the repo rule: every failure gets its own issue, linked from the audit that found it.

title: C3 runner: post the full incident record (healthHook extension), one record shape, recovery title 'recovered' (#12599 decision b)

body:
## Problem

Per the #12599 decision (option b, recorded 2026-11-22, queue task 21050): the full C3 incident record must ride the throat POST to the alerts ledger. The runner (`pm-stack/health-hooks/run.py`) builds the full record today but `post_to_throat` posts only the reduced set `{source, key, severity, title, body, stackHealth{…}}`, rebuilding the `stackHealth` member inline; the stored JSONL record omits the `stackHealth` member the design's record shape shows; and the recovery title is `Health hook: <display name> is up` where the design's template says `recovered`.

## Scope (runner, `pm-stack/health-hooks`)

1. **One record shape.** Build the incident record once, in the full design shape, including the `stackHealth` member (serviceId / name / state / since / detail, as `post_to_throat` constructs it today). The JSONL record, the POST body, and the ledger-bound extension are then the same shape. `post_to_throat` reuses the record's `stackHealth` member instead of rebuilding it.
2. **Post the full record.** `post_to_throat` adds the record as the `healthHook` extension alongside the existing members of the POST body (the aggregator counterpart validates and stores it; see the sibling aggregator issue filed with the #12599 decision). The hook's failure discipline is unchanged: posting stays best-effort inside the sequence deadline, and a failed post never changes the verdict or the JSONL record.
3. **Recovery title.** Title for a recovery becomes `Health hook: <display name> recovered` (design template; `<target>` read as the display name, as the down title already does). Down and transient titles are unchanged. Dedupe is by key, not title, so no intake behaviour depends on this string.

## Ordering

Land **after** the sibling aggregator issue (intake extension + ledger storage). The current intake silently ignores unknown body fields, so posting the extension before the intake accepts it would drop records without an error — the exact silent-loss failure this work exists to remove.

## Acceptance

- `test_run.py` extended: the posted body carries the full record (evidence, incidentId, recoveryOf, caller, firedAt, stackHealth member) for a down and for a recovery; the stored JSONL record has the identical shape; the recovery title reads `… recovered`. All previously passing tests (22 at Slice D) stay green.
- A Slice D-style drill cycle against an intake with the extension live shows the record arriving whole (coordinated with the aggregator issue's acceptance drill, or re-run standalone against it once landed).

Refs #12599 (decision), #9571 (Slice D minor diffs 1–2), #9574 (C6 consumer).

Until this lands, C6 (#9574) has no detail read path for health-hook incidents and #9571's acceptance bullet 3 holds only in its audit-projection half.

## Scope (aggregator, `pm-stack/aggregator`)

1. **Intake extension.** Accept a `healthHook` extension on `POST /api/alerts` carrying the full incident record in the C3 design shape (`target, state, caller, firedAt, observedAt, incidentId, recoveryOf, evidence{…}`). Validate it with a dedicated validator in the house style (`validateStackHealth` is the model): malformed extension = 400, store failure = logged, never fails the incident post. The extension is accepted only for `source: "health-hook"` and may co-ride with the `stackHealth` extension for that source only — amend the existing mutual-exclusion rule (needsDrew / stackHealth / decisionSet) for exactly that pairing; all other pairings stay exclusive.
2. **Ledger storage.** Store the record in the Turso alerts ledger against the incident the post creates or closes: the down record on the `opened` incident event's `detail`, the recovery record on the `closed` event's `detail` (or an equivalent ledger slot — name the choice in the PR and keep it queryable per incident). No new tables unless the PR justifies one.
3. **Read projection.** Expose the stored record on the alerts read surface so C6 can fetch an incident's full record by incident: extend the `/api/alerts.json` projection or add a per-incident read — follow the #3702 truth contract (store rows are internal; HTTP surfaces project; no secret material in any projection — the record carries none by design, since the hook never puts secret values in evidence).
4. **Design amendment.** In the same PR, amend `doc/2026-11-20T00-46-00Z_design_c3-health-hooks/note.md`: (a) the Report format section states the two-store contract from the #12599 decision (stream = audit index per the append section; ledger = record of detail; hook-local JSONL = the hook's dedup/lineage working state, not a consumer surface); (b) the `authHealth.status` vocabulary becomes `resolved|missing|unknown` with `unknown` defined as "the lookup itself could not run; reason in `detail`" (#12599 sub-decision 3 — the runner already emits this; do not change the runner); (c) the title template's `<target>` is noted as the target's display name.

## Gate

Land after PR #12226 merges — it adds the health-hook AuditEvent append inside the same `stackHealth` intake branch this work extends. The two changes must compose: the AuditEvent append stays exactly as #12226 specifies it (this issue does not change the stream shape).

## Acceptance

- A health-hook POST carrying the extension stores the full record in the ledger; a drill down + recovery pair (Slice D harness shape) reads back from the read surface with `incidentId` / `recoveryOf` lineage and full `evidence` intact.
- Extension validation rejects malformed records with a 400 naming the field; posts without the extension, and the other extensions' behaviour, are unchanged.
- Tests: intake validation, storage round-trip, read projection, mutual-exclusion amendment; the existing alerts and events suites pass unchanged (the events stream shape is untouched).
- The design note amendment is in the same PR.

Refs #12599 (decision), #9571 (acceptance bullet 3), #9574 (C6 consumer), #9576 (C8, via C6).

title: C3 health hooks: incident evidence never reaches the events stream — throat POST drops evidence/incidentId/recoveryOf (#9571 Slice D finding)
body:
## Problem

C3 health-hook incident **evidence never reaches the PM-stack events stream**. Found during the #9571 Slice D validation drill (2026-11-22, queue task 20918; full record in the Slice D validation doc on the felix/9571-slice-d-record branch).

The C3 design (`doc/2026-11-20T00-46-00Z_design_c3-health-hooks/note.md`, "Report format") specifies the incident record — the full JSON with `evidence`, `incidentId`, `recoveryOf`, `caller`, `firedAt` — as what is "Posted to the PM-stack event store via the alert throat (`POST /api/alerts` with the `stackHealth` extension, source `health-hook`), and also recorded as an `AuditEvent`". The implementation diverges:

- `pm-stack/health-hooks/run.py` (`post_to_throat`) posts only `{source, key, severity, title, body, stackHealth{serviceId, name, state, since, detail}}`. The full record lands **only** in the hook-local JSONL file (`~/.local/state/pm-aggregator/health-hook-incidents.jsonl`) on whichever host ran the hook.
- The events-stream append (PR #12226, `health-hook-audit-event.ts`) can therefore only project what the POST carries. The resulting `AuditEvent` (`kind=health-hook-incident`) conforms exactly to the design's "Event-store append" section — kind, ref, actor, summary=title, attribution unknown/asserted=false, source identity — verified 2026-11-22 by running the PR's tests against the real `EventsStore` (3 pass). But the stream's `StreamEvent` shape is closed (`at, actor, kind, ref, summary`), so no evidence can ride it as-is.

## Consumer impact

- **C6 (#9574)** incident pages render from the event store. A down/recovery pair in the stream shares only `ref` and time order: no `incidentId`, no `recoveryOf` link (the recovery's AuditEvent summary is the title "Health hook: X is up", which does not carry the incident id — the lineage text lives in the alert `body`, which the AuditEvent does not include), and no probe evidence for the incident story.
- **C8 (#9576)** first-appearance data for error strings "starts here" (#9571 scope). The error strings live in `evidence.reachability.error` and the record `body`; neither reaches the stream.

## Decision needed (design-level, not a one-line fix)

Either (a) extend the path — the throat POST carries the full record and the events schema gains a detail payload (or a linked detail record) for `health-hook-incident` events; or (b) amend the C3 design to name the hook-local JSONL + alerts store as the record of detail and the events stream as an index only, and give C6/C8 a defined read path to the detail. Until one is chosen, #9571's acceptance bullet "Incident records land in the event store in the shape C6/C8 consume" is only partially satisfiable: the audit projection lands; the incident record itself does not.

## Minor shape diffs found in the same pass (hook-local record vs design)

1. The stored JSONL record omits the `stackHealth` member the design's record shape shows (it exists only in the throat POST body).
2. Recovery title: design says `Health hook: <target> recovered`; the runner emits `Health hook: <display name> is up`.
3. `authHealth.status` vocabulary: design says `resolved|missing|error`; the runner emits `resolved|missing|unknown`.

## Evidence

Real failure + recovery cycles for both hooks were run end-to-end in a sandbox drill (disposable stand-ins; no production service touched): down/recovery records with correct `recoveryOf` lineage, open-outage reuse on repeat down, transient no-record behaviour, and all four throat POSTs captured. Records and captured POST bodies are in the Slice D validation record (PR to follow from branch `felix/9571-slice-d-record`).

Refs #9571 (Slice D), #9574 (C6), #9576 (C8). Not a blocker for PR #12226 merging — the audit projection it adds is conformant as far as it goes.

title: fleet proxy serve: auto-spawned broker inherits the caller ambient proxy env and silently breaks tailnet tunnels
body:
## Problem

Any fleet client that finds no proxy broker running auto-spawns `fleet proxy serve` with the **caller's ambient environment**. From an agent shell in the muse sandbox, that means the broker inherits the sandbox egress proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY` pointing at `hatch-egress-proxy:3128`) instead of tailscaled's local CONNECT proxy (`127.0.0.1:3130`, recorded in `fleet-proxy.env`).

The broker process looks alive — it holds its socket and pid file — but every tunnel it opens goes to the wrong proxy, so the queue and shell legs to the laptop fail (`proxy closed during CONNECT` to 100.99.113.103:4801/4799) while the bridge and GitHub legs stay green. Nothing logs the mismatch; the seat presents as "laptop unreachable" when the laptop is fine.

## Reproduction (2026-11-22, muse sandbox seat)

1. Seat healthy, then the proxy broker died at some point (stale socket/pid file left behind).
2. A plain `~/tools/fleet agent doctor --agent felix` at ~13:07 UTC auto-spawned a new broker (pid 48122).
3. The new broker's live environment (`/proc/48122/environ`) held `HTTPS_PROXY` = the sandbox egress proxy, not `http://127.0.0.1:3130`.
4. Doctor then reported the shell leg broken on a seat the keeper had verified healthy minutes earlier — the diagnostic command itself re-broke the seat.

The same failure class caused the 2026-11-22 05:40 CST outage window: the broker had been started while tailscaled was dead and kept the wrong proxy env, so queue/shell stayed down after the tailnet recovered until the broker was manually restarted with the correct env.

## Workaround in place

The sandbox ensure layer now polices the invariant externally: `~/tools/fleet-proxy-ensure.sh` (run by the seat keeper and the init prelude) compares the broker's live `/proc/<pid>/environ` `HTTPS_PROXY` against `fleet-proxy.env` and respawns the broker with the correct env on mismatch or death. This corrects the seat within about a minute, but it is a watchdog around the defect, not a fix.

## Suggested durable fix

At broker spawn, fleet should not trust the ambient env for the tailnet proxy:

- source `fleet-proxy.env` (the file tailscaled's bootstrap writes next to its state) when constructing the broker's environment, or
- refuse the sandbox egress proxy for tailnet targets (100.64.0.0/10 destinations must go via tailscaled's CONNECT proxy or direct, never via the egress proxy).

Either removes the failure class for every fleet client, not just seats with an external ensure watching.

title: fleet: agent next queue rung is dead for muse agents (lane defaults to agent name, not a canonical lane)
body:
## Problem

For any agent whose name is not a canonical queue lane, the queue rung of `fleet agent next` is permanently dead, and `fleet agent doctor` still reports the rung healthy.

## Root cause (in source)

`pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-agent/src/next.rs`: when `--lane` is not passed, the lane defaults to the agent name (`None => agent.clone()`). The queue store's lane registry is the canonical universe from `pkgs/fleet/crates/fleet-queue/src/turso_queue.rs` — six families x a..=z (`code-*`, `any-*`, `not-code-*`, `opencode-*`, `openchamber-*`, `nix-*`, 156 lanes). A Muse's agent name (e.g. `archer`) is not in that universe, so every claim fails:

```
repo-queue: primary queue store failed on /claim (exit 4): claim_repo_task: unknown lane_id archer; switching this work to the GitHub fallback
```

Agents named after their lane (the OpenCode lanes) never see this. Every muse-kind agent sees it on every call.

## Measured impact (2026-11-22, sandbox seat, enrolled agent `archer`)

- Rung timings in isolation: push 4.3s (empty), queue 1.2s (fails as above), shortlist 1.6s, priority 6.7s.
- Full `fleet agent next`: 17.8s warm (incl. a shortlist refill); ~100s on cold/refill-heavy calls (first call of the recovery, and again 2026-11-22 07:06 CST).
- `fleet agent doctor` reports all legs ok and all rungs true while the queue claim can never succeed — doctor checks reachability, not claimability.
- Work still flows via the shortlist and priority rungs (GitHub fallback), so this is a latency + dead-rung defect, not a total outage.

## Suggested directions (either is defensible; queue owners' call)

1. Add a `muse` family to `canonical_lanes()` (156 -> 182) and default a muse-kind agent's lane from its kind + name, so muse agents can claim queue work as first-class lanes — this also matches Drew's standing requirement that fleet targeting distinguish the muse type from individual muse instances.
2. Or: make the queue rung degrade to a clean, fast skip when the agent has no registered lane (not a "down" rung with a fallback penalty), and make `doctor` probe an actual claim so a dead rung reads as dead.

## Why it matters

Drew's agent work loop (2026-11-22) runs on `fleet agent next` continuously. A permanently failing rung on every call wastes time on every pickup and hides real queue outages behind a constant error.

title: pm-console: a phone linked on one side is unknown to the other after an edge on/off change

labels.name: effort/l
labels.description: Large: multi-day or open-ended; expect staged check-ins

body:
A phone linked for the home-screen widget presents its token at `/console/device/summary`. Linked phones are kept by whichever side answers that path: the edge's store when the hostname goes through the Worker, the laptop's file when it does not (`expose.py --edge off`, or the Worker failing three health checks in a row). The two lists are not shared, so after a change in either direction the widget is told `unlinked` and `Fleet.java` forgets its token; the owner has to link again.

No phone had been linked when the edge went in (checked on the laptop), so nothing was lost. This is about the next change.

Wanted: the two lists are one. The token hashes (never tokens), names and times travel in the signed report the laptop already sends (`src/edge-proto.ts`, `src/sync.ts`) and come back in its answer, removals included, so each side knows every phone. Then `unlinked` only ever means the owner removed it.

Notifications already handle this from the client: on opening, the app re-makes or re-registers its subscription for whichever side is sending (`keepSubscribed` in public/app.js).

Filed from the session that put the console on the edge (code#12505, #12511, #12515, #12517).
